> “**An endless night has arrived on Great Bear Island. Use your wits, and whatever you can find, to survive.**”
**4 Days of Night**, abbreviated as **4DON**, was an annual Halloween-themed event in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.
It was discontinued in 2020 after being replaced by _[Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md)_, a 2 week event that was shortly turned into a standalone challenge.
- Light sources (ex. [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), [flares](./Flare.md), and [fires](./Campfire.md)) last twice as long as usual
- Strategically located [Pumpkin Pie](./Pumpkin%20Pie.md) with [warming](./Warming%20Up.md) and [wildlife](./Wildlife.md) deterrent capabilities
- [Jack-o-Lanterns](./Jack-o-Lantern.md) that mark the location of rare loot and valuable loot caches

4 Days of Night is one of two temporary in-game events that have been hosted, along with [Winter's Embrace](./Winter%27s%20Embrace.md). In 2016, the event was introduced to the regular mode making participation was mandatory to all players as there was no way to avoid participating the event at all. As of 2016, 4 Days of Night was only available to Steam users and was not accessible on console versions of the game.
In 2017, the event was sequestered to a beta branch of the game available through the Steam client, meaning that participation is entirely optional.

Since the event is essentially a new game, all stats and settings are reset for the duration of the event. As gamma contrast have to be adjusted again, it's worth looking up the value of the setting before downloading the new content, in order to keep the darkness at the same level during the event.

4 Days of Night for 2018 has introduced new daily challenges, as well as two new badges, the Twilight Badge and Midnight Badge. Players must survive two real-time hours per day for any two days of the event to earn the Twilight Badge, and survive two real-time hours per day for all four days of the event to earn the Midnight Badge. Players could also now choose to participate in the event by selecting the mode from the main menu and was also made available for console for Playstation 4 and Xbox One.
"_Wildlife have vanished. Use this time to explore and gather supplies for the long nights ahead. Survive at least two real-time hours to make progress towards 4DON Rewards._"
"_Wolves have returned to Great Bear Island, watch out! Survive at least two real-time hours to make progress towards 4DON Rewards._"
"_With the Aurora in the sky, wolves are even more dangerous. Beware! Survive at least two real-time hours to make progress towards 4DON Rewards._"
"_A monster blizzard has arrived. Don't stray too far from your fire, or else! Survive at least two real-time hours to make progress towards 4DON Rewards._"

![XpMode FourDaysOfNight resources.assets 566](../assets/XpMode_FourDaysOfNight-resources.assets-566.png) During the event the player will have to explore and scavenge in the world partially submerged in darkness. The primary goals of the game are still the same but some things have been changed since the player would get stuck otherwise. This means crafting, reading and repairing are possible to do in complete darkness. The visibility limitations of fog, storms and blizzard are even more apparent in the night, but likewise a starry sky can provide almost day-like view outside. It can however be easier to sleep off a blizzard, as a regular sleeping pattern is not as important when there is same amount of light outside all day.

Only a set amount of regions are explorable during the event, with the rest being blocked off (ex, the rope to Timberwolf Mountain is missing in Pleasant Valley). Only Coastal Highway, Pleasant Valley, Mystery Lake, Winding River, Cinder Hills Coal Mine, and The Ravine are explorable, but Jack o' lanterns only spawn in the first 3 regions.
There appears to be a slight increase to the amount of [lantern fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) and [jerry cans](./Jerry%20Can.md) spawning in houses.

Outside some houses, small bowls containing a mix of 3-4 [candy bars](./Chocolate%20Bar.md) and [energy bars](./Energy%20Bar.md) can be found. During the event, the candy bar has its calorie value raised to 2500, although the energy bar still only provides 500 calories.

The in game clock in the top right on the HUD does not move from midnight during the event, but rather switches between early night (the moon is placed in the left side) and late night (the moon is placed in the right side).
- Since the sun never rises, items such as [magnifying lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md), among others, are essentially useless.

- A discrepancy was created with the 2018 version, with the Pumpkin Pie being made available on Day 4 with a description that it will ward off wildlife, despite Day 4 featuring a blizzard and therefore containing no wildlife whatsoever.

Bread is about 2 parts flour to 1 part water. Add equal parts salt and rising agent, a small pile about the size of a quarter (Yeast if you're lucky, baking soda if you're not.) Raw dough should be tacky but not wet after kneading. Heat at 400F/200C for 30 minutes if the oven works. As a plant goes to seed in the fall, a period of hibernation sets in until spring. As the weather warms, plant seeds into loose soil with plenty of sun. Keep moist but not wet. If the final frost has not passed, keep seedlings indoors at night, as a single shock of cold can stun if not kill young plants outright. This quest corresponds to a cache locked behind a combination lock found on Floor 1 of the [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) mine near the entrance and near a [Receiver](./Receiver.md). The quest begins after picking up all 3 Forest Talker notes in the mine. You will get a document called "[Forest Talker Letter](./Forest%20Talker%20Letter.md)."
- One of the numbers involves a light system on the second floor. Find the Marker to see the light

Clue two is found on floor 2, in the area where there's a bed and 3 lockers. It's up on a wooden rampart with a corpse and a marked X on the floor. By standing on the floor, you see a light flash in the distance. By counting the number flashes, you will get the second number

Clue three is found on 5-6 signs on the 2nd and 1st floors. Presumably you've grabbed the detonators on floor 2 near the area with the bed and 3 lockers. Grabbing the detonators allows you to use the bolt cutters to cut the chain lock on the fence door nearby. Grab all the items you want to bring with you from the mine. Cut the chain. Then proceed towards the exit. You will find a series of signs, each with a letter marked off with an X. After noting the signs on floor two, take the elevator and go to floor 1. Continuing on you want to follow the exit signs. When you assemble the crossed out letters they spell out the first number.

Eventually you will reach the area with the phone and it will ring. Walking past it you will see a wooden structure with a square marked on its face. This is the door with the combination lock. Put in the combination to unlock the cache.
Once you find all of the notes, you can pick the lock without knowing the combination, similar to opening a [safe](./Safe.md).

**A Sewing Primer** is a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) used to improve the [Mending](./Mending.md) skill. It can also be used as Fuel when starting a [Fire](./Fire.md).

_A Sewing Primer_ can be researched for 5 hours that can be broken into multiple 1-hour minimum research sessions. 10 [Mending skill points](./Mending.md#Skill_levels) are awarded on completing the research. By selecting the Settled Mind [Feat](./Feats.md), research time will be reduced by 20%, putting it at 4 hours.
- [Warmth](./Warmth.md), [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Thirst](./Thirst.md), and [Hunger](./Hunger.md) exceed 0%

If the player's fatigue, thirst or hunger meters go down to zero or if the environment becomes dark during a research session, the session will be terminated instantly. The hour of research that was in progress will not be completed and any time that had already been spent will be wasted. For a multiple-hour research session, only the incomplete hour will be lost, all the previous hours will still count towards completion of the book.

**A page from an old newsletter.** is a [Collectible](./Collectibles.md) in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) found on a table next to the [Trader](./Trader.md) [Radio](./Radio.md) in [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) in [Mystery Lake (region)](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md).

As discussed at our last meeting, we're pleased with how many volunteers have stepped up to host a radio for our new emergency network plan. As of tomorrow, we'll have civilian broadcast capability from nearly every community on Great Bear. We're confident this will give us good coverage for enabling two-way emergency transmission from the coast all the way to the Far Territory.
If you're near one of these locations, and would like to volunteer for a shift monitoring the radios, please see the Corps officer in your locale about signing up.
With tremors increasing, building a durable radio network could make all the difference when the big one hits.

The Abandoned Harris Home can be found by following the road that splits through the Old Island Connector region.

The Abandoned Harris Home consists of three ruined buildings. Outside, a swing set, a bench, a [car](./Car.md), and a mailbox are also present; a [deer](./Deer.md) carcass and a few pieces of [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) may lie in the vicinity.

Behind the building is a [Basement (Crumbling Highway)](./Basement%20%28Crumbling%20Highway%29.md) accessible through a bulkhead door, with a few supplies that may be found inside. The basement provides a cold but indoor sheltered place to sleep.

Provides some shelter **Abandoned Lookout** is small, abandoned lookout tower located to the north in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md).

Abandoned Lookout is a tower that sits on a hill to the far north-west of the [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) and north-east of [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md). The Abandoned Lookout is situated very close to the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) transition area for [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md). This makes it a stop for almost anyone heading to Pleasant Valley. The lookout is much more sparsely decorated compared to the [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md).
It's possible to deploy a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) from the embankment on the south side of the lookout.

While it can be a useful camp, Abandoned Lookout generally makes a poor base. It lacks the luxury of having many storage containers, which is a problem for anyone looking to survive for a long period of time. It also lacks a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), and is very far from any buildings to scavenge from. It also does not have many renewable sources of food (i.e., game or fish), fuel, or medicinal flora close by.
The [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) and [Jackrabbit Island](./Jackrabbit%20Island.md) make for much more suitable safehouses.

- Unlike other houses and non-destroyed structures, entering Abandoned Lookout does not cause a loading screen to appear. Instead, the when the door is opened, the player may walk inside, with no change of scene. This allows the player to see through the windows outside, as well as a quick way to enter and exit the safety of a home.
- Because of the many flights of stairs you need to climb to reach the main section of Abandoned Lookout, it is not an ideal place to go when you are evading hostile wildlife.
- The height of the lookout does provide protection for the player from attackers below.
- The height of the lookout also allows the player to get a view of their surroundings without having to do much exploration.

**Abandoned Mine No. 5** is a vacant coal mine that runs most of the length of Desolation Point.

It is abundant in [Coal](./Coal.md), which burns at very high temperatures. Coal can be used in most fires, but it is particularly important for fueling the [Furnace](./Furnace.md), which, along with the [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) allows the player to craft certain key items. A [Torch](./Torch.md) is always found near the eastern access entrance, regardless of difficulty. It also has a [Salt Deposit](./Salt%20Deposit.md) located about halfway through.

The mine is dark but predominately linear. It is highly recommended that anyone venturing into the mine brings with them a light source, such as a [Flare](./Flare.md) or a fueled [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md).

While it is feasible to make it through the cave without a portable light source, it can be almost impossible (particularly during the day), and it is easy to miss important loot that might be scattered about.
**Categories:** Caves, Indoor locations, Locations, Locations in Sundered Pass · **Source:** [Fandom](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Abandoned_Mine)

Has an interior **Abandoned Mine** is a mine located in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md), close to [Reluctant Shortcut](./Reluctant%20Shortcut.md).

It is located a short walk down the hill from the cabin at [Final Refuge](./Final%20Refuge.md), and then up a small plateau and across a tree bridge (past [Bolt Chopper's Haven](./Bolt%20Chopper%27s%20Haven.md)) into the mountains, then past Reluctant Shortcut. The mine, being an interior space, is a naturally large indoor cavern, converted into a mine long since abandoned. It is quite linear in its layout, with [Coal](./Coal.md) and [Stones](./Stone.md) occasionally found on the cavern floors along with [Barrels](./Barrel.md) and [Crates](./Crate.md). The coal may be useful to survivors who are trying to survive at [Unyielding Inundation](./Unyielding%20Inundation.md) or [Placid Notch](./Placid%20Notch.md), in order to help make up for the lack of firewood on the alpine plateau.

A [Hidden Cache](./Hidden%20Cache.md) can be found near the middle of the mine, next to a large pillar. A small path diverging from the exit can be found after this point, with the path to the right leading to a break area with a table, a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md), and several [Lockers](./Locker.md).
The exit leads to a large field on the other side of the mountain, later branching into 3 paths with several [Wolves](./Wolf.md):
- A path to the left down a [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) ([Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) needed) section to the marsh behind the [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md).
- A path to [Second Pillar](./Second%20Pillar.md), across a pond with [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) and down a one way drop, then across a tree bridge.

**Accelerant** is a tool that aids in lighting fires. It comes in a container labeled _Quickflame_ and stacks in the inventory.
One entire bottle of accelerant or 0.3 liters of [Kerosene](./Kerosene.md) when starting a fire to increase the probability of the fire igniting by 40%.

As accelerant is non-renewable beside from the rare spawn chance from [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md), [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) can be acquired from cooking fish. Accelerant is lighter than 0.30 L of kerosene (0.24 kg plus the 0.10 kg container). In other words, it is best to use kerosene to start fires and keep accelerant on the player for emergencies, such as when starting a fire to hold wolves at bay, or when in imminent danger of freezing to death.

[Acorns](./Acorns.md) can be found in the wilderness beneath [Oak Trees](./Oak%20Tree.md) by searching patches of discolored snow beneath the trees. Acorns can be shelled into [Prepared Acorns](./Prepared%20Acorns.md) and either cooked to make [Acorns (Cooked)](./Acorns%20%28Cooked%29.md), or bundled into [Prepared Acorns (Large Portion)](./Prepared%20Acorns%20%28Large%20Portion%29.md) and cooked into [Acorns (Cooked - Large Portion)](./Acorns%20%28Cooked%20-%20Large%20Portion%29.md). At this point they can be consumed as a food item, but they may also be hammered with a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) into Acorn Grounds.
Acorn Grounds can be used to make [Cup of Acorn Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Acorn%20Coffee.md), or can be used as an ingredient to make several Recipes.

**Acorns (Cooked - Large Portion)** are a natural [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.
Acorns (Cooked - Large Portion) are worth 4 times the calories than that of [Acorns (Cooked)](./Acorns%20%28Cooked%29.md), but also weigh 4 times more than regular Acorns (Cooked).

It is much more efficient to turn [Prepared Acorns](./Prepared%20Acorns.md) into [Prepared Acorns (Large Portion)](./Prepared%20Acorns%20%28Large%20Portion%29.md) and then cook the large portion, as it costs 0.25 liters of [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) to cook one Prepared Acorns into Acorns (Cooked - Large Portion) versus 1.0 liters to cook 4 Prepared Acorns into 4 separate [Acorns (Cooked)](./Acorns%20%28Cooked%29.md).

1 Acorns (Cooked - Large Portion) can be processed into [Acorn Grounds](./Acorn%20Grounds.md) using a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md). The action is performable everywhere and takes 10 minutes of in-game time.

**Acorns (Cooked)** are a natural [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.

Cooked Acorns, while not a calorically dense food, having just over half the calories of a [Cat Tail Stalk](./Cat%20Tail%20Stalk.md), do have the small perk of not draining thirst. However, since Acorns cannot be eaten raw and require water to cook, they still require the use of extra water and must be prepared first. Cooking [Prepared Acorns](./Prepared%20Acorns.md) in portions of four (0,5L water) is more resource efficient than one at a time (0,25L per acorn)

4 pieces of Acorns (Cooked) or 1 piece of Acorns (Cooked) - Large Portion can be processed into [Acorn Grounds](./Acorn%20Grounds.md) using a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md). The action is performable everywhere and takes 10 minutes of in-game time.

Hardy seeds of [Oak Trees](./Oak%20Tree.md), **Acorns** can be found at the base of any dormant oak tree, buried underneath patches of snow. The trees themselves are distinguished by their stout stature and sprawling, bare branches compared to the surrounding conifers.

Each Oak Tree contains 1-3 buried Acorn patches at their base. These patches can be distinguished as brownish speckles in the surrounding white snow. Harvesting a patch always generates 1 "Acorns" material for the player.

Some patches may have already been harvested, consisting of a dug up patch of bare ground. Whether this implies that other animals/survivors may have eaten or collected them is unknown. Some unharvested patches appear as black spots of disturbed earth, others as brown dots upon the snow.

Acorns must be shelled into [Prepared Acorns](./Prepared%20Acorns.md) before they can be cooked into the aptly named [Acorns (Cooked)](./Acorns%20%28Cooked%29.md), which can either be eaten or turned into [Acorn Grounds.](./Acorn%20Grounds.md) Once prepared, four acorns can be combined into one large batch of acorns.
| [Fishing Lure (Acorns)](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28Acorns%29.md) | None | - 1 × [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) - 1 × [Crow Feather](./Crow%20Feather.md) - 1 × [Acorns](./Acorns.md) |
| [Prepared Acorns](./Prepared%20Acorns.md) | None | - 1 × [Acorns](./Acorns.md) |
- 1 tree = ~2 patches along the route from [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) entry point overlooking a pond near a fallen tree bridge.
- 6 trees on top of the cliff between the [Rickety Foot Bridge](./Rickety%20Foot%20Bridge.md) and the climbing spot.
- Several (5) trees near/behind the arch southwards (straight) from the [Many Falls Vista](./Many%20Falls%20Vista.md) climbing spot. This area is patrolled by a wolf most of the time.

- 1 tree = ~3 patches directly in front of the middle entrance to the northern ice cave. Reachable by going north from the rope climb or [Hushed River](./Hushed%20River.md), passing a small pond and then continuing along the rock.
- 2 trees = ~5 patches underneath the climb on the route to [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) transition cave.
- 10 trees = ~22 patches scattered around the [Picnic Area](./Picnic%20Area.md) and [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md).

- 4 trees = ~10 patches between the [Derailment](./Derailment.md) and [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) (1 tree on one side of the tracks, 2 on the other, one located around the bend heading towards [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md)).
- 3 trees = ~8 patches located north of the [Frozen Creek](./Frozen%20Creek.md) and west of the [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md)
Timberwolf Mountain contains several loose groupings of Oak trees. There are at least:

- 7 trees = ~17 patches above the ropeclimb from [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md), around the two [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md). Visible from [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md), beware a pack of 2-3 [Wolves](./Wolf.md) in the area.
The [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) is densely populated by Oak trees, as the region itself is rather small. There are at least:
- 14 trees = ~32 patches along the short section of rails between [Distempered Flatcars](./Distempered%20Flatcars.md) and [Loitering Marsh](./Loitering%20Marsh.md).
- 2 trees = ~6 patches near the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) transition spot.

**Advanced Guns Guns Guns!** is a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) used to improve the [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) skill. It can also be used as Fuel when starting a [Fire](./Fire.md).

_Advanced Guns Guns Guns!_ can be researched for 25 hours, which can be broken into multiple research sessions. 10 [Rifle Firearm skill points](./Rifle%20Firearm.md#Skill_levels) are awarded on completing the research.
- [Warmth](./Warmth.md), [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Thirst](./Thirst.md), and [Hunger](./Hunger.md) exceed 0%

![Afflictions icon](../assets/Afflictions_icon.png) **Afflictions** are mostly temporary medical conditions that affect the player's ability to survive.
Afflictions can be acquired by the player through gameplay, and any current active Afflictions can be viewed in the menu.
- Positive afflictions: Referred to in-game as **Benefits**, confer favorable effects and are identifiable by a green status icon
- Negative afflictions: Referred to simply as **Afflictions**, inflict harmful effects and are represented by a yellow risk or red afflicted status icon.

Benefits are temporary status effects that provide positive effects to the player. They are gained by consuming certain foods, drinks, or recipes, wearing specific accessories, using First Aid items, or by avoiding starvation.

## Afflictions

Afflictions are temporary or permanent status effects that cause Condition loss or detrimental effects to the player. Most afflictions are treatable, however treatments may require multiple doses (and time between each dose) to cure. Treatments are mostly affliction-specific, and when taken must be selected to treat affliction for their effect.
Acquiring an Affliction will always list the origin. A list of Affliction sources include:
There are 39 different Afflictions, which can be sorted into two categories: injuries and diseases.

Injuries are Afflictions that cause instantaneous damage to the player, and can be caused by falling, animal struggles, exposure to the elements, and steep terrain. Frostbite is a notable exception, being a permanent injury that occurs after the "Frostbite Risk" reaches 100%.

Diseases are Afflictions that build up as a visible yellow "Affliction Risk" and then physically deteriorate the body once the meter is full, with most diseases requiring some form of treatment in order to heal the player (though some will pass over time.) Though rare, some diseases are purely psychological in nature, but can be just as detrimental to a player's survival as a physical disease.

Players are able to view the percentage of any existing risk of disease in the Status Menu. This risk may cause disease either by reaching 100% or through a dice roll based on the current risk percentage at a certain point in time (Ex. [Dysentery](./Dysentery.md), [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md), [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md))

Actions that increase risk of disease include drinking unsafe water, consuming raw, spoiled, or predator-based food, and spending too much time indoors or in freezing cold. Players must be aware of these risks and how to manage them in order to avoid the Afflictions they may cause.

This is the mission transcript for mission 4 [Aftermath](./Aftermath.md) of [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md).
## Leave the Community Hall.
_As Astrid makes her way to the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md), the [Receiver](./Receiver.md) rings at the entrance again and Astrid picks it up._
Molly: "I want to know something. Why did you work so hard to help those strangers? Would they have done the same for you?"
Molly: "I doubt they would. You probably work all day, every day. Bust your ass to help people. Delivering babies or researching or whatever it is you do. Does anyone really notice?"
Molly: "I could have been something, too. Something more than a farmer's wife. Something more than a cattleman's daughter."

Molly: "Don't patronize me. I could have been something, but I let him stop me. I let myself be small so he could feel like somebody. I gave up everything for him, and to him I didn't even exist. I let him make me small. Less than nothing."
Molly: "There's different ways to hurt people. Some ways heal, others never do. And I told you, the wolves killed him. Nevermind that. I called to tell you something."

Molly: "There's an old radio tower. Top of the hill overlooking my farm. You can see the tower from my porch. Not sure if you can get it working, but the radio up there'd be good enough to reach Perseverance Mills. You can maybe find out about your guy. The precious mystery thing you hope he has."
Molly: "Well, I didn't know if I'd work. And...also. Girl gets lonely out here, I guess. It was nice to have someone to talk to."

_Molly hangs up, and Astrid does in suit. The blizzard that Father Thomas mentioned would arrive has finally come, and Astrid risks her life to make her way to [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) in the whiteout._
## Go to Signal Hill.

Astrid: "You're alive. Dammit Mackenzie...you're alive. And on your way to Perseverance Mills. I've got to get there."
Molly: "We both left our man behind. We both like to be alone. We're both hiding from our pasts."

Molly: "Yes, you do. I didn't kill him, you know. I wanted to...so many times. I just never had the courage. And as bad as it got at times...at least I wouldn't be alone. Being alone would be worse. That's what I told myself."
Molly: "I didn't kill him, but I may as well have. I watched while the wolves surrounded him. I knew what was coming. I had a rifle in my hands. I could have helped him."

Molly: "It all happened, in slow motion. You know, like a ballet. They were so...quiet. And confident. Like there was no other way it could end. And I just stood there, frozen. He was yelling at me to shoot. But...I couldn't They circled, and then they were on him. Like a force of nature."
Molly: "All of them. We've been in the background, in the shadows. Invisible. Overlooked. For too long. Uh-uh. Not any more."
Molly: "Ha! Maybe not. But it'll do for now." _Molly breaths a sigh of relief_ "It feels good to be on this side of the hunt. So I'm making up for lost time. Take care of yourself, Doctor."
Molly: "Tell me one last thing. Your pilot. The one you left behind? He one of the good ones?"
Astrid: "Yes, he is. But things are...complicated...between us. Let's just say...I wouldn't want to find him with an arrow in his back."

Molly: "Then I hope to never meet him. It's been good talking with you, Astrid. For a little while, you took the loneliness away. I hope you find what you're looking for. I hope you can help those people up in Perseverance Mills, and...find some peace for yourself."

**Airline Food - Chicken** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Consuming Airline Food - Chicken provides up to 620 calories of [energy](./Hunger.md) and 5% [hydration](./Thirst.md). When they were first released in the Crossroads Elegy update, they were exclusive to the area surrounding the [plane crash](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md). As of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) update, this food can be found in the [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), with their abundance affected by [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).
Airline Food - Chicken can cause [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md), and [decays](./Decay.md) more slowly when outdoors.
- There is no option to heat this over a fire spot, and the item will not become "Hot" by dropping them on the ground near an active fire.

![Airplane](../assets/Airplane.jpg) An **Airplane** is a rare stationary [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) found in _The Long Dark_.

The only intact planes that can be found are the various abandoned airplanes found near [Field 31](./Field%2031.md) in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) region. These planes contain 2 storage hatches on the sides that can be looted. 4 doors on the sides can be entered into the passenger or pilot seats and often contain small amounts of loot inside the cabin. The inside can serve as temporary shelters from hostile wildlife and the cold or can be used as places to sleep.

![Crashed Plane Mystery Lake](../assets/Crashed_Plane_Mystery_Lake.jpg) Occasionally, smaller [Plane Crashes](./Plane%20Crashes.md) can be found in the Lower Great Bear regions, but are always completely destroyed when the player finds them, with small amounts of loot and presumably the dead body of the pilot found nearby. The 2 storage hatches are still intact and can be looted and the cabin can be entered and sheltered in.

Other crashed planes are rarely found on the Island, and are almost always destroyed if a survivor does find one. Notable examples of planes include the [Crash Site (Pleasant Valley)](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md), the destroyed cargo plane found strewn across [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) (see [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md)), and [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md).

Alan's Cave is not a true cave but it provides some protection against wind chill. It can be found just west of a hunting stand on the eastern side of the region. A frozen river can be found nearby which leads north to [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), and south to [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md). There is also a rabbit area there.

In [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), a [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) is hidden in this cave. The [Crumpled Note](./Crumpled%20Note.md) marking it on the map can be found on the second level of the dam.

violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Alice McLeod's Journal 01**_
Lost my records from the previous months when my digital recorder stopped working. Going to keep notes in this journal until I figure something else out.
...can't believe it took me so long to find the Prototype! It's hinted at in various notes and cylinder recordings I was able to find but the people who hid it, hid it well...
...some exterior damage but it's remarkably intact given how long it's been out here...
...took more than a week just to melt it out of the ice. I never thought so much of my engineering work would involve carrying jerry cans of oil over vast distances...
...the engine appears to be in good shape. After some tinkering I was able to get the firebox going and a couple of cans of oil was enough to get most of the train's systems working again.

...I've checked the false wall at the end of the tunnel and I'm pretty sure I can break through it without damaging the train too much. I hesitate to risk it considering how long it's taken me to get it back into working condition but I need to explore more of these islands and the train is my only way.
...leave my tools and the workshop here for now, but will come back for them when I can. Over the past months, it's come to feel like home.
Tomorrow, this train and I leave this tomb. Who knows what we will discover deeper into the island chain.

The **almanac** is a tool that can be used in the [Whiteout](./Whiteout.md) [challenge](./Challenge.md). The almanac contains predictions for blizzards during the thirty days of the challenge. The blizzard placement is somewhat randomized, however the blizzards increase in category and frequency as time passes.
The almanac is accessible through the journal. Each day will be marked with a red "X" when it passes.
- An almanac is an annual publication that includes information such as weather forecasts, farmers' planting dates, tide tables, and tabular information often arranged according to the calendar.[^1]
- While the almanac in the game was previously formatted like a calendar, after the Faithful Cartographer update it now has eight days per week.

The almanac was first introduced in version [0.346](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.346) - also known as the Penitent Scholar update - to support gameplay for the [Whiteout](./Whiteout.md) [challenge](./Challenge.md).

Provides some shelter **Ambler's Lake** is a small lake located in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md). It is located a short walk down the hill from the cabin at [Final Refuge](./Final%20Refuge.md) and [Unyielding Inundation](./Unyielding%20Inundation.md).

The lake features an abundance of [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md) plants growing around its shoreline, and features a single Ice [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) near its center. Far to the east is a very long [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) cliff that leads to [Roamer's Cave](./Roamer%27s%20Cave.md).

It is advised to use caution in the area and to be armed, as the open plain is stalked by several packs of [Tmberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) who may attack survivors who attempt to bring their catch back to the cabin at Final Refuge.
A [Moose](./Moose.md) can appear to the west of the lake, and a [Bear](./Bear.md) regularly patrols the area.

The **Ammunition Forge** is a firebox in _The Long Dark,_ introduced in the Errant Pilgrim update alongside [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). The Forge is used to craft [Bullets](./Bullet.md) for [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and [Revolver](./Revolver.md) ammunition. Use of the Ammunition Forge, Ammunition Work Bench, and [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) are the only means to increase the [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) skill.

The Ammunition Forge is the small forge next to the main workstation used for Gunsmithing; it can be found in the [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) and [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) regions. Use of the Workbench requires light, but the forge itself automatically produces light when a fire is active inside.
In the Bleak Inlet workshop, electrified wires present around the room will be active during an Aurora, and will cause [Burns](./Burns.md) on contact and rapid condition loss.
Normal crafting and forging is not possible at the Ammunition Workbench, only the production of Gunsmithing items. The Ammunition Workbench can be used to craft the following:
- ![Can of Gunpowder icon](../assets/Can_of_Gunpowder_icon.png) [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md) 0.5 kg (1.1 lbs)
An Ammunition Forge is present to the bottom left of the Work Bench, which must be lit and fueled to produce:
Unlike a regular [Forge](./Forge.md), the temperature does not need to be raised above +150 C in order to cast bullets.
The Ammunition Workbench is unique across all of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) to two locations:
- The [Workshop](./Workshop.md) of the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)

The Ammunition Workbenches in both locations are initially sealed away behind electronically-locked doors which can only be opened during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md), and require an Access Code found on a collectible note left in isolated corners of their respective region. The code for the Workshop in the [Cannery Pier](./Cannery%20Pier.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) can be found in [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md) on the high plateau. The code for the workshop at [Blackrock Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) can be found in the mine at [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md), in a locker near where the detonators are found in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md). Once the codes are retrieved and the doors are unlocked during an Aurora, they will remain unlocked and can be opened at any time.
- [Car Batteries](./Car%20Battery.md) are extremely heavy (15kg); use a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) to harvest them into lighter [Scrap Lead](./Scrap%20Lead.md) (1.5kg).
- Crafting [Bullets](./Bullet.md) requires 1 hour of fuel per unit inside of the lit Ammunition Forge (attached to the Ammunition Workbench).
- Higher Gunsmithing Skill increases the quality of produced Ammunition, reducing the likelihood of misfires (0% chance of misfiring at Level 5 Gunsmithing).
- At level 5 Gunsmithing Skill, Revolver and Rifle ammunition may be disassembled for all of their components, allowing lossless conversion of one type into the other.
- As of Hesitant Prospect (November 2020) an average world contains 55 Car Batteries, or enough lead to produce almost 2,000 Bullets.

- The Ammunition Furnace attached to the Ammunition Workbench is the only firebox which cannot be used for cooking (possibly due to the danger of ingesting lead). A nearby [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) inside the Workshop, or one just outside its door may be used instead.

- The Ammunition Workbench is accessible in Interloper and Custom (with Firearms disabled), but has little use other than crafting [gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md), which can only be used as an accelerant for campfires due to the lack of firearms. As of Perilous Constraint, the Ammunition Workbench can be used to craft [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md), giving it a use in worlds that do not have firearms.
- No [Bed](./Bed.md) is present inside in the workshop. It is recommended to bring a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) to spend extended periods of time crafting ammunition.

- [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) is home to multiple packs of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), several [Moose](./Moose.md), and a [Bear](./Bear.md). One large pack will always guard the cannery entrance, and another will likely patrol the ice beneath the workshop.

- Bleak Inlet is very cold and windy with few shelters, natural or artificial. It also has an above-average number of Auroras at night. While its weather is less severe weather than [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), it is comparably cold to [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) and [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md).

- Accessing Bleak Inlet can be difficult: requiring either traversing [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and a cave, or two [rope climbs](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) from [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md).
- Accessing the workshop itself requires a short rope climb inside of the complex, which prevents the player from bringing large amounts of crafting materials in one trip.

- Retrieving the code for the prison workshop is much more dangerous compared to Bleak Inlet. It requires the player to climb up to the mine from the northern end of the ravine that runs through the middle of the region, along a route with two long rope climbs that have no shelter between them. A wolf might spawn at the end of the ravine. Nevertheless, there are nearby caves prior the first and after the second rope and an edge for a quick rest at the middle of the lower rope. The upper level is free of wolves.

- The mine contains one section with the poisonous fog from [Episode 4: Fury, then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md). The timer is generous to compensate for the permadeath nature of survival, but it is possible to get caught in the fog if the player does not have sprint stamina or is injured. The elevator crank is also required to raise the elevator at the end of the fog section.
- Once the code note has been retrieved, the same process must be followed as the door at the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md).
- There are no mandatory rope climbs to reach the workshop in Blackrock, which means a much larger amount of materials can be brought on a crafting trip.
- Both Access Code notes to unlock either workshop door need only to have been read to unlock their respective doors, and do not need to be added to the player's collection (though it has no weight).

I am heading out on a grid search. None of the locals have offered to help. And these blasted lights in the sky keep coming and going. Power only comes back at random.

The Angler's Den is centrally located by one of the region's low-lying rivers. Despite its compact size the cabin hosts several useful features inside, including: bed, [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md) and [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) as well as a storage trunk.

The cabin itself contains ample loot, including food and clothing, including potentially [mukluks](./Mukluks.md), [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md), [snare](./Snare.md), and a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) atop of the bunkbed. A [note](./A%20Note%20Left%20Behind.md) can be found near the Workbench. Outside on the deck several [flares](./Flare.md) or [marine flares](./Marine%20Flare.md) may be found.

With its central location, ample storage, and workbench the Angler's Den makes for a suitable [Safe House](./Safehouse.md). [Deer](./Deer.md) and a rabbit grove may be found nearby, providing plentiful food as well as a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) near [Broad Falls](./Broad%20Falls.md), enabling longer-duration fires to be lit outdoors. If lamp oil is needed, that can be obtained by fishing in [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md). The one major disadvantage of this base are the [Wolves](./Wolf.md). While they generally don't spawn immediately surrounding the cabin, they spawn on every trail leading to and from the cabin, which can make visiting other parts of the region more challenging.

Animal Fat is produced when Harvesting [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) Carcasses and can be eaten for calories, though at the high cost of acquiring [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md), regardless of [Cooking Skill](./Cooking.md). The option to harvest Animal Fat does not appear when in the Carcass Harvesting menu, as it is automatically produced when Harvesting raw meat (either directly from the Carcass or from a Quarter bag). Producing Animal Fat is somewhat similar to how cooking fish produces [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md).
There is 50% chance of acquiring [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) even at 100% condition, which rises to 90% chance when condition drops below 75%.
- [Deer](./Deer.md) yield the highest base amount amount of fat with 0.20 kg for every kg of meat harvested. Stags produce more fat due to being larger than Does.

- [Moose](./Moose.md) have the second highest ratio of fat with 0.15 kg per kg of meat. This is less than Deer, but due to the amount of raw meat on a Moose, they technically produce the most Animal Fat of any animal.

- All predators ([Wolf](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), [Bear](./Bear.md), [Cougar](./Cougar.md)) will yield 0.10 kg of Animal Fat per kg. Bears produce the most fat of any predator due to their large bodies.
- [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) have no harvestable meat and thus no Animal Fat.
- [Ptarmigans](./Ptarmigan.md) and [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) do not produce any Animal Fat despite having harvestable raw meat.
Animal Fat cannot be Cooked on a fire to be eaten safely, but it can be used in the following recipes:
| [Cooking Oil](./Cooking%20Oil.md) | None | - 1.00 kg × [Animal Fat](./Animal%20Fat.md) |
| [Cooking Oil](./Cooking%20Oil.md) | None | - 1.00 kg × [Animal Fat](./Animal%20Fat.md) |

| [Pemmican Bar](./Pemmican%20Bar.md) | None | - 0.50 kg × [Cured Meat](./Cured%20Meat.md) - 15 × [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) - 0.50 kg × [Animal Fat](./Animal%20Fat.md) - 0.05 kg × [Salt](./Salt.md) |

| [Pemmican Bar](./Pemmican%20Bar.md) | None | - 0.50 kg × [Cured Meat](./Cured%20Meat.md) - 15 × [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) - 0.50 kg × [Animal Fat](./Animal%20Fat.md) - 0.05 kg × [Salt](./Salt.md) |

**Anna Island -- Track Section 2** is a [Region](./Region.md) on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)._
- Anna Island -- Track Section 2 contains a turn circle to the west that allows you to turn the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md) around.

- The west of the map leads to [Anna Island -- Track Section 1](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%201.md), while the east leads to [Anna Island -- Track Section 3](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%203.md).

- The western section of the map houses a Railyard and a Repair Depot for repairs and refueling. This region's Repair Depot contains the unique [McLeod Ultra-Efficiency Whale Oil Heater](./McLeod%20Ultra-Efficiency%20Whale%20Oil%20Heater.md) inside.
- There is one [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) next to the western Railyard's Repair Depot, and one Water Tower and [Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md) together at the middle railyard near Criss Cross.
- Parts of the ocean can be used for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) by creating Free Form Ice Fishing Holes.

A small set of tracks goes into a mountain tunnel in this region, but the tunnel there is collapsed. Turning the train around and attempting to ram the tunnel will result in possibly getting the train stuck.
- To Anna Island Track Section 1 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 1](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%201.md))
- To Anna Island Track Section 3 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 3](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%203.md))

- Past the East Tunnel is a rock formation that goes out to see. Walking across you will find a burned out Campfire, a [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md), and 5 [Green Maple Sapling](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md).

- The second campfire is in a cave just south of the middle section of Criss Cross, direct center of the map. 2 entrances give way to a rock tunnel, with the campfire located in the middle with some [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md), a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), and some [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md).
- There is an unmarked [Whale Bone Shrine](./Whale%20Bone%20Shrine.md) just south of the previous Campfire tunnel, though there is no loot nearby.
- Some [wolves](./Wolf.md) can be found in several places in the region. Notably, at the Railyards and Criss Cross.

**Description:** A mountain track region that transitions to the next major island and 3 other Track Sections on Anna Island.

**Connecting Regions:** [Anna Island -- Track Section 3](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%203.md) [Anna Island -- Track Section 5](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%205.md) [Anna Island -- Track Section 6](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%206.md)
**Anna Island -- Track Section 4** is a [Region](./Region.md) on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)._

One of the many coastal rail regions on Anna Island, this Track Region is unique in that it transitions to 4 other regions. This will be the first proper region where the player can use the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md), having just recently acquiring it from Track Section 6.
- Western most corner leads to a bridge with an Aurora Gate that must be raised during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md). Leads to the next major island (early access part not out yet.)

There is one [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) next to the [Repair Depot](./Repair%20Depot.md), and an [Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md) just outside the Depot walls. The Repair Depot also contains enough supplies to repair the Train, as well as a place to safely rest.

Despite the map showing a set of tracks at the eastern Railyard that the player can use to turn around and head east, these tracks do not exist, and only form a Y out of the Section 6 tunnel. The tracks leading out of the previous region will always take the player west as a result, so the player will have to circle around Anna Island fully to return to [Port Remnant](./Port%20Remnant.md).
- To Anna Island Track Section 2 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 3](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%203.md))
- To Anna Island Track Section 2 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 5](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%205.md))
- To Anna Island Track Section 2 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 6](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%206.md))
- There is a [Repair Depot](./Repair%20Depot.md) at the western Railyard, just before the Aurora Gate bridge.
Much like the other Track Section regions, wildlife is quite sparse and only appears in a handful of locations.

**Connecting Regions:** [Port Remnant](./Port%20Remnant.md) [Anna Island -- Track Section 4](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%204.md) [Anna Island -- Track Section 6](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%206.md)
**Anna Island -- Track Section 5** is a [Region](./Region.md) on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)._

This is the first of the 6 Track Section regions of Anna Island, and will unfortunately have to be traversed by foot on your first trek through the region. The region is very long, so patience and preparedness are required to traverse it on foot.

A metal gate blocks the path to the most western section of the map, barring access to [Anna Island -- Track Section 4](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%204.md). A hidden mountain passage can be accessed via a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) that leads to [Anna Island -- Track Section 6](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%206.md) (the player is lead there via the [Map (Train)](./Map%20%28Train%29.md) note while following the trail of clues left behind by Alice McLeod), which will lead to the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md).
A single [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) is found in the middle of the map to help the Survivor rest while walking through the region, and two Railways can be found to the East and West of the map.
Two unmarked ponds filled with [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) and [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) can be found to the most eastern and western Railways of the map, close to the region transitions.

When revisiting the region with the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md), there is one [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) by the East Railyard near Transition to [Port Remnant](./Port%20Remnant.md) and one [Whale Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md) by the West Railyard near Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 4](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%204.md) that can be used.
[Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) is possible in this region by taking the [Path (Track Section 5)](./Path%20%28Track%20Section%205%29.md) down to the sea.
- To Anna Island Track Section 4 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 4](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%204.md))
- To Anna Island Track Section 6 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 6](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%206.md))

Your first walkthrough through this area will be an annoying one, as you will not have the train to quickly travel the region. Traveling here at night or during a blizzard can be detrimental because of the lack of shelter, so make sure you are prepared before entering the region. Several animals can be hunted and the Railyard ponds can be foraged if you are lacking in calories.
Returning with the train will make travelling through the region much easier on your second return however, trivializing survivability concerns.

**Anna Island -- Track Section 6** is a [Region](./Region.md) on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)._

A mountainous region hidden from the rest of Anna Island, Track Section 6 is initially accessed on foot via a mountain passage from [Anna Island -- Track Section 5](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%205.md), and the rail line leading out of the region goes to [Anna Island -- Track Section 4](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%204.md).

The northern section of the region is a mountainous series of bridges overlooking a deep chasm, similar to the hike to the [High Peak Plateau](./High%20Peak%20Plateau.md) in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md), eventually breaking way to the site of a rusting orange train trestle. Once the player finally finds the tracks again, a metal gate blocks the path out of the region, forcing you to head west to the Train Shelter where you can find the train and return with it to ram the gates and escape the region.

In the southwestern most section of the map, the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md) is hidden here. It is in this region that the _Iron Road_ expansion truly opens up, unlocking the rest of Anna Island now that you can destroy the various metal fences that block exploration around the Island with your newly acquire iron train.

A small detail that can be observed is that when entering Track Section 5, the tunnel leading out shows evidence that it was once bricked up, but was destroyed. [Alice McLeod's Journal 01](./Alice%20McLeod%27s%20Journal%2001.md) mentions that she used the Prototype Train to ram the brick wall and force her way into the region to hide the train at the shelter, before leaving it behind for the next person to pick up her Wax Cylinders.
There is no [Whale Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md) or [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) in this region.
- To Anna Island Track Section 4 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 4](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%204.md))
- To Anna Island Track Section 5 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 5](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%205.md))

There is a single bed, [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), and [Bed](./Bed.md) at the shelter at the Train Shelter, as well as some plants here and there that can be found. The Train Shelter itself has very few resources that can be picked up or harvested. The Train Shelter does not support [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md). All in all, there is very little reason to return to this region after acquiring the train.

**Antibiotics** are an artificial medical item used to treat [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_.

Antibiotics are commonly found inside of first aid kits and medicine cabinets, but may be found indoors, outside (usually at campfires or near [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md)) or in containers. They are usually found in groups of 6 pills, though more or less may be found; they are always found in multiples of 2.
- [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) (1 dose and 10 hours Sleep, or 12-24 hours if untreated)
- [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) (10 doses and 10 days Sleep on Stalker (20 days on Interloper))

One dose of Antibiotics consists of 2 Antibiotics pills. A single pill cannot be used, therefore they should be carried in multiples of 2. The effect of antibiotics is not generalized throughout the body, and each dose will only treat one injury, and should be applied to the injuring requiring them as treatment (e.g. "Food Poisoning" and "Dysentery" will display as separate Afflictions, with each requiring separate doses to treat).

- Upon reaching Level 5 [Cooking Skill](./Skills.md), all artificial foods and cooked meats may be safely eaten regardless of condition (including "Ruined" food), making Food Poisoning and Intestinal Parasites only possible through the consumption of raw meat.

- Infections, Dysentery and Intestinal Parasites are permanent and lethal if left untreated, though Food Poisoning is not lethal in of itself and will dissipate naturally with time (12-24 hours), but will reduce maximum Condition to 15%, making it potentially dangerous.
- Antibiotics cannot be crafted and Reishi Mushrooms do not regrow; however Antibiotics are renewable via [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) and [Trading](./Trader.md).

- The condition of Antibiotics [decays](./Decay.md) slowly over time (based on Survival Mode). Upon reaching 0% Condition, they will disappear if inside of a container. Ruined 0% Antibiotics can still be used through the Radial Menu, although this will consume all 6 pills at once. It is therefore advisable to drop the other four pills on the floor first, before consuming Ruined Antibiotics.
- Antibiotics are typically a prescription-grade drug derived from Penicillin, which is the case in _The Long Dark_ as they are labeled as "Pharmacillin".
- In The Long Dark, Antibiotics must be applied directly to treat a specific injury (similar to a Bandage), unlike real-world orally-taken drugs which generally distribute through the body.

**Antiseptic** is a [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) item used to remove [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md) gained from hostile [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) attacks.

Antiseptic bottles are most commonly found in [First Aid Kits](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md) and [Medicine Shelves](./Medicine%20Shelf.md), although there is a slight chance for them to be collected from most containers. They may also be found out in the open (e.g., on shelves).
A full bottle contains around 0.50 L of fluid, which is enough for 5 treatments of Infection Risk associated with [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) from Predator [Struggles](./Struggle.md).
Antiseptic is usable through either the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md) First Aid tab or the inventory, but only when an Infection Risk Affliction is present.
- [Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Wound%20Dressing.md) is an alternative to antiseptic.

**Anxiety** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) found within _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is one of two unique Afflictions found only within the [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) [Challenge](./Challenge.md).

If the survivor is within 200m (~656 feet) of the Darkwalker they will be afflicted with Anxiety, accompanied by a unique audio cue and dialogue. A message box will appear in the middle of the screen, detailing the distance between the survivor and the Darkwalker. While afflicted with Anxiety actions which accelerate time (Sleep, Pass Time, Craft, Sharpen, Clean, Harvest, Research, etc.) are impossible. If the survivor was asleep when the Darkwalker approached, it will automatically wake them. The closer the the survivor moves toward the Darkwalker, the more bloody the visual effect will appear.

![Archery](../assets/Archery.png) **Archery** is a Survival [Skill](./Skills.md) that involves the use of a [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) to hunt [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md).
Archery's ability to deal ranged damage means that a player can attack animals (and especially predators) from positions of relative safety.
Archery requires some practice to use effectively and several factors should be taken into consideration with its use:
- _Draw speed:_ the draw speed for a Survival Bow is a lot slower than aiming the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) (in particular fast variants like [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md))

- _Horizontal sway:_ when drawn, the bow will sway from left to right, affecting the arrow's flight path accordingly. When it tilts to the right or left, the arrow will fly a bit to the right or left of the centre of your aim. The sway increases if the player is [tired](./Fatigue.md).
- _Vertical targeting:_ an arrow's flight trajectory forms an arc. Farther targets may require aiming higher.
- _Arrow flight speed:_ arrows fly much slower than bullets, so the target's movement should be taken into consideration.
- _Usability:_the bow, unlike the rifle, cannot be fired while crouched until the player reaches Archery skill Level 5.
- _Variants:_ bows and arrows both have variants that will affect damage type, available targets, resources used for crafting or trading and much more.

The Survival Bow is a crafted weapon used to fire Arrows ([Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) and [Fire-hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) are crafted while [Manufactured Arrows](./Manufactured%20Arrow.md) are [traded](./Trader.md) for and can't be harvested). There is no aid to aiming or aim-down-sight like on the firearms, and the survivor must estimate when aiming. Bow condition will degrade about 1-2% per shot based on skill and cannot be repaired. However, the Survival Bow can be crafted at any point and there are loose spawns to be found in many regions (except on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) and [Misery](./Misery.md)).

- Arrows are retrievable; hitting soft targets such as snow will leave the arrow sticking out where it hit the snow, whereas arrows shot at hard surfaces like ice, rocks or metal will send the arrow flying around and bouncing, which can make them harder to find (their thin model makes them nearly invisible from even short distances, forcing the player to look around for where they may have bounced to).

- Arrows will loose condition every time they are shot, not from the shooting itself but from hitting its target. Arrows at low condition will eventually break, leaving behind a broken arrow model that can be retrieved and broken down to its bare components (except for the Manufactured Arrow)

- Arrows may be collected all at once by left-clicking on animal carcasses or collected one-by-one my left-clicking directly on the arrow model itself (this can be done while the animal is alive, at great risk to the player).
- [Bushcraft Bow](./Bushcraft%20Bow.md) (crafted item once its recipe has been obtained from the Trader)

[Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) are reusable, craftable, harvestable ammunition. Simple Arrows instantly kill Rabbit and Ptarmigan, and deal high damage (comparable to the Hunting Rifle) to big game with a high rate of Blood Loss on the body part struck (with Head, Neck and Torso being the best targets). Blood Loss from Simple Arrow hits is lethal (except to [Moose](./Moose.md)), though large game (such as [Black Bear](./Bear.md)) may take hours and run long distances before death.

Simple Arrows take 4% condition damage when striking snow, 24% when striking an animal, 30% when striking wood, and 55% when striking metal or ice. Simple Arrows become [Broken Arrows](./Broken%20Arrow.md) at 0% condition, which may be harvested for one [Arrowhead](./Arrowhead.md) and two [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md).
Simple Arrows persist in the world and may be retrieved later, even if stuck in an animal carcass which decays completely.

Fire Hardened Arrows function similarly to Simple Arrows, are much easier to craft (only requiring five [Sticks](./Stick.md) and five Crow Feather and any fire source, rather than [birch saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) and [forging](./Forge.md)), but will only kill [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigans](./Ptarmigan.md). They do not injure larger animals, but can cause them to flee if striking/landing near an animal undetected, or have a chance of scaring a charging [Wolf](./Wolf.md). Simple Arrows cause Morale damage to [Timberwolf Packs](./Timberwolf.md) engaged with the player.

Fire Hardened Arrows take 7% condition damage when striking snow, 47% when striking an animal, 59% when striking wood, and 100% when striking metal or ice (they may still survive hard impacts if at full condition). Fire Hardened Arrows become [Broken Fire Hardened Arrows](./Broken%20Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) at 0% condition, which may be harvested for one Crow Feather.
Fire Hardened Arrows stick into terrain and Rabbit/Ptarmigan, but fall to the ground (broken or not) when striking other animals.

A significant upgrade from the Simple Arrow, [Manufactured Arrows](./Manufactured%20Arrow.md) inflict 12.5% more damage and are twice as durable compared to Simple Arrows due to their steel alloy arrowhead and synthetic fletching and visually-striking red shaft. They have two downsides however:

- They are only acquired by trading with the [Trader](./Trader.md), which requires building up significant Trust with him (and requiring two cured hides, water and two ptarmigan feathers for every single arrow traded).
- [Broken Manufactured Arrows](./Broken%20Manufactured%20Arrow.md) cannot be harvested and rebuilt. The unique metal arrowhead is always lost when broken and the fletching doesn't give crow feathers.

Manufactured Arrows take 2% condition damage when striking snow, 12% when striking an animal, 15% when striking wood, and 27.5% when striking metal or ice. Manufactured Arrows become [Broken Manufactured Arrows](./Broken%20Manufactured%20Arrow.md) at 0% condition.

**Hunting** animals to kill and then harvest their flesh is an efficient means to acquire [Food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) and materials. Shooting animals with projectiles, such as arrows, is the most effective way to kill game while completely bypassing the animals' natural defenses. Arrows move too quickly to be blocked or dodged and can be fired from outside the animal's zone of perception.

Critical hits are random occurrences, but are more likely in an animal's designated critical areas. Shots to the head and neck seem to have the best chance to cause a critical hit, with shots to the front shoulder and chest being second. Shots to the feet are immune to critical hits.

Direct hits to an animal with an arrow that are not a critical hit will cause a bleeding wound. Animals will bleed out according to which area they were shot in. Multiple shots to the same area will not make the animal bleed out any faster. However, shooting an animal in an area that bleeds faster than a previous wound it has already received will cause the timer to reset and the amount of time to bleed out changes to the amount of time required for the new wound. This makes it beneficial to just wait in most cases, especially when shooting again could provoke the animal to attack, or flee meaning the animal would have to be tracked down again. Also, waiting via sleeping, passing the time, reading, etc. counts as time towards bleeding out, but the animal will move at an accelerated speed so will wander just as far as if you had waited in real-time.

Archery Skill is increased by scoring hits on live wildlife with the Survival Bow, by crafting Simple Arrows at a workbench, or by fully reading the [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) "_Stay on Target"._ Multiple copies of _Stay on Target_ spawn in each save, most of them at fixed loot spawns (see its section in the Research Book page), each granting skill points when fully read.
- Striking a live animal (except [Crows](./Crow.md)) with any arrow type grants one skill point.
- Crafting a Simple Arrow grants one skill point (Fire-hardened Arrows don't grant any skill point when crafted)

- _[Stay on Target](./Stay%20on%20Target.md)_ grants 10 skill points for five hours of reading or 11 skill points when using the _Book Smarts_ [Feat](./Feats.md) and four hours of reading when using the _Settled Mind_ Feat.

But we also sourced rock and stone from some quarries at the foot of that big mountain. I guess that’s why we were all there? Blackrock Mountain. There were mining folk all around that valley, so it was easy to find help to put the bones up on that prison. Some died, some would wander off. But we all got paid and the thing got done. Can’t say much for the mean look of the place but we built ‘er strong.
Nice enough place in the summer months, Great Bear, but those winters were evil things, I tell you. Wind came whippin’ down from the mountain, screaming after ya.

My husband got recruited by some old navy buddy of his. This was the early 50s, and we weren’t exactly in a good spot then. As I found out later from some of the other wives, no good road leads to Blackrock.

We had a little cabin in a hamlet a ways away from the prison. A lot of the staff lived nearby, but not all. Some put as much distance between them and the prison as possible. Even when winters made that a tough go when you had a shift.

I tried not to think about what went on up there. It changed my husband, somehow. He was a sweet man, if a little lost and unlucky in his work. Like a lot of men were back then. But our time on Great Bear, at that place, well, it left him sad in a way I can’t explain.
I tended a garden and wrote endless letters to my sisters. That’s how I remember those years. Endless writing, waiting to leave as the seasons passed.

I knew one of the first wardens out there. I cooked for him just like I cooked for the rest of them. Got to know him pretty well, as you do with folks like that. That fellow would throw these questions at me over dinner, “whadda ya think about this, about that.”
I mostly shrugged when he tried this on me. What did I know? But I had been doing the same cooking during the war. I was used to it.

He had a good head on his shoulders. Good enough for those kinds of men anyway. But he had some funny ideas about punishment. Lots of lectures and preaching type-stuff, that the land would fix them, the prisoners I mean. The Blackrock Mountain. That being in that terrible place was their mission. I never understood any of it.

I was in the first group of guards they brought out there. And it was my first job. I was just a kid still, really. Green like the trees on that freezing island.
But that was the point, I think. That place shaped the guards as much as the men they locked up there. Some of us felt sorta locked up too. Right alongside the inmates.
After a few years, I did my bit, shook their hands, and left. That was the last I saw of Blackrock.

The frequency of auroras is increased for this challenge, although they will not occur every night. As a result, it is often necessary to pass time at a location before a Buffer Memory can be accessed. The Buffer Memory displayed on screen will change periodically per Aurora, although only one Buffer Memory is needed at each location in order to complete the challenge.
The difficulty uses Voyageur settings, except for the aurora frequency, and possibly the aggressiveness of wolves.

The player starts out in the [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) fully rested, fully hydrated, and with 2000 calories, and at night with an Aurora already present. The player will have a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) and a [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md), in addition to some miscellaneous items and clothing.

In the [As The Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md) challenge, will always spawn in the [Fallen Lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md) at [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) at the start of the Challenge, with the weather set to windy.

The game is set to [Interloper](./Interloper.md) difficulty, meaning that wildlife are highly aggressive and high-tier loot (MREs, Expedition Parkas, Firearms, etc.) cannot be found. However, the rarity of loot is set to [Stalker](./Stalker.md), with clothing and food being very plentiful once leaving Bleak Inlet. In this challenge, you cannot heal [Condition](./Condition.md) by sleeping and [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) is disabled, making the only way to heal by finding and using rare [Emergency Stims](./Emergency%20Stim.md). [Deer](./Deer.md), [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md), and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) will not spawn, though [Deer Carcasses](./Deer%20Carcass.md) are still available to scavenge. [Crafting](./Crafting.md) and [Hunting](./Hunting.md) is not advised, as there is plenty of Clothing and food to allow the player to quickly run from region to region to complete the challenge.

Interloper difficulty means that you will not be able to loot warm manufactured clothes or firearms at any point during this challenge. With the amount of time it takes to prepare a bow and hide clothing, plan on completing the challenge without either. General Interloper gameplay advice applies to this challenge, with some additional points

- Predator spawns are slightly reduced compared to [Interloper](./Interloper.md), but encounters are significantly more dangerous due to the lack of healing except for [emergency stims](./Emergency%20Stim.md). Plan travel routes around avoiding their spawn areas.

- Always carry a [stone](./Stone.md) that you can aim at a [wolf](./Wolf.md) while standing on a torch/flare to scare it away. You can also, out of spite, throw it at a [bear](./Bear.md) after it just attacked you and ruined your run.

- Consider using the [Daisy Chaining](./Daisy%20Chaining.md) strategy to conserve [Condition](./Condition.md) when moving between [regions](./Region.md). By the time you leave the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region, you should have enough warm [clothing](./Clothing.md) to keep yourself from freezing too often.

- Avoid travel through predator territory at night: clear weather brings the chance of an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) which increases animal aggression and strips you of any means to ward predators off except for the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md), while bad weather will obscure your vision and impede travel.

- A [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) can often be found on the second floor of the [Fallen Lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md) immediately upon spawning. However, in the event the [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) does not spawn, you will likely not find a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) until reaching [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) or [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), so make sure you know where the nearest naturally-spawning bed is at all times.
- The lack of high-tier [clothing](./Clothing.md) gives you more carrying capacity; consider carrying more water and firewood than normal.
- Stop regularly during travel to warm up at fires; you lose 20% condition in 5 minutes of real time (1 hour in-game) from freezing.

- Making hot food/beverages while at the fire can be advantageous as it provides the [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md) benefit, in addition to immediately restoring some of your warmth upon consumption. Be aware that you can drop a beverage near a fire and it will warm up without taking a cooking slot on the fire.

- The transition cave from [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) to [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), the forge at [Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md), and the forge in the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) should provide more than enough [coal](./Coal.md) to ensure that you can easily restore lost warmth while traveling.

- Consider not visiting major loot spots unless they are on your path through a region. Locations such as the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) and [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md), for example, will likely contain great loot spots, but also require traveling through [wolf](./Wolf.md) territory.

- Food can be quite scarce, especially in the beginning of the challenge. Always weigh the pros and cons of running at the expense of extra caloric expenditure for the benefit of retreating from cold sooner.

- Familiarize yourself with the rules surrounding [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) and which foods cause it at what condition. Contracting food poisoning can do a serious number on your condition and it is generally only worth risking if you are at risk of losing condition due to hunger and if you are prepared to deal with it.
- Food poisoning will not decrease your condition while it is treated and you are sleeping. Sleep as much as possible while recovering to prevent as much condition loss as possible.
- Since food poisoning will not bring your condition below 15%, if your condition is already at or lower than that amount, contracting it is always preferable to losing condition due to hunger.

- Because [condition](./Condition.md) can only be regenerated with [emergency stims](./Emergency%20Stim.md), it is almost always worth eating food if you have it and if you are hungry. Eating food will reduce your weight and there is no benefit to delaying eating.
- When possible, try to travel close to structures / walls / cliff or mountain faces to benefit from wind protection they may provide.

IT IS ADVISED TO READ THE ENTIRE WALKTHROUGH BEFORE STARTING. AT THE VERY LEAST, READ A FEW STEPS AHEAD TO BE AWARE OF WHAT CHALLENGES AWAIT YOU AND WHICH RESOURCES ARE WORTH PRESERVING FOR SPECIFIC POINTS IN YOUR TRAVELS.

The route in this walkthrough is tailored for players less familiar with this challenge. There are more time-efficient routes and routes with less backtracking. However, this route is safer at the expense of time. Thus, it is a good route to gain experience with this challenge in preparation for more challenging routes in future runs.

This step will be the most thorough and exhaustive, as it is the most important part of the challenge. Principles in this part of the walkthrough will generally be applicable to the remainder of the walkthrough, but may not be as critical in the future as gear and resources become more abundant.
