**As the Dead Sleep**is the 7th [Challenge](./Challenge.md) to be added into the game. In the challenge, you have to visit 5 graves in marked locations around [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). It is considered the hardest Challenge currently in the game (even harder than [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md)), and was inspired by the community-created "Deadman" custom difficulty.
> “**Visit all the grave sites listed on your map. There is no time limit. As your life ebbs, death is the only barrier.**”
You will always spawn in the [Fallen Lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md) at [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) at the start of the Challenge, with the weather set to windy.

The game is set to [Interloper](./Interloper.md) difficulty, meaning that wildlife are highly aggressive and high-tier loot (MREs, Expedition Parkas, Firearms, etc.) cannot be found. However, the rarity of loot is set to [Stalker](./Stalker.md), with clothing and food being very plentiful once leaving Bleak Inlet. In this challenge, you cannot heal [Condition](./Condition.md) by sleeping and [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) is disabled, making the only way to heal by finding and using rare [Emergency Stims](./Emergency%20Stim.md). [Deer](./Deer.md), [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md), and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) will not spawn, though [Deer Carcasses](./Deer%20Carcass.md) are still available to scavenge. [Crafting](./Crafting.md) and [Hunting](./Hunting.md) is not advised, as there is plenty of Clothing and food to allow the player to quickly run from region to region to complete the challenge. ![As the Dead Sleep Journal](../assets/As_the_Dead_Sleep_Journal.jpg) The 5 graves are in the following locations:
The most common route for completing this challenge requires visiting the graves in the following order:

1. Head for [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) via [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and scavenge the area for supplies, including the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md). An Emergency Stim sometimes spawns inside, useful for the grave in Ravine Basin.

2. Leave Broken Railroad into Forlorn Muskeg and then for the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) via [Marsh Ridge](./Marsh%20Ridge.md) and [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md). It is advised to loot [Milton](./Milton.md) as it is the first place to have a large amount of decent gear, mainly clothing, food, and water. Proceed into the Hushed River Valley and find the grave.

3. From there, most players will head back through [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) and into [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md). The path can diverge to two points from here based on the player's preference:

As the player visits each grave, the thoughts of the survivor will be displayed on screen. They will be displayed in the same order no matter what order the graves are found. Notes are generated in the player's inventory when a grave is visited. The quotes are as follows:
1. I found the water. Like I promised. Where the rivers meet the sea. A bitter and empty place. You were right. ([Memento Mori 1](./Memento%20Mori%201.md))
2. We were all so cold. More than we could take. No escape from it. Please forgive me. ([Memento Mori 2](./Memento%20Mori%202.md))
3. I left you behind. My guts freezing. My feet on fire. Each step a hundred years. It was too far, too far. ([Memento Mori 3](./Memento%20Mori%203.md))
4. Why couldn't you hold out? Why couldn't I let go? Are you at rest? Is there sky above where you are? ([Memento Mori 4](./Memento%20Mori%204.md))
5. The world falling away. Did you know already, somehow? Before you left us? The lights, they used to go on. ([Memento Mori 5](./Memento%20Mori%205.md))

Interloper difficulty means that you will not be able to loot warm manufactured clothes or firearms at any point during this challenge. With the amount of time it takes to prepare a bow and hide clothing, plan on completing the challenge without either. General Interloper gameplay advice applies to this challenge, with some additional points. If you are having trouble completing the challenge, consider following the [As the Dead Sleep Challenge Walkthrough](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep%20Challenge%20Walkthrough.md).

- Predator spawns are slightly reduced compared to Interloper, but encounters are exponentially more dangerous due to the lack of healing except for stims. Plan travel routes around avoiding their spawn areas.

- Consider using the [Daisy Chaining](./Daisy%20Chaining.md) strategy to conserve Condition when moving between regions. By the time you leave the Mountain Town region, you should have enough warm clothing to keep yourself from freezing too often.

- Avoid any travel at night: clear weather brings the chance of an Aurora which increases animal aggression and strips you of any means to ward predators off except for the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md), while bad weather will obscure your vision and impede travel.

- A bedroll can often be found on the second floor of the lighthouse immediately upon spawning. However, in the event the bedroll does not spawn, you will likely not find a bedroll until reaching Hushed River Valley or Mystery Lake, so make sure you know where the nearest naturally-spawning bed is at all times.
- The lack of high-tier clothing gives you more carrying capacity; consider carrying more water and firewood than normal.
- Stop regularly during travel to warm up at fires; you lose 20% condition in 5 minutes of real time (1 hour in-game) from freezing.

- Making hot food/beverages while at the fire can be advantageous as it provides the [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md) benefit, in addition to immediately restoring some of your warmth upon consumption.

- The transition cave from Bleak Inlet to Forlorn Muskeg, the forge at [Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md), and the forge in the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) should provide more than enough coal to ensure that you can easily restore lost warmth while traveling.

- Consider not visiting major loot spots unless they are on your path through a region. Locations such as the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) and [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md), for example, will likely contain great loot spots, but also require traveling through wolf territory.
A grave headstone similar to the ones in this challenge is found outside of the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md).

**Description:** Deep valleys and high plateaus connected by rope bridges overlooking burnt, decaying trees subject to an ancient forest fire.
**Connecting Regions:** [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) (through multiple different connection points)
**Hazards and Survivability:** Lots of high rope bridges. Weather can often be poor. Some shelters scattered throughout.
> “__For advanced players. A climber's paradise dotted with narrow ravines, towering cliffs, and multiple high plateaus. Its burnt forests and mining settlements also hint at a darker history. __”
> “__For advanced players. A climber's paradise dotted with narrow ravines, towering cliffs, and multiple high plateaus. Its burnt forests and mining settlements also hint at a darker history. __”

**Ash Canyon** is the 11th [Region](./Region.md) added to _The Long Dark_ and was released on December 7th, 2020 in the Hesitant Prospect update. It was first announced in 2020 along with the Halloween event and subsequent [Challenge](./Challenge.md): [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md).

Ash Canyon can be accessed from two locations in eastern [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md): the eastern end of the [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md) basin which leads to [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md), and a transition cave east of [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md) to [Pillar's Footrest](./Pillar%27s%20Footrest.md).

The region is relatively cold (-25°C / -13°F) and consists almost entirely of wilderness: charred forests, frozen wetlands and high plateaus separated by deep canyons. A variety of bridges (artificial and natural) connect the higher elevation areas.

Traveling to higher elevations requires either lengthy detours or multiple rope climbs from the lower areas of the region. While traveling at higher elevations, there is little risk of hostile wildlife, but traversing rope bridges can pose serious risks since falling from them is fatal. In addition, the limited availability of food, especially on Stalker and Interloper with the presence of [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) in wolf and bear meat, will likely prevent lengthy stays in the upper areas without utilization of starvation tactics.

Three pieces of gear are exclusive to Ash Canyon: the [Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md), [Crampons](./Crampons.md) and the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) (not to be confused with [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md)).

The crampons and technical backpack are located inside of the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md) by a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) to the region's northwest. Similar to other mines on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), the Gold Mine's interior is dark and warm; its interior also contains shallow pools of [cold water](./Environmental%20Hazard.md) and an underground waterfall which must be passed through. The [Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md), a unique variant of the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), will always spawn in the region, though its exact location will vary in each playthrough.

Despite the challenging environment, these items make exploring Ash Canyon and other regions easier. The backpack increases carry weight, and crampons help during rope climbs and navigating steep hills. The Curator's Rifle has 33% longer range than a normal rifle, which makes hunting [Bears](./Bear.md) and [Moose](./Moose.md) somewhat safer.

Ash Canyon features steep terrain and numerous plateaus separating lowland areas (like [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md)), and offers a few man-made shelters, many of which have been severely damaged (like [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md)).

A defining feature of the Canyon is its challenging terrain: specifically numerous [Rope Climbs](./Rope%20Climbing.md), slopes which can be slid down but not climbed, and regular extreme cold. At first some locations are only accessible via winding paths through cliff sides and tunnels, but once discovered mountaineering ropes may be deployed for shortcuts in the future. [GO! Energy Drinks](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md), [Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md), and [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) are useful for emergencies, but strategic planning is best (e.g. avoiding climbs whenever possible, and careful planning).

Numerous shallow and unnamed caves litter Ash Canyon, providing wind protection and resources, but little warmth bonus. As of to Patch 1.93+ all Ash Canyon caves provide some warmth bonus, if slight, acting more similarly to caves in other regions. Constant cold, harsh weather and limited shelter necessitates regular use of [Campfires](./Campfire.md), especially overnight to avoid freezing. Firewood and sticks are abundant throughout the region, as are other natural resources including: [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md), [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md), [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md), [Birch](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) and [Maple Sapling](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md).

Wildlife is sparse throughout Ash Canyon and mostly confined to lower elevations, although there are a few rabbit groves at higher elevations and a bear spawn near [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md). Wolves of Ash Canyon tend to patrol the narrow passages in the lowest areas of the region, preventing easy travel to [Angler's Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md) and [Broad Falls](./Broad%20Falls.md). However, this means that one can travel through higher elevations with meat and hides without attracting predators, the only exception being the Bear near [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md). When entering the region from the Deer Clearing cave in Timberwolf Mountain, it's possible to reach the Mine without a single wolf encounter, although this route requires three consecutive rope climbs up an exposed cliff face. Few [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) are present and a Moose may spawn at the bottom of the rope climbs in the west; a second moose may spawn in the southeast in Bitter Marsh near the broken fishing hut (which provides shelter from wind and animals).

Similar to [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), Ash Canyon contains [Hidden Caches](./Hidden%20Cache.md). Although fewer, these contain mid-tier loot hidden in crevices, such as near [Stone Shelf Cave](./Stone%20Shelf%20Cave.md).

Work Benches are also present, including one inside Angler's Den and an outdoor bench at Miner's Folly. Arrowheads may be found at some locations (e.g., Angler's Den), enabling limited access to hunting without the need to cross several regions to the closest [Forge](./Forge.md).

[Homesteader's Respite](./Homesteader%27s%20Respite.md) provides an attractive base option. Once reached for the first time (from above), a climbing rope may be deployed for easier future access from below. It is also not necessary to climb down, as the landslide near the homestead provides a safe path to scramble down. With the nearby broken fishing hut and a lack of nearby predators, this is possibly the most sustainable base in the region, although fuel will have to be carried up as none spawns on the ledge the cabin is on.

[Angler's Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md) is also a popular base option, given that it is very central and has everything a player might need, including a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), [bunk bed](./Bed.md), and a chest. There's also three [arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md) that always spawn there, allowing Interloper players to start hunting without a long trip to [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md) for forging. Both [Deer](./Deer.md) and Rabbits can be found nearby, and the fishing hut at [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md) is not too far away. The major disadvantage of this location is that leaving the immediate area can be difficult, due to wolves in the narrow passages.

A final option for a base is [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md). Most players will prefer to live in the [Foreman's Retreat](./Foreman%27s%20Retreat.md) nearby, as it offers a stove, fireplace, and plenty of storage. The nearby Bear can be hunted, providing a large amount of food, and a few Deer can spawn nearby. A [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) near a Work Bench allows crafting without catching [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md). Fuel is somewhat limited, however [Coal](./Coal.md) can be found in a large [Cave](./Cave%20%28Ash%20Canyon%20location%29.md) nearby.

> “__I may not be able to stop this darkness from coming. But I'll be damned if I'm going to let it happen without a fight. __”
> “__I may not be able to stop this darkness from coming. But I'll be damned if I'm going to let it happen without a fight. __”
**Doctor Astrid Greenwood** is one of two playable protagonists in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. She is playable in Episode 3 and Episode 5.

Dr. Astrid Greenwood is a freelance medical doctor and the ex-wife of Will Mackenzie. After an unexpected confrontation between the two sometime before the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), Astrid seeks Will out after years of being apart. Will's skill and determination as a bush pilot make him Astrid's best hope to reach an isolated town in the north of Great Bear Island, where a patient of hers awaits treatment. After hesitating at first, Mackenzie agrees to fly her out in bad weather. During a tense conversation alluding to a shared, devastating loss, a bright flash of light blazes across the sky. The First Flare event sends their small plane crashing to the ground in the northern wilderness. The two are separated and forced to survive in the unforgiving reality of the Quiet Apocalypse.
Players experience [Story mode](./Wintermute.md) through both [Will Mackenzie's](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) and Astrid's point of view.
Astrid is indigenous with short, brown hair and green eyes. She wears a tan jacket over a red sweater, with a green scarf, a pair of blue jeans, and brown boots.

Astrid is a doctor--a researcher more than a medical provider, she says--who goes above and beyond to try to help those in need. She generally has a serious, no-nonsense demeanor, in comparison to [Will Mackenzie's](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) much more sarcastic tendencies.

Through Episode 1, we learn that Astrid was married to Will Mackenzie, but they were separated due to an unknown incident, likely the death of their child. She is a doctor who used to work at The Center, which is implied to be a health research department. It was brought to her attention that someone was sick in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), likely by someone she knows. She had left The Center, and implied to have stolen something from it.

She meets Will an unknown amount of time after asking to be sent to Great Bear Island in poor weather conditions, and he reluctantly agrees. After having a shared conversation about their loss, Astrid witnesses the First Flare along with Mackenzie and crashes into Great Bear.

Shortly after the crash, Astrid makes her way to [Milton](./Milton.md), leaving the case and her pack behind, possibly due to injuries. Upon arrival, she finds the [schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md) burning down, along with the people inside it. She tries to save them, but is attacked by a group of convicts, including [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md), and is forced to defend herself, which includes stabbing Hobbs. She is pursued to the Tunnel and crawls under the prison bus, writing 'PERSEVERANCE' in blood before escaping to the other side.

[Molly](./Molly.md) is out hunting and makes her way to the other side of the tunnel. After looking into a car with a frozen corpse, she hears a crow cawing behind her. She goes to investigate to find Astrid frozen and half-dead, buried in the snow.

She brings Astrid back to her farmhouse and sets up a bed in the kitchen. After Astrid asks some questions, and learns about the power outage, Molly leaves to find some food. She comes back with a bag of meat and offers to have meat and tea, before asking Astrid some questions. Upon asking if Molly had a husband or any family, she grows more defensive and leaves the house. Astrid gets up and looks to see if she can find out more about Molly.

Soon after, she hears the rotary phone ringing and when answered, Molly explains that she has gone to the barn and is now surrounded by a pack of wolves. She tells Astrid to retrieve the basement key under a vase and grab her spare revolver and some rifle ammo, and explicitly says to stay out of anything else. She tells her to follow the storm lines to reach the barn. Upon entering the basement, about halfway to the weapons cupboard, a small earthquake occurs, revealing a hand from underneath a blanket on a bed. When inspected, Astrid finds a dead body, similar to the painting she found.

Astrid retrieves the revolver and rifle ammo and leaves the basement, to find a heavy blizzard raging outside. She follows the storm lines and reaches the barn, maybe attacked by a wolf or two, to find a wolf carcass with two arrows pelted into it. The rotary phone rings again and Molly says she found her old bow and shot a wolf which got inside and left. Astrid tells Molly that she found the body, and Molly panics and gets angry at Astrid. Upon hanging up, Astrid finds a map of Pleasant Valley as well as a flyer for the Thomson's Crossing [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md). She believes perhaps there are supplies or other survivors inside it.

When approaching [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), she sees smoke, indicating there are other people there. When entering the Community Hall, she finds several sick [survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md) wrapped up in beds a well as [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md). Father Thomas proceeds to greet Astrid and thinks that she is from the recent passenger airliner crash, and upon denial Father Thomas thinks that perhaps Astrid has memory loss. However, he says that Astrid is in much better shape than the other survivors and thinks maybe she could help. After explaining she is a doctor, she offers to check on the survivors and see if there's anything serious that needs to be treated.

Upon examination, most of the survivors only have hypothermia or other easily healable afflictions, but however finds a survivor, Dimitri, to have type one diabetes, and needs insulin in order to survive. Father Thomas explains that insulin must be found in Dimitri's own luggage, and that as well as finding the insulin, they must also find the ID's of the friends and family of the survivors to provide closure, to regain hope. When Astrid goes to leave Father Thomas gives her his cross necklace, as he believes "its the only way he can pray for those fallen in the crash" while also taking care of those in the community hall. The rotary phone rings and Molly asks why Astrid wants to help people. She leaves a gift for Astrid in a car next to the playground.

Astrid arrives at the [crash site](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md), and gathers the ID's from the frozen corpses. However, among the wreckage, she finds someone alive crushed under a seat - Gwen. When examined, Astrid finds she is in shock, has frostbite and lost a lot of blood, but however will save her despite these injuries. Next to Gwen, she finds Dimitri's suitcase, along with his insulin. Finding everything she needed, Astrid painstakingly carried Gwen to the community hall. In a derelict house down the only exit of the plane crash, she finds the rotary phone ringing again. Molly reveals that she is spying on Astrid. When asked more about the dead body, Molly asks if not being able to help someone counts as murder. Astrid says it depends on circumstance and intent. Molly says that she didn't inflict the accident, but her intent was to kill him.

When returning to the community hall, she places Gwen on a newly provided bed and gives Dimitri his insulin. She returns all the ID's she found but 3 were still missing off the passenger manifest. Father Thomas is pleased but explains that a monster Blizzard usually comes this time of year. Usually they would hunker down with a full pantry and a warm fire, but with the increased weather intensity and dwindling supplies he is afraid they will not make it through the storm. Astrid offers to gather supplies before the storm hits, and also says how she couldn't find three passengers on the manifest. Father Thomas suspects that those survivors are out there and asks Astrid to return them.

Astrid gathers the supplies and returns the survivors, and Father Thomas is forever grateful for the things Astrid did for them. Astrid offers to give the necklace back but Father Thomas insists she keeps it, to help keep God and him on her side on her adventure. Astrid, while insisting to not be religious, takes the necklace. Father Thomas sees that Astrid has a burden, and while doesn't want her to seek faith or change her mind, tries to tell her to share her burden with someone. When asked how to get out of Pleasant Valley, Father Thomas knows of a coal mine which may lead to Perseverance Mills, and draws it on her map.

When Astrid prepares to leave, the rotary phone rings again. Molly tells Astrid that the wolves had killed her husband, and she didn't do anything to stop it. She also says that on Signal Hill, there is an intact radio which may allow Astrid to contact Perseverance Mills - Astrid exclaims why Molly didn't tell her earlier, and Molly was afraid it might not work. Molly ends the call saying how despite being a doctor, Astrid never gets noticed or praised for her work, and that Molly's husband belittled and abused her. She asks Astrid if those survivors would do the same to her, and Astrid shrugs it off.

Despite the raging blizzard outside, Astrid trudges on toward signal hill, and finds a convict with arrows lodged in his back outside of the control room. When entering the control room, she tries the radio. It doesn't work. Disappointed, she goes to bed and prepares to leave Pleasant Valley.

However, she awakes in the middle of the Aurora, to find the the lights on and the radio working. She scrambles towards the radio and tunes in to find Mackenzie and Perseverance Mills attempting make contact, with both voices being much clearer than what is heard with Mackenzie, and hears more when he gets cut off. She is unable to respond or speak to any of them. The rotary phone rings, and this time, Molly explains how she was standing outside, with her rifle, while her husband was surrounded. How he was screaming at her to shoot, but she was frozen. Molly says that she doesn't regret it, that although he was company, she was abused and made feel small, and that no one should mess with people like them. She says if Astrid would mind if for some reason Mackenzie had crossed her path and was shot, and Astrid replied that she would prefer to find him without an arrow in his back. Molly then says that she hopes they don't cross paths, before saying goodbye for the final time.

With the knowledge that her ex-husband is alive and newfound hope, Astrid leaves Signal Hill and heads into the coal mine. In the middle of going through the tunnel, experiencing several small earthquakes, a bigger earthquakes causes her to get crushed by fallen rocks, blocking her path behind. She moves forward to find a broken elevator and 3 broken fuses, and is forced to replace them.
She rides the elevator up and exits the mine into Desolation Point, and witnesses several beached whales and a shipwreck. The episode ends while she delivers a monologue.

Astrid is seen very briefly at the end of Episode 4. Having commandeered a boat and some blankets from the Coastal Highway region, Astrid has sailed her way to Perseverance Mills, where she is encountered by the locals. A guard initially mistakes her for a runaway who has broken quarantine, but recognizes her as an outsider. A [woman](./Jane%20Yang.md) that had been on the phone call in the Episode 3 flashback appears, but realizes that Astrid does not have the hardcase with her.
In [Story](./Wintermute.md) mode each survivor has slightly different skills, these skills are not shown in game directly, but some can be extrapolated from gameplay. Astrid has:
- Astrid wears a blue scarf with birds on it at the start of Episode 1, but it is mostly destroyed and its remains are used by Hobbs to make a makeshift arm sling.

- Astrid Greenwood is voiced by [Jennifer Hale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Hale). Hale's other notable works include [Commander Shepard](https://masseffect.fandom.com/wiki/Commander_Shepard) (female) in the _[Mass Effect](https://masseffect.fandom.com/wiki/Category:Games)_ series, [Jennifer Mui](https://mercenaries.fandom.com/wiki/Jennifer_Mui) in the _[Mercenaries](https://mercenaries.fandom.com/wiki/Category:Games)_ series, and [Naomi Hunter](https://metalgear.fandom.com/wiki/Naomi_Hunter) in the _[Metal Gear Solid](https://metalgear.fandom.com/wiki/Category:Games)_ series, among many others.
- Astrid evidently enjoys driving [steam locomotives](./Steam%20Train.md), as this is the only time she laughs in the entire game.
[^2]: Visible as +15% calories from cooked food, for example a [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) having 115 kcal instead of 100.

**Astrid's Hardcase** is a [Tool](./Tools.md) and [Collectible](./Collectibles.md) found throughout most episodes of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). It belongs to [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) and is one of the main plot points of the Wintermute story.
> **The mysterious case. Astrid definitely doesn't want to talk about what's inside. Which means...she's probably not supposed to have it.**

In the mission [Memories](./Memories.md), Astrid arrives with it at the [Jackrabbit Remote Transport](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md) hangar and after a short cutscene is treated as a tool. It is treated as a tool and weighs 5.00 kg, and is a required object to be placed inside the floatplane in order to progress the mission.

It is found near the wreckage of the [crash site](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) in the beginning of [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) and is picked up by [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) and carried for the rest of the episode. It weighs 0.00 kg after at this point and acts as a Collectible for the rest of the game.

The Hardcase is carried over into [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) as a key item but does not play much role in the story until the ending cutscene, where [Mathis](./Mathis.md) finds Mackenzie and tortures him for information on how to open it. The episode ends with Mathis knocking out Mackenzie.

[Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) requires the player to retrieve it once more after it is stolen by [Convicts](./Convicts.md). It is re-acquired near the end of the Episode, in the Warden's office.

As of Episode 4, it is revealed that the case contains the cure for an unknown illness which is affecting the inhabitants of [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), and that [Mathis](./Mathis.md) intensely desires having the case for his own curiosity, as well as to spite [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md).

The Hardcase is treated as the MacGuffin for the Wintermute story, as the entire plot is centered around its safe passage and delivery, despite the fact that case is treated as nothing more than a key item that stays in the player's inventory, otherwise being unimportant gameplay wise.

At the end of [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md), it is revealed that the case contains experimental vaccines against [Alzheimer's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alzheimer%27s_disease).

> “**An old friend of mine, lives alone in a cabin in the hills near [Perseverance](./Perseverance%20Mills.md). Goes by the name Atwood. People in town will know how to find them. You need to get them this message as soon as possible.**”

**Dr. Janet Atwood** is a woman who lives at the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md) facility, near [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md). In the final chapter of [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) promises [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) that he will take a message ("_Wintermute_") to Atwood.
Being unable to get a message out on the repaired shortwave radio before it is destroyed by the Aurora, Jeremiah tasks Mackenzie with delivering a message to a person named Atwood.

Jeremiah knows who Atwood is but does not reveal much about her, only referring to Atwood as "them." He instructs Mackenzie to deliver the message "Wintermute" to her in his stead (since he is unable to travel after being wounded and bed ridden by the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md)), stressing the urgency of this code word and that it may be the most important message Mackenzie will ever deliver in his life, but not specifying the meaning behind it. Mackenzie eventually heads through the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) to [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) per Jeremiah's instruction, but is ultimately captured by [Mathis](./Mathis.md).

In [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), Atwood is revealed to be [Jace's](./Jace.md) thesis professor, which means she was probably a doctor in astrophysics and/or medicine sciences. Jace also reveals that Atwood is a woman, a detail that Jeremiah did not previously provide.

While originally staying behind to prevent the [Convicts](./Convicts.md) at [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) from heading to the Suzuki Radio Telescope, Jace eventually recruits Mackenzie to keep them in line. Once it is revealed that the Convicts plan on overtaking the whole Island however, the duo eventually destroy the Prison in order to escape from the Convicts. The Episode ends with Mackenzie and Jace heading to Perseverance Mills to find Atwood, with the two bracing for the eventual fallout of Mathis and his gang following them to exact their revenge.
Atwood is slated to appear in the upcoming [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md).
- Atwood was originally described as a woman that lived alone in a cabin near Perseverance Mills in Predux Episode 2, but this detail was changed in the Redux storyline.

- A cut side mission in Predux [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), [Jeremiah's Hideout](./Jeremiah%27s%20Hideout.md), reveals that Jeremiah had a secret correspondent that he wrote to frequently, despite supposedly being a lonely hermit. Jeremiah tasks Mackenzie to burn [his letters](./Jeremiah%27s%20Papers.md) but not to read them, as in his words "reading them won't do you any good, so no peeking." Whether or not Atwood was the recipiant of these letters is unknown.

> “**There's a hidden bunker in Forlorn Muskeg that can only be opened when the aurora is active.**”

**Aurora Hatch** is a side mission in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md) and replaces the former side mission [Jeremiah's Hideout](./Jeremiah%27s%20Hideout.md), leading towards the same hatch. Completing the mission allows access to a prepper cache, which contains many supplies. However, the hatch can only be opened during an aurora. If the player does not leave the bunker by the time the aurora event has finished, the hatch may lock itself with the player still inside. Checking the time frequently while inside is advised.

The mission is started by finding the Hunting Lodge cache from the side quest "[Mystery Lake Supply Caches](./Mystery%20Lake%20Supply%20Caches.md). It contains a letter ([Aurora Hatch Door Entry Code](./Aurora%20Hatch%20Door%20Entry%20Code.md)) leading towards the hatch which also gives you the entry code for a door inside the bunker.
The bunker is located north of the [Shortwave Tower](./Shortwave%20Tower.md) in the Forlorn Muskeg region.

Upon arriving at the bunker, the player will have to wait for an aurora to happen, which they can do e.g. directly next to the hatch in the wilderness or inside a near cave, located west of the hatch next to the waterfall. In Hardened Survivor mode, the area is guarded by three wolves, so both getting from the cave to the hatch and camping next to it might have its difficulties.
Inside the bunker, first a door has to be unlocked with the given entry code. After that, the prepper cache contains lots of food and drink and also some medical supplies.

It is possible to utilize the scripted aurora even which starts right after the survivor finishes forging the anti-bear spear to reach this location with much less interaction with wildlife, take an easier route through [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and still arrive during the aurora to open the hatch.
This method results in encounter with only 2-4 wolves and even on hardened survivor will not cause the three guarding wolves to spawn.
Brew yourself a cup of coffee as at this point the survivor is probably half tired, but do not sleep.
Walking from the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) to the exit of [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) should be without meeting a single wolf.

After arriving to Forlorn Muskeg, hug the left cliff. With some luck this will attract 0-1 of the 2 wolves normally guarding the portion of the railtrack right in front of the Region transition. You do not necessarily have to shoot it, but ammo should be plentiful at this point.

Afterwards continue hugging the left cliffside, but beware of sprained wrists. You should see 2 other wolves in the small forest between you and the water. Shooting a wolf from safe distance, at this point, is preferred to scaring it, as it will make the other one run further away, and sometimes lock it in a "fleeing mode" where it will flee if you just aim the rifle at it (not reliable).

After dispatching these wolves continue a bit towards the Radio Tower, there is a place where the cliff (before the where the creek meets the Muskeg) has a patch of snow that is walkable, utilizing this route will make you avoid 2 more wolves outright.

After reaching the [Hat Creek](./Hat%20Creek.md) follow it upstream and take the first right, you will arrive to the forest behind the Radio Tower and should see the hatch light blinking at the other end of it, no wolves have spawned at this point.

At this point it is advised to save (there will also be a checkpoint inside but to be sure) as you do not have much time before the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) ends. Loot the prepper cache but do not stay inside, as the hatch will lock after the Aurora ends, and the travel here already used up a large portion of the time.

Upon successful completion of "[What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md)" Main Story Mission and starting "[Renewed Hope](./Renewed%20Hope.md)," then it will guarantee an Aurora Spawn every night until you complete Episode 2. Each Aurora lasts for 6-8 hours of in-game time.
- [Cloth](./Cloth.md), [Books](./Book.md), [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md), [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md), [Bandages](./Bandage.md), [Stacy's Grape Soda](./Stacy%27s%20Grape%20Soda.md)

Before the REDUX Update in December 2018, this bunker was a side quest given by Jeremiah as a [Trust](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md#Trust) reward. The bunker was called Jeremiah's Hideout.

![Story mode concept art of aurora affecting the electronics in street lights and vehicles.](../assets/Aurora_-_art.jpg)_Story mode concept art of aurora affecting the electronics in street lights and vehicles._
> Methuselah: "And everything dependent on it. Animating it. Or destroying it. Perhaps both."

The **Aurora** is a type of weather in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. They are a reoccurring phenomenon that is the result of a [geo-magnetic storm](./First%20Flare.md) which ended civilization on Earth. Auroras create bright, colorful lights in the night sky, make predators more dangerous, and temporarily power electronics like the [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md).

Auroras are unusual weather events on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) similar to the Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis), where bright, multi-colored lights are visible in the night sky. The Aurora is unusual in that it makes [predators](./Wildlife.md) more dangerous (while herbivores flee), and temporarily powers electronics (e.g. [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md), Flashlight, vehicle headlights, and hazards like [exposed wires](./Burns.md)). The post-apocalyptic setting of The Long Dark takes place after the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), the first such aurora which destroyed civilization. The cause of these unnatural auroras is unknown, but may be the result of an aggressive [Coronal Mass Ejection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronal_mass_ejection).

The Aurora has a set percentage set of occurring several times in a single night. Each potential aurora moment is checked internally to see if the game will start the event. The Aurora can first occur at dusk, which is noticeable because there is a chance that the Aurora sound cue and music will start playing before the sun sets completely and the player will be able to see the Aurora lights in the sky overtop the sunset colors. This first type will usually stop around one third of the night through. The second potential time for an Aurora to start happens roughly after a quarter of the night has passed. The last potential Aurora start time is at the very end of the night, from about two hours before sunrise to nearly starting at the same time as the first dawn colors appear. This last Aurora type is the shortest of the three, lasting sometimes as short as two hours.
- During an aurora, predators are more dangerous and electrified hazards are present in industrial areas via electrified wires.
- Like clear daytime weather, Auroras allow [Surveying](./Charcoal.md) but do not allow the use of [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) to start campfires.

- The night after a [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) is repaired will always be an aurora. Note that the aurora will happen after the last item required for the repair is inserted, even if the Transmitter hasn't been switched on yet.

- Completing a trade at night at the [Trade Drop Box](./Trade%20Drop%20Box.md) will instantly trigger an aurora as long as there is enough time left in the night. If the trade is completed during the day, the aurora will always trigger on the following night.

- The daytime equivalent to the Aurora is [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md), which only occurs in regions of [The Far Territory](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md) (though it does not create aurora predators and creates [Afflictions](./Insomnia.md) that the Aurora does not).

Note: [Flashlights](./Flashlight.md) "high beam" mode are effective deterrents against aurora predators (during an Aurora); however, although the [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) will also power them, flashlights will be ineffective at deterring non-aurora predators during the dynamic event.

Aurora frequency is based on game mode and region. More challenging modes (e.g. [Interloper](./Interloper.md) in Sandbox, Hardened Survivor in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md)) have more frequent weather changes and more auroras. Aurora frequency is one of the settings in Custom Mode, allowing the player to choose how common auroras will be. Each region has its own custom level for weather and dynamic events: [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) and [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) having the highest chance of aurora per night. In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), the first aurora (The First Flare) begins during a cutscene, with following auroras in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) and onward. A Wintermute-exclusive elevator at the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) becomes operational during Episode 2. Auroras are also more common during the [Archivist](./Archivist.md) [challenge](./Challenge.md).

In **[Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md)** and most challenges, auroras are uncommon but can occur in any region at night. When the Aurora is active, all electronics will come to life, including your own tools like the [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) and the [Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md). House lights flicker; car high beams will turn on and off, streets will be illuminated by lampposts once more; signs advertising the [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) or [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) can be seen from afar; [computers](./Computer.md) will turn on, sometimes revealing information from before the Flare in the form of [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) collectibles; TVs will buzz with static, radios in buildings and [cars](./Car.md) can be interacted with and, if they are turned on, will play classical music. In [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), the elevator that leads down to the lower section of the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) in Coastal Highway (located near the [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md)) becomes temporarily operational, allowing the player to access an entire underground area with high-level loot and many hazards brought on by the electricity.

Auroras have two distinct "power stages". Roughly one in-game hour after the start, the aurora reaches its full power. Likewise, roughly one hour before the end, the aurora descends to its buildup stage. Until then, only some of the effects listed below occur. Hard Interrupts occur at the start and end of the full power stage. For example predators will immediately run away, even if currently stalking or even mauling the player.

The [flashlight's](./Flashlight.md) battery can be recharged when the aurora is active. However, it will immediately die when the aurora ceases, rendering the flashlight useless until the next aurora.

In **[Story mode](./Wintermute.md)** the aurora first appears during a cutscene near the start of the game, with Will [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) waking after a [plane crash](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md). This initial, intensely bright aurora is hereafter referred to as the "First Flare", where it destroys most electronic technology. Further auroras appear in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), and periodically afterwards.

The cause of the auroras and their effect on electrical devices are not fully explained in Wintermute. Their impact on electrical systems and the unusual brilliance, along with The Long Dark's store description and survivor sandbox prompt text describes their cause as a "geo-magnetic storm", which could mean a powerful solar flare, or coronal mass ejection (CME) from The Sun hitting Earth, similar to [The Carrington Event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrington_Event).

Bulkhead-style doors in [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) ([Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)) and [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) ([Blackrock](./Blackrock.md)) are electrically powered, and can only be opened during an active aurora. Both doors additionally require a passcode to unlock (by using their [Keypad](./Keypad.md), which must also be powered). Once these doors are opened they do not require additional auroras to be traversed.

[Milling Machines](./Milling%20Machine.md) are electrically powered devices used to repair damaged [tools](./Tools.md) and [firearms](./Hunting%20Rifle.md). They may only be found in the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) ([Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)) and [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) ([Blackrock](./Blackrock.md)), and require an active aurora and [scrap metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) to operate. ![A bear during an aurora](../assets/Aurora_Bear.jpg)_A bear during an aurora_

Predators during an aurora are upgraded to "Aurora Predators", which are more aggressive (detection radius) and dangerous (more health). When an aurora begins wildlife will flee and be replaced with their aurora counterparts (e.g. Wolf -> Aurora Wolf). Herbivores (Rabbit, Deer) will flee during an aurora, and not re-appear until it ends; fish and crows are unaffected by auroras.

Light sources which wildlife fear (lit [torch](./Torch.md), [campfires](./Campfire.md)) are ineffective against aurora predators; however aurora wildlife fear artificial lights which become powered during auroras (streetlamps, vehicle headlights, flashlight's "high beam" mode).

Auroras provide temporary power to exposed electrical wiring on the floor or hanging from the ceiling and will electrify water sources that have wires in them. These wires/water sources are extremely dangerous and can kill in seconds. Each brush with a wire will instantly give a [Burn affliction](./Burns.md) to the player, reducing their condition by 25% per touch. Standing on a wire or in electrified water will give repeated instances of Burns, killing the player in four 25% ticks of damage. This usually takes less than two seconds.

Walking on exposed wiring/water when no aurora is present is safe, but caution should be taken during the night, as the weather could change to an aurora and electrify the survivor, especially during time acceleration while standing on/in a hazard (sleeping, passing time, crafting, harvesting, etc).
- [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md): Carter Hydro Dam & Environs; Upper and Lower

The [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) features an electric elevator which must be powered by an active aurora to go down to the rest of the mine. This elevator can only be used during an aurora. If the weather changes while the survivor is inside the mine, they will become trapped until the next aurora, potentially for many days, making it likely they will starve, dehydrate or die from [cabin fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md).

- Auroras are a real-world phenomena of brightly colored lights in the sky, normally only visible at high latitudes (close to the north or south poles). They can occur during the day, but are normally too dim to be seen except at night. They are created when radiation from The Sun enters the Earth's magnetosphere.

- [The Carrington Event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrington_Event) may be an inspiration for _The Long Dark_. Like "The First Flare", it was a geo-magnetic storm during the 1–2 of September 1859. It resulted in widespread auras at low latitudes: Hawaii, Cuba, Queensland, Japan and Colombia. It caused telegraph pylons to throw sparks, shocked operators, powered telegraphs (even when turned off), and was bright enough to allow reading at night.

- Radios found in buildings or inside vehicle consoles can be turned on/off through interaction. If "on" during an aurora, they will play "Glenn Gould performing Bach: Goldberg Variations, BWV988 - Variation 6 Canon"
- Desktop and Laptop Computers found in many locations can be interacted with during an aurora to receive a collectible "Buffer Memory", a short textual note or email from various characters.

- "Buffer Memory" in computer science are a region of a memory used to temporarily store data while being moved. This may suggest that auroras not only damage and power electronics, but move or manipulate data. ![Another shot of the real-world aurora in Nova Scotia, October 2024.](../assets/Aurora_Oct_2024_Nova_Scotia.jpeg)_Another shot of the real-world aurora in Nova Scotia, October 2024._

**_BLACKFROST: The Long Dark II_** is the sequel to [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). It is a first-person, open-world, survival, RPG video game developed by [Hinterland Studio Inc.](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md)

A teaser was announced in 2025 and the game was set to release in Early Access in 2026, after the completion of [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) for _The Long Dark_. However, at the beginning of 2026, the Early Access was delayed to 2027 as developers were taken off the _BLACKFROST_ team to aid in planned updates and DLC for _The Long Dark._

"A year after the Aurora’s appearance & the world went dark, the people of Harmont & its vast wild environs struggle to survive the Quiet Apocalypse. Survive alone or with others against a host of new hazards & a fresh new survival sandbox from a pioneer of the genre. Live together. Die alone."

After 10 years of developing the first game, this is a big moment for the team. While we complete the final episode of our WINTERMUTE story mode slated for release in 2025, we wanted to use the platform of the The Game Awards as an opportunity to share our vision for the future of survival games.

Years ago, I asked myself what the future of THE LONG DARK could look like. Despite pouring everything we have into that game, I still felt there were things I wanted to do with the setting, the mechanics, but also things that just aren’t possible within the current game. I knew we would have to build something new, with foundations that could support our grand vision. When we started THE LONG DARK, we had no idea we’d be building it and supporting the community for 10 years. With BLACKFROST, we asked ourselves -- what if we _started\_ a project as though we knew it would last for 10 years, or even longer? What different decisions might we make?

BLACKFROST builds on a decade of construction, experimentation, and community-informed development of an experience we love dearly. It expands beyond the ego-centrism of THE LONG DARK and asks you, not how far you will go to survive, but how far will you go to survive for others?

The “others” could be other players in co-op, but also other survivors in the world. NPC communities hiding out from the dangers of the aurora, the radioactive “black frost”, and a whole host of new threats they experience in the city of Harmont and the vast wilderness surrounding it. What new scenarios, gameplay mechanics, and stories could such a setting inspire?

We aren’t saying too much more about BLACKFROST at this point, as we are focused on completing our obligations around THE LONG DARK 1. But we hope this early look is compelling and exciting for you. We hope to enlist you in the coming months and years, in helping us build the future of survival games.

BLACKFROST won’t launch until 2026, so this is a very early moment in time for the project. And for those of you who have grown up with THE LONG DARK over the years, BLACKFROST is not the end. It is only the beginning of the next chapter. We see both THE LONG DARK 1 and BLACKFROST co-existing for a long time, with each game having a distinct point of view around the ‘Quiet Apocalypse’. They will be complementary, preserving the investment of time and money you have put into TLD over the years.

But with BLACKFROST, we are pushing our philosophy and vision for survival forward in ways we could have never believed possible when we first launched TLD back in 2014. We can’t wait to show you more of what we are building. We hope you are as excited as we are!

For now, please take a moment in your busy day to enjoy this view into the new world we are creating for you. I think it is as beautiful as it is dangerous, full of adventure, mystery, and opportunity. A place you want to survive in.

BLACKFROST: The Long Dark 2 is the sequel to the hit survival game, THE LONG DARK, launched on Early Access and honed over 10 years of open development. It is the evolution of the survival sandbox, refining every aspect of the original, and introducing co-op to the formula. Conceived of and developed by Hinterland, the same creative team that brought you the original.
The game will feature the return of various [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) and Tools already familiar to those who have visited [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).

Experience the Quiet Apocalypse as survivors in the northern industrial city of Harmont and its vast environs. A year has passed since the Aurora first appeared in the sky, rendering all technology inert, with survivors just starting to emerge to face their new reality in its aftermath. Surrounded by a majestic, rugged wilderness, encounter the remnants of an isolated society still coming to terms with how the world has just been forever changed. How will you choose to survive?

Survive as a lone wanderer in this frozen wasteland of city, town, forest, and farm, or huddle together as a group of survivors in whatever shelter you can make for yourselves. As solo players, decide how much you’ll learn to live with NPC survivor communities struggling to find their way in this harsh world. As co-op players, lean on each other and combine your skills and efforts to eke out another day of existence in the hostile environment. Alone or together, choose your own path to survival.

Built on the foundation of survival gameplay pioneered and perfected by THE LONG DARK over 10+ years of development, BLACKFROST evolves every aspect of the survival formula to its 2.0 iteration, setting the table for the next generation of survival games. Build your own survivor, customize traits and skills, collect scars and stories, and experience a life as a survivor in this beautiful yet dangerous world. Many games have tried to bring survival mechanics to their open-world RPGs, but BLACKFROST is the first survival game built ground-up as a survival RPG.

Experience the fantasy of wilderness survival at a 19th-century level of technology due to the aurora’s effects on the world and its inhabitants, and enjoy the same deep simulation of survival in nature from THE LONG DARK but with a new twist. Cities and towns offer new opportunities, and new hazards to your survival, introducing a fresh take on the established survival formula. The wilds are dangerous, but sometimes the city is where the real threats lie.

Survival is as much about what’s in your head as what’s in your pack. With BLACKFROST, your success is no longer just about your physical Condition. BLACKFROST’s new Will to Live system adds elements of psychological survival to the mix, introducing Resilience and its sub-stats to the well-established mechanics. Manage your doubts and fears, and find comfort in the small things if you want to survive.

Urban risks. The deep freeze of an intense northern winter. Extreme weather events. Aurora Storms. And the dreaded radioactive Blackfrost, emitted by the reactor complex looming on the horizon. Layered on the dangers from wildlife and other survivors you encounter along the way, BLACKFROST introduces a whole host of new hazards to the survival sandbox.

The innovative Permalife system turns every death into a new adventure. Accumulate new risks and fears for your survivor as you move through the world and succumb to various hazards. Face your fears, overcome their downsides, and strengthen your Survivor’s story in the world. Make your mark. (Classic Permadeath still an option!)

BLACKFROST is being built using Early Access to maximize the player feedback loop and the team’s ability to iterate in a cycle of constant improvement. This builds on Hinterland’s longstanding reputation as a pioneer of the Early Access model with THE LONG DARK, being the first game to exist simultaneously on multiple early access platforms and on PC and console at the same time (Xbox Game Preview launch title in 2015). Similarly, BLACKFROST will be built a piece at a time, and will launch without the game’s complete planned world or feature set. We believe this is the ideal approach to work towards strength in community-informed iteration and development, but it’s not for everyone, so please make sure you are comfortable with this approach before you jump in! More details of how the team plans to handle roadmaps, timelines, and player feedback will be released closer to the 2026 launch.

Badges are unique unlockable challenge based achievements (not to be confused with regular [achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md)) that can be acquired from playing [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

As their name implies, Badges are awarded as commemorative status symbols, and are earned after accomplishing certain in game tasks. They do not, however, provide any active gameplay benefits, unlike [Feats](./Feats.md). Most Badges are acquired from simply completing [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) [Challenge](./Challenge.md) scenarios, whereas others require the player to perform specific tasks to unlock them, similar to Feats. Some Badges are acquired through exclusive timed events, and are thus impossible to unlock once the event passes.
Badges can be viewed in Survival Mode main menu, under the Challenges and Badges menu, alongside Feats. They can also be viewed in the Badges section of the in-game pause menu while in Survival Mode.

The Balaclava is a type of headgear in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is a rare item and additionally cannot be found on Interloper difficulty.
When worn along with an outer hat, the Balaclava loses its windproof resistance and protection bonus. This is because windproof and protection bonuses are only added from outer gear.
Despite this, the balaclava is just as good as the [Wool Toque](./Wool%20Toque.md), and should always be used as an inner hat slot, as the decay rate is slower than the wool toque.

**Windproof bonus:** [Windproofness icon](../assets/Windproofness_icon.png)0 °C(0 °F)
> “**Law-enforcement body armour. Great Protection, but very heavy. You won't win any sprints wearing it.**”

The Ballistic Vest provides the highest [Protection](./Clothing.md#Protection) rating in the game at 50%. However, it is very heavy, weighing in at 6kg (13.2lbs). It is the heaviest clothing item in the game, and is comparable to heavier items such as animal quarters or the [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md) in terms of item weight. In addition, it reduces the player's [Stamina](./Stamina.md) bar by 40%, the highest mobility penalty any worn clothing offers.

The lack of windproof or warmth bonuses forces the player to choose between equipping it for the protection bonus, or leaving it behind, preserving mobility and carrying capacity. However, the trade-off for extreme protection may be worth it if players find themselves ending up in lots of struggles, or plan to journey through dangerous territory such as regions that are inhabited by [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) packs. It is most useful early-game when the player may not have sufficient resources to fend off attacks, especially on Interloper, or when playing a custom game in which condition loss is difficult to replace (i.e. Deadman).

With the weight reduction that is granted to equipped clothes/accessories, it is usually better to wear the vest if you are already carrying it, unless you need more sprint stamina; e.g., for [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) or when crossing [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md).

The vest also gives its own unique buff called [Armoured](./Armoured.md). Armoured's actual effects are still debated: some say it has no actual effect at all, and simply informs the player of their high defense. Others suggest it reduces the risk of receiving negative [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) from fights--for example, lowering the risk of [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) or [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md)/[Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md).

The Protection stat is meant to reduce wildlife damage by 1% per 1 protection, meaning equipping the vest cuts wildlife damage in half at minimum. This also means that acquiring 100% or more protection will make the player **_invulnerable_** to wildlife damage.

The Ballistic Vest can only be found inside of the main building of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), located in [Blackrock.](./Blackrock.md) It spawns at the end of the hallway in Cell Block C, next to a corpse. Getting there requires the player to travel around the rear of the prison past multiple wolves and a bear, and then make a very short rope climb, following by walking inside the darkness and collapsed corridors of the ruined prison.
- Directly decreases Moose and Bear direct struggle damage done to the player by a large amount.
- Takes less over-time decay damage and takes heavily reduced decay from weather like blizzard and freezing water.
- Reduces damage from bears and moose struggle, but apparently not from wolf struggle... Does not reduce damage from falling or anything else.

- Ballistic vest's condition does not change the amount of protection you get from it. It will protect at full efficiency whether at 99% condition or 1% condition, but cannot of course be used when fully ruined.

- The maximum protection possible is 106%, achievable by equipping [Ski Boots](./Ski%20Boots.md)/[Combat Boots](./Combat%20Boots.md) (10%), [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md)/[Wolfskin Pants](./Wolfskin%20Pants.md) (10%), [Tactical Gloves](./Tactical%20Gloves.md) (7%), [Moose-Hide Cloak](./Moose-Hide%20Cloak.md) (20%), [Cougar Hide Wrap](./Cougar%20Hide%20Wrap.md) (6%), [Crampons](./Crampons.md) (3%), and the [Ballistic Vest](./Ballistic%20Vest.md) (50%).
- The Ballistic Vest goes into the accessory slot, not the jacket slot, making it the 4th item to use the accessory slot.

A **Bandage** is a [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) cloth used for stopping bleeding or limb immobilization in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Bandages are used to stop [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md), preventing the player from rapidly losing [Condition](./Condition.md) from bleeding out. They are often found in [First Aid Kits](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md) and [Medicine Shelves](./Medicine%20Shelf.md). They can also easily be created by harvesting a single [Cloth](./Cloth.md) and [Crafting](./Crafting.md) 2 of them anywhere in 15 minutes.
- Caution is required to prevent bleeding out while crafting them while at already low Condition. As such, it is advisable to keep a few bandages in one's inventory in case of emergency.
- Blood Loss also attracts predators by giving the player maximum [Scent](./Scent.md), and can quickly lead to death if the player is attacked while crafting Bandages.

**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**
The **Bank Manager's House** is a location in [Milton](./Milton.md) in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. It is labeled as **[Milton House](./Milton%20House.md)** in Survival Mode.

It is a residential building consisting of a kitchen with a [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), a bedroom and bathroom. The Bank Manager's House needs to be opened with its own respective key before entering in Story mode.

The house is located in [Milton](./Milton.md) a short walk from [Milton Post Office](./Milton%20Post%20Office.md) in the direction of [The Arch](./The%20Arch%20%28Mountain%20Town%20location%29.md) and the [Shortwave Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md). From the outside, the house can be identified as a green colored building with stairs up to the front door and a Canadian flag. The interior has a unique floor plan and yellow striped wallpaper. It is also one of the few smaller houses in Milton with a wood-burning stove.

The house is initially locked but can be opened once [Will](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) has found the [Bank Manager's House Key](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House%20Key.md) in a desk drawer in [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md). The code to the bank vault can also be found in the house, making the house a compulsory location for the main questline of [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md).

**Barb's Rifle** is a unique variant of the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

The unique perk of Barb's Rifle's is that it degrades 18% slower than the standard hunting rifle, this means a full condition Barb's Rifle can fire up to 89 shots at base [Rifle Skill](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) before breaking. This durability comes at the cost of weight as it's custom stock increases the gun's base weight to 4.50 kg, which is 0.50 kg heavier than the Hunting Rifle.
Barb's rifle also features a unique set of iron sights with a pointed front sight post, letting you better see where your shot will land.
Successful hits on live animals provide experience to the [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) skill.
Barb's Rifle will spawn once per world in various states of repair. It is found in a set of randomly selected [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) locations, such as:
- In one of the [Fishing Huts](./Fishing%20Hut.md) near [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) leaning against the wall next to the stove.
- Total durability is 18% more than Hunting Rifle (Uses 1.125%-0.5625% condition per shot based on [Rifle Skill](./Rifle%20Firearm.md))

- With [Rifle Skill Level 5](./Rifle%20Firearm.md)'s 50% reduction in per shot durability use, Barb's Rifle can fire up to 178 shots from full condition before breaking. This makes it one of the best rifles for use on [Stalker](./Stalker.md), since it's higher durability and the reduced amount of cleaning kits available means you can stretch your materials further and spend less time repairing at a [milling machine.](./Milling%20Machine.md)

- The rifle appears to have been painted with a military olive green paint that has long since faded showing the fir wood furniture underneath, the stock depicts an image of a roaring bear on each of it's sides, and there are 12 tally marks on the rifle's side.
- Barb's Rifle has a unique stripper clip painted in green camo that can be seen when reloading.
- Barb's rifle is the most cost-effective rifle to repair, this makes it the best variant for long term use.
- Despite the description mentioning the rifle being more reliable, it has the exact same jamming rate and threshold as all other rifles.
- Barb's rifle belongs to Barbara Quincy, owner of the [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md), according to a [Buffer Memory.](./Buffer%20Memories.md#Coastal_Highway)
- Barb's rifle is based on the No. 4 Rifle, a later version of the Lee-Enfield rifle, albeit with a different magazine. On the actual rifles, the magazine did not change much.

Has an interior The **Barn** (Not to be confused with the one at the [Pleasant Valley Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md)) is a small indoor hay storage shed south of [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) and close to [Heartbreak Bridge](./Heartbreak%20Bridge.md).

Inside, two hay beds can be found although they provide very little warmth. A wooden shelf can be found with a few basic items as well as a possible bedroll spawn. A Revolver may be found hidden in a hay stack. A hidden obstacle course to the upper storage area with the ladder can be found by walking to the west of the door and up the wooden planks. Up in the rafters is a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) often containing [Maple Syrup](./Maple%20Syrup.md) and a [Fleece Cowl](./Fleece%20Cowl.md). Close to the corpse, next to a hay bale, a possible spawn of a [Rabbitskin Hat](./Rabbitskin%20Hat.md) even on Interloper difficulty.

In [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) the Barn is named **Molly's Barn** and is the final location the first mission in the episode, [Trauma](./Trauma.md). The mission requires you to help [Molly](./Molly.md) who has been trapped in the barn by wolves and she is attacked by a [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) before killing it with her bow. The upper rafters can be explored but don't contain anything.

The Baseball Cap is a simple black and white hat that can commonly be found in many locations.

**Basement (Crumbling Highway)** is a sheltered indoor location in [Crumbling Highway](./Crumbling%20Highway.md), behind one of the houses in the [Abandoned Harris Home](./Abandoned%20Harris%20Home.md) location.
The interior has no bed or firebox, but is sheltered and can provide a place to sleep when transiting the area.

Contains a tool [Cabinet](./Cabinet.md) and a [First Aid](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md) box, as well as a [Washer](./Washer.md) and [Dryer](./Dryer.md) potentially containing some [clothing](./Clothing.md).
A [Wolf](./Wolf.md) spawn point can be found just outside across the road, therefore caution is advised when visiting this location.

Has an interior **Basement (Sundered Pass)** is an unmarked location in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md).
The Basement is located under one of the destroyed buildings in [Old Settlement](./Old%20Settlement.md), and can only be accessed through the [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) Tale.
There is a [Bed](./Bed.md), a [Washer](./Washer.md) and [Dryer](./Dryer.md), food, water, and materials. 4 unique [Cans](./Can.md) can be harvested for a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) each.

The area above consists of several ruined buildings and one intact two story [cabin](./Cabin%20%28Sundered%20Pass%29.md). The area around the settlement is patrolled by several large packs of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), making coming and going very difficult.
Despite being underground, the basement does not protect against [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) and [Insomnia Risk](./Insomnia%20Risk.md).

A **Basin** is a single metal pan located on a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) in the [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) in the [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) in the [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) region. Interacting with it will allow a survivor to harvest a variable amount of either [Water (Unsafe)](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md) or [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) (0.20-0.70L). Various buildings use the same metal pan model of a Basin, but the Quonset Garage is the only location with an interactable Basin.
Water inside the Basin will slowly go bad as the days in Survival Mode progress. If the water is not claimed, the initially clean water has a chance to turn into dirty water.

![A rowboat and loose items found while beachcombing.](../assets/Rowboat.png)_A rowboat and loose items found while beachcombing._ **Beachcombing** is a gameplay mechanic in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md),_which allows the player to acquire otherwise non-renewable items.

Items can wash up along the icy shoreline regions of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) ([Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) and [Crumbling Highway](./Crumbling%20Highway.md)). Rarely the player's character must stand atop [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md) to gather these items, but most of the time a player can safely stay on normal ice or the shore.

These small, lootable items can be found in many locations along the water, usually in small clusters. The quality and quantity of items will depend on difficulty setting. These items will respawn progressively (it is not necessary for a blizzard to occur).

Bear Creek Campground is a campsite by a small creek that runs from the north, down to the ocean at the south.

There is a small cabin on a hill nearby, but otherwise, there is no real shelter at the campground. [Cat tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) and [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) can be found in the area, as can a [Bear](./Bear.md). A corpse or [Deer](./Deer.md) carcass may also spawn in the campground.

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

The **Bear Hide Bed** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) and [Bed](./Bed.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.

A lavish wooden bed with a mattress and very warm Black Bear bedsheet, the Bear Hide Bed can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).
This bed can be [Slept](./Sleep.md) in and gives a [Warmth](./Warmth.md) bonus of +10 °C (+18 °F):
- This is the warmest bed value in the game, but the Bear Hide Bed requires the highest crafting/material times of any bed option as a tradeoff.

- It restores _twice_ the [Condition](./Condition.md) of a normal bed. On [Interloper](./Interloper.md)/[Misery](./Misery.md), it provides the greatest Condition recovery of all the bed types in the game.

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The bed can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value, the bed cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the bed will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).

The **Bear Hide Rug** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.

The Bear Hide Rug is the only Decorations item crafted by the player that does not need the [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) or a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md) to craft. Instead, it can be crafted at any [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), but need [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md).

The rug is quite large, being the size of a [Car](./Car.md) or [Truck](./Truck.md). As such, it requires a lot of clear space and thus will not fit into smaller Safehouses due to how much room it takes up. The head of the bear is the only part of the Rug that is not flat, and can be walked over as if it is a small bump in the floor.
This item cannot be harvested. The only option is to pick up, move or destroy it (destroying the rug will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).

**Bear Meat (Cooked)** is a cooked [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.

Cooked Bear Meat is obtained by using a lit [Fire](./Fire.md) and improves the [Cooking](./Cooking.md) skill. Cooking increases its condition by 50%, makes it decay 4 times slower than raw meat, and adds a reduced chance of [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) over raw meat.
Using a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) reduces cooking time by 25%. Cooked food on an active fire for too long will burn it, destroying the item and damaging a Cooking Pot if used.

A **Bear Quarter** is a section harvested from a _[bear](./Bear.md)_. You can obtain bear quarters by _quartering_ a bear carcass. To quarter an animal, you have to go into the harvest menu, then select the quartering action. For a bear, this will always take 2 hours. You can only quarter a bear if its less than 50% frozen.

After quartering, the carcass will despawn, leaving behind 5-8 quarters, as well as its [Fresh Gut](./Fresh%20Gut.md) and [Fresh Black Bear Hide](./Fresh%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md). It will also leave behind the bears legs and blood, but this cannot be picked up, and it will soon despawn. As quartering only takes 2 hours for bears, vs. the hours taken to harvest all the meat, guts, and hide by hand, and quartering still gives you all necessary parts, it makes transport and harvesting easier, especially if a blizzard is coming or if it will soon be night.

Unlike directly harvesting a fresh carcass' meat, you will still need to harvest a quarter for its meat. 50% of the quarters total weight will be turned into usable [Bear Meat (Raw)](./Bear%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md). Any remaining raw meat left inside the bag will be lost if the Quarter's Condition reaches 0%, with bags spoiling within 1 day of harvesting.
