**Repair:** 1 × [Cloth](./Cloth.md) 1 × [Cured Black Bear Hide](./Cured%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md) 50% Condition (62.5% Mending Lv.5)
> “**Bedroll crafted from Bear Skin. Heavy, but very warm. The smell might scare animals away.**”

The Bear Skin Bedroll is a variant of the [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), and is crafted from 2 [Cured Black Bear Hide](./Cured%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md) at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md). It fulfils the same role as bedrolls: allowing [sleep](./Sleep.md) at any location indoors or outside. Bear Skin Bedrolls are much warmer than normal bedrolls, have a chance of scaring nearby [wolves](./Wolf.md) when carried, reduces the chances of [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) attacks when sleeping, and heals condition faster than a bedroll.

Bear Skin Bedrolls like the bedroll must be deployed to use ("use" in the inventory, or via the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md)). When deployed they may be slept in indoors or outside, restoring fatigue and also condition if all 4 needs are met. The rate of Condition restored when using a Bear Skin Bedroll is the same with beds (1% per hour faster compared to the bedroll) (see [Sleep](./Sleep.md)). Bear Skin bedrolls are much warmer than bedrolls (12 °C (21.6 °F) vs 5 °C(9 °F) and even many beds. It now takes 35 hours to craft.

When carried the Bear Skin Bedroll provides a chance to scare [wolves](./Wolf.md) when they detect the player, causing the wolf to flee. It also provides a reduced chance of wildlife attacks when sleeping (on Stalker and Interloper).

However it is heavier (3 kg vs 1 kg) than a bedroll, and requires cured black bear hides to repair. Bear Skin Bedrolls decay slowly over time, and quickly while being used. When used Bedrolls provide warmth based on the bedroll's current condition (similar to [Clothes](./Clothing.md)).

- The Bear Skin Bedroll is useful or even life-saving in cold or remote regions ([Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), and [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md)), and on harder survival modes (with colder world temperatures and faster [Condition](./Condition.md) damage from [freezing](./Needs.md)).

- Care should be taken not to freeze to death (Stalker and Interloper) while sleeping with a bedroll, especially outside. This includes checking the current temperature, weather conditions, fire duration, and not sleeping for many hours at a time.
- Sleeping without a bedroll is possible inside [cars and trucks](./Vehicle.md) by entering the vehicle and selecting "sleep" from the Radial Menu (campcraft).

- Thanks to the high warmth bonus it gives, one can carry less firewood when travelling. They can also sleep outdoors with a lowly-heated campfire on higher difficulty without the fear of freezing to death.

- Bear Skin Bedroll is best used when huddled inside a vehicle. Any vehicle will offer windproof protection as well as +5 degree of ambient temperature. With the bedroll equipped, one can effectively get a bonus of +17 degree inside a vehicle. This is extremely useful to get through a sudden [blizzard](./Weather.md) when there is no immediate shelter nearby.
A possible spawn location can be found on [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) inside the [Pensive Lookout](./Pensive%20Lookout.md) below a corkboard on Pilgrim, Voyageur and Stalker difficulties.
Additionally, in the Tales from the Far Territory DLC, a crafted bear skin bedroll can spawn inside the Coal Tower of the [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) region on all difficulties.

> “**Ten inches of cold hard steel might do what a bullet can't. I'm convinced– a spear's the way to kill that bear.**”
The **Bear Spear** is a weapon only available in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).

The Bear Spear weighs 4.00kg, cannot be harvested, and disappears after completing [What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md). It is treated as a Collectibles, but this is to prevent it from being dropped and lost. The red ribbon on the Spear is one of the few items in the game to have dynamic ragdoll physics, moving in the wind as the player turns.

The player uses the spear by creating a defensive posture and then bracing for a bear charge, then thrusting the spear into the bear. To brace for the attack, hold LMB on PC to "Set Spear", which will deplete stamina and restrict the player from moving and pivoting approximately 30 degrees to either side. It takes about half a second between starting to brace, and the spear to become active.

If the spear is active when the Old Bear collides with them, a special "spear struggle" will ensue in which the player buries the spearhead into the beast's chest and can click repeatedly to fill the bar and win the struggle. Struggling for too long will result in the Old Bear scratching the player with its claws halfway through the struggle, resulting in [Laceration](./Laceration.md), [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md), and [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) Afflictions. Failing to fill the bar after 9 seconds will result in the bear breaking from the spear, and "punching" the player with his right paw, knocking them out.

Successfully defeating a bear in a Spear Struggle will use a large portion of the player's stamina, so it is advisable to wait a few moments after a struggle before beginning a new Spear Struggle. If the spear is not yet active when a bear attacks the player, or if the player's stamina is too low to set the spear, the bear will attack the player normally and they will be defenseless in the [Struggle](./Struggle.md).
Wolves fear the bear spear. And it can be used as an effective deterrent against them. Provided the player sets the spear just as the wolf charges.

The Bear Spear is rumored by [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) to be the only weapon that can kill the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md). Jeremiah tells [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) the story of the Old Demon Bear and a magical spear forged to kill it long ago, and the trapper tasks the pilot to find it in the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md).

Mackenzie makes his way to the Hunting Lodge but finds a [Broken Bear Spear](./Broken%20Bear%20Spear.md) instead, and is forced to repair the Broken Bear Spear in the [Forge](./Forge.md) in the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) by crafting a [Spear Head](./Spear%20Head.md). By the end of the mission, Mackenzie fully repairs the Spear to its original glory and returns to Jeremiah.

Mackenzie is tasked with finding [Transponder Parts](./Transponder%20Parts.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and encounters the Old Bear, using the Bear Spear several times to defend himself from the beast. After acquiring 3 Transponder Parts, Mackenzie is ambushed by the Old Bear and unconsciously dragged away.

Mackenzie awakens inside the [Old Bear's Den](./Old%20Bear%27s%20Den.md) unarmed, and is forced to sneak and crawl his way through the caves until he finds the Bear Spear. After successfully completing a Bear Struggle 3 times with the Spear, Mackenzie kills the Old Bear by impaling it in the neck. Mackenzie leaves the Spear impaled into the Old Bear and leaves the cave, and the Spear is never used again afterwards.

This weapon cannot be crafted in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), but has been hinted in a Dev's Diary that it will be implemented into the sandbox in the future ([Source](https://www.thelongdark.com/news/episodes-one-and-two-redux-survival-mode-update/)).

It can currently be found and spawned in Survival Mode via console commands, but cannot be used properly against Bears. Despite being unable to be broken down in Wintermute, a harvest option is present. Harvesting the Bear Spear generates 1 [Spear Head](./Spear%20Head.md) and 1 [Cured Maple Sapling](./Cured%20Maple%20Sapling.md).

- The Bear Spear and the story of the "[Demon Bear](./Old%20Bear.md)" told by [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) are references to "The Beast Spear" from the fantasy manga ["Ushio & Tora" (うしおととら)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ushio_%26_Tora) written and illustrated by Kazuhiro Fujita. Both stories feature a supernatural weapon forged by a character driven mad for revenge to kill 'evil spirits', including a red cloth tied around the spear's neck.
_The [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) defending a shortwave tower, with the Bear Spear in hand_
- Added to game.

The road is blocked by an enormous landslide just to the southeast of this location. There is no passage on ground level.

A series of ledges form a path that crosses the road above Bear's Bend on top of rocks that form a natural bridge. This rock bridge and ledge path is the only way to get from one side of the blockage to the other side, other than taking the long route all the way past [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md).
- To the northwest: near [Forager's Remnant](./Forager%27s%20Remnant.md), with a [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section.
- To the east: past the unnamed trailer close to the road, about half-way between Bear's Bend and [Grand Meadow](./Grand%20Meadow.md).

The beginning of the ledge path is relatively easy to find from either direction. However, the ledges themselves can be confusing, especially around the spot where the three paths meet. When coming from the trailer in the east, following the path towards Creek Bed Cave requires a 180° turn that may be easy to miss, particularly in low visibility.

There is no shelter down at Bear's Bend, but the ledge path through the mountains above allows access to a small cave. Rabbits can be hunted in front of the cave, and a small number of various plants can be harvested in several spots along the ledge path, including [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) and [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md).

_For the unique bear found in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), [The Hunted, Part One](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20One.md) and [The Hunted, Part Two](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Two.md), see [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md)._

> “**He'll come for you when you're not expecting it. But you won't miss it. It won't be subtle. It'll sound like a ton of muscle and bone bearing down on you like a freight train of hate and hunger.**”
**Bears** (also known as **Black Bears**) are large, dangerous [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) predators in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Bears are large solitary predatory [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md). Bears normally hibernate throughout the winter, but the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) and subsequent aurora has awoken them from their slumber. They are now regularly found exiting their bear cave (often with bones inside), or roaming the area near them in search of food, attacking human survivors if they are spotted.

They are among the toughest and most dangerous animals on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), easily overpowering any human survivor with just their sheer size. While not as aggressive as [Wolves](./Wolf.md), Bears are highly territorial and will charge and [maul](./Struggle.md) their victims. They are significantly harder to avoid/kill compared to the common Wolf, requiring the player to be alert and prepared should they come across one.

A [Black Bear Carcass](./Black%20Bear%20Carcass.md) may be harvested for 25.00-40.00 kg of [raw meat](./Bear%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md), 1 [Fresh Black Bear Hide](./Fresh%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md), and 10 guts. Bear hides can be cured to craft [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md) or [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md).

Bears have three paces: walking, charging, and fleeing. Typically they wander near their bear caves at a slow walking pace, with little interest in their surroundings, but occasionally stop to forage or look around. Bears do not hunt other animals, unlike Wolves. Bears are the only animal whose breath is seen as they wander around.

Bears are relatively quiet, but their soft-padded footsteps can be heard from a distance. At closer distances their grunts and snorts may be heard, and if the bear detects the player they will bellow, growl, and begin to follow them. Crows have a unique "bear call" which can be heard when a bear is stalking the player, and the standard "dangerous wildlife" music will start playing.
Charging bears usually stand on their hind legs and roar, with their heavy breath "huffing and puffing" as they rapidly charge after the player.
A fleeing bear will whine, moan, and "scream" as it rapidly runs away from the player if they successfully drive/scare it off.

All Bears have a specific den as their home, usually a dedicated [Warm Bear Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) or a rocky outcropping in the side of a rockface. Each den is immediately identifiable by the remains of yellowing skeletons near their entrances (normally of deer, but sometimes of human). A bear will often return from roaming to their den after dusk, taking the most direct path (even if it is kilometers away) to try and sleep inside for the night. A frightened bear often flees for a time before attempting to return to their den.
- Sleeping or spending time in bear caves is dangerous, as a Bear can return and attack the player during their sleep if they spot the player.
- Not all dens are inhabited in at all times, as a Bear will often take many in game hours to return to their cave, even after dusk.
- Sleeping in a cave with very high [Scent](./Scent.md) is generally a very bad idea, as the Bear will often leave its normal patrol to come to you
> “**Bears can smell blood from over 20 clicks away. You get out there, you cut yourself enough that you bleed, and he'll come to you. I'm sure of it.**”

Bears have the most sensitive noses of any predator wildlife animal, and will travel great lengths (up to over half of the game map) to find the player if their Scent is too high, far outside of their normal patrol pathways. This can make sleeping in a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) in the snow, buildings, or caves (even non-bear den caves) very dangerous if the Bear finds them, as they will attack the player in their sleep. This can be used to the player's advantage when hunting them, as long as the player is prepared to wait very long periods of time for the Bear to come to them, as the Bear will still walk at its normal slow walking speed upon detecting the player's Scent (unlike Wolves who walk quickly to the player's location).

![A sleeping bear.](../assets/Sleeping_Bear.jpg)_A sleeping bear._ Bears occasionally return to their den to sleep for the night when dusk falls, in which they lie down to try and continue hibernating, often snoring quite loudly. In this state, a bear can be awoken by normal stimuli such as gun reports, lit flares, or simply being too close.

Bears will follow any player they detect and attack the player at close distances. If the player moves far enough away, the bear will give up its pursuit. Bears will also charge if they detect the player and the player shoots at them; shots from undetected players usually cause bear to flee, even if not struck by the round.

Bears are attracted by [Scent](./Scent.md). Baiting with dropped scent items while being pursued by a bear will distract them (unless charging). See: [Baiting](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys). ![A bear held at bay by a campfire.](../assets/Bear_Campfire_Close.png)_A bear held at bay by a campfire._

Bears are only held at bay by certain fires. [Campfires](./Campfire.md) and [flares](./Flare.md) (held in hand) will prevent a bear from charging the player unless it is already within a certain distance. It will wait outside the radius of the fire until the player leaves the safety of the fire or it is scared away. While being held at bay, bears can be scared away by hitting it with a thrown burning torch (short flee), weapon shot that misses (long flee), weapon shot that hits (longest flee). Approaching a bear while it is held at bay will cause it to overcome its fear and charge. They will walk or charge around a lone lit torch on the ground, but it will not stop them, nor will throwing torches or flares at them cause them to flee while they are not held at bay.

Bears flee from [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) reports and from the landing site of flare rounds; the Distress Pistol can prevent a charging bear from attacking even at very close distance. Bears are also frightened of bullets and arrows striking near them, but only from undetected players; they will charge attackers if they can detect them (barring Distress Pistol fire).

Bears will flee from [bow shots](./Survival%20Bow.md) only under certain conditions[^3]. If a bear is shot from outside the range from which it can detect the player, the bear will flee[^4]. If a bear has detected the player, shooting the ground beside the bear (rather than shooting the bear) can cause the bear to flee[^5].
Hunting Bears with a [Revolver](./Revolver.md) is not advised, as the sheer body weight will absorb any damage from the shot (though they will still bleed to death, even from 1 gunshot wound).
An exploding [Noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md) will scare off a charging bear, as long as the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) isn't active.

[Stones](./Stone.md) deal no damage if striking a Bear, and a Bear will chase those who throw stones at them (if detected). Stones thrown by undetected players will distract nearby bears to investigate for a few seconds.

![Aurora Bear](../assets/Aurora_Bear.jpg) Like all predators, the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) will produce an Aurora Bear, a much tankier, less fear prone version of the Bear. It also becomes more perceptive and can detect the player from further away. Extreme caution is advised while the Aurora is out and a Bear is nearby. It can often take up to 6 well placed headshots on an Aurora Bear to fell them. Getting mauled by an aurora bear is extremely dangerous. Due to its heightened senses, it can detect and charge the player before any action can be taken, leading to consecutive maulings until death.
- Aurora Bears do not fear [Flares](./Flare.md), [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), or lit [Torches](./Torch.md).
- They also do not fear [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md), and will turn towards the player's direction and most likely charge them if one explodes.

- They fear [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) high beams and will temporarily stop a charge as long as they are on (unlike charging wolves, they do not stop in their tracks for a few moments once the light is turned on. Turning the light off will make them immediately resume their charge).

- They will stay away from lit [Campfires](./Campfire.md), but will still stay close by and stalk the player. They will eventually overcome their fear of the fire and attack the player if they do not attack the bear or leave the area.
- Gunshots are not effective at frightening Aurora Bears, as they will instantly charge the player unless they cannot see where the shot came from.
![A Bear and Moose ignoring one another.](../assets/Moose_and_Bear.jpg)_A Bear and Moose ignoring one another._ Bears will ignore all other forms of Wildlife:
- [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md), [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), and [Deer](./Deer.md) will flee from Bears. Bears do not attack these animals despite being carnivorous.
- [Wolves](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), and [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) will also flee from the presence of Bears. Bears do not attack these animals.
- Bears run away when the [Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) is close to them, and will die once [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) reaches 100%.

![Player's view of a bear mauling.](../assets/Screen_Shot_2016-07-12_at_5.47.12_pm.png)_Player's view of a bear mauling._ If provoked with weapons or approached too close, a bear will charge and maul the player. Bear struggles are different from [Wolf](./Wolf.md) struggles in that the player will always lose, getting mauled and eventually passing out. After mauling the player, the bear will walk away but may maul the player again if they do not flee immediately.

Bear attacks cause massive [Condition](./Condition.md) loss, [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md), [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md), and usually ruins a worn [Clothing](./Clothing.md) item (typically one worn on the head, accessory or shoes). Attacks from Bears are usually not fatal at high Condition.
- After a struggle, move a safe distance from the bear before applying [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md); staying too close to the bear may cause it to maul the player again.

- Bears require physical contact to begin a struggle, so attacks can avoided by using terrain blockers, doors, narrow spaces, cliff sides, and the interiors of [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md) and structures.

- Bear attacks typically are non-lethal at high Condition, but cause 90% Condition loss (reduced by clothing protection) (e.g. pre-struggle: 72% Condition, post-struggle: ~7% with no protective clothes).
- After a struggle, random items from the player's inventory will usually fall onto the ground—typically their weapon or held item at the start of the struggle.
- Significant condition damage is usually inflicted on some of the clothing item(s), often ruining one.
- Bear struggles cannot be won (except in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) with the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) against the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md)).

Bears may be hunted with any ranged weapon (except Stones) and suffer from blood loss, so a single round is lethal (but may take many hours for the animal to bleed out). A single rifle shot may even kill a bear instantly if it strikes their head and is a "critical hit", but usually bears survive multiple rounds and will immediately charge or flee depending if the player was detected.

Before going on a bear hunt, it's generally a good idea to pare down the pack or to bring along a [Travois](./Travois.md), as there is a lot of [meat](./Bear%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md) on a bear, which will almost certainly [overload](./Encumbrance.md) a player carrying a full set of gear.
Critical hits cause the animal to instantly die after being hit by a shot. The following table contains the critical hit chance based on the location that was shot on the animal.
The critical-% for flare gun seem to be currently bugged (i.e. defaulting to rifle bleed-out numbers)
| Weapon — Head | Weapon — Neck | Critical Hit Chance — Torso | Critical Hit Chance — Hips | Critical Hit Chance — Limb | Critical Hit Chance | Critical Hit Chance |
| [Hunting Rifle icon](../assets/Hunting_Rifle_icon.png) | [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) | 15% | 10% | 5% | 3% | 3% |
| [Distress Pistol icon](../assets/Distress_Pistol_icon.png) | [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) | 60% | 90% | Guaranteed | Guaranteed | Guaranteed |
| [Survival Bow icon](../assets/Survival_Bow_icon.png) | [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) | 15% | 10% | 5% | 3% | 3% |
| [Revolver icon](../assets/Revolver_icon.png) | [Revolver](./Revolver.md) | 3% | 2% | 1% | 0% | 0% |

All shots that cause blood loss are lethal, but may take many hours based on which body part was struck. Multiple shots do not stack blood loss. A shot that hits a higher blood loss area will override blood loss from a shot in a lower blood loss area. Conversely, if shot in an area of lower blood loss after being shot in area of higher blood loss, the shot that hit the area of lower blood loss will override the blood loss from the first shot. Therefore, if you land a head shot which causes a bear to flee, shooting it in the hindquarters or limbs will cause the bear to bleed out more slowly. As such, you should not fire a second shot in that scenario and instead simply follow the bear until it bleeds out from the head wound.
| Weapon — Head | Weapon — Neck | Bleed Out — Torso | Bleed Out — Hips | Bleed Out — Limb | Bleed Out | Bleed Out |
| [Revolver icon](../assets/Revolver_icon.png) | [Revolver](./Revolver.md) | 80 min | 120 min | 320 min | 480 min | 640 min |
| [Hunting Rifle icon](../assets/Hunting_Rifle_icon.png) | [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) | 60 min | 90 min | 240 min | 360 min | 480 min |
| [Survival Bow icon](../assets/Survival_Bow_icon.png) | [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) | 45 min | 60 min | 375 min | 240 min | 240 min |
| [Distress Pistol icon](../assets/Distress_Pistol_icon.png) | [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) | 30 min | 45 min | 50 min | 140 min | 140 min |

- Bull-Fight: Shoot from close to a position that bears cannot attack, perhaps luring or baiting the bear into range first. Shoot the bear, enter cover. Let it charge and fail. Follow until it bleeds out.

- [Hunter's Blinds](./Hunter%27s%20Blinds.md): Some bears wander near hunter's blinds like [Unnamed Pond](./Unnamed%20Pond.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md). These structures provide protection against predators while allowing the use of ranged weapons.
- Stealth: Shoot from a hidden location, ideally with the survival bow and track until dead.
- Unwise: Shoot repeatedly as it charges hoping for first or second shot critical hit to drop the bear before it reaches you.

- Stall with Fire: Get close enough to the bear for it to follow you (but not charge, do not shoot yet), make a quick fire (best with accelerator) then wait behind the fire for the bear to approach. About midway, the bear will go on its hind legs and roar, then charge but stops in front of the fire and stays in a waiting stance. This will provide a significant amount of time to shoot the bear in the head (choose your favorite weapon), the bear then runs away. Follow until it bleeds out.

- Goading: Agitate the bear into following (but not charging) and lead it to a more advantageous location for hunting, or even back to a [safe house](./Safehouse.md). You can also shoot and retreat to safety, such as inside a vehicle. Avoid loading screens (inside a mine or building interior), since that may cause the bear to de-spawn. As the bear starts to wander off, exit your hiding spot and agitate it again to draw it back. After a few hours (in-game) the bear should die relatively close by. This process can be time consuming depending on distance and bleed out time, but is relatively safe, minimizes risk of losing the wounded bear, and makes harvesting convenient.

It is worth noting that after killing the bear, it is more time-efficient to Quarter the bear than to harvest the hide and guts individually. However, the body of the bear that would be destroyed by quartering is also large enough to grant protection from the wind (Wind Shield) to campfires and crouching players, which can be useful for players looking to harvest the bear's meat on the spot.

Bear spawns vary by region and Survival Mode. In some regions (Coastal Highway and Desolation Point) bears always spawn in the same location(s); in other regions (Mystery Lake and Pleasant Valley), bears have multiple possible spawning locations which only some may be be occupied in a given save file. The following list is a list of possible bear locations:
- A cave west of [Angler's Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md), below [Runaway Bridge](./Runaway%20Bridge.md) (refresh).
- [Cliff Cave](./Cliff%20Cave.md), to the northwest of [Bricklayer's Retreat](./Bricklayer%27s%20Retreat.md) and due west from [Whistling Perch](./Whistling%20Perch.md).
- In the west part of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), inside the courtyard the player escapes into from the prison in [Episode 4.](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md)

- A rare spawn at the three cars on the plateau near [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md) (refresh). Note: This is not a permanent bear spawn, but is rolled every three days between a rabbit, a deer or a bear.
- A cave slightly east of [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md), on the island.
- Next to [Broken Bridge](./Broken%20Bridge%20%28disambiguation%29.md), along the highway.
- Northwest corner, north of the [Hushed River](./Hushed%20River.md) and [Offset Falls](./Offset%20Falls.md).
- In a cave near [Three Strikes Farmstead](./Three%20Strikes%20Farmstead.md) (this spawn seems to be currently bugged).
- North of [Burned Ridge Cave](./Burned%20Ridge%20Cave.md) and the [Crash Site (Pleasant Valley)](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md).
- East of [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md), in front of the trail down to [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md).
- In an unnamed cave near the cargo container east of [Andre's Peak](./Andre%27s%20Peak.md) between the two rope climbs.

- Bears base their appearance off of the [American Black Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_black_bear) (**_Ursus americanus_**), a species of Ursidae found in North America. Their sizes vary, but they are typically half the size of the Bears founds in game until they reach adulthood. The American black bear is also known for being timid. Often scared off by loud noises or just the sight of a human, however the Aurora has made the local bear population far more aggressive.
- [General] Bear sound effects no longer play when a carcass is removed from the world.
- Tuned Revolver effectiveness when used against Moose (reduced) and reduced critical chance against Bears.
- [ALL] Fixed issue where injured Bears reset their status when players enter an interior or Pass Time.
- [Survival Mode] Fixed issue where Bears could be stuck on broken ice in Desolation Point.
- [Both] Fixed issue where player camera would be inside the Bear mesh during carcass harvesting.
- Fixed issue with a series of multiple exertion sounds being played after a Bear struggle.
- Fixed issue with drawn Survival Bow movement speed retained after Wolf or Bear struggle
- Delay condition-loss from Bear struggle until the struggle animation is complete. (This does not apply to Wolf struggles.)
- Overhauled struggle audio for both Wolves (to account for new first-person presence) and for the Bear struggle (to make it more impressive).
- Bears are now spawned facing outwards from Dens. This helps fix some pathing issues when the bear attempts to leave the Den.
- Fixed issue with player health being reset to 100% if loading a save after a Bear attack.
- Re-balanced harvestable meat and gut yield for Bear, as well as Caloric value of Bear meat.

A **Bed** is a type of furniture or a small, pre-built construction that frequently appears in houses and cabins, with some variants appearing in other buildings and even in some caves. Beds can be used to restore [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) by [Sleeping](./Sleep.md) and grant a [Warmth](./Warmth.md) bonus while being used.

Planning exploratory travel, especially if the player chooses not to bring along a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), requires careful consideration of bed locations (especially higher-level [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) difficulties) since not all houses/caves have beds, and no bed variants can be broken down, moved, or crafted. Additionally, sleeping is one of the only ways to restore fatigue and recover significant amounts of [Condition](./Condition.md), and, no matter how tired, the player cannot sleep directly on the floor or on non-bed furniture such as couches or chairs.

While the player may sleep in a Bedroll, [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md), or certain [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) interiors instead of a bed, these other options may not be available, or may be impossible to craft early in game. Using any of these alternatives also often comes with a higher risk of freezing or being attacked by predators.
There are several variants of bed, some found only in specific types of locations, and each providing a different amount of [Warmth](./Warmth.md) when slept in.
- Bunk Bed (usually in cabins or other remote structures. Only the lower bed can be used) provides + 3-6°C ( +5.4-10.8°F )
- Mattress (found on the floor in some large industrial or community buildings/trailers) provides + 3-5°C ( +5.4-9°F )
- Sticks and Leaves (a makeshift bed made of conifer branches and leaves often found in a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md)) will provide + 2°C ( +3.6°F )
- Medical Cot (found inside the crashed [Final Approach](./Final%20Approach.md) helicopter) provides + 2°C ( +3.6°F )
- Blanket (a blanket and pillow thrown over a cardboard box, found in abandoned [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md) and trailers) provides + 2°C ( +3.6°F )

Additionally, the inside of [Car](./Car.md), [Truck](./Truck.md), [Tractor](./Tractor.md), [Airplane](./Airplane.md), [Helicopter](./Helicopter.md), and [Earth Mover](./Haul%20Truck.md) interiors can be used as beds with or without a bedroll by opening the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md), selecting "campcraft", and selecting "sleep". Sleeping in a Vehicle provides a + 3°C (+5. °F) Warmth bonus. Sleeping with a Bedroll will raise the Warmth temperature to whatever the Warmth of the Bedroll is.

The player also has the ability to create beds via [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) ([Rustic Bed](./Rustic%20Bed.md), [Quilted Bed](./Quilted%20Bed.md), [Bear Hide Bed](./Bear%20Hide%20Bed.md)).
Some beds confer greater restoration of [Condition](./Condition.md) than others. On [Interloper](./Interloper.md), sleeping 10 hours with no afflictions or teas yields the following recoveries:

The Bedroll is a tool which allows [sleep](./Sleep.md) at almost any location indoors or outside. It cannot be crafted but can be found at multiple locations in most [regions](./Region.md). The Bedroll requires 2 [cloth](./Cloth.md) and a [Sewing Kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md) or [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) to be repaired.

Bedrolls must be deployed to use ("use" in the inventory, or via the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md)). When deployed they may be slept in indoors or outside, restoring fatigue and also condition if all 4 needs are met. The rate of Condition restored when using a Bedroll is slower than with a proper beds or a [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md) (see [Sleep](./Sleep.md)). When used Bedrolls provide warmth based on the bedroll's current condition (similar to [Clothes](./Clothing.md)).
The Bedroll is lighter than the [Bearskin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md) (1kg vs 3kg). Bedrolls decay slowly over time, and quickly while being used.

As of Part 3: Frontier Comforts update for those who purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion, the bedroll can be [improved](./Improvised%20Down%20Bedroll.md).
- Inside a Pipe at the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) where the [Exit](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md#Exit) to the Lower Dam leads.
| [Improvised Down Bedroll](./Improvised%20Down%20Bedroll.md) | None | - 1 × [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) - 3 × [Cloth](./Cloth.md) - 10 × [Ptarmigan Down](./Ptarmigan%20Down.md) |

- Bedrolls are useful or even life-saving in cold or remote regions ([Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), and [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md)), and on harder survival modes (with colder world temperatures and faster [Condition](./Condition.md) damage from [freezing](./Needs.md)).

- Care should be taken not to freeze to death (Stalker and Interloper) while sleeping with a bedroll, especially outside. This includes checking the current temperature, weather conditions, fire duration, and not sleeping for many hours at a time.
- Sleeping without a bedroll is possible inside [cars and trucks](./Car.md) by entering the vehicle and selecting "sleep" from the Radial Menu (campcraft).

**Beef Jerky** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Beef Jerky features a high energy density, making it a valuable food item. Additionally, Beef Jerky can never cause [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md), and [decay](./Decay.md) extremely slowly especially outdoors (100 days per 1% Condition).
- Beef Jerky's logo, coloration and font is likely based on the real-life "Jack Link's" brand, which is also rich in preservatives like description.
- The back of the bag lists "Ingredients: Beef, Sugar, Soy Sauce, Salt, Cayenne Pepper, Natural Flavours" and that it was "Made in Canada"

**Beneath a Starry Sky** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is obtained after surviving for three consecutive nights outside in a single [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) game. It is most easily done on Pilgrim, but will often be acquired through normal gameplay on harder difficulties. It is highly recommended to pack sufficient warm clothing, materials for starting a fire, and food and drink, and survive inside a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md).

Outside refers to being anywhere but inside a building or other structure that has an interior loading screen. Therefore this achievement is obtainable whilst being inside of a train carriage among other structures. However, it is not obtainable in caves.

The best structure to use is a [fishing hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md), as these have protection from the wind, a pot belly stove, and a fishing hole that is an excellent source of food if the player has brought [fishing tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md). In addition, animals will not enter the huts, regardless of whether they have a door or not. Using a fishing hut with a door still counts as being outside.
Another alternative are the railway cars such [Poacher's Camp](./Poacher%27s%20Camp.md). However, unless the railway car has a fire barrel, the stay may be uncomfortably chilly.

**Big Cat Killer** is a [feat](./Feats.md) in The Long Dark. It was first made available in version 2.28 when the Cougar (now commonly called "[Cougar 1.0](./Cougar.md#Legacy_Information:_Cougar_1.0)") was released. The feat is considered "legacy" because it can no longer be acquired in the current versions of the game, but can still be earned using an older version.
- Big Cat Killer halves detection range, sight, hearing, and smell from all animals, allowing the player to get **much** closer to all [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) before detection.

- Unlike all other Feats, progression for Big Cat Killer required killing all three [Cougars](./Cougar.md#Legacy_Information:_Cougar_1.0) in the same save file. It also didn't show the percentage progress in the menu.

- The only legitimate way to obtain Big Cat Killer is to clear out your survival profiles, play version 2.28 or 2.29 (versions with the old Cougar) and kill three Cougars in the same save file. This process is equivalent to having obtained the Feat in the old version during the short time it was available.
- Big Cat Killer has been deemed a legacy Feat due to it "no longer seeming appropriate" for the reworked Cougar. It's planned to be replaced with a different "Cougar-related" Feat.

Birch Bark Tea is a renewable crafted medical and food/drink item which when consumed, restores 100 Calories, 30% Hydration and grants the benefit "[Restore Condition](./Restore%20Condition.md)". Additionally it may grant benefit "[Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md)" if the beverage is also hot. Cooking Birch Bark Tea increases [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Skill.
Restore Condition heals 5% Condition (2.5% per hour, for 2 hours), regardless if the player is awake/asleep, or even if [Needs](./Needs.md) are not met. Drinking multiple teas stacks this condition.

To cook Birch Bark Tea, one [Prepared Birch Bark](./Prepared%20Birch%20Bark.md) (2 [Birch Bark](./Birch%20Bark.md)) and 0.25 liters of [potable water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) must be cooked for 10 minutes at a lit [Fire](./Fire.md) with a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) or [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md). Birch Bark can can be found in the wilderness near lone birch trees or abundantly at birch forests, typically in single pieces after [High Winds or Blizzards](./Weather.md). Raw Birch Bark cannot be consumed directly and must first be crafted into Birch Bark Tea.

- The effects of Restore Condition are continuous, despite the player being awake, asleep, or even actively losing Condition (e.g. from a [Need](./Needs.md) not being met).

- Drinking multiple Birch Bark Teas will add 2 hours onto the Restore Condition buff for each Birch Bark Tea drank and the effect will not be wasted if one already has the buff. The rate of recovery, however, will not change.
- Teas may be heated/reheated to grant the Warming Up Benefit by placing them on a fire's cooking spot, or nearby a lit fire.
- Teas are more weight efficient than Water for the Hydration they grant. (0.1kg of a tea grants 30% Hydration, equivalent to 0.25kg of water).
- Introduced. [1.48](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog%20%E2%80%94%20Archive%201.md#1.48) (6 May, 2019)
- It is possible to survive exclusively on Birch Bark Tea, especially on easier difficulties or by using the [starvation strategy](./Hibernation.md) (only eating just before sleep).
- Birch Bark Tea is disabled during the [Challenge](./Challenge.md): [As the Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md), but Birch Bark may still be collected and used as Tinder.

- [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) is the only item which can restore all 4 [Needs](./Needs.md) (if consumed while hot), but Birch Bark Tea functions similarly with its Benefit "Restore Condition", since this heals Condition (2.5% hourly) faster than Fatigue damages it (1% hourly), so it is possible to survive indefinitely without Sleep by drinking 1 cup of Birch Bark Tea every 3 hours (albeit at 0% Fatigue, moving slowly and unable to climb/sprint).

Birch Bark is a multi-purpose item which may be used raw as Tinder for [Firestarting](./Fire%20Starting.md), or crafted into [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md), a food and medical item.

To craft Birch Bark Tea, two units of Birch Bark must be crafted into one [Prepared Birch Bark](./Prepared%20Birch%20Bark.md) (5 minutes in-game, no tool/light required) and cooked with 0.25 liters of [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) and 10 minutes at a lit [Fire](./Fire.md) with a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md), [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md), or [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md). Consuming Birch Bark Tea restores 100 Calories, 30% Hydration and grants the benefit "[Restore Condition](./Restore%20Condition.md)" and potentially "[Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md)" if the beverage is also hot. Cooking Birch Bark Tea increases the [Cooking](./Cooking.md) [Skill](./Skills.md).

Birch Bark can can be found in the wilderness near lone birch trees or abundantly in birch forests. It's commonly believed that bark respawns after strong winds or blizzards, but this is untrue. Radial spawns (bark, branches, coal, stones ect.) simply spawn on a randomized timer, independent of any weather conditions.
Raw Birch Bark cannot be consumed directly and must first be crafted into Birch Bark Tea.

The Benefit "Restore Condition" heals 5% Condition (2.5% per hour, for 2 hours), regardless if the player is awake/asleep, or if [Needs](./Needs.md) are not met. The Benefit does not stack however, and drinking multiple cups of Birch Bark Tea within 5 hours of one another wastes part of this Benefit.
Prepared Birch Bark (0.05kg) has half the weight of it's materials (2 Birch Bark, 0.10kg), and no form of Birch Bark/Birch Bark Tea [decays](./Decay.md).

One of the largest birch forests is in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), South/Southwest of [Stone Shelf Cave](./Stone%20Shelf%20Cave.md). Lone birch trees can be found sporadically in all regions.
- [Prepared Birch Bark](./Prepared%20Birch%20Bark.md) cannot be used as [Tinder](./Tinder%20Plug.md), unlike it's unprocessed form.

- The effects of [Restore Condition](./Restore%20Condition.md) are continuous, despite the player being awake, asleep, or even actively losing [Condition](./Condition.md) (e.g. from a [Need](./Needs.md) not being met).
- [Prepared Birch Bark](./Prepared%20Birch%20Bark.md) weighs 0.05 kg, half of what two Birch Bark (their crafting materials) weigh.
- Teas may be heated/reheated to grant the [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md) benefit by placing them on a fire's cooking spot, or nearby a lit fire.
- Teas are more weight efficient than Water for the Hydration they grant (0.1kg of a tea grants 30% Hydration, equivalent to 0.22kg of water).
- Birch Bark, [Prepared Birch Bark](./Prepared%20Birch%20Bark.md), and [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) never [decay](./Decay.md).
- It is possible to survive exclusively on Birch Bark Tea, especially on easier difficulties or by using the starvation strategy (only eating just before sleep).

- [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) is disabled during the [Challenge](./Challenge.md): [As the Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md), but Birch Bark may still be collected and used as [Tinder](./Tinder%20Plug.md).

- [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) is the only item which can restore all 4 [Needs](./Needs.md) (if consumed while hot), but [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) functions similarly with its benefit [Restore Condition](./Restore%20Condition.md), since this heals Condition (2.5% hourly) faster than [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) damages it (1% hourly), so it is possible to survive indefinitely without sleep by drinking 1 cup of [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) every 5 hours (albeit at 0% [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), moving slowly and unable to climb/sprint).

- Birch Bark is a real-world item acquired from Birch trees of the genus _[Betula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birch_bark)_, found across Eurasia and North America. It has a consistency and workability similar to that of cardboard, and has been used in a number of industries for hundreds of years including the making of paper, storage containers, canoes, shoes and roofing.

- Consumption of Birch Bark or Birch Tea has no significant documental medical benefits, though it is commonly drunk ("[Birch Beer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birch_beer)") in North-Eastern United States and Newfoundland (Canada).

- Real-World Birch Bark is typically harvested directly from the trunks of dead trees (removing bark from live trees is hazardous to their health), which is partially supported in-game where only loose pieces from the ground are acquired. However in survival situations (rather than in luxury industries), removal of birch bark from live trees (injuring/killing them in the process) is more common.

Provides some shelter **Bitter Marsh** is a small, shallow pond located towards the eastern end of [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), in the marshy, burned-out area. [Homesteader's Respite](./Homesteader%27s%20Respite.md) looms on a cliff overhead, and can be reached via a [Rope Climb](./Rope%20Climbing.md).

The most notable feature of this location is the small, partially destroyed [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) found on the lake. Despite being destroyed and offering little shelter from wind, predators, and weather, it does have a [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md) inside it, which will stay lit no matter the weather, helping keep the player warm as they fish. A small burned down cabin can also be found nearby, with a metal container and a few pieces of low-tier loot inside. A lot of [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md) plants surround the area. A [Moose](./Moose.md) can also be found nearby, along with a few wolves which may sniff out players who try to carry too much fish.

**Wintermute:** Yes A **Black Bear Carcass** is a harvestable "object" found after [Hunting](./Hunting.md) a [Bear](./Bear.md). [Crows](./Crow.md) will fly around a Bear Carcass and always drop 5 [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) around the carcass at a time. Bears are massive creatures, and their carcasses can be used as makeshift cover to provide a [Wind Shield](./Survival%20Overlay.md#Windshield_and_Scent) when harvesting them, a distinction also shared with a [Moose Carcass](./Moose%20Carcass.md).

A Bear Carcass may be harvested for 25.00-40.00 kg of [raw meat](./Bear%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md), 1 [Fresh Black Bear Hide](./Fresh%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md) and 10 guts. Bear hides can be cured to craft [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md) or [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md). On Stalker and Interloper modes, Bear meat carries the risk of [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md).

![Blackcrock Prison](../assets/Blackcrock_Prison.png)_Blackcrock Prison_ Blackrock is a side mission in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) must search for clues about the presence of [Blackrock](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) prisoners in Pleasant Valley, as well as finding out that [Molly](./Molly.md) has been hunting them.
| Significant locations | [Forest Cave](./Forest%20Cave%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%20location%29.md), [Hilltop Cave](./Hilltop%20Cave.md) |

The mission is initiated by finding the prison guard's body. The body is located on the right side of the road just after crossing [Heartbreak Bridge](./Heartbreak%20Bridge.md) on the way to [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md) from [Barn (Molly's)](./Barn%20%28Molly%27s%29.md). The prison guard's body will contain an improvised knife and a Blackrock Penitentiary Memo collectible. Follow the trail of blood to the outbuilding. Inside will be a prisoner's body with a blood stained convict note. Another prisoner's body is found further off the road in the same direction at the [Forest Cave](./Forest%20Cave%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%20location%29.md). To complete the mission, follow the road towards [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md), but turn left a short distance after crossing the unnamed bridge. The abandoned camp is located at [Hilltop Cave](./Hilltop%20Cave.md). Deep inside the cave on the left is an ammunition can cache filled with supplies: 20 [revolver ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md), [accelerant](./Accelerant.md), [MRE](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md), [flare](./Flare.md), [antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md).

- Mission description has been updated from "It appears a number of survivors from the Blackrock prison bus crash have found their way into Pleasant Valley. Investigate to see if the events in Milton have followed you through the mountains."

**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**

**Blackrock Blues** is the first mission in [Episode 4: Fury, then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md). In this episode, Will has to get medical supplies to help heal [Franklin](./Franklin.md) after [Mathis](./Mathis.md) beat him up.
| Mission details — Start location | Mission details — Blackrock Federal Penitentiary |
When Will awakens, he will be in a cell, and hear the voice of [Franklin](./Franklin.md). Stand on the toilet to talk to him and learn more about Blackrock.

Following the cutscene, the player will want to leave the prison and search the vehicles and buildings around the prison yard. These will yield a number of useful items, such as granola bars, flares, a prybar, fuel for fires, and low-tier clothing. One of the buses contains a note which will start the [Dark Star](./Dark%20Star.md) quest. If the player gets cold while searching, it's possible to stand next to the fire barrel by the prison doors, which doesn't go out.

Follow the signs to get to the infirmary. Once there, try the front door. It will be locked, so the player will have to go out of the prison yard via the two doors left open and enter the small forested area north of the prison. There are a number of wolves here, which can be dealt with using flares, torches, or stones. If passing close to the cliffs, it's possible to bypass many of the wolves and pickup the key from a dead guard, which will start the [Blackrock Lockers](./Blackrock%20Lockers.md) side quest.

Re-enter through another gate (left open) in the fence, and pass through the guard accommodations. Searching these will yield some food and clothing. When finished searching, climb upstarts and leave the accommodations. A catwalk will lead to the Infirmary. Once inside the infirmary, [Jace](./Jace.md) will call. Answer the phone and learn about her role in keeping [Donner](./Donner.md) in solitary. Searching the infirmary will yield a note telling the player where to find the key to the front door of the prison. After leaving the infirmary, cross the courtyard you originally started in to find the exit along the wall to the left.

Shortly before exiting, the player will come to a weapons locker. This can provide up to two [noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md), a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md), and a few [Flare Shells](./Flare%20Shell.md), depending on the difficulty. Once outside the prison, head along the main road in a generally southward direction, then turn east and cross an old log bridge. Across this bridge, a large patch of blood-stained snow will be visible near two pickup trucks. Follow this track to the south for a bit, then turn east towards [a cave](./Cutty%27s%20Cave.md). The required medicine will be on the body of the dead prison guard.

With the medicine in hand, follow the main road back to the prison. Before dropping off the medicine, place any items found along the way in a safe location (the locker in the guardhouse is recommended), else they'll be confiscated. The mission ends when the drugs are delivered at the jail's door.
- The name of this mission may have been inspired by "Folsom Prison Blues" a country song about prison life written by Johnny Cash.

**Blackrock Foothills** are a [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md)-exclusive region, which consists of the wilderness near the region of [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md). It eventually leads to the [Suzuki Environs](./Suzuki%20Environs.md) and the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md), accessed through an abandoned and unstable mineshaft.

The Foothills are a small, barren region just downstream from the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md) in [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md). Given it's nature in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md)'s plot, it is a rather linear region, with few locations within. Much of the region consists of rough, winding chasms and gullies, with some flatter basins here and there. Wolves can be found intermittently, though typically in the more open areas during the first portion of the map.

violations.context: #### **Ruined Cabin**
A burnt out cabin, situated on a small, reinforced overlook near a frozen pond. A prybar can be found near the front door, with a Cooking Pot and Firelogs behind it.

A huge, seemingly bottomless ravine with an inaccessible frozen river at the bottom. Given the many fallen trees, it is probably geologically unstabe. The player is forced to walk across a fallen tree to cross it.

A pair of abandoned logging trailers, aswell as a small covered shed in a flat clearing. Both trailers are accessible by the player, with the trailer marked "Foreman's Office" containing the [Blackrock Foothills Map](./Blackrock%20Foothills%20Map.md), a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md), and two [Flare Shells](./Flare%20Shell.md), among other loot. There is a fire barrel in the small area in front of the trailers, with two pieces of [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) inside of the nearby shed.

A set of two industrial cable cars used to cross the region's rapids to access the Unstable Mine. The cars are manually crank-operated, with the movement of one being able to move the other. Mackenzie is forced to cross various fallen trees to reach a rocky island in the middle of the river, which is high enough to reach one of the cars, as they were left in the middle of the river. It is the only way to access the Abandoned Mine in the Blackrock Foothills. The system itself is poorly maintained; given that they sport large gaps in their floors, and because Mackenzie is able to easily destroy the Pulley Mechanism with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md).

The Unstable Mine is, technically, a transition zone between the Foothills and the Suzuki Environs, with it featuring a number of [Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) mechanics such as [Toxic Gas](./Chemical%20Hazard.md), [Respirators](./Respirator.md), and [Canisters](./Canister.md). Two Episode 5-exclusives can be found here, in the form of the [Crank Light](./Crank%20Light.md) and Gas Lamps, alongside the Wintermute-exclusive [Bolt Cutters](./Bolt%20Cutters.md). The mine consists of five floors (technically, levels), with manual, crank-operated elevators connecting them, requring two people to function. Minecraft Tracks lead throughout each floor, usually helping to direct the player on where to go.

Almost every floor of the mine has at least one area full of posionous chemical gas, which the player is forced to remove by opening Clean Air Valves so Jace can follow them. The player is also forced to light the Gas Lamps on each level, as Jace is claustrophobic and deeply afraid of the dark. There are a number of puzzles within. The only area with no gas or puzzles comes is the Fifth Floor, which contains a large, sealed exit leading to the Suzuki Environs and the Radio Telescope itself. After exiting the mine, this exit point collapses rather violently.

- According to a line from Jace, a couple of hikers disappeared within the Unstable Mine the year prior, and although Search and Rescue were able to get inside, the search was called off due to the mine's instability. There is a high chance that the corpse Mackenzie aquires the Respirator from may have been one of these hikers, having died in a sudden collapse caused by the mine's unstable nature.

- There is a paved segment of road in the clearing where the Logging Camp is situated, and according to the [Blackrock Foothills Map](./Blackrock%20Foothills%20Map.md), it seems the road leading to it most likely led out of the region. It is unknown when the road became inaccessible, though it may be implied this alternative path is the one that the Convicts take to find Jace and Mackenzie.
- While the Player doesn't physically walk to the Unstable Mine's entrance, it may have been planned for them to walk to it based on the out-of-bounds space in the region, among other things.[^2]

**Blackrock Locker Keys** is a side mission in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).

To start the mission, the player must find any of three locker keys scattered around the [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) region. Each key unlocks a locker in prison guard barracks at the [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md). Finding and using all keys will complete the mission.

- Blackrock Locker Key #2 is located in a small forest area north of Blackrock Prison on the [Dead Prison Guard](./Dead%20Prison%20Guard.md) corpse. The locker contains 5 [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), [Combat Pants](./Combat%20Pants.md) and [Military Coat](./Military%20Coat.md).

- Blackrock Locker Key #8 is located inside a [Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md) at the bottom of the staircase leading from [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) back to Blackrock Prison. The locker contains 12 [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md), [Revolver](./Revolver.md) and [Flare Shell](./Flare%20Shell.md).

- Blackrock Locker Key #3 is located at an un-named farm in the south of the region, a short walk east of [Blocked Bridge](./Blocked%20Bridge.md). The locker contains 5 [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), an [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md), and the [Archival Report](./Archival%20Report.md).

- After the first time, it is impossible to crawl through the infirmary window again, but with a bit of wiggling it is possible to step up the tiny ridge (on the left side, near two "chimney" pipes) which separates you from being able to jump down to the doors of the infirmary. Thus saving you the return trip around the wolves.

To make a tough winter even tougher, we have got some new reports of that unusual wolf we dealt with last year. It's back, apparently. We had hoped its roaming had taken it far afield and away from the grounds, but these sightings, and its aggressive behaviour, are conclusive.
To help us understand if this is an issue with a single animal or part of some larger pattern on the island, we have engaged the regional ecologist to conduct a short study and give us some options.
In the meantime, stay vigilant when outside the grounds or away from your vehicles when traveling.

Blackrock is a maximum-security prison built in the shadow of Blackrock Mountain in the early 20th century. The brutal island wilderness that surrounds the prison is one of the reasons the site was chosen as a prison meant to hold "the worst of the worst" of [convicted criminals](./Convicts.md).

Sometime during or after the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), when the [aurora](./Aurora.md) first appeared in the night sky, a Blackrock prison bus carrying a dozen inmates crashed at the mouth of the collapsed mountain tunnel outside the town of Milton. A few of the inmates attempted to escape, and one of their corpses can be found a short distance away from the bus in Story and Survival modes.

After the First Flare, riots broke out in the penitentiary, with the inmates overwhelming the guards. The prisoners swiftly took over the facility, gaining control of the local arms stockpile, incarcerating the [prison warden](./Franklin.md), and executing the prison workers one by one in a marsh just outside the prison gates. After finally gaining their newfound freedom, the convicts found themselves in a new kind of prison; being surrounded on all sides by an unforgiving wilderness with no option of calling for help.![Iconic outside view of the Blackrock Federal Penitentiary](../assets/Blackrock_Federal_Penitentiary_%E2%80%94_outside_view.png)_Iconic outside view of the Blackrock Federal Penitentiary_Early in the story, in Episode 1, [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) cryptically mentions that, shortly before [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) arrived, she heard a group of people chasing a stranger who passed through town, possibly referring to the inmates and [Dr. Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md). Also revealed later in Episode 1--it seems Astrid passed through the town of Milton and somehow managed to escape through the collapsed tunnel through the Blackrock bus. She is likely the person who left the message scrawled on the bus's floor--a single word written in blood: [PERSEVERANCE](./Perseverance%20Mills.md).

In the REDUX version of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), an inmate named [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) appears as a minor character, having escaped the bus and helped caused the deaths of dozens of Milton residents by locking them in the [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md), which caught fire during an [aurora](./Aurora.md) event.

Blackrock is the primary setting for [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) of Wintermute, where Mackenzie is held captive by the remaining inmates, led by [Mathis](./Mathis.md). The majority of the episode follows Mackenzie helping the inmates with their plan to release Mathis's son Donner from solitary, and Mackenzie's efforts with Jace to prevent Donner's release. By the end of the episode, Blackrock is destroyed by an explosion caused by the inmates themselves and Jace, which leaves the entire facility in flames.

In Survival Mode, the main prison building has burnt down (similar to the aftermath of Episode 4) making it mostly inaccessible. However, a small portion featured in the escape sequence at the end of [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) is accessible through the Warden's office, via a rope in the back section of the penitentiary. This inside location is the only spawn location for the [Ballistic Vest](./Ballistic%20Vest.md), inside Cell Block C through the rubble, where it is guaranteed to spawn and always at 100% condition. The front reception desk is also accessible, but the rest of the prison is caved in behind it.

In addition, if you own the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC, the unique [Warden's Revolver](./Warden%27s%20Revolver.md) can be found in three different places inside the prison. It can be found:
- Behind a piece of debris in the main prison hall entrance, to the right most back side.

The outside grounds are fully accessible in Survival Mode. This includes the infirmary, a guard tower, and, after retrieving the passcode from the depths of the mine at [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md), the workshop locked behind a [Keypad](./Keypad.md). Once the workshop is opened, the player will have access to a [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) and [Ammunition Workbench,](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) one set of only 2 in the game, with the other being on the other side of the island at the [Cannery Pier](./Cannery%20Pier.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). Regular [Wolves](./Wolf.md) also spawn in both the front yard of the prison near the buses and cars, and in the small forest behind the prison. Unlike most areas with closable gates, the wolves are capable of pathing through the gates if they are left open, which may leave wolves wandering the open grounds. Large amounts of mid-tier and high-tier loot, easy access to rare crafting stations, abundant resources on grounds, along with [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) Groves and a potential [Bear](./Bear.md) spawn location inside the rear section makes for an ideal [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) in the region. Since the wildlife refresh in December 2024, it is possible for a [Moose](./Moose.md) to spawn outside the gate house.

- Navigating the penitentiary grounds can be complicated due to a number of permanently locked gates which separate the infirmary and workshop from the guard barracks, necessitating a detour through the outer prison yard and running the risk of a wolf attack. However, once in the guard barracks, it is possible to access a roof adjacent to the infirmary through a short series of catwalks and drop down to the infirmary entrance. This is a one-way shortcut.
- Despite the gatehouse being the only interior within the penitentiary with a stove, it is not safehouse customizable.
- There currently exists a bug wherein spending multiple days within the penitentiary will not be counted in one's journal as time spent in Blackrock.

> “__For intermediate players. Home to Blackrock Penitentiary, this Region’s icy rivers, deep ravines, and challenging weather act as a natural extension of the notorious prison. Its many caves and winding roads offer additional security if a storm moves in.

**Blackrock** is the 12th [Region](./Region.md) to be added to [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) (with the [Perilous Constraint](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog.md) update in December 2021), and is the setting for [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md). It is centered around the [titular mountain](./Blackrock%20Mountain.md) and federal penitentiary.

In Survival Mode, Blackrock connects to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) near the [Long Curve](./Long%20Curve.md) through a pair of transition zones: [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md) and [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), with an ice cave connecting them. It also connects to [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) through a transition cave.

This region is the first to contain [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md) and the [Ballistic Vest](./Ballistic%20Vest.md), which were added to Survival Mode in the [Perilous Constraint](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog.md) update.

- Noisemakers are a crafted at an ammunition workbench, but must first be found before they can be crafted (only found in Blackrock and a Bleak Inlet memento cache). Similar to flares, they excel at scaring wildlife particularly breaking Timberwolf pack morale.
- The Ballistic Vest is an accessory which provides massive protection from wildlife attacks (50%) at the cost of reduced mobility and carry capacity.

Blackrock is listed as a medium difficulty region, but surviving there can be challenging even for the well prepared. Natural resources are abundant in the countryside, and the region has an abundance of structures and vehicles for loot and shelter. Blizzards are frequent in Blackrock and make navigation difficult.
The greatest hazard in Blackrock is its high predator density; timberwolves, wolves, and numerous bears.

The local [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) at the prison allows crafting [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md) and creating new ammunition, along with a [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) for repairing gear.

Blackrock features the highest density of Predator Wildlife of any region. Timberwolves will frequently pursue a survivor indoors or along the base of cliffs for hours: exacerbating the dangers of [starvation, dehydration, freezing](./Needs.md), or [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md).
- [Deer](./Deer.md), [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md), and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) are commonly found throughout the region. [Deer Carcasses](./Deer%20Carcass.md) can also be found sporadically.
- [Wolves](./Wolf.md), though quite rare, appear in this set areas in this region away from Timberwolves.
- Wolves always spawn in the [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) and at the bottom of the river near [Fool's Corner](./Fool%27s%20Corner.md).
- They can very rarely spawn near the entrance to [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md), behind the [Blocked Bridge](./Blocked%20Bridge.md).
- [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) are the main hazard of this region, found throughout most if not all major roads, fields, and pathways.
- There are 3 potential [Bear](./Bear.md) spawns in the region ([Lineworker's Hideout](./Lineworker%27s%20Hideout.md), [Bear's Bend](./Bear%27s%20Bend.md), [Cliff Cave](./Cliff%20Cave.md)).
- [Cougar](./Cougar.md) appear if enabled, and are found in the mountains to the northeast.

- [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) is surrounded and infested with predators, but offers vast storage space, a crafting bench and ammunition workbench, and hunting outside the yard. An indoor connection to the western Blackrock is close by via the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md), useful in poor weather.
- The [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md) with its workbench and outdoor fire barrel.

| - [Bear's Bend](./Bear%27s%20Bend.md) - [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) - [Blocked Bridge](./Blocked%20Bridge.md) - [Bricklayer's Retreat](./Bricklayer%27s%20Retreat.md) - [Cliff Cave](./Cliff%20Cave.md) - [Cook's Farm](./Cook%27s%20Farm.md) - [Creek Bed Cave](./Creek%20Bed%20Cave.md) - [Cutty's Cave](./Cutty%27s%20Cave.md) - [Fool's Corner](./Fool%27s%20Corner.md) - [Forager's Remnant](./Forager%27s%20Remnant.md) - [Foreman's Clearcut](./Foreman%27s%20Clearcut.md) - [Grand Meadow](./Grand%20Meadow.md) - [Jailer's Residence](./Jailer%27s%20Residence.md) | - [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) - [Lineworker's Hideout](./Lineworker%27s%20Hideout.md) - [Mule Bridge](./Mule%20Bridge.md) - [Narrow Bridge](./Narrow%20Bridge.md) - [No Road Cave](./No%20Road%20Cave.md) - [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md) - [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md) - [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) - [Wedge Cave](./Wedge%20Cave.md) - [Whistling Perch](./Whistling%20Perch.md) - To Cave System (Region Transition to [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md)) - To Keeper's Pass North (Region Transition to [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md)) |

There is also 1 [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) that is found near Mule Bridge and a [Trailer (Blackrock Region)](./Trailer%20%28Blackrock%20Region%29.md). [Blackrock Mountain](./Blackrock%20Mountain.md) is also a major landmark seen throughout most of the region.
- Blackrock Mountain was first revealed as an in-game location in [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md).

- In Episode 1 of Wintermute, [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) describes Blackrock Penitentiary as housing "the worst of the worst". Given Great Bear's remote island geography, and the expense to staff and maintain such a prison, Blackrock is likely a "super-maximum security" (SUPERMAX) penal colony facility.
- Shortly before [The First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), a bus from Blackrock Penitentiary crashed in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), allowing the prisoners aboard it to escape.

- The Blackrock Mountain region contains three possible [moose](./Moose.md) spawns: the first is directly outside the prison roaming the small bog, the second is near [Cook's Farm](./Cook%27s%20Farm.md), and the third is outside of [Bricklayer's Retreat](./Bricklayer%27s%20Retreat.md) on the frozen pond.
