> “**Once home to a thriving industrial Cannery, seismic instability has cut Bleak Inlet off from the rest of the Great Bear mainland. Inaccessible and in the heart of Timberwolf territory, exploring Bleak Inlet is not for the faint of heart. The Cannery industrial complex holds a useful treasure for those hardy enough to access it.**”

**Bleak Inlet** is the 10th [Region](./Region.md) to be added to [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). It was released in the Errant Pilgrim update in December 2019. The region connects to [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md).

Bleak Inlet is a cold and windy region of ruined coastal industry, and a ring of wilderness around its namesake inlet of [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md). Entry to Bleak Inlet can be gained through a cave system from [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) or via a ledge by climbing into [The Ravine's](./The%20Ravine.md) basin.

It is the first region to feature packs of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) in [Survival mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), and two unique workstations: the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) and [Ammunition Workbench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md). An abundance of wildlife is present throughout the region, including many [Deer](./Deer.md), [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md), multiple [Moose](./Moose.md) and a roaming [Bear](./Bear.md). The inlet has two ice fishing huts, offering another renewable source of food.
The region also provides a third spawn location for the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) (atop the [Fallen Lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md)).

Initially, the high elevation areas around [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md) can only be accessed via [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md). Once on this plateau, the player may deploy a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) at a climbing point to allow bi-directional access between higher and lower elevations.
An electrically powered keypad-activated door seals the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) (similar to those in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md)).

Bleak Inlet was formerly an industrial region which supported the now ruined [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) (maker of the [Tin of Sardines](./Tin%20of%20Sardines.md) brand food). The cannery complex consists of ruined warehouses, docks, piers, sheds, semi-trailers, a sealed trawler and a trailer. All of these structures are extremely cold, with only the trailer providing proper shelter.

The Cannery plant off the pier is a [Workshop](./Workshop.md) that houses specialized equipment: the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) which allows repair of damaged or ruined tools and weapons, and the [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) which allows crafting new [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) or [Revolver](./Revolver.md) ammunition with the [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) Skill.

- There are three entrances to the complex: the front gate, side entrance, or coast. Entering the complex from all directions risks encountering a [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) pack in the courtyard. Once inside the complex, a Rope can be climbed and parkour route taken along the roofs of structures leading to The Cannery's main door.

- Access inside the Cannery is initially barred by an unpowered and electronically locked door. The passcode to this door can be found on a note inside the [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md). Once this note is read or picked up, the door's keypad can be accessed at night during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md) to open it.

- Notable loot include an abundance of [Tins of Sardines](./Tin%20of%20Sardines.md), [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md), and [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md). A [Safe](./Safe.md) with high quality items is at ground level in a ruined building, and a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) may spawn on the pier.

- A breakroom with a door off the docks contains a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) and [Bed](./Bed.md); however, like all the ruined buildings in the cannery complex, this room is only partially sheltered. To avoid freezing, it may be necessary to sleep in the cannery trailer.

- The breakroom and the room with the locked door have the same behavior as [warm caves](./Warm%20Cave.md): they have an air temperature bonus, do not contribute to cabin fever risk, and campfires can be lit on the floor, including with a [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) if the player stands in the doorway, which acts like a shallow cave. These can make ideal locations for cooking because they are wind-sheltered and the full campfire duration bonus can be achieved by standing in the doorway.

Bleak Inlet is a little short of houses, let alone _safe_houses. There are two enterable structures that could serve this purpose: the first being the [Cannery Worker Residences](./Cannery%20Worker%20Residences.md). One of the four of these buildings has a [bed](./Bed.md), [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md), and some storage. Some wildlife might spawn nearby, including a Bear, as well as a notable Rabbit and Deer spawn near the [Fallen Lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md).

Another possible safehouse is a small cabin located in a secluded corner of the map. It contains a [Rim Grill](./Rim%20Grill.md), bed, and decent storage. Deer and Rabbits will spawn nearby, as well as Rose Hips and occasionally [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md).
Bleak Inlet is a moderately large map with a cold, windy climate and few indoor locations, making it challenging for even skilled survivors. |- |

Additionally, 1 [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) spawns in the hills between Summit at Ravine's End and Pensive Lookout. There are also a number of small, unnamed caves scattered throughout the region. A single [Cabin](./Cabin.md) is found to the northeastern most portion of the map and several [Trailers west of the Cannery](./Trailers%20west%20of%20the%20Cannery.md) can be found.
- [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) is home to multiple packs of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) and several [Moose](./Moose.md) and [Bear](./Bear.md).

- The weather of Bleak Inlet is very cold and windy with few shelters, natural or artificial, and has an above-average number of Auroras at night. On average its weather is less severe weather than [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), but comparably cold to that of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md).

- Accessing Bleak Inlet can be difficult: requiring either traversing [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and a cave, or two [rope climbs](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) from [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md).

**Blood Loss** is caused by a [Wolf](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), [Cougar](./Cougar.md), or a [Bear](./Bear.md) [Struggle](./Struggle.md), a Timberwolf "bite-and-run" attack, or by falling off of a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md).
> “**You are bleeding from a wound. If left untreated, you will continue to weaken until you die.**”

Suffering from Blood Loss is a life threatening affliction and will eventually kill the player if left untreated. [Condition](./Condition.md) will be lost at a rate of 30% per hour and blood drops will fall wherever the character walks. Active Blood Loss will always maximize the [Scent](./Scent.md) meter, quickly drawing other predators to your location.

Blood Loss from predator [Struggles](./Struggle.md) is always paired with an [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md), while Blood Loss from falling off a Mountaineering Rope is not. Infection is treated as a separate but equally dangerous affliction.

- Blood Loss is often accompanied by [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md), or [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md). Always make treating Blood Loss your priority if you can to avoid bleeding out.

- Blood Loss can be treated by applying a [Bandage](./Bandage.md). As of the "Faithful Cartographer" update, [Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Wound%20Dressing.md) will only treat Infection, it can no longer be used as a bandage.

- It is possible to suffer from multiple instances of Blood Loss as a result of multiple attacks or even a single wolf attack. The effects are cumulative and each instance has to be treated separately.
- Blood Loss will draw predators to the player through the [Scent](./Scent.md) of fresh blood, and gives maximum Scent value. Treating the Blood Loss will remove this odor.

- [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md) is always paired with Blood Loss, so use Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing or [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md) to heal it before it develops into an [Infection](./Infection.md).

**Bolt Cutters** are a [Tool](./Tools.md) used briefly in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) to open locked gates at specific points in the story. Bolt Cutter can then be carried or dropped after this point and serve no other function for the remainder of the Episode.

In the mission [Aftermath](./Aftermath.md), they are found in the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) middle level after [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) falls deeper inside the mine due to an earthquake. They are used to open a single locked gate in order to access more of the mine level, but serve no other purpose afterwards for the rest of the Episode.

In the mission [The Detonators](./The%20Detonators.md), they are once again used to open a single gate after finding the [Detonators](./Detonators.md), but serve no other purpose afterwards for the rest of the Episode.

In the mission [The Cold, Broken Road](./The%20Cold%2C%20Broken%20Road.md), a pair of Bolt Cutters is seen in an unreachable area with several supplies before the floor collapses. A wieldable pair is found later in the mine, and are used to open a single locked gate.

Bolt Cutters appear in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) as part of the [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md) questline in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md). It is now classified as a Collectible instead of a Tool, and is stored in the Mementos section once obtained.

Location: head to the [Headframe Building](./Headframe%20Building.md) to open a locked door (with the [Foreman's Key](./Foreman%27s%20Key.md)) in order to obtain [Foreman's Site Report Day 45](./Foreman%27s%20Site%20Report%20Day%2045.md) and some [Bolt Cutters](./Bolt%20Cutters.md). Going to the bottom level of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), the Bolt Cutters and are used to open a single gate in order to obtain the [Mine Gate Key](./Mine%20Gate%20Key.md).

This Tool was first introduced in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) to cut open the gate to the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) in the mission [You Fix My Rifle?](./You%20Fix%20My%20Rifle%3F.md), but have been removed since the Redux version was released.

A **Brand** was a [Tool](./Tools.md) introduced in the [Tireless Menace](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.321_%28Tireless_Menace_Update%29) update in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) during the Alpha builds of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ and was eventually cut in the Faithful Cartographer update. It is currently considered [Cut/Discontinued Content](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md), but can still be experienced by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).

The mechanic of taking [Torches](./Torch.md) from active fireboxes was used before the introduction of Brands, but due to the similarities between the Brand and the Torch, the Brand was cut and its role in the game was entirely replaced by the Torch.

Brands are hand held fire and light source despite being just a [Stick](./Stick.md) on fire, behaving similarly to an improvised active [Torch](./Torch.md) (often being dubbed "Mini Torches") by dimly lighting up your surroundings and providing a small bit of Warmth. Unlike Torches however, they cannot be manually extinguished, and behave similarly to an active [Flare](./Flare.md), and can only be dropped and picked back up. Brands cannot be thrown, but instead can be [Brandished](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md#brandishing) (swung sideways) to scare away [Wolves](./Wolf.md). Brandishing a Brand will use up 5% of the [Stamina](./Stamina.md) and around 10 minutes of its fire duration per swing.
Brands are the only Tool in the game that cannot be added to the Backpack, and will disappear from the game world after they burn out and are picked up.
Wolves have a chance to be scared away when detecting the character if a Brand is carried and lit.

Brands are taken from any active [Fire](./Fire.md) via a special button "Remove Brand," so long as the Fire has a lifespan greater than 10 minutes. Removing a Brand diminishes a Fire by 10 minutes and 1°C.
- Taking a Brand while holding a Torch, Flare or another Brand will cause the held item to be dropped.

With the Brand in hand, you can Brandish the item with RMB. This gives an additional chance to scare off Wolves that are actively stalking you, but is only effective when the Wolf is near but not yet charging.

The lit Brand burns for 30 game minutes and cannot be extinguished, except when blown out by overly windy [weather](./Weather.md) or by mishandling. Once they burn out, they are mostly useless as they cannot be re-lit or harvested for the stick. They cannot be added as fuel for Fires.

- Brands lose Condition as they burn or being brandished with. When they burn fully, they reach 0% Condition and become ruined. However, if they are extinguished through other means, they fail to become ruined but cannot be re-lit at all.

![Brand light](../assets/Brand_light.png) The Brand displays flickering orange flames when it is first created that gradually diminish as condition is lost. Area lighting also diminishes as the flame dies.

- If a Brand is already burning in the game when another one is pulled from a fire, the new brand animation will echo the previous brand, causing it to seemingly burn out early. The animation can be reset to mirror the actual brand by dropping it.

A fire held in the hand is much warmer to the character than fire burning nearby. Holding a burning brand raises the [Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md) temperature by 5°C. So, taking a Brand from a fire actually grants a bonus of 4°C for its duration.
- A dropped Brand in proximity also raises the “feels like” temperature 5°C. To get proximity, crouch over a brand on the ground or relocate it to on a shelf or table or such.

- **EXPLOIT:** Light a 1 hour fire. Take out 6 Brands and crouch over them. Feels like temperature will be increased +30°C for 30 minutes vs. original fire’s +7°C for an hour. **Warm up faster and in colder weather with less fuel!**

- Note: Lit Brand can be used to start fire. With use of this, it is possible to start fire indoors even if you haven't any [firestrikers](./Firestriker.md)/matches (start fire outdoors with a Magnifying Lens and then take a Brand and use it to start fire indoors. You can start fire indoors with use of only renewable materials).

The brand has been specifically targeted by the developers to be very hard to keep in the character's inventory. For this reason, many of the normal object-handling functions are disabled and using the brand in some ways will actually result in buggy behavior.

- If a Brand on the ground is selected, the LMB function to pick it up is purposely disabled. If the brand is still lit, spacebar can be used to place the Brand in one’s hand. However if it is not lit, the spacebar option remains highlighted but will not work.
- When a held Brand is not lit, it is automatically dropped whenever another object is selected or inventory is opened.

- Note that the held Brand is still in the inventory despite all efforts to influence it otherwise. Viewing inventory will show it there as a burning stick whether it is actually still burning or not. It can from there be dropped. If its condition is still higher than 0%, it can also be equipped.

- Opening a container while carrying a Brand will allow the Brand to be placed in the container. Placing a burning Brand in a container will extinguish it. Note: Any ruined item placed inside a container should now disappear.
- It is impossible to get rid of an extinguished Brand once it has been dropped on the ground. It can only be relocated in the world using RMB.

**Breyerhouse Pie** is a food item in _The Long Dark_, it is learned from a unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) and is made with a [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md).

Breyerhouse Pie offers significant benefits to a survivor with a maxed cooking skill. Its meat ingredients contain only 850 calories (1062 with level 5 cooking) when cooked separately, but a cooked pie doubles the calorie count to 1700 (In reality 2125 calories because of level 5 cooking). It also uses the same amount of oil and flour needed to make two bannocks, which would be 500 calories at level 5 cooking, so it's more efficient in that regard as well. On top of its nutritional value, it has a weight of just 0.3 kg. This gives it an effective energy density of 7083 calories per kilogram (easily beating all packaged foods) and making it one of the most energy dense foods in the game.

The Breyerhouse Pie does have some notable downsides. Its moderate decay rate means a survivor needs to be careful about leaving any cooked pies in containers where the pies will disappear upon reaching 0% condition. The oil and flour needed for cooking can be hard to come by depending on the difficulty level being played. Finally, consuming it does reduce a survivor's max stamina by 15%, although only for an hour, and its other effects are all beneficial.

While the game interface shows it is intended to have a positive impact on [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), it presently does not reduce [Cabin Fever Risk](./Cabin%20Fever%20Risk.md), cause Cabin Fever Risk to fall more quickly while outdoors, nor lower the time to heal Cabin Fever while outdoors.
Breyerhouse Pie produces a [Scent](./Scent.md) which attracts [predators](./Wolf.md), and may be dropped as a [decoy](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys).
The ingredients of this pie are the opposite of [Stalker's Pie](./Stalker%27s%20Pie.md), requiring Prey [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) meat instead.

![Breyerhouse trucks in the Maintenance Yard.](../assets/Maintenance_yard.jpg)_Breyerhouse trucks in the Maintenance Yard._ **Breyerhouse** was a logging company which was active in multiple regions of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) the prior to [The First Flare](./First%20Flare.md).

The company performed logging in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), which The [Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md) allege was illegally harvesting of [old growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old-growth_forest). This timber was exported via railcar along the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) to the [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md) in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), with [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) being the maintenance center for the line. Multiple [trucks](./Truck.md) and ruined railcars of this industry can be found in these regions, some of which bear the Breyerhouse logo.

It is unclear if Breyerhouse constructed the Trans-Island Railway Line, or merely acquired it after [coal mining](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) or the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) ceased operations.

- The name Breyerhouse is possibly inspired by [Weyerhaeuser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weyerhaeuser), a timberland real-estate trust and wood product company headquartered in Seattle, Washington.

- The Hinterland Studio Inc. offices in Downtown Vancouver are located in the [building](https://www.historicplaces.ca/en/rep-reg/place-lieu.aspx?id=8781) which formerly served as the headquarters of [MacMillan Bloedel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacMillan_Bloedel), a Canadian Forestry company which was bought out by Weyerhaeuser in 1999.

**Bricklayer's Retreat** is a cabin located to the east of a pond, near the southeastern limit of [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md).

Quite similar to the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md) in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), this cabin provides basic weather and cold protection, along with a fireplace. However, this cabin does not have a closable door. A [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) can be found just outside the hut; it will receive the fireplace's warmth, but you will not have any wind protection.Its roof can be repaired using woodworking tools to increase the temperature bonus it grants by +3 C. In Story Mode, a [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) and some [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) can be found inside, along with one of the few [Bedrolls](./Bedroll.md) in [Episode 4: Fury, then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md).
A [Moose](./Moose.md) wanders around the small frozen pond in front of the cabin, usually to the northern side.

A **Broken Arrow** is a tool that is produced when a [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md) becomes too badly damaged. It can occasionally be found in the game world, often embedded in the carcasses of hunted [Deer](./Deer.md) near [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md).

Harvesting a Broken Arrow yields 2 [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) and 1 [Arrowhead](./Arrowhead.md), one less feather than harvesting a useable arrow. Therefore, harvesting an arrow before it breaks does conserve one feather at the cost of one less use per Arrow Shaft. It has no other use than to be broken down.

**Broken Body** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

The player must survive a [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) game set to the [Misery](./Misery.md) Experience long enough to acquire the [Broken Body](./Broken%20Body.md) Affliction (hence the namesake of this achievement).

Using the [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md) method can be a way to make time move faster, but the player must ensure that they survive long enough while having to combat the other 4 stages of Misery. The same survival strategies found on the [Survival Mode/Interloper Tips](./Survival%20Mode%20%E2%80%94%20Interloper%20Tips.md) can be a good start to learn how to survive on Misery, as Misery is just a harder version of Interloper but by a small margin.
Over time at fixed intervals, the survivor will be [Afflicted](./Afflictions.md) with the 5 Stages of Misery; permanent conditions unique to Misery making survival increasingly challenging.

Stage 1 and 5 are always [Diminished Form](./Diminished%20Form.md) and [Broken Body](./Broken%20Body.md) respectively, with stages 2-4 randomized between: [Haunted Mind](./Haunted%20Mind.md), [Frigid Bones](./Frigid%20Bones.md), [Rheumatic Joints](./Rheumatic%20Joints.md), and [Sour Stomach](./Sour%20Stomach.md).

**Broken Body** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) found within _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is one of 6 unique Afflictions that can be encountered only within Misery Mode experience.
You have lost the ability to recover Condition and are twice as vulnerable to physical damage.__”

Broken Body is a permanent Affliction unique to [Misery Mode](./Misery.md) which occurs from Stage 5 of Misery (Day 47). It completely disables Condition recovery and doubles all sources of Condition drain.
- All forms of [Condition](./Condition.md) recovery are disabled (Passive from met [Needs](./Needs.md), [Sleep](./Sleep.md) and all [Items](./Emergency%20Stim.md))

- All negative condition drains are affected. This includes negative afflictions, falling into [weak ice](./Weak%20Ice.md), fall damage, starvation, contact with [fire hazards](./Burns.md) (electricity and flames), and so on.

- Despite doubling all negative sources that drain Condition, Broken Body does not affect the final damage dealt by post-[struggle](./Struggle.md) attacks from [Bears](./Bear.md), [Moose](./Moose.md), and [Cougars](./Cougar.md). The only exception is [wolves](./Wolf.md).
- This means that if the player is ever attacked by any of these creatures, having 100% protection will not result in an instant game over.
- Has synergy with the Misery affliction "[Rheumatic Joints"](./Rheumatic%20Joints.md), which causes 4% Condition loss when receiving a [Sprain](./Sprained%20Ankle.md).

- Has synergy with the Misery affliction "[Sour Stomach](./Sour%20Stomach.md)", which disables the benefit from [Cooking Skill](./Cooking.md) level 5 preventing [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) risk when eating cooked or [artificial food](./Tin%20of%20Sardines.md).

- Has synergy with the Misery affliction "[Frigid Bones](./Frigid%20Bones.md)", which reduces the survivor's [Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md) temperature and the rate which [Warmth](./Warmth.md) refills.

- Has negative synergy with the Misery affliction "[Haunted Mind](./Haunted%20Mind.md)", which reduces Condition recovery from [Sleep](./Sleep.md) by 50%, while Broken Body disables all forms of Condition recovery completely.

The bridge is an unremarkable, completely destroyed railroad bridge in the region, with a [Truck](./Truck.md), [Train Shuttle](./Train%20Shuttle.md), [Rabbit Grove](./Rabbit%20Grove.md), and dead bodies with some loot can be found near the starting area of the bridge.

If players purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion, however, the bridge is converted into a partially destroyed bridge, with a section of railroad allowing access to the other side as a path towards the [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md). On the bridge itself is another Truck and a dead body with a [Backpack](./Backpack.md).

A ravine lies below the bridge with a [Mementos](./Mementos.md) pointing to it. Climbing down below reveals a [Supply Bin](./Supply%20Bin.md) with various supplies, with the [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section to access the ravine found west of the frozen pond behind the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md).

- The bridge was originally nothing but a broken in half railroad bridge since the debut of the Broken Railroad [Region](./Region.md). The addition of the Tales from the Far Territory Expansion patched the game to include an unstable railroad footpath, finally making the bridge crossable.
- The bridge is still broken in various [Challenges](./Challenge.md) however, even with the Expansion installed.

The **Broken Metal Bed Frame** is an intractable stationary object in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. **Description:** An old [Breyerhouse](./Breyerhouse.md) maintenance yard with the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) running through the mountain.
**Connecting Regions:** [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) (through [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md))
**Hazards and Survivability:** Although the weather is fairly mild, many predators roam the region.

> “**For intermediate players. Previous seismic activity means this section of the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) is dramatically interrupted. Be careful you don't become lost in its many twisting routes. Connects to Forlorn Muskeg and the Far Territory.**”

**Broken Railroad** is the 7th [region](./Region.md) to be added to _The Long Dark_. It is one of 3 regions visited during the course of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md).

Broken Railroad is described as a section of the Trans-Island Railway Line that was ravaged by earthquakes prior to the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), making navigation rather difficult. The region is connected to [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md). It is a relatively small region with mild weather, but is home to many [predators](./Wildlife.md): 6-8 [wolves](./Wolf.md) and a [Bear](./Bear.md), which can be difficult to avoid in the narrow, hilly, and heavily forested region. Beware that the (only) bear cave in this region is NOT marked with bones, unlike other bear caves.

A [Forge](./Forge.md) is located inside the [Maintenance Yard,](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) which allows the forging of improvised tools and arrowheads. Abundant loot can be found inside the Maintenance Shed and the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) nearby. The outside office in the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) has a bed and behaves like a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md), making it one of the few outdoor locations with indoor warmth insulation for preventing [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md).

This region will connect to the [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md) and [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) regions, if players have purchased the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC.

Broken Railroad, similar to [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) is a very small region that is quite isolated from the rest of Great Bear Island. It has several rabbit groves scattered throughout, but is very limited in game, with only 2-4 [Deer](./Deer.md) spawning west of the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md). [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) is possible in the pond behind the Yard by using Free Form Ice Holes, though care must be taken not to attack the nearby Bear or Wolves. If planning to stay here for an extended time on Stalker or Interloper, it is wise to get cooking to Level 5 as soon as possible, which will enable the player to hunt wolves and the bear and provide ample food. 4-5 [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md) can spawn throughout the region.
- To Far Range Branch Line (Transition to [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md)) (Only available with [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md))
- Prior to Rugged Sentinel, the winding path and footbridge was inaccessible except by scaling the rocks.

- A Rope Climbing anchor point (initially with no deployed [mountaineering rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md)) leads into a ravine along the western side of the region where the stream terminates. An abundance of items may be found below, including: hunting rifle, rifle ammunition, [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), [Wolf Carcass](./Wolf%20Carcass.md), 2 Deer Carcasses and cattails. Beneath the Broken Bridge is a bin likely containing wood, food or fire starting tools. The climb back out is long, requiring high fatigue, resting at the ledge mid-climb, sleeping in a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), or using an [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) to complete the climb.
- This region shares some characteristics with [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), including its small size, intermediate difficulty level, high predator density, and presence of a forge.

**Treatment:** 2 x [Bandage icon](../assets/Bandage_icon.png) [Bandage](./Bandage.md) and 4 x [Painkillers icon](../assets/Painkillers_icon.png) [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md)
**Alternate Treatment:** 2 x [Bandage icon](../assets/Bandage_icon.png) [Bandage](./Bandage.md) and 2 x [Rose Hip Tea icon](../assets/Rose_Hip_Tea_icon.png) [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md)
**Broken Ribs** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) only acquired from a [Moose](./Moose.md) [Struggle](./Struggle.md).
> “**One or more of your ribs are broken. You cannot climb, and your mobility will be reduced until this injury heals.**”

- Additionally, it's impossible to use [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) sections until this Affliction has healed (this can be temporarily bypassed by using an [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md)).

Broken Ribs does not alter movement speed, as the survivor can still sprint (despite the fact that this would be agonizing to experience). Broken Ribs can be a concern if the player is trampled by a Moose in a location that cannot be escaped without using a Climbing Rope should the player not have an Emergency Stim/supplies to treat the Affliction.

Should the player use a Stim in order to climb a rope, the lost carrying capacity is not temporarily restored by the stim: only the ability to climb is granted, hence the player should drop sufficient weight to be unencumbered even with Broken Ribs before using the Stim.

Healing Broken Ribs requires a treatment of 2 [Bandages](./Bandage.md) and 4 [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md) (or 2 cups of [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md)), followed by a Recovery Time of 120 hours (5 days). Recovery Time **WILL** count down for the Affliction even if medical treatment is not performed, but will never fully heal.
- Wearing a [Ballistic Vest](./Ballistic%20Vest.md) during a Moose Struggle will lower the Recovery Time of Broken Ribs by 30% (-36 hours).

- It is possible to acquire multiple Broken Ribs at once, and each instance of the Affliction must be treated separately. While having extra Broken Ribs does not further hinder the player's carrying capacity or stamina, they take incrementally longer to heal.
- Acquiring a new instance of Broken Ribs (regardless of whether or not the first was healed) will increase the Recovery Time by an additional 48 hours.
- The second Instance requires a Recovery Time of 168 hours (7 days), the third takes 216 hours (9 days), etc., with the maximum Recovery Time being 991 hours (41 days).

One method to quickly pass time is to purposely contract [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md) to quickly lose [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), allowing the player to Sleep for longer periods of time. Any Condition lost from the affliction will be quickly healed while sleeping.

Broth is a [Food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in **_[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_**. It is made using a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) and a fire, and can rarely be found as loot. It is capable of providing the [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md) benefit when cooked or reheated by a fire. Broth can be rarely found as loot inside of containers or as a loose item in domestic environments: such as inside the houses of [Milton](./Milton.md), [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), or [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md).

> **The Aurora can bring old Computers back to life, restoring old data left in their memory banks. These artifacts provide a glimpse of Great Bear before the lights went out.**

**Buffer Memories** are narrative [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md) found in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) on [Computers](./Computer.md) powered by the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) that provide insight into the lives of the residents of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) before the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md). They are also the main objective of the [Archivist Challenge](./Archivist.md).

Buffer Memories are only active and obtainable during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md); they may not be obtainable right away when the Aurora starts despite the computer screens lighting up. It can take up to 30 minutes of in-game time for the screens to become clickable. While only a single memory is displayed per night, it is possible to trigger the appearance of another one of the available memories by leaving and re-entering the scene where the computer is. This is not a systematic change and may take several reloading of the scene or interior for the change to take place or not work at all, forcing you to wait for the next Aurora. For screens like the laptop out in the open at the [Shortwave Tower](./Shortwave%20Tower.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), leaving the region entirely is necessary but isn't guaranteed to change the memory.

| Filename: LOG\_UPLOAD(4).doc (1/5) / Bear activity around the Mystery Lake Region is pronounced, although human interaction by all accounts is very rare. This is to be expected this time of year, and based on the available data we can make the following conclusions: |

| Filename: LOG\_UPLOAD(9).doc (2/5) / Suggests adaptation to the new seasonal high temperatures. Recommend further study to confirm shift in migration. Previous observations confirm their presence. |

| Filename: LOG\_UPLOAD(2).doc (3/5) / What a time to be out here, Shari! I made the right decision. Observations are going well, and I hope to be done with research here on the southern end of the island by the end of the week. Locals tell me I should have through the end of the month before any weather starts getting in the way of my plans to head north. Tell Dr. Chase the data look promising wrt his publication date. |

| Filename: LOG\_UPLOAD(11).doc (4/5) / Predatory species, if introduced could see a profound devastation of Mystery Lake’s local fish stocks. We will need to follow up to check whether there are attempts to introduce these invasive species deliberately. |

| Filename: LOG\_UPLOAD(3).doc (5/5) / Will be expecting their return this winter, but end results remain unknown. I hope to gather additional data on this phenomenon next spring. Continued logging could be a factor to consider. |

| Email exchange between Geoff and Teddy Wallace, two brothers, 21 and 25, Dam employees |

| Subject: Lower Dam sketchy windows (1/10) / From: Ted Wallace / To: Geoff Wallace / Hey Geoff, just finished my shift. Couple things -- keep an eye on the windows in the Lower Dam. The wind’s really been picking up down there this week and those old windows don’t look too sturdy. Just stay safe when doing your rounds, brother. This whole place is falling down around us. |

| Subject: Keep your head up (2/10) / From: Geoff Wallace / To: Ted Wallace / Teddy, just a heads up for when you clock in tonight, old McPherson finished off a whole bottle again and is sleeping it off in his office. Not the first time, I know, but the schedule is still the schedule. FYI I patched some concrete around Turbine #2 today. It might still be wet when you get here. |

| Subject: Clarke visit (3/10) / From: Ted Wallace / To: Geoff Wallace / Geoff, please plan on backing me up when Mr. Clarke visits next week. McPherson won’t say it, but we need more help out here. You and I can’t get this work done on our own. Not sure why you can’t just see things my way for once. |

| Subject: Re: Clarke visit (4/10) / From: Geoff Wallace / To: Ted Wallace / Roger that on the meeting with Clarke, Teddy. It’ll work out. I’m still grateful for the work, even if this whole project is pretty crazy. Once I patch my boat this Spring you’ll see it was worth it. Back out on the water, finally! Have a good shift. |

| Subject: Guess who's back? (5/10) / From: Ted Wallace / To: Geoff Wallace / Geoff, don’t forget to talk with McPherson after you clock in today. Remember that trapper we hired to clear wolves from Winding River last Fall? McPherson found him lurking inside the fence line yesterday, uninvited. He slipped away as soon as McPherson spotted him, but we’ll want to keep an eye out, after what happened last year. We don’t want that guy just wandering around. He’s been out in the woods a long time, and is so...unpredictable. Creeps me out. |

| Filename: MCPHERSON\_46.DOC (6/10) Vaughn left through the Winding River exit again without his safety harness. I've asked Teddy Wallace to check his gear next time Vaughn has work out on that side. Has my request for additional help been processed yet? Some of these guys are loose cannons. |

| Filename: MCPHERSON\_12.DOC (7/10) Witnessed Benton improperly accessing service panel #7 on the second turbine. He will get himself killed, or lose an arm to an electrical burn the next time he does this. |

| Filename: MCPHERSON\_54.DOC (8/10) he didn't say, but what he did find was Hays on the ground in the main bathroom. He said he slipped on water from the ongoing leak we've been dealing with. A fractured elbow, which means we're down a man during the refit. |

| Filename: MCPHERSON\_22.DOC (9/10) Conduit D caught fire in the lower corridor, but the suppression system failed. The Wallace brothers were first to arrive and managed to contain it. I'd like to see their response recognized by the company, which you can read in the attached memo. |

| Filename: MCPHERSON\_33.DOC (10/10) We spotted that local trapper again, our "ghost." This time he was lurking out beyond the boundary of the Dam's property. He seems to know some hidden trails to pass over to Winding River without dealing with our fence line. If in next quarter's budget, please send some company reps to make contact with him. We badly need the local help, and he might be a good contact. |

| Filename: diary\_3.doc (1/13) / After a long walk around town, I found myself in front of St. Christopher’s again. Even with Father McGill gone many months now, I still find some joy in tending what’s left of the back garden and sweeping out the dust from the Sanctuary. It warms my heart that several of us have banded together to keep the place feeling alive, at least for now. I know our little chores have eased the feeling of being left behind. Ah, Milton. |

| Filename: diary\_4.doc (2/13) / With the weather turning cold again, and Jason gone more and more, I have been walking a lot. It is a balm to the slow, freezing, stillness that creeps up on us every year. And sometimes, with a gentle breeze pushing my hair back as I look down over the Basin, I don’t miss Mass at all. God is with us here, in this place. |

| Filename: diary\_5.doc (3/13) / Jason left again this morning on another trip. Americans out of Anchorage this time. Here to see just how wild it gets on Great Bear. You would think they'd get enough of that at home. They will get all they can stomach, and maybe more, but at least they have the best guide on the Island to show them the way. I try not to cry when he leaves, but I always see something of our little family in his tired face. And when I do, his belief makes my own stronger. So I cried a little, just for a moment. This time Steph saw me getting upset which seems to bother her more and more as she gets older. Even at ten, her resolve and sharp eyes warm my heart. I see her father in her face, too. |

| Filename: diary6.doc (4/13) / I ran into Susan yesterday and asked her how the video chat sessions with Father McGill were going. She did not say much. But then again she didn’t come to our reading last week or the week before either. I know those of us left behind are not what she really wants, but it is all we have. I wish she could see that. It is so easy to be afraid of friends, and of love. And she has enough of her own grief after what happened. Out here, isolation can become its own special wound. I will check in on her again next week. |

| Filename: diary\_7.doc (5/13) / I walked Steph to the schoolhouse this morning, and then went up to the park on my lunch break. I brought some cheese and an apple, and read a bit at the benches up there. It was cold and bright, at first. Great weather for eating and thinking. The basin looked gorgeous, in that way you see all over Great Bear, where each day’s horizon feels unique somehow. / As soon as I tossed my apple core over the edge, it started lightly snowing. A vast, grey haze had settled over the valley below. A wolf howled, but from somewhere far away. Even as things have changed over the last years, and neighbour and friends have moved to the Mainland, I still do not regret our choice to remain here. I think Steph is starting to see this and understand it too. There is something wild, hard, and stubborn growing in her, but also kind. I smile when I think about it, perhaps selfishly. Rejecting pride also means finding ways to leave control behind, and let others, even your own daughter, find her own way from time to time. A good day. I hope my apple sprouts a tree this spring. |
| Filename: CHRIS\_JOURNAL(1).DOC (6/13) Mail today! First piece in three days, all the way from the east coast even. Gives me something to do, finally. |
| Filename: CHRIS\_JOURNAL(2).DOC (7/13) Higgins wasn't at his spot this morning. Odd. Can't remember the last time that happened. |

| Filename: CHRIS\_JOURNAL(3).DOC (8/13) After three years here, it's starting to feel like home. Still, we get fewer and fewer pieces of mail. For the all the letter writing folks in Milton get up to, it's a shame they receive so few responses. |

| Filename: CHRIS\_JOURNAL(4).DOC (9/13) A small package came in this morning and it's been in shipping limbo for a while, by the look of it. No surprise these days, but a minor miracle it got all the way here from Toronto. If freight has opened back up again, that's a great sign. |

| Subject: How are things? (10/13) / From: Peter Good / To: Dan Presnell / Hi Dan, hope you are well. Have you had any luck getting any pharmaceuticals delivered out there in the Valley? My usual Mainland contact has stopped returning my calls and emails. Supplies are low, and people are starting to notice the delay. / Peter |

| Subject: School Trip (11/13) / From: Dak / To: Peter Good / 15 Candy Bars, 10 packets of Beef Jerky, 5 cans of peaches, 15 bottles of Water. (Who knew kids could eat this much in a weekend?) / Add this to next order, please.\** |
| Subject: Please! (12/13) / From: Peter Good / Depot 23 / Antibiotics, painkillers, antiseptic, whatever you have. We're down to nothing and it's all my fault. |

| Subject: Patience (13/13) / From: Peter Good / To: Hank McDermott / Hank, I can barely get dog food delivered out this far right now. Quit asking me to restock the beer fridge. You'll just have to wait like the rest of us. Believe me, when they arrive, I'll buy you one myself. / - Peter |
There are four buffer memories in Timberwolf Mountain, all found at the Chasm Cave down in [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md).
| Filename: Robbie\_09.doc (1/4) / The jumpseat's all there is, so I said sign me up. Got to get home ASAP. There’s a chance it’s too late anyway. |
| Filename: Robbie\_11.doc (2/4) / They're promising me a bumpy ride. Sounds about right. Nothing and no one left this far north. |
| Filename: ForAngie.doc (3/4) / I made it down somehow. Ankle’s twisted up good. This damn computer’s going to make it longer than me, looks like. Angie, I'm sorry. |
| Filename: ForAngie2.doc (4/4) / One more trip up north. The way things are going it'll be the last, either way. But walking away right now feels good, if there's any good left in all of this. |

There are eight buffer memories in Coastal Highway, found at the Fishing Camp (at the Rabbit Grove on [Interloper](./Interloper.md), since the house at Fishing Camp is destroyed) and at the Quonset Garage.

Found on a laptop computer inside the cabin at the furthermost edge of [Fishing Camp](./Fishing%20Camp.md). This cabin is broken when playing Interloper - on that difficulty, the laptop is instead found in the cabin at [Rabbit Grove](./Rabbit%20Grove.md).
| Filename: LOG-09.doc (1/5) / Barren catch today. Winds picked up and turned offshore, so I had to come in early. As expected. |
| Filename: LOG-014.doc (2/5) / Caught sight of another giant trawler today, maybe 10 miles off. Definitely American, but couldn’t tell you its home port. I bet they’re busier than I am. |

| Filename: LOG-856.doc (3/5) / With prices as they are, it pays to fish. But only if I can get the damn things into my boat. The funding and supplies to refit they promised if I helped with that fish survey don’t seem to be showing up. At this rate I’m better off them sending me chewing gum to patch up my dory. |

| Filename: LOG-856.doc (4/5) / With all the lines I put out today, I was happy to get some decent returns. Been a while since I put down numbers like that in my book. It’s not anything like a recovery, but it lines up with the idea I’ve been havin about the Mainland fleet and their movements. |

| Filename: LOG-856.doc (5/5) / My ropes are fraying so badly I don’t think another repair for some of these lines is going to do it. I wonder when I can expect delivery of the supplies I ordered. A sailboat without a sail doesn’t do anyone any good. |

| Filename: BARBARA .doc (1/3) / Zero customers today, a new record! Just as well. The morning was better spent out on the dock with my binoculars. More and more ships passing, heading south. What will they find on The Mainland, I wonder. A warmer welcome? Not likely. Word processor Journal, by Barbara Quincy, Garage Owner, female, 62 |

| Filename: BARBARA (2).doc (2/3) / Tanker truck finally made it down here from up-Island. Wasn’t our regular driver, rather some guy they drafted into the job at the refinery it sounds like. He couldn’t say when the next trip down would be. It doesn’t seem too bad, seeing as we don’t get too many passing through these days. Bothers me more that the refinery is having trouble filling their orders. I can’t imagine propane and heating oil are in good shape if they can’t even ship out their gasoline on time. Even with more and more electric cars making their way out here, finally, we still need that delivery. |

| Filename: BARBARA (5).doc (3/3) / Apparently a small tree tipped over in the storm last night. It was leaning up against the side of the Garage when I pulled up this morning. And what did I see walking around up there? A wolf. I almost choked on my coffee. I left her be, and when I went out later she was gone. Bill Farney stopped to fill his truck with some of his crew and they were able to chop it up. I paid them in timber. Even now, the Island still has a few tricks I haven’t seen before. Folks at my old plant on The Mainland would have lost it if they saw this. |
There are nine total buffer memories in Desolation Point, split between the Lonely Lighthouse and Hibernia Processing.

| Filename: LOG-0236.doc (1/4) / Quake activity getting worse. There’s a fine crack forming along the base of the structure. We need to bring out a crew again to fix it, and soon. None of the little quakes have knocked the lamp too bad, and we’ve had zero downtime, thank God. |

| Filename: LOG-0157.doc (2/4) / Water is leaking through the floor around the drive mechanism up top. The sealant up there looks shot. I went down to Hibernia the other day to see if they had a bit of something I could patch it with, but no luck. A useless bunch, like always. But the fellows there have their own problems, by the looks of it. |

| Filename: LOG-0162.doc (3/4) / The main drive jammed up last night, but no damage to the lens or other components as far as I could tell. A lot of grease and some work with the mallet got it going again. That’s the third time this month we had a breakdown at night. Seas are rough enough this time of year. Anyone coming around the point doesn’t need us making it harder on them. |

| Filename: LOG-0171.doc (4/4) / An odd fellow tuned up yesterday, banging on my door. He was frozen solid, and said he’d come through the old mine, up the coast from the Townsite. I warmed him by the fire and gave him hot tea, some of my last. He had dark stories about goings on around the rest of the island, and claimed he was heading north up the highway. The worst of things since the Collapse hadn’t reached us down here at the Point yet, he said. I warned him about the damage to the road and bridges he was going to run into, but it didn’t faze him. He was sleeping right there on the damn floor in front of the stove when I left him. When I came back down after working some on the lens, he was gone. |

| Subject: OoO (1/5) / From: Manny / To: Greg / I just landed at Great Bear Island. DeepWild flew me out from the Mainland by float plane. Should be quite the trip. Remember, I’ll be out of reach for the next two weeks. If it’s all they promised, I’ll be a new man when I get back. |

| Subject: NOTICE (2/5) / From: DeepWild Adventure / To: Manny Douglas / We are sorry to inform you that due to ongoing instability in our fuel supply chain, we will have to re-time your planned extraction from our DeepForest Experience on majestic Great Bear Island. / Please be aware, it may take up to 7 business days before we can reschedule. / Thank you for your understanding and patience, / DeepWild |

| Subject: URGENT (3/5) / From: Manny / To: DeepWild Adventure / I was told exit plans for this trip were guaranteed! “Gold Plated Exit,” you told me. What happened to that promise? When can I expect a response? |

| Subject: CONTACT (4/5) / From: Manny / To: Greg / Greg, when you get this, contact my lawyer and fill them in on what’s happening out here. I can’t get a response from DeepWild and at this point I don’t expect one. |

| Subject: Safe? (5/5) / From: Manny / To: Greg / I’m still holed up with some locals. I’m not sure they’ve ever left this island or would even know how to. They seem to be losing patience with me. Have you had any luck? |
There are nine buffer memories in Broken Railroad, split between the interior Maintenance Shed and exterior Maintenance Yard.

| Subject: Checking in - trespassers (1/9) / From: Jerry Baltimore / To: Rick Dennis / Mr. Dennis, / I took one of the trucks over the Muskeg last night. I think you should know there’s some strange stuff going on over there on the run in to Mystery Lake. I saw a man on the tracks, but he bolted before I could get very close. A couple minutes later as I got closer to the tunnel, some idiots started throwing stones at my rig. Charlie took the truck back out to the Shed this morning, as I’m staying over here at the Breyerhouse Camp near Carter Dam to finish up. But if you’re wondering why the windshield has a big ‘ol crack in it, that’s why. / Jerry Baltimore, Crew No. 2 |

| Subject: Update - Forest Talkers? (2/9) / From: Jerry Baltimore / To: Rick Dennis / Mr. Dennis, / We were out in the hills above the Coastal Highway this morning when we saw a couple guys messing with our truck. We chased after them but they had a head start and scampered away before we could get back up there. We found an old knapsack nearby with some papers in it talking about “Forest Talkers”. Some kind of new green group, I bet. They must have done something to the truck, as it was bucking and lurching after that on the drive back to the Lake, including over the trestle! We figured water in the gas tank, but no matter. Was damn scary. / What does management plan on doing about these guys messing with us? Are you going to back us up? / J. Baltimore, Crew No. 2 |

| Subject: Re: Re: Update - Forest Talkers? (3/9) / From: Jerry Baltimore / To: Rick Dennis / Mr. Dennis, / Thanks for getting back to me. It’s good to know you passed on the word to management about getting more security out to the Shed. Even if we can’t always keep an eye on everything when we’re out working, it’s good to know our gear should be safe overnight there. / Jerry, Crew No. 2 |

| Subject: Status update (4/9) / From: Jerry Baltimore / To: Rick Dennis / Mr. Dennis, / The tremors are getting worse. Any word from above on whether we still have to take the short way to Coastal Highway? Even with a stable trestle, it’s a nervous-enough trip as it is. And our gear is already out in the open over there for the eco hippies still running around the woods this year. I know it’s more gas, and a longer trip, but if we take the long way ‘round, me and the guys would feel a lot better about things. We all thought you should know. / Jerry |

There are ten buffer memories in Pleasant Valley, split between Signal Hill and the Rural Store at [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md).

| Filename: easton\_journal\_1.docx (1/5) / First day on the job! Besides the usual reports, the weather service asked me to keep a personal log of some kind. It sounds like the fellow who was here before me had a touch of cabin fever towards the end, and they thought it would be good for me to write a bit. And with the interference the weather service guys have been seeing this year getting the emergency weather warnings out, there might be some downtime anyway. But the good news is that when we are on the air, they are going to let me broadcast a little bit of music as well. Should be fun. |

| Filename: easton\_journal\_15.docx (2/5) / Found myself whistling Richard Strauss tone poems the whole way up the hill this morning. Maybe Don Quixote a little later today? Then again, that’s more a piece for the Mainlanders these days. No windmills out here, only wind. We’ll go with Zarathustra instead. It’s been nice to get airtime between weather reports to broadcast some music, something to perk up the sleepy days out here in the Valley. |

| Filename: easton\_journal\_19.docx (3/5) / After a long shift, these notes start to feel more and more like a confessional. Tough for whoever the weather service ends up replacing me with up here. They’ll have to read through these things! Then again, I’m starting to mumble and sing to myself while I work, Glenn Gould-style. It’s probably better to write some of it down...haha. |

| Filename: easton\_journal\_30.docx (4/5) / My folks were pretty down and out this morning before I left. I promised my dad I’d see about switching up the playlist a little today. Maybe some Beatles would cheer him up? It’d be nice if the store at the Crossroads could get coffee delivered back up here to the Valley, finally. I miss that little mocha machine we had at the Conservatory. The practice rooms were tiny, even smaller than this Hut. A hot cup always made the hours drift by a bit quicker. Still, even spending all day in this weather station, I don’t miss the Mainland. |

| Filename: easton\_journal\_43.docx (5/5) / Great news! I got word yesterday there might be a piano again down in Milton. Only a dusty old upright, it sounds like, but still. The manager at the Credit Union pulled some strings and had one delivered from the Mainland, so the school could do sing-alongs and stage some plays. I had been down there a few times to play some Bach on the Church’s old organ, but it’s just not the same. I have to gas up my dad’s truck tomorrow, so I might drive down there and take a look. I hope it’s been tuned since it came off the ferry! |
Found on the desktop computer inside the Rural Store at [Thompson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) - across the street from the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md).

| Subject: Re: Family update (1/5) / From: Dan Presnell / To: Marie / Dear Marie, / It was great to hear from you, and yes, I am still out on Great Bear! It’s been a brutal early winter. We’ve had one road closure due to avalanches already, which in all my years here I can’t remember ever coming this early. Farmers didn’t even have time to get their hay in from the fields, the snow moved in so quick. At least I hope it’s the weather. There are other stories floating around that aren’t so easy to understand these days. Thankfully the late autumn deliveries were decent enough this year, and the store is as stocked as I could hope at the moment. But there are some desperate people here in the Valley. They don’t talk to me very often about how things are going for them, but I can see it on their faces. / Give my best to Greg and the little ones, / Danny |

| From: Dan Presnell (2/5) / To: Jim Galveston / Dear Mr. Galveston, / My last shipment from Better Food Vendors was incomplete. Although they are clearly listed on the invoice, I couldn’t for the life of me locate any Pinnacle Peaches or Big Moose Kicks Coffee in the pallet delivered to my shop. With winter coming soon, it’s very important that I get these missing items delivered as soon as possible. We’re a small community, but my stock runs out fast, and with shipping already so bad...Fruit, not to mention coffee, is rare out here on Great Bear Island. But they might as well be staples to us. This might be hard to imagine, but we Islanders have little by way of comforts and these items are cherished. I hope you understand the predicament this error puts me in. / If you could please look into this issue and let me know how we can clear it up, I would appreciate it very much. / Regards, / Dan Presnell |

| Subject: ATM Removal (3/5) / From: Dan Presnell / To: SERVICE REQUEST / Dear Service Manager, / I am confirming disconnect of our single, J735 model ATM at our store here on Great Bear Island. It’s been more than a year, and an empty ATM is about as useful as you can imagine. It’s kind of a bad joke just letting it sit there empty these days, but I don’t really mind. More to the point, it’s your property, so please let me know if you have any other service trips planned to Great Bear this year. I could even truck it down to Milton if it would be easier to pick up there. / Please update me on if this is possible or not, at your earliest convenience. / Regards, / Dan Presnell, Customer No. K35812 |

| Subject: Long time no chat (4/5) / From: Dan Presnell / To: Doug / Hey Doug! / Hope you’re good. I wanted to ask you about old Tom Joplin, do you remember him? He lives over on Skeeter’s Ridge. He’s started saying some funny stuff the last couple weeks whenever he visits the store. He doesn’t look well, but you know, we’ve never gotten along really well. Especially since Linda got sick. She knew him best, from Milton. / Does he have any other family on the island that you remember? I’d rather not head over there and check on him myself. He might not even see me if I did. / It’s not the same here since you and Denise moved away! I guess I could get down to The Mainland to visit more often. I think about leaving for good more and more. With no one left to talk me out of it, it’s looking more likely than ever. But there’s still the winter ahead, no matter what I decide. / Just let me know about Joplin if you can. And remember brother, don’t be a stranger! / Danny |

| Subject: URGENT: Ongoing supply problems (5/5) / From: Dan Presnell / To: Jim Galveston / Mr. Galveston, / Forget the Peaches and Coffee, your man didn’t even make it out here this month! When can I expect him? Do I have to remind you I pay in full and in advance for these shipments? I pay what I do because they are vital for our daily lives way out here. In the past the money was enough to remind you of this fact, but times have changed it looks like. / I am available anytime, please email me. Phones are unreliable out here. / Dan Presnell |

It is possible to reload these memories, obtaining two memories from the same computer in one night. If a particularly long Aurora occurs that lasts most of the night, leaving and re-entering the building on occasion causes a new memory to load. The chance of getting a new Memory is not guaranteed as previously viewed Memories have the same chance to reappear (i.e. in a location that has four Memories, each one has a 25% chance to appear on each attempt).

Computers that are outside, such as the Timberwolf Mountain Chasm Cave laptop, do not benefit from this method, although the computer in the exterior of the Maintenance Yard in the Broken Railroad region is an exception to this caveat (you can alternate between this computer and the one inside).

**Building Blackrock** is a series of [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md) found in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story that reveal the history of Blackrock.
- Part One is found on the first toilet in the bathroom of the Guard Barracks at the Prison Yard (areas with lockers for [Blackrock Lockers](./Blackrock%20Lockers.md))
### Part One:

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Building Blackrock, Part One**_

Blackrock’s establishment as a maximum-security incarceration complex is a mixture of truth, legend, and good old-fashioned hyperbole. But its founding is without question bound up with the history of Great Bear Island.
Local communities, almost as a rule, steer clear of the Penitentiary. Whether that is due to reasonable caution or unreasonable fear, no one can say.

There are still others who claim that nothing can match the harshness of winter living on Great Bear, and that Islanders should feel secure in their own hardy resilience. They are tougher than any prison inmate.
### Part Two:

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Building Blackrock, Part Two**_

Little is known about Blackrock Penitentiary's original architect, G.W. Jahnn. A pipe organ builder and designer by trade, he switched to institutional design after emigrating to Canada in the late 19th Century.

In terms of his design influences, the official records only note his intense interest in Egyptian monuments, British social theorist Jeremy Bentham, and a somewhat peculiar fascination with the music and astronomy of ancient Greece.
All in all, his work, and the prison itself, make for a remarkable and unusual contribution to the rugged landscape of Great Bear Island.
### Part Three:

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Building Blackrock, Part Three**_

Nothing in Blackrock's design could outweigh the influence of the surrounding landscape on the mission of the Penitentiary. The rugged valley surrounding the prison grounds has always been itself a secondary deterrent.

Before the first stone was laid for the Penitentiary, gold miners and prospectors made their way to the region to try their hand at finding fortune in the shadow of Blackrock mountain. Many died, and few found the gold they were looking for.
Still, it's said the many streams and rivers that surround the prison grounds still carry gold, even in winter.

Bullets are a material for crafting ammunition at the [Ammunition Workbench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) and [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md). Six bullets are produced from one [Scrap Lead](./Scrap%20Lead.md) at the Ammunition Forge (found with the Ammunition Workbench), which must be lit and with 1 hour or more fuel inside of it. Scrap Lead is obtained by harvesting a [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md) (found beneath the hood of some cars and trucks) with a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md); one Car Battery will always yield six Scrap Lead; each piece of Scrap Lead may be crafted into six [Bullets](./Bullet.md), so one Car Battery always allows the crafting of 36 Bullets.
Each bullet can be crafted into one [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md) or [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md).
Bullets may also be acquired by harvesting Revolver or Hunting Rifle Ammunition (with higher chance of receiving them, at higher Gunsmithing skill).

- Crafting Bullets requires a lot of fuel and time: 1 hour per Scrap Lead (6 Bullets) produced.
- Not all vehicles have batteries, only ~50% will have one. Chance depends on the difficulty level, on Interloper it's very low.
- Batteries can also be found outside of cars in different locations, such as Hibernia and many others.
- Car Batteries weigh 15kg, but can be harvested with a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) into 6 pieces of **Scrap Lead** weighting just 1.5kg.

- Car Batteries and Scrap Lead are useless on Interloper difficulty because firearms never spawn, as well as [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) Episodes because there is no access to an [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md).
- It is advised to craft a lot of bullets first if your gunsmithing skill is low, since crafting them also give experience points, so wasting ingredients can be avoided.

- Despite bullets for the Revolver and Hunting Rifle Ammunition being of different lengths, the Bullet object model used for both ammo types is the same size. Rifle rounds typically have longer bullet lengths than pistol rounds, but using a Bullet for hunting rifle ammunition does not affect its lethality. Evidence that different bullets existed can be seen in cut icons found in the game files.
- [Custom Mode] Bullets now spawn correctly, when Low Availability Resources is enabled, in Custom Mode.

Has an interior **Bunker Alpha** is one of the bunkers that can be found as part of the [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) Tale in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md).

This bunker can only be found after having fixed the [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) at the [Shortwave Tower East](./Shortwave%20Tower%20East.md) near [Muskeg Overlook](./Muskeg%20Overlook.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), then traveling to Bleak Inlet when the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) is active with the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) in hand. Prior to this, the entrance is completely covered by snow, and cannot be uncovered.
The bunker is somewhat U shaped, with the front door closed upon entering (some [Crates](./Crate.md) are also at the entrance).

The front door gives way to a kitchen with 2 [Beds](./Bed.md), a sink with [Stored Water](./Stored%20Water.md), 2 [Canned Corn](./Canned%20Corn.md), and 2 [Canned Ham](./Canned%20Ham.md), with several hatches next to the beds.

The back kitchen has a door to a hallway intersection. The left path leads to a bathroom with a [Towel](./Towel.md) and [Industrial Toilet](./Industrial%20Toilet.md). The path to the right leads to a storage closet at the end of the hall with [Security Chief's Log 14](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%2014.md), with another door leading to a research lab with [Interview Transcript 4](./Interview%20Transcript%204.md).

Has an interior **Bunker** **Beta** is one of the bunkers that can be found as part of the [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) Tale in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).

This bunker can only be found after having fixed the [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) at the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md) near [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md), then traveling northwest with the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) when the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) is active, at the west end of the map, due south close to [Three Strikes Farmstead](./Three%20Strikes%20Farmstead.md)/due north of [Long Curve](./Long%20Curve.md) and past a Bear Cave (beware the potential Aurora [Bear](./Bear.md) when traveling to uncover the bunker). Prior to this, the entrance is completely covered by snow and cannot be uncovered.
The room behind the front entrance is a small storage room with 2 [Metal Containers](./Metal%20Container.md), [Work Boots](./Work%20Boots.md), and 2 [Flares](./Flare.md), with a hallway just ahead.
Moving forwards across the hallway leads to a bathroom with an [Industrial Toilet](./Industrial%20Toilet.md) and a [Towel](./Towel.md), but not much else.

Turning left of the hallway leads to a kitchen with [Stored Water](./Stored%20Water.md), 3 [Canned Corn](./Canned%20Corn.md), 1 [Canned Ham](./Canned%20Ham.md), 1 [Pinnacle Peaches](./Pinnacle%20Peaches.md), 2 [Beds](./Bed.md), a [Trash Can](./Trash%20Can.md), a [First Aid Kit](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md), 1 [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md), 2 [Recycled Cans](./Recycled%20Can.md), 1 [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), and [Security Chief's Log 23](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%2023.md).

Turning right of the hallway leads to a machine storage room, with 1 [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md), 1 [Replacement Fuse](./Replacement%20Fuse.md), 1 [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), 1 [Wire Bundle](./Wires.md), and [Interview Transcript 12](./Interview%20Transcript%2012.md).

As with most of the other bunkers unlocked during [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md), the bunker does not a particularly practical safe house, despite its plentiful loot. In addition to being isolated, it is very dark inside, requiring a light to navigate, and lacks a fireplace. While it may be useful for providing emergency shelter if caught in a blizzard, there are much better locations to turn into a safehouse in the region.

This bunker can only be found after having fixed the [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) at the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md) near [Milton](./Milton.md), then traveling to the Valley with the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) when the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) is active. Prior to this, the entrance is completely covered by snow and cannot be uncovered.

This bunker offers the only permanent man-made structure in the entire region, and features a few underground rooms. The layout of the bunker is very L shaped, with the initial room being a the research lab with a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) and then turning into a kitchen with 2 [Beds](./Bed.md) and a nearby bathroom with an [Industrial Toilet](./Industrial%20Toilet.md).

There is lots of food present in the kitchen, such 2 [Canned Corn](./Canned%20Corn.md), 1 [Canned Ham](./Canned%20Ham.md), and 1 [Tomato Soup](./Tomato%20Soup.md). A toilet and [Stored Water](./Stored%20Water.md) can provide a limited supply of [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md). There are also several [Cloth (Object)](./Cloth%20%28Object%29.md) lying on the ground which can be harvested, helping supplement the limited availability of [Cloth](./Cloth.md) on the map.

2 Collectibles for the Tale are found here; [Security Chief's Log 6](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%206.md) is found in the kitchen, while [Interview Transcript 14](./Interview%20Transcript%2014.md) is found in the lab.

Of all the bunkers in Signal Void, this one is the most useful as a safehouse. In addition to offering excellent shelter during blizzards, the bunker has good hunting nearby, and is the only place in Hushed River Valley with a workbench. Its relatively central location and larger size makes it superior to the [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) overall. Its major downsides are that it is dark inside and a lack of other facilities: the closest [Forge](./Forge.md) is [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and to replenish ammunition it's a long trek to the [Workshop](./Workshop.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md).

This bunker can only be found after having fixed all the [Transmitters](./Transmitters.md) in Lower Great Bear AND visiting all three other bunkers, as required by the mission objectives. Then return to Forsaken Airfield when the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) or a [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) event is active to locate it. Prior to this, the entrance is completely covered by snow, and cannot be uncovered without the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md).

This is the largest of all the bunkers discovered in the [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) tale, and features a bedroom with four beds, a bathroom, a kitchen, a workshop, an office, and several storage rooms. This location counts as "underground" in the Frontier, therefore staying here when Glimmer Fog is active will prevent the player from getting [Insomnia](./Insomnia.md). In addition to the notes required to complete the Tale, the bunker contains a wide variety of high-tier [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), [clothing](./Clothing.md), and [tools](./Tools.md). The [Security Chief's Rifle Holster](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Rifle%20Holster.md) can be found here, inside the kitchen area, as well as 5 [Canned Corn](./Canned%20Corn.md) and 5 [Canned Ham](./Canned%20Ham.md).

Despite the bunker's large size and plentiful loot, it is not a particularly practical [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) in the region, as it is not easy to find, it's rather isolated, has no indoor fireplace, and is very dark, requiring a light source to navigate. That being said, the bunker is not far from [Justy's Hovel](./Justy%27s%20Hovel.md), which may make it a good location for players using the Hovel as a safe house to wait out Glimmer Fog or for crafting on the workbench.
The player is required to return here as part of [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md), to find one final secret hidden within the bunker; a hidden room in a closet storage area.

- Given the size of the bunker, it is highly likely that it, along with the [other](./Bunker%20Alpha.md) [three](./Bunker%20Beta.md) [bunkers](./Bunker%20Gamma.md) and the [prepper caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md), were built as fallout shelters in case of nuclear war.

**Bunker Rifle** is a unique variant of the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

The Bunker Rifle stands out from other rifles on [Great Bear](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), as it features a grey-blue polymer furniture resembling more modern hunting rifles. Optimized for maximum weight savings, it features cutout holes on the stock and grip; reducing its total unloaded weight to a mere 1.50 Kg, as well as halving the rate of aim stamina drain. The rifle is extremely fragile and will degrade a whopping 4% condition per shot fired. At 100% condition, it can fire up to 25 times before breaking, and up to 50 times total with [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) level 5. As a slight consolation, the rifle is slightly easier to fix with Firearm cleaning kits and gains 1% more condition per repair, however, the player should still expect to burn through a lot of cleaning kits (or time at the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md)) if planning on using this weapon.
The Bunker Rifle also features a unique set of iron sights with a pointed front sight post, letting you more accurately see where your shot will land.
Successful shots on live targets provide experience in the [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) skill.

Only obtainable as a trade item through [Sutherland](./Trader.md), the Trader, after completing [Special Request #4](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md). It will then appear as a potential trade, and can be ordered repeatedly (this can make them disposable backups to counter the condition loss when multiple are ordered, compensating for the finite number of [Firearm Cleaning Kits](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md) in the world).

- The name and description of this rifle is related to the various [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md) on the Island, and it may be possible that this rifle originally belonged to Sutherland's brother Wyatt.
- If so, Wyatt may have ordered several surplus rifles for survival reasons (possibly for his friends and family or as backups). This may also be the reason why Sutherland has so many to trade.

- Contrary to in-game depictions, polymer furnished hunting rifles are better suited for the harsh temperatures and extreme moisture on the island over the older wooden furniture rifles, as wood is prone to cracking and warping in these severe conditions.
