**Burdened** is a unique [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ only encountered in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) when consuming certain [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Recipes. It was added in the Part 3 update to the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md).

Burdened is acquired from consuming certain recipes that effects a survivor's [Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md) by temporarily lowering their maximum total carry weight by 3kg for 1 hour. This can be an especially dangerous Affliction to acquire when a survivor is already under the negative effects of low carrying capacity gained from low [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md).

The effect of this Affliction does not stack, and each application will not override the previous Affliction. Partially eating the previously mentioned foods only adds a partial amount of Burdened Recovery Time.

A symbol similar for the Burdened Affliction icon appears in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) whenever [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) is carrying a [Crash Survivor](./Crash%20Survivor.md).

**Burdock Tea** is a medicinal [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) drink brewed from [Prepared Burdock](./Prepared%20Burdock.md) Roots.
It was added in the free update portion of the Part 3: Frontier Cooking for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.

- [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) (1 dose and 10 days Sleep on Stalker (20 days on Interloper))

Compared to Reishi Tea, Burdock Tea takes more effort to find materials for and then cook into tea, with [Burdock](./Burdock.md) saplings being less plentiful to find compared to [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md).

**Burdocks** are a sapling plant that were released with the free update Part 3: Frontier Comforts portion of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.
Burdocks are a dark brown, medium sized sapling that can be found on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), and can be harvested for a single [Burdock Root](./Burdock%20Root.md).

Burdocks need a [tool](./Tools.md) to be harvested, similar to [Maple](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md) and [Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md). [Hacksaws](./Hacksaw.md) cannot be used to harvest Burdocks, as the objective is to harvest the roots of the plant, not the stem. As a result, they take three times as long to harvest since they need to be dug out of the ground rather than cut down.

[Improvised Hatchets](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md)/[Hatchets](./Hatchet.md), [Hunting](./Hunting%20Knife.md)/[Improvised Knives](./Improvised%20Knife.md), and [Prybars](./Prybar.md) can also be used to dig up the roots, offering a wider range of harvesting options than Maple and Birch saplings.

Each plant yields one Burdock Root, which can be [prepared](./Prepared%20Burdock.md) and eaten raw, or made into a [tea](./Burdock%20Tea.md). Burdocks saplings do not respawn once harvested, and leave a dark hole in the ground where they once grew. Burdock spawns are randomly generated and may vary across playthroughs, leading to spots that had burdocks on previous playthroughs now being empty. The following list of locations cover all possible spawns regardless of loot table.
- A single plant near the cave after the three root climbing sections with rose hip trees that leads to the bridge going over [Shattered Cove](./Shattered%20Cove.md).

On the charcoal map, you can see a group of rock formations, the burdocks are in-between those large rocks and easily visible from the road when looking for that piece of river bank.
- 5 plants on the north edge of the pond if you're standing in [Bricklayer's Retreat](./Bricklayer%27s%20Retreat.md). They're at the foot of a cliff, at the top of which ptarmigans are nesting.

- A single plant can be found on the left side of the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) shed.

This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.
**Buried Echoes** is the second [Tale](./Tales.md) released for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

As of V 2.27, Buried Echoes can be started on a new playthrough out of order as soon as the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) is acquired, as long as [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) has been completed on the current or another playthrough and its associated Badge is acquired. The [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) will need to be repaired before this Tale can be started if played out of order.![Buried Echoes Icon](../assets/Buried_Echoes_Icon.png)
_This section may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark._

Continuing the events of the last Tale, the survivor decides to follow clues left behind by the Security Chief's Logs to investigate the mystery of Rüdiger's experiments. The Logs mentions a machine in the heart of a nearby mining complex, so begin heading to the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) while carrying the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md). Since the repaired [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) broadcasts its radio coverage into the Zone, there is no need to search for another Transmitter or parts to fix one while you are there.
- Use the Handheld Shortwave to track down the crashed helicopter mentioned in the journal entry.
- Search the Concentrator and Headframe facility for clues or tools to help locate Rüdiger's experiment.

Entering the Zone will prompt you with an objective to find any sign of life in the region. A signal can be located near the [Boss's Settlement](./Boss%27s%20Settlement.md) when the Handheld Radio becomes active, at the corner of a ruined cabin. Uncovering it produces a lockbox containing some simple supplies and a [A Page From A Journal](./A%20Page%20From%20A%20Journal.md) written on 18-June-91. The Author of said note writes of the strange events surrounding the region: toxic chemicals, sick wolves, and inaccessible areas in the mine, as well as a [Helicopter](./Helicopter.md) that crashed in the mountains near the water pumps.

Head to the [Old Corral](./Old%20Corral.md) near [Unquenched Extraction](./Unquenched%20Extraction.md). When the Handheld Radio is powered, head east into the hills to find the crashed helicopter to uncover a lockbox buried under the tail section. Claim the [Foreman's Key](./Foreman%27s%20Key.md) inside and the [Security Chief's Log 31](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%2031.md) that was also uncovered in the nearby snow.

After grabbing both items, head to the [Headframe Building](./Headframe%20Building.md) to open a locked door in order to obtain [Foreman's Site Report Day 45](./Foreman%27s%20Site%20Report%20Day%2045.md) and some [Bolt Cutters](./Bolt%20Cutters.md).

Return to the surface and head to the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md). From here, head to the top floor and walk outside across the trestle to open the mine door in the mountains. The door is locked, prompting a message to explore the rest of the mine for a means to open it. Before exploring the mines, head to the 7th floor of the Concentrator and locate a [Respirator](./Respirator.md) in the offices, as you will need it to safely explore the mines. Afterwards, head all the way back to the Headframe Building and go all the way down to the bottom of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md).

Heading below to the lowest level of the elevator shaft and entering the door will put you in a room either a building to the right that can be unlocked with the Foreman's key for [Foreman's Site Report Day 64](./Foreman%27s%20Site%20Report%20Day%2064.md). Collect it and head left from the mineshaft elevator door and continue onwards until you find a large airshaft cavern with a catwalk going around it. A nearby locked gate can be opened with the Bolt Cutters and a Corpse can be looted for the [Mine Gate Key](./Mine%20Gate%20Key.md).

Head back up to the mountain mine entrance and unlock the gate. [Security Chief's Log 32](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%2032.md) can be found in the gated area to the right upon entering. Head down the minecart railroad until you find a Supply Bin with [Foreman's Site Report Day 38](./Foreman%27s%20Site%20Report%20Day%2038.md) on it. Continue down even further until you find a room with a several crates and yet another [Security Chief's Log 33](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%2033.md). Head down the tunnel made of concrete to find the machine that was built inside the mine, and approach the console. The player will pass out from touching it and will reawaken to find that an Aurora/Glimmer Fog event has activated the machine. After this, head into the nearby control room to find [My Testament](./My%20Testament.md), [Security Chief's Log (illegible)](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%20%28illegible%29.md), [Foreman's Site Report Day (illegible)](./Foreman%27s%20Site%20Report%20Day%20%28illegible%29.md), and [The Security Chief's Remains](./The%20Security%20Chief%27s%20Remains.md).

A [Faded Photograph](./Faded%20Photograph.md) is added to the player's inventory when picking up the Security Chief's final log, read it and you will be instructed to lay her remains to rest at the [Enduring Waterfall](./Enduring%20Waterfall.md). Before leaving, be sure to pick up the ultimate prize of this Tale, the [Foreman's Tool Belt](./Foreman%27s%20Tool%20Belt.md), if you haven't already. Returning to the previous room with the minecarts and walking down the tunnel filled with water will lead the player to open another locked door to the Level 1 section of the mine, and a nearby shoe conveyor can be taken to the [Conveyor Room](./Conveyor%20Room.md). Travel to Enduring Waterfall to the south west of the map and lay the Chief to rest by placing her remains in the open snow close to the fallen tree bridge, thus ending the Tale.
The Tales from the Far Territory is to be concluded in the third and final Tale [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md)...

Provides some shelter **Burned Ridge Cave** is one of several caves dotted throughout [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).

Burned Ridge Cave lies just south-west of [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md) on the western most side of the region. It is not far from the plane [crash site](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md), and lies just off a path down the mountain. This is a prime location to rest at when rescuing a survivor of a crash. The cave is deep enough for cover from the wind, but also allows you to build a fire. There is also a makeshift bed inside the cave, which is useful if the player is not carrying a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md).
[Rose hips](./Rose%20Hip.md), and maybe a frozen [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md), can be found nearby.

> “**You have sustained serious burns. Your general Condition will be reduced until you treat the burns, or you heal naturally.**”

**Burns** can commonly be caused by standing or walking over a lit [Campfire](./Campfire.md), walking into electrified wires during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md). Suffering from Burns immediately lowers the player's [Condition](./Condition.md) to 75% if it was over 75%, and prevents Condition from being healed above 75% while in effect.

The player can only suffer from 1 instance of the Burns affliction, having the appropriate affliction image from the damage source (fire for fire burns, electric bolt for electrical burns). Each instance of Burns must be treated before Condition recovers over 75%. Acquiring more Burns will not produce a separate Affliction to treat (ex. [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md)), despite more Burns appearing on the screen.
- Walking into open fires (ex. Campfires, any large burning fires found in certain episodes of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md))
- Walking into electrified water during an Aurora. ([Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) middle level)
- Holding a [Noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md) until it explodes or having them explode too close to the player.

Pressurized steam from the exploded pipes in the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) in [Episode 4: Fury, then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) does not give Burns but [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) will behave as though it will. Instead, the steam from the pipes lowers Condition.

Without treatment Burns will heal after 30 hours, but can be Treated and removed immediately for one [Bandage](./Bandage.md) and two [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md)/one cup of [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md).
- Campfires, downed wires, and electrified water also cause heavy and constant Condition loss as long as they are touched, resulting in swift death.

- Downed wires on the ground or hanging from above should be avoided during dusk and night, even if an Aurora is not currently active, since an Aurora could start while the player is standing atop them and die before being able to walk to safety.

- Notable locations with downed wires and electrified water include the interior of the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md), and Cinder Hills Coal Mine's "middle" level (accessed via elevator from [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) during an Aurora).

- Care should be taken when in an area with downed wires and [Wolves](./Wolf.md) (namely the [Cannery Workshop](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md)), as they can pin the player on a wire. In scenarios such as this, death from Condition loss occurs in less than a second, even at maximum health.
![PrisonBus](../assets/PrisonBus.jpg) **Buses** are a stationary [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) found in _The Long Dark_.

Buses are primarily found in the [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) region, particularly in the [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) yard. They can be entered and provide shelter from Windchill, but do not provide bonus Warmth. [Campfires](./Campfire.md) can be started inside the backs of Buses. Loot can often be found inside, including Clothing and a possible [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) spawn. The hood of a Bus cannot be opened to obtain a [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md). Despite having open doors, [Wolves](./Wolf.md) cannot enter Buses.

So far, all Buses are owned by the Blackrock Prison, as no other Bus variant is found in the game. 2 Buses can be found in the Blackrock Prison yard, one in the parking lot, and 1 in the garage near the ammunition workshop.

A single [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) can be found near the town of [Milton](./Milton.md) in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) Region, and is the only example of a Bus located outside of Blackrock.

The **Bushcraft Bow** is a variant of the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) in _The Long Dark,_ whose recipe can be acquired from the [Trader](./Trader.md), after completing [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md).

The Bushcraft bow is a handmade penobscot bow with a cloth wrapped handle, black stripe tips, and distinct green colored string. It deals the most damage to [wildlife](./Wildlife.md) when compared to other bows, and degrades slightly slower than the survival bow, however, the Bushcraft Bow has the potential to break much earlier than other bows; starting at 50% condition instead of 15%.
- Total durability is 20% more than Survival Bow (uses 1.6%-0.8% condition per shot based on [archery skill](./Archery.md))
- Can break earlier, risks breaking under 50% condition, all other bows risk breaking below 15% condition

Obtaining the [Bushcraft Bow Blueprint Card](./Bushcraft%20Bow%20Blueprint%20Card.md) is required to unlock the crafting blueprint, as this bow does not appear naturally in the game world. It is available from the [Trader](./Trader.md) after completing [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md). It will always appear as a trade when unlocked and the card can only be purchased once.
This cost is lowered when the player has gained enough Trust to get a discount from the Trader, reducing the trade cost to:

One key note about this bow is that it requires 2 [**Green Birch Saplings**](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md), not 2 [Cured Birch Saplings](./Cured%20Birch%20Sapling.md). This is the only tool in the game that requires an uncured item to craft. If you plan on getting this tool from the Trader eventually, make sure to save some uncured Birch saplings in storage, as although it is a renewable material, [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) can only yield so many Green Birches in a set amount of time.

- The Bushcraft bow's recipe card is available for purchase on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) and [Misery](./Misery.md) difficulties, provided the player has completed the entirety of [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md).

- At base archery skill the Bushcraft Bow can fire 31 times before hitting the breaking threshold at 50% condition. This rises to 62 guaranteed uses once the player attains level 4 archery skills. On average, the bushcraft bow will be able to fire more shots than the survival bow despite its higher breaking chances.

- Breaking chance increases quadratically as bow condition degrades, and follows this pattern: 4% break chance at 40% condition, 16% break chance at 30% condition, 36% break chance at 20% condition, 50% break chance at 15% condition, and 81.72% break chance at 5% condition.

- The damage modifier from the bow stacks with the [manufactured arrow's](./Manufactured%20Arrow.md) damage bonus allowing the player to inflict large amounts of damage to animals, the most notable breakpoint being neck shots (not headshots) on [moose](./Moose.md) become instant-kills with this setup.
- The Bushcraft Bow is based on a Penobscot/Wabanaki type of cable-backed bows, thought to be one of the first composite bow designs in history.
- The bow being crafted from [Green Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) is an accurate real-world representation of how cable-backed bows can be made from poor-quality wood.

Has an interior The **Cabin (Sundered Pass)** is an unmarked location in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) at the [Old Settlement](./Old%20Settlement.md).

The area around the Old Settlement consists of 3 ruined buildings and one intact two story cabin. The area around the settlement is patrolled by several large packs of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), making coming and going very difficult.
The ground floor of the cabin is snowed-in, so the two doors are covered by snow and are unusable. Walking behind the cabin and onto the roof the player can find an open window to walk inside.

Stepping inside, the window will place the player on a [Bed](./Bed.md) on the second floor. A [Trunk](./Trunk.md) and several [Crates](./Crate.md) are found on the floor, with a staircase leading downstairs into a kitchen.

The 2 doors on the first floor can be opened, but are blocked by snow, imprinted with the shape of the doors. The Fireplace is also covered in snow, and cannot be used. A small kitchen with [Stored Water](./Stored%20Water.md) and several [Drawers](./Drawer.md) and a [Cupboard](./Cupboard.md) is downstairs, with more Crates below the stairwell.
Despite being slightly underground due to an avalanche, the interior does not protect against [Insomnia Risk](./Insomnia%20Risk.md), even when on the first floor.

> “**You've been indoors so long you are starting to feel very uneasy. Spend some time outdoors before it gets worse!**”

**Cabin Fever Risk** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) that is caused by spending time indoors. This Affliction only appears when playing on the [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md), [Stalker](./Stalker.md), [Interloper](./Interloper.md), [Misery](./Misery.md), or enabled on [Custom](./Custom.md) experiences in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), or Hardened Survivor in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).
Starting a Survival Mode game with the Settled Mind [Feat](./Feats.md) selected will automatically prevent Cabin Fever Risk, and [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), from ever developing.
The Affliction Risk for Cabin Fever is calculated by the amount of time a survivor spends indoors in the last 150 hours:
- Spending 113 hours out of the past 150 hours (6.25 days) indoors begins the Risk. This averages ~18 hours/day, or 75% of your time.

- This affliction is removed when this number drops below 110 out of the past 150 hours, or is replaced by the affliction [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) if it goes above 125 hours out of the past 150 hours.

When suffering from Cabin Fever Risk, working on an item at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md)/[Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md)/reading a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md)/[Cooking](./Cooking.md)/Repairing WILL increase the Affliction Risk meter, despite the fact that the survivor is keeping their mind occupied at the time.
There are also a few exterior buildings that give a warmth bonus and do not progress Cabin Fever despite appearing to be an indoor space:

Spending more time outdoors will gradually cause the Risk to subside. Sleeping in [Warm Caves](./Warm%20Cave.md) or [Snow Shelters](./Snow%20Shelter.md) is generally the safest way to remove Cabin Fever Risk. Great care should be taken to not return to the indoors too quickly once the Risk has subsided, or the Risk will return. Failure to manage Cabin Fever Risk will result in the player contracting [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md).

Some [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Recipes increases the amount of time considered as spent outdoors when consumed, based on the amount eaten. However, they require many ingredients to make and give only a few hours of additional time at most.

**Cabin Fever** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. This Affliction only appears when playing on the [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md), [Stalker](./Stalker.md), [Interloper](./Interloper.md), [Misery](./Misery.md), or enabled on [Custom](./Custom.md) experiences in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), or Hardened Survivor in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).
Starting a Survival Mode game with the Settled Mind [Feat](./Feats.md) selected will automatically prevent [Cabin Fever Risk](./Cabin%20Fever%20Risk.md), and Cabin Fever, from ever developing.
> “**You've been indoors so long you feel like the walls are closing in. You will be unable to sleep indoors for 24 hours.**”

Cabin Fever prevents survivors from [Sleeping](./Sleep.md), Passing Time or [Researching](./Research%20Book.md) indoors for 24 hours. The affliction first appears as "Cabin Fever Risk" if a survivor has spent more than 18.83 hours per day (averaged over the last 6 days) indoors[^1]. The risk increases by staying indoors until reaching 100% when it is replaced by the affliction Cabin Fever.
Cabin Fever Risk can be reduced by spending time outside, whereas full-blown Cabin Fever will expire after 24 hours spent outside.

A grace period for Cabin Fever was introduced in [version 0.326](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.326) during the first 50 days in Voyageur and 25 days in Stalker; there is no risk of cabin fever in Pilgrim, and no grace period in Interloper.[^2]

- **Note**: "indoors" includes some locations without a loading transitions to enter them, including the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md), [Pleasant Valley Farmstead's](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) porch, and the [Lookouts](./Abandoned%20Lookout.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) and [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), and the side passage of the train tunnel in [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md).
A reliable way to determine exterior locations is to attempt to create a [Campfire](./Campfire.md), if the error message "CANNOT START CAMPFIRE INDOORS" appears then the location is indoors.
There are also a few exterior buildings that give a warmth bonus and do not progress Cabin Fever despite appearing to be an indoor space:
Cabin Fever and Cabin Fever Risk can be dealt with in a number of ways, even on Interloper (see below for Interloper specific tips).

- Gather firewood and spend time inside a [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) (in Mystery Lake, Coastal Highway, Pleasant Valley, Timberwolf Mountain, Bleak Inlet, Forsaken Airfield or Sundered Pass). This method works on all difficulties and can provide food, water and lantern fuel, but requires fuel to stay warm on most days as well as [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) (and a [tool to break ice](./Heavy%20Hammer.md)).

- Spend time in the rear of a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md). These give an air temperature bonus near their rear section, and with good clothing a survivor stay warm 24/7 without a fire (except during colder hours/blizzards on Interloper). Spending one day out of every six inside of a cave this way will eliminate Cabin Fever risk. **Note**: this does not apply to large transition caves that have their own loading screens, as these locations are considered "indoors" and will increase cabin fever.

- Spend time inside a [Car](./Car.md) or a [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md). Both allow sleeping 'outdoors' without a bedroll (through the "Campcraft" section of the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md)). Snow Shelters give a +15°C temperature boost, but should be made away from areas predators frequent and require maintenance. Cars give a +5°C temperature boost and are accessible early in the game. Spending 6 hours a day in cars sleeping, repairing, or simply passing time is enough to stave off Cabin Fever forever.

Some [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Recipes increases the amount of time considered as spent outdoors when consumed, based on the amount eaten. However, they require many ingredients to make and give only a few hours of additional time at most.
| [Breyerhouse Pie icon](../assets/Breyerhouse_Pie_icon.png) | [Breyerhouse Pie](./Breyerhouse%20Pie.md) |
| [Coastal Fishcakes icon](../assets/Coastal_Fishcakes_icon.png) | [Coastal Fishcakes](./Coastal%20Fishcakes.md) |
| [Dockworker's Pie icon](../assets/Dockworker%27s_Pie_icon.png) | [Dockworker's Pie](./Dockworker%27s%20Pie.md) |
| [Prepper's Pie icon](../assets/Prepper%27s_Pie_icon.png) | [Prepper's Pie](./Prepper%27s%20Pie.md) |
| [Stalker's Pie icon](../assets/Stalker%27s_Pie_icon.png) | [Stalker's Pie](./Stalker%27s%20Pie.md) |
On [Interloper](./Interloper.md) or [Misery](./Misery.md) Experience, Cabin Fever Risk can develop immediately since there is no grace period.

Cars are useful for warding off Cabin Fever, but must be used during the warmest hours (4-5 hours before sunset, and 2-3 hours after). One can pass time using the bedroll giving a +3 degree boost for a total of +8 degrees without sleeping. Even with no fur clothing at all it is possible to pass time 3-4 hours in a car at the end of a day in the first 30-40 days before the world temperature begins to rapidly drop.

During late game Interloper, crafted fur clothing are required due to the colder world temperatures, making the rears of [Warm Caves](./Warm%20Cave.md) more effective without risking [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md). However if a blizzard occurs inside an outdoors cave, it is possible to freeze full even in high-quality fur clothing and dual bearskin coats, so sleeping/passing time for shorter times is safer, as well as stockpiling hot fuel (sticks, coal) to create a fire if necessary.

In exceptional cases it is possible to get trapped in an indoor area while afflicted with cabin fever, such as in a safe indoor space with a blizzard outside, or becoming trapped in the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) middle layer when an aurora ends.

Provided that [Condition](./Condition.md) and [Needs](./Needs.md) are not too low initially, this may not be much of a threat in itself, as even complete exhaustion (0% Fatigue) causes very low Condition loss (1% per hour, compared to 20% per hour from Freezing). Even spending a day outside completely exhausted will only cause ~24% Condition loss, which can be easily recovered afterwards with a single night's rest even on Interloper.

The main problem of Cabin Fever when trapped indoors can lie purely in gameplay: As the character simply needs to wait for the blizzard to subside, or another Aurora to appear, or whatever is necessary to roam freely again, but all the usual ways of accelerating the passage of time are forbidden. You could just leave the game open, and do something else IRL, but this will usually not be a practical option.

[Harvesting](./Harvesting.md) however is also an effective way to make time pass quickly, and is still allowed. In order to not destroy the whole inventory, a player will start to break down any piece of equipment, and then cancel the process before it completes. This can be repeated indefinitely on one single item, ideally passing about 1 hour at a time.
- Cabin Fever was first introduced in the [Tireless Menace](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/10546-the-long-dark-sandbox-updated-to-v321-tireless-menace/) update.

- When suffering from Cabin Fever Risk, working on an item at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md)/[Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) or reading a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) WILL increase the Affliction Risk meter, despite the fact that the survivor is keeping their mind occupied at the time.

- Cabin Fever is not a diagnosable disorder; however, it can be considered as a syndrome characterized by the overlapping of psychological symptoms that can have real impacts on a person’s behavior and well-being. It’s most often characterized by combinations of boredom, anxiety, irritability, and restlessness. To be restricted indoors and significantly restricted in your choices and activities has been found stressful even for those people used to cold weather.[^3]
- Added a grace period for Voyageur and Stalker and removed the affliction entirely on Pilgrim.
- Added the Settled Mind [Feat](./Feats.md) to the game, which eliminates Cabin Fever.

[^1]: Forum post mentioning tests performed to find exact hour count to trigger CF [https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/13627-snowballs-in-hell/page/15/](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/13627-snowballs-in-hell/page/15/)

[^2]: _Hinterland Forums_. [HOTFIX! The Long Dark Sandbox v.326](http://hinterlandforums.com/index.php?/topic/10658-hotfix-the-long-dark-sandbox-v326/&do=findComment&comment=63876). Retrieved April 23, 2016.
[^3]: _The Atlantic_. [1](https://www.theatlantic.com/health/archive/2019/01/polar-vortex-stuck-indoors-let-me-out-please/581749/). Retrieved February 2, 2019.

The cabin is a secluded, weathered cabin dominating one side of the map. It is near the bottom of the hill from [Pensive Lookout](./Pensive%20Lookout.md), but otherwise it is not very close to any other structures/landmarks. If the player doesn't mind a more cold residence, the cabin could serve as a decent safehouse, although its disconnected state from the rest of the region makes it more for players who like the survival experience of [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) but prefer the safety of houses. Inside the building the player will find slightly low amounts of loot, although there are some [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) and [Marine Flare](./Marine%20Flare.md) spawns. There are plenty of wooden objects to break down though and a 2-slot [Rim Grill](./Rim%20Grill.md) to burn them on. The player should be aware that if they track around the right side of the house they will find a firewood bin (which is normally locked, but can be unlocked using a prybar), and a possible can of [Stump Remover](./Stump%20Remover.md) next to it.

This cabin and the [Cannery Worker Residences](./Cannery%20Worker%20Residences.md) are some recommended safehouses in the area. Although you could count on your hands the number of enterable locations in this region, these two definitely serve the best. The cabin sits in a secluded area on the eastern end of the map, surrounded by scrub brush, rose hips and wildlife. Due to the hole in its roof, it provides slightly lower temperatures, but it probably has the densest and most storage on the lower part of the region, and plenty of deer spawn nearby making it unnecessary to voyage westward. Timberwolves might become a light problem, though.

**Camber Flight Porridge** is a food item in _The Long Dark_, it is learned from a unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) and is made with a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md).

Acquiring the Recipe Card for Camber Flight Porridge requires traversing the long and cold Far Range Branch Line, Transfer Pass, and the cold, windy and exposed plains of Forsaken Airfield.
It's Recipe Card can be found inside the kitchen of the [Main Hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md).

**Discover an old manual instant camera. Take photos anywhere in the world and add them to your Album. Craft photos into wall-hangings for your personal Safehouse. Find Colour, Black & White, or Sepia-toned film stock. Be a photographer at the end of the world.** Official Description

The **Camera** is a [Tool](./Tools.md) found in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)._ It is available for players that purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion, and is designed to be an in game photo/screenshot system for custom photos.

It is one of the few items that cannot be dropped or placed in containers so it cannot be lost, similar to the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) and [Respirator](./Respirator.md).

The Camera is an Instant Camera model that can print photos right after they are taken. Photos taken can not be turned into [Polaroids](./Polaroids.md) to unlock Vistas. Only 1 Camera exists in the entire game.

It can be found sitting on one of the control panels at the [Station Bunkhouse](./Station%20Bunkhouse.md) in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md), with a starting box of [FastFilm-500](./FastFilm-500.md) next to it.

Photos can be taken by equipping the Camera and aiming it with "Right Mouse," which produces a square box on the screen that will become the taken photograph. Once the Camera is shot, the survivor takes the photo out and watches it develop right in front of them before putting it away.

Photographs taken with the Camera appear in a special section of the [Journal](./Journal.md) called the Photo Album, which lists the Region and location of where the photo was taken. Photos can be Discarded, Annotated (the player can write a story on it), or Examined in this menu. While it is unknown if there is a limit to how many photos can be taken, it is more than than the 20 blank slots one starts with.
Photos taken can be placed inside a constructed [Framed Photo](./Framed%20Photo.md) and placed inside a player's [Safehouse](./Safehouse.md) as a [Decoration](./Decorations.md).

![From left to right: Sepia, Colour, Black & White of Barn (Molly's)](../assets/Camera_Colour_films.jpg)_From left to right: Sepia, Colour, Black & White of Barn (Molly's)_FastFilm is required to make the Camera work, and the film used effects the coloring of the photograph taken. They are commonly found in various locations around Great Bear Island, mostly hidden in houses and cabins. A single FastFilm contains enough film for 6 Shots. Running out of film in the Camera will cause the survivor to reload another FastFilm of the same color type into the Camera.
- ![FastFilm 500 icon](../assets/FastFilm-500_icon.png) [FastFilm-500](./FastFilm-500.md) (Colour-toned)
- ![FastFilm 500BW icon](../assets/FastFilm-500BW_icon.png) [FastFilm-500BW](./FastFilm-500BW.md) (Black & White-toned)
- ![FastFilm 500SPA icon](../assets/FastFilm-500SPA_icon.png) [FastFilm-500SPA](./FastFilm-500SPA.md) (Sepia-toned)

Swapping to different film types into the Camera simply requires the player to press the "R" key when the Camera is equipped, where it cycles through the order Colour, Black and White, and Sepia film if the player has them in their inventory. Manually swapping through different film colors will also reload the Camera with fresh film from the player's inventory, if film Shots of a particular color inside the Camera is running low.
There is currently not an option to unload all film from inside the Camera in the Backpack options.
- Despite not being a weapon, aiming the Camera at a [Wolf](./Wolf.md) that cannot reach you will scare it off like any other weapon (or cause it to agro and charge).

- The Camera was originally teased as "A Photo Mode for THE LONG DARK, but contextualized with an in-game camera and Dark Room chemicals so that you can process your own film." This meant that the original Camera used a model that required its pictures to be processed first before they could be displayed, which was also shown in the teaser image showing polaroids hanging out to develop.

- An interview by Hinterland later revealed that the Dark Room was cut "because it would have required electrical equipment that we'd only be able to let players use during an active aurora. We came up with a good solution that is true to our lore and also gives players a lot of freedom for self-expression."[^1]
- The Camera has the brand "Kontakt" etched into the front and back, which may be a reference to Kodak cameras.

- The quality of an image taken with the camera is directly affected by Motion Blur (Settings > Visuals > Quality). High levels of Motion Blur result in extremely blurry photographs, whereas "none" results in crystal clear images.

The Camp Office's location makes it arguably the best [safehouse](./Safehouse.md) in most [gameplay modes](./Survival%20Mode.md#Experience), as it is centrally located both midway other [Regions](./Region.md) on [Great Bear](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), as well as within Mystery Lake itself.

Nearby key locations are: [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md), [ice fishing huts](./Fishing%20Hut.md) scattered about, [cat tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) around the lake perimeter, and a [rabbit](./Rabbit.md) grove nearby between the [Deadfall area](./Deadfall%20Area.md) and [Trapper's homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md). [Deer](./Deer.md) and [wolves](./Wolf.md) may wander the area, with additional Deer spawns on the Lake and the clearing between the Office and [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md), as well as a [moose](./Moose.md) sometimes frequenting the train tracks some distance from the building.

The Office has two entrances (front and back), and two floors. The first floor features a [work bench](./Work%20Bench.md), a first aid box next to the back door, and a potbelly stove. A [potato sack](./Potato%20Sack.md) can potentially spawn under the staircase. Next to the stairs is one of the [Radios](./Trader.md#Radio_Locations) necessary to contact the Trader (if enabled).

The second floor sometimes features a corpse that may spawn at the top of the stairs, a wood burning stove, two bunk beds, a dresser, a shelf, a cupboard, a table, and chair. Near the desk upstairs is a [note](./Notes.md) left behind.

All the containers combined: Dresser (2 x 10 kg), Cupboard (15 kg), and [File Cabinet](./File%20Cabinet.md) (4 x 10 kg) offers a total **75 kg (165 lbs)** of guaranteed indoor storage, an additional 10 kg (22 lbs) with Workbench and First Aid shelf added, plus a wide and a tall shelf. Running the 3 indoor [cooking](./Cooking.md) slots simultaneously - while [fuel](./Fire.md#Types_of_Fuel) intensive - makes it possible to cook large amounts of meat relatively quickly.

There is also a [metal container](./Metal%20Container.md) outside behind the building, ideal for storing both perishables such as meat, and items intended to be left uncured, like [Green Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md). Keep in mind that Ruined items disappear when they reach 0% condition inside a container, so consider storing food on the ground instead.

It is implied in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) that [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) would regularly shelter in the Camp Office, judging by the amount of discarded [Pork and Beans](./Pork%20and%20Beans.md) cans left around.
This location is one of the most iconic places in the game as an important central location in the first region to be released.

A **Campfire** is an open [Fire](./Fire.md) that can be placed into the outdoors. Campfires can cook meat to make it safer to eat, melt snow into [Water](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md) and [sterilize](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) it, make beverages, heat canned food/beverages, scare off predators and create [Torches](./Torch.md).
Campfires can be placed with the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md) outdoors on the ground, provided the following conditions are met:
- Optionally: [Accelerant](./Accelerant.md) or 0,1L of [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) can used when starting a fire, guaranteeing it will light and light faster.
- Cannot be started inside most interior locations or mines. ([Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) and [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) are exceptions)
- [Strong Winds](./Survival%20Overlay.md) or Blizzards prevent unsheltered fires from being created. **Note:** wind changing directions can cause previously sheltered fires to be blown out.

![old campfire](../assets/The_Long_Dark_-_Campfire.jpg)_old campfire_ Campfires can be used like all other fires, but unlike contained fires, they are vulnerable to high winds. The Wind Shield icon can be useful for locating an area that is not currently being blown by wind.
An indicator that a fire is about to blow out is its smoke will be blowing away sideways instead of rising up.

- Attempting to fuel to a windblown fire may prompt that it is "too windy to sustain the fire". In other cases fuel may be added but the maximum possible life of the fire is limited to 9 minutes, making most fuels extremely wasteful and refueling tedious.

- Periodically feeding sticks to a windblown fire may be useful if one finds oneself still in dire need of warmth when their fire starts to go out. The wind may also eventually shift, allowing the player to extend the fire's life beyond the 9-minute cap.
- Windblown fires can still be useful for short tasks, like brewing beverages or heating cans or boiling the smallest amounts of water.

Campfires which run out of fuel will persist as a burnt out campfire, from which [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md) can be harvested based on how much fuel was burned (up to 50 pieces of charcoal), or left to gather over successive fires.

- Burnt out campfires can be found pre-generated in all regions, to suggest the activity of other survivors. If such fire exist indoors or in other locations where a campfire could not normally be started, the player can relight them.
- Pulling a Torch from a lit campfire will reduce its lifespan by 10 minutes, and cannot be used if the Campfire has less than 10 minutes left to burn.

- Just before a campfire burns out, it may persist with a duration of "embers" for a few minutes, allowing more fuel to be added on. Whether and for how long embers will linger seems to depend on the ambient conditions (wind/cold) and strength of the fire.
- At extremely cold temperatures (0 degrees C or colder) fuel burns much slower, making it more efficient.

- Lit Torches, [Flares](./Flare.md), and [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md) can be used to start a campfire. At low [Firestarting skill](./Skills.md) and/or higher difficulties, this is an effective way to conserve matches.
- Torches may be pulled from a campfire, allowing the fire to be transported or excess fuel conserved by breaking the torches down into sticks.
- Pulling a torch from the fire will reduce the duration by 10 minutes and the temperature by 1 degree Celsius.
- The [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) is the only infinitely renewable firestarter and must be used during sunny daylight.
- Few outdoor locations provide perfect protection for a fire, but caves notable enough to be marked on the map are typically fully sheltered, even in the colder area near the lip of the cave.

- [Bear Carcass](./Black%20Bear%20Carcass.md) and [Moose Carcass](./Moose%20Carcass.md) are large enough to block wind for a campfire, making them an unusual example of a windshield the player has some small agency in positioning. They can also be used to warm the player and keep the carcass from freezing while harvesting it.
- Using sticks and pulled torches to light several campfires in rapid succession is a cheap, efficient method of rapidly training the Firestarting skill.
- Stepping into an active campfire will result in [Burns](./Burns.md) and constant Condition loss.

- Despite having only two cooking slots, some food items (e.g. coffees, teas, canned foods) can be heated up by dropping near the campfire, but there is still a risk of burning them away if left for too long.

- Starting multiple fires may be desirable to mass produce food and water, making closely placed campfires the logical choice. The only downside is that each active campfire will require larger amounts of fuel to keep each one going.
- Most hostile [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) will be held at bay by an active campfire, or at least won't directly cross one. Hastily lighting a fire can be a life saver.

- Right clicking valid cooking slot items can be used to place them in a cooking slot or to transfer items currently cooking from one fire to another. This will not reset the timer, regardless of the distance between fires. This can be very useful when one needs to move from a windblown fire to a sheltered fire.
- Special green campfires imbued with magic can be found during the [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) challenge.

Can openers allows players to open [canned foods](./Cooking.md#Canned) without losing between 10% and 30% of the food as spillage via smashing open. While either a [Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) or [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) will also allow the player to open a can without spillage, a Can Opener is only used to open cans. Using a Can Opener allows the player to preserve those tools' condition for other uses. Using a Can Opener also allows the canned food to be eaten and yield a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) after consumption, whereas smashing the can open will not.
A Can Opener will degrade by **2%** each time it is used. The Can Opener will not degrade in any other circumstances.
It can also be repaired 1 unit of Scrap Metal. Repairing restores 25% condition and takes 45 minutes.

Cans of Gunpowder can spawn rarely in high loot quality locations of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), such as [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md), [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md), or [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md) basement. They can also be found in [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md) of any type and inside of [Safes](./Safe.md).

A large amount of pre-placed Gunpowder cans are located within [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), namely 2 can spawn on the catwalks/roofs leading from guard barracks to the infirmary, 1 is almost always located on the workbench and 1 is inside Cellblock C inside the guardroom near the cells. A large amount of [Dusting Sulfur](./Dusting%20Sulfur.md) and [Stump Remover](./Stump%20Remover.md) are also scattered throughout the prison meaning even more gunpowder can be crafted.
At least 1 Gunpowder can will be located inside [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) mine, usually located at level 2 on the bottom of the collapsed wooden stairs in the main room.

- [Gunpowder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/gunpowder) (black powder) consists of a mixture of [sulfur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/sulfur) (S), [charcoal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/charcoal) (C), and [potassium nitrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/potassium_nitrate) ([saltpeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/saltpeter), KNO₃). The sulfur and charcoal act as fuels while the saltpeter is an [oxidizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/oxidizer).

- The in-game recipe actually creates black powder (considering ingredients), which in real life would be almost useless to reload any modern rounds due to much slower combustion and therefore lesser kinetic energy of bullets. Using ammunition crafted in that way could result in jamming of the barrel. Black powder also leaves a lot more residue in the firearm, causing the need to clean it more often.
- In previous versions, a glitch was present where reloading save files or exiting/entering buildings would refill dropped cans of gunpowder to their maximum of 0.5kg.

A **Canister** is a [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) item found in _The Long Dark_ that was added in the Part 4 Buried Echoes update for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon.

Canisters work in tandem with a [Respirator](./Respirator.md), are used to prevent [Suffocation](./Suffocation.md) from toxic gases found inside mineshafts, as well as preventing [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md) from occurring when walking around [chemical spills](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) on the surface of the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md).

Canisters degrade quite rapidly and only filter air for 45 seconds. This tradeoff is offset, however, by how plentiful the quantity of Canisters often are, as they can be found in many areas around the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md). Ruined Canisters are automatically replaced with a fresh one while a Respirator is being used and placed back into the player's inventory. As such, it is best to dispose of ruined Canisters in a storage container to remove them from the game world, as to not confuse the player when useful Canisters can be claimed, as well as to lower [Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md).

Canisters occasionally spawn in other regions outside of the Zone of Contamination but are incredibly rare. They have a higher chance of being slightly more common loot items in the [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) region, but become virtually nonexistent when searching in all other regions.

**Canned Pineapple** is a canned [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_ found only when trading with the [Trader](./Trader.md).

Consuming Canned Pineapple restores a moderate amount of calories and hydration. It may also be warmed by a [Fire](./Fire.md), to make progress in [Cooking](./Cooking.md) [Survival Skill](./Skills.md), and consumed while hot to grant the benefit [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md). Canned Pineapple has relatively low energy density (on par with that of cooked meats), making them relatively inefficient as a travel food.

Like other canned foods, Canned Pineapple may be opened with a [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md) or [bladed tool](./Tools.md), or smashed open (with no tool) but spilling some of its contents. If opened with a tool a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) is received after consuming the contents.

Canned Pineapple cannot be found as loot and is only acquired from the Trader, making it more difficult to acquire than similar [Pinnacle Peaches](./Pinnacle%20Peaches.md) but unlike other canned goods Pineapples are renewable.
- Unlike other canned goods that must be opened with a bladed tool, Canned Pineapples does not have an open can icon in the Backpack after being opened.

That old radio tower is supposed to relay the weather, but half the time the damn thing is offline. And since the landslide last summer we can't even get up the road anymore to check out what's going on.

Has an interior The **Cannery Pier** is a section of the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), and houses the [Workshop](./Workshop.md).

The pier is inaccessible to the player and [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) while following the ground level pier. It can only be accessed by the player by climbing the [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section in the warehouse and passing through an obstacle course. The obstacle course will take you over a downed crane, a derelict house and several cargo containers connected by boards in order to reach pier. The pier offers access to the Workshop in which the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) and [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) are found. Additionally, a normal [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), along with two [Fire Barrels](./Fire%20Barrel.md), can be found; one inside the workshop, the other just outside the door.

A [Keypad](./Keypad.md) and [Cannery Memo](./Cannery%20Memo.md) are found inside a warm area with a Fire Barrel, and the code to the keypad is found in the mountains at [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md). At the end of the Pier is a [Backpack](./Backpack.md) and some supplies, but nothing else aside from some [Pallets](./Pallets.md) is behind the Workshop.

- As the pier is a safe spot from Timberwolves, and it provides a good view of both the ice surrounding and some parts the cannery compound, it can be used as an easy way to snipe wolves before leaving the area. The main issue with this location that prevents it from being a useful place to store items is of course the obstacle course, as it lacks an unlockable shortcut and must be traveled through again to reach the pier.

- A way to bypass this is to place a deployed [Travois](./Travois.md) on the lower pier close to the frozen ocean and simply interacting with it on the ocean. This will teleport the player onto the pier and they can place the Travois down and bypass the obstacle course.

- Rarely after exiting the Workshop, timberwolves can glitch onto the pier and attack the player despite there being no path up from the ice below. [[1]](https://i.imgur.com/YrTVkDw.png) [[2]](https://i.imgur.com/FDAu161.png)

- The obstacle course can be skipped entirely by placing a deployed [Travois](./Travois.md) with an item inside on the lowest pier at the Cannery Pier, then placing the handles near the edge. Walking on the ocean below will then give the player the option to pick up the Travois, wherein the player will teleport up to the pier.

Has an interior The **Cannery Worker Residences** is a collection of houses that once probably housed some of the employees of the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md).

There are four houses at the location, two of which are burned, and one of which is boarded-up. The last is enterable and contains a fireplace for cooking. Outside on the frozen water is an ice fishing hut; just a little further is a good place for [beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md). South of the site is the [Fallen Lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md), which provides a 6-burner [stove](./Stove.md) (the only one not indoors) for efficient cooking and a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) found in an [Emergency Kit](./Emergency%20Kit.md) at the top of the Lighthouse.

As mentioned above, the worker residences can serve as a good safehouse in the region. Although a bear and timberwolves may prowl the area, deer and rabbits can also spawn near the lighthouse, and the nearby fishing huts help provide a full range of renewable food sources. The Residences are also centrally located in the region, allowing for easier access to several other notable locations.
The habitable building contains some mid-level loot, as well as a decent amount of storage. However, it is not a base the player should expect to spend much time in, but neither is the region.

Car Batteries are the heaviest object in the game, weighing 15kg (33lbs), found under the hoods of a [Car](./Car.md) or [Truck](./Truck.md) in any region that has them. Regions such as [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), and [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) have the most cars, thus have the most Car Batteries to loot.

They can be harvested with a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) for [Scrap Lead](./Scrap%20Lead.md), required for crafting ammunition with the [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) skill at the [Ammunition Workbench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md). It takes 30 minutes to harvest a Car Battery. One Car Battery will always yield six Scrap Lead; each piece of Scrap Lead may be crafted into six [Bullets](./Bullet.md) at an [Ammunition Forge](./Ammunition%20Forge.md), so one Car Battery always allows the crafting of 36 Bullets.

For players that have the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC installed, one car battery will be needed to fix each [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md). These batteries usually spawn near the transmitting stations, but may have to be looted from nearby vehicles:
- A Battery spawns in a [Supply Bin](./Supply%20Bin.md) near the [Shortwave Tower East](./Shortwave%20Tower%20East.md) Transmitter in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md).
- The [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md) Transmitter does not have a Battery near it in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md). One must be scavenged near the town and brought up to the Transmitter.
- [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) has a Battery inside the Radio Control Hut in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
- The [Control Tower](./Control%20Tower.md) has all the materials needed to repair the Transmitter nearby in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md).
- [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md) has a battery inside the substation for the Transmitter in [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md).
- [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) has multiple inside for the Transmitter in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md).
The [Trader](./Trader.md) also requests 1 battery in his trades for [Recipe Cards](./Recipe%20Cards.md) or Blueprints.

A select number of special areas contains around 5 Batteries in an indoor space. These batteries are typically not located near a Transmitter, and are useful if the player has run out of Car Batteries to use for trading or Gunsmithing.
| [Scrap Lead](./Scrap%20Lead.md) | None | - 1 × [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md) |

Eventually all [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and [Revolver](./Revolver.md) ammunition will become depleted; crafting is the only way to obtain more ammunition outside of trading with the Trader.

- Car Batteries may be found by lifting the hoods of cars and trucks. Not all vehicles have batteries, only ~50% will have one. At least on Interloper mode you should be prepared to haul car batteries from other maps to transmitters you want to repair.
- They weigh 15kg, but can be harvested with a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) into 6 pieces of Scrap Lead weighing just 1.5kg. A convenient and safe way harvest Car Batteries is inside of their vehicle.
- In prior versions, Car Batteries and Scrap Lead were useless on Interloper difficulty because firearms never spawn. This was changed with the introduction of Transmitters.
- They are still useless in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) episodes 1, 2, 3, and 4 because there is no [Ammunition Workbench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md).
- A [Travois](./Travois.md) is extremely useful for hauling car batteries over longer distances.
- 12-Volt Lead-acid car batteries have 6 cells inside (2 volts per cell), which is why a Car Battery can be harvested for 6 pieces of Scrap Lead (one per cell).
- The car battery bears the logo of the in-game company "ZAP." The same logo can be found on the [energy bar](./Energy%20Bar.md).

**Cars** are small 4-door [vehicles](./Vehicle.md) found abandoned by the road in the savage Canadian wilderness. Cars are not the best place to set up a base, but they do provide protection from the wind and predators. It is possible but risky to [sleep](./Sleep.md) in a car by choosing the bedroll icon (even without a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) in your inventory) from the radial menu. A car's lights will flicker and its radio will have power during an aurora.

Cars are remnants of former human society before the apocalypse. They have been rendered useless hunks of metal due to the [aurora](./Aurora.md). Cars are suitable as temporary sanctuaries from predators and the cold, and may even hold some basic supplies like food and water. All cars have searchable glove compartments in the passenger side and visors on both sides. A [prybar](./Prybar.md) will allow the player to force open the trunk, if it is locked. It is not possible to drop items inside a car. Under the hood, many cars contain a [battery](./Car%20Battery.md), which can be harvested into [scrap lead](./Scrap%20Lead.md) using a [hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md); since lead is needed for [making ammunition](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md), car batteries can be a critical, limited resource.

Entering a car will add a windproof protection as well as a bonus ambient temperature of +5o C. If there is no bedroll, the car will offer a bed warmth bonus of 3o C, but if there is a bedroll, the bedroll value will be used instead. Therefore, it is recommended to use a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) of higher condition than 60%.
- There is a chance that a [rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) or [revolver](./Revolver.md) may spawn in some cars
- Trunks, hoods, doors and gas caps are all able to be opened on cars. Hoods and gas caps can be left open.
- Car radios can be turned on and off, however they only function during an aurora, and only play classical music.

**Carcass Harvesting** is a Survival [Skill](./Skills.md) that is used to harvest meat, hides, and Guts from [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md). There are 9 types of harvestable animals in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, and apart from [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), all animals can only be harvested at the location of the carcass, unless that animal has been quartered. Higher levels in the carcass harvesting skill reduce the amount of time required to harvest and increase the amount that can be harvested by hand from a frozen carcass.

![A slain Moose Carcass](../assets/Deadmoose.png)_A slain Moose Carcass_ Players can only harvest at the location of the animal, which cannot be moved by the player. The only exceptions to this are rabbits and ptarmigan, which can be picked up and harvested at any location.

- In order to harvest a carcass, the player needs to have a tool on them, as any non-ravaged carcass (other than rabbits and ptarmigan) cannot be harvested with bare hands, regardless of Carcass Harvesting skill level. Once a carcass has been harvested with a tool, to any degree, the player will be able to use their hands. This is shown by the carcass having exposed flesh.

- Choosing to harvest a carcass barehanded below Carcass Harvesting Level 3 _will always result in 8-17% of the unharvested usable meat to be lost_, even if the hide/guts/feathers was harvested instead. This is similar to smashing cans open without a tool before reaching [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Level 3. As such, it is best to use a tool to extract the raw meat first before choosing to harvest the hide/guts/feathers without a tool.

- A carcass deteriorates over time, based on how frozen it is, which lowers the condition of the harvestable meat. Once said condition reaches 0, the carcass will become unable to be interacted with, so any remaining meat, hide, feathers, and guts will be lost.
- The player cannot harvest more than 5 hours worth of materials from a carcass (this usually applies to Bears and Moose, even with a Hunting Knife which reduces the most harvesting time).

Carcass harvesting is messy, and the raw animal parts the player takes will emit an [odor](./Scent.md) that attracts predators from greater distances than usual (indicated by a icon of three wavy lines on the upper center area of the HUD). Cooking the meat and curing hides and guts reduces or eliminates the intensity of the scent.

Players can harvest carcasses by hand, but can decrease the amount of time needed for harvest with certain types of equipment. In most cases, any bladed tool will harvest faster than using one's hands, however, in a few situations (e.g., when harvesting guts with only a hatchet available or harvesting hides at high skill level) harvesting by hand may be slightly faster.

A 100% frozen carcass cannot be harvested barehanded if the carcass is intact, regardless of skill level, and requires a tool to break the carcass open first. After this, a frozen carcass can be harvested barehanded depending on carcass frozen state:
Survivor's skill level also affects the freeze level at which unfrozen meat harvesting speed is used:
- Levels 1~3: Carcasses below or equal to 50% freeze level use the unfrozen meat harvesting speed.
- Level 4: Carcasses below or equal to 75% freeze level use the unfrozen meat harvesting speed.
- Level 5: Carcasses below or equal to 100% freeze level use the unfrozen meat harvesting speed.

This makes Hatchets & Hacksaws good starting tools for meat harvesting, since they have better frozen meat harvesting speed, but end up losing that situational bonus at higher levels, and as such get completely outclassed by hunting knives at skill level 5.

Carcasses can be obtained through [Hunting](./Hunting.md), [Trapping](./Trapping.md), or by scavenging for any existing ravaged carcasses.
A carcass can exist in two different states: Ravaged or Normal. A third state, Frozen, can occur if a carcass fully freezes over.

A ravaged carcass has a significant lack of meat on the corpse, depending on how long the carcass was being fed upon by a Wolf if it was killed by one after world generation, or if it spawned into the world ravaged. A frozen carcass generally requires a tool to harvest the carcass, depending on the player's carcass harvesting skill level. A normal carcass has either been recently killed or has been warmed up by a nearby [Fire](./Fire.md).

Harvesting a whole freshly killed animal often takes several hours to complete. Players can instead choose to quarter an animal, which harvests the hide and guts, and additionally harvests the meat into "quarters" with a weight of up to 10 kilograms (roughly 22 pounds), each of which contains half their weight in harvestable meat. Depending on the harvestable meat, a Wolf may yield only one "quarter", while a Moose may yield up to nine "quarters".
| [Deer](./Deer.md) (Stag) | 25.00 kg / _(55 lb)_ | 25.00 kg / _(55 lb)_ | 5 (5kg per bag) |
| [Deer](./Deer.md) (Doe) | 15.00 kg / _(33 lb)_ | 15.00 kg / _(33 lb)_ | 3 (5kg per bag) |
| [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) | 0.00 kg / _(0 lb)_ | 0.00 kg / _(0 lb)_ | 0 |
| [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) | 5.00 kg / _(11 lb)_ | 10.00 kg / _(22 lb)_ | 1-2 (5kg per bag) |

To quarter an animal, players have to interact with the animal carcass and select the _Quarter_ option. Players are notified of the amount of time and the number of calories that will be spent while quartering. A bladed tool must be used in order to begin quartering, and all bladed tools take the same amount of time to quarter a carcass. Quartering can be interrupted and resumed without loss of progress, so if the player wishes to do other things intermittently while quartering, they can interrupt the action whenever they feel the need and resume where they left off.

Quartering a carcass yields Skill points at a ratio of 1 point per hour spent harvesting and will destroy the carcass in the process, leaving behind a blood stain, the creature's legs, and any unharvested meat, hides, or guts. After quartering a carcass, any overhead [Crows](./Crow.md) despawn, so if one requires [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) from the corpse sitting out, they may want to take this into account.

Quartering may be the safer option if there are nearby predators or potentially dangerous weather conditions, as the quarters can be harvested elsewhere at a later time. Quartering automatically harvests the hide and guts and place them on the ground, and is usually the fastest way to harvest large animals with lots of guts, namely Moose and Bears.

"Meat bags" created by quartering are much heavier than the meat they contain (or the meat you would get if you harvested the carcass outright). This should be taken into account as weight management is always important.

The [Travois](./Travois.md) (requires [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC) is very useful for transporting a quartered animal as it can carry all but the highest maximum weight bag harvests (carry capacity of 75.00kg). If there are excess bags these could be harvested and the meat carried being half the weight of the bag as a workaround. The other big advantage is that currently there is no [Scent](./Scent.md) from a Travois; combined with the greater comparative speed of movement provided, they are ideal for this purpose.
Players can increase their carcass harvesting by harvesting meat, guts, or hides from a carcass.

The player will gain about 1 skill point per hour spent harvesting. If possible, one's hands should be used to acquire skill points faster. However, 1 kg (2.2 lbs) of meat will require 30 min with the Basic Harvesting skill. Therefore a large-sized Moose can take more than one day to be fully harvested (including hide and guts).

A limited increase can be obtained from the [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) _[Field Dressing Your Kill, Vol. I](./Field%20Dressing%20Your%20Kill%2C%20Vol.%20I.md)_, which allows players to increase their Carcass Harvesting by 10 skill points with 10 hours of research.

The cardboard box is a cardboard container, coming in various sizes and shapes. Some cardboard boxes may have items hidden inside them, but cardboard boxes cannot be searched. Instead, they must be broken down, similar to [wooden crates](./Crate.md), to access the potential loot inside. However, very few cardboard boxes contain possible loot, and they are usually in very specific locations, so breaking down every cardboard box you see might be a waste of time. Cardboard boxes can be found in almost every [Region](./Region.md) and are mostly present to provide the player with tinder plugs and fill up empty space in a room or outdoor setting.
- Small cardboard boxes with [Granola Bar](./Granola%20Bar.md) or [Chocolate Bar](./Chocolate%20Bar.md) brand packaging on them in stores said items inside them.
- Small cardboard boxes yield less tinder plugs than larger ones, and usually are not the ones to contain items
- Large boxes yield 3 tinder plugs when broken down and have the chance to contain items if they are present in certain locations.

- Flat boxes are flat pieces of cardboard, usually found leaning against a wall or on the floor. Loot can sometimes be found hidden underneath these boxes. The amount of tinder plugs acquired when breaking one down varies on its size.
- Torn boxes are flat pieces of cardboard that are frayed and found on the ground. They generate 1-2 plugs.

All cardboard boxes can be broken down, yielding 1-3 [Tinder Plugs](./Tinder%20Plug.md). They can be broken down by hand, or using a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), to break them down faster. Large cardboard boxes yield 3 tinder plugs and take 27 minutes to harvest. (Add other times here)

**Cardboard Matches** are [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) Tools and a small light source in _The Long Dark_.

Each match weighs a mere 5 grams (0.005kg), but there are always 20 found together in one box. Using a Cardboard Match does not increase the base chance of successfully lighting a fire. Irrespective of real-life cardboard matches which are attached to a striker, these matches can be split into smaller stacks and are still usable.

Light sources are equipped with the '1' key by default. Hold the left mouse button to strike the match for a small light source that lasts for a few seconds. While a lit match is held, your "Feels Like" temperature will rise by a few degrees. Sadly, such a small fire will not deter [Wolves](./Wolf.md).

Lighting a match will cause the survivor to hold it closely in their hand, where it will create light for 13 seconds until the fire travels down the stem and reaches the survivor's fingers, where they drop it in pain. Running with a lit match will cause the flame to grow brighter, causing it to burn out faster.
Pressing H with a lit match will cause the survivor to flick the match into the distance, where it disappears and the light is extinguished.

- [Firestrikers](./Firestriker.md) and [Wood Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md) are preferable to Cardboard Matches at low firestarting skill. This will likely save matches from failed fires, thanks to the firestrikers higher Bonus Chance.
- When selecting Cardboard Matches as a light source, the handheld model is always that of Wood Matches.
- Using a lit [Torch](./Torch.md) to start campfires is an effective way to save matches/firestriker durability.
- Cardboard Matches are branded with the logo of "_Trusty Matches"_, the manufacturer of Wood Matches.
- Selecting Cardboard Matches will always use the Wood Matches model in the first person hand model.

- Despite being contained inside a cardboard box, no tinder is given or harvestable when wooden matches are used up unlike cardboard boxes present across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).

**Cargo Containers** are locked containers found in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) that can only be opened with a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md).

Cargo Containers are loot-filled blue-green shipping devices scattered across Timberwolf Mountain from a crashed cargo aircraft on the [Summit](./Summit.md). All Cargo Containers feature two locked compartments which require a Hacksaw to open. Each compartment holds a specific type of resource (e.g. Canned Food, Firestarting, Clothes, Medical), some of which may be found near the container beside/on a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md).

- If the Hacksaw used to unlock the compartment is low condition (<50%) and the tool breaks on use, there is a chance the cargo door will become **permanently ruined**: preventing its cargo from ever being accessible.

- Items inside Cargo Containers, like other Containers will [Decay](./Decay.md) slowly over time (based on Game Mode). Ruined (0% Condition) Clothes will become unwearable, and ruined food and medical supplies will disappear unless removed before they decay completely.
- About half of all Cargo Containers do not spawn in Interloper mode, and those which do appear contain less and lower quality loot.

- 2-3 green Wooden Crates which may be broken down for Reclaimed Wood may be found near Cargo Container sites (these crate are always present, even on Interloper when Cargo Containers themselves may not spawn).

In the 1960s, a small hydroelectric dam was built on the Carter River. The project was engineered and financed by industrial magnate, Richard Carter, who intended to use power from the dam to sustain a small town he planned to build for the growing workforce across his mining empire. Unfortunately, a combination of setbacks due to seismic activity (Which resulting in several deaths and forced the shutdown of one of his mines) and a drop in the price of coal and copper in the late 1960s bankrupted Carter, who abandoned the nearly completed project. In the 1980s, there were multiple attempts to modernize Carter Dam and bring it back online, but by then changes to the local climate and hydrodynamics of the Mystery Lake area, as well as external public pressure in support of the newly minted Mystery Lake Provincial Park, resulted in Carter Dam being shut down for good in the late 1990s. Labour disputes and early eco-activism by a small group of environmentalists -- billing themselves the "Forest Talkers" -- resulted in the sudden closure of the dam, primarily for the employee's safety. A skeleton crew of maintenance workers were actually trapped in the Dam for days until mediators could extract them. No violence was reported, but the event served to galvanize the Forest Talkers, who felt their success in keeping Carter Dam shut down validated their continued work to protect Great Bear's further development and exploitation.
- Added to game.
