> “**The old Carter Dam -- it's a mess. Multiple quakes have left it pretty unstable. Nobody really goes in there anymore.**”

**Carter Hydro Dam** is a hydroelectric dam containing two generation turbines. It exists as two separate loading levels, each of which has an exit to the outside and serves as part of a series of transition zones (along with [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md)) between [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) and [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
The dam is featured in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).

The dam is a vast multi-level complex with many lockers, boxes, drawers, and other containers to search. It also contains three [Work Benches](./Work%20Bench.md), a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) and usually a lot of valuable loot (possibly including high-quality clothing, tools, [ammo](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), a pistol and a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md)). In the event of an aurora touching any of the cords in the dam will inflict a burn and will damage the player.

The dam was constructed on the Carter River in the 1960s. It was engineered and financed by the industrial magnate Richard Carter, who planned to use it to power a small town he was going to build for his mining workers. Due to seismic activity, and a drop in the price of coal and copper in the late 1960s, the project was nearly abandoned. There were attempts in the 1980s to modernize the dam and bring it back online, but hydrological changes in the [Mystery lake area](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) and public support for a newly created _Mystery Lake Provincial Park_ resulted in the dam being "shut down for good" in the late 1990s.[^1]

Following [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md), there was an unsuccessful attempt to re-open the dam, led by the CEO of Carter Hydro Energy, Robert Clarke.[^2] A skeleton crew was working in the dam, but were trapped inside by the [Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md), an eco-activist group. The workers were reportedly trapped inside the dam for days before mediators were able to extract them. While the incident was not violent, it resulted in the dam remaining closed and has been used as an example by the [Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md) to validate their continued work.[^3]

[Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md) will be found somewhere in or around the dam, its exact location varying between playthroughs. This rifle is 1.0 kg lighter than a normal [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), with a higher rate of fire and reload speed, however it's only half as durable, requiring more frequent [cleaning](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md).

Outside of the upper dam entrance is a fenced storage yard. On Interloper a [wolf](./Wolf.md) has a small chance of spawning in here. Across the tracks from there are two trailers; one apparently for accommodations as has bunk beds, the other for administration.

In earlier releases of the game, the dam was inhabited by a [wolf](./Wolf.md) dubbed _Fluffy_ by The Long Dark community. She would appear in the generator room and--like other wolves in the game--would chase and attack the player. Fluffy would not appear in Pilgrim difficulty and would only appear after a 12 to 24 hour safe period in Voyageur difficulty.[^4]

Following the update to version 1.0, Fluffy was completely removed from the Survival mode, with developers stating that she had escaped.[^5] In [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of story mode, a dead wolf is found laying in the hallway adjacent to the generator room--possibly some other wolf, less navigationally adept than Fluffy.
Fluffy was eventually relocated to [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). She's found residing in [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) where the Ammunition bench is.
Behind the metal hatch to the Upper Levels at the top of some stairs (in the dark), a frozen corpse often spawns. Note the broken arrows and something hanging from the latch nearby.

The exit door found in a storage room at the bottom of a staircase goes to Winding River; it is one-way. The door is an emergency exit and does not have a handle on the outside, making getting back into the dam difficult.

While the player may re-enter the lower dam through a broken window above the platform across the river, it is a dangerous, or at least inconvenient trip across a narrow ledge on the front of the dam itself.

The entrance from Winding River is also one-way. It may be accessed through a high window at the top of a mound of snow, but it is unreachable once the player drops down into the building. Reaching the window requires walking across the narrow front of the dam, accessed through the broken fence near the one-way exit.
_This section may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark._

![The Generator Room in story mode.](../assets/Carter_hydro_dam_in_story_mode.jpg)_The Generator Room in story mode._ The dam plays an important role as a location in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of story mode. In story mode, the dam has a significantly different layout, with walkways across the Generator Room, an elevator, additional rooms, and a staircase leading up to the offices on the floor above the [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) entrance level.

Cat tails are harvestable plants found in the world of [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md) near sources of fresh water, such as frozen ponds, marshes, creeks, and rivers. Like other plants, they do not grow back once harvested. After harvesting, they leave no trace behind, unlike [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) and saplings, which leave behind an empty bush, and a stump respectively.

They are one of the most plentiful sources of [Forage](./Foraging.md) in the game. There are over 1000 individuals Cat Tail plants found through the game world, making it one of the most common types of plants that can be foraged (even more with [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) installed, upping that number to over 2000).
Cat tails can be harvested without a tool. Upon harvesting, they provide both a single [Cat Tail Head](./Cat%20Tail%20Head.md), and a single [Cat Tail Stalk](./Cat%20Tail%20Stalk.md).

The Cat Tail Head acts as a form of Tinder, and can be used as such, providing a +0% chance to starting a fire (like all other tinder). The Cat Tail Head cannot be added to an active [Fire](./Fire.md) as fuel.

The Cat Tail Stalk is a [Food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item that can be consumed for 150 calories. Doing so does not drain your [Thirst](./Thirst.md), unlike most other foods. Cat Tail Stalks are a staple food source that all survivors should carry. It is especially helpful in the early game when food is scarce, or on harder difficulties like Interloper.

Cat Tails can be found in every [Region](./Region.md), and are always located near freshwater lakes, streams and rivers. Cat tails can be alone, or near loose groups of others. They cannot be found near saltwater. (However freshwater rivers flowing into the ocean can have cat tails). They are especially prominent in the Forlorn Muskeg region.

Similar to many other [regions](./Region.md) on Great Bear Island, Ash Canyon features a large, explorable **Cave System** located in the far north of the map. It is near [Long Falls](./Long%20Falls.md) and ends up in the mountains, with 2 paths that lead to either [Wolf's Jaw Overlook](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md) or [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md). Like most other explorable caves, it's warm enough to keep even a poorly clothed character above freezing.

This cave has some similarities to the [ice caves](./Ice%20Cave.md) of the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) in that it contains a waterfall at the bottom entrance. Going through waterfalls will soak the player and completely drain the temperature bar, as well as extinguish any held light source (excluding the [marine flare](./Marine%20Flare.md)). Also, as with the ice caves, this location requires the use of a [mountaineering rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) (which always spawns pre-attached) to traverse from one entrance to the other. The cave may contain a [Wolf Carcass](./Wolf%20Carcass.md), a [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md), and a [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) in the room containing the rope, as well as [coal](./Coal.md) scattered in different areas throughout. Another frozen corpse, a wolf carcass, or both can spawn on the second level overlooking the lower area by a blocked slope.

Unlike the ice caves, this cave has no natural sources of light. It is not very long, but a light source or two is needed to make it through, as navigation can otherwise be nearly impossible. While passing through the waterfall and surrounding puddle near the lower entrance, it is also advisable to unequip any clothing to prevent them from becoming soaked and subsequently freezing.

**Description:** Transition Zones, Dark tunnels winding through the slopes separating regions.

**Connecting Regions:** [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) and [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md), [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) and [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md), [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) and [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) and [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md)

There are several cave systems located on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) that serve as indoor Transition Zones between major regions. 2 of them are named Coal mines, while 7 of them are unnamed (simply called **Cave** when approached). Being indoor areas, they do not show up on any local maps, and cannot be surveyed with [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md) since they are indoor areas (save for the entrances/exits to the cave systems).

Despite appearing to be unique isolated areas on the island, every cave system is considered parented to a particular region (this can be seen when opening a map inside a cave system). While this would otherwise be considered trivial information, this detail can come in handy when attempting to wait out/escape the [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) while playing [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md), and also affects the "days spent in" record for a region.

Located between the upper area of [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) and a cliff overlooking [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), this coal mine is rich in coal, containers, and sometimes tools, as well as a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) that can be found inside.

Located between [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) and the [Old Island Connector](./Crumbling%20Highway.md) (Crumbling Highway), this coal mine is rich in coal, containers, and sometimes tools, as well as a work bench that can be found inside. There are several collapsed portions of the mine that must be crouched under in order to pass through.

Though technically not a cave system, the Carter Hydroelectric Dam Environs is an indoor Transition Zone (see [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) for more details) that connects [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) to [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md).

This cave system is located between the northwestern area near the [Hilltop Cave](./Hilltop%20Cave.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) and the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) regions.

The long and winding tunnels coupled with the low light make navigating this cave difficult. It is highly recommended that players venturing into the cave have a light source such as [matches](./Matches%20%28disambiguation%29.md), a fueled [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), or several [flares](./Flare.md). No [animals](./Wildlife.md) are present in this transition cave, but several [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), both human and [deer](./Deer.md), may be found throughout the tunnels. Many [Cairns](./Cairns.md) can also be found throughout the cave.

The cave has a relatively linear layout. One end is found in the south of the the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region, and accessed via the climbing spot at the [Picnic Area](./Picnic%20Area.md). The other is found southeast of the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) in [Mystery Lake.](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md)

The cave contains no [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md), but there are several [Sticks](./Stick.md), logs, and pieces of [Coal](./Coal.md) found in the cave. A rabbit carcass and a soda might also spawn in the cave.

The second transition cave in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) is on the northernmost part of the map, close to the [Trailer (Mountain Town Region)](./Trailer%20%28Mountain%20Town%20Region%29.md) and [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md). The cave is rather short and unremarkable, but contains a few pieces of coal and some sticks.

A very dark linear but winding cave with very little notable features, this cave connects to the lower elevations of [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) (close to [Ravine's End Waterfall](./Ravine%27s%20End%20Waterfall.md)) and to the slightly higher elevations of [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), not far from the [Muskeg Overlook](./Muskeg%20Overlook.md). It forms a path inside that splits into 2, only to ultimately reconnect to form a loop. One part of the path forces the player to climb a small cliff using roots; a moss bed is laid out at the base of the cliff. The other path is a straight line accessible by crouching and weaving through a narrow passage.

The entrance to this cave system starts in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), specifically near the [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md). It is filled with the usual bits of Coal and fallen Sticks from holes in the ceiling, but contains notably also contains a chamber in the center of the cave system that spawns a corpse next to a campfire with some loot. The exit to this cave system leads to the upper plateau area of [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md).
The cave does NOT contain a rope climb, only two "root climbs". As such it is possible to traverse it while being overloaded.

The entrance to the cave in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) can be found by following the frozen river uphill which is right next to [Andre's Peak](./Andre%27s%20Peak.md). A [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) bush can be found right in front of the cave. It is a very dark cave and requires an artificial light source. It contains two small cliffs with roots that can be climbed. The lower part of the cave may also contain a ravaged wolf carcass very close to the exit towards [Blackrock.](./Blackrock.md) Caution is advised since the cave also contains pools of cold water that can wet the players clothing, though some of them cannot be seen. Whether this a bug or an intended feature is unknown.

The entrance to the cave system is easy to get to as both Keeper's Pass regions are rather linearly structured. The inside of the cave itself contain a torch on the North side, a possible deer carcass with some arrows sticking out of it on the south side, a dead end where a [Wool Toque](./Wool%20Toque.md) may spawn and a large shining moss covered room containing a backpack with randomized loot and a [Marine Flare](./Marine%20Flare.md) which may be hard to spot due to its color, but lies near the spiky rock in the middle of the room.

The cave is very easy to navigate, featuring only a simple loop on the north side and a couple of dead ends. When going north to south choose the second right split (the last one that isn't a dead end), you should arrive at a place where there are stalactites in the hallway, take a left and you should be in the well lit moss covered room, it should now be a straight path to the exit, in the room with the deer carcass climb a little ramp to reach it.
This Transition Cave is by far the largest and longest cave in the game, so be prepared to bring plenty of light sources.
The entrance to the cave in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) can be found slightly south of the crashed [Helicopter](./Helicopter.md) in the mountains on the east of the map.

A second path in the middle of the cave system will allow the player to climb their way up a Rope Climb section to travel to [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) instead. The entrance can be found halfway up the eastern path from the [Last Lonely House](./Last%20Lonely%20House.md) to the [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md).

Cedar Firewood can be harvested from downed Cedar Limbs found outdoors with a [tool](./Tools.md). It can also be found inside of structures, firewood bins, rotten tree trunks, or near campfires and corpses. It can also be found by [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md).

- Cedar Firewood increases the chance of starting a fire (+15%), which is useful at low [Firestarting Skill](./Skills.md). [Sticks](./Stick.md), [Accelerant](./Accelerant.md), [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md), [Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md), [Wood Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md), and [Firestrikers](./Firestriker.md) also increase Firestarting chance.

- Small Cedar Limbs yield 3 Cedar Firewood with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), or [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md). They take 45 minutes to harvest with a hatchet, 58 minutes with an improvised hatchet, and 1 hour and 30 minutes with a hacksaw.

- Large and Small Cedar Limbs cost tools the same condition per use (4%), making Large limbs more tool-friendly to harvest, except with the Hacksaw which cannot harvest Large Cedar or Large Fir Limbs.

- A single piece of Cedar firewood has a fire duration of 60 minutes, so its 120 min/kg is more weight efficient than the 90 min/kg of [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md). However, Fir Firewood is more tool-efficient, since harvesting any limb costs 4% durability and Small Fir Limbs yield 4.5 hours of fuel (4.0 for Cedar) and Large Fir Limb yields 6.0 hours of fuel (5 for Cedar).
- Cedar Firewood has the same weight efficiency as [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md), with two pieces of Reclaimed Wood being identical to one piece of Cedar Firewood.

- Cedar Firewood, [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md), and [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) can be used to craft various [Decorations](./Decorations.md) that can be used in [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md).

A **Cedar Limb** is one of the many stationary interactable objects found in _The Long Dark_. They respawn randomly in the world over time under trees, making them a renewable [material](./Materials.md).
There are two variants of this object: small and large. Both can be turned into [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) and [Tinder Plugs](./Tinder%20Plug.md).

In addition to Cedar Firewood, these limbs will always yield one [Tinder Plug](./Tinder%20Plug.md) when harvested. This, along with cedar being easier to start than [Fir Fireword](./Fir%20Firewood.md), means that breaking down a Cedar Limb will provide all the resources needed to start a fire.

It's commonly believed that limbs respawn after strong winds or blizzards, but this is untrue. Radial spawns (sticks, branches, coal, stones ect.) simply spawn on a randomized timer, independent of any weather conditions.
Small limbs will provide 3 firewood and 1 and can be cut up using a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) (45 min), [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) (58 min), or [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) (90 min).
Large limbs cannot be cut up with a Hacksaw, and take 60 min to harvest with a normal Hatchet, or 78 min with an Improvised Hatchet. Large Cedar Limbs are very rare and only appear in set locations:
- In [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md), in the incropping with [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) turning left right after the bridge exiting from [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md)

**Challenge Mastery** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is obtained after successfully completing every [Challenge](./Challenge.md), with the exception of [As the Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md) and [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md). This achievement is one of the more challenging ones to get, as some challenges are easier to complete than others, especially for players who don't know Great Bear Island very well and are newer to the game.
- [Nomad](./Nomad.md): Generally the easiest challenge for new players. Good tour of Great Bear for those who are not familiar.
- [Archivist](./Archivist.md): Also quite easy, though travel at night during the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) can be hazardous due to aggressive predators.

- [Whiteout](./Whiteout.md): Usually not too difficult, however this depends on RNG. Most supplies can be found in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), though sometimes a trip to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) or [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) is necessary.

- [Hopeless Rescue](./Hopeless%20Rescue.md): Easy for players who know their way around [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), and [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md). If not, it is very difficult. [Coffee](./Tin%20of%20Coffee.md) can make this challenge much easier.

- [The Hunted, Part One](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20One.md): The [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) is aggressive but can be scared off the same way as [wolves](./Wolf.md). Keeping a good supply of [torches](./Torch.md) and knowing [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) and [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) makes this much easier.

- [The Hunted, Part Two](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Two.md): As long as the player uses torches and flares to scare off wolves, there should be enough bullets to deal with the bear. Not too difficult.

**Challenges** are special survival scenarios within [_The Long Dark's_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md) [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) sandbox. In addition to the normal survival mechanics, Challenges contain narrative-based objectives, unique gameplay and enemies not normally found in normal survival mode, and in some cases, a time limited objective. Challenges can be found within the Survival main menu as their own separate game mode.

There are currently eight challenges in the _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. Completing a Challenge will unlock a [Badge](./Badges.md) as proof of completion and allows the player to compare their completion time with other players. Completing all of them (excluding difficulty 6 challenges) yields the _Challenge Mastery_ [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md).

_This section may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark._

[Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) contains many residents that once thrived in the various regions and towns across the Island before and after the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md). Many are found and interacted with in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) also contains its own references to many of the Island's inhabitants, but many characters and locations found within Wintermute have been changed, suggesting an alternate timeline of events takes place in Survival Mode.
Wintermute places a large focus on interacting with several inhabitants of Great Bear Island. Several story points only progress when speaking with or accepting quests for many central characters.

William Mackenzie is the central protagonist of the story of _The Long Dark_. The current caretaker of [Jackrabbit Remote Transport](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md), Mackenzie is tasked by Astrid Greenwood to help fly herself and a [Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) to the local to Great Bear Island. During the flight, their plane crashes into the mountains of the island, with Mackenzie being trapped at the bottom of a nearby ravine. Stranded far from the closest human civilization while being lost, wounded, and alone, Mackenzie must quickly master basic wilderness survival skills if he's to last long enough to find Astrid and understand how his world has just changed forever.

Astrid Greenwood is the deuteragonist of the story of _The Long Dark_. A researcher wishing to travel to Great Bear Island with a mysterious Hardcase, Astrid is separated from Mackenzie after their small plane crashes to the ground in the northern Canadian wilderness. The two are separated and forced to survive in the unforgiving reality of the Quiet Apocalypse, as Astrid is forced to continue her journey to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) alone and without the Hardcase.

An old, blind woman living alone in the [Milton House](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md), Grey Mother is the only survivor found in [Milton](./Milton.md) after a nearby [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) containing several Convicts abducted everyone in town and forced them into the [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md) before it burned down with everyone inside. She successfully defended herself with a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and slowly helps Mackenzie find Astrid after warming up to him.

In Survival Mode, Grey Mother's home is ransacked, with knocked over furniture and several bullet holes in the wall facing away from her overturned rocking chair and blanket suggesting that she was taken by Convicts and placed with the other residents of Milton inside the Old Schoolhouse before it burned down.

A mysterious old man that seems to be able to travel around the Island with no difficulty despite its treacherous conditions, Methuselah is a "guardian angel" that appears to Mackenzie multiple times after he crash lands on the Island. He explains to the Mackenzie that the world is changing, and that human acts of neglect towards nature are being repaid by the onset of the "Quiet Apocalypse," and that he must condition himself to survive in this new world.

Hobbs is a Convict that can be encountered by Mackenzie at [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) bleeding on a couch. He reveals that he helped gather many residents of Milton into the Old Schoolhouse before it caught on fire, and was subsequently stabbed by Astrid with a knife, which is currently still inside him. Mackenzie can choose to plunge the knife deeper into Hobbs which will kill him, but his fate is unknown if Mackenzie removes the knife.

In Survival Mode, the Paradise Meadows Farmhouse contains signs of a struggle, with a bloodstain near the couch that Hobbs rested on and several books strewn around the couch being the only sign of Hobbs' presence.

An old hermit trapper living within the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), Jeremiah is found being mauled by a bear at the end of Episode 1 and is saved and nursed back to help by Mackenzie. He is the deuteragonist of Episode 2, tasking Mackenzie to kill the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) stalking them if they are to ever leave the area. He ultimately tasks Mackenzie with delivering a message to his friend Atwood at Perseverance Mills; Wintermute.
Jeremiah's homestead is vacant in Survival Mode, suggesting that he may have been successfully killed and eaten by the Old Bear.

Mathis is the central antagonist of Wintermute. Found at the end of Episode 2 taking Mackenzie hostage, he is revealed to be the leader of a gang of [Convicts](./Convicts.md) in Episode 4, who have made their home base of operations inside a Federal Penitentiary in the [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) region. Cold and unempathetic to the suffering of others, his current goal is to free his son Donner and escape the Island, possibly with his Convict army in tow to conquer other parts of the world.
He is voiced by [Elias Toufexis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Toufexis) (previously Gord Marriott in Episode 2).

Molly is a local of [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) who has lived most of her life on [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md). A former widow of a farmer, she finds Astrid's nearly frozen corpse after she escaped the madness that gripped Milton. After nursing Astrid back to health, she leaves the hope to go hunting, before Astrid discovers the corpse of Molly's husband and frees her from a [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) attack at her [Barn](./Barn%20%28Molly%27s%29.md), Molly leaves the farmhouse and begins stalking Astrid around the Valley, while also hunting any nearby Convicts.
Her fate in Survival Mode is unknown, with her nearby [Barn](./Barn%20%28Molly%27s%29.md) having a Timberwolf sized hole in it but no dead Timberwolf, suggesting that she was eaten.

A Christian priest that once resided over the dwindling population of [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), Father Thomas has received a new flock after the First Flare caused a [passenger airliner](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) to crash into the northern mountains. His main purpose is to look over the Crash Survivors in Episode 3, literally and metaphorically guiding the lost souls of the plane crash safely to his sanctuary located within the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md), will also offering guidance regarding the local topography to Astrid.
Thomson's Crossing Community Hall is vacant in Survival Mode, and Father Thomas is nowhere to be found, subsequently dooming all survivors of the Plane Crash.
2 Convicts that serve as the right and left hands of Mathis, Vachon and Heller serve as the secondary antagonists of Episode 4, taking orders directly from Mathis himself to keep an eye on Mackenzie.
The former warden of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), Franklin has been captured by Mathis and his Convicts and is ultimately executed by Mathis.

A young graduate student in astrophysics, Jace has become trapped in a guerilla war against the Convicts of Blackrock Prison, teaming up with Mackenzie to prevent their further expansion into the nearby wilderness. She is ultimately rescued by Mackenzie, and the two journey to Perseverance Mills in search of Atwood at the end of Episode 4.

Jace's thesis professor and a resident of Perseverance Mills as well as the friend of Jeremiah, Atwood is currently a woman that Mackenzie is in search of in order to pass the message "Wintermute" along to.
Originally appearing in 2 cameos in Episodes 3 and 4, Jane Yang is a resident of Perseverance Mills that tasks Astrid Greenwood with coming to the Island to help her people.

A woman that is heard briefly in a cutscene in the beginning flashback of Episode 1, while Mackenzie is still in the [Jackrabbit Remote Transport](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md). She is possibly a secretary or someone that works for the company, as she phones Mackenzie to deliver a message that someone is arriving. Her voice can barely be heard over the call, but subtitles reveal what she is saying. Her phone call with Mackenzie is interrupted when Astrid Greenwood arrives. Her name appears in the credits for Episode 1 and 2.
Astrid Greenwood and Will Mackenzie had a son at one point in the past, with his death affecting the two and causing a divorce (and Astrid to reclaim her maiden name).

The son's name is never mentioned, but is brought up the start of Episode 1 during Will and Astrid's conversation about flying to Great Bear Island. Mackenzie initially mistakes Astrid's desire to fly to the Great Bear as a way of bringing their son back, but Astrid rejects this idea, starting an argument between the two that neither feels empathy for the mourning of their son.

Despite the divorce, both Will and Astrid kept their wedding rings, possibly to remember the good times they had with their son and former spouse. Will later sympathizes with Grey Mother's predicament regarding her own daughter after having lost his own, saying that "Losing a child is like..." with Grey Mother finishing him, "Like losing your life".

The owner of [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) and former husband of Grey Mother, Martin Barker is found dead during the course of Episode 1, being eaten by a Wolf. He can also be found dead in Survival Mode as a possible spawn for the [Paradise Meadows Farm Key](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm%20Key.md).

The deceased daughter of Grey Mother and Martin Barker, she is a woman that Grey Mother occasionally confuses for Astrid when helping Mackenzie. She is currently buried at the cemetery at [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md).

A Forest Talker can be found at [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md) in Episode 2 and gives the [Lake Gunshots](./Lake%20Gunshots.md) side mission. He is fully voiced, but cannot be seen when initially met. Depending on choices made during his questline, he will live and reward Mackenzie with [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md) or will be found dead outside his cabin with an arrow stuck in him.

Hank is center focus of the side mission [Hank's Hatch](./Hank%27s%20Hatch.md). He was once a fire watch man who lived in the [Fire Watch Lookout](./Lookout%20%28Mystery%20Lake%20location%29.md) in Mystery Lake and began prepping for any upcoming future disasters. Across the mission, his relatives Angela, her mother, are both found dead trying to make their way to the underwound bunker he created. By the time the player finds him, he is found dead on the floor inside his prepper bunker having died from an infected leg wound from a recent wolf attack.

- "Hank" is a nod to the protagonist ["Henry"](https://firewatch.fandom.com/wiki/Henry) from the videogame _Firewatch_. Hank (a common nickname for Henry) shares many similarities with his counterpart, including taking a job working in a fire tower to be away from other people. In his journal, Hank complains about "the chatty lady" on the radio, a reference to [Delilah](https://firewatch.fandom.com/wiki/Delilah), Henry's supervisor in _Firewatch_ who communicates with him by radio throughout the game and also occasionally refers to him as "Hank". Hank's Journal refers to him finding a "weird old bunker," also a reference to the plot of _Firewatch._

- In his second journal entry, found in the bunker, Hank mentions hearing someone trying to get in. He does not open the door for them, and then dies from an infected leg wound from a Wolf attack. The body found outside, presumably the person trying to enter, has antibiotics and antiseptic on them. Had he let them in, they both may have survived.

He shares the same model as Martin Barker, but with different facial features. Curiously, his corpse appears at the start of [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) inside a car as Molly is patrolling.
_"Hank" at the start of [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), but with facial hair_

In Episode 2, while attempting to get a radio message out on a repaired radio, Will Mackenzie and Jeremiah hear a man on another frequency calling from Perseverance Mills desperately calling anyone for aid from another party that is currently heading to the Island. The broadcast is interrupted when the radio the 2 men are using dies. This same broadcast can be heard again by Astrid Greenwood in Episode 3, from another perspective.

Various Convicts of Blackrock Prison roam the Island in many of Wintermute's Episodes. All appear to be men, with many being found dead across every Episode. Some can be seen alive as part of Mathis' gang in Episode 4.

The deceased husband of Molly, his body is found in the basement of the [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) in Episode 3. While a backstory is never fully given, Molly alludes to a possible abusive relationship stemming between the two of them that ultimately resulted in his recent death at the hands of wolves.

Gwen is a plane Crash Survivor found by Astrid Greenwood in Episode 3. She is found near the tail section of the [Crash Site](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) trapped underneath a plane seat. She is suffering from extreme hypothermia and her right leg is [bleeding badly](./Blood%20Loss.md), only barely being kept alive by a nearby fire, and is later rescued and taken to the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md). She wears [Work Boots](./Work%20Boots.md), [Jeans](./Jeans.md), and a [Thin Wool Sweater](./Thin%20Wool%20Sweater.md).
In Survival Mode, a blood stain appears at the tail section where she is found in Wintermute, suggesting that she was taken away by some force, either predator wildlife or another survivor.

3 Crash Survivors found scattered across Pleasant Valley in Episode 3 in the [Coming Storm](./Coming%20Storm.md) mission. Much like Gwen, they must be rescued by Astrid and returned to the Community Hall.

A plane Crash Survivor found in the Community Hall in Episode 3, he is only notable because he forces Astrid to head to the plane crash site in order to retrieve his [Insulin](./Insulin.md), as he suffers from the [Hyperglycemic Risk](./Hyperglycemic%20Risk.md) affliction. The [Suitcase](./Suitcase.md) holding his Insulin at the [Crash Site (Pleasant Valley)](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) is labeled "[Suitcase belonging to Dimitri S.](./Suitcase%20belonging%20to%20Dimitri%20S..md)"

The passengers of the crashed plane found inside the Community Hall in Episode 3. The living survivors have very few voice lines aside from coughing, moaning or pleading Astrid to find their missing companions Logan, Ava, or Wade. A list of names for the crash survivors includes:

Donner is an unseen character that is the center focus of the Convict's motivations in Episode 4. The son of Mathis, his father desperately tries to free him from the solitary cell of Blackrock Prison. He is described as a once in a generation criminal, too psychopathic to ever return to normal society.

2 men seen in the ending of Episode 4 at the docks of Perseverance Mills. They are alarmed and confused at the arrival of Astrid and believe she is a quarantine breaker. They are eventually accompanied by Jane Yang, who quickly takes control of the situation when she recognizes Astrid.
They appear in [Cooper's Blind](./Cooper%27s%20Blind.md) in Episode 5, but have no lines of dialogue.

Survival Mode is unique in that it has no real plot found outside of the [Tales](./Tales.md) found within the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md). [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) reveal the existence of various Great Bear Island inhabitants of various locations encountered in Wintermute, but the player character does encounter any other humans aside from the occasional [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md). Below is a list of characters mentioned only in Survival Mode:

[Rüdiger](./Dr.%20R%C3%BCdiger.md) is the central focus of the Tales of From the Far Territory storyline. Very little is known about him, other than that he is responsible for the creation of a large machine inside the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), as well as ordering an unknown experimentation on several people.

Former [Security Chief](./The%20Security%20Chief.md) under the employ of Rüdiger. [The Security Chief's Remains](./The%20Security%20Chief%27s%20Remains.md) can be found, as well as the [Security Chief's Rifle Holster](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Rifle%20Holster.md). Name mentioned in [Security Chief's Log 31](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%2031.md), with her full name and image displayed on [Security Chief's ID Badge](./Security%20Chief%27s%20ID%20Badge.md).

The former head [Foreman](./The%20Foreman.md) of the Langston Mine, The Foreman was responsible for ensuring that the mine operated safely as well as helping oversee the construction of Rüdiger's machine inside the mine. His fate is unknown, but his [Tool Belt](./Foreman%27s%20Tool%20Belt.md) is found inside the control room of the Glimmer Fog machine deep inside the Mine.

The [Project Medical Officer](./Project%20Medical%20Officer.md) was employed by Rüdiger to study the mental effects of the Langston Mine workers after they were exposed to The Machine. He receives the most attention in [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md), but is mentioned a few times in the two remaining Tales.
An unknown man affected by an unknown mentally degrading condition, Patient 7 only appears in the Interview Transcripts left by the Project Medical Officer in Signal Void.
Below is a list of names involving any characters mentioned or found in Wintermute/Survival Mode in notes. Sometimes they appear as corpses.
### Wintermute

- Bank Manager - Manager of the [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md). Owner of Bank Manager's House, [Bank Manager's House Key](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House%20Key.md), [Bank Vault Code](./Bank%20Vault%20Code.md)

- any others who made it to the Community hall and perished. Their remains were stored in the basement.

It can be acquired easily after [lighting a fire](./Fire%20Starting.md) and allowing it to burn out or by looting containers, either outdoors or in a [firebox](./Fire.md#Contained_fires). Once a fire has burned out, the charcoal can be looted from the remnants. Stoves and naturally-generated campfires normally already contain some charcoal.

A fire must burn for at least one hour before charcoal will generate after the fire burns out. Charcoal will continue to "pile up" as wood is burned in a firebox/campfire, and will not be destroyed even when new fires are started (Charcoal generated will always stay in that firebox until it is removed).

The primary use of Charcoal is sketching Maps. The player must be outdoors, and only the area within the player's view can be sketched. Equip the Charcoal and an option will appear asking the player if they wish to survey the local area. The player can't survey when visibility is poor:

Surveying takes 15 minutes of in-game time, which will be sped up for the player and consume 1 Charcoal in the process. This will fill out the map with the player's immediate surroundings, including resources and carcasses that are directly visible to the character. The higher the player's current elevation, the more of the surrounding map is filled out.
Surveying can also be used to "ping" the area a player is in, even if it is already mapped. This can be useful if you find yourself lost.
There is no Charcoal in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), since maps are automatically given filled out to the player.
If the player finds a [Polaroid](./Polaroids.md) and travels to the survey spot located on the map, the player can survey large swaths of the local region map instantly.

- In real life, Charcoal does not form in significant quantities when wood is burned in a fire. This is because the draft produced by the burning charcoal tends to draw in enough air to keep itself alight. This is not the case in a camp fire, though, because some wood near the edges won't be fully consumed.

**Cheat Death** is a mechanic in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, allowing the player to escape a previously lethal situation at the cost of increased difficulty. Cheat Death was added for free in the Part 5 update of [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md).[^1]
This option is available for every difficulty Experience except [Misery](./Misery.md), and is not present in [Challenges](./Challenge.md).[^2]

Cheat Death is an optional change to The Long Dark's permadeath system which adds new gameplay to players who aren’t ready to lose their favorite survivor after dying. Cheat Death may be performed up to 3 times (for 4 total lives), with progressively harsher penalties each time. Each extra life is symbolized by a Campfire that can be seen upon quickly checking your status in the pause screen. If the player chooses to persist upon death, an extra life is used up, and the Campfires will become extinguished starting with the left, middle, right Campfire. Once a player dies a 4th time, the player will fade away into The Long Dark.
Upon reaching 0% [Condition](./Condition.md) while playing Survival Mode, the player will be presented with two options.

- Survivor [Skills](./Skills.md), inventory, collectibles, [Tales](./Tales.md) progress, [Survey](./Surveyed%20Locations.md) Progress, and [Achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) progress are lost.
- [Feat](./Feats.md) progress (unless playing on [Custom](./Custom.md)) and sandbox statistics are preserved (if the player chooses to record them).
- Ability to keep some carried items from the time of death, and later recover missing items.

- Retain [Skills](./Skills.md), [Tales](./Tales.md), [Survey](./Surveyed%20Locations.md), [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md), [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md), and certain [Achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) progress.

![Cheat Death Choice](../assets/Cheat_Death_Choice.jpg) If the player closes the game at this point, the save file will be wiped by default. Choosing "Cheat Death" allows the player to continue playing in the same Survival Sandbox, but at a cost...
![Cheat Death Consequences](../assets/Cheat_Death_Consequences.jpg)If the player chooses to Cheat Death, they will be presented with a list of consequences for this option.
> “**Progress for achievements that require completion within a single game will be reset.**”
Timers for [Achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) that require cumulative play time will be reset, and must be started from the beginning:

The player's [Condition](./Condition.md) and [Stamina](./Stamina.md) recovery will be halved when they awaken ([Weakened State](./Weakened%20State.md)).
> “**Your old pack is still in the world. Find it to recover what's left of your items.**”

Many items in the player's inventory will be missing when they wake up. Some items will be carried over to their new life, but many will be lost until they are recovered by finding the [Recovery Backpack](./Recovery%20Backpack.md).
> “**You will choose between a painful short-term penalty, or a more forgiving but permanent one.**”
The player will be given the choice of the severity of a penalty for choosing to Cheat Death (see next section).

The player cannot choose where to respawn, but how they will respawn (see later section).
The player can choose their [Cheated Death Penalty](./Cheated%20Death%20Penalty.md). The player can mix the two penalty types per death as they please:
- Max [Condition](./Condition.md) reduced by 50% for the first death, 60% for the second, 75% for the third.
- Max Condition PERMANENTLY reduced by 25% for the first death, 35% for the second, 50% for the third.
## Respawn
![Cheat Death Respawn](../assets/Cheat_Death_Respawn.jpg) When you Cheat Death, you'll be given the option to respawn somewhere inside the region you just died, or in a safe but far away location:

- **Close, Risky Respawn** will always put the player outdoors near danger in the same region you died in, and most of the time the hike back to where you died will be halfway across the map, but sometimes it will be shorter.

- **Far, Safe Respawn** will always send the player in or near an indoor location that they may or may not have already discovered in another region. "Safe" is relative, since based on the condition of clothing and remaining inventory, survival may still be a challenge. It is possible to be sent to a region the player has not explored yet, may be a neighboring region or one quite distant (ex, from [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) all the way to [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md)).
Once the respawn conditions are chosen, the player will be asked to confirm, allowing them to cancel Cheat Death or amend their previous choices.

If the player accepts the terms of Cheating Death, the survivor will wake up looking at their hands and commenting in their confusion if they really just died. Upon awakening, the following occurs:
- Approximately one in-game day will pass between their death and respawn, dependent on the safe/risky choice and time of day.
- All previous [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) and Affliction Risks are cured (including the incurable [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md)).
- The player can respawn at varying levels of daylight, such as in the middle of the night or during the morning/evening.

- The player will be afflicted with their chosen [Cheated Death Penalty](./Cheated%20Death%20Penalty.md), along with [Weakened State](./Weakened%20State.md). Weakened State gives the player very low Condition and [Stamina](./Stamina.md) recovery, and will always give the player a _Black and White_ screen. Always take this into consideration when choosing how to respawn, as this can make it difficult to see one's surroundings when you respawn in an already critical state, especially if the player happens to respawn at night.
- Your previously worn Clothing will be intact but will be heavily torn (in the 20% yellow range), resulting in the player easily freezing.
- The player will also typically respawn with low [Warmth](./Warmth.md), or other low [Needs](./Needs.md).
- Some items the player was carrying will still remain in their backpack, but most will be lost where they died in a [Recovery Backpack](./Recovery%20Backpack.md).

- The Recovery Backpack will be somewhere in the region you last died in, and is represented by a Campfire icon on the region map. The backpack will also be located next to a recently burned out [Campfire](./Campfire.md), as if someone else found your remains. Many items you were carrying when you last died being lost upon opening it (Some of your items can also be around the campsite), suggesting that whomever found your remains took some of your belongings.
- Recovery Campsites can appear in multiple locations with the same region, so do not expect your items to always be in the same location.

- Dying before reclaiming your Recovery Backpack and Cheating Death a second time will remove the first Backpack from the game world and generates a second one. The previous campsite will be removed from the Map and a second campsite will appear at a new location. This will result in the loss of all lost items tied to the Recovery Backpack from your first life if you did not recover them, **_including unique, one-of-a-kind items_** that can be found only once in the game world. The only exception to this is that any items around the first campsite rather than inside the Recovery Backpack will remain in the game world, but finding this camp can be troublesome without the icon on the Map.

- Example: dying with [Barb's Rifle](./Barb%27s%20Rifle.md) and not having it in your inventory when you awake, then dying and cheating death a second time before it was recovered will result in the permanent loss of the rifle on that playthrough.

**Cheated Death Penalty** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) acquired after choosing to [Cheat Death](./Cheat%20Death.md) in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

![Cheat Death Penalty](../assets/Cheat_Death_Penalty.jpg) The punishment for cheating death and continuing your save file always involves choosing between a great penalty that is temporary, or a smaller penalty that is permanent. The player can choose a mix of the two choices and their consequences as they die. Both penalties impact the [Condition](./Condition.md) bar, and will always be paired with the [Weakened State](./Weakened%20State.md) Affliction upon awakening after cheating death.
Choosing "Short Term Penalty" will result in a massive reduction in max Condition and a lengthy Recovery Time, but it will eventually heal.
| [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md) | -50% Condition | -60% Condition | -75% Condition | 240 hours (10 days) |
| [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md) | -50% Condition | -60% Condition | -75% Condition | 480 hours (20 days) |
| [Stalker](./Stalker.md) | -50% Condition | -60% Condition | -75% Condition | 480 hours (20 days) |
| [Interloper](./Interloper.md) | -50% Condition | -60% Condition | -75% Condition | 720 hours (30 days) |
Dying multiple times and choosing the "Short Term Penalty" Cheat Death option does not cause the Recovery Times to stack if the previous penalty time had not yet elapsed.
Choosing "Permanent Penalty" removes the lengthy Recovery Time, but will add a permanent reduction to max Condition for the rest of the game. The Condition loss is the same across all Experiences.

**Chemical Boots** are a footwear [Clothing](./Clothing.md) in _The Long Dark_. They are a tool for more safely crossing [Chemical Hazards](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) on the surface of [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md).

Chemical Boots protect against [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md) when standing in Chemical Hazards on the surface of Zone of Contamination, but not against inhaled chemical fumes from these areas (which require a loaded [Respirator](./Respirator.md)). Chemical Boots are immune to the corrosive effect of Chemical Hazards; unlike other footwear, which rapidly decays when standing in these areas.

Chemical Boots cannot be harvested or repaired, with 2-3 pairs found in The Zone: in [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md), [Conveyor Room](./Conveyor%20Room.md), [Headframe Building](./Headframe%20Building.md) or [Idle Camp](./Idle%20Camp.md).
Possible to acquire from the [Trader](./Trader.md) for 2.00 L [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md), 4 [Coal](./Coal.md) and 5 [Cloth](./Cloth.md)

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

[Chemical Hazard Barrels](../assets/Chemical_Hazard_Barrels.jpg) A **Chemical Hazard** is an [Environmental Hazard](./Environmental%20Hazard.md) located only in the industrial areas of the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) [Region](./Region.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ and is the reason for the Region's namesake. They are a result of past mismanaged waste disposal by the Langston Mining Corporation during the coal and uranium extraction operations of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), with the company's negligence and lack of care for the environment being another example of negative Mainlander influence upon [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). The presence of these chemical spills has also contributed to the Region's lack of healthy [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md), and have indirectly created the [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md). For players who have installed [The Long Development](./The%20Long%20Development.md), a Chemical Hazard can also be found at [Forsaken Shore](./Forsaken%20Shore.md).

![The Chemical Barrels found near Chemical Hazards, as viewed up close.](../assets/Chemical_Barrel.jpg)_The Chemical Barrels found near Chemical Hazards, as viewed up close._ Often found when traveling near manmade buildings and roads within the Zone, Chemical Hazards can be instantly recognized either as sickly phlegm-yellow colored patches of snow or as unnaturally orange colored of ice. Contaminated snow will often have ruptured chemical barrels with biohazard signs carelessly strewn in the snow, wherein contaminated ice will often be found in the frozen ponds located directly near the mining complex itself. Even from afar, signs that a Chemical Hazard are present are evident by the many dead/dying trees unfortunate enough to located in proximity to a chemical spill. Harvestable plants and healthy Wildlife will never be found near Chemical Hazards, forcing a survivor to look elsewhere for hunting and foraging opportunities.

Walking into a Chemical Hazard will result in a survivor coughing and choking on the contaminated air, and the 4 corners of the screen will begin to slowly turn yellow, indicating that they are being poisoned by the air. Continued breathing of these fumes will begin adding to a player's [Chemical Poisoning Risk](./Chemical%20Poisoning%20Risk.md), with prolonged exposure resulting in the [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md) [Affliction](./Afflictions.md).

Equipping a [Respirator](./Respirator.md) with plenty of fresh [Canisters](./Canister.md) will instantly stop Chemical Poisoning Risk buildup and cause any yellowing in the corners of the screen to slowly dissipate. If a Respirator runs out of Canisters, then the corners of the screen will begin to flare up and warn the player that they are being poisoned by the air.

Simply walking through a Chemical Hazard will degrade all 3 Footwear [Clothing](./Clothing.md) slots, rapidly destroying the Condition of a survivor's shoes and socks within seconds if a survivor does not leave a Hazard. The outermost Clothing layers will always Decay first, starting with the shoes slot, the right socks slot, and then the left socks slot. A visceral tearing sound will always play when a survivor's footwear rapidly decays and reaches red condition levels (less than 15% Condition)before being completely ruined.

If a player attempts to circumnavigate this issue by simply removing their footwear Clothing and walking through a Hazard, be aware that walking barefoot through a chemical patch will still result in Chemical Poisoning Risk buildup, as well as a potential [Warmth](./Warmth.md) loss/[Frostbite](./Frostbite.md) Risk.

Walking through a Chemical Hazard with [Chemical Boots](./Chemical%20Boots.md) equipped is the only way to prevent footwear from being destroyed and prevent Chemical Poisoning buildup. As such, great care must be taken to preserve the overall Condition of any Chemical Boots acquired when traveling throughout the Zone, as they cannot be repaired via [Mending](./Mending.md) and hostile Wildlife [Struggles](./Struggle.md) have a chance to greatly damage Chemical Boots.

Despite being contaminated with industrial chemicals themselves, Poisoned Wolves will refuse to enter Chemical Hazards, and will often go great lengths to run around them even if this costs them an opportunity to attack the player. Standing in a Hazard will cause a Poisoned Wolf to stop and growl at the player, and aiming a weapon at them will cause them to flee. This can be used as a possible exploit to drive Poisoned Wolves away if a survivor is properly equipped to stand within a hazard without being damaged, but is not advised. Any other Wildlife will also refuse to enter Chemical Hazards if they are driven near one.

A **Chemical Poisoning Risk** is an [affliction](./Afflictions.md) that can develop into [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md) if left untreated. Proximity to [Chemical Hazards](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) will add toxicity at a rate of 3% per minute for up to a maximum of 100% toxicity. The player will receive the [Chemical Poisoning Risk](./Chemical%20Poisoning%20Risk.md) affliction once they reach 20% toxicity and the [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md) affliction at 100% toxicity. By remaining away from Chemical Hazards, 10% toxicity will be removed per hour after a half hour delay. If a treatment is applied, the Chemical Poisoning Risk is removed without developing further into [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md).

![An example of a Chemical Spill in the Zone. Notice the sickly phlegm-yellow fumes surrounding the nearby barrels and dying trees.](../assets/Chemical_Spill.jpg)_An example of a Chemical Spill in the Zone. Notice the sickly phlegm-yellow fumes surrounding the nearby barrels and dying trees._The Zone of Contamination contains various spilled [chemical patches](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) on the surface. These patches are easy to identify from a distance from the fumes that hang around the surface. Dying/dead trees, toxic barrels strewn in the snow, and sickly orange ponds pumped full of chemicals good identifiers that chemical patches are in the area.

A Chemical Poisoning Risk alert will not immediately notify the player unlike other Risks, so situational awareness is a must when passing through a hazard. Simply walking near a Chemical Hazard will generate a buildup of a yellowish substance in each of the corners of the screen the longer one stays inside, and if a player stays inside a Hazard for too long, the survivor will begin to cough occasionally. If a player is inside a Hazard for too long, their footwear will degrade and begin to audibly generate a violent tearing sound. Chemical spills can be very hard to see during the night or during foggy weather, so it is best to stay away from roads/railroads/ponds when close to the mine.
Chemical Poisoning Risk is also acquired engaging in a struggle with a [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md).

Chemical Poisoning builds up in one of 2 ways, lungs and skin. Equipping a [Respirator](./Respirator.md) fitted with [Canisters](./Canister.md) while passing though a Chemical Patch reduces the player's vulnerability to Chemical Poisoning. Wearing footwear while walking through Patches will also alleviate Poisoning, though wearing anything but [Chemical Boots](./Chemical%20Boots.md) results in footwear Condition rapidly corroding. [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) [Struggles](./Struggle.md) can also slowly generate a moderate amount of Chemical Poisoning buildup for however long a Struggle lasts.

If a player does build up Chemical Poisoning Risk, simply leaving the hazardous area and waiting several hours in a clean environment will cause the toxins to gradually dissipate from the survivor's body, similar to how you clear [Cabin Fever risk](./Cabin%20Fever%20Risk.md).

The only treatment to Chemical Poisoning is to spend time away from contaminated areas; but additional buildup can be avoided by wearing ![Chemical Boots icon](../assets/Chemical_Boots_icon.png) [Chemical Boots](./Chemical%20Boots.md) in toxic areas and wearing a ![Respirator icon](../assets/Respirator_icon.png) [Respirator](./Respirator.md) (with a loaded![Canister icon](../assets/Canister_icon.png) [Canister](./Canister.md)) in toxic gases from the Chemical Hazards, and avoiding struggles with Poisoned Wolves.
If enough Chemical Poisoning Risk builds up, the player will be afflicted with [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md).
This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

**Chemical Poisoning** is a disease [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) mainly encountered in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) region of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) once [Chemical Poisoning Risk](./Chemical%20Poisoning%20Risk.md) is fully enveloped. It was added in the Part 4 Buried Echoes update for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon.
Being Afflicted with Chemical Poisoning immediately reduces the player's max [Condition](./Condition.md) to 80% (similar to [Burns](./Burns.md), but Condition lost is -20% instead of -25%).

This Affliction can be purged immediately by using an [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) to flush the body of toxins, or by waiting 72 hours for the disease to pass. Unlike other regions, Stims are quite plentiful in the Zone of Contamination, with many being found inside the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md).

A side effect of contracting Chemical Poisoning is that the player will lose the [Well Fed](./Well%20Fed.md) bonus, along with the Condition bonus it provides, even if the player's [calorie store](./Hunger.md) is above 0.

Unlike Burns, it is possible to have multiple stacks of Chemical Poisoning, causing even more Condition reduction to occur if not treated. The player can have up to 4 different Chemical Poisoning Afflictions (minus 20% Condition each time), with a 5th killing the player.
Using an Emergency Stim will only clear 1 Chemical Poisoning Affliction if multiple are acquired.

> “**A thief has stolen an Artifact from the Church at Thomson's Crossing. In a remote town, it's likely the Artifact has great value to the residents. See what you can do to locate the item and return it home.**”

**Church Artifact** is a side mission in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) must search for clues about the whereabouts of an artifact that was stolen from the church in [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) and return it to the church.
- Investigate the cabin near [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md), the police suspect was last seen there
| Significant locations | [Draft Dodger's Cabin](./Draft%20Dodger%27s%20Cabin.md), [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md) |

To start the mission, the player must find the [Diocese Report](./Diocese%20Report.md) inside the church which contain information about the missing artifact (the [Church Flyer](./Church%20Flyer.md) is optional). The player must then travel to the [Draft Dodger's Cabin](./Draft%20Dodger%27s%20Cabin.md). Under the bed in the cabin is a suitcase which contains a letter saying that the artifact is hidden in the basement of the house at [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md).

There is no direct path to Skeeter's Ridge from Draft Dodger's Cabin because a cliff face separates the two. Instead, the player must travel towards [Derelict Cabins](./Derelict%20Cabins.md) on the right side of the in-game map. Then the player can follow the main road back towards the crash site.
(After you rescue Gwen, you will be able to climb the cliff behind Draft Dodger's Cabin to Skeeter's Ridge, as the trees will fall and become a bridge.)

Once near the crash site, instead of entering the plane, continue to the left around the rock outcropping. A small group of burned-down houses constitute Skeeter's Ridge. One of the houses will have a bulkhead door leading down into the basement where the artifact can be found behind some loose boards beneath the clothes dryer.

Once the artifact is retrieved, it must be brought back to the church and placed on the altar. The player must then wait a full day and return to the church. Inside the church to the right of the altar, there is a blue table that will have a [Rabbitskin Hat](./Rabbitskin%20Hat.md) and a [Thankyou Letter](./Thankyou%20Letter.md) from [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md).

**Cinder Hills Coal Mine,**also known as "Abandoned Mine", is a series of mine tunnels located in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), with one section that acts as a connection to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
This mine has three levels: in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) these levels are separate areas, and in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) all three mine sections are interconnected.

- The Upper Level of the mine connects northern [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) (near [Abandoned Lookout](./Abandoned%20Lookout.md)) to southern [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) (near [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md)).

- The Lower Level of the mine is in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) near the [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md) and is relatively small. An electric-powered elevator in its depths leads up to the Middle Level of the mine, which becomes useable only when powered at night during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md).

- The Middle Level offers a series of interconnected tunnels with rich loot, but also [electrified hazards](./Burns.md). It can only be accessed via entering the Lower Level and using the elevator during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md).
The Feels Like temperature inside of mines is very warm on all Game Modes, and since no animals spawn inside they can serve as dark but safe shelter.
Cinder Hills Coal Mine is similar to [Abandoned Mine No. 3](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md). They both have long, dark tunnels that connect the two regions together.

Caution should be taken when exploring the Middle Level of the mine: electrified wires and electrified water can kill the reckless, and those who take too long will become trapped when the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) ends and the elevator becomes unpowered. This hazard can be partially offset by leaving a stockpile of food, water, and a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) inside the middle level beyond the elevator.

The Cinder Hills Coal Mine is an abundant and renewable source of [Coal](./Coal.md) fuel. Coal is highly valuable to heat a [Furnace](./Furnace.md) hot enough to forge [Arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md), [Improvised Hatchets](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), and [Improvised Knives](./Improvised%20Knife.md). Coal is also useful on Stalker and Interloper in extremely cold survival situations, to increase Ambient Temperature hotter than wood fires. Coal respawns inside mines after several days.

[Tools](./Tools.md), First Aid supplies, and [Clothing](./Clothing.md) can be found on Corpses, in [Lockers](./Prybar.md), or scattered about. A [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) can also be found in a room in the center of the mine, though it requires a light source to use.

Mines are not large but are pitch black beyond their entrances at all hours of day, and feature numerous dead ends or circuits. They can make navigation extremely difficult without a light source. It is advised to bring a [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), [Torch](./Torch.md), or [Flare](./Flare.md) while exploring them.
If you get trapped within the mine, there will always be another aurora scripted to start at 8:30pm the following night, allowing the player to escape.

- Ensure that any supplies you wish to transport between levels are on your person rather than the elevator floor; mechanically, the elevator does not physically 'travel' between levels, so items dropped onto it are not carried up or down, and will instead remain on the floor they were originally placed.

**Cleaning** or **Firearm Cleaning** is a secondary Survival [Skill](./Skills.md) that is used to repair [Hunting Rifles](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and [Revolvers](./Revolver.md). Higher levels in the cleaning skill reduce the amount of time required to clean and increase the amount of condition restored to a firearm by cleaning.
Cleaning involves using the [Firearm Cleaning Kit](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md) to keep a firearm in optimal condition.

The Cleaning skill is only visible when maintaining a hunting rifle or revolver and is not an official survival skill in the player's journal. Players start with 30 skill points, and gain 1 additional skill point each time a gun is cleaned.
Players can clean their firearms with an aptly named firearm cleaning kit any time of day; light is not required.

To clean a weapon, players have to select the "Clean" menu option while viewing the gun to repair in the inventory menu. The amount time perform one cleaning and the amount of condition restored to the weapon by each cleaning is listed on the right-hand side of the screen.
Currently, players will always have a 100% chance of success while cleaning and cannot fail. Activating the start button on the bottom right will launch an attempt.

Cleaning a firearm consumes 5% condition from the firearm cleaning kit and restores some condition to the weapon based on the player's [skill level](#skill-levels). Each rifle cleaning kit can be used up to 20 times for repairing a firearm.

Players need a Firearm Cleaning Kit before they can start cleaning rifles and revolvers. Cleaning kits can be found while scavenging in containers and buildings that are likely to contain tools or guns (e.g., [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md)). Cleaning Kits are always found in 100% condition.

Providing a decent warmth bonus, this cave is perfect to overnight in while wandering in the highlands. The lake in front of the cave is often frequented by [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and a possible [Moose](./Moose.md) spawn, making this place a good spot to rest in the central area in the region.

Although Climber's Cave is safe from hostile fauna and will not cause [cabin fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), its usefulness as a long-term base is severely limited by the lack of any food source other than rabbits and [cattails](./Cat%20Tail.md) in the nearby area. Additionally, the cave can become very cold during early-morning blizzards, which may necessitate a fire to stay warm. Overall, Climber's Cave is more suited for short-term stays than long-term living.

Climbers cave usually contains a high grade piece of clothing, for example [Snow Pants](./Snow%20Pants.md), and some food in form of cooked [Venison](./Venison%20%28Cooked%29.md) and a cup of [Herbal Tea](./Herbal%20Tea.md). It also contains randomized loot from a backpack, firewood and charcoal inside the burnt out campfire.

Going towards the right edge of the mountain, atop witch the cave is located (east, direction of Bitter Marsh), the survivor can find a medium size climbing rope going down, underneath which there is a small cave (left when looking at the bottom of the rope), inside which is possibly 10 [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md) and on a short ledge behind a pair of [Cargo Pants](./Cargo%20Pants.md) and a hunting knife hidden in a nook of the cliff, not far from the rope bridge over Shattered Cove.

This location is however best reached by dropping a one way slope from the same side of the mountain, but slightly above the [Climber's Cave](./Climber%27s%20Cave.md), the route is visible on the wiki map of [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), as this will save you one trip of the rope, as well as allowing you to reach a shallow cave at the far bottom of the map, possibly containing another 10 rounds of [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md). The beginning of this route is beneath a large overhang rock pass, visible on the right when standing above the [Climber's Cave](./Climber%27s%20Cave.md). There is a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) and a pair of [Ski Boots](./Ski%20Boots.md) buried in the snow under the overhang.

When climbing up the hill forming the back side of the [Climber's Cave](./Climber%27s%20Cave.md), the survivor will eventually arrive at a fallen tree forming a bridge before crossing a "hidden" cache can be found in the nook of the cliff,

Continuing across the fallen tree bridge (going East in the direction of Pillar Footrest), climb the slope to your right, then turn left and walk towards the outcropping in that direction, you will find a small nook with several items, usually including a small amount of ammo and food.

(In the past, a broken rifle could be discovered in the place of the minor loot, it was not harvestable, but around it partially buried in the snow were ~8 [Revolver Shell Casings](./Revolver%20Shell%20Casing.md) a [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md), [Stump Remover](./Stump%20Remover.md) and an [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md).)
