"_Out in the wilderness, clothing is like armour against the elements. Wear layers to stay warm. And remember, wind is your enemy! Clothing offers different protection from cold and windchill. Your clothes can get wet from blowing snow or if you fall into water, which makes them ineffective and increases your risk of hypothermia or even frostbite. Keep your clothes as dry as you can! Finally, clothing can protect you from physical injuries as from falling or tangling with wildlife. Balance all these factors against the weight and mobility cost of your combined clothing._"

**Clothing** is the term for items that can be equipped to provide bonuses to the player throughout their playthrough. Clothing does not have any requirements to wear. A player's total clothing bonus can be seen on the status screen.

In all difficulty levels, the player will start out with a few items of low-grade clothing. In the early game, one of the highest priorities is finding good quality clothing. It's possible to find clothing nearly everywhere, but some of the most common locations where clothing may be found include houses (bedrooms in particular), cabins, lockers, car trunks, suitcases, and [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md). If the player is struggling to find clothing, specific locations to search include [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), the [plane crash](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), the town of [Milton](./Milton.md), or the [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) found at the [Summit](./Summit.md) (bring a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) for here).

![Temp icon](../assets/Temp_icon.png) The **Warmth** bonus provided by clothing protects against the chilling ambient temperatures experienced by the player character. Each equipped clothing item contributes a specified number of degrees to the warmth bonus. The bonus is a constant effect that increases the "Feels Like" temperature. However, as clothing deteriorates, so too does the level of warmth it provides.
The highest possible warmth bonus that can currently be achieved is 44°C (79.2°F) (or 37.5°C on Interloper).

[Aviator Cap icon](../assets/Aviator_Cap_icon.png)/[Balaclava icon](../assets/Balaclava_icon.png)/ [Technical Balaclava icon](../assets/Technical_Balaclava_icon.png)/[Wool Toque icon](../assets/Wool_Toque_icon.png)
[Aviator Cap](./Aviator%20Cap.md)/[Balaclava](./Balaclava.md)/ [Technical Balaclava](./Technical%20Balaclava.md)/[Wool Toque](./Wool%20Toque.md)

![Windproofness icon](../assets/Windproofness_icon.png) The **Windproof** bonus provided by clothing protects against the additional heat loss experienced by the player due to windchill. Even when your gear's warmth rating is higher than the environmental temperature, when its windproof rating is lower than the windchill, you will lose heat. The windproof effect only increases the "Feels Like" temperature by the absolute number of degrees of windchill affecting the player.

Only the outermost layer of clothing contributes to the player's windproof bonus, which severely limits how much you can stack it. There are only 7 clothing slots that count towards the Windproof rating. These are: Head (1st slot), Outer Torso (1st slot), Outer Legs (2nd slot), Hands, Outer Feet (boots), and Accessories (both slots). This means inner hats, 2nd jacket, sweaters & shirts, 2nd pants, inner pants, and socks do not add to the windproof rating when fully geared, even if they have a Windproof score. Their windproof score only applies when no outer layer is worn over them. The accessories are an exception to this rule, however. Both accessory slots contribute to the player's windproof bonus.

![Waterproofness icon](../assets/Waterproofness_icon.png) The **Waterproof** bonus provided by clothing measures how resistant clothing becomes wet during outdoor activities and how fast they dry off.
- Clothes become wet by simply being left outside or inside [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md), if it's snowing, if a Blizzard is present, or being near certain wet locations.
- Clothing will become completely wet if the player falls through [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md), or when passing through a [waterfall](./Environmental%20Hazard.md#Waterfalls).
- One can also remove all clothing when going through a waterfall to avoid them getting wet, then simply put them back on.

- Walking through [shallow water puddles](./Environmental%20Hazard.md#Cold_Water_Puddles/Streams) will only soak your feet; remove boots and socks before walking through water to prevent them from becoming wet.
- Certain waterfalls with splashing water, such as the ones in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), also make the player's clothing wet by standing near them for long periods of time.
- Clothing will gradually dry when worn or dropped in a dry interior location. They rapidly dry when beside a [Fire](./Fire.md).
- Clothes cannot become wet if they are placed indoors or in the player's Backpack, even when passing through waterfalls/falling through Weak Ice.
- Wetness counters windproof protection. As clothes become wet, each% of wetness removes 1% of windproof. 100% wet equals 0% Windproof.
- Each 1% of Wetness makes clothing heavier than its initial weight (ex. a 1.00kg hat at 50% wetness will weigh 2.00kg).
- Clothing that becomes 100% Wet will weigh twice as much and begin gradually freezing over to 100% Frozen.
- Fully Wet clothing and 0% Frozen equal -15%°C and 0% Windproof as well as weighing twice as much as normal.

- Each 1% of Frozen makes clothing warmth decrease by 0.1 Wearing 100% frozen clothing also increases the likelihood of [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md) and will ultimately lead to [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md) (even if the player's other clothing is warm enough to counter the frozen clothing).
- Freezing counters the warmth protection. Each% of freezing diminishes warmth protection, and clothing becomes much heavier.
- A clothing at 50% Frozen = -15% + (-37%) more warmth. A 100% Froze clothing = 0% warmth & 0% Windproof.
- The time needed to reduce Frozen or Wet status depends on weight and Waterproof rating of the clothing as well as if a fire is active and nearby. When unfrozen, clothing becomes 100% wet again.

![Protection icon](../assets/Protection_icon.png) The **Protection** bonus provided by clothing provides a reduction in physical damage that the player may experience through falls, burns, or attacks from wildlife.

Only the outermost layer of clothing contributes to the player's protection bonus (the only exception to this is if the Ballistic Vest is worn on the inner Accesory slot). Layered clothing does not help mitigate the effects of damage beyond the outermost layer. Inner clothes eg. underwear, socks, 2nd coat, 2nd pants, or shirts, do not contribute to protection bonus. The accessories are an exception to this rule, however. Both accessory slots contribute to the player's protection bonus.

Protections works as follows: For every 1 protection you have, you receive 1% less damage from wildlife attacks. If you have 100% or greater, you become **_invulnerable_** to wildlife attacks (at the cost of clothing being damaged). Protection also reduces the damage done by the afflictions [Minor Bruising](./Minor%20Bruising.md), [Major Bruising](./Major%20Bruising.md), and [Laceration](./Laceration.md). Protection does not however, reduce the risk of receiving negative afflictions from fights. No matter what protection you have, you can still always get [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md), [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md), [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md), ect.

![Mobility icon](../assets/Mobility_icon.png) The **Mobility** penalty provided by clothing constricts the survivor's ability to move, reducing the maximum length of time that a player can [Sprint](./Stamina.md) while worn. The penalty is cumulative when wearing multiple pieces of clothing that cause a mobility penalty (e.g., a coat that reduces mobility by -5% and a pair of gloves that reduce mobility by -4% would yield a total penalty of -9%).
The highest possible mobility penalty that can currently be achieved is -100% (technically -126%, but capped at -100%)
[Deerskin Pants icon](../assets/Deerskin_Pants_icon.png)/[Wolfskin Pants icon](../assets/Wolfskin_Pants_icon.png)/[Snow Pants icon](../assets/Snow_Pants_icon.png)
[Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md)/[Wolfskin Pants](./Wolfskin%20Pants.md) /[Snow Pants](./Snow%20Pants.md)
[Deerskin Pants icon](../assets/Deerskin_Pants_icon.png)/[Wolfskin Pants icon](../assets/Wolfskin_Pants_icon.png)/[Snow Pants icon](../assets/Snow_Pants_icon.png)
[Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md)/[Wolfskin Pants](./Wolfskin%20Pants.md) /[Snow Pants](./Snow%20Pants.md)

![Item condition icon](../assets/Item_condition_icon.png) The **Condition** of clothing affects how well it does the job it's designed to do. As clothing deteriorates, it will contribute less to the players warmth and windchill protection. A piece of clothing at 50% condition rated for +2.0 degrees of warmth will only contribute +1.0 degrees. If clothing reaches 0% condition, it will become Ruined and can't be repaired, though it can still be harvested for raw materials.

![Weight icon](../assets/Weight_icon.png) The **Weight** of clothing is how much it weighs when carried, worn, or placed in a container. When worn, clothing only contributes 75% of its weight towards the player's carrying limit. Wet clothing also increases clothing weight by 0.01kg per 1%.
The heaviest clothing weight that can currently be worn is 29.65kg (this number jumps to 58.55kg when 100% Wet, though Improvised Crampons cannot get wet due to being 100% Waterproof)

Has an interior The **Co-op** is a location found in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), and serves as one of the few explorable locations of the town.

A store, post office, and local co-op for the unfortunate, it is located in the middle of town close to the Medical Clinic. The stores suffers from a similar fate as the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) in [Milton](./Milton.md), with its gas pumps having run dry, its ATMs being out of cash, and regular supply shipments being rare.

The outside has a single gas pump. The inside has a post office to the back left, a freezer to the back right, and a register to the right. Several items can be found inside still on the shelves, such as food, first aid, clothing, and other items. A second entrance to the building can be found in the back next to the bathroom.
Several items not found anywhere else on Great Bear Island are found inside the store, such as unique company brand cardboard cutouts for fishing lures and various foods and medicines.
[Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) arrives at the Co-op while searching for clues as to the town's disappearing populace, and briefly explores the store.

Coal is a fuel source for fires, and the only fuel which can heat Forges hot enough for Forging (150°C) to craft items. Each piece of coal added to a fire grants 1 hour of fuel and 20°C to its temperature. This makes it the most efficient fuel both for temperature and weight efficiency. Coal cannot be used to start a fire. It may be added once a fire has been started with another fuel (e.g. a [Stick](./Stick.md)).

Coal is found on the floor abundantly inside mines, some caves, and rarely along streambeds. Finite amounts of Coal are present at [Forges](./Forge.md) on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). The most abundant sources of coal are [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) and [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md).
- Coal is crucial for staying warm in Stalker and Interloper modes, where fires do not overcome ambient temperature, or prevent [freezing](./Needs.md).

- Due of the proximity of [Abandoned Mine No. 3](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md) to [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md) (and its forge), [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) is usually easier to forge at and sustainable for re-stocking than forges located in the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md), [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md), or [Hangar Basement](./Hangar%20Basement.md).

**Coastal Fishcakes** is a food item in _The Long Dark_, it is learned from a unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) and is made with a [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md).

Coastal Fishcakes can be unlocked for cooking by finding their [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) In the [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md) in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) in one of three locations: in the upper-left corner of the tack board, underneath the 3 metal cabinets, or on the stairs leading up to the top of the lighthouse.

Although Coastal Fishcakes are not the most calorie-dense food out there, their effects of increased [stamina](./Stamina.md) and carrying capacity can be exceptionally useful for players who need to do a lot of [rope climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md). The two [potatoes](./Potato.md) required to cook this are also fairly easy to find in most regions. The one disadvantage is that [rainbow trout](./Rainbow%20Trout%20%28Raw%29.md) is not obtainable on any inland maps, which are often the ones that require the most rope climbing. Additionally, both the pies and the fish needed to cook them do not keep especially well.

**Description:** A large frozen bay and coastline with a ruined highway crossing around it.

**Connecting Regions:** [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) (via [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md)) [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) (via [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md)) [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) (via [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md)) [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) (via [Old Island Connector](./Crumbling%20Highway.md))
**Hazards and Survivability:** The region has plentiful resources, but there is also a high concentration of [Wolves](./Wolf.md) and three [Bear](./Bear.md)-patrolled locations.
> “**For intermediate players. A weather-battered coastline rich in shelters and resources. Watch out for wildlife.**”

**Coastal Highway** is the 2nd [Region](./Region.md) released in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. The region is named after a section of the [Great Bear Highway](./Great%20Bear%20Highway.md) that wraps itself around a local lagoon, giving the region a C shape.

The region is a relatively warm crescent of steep hills and switchbacks surrounding an icy bay; a highway follows the coast with settlements along it. The bay's ice shelf features many [Fishing huts](./Fishing%20Hut.md), and further out two islands: [Jackrabbit Island](./Jackrabbit%20Island.md) and [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md). Several [Wolf](./Wolf.md) packs live in the area, and further out the bay's ice becomes thin and dangerous to walk upon.

Coastal Highway connects to [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) through the [Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md) to the north-west, [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) through the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) to the north, and [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) through the [Crumbling Highway](./Crumbling%20Highway.md) and [No. 3 Coal Mine](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md) to the south-east.

Compared to the nearby [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), it has more resources and overall warmer temperatures; however there are more abundant [wolves](./Wolf.md) and [bears](./Bear.md), particularly near the [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md), [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md), and [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md).

Coastal Highway also has two notable benefits compared to regions further inland. First, like in other coastal regions, [beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) is possible, giving the player easy and renewable sources of clothing, tools, medications, and fish, among other items. Second, Coastal Highway is the only region in the game with a [Trade Drop Box](./Trade%20Drop%20Box.md), meaning that it is the only region where goods can be directly exchanged with the [Trader](./Trader.md). This makes Coastal Highway a prime candidate for long-term habitation, and makes it one of the most important regions in the late-game.
Coastal Highway differs from most other regions in some regards, which may require adaptations to playing style.
- There are no proper [Warm Caves](./Warm%20Cave.md). The bear dens are just sheltered nooks.
- Two-slot cooking opportunities are only available indoors in a heavily wildlife-infested area, or using [campfires](./Campfire.md).

- The entrance to the Cinder Hills Coal Mine near the [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md) has a portion which is only accessible via an elevator which is only powered during an aurora. In past versions of the game, this Aurora Mine was considered highly dangerous, as players could become trapped underground for extended periods of time if they failed to leave before the aurora ended. However, in current versions of the game, if a player becomes trapped after the end of an aurora, there will always be a scripted aurora at 8:30 PM the following night allowing them to escape, making the Aurora Mine much safer to traverse.

One notable feature of this region is that, depending on the Experience chosen, many houses and cabins throughout the region spawn destroyed. On [Interloper](./Interloper.md), [Misery](./Misery.md), and the [As the Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md) Challenge, half of the available structures are destroyed. This can make certain locations contain very few structures to loot/shelter in. All trailers in the region will remain intact, regardless of difficulty however.

One piece of exclusive gear will be found in the region: [Barb's Rifle](./Barb%27s%20Rifle.md). This rifle is considerably more durable than the normal rifle, but is 0.50 kg heavier. Its exact location will vary in each playthrough.
- To Abandoned Mine (Transition to [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) Upper Level to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md))
- To Abandoned Mine (Transition to [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) Middle Level that leads to Lower Level)

Additionally, there are several indoor locations spread across the region that are recorded in the [Journal](./Journal.md). These locations are labeled [Coastal House](./Coastal%20House.md), Cabin, Fishing Cabin, and Trailer.
Many of these buildings will spawn destroyed if playing on [Interloper](./Interloper.md)/[Misery](./Misery.md) (labeled as I/M).
- [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) contains 7 (3 on I/M) [Coastal Houses](./Coastal%20House.md), with one on the outskirt of the town.
- [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md) has 1 Trailer and 1 Coastal House (the House can spawn boarded up, even on lower difficulties).
- [Waterfront Cottages](./Waterfront%20Cottages.md) can contain 1-2 [Coastal Houses](./Coastal%20House.md) (0 on I/M).
- There are 3 cabins south of [Abandoned Lookout](./Abandoned%20Lookout.md), below the cliff (2 on I/M).
- A Cabin is found east of the previous Trailer/west of Abandoned Lookout Cabins/north of The Tooth.
- A Cabin northwest of [Fishing Camp](./Fishing%20Camp.md), south of [Bear Creek Campground](./Bear%20Creek%20Campground.md) (spawns destroyed on I/M).
Additionally, a [crashed plane](./Plane%20Crashes.md) can be found to the east of Coastal Townsite, up in the hills past the Cabin on the outskirt of town.
There are several locations for [Safehouses](./Safehouse.md) in the Coastal Highway, including Jackrabbit Island and Quonset Garage.
- Pros: A central location with plentiful resources, abundant storage, an indoor workbench, bed, and fire barrel. Numerous vehicles nearby for storage or escape from predators.

- Cons: Multiple predators around the Quonset, including wolves, a bear and moose spawn. Very dangerous, especially if on Stalker and Interloper. No nearby cave (but fishing huts) for Cabin Fever; vehicles are quite cold.

- Pros: Centrally located, direct access to multiple key regions and to the [Trader](./Trader.md) while being secluded from predators. Has 2 rabbit groves on the island, and 1 nearby (towards Misanthrope) as well as fishing, abundant sticks, and close access for [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md). Several possible bear spawns in the vicinity but none come close to the island.

- Cons: Somewhat unreliable [Fir Limb](./Fir%20Limb.md) / [Cedar Limb](./Cedar%20Limb.md) spawns, a [Travois](./Travois.md) is recommended to haul in bigger loads from elsewhere. No place for indoor fires ([Fireplace](./Fireplace.md), [barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) or [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md)). No nearby cave for Cabin Fever, only Fishing Huts. Wolves and Timberwolves can spawn near Fishing huts.

- Pros: multiple rabbit groves (2 over hill, 1 near the bridge, 2 at Jackrabbit Island) and fishing shacks, and close to the coast for beachcombing. Centrally located in the region, and has a workbench (outdoors).

- Cons: Multiple wolves may spawn nearby, as well as a bear up the road or atop the hill. Workbench is outdoors. No place for indoor fires (fireplace, barrel or pot belly stove). No nearby cave for Cabin Fever.

- Many photographs on walls or nightstands inside the houses of Coastal Highway are [Hinterland's](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md) developers, or their friends and family; this includes "Stacyplays" (aka Stacy Hinojosa) a YouTuber who ran a "let's play" series during The Long Dark's alpha/beta (2014-2016). The item [Stacy's Grape Soda](./Stacy%27s%20Grape%20Soda.md) is also named after her.

Most structures except for [Quonset Gas Station](./Quonset%20Garage.md) have a random chance of being burnt down and inaccessible.
In addition to a relatively large number of wolves often patrolling the area, a [bear](./Bear.md) and a [moose](./Moose.md) may also wander by, so caution outdoors is almost always advisable.

The **Coffee Table** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.
A makeshift wooden table, a Coffee Table can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The table can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value, the table cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the table will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).
The Coffee Table can be harvested with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) in 1 hour 30 minutes for 5 [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md).

**Coho Salmon (Cooked)** is a cooked [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.
At 0% condition food disappears if inside of a container, but not outside of containers or in the player's inventory.

Using salmon on a lit [fire](./Fire.md) yields Cooked Salmon. Cooked fish increases its condition by 50%, decays 4 times slower than raw meat, and has a reduced chance of [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) over raw meat, while decreasing its weight by 35%. Cooked salmon's energy density is 455 calories-per-kilogram. Cooking fish also yields a small amount of [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md).

Cooking Salmon improves the [Cooking Skill](./Skills.md#Cooking) and requires a lit fire and 10 minutes. Using a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) reduces cooking time by 25%. Cooked food on an active fire for too long will burn (twice its 'Ready' cooking time), destroying the item and damaging a Cooking Pot if used.

**Coho Salmon (Raw)** is a raw [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.

**Coho salmon** are hefty saltwater fish found sparsely under the ice off the coast. They can be caught by [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) using [fishing tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) or found by [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md). Fresh salmon can be between 2.8 and 5.5 kg raw.
At 0% condition food disappears if inside of a container, but not outside of containers or in the player's inventory.

Using salmon on a lit [fire](./Fire.md) yields Cooked Salmon. Cooked fish increases its condition by 50%, decays 4 times slower than raw meat, and has a reduced chance of [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) over raw meat, while decreasing its weight by 35%. Cooked salmon's energy density is 455 calories-per-kilogram. Cooking fish also yields a small amount of [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md).

Cooking Salmon improves the [cooking skill](./Skills.md#Cooking) and requires a lit fire and 10 minutes. Using a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) reduces cooking time by 25%. Cooked food on an active fire for too long will burn (twice its 'Ready' cooking time), destroying the item and damaging a Cooking Pot if used.

![The Collectibles screen in story mode.](../assets/Collectibles.jpg)_The Collectibles screen in story mode._ **Collectibles** are special items that can be collected but do not have any extra carry-weight. Once found, collectibles can be 'examined' at any time through the [Journal](./Journal.md) menu in the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md).

In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), collectibles come in various forms; the most common are single page notes, which can be read, as well as keys and other items, many of whom are related to various Missions or Side Missions.
- [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) - cached emails or similar electronic messages that can be found on some intact computers in the world during [Aurora](./Aurora.md) events.
- [Cairns](./Cairns.md) - Cairns are small stacks of stones with red cloths; when clicked on at close range, they will display text in tribute to some of the original supporters of _The Long Dark_.
- [Polaroids](./Polaroids.md) - Allows the player to survey a large portion of the regional map.
- [Surveyed Locations](./Map.md#Surveying) - Keeps track of locations required to unlock the [Faithful Cartographer](./Faithful%20Cartographer.md) achievement.
- [Transmitters](./Transmitters.md) - Transmitters can be repaired to help the player find [Supply Caches](./Supply%20Cache.md).
- [Mementos](./Mementos.md) - Mementos are useful hints for survivors which might lead to loot or new locations in regions.
- [Recipe Cards](./Recipe%20Cards.md) - Unlock powerful Unique Recipes for the player to craft with a [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md) or [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md).

This is the mission transcript for mission 3 [Coming Storm](./Coming%20Storm.md) of [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md).
## Locate and return the missing survivors.
[Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md): "Still some names missing from the passenger manifest. Became delirious and wandered off, maybe."

_A new addition to the entrance to the hall is present, an [Emergency Kit](./Emergency%20Kit.md), perhaps left by Molly? Either way, Astrid takes the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) and [Flare Shells](./Flare%20Shell.md) and begins searching for supplies and the 3 missing [Crash Survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md)_

_After rescuing the 3 missing survivors, and stocking the [Storage Cupboard](./Storage%20Cupboard.md) with all the needed supplies, Astrid finds Father Thomas standing on the stage in front of a podium, overlooking his flock._

[Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md): "Thank you for your efforts. You have likely saved the lives of all these people. They now have a fighting chance to last through this storm. You have done God's work here and He will forever look favourably upon you."
Astrid: "Thank you, Father. Do you think while looking favourably on me, He could also help me find a way out of here?"
Father Thomas: "As I said, the usual paths are blocked. But, the blizzard...it may have displaced enough snow to..."
Astrid: "I'll take my chances. I really need to get to Perseverance Mills. If things are this bad here, they'll be worse... Look, I just need to get there. Can you help me?"

Father Thomas: "An entrance to the old coal mine. If the blizzard moved enough snow, you might be able to get in there. It passes through the mountain."

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _Father Thomas puts his glasses back on_
Father Thomas: "After that, you'll find the highway - it follows the coastline. Follow the highway and, god-willing, you'll get to Perseverance Mills. Here...I'll draw it on your map for you..."

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _Astrid hands him a map_

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _He draws on the map and hands it back to her_
Father Thomas: "My thanks to you, my child. And if you'll permit an old priest an indulgence. I'd like to share some wisdom with you."
Father Thomas: "I don't say this as an attempt to sway your thinking or help you find faith. But find something...someone...to help with your burden. Otherwise, it will consume you."
Astrid: "Look around you, Father. I think the Lord may have his hands full right now. Whatever burdens I may have, they're mine to bear. And mine alone."
Astrid: "I'll keep it in mind, Father." _produces the [Rosary](./Rosary.md)_ "Here. You should take this back."

**Characters:** [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md) [Survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md)
**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**
> “**A whiteout blizzard is on the way. Find the three missing Survivors and collect enough supplies in the Hall kitchen to keep everyone alive until the storm passes.**”

**Coming Storm** is the third mission in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) must find the remaining survivors and stock supplies in the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md) to last through the blizzard.
Note The quantities above match that of the Capable Survivor [difficulty](./Wintermute.md#Difficulty). In the Hardened Survivor difficulty, the supplies required are approximately 20-25% more.
The mission begins in Community Hall and is divided into two parts: Find and return three survivors, and stock the hall kitchen in preparation for a blizzard.

There are three crash survivors in Pleasant Valley. To find a survivor, travel within the radius marked on the player's map. Once inside the radius, the player can shoot a flare into the sky with a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md). A few seconds later, the survivor will shoot a flare into the sky, alerting the player to their location. If the survivor still cannot be found, a second flare can be fired and the survivor will respond.

Each survivor is found lying next to a [campfire](./Campfire.md). This campfire will be an "infinity fire", meaning that it will never burn out. This can make it a useful place to spend the night or cook food.

Each survivor needs to be carried back to Community Hall. These survivors have the same mechanics as Gwen. For instance, they have condition (health) as well as warmth and hydration needs. Survivor condition will go down if they are attacked by [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) or if either of their needs are depleted. The player can address a survivor's warmth need by placing them near a fire or indoors, and can address their thirst need by using the "diagnose" interface to give potable water. The Survivor's condition will improve as long as their needs are met.

You can equip a pistol or marine flare while carrying a survivor on the PC version. Simply pick up the survivor, press the right mouse button to put them back down but instead of left clicking to do so, press your flare or gun hotkeys (1 or 2 respectively on the keyboard). It will select the first of that item in the list so if you want a marine flare be sure not to carry a standard red flare. If you equip a pistol you can fire and reload it while carrying. You can also equip a rifle but you won't be able to fire it unfortunately.

Inside the kitchen is a large cupboard, with a unique interface that shows the same list as the journal. Items placed in the cupboard will be noted in the progress towards the needed amount. Items can be added and removed from the cupboard at will until all of the needed quantities are inserted. At that point, it is no longer possible to add or remove items from the cupboard. Note, if extra quantities of a type of item are inside the cupboard at the time of completing the task, the player can no longer remove them. For that reason, it is wise to keep any extras outside the cupboard, either on the ground or in other cabinets.
- [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md) is a fairly common medical item, and can be found in first aid kits on the walls or shelves of many buildings.

- [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) is quite numerous and can be found on trees throughout Pleasant Valley. They can be crafted into [Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Wound%20Dressing.md) quite easily, as they do not require a workbench to create.

- 5 [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) can be found on a fallen tree and right next to it in the river just behind the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md), another 5 are on top of a hill when going straight from the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md) to the fishing hut at [Pensive Pond](./Pensive%20Pond.md), 4 just to the left of the boulder, behind which is the 3rd bunker, and 4 more next to the river/ice crossing (1 on a branch facing away from the road) when following the road behind the church, netting you 6 easy [old man's beard wound dressings](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Wound%20Dressing.md), this coupled with on average 3-4 antiseptics in the town itself and 1 antiseptic in the 3rd bunker should be sufficient.
- Completing the [_The Big One_](./Tall%20Tales.md) side mission will yield a 3750 calorie fish.
- A large quantity of [MREs](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md) and canned food can be found inside [Joplin's bunkers](./Joplin%27s%20Bunker%20Raid.md).
- Nearly 7000 calories can be accounted for by using [Airline Food](./Airline%20Food%20-%20Chicken.md), recovered during [Fallen Star](./Fallen%20Star.md)

- On Capable Survivor, there is a hatchet present in the building with the Church Artifact and on Hardened there is one nest to a crate just outside the [Pleasant Valley Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) outdoors barn second correction: in hardened survivor difficulty (untested in other difficulties) a hatchet can be found in the run down building near the prisoners corpse. There is also a hatchet to be found on Three Strikes farmstead, in the open barn building, opposite side to Forest Talkers cache.

- Coal boxes are adjacent to most of the residential houses in Pleasant Valley and contain [coal](./Coal.md) and [tinder plugs](./Tinder%20Plug.md). Each piece of coal contributes one hour of burntime.
- Several residential houses and the community garden in [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) contain crates which can be broken down by hand for [reclaimed wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md).
- [Sticks](./Stick.md) and branches can be found scattered on the ground in certain areas.
- [Cedar firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) and [Fir firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md) are found in most caves.
- [Joplin's third bunker](./Joplin%27s%20Bunker%20Raid.md) contains 10h of burntime of [firelogs](./Firelog.md)

- [Bandages](./Bandage.md) can easily be crafted using [cloth](./Cloth.md) harvested from [clothing](./Clothing.md) and curtains found in residential areas. Crafting bandages does not require a workbench.
- [Kerosene](./Kerosene.md) can be found as tins of [lantern fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md), or in [jerry cans](./Jerry%20Can.md). [Accelerant](./Accelerant.md) is not kerosene.
- Large quantities of kerosene can be found in jerry cans in [Joplin's bunkers](./Joplin%27s%20Bunker%20Raid.md). One jerry can is usually enough to satisfy the requirement.
- Kerosene is harvested when cooking fish. [Fish](./Ice%20Fishing.md) can be caught at [Pensive Pond](./Pensive%20Pond.md).
- [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md) can be scavenged from first aid kits, and are quite abundant and lightweight.
- [Prepared reishi mushrooms](./Prepared%20Reishi%20Mushrooms.md) can be crafted using [reishi mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) found on tree stumps throughout the region.
- Several [distress pistols](./Distress%20Pistol.md) can be found in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md):
- [Flare shells](./Flare%20Shell.md) can be found at the aforementioned locations, as well as at [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) and near crash survivors.

**Community Hall** is a building at [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) within [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md). It is a major location within [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).

Community Hall is the largest building in [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md). The building contains a kitchen with a [Stove](./Stove.md), mess hall with a [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md), bathroom with a [Toilet](./Toilet.md), and a small office. Next to the back entrance is one of the [Radios](./Trader.md#Radio_Locations) necessary to contact the Trader (if enabled). The nearest work bench is at the [Pleasant Valley Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md), but it can be disassembled and [rebuilt](./Work%20Bench.md) in the Community Hall using [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md).

It is a perfect location for a [Safe House](./Safehouse.md), as it contains a 6-slot Stove, [Beds](./Bed.md), several [Crossroads House](./Crossroads%20House.md) to loot nearby, and the 200.00kg [Storage Cupboard](./Storage%20Cupboard.md), the largest container in the game.
**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**
In Episode 3, the Community Hall is inhabited by the plane crash survivors and overseen by [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md).

Although there are many items in the building that can normally be broken down or interacted with to harvest resources (e.g., ripping curtains for [cloth](./Cloth.md)), these actions are not available as options inside the Community Hall.
The fireplace, however, is an "infinity fire," meaning that it never burns out. This makes it a useful place to boil [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), cook, and refill the warmth need.

![A computer during the aurora](../assets/Maxresdefault.png)_A computer during the aurora_ **Computers** are stationary objects in The Long Dark. Un-interactable under normal circumstances, but during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) their display will sometimes illuminate to show the contents of a recently closed log/diary, as a nod to the civilization on Great Bear before the lights.

While traveling in your game, you might stumble upon a laptop or desktop computer. Although sometimes the position that they've been placed in is rather annoying, and they cannot be moved, picked up, or used in any way unless an aurora is active,

Laptops and computers are still a valid piece of backstory to the Long Dark, and can be used to collect [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) during an aurora. They also play a large role in the [Archivist](./Archivist.md) challenge.

During an Aurora, some of these computers will flash on to display a message, called a Buffer Memories. Each computer that _will_turn on in the game has at least three buffer memories, and computers that are active during an aurora will slowly cycle through the list, so if you wait long enough you might be able to catch more than one buffer memory on the same computer. Don't be fooled though - not all computers turn on. Generally if you've found a computer that didn't turn on during the Aurora, chances are there's another one in the building that did.

This 7 story tall building is enormous from both the inside and outside. From the top, the player can observe the entire surrounding area.
Each floor is quite tall with steel beams spanning across the ceiling. On the ground are countless different pieces of machinery and objects.

- Ground floor: Delivery area with toolboxes and metal containers to loot. There are also coal pieces next to the minecart. On this floor are the two exits leading to the mine pit area. [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md) may spawn behind a large sheet of corrugated metal in a back corner of the room.
- Second floor: Here are the concentrator machines located. Lockers a few containers and a control room to loot.
- Third floor: The walkways of the concentrators. Basically no loot except a few rounds of rifle ammo.

- Fifth floor: Conveyor chutes. A hopper machine at the opposite end of the floor leads onto a series of pipes below (where a backpack can be spotted laying from above), when these are followed they lead onto a walkway from which an otherwise inaccessible control room can be entered, this secret room may contain high-tier loot including a [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md), Ammo, Clothing, Emergency Stim and the [Miner's Flashlight](./Miner%27s%20Flashlight.md).
- Sixth floor: Minecart entrance from the mountain (exit to the mountainside mine entrance). Little amount of loot. [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) spawn on a work table on this floor.

- Seventh floor: Office area with a kitchen and a storage room where the [Respirator](./Respirator.md) is located. Has [Food And Drinks](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), [Bag of Salt](./Salt%20%28Bag%29.md), stored water container, a [Safe](./Safe.md), a [Medical Locker](./Medical%20Locker.md), [Clothing](./Clothing.md), etc.

It is important to note that all the floors are abundant in items that can be broken down ([Crates](./Crate.md), [Cardboard boxes](./Cardboard%20Box.md)) and have debris scattered on the floor ([Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md), [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md)). [Coal](./Coal.md) can also be found scattered around.
There are no beds in the building, but it is possible to sleep in the car on the ground floor.
There are also no indoor fireplaces. The best option is to cook outside at the delivery area entrances or at the exit to the mountain on the sixth floor.
The Concentrator is based off of the [Britannia Mine Museum](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Mine_Museum) in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

**Condensed Milk** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.
Consuming Condensed Milk replenishes a moderate amount of thirst and large amount of calories. It may also be warmed by a [fire](./Fire.md) to grant the benefit [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md).

Like other [canned](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) foods, Condensed Milk may be opened with a [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md) or [bladed tool](./Tools.md), or smashed open (with no tool) but spilling some of its contents. If opened with a tool, a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) is received after consuming the contents.

Condensed Milk is relatively rare, but may be found inside homes, usually in cupboards or on shelfs. It is essentially an upgraded [Pinnacle Peaches](./Pinnacle%20Peaches.md), offering a similar hydration and more calories per weight.
Contrary to its in-game description, Condensed Milk [spoils](./Decay.md) quickly compared to other processed food.
- Condensed milk is packaged as a product called _Little Cow: Condensed Milk_ with a picture of a cow, fittingly.

![Condition icon](../assets/Condition_icon.png) **Condition** is a player statistic that represents health as the total amount of damage that can be taken before dying. Condition can be lost immediately through Injuries, indirectly through [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md), or through deficiencies in [Needs](./Needs.md).

When the player falls below 10% condition, the display becomes blurred and begins to sway, with visibility decreased and sound muffled except for the sound of a heartbeat. As condition drops lower and lower, these effects are made more and more pronounced. Movement is still possible at a normal rate, but can be more challenging as the survivor will stagger around uncontrollably even when crouched.

![Condition](../assets/Condition.png) Injuries instantly subtract a percentage of the player's condition. Incidents such as a short fall or a [Laceration](./Laceration.md) from a struggle with a [Wolf](./Wolf.md) can cause minor to moderate injuries. The associated condition loss is immediate and usually does not have any long-lasting effects beyond the condition loss itself.

On the other hand, certain [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) such as [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) or [Infections](./Infection.md) drain the player's condition until either the affliction is treated or the player slips into the Long Dark. However, a few afflictions limit the maximum condition that the player can reach. Most afflictions last until treated fully, including rest if required. After the affliction has been removed condition may be restored normally.

When a [Need](./Needs.md) reaches 0, the player begins to lose condition. Failing to satisfy needs will consistently drain condition until the need meter is brought above zero. When the player has not had sufficient rest, nutrition, or hydration, condition loss is relatively slow. If the player does not have sufficient warmth, condition loss is very rapid and requires the player to quickly react to prevent death. See below for the condition drain rates when a need reaches 0.

Some Afflictions cause Condition damage. Falling through [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md), [Bruises](./Minor%20Bruising.md) (from [Falling](./Rope%20Climbing.md)) and Lacerations (from [Struggles](./Struggle.md)) cause instant Condition damage based on [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) (or length of fall). Falls above 50m are instantly lethal on contact with the ground, as are Falls/entering a killbox (e.g. attempting to climb beneath the [Raven Falls Trestle](./Raven%20Falls%20Trestle.md) ([The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md)) or the gorge below [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) ([Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md)) see [Environmental Hazard](./Environmental%20Hazard.md)). [Torn Clothing](./Torn%20Clothing.md) affects the Condition of worn [Clothing](./Clothing.md), rather than the player's Condition.

While most Afflictions damage Condition, which can be recovered with enough rest, some Afflictions reduce or increase the overall size of the Condition bar, increasing or simply preventing Condition recovery up to a certain point.

[Well Fed](./Well%20Fed.md) is acquired after [Calorie Store](./Hunger.md) is kept above 0 calories for 3 days, and increases max carrying capacity by 5kg (11 lbs) and increases Condition by 5%, but is lost if Calorie Store reaches 0 calories. [Unburdened](./Unburdened.md) temporarily increases max Condition by 10% for 3 hours. If both Afflictions are acquired, this can make the maximum length of the Condition bar stretch to 115%, the highest it can possible be.

A "+" Plus symbol and the color blue is used to denote any condition gained when the player's Condition passes 100%. If either previously mentioned Positive Affliction is lost, extra Condition over 100% is instantly lost as well, sending the player's condition back to 100% if they were already over it.
| [Well Fed icon](../assets/Well_Fed_icon.png) | [Well Fed](./Well%20Fed.md) | Temporarily increases Condition bar by 5% |
| [Nourished icon](../assets/Nourished_icon.png) | [Nourished](./Nourished.md) | Temporarily increases Condition bar by 10% |

[Frostbite](./Frostbite.md) afflictions lower the maximum Condition bar by 10% per instance, and is the only [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) with no treatment (making its effects permanent). Up to 5 instances of Frostbite can be present at once on one body part (reducing maximum Condition by 50%), with up to 10 (11 temporarily with the extra 15% acquired from [Well Fed](./Well%20Fed.md) and [Unburdened](./Unburdened.md), until Unburdened wears off) instances resulting in death.

[Burns](./Burns.md) reduce maximum Condition by 25%, [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md) by 20% per stack of poisoning, both will not allow condition to heal above the lowered maximum threshold until at least one instance of said Afflictions is healed. [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) permanently reduces the Condition bar by 2% per day until cured (minimum of 20% per 10 days on Stalker, minimum of 40% per 20 days on Interloper.
Theoretically, the largest Condition Bar debuff would be -325% acquired from all 5 body parts having 5 instances of Frostbite, plus one instance of either Burns or Chemical Poisoning.

| [Intestinal Parasites icon](../assets/Intestinal_Parasites_icon.png) | [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) | Permanently reduces max Condition bar by 2% daily until cured |
Condition normally restores to 100% but can be limited to less by certain [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md). Players can restore lost condition using four different methods.

[Sleep](./Sleep.md) is the most common method of restoring condition. All four needs must be met for the player to restore condition during sleep. The rate of return is dependent on the bed used and the number of hours slept, with longer periods granting higher returns. [Cup of Herbal Tea](./Cup%20of%20Herbal%20Tea.md) can also help the player achieve a more restful sleep. For more detailed info on this vital mechanic, have a look at the [sleep](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep?so=search#Restoring_condition) page.

Condition is restored at a rate of 25% each day, or just over 1% every hour as long as all four [Needs](./Needs.md) are above 0 and the player has no Afflictions which negatively affects condition (such as [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md)). This passive regeneration improves the player's condition while awake, but is slower than the condition recovery from sleeping.

Death occurs when the survivor's Condition reaches zero, providing a brief explanation for the cause of death:

- "YOU FADED INTO THE LONG DARK..." - typically occurs when the player dies from 1 or more Needs being empty/environmental damage (freezing to death while sleeping, or from [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md), [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md), or [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md)). Small falls that finish the player off via [Major Bruising](./Major%20Bruising.md) or [Minor Bruising](./Minor%20Bruising.md) will also trigger this. Most other deaths generate this message by default.
- "YOU BURNED TO DEATH" - standing in a lit [Campfire](./Campfire.md) or open flames found in Wintermute Episodes will generate this message when the player dies.

- "YOU DIED FROM LOSS OF BLOOD AND SHOCK FROM A (WOLF/BEAR/COUGAR) ATTACK" - displays when the last point of damage occurs from a [Wolf](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), [Bear](./Bear.md), or [Cougar](./Cougar.md) struggles. A killing bite from a passing Timberwolf or slash from Cougars will also trigger this (via [Laceration](./Laceration.md), Minor Bruising, or Major Bruising).
- "YOU DIED FROM INJURIES SUSTAINED FROM A MOOSE ATTACK" - appears after death by [Moose](./Moose.md) Struggle.

- "YOU DIED FROM (AFFLICTION)" - displays when the player dies from [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md), [Dysentery](./Dysentery.md), [Infection](./Infection.md), [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md), [Suffocation](./Suffocation.md), or [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) while awake.
- "YOU DIED FROM (AFFLICTION) WHILE SLEEPING" - Die from Blood Loss, Dysentery, Infection, Scurvy, Suffocation, or Food Poisoning while sleeping.
- "YOU DROWNED AFTER FALLING THROUGH CRACKED ICE" - occurs if the player dies while falling through [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md).
- "YOU DIED FROM DROWNING" - occurs after falling into the large moving rivers in [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) or [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md).

- "YOU DIED FROM MASSIVE INTERNAL INJURIES AFTER FALLING" - falling from an extreme height or passing through an [instant kill barrier](./Environmental%20Hazard.md#Instant_Kill_Barriers) will trigger this. Can also occur when stamina is too low and falling from a [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section.

- "THE DARKWALKER HAS DEVOURED YOU" - if the Darkwalker in [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) catches you, a cutscene will play before the player is killed and generate this message.

- "(Crash Survivor) HAS DIED FROM (Affliction)" - occurs in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) when transporting the [Crash Survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md) (Gwen, Ada, Logan, and Wade) if they die from an Affliction (Blood Loss, [Exposure](./Hypothermia.md), or [Dehydration](./Dehydrated.md)).
- "(Crash Survivor) HAS DIED FROM A WOLF ATTACK" - occurs if a Crash Survivor is killed by a [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) in Episode 3.

- "YOU DIED FROM GUNSHOT WOUNDS" - occurs when shot by [Convicts](./Convicts.md) in the [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) Yard in the mission [Donner (mission)](./Donner%20%28mission%29.md) [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md).

- "MISSON FAILED - THE CONVICTS RE-CAPTURED MACKENZIE" - occurs when Convicts break down one of the two doors down at the end of Episode 4 in the mission Donner (mission) and the player does not escape fast enough.

- If the player dies in Survival Mode, they have an option to [Cheat Death](./Cheat%20Death.md) (for 3 more extra lives) and continue their save, or chose to end their run and Die. If the later option is chosen, an option to "Save the journal" is available, which will add that save's journal statistics to the global statistics. In [Challenges](./Challenge.md) the Challenge ends in failure and must be restarted.
- In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) (Story Mode) the player has the option to restart from a prior save/autosave checkpoint upon death.
Progress towards [Feats](./Feats.md), [Achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md), and certain [Badges](./Badges.md) persists even after death.

**Conductor's Dropoff** is a location west of the [Vacant Depot](./Vacant%20Depot.md) in the [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) region. It can be found by climbing up a hill near some frozen ponds and is easily identifiable by the dirty grey snow, but the location offers nothing but a scenic vista of the eastern unplayable section of the map. Despite the location name, there are no corpses or loot dropped off at the top or bottom of the cliff. The location has no notable loot, save for some [Stones](./Stone.md) and a [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) Nest that spawns nearby.

Contemplation Bridge is one of many bridges in the region. It serves to connect the main road that runs from [Long Curve](./Long%20Curve.md) to [End of the Road](./End%20of%20the%20Road.md).
Contemplation Bridge is east of [Pleasant Valley Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md). Some [cat tail](./Cat%20Tail.md) plants can be found growing by the river bank near the bridge.

The name might refer to someone "contemplating" jumping off in an act of suicide, since there is a considerable drop from the bridge to the ground below. A less dark interpretation might be the name simply emphasizes the tranquility and a natural beauty of a pleasant spot in a once Pleasant Valley.

The **Contraband Storage** Locker is a unique [Locker](./Locker.md) found at the gate entrance to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) during [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md).

It serves as a quick way to store any items found by the player while exploring the outskirts of the region during the episode, such as food, clothing, and weapons, in order to prevent them from being permanently taken by the [Convicts](./Convicts.md) when returning to the Prison to progress the narrative.

Has an interior The **Control Tower** is building in [Field 31](./Field%2031.md) in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) Region.

The access is possible through a double door, there is no loading screen upon entering. There is no bed or other facilities. A [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) may spawn at the top of the tower on the console.

At the top floor of the building can be found the [Field 31 Operation Memo](./Field%2031%20Operation%20Memo.md) that allow the survivor to start the [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) [Tale](./Tales.md). A [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) can be repaired and provides radio coverage for the region and the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md).

As with other buildings around the airfield, there is a fair amount of furniture, boxes, etc. that can be broken down for crafting materials. Likewise, the small storage room across from the entrance double doors may contain a little bit of loot and some objects that can be broken down.

The **Convenience** **Store** is the inside store found at the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md). The front and back doors to the station are both initially locked in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), and require a [Prybar](./Prybar.md) to open.

Inside the gas station, the player can find the main store floor, an office, and a bathroom. a [Bed](./Bed.md) and [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) can be found in the back office. [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), several containers, processed food items, and lots of breakable wood/metal are found all over the shop floor.

Upon meeting [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) she will suggest to [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) to visit the local gas station for supplies. 2 notes, [Orca Gas Store Notice](./Orca%20Gas%20Store%20Notice.md) and [Highway Robbery](./Highway%20Robbery.md) are found inside the station. The front door to the store will be open and will have the lights on when first found, as [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) will be found inside.

The gas station also serves as a prime example of the already dire situation of the people of Great Bear prior to the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md). Gas prices appear to have been extremely high, and, ultimately, gasoline seems to have run out entirely based on the red X's on the gas station sign. Comments from characters and notes/signs throughout the store and other buildings in town (mostly in Story mode) also suggest cash had been depleted and that even staples such as milk were hard to come by. The island seem to have suffered some of the worst effects of the wider economic crisis in _The Long Dark_ universe.

violations.context: #### _Previous Versions_

Prior to the Redux Update to Wintermute, Grey Mother and Will Mackenzie had additional dialogue over a moral dilemma around raiding the gas station in order to provide food for her. This included Grey Mother saying she misjudged Will if he does not steal from the store and instead procures food for her via other means, remarking that he "might just have what it takes to survive this winter."
If the player instead chose to steal from the store, she would express her joy over how "that Mainlander store owner finally had what was coming to him", much to Mackenzie's dismay.
Several signs around the store show just how desperate the Canadian economy was during [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md):
- The front door has a note saying "_No Cash_" and the ATM logo being crossed out and also saying in red "No Cash"

- The large sign outside near the pumps showing gasoline prices says $8.88 per gallon for regular and diesel, but is crossed out in red with a note saying "No Gas." The electric vehicle charging sign is not crossed out however

- A sign near the register counter displays currency exchange rates "$1 CAD = $0.23 USD." In Wintermute, the note [Orca Gas Store Notice](./Orca%20Gas%20Store%20Notice.md) can be found telling the store owner that store deliveries have been reduced to every quarter of the year.

Has an interior The **Conveyor Room** is a side building sandwiched between the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md) and the [Headframe Building](./Headframe%20Building.md). Its role is to bring ore to the surface and deliver it to the Concentrator via 3 conveyor belts connected between all 3 structures.

The Conveyor Room is a small building connecting to the second floor of the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md), the second floor of the [Headframe Building](./Headframe%20Building.md) and the 1st Level of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md). It also has two entrances from the outside.
Loot is scarce and can be obtained from [Lockers](./Locker.md) or from the ground. [Hacksaws](./Hacksaw.md) can also be found.

> **An escaping convict left some hidden caches to help the other convicts following him.**

To start the mission, the player must find a note at [Cook's Farm](./Cook%27s%20Farm.md) in [Blackrock Mountain](./Blackrock%20Mountain.md) region. This will add 4 points of interest on the survivors map.

- Cache 1 is located behind a stone in the "roots" of a fallen tree where the cliff face and the mountain meet above the [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md). Getting there is very easy, start at the [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md) and go towards the Mountain then along the bottom of it to the left. In survival a [Prepper cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) may spawn in this location instead.

- Cache 2 is located inside the mountain pass which leads to fools corner, in survival a rope to the creek would be there, the entrance to this pass is just after the No road cave ([aggressive wolf cave](./Blackrock%20Rumours.md)) and is actually visible on the in-game map. The cache itself is hidden behind a jagged rock on the right side of the pass.

- Cache 3 is located at the very top of the mountain above [Foreman's Clearcut](./Foreman%27s%20Clearcut.md). To reach it by follow the road, beware of a pack of timberwolves patrols here, and then take the first left steep path up the mountain. Keep more to the right of this path and at the very top on a big flat rock outcropping (more in the middle of the mountain than the edge), the cache is hidden behind one of the trees.

- Cache 4 is located at the foot of the second electrical power pole that is on the right side of the road (when going from [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md)), it´s the one visible but unreachable from the road. One way of reaching it is by going through the "tunnel/pass" and then backtracking a long way around it´s outside face, beware of a pack of timberwolves near the farm. The other way is to climb up to the previous Power pole, then climbing down a mountaineering rope (survivor must not be over-encumbered) and taking the first left up a steep path. After reaching the pole the cache should be easily visible on the right.

> “**The bad men...the bad men CAME. Took my things. Tried to take my house. Thought they were safe because Grey Mother can't see. They were wrong.**”

The **Convicts** are a group of hostile survivors on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) that appeared after the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md). They act as human antagonists for the other survivors on the Island, and were originally members of a maximum security penal colony prison.

The Convicts are former inmates that were detained at [Blackrock Federal Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) prior to the First Flare. During the event, most of the Convicts escaped their cells inside the Penitentiary, overpowering the prison personnel and brutally executing the staff outside the walls of the prison and taking the Warden [Franklin](./Franklin.md) hostage before taking over the local Blackrock region. A separate group of fifteen individuals was being carried in a [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) to the prison, but were freed after the bus crashed during the First Flare, leaving the bus in the middle of a rubble pile on the road to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) just outside of [Milton](./Milton.md).
There were 15 Convicts traveling aboard the Crashed Bus. The [Prison Transport Manifest](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md) includes the names:
Of these individuals, 4 escaped into the nearby town of Milton, including [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md), with many others dying in the bus crash and being buried under the avalanche.

The rest made their way to [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) and later [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md). At least 8 convicts made their way to Pleasant Valley; [Vachon](./Vachon.md), [Heller](./Heller.md), [Mathis](./Mathis.md), Leclerc, and 4 other dead convicts found in the mission [Blackrock (mission)](./Blackrock%20%28mission%29.md). A [Dead Prison Guard](./Dead%20Prison%20Guard.md) is found giving chase to the convicts until he was killed by a convict, with an [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) stabbed into his side, all the while carrying the [Blackrock Penitentiary Memo](./Blackrock%20Penitentiary%20Memo.md). Some time after their arrival in the region, [Molly](./Molly.md) began hunting and killing many of the convicts with her [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), causing the remaining Convicts to scatter and leave the region.

An unknown quantity of unnamed convicts appear inside the Blackrock Prison. They are alive and many of them appear near the end of the episode operating spotlights and shooting at Will Mackenzie. They have no real interaction with Mackenzie, only appearing in cutscenes or as dead bodies after the Prison explosion. They currently rally behind Mathis as he attempts to free his son [Donner](./Donner.md) from the prison, and will likely follow him if he ever leaves the Prison behind to conquer Great Bear Island.

Some inmates managed to escape, though the [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) of a unnamed convict can be seen only a few meters from the bus. Several other surviving convicts travelled to the nearby town of [Milton](./Milton.md), taking most of its residents hostage. Some of the convicts, including [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md), locked the remaining Milton residents inside the schoolhouse; an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) event then ignited a fire within the schoolhouse. Dr. [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) attempted to rescue the trapped townsfolk, but the inmates prevented her from doing so. Thus, the town's entire population, except for Grey Mother, died in the fire. Astrid was injured during the struggle, but managed to stab Hobbs and escape to Pleasant Valley through the Bus.

A bald convict was found dead near [Grey Mother's House](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) by [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). Judging by the blood trail, he attempted to enter [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md)'s home and was shot, fatally wounding him. Hobbs, who had stolen a safety box belonging to Gray Mother, was later found by Will, mortally wounded in [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md). After explaining to him what they did to the local residents, Will chose to either leave or execute him.

A single convict is found dead near the [River (Southern Access)](./River%20%28Southern%20Access%29.md) carrying the [Convict Journal Entry](./Convict%20Journal%20Entry.md) and may have come from the Crashed Prison Bus. A resident of Milton whom managed to escape the town into [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) mentions evading a convict by falling off a cliff, as written in the [Blood Soaked Note](./Blood%20Soaked%20Note.md).

In [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), it is revealed that most of the convicts from the crashed bus managed to escape into Pleasant Valley through the other side of the tunnel in Milton, with Astrid having been the last to make it through before the tunnel fully collapsed. [Molly](./Molly.md) begins hunting several of them down after Astrid awakens, with the doctor later finding their corpses with arrows shot through them. [Vachon](./Vachon.md) would later mention in Episode 4 that Leclerc was found with an arrow through the chest. It is implied that Mathis, Vachon, and Heller escaped into [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) by the time Astrid woke up, and encountered Mackenzie.

At the end of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), Will is attacked and captured in [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) by [Mathis](./Mathis.md), who had escaped the bus and made his way through the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) into the Dam. In [Episode 4: Fury, then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), Will manages to escape from Mathis and two other convicts: [Heller](./Heller.md) and [Vachon](./Vachon.md). He is recaptured and imprisoned, however, and awakens inside Blackrock Prison. He is then forced to assist the Convicts under the threat of death: both to his own life and that of the prison warden [Franklin](./Franklin.md). At the end of the episode, an explosion destroys much of the prison, giving Will a chance to escape. During the ending cutscene, Will is cornered inside the power plant by Mathis, Heller, Vachon, and two other unnamed convicts. The episode ends with Will jumping into the river that runs through the plant to escape the convict gang.
- The names of prisoners on the Prisoner Manifest are names of the Hinterland Dev Team.

- The only other minor character convict who's acknowledged is Leclerc. Heller mentions having gone out looking for him and Vachon says he was found dead with an arrow in his chest, likely Molly's work.
- Of the 4 main convicts, Mathis and Hobbs are the only prisoners to have their name printed on their orange Jumpsuit, with Vachon and Heller missing theirs.

**Cooked Potato** is a cooked [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

**Cooked Potato** is obtained by placing a [Potato](./Potato.md) upon a cooking slot of a lit [fire](./Fire.md) for 60 minutes, and increases its condition by 50%. Collecting a finished one improves the [cooking skill](./Cooking.md).
Using a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) or [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md) reduces cooking time by 25% and increases burn time by 50%.
Cooked food left on an active fire for too long will burn, after another 80% of "Ready" time (for the potato after 40 minutes), destroying the item and damaging a Cooking Pot/Skillet if used.

**Cooking Oil** is an inedible [ingredient](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

The basic use for Cooking Oil is creation of various recipes. They are often found inside kitchens and pantries out in the open. Also it can be crafted via the Cooking menu (Skill Level 1) from Animal Fat that drops while harvesting carcasses.
Cooking Oil is composed of 0.75 L of Oil, and each recipe that requires it needs 0.05 L of Cooking Oil, making 1 bottle useful for 15 recipes.

As with other ingredients stored in a container (such as [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) and [Water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md)) the glass jar the oil is contained in generates automatically when Cooking Oil is produced, and disappears when the oil is used up. It is not possible to divide Cooking Oil into smaller portions.
Cooking Oil was originally measured in Spoonfuls, with one Cooking Oil having 15 Spoonfuls. This measurement changed to just weight in a subsequent update.

A **Cooking Pot** is a tool primarily used for melting snow, boiling water, and [Cooking](./Cooking.md) food. A cooking pot will reduce the amount of time required for food inside it to cook by **20%** and will allow for the creation of broths, stews, and porridges that cannot be cooked directly by the fire.

A cooking pot can melt or boil up to 2.00 liters of snow or water at a time. The amount of time required to melt snow per liter does decrease a bit when using a Cooking Pot, compared to a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md).
A Cooking Pot will degrade by **5%** if its contents are burned or boiled dry. The Cooking Pot will not degrade in any other circumstances.
It can also be repaired with [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md) or [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) for 1 unit of Scrap Metal.
Cooking Pots typically spawn in houses and buildings with kitchens, especially kitchens with wood-burning cooking stoves.
- Large chamber of northern ice cave system, near the entrance closest to [Mammoth Falls](./Mammoth%20Falls.md)
- Potential [snow shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md) campsite in between [Lonely Cave](./Lonely%20Cave.md), [Cloudtop Falls](./Cloudtop%20Falls.md), and [Stairsteps Lake](./Stairsteps%20Lake.md)
- [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) and the other houses in Milton
- [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) in the room where the [Memento](./Mementos.md) is found
- [Station Bunkhouse](./Station%20Bunkhouse.md) on the table near the potbelly stove

It is not guaranteed that every region will spawn a Cooking Pot. Some regions, like [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) and [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), may have no Cooking Pots in a given game.

A **Cooking Skillet** is a tool primarily used for melting snow, boiling water, and cooking food. They were introduced in the Part 3: Frontier Comforts update for players who purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion, and are used for cooking advanced food Recipes.

A cooking skillet can hold up to 1.00 liters of liquid for melting snow or boiling water. This makes it inferior in this respect to the [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) given it weighs the same. However, it does allow more recipes to be cooked compared to the pot.

A cooking skillet will degrade by 5% if its contents are burned or boiled dry. The cooking skillet will not degrade in any other circumstances. If damaged, it can be repaired in 60 minutes with 1 unit of [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) with [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md), increasing the item's condition by 30%. Alternatively, a cooking skillet can be harvested in 90 minutes for 1 unit of Scrap Metal with a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md).

Skillets typically spawn in houses or buildings with kitchens, especially kitchens with wood-burning cooking stoves (e.g., in [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) and the [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md)).
- [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) and the other houses in Milton
- [Cabin (Sundered Pass)](./Cabin%20%28Sundered%20Pass%29.md), lower level in the kitchen area

It is not guaranteed that every region will contain a skillet. Some regions, like [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) and [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), may have no skillets in a given game.

**Cooking** is a Survival [Skill](./Skills.md) that is used to prepare or craft [Food and Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md). Cooking offers several benefits, including increasing the condition of raw food and reducing the risk of [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md). There are many different types of food in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, each providing different amounts of calories and special buffs and debuffs only available by using this Skill. Cooking also has a larger variety of training options than any other Skill, due to the number of food types and drinks that can be cooked.

![old menu](../assets/Cooking_menu.png)_old menu_ Cooking is one of the easiest skills to train in _The Long Dark_, as players can increase their skill by cooking any food or drink item. There are dozens of options for fish, meat, harvestable plants, tradeable cooking ingredients and a vast number of dishes and drinks that the player can craft; each of these options grants cooking experience, making Cooking as a skill the easiest to level up in the game. For players who own the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC especially, the update "Frontier Comforts" added an entire cooking system with new dishes, recipe cards that can be collected throughout Great Bear and new ingredients all around the island..

Players can cook food and drinks on any [Fire](./Fire.md) using the one-to-six possible cooking slots depending on the type of fire. There is no difference between cooking over a [Campfire](./Fire.md#Campfire) and [contained fire](./Fire.md#Contained_fires) (Campfire, Rim Grill, Pot Belly, Fire Barrel, etc.).

Players can then select the food item, drink or cooking container from the radial menu or inventory and place it next to the fire in a designated cooking slot. When using a cooking tool, the player can "use" the placed [can](./Can.md), [cooking pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) or [skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md) to select which food or drink to cook.
Players need a Fire before they can start cooking, and certain pieces of equipment can be used to assist with cooking.
