This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.
> “**Recipes and new ingredients open a range of possibilities for food preparations that can offer different gameplay effects.**”

Enhanced Cooking Recipes were added in the Part 3: Frontier Comforts update, available for players who purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) Expansion. Cooking Recipes have a different classification from normal cooking:

- They require multiple ingredients to create rather than simply cooking one item, and tend to take longer to prepare than normal foods, but can be worth the effort to create as they can provide unique benefits that can increase/decrease Afflictions.
- Enhanced Recipes require additional time to be "prepared" rather than simple placing them in a container and cooking them.
- Unlike regular cooking, Enhanced Cooking requires fresh ingredients, I.E. non-Ruined food items, to prepare recipes.
- Some recipes require the player to reach a certain Cooking skill level before the player is allowed to make them.

There are currently 24 recipes in total, separated into 3 categories via container used to prepare them. A full list can be found in the unique Recipe Book menu of the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) (Cooking Pot icon).

- 13 Unique Recipes can be found on [Recipe Cards](./Recipe%20Cards.md) that are spread out all over Great Bear and must be collected by the player first before they appear in the Cooking Recipe menu. Once the Recipe Card is obtained, it can be identified in the Cooking Recipe menu via a![Unique Recipe Star icon](../assets/Unique_Recipe_Star_icon.png)white star. These recipes require the most ingredients to make and the highest Cooking Skill Levels, but they offer the greatest Affliction boosts. Unique Recipe Cards can be tracked in the Collectibles menu of the [Journal](./Journal.md).

All Recipes require the player to "prepare" the ingredients before they are placed in a container. This is different from cooking non-recipe foods, as the player would normally place them in a container and immediately begin cooking.

- Only fresh Ingredients can be used; Ruined 0% Condition items cannot be cooked with, unlike cooking 0% meat/canned goods. The menu will say you have the materials but will refuse to let you use them if they are Ruined (this can be bugged and the game will occasionally let you use them anyway).

- Keep in mind that once the player commits to cooking a recipe in a container, 11-20 minutes always passes (a "preparing" message appears, accompanied by chopping, scrapping and cooking sound effects while time acceleration occurs. This can be cancelled at any time.) before said item appears in the container and starts cooking (time resumes normally after the "preparing" stage).

- This can potentially result in the fire going out while preparing, requiring it to be relit again and the "preparing" section started again. Always place extra fuel in the fire when creating recipes.
- Once a Recipe is finished being prepared, an uncooked version of it will appear on the fire (Cooking Experience is gained from preparing successfully).

- If an unfinished/uncooked Recipe is removed from the fire container before it is finished cooking, a warning will appear asking if the player wishes to discard the item. Removing the item in this state will permanently remove it from the game world, wasting cooking ingredients.

Ingredients are used solely for recipes and most cannot be consumed on their own (except for Carrots). You can find these Ingredients as regular loot all around the island or you can trade for them with the Trader; in the late-game, most places have been looted by the player and most Ingredients have reached 0% Condition, making Trading an almost mandatory step if a player wants to keep engaging with the Cooking system at this stage.

If a food item is picked up before cooking is complete, it will still be raw, and will require the full cooking process to start over. Food items can be moved (by right-clicking) between cooking spots without losing the progress. A fire that briefly goes out pauses the cooking process; if the fire is quickly relit, cooking will resume without an additional time penalty.

Food left on an active Fire after it finishes cooking will burn into inedible food after a set amount of time. Burnt food items are unusable and will disappear when picked up. Recycled Cans, Cooking Pots and Skillets will degrade by 5% if food is burnt. Food cooked in a Cooking Pot or Skillet will take 50% longer to burn compared to food cooked directly by the fire or in a recycled can.
- Cooking any food, drink, or recipe mentioned above and then removing them from the fire before they burn (1 skill point)
- This excludes melting and boiling water, or warming up food that has already been cooked.

- A limited increase can be obtained from the [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) _[Wilderness Kitchen](./Wilderness%20Kitchen.md)_, which allows players to increase their cooking by 10 skill points with 5 hours of research (or 20 skill points with the Book Smarts [Feat](./Feats.md) and a 20% reduction in Research time with the Settled Mind Feat).

Skill increases by 1 point per item cooked (or prepared) - regardless of its weight or for how long it cooked. _(E.g., cooking a 100 mg morsel of Rabbit in a Cooking Pot for 3 minutes results in the same increase as cooking 1 kg of Moose Meat on a bare campfire stone for 1.5 hours!)_

Has an interior **Cooper's Blind** is a location found in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md). The bar is owned and run by [Cooper](./Cooper.md), and serves as one of the few explorable locations of the town.

The bar contains an outside patio on the ground and first floor. There are 2 entrances to the bar, in front of the building and the upper back side. A 3rd entrance leads to the bar/kitchen area itself, but cannot be entered.

The first floor has many seating booths, a bath room, a fireplace with a large wooden bear carving, a piano, and the bar. An ATM and 2 dart boards can also be found near the front entrance. A set of stairs leads to the upper area overlooking the main floor, and leads to an office and a storage room.

[Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) arrives at the bar while searching for the town's local doctor, Dr. Larsen. She meets Cooper and several of the town's residents inside, currently waiting out a quarantine placed by Dr. Larsen. Cooper updates Astrid on the town's current problems before giving her a key to the nearby Medical Clinic.

Astrid eventually returns to the bar after finding out the truth regarding the several missing people, and warns everyone that they need to evacuate. before they can, [Mathis](./Mathis.md) and his Convicts show up and hold everyone hostage in the bar, eventually threatening to burn it down. The residents of the town eventually flee the town, but the bar remains as one of the few buildings not burned down in the town.

**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**

**Cooper** is a minor character that appears in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).
Cooper wears a green toque and an apron sporting the Cooper's Blind logo. He wears a green inner shirt and a blue outer jacket.

A resident of [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), Cooper is the barkeep and owner of [Cooper's Blind](./Cooper%27s%20Blind.md). Not much is known about his past, but he presents himself as an easy going fellow that wishes to keep the Bar Patrons warm and fed during the town's quarantine; as well as give out booze to the thirsty whenever they ask.

> “**Every day, another "refugee" from the cold, or three, showing up and camping out here at the bar... \[\] I'm happy to be able to help. As long as there's wood for the fireplace and booze for the patrons, that is.**”

[Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) is instructed by [Jane Yang](./Jane%20Yang.md) to look for the local town doctor, and visits Cooper's Blind. Inside, she meets Cooper standing by the bar and makes conversation with him. Cooper gives Astrid the [Brass Key](./Brass%20Key.md) to [Dr Larsen's Clinic](./Medical%20Clinic.md).

Cooper reappears still holed up inside Cooper's Blind. He offers Astrid a whiskey to warm her up since she has been out in the cold for so long after sundown, which she accepts. Cooper then listens to Astrid's pleas for the townsfolk to evacuate Perseverance Mills before Jane Yang appears to attempt to calm the doctor down and prevent her from alarming the other residents of the town. [Mathis](./Mathis.md) appears shortly thereafter and his gang of [Convicts](./Convicts.md) take over the town.

Cooper does not make any other appearance after this point, but is presumed to have been taken hostage by the Convicts inside his bar. He is also not seen at the end of the episode, but it can be inferred that he escaped the town and is now residing in the bunker underneath the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md), along with the other town survivors.

A **Corpse** (sometimes labeled as just [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md)) are the remains of seemingly recently deceased people. Corpses differ slightly from a Frozen Corpse as they have less snow covered on their bodies, but their skin is a dark purple/black color from severe frostbite. They are usually found outdoors, although some can be found indoors, in caves, or crushed under structures or other landmarks.

Corpses can be searched for modest loot. Tools or weapons can often be found nearby. Sometimes, corpses will spawn with items in-hand. [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) also can spawn near corpses, and [Crows](./Crow.md) can be spotted circling above some spawned corpses.

The causes of death and identities of frozen corpses are almost universally a mystery, although the Hinterland Forums community has given some of these corpses [unofficial backstories](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/38131-tsd-the-sitting-dead/). The bodies also do not defrost, regardless of surrounding temperature, and they are essentially useless and inert once looted (although the can technically serve as storage containers, albeit macabre ones).
Occasionally in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), a [Dead Prison Guard](./Dead%20Prison%20Guard.md) or dead Convict can be found.

A **Cougar Claw Knife** is a [Tool](./Tools.md) that can be crafted at a [Forge](./Forge.md) after finding and killing the elusive and lethal [Cougar](./Cougar.md) for its [Cougar Claw](./Cougar%20Claw.md).

The Cougar Claw Knife is functionally similar to the [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), but must be [Forged](./Forge.md) with a [Cougar Claw](./Cougar%20Claw.md); It weighs 0.10kg more and harvests meat from animal carcasses around 10% faster; and harvests Hides around 33% faster if compared to the Improvised Knife. It is noticeably faster at filling up the struggle bar compared to the hunting knife and causes wolves to bleed out slightly sooner afterwards, although its chances to cause an early-flee remain tied with the other knives (see: [Wildlife Struggles](./Struggle.md)).

Cougar Claw Knives are particularly useful on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) and [Misery](./Misery.md), where Hunting Knives never spawn, or in [Custom](./Custom.md) sandboxes with Loot Frequency set to "Low".
- Has faster unfrozen/frozen meat harvesting speed than Hunting knife ([Survival Knife](./Survival%20Knife.md) has faster frozen meat harvesting times).

Harvesting the knife gives 1 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) and 1 Cougar Claw after 50 minutes. This can allow it to be reforged if the player does not wish to hunt more Cougars for claws, provided that they have a Forge and materials on hand to make a new one.

The knife can be repaired using a [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md) and the [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) skill, restoring 3% condition to the tool (5% if Sharpening level is high enough) and using 5% condition on the Whetstone. The [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) or [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) may repair a non-ruined knife to 100% condition for one scrap metal, during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md).

A **Cougar Hide Wrap** is a craftable [Clothing](./Clothing.md) worn on the outer layer of the head.
Cougar Hide Wraps are crafted using [Cured Cougar Hide](./Cured%20Cougar%20Hide.md). Only 1 Cougar Hide Wrap can be worn at a time, specifically in the outer head slot.

It is the warmest head item in the game by a wide margin, beating the [Wolfskin Hat](./Wolfskin%20Hat.md) (the warmest hat in the game) by 1 degree in Warmth bonus and 2 degrees in windproofing, and tied for the heaviest (again with the Wolfskin Hat) at 1.00kg. Additionally the Cougar Hide Wrap is slightly more waterproof, protective, and decays slower than other headgear.

A Cougar Hide Wrap can be harvested and re-crafted to restore its condition, recycling a Cured Cougar Hide at the cost of time and other resources (similar to a [Moose-Hide Cloak](./Moose-Hide%20Cloak.md)).
Acquiring a [Fresh Cougar Hide](./Fresh%20Cougar%20Hide.md) to cure and craft the wrap may prove challenging since it involves facing against one of Great Bear Island's deadliest predators.

A **Cougar Quarter** is a section harvested from a [Cougar](./Cougar.md). You can obtain Cougar quarters by _quartering_ a [Cougar Carcass](./Cougar%20Carcass.md). To quarter an animal, you have to go into the harvest menu, then select the quartering action. For a Cougar, this will always take 2 hours. You can only quarter a Cougar if its less than 50% frozen.

After quartering, the carcass will despawn, leaving behind 2 quarters, as well as its [Fresh Gut](./Fresh%20Gut.md) and [Fresh Cougar Hide](./Fresh%20Cougar%20Hide.md). It will also leave behind the Cougar's legs and blood, but this cannot be picked up, and it will soon despawn.

Unlike directly harvesting a fresh carcass' meat, you will still need to harvest a quarter for its meat. 50% of the quarters total weight will be turned into usable [Cougar Meat (Raw)](./Cougar%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md). Any remaining raw meat left inside the bag will be lost if the Quarter's Condition reaches 0%, with bags spoiling within 1 day of harvesting.

This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.
> “**A deadly hunter, the Cougar stalks the rocky crags and ravines around Great Bear and may be your greatest nemesis yet.**”

The **Cougar** is a [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) predator in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. They were initially added in Part 5 of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC (June 2024) but were promptly removed to be reworked and re-released in Part 6 (Dec 2024).

They only appear in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), as well as [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of Wintermute during the [High Energy](./High%20Energy.md) mission, and do not appear in [Challenges](./Challenge.md). They can be toggled on or off in pre-existing saves or tweaked in [Custom](./Custom.md) Mode.

Cougars are territorial "alpha-predators" and pose a serious threat on all Survival Mode difficulties (except [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md), where they are disabled). They predominantly inhabit the outer rims of [Regions](./Region.md) and possess a large detection range (particularly on [Stalker](./Stalker.md)). Co-existence with Cougars is possible by avoiding areas they inhabit and refraining from hunting them. The Cougar reacts to player behavior and will increase its territory size, the number of territories and the number of Cougars in a single region based on how the player interacts with it.

Cougars have a grace period where they do not appear in the game world for some time when first enabled. The grace period varies in each difficulty by a substantial amount. Once the grace period is over, a cutscene will play to inform the player Cougars are now present in the world. The cutscene will only be played once per save file.

Cougar Territory is indicated to the player by a variety of markings, sounds and signs that are specific to the Cougar. Simply avoiding the territory entirely will almost guarantee a player will never encounter a Cougar, which is made even easier by the fact that a Cougar-specific icon automatically appears on any given region map as soon as the player enters the area, as long as the cutscene has already been played. In the case of a completely blank map, a floating Cougar icon will appear when the player opens the map.

Like the Moose, the Cougar does not bleed out and typically requires multiple rounds of ammunition or arrows being shot to go down. It is however possible, albeit rare, to down a Cougar with a single, lucky critical shot to the head, neck or torso. The Cougar is very sturdy and has the highest detection range of any animal, with its line of sight being as high as 300 meters away from the player's position (line of sight detection radius increases with difficulty). Cougars do not typically leave their Territory unless the player's [Scent](./Scent.md) is high. This commonly occurs if multiple Cougar Territories are active and the player is carrying meat from hunted animals around.

Increasing aggression on behalf of the player will be the only factor in how often a player encounters Cougars and how easy it will be to avoid them. Cougars are a particularly tough predator, requiring multiple [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) shots or [Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) even at the highest [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) or [Archery](./Archery.md) skill levels and they do not bleed out. Like other predators, they become exponentially more dangerous during the [Aurora](./Aurora.md).

> “**The most deadly and ferocious predator you will encounter in The Long Dark. The Cougar's relentless stalking can be mitigated, but only for a time. Choose wisely. Disable if you are unready to be stalked by this predator in your game.**”

New and existing survival sandboxes have the choice to include Cougars in their game. Cougars will not appear if the option is disabled when starting a sandbox (the Cougar Hide Wrap Blueprint will also be removed from the crafting menu).
The toggle to disable Cougars is not present on [Misery](./Misery.md), where Cougars are enabled by default.
Cougars are disabled on [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md), so the toggle is not present (unless enabled in [Custom](./Custom.md)).
Killing a Cougar will produce a [Cougar Carcass](./Cougar%20Carcass.md) which can be harvested for the following items:

True to their title as a "super predator," a Cougar's behaviour is a combination of the many traits belonging to other dangerous wildlife on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), with its own specific behaviours as well.
- A Cougar's basic movements and stances are similar to [Wolves](./Wolf.md)/[Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md).
- They have two attack types, a "hit and run" Swipe and Struggles, while also dodging and keeping their distance from the player, similar to [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md).
- They are considerably sturdier than other wildlife and their senses (particularly sight and smell) are heightened, much like [Bears](./Bear.md).

- They are often heard from their vocalizations long before they are encountered and have their own unique warning music when they are close, similar to the [Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md).

- **Territory Patrol**: Cougars will patrol a set area of a region on the map marked as Cougar Territory, usually located in a mountainous location. Their vocalizations can be heard a considerable distance before the player happens upon them, similar to Wolves howling in the distance. Cougar Territory will also be filled with other warnings, such as bloody scratched trees or gory carcasses.

- **Initial Player Detection**: Cougars have the highest detection range of any animal, with their line of sight being as high as 300 meters away from the players position (line of sight detection radius increases with the Experience difficulty). Once a Cougar gains sight of the player, its vocalizations change and a unique danger audio track will play. The Cougar will begin slowly stalking the player until line of sight is lost. If a Cougar is very close when spotting the player, a loud audible growl is heard close by before the audio track begins playing.

- **Engaging Player**: Aiming weapons at Cougars when they are stalking the player does not cause them to charge, but missed gunshots/arrows that land too close to them will immediately cause the Cougar to begin chasing the player down. If a Cougar stalks the player for long enough without being provoked, they will charge the player, meaning they cannot be outwalked.

- **Charging Player**: The Cougar will rapidly charge and close in on the player's position, with two possible outcomes occurring. Both outcomes result in the Cougar temporarily retreating before stalking the player again:

- The Cougar is shot at close range (hit or miss) before the Cougar reaches the player. This causes the Cougar to preform a ''swiping'' glancing attack instead of a Struggle, damaging the player and knocking their weapon out of their hand to leave them defenseless.

- The Cougar successfully charges the player without being harmed and a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) ensues, causing the player to black out. The player will wake up with [Severe Lacerations](./Severe%20Lacerations.md) and some of their items from their Backpack lying on the ground. The Cougar will be seen running away to a safe distance before engaging the player again some time later.

- **Stand Ground**: If the player positions themselves on terrain that the Cougar cannot reach, they will stand their ground and growl/hiss at the player, similar to Wolves (they show no fear of aimed weapons, unlike Wolves) while swiping at the air threateningly. If shot with a firearm in this stance, they will run off for a time but will eventually return to stalking the player.
- **Fleeing**: Cougars that flee from players have a chance to lose sight of them, returning back to Territory Patrol behaviour.

- **Leaving Territory**: Cougars can leave their Territory if the player's [Scent](./Scent.md) is high. This commonly occurs if multiple Cougar Territories are active and the player is carrying meat from hunted animals around. Cougars typically return to their Territory if they lose sight of the player.
- Its walking speed is on par with Wolves while its charging speed is on par with a Bear or Moose charge. This means a player cannot outrun a charging Cougar.

- The Cougar prowls close to the ground and can quickly pivot on its feet to face the other direction, twisting its midsection to make tight turns. This makes it the fastest turning predator when it comes to charging, making it impossible to "Bear/Moose dance" by walking around a continuously charging Cougar.

- If hit from afar, the Cougar appears to always run away to a set distance before coming back, similarly to how Wolves/Moose/Bears behave when scared. If the Cougar loses sight of the player, it can go back to its basic patrolling behavior and ignore the player until further provoked.
- If the player enters an interior while being stalked, the Cougar will despawn and respawn somewhere in its Territory, like most wildlife.

- Cougars do not typically leave their Territory unless the player's [Scent](./Scent.md) is high. This commonly occurs if multiple Cougar Territories are active and the player is carrying meat from hunted animals around.

Cougars do not fear a lit [Flare](./Flare.md), [Marine Flare](./Marine%20Flare.md), [Torch](./Torch.md), or contained fire. They do however avoid a lit [Campfire](./Campfire.md) as well as the player if they stand close to one. Cougars that chase the player will circle around a lit Campfire to avoid getting close to it while attacking.
Cougars display a variety of different vocalizations as they prowl their territory, indicating behaviour changes, location or warnings.

- **Idle**: Cougars let out distant squeaks/meows when they are unaware of the player, often stopping as they meow. If close enough to the Cougar, the sound of branches snapping can sometimes be heard as they move around (this sound becomes louder the closer the Cougar is to the player). These vocalizations can be continuously heard far off in the distance and serve as an early warning to the player that they are near their Territory.

- **Detection**: Cougars begin aggressively growling in response to the player's presence in order to drive them out of their territory. Cougars that are very close to the player once they are first spotted will emit an incredibly loud growl.
- **Stalking**: If a Cougar is stalking the player, they will occasionally growl/hiss at them. The sound of branches snapping is very audible in this phase.
- **Charging**: When close enough, a Cougar gives out a series of quick high pitched snarls and growls as they aggressively charge the player.

![An Aurora Cougar](../assets/Aurora_Cougar.jpg)_An Aurora Cougar_ Like all predators, the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) will produce an Aurora version of the animal. The Aurora Cougar is a much more aggressive, less fear prone version of the Cougar.
- Aurora Cougars do not fear lit [Flares](./Flare.md), [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), or [Torches](./Torch.md).
- They also do not fear [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md), and will turn towards the player's direction and most likely charge them if one explodes.
- They are even more aggressive than normal, immediately charging after the player once they detect them regardless of the distance, rather than slowly stalking them and charging when close.
- Aurora Cougars are the only Aurora Predator that _do not fear [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) high beams_.
- They will stay away from lit [Campfires](./Campfire.md), but will still keep close by and stalk the player.

- [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md), [Deer](./Deer.md), [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), [Moose](./Moose.md): These animals immediately flee from a nearby Cougar. Strangely, Cougars will not attack Prey animals despite Deer Carcasses being found in their territory.

- [Wolf](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md): When a Cougar is nearby, Wolves will immediately flee from the area. They will keep their distance until they feel it is safe enough, at which point they will stop fleeing and revert to their normal patrolling behavior. If they pass through a Cougar's territory, Wolves will not flee unless the Cougar is in close proximity. Cougars do not attack Wolves.
- Timberwolves packs that have spotted a player will continue to hunt the player, and do not fear a nearby Cougar.

- Other Cougars: If 2 Cougar Territories are active in a region and both Cougars come across one another, they ignore each other. If both detect the player, the closest one will attack the player while the one farthest runs away (they do not take turns attacking the player like Wolves).

- Despite not appearing in the Challenge [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md), Cougars run away when the [Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) is close to them and will die once [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) reaches 100% (if spawned with console commands).

For new saves, this grace period begins immediately. For existing saves, the grace period is added concurrently to days survived. After the earliest arrival day has passed, there is a 50% chance for the Cougar to become active on each day. The Cougar is guaranteed to arrive by the last day of the arrival window.
Using Custom settings, the Cougar arrival time seems to be connected to the Cougar Spawn Chance setting as follows:

After the Cougar grace period is complete and provided the player is in a [region](./Region.md) where Cougars can spawn, a cutscene will play to alert the player. This will typically happen whenever the survivor next exits a building with a loading screen, transitions between regions or sleeps.

There are five different Cougar Arrival Cutscenes, but the backgrounds are changed based on each [region](./Region.md), and the cutscenes also reflect [weather](./Weather.md) and time of day. Dragging a [Travois](./Travois.md) can delay the cutscene until it is dropped. Likewise being in a [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md) or indoors can prevent it playing until leaving the shelter.

Once a Cougar Arrival Cinematic has played in a save, Cougars can spawn in a number of specific regions exclusively inside set Territories that they linger in. A Cougar Territory is shown as a special icon on the map that will appear as soon as the player enters the region. There is always only a single territory present, when the Cougar first begins spawning.

As a response to player behaviour and aggressiveness, the game will spawn more Cougar Territories. Engaging with, killing or damaging a Cougar in its territory will cause another Cougar to appear on the map alongside its own dedicated territory, up to a maximum of three Cougar Territories at once. Being attacked by a Cougar can also spawn more Territories. This is called the Threat Level mechanic.

Threat Levels are region specific and start at level 1. If you encounter a Cougar and engage it, the Threat Level in that region will increase. Each Threat Level spawns an additional Cougar in the region, up to a maximum of three Cougar Territories in a single region. There is a cooldown (15 minutes) to how quickly the Threat Level increases during a Cougar encounter. If you take too long to kill the Cougar, the Threat Level can go all the way up to level 3 during a single encounter.

The Threat Level of a region drops by 1 after 5 days, which means additional Cougar Territories will start despawning after 5 days, if you do not interact with any Cougar. The Threat Levels will keep diminishing every 5 days, until only one Cougar Territory is active in the map. Cougar Territories will despawn in the reverse order of appearance.

Cougar Territories begin as a relatively small part of a region, but slowly increase in size as the survivor spends more time in that region. Territory size is not indicated on the map, it will only be noticed by how far the Cougar will end up patrolling and where markings can be seen. Territory size resets back to its original size after its associated Cougar is killed.

A killed Cougar respawns after 20 days on Voyager difficulty, 15 on Stalker and 10 on Interloper, in its original territory. _Note: Cougars seem to be respawning after only 24 hours at the moment, likely due to a bug._
- Cougar Territory marking on the region [Map](./Map.md) (a section appears filled out with its own icon even if the player never [surveys](./Charcoal.md)).
- Cougar sounds (see the **Sounds** paragraph of the **Behaviour** section. You will always hear them before running into them)
- The Cougar Theme music that will begin playing when inside a 200-meter radius around the Cougar
- [Ravaged Deer Remains](./Ravaged%20Deer%20Remains.md) (an unharvestable [doe](./Deer.md) carcass with a broken neck and numerous lacerations)
- Cougar pawprints (visually similar to very large cat paws) on the same timer as all footprints and pawprints

After the difficulty-appropriate grace period and the short cutscene, Cougars may then spawn in any eligible region. Initially, the Cougar will spawn in only one location (territory) in each region. Interaction with the Cougar will cause the Threat Level to go up and spawn additional Cougar Territories within the same region, up to a total of three territories each containing a Cougar. If left alone for 5 days, an expansion territory and its Cougar will de-spawn. Only the initial territory remains when a player doesn't interact with the Cougars. Killing a Cougar does not prevent new Cougars from spawning, so killing a cougar can cause a new one to appear on the way back from the kill.

Cougars take large amounts of damage to kill. Higher [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) and [Archery](./Archery.md) skill level marginally affects the amount of damage done to a Cougar (Arrow and Bow types do effect damage output of bows, but this chart uses base [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) and [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md) as a reference).

Avoid carrying any unnecessary items that will slow the player down. Always ensure that your [Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md) is at least 5.00-10.00kg below the max carry capacity to be safe. Always ensure that the survivor is well rested to avoid low [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) and thus low [Stamina](./Stamina.md) for sprinting when a Cougar charges. Familiarize yourself with the area in and around a Cougar's Territory and learn what buildings, shelters, and other hostile wildlife are in the general area.

Always bring a high Condition [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) or [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) with plenty of high grade ammunition (20 [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md)/10 Arrows), as the Cougar does not go down easily. Consider taking a backup weapon, such as a [Revolver](./Revolver.md), in case the Cougar swipes the player's main weapon away, to not be rendered defenseless. Make sure your Clothing is in high condition and you are warm enough to avoid freezing should [Torn Clothing](./Torn%20Clothing.md) occur. Keep repair supplies handy should they become too damaged. Always begin a hunt when your [Condition](./Condition.md) is relatively high to avoid risking death. Consider avoiding hunting Cougars until your [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md)/[Archery](./Archery.md)/[Revolver Firearm](./Revolver%20Firearm.md) [Skills](./Skills.md) are at least Level 3 or above, as the accuracy and damage bonuses are more helpful.

Avoid hunting a Cougar at night or during foggy weather, as this make the player an easy target in the darkness. Heavy fog at night is possibly the worst time to hunt a Cougar, as the big cat's heightened senses far surpass the player's and makes it easier for an ambush to occur. Carrying [Scented](./Scent.md) items can be more of a burden if the Cougar finds the player early, unless the player has a specific location prepared to lure the Cougar to.
Aurora Cougars are even more deadly than usual, so great care must be taken if hunting an Aurora Cougar. It is otherwise generally advised to simply avoid an Aurora Cougar if possible.

It is generally a good idea to build up multiple [Safehouses](./Safehouse.md) filled with useful supplies in the region in case the Cougar successfully gives the player Severe Lacerations, as the player will need to recover for the next 72 hours and cannot sprint to escape danger very easily. Having the necessary supplies to hunker down while on the mend is vastly preferable than scrounging for what you need while in an emergency. Always ensure a steady supply of food, potable water, medicine, and firewood is on hand that the player can use.

Make sure to carry plenty of First Aid supplies should a Struggle occur, as a Struggle often results in 3 Blood Loss occurring and gaining Severe Lacerations. The minimum amount of supplies should always be carried or close by should a Struggle occur.

- 3-9 initial![Bandage icon](../assets/Bandage_icon.png) [Bandage](./Bandage.md) for Blood Loss. At least 9 are needed to fully heal from [Severe Lacerations](./Severe%20Lacerations.md), 2-3 for the for the Struggle, 6 for the remaining Blood Loss over the next 72 hours.

- 3-9 initial ![Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing icon](../assets/Old_Man%27s_Beard_Wound_Dressing_icon.png) [Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Wound%20Dressing.md)/ 1.00 L ![Antiseptic icon](../assets/Antiseptic_icon.png) [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md) for Infection Risk. There can be 9 Infection Risks from Severe Lacerations, 2-3 for the Struggle, 6 from the remaining Blood Loss over the next 72 hours.

- Plenty of Food,![Water (Potable) icon](../assets/Water_%28Potable%29_icon.png) [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), and ![Birch Bark Tea icon](../assets/Birch_Bark_Tea_icon.png) [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) to recover from attacks if the player needs to retreat. Recipes that restore Condition are also helpful.

- A ![Sewing Kit icon](../assets/Sewing_Kit_icon.png) [Sewing Kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md)/![Fishing Tackle icon](../assets/Fishing_Tackle_icon.png) [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) and plenty of ![Cloth icon](../assets/Cloth_icon.png) [Cloth](./Cloth.md)/![Cured Leather icon](../assets/Cured_Leather_icon.png) [Cured Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md) to repair damaged Clothing. Spare backup Clothing is also helpful.

- An ![Emergency Stim icon](../assets/Emergency_Stim_icon.png) [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) if the player is attacked and needs to run away fast (though you cannot outrun the Cougar forever).

- A ![Bedroll icon](../assets/Bedroll_icon.png) [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) of some kind in case the player ends up in a building without a bed and ![Cup of Herbal Tea icon](../assets/Cup_of_Herbal_Tea_icon.png) [Cup of Herbal Tea](./Cup%20of%20Herbal%20Tea.md) to help recover Condition while sleeping.

Cougars possess two types of attacks, a 'glancing blow' and a Cougar Struggle. Both occur when a Cougar makes physical contact with the survivor. The number of shots you've taken at the Cougar will determine, which type of attack the Cougar will use on its next charge:
- If you shoot at the Cougar _once_, it will use the Glancing Attack and it will keep using the Glancing Attack only, until you have taken more than three shots at it.
- When you attempt to shoot the Cougar _more than three times_, it will switch to the Struggle Attack on the next charge.

The shots do not have to hit, it's enough to shoot in the direction of the Cougar for the shot to register. The Cougar also needs to be close enough to charge you for the shot to register and increment the counter.

After a Cougar Struggle the shot counter is reset to zero. This means you need to get one shot in again to prevent a second Struggle. This shot counter seems to even persist if you leave the region or pass time. So if you shoot at a Cougar, then leave the region, it can be good to note down how many shots you've taken.

Glancing Attacks only occur when the player has taken 1-3 shots at the charging Cougar with a ranged weapon (e.g. [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md)). Glancing Attacks are somewhat similar to [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) "bite-and-run" attacks, where The Cougar deals damage to the player as it attacks and swipes the weapon out of the survivor's hand.

Cougar [Struggles](./Struggle.md) are an event (similar to [Bear](./Bear.md) or [Moose](./Moose.md) struggles), featuring a mauling cutscene and do not grant the option for the survivor to defend themselves.

The Cougar only uses its Struggle Attack in two cases: if it reaches the survivor before the survivor has managed to shoot at it at least once, or if the survivor has taken four or more shots at the Cougar.
- Additionally: Severe Lacerations applies 2-3 [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) and 2-3 [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md) immediately.

1. **Note**: "Severe Lacerations" affliction lasts for 72 hours and during this time your maximum Condition is limited to 50%. Severe Lacerations has a chance to periodically, i.e. every 12 hours, apply new Blood Loss and Infection Risk (requiring a [Bandage](./Bandage.md) and [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md)). This makes Time Accelerating ([Sleep](./Sleep.md), Pass Time, Crafting, Harvesting, etc.) dangerous while afflicted.
2. **Note**: Blood Loss causes 30% Condition loss per hour **and each application stacks**. This can quickly kill a survivor without enough bandages.
After a Struggle the Cougar will be running away to a safe distance before engaging the player again some time later.

A Cougar's health remains the same once damaged, and sometimes retreating is the best option when the player is severely wounded. Having a fall back plan beforehand and retreating to your Safehouse full of supplies to heal up if things don't go well is generally the best way to ensure your survival.

- In similar fashion to other animals, Cougars will stalk the player to the edge of its territory once it spots them. If a car or building is nearby, the player can lead the Cougar along until they reach it, taking up position with their weapon of choice near the door. From there, you can engage the Cougar, entering the building or car to reset the Cougar's position when it gets too close. In most instances, you are only able to get 1 shot off before the Cougar closes the distance, so caution is advised.

- If the player happens to have a [Ballistic Vest](./Ballistic%20Vest.md) or any high protection clothing on hand (above 50% protection is preferable), you'll be able to greatly reduce the damage taken by the Cougar's glancing blows.

- If the player can reach high ground inaccessible to the Cougar (such as the edge of a rock or a fallen tree), the Cougar's pathfinding will get confused and open up the opportunity for an easy kill.

- Unlike all other animals, the Cougar seems to have no fear of distress pistol shots. Distress pistol damage on Cougar is negligible; it would take tens of flare shells to kill a Cougar with it. Similar to the Moose, Distress Pistol shots on Cougars cannot crit.
- Similar to bear, the Cougar seems to avoid coming close to campfires, so making one can provide a safe spot to shoot at him or to retreat back to.

- A charging Cougar moves very quickly and usually not in a straight line. Approaching the Cougar sneakily significantly reduces the chance to be detected and opens up the possibility of firing a shot calmly ([Archery](./Archery.md) level 5 required if a bow is used).
- When faced with a charging Cougar, it is better to shoot and miss than to risk not being able to shoot in time and getting caught up in a struggle.

- Attacking a Cougar will cause additional Cougars to spawn in different locations in the same region. These will de-spawn after a number of days, but caution is advised, when travelling back to base after a Cougar encounter.

The Cougar was initially implemented in patch Tales From The Far Territory DLC part 5 (June 2024), but was reworked in the Part 6 (December 2024) DLC patch. The following section contains deprecated information about this legacy (Cougar 1.0) version, of which only some mechanics are still reflected in-game.

The Cougar used to occupy a region once the survivor had spent enough consecutive days there. Cougar Threat could be mitigated by regularly traveling between different regions. Once a Cougar occupied a region it would remain there until killed or the survivor remained outside that region for a period of days.

![A warning that a Cougar will arrive in 5 days](../assets/Cougar_Arrival.jpg)_A warning that a Cougar will arrive in 5 days_The Cougar will encroach on any region the survivor has lived for too many consecutive days in. During this time is is still possible to travel outside without risk of a cougar attack.

- A warning message _"Cougar Encroaching"_ (in white) would appear at the top of the UI when The Cougar begun traveling to the current region, providing 2-5 days notice to leave the region or prepare.
**Note**: all Indoor areas and transition mines/caves are children to a region, and were counted for cougar presence.

If the survivor remained within the same region when the Cougar arrived, that region would become infested and the Cougar would begin hunting them until they or it are killed, or the survivor fled the region for a number of days. Once arrived the Cougar could attack at **any time while outdoors.** It beared multiple similarities to The Darkwalker.
This den could be temporarily destroyed by throwing **THREE** [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md) at it, collapsing the cave and suppressing Cougar activity across the Island for a long time.

Once the survivor begun attacking the den with Noisemakers, The Cougar would begin hunting them immediately until the den was destroyed. Contrary to developer's statements, the Cougars were a scripted event by, essentially, teleporting onto the player on a random occasion and trigger a struggle before fleeing and vanishing should it not be killed.

The Cougar originally teleported onto the player and began a struggle if the player was in an infested area. A cutscene would play as the Struggle began, with a surviving player being given the option to choose at least one weapon in their inventory to counter-attack and fire a single shot at the retreating animal:
- Strike (fire a single [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Revolver](./Revolver.md), or [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) shot, or faint after 10 seconds)

If "Strike" is chosen the selected weapon will draw, and the survivor will have 10 seconds to aim and fire a single shot at the retreating cougar. The cougar will flee in a random direction, which may be obscured by terrain or obstacles, as the game speed is set to slow motion. After taking one shot or waiting too long (10 seconds pass) the survivor will faint, awaking a short time later.
- If the shot hits: The Cougar it will be found dead nearby when the survivor awakes. The Cougar infestation in the region will also end for a time.
- If the shot misses: The Cougar will escape and continue hunting the survivor. Can result in a new cougar struggle as early as 2 hours later.

- The Cougar is based off of the Cougar (**_Puma concolor_**), a species of Felidae found in North American and known by over 40 different English names. The most common names for this species include Puma, Cougar, Mountain Lion, Panther, and Catamount (the later meaning cat of the mountain).
- Cougars and cats in general do not typically move around with all of their claws permanently extended as shown in game, as they are usually retracted inside the paws to protect them.

- Killing 3 Cougars formerly unlocked the ["Big Cat Killer" Feat](./Feats.md). The Feat was introduced in the 1.0 release of the Cougar for 4 days, but was demoted to a legacy feat after the 2.0 re-release.
- There were 4 [Notes](./Notes.md) added with the Redux Cougar that give tips on avoiding an encounter with a Cougar:
- It is implied by [The Foreman](./The%20Foreman.md) and the description of [Rüdiger's Watch](./R%C3%BCdiger%27s%20Watch.md) that [Dr. Rüdiger](./Dr.%20R%C3%BCdiger.md) was once attacked by a Cougar.
- The Cougar was reworked due to the majority of players disliking the old Cougar system.

- Temporarily removed from the game by Hinterland due to poor reception and heavy player criticism of the Cougar's initial overall gameplay functionality and mechanics. Will be returned in a future update.

**Crafting** is a menu in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ found within the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md). It can be accessed by the default hotkey "K" or from the hammer and anvil icon at the top of the game menu.
On the left of the screen are tabs that allow you to view blueprints by category. By default it will show **All** blueprints, but they can be filtered to only show:

Below the blueprints are 6 submenus allowing you to filter for specific creation methods for items. By default it will show **All** blueprint creation methods but can be changed to only show items that can be crafted at:

Some items in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) Episodes require finding their blueprints in order to craft, and are usually unlocked when progressing through the story and completing side missions. Other Blueprints are not available in Wintermute at all.
Survival Mode has all blueprints unlocked from the start except for the [Noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md) blueprint, which is unlocked when one is found in game.
- Some items can be crafted faster at a Work Bench by using [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md) or [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md).

**Windproof bonus:** [Windproofness icon](../assets/Windproofness_icon.png)0 °C(0 °F)
> “**Traction, for your feet. Rope climbing drains less Stamina, Sprains are less frequent, and you can travel with more confidence over Weak Ice.**”
When worn in any accessory slot, Crampons grant the Benefit [Sure Footing](./Sure%20Footing.md), which has several effects:
- Decreases drain rate of [climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) stamina by 40% (allowing you to climb further without stopping). (This is a bug, should be 60%)
- While climbing at <25% [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), gain significantly increased [climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) speed compared to not wearing crampons at this fatigue level.
- Increases the (invisible) timer of [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md) by 1 second (aka 20% more time to move off Weak Ice, before falling in).
Note: Crampons **do not** decrease the amount of Fatigue lost during climbing, and **do not** make you climb faster (unless at <25% fatigue).

Crampons are particularly useful in [regions](./Region.md) with multiple [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) climbs, such as [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), and [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), or in areas with Weak Ice such as [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) or when [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md). Shoes/Boots must be worn in order to equip Crampons.

- [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) - A pair is always found next to the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) in the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md). The trek there is long, cold (-25°C (-13°F)) and with [predators](./Wildlife.md) in maze-like geography.

- [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) - A pair _has a chance_ to spawn in the [Backpack](./Backpack.md) at the middle of the [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md), overlooking the cliffside to [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md).
[Improvised Crampons](./Improvised%20Crampons.md) are a more easily acquired--though less effective--alternative that can be crafted at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md).

Crampons can be repaired with 2 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) using [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) or [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md). Repairing Crampons counts towards the [Mending](./Mending.md) skill, rather than the [Repair](./Repair.md) skill.

- If the player's footwear (shoes and 2 socks slots) are removed (whether by the player or their footwear is ruined) then their Crampons will automatically be removed, removing the [Sure Footing](./Sure%20Footing.md) affliction.
- Despite being designed to attach to shoes, the player can wear Crampons on their socks, which should not be possible.
- Wearing Crampons in the outer Accessory slot (right) and another Accessory in the inner (left) will protect that Accessory from damage during wildlife attacks (until the Crampons are destroyed).
- Crampons are very useful for [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md), as they increase the fall time by 1 second.
- Like other clothing, Crampons [Decay](./Decay.md) slowly over time, even slower indoors. Decay is persistent across all Regions and is based on in-game date.

- In the [Perilous Constraint](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/The_Long_Dark/Changelog/Archive_2#1.98_%28Perilous_Constraint_Update%29) update, when attempting to repair the Crampons without the Simple Tools or Quality Tools would give an error message stating a Sewing Kit is required.
- Crampons are metal spikes attached to the underside of boots to increase traction on steep or rough terrain, particularly mountain climbing or traversing ice.

- _The Long Dark_ crampons are a "strap-on" style, being an accessory to footwear. Other types include "stepped into" footwear, using vice-like designs to grasp the foot, or specialized boots with integrated crampons (aka "cleats").

- Originally after launch crampons could not be repaired, making their durability finite, until a repair function was later added. (between [Errant Pilgrim (Dec 2019) and Perilous Constraint (Dec 2020)](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog.md)).
- Scrap Metal may be obtained by [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md), making the repair of crampons renewable (provided they are not at 0% condition).

The **Crank Light** is a [Tools](./Tools.md) item found exclusively in [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) in the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story.

It is found inside the first area of the mine in [Blackrock Foothills](./Blackrock%20Foothills.md) in Part 2 of the Episode. It is a portable [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md), albeit it does not require the need of an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) to power it thanks to the hand crank on the side that can be used to charge the internal battery.
- The battery itself lasts for around 19 seconds before it must be cranked to recharge it again, requiring frequent cranking.
- The light must be cranked repeatedly to charge the battery. The faster the "crank" button is pressed, the faster the light is cranked.
- It takes around 9 seconds to fully charge battery's supply by cranking it at it's fastest cranking speed.
- Objects in the environment cannot be interacted with while the light is being cranked.
The item can be carried through Part 2, but is lost when playing as Mackenzie again in Part 4 of the Episode.
- [Jace](./Jace.md) shows no reaction to the Crank Light when it is used around her, despite her fear of the dark. The player must light Gas Lamps to proceed ahead through the mine as a result.
- The Crank Light is not recharged by the Aurora or [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md), if one is out, and must still be manually cranked to recharge the battery.
- Added to game.

The **Crash Site** is a crashed airliner brought down by the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), not far from [Burned Ridge Cave](./Burned%20Ridge%20Cave.md). This location, lacking an official name, was added to [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) and [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) in game version 1.6 with the release of [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md).

The scattered debris of the passenger airliner is mostly centered around Skeeters' Ridge. The back section of the plane cabin is accessible by one of the plane passenger doors. The site can also be reached by a path on the opposite of the debris field.

The area is well known for having many [Suitcases](./Suitcase.md), which often contain large amounts of low, mid, and occasionally high-tier Clothing. Closer to the airplane's broken fuselage, there are often many pop cans, and [packages of](./Airline%20Food%20-%20Chicken.md) [airline food](./Airline%20Food%20-%20Vegetarian.md). There are also many [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) scattered amongst the suitcases and wreckage. Overall, the area can provide a lot of useful supplies for new survivors.

Unlike the crate-filled [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md) that broke off on the summit of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) or the small private plane crash site in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), the death toll of this aurora-induced tragedy is apparent. There are no survivors outside of Story mode, and many of the passengers bodies can be found within the crash site area.

> **Then yesterday, the crash survivors started showing up....Best thing we can do is keep these people warm and fed and....then we'll see what the Lord has in store.**

**Crash Survivors**are a group of passengers who survived an airline crash in the [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) region. They are only found in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).

Many survivors managed to find their way toe the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md) on their own, but are not doing very well. [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) is tasked with diagnosing and caring for them when she first arrives, with [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md) watching over them to make sure they recover.
Four other Crash Survivors are found outside of the Community Hall during the episode who must be rescued and delivered safely to the Hall to progress the story.
- The first, Gwen, is found at the ruined airliner itself. The other three are found on the map after Astrid has brought Gwen to the community center.
- Wade is found near [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md), close to the bridge on the end of the property furthest from the main road.
When Astrid Greenwood finds these survivors, she needs to carry them back to the Community hall and place them on an empty bed. Once they are there, she cannot interact with them further.

When Astrid is carrying a survivor, Astrid cannot sprint, her walking speed is reduced to a crawl, she cannot use weapons, and she cannot interact with items or [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md) (although she can open building doors and bunker hatches). A small icon next to the Sprint Bar similar to the [Burdened](./Burdened.md) Affliction icon will appear as long as Astrid is carrying a Survivor. Placing a Crash Survivor down will remove these debuffs.

Survivors have their own [Warmth](./Warmth.md) and [Thirst](./Thirst.md) bar that steadily depletes, as well as a [Condition](./Condition.md) bar. Astrid may treat these survivors by interacting with them and choosing the "Diagnose" option. Survivors may only drink [Potable Water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), and like Astrid or [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md), will drink until their thirst is quenched or the water runs out. Warmth is addressed by bringing them indoors or placing them by a fire. One can place them on beds and bedrolls providing the warmth bonus accompanying the bed/bedroll. It is not possible to give any clothing to a survivor. A Survivor's Condition bar will steadily recover just as a player's will so long as their Needs are satisfied.

Survivors may be attacked by a [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md). A wolf will approach the survivor, stop, and then bite them on the ground. This will cause them to lose 25% Condition, and Astrid will need to treat their bleeding with a [Bandage](./Bandage.md). A [Bear](./Bear.md) will ignore a crash survivor, and if Astrid is attacked by one while holding a survivor, the survivor will simply fall to the ground and not be injured.

![The 2 options for interacting with a lost Crash Survivor.](../assets/Crash_Survivor_Diagnosing.jpg)_The 2 options for interacting with a lost Crash Survivor._ Crash Survivors can be diagnosed with the following Afflictions and the following treatments:
- ![Concussion icon](../assets/Concussion_icon.png) [Concussion](./Concussion.md) - No treatment
- ![Hypothermia Risk icon](../assets/Hypothermia_Risk_icon.png) [Hypothermia Risk](./Hypothermia%20Risk.md) - Warm survivor
- ![Hypothermia icon](../assets/Hypothermia_icon.png) [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md) - Warm survivor
- ![Blood Loss icon](../assets/Blood_Loss_icon.png) [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) - Use [Bandage](./Bandage.md)
- ![Dehydration Risk icon](../assets/Dehydration_Risk_icon.png) [Dehydration Risk](./Dehydration%20Risk.md) - Drink [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md)
- ![Dehydrated icon](../assets/Dehydrated_icon.png) [Dehydrated](./Dehydrated.md) - Drink [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md)
- ![Hyperglycemic Risk icon](../assets/Hyperglycemic_Risk_icon.png) [Hyperglycemic Risk](./Hyperglycemic%20Risk.md) - Administer [Insulin](./Insulin.md)
The North Star Charters Flight 7030 was carrying the following passengers when it crashed:
- The pilots and any others who made it to the Community hall and perished. Their remains were stored in the basement.

- The 3 missing Survivors will always be found near a campfire that will burn eternally, keeping them warm and keeping any wolves at bay. This can be a great place to create water, treat the survivors, and warm Astrid up before bringing them to the Community Hall.

- Logan, Ava, and Wade are marked on the map in a large radius. If the player is having trouble finding them, Astrid may shoot a flare from a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) while in the radius. The survivor will respond by shooting a flare back.

**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**
> “__Hey...you think they put me on that bus for my good behaviour? That's the bus to Blackrock. __”
> “__Hey...you think they put me on that bus for my good behaviour? That's the bus to Blackrock. __”
> **Blackrock's bus drivers have what many consider to be the cushiest and safest job at the Penitentiary.**

The **Crashed Prison Transport Bus** is a location in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region, located to the south of [Milton](./Milton.md), past the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md).

The bus, which was carrying the [Convicts](./Convicts.md), inmates to [Blackrock Federal Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) prior to the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), is half-buried in snow and rubble from the collapsed tunnel and cannot be entered. The [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) of an inmate can be found nearby and looted. A briefcase can also be found nearby, containing the [Prison Transport Manifest](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md).

![Perseverance](../assets/Perseverance.jpg)![Perseverence logo](../assets/Perseverence_logo.png) Although the locale can be encountered at any point while exploring Milton, it must be visited as part of the main [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) questline. [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) sends [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) to investigate the tunnel, where he finds the bus crash and the collapsed tunnel. A cutscene shows Mackenzie noticing the scrap of clothing in the bus door, and then revealing the word _PERSEVERANCE_ written in blood on the floor inside the bus, presumably by [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md), leading Will to believe that Astrid made her way to the town of [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md).

- Before the tunnel collapsed, it was possible to travel directly to [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) and then later to [Long Curve](./Long%20Curve.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
- This is evidenced by Astrid having escaped through the tunnel and having been found by [Molly](./Molly.md) near Long Curve.

- With the release of Episode 4, the above theory has been confirmed, as continuing along the road from [Long Curve](./Long%20Curve.md) towards [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) leads to [Mirthless Fork](./Mirthless%20Fork.md), from which it was originally possible to go either towards Milton or [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md).

- Due to the collapse of the tunnel, it is currently only possible to travel towards Blackrock from there, and getting to Keeper's Pass South requires a continuous route through [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) and [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).

Provides some shelter **Creek Bed Cave** is a small cave located in [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), near the region's southwestern-most point.

There is a small tuffet in the cave, allowing [sleep](./Sleep.md) without a bedroll. Various plants grow near the cave, and rabbits are often to be seen on the frozen creek in front. Deer may also spawn just outside the cave, and there is ample foraging in the wilderness surrounding the cave. Additionally, this is one of the few areas of Blackrock that doesn't have many predators, making it a possible location for a [Safe House](./Safehouse.md).

Nearby locations include [Narrow Bridge](./Narrow%20Bridge.md) to the east, and a path leads north towards a series of ledges that allow passage over the blocked road at [Bear's Bend](./Bear%27s%20Bend.md).

Has an interior A **Crossroads House**is a type of house or shed found throughout the [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) town in the [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) region. Many of these buildings have the same layout as the [Coastal House](./Coastal%20House.md) and [Milton House](./Milton%20House.md).

Some of the buildings in the town are boarded up or destroyed. The homes closest to the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md) are in relatively good shape, but the ones across the bridge on the road to the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) tend to be boarded up and seized by the bank or ruined, but occasionally the house across the bridge is intact. The name "Crossroads House" comes from the former name of [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), Rural Crossroads.
This type of building has only 1 floor, with 1 door leading to the kitchen. They are composed of:
- A kitchen with a [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), [Fridge](./Fridge.md), [Freezer](./Freezer.md), [Oven](./Oven.md), and [Drawers](./Drawer.md)
The layout for this building has 2 different layouts, but tends to be filled with large amounts of food and [Cooking Pots](./Cooking%20Pot.md).
These homes are much smaller buildings with a single door leading to the front hallway. They have a stairwell that leads the bedroom, with the ground floor containing a kitchen and nearby bathroom.

> “**Pay attention to your surroundings and you might glean information that's important for your survival. For example, a murder of Crows circling up ahead might suggest an animal carcass -- or even a human corpse -- might be nearby!**”
**Crows** are non-interactable, animated [wildlife](./Wildlife.md) objects in [The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Crows are flying black birds with conspicuously loud cries. They never land and their primary purpose is to draw the player to certain areas of interest. Crows cannot be harmed with projectiles from [revolvers](./Revolver.md), [hunting rifles](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [bows](./Survival%20Bow.md), and [flare guns](./Distress%20Pistol.md), and they cannot be harmed with thrown objects such as [flares](./Flare.md), [torches](./Torch.md), and [stones](./Stone.md) (if they are low enough to the ground that is) as they do not technically have collision models/death animations.

Periodically, [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) will fall to the ground underneath circling Crows (1 Feather will fall per crow flying overhead). Once on the ground, the feathers remain until picked up, making these locations valuable as the only source of crow feathers for [Crafting](./Crafting.md).

Crows will appear circling over frozen corpses and animal carcasses during calm weather. Their loud cries are intended to call the player's attention to the area so it will not likely be missed, however, they may be difficult to spot due to trees or terrain obscuring them.

Aggressive crow calls distinct from those made by circling or passing crows can be heard in the vicinity of a [Bear](./Bear.md), but no crows will actually be visible. This sound may also be heard around dead bears as well, making locating a fresh bear carcass somewhat easier, as they can then be "heard" in addition to being seen.

Crows will disappear when high winds or snow strike and reappear when weather clears. Once a non-human carcass has disappeared after decaying or being fully harvested, the circling crows will disappear with it.
Occasionally a group of crows will be seen flying in "V" formation in a straight path across the map. The timing of their flight has no significance and is purely cosmetic.
- Crows appear to be based off the [American Crow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_crow) (**_Corvus brachyrhynchos_**), a species of Passeriformes found all across North America.

- In various points throughout [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), a single crow can be spotted perched upon an object (such as a log or stump) in area the player is required to pass through. The crow remain in place but will fly off when approached, and like all crows cannot be harmed. This is the only time a single crow appears by itself, as they typically fly around the map/ fly over dead bodies in groups only.
- [Wintermute] Fixed issue where crows would circle locations with no corpses present.
- [Both] Crows will no longer sometimes fly too low and into the ground as the weather changes.
- Fixed issue that could cause large numbers of crows and crow feathers to spawn in specific locations.

**Description:** A transition zone between [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) and [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) featuring the ruins of the [Great Bear Highway](./Great%20Bear%20Highway.md).

**Crumbling Highway** (also known as the **Old Island Connector**) is the 3rd Transition Zone [Region](./Region.md) released for _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It connects [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) and [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md). It is the smallest outdoor map in the game.

The eastern end of the area sits [No. 3 Coal Mine](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md), which leads to Desolation Point. On the western side of the region lies an entrance to Coastal Highway. A frozen coastline curves along the south side of the road.
There is also a relatively large amount of fuel and medicinal resources scattered about, as well as two vehicles and two shallow caves.
A couple of wolves patrol this zone in 3 different areas. Because the region is so compact, it can be difficult to bypass predators without taking extra precautions.
- [Basement (Crumbling Highway)](./Basement%20%28Crumbling%20Highway%29.md) (unmarked indoor location tracked in the [Journal](./Journal.md))
- 2 [Warm Caves](./Warm%20Cave.md) that can be found near Road Collapse and The Arch.

Coffee is useful for [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) by restoring fatigue, since fatigue affects climbing speed and climbing at low fatigue is dangerous. However, climbing is the only action which coffee does not reduce the rate of fatigue drain through Fatigue Reduced.

Another application of coffee is to restore [carry capacity](./Encumbrance.md), which is diminished below 50% Fatigue (slowing movement). One cup of coffee restores 10% of Fatigue. At 0% Fatigue [Condition](./Condition.md) is drained, so drinking coffee would temporarily avoid this damage.

Other items which restore fatigue, such as the [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) and [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md), are rare. Additionally, these items have other uses, side effects, or may not be obtainable on all difficulty settings. It is advisable to save coffee for more specialized uses and use other hot beverages, such as [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) or canned food, to obtain [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md).

**Curator's Rifle** is a unique variant of the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

The Curator's Rifle in addition to looking fancy, offers an increased range of 33.3% over the standard Hunting Rifle [Around 66 meters]. Unlike the other variants this bonus comes with no downside, making it a direct upgrade to the standard Hunting Rifle.

The small range increase makes this variant superior at sniping distant [Bears](./Bear.md) or [Moose](./Moose.md), leaving more time for you to react to a potential charge, though the rifle's tendency to sway and scarcity of rifle ammunition makes this bonus risky to use.
Successful hits on live animals provide experience to the [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) skill.

The range increase is applied to a ray-trace fired from the center of the screen when a shot is fired, normally the standard Hunting Rifle ray-trace range is about 50 meters long, but the Curators Rifle's is just over 66 meters long. Past this range the weapon will be unable to damage any [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md). These are the base ranges when at [Rifle Skill Level 1](./Rifle%20Firearm.md), at level 5 a 40% bonus is applied to these ranges which combined with the Curator's Rifle's 33.3% gives the rifle a potential maximum range of just over 86 meters or a 73.3% additional range over the base 50.
The Curator's Rifle will spawn a single time per world in various states of repair in a set of randomly selected [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) locations such as:
- Next to a corpse on the ledge along the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md) path near [Wolf's Jaw Overlook](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md).
- Next to a corpse by the tree at [Wolf's Jaw Overlook](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md) near the rose hip climb.
- In the cave with the bed at the top of the [Runaway Bridge](./Runaway%20Bridge.md) plateau across the fallen tree.

- The rifle's furniture appears to be made out of now old and faded purpleheart wood and has a golden action with deer engravings on the sides, its premium construction materials give it a striking beauty.
- A small detail is that the 5-round stripper-clips used to load the gun are also made of the distinctive gold plating that matches the gold engravings on the rifle.
- The rifles small upside and lack of downside makes it unique compared to the other variants which usually have a downside to compensate for a large bonus.

- The Curator's Rifle's model originally appeared as a [second hunting rifle](./Hunting%20Lodge%20Rifle.md) in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) that could be found during the quest [You Fix My Rifle?](./You%20Fix%20My%20Rifle%3F.md). This rifle model was later removed from the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story mode following the Redux update.
_The [Hunting Lodge Rifle](./Hunting%20Lodge%20Rifle.md) shares the same engravings, without the Purplewood and with silver metal._

**Cured Black Bear Hide** is the Cured fur and skin of a [Fresh Black Bear Hide](./Fresh%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md). It can be used as a [Material](./Materials.md) for crafting or repairing [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md) and [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md).

Fresh Black Bear Hide acquired by harvesting a [Bear Carcass](./Black%20Bear%20Carcass.md) and can be cured by leaving them indoors for 12 days (in-game). Cured black bear hides are used for crafting or repairing Bearskin Coats and Bear Skin Bedrolls. Once cured, the hide will take on a darker complexion, and can then be used for crafting.

Black bear hides can be hard and resource-expensive to obtain, since they requiring the shooting of a bear with a [weapon](./Tools.md), as there are no naturally occurring bear carcasses. **Cured Fish** is a [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Cured Fish can only be acquired by placing any type of raw fish with condition higher than 40% inside a [Meat Curing Box](./Meat%20Curing%20Box.md) filled with [Salt](./Salt.md) for 7 in-game days. Placing meat inside a Meat Curing Box will instead produce [Cured Meat](./Cured%20Meat.md).

Cured Fish has no [Scent](./Scent.md) and is completely safe to consume in high (above 75%) condition. Cured Fish in 20%-75% condition has a very low food (1%) poisoning chance. Additionally, cured fish inherits the condition of the meat you insert to the box (Eg, putting in a 86% condition fish will result in a 86% condition cured fish).

On its own, Cured Fish is an amazing food source, having high calories of 900 while weighing only at 0.20 kg, which is much lighter than a cooked fish. Cured Fish also lasts much longer than the typically cooked fish. This makes Cured Fish a very valuable end-game food should the player eventually run out of non-renewable food sources. One downside of curing fish is that all Vitamin C units are lost, regardless of the source fish. Cured Fish has no Vitamin C content which is a factor when considering [Scurvy](./Scurvy%20Risk.md) risk.

It doesn't matter the weight or calories of raw fish input, the output is always the same: 1 whole raw fish => 0.20 kg Cured Fish with 900 kcal. The best strategy is to cure small and low calories fish, with less than 900 kcal/fish, because it will increase the calories when it transforms into Cured Fish.

If the player ate from a raw fish, the leftover fish will cure at a weight ratio of 20/1 (1 kg leftover raw fish => 0.05 kg Cured Fish). So, in order to obtain maximum calories from curing a raw fish bigger than 4kg, it can be partially eaten until it reaches 4 kg (risking [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md)), then cure 4kg leftover raw fish into 0.20 kg Cured Fish.

Cured Meat can be produced by placing any type of raw meat with condition higher than 40% inside a [Meat Curing Box](./Meat%20Curing%20Box.md) filled with [Salt](./Salt.md) for 5 in-game days. Placing fish inside a Meat Curing Box will instead produce [Cured Fish](./Cured%20Fish.md).

The meat has no [Scent](./Scent.md) and is completely safe to consume in high (above 75%) condition. If a predator meat is cured, there will be no [Risk of Intestinal Parasites](./Risk%20of%20Intestinal%20Parasites.md). Cured Meat in 20%-75% condition has a very low food poisoning risk (only 1%). Additionally, Cured Meat inherits the condition of the meat you insert to the box (Eg, putting in a 86% condition meat will result in a 86% condition cured meat).

On its own, Cured Meat is an amazing food source, having high calories of 900 while weighing only at 0.25 kg (0.20 kg for fish), which is 0.75 kg lighter than a cooked meat. Cured Meat also lasts much longer than the typically cooked meats. This makes the meat a very valuable end-game food should the player eventually run out of non-renewable food sources.

The calories of raw meat put in the curing box don't affect the calories of the cured meat; the output is always the same Cured Meat, using 4/1 or 5/1 weight ratio (eg: 1kg raw meat => 0.25 kg Cured Meat with 900 kcal or 0.20 kg for fish). The best strategy is to cure raw meat with less than 900 kcal/kg (rabbit, ptarmigan, wolf) because it will increase the calories when it transforms into Cured Meat (TLD version 2.35).
