**Curing** is a mechanic in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md), which converts raw resources into crafting items.

Some raw resources from [plants](./Wildlife.md#Plant_and_Fungal_Species) and [animals](./Wildlife.md) cannot be used for crafting in their initial state, and must first be cured: these include [Birch Sapling](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) and [Maple Sapling](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md), all types of [Animal Pelts/Hides](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Materials#Fresh_Hides), and [Fresh Gut](./Fresh%20Gut.md) from animals.

These items may be cured by dropping them on the floor or otherwise placing them inside an 'indoors' location (most caves and artificial structures, including many without a Loading Transition, such as the [Stone Church](./Stone%20Church.md) and [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md)). As these raw items continue to lay on the floor indoors, they will display a "X% Cured" progress by looking at the item, showing their current status until they become fully cured. This increases until the item is 100% cured, where the item will automatically become fully cured will change to a darker texture, and is ready for crafting use.
- Curing takes place over in-game time, even if the player is not present (such as outside of a building, or in another region).

- Fresh Hides and Guts [Decay](./Decay.md) their condition over time, becoming destroyed upon reaching 0% Condition ("Ruined"). This is especially a problem when playing on Interloper, as fresh items can be lost if not cured fast enough. Curing items fully prevents them from further decaying condition. The item's remaining condition has no effect on item(s) created by it.
- Fresh items which are partially cured may be picked up, resuming their decay but retaining their "X% Cured", which is can progress as soon as they are dropped/placed indoor again.

- Curing items placed inside a container indoors will also cure, but at a slower rate. Many small caves can also be used for curing, but items should be placed as far as possible from the entrance; if they are curing, the "Cure%" will appear on the item.
- In-Game time is required to cure items, and is a fixed rate, not dependent on temperature.

- "Curing" is a real-world process which includes salting, drying, and smoking. It is the process of preserving items or materials, often through desiccation (drying out) or treatment with a chemical/compound (such as salt).
- In _The Long Dark_, raw meat and fish can be cured using a [Meat Curing Box](./Meat%20Curing%20Box.md), to make [Cured Meat](./Cured%20Meat.md), which has a much slower decay rate.

- In early builds of _The Long Dark_ (alpha/beta), Deer Hides provided "Fresh Leather" when harvested; this item could be converted into "Cured [Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md)" by curing it, and then used for repairing clothing. Cured Leather is still present in _The Long Dark_, but is only obtainable by Harvesting leather footwear, gloves, the Moose-Hide Satchel, and [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md).

- The "Fresh Leather" item is still present in The Long Dark, and may be still be cured into Cured Leather over 5 days, but is extremely rare and cannot be created in any way outside of world generation at game start. Fresh Leather also decays over time, like animal hides and guts, making it even more difficult to find the already rare item before it decays to 0% condition inside a container and is deleted.

> **Use our custom toolbox to craft a unique experience between Survival and Exploration - an experience all your own.**
**Custom** is the 6th [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) Experience in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Custom is different from the other 5 difficulty Experiences in that it allows the player to instead create their own difficulty. This mode presents over 50 different variables which can be adjusted to the player's liking. Creating a Custom Experience Mode generates a code, which may be shared with other users for the same experience, including across game platforms.
**NOTE:** [Feats](./Feats.md) progression will not occur when playing on a Custom Experience save file, but [Achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) can still be earned.
- [Animal](./Wildlife.md) behaviour, spawns, detection radius, grace period, and an option for passive wildlife.
- The option to enable [Cougar](./Cougar.md) and [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) in the game settings.
- Endless Night (The sun will never rise): Completing the [Challenge](./Challenge.md): [Escape The Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) is required to unlock this.

Concretely, this setting affects the timespace aspect of the Experience, slowing various aspects of the game world down. In x4 you can walk 4x more before a day ends unlike in 1x. This essentially makes the world feel "slower".
1. Player/Wildlife movement speed is still the same, but all other aspects regarding the way time affects the world and the player is slowed.

2. Management activities are directly linked to the multiplier. Time passage related to activities like minutes passing during travel don't initially feel slower, but it becomes evident eventually that time passes slower.

3. [Needs](./Needs.md) drain/[Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) accumulation/item Decay is significantly slowed the higher the length of day multiplier is. Example: you can travel 4x farther in 3 miles with poor clothing on before [Frostbite Risk](./Frostbite%20Risk.md) develops into [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md), as the Frostbite Risk meter fills slower. This can essentially make the game far easier than normal, as the player doesn't have to worry about carrying as much food/worrying about Affliction Risks. The downside to this setting is that it can result in the game feeling too unchallenging/Afflictions taking MUCH longer to heal.
4. Time speeds up normally when your character starts an "action" (ex: passing time for sleep, crafting, harvesting, researching a book for 1 hour will still count as 1 hour as if it was 1x length).

The player community has given unofficial names to two of the most commonly used custom experiences. One of them has been dubbed **Gunloper**, which is an Interloper base game where rifle/revolver spawns are enabled. The other is **Deadman**, which is an Interloper base game where passive healing is disabled, and Birch Bark Tea cannot be crafted (similar to [As the Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md)).
- Deadman Challenge (DMC): custom Interloper where passive regeneration and [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) are disabled (similar to As the Dead Sleep)
- NOGOA: No One Gets Out Alive challenge - a specific custom file that has all the settings on their most harsh and spawns you at midnight in a blizzard (Code: 8sHM-/z8P-Dz+3-QZym-XQIC)
- Outerloper: Interloper, but where the player can't enter any building (self-enforced rule)
More custom challenges can be found [Here](https://steamcommunity.com/app/305620/discussions/9/4515505814159739321/).

The following is a list of settings the player can manipulate as they create their own Survival Experience. Selecting a difficulty will generate a preset variable list, and the player can further modify the list to their liking.

The following list contains discontinued features that existed in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ throughout its early access versions but were removed and/or replaced. It also includes content found through the game's life that was cut and never made it into the game. Some icons remain in the game's files to this day, but cannot be spawned in game.
Several items/mechanics have been cut from the game over the years. Many items found below are still in the game files, but cannot be accessed normally.
> “**The Brand is a burning stick that serves as a small torch. Provides a bit of light, and might be useful against wildlife.**”

There was a tool called a [Brand](./Brand.md) in the early Alpha that was just a stick on fire. It could be taken only from active fires (campfires, etc). It was not throwable, but could instead be brandished. This item could not be placed in the player's backpack, weighed 0.30 kg, and would disappear from the game world after it burned out and was picked up.
It was eventually cut in the Faithful Cartographer update and replaced by taking [Torches](./Torch.md) out of fireboxes instead. This item is still in the Wintermute game files.

There was a cut Mechanic where a player could brandish (swinging sideways) their [Flares](./Flare.md), [Torches](./Torch.md), and Brands to scare away wolves. Before the introduction of Brands it was only possible to brandish Torches at the expense of around 12% [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) and 15% of the torch condition per swing, after the introduction of Brands it became possible to swing all three types of light sources at the expense of 5% of [Stamina](./Stamina.md) and around 10 minutes of fire duration of Torches and Brands. This feature was removed and reverted back to throwing torches and flares at wildlife instead.

A Shovel was originally in the game as seen on the title screen but was never found outside of console commands. It has no item description or gameplay functionality. This item was removed from the title screen menu in 2017 with the release of V1.00 (Wintermute Predux Update). It was most likely either going to be used to build a [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md), with earlier in-game art icons showing shovels being used to build them, or was just a simple scenery item for the title screen.

It can be found in the mission [Memories](./Memories.md) in [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), next to the bathroom, but cannot be picked up. This item is still in the Wintermute game files but has no description or backpack model.

Raph responded that this item was meant to be used for 'internal purposes' and never meant to be in public game. [https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/47078-april-dev-diary/page/6/#findComment-297548 source](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/47078-april-dev-diary/page/6/#findComment-297548_source)

A Fire Axe remains in the game files as far back as 2015, but cannot be found outside of console commands. It has an item description but can only be used during [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md), and has no other functionality. This item is still in the Wintermute game files, has a model, and can be repaired in 1.5 hours with 1 Scrap Metal and 1 Fir Firewood.

Raphael von Lierop, creative lead of the game, responded that the item was used for prop only. [https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/47078-april-dev-diary/page/6/#findComment-297548 source](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/47078-april-dev-diary/page/6/#findComment-297548_source). 2 Fire Axes appear on the [Fukkatsu Maru](./Fukkatsu%20Maru.md) in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) (2026), but it is treated as an environmental prop and cannot be used.

There is an item in the Wintermute game files called the Compression Bandage. It has no Backpack model, and can only be dropped. It was likely replaced by the regular [Bandage](./Bandage.md), and may have been used to heal Sprains.

There is an item in the Wintermute game files called the Accelerant, but it is different from the normal [Accelerant](./Accelerant.md). The description of this item suggest that it was originally going to be used to fuel charcoal fires. The item does not have a backpack model, but has a physical model. It weighs 0.10kg.

There is an item in the Wintermute game files called the Flint and Steel. It is a Fire Starting tool that does not have a backpack model, and takes the form of a green plastic first aid box when dropped. Unlike most other items, the Flint and Steel is immediately picked up, and cannot be examined. It was most likely replaced by the [Firestriker](./Firestriker.md).

An option for Heated Seats would appear during an Aurora inside several trucks in [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) following the Perilous Constraint update. Hovering over the dashboard would make the option appear, but ultimately did not raise the player's [Warmth](./Warmth.md) since the feature was not complete (given the obvious string of gameplay code presented). The option was ultimately removed in a patch, and Heated Seats as a potential mechanic have yet to return.

The [Camera](./Camera.md) was originally teased as "A Photo Mode for THE LONG DARK, but contextualized with an in-game camera and Dark Room chemicals so that you can process your own film." This meant that the original Camera used a model that required its pictures to be processed first before they could be displayed, which was also shown in the teaser image showing polaroids hanging out to develop.

- An interview by Hinterland later revealed that the Dark Room was cut "because it would have required electrical equipment that we'd only be able to let player use during an active aurora. We came up with a good solution that is true to our lore and also gives players a lot of freedom for self-expression."[^1]

A unique [Ravaged Wolf Carcass](./Wolf%20Carcass.md) item exists in the game files for Survival Mode that features [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md). Normally only small carcasses of Rabbit or Ptarmigan can be transported, but this one is unique in that it can be transported in the backpack and can be fully harvested at any time, similar to animal Quarters (but meat, gut, and hide can be harvested). This item likely exists for development testing purposes, since it weighs 0.00 KG.

An [uncured](./Curing.md) variant of [Cured Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md) was originally present in the earlier builds of the game and was present past the 1.00 launch of the game. [Fresh Leather](./Fresh%20Leather.md) was originally harvested from animals instead of animal hides, and would cure indoors for 5 days before becoming Cured Leather. Eventually animal hides would replace Fresh Leather, but the item could occasionally be found in the game world, with indoor spawns of the items eventually turning into Cured Leather over time. This item has ultimately been removed from the game's loot tables in Survival Mode, and is impossible to find anywhere without console commands, and only appears in Survival Mode.

In a previous event that ran for 4 years every October, Hinterland introduced a game mode called the [4 Days of Night Event](./4%20Days%20of%20Night%20Event.md). 2 items unique to this game mode, [Pumpkin Pie](./Pumpkin%20Pie.md) and a 2500 calorie [Candy Bar](./Chocolate%20Bar%20%284%20Days%20of%20Night%29.md), have since been removed from the game, and are unable to be found outside of console commands. Several other items, such as [Jack-o-Lanterns](./Jack-o-Lantern.md), have also been cut but are still in the game files.

A second version of the Pumpkin Pie would appear in the 2020 [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) release, with a new description. Both Pumpkin Pies are still found in the Wintermute game files.

3 limited time game modes/events have been discontinued over the course of the game's lifetime. They are currently inaccessible even via the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md) (having been patched into and out of the game via their own unique update), and feature unique gameplay modifiers sometimes not found even in Custom Survival Mode experiences. Several limited time event [Badges](./Badges.md) could be earned from playing these game modes, and are still shown in the Badges screen even for players that have never participated in the events.
- Ran from June 29th to July 31st. Introduced the [Ketchup Chips](./Ketchup%20Chips.md) and [Maple Syrup](./Maple%20Syrup.md) items, as well as 2 unique Badges.

- Originally a 2 week long event (October 29, 2020 to November 12, 2020), this game mode replaced 4DON since players were upset with how short the Halloween event 4DON was, not being able to find time to play the limited 4 day long event. Escape the Darkwalker is currently the only game mode that was turned into a permanent addition to the game as a Challenge.

When the Long Dark entered in Early Access, [Struggle](./Struggle.md) with hostile [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) underwent several changes throughout its development.

Initially, once a Wolf pounced on the player, the player had to click the left button of their mouse to build up strength as indicated in a red progress bar and once it was full, they could click the right button of their mouse and repeat until the process kills the wolf or causes it to flee from the player. This method proved very difficult to players, often proving fatal.

In Early Access update 0.163 (Released November 2014), the struggle system underwent a complete overhaul and behaves similarly the way it behaves in full release version except that there was no weapon choice to fight the wolf. If the player had a knife on them (backpack), the game would automatically choose this weapon to fight the wolf. Also, gone is the build up strength mechanic and introduced the "Fight" button by just clicking the right button of the mouse until the wolf flees.
Finally, in Early Access update 0.423 (June 2017), it introduced weapon choice to select right before the struggle (the game would be slowed down for few seconds to give you enough time to react).

Early Survival Mode gave the player the option to toggle or hold the ability to run, and the player could always run without a cooldown (infinite running) or effecting [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md). Becoming Exhausted however would prevent the player from running. Eventually, this system was replaced in the Deep Forest update, giving the player a [Stamina](./Stamina.md) meter, and endlessly running was instead replaced by occasional Sprinting that lowers Fatigue quickly.

Early Survival Mode gave players the menu option to spend time and calories searching the area for fuel. This system was eventually replaced in the Deep Forest update, providing a Direct Harvesting and Foraging system that is still in place today, adding Sticks and Harvestable Objects throughout the game world.

Originally, searching a container would yield items as the search bar filled up. Multiple items inside a container would appear halfway through the search until the bar was fully filled and could be claimed or left inside. It was eventually changed so that items are only yielded once the search bar reaches 100%.
Maximum Calories for the earliest time was capped at 3000 stored calories. It was eventually changed to the current 2500 Calorie Store.
Drop Decoy originally allowed you to drop any food in your inventory as [Baiting](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys) for predators. It was eventually changed so that only meat and guts could be dropped.

Several items and their in-game models have been changed throughout the years, mostly from the early Alpha days to the present. Below is a list of name/model changes (items with changed names will have the current name in a hyperlink):

Most of the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) backgrounds have changed from an actual book to stylized floating text. A physical book can still be heard closing when closing the Survival Menu despite the modernized changes.

The survival skills originally did not have a dedicated menu, but instead appeared when they were leveled up similarly to [Secondary Skills](./Skills.md#Secondary_skills). Eventually players could see their survival skills in the "basic skills" tab in a book, before it was changed to a modern-style book.

In the pre-alpha version, players would have a digital clock shown on HUD UI stating the exact time of day (could be changed to 12 or 24 hour display). This was later removed and replaced by "Time of Day" which showed how many hours of either light or darkness are left until the next 12 hours of the day begins.
Time of day would later undergo a few changes until it was replaced with the current rotating sun and moon icons.

Many of these features were in the original Predux releases of [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) and [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) and were removed following the Redux re-release.
The original Wintermute Storyline was largely changed in the Redux rerelease, heavily changing the plot and mission structure of the story. The original missions went in the following order:

In the pre Redux version of [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), Jeremiah would walk over to the middle of the floor and open a hatch with a ham radio inside after Mackenzie left in order to send a message out to an unknown party. This hatch is still present in the floorboards of the cabin to this day, but cannot be opened. The same radio was reworked into the mission [Signal to Noise](./Signal%20to%20Noise.md), as Mackenzie must now repair it with Jeremiah.
Several side missions were cut or reworked into the Redux version of Episode 1 and 2:

- [Light Up The Night](./Light%20Up%20The%20Night.md) was cut from Episode 1 and was replaced by [Highway Robbery (mission)](./Highway%20Robbery%20%28mission%29.md), and was unlocked by raising Grey Mother's Trust.

- [Forge Blueprints (mission)](./Forge%20Blueprints%20%28mission%29.md) was cut from Episode 2 entirely, and was given by Jeremiah as a reward for raising his Trust. The player would go to the [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) and unlock the ability to Forge improvised tools.

- [Jeremiah's Hideout](./Jeremiah%27s%20Hideout.md) was a location replaced by the [Aurora Hatch](./Aurora%20Hatch.md) in Episode 2 following the Redux re-release. Jeremiah would give the player the side mission once their Trust level was at max and would ask Mackenzie to burn some of his old letters.

> “**Trust. A hard thing to come by these days. Many people you meet will be suspicious of you. But most of them have needs they may not be able to fulfill without your help. Helping them will earn you Trust, which will in turn unlock useful Knowledge, Locations, Items, and more. Check the character's Trust entry in your Journal to learn more about them, their needs, and how they can help you.**”

In the original Wintermute releases of Episodes 1 and 2, [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) and [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) could be given items to build up their trust with Mackenzie. Taking or breaking down items from their homes would lower trust, whereas bringing them items they wished for would increase trust (sticks, cured rabbit pelts, etc). Having a higher Trust would grant the player access to additional dialogue options, which would reveal more worldbuilding information or give access to entire side quests (such as finding a Distress Pistol in Episode 1 or Jeremiah giving the coordinates to [Jeremiah's Hideout](./Jeremiah%27s%20Hideout.md)). The system was ultimately removed following the Redux re-releases of both episodes and was replaced with standard dialogue options. Trust rewards always maxed out at 375 Trust, making donating more items useless. Unlocked Trust items/knowledge/blueprints would remain unlocked, even it Trust fell below the unlocking requirements.

It is possible to steal food items from Grey Mother and Jeremiah by opening canned goods and canceling halfway through, thus claiming the item and not lowering Trust. Jeremiah will know the player has taken his things even when he is passed out at the start of Episode 2.
- 25 Trust: Knowledge: Milton History - Worldbuilding information about the history of Milton. (Gives [Town of Milton](./Town%20of%20Milton.md) [What I Know](./What%20I%20Know.md) Knowledge)
- 50 Trust: Gameplay Tip: Sharpening - Gameplay tip about how to maintain Bladed tools. (Gives [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md))

- 75 Trust: Knowledge: The Collapse - Worldbuilding information about the Collapse. (Gives [History of The Collapse](./History%20of%20The%20Collapse.md) Part One [What I Know](./What%20I%20Know.md) Knowledge)
- 125 Trust: Cache Location - The location of a Supply Cache, updated on your Map. (Gives new [Milton Supply Caches](./Milton%20Supply%20Caches.md))
- 175 Trust: Side Mission: Distress Pistol - Information about where you might find a Distress Pistol. ([Light Up The Night](./Light%20Up%20The%20Night.md))
- 225 Trust: Blueprint: Rabbit Skin Mittens - Unlocks the Crafting Blueprint for Rabbit Skin Mittens.

- 300 Trust: Knowledge: [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) - Worldbuilding information about Perseverance Mills. (Gives [History of The Collapse](./History%20of%20The%20Collapse.md) Part Two [What I Know](./What%20I%20Know.md) Knowledge)
- 375 Trust: Item: [Mountaineering Boots](./Mountaineering%20Boots.md) - Grey Mother gives you with Mountaineering Boots. (sic) (Gives [Mountaineering Boots](./Mountaineering%20Boots.md))

With the original Predux release of Episode 1 and 2, Mackenzie would appear in 3rd person in each cutscene. He would always wear his default clothing, regardless of what was chosen to be worn by the player, and was far more expressive and interactive when meeting with other characters.

Following the Redux updates, all cutscenes were replaced with a first person perspective and were completely redesigned from Makenzie's perspective. All cutscenes in future Episodes still feature first person character interactions to date.

As part of the [Survival School (Predux)](./Survival%20School%20%28Predux%29.md) mission, Mackenzie needed to repair [Jeremiah's Bearskin Coat](./Jeremiah%27s%20Bearskin%20Coat.md) in order to learn about [Mending](./Mending.md). This was the same coat that Jeremiah was wearing when the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) attacked him at the end of Episode 1. The coat was not a Collectible, but rather a [Clothing](./Clothing.md) item, and had no clothing stats, could not be worn, and weighed 5.00 kg. It would be repaired with 1 [Cured Black Bear Hide](./Cured%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md), and later be returned to Jeremiah.

The **[Bolt Cutters](./Bolt%20Cutters.md)** were a tool found exclusively in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). They could be found in the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) and were used to open the gate that led to the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md).

The bolt cutters were removed from the game entirely after the Redux update, however they were re-introduced in the ending of [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) as a puzzle tool, and later in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), both being used to cut open a single gate again. They were also introduced in Survival Mode as part of the [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md) Tale, and are used to cut open several gates as part of the Tale to access parts of the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md).

[Jeremiah's Knife](./Jeremiah%27s%20Knife.md) was a tool found exclusively in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). It was removed from Episode and the game entirely after the Redux update, however the icon can still be seen occasionally in Survival Mode when crafting at a Work Bench. The knife is still present as a spawnable object in the Wintermute game files. It has been seen in an official trailer as late as December 5th 2023, as well as an icon for Misery Mode during the May 13th 2024 News update.

Jeremiah's rifle originally breaks after Mackenzie fires it at the end of Episode 2, with an entire mission dedicated to fixing [Jeremiah's Broken Rifle](./Jeremiah%27s%20Broken%20Rifle.md) while looking for your own rifle. A unique Hunting Rifle would be found in the mission [You Fix My Rifle?](./You%20Fix%20My%20Rifle%3F.md) and was used for the rest of the Story. The Hunting Lodge Rifle was eventually replaced by the [Broken Bear Spear](./Broken%20Bear%20Spear.md), with a Jeremiah's Rifle being available from the start of Episode 2 in the Redux [The Wounded Trapper](./The%20Wounded%20Trapper.md) mission. Features of the [Hunting Lodge Rifle](./Hunting%20Lodge%20Rifle.md) would later be recycled into the [Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md) and [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md).

In the Predux version of [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) and [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), several collectibles did not make the transition to Redux:
- A [key](./Lock%20Box%20Key%20%28Predux%29.md) on the body of [Martin Barker](./Martin%20Barker.md) was cut from the game.

- The key would open a lockbox containing an [Emergency Kit Note](./Emergency%20Kit%20Note.md) inside. This same lockbox would later be found next to [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) in the Redux, minus the note, and would be filled with [Cash](./Cash.md) instead of Emergency Supplies.
- [Jeremiah's Broken Rifle](./Jeremiah%27s%20Broken%20Rifle.md), and [Jeremiah's Repaired Rifle](./Jeremiah%27s%20Repaired%20Rifle.md) would be cut from the game.
- A side mission involving burning [Jeremiah's Papers](./Jeremiah%27s%20Papers.md) would be replaced by the side mission [Aurora Hatch](./Aurora%20Hatch.md).
- Mackenzie was required to shoot and cut the ear off of the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) and then return it to [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) in order to prove that the Old Bear was slain.

- An early version of the [Revolver](./Revolver.md) was planned but ultimately never introduced into the game until the Steadfast Ranger update, including [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md) and [Revolver Shell Casings](./Revolver%20Shell%20Casing.md). Textures for Revolver Ammunition can be found as early as the Early Access Launch Update.
- Hinterland released a teaser image of the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) in their News Update shortly before the Wintermute Redux update.
- An early screenshot showed the [Spray Paint](./Spray%20Paint.md) with a blue cap instead of the orange cap in the final release.

Several icons/textures for items can be found in the game files as far back as the alpha builds, yet these items have not been seen or used in game yet. They are considered cut content. Some gear icons can be spawned but do not have real gameplay functionality.
- The Wolf Carcass is a Wolf Carcass that can be carried around and harvested, likely for testing reasons.
- Newsprint Insulation can be harvested for a Newsprint, also likely for testing purposes.

> “**The first man to attempt escape from Blackrock, Bill Cutty is a something of a local legend. No trace of him was ever found. Word of his possible success only reached the prison by way of the cryptic letters received by his former cellmates.**”

This cave is best accessed by going down the road from the prison, then taking a left, followed by a right near two pickup trucks. As with most caves, this one provides a warmth bonus and can be used to cure hides. Its most notable feature is the dead prison guard outside, which can be looted to yield the [Blackrock Infirmary Medication](./Blackrock%20Infirmary%20Medication.md) needed to treat [Franklin](./Franklin.md) in the first mission of Episode 4. The cave also has a leaf bed, which provides a small warmth bonus. Be careful when visiting, for a pack of [wolves](./Wolf.md) prowls the area.

**Daisy Chaining** is a fan made gameplay term (similar to [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md), and [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md)) that refers to the practice of using [Torches](./Torch.md) to move a fire from one location to another, and to keep warm along the way, whilst using the least [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) resources as possible. This practice helps conserve [Wood Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md), [Cardboard Matches](./Cardboard%20Matches.md), and [Firestrikers](./Firestriker.md) that may already be in short supply, deters wolves from attacking you, as well as to preserve resources for late game runs.

Daisy Chaining is primarily more useful on higher difficulties [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) games (Interloper, [As the Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md)) in order to keep a starting player with low [Warmth](./Warmth.md) Clothing from freezing, as they move from location to location in order to scavenge materials to improve their odds of survival. Lower difficulty options tend to be more forgiving in terms of starting clothing, available clothing and resources, and overall lower [Needs](./Needs.md) restrictions, and is thus less useful of a gameplay tactic.
Even on easier gameplay settings, Daisy Chaining is a useful gameplay strategy for late game Fire Starting resource preservation.

Daisy Chaining begins when a player creates a fire in a [Campfire](./Campfire.md) or other Firebox. By adding more fuel, the player can pull multiple Torches out and store them for later use. Once a player has enough Torches, the last lit Torch that is pulled out is then used as a source of light and heat to keep a player warm in their travels (albeit temporarily if they have low Warmth Clothing).

As the player travels throughout the game world, great care must be kept to keep the lit Torch from being blown out by strong winds, or being extinguished by waterfalls. Players should also avoid hostile [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) in their travels, as this could extinguish the Torch early. It is also recommended to collect Fuel in order to create a new fire for later use.

When the overall Condition of the Torch begins to reach its end point, the player then tosses the lit Torch onto the ground and then procures another Torch from their inventory. Then, by walking up to and interacting with the dying Torch, the player can pass the fire of their dying Torch to the newer, higher condition one present in their hand.

This practice of chaining fires can continue until the player runs out of spare Torches to pass on the flame, or finds a suitable location to warm up. It is then advised to create a Fire with the currently lit Torch with any spare Fuel found along the way, to either create more Torches or to make use of the dying flame in order to cook Food/Drinks or boil Water.

The chain will end at some point, either by the player's hands or by the environment, but can be started again once enough Fuel is present to procure more Torches, but the player must use another match to start a new chain.

**Damaged Tracks** are sections of train tracks that are highly damaged on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md). They appear as warped, rusted, and chipped train track, with damaged cross ties. Driving over them can damage the [Prototype Train's](./Prototype%20Train.md) Wheels.

- Full reverse or full acceleration at speed 1 will cause an intense amount of screeching and train bobbling, resulting in condition damage to the wheels. The louder the screeching of metal becomes, the more damage is being done to the Wheels.
- Faster train movement will cause exponentially increased levels of damage to the wheels, up to 28% condition loss or more on one section of damaged track.
- The track section can be repaired if you have a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), and do not require Scrap Metal. Each repair section takes 2 hours and repairs the tracks completely.

- Alternatively, you can avoid repairing the tracks and damaging the train by alternating between speed settings 1 and Neutral to slowly move the train. This will prevent any damage to the Wheels when passing through this hazard.
- Sometimes a parallel track can be found that prevents contact with these rails to begin with. Spending some time to use them can help preserve your train's condition in the long run.

Most items will gradually **decay** over time in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. Tools degrade only when used, while [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), [Clothing](./Clothing.md), and some [Materials](./Materials.md) decay over time.
All materials, tools, clothing, and food items have a condition amount ranging from \*100-0%.

Items with \*0% decay will feature a red **RUINED** message in the inventory menu and cannot be repaired. Ruined items can only broken down for materials or disposed of (although food items can still be eaten at the risk of [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md)).

Items that are Ruined while in the player's inventory and are then placed inside containers **WILL DISAPPEAR** from the game world forever, unless they can be harvested. This can be useful to remove Ruined repair items ([Sewing Kits](./Sewing%20Kit.md), [Whetstones](./Whetstone.md), [Fishing Tackles](./Fishing%20Tackle.md)) or other commonly found tools ([Flare](./Flare.md), [Canister](./Canister.md), ect.)

How fast items decay over time depends on the item, outdoors or indoors, whether a clothing item is worn or not, and the selected difficulty. Typically, food stored outdoors will decay slowest, whereas the opposite (indoors) will decay the fastest. Notable exceptions are canned food and soda.

Using Stalker difficulty as a base, items decay at 80% on Voyageur and 25% as fast on Pilgrim. Interloper items decay at 200%. The corpses of animals killed by the player will decay in three days, no matter the difficulty level.
The decay values in the tables below are based on Stalker difficulty and are extracted from the game files.

[Food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) decays at different rates, depending on whether it is stored outside or inside. Currently, the game also considers sheltered locations without a loading screen, such as the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md), the [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md) or caves, to be **outside**.

Only painkillers, antibiotics and water purification tablets decay over time. Fortunately, there are craftable alternatives ([Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md), [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md)) that do not decay, and otherwise, one may trade for them with the [Trader](./Trader.md). [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md) only decays when used, similar to tools.
Storing these supplies inside does not alter the rate of decay. Ruined meds may still be used through the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md), and will not stack if dropped and picked up.

Tools will only decay condition when they're used. Once their condition goes below a set threshold, they gain a chance to break on use that increases linearly as the condition falls below the threshold.
Tools used to craft recipes, harvest carcasses, and clear ice holes will decay condition over time.
| Name | Crafting (%/hour) | Harvesting animals (%/hour) | Clearing ice fishing hole (%) |

Weapons decay, but only when fired. Once their condition goes below a set threshold, they gain a chance to break on use that increases linearly as the condition falls below the threshold.

[Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md), [Manufactured Arrows](./Manufactured%20Arrow.md), and [Fire Hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) decay, but only when they're used. Total arrow durability is variable and depends on a material table to determine it's condition loss; with the hardness of the material and the angle at which the arrow impacts the target determining the amount of degradation received. After a hit takes an arrow's condition below 0% it will turn into it's broken variant then fall to the ground where it may be retrieved.

**Decorations** is a section of the Backpack in the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) that contains all items that can be carried around and placed inside an interior as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature. The following Decorations cannot be crafted, but are already present within many interiors. They can be moved as normal while in Customization Mode, but can also be placed inside the player's backpack and carried around between [safehouses](./Safehouse.md).
- When taken, this type of Decoration has a unique icon and weight, cannot be harvested for materials, and is placed in the Decorations section of the Backpack inventory.

- When destroyed, they are permanently removed from the interior. Caution is advised when doing this, as destroying these Decorations means they cannot be crafted/taken from another location to be placed into another interior.

- Lootable Decorations cannot be destroyed in the player's Inventory or in a [Safehouse Decoration Box](./Safehouse%20Decoration%20Box.md). They must be placed in a Saferoom before the option appears.
- There can be multiple versions of an item with the same name, but with different weights and models.
- Some of these items display a different name when examined in Customization Mode (ex [Backpack](./Backpack.md) is "Back Pack" or [Metal Lamp](./Metal%20Lamp.md) is "Lamp").

- Carrying multiple Decorations adds up quickly. The heaviest Decorations are 5.00kg, while the lightest tend to be 0.05kg. Using a [Travois](./Travois.md) can be helpful for transporting large amounts of heavy Decorations.

The following items are found in some interiors and can be moved around in Customization Mode, but cannot be placed into the player's inventory. This makes them specific only to the interior they are found in.
- Moderately large/very large objects (large pipes, [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md), whale bones in [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md), girders, live wires) cannot be destroyed.
- If the option to destroy large highlighted items is present, this will permanently remove them from the interior. Caution is advised when doing this, as destroyed items cannot be returned.
- 90% destroyable items are Containers or Harvestable Interactable Objects, and are not listed here due to having their own dedicated pages.
- Destroying Harvestable items is faster than harvesting them, but the player does not gain resources.
- Larger [Crates](./Crate.md) and [Cardboard Boxes](./Cardboard%20Box.md) are destroyed rather than picked up as Lootable Decorative items.
- Most items take 12-30 minutes to destroy, with the largest items taking the most time to destroy.
- Unsearched containers or containers that have items stored inside cannot be destroyed, and produce an error message. They must be searched/cleared out before they can be destroyed.

- [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) and [Corpses](./Corpse.md) are the only container that cannot be destroyed, but rather "Respectfully Removed." A candle icon will display as the Corpse is removed over time.

The **Decorative Art** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.

A small, octagonal portrait of scraped together wood painted and shaped in the image of a mountain backdrop, Decorative Art can be crafted anywhere by the player, but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).

Once crafted, the item is automatically placed into the player's inventory. It can only be placed on walls when in Customization Mode. It can later be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory or destroyed (yielding no resources).

Suggested locations to gather enough wood and materials for the achievements are [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) and [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md). Be aware that the fire duration is limited to 12 hours and you have to add more fuel. Be sure to choose an appropriate place for the campfire in order to avoid windblow. While Hibernia and the Dam have plenty of wood, neither has a spot protected from wind from all angles. Hauling the wood to a nearby cave will give you a protected place to keep your fire burning without the wind stealing 10 hours of burn time and extinguishing your fire. Once done don't forget to pick the [charcoal](./Charcoal.md) and to dance in circle around the fire to celebrate the reached achievement!

**Wintermute:** Yes A **Deer Carcass** is a harvestable object found after [Hunting](./Hunting.md) a [Deer](./Deer.md). They can occasionally be found as ravaged carcasses dispersed across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), or can be left after Deer are hunted by [Wolves](./Wolf.md). [Crows](./Crow.md) will fly around a Deer Carcass and always drop 3-5 [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) around the carcass at any time.

Depending on whether the player hunted a [Deer](./Deer.md) or a Doe, a fresh deer carcass contains between 8.00 and 12.50 kg of raw meat, two pieces of [animal fat](./Animal%20Fat.md) as well as two fresh [guts](./Fresh%20Gut.md) and one fresh [Deer Hide](./Fresh%20Deer%20Hide.md). The type of deer only influences the meat amount but doesn't change the materials drop. Carcasses can be harvested barehanded or with a variety of tools, each changing the time it will take to harvest the drop.

A carcass can be either untouched or ravaged. An untouched carcass has not been harvested by the player nor eaten by a wolf. Once the player harvests something from the carcass, no matter how little, it will become ravaged. Carcasses found in the wild will spawn already ravaged while the deer hunted by wolves will start as untouched but will become ravaged very soon after the kill once the wolf begins the feeding animation. A fresh untouched carcass cannot be harvested barehanded; only ravaged carcasses can be.

Carcasses will slowly freeze, increasing the time needed for the player to harvest its contents. Meat left on the carcass decays quickly, regardless of the carcass freezing. Starting a fire near a frozen carcass will thaw it, making it faster to harvest by increments. Harvesting tools include the Hacksaw, the Hatchet, the Hunting Knife, the Improvised Knife, the Improvised Hatchet, the Cougar Knife and the Survival Knife. Each has a different harvesting time, influenced by the [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) skill and how frozen the carcass is.

A carcass can also be quartered into bags of meat to be taken elsewhere for harvesting. The quarters are heavier due to the inclusion of parts not otherwise used, but this does make for easier transport and less time at the site. Frozen carcasses are more difficult to quarter.
Buck and Doe carcasses contain slightly differing amounts of meat upon their corpses, with Bucks having slightly higher amounts of raw Venison.

Two caves are present at Deer Clearing: the [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) transition cave is in the south, which is a winding cavern with many dead ends. This cave can provide shelter from the elements. The other cave is shallow and may yield containers with loot, including a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), [Dog Food](./Dog%20Food.md), and [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md).

Two [Green Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) as well as some [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) can be found in front of these caves. True to its name, 0-8 [Deer](./Deer.md) may be found in the area. A possible [bear](./Bear.md) can occasionally patrol a nearby area. [Wolves](./Wolf.md) that patrol nearby may come near the area to hunt Deer, providing free meat opportunities. Wood limbs and [sticks](./Stick.md) are abundant.

**Deer Quarter**s are sections harvested from a [Deer](./Deer.md) carcass. Deer quarters can be obtained by going into the harvest menu after killing a deer. While in the harvest screen, switch to the right side of the screen putting you in the quartering screen. Unlike harvesting the meat directly, you cannot quarter a deer with your bare hands, even if the carcass is not frozen. You cannot quarter an animal if it is 50% frozen or more.
Unlike the misleading term "quarter", a deer carcass will have 4-5 quarters, and having five makes it technically a fifth, not a quarter.

When a deer is quartered, you also get the [Fresh Gut](./Fresh%20Gut.md) and [Fresh Deer Hide](./Fresh%20Deer%20Hide.md). Quartering a deer will always take 1 in-game hour, making it more time efficient. However, you still need to harvest the quarters for usable [Venison (Raw)](./Venison%20%28Raw%29.md). Any remaining raw meat left inside the bag will be lost if the Quarter's Condition reaches 0%, with bags spoiling within 1 day of harvesting.
Also, only 50% of a quarters weight will be useable meat, more than likely as a drawback for the quick harvesting time.

**Deer** are medium sized grazers in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. They are a valuable resource, offering the potential for substantial amounts of meat and materials for relatively little risk.

Deer are timid wanderers that can be found in all main regions, as well as in some transition zones. They spend much of their time meandering through the snow but will bound away whenever they detect the slightest hint of danger.

[Wolves](./Wolf.md) are the main predator of deer and will stalk and chase them down on sight. Acquiring a deer for yourself may require stealing a fresh kill from a hungry wolf, particularly early in a the game. Another option is to search for the ravaged deer carcasses that spawn in all major [regions](./Region.md), which will have [Crows](./Crow.md) circling overhead. These carcasses do not have much meat on them, but do have one hide and two guts, making them a good source of clothing in the early game.

Deer are a great source of food, typically yielding more than 9kg of nutritious [meat](./Venison%20%28Raw%29.md). Additionally [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md) and [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md) can be crafted from [Cured Deer Hide](./Cured%20Deer%20Hide.md) and their [Cured Gut](./Cured%20Gut.md) may be employed in constructing several useful items.

Oddly, the player's sprint ability is actually sufficient to almost keep pace with a running deer. This is most useful for keeping them in sight during bleedout from a gunshot or arrow wound, as it is not currently possible to take down prey with close-quarters attacks.

Most Interloper players will want to harvest five deer carcasses soon after they get a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md), in order to make the deerskin pants and boots, as these are the easiest pieces of animal clothing to make. The guts are also useful for making a [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), which is the only sustainable ranged weapon in Interloper, along with [Snares](./Snare.md), which make catching rabbits much easier.

![Deer carcass](../assets/Dead_deer.png)_Deer carcass_ A fresh [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md) contains between 8.00 and 10.00 kg of raw meat, as well as two guts and one Deer Hide. Carcasses will slowly freeze, increasing the time needed for the player to harvest its contents. Meat left on the carcass decays quickly, regardless of the carcass freezing. Starting a fire near a frozen carcass will thaw it.

A carcass can also be quartered into bags of meat to be taken elsewhere for harvesting. The quarters are heavier due to the inclusion of parts not otherwise used, but this does make for easier transport and less time at the site. Frozen carcasses are more difficult to quarter.
Stag and Doe carcasses contain slightly differing amounts of meat upon their corpses, with Stags generall having higher amounts of raw Venison.

Deer have two paces: walking and fleeing. Typically they stick to a defined area, wandering about randomly within its invisible borders. Occasionally, a wandering deer will pause and bow its head as if to graze. They will sprint away a short distance if they detect a nearby predator or person but will still try to return to their designated area. If they are spooked a second time, they tend to run much farther. Occasionally deer will double back while running and may actually run right at the player without turning away.
Instinctively herd animals, deer are usually seen in groups of up to five, and gravitate back to their fellows after being chased.

If a wolf detects a deer, it will start stalking it in a manner similar to when it detects the player. If the deer manages to outrun the wolf or break line of sight for some time, the wolf will give up and return to it's original hunting grounds. However, if the wolf gets close enough to the deer, it will start relentlessly chasing it down until the deer dies. If a wolf gives chase in this way, other wolves are encouraged to also chase the same deer. This can result in the deer actually being killed by a wolf different from the one that started chasing it. Only the killing wolf will feed, all others will resume patrols.

Carefully driving deer towards wolves can act as a distraction to briefly clear an area of the predators. Alternatively, the player may attempt to drive away or kill a wolf feeding on a recently downed deer, thereby allowing the player to harvest most of the carcass(es) while conserving ammunition.
- Other Deer will generally stay close to one another in a herd as high as 2-4 Deer, but will run away if another Deer is startled/attacked. The surviving Deer eventually return to grazing.
- [Wolf](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) will stalk and eat a Deer if they get the chance. A fleeing Wolf will also scare a Deer away.
- [Bear](./Bear.md) and [Cougar](./Cougar.md), will not attack a Deer, but Deer always run away when one is nearby.
- Darkwalker: Deer always fly away in fear if the Darkwalker gets too close to them. [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) will eventually kill all animals if it builds up enough.

- The Player: Deer will always run off if they detect the player. If a Deer is shot by the player, they will begin bleeding and will run non-stop to get away from the player before eventually dropping dead. While running, they will often erratically run around in circles in their terrorized wounded state, making tracking them harder.

The only possible interaction with deer is to scare them. They run away from most everything. Once the player is close enough to be detected by the deer, it will run. Hearing gunshots and shooting an arrow into the snow near them is also sufficient to get them to bolt. Crouching and remaining still will lower the range at which the player is detected. Remaining still and crouched when within a nearby deer's field of vision also reduce the chance of being detected.

Deer may be driven along by repeatedly scaring them. They tend to run directly away, so positioning yourself opposite them from where you would like them to go is often sufficient to steer them properly.

It is possible to kill a deer with one shot, though this is a function of scoring a "critical hit". Deer not critically shot will typically run, dripping blood, until they die. It may be noted that while the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) may cause more critical hits and is therefore more likely to drop a deer immediately, the Survival Bow does cause significantly faster bleedouts, which reduce the length of chasing and tracking.
Critical hits cause the animal to instantly die after being hit by a shot. The following table contains the critical hit chance based on the location that was shot on the animal.
| Weapon — Head | Weapon — Neck | Critical Hit Chance — Torso | Critical Hit Chance — Hips | Critical Hit Chance — Limb | Critical Hit Chance | Critical Hit Chance |
| [Hunting Rifle icon](../assets/Hunting_Rifle_icon.png) | [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) | Guaranteed | 50% | 40% | 25% | 10% |
| [Distress Pistol icon](../assets/Distress_Pistol_icon.png) | [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) | Guaranteed | 50% | 40% | 25% | 10% |
| [Survival Bow icon](../assets/Survival_Bow_icon.png) | [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) | Guaranteed | 50% | 40% | 25% | 10% |
| [Revolver icon](../assets/Revolver_icon.png) | [Revolver](./Revolver.md) | Guaranteed | 25% | 20% | 13% | 5% |

![Wounded deer running away](../assets/Deer_running_away.png)_Wounded deer running away_ All shots cause bleeding wounds. Deer will bleed out according to which area they were shot in. Bleeding wounds do not stack. That is, multiple shots to the same area will not make it bleed out any faster. Shooting a deer in an area that bleeds faster than a previous wound will cause it to bleed out as if the faster wound were caused first.
| Weapon — Head | Weapon — Neck | Bleed Out — Torso | Bleed Out — Hips | Bleed Out — Limb | Bleed Out | Bleed Out |
| [Hunting Rifle icon](../assets/Hunting_Rifle_icon.png) | [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) | Instant | 15 min | 45 min | 60 min | 240 min |
| [Survival Bow icon](../assets/Survival_Bow_icon.png) | [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) | Instant | 10 min | 22 min | 40 min | 120 min |
| [Revolver icon](../assets/Revolver_icon.png) | [Revolver](./Revolver.md) | Instant | 20 min | 60 min | 80 min | 320 min |
| [Distress Pistol icon](../assets/Distress_Pistol_icon.png) | [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) | Instant | 8 min | 15 min | 30 min | 80 min |

The simplest strategy for killing deer is to herd them toward wolves. Wolves always kill deer once they catch them, so no long tracking is required. Once a wolf kills the deer, the decision must be made how to deal with the wolf. Scaring it away with fire or a thrown torch or stone is possible, though the latter two options may not work. Another option is simply waiting for it to eat its fill and coming back for the leftovers. The downside to waiting is that there will be little meat left once the wolf has finished its meal.
Yet another option is to kill the wolf with a ranged weapon while it is distracted or provoke it to attack and fatally injure it.

- Crouching allows one to travel with less chance of being detected, so crouching, combined with positioning oneself in the path of a walking deer and not moving, can provide opportunities for ambush for a single close range shot at a deer's head. Sprint to keep animal in sight if it flees with a bleeding wound. If the player loses track before the animal dies, the blood trail may help relocate it. Otherwise, the player may have to search the area the deer was running towards if too much time has passed.
- Longer range shooting is also quite possible once one learns how properly to aim. Deer movement is rather simple while walking and therefore predictable before they bolt.

- Flushing deer to run can also be used counter-intuitively to get them to run towards the player, allowing for close range shots. Fleeing deer occasionally double back, especially if their paths are blocked by terrain. A dynamic shot may then be taken on the deer as it charges toward or immediately after as it is moving away. Broadside attempts may be difficult to time correctly, but are also possible.

- The Deer appears to be based off the [White-Tailed Deer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-tailed_deer) (**_Odocoileus virginianus_**), a common North American Cervidae. They are not to be confused with Elk or Caribou, a much larger but different species of Cervidae.
- [General] Fixed a crash that could occur if a Stag or Rabbit was removed from the world, while being chased by a Predator.
- [Gameplay] Stags now check for collision when falling after death, to avoid falling into objects.
- [WINTERMUTE] Removed deer carcass from the Survival Bowl sequence in Episode One that could cause a crash.
- [Survival Mode] Prevented deer from fleeing to inaccessible areas in the Ravine transition
- [Wintermute] Fixed deer carcass disappearing at the opening of Episode One if Player interacts with, saves, then reloads game.
- [Both] Reduced Deer carcass quartering time to 60 minutes, to improve balance against Bear and Moose quartering times.
- Made deer corpses in Desolation Point cave start unfrozen, and made corpses thaw when inside caves.

- All wildlife spawns are now more dynamic, and will change over the course of a game. Wolves, Deer, and Rabbits all refresh on different intervals, reflecting their relative mobility and travel/migration patterns.
- Wolves will now stop to feed on fresh Deer kill. The amount of meat that can be retrieved from a carcass is affected by how long a Wolf feeds on it.
- Updated all Wolf spawn regions, and added new Wolf and Deer spawn regions to the world.
- Randomized all Corpses (Deer and Human) in Lake Region, apart from a few that remain for environmental storytelling purposes.
- Added a new Raw Material type: Leather. Leather is required to repair boots. It can be harvested from existing boots, or from Deer.

**Deerskin Boots** are a type of craftable [Clothing](./Clothing.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Deerskin boots are among the best boots available. [Insulated Boots](./Insulated%20Boots.md) and [Ski Boots](./Ski%20Boots.md) offer more warmth and windchill, but have higher mobility penalty and weight.

Deerskin boots are comparable to the rare [Mukluks](./Mukluks.md), which are 0.5kg lighter but offer slightly less protection and less waterproof (Deerskin/Insulated Boots 50% vs. Mukluks 40%). The primary advantage of Deerskin Boots possess over Mukluks is their reliability in acquisition: they can be crafted in all game modes (including [Interloper](./Interloper.md)), and do not require [Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md) for repairs.

> “**Warm, supple, and tough. Offers a great combination of mobility and warmth. Wear these to feel like the Mad Max of the North.**”
**Deerskin Pants** are a type of craftable [Clothing](./Clothing.md) made from [Cured Deer Hide](./Cured%20Deer%20Hide.md) and [Cured Gut](./Cured%20Gut.md).

Deerskin Pants are less warm compared to [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md), yet require more materials to craft. However, in an early [Interloper](./Interloper.md) game when the player has only a single pair of [Jeans](./Jeans.md), crafting the deerskin pants may be slightly preferable because they can be _added_ onto the player's existing outfit (two slots for outer legs), whereas using the Deerskin Boots would require swapping out whatever boots the player is already wearing.

They offer the highest protection, water- and windproofing bonuses of all available outer legwear and are only surpassed by the rare [Snow Pants](./Snow%20Pants.md) and the hard to obtain [Wolfskin Pants](./Wolfskin%20Pants.md) in terms of warmth. They are, however, also second only to Wolfskin Pants in terms of weight, and are tied for both the worst warmth-to-weight ratio and mobility penalty.

Deerskin pants are an excellent outer layer if combined with lighter pants that focus on warmth bonus or warmth-to-weight ratio. Wearing two pairs of deerskin pants is possible but will add up to significant mobility reduction and encumbrance.
Since they can be repaired with deer hides instead of cloth they are arguably one of the best choice for late game leg clothing, alongside Wolfskin Pants.

They are possible to obtain reliably and relatively early in the game by harvesting [Deer Carcasses](./Deer%20Carcass.md) that can be found at several locations in all [regions](./Region.md) or obtained by actively [hunting](./Hunting.md).

A series of ruined buildings near the bay, the area is located almost dead center of the map. It is likely the first point of interest the player will see on the horizon when they leave the [Lighthouse (Port Remnant)](./Lighthouse%20%28Port%20Remnant%29.md). The area is an old series of whaling warehouses and docks.

A series of planks leads to the upper room overlooking the floor, with a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md), hay [Bed](./Bed.md), and [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) (the only one on Anna Island) inside.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: **Details**
**Connecting Regions:** [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) (via [Old Island Connector](./Crumbling%20Highway.md))
**Hazards and Survivability:** Lots of shelter and moderate weather, but prey game is limited and there is abundant hostile wildlife.
> “**For intermediate players. Several key shelters, plenty of hostile wildlife, and harsh weather conditions to be found around these remnants of a once-thriving whaling industry.**”

Desolation Point is described as a stretch of coastal highway pockmarked with the abandoned remnants of a formerly thriving whaling industry. It can be found by going to the end of the [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), passing through the Commuter's Lament, and continuing onward through [Crumbling Highway](./Crumbling%20Highway.md) and No. 3 Coal Mine.

Desolation Point is one of the smallest regions in the game: walking from the end of the [Abandoned Mine](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md) to [Broken Bridge](./Broken%20Bridge%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md) takes roughly 7-8 minutes in real time. Despite this, it has 16 locations to discover including the connector mine (named "No. 3 Coal Mine") with Crumbling Highway. The region's small size can be useful in poor weather, as it is much harder to get lost here than in a more open region such as [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) or [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), and shelter is rarely far away.
Desolation Point has a [explorable cave](./Cave%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md) that might be inhabited by a wolf.

| - [Abandoned Mine No. 5](./Abandoned%20Mine%20No.%205.md) (2 entrances) - [Blocked Highway](./Blocked%20Highway.md) - [Broken Bridge (Desolation Point location)](./Broken%20Bridge%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md) - [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) - [Katie's Secluded Corner](./Katie%27s%20Secluded%20Corner.md) - [Little Island](./Little%20Island.md) | - [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md) - [Matt's Truck](./Matt%27s%20Truck.md) - [Stone Church](./Stone%20Church.md) - [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md) - [Waterfall](./Waterfall.md) - To No. 3 Coal Mine (Region Transition to [No. 3 Coal Mine](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md)) |
- A single [Cave](./Cave%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md) located close to the Waterfall.

There is an abundance of hostile wildlife in this region; 1 bear and 5-8 wolves patrol within this small and snaking stretch of coastal land. While firearm resources, bow resources, and non-predator fauna spawns may be limited, there are often many crafting resources and sometimes a fair number of medical supplies, depending on the difficulty level. This, in turn, can allow the player to win more wolf struggles and reserve rifle ammunition for bears.
For players who own the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC, this is one of the few regions that doesn't have a [cougar](./Cougar.md) spawn.
Although Desolation Point is listed as a moderate difficulty region to survive in, largely due to its predator density, with good planning, surviving here long-term is very much possible.

One challenge that may arise with living in Desolation Point long-term is the relative lack of game, especially on Stalker and Interloper where [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) are a concern. While there are a number of [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) groves scattered throughout the map, along with a possible [Moose](./Moose.md) spawn near [Matt's Truck](./Matt%27s%20Truck.md) and a few ravaged [Deer Carcasses](./Deer%20Carcass.md), living deer aren't so easy to find. Only 2-4 [Deer](./Deer.md) spawn in the region, and they are found near [Little Island](./Little%20Island.md) and the frozen bay west of the [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md). The region's food sources are further limited by its lack of [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md). Ice fishing using [Ice Fishing holes](./Ice%20Fishing.md#Free-Form_Ice_Fishing_Holes) is possible along almost the entire coastal area, with locations like [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md) and [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) providing plenty of shelter within the immediate area of suitable ice.

A good long-term strategy for food is to set out as many [Snares](./Snare.md) as possible to catch rabbits, and to make ice fishing holes near bases. [Fishing Lures](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28Wire%20Bundle%29.md) and [Fishing Tip-Ups](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md) can help automate the fishing process, and there are sometimes fish and animal carcasses that wash ashore and can be recovered by [beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md). With a bit of careful planning, players should be able to acquire plenty of food to avoid starvation, even on Interloper difficulty.

With the release of [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), Desolation Point has become home to several [salt deposits](./Salt%20Deposit.md), which can be useful to help [preserve the fish](./Cured%20Fish.md) and [predator meat](./Cured%20Meat.md), providing for ideal travel food and eliminating any risk of [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md). The one challenge is that the [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) required to build the [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md) and [Meat Curing Box](./Meat%20Curing%20Box.md) can't be found anywhere close to the region.

With [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) offering enormous amounts of harvestable materials, the mines offering lots of [Coal](./Coal.md), and the [Forge](./Forge.md) in [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md). maintaining and replacing tools should not be too difficult in Desolation Point. Hibernia also offers a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), and extra supplies for crafting and repair (such as saplings and harvestable clothes) can wash ashore and be found via [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md). Overall, the region is good for players who intend to do a lot of crafting.

One of Desolation Point's most notable features is its isolated location on the far east of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). While this may not be a concern for players who like to stay put in one area, it can be more problematic for players who prefer to travel around the island and lead a more nomadic lifestyle. As a point of reference, travelling from the [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md) or [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) in neighbouring [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) takes about 15 minutes in real-time, or about three in-game hours.
The lighthouse has a bed, a potbelly stove, plenty of storage and an amazing view of most of the region, weather permitting. This can be helpful spotting wolves in the immediate area.

Two walking bridges connect the lighthouse to the main access road. There is also a rear path through a broken fence behind the lighthouse (use caution), that provides a shortcut to the Riken and the Hibernia processing plant. A number of wolves may patrol the entry road or along the ice below.

Hibernia Processing features large amounts of reclaimed wood, metal, and numerous trailers with beds. Plenty of storage is available, and a workbench and fire barrel are located downstairs. Many key tools can be found there: including the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), and [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md). Multiple wolves and a bear can be close by, often just outside the the compound's perimeter fence.

The Riken is a beached ship that features a [Forge](./Forge.md), which can be used for cooking and metalworking if fueled with [Coal](./Coal.md). It can be very cold without high quality [Clothing](./Clothing.md), but its rooms and upper decks contain beds, storage, fuel, coal and items which can be broken down into [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md). Several green Wooden Crates can be found in the ship's belly, and when broken may contain useful items.

A key function of The Riken is that once industrially produced tools are depleted ([Hunting Knives](./Hunting%20Knife.md), [Hatchets](./Hatchet.md), and Bullets), its Forge can be used to craft makeshift versions with [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), [Cloth](./Cloth.md), and [Coal](./Coal.md) (the [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md), and [Arrowhead](./Arrowhead.md)). The Riken's Forge is one of only four in the game; the others are in the barn of the [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), at [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md), and, with the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion, in the basement of the [Main Hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md).

The ship's uppermost deck can serve as a vantage point to look for and/or hunt [Wolves](./Wolf.md), [Deer](./Deer.md), or a [Bear](./Bear.md) that wander nearby. Also, [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) for scavenging and [Little Island](./Little%20Island.md) to hunt rabbits and collect firewood are close by.

Diminished Form is a permanent Affliction unique to [Misery Mode](./Misery.md) which occurs from Stage 1 Misery (Day 2). It permanently reduces the maximum carry weight of the survivor and grants a [Mobility Penalty](./Stamina.md) to sprinting. Additionally it reduces the chance per-attack during a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) that the hostile wildlife will flee.
Note: Diminished Form does 'not' affect Climbing Stamina, if starting a climb at 100% of **_current_** Stamina, similar to other Stamina penalties like wearing [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md).

The **Distress Pistol Kit** is an item found at the beginning of [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) in the mission [Memories](./Memories.md). It is found inside the [Jackrabbit Remote Transport](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md), and is one of 3 extra items that can be placed inside Mackenzie's Floatplane (along with [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) and [Astrid's Backpack](./Astrid%27s%20Backpack.md)) before takeoff.
If the player chooses to put the Distress Pistol Kit in the plane's hatch, it will break open once the plane crashes and following items can be recovered for use:

The Distress Pistol is the only weapon available in Episode 1, yet another one (along with the same amount of Flare Shells) can be obtained from the [Highway Robbery](./Highway%20Robbery%20%28mission%29.md) stash. It's only useful to scare off or kill the [Wolves](./Wolf.md) in the area, though the torch-and-rock method is a far cheaper way of scaring them and the extra meat is unnecessary given the abundance of food in Episode 1. It's also less useful on Green Survivor, as Wolves always flee from the player on sight.

The **Distress Pistol** (often called a **"Flare Gun"**) is a single-shot weapon in _The Long Dark_.

The Distress Pistol is a break action, single-shot weapon which fires [Flare Shells](./Flare%20Shell.md) (not conventional [Flares](./Flare.md), or [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md)) as glowing red balls of light. Similar to the [Revolver](./Revolver.md), Distress Pistols serve primarily as defensive weapons since their report upon firing will frighten all nearby [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md): notably including [Bear](./Bear.md) and [Moose](./Moose.md) (the only item to deter both charging animals guaranteed, assuming a direct hit). Wildlife struck by a round will either die immediately, or bleed to death over the following hours (Moose and Cougar being the exceptions since they don't bleed). Unlike all other animals, the [Cougar](./Cougar.md) seems to have no fear of Distress Pistol shots.

Rounds from the Distress Pistol are accurate but follow a heavy arcing trajectory, similar to that of thrown [Stones](./Stone.md) (and greater than [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) from the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md)); this, along with the Distress Pistol's effectiveness at scaring nearly all Wildlife, makes landing hits with the weapon challenging, especially from long distances or while animals are moving.

Rounds fired from the Distress Pistol produce large amounts of red light and burn for 20 minutes (in-game), during which [Wolves](./Wolf.md) and [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) will be unable to approach the round's landing site. Unlike Revolvers or Hunting Rifles, spent Flare Shells casings cannot be collected and reused to make more Flare Shells, as they do not appear at the player's feet once ejected from the Distress Pistol. Flare Shells cannot be crafted at an [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md).
Single Flare Shells may be found rarely inside of containers on Pilgrim, Voyageur and Stalker modes.

The Distress Pistol is a weapon can be equipped from the Radial Menu, the Weapon Hotkey ("2") or directly from the Inventory. While equipped: Aim ("RMB") and fire ("LMB"). Reload with "R", and "H" to Holster (By default). The weapon is single-shot and holds only one round, so it must be reloaded manually each time it is fired.

The Distress Pistol has unique 2 reloading animations after firing: the normal reload wherin a shell is ejected, the Pistol is closed, and pressing "R" starts a reload, and a second animation wherin the Pistol is reloaded halfway through its firing animation by simply pressing "R" after the Shell is ejected, thus loading a Shell early and shortening reloading times.

Launched rounds fire at a low velocity and arc heavily before impacting a solid surface. Rounds hitting hard surfaces at an oblique angle may glance or bounce before coming to rest. Flares which hit surfaces, especially soft targets at perpendicular angles stick in place. Rounds burn brightly for 20 game minutes and emits localized smoke but may not be retrieved or used to start [fires](./Campfire.md). Wolves and Timberwolves will avoid the immediate proximity of a rounds burning (~15m) (the same behavior as with dropped/thrown emergency Flare, Marine Flare, Torch and Campfires). Spent rounds remain visible even after they have burnt out.

In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md): [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) during the mission [Coming Storm](./Coming%20Storm.md), firing a Distress Pistol close enough to a [Crash Survivor](./Crash%20Survivor.md)'s location (their circle on the map) will result in them responding with a Distress Pistol shot of their own into the air, allowing [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) to find their location more easily.

Animals within earshot (~30 meters) of the report flee immediately, with the exception of the Cougar which has no fear of the Distress Pistol. Additional animals within visual of the impact site will also flee. The one exception is during the Aurora: if the shell doesn't hit, animals will continue their charge even after shooting the distress pistol.

Distress Pistol rounds which hit an animal will almost always kill. Either immediately (on a critical hit), or shortly after from [blood loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) (except [Moose](./Moose.md) and [Cougar](./Cougar.md) which cannot bleed out and cannot be critically hit with a Distress Pistol). While the animal is bleeding the burning round will remain attached to the fleeing animal for several in-game minutes, trailing smoke and glowing bright red.
Critical hits cause the animal to instantly die after being hit by a shot. The following table contains the critical hit chance based on the location that was shot on the animal.
