Distress Pistols are typically found inside orange [Emergency Kit](./Emergency%20Kit.md) cases accompanied by up to 8 Flare Shells but may be found caseless, next to a [corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md). (As it is in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md)) The Distress Pistol can also be found in a stockpiler's type of prepper cache on any difficulty other than Interloper/Misery.

- On a ledge south of [Anglers Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md). This ledge is _unreachable_ from the river level, requiring an approach from above by crossing [Runway Bridge](./Runaway%20Bridge.md), into the meadow area, and near the rope up to [High Meadow](./High%20Meadow.md)
- In a case inside the break room behind the main building (the one with the rope up) in the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md). This case is always _empty_
Note: only second and third spawn is present on Interloper/Misery, not guaranteed to spawn
- In a backpack leaning against a canoe on [Misanthropes Island](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md), on the side nearest to the [Waterfront Cottages](./Waterfront%20Cottages.md)
- Under a bunkbed on the second floor of [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md). Note this pistol spawns without a case or Flare Shells, but some may be found on a nearby shelf
- In a case at an unnamed cave below [builder's bridge](./Builder%27s%20Bridge.md) at river level. A rope at one end of the road is used to get down
Second spawn: In the bathtub inside [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) (not guaranteed to spawn)
- In a case inside the basement of the [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md), on a desk
- In a case inside the [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) Control Hut, on the shelf next to the door
- In a case inside Pleasant Valley Outbuildings barn, second floor on the metal shelf
- In a case located at the tail of crashed plane, where player can find a survivor in Episode 3 of Wintermute
- In a case next to a [corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) in the upper area of the [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md) of the crashed cargo plane, atop the [Summit](./Summit.md) (contains 3 flare shells)
- In a case, hidden at the west wall in the cavern with scaffolders in Forgotten Exploration tunnel
Note: guaranteed spawn, other difficulties have rifle spawn instead of distress pistol in Langston Mine
- In [The Hunted, Part One](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20One.md), there is a case in the [basement](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md) near where that scenario begins
- In [Hopeless Rescue](./Hopeless%20Rescue.md), all Distress Pistol and Flare Shell spawns are disabled except for the case inside the Tail Section of Timberwolf Mountain

- In [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) during the [first mission](./Memories.md) (inside the Hangar, before departure) [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) may choose to load a Distress Pistol Case onto his floatplane; if he does, then it will be available on the ground near [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) after [The Crash](./The%20Crash.md). Another second Distress Pistol with ammunition may be found by completing [Highway Robbery](./Highway%20Robbery.md)
- In [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) inside the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) a case is inside the first-floor bathroom

- In [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) at the Crash Site, Astrid can find a distress pistol with 7 rounds in one of the sections. One may also be found in the hallway of the [Community Center](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) after completing the Mission "[Fallen Star](./Fallen%20Star.md)"
- In [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), if playing on lower difficulties a Distress Pistol will spawn in the gatehouse by the exit of the [Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md)

- When loaded and held, the Distress Pistol's firing hammer is cocked. This is the only indicator that the weapon is loaded (other than the lit icon in the corner, which is white when loaded, and grey when unloaded), since similar to the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), the Distress Pistol is single-shot and numerically displays carried but not loaded ammunition (unlike the [Revolver](./Revolver.md) and [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md)). Distress Pistols display their loaded ammunition in the Inventory menu. Because of this, caution should be taken to verify the Distress Pistol is loaded before entering dangerous situations.

- One way to verify if the flare gun is loaded to look at the flare shell icon while the weapon his held. If the icon is a light grey in color, it is unloaded, if it is white, there is a shell loaded. This is also the same with the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), however it is less applicable because your character automatically "reloads" the bow after each shot.
- The [Hopeless Rescue](./Hopeless%20Rescue.md) Challenge requires the flare gun to complete its main objective.

- The flare round that is launched and glows is a model of the shell part of the ammunition that should have been left in the gun after firing. (Meaning the flare gun shouldn't be empty after firing, an empty shell should remain.)

- A bug was present (patch 1.72) between January 22nd and March 26th of 2020 which prevented Distress Pistol rounds from damaging animals in Survival and Wintermute. The result of this bug caused direct hits with the Distress Pistol to bounce harmlessly off animals and land on the ground, merely frightening them.

**Dockworker's Pie** is a food item in _The Long Dark_, it is learned from a unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) and is made with a [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md).

Dockworker's Pie is a relatively simple recipe requiring mostly common ingredients and featuring a powerful Condition restoring effect, similar to [Prepper's Pie](./Prepper%27s%20Pie.md). Compared with Prepper's Pie, Dockworker's Pie requires more artificial ingredients, with the most limited being [Potatoes](./Potato.md). [Coho Salmon](./Coho%20Salmon%20%28Raw%29.md) and [Rockfish](./Rockfish%20%28Raw%29.md) are both saltwater fish that can be acquired by [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) in any Coastal Region (e.g., Bleak Inlet), with Coho being 'uncommon' and Rockfish being 'rare' (note: rare fish can be increased in frequency with [Lures](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28disambiguation%29.md), at the cost of taking longer before a bite).

The Recipe Card for Dockworker's Pie is found inside of the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) [Workshop](./Workshop.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), which is sealed by an electronically locked door (requiring the key code found on a note in [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md), and an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md) at night to power the door). The Last Resort Cannery can be difficult to access: being very cold, windy and infested with a pack of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md).
Dockworker's Pie produces a [Scent](./Scent.md) that attracts [predators](./Wolf.md). It may be dropped as a [decoy](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys).

Consuming Dog Food restores a moderate amount of calories and small amount of hydration. _It cannot be warmed by a [fire](./Fire.md)._

Like other canned foods, Dog Food may be opened with a [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md) or [bladed tool](./Tools.md), or smashed open (with no tool) but spilling some of it's contents. If opened with a tool a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) is received after consuming the contents.
It has relatively high chance of causing [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) at low condition, compared to other canned foods.
- A possible explanation for Dog Food having such a high food poisoning chance, is the variance between animal grade and human grade foods.
- The side of the can lists "Ingredients: Turkey, Beef, Chicken, Water, Calcium, Vitamin A, Vitamin D, Vitamin K."
- Dog houses are occasionally found on the Island (like in [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md)), but dogs are never found.

**Don't Starve** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is obtained after keeping Calorie store ([Hunger](./Hunger.md)) from reaching 0 calories for 10 days in a single [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) game. Although it is easiest to obtain on [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md), there is generally enough manufactured food available in most regions early on that it will often be obtained through normal gameplay on [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md) and [Stalker](./Stalker.md).

| Characters | [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) / [Mathis](./Mathis.md) / [Vachon](./Vachon.md) / [Heller](./Heller.md) / [Jace](./Jace.md) / [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) / [Jane Yang](./Jane%20Yang.md) |

**Donner** is the fifth and final mission in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, Mackenzie fetches the [hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) from the warden's office and escapes Blackrock with [Jace](./Jace.md) after [Mathis'](./Mathis.md) attempts to free his son [Donner](./Donner.md) with dynamite fails.
| Mission details — Start location | Mission details — Blackrock Federal Penitentiary |
| Items recommended | [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), [bandage](./Bandage.md) |

The mission starts with a cutscene where Will, tied to a chair, sees the deceased [Franklin](./Franklin.md) being wheeled out of the prison on a gurney. [Mathis](./Mathis.md) then enters his cell, and after revealing that Franklin told him about Will's communication with [Jace](./Jace.md) and their efforts to obstruct Donner's release, decides to execute Will. Just before the killing blow, however, an explosion rocks the prison. Will's chair is broken, and Mathis runs to solitary to find the source of the explosion. Follow Mathis towards solitary to start another cutscene, where Mathis once again threatens to execute Will. However, shortly before Mathis grabs him, a door will slam shut between the two, and [Jace](./Jace.md) will talk over the loudspeaker, informing the convicts that she, not Franklin or Will, was obstructing Mathis' plans all along.

To get out of the prison, head down the hallway, turn right, go through a door on the left, duck under a filing cabinet, and go through two more sets of doors. This will lead to an air duct, which can be travelled through. From there, run up the stairs, duck under another filing cabinet, and enter an office to the right. Use a ramp to climb onto a desk and through a broken window, then run upstairs to the Warden's office. This must all be done quickly to avoid [suffocation](./Suffocation.md).

Once in the warden's office, get the [hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md), then talk to Jace. Jace reveals she's at the power plant, and urges Will to run, as she doesn't know how long the lockdown will last. Immediately after the conversation, the convicts can be heard beating on doors trying to get to Will. Head down the hallway and for the exit. From there, go down the fire exit and head to the right, then go through a board to get down into the yard.

Once in the yard, care must be taken to avoid the spotlights. Observe each light for a few moments to see its pattern, then sprint around it. If caught in a spotlight, Will will be shot at, causing significant condition loss and bleeding. Note that the convicts aren't 100% accurate, so it is sometimes possible to sprint through a light and take no damage. It is recommended not to save the game in this area, as the spotlights will reset to their original position when loading. It is therefore possible that Will will be directly inside a spotlight when loading.

Head for the entrance to the steam tunnels. From there, follow the same route as in Episode 2, but speed is needed on part of this run to avoid suffocation. Again, avoid live wires, fires, and steam leaks. Light from a storm lantern can prove helpful here, but is not necessary. From there, head to the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md), entering via the two main doors.

Once in the Power Plant, a cutscene will play where the player finally meets [Jace](./Jace.md), and the two will chat for a bit... until they realize that Mathis and his gang have followed them through the steam tunnels to the power plant! As Mathis begins to taunt the two, [Heller](./Heller.md) will interrupt Mathis to tell him that [Donner](./Donner.md) is in bad shape. Mathis then attempts to kill Will, and the two struggle until Will manages to stun Mathis long enough to grab Jace and jump into the river below. Another cutscene follows, where Will and a half-frozen Jace reach the shore, and Will offers to light a fire to warm the two of them up once more.

The final scene of the episode shows [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) reaching [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) by canoe, where two unknown survivors note that she is alive, and mention she's not an escapé from a quarantine. [Jane Yang](./Jane%20Yang.md) then appears to attend to her, and realizes that she doesn't have the [hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md). This inadvertently reveals that the case contains a cure for the disease afflicting the inhabitants of the town.

- Given that Jace called all phones in the region via the party line whenever she spoke to Will, it's likely that Mathis was listening in to Mackenzie's last conversation with Jace from the phone in the warden's office.
- You can stash items in the lockers in the steam tunnels and you can retrieve them when escaping however even if you have a firearm such as the revolver with you, you can't use it to fight Mathis.

- If you load the auto save at the beginning of the chapter it will put you into the cutscene of being tied to a chair. However once the cutscene ends Mathis will not appear at the end of the hall and the interaction with him will not happen. This will allow you to walk to the end of the hall there's nothing down there however walking into certain areas such as the hole in the wall will cause the walls to disappear. The only way to fix this is to load a save before you return to the prison.

> “__The man in solitary, the son of Mathis. The reason places like Blackrock exist.

Even post-Collapse, Donner lives apart from anything resembling the regular order of society. And Mathis will stop at nothing in order to unleash his malevolent, unredeemable nature on the world. Starting with Great Bear Island.__”

**Donner** is an unseen character that is the driving motivational force behind the actions of [Mathis](./Mathis.md) and the [Convicts](./Convicts.md) in [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), eventually making a brief appearance in [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md).

> “**Donner is a once-in-a-generation criminal. Donner gets out...he will make it his personal mission to find and hurt every living human he can get his hands on...between Blackrock and the Mainland. Just for shits and giggles.**”

First mentioned by [Vachon](./Vachon.md) and [Heller](./Heller.md), Donner is a prisoner locked in the solitary isolation wing of the [Blackrock Penitentiary Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) located on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). Evil to the core, Donner is described as being a chip off the old block and then some compared to his father, [Mathis](./Mathis.md). He is currently serving a life sentence in Blackrock, as there is no "going back to regular society" for a man such as Donner.

Mathis cares deeply for his son and is willing to do anything to free him, going so far to beat the prison Warden [Franklin](./Franklin.md) to death to acquire information on how to open Solitary and forcing [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) to risk his life in the hostile wilderness in order to acquire old mining detonators to blast open the wing of Donner's cell. Simply hearing Franklin utter Donner's name was also enough to cause Mathis' mood to instantly sour as he begin savagely beating Franklin.

Due to the combined actions of Will Mackenzie and [Jace](./Jace.md), an explosion destroyed Blackrock Prison and unintentionally freed Donner. He is last mentioned by Heller at the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md) to be critically wounded but alive, and needs immediate medical attention.
> “**D.... Dad? I saw it. Lights. The lights. They called to me. And. I found... water. Black water. It was all... lights and black water. Then... nothing. Nothing but dark.**”

Donner finally makes an appearance in Episode 5, being heavily wounded and suffering from internal bleeding from the Prison explosion. His father travels to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) with him and forces [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) to find a way to heal Donner by threatening to kill [Jane Yang](./Jane%20Yang.md), with the doctor being forced to head to a distant SAR Station to find a [Trauma Kit](./Trauma%20Kit.md) for its advanced First Aid uses.

She eventually retrieves it and heals Donner's external wounds with the kit to the best of her abilities. Astrid tells Mathis that unless she gets better equipment, she won't know how bad the internal damage is to Donner's body. Just before Mathis is about to kill Astrid, Donner then speaks to his father about how he saw the [lights and black water in his dreams](./Aurora.md), before eventually perishing from his wounds.

Located to the southwestern most section of the map, it is a lone cabin located near the sea. A [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) pack is often found near the area.
The cabin consists of 1 room, with cabinets and a bed, and several animal themed trophies along the walls. A trap door leads to a room under the cabin that stores a boat on the water.
A unique [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) can be found on the ice, this one designed to be on land all year round.
[Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) heads to this Cabin in search of one of the three missing persons from [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md).

All that is left is the irrational. And I do not want to go down that road quite yet. Ever since the night we lost power everyone has looked to me for an answer but my limited journals are useless without a connection to the mainland.
I will press on, but I fear it is time to involve law enforcement. In whatever fashion the law remains on this tragic island in the middle of this catastrophe.
Doing my duty, I will pursue the leads that I can, as I can. I have enlisted the local Constable as well.
He is here lately on his usual rotation, if also eager to leave once he saw the basic quarantine I pushed for. But he is hardy and seems dependable enough.

Draft Dodger's Cabin is located west of a river and east of [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md) and [Burned Ridge Cave](./Burned%20Ridge%20Cave.md).

Although there are few supplies inside, some of the furniture can be harvested for [cloth](./Cloth.md) and [reclaimed wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md). [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) and [rose hips](./Rose%20Hip.md), as well as [rabbits](./Rabbit.md), may be found around the cabin.

As the name suggests, the isolated cabin is one of the few indoor shelters in the immediate area. It may also suggest this cabin was once used to by someone to avoid a military draft. During the Vietnam War, Canada was a popular refuge for conscripted servicemen avoiding the draft, which may have inspired the location. Inside, a forgotten food or drink item might also be found tucked into a corner, and a warm bed sits against one wall. While the amenities are simple, they can be life-saving in harder difficulties.

A **Drawer** is one possible type of storage container in the game that comes in many forms and can be found in every area in the game.
Food Drawers are found in some large kitchens next to [Cupboards](./Cupboard.md). They often yield [Food and Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) items and have a storage capacity of 15.00kg.
Some Tables, most commonly found in Trailers, have one Drawer that can be searched. They often yield [Material](./Materials.md) items and have a storage capacity of 5.00kg.

Blue [work benches](./Work%20Bench.md) have one Drawer that can be searched (in opposition to the white work benches that don't have any drawers). They often yield Material items and have a storage capacity of 5.00kg.
Desks have four Drawers that can be searched. Two are large while two are small Drawers and have a storage capacity of 10.00kg and 5.00kg respectively. They often yield Material items.
Fishing Huts contain two types of storage, one of which has two Drawers. They often yield Material items and have a storage capacity of 10.00kg.

The smaller red toolboxes have two small drawers. They often yield Materials and [Tools](./Tools.md) and have a storage capacity of 5.00kg. They can occasionally be found stacked on top of the large toolbox cabinets
The large red toolboxes has two small drawers and one large drawer. They often yield Materials and Tools. The small Drawers have a storage capacity of 5.00kg, while the large one is 20.00kg.

Dressers are found in many residential homes, in the bedroom. They have six drawers, but three are broken and cannot be searched. They often yield [Clothing](./Clothing.md) items and have a storage capacity of 5.00kg. Sometimes, loose spawn items can be found inside the open drawers.

**Windproof bonus:** [Windproofness icon](../assets/Windproofness_icon.png)1.0 °C(1.8 °F)
> “**A simple cotton button-down shirt you'd wear to a boring office job. Good thing computers don't seem to work anymore!**”

A common starting item, the dress shirt is one of the worst clothing items in the game. The Dress Shirt only offers a little warmth and a small windproof bonus. While the windproof bonus does at least allow it to outclass the [T-Shirt](./T-Shirt.md#overview), if it is worn as an inner layer the windproof bonus will be lost, thus rendering the Dress Shirt to the exact stats of a T-Shirt. As a result, the Dress Shirt should be replaced and harvested for [Cloth](./Cloth.md) as soon as possible, as almost anything will be better.
The [Sweatshirt](./Sweatshirt.md) serves as a direct upgrade, offering all of the stats of a Dress Shirt alongside a slight waterproofing and protection bonus.

The **Dresser** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.

A makeshift wooden dresser, a Dresser can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md). Each of the 3 drawers have a storage capacity of 10.00 kg, giving it a total of 30.00 kg of storage space.

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The dresser can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value, the dresser cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the dresser will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).

The island itself is very steep on its south side, and can be accessed by climbing the stairs at the [Cove](./Cove.md) via a short cave, or by walking towards the gentler east and north sides. Several rabbit groves can be found on the island not far from the cabin, and an abandoned camp, with a backpack, possible deer carcass, and a [snow shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md), may be found towards the center of the island. Placing several snares on the island will provide the player with food for a long time. Birch and maple saplings may appear on the island.

Driving Gloves can commonly be found in [cars](./Car.md) and buildings, but offer very little protection against the [cold](./Warmth.md). Only [Improvised Hand Wraps](./Improvised%20Hand%20Wraps.md) offer less protection from the elements. However, wearing leather gloves if there are no other options will at least prevent [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md).

More notably, driving gloves weigh relatively little and can be harvested for [Cured Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md). Harvesting Driving Gloves is also less time-consuming than harvesting boots or many other common sources of Cured Leather.

> “**A chemical compound sometimes used as a pesticide. Could be useful when crafting Ammunition.**”

Dusting Sulfur is used to craft [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md), a resource for [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md). This may only be done at the [Ammunition Workbench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) or at [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md). Bags of dusting sulfur can be found in many former industrial and agricultural sites on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).

0.10 kg of gunpowder may also be used as an accelerant for [starting fires](./Fire%20Starting.md). This gives dusting sulfur a use on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) difficulty despite firearms not being present.
- In the right Trailer from the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), under toppled over metal shelves.
- [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) Warehouse (near the trailer, upper floor)

- Dusting Sulfur is branded as the product "Grow Well", with dusting sulfur as an active ingredient. It is likely meant to be an insecticide/fungicide/Disease repellant used in gardens and landscaping.

**Treatment:** 2.00L x [Water (Potable) icon](../assets/Water_%28Potable%29_icon.png) [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) and 2 x [Antibiotics icon](../assets/Antibiotics_icon.png) [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md)

**Alternate Treatment:** 2.00L x [Water (Potable) icon](../assets/Water_%28Potable%29_icon.png) [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) and 1 x [Reishi Tea icon](../assets/Reishi_Tea_icon.png) [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md)/
> “**You drank non-potable water and are now suffering an intestinal disease. You will weaken and die of dehydration unless you can treat it.**”

**Dysentery** is a lethal disease that can be contracted by drinking [Water (Unsafe)](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md). Drinking Unsafe Water does not immediately guarantee Dysentary due to RNG calculation chance, but generally speaking; the more Unsafe Water you drink, the greater your chance of contracting the disease.

While in effect, [Condition](./Condition.md) will not be restored during [Sleep](./Sleep.md), coupled with approximately 4% Condition loss per hour. The [Thirst](./Thirst.md) and [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) bars will also rapidly empty, further compounding the loss of Condition once those [Needs](./Needs.md) empty.

- Treatment includes consuming 2 [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md) or a cup of [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md)/[Burdock Tea](./Burdock%20Tea.md), followed by cumulatively drinking 2.00 L [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), then followed by 10 cumulative hours of [Sleep](./Sleep.md).

- The treatment process cannot be done out of order: medicine and water must first be fully consumed before the 10 hours of rest will begin to count towards the healing process. (Make sure medicine and water have 2 check marks next to them before sleeping).
- After consuming the required medicine, the player will stop losing Condition, but thirst will still deplete rapidly until the sleeping recovery time is completed.

**Easter Eggs** are hidden messages, images, or features typically placed in software to reference other forms of media. They may also be well placed hidden secrets found in the game. Below is a list of secrets, obscure knowledge, and Easter Eggs in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

- _The Long Dark_ features a large number of hidden loot items both indoors and outside. Such items are usually small (e.g. [firestrikers](./Firestriker.md), [matches](./Wood%20Matches.md), [ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md)) and atop shelves, desks, between/underneath furniture, or otherwise in difficult to find locations. CROUCHING ("Control" by default) can be helpful or required in finding such hidden items. Most notably a [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) hidden inside the [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) (Mystery Lake), and a hidden stash of supplies inside [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) (Desolation Point) which requires crouching up and inside a pipe.

- [Safes](./Safe.md): Safes are heavy metal storage containers which are initially locked. They contain some of the highest loot tables in _The Long Dark_, being able to contain rare items such as [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md), [Mukluks](./Mukluks.md) and [Gauntlets](./Gauntlets.md). Safes have static locations ([Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) (Forlorn Muskeg), [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) (Mystery Lake), [Carter Hydro Dam & Environs](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) (upper) (Mystery Lake) and are opened by rotating their dial left until a "click" is heard, then right until a second click, and then left again until the third click.

- [Hidden Caches](./Hidden%20Cache.md): these small, orange-lidded containers are filled with high level loot on all difficulties and are concealed in remote and inhospitable regions, particularly in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md).

- [Secret Mountain Path](./Secret%20Mountain%20Path.md) - this Bleak Inlet area contains a small amount of loot and acts as a shortcut between the eastern and western halves of the region. It is initially walled off by Scrub Bushes from the eastern side, which cannot be traversed until they are harvested by a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md).

- Access to [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)'s [Cannery Pier Workshop](./Cannery%20Pier.md) is initially blocked by a shut electrically powered door. Access requires reading a note (does not need to be picked up, but item has no weight) inside [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md), Bleak Inlet. Once the access code has been read, the door may be unlocked by entering [The Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) (braving harsh cold, wind, and [Timberwolf packs](./Timberwolf.md)), ascending a Mountaineering Rope inside a structure, and navigating a [parkour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkour) route around the upper level of the compound. This leads to the Workshop entrance, where the electronic door may be unlocked at night during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md), granting access to [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) and the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md).

- [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) - the middle level of the mine is a series of interconnected tunnels with rich loot on all Game Modes, but also [electrified hazards](./Burns.md). It can only be accessed via entering the Lower Level (Coastal Highway) and using the elevator while it is powered during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md).

- [Misty Falls Picnic Area](./Misty%20Falls%20Picnic%20Area.md), [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) - an unnamed cave filled with glowing flora may be found along the mountain beside the picnic area, which features a unique interior layout, as well as potentially frozen corpses and loot.

- [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) is an obscure game mechanic which causes select items to randomly spawn in coastal regions ([Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), [Crumbling Highway](./Crumbling%20Highway.md), and [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)). These items may be found near where the ocean meets the ice, typically in or near areas of dangerous Weak Ice. This allows many otherwise non-renewable resources to theoretically become sustainable (e.g. [Cloth](./Cloth.md), [Cured Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md), Saplings). Note: not all items may be found via Beachcombing, and item(s) present at a Beachcombing location prevent future spawns, requiring their removal before a item may spawn.
## Easter Eggs

- If a survivor's hydration is low, they will mention "That guy who drank his own pee doesn't sound so crazy right now" referencing [Bear Grylls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear_Grylls) [drinking his own urine](https://www.google.com/search?q=bear+grylls+pee&rlz=1C1GCEA_enUS1043US1043&oq=bear+grylls+pee&gs_lcrp=EgZjaHJvbWUyBggAEEUYOdIBCDMzMTFqMGo0qAIAsAIA&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8#fpstate=ive&vld=cid:654e5bb1,vid:axVPg5EtvKs,st:0).

- In [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), after [Will Mackenzie's](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) 3rd encounter with the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) after acquiring the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md), the bear will back off, with Will remarking "not so tough now that I'm all Grizzly Adams?" referencing [John Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_%22Grizzly%22_Adams).

- The director's name of _The Long Dark_, Raphael Von Lierop, can be seen briefly on a computer monitor in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) during the flashback with Astrid.

The entire mission [What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md) with the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) hunting Mackenzie (a crashed bush pilot) is a reference to the film [The Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Edge_%281997_film%29).

- During an [Aurora](./Aurora.md), if you click on a [Radio](./Radio.md), either in a [Car](./Car.md), [Truck](./Truck.md), or on a table, classical music will play. The music that plays has been identified to be Glenn Gould playing Bach on piano.
A number of locations are named after [Hinterland's](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md) developers.
- Most of the names on the [Prison Transport Manifest](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md) are named after Hinterland developers

- Mystery Lake is a reference to the mystery lake school division in North Manitoba Canada where the developers did a career day video call with local middle school students in 2013 to promote video game development in Canada.
- The [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md) is based off of the [Britannia Mine Museum](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Mine_Museum) in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.
- The [Haul Truck](./Haul%20Truck.md) is most likely based off the one in front of the museum.

- [Stacy's Grape Soda](./Stacy%27s%20Grape%20Soda.md) - is named after "Stacyplays" (aka Stacy Hinojosa) a YouTuber who ran a "let's play" series during The Long Dark's alpha/beta (2014-2016). It is slightly rarer than other types: Orange Soda, and Summit Soda.

- Brand References - many in-game items are references to real-world brands in name and/or appearance such as [Orange Soda](./Orange%20Soda.md) (Fanta), [Summit Soda](./Summit%20Soda.md) (Mountain Dew/Sprite), Beef Jerky ([Jack Link's](./Beef%20Jerky.md)), and [Firestriker](./Firestriker.md) (Aurora Fire Starter 440C). The Flashlight appears to be loosely based on a 1920s vintage Ever-Ready flashlight, however uses a LED bulb as opposed to the Ever-Ready's fluorescent bulb.

- The [Revolver](./Revolver.md) in-game most closely resembles a [Smith & Wesson Model 27](https://guns.fandom.com/wiki/Smith_%26_Wesson_Model_27) or [28](https://guns.fandom.com/wiki/Smith_%26_Wesson_Model_28) (leaning more towards the former), which both use .357 Magnum ammunition; however, in-game Revolver Ammunition appears to be .32 S&W Long or .38 Special.

- A cut image of a [.44 Magnum Bullet](../assets/Revolver_44_Mag_Bullet_icon.png) can be found in the game files, suggesting that the Revolver could also be a [Smith & Wesson Model 29](https://guns.fandom.com/wiki/Smith_%26_Wesson_Model_29).
- The [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) is inspired by the Lee-Enfield bolt action rifle, which was Britain's standard issue rifle until the 1960s and was used by the Canadian Rangers until 2015.
- The [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) closely resembles the real-life [Orion flare gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flare_gun).

- [First Aid Kit](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md) - these wall-mounted containers filled with medical supplies are a reference to the [Swedish folk duo of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Aid_Kit_%28band%29#2012%E2%80%932013), who composed and performed the song "[Lion's Roar](https://youtu.be/gekHV9DIjHc)", used in _The Long Dark's_ intro for Wintermute (Story Mode).
- [Cups of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) - every coffee cup has the Hinterland Studios logo on the front of the cup. This is the most blatant and easiest to find Easter Egg in the game.
- The description of the [Hoodie](./Hoodie.md) might be a reference to the Hinterland Developers.

- Photographs on walls and nightstands inside of houses in [Coastal House](./Coastal%20House.md), [Milton House](./Milton%20House.md), and [Crossroads House](./Crossroads%20House.md) in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), and [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) respectively are pictures of [Hinterland](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md) developers, their friends or family; including "Stacyplays" (aka Stacy Hinojosa) a YouTuber who ran a "let's play" series during _The Long Dark's_ alpha/beta (2014-2016). Each picture has been digitally downgraded to fit in the the game's graphical aesthetic style.

- The item description of the [Spelunker's Lantern](./Spelunker%27s%20Lantern.md): "A light for deep, dark places, when other lights go out." is a direct reference to the [Phial of Galadriel](https://tolkiengateway.net/wiki/Phial_of_Galadriel) from Lord of The Rings: "It will shine still brighter when night is about you. May it be a light to you in dark places, when all other lights go out."
- The [Achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md), [Too Greedily, too Deep](./Too%20Greedily%2C%20too%20Deep.md) is yet another reference to Lord of the Rings:
- **Saruman: "**Moria... You fear to go into those mines. The dwarves delved too greedily and too deep. You know what they awoke in the darkness of Khazad-dum... shadow and flame."

- The Achievement [Something Wicked](./Something%20Wicked.md) is a reference to a quote from one of the three witches in Shakespeare's [Macbeth](https://nosweatshakespeare.com/quotes/famous/something-wicked-this-way-comes/):
- **Second Witch**: "By the pricking of my thumbs, Something wicked this way comes."

A number of rocks contain faint images of cavemen, monsters or graffiti, typically in an abstract art form or extremely low resolution. These rocks are found in all regions, but are most common in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) near the entrance to [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md), as well as [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md).

The side mission [Hank's Hatch](./Hank%27s%20Hatch.md) contains many references to [Firewatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firewatch). "Hank" is a nod to the protagonist "Henry" from the game. Hank (a common nickname for Henry) shares many similarities with his counterpart, including taking a job working in a fire tower in a nature park to be away from other people. In his journal, Hank complains about "the chatty lady" on the radio, a reference to Delilah, Henry's supervisor in Firewatch who communicates with him by radio throughout the game and also occasionally refers to him as "Hank". Hank's Journal refers to him finding a "weird old bunker," also a reference to the plot of Firewatch.
During the mission [Memories](./Memories.md), several callbacks to previous builds of the game can be found in the [Jackrabbit Hangar](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md):

- An old map of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) can be seen on the time table board behind Mackenzie when first starting the mission. This map was the first official map of the Island that was never put in the game.
- The old version of the [Hinterland Studio Inc.](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md) logo can also be seen on the wall.
- The shovel found on the old builds of the game's title screen can be found next to the bathroom.

Has an interior Echo One is a radio hut and tower positioned on the southmost point of the [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) plateau. Inside the hut on a desk, the player can find a note that provides the code to the electronic lock on the pier warehouse door to the [Workshop](./Workshop.md) at the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md).

The radio hut is positioned on the southern tip of the plateau, overlooking the entire region. Inside the hut, the player can find decent amounts of loot, some good storage, and the essential keycode to unlock the door to the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) and [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md). Some firewood can be found around the site, as well as a few harvestable wooden objects. Inside the player can escape from the cold and hostile wildlife.
The radio hut has some qualities that make it a potential safe house, but its position ultimately makes it inadequate.

Although it is safe from predators and has a fair bit of storage, the only way to travel between the upper and lower part of the region is by a climbing rope area at [Pensive Lookout](./Pensive%20Lookout.md), and the player has to supply and deploy their own rope (assuming there is not one hanging on the outer wall of the lookout), making the lookout a better choice if the player desires to live on the plateau at all. Likewise, traveling to other regions from the plateau requires the player climb a rope to move beyond the connecting transition area. It also doesn't have a firebox or workbench.

The station is visible from all around the map on a clear day, but the path to reach the site is not immediately obvious. While most of the region can be accessed through Forlorn Muskeg, the station and the rest of the plateau can only be reached by climbing down into The Ravine basin, then continuing along the frozen waterway.

Depending on the player's goals, it may be more efficient to enter via this path the first time visiting the region. Though it requires up to two climbing ropes, it allows the player to unlock the workshop, without backtracking and making repeated trips.

As mentioned in the [Cannery Memo](./Cannery%20Memo.md) written by a worker for the cannery, they have 'rigged something up in the old cannery workshop,' and mentions, 'don't forget to get the code from the old radio station.' The code can be found in the form of [Communication Report](./Communication%20Report.md), which can be found resting on the keyboard of the computer on one of the desks.

Players who make it to the pier will find that a heavy metal door and electronic keypad block their path. The keypad can only be used during the [aurora](./Aurora.md), and without retrieving the paper from the radio hut, the keypad will remain locked.

> **Did Astrid survive the crash? Keep your eyes open for signs of her passing, while you explore the wilderness around you.**

**Echoes of Astrid** was the second mission of the Predux [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).

Make your way away from [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) and continue following the torn fragments of Astrid's Scarf until you see a pond. Many [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) are around the area that can be hunted with [Stones](./Stone.md) if desired. Make your way up the hill into the cave system.

Inside a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) with a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) and [Torch](./Torch.md) will be on the right. Take both and then equip and light the Torch to face the darkness ahead. A note called [Lost in the Storm](./Lost%20in%20the%20Storm.md) can be found in a dead end section of the cave ahead. Keep going through the cave to the other side. A [Wolf](./Wolf.md) feasting on a [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md) is on the other side. Either attack it with Stones or ignore it and make your way to the road.

Follow the road past [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md) until you find a Trailer on the mountainside. Loot it and then sleep if you are tired enough. When done, follow the road down the mountain to [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md). Another Wolf is outside feasting on a Deer Carcass so watch out. Inside the church you can find 2 notes, [Pastor's Note](./Pastor%27s%20Note.md) and [Hymnal](./Hymnal.md).

Continue down the road to the town of [Milton](./Milton.md) and head up to the house on the hill with smoke coming out of the active chimney. Walk inside to meet [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md). After the cutscene ends you will chat with her via dialogue options. Ask her anything you want and then exit the dialogue and the mission will end.
Several plot points and locations have been replaced/altered since the Redux re-release of Episode 1:
- The camera does not automatically turn and stop the player to show context sensitive situations, such as redirecting the camera towards Mackenzie's Crashed Plane.

- The player is forced to climb a [Rock Climb](./Rock%20Climb.md) near the Rabbit pond, walk through a cave to [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md), then walk down the road past [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md) and the [Wood Lot](./Wood%20Lot.md) before reaching the Town of [Milton](./Milton.md). The Redux version changed the map to add a small canyon between the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md) and the Rabbit Pond and removed the Rock Climb up to the cave, drastically shortening the walk to Milton.

- The first [Wolf](./Wolf.md) encounter with a [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md) is not found in the canyon (since it does not exist yet), but on the other side of the cave near Spruce Falls Bridge.
- A Wolf is scripted to be on the Spruce Falls Bridge, and can serve as the player's first [Struggle](./Struggle.md) encounter.
- A Wolf is scripted to kill a [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) a short walk away from Spruce Falls Bridge.
- A second scripted Wolf eating a Deer Carcass is found outside of St. Christopher's Church.
- Because of the longer walk, the [Milton Water Tower](./Milton%20Water%20Tower.md) is located next to the entrance to town, rather than the middle of town in the Redux version.

- The [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) [Mailbox](./Mailbox.md) is on the left side of the walk up to the house, but the Redux version changed it to be on the right side.

- A 3rd person cutscene plays when entering the Milton House between [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) and Mackenzie. This scene was completely remade in the Redux version, and all future cutscenes would be first person.

- The dialogue options are static text on the screen that alternates between Mackenzie and Grey Mother, and are not voiced. In Redux, all lines are voiced. One Dialogue option has been removed from Redux. The "House?" option has been removed, and hints that taking Grey Mother's things will displease her ([Trust](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md#Trust) System).

- Grey Mother mentions that Milton has been through 5 days of hell, referencing Mackenzie being stranded in the ravine for the last 5 days. This line is absent in the Redux version, since only 2 days have passed.

- It is implied however that Astrid was passed out for 5 days between the events of Episode 1 and the start of [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) in the Redux timeline.

**Emergency Stim** is a [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) item in _The Long Dark_. Upon use, it will restore some of the survivor's [Condition](./Condition.md) and grant them unlimited energy for sprinting and rope climbing for one minute.
Emergency Stims are rare, powerful, and single-use only. When used, the Emergency Stim will:
- Grant unlimited [Stamina](./Stamina.md) (e.g. for Sprinting/Robe Climbing) for 60 seconds.
- Allow Sprinting, even if the survivor has [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) which would normally prevent it (see below).
- Allow climbing up/down deployed [Mountaineering Ropes](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md), even if the survivor has [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) which would normally prevent it (see below).
- Inflict [Exhausted](./Afflictions.md) after 60 seconds (drops the survivor's [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) to 0%).

Note: Afflictions such as [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md) (which prevents climbing) and [Sprained Ankles](./Sprained%20Ankle.md) (which prevents sprinting) are ignored while under the effects of the Emergency Stim; however, the survivor cannot use climbing ropes if [encumbered](./Encumbrance.md), nor sprint if they are carrying 10 kg (22 lbs) or more over their maximum carry weight, even while under the effects of an emergency stim.
- Draining [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) to 0% can be useful to more quickly recover from afflictions that require sleep, such as [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md).

Emergency Stims may be found rarely in most regions (8-10 across an entire world on [Interloper](./Survival%20Mode.md)) in high-tier loot areas, [First Aid Kits](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md), beside [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), or hidden beneath/around furniture. They can also be acquired by trading with the [Trader](./Trader.md), but are only unlocked after reaching 400 [Trust](./Trader.md#Trust), and not on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) or [Misery](./Misery.md).

- On the trek to the rope anchor above the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md) entrance in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), one will spawn along the rock walls on the left side if approaching from [Wolf's Jaw Overlook](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md) (removed on Interloper).
- Inside of the barn at the [Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
- [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md). (ver. 2.52 currently bugged under snow and only accessible using campfire trick)
- [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) between [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) and [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
- Inside the [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md) either on the ground or on the desk
- Inside Cellblock C of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) inside the room with red chairs, beneath the table the chairs are around
- Emergency Stims in The Long Dark are "autoinjectors", a real-world medical device: usually a single use, disposable, spring-loaded syringe injector used to quickly self-administer a specific drug.
- The Long Dark's animation for an emergency stim is realistic: appearing to depict the autoinjector being pressed to the survivor's thigh.
- Given their gameplay effects and description, emergency stims in The Long Dark are likely loaded with hydrocortisone.
- While under the effects of a Emergency Stim, the player is able to fully sprint in any direction, including backwards.

![Weight icon](../assets/Weight_icon.png) **Encumbrance** is a player statistic that represents the total amount of weight the player can carry and how it effects their movement speed in the world.

Players can see the total weight of the items they are carrying on the Backpack screen from the Status [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md). This will include items they have equipped as well as those carried in the inventory. The Backpack screen truncates the amount of weight to two decimal places.
The player's normal carrying capacity starts at 30 kg (66 lb). This baseline can be increased by:
| [Moose Hide Satchel icon](../assets/Moose-Hide_Satchel_icon.png) | [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) | 5.00 kg _(11 lb)_ | Wear Satchel | Satchel is taken off or ruined |
| [Well Fed icon](../assets/Well_Fed_icon.png) | [Well Fed](./Well%20Fed.md) | 5.00 kg _(11 lb)_ | Avoid starvation for 72 hours | When Calorie Store reaches 0 |
| [Technical Backpack icon](../assets/Technical_Backpack_icon.png) | [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) | 5.00 kg _(11 lb)_ | Acquire Backpack | Never |

| [Unburdened icon](../assets/Unburdened_icon.png) | [Unburdened](./Unburdened.md) | 3.00 kg _(6.6 lb)_ | Consume: [Ptarmigan Pie icon](../assets/Ptarmigan_Pie_icon.png) [Ptarmigan Pie](./Ptarmigan%20Pie.md)[Rabbit Pie icon](../assets/Rabbit_Pie_icon.png) [Rabbit Pie](./Rabbit%20Pie.md)[Venison Pie icon](../assets/Venison_Pie_icon.png) [Venison Pie](./Venison%20Pie.md)[Porter's Soup icon](../assets/Porter%27s_Soup_icon.png) [Porter's Soup](./Porter%27s%20Soup.md)[Pemmican Bar icon](../assets/Pemmican_Bar_icon.png) [Pemmican Bar](./Pemmican%20Bar.md) | 3 hours |
| [Travois concept](../assets/Travois_concept.jpg) | [Travois](./Travois.md) | 75.00 kg _(165 lb)_ | Carry Travois | When put down |

These effects can be stacked, meaning that the player can increase their normal carrying capacity by up to 15 kg (33 lb). However, since there is a limit to how many satchels/backpacks the player can equip (only one of each can be equipped at a time), 45 kg (99 lb) is the highest-possible carrying capacity in the base game.

If [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) has been purchased, players can temporarily increase their normal carrying capacity by an extra 3 kg by achieving the [Unburdened](./Unburdened.md) Affliction, gained by eating [Ptarmigan Pie](./Ptarmigan%20Pie.md), [Rabbit Pie](./Rabbit%20Pie.md), or [Venison Pie](./Venison%20Pie.md). Unburdened only lasts for 3 hours but if all other ways to increase max carry weight are acquired, this extra 3 kg creates the highest-possible carrying capacity in-game at 48 kg (105 lb).

Using a [Travois](./Travois.md) does not directly increase a player's carry weight, but it's capacity to carry up to 75 kg while also being dragged behind the player is a notable addition to the carry weight formula. Keep in mind that more weight on a Travois will slow the player down.

The amount of weight the character is carrying increases the rate of [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md). When Fatigue reaches 50%, the max carrying capacity will begin to decrease, slowly at first but the rate will rapidly increase as your Fatigue gets closer to 0%. Encumbrance penalties apply as normal as a survivor becomes more drained. Once the 'Exhausted' Fatigue state is reached, the max carry limit will be half the normal value (30 kg becomes 15 kg). The fatigue meter is primarily restored with [Sleep](./Sleep.md), and, once the player has regained at least 50% of their fatigue, (equivalent to 6 hours of sleep) the maximum carrying capacity is restored. [Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) may also offer minor relief from a low fatigue meter.

[Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md) from a [Moose](./Moose.md) [Struggle](./Struggle.md) will remove 25% of maximum carrying capacity until healed. [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) will also weaken a survivor to the point where they will lose 5 kg of carrying capacity until healed. If the [Burdened](./Burdened.md) Affliction is gained, then max carry capacity will be reduced by 3 kg for 1 hour.
| [Fatigue Reduced icon](../assets/Fatigue_Reduced_icon.png) | Low [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) | -0.01 kg to -15.00 kg _(0.02 - 33.09 lbs)_ |
| [Burdened icon](../assets/Burdened_icon.png) | [Burdened](./Burdened.md) | -3.00 kg (-6.6 lb) for 1 hour |
| [Broken Ribs icon](../assets/Broken_Ribs_icon.png) | [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md) | 25% reduction until healed |
| [Scurvy icon](../assets/Scurvy_icon.png) | [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) | -5 kg (-11 lb) |
| [Diminished Form icon](../assets/Diminished_Form_icon.png) | [Diminished Form](./Diminished%20Form.md) | permanent -5 kg (-11 lb) |

Detrimental effects to movement occur gradually relative to the amount of weight over capacity. There are certain thresholds that heavily affect movement speed, for example a player with exactly 9.99 kg (22.02 lbs) over capacity can still sprint, but a player with 10.00 kg over capacity cannot. Being more than 29.5 kg over capacity makes the player unable to move. Being aware of these thresholds is important to properly select the amount of loot you can carry.
The baseline Carrying Weight for this example starts at 30/30kg. For every 1kg over Carry Weight, -3.3% movement penalty is applied.
| 30/30 kg | 0% | The maximum weight a player can carry without penalty. / The maximum weight for [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md). |
| 31/30 kg | -3.3% | Slight slowdown. Player can no longer Rope Climb. / [Sprain Risk](./Sprain%20Risk.md) appears. |
| 50/30 kg | -66.6% | The player's walking speed is significantly decreased to a crawl. |
| 60/30 kg | -100% | The player is completely immobile, and can no longer walk. |

Harsh winds and the terrain directly effect a player's movement as they traverse the world, slowing or speeding the player when encountered. Note that the Celestial Navigator [Feat](./Feats.md) adds a 10% bonus walking speed during a clear night or aurora.
Do note that light winds currently slow down the player more than heavy winds do, likely due to a bug.

The [Travois](./Travois.md) will apply a penalty to the player's movement speed when dragged behind them. This penalty increases as more items are added to the satchel. Putting items into the Travois instead of carrying them on player's person is always the better choice, as it does not slow the player down as much.

It is very easy to exceed your carry capacity in The Long Dark, especially on more loot-rich game modes such as Voyageur or Pilgrim. A well equipped character carrying minimum reserves of food and firewood, a basic assortment of tools and a weapon will almost automatically exceed the base capacity. It is hence not always desirable to stay within capacity. Especially when transporting greater amounts of loot, like after successfully hunting an animal, or when moving acquired loot out of a region, exceeding capacity often cannot be avoided.

However, aware of this limitation, a player should carefully consider what equipment to bring, and what to leave behind at a shelter. This especially includes tools and weapons, as those usually weigh in very heavily, but also food and firewood. Even the selection of clothing can be put to question. Balancing the amount of equipment you deem useful against your desired mobility is a key strategic element of The Long Dark.
- Within carry capacity: desirable, but with good equipment can be hard to achieve without adding to it with the Well Fed buff or the Moose-Hide Satchel.

- Up to 5 kg (11 lbs) above capacity: adequate if [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) is not on the player's route as the slow down is negligible. It is advisable to stay within this limit for tasks that require substantial mobility and carry reserves, such as exploring and looting part of a region.

- 5 kg (11 lbs) to 10 kg (22 lbs) above capacity: generally acceptable as the amount of slow down is moderate, chances for sprains are still within reason, and sprinting for emergencies is still available. This is the sane maximum of equipment a player should bring for any task other than reallocating loot to a different shelter.

- 10 kg (22 lbs) to 15 kg (33 lbs) above capacity: still within reason for hauling loot over relatively safe and open terrain, but the inability to sprint must be kept in mind to properly alter behavior towards predators.

- 15 kg (33 lbs) to 20 kg (44 lbs) above capacity: generally inadvisable as the slow down is very pronounced, and even [bears](./Bear.md) can no longer be escaped. At this point it is probably faster and definitively safer to take a route twice with considerably less weight.
- More than 20 kg (44 lbs) above capacity: the player is so slow that dropping excess loot becomes inevitable. Highly dangerous, and in any case inefficient.
[^1]: Roads provide 50% walking speed boost compared to snow, concrete, or metal terrain.
[^2]: Max Bonus & Penalty for Heavy Wind are applied when walking with or against oncoming winds respectively.
[^3]: Stepping indoors (Back of a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) or building interiors) slows the player down instantly
[^4]: Blizzards do not slow the player down despite the raging windstorm, likely for balancing reasons.
[^5]: Moving diagonally at a 45° angle increases movement by 3%, 50° angle by 21% (controller only), and using a controller emulator to hit both angles increases speeds by 42%.

**Energy Bar** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Consuming an Energy bar provides up to 500 calories, and does not [dehydrate](./Thirst.md). It weighs a mere 0.10 kg, and has high energy density of 5,000 calories-per-kilogram (second only to [Salty Crackers](./Salty%20Crackers.md)). Like other packaged food and drink, the Energy Bar can be found anywhere uncommonly, most often inside of houses, shops, [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md), and on [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md). It is also the only food item that can be found in a [First Aid Kit](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md).
Because of its small weight, energy efficiency, and not causing dehydration (unlike the Salty Crackers), it is a valuable food source for traveling.
- The ingredients on the back list: "Dates, Almonds, Flax Seeds, Coca Nibs, Honey, Salt, Natural Flavours."

**Energy Boost** is a positive [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) gained by drinking [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) or injecting yourself with an [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md).

**Environmental Hazards** are dangerous obstacles occasionally encountered while playing _The Long Dark._ While many are minor, some can be life threatening and will cause [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) if not approached and handled with caution and respect.

![An example of ankle deep, cold standing water](../assets/Cold_Water_Puddle.jpg)_An example of ankle deep, cold standing water_Occasionally, puddles of cold, ankle deep standing water or flowing water can be found inside caves and serve as a floor hazard for the player. Walking through or standing in a puddle/flowing stream will drench the player's footwear, slowly making the Socks and Shoes Clothing slots wet and partially lowering the player's [Warmth](./Warmth.md). Wet clothing can be avoided by simply unequipping the player's footwear clothing and passing through the puddle, but this will not stop the player from taking Warmth damage.
Walking through a puddle will also generate a unique audio response from the survivor not found anywhere else in the game.

![An example of an unavoidable waterfall in an Ice Cave](../assets/Waterfall_Ice_Cave.jpg)_An example of an unavoidable waterfall in an Ice Cave_ Waterfalls can occasionally be found inside [Ice Caves](./Ice%20Cave.md), and serve as an unavoidable hazard. Simply standing near one will slowly wet the player's clothing. Passing through one will full drench all of the player's outermost Clothing layers to 100% wetness and will automatically lower the player's Warmth to 0. Warming up afterwards becomes a priority if choosing to pass through such a hazard fully clothed, as your wet Clothing will immediately begin freezing over. If one must pass through a waterfall, simply remove all Clothing and walk through, then re-equip all clothing to start warming up again.

Any light source currently active and held will be extinguished when passing through a waterfall. This includes Matches, Flares, and [Torches](./Torch.md), and, oddly enough, active [Storm Lanterns](./Storm%20Lantern.md). Lit Flares and Torches will of course go out if thrown through a waterfall. Active [Flashlights](./Flashlight.md) are not affected by waterfalls.
Keep in mind that most waterfalls also have streams of cold water flowing on the ground on one side, so the player's feet can get wet before approaching/after passing through a waterfall.
- [Reclusive Falls](./Reclusive%20Falls.md) and [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) is a waterfall covering an Ice Cave

Live, energized wires are a serious environmental hazard located inside or near many industrial buildings across the Island. They are identified by their exposed insulation and rapid sparking during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md). They are normally safe to walk across during the day, and are not affected by [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) despite its tendency to power up electronic equipment.

Touching a live wire will give the [Burns](./Burns.md) Affliction and cause rapid [Condition](./Condition.md) loss. Great care should be given when walking or even sleeping on downed wires during dusk or the night, as an Aurora can activate and kill a survivor exposed to live wires rather quickly.

![Electrified water can kill in seconds](../assets/Cinder_Hill_Coal_Mine_Story.png)_Electrified water can kill in seconds_ Some bodies can serve as a serious electrical hazard during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md), due to the amount of electrical current passing through. Standing in these bodies of water will cause rapid [Burns](./Burns.md) and [Condition](./Condition.md) damage, and will outright kill the player in seconds if the player doesn't leave.

![An example of cracked Weak Ice and a warning symbol](../assets/WeakIce.jpg)_An example of cracked Weak Ice and a warning symbol_ [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md) is the most commonly encountered water hazard found in _The Long Dark_ and can be found in all coastal regions and certain fresh bodies of water. Stepping on thin ice will be accompanied by the audible sound of ice cracking and the ice at the player's feet visibly cracking, as well as a red Exclamation Point Symbol appearing in the middle of the screen. It is advised to immediately turn around until the Exclamation Point Symbol disappears, informing the player that they are on stable ice again.

Being exposed exposed the extreme cold water causes: 10% [Condition](./Condition.md) damage on any mode other than Pilgrim, makes all Clothing 100% wet, and induces [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md). Wet clothes are a serious hazard not only from continued Condition loss due to [Freezing](./Needs.md), but also from the risk of the clothing freezing over and inducing [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md).

[Crampons](./Crampons.md) and [Improvised Crampons](./Improvised%20Crampons.md) can provide the player with a little extra time on Thin Ice with the [Sure Footing](./Sure%20Footing.md) feat (6 seconds instead of 5 seconds).

While very rare, some abandoned mineshaft tunnels contain clouds of toxic underground gases that accumulate in one spot due to the poor ventilation. Passing through these clouds will immediately give a [Suffocation](./Suffocation.md) Risk as the survivor begins coughing from the dirty air. Failure to quickly pass through these Hazards will result in an instant death after a set timer that appears on screen reaches zero.

Toxic gases can be quickly sprinted through in most cases, even with the speed penalty that indoor spaces give to the player. Some toxic gas corridors inside the Langston Mine cannot be sprinted through easily without wearing a [Respirator](./Respirator.md) with fresh [Canisters](./Canister.md) however. One other factor to consider with the Langston is that many gaseous corridors have loot that is too dangerous to gather without wearing a Respirator.

While impossible to see with the naked eye until it is too late, some very rare locations in the game will instantly kill the player if they pass through them when attempting [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md). Most instant kill barrier locations are located outside the map boundaries of regions, but a few notable locations where death barriers are present include:

- All cliffsides surrounding the [Ravine Basin](./Ravine%20Basin.md) in [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md) should be treated with utmost caution, as they contain death barriers. Use the [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section to get down safely.

- [Broken Bridge (Broken Railroad location)](./Broken%20Bridge%20%28Broken%20Railroad%20location%29.md) on the other side leading to [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md), the base is an instant kill area.
- The nearby cliff near [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) leading down to the ravine has a death barrier.
Other minor locations with instant kill barriers can be found in [this video by Bashrobe](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NIYBONWH24s).[1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NIYBONWH24s)

_"Mackenzie and Dr. Greenwood are separated after their plane crashes deep in the Northern Canadian Wilderness. Struggling to survive, Mackenzie explores the small town of Milton, where he begins to understand the scope of this quiet apocalypse."_
**_Do Not Go Gentle_** is the first episode in the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story mode. It is followed by [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md).

In this episode, [Will Mackenzie's](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) plane has crashed due to a [mysterious geomagnetic event](./First%20Flare.md). He and fellow traveler [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) are now separated and Mackenzie does his best to survive. His journey takes him to the small town of [Milton](./Milton.md). Dr. Astrid Greenwood unexpectedly shows up at the workplace of bush pilot Will Mackenzie. She and Will have not seen each other in years, and their parting was not under ideal circumstances. She asks him to take her to a small village in the mountains. It is late in the evening and the weather is bad. She refuses to tell him why, and what the contents are in the metal locked briefcase she is carrying. When he protests, she becomes frustrated and starts to leave. He stops her and reluctantly agrees to take her.

During the trip, a [geomagnetic event](./Aurora.md) occurs, depriving the plane of power, sending the plane into a rocky ravine. Will finds himself alone, injured, in the dark in freezing temperatures, and with no sign of Astrid.

**_The Light At The End Of All Things_** is the 5th and final chapter of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is preceded by [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md).

Hinterland released Episode 5 of _The Long Dark_ for free to all current owners on March 31, 2026. It takes place in both the mysterious [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) and [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md) and completes the story of Mackenzie and Astrid, while also tying up most of the loose threads left within the story (including the conflict involving [Mathis](./Mathis.md) and his gang of [Convicts](./Convicts.md), the contents of [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md), what caused the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), and the message Mackenzie must carry to [Atwood](./Atwood.md), "Wintermute").
Both Mackenzie and Astrid are playable characters in the Episode, switching perspectives between multiple parts of the story between missions.

Perseverance is the first chapter of Episode 5. [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) is the only playable character in this chapter. The chapter takes place at [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) and in the surrounding Perseverance Countryside. It contains 3 different missions. ![Missions story ep5 Perseverance](../assets/Missions_story_ep5_Perseverance.png)
"_A strange illness has taken hold in Perseverance Mils. People are missing. Investigate the town and see what you can find out._"

It is the first mission of the game. This mission starts with a conversation between [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) and [Jane Yang](./Jane%20Yang.md). Jane states there are some missing people of the town. Hence, in order to find out what happened to these missing people, Astrid goes to the Cooper's Blind and Dr. Larson's clinic. ![Missions story ep5 ToThoseWhoAreMissing](../assets/Missions_story_ep5_ToThoseWhoAreMissing.png)

The player plays as [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) while accompanying [Jace](./Jace.md) to the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md), containing 2 missions. ![Missions story ep5 TheLongBrokenRoad](../assets/Missions_story_ep5_TheLongBrokenRoad.png)
![Missions story ep5 ToSARandBack](../assets/Missions_story_ep5_ToSARandBack.png) The player takes control of Astrid again for a single mission.
The player takes control of Mackenzie again for the last mission. ![Missions story ep5 Conflagration](../assets/Missions_story_ep5_Conflagration.png)
- Bar Patron - Ashley O'Connell, Caitlyn Bairstow, Ceara Morgana, Joe Allard, Shawn Youngchief, Victor Hunter
- [Convicts](./Convicts.md)/Sentries - Michael Daingerfield, Victor Hunter / Joe Allard, Victor Hunter
- In an interview with the popular YouTuber Zaknafein, Raphael van Lierop said in response to player criticisms that "Episode 5 was made for people who like Wintermute."
- Of all five episodes, this one focuses the least on [survival](./Survival%20Mode.md), and the most on storytelling.

With the exception of Waterfall Cave immediately to the right, Eric's Falls is the sole named location in the area. [Cat tails](./Cat%20Tail.md), [Green Maple Saplings](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md) and [Green Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) as well as some [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) are in the area. [Wolves](./Wolf.md) and a [bear](./Bear.md) may patrol nearby.

The cave can be a possible base location as it provides a 10°C degree bonus, and because there is a lot of [wildlife](./Wildlife.md) in the area including [deer](./Deer.md), plenty of [rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [wolves](./Wolf.md) and a [bear](./Bear.md), provided the player knows how to deal with the latter two effectively. Since Part 6 (December 2024) DLC patch, there is a possible [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) spawn on the ice in front of the falls which would make locating a base in the cave problematic. The player must return to the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md) at [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md) to fix or craft [arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) since that is the only location on Timberwolf Mountain containing a [workbench](./Work%20Bench.md).
There is a [Cargo Container](./Cargo%20Container.md) along the river. (Does not spawn in Interloper):
- Upper door: [Airline Food - Chicken](./Airline%20Food%20-%20Chicken.md), [Airline Food - Vegetarian](./Airline%20Food%20-%20Vegetarian.md) and [pinnacle peaches](./Pinnacle%20Peaches.md)
- Lower door: [antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md), [antiseptics](./Antiseptic.md), [bandages](./Bandage.md) and [painkillers](./Painkillers.md)

Eric's Falls can be reached by walking through the cave at [Secluded Shelf](./Secluded%20Shelf.md) and climbing down the [rope](./Rope%20Climbing.md) to the left, or by following the path from [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md).

If the player places a [climbing rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) at the spot on the level of Eric's Falls, the player can descend to the [Engine](./Engine%20%28East%29.md) area. Placing a rope here will significantly decrease the time needed to get from the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md) to the [Summit](./Summit.md), since the player will no longer have to walk all the way around through Deer Clearing.
