In Escape the Darkwalker, the time is permanently set to dusk and the player is stalked by an invisible entity known as The Darkwalker which will try to devour them. To win, all 10 diary pages ([On the Nature of Darkwalkers](./On%20the%20Nature%20of%20Darkwalkers.md)) must be collected and the entity banished in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md). The Darkwalker cannot be hurt or killed, merely avoided or slowed by painting glyphs to lure or ward it away.

Any [Region](./Region.md) may be selected to start, but after ~30 real-time minutes the current region will fill with [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md), forcing the player to leave (smaller regions have less time until they are enveloped in Toxic Fog). Toxic Fog ruins food and water and damages [Condition](./Condition.md). Strategy will be required to plan how one travels through the world.

Completing Escape the Darkwalker rewards the player with 2 [Badges](./Badges.md), the [Feat](./Feats.md) "Darkwalker," and the "Endless Night" option for [Custom](./Custom.md) [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

![Escape the Darkwalker Startup](../assets/Escape_the_Darkwalker_Startup.jpg) Upon starting _Escape The Darkwalker_ an extinguished campfire and supplies can be found close by, along with an introductory note called [On the Nature of Darkwalkers](./On%20the%20Nature%20of%20Darkwalkers.md). There are ten [Diary Pages](./Diary%20Page%20%28Darkwalker%29.md) to be collected, one in each major region (excluding [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md)) beside a green campfire. All region maps are fully revealed and display the locations of each Green Campfire. The Blackrock, [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), and [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md) regions cannot be explored in this challenge.

Once all notes are collected, the player must head to Ash Canyon to complete the challenge in the Ritual Circle located on the map and wait for the Darkwalker. The [On the Nature of Darkwalkers](./On%20the%20Nature%20of%20Darkwalkers.md) note does not need to be collected to complete the Challenge.

The Darkwalker is indestructible and intangible. It moves through terrain and buildings irrespective of elevation. It constantly chases the player across all regions, indoors, vehicles, mines, and caves. Audio cues and music will play based on its current distance. The Darkwalker moves at 2 meters (~6.56 feet) per second, increasing for each collected diary note (up to to 4m/s).

- The Darkwalker's speed is not tied to real-time movement. Care should be taken with time-accelerating tasks such as [sleeping](./Sleep.md) or [harvesting](./Harvesting.md), especially with many notes collected.
- The first 15 minutes of a game are a 'grace period' before The Darkwalker will spawn and it is not tied to real-time; one hour of a time-accelerated task equals 30 seconds on the timer.

- Within 200 meters (~656 feet), The Darkwalker's exact distance is shown, and the player is afflicted by "[Anxiety](./Anxiety.md)" (preventing [Sleep](./Sleep.md) and passing time) unless a Ward glyph is present. If a Ward expires and The Darkwalker is/enters within 200m, the player will immediately wake up.

- Within 50 meters (~164 feet), the Anxiety affliction is replaced by [Fear](./Fear.md), which causes a constant, heavy [Condition](./Condition.md) loss (approximately 50% per minute in real time). The Darkwalker's footprints also become visible.
- At 0 meters, The Darkwalker becomes visible and devours the player, killing them instantly.
[Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) fills an entire region after ~30 real-world minutes within in; larger/smaller regions have their toxic fog timers adjusted accordingly.
- Toxic Fog [spoils](./Decay.md) all food and drink (even normally non-spoiling items like [cup of coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md)) and causes constant [condition](./Condition.md) loss.
- Current Toxic Fog progress is shown for each region by viewing it on the map. A UI element will appear if less than half of the region's timer remains, turning red below 2 minutes remaining.
- Toxic Fog in a region also RUINs all food in your backpack, indoors, outdoors, and animal carcasses. Instantly kills all wildlife.

- **The toxic fog timer considers mines/caves as part of their parent-region.** (e.g. "[Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md)" is considered [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md)). Toxic Fog will fill these regions when they or their parent region's timer is met.

Each of the 10 major zones (excluding [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md)) contain one 'green campfire', with unlimited fuel and a ward glyph lasting 5 hours (in-game). Once this glyph's time is spent, the fire will be extinguished. Each green campfire has one unique Diary page, a Can of Glyph Spray Paint, a [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md), and high quality loot nearby.

[Spray Paint](./Spray%20Paint.md) is replaced with green [Spray Paint - Glyph](./Spray%20Paint%20-%20Glyph.md), which makes anti-Darkwalker glyphs instead of informational markings. Cans of Glyph Spray Paint are found sporadically in the game world as loot, contain 4 sprays, and can always be found near a Green Campfire.
- _Lure -_ Draws the Darkwalker to a location. Lasts 1 hour in-game, or until reached by The Darkwalker. Only one Lure can be placed per region at one time.

- _Ward -_ Fortifies a small area (200m), preventing The Darkwalker from approaching for up to 2 hours (in-game). Wards are only active if the player is nearby. Only one Ward can be placed per region at one time.
- _Dispel Fog -_ The progress of one region's toxic fog is reduced by 50% of current progress (most effective just before Toxic Fog appears). **Useable o_nce per playthrough._**
- _Banish - (**unlocks once all 10 diary pages are collected**)_ Must be used inside the banishing circle of [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) to complete the challenge.
### Misc.
Difficulty is set to [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md) and [Feats](./Feats.md) cannot be selected. All [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) spawn, including a 24 hour (in-game) grace period before predators can spawn.

- Time of day is permanently dusk, making the world colder and darker. [Auroras](./Aurora.md) and [blizzards](./Weather.md) are disabled, but Toxic Fog will slowly develop over time in a region, making traveling difficult.
- The player begins with a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), random clothes, food and other supplies.
- The spawn rate of all animals is heavily reduced. Although bears and wolves can still spawn, they are much less common compared to normal survival saves.
- All maps are fully revealed with the location of both the player and each green campfire shown, similar to [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).

- [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) is dangerous since The Darkwalker can move faster than a climbing player. Wards only protect the first few meters of a climb, so a head start (or Lure glyph) is highly recommended.

- Currently, both the Challenge [Badge](./Badges.md) _"Escape the Darkwalker_ and _Deadly Dreamer Badge (2020)"_ and the feat _"Darkwalker"_ have the same requirements: collect 6 diary pages in a single run and are earned simultaneously. Originally the _Escape the Darkwalker_ Badge (previously called Escape the Darkwalker Umbra\] required the player to survive for 60 real world minutes.
- Facing the Darkwalker in the Ritual Circle should be done cautiously, as the Darkwalker's Fear and Anxiety can still cause Condition to drain, potentially killing the player.

The route taken greatly affects the difficulty of _Escape the Darkwalker_. It can be beneficial to start in a western region, leaving [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) and [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) for last. Some starting location benefits are listed below:
- _Bleak Inlet_: Allows 24 hours to collect its diary page and escape before [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) may spawn, and a Moose-Hide Satchel from the fire.

- _Hushed River Valley:_ Yields a revolver and completing two mandatory rope climbs to the fire before The Darkwalker can spawn. It also grants easier access to two rope climbs from Mountain Town to Forlorn Muskeg/Mystery Lake easier with a slower Darkwalker.

- _Desolation Point_: Abundant loot at [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md), [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md), and [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md) and safe passage through the mines and Crumbling Highway.
- _Broken Railroad_: Abundant loot at [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) and [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md), and 24 hours before wolves may spawn in the narrow region.

- _Coastal Highway_: Abundant loot at [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) and access to the narrow regions of [Crumbling Highway](./Crumbling%20Highway.md) and [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) with a slow Darkwalker and potentially no wolves.
- _Forlorn Muskeg_: Poor loot but easy access to multiple zones: Broken Railroad, Bleak Inlet and Mountain Town.
- _Mountain Town_: Abundant loot in [Milton](./Milton.md) (especially clothing) and the two rope climbs in Hushed River Valley with a relatively slow Darkwalker.
- _Mystery Lake_: Good loot at [Lake Cabins](./Lake%20Cabins.md) and [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), and flexibility between Mountain Town, Forlorn Muskeg and Coastal Highway.
- _Pleasant Valley_: Good loot at [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) and [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) early on. Requires considerable backtracking late in the game.
- _Timberwolf Mountain_: Access to [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) before the Darkwalker arrives, if a hacksaw can be found.

- Large open regions ([Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md)) are safer, while smaller regions ([Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md)) and transition regions/caves/mines are more dangerous due to a lack of maneuverability.

- Fog is a serious threat primarily when backtracking through a region ([Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md)). Plan for this when traveling, and avoid running out the timer unless you are close to the exit and not returning.
- If moving through a transition region/cave/mine, check the map to see what region the fog timer counts towards.

- When retrieving the page from [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) or [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) (depending on how far you are in your run) consider putting a lure deep in the region and waiting for the Darkwalker to pass you as it moves to the lure. This can make passing through the narrow entrances to these regions much safer.
### The Darkwalker
- The Darkwalker's initial speed is slower than a player in all scenarios, but with all notes it is faster than you if you are encumbered, making sprinting mandatory at points and sleep difficult.
- As long as you are not encumbered or injured (i.e. sprained ankle), _you are always faster than the Darkwalker_, even at empty fatigue and ten notes collected.

- Entering a different region causes The Darkwalker to follow at the same relative distance and direction. For example if you enter a new area with the Darkwalker 300 meters behind you, it will be 300 meters behind you in the new region. Note that since your orientation in the new map might be different than when exiting the old map, placing down a lure at at the start will maximize the distance required for the darkwalker to reach you.
- The Darkwalker moves in a straight line through terrain, with Lure glyphs taking priority over the player.

- If trapped in a narrow locations with The Darkwalker blocking the exit (e.g. inside "[Carter Hydro Dam and Environs](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md)"), place a Ward and sleep/pass time. The Darkwalker will often move out of the way (while keeping the same distance), allowing one to proceed.
- Wards are useful to grant more time to loot, repair or cook if The Darkwalker is nearby. They are only active if the player is nearby (draining their duration).
- Only one Ward may be present per region at a time. To place another Ward, the previous must be fully depleted.

- If the Darkwalker is within 200 meters of the player, placing a Ward glyph will NOT make it retreat, it will only halt the Darkwalker from closing in. Wards should only be placed when the player is more than 200 meters away.
- Lure glyphs are useful in narrow spaces ([Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) and [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md)) to bypass The Darkwalker.
- If both a Lure and a Ward are active, The Darkwalker will ignore the Ward to chase the Lure.
### Misc.
### Misc.
- Minimize weight: less weight means faster movement. Drop unnecessary clothes, tools, and food. Fatigue affects movement, so stay rested.

- Keeping weight below the encumbrance threshold for zero fatigue will allow you to always outrun the Darkwalker in a linear direction. This is 15 kg/33 lbs for a player with no capacity buffs, but will increase to 20 kg/44 lbs after acquiring the satchel and again to 25 kg/55 lbs after receiving the Well Fed buff.
- Balance time between travel and sleep. Sleep is usually safe if the Darkwalker is not nearby.

- Looting is generally unnecessary for this challenge since every green campfire has high-tier loot. If you need to supplement this, stick to containers and structures along the shortest path through a region; Voyageur settings mean you will likely find more than enough to sustain yourself.
- Avoid time consuming tasks such as [hunting](./Hunting.md), [harvesting](./Harvesting.md) and [mending](./Mending.md) clothes.
- [Flares](./Flare.md) and [Torches](./Torch.md) and [Storm Lanterns](./Storm%20Lantern.md) are useful for traversing caves and mines.
- [Flares](./Flare.md) and [firearms](./Revolver.md) are effective at frightening [predators](./Wolf.md).

- [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md), [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md), and [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) allow more sprinting and rope climbing with less rest, or bursts of speed during emergencies.
- [Bandages](./Bandage.md) are useful for treating [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md), which prevent [sprinting](./Stamina.md) and [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md).

- You can usually ignore sprained wrists; as long as only one is sprained, you can still use revolvers, flares/flare pistols, and the lantern. You will need to bandage it or sleep if you are making a rope climb, however.

- Raphael Van Lierop (lead designer of _The Long Dark_) gave insight to the design of _Escape the Darkwalker_ and its predecessor [_4 Days of Night_](./4%20Days%20of%20Night%20Event.md); stating that fans were unhappy with 4DoN: those who missed the timed event missed content and [Badges](./Badges.md), and those who played felt the mode was too simplistic. Thus Escape the Darkwalker was made as a more polished, feature-rich, and permanent game mode.

- The Darkwalker is invisible during most gameplay, but can be seen when killing the player/banishing it as well as in official "[ESCAPE THE DARKWALKER](https://www.thelongdark.com/news/darkwalker/)" media. It is a vaguely humanoid entity of black smoke, green light, and three wolf skulls.

- Escape the Darkwalker bears many similarities to the works of horror writer [H.P. Lovecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._P._Lovecraft)—particularly esoteric journal writings, [invisible and malevolent monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Horror_at_Martin%27s_Beach), and creation of [magical glyphs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elements_of_the_Cthulhu_Mythos#Signs_and_symbols) to ward monsters away. "[The Nameless City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Nameless_City)" in one such journal note is a direct reference to his work of the same name.

- Users on the official Hinterlands Forums and reveal streams regularly joked that The Darkwalker was the ghost of "[Fluffy](./Wolf.md)", a fan-favorite unique wolf 'killed' in previous versions of _The Long Dark_.

- With Auroras disabled, the [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) is useless. The [ammunition workbenches](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) present within the [Workshop](./Workshop.md) and the [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) are locked behind electronic doors and cannot be opened, thus making [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) impossible. The elevator that gives access to the middle level of the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) is also inaccessible without the Aurora.

- With Endless Night enabled, the [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) and [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md) are useless. Ignoring the The Darkwalker and Toxic Fog, this makes "Endless Night" mode (including for Custom Sandboxes) lethal from dehydration, since matches/firestrikers are a infinite resources and potable water is non-renewable.

- If The Darkwalker reaches (kills) the player while climbing a rope but before the player dies from [Fear](./Afflictions.md), the death cutscene will play as a hybrid of being devoured by The Darkwalker while falling from the rope.
- A glitch makes it possible to get the Darkwalker feat currently. This can also happen with getting the Escape the Darkwalker badge without getting the pages.

**Windproof bonus:** [Windproofness icon](../assets/Windproofness_icon.png)6.0 °C(10.8 °F)
> “**Heavy down-filled parka made using high-end materials. The kind of parka worn by people who know what they're doing.**”

Expedition Parkas are rare, warm and very lightweight clothing. It offers a warmth bonus of 4.0 °C and windproof bonus of 6.0 °C, with a small mobility penalty, protection bonus, and 50% waterproofing, all while weighing only 1.5 kg. The [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md) offers the same warmth bonus, a much bigger protection bonus, and slightly better waterproofing, however it is twice the weight of the Parka, offers less wind proofing, and has a much higher mobility penalty. The [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md) offers more warmth, waterproofing, and protection, but weighs 5 kg, and has a high mobility penalty. This makes the Expedition Parka not only the best man-made coat in the game, but arguably the best coat in the game as well, due to its well-rounded stats.

An Expedition Parka is very likely to spawn inside one of the cargo containers in the [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md), in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) (except on Interloper). One is likely to spawn inside, but up to 5 may be present inside the [container](./Cargo%20Container.md).

Elsewhere the parka is extremely rare, only appearing inside [safes](./Safe.md), and high loot locations such as [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md), [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md), [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md), [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md), or [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md).

The Expedition Parka is also known to spawn in the cabin of the first blue pickup truck on the [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), and [Brittle Cave](./Brittle%20Cave.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md).
It can also spawn in the train car in the abandoned passenger rail car in the [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md)

**Extra Supplies** is a side mission started in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In the mission, the survivor gathers extra supplies for [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) to help her survive the upcoming record low temperatures and heavy snowfall. The mission can only be completed in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), prior to the survivor [leaving Milton](./Paradise%20Lost.md).
> “**Grey Mother will need extra food and fuel if she is to survive alone for much longer.**”

To start the mission, the survivor can find the below note at [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) after completion of the main mission [The Grey Mother](./The%20Grey%20Mother.md):
Once the [note](./Winter%20Forecast.md) is found, Mackenzie can start gathering additional materials.

During the course of the main mission, Mackenzie explores the houses around the town of [Milton](./Milton.md), the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md), and [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md). Supplies can be gathered from these locations and delivered to Milton House to meet the objective. Supply caches containing food can also be found by completing the side missions [Milton Supply Caches](./Milton%20Supply%20Caches.md) and [Highway Robbery](./Highway%20Robbery%20%28mission%29.md).

If additional food is needed, [Deer Carcasses](./Deer%20Carcass.md) can be harvested for [Venison (Raw)](./Venison%20%28Raw%29.md) and [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) can be [snared](./Snare.md) at Paradise Meadows Farm or at the pond behind the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md). The meat can then be cooked at the fire at Milton House.

![The Firewood Bin located outside Grey Mother's House where fuel can be deposited to complete the mission](../assets/Firewood_Bin.png)_The Firewood Bin located outside Grey Mother's House where fuel can be deposited to complete the mission_ Firewood can be gathered at the [Wood Lot](./Wood%20Lot.md) on either side of the town. [Coal](./Coal.md) can be found in the cave behind the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md), as well as in front of the school house. Additionally, furniture and crates within the houses around the town of [Milton](./Milton.md) can be broken down for additional [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md).

After finishing the side mission tasks, a [Mackinaw Jacket](./Mackinaw%20Jacket.md) can be found on the bench where the Winter Forecast note was originally found, presumably left there as a silent thank you from Grey Mother.

**Face the Impossible** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.
This achievement is obtained after you have survived a whole day on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) Experience mode in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

The easiest way to unlock this achievement is to find a [Bed](./Bed.md) indoors and simply stay put while sleep/pass time until 1 day passes. For players intending on surviving for longer periods of time, a guide to Interloper can be found [Here](./Survival%20Mode%20%E2%80%94%20Interloper%20Tips.md).

The easiest way to unlock this achievement is to find a [Bed](./Bed.md) indoors and simply stay put while sleep/pass time until 1 day passes. For players intending on surviving for longer periods of time, a guide to Interloper can be found [Here](./Survival%20Mode%20%E2%80%94%20Interloper%20Tips.md).
- Try to find an indoors location as fast as possible, the cold weather will kill you in a few minutes/hours.

You have no [matches](./Matches%20%28disambiguation%29.md) when first starting but you need to find something to get hydrated. After the cold, the [Thirst](./Thirst.md) is the second most important [Need](./Needs.md) to satisfy at this difficulty. The best choice is probably to reach a building with a [toilet](./Toilet.md) and gather some water. This is much easier than finding matches and boiling water. If you are lucky you can also find a drink that can restore your thirst and [hunger](./Hunger.md) level.

- If you have been lucky and still have high condition you don't need to sleep or eat. [Cat tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) are an easy and risk free food to harvest that can be found nearly everywhere, they don't reduce the hydration level, which is great considering the limited amount of water that you could have found. Remember that you don't have a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) so you need to find a bed (caves and cars won't work due to the low temperatures inside at this difficult level).

Provides some shelter **Fallen Lighthouse** is the collapsed ruin of a former lighthouse, similar to the intact building in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). It is an iconic landmark used associated with the region.

The remnants of the tower sit on the top of a hill, with frequent rabbit and deer spawns nearby. Inside the lighthouse, the player will find a six-burner [stove](./Stove.md), [dusting sulfur](./Dusting%20Sulfur.md) or a [sewing kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md), a plastic container, as well as some firewood. If the player climbs the lighthouse stairs to the top, they can find an [Emergency Kit](./Emergency%20Kit.md).

Despite its notoriety, the lighthouse does not serve as a good safehouse, as it leaves the player exposed to the cold and unable to cure hides, guts, or saplings. It also lacks a bed, workbench, and other useful features.

Despite these Imitations, it can make a good temporary camp for those well-supplied with firewood and/or warm clothing. It is conveniently positioned near the [Cannery Worker Residences](./Cannery%20Worker%20Residences.md) (a better safehouse option), and its outdoor six-burner stove makes it an optimal location for efficient cooking and for cooking skill improvement. Nearby, deer and rabbit spawns can be found, in addition to ice fishing huts. It is a good place to spend a day or three, while probably spending the night somewhere else.

The Fallen Lighthouse provides a good view of the player's surroundings, only bested by the radio hut on the mountain; on a clear day, it's possible to see most of the major locations in Bleak Inlet from its top. Although the aspects of the location and terrain around it would make for a good safehouse, it might be challenging for the player to make it through a night there, as the nights can get very cold and timberwolf attacks are possible. The shores around the lighthouse are also the only place in Bleak Inlet where [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) is possible, potentially making it vital to a long-term strategy for surviving in the region.
Aside from this, it makes a somewhat good location for a base of operations, only sleeping somewhere else might be required.

Astrid: "So far, yeah. But there are people in town who won't be if I don't get going."

Molly: _Sighs_ "I wouldn't get your hopes up. A few days in this weather, and with the wolves prowling...doubt you'll find anyone alive out there."
Molly: "Fair point. But if you want to live, check out the trunk of that blue sedan, over by the swing set."

She opens the lower hatch door and steps inside, walking to the back of the plane only for the platform she is standing on to collapse. She stops to bask in the destruction before her, with the plane split into 3 parts with several dead bodies and suitcases strewn all around like ragdolls. Crows fly noisily over the frozen corpses._
## Find the passenger IDs. [0/10] Find Insulin for Dimitri.
_Astrid begins searching for IDs on the first of the bodies, the skin frozen purple by now._
_She continues searching for IDs and Dimitri's Insulin until she finally arrives at the tail section, where she finds the body of one of the plane's crew with a manifest._

_She finally reaches the tail section, and a single crow perches nearby before flying away when approaches. Astrid finds a suitcase with a name on it "[Suitcase belonging to Dimitri S.](./Suitcase%20belonging%20to%20Dimitri%20S..md)" and finds the Insulin inside_

_Having found the Insulin and all the IDs, Astrid treats Gwen's [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) and picks her up. Gwen and Astrid may say many lines regarding their situation, which can be found here: [Survivor Monologue](./Survivor%20Monologue.md)_

Astrid carries Gwen to [Burned Ridge Cave](./Burned%20Ridge%20Cave.md) and puts her down, then_ _starts a fire to warm her up, and diagnoses her._ _After warming up and making it out of the cave, then later traveling down the mountain and across a tree bridge, a Receiver rings inside an abandoned, destroyed house. Astrid puts Gwen down and answers it_

**Characters:** [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md) [Crash Survivor](./Crash%20Survivor.md) [Molly](./Molly.md) [Jane Yang](./Jane%20Yang.md) (flashback)
**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**
> “**Survivors of an airline crash in the mountains have found their way to the Community Hall in Thomson's Crossing. There might be others out there in need of help. Can you save them?**”

**Fallen Star** is the second mission in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) meets [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md) and learns about her predicament.
The mission starts in the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md). Walk to each survivor in the hall and diagnose them.
- Eric has [Dehydration Risk](./Dehydration%20Risk.md) and needs 0.50 L of [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md)
- Dimitri has a Diabetes wristband and has a [Hyperglycemic Risk](./Hyperglycemic%20Risk.md). He needs [Insulin](./Insulin.md), which is not here

Most survivors will have hypothermia or concussions and won't require treatment. Others can be treated using medical supplies from the player's inventory. Talk to [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md) after diagnosing all six survivors.

Leave Community Hall and head to the [Crash Site](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) to find Insulin. The most straightforward way to reach it is to follow the road which runs up the right side of the in-game map. Upon reaching the plane, enter the plane through the door on the left near the cockpit. Continue through the front section of the plane and drop out the back. Note that it is not possible to return once dropping off the front section.

There will be nine bodies scattered behind the front section. Search each body and take their IDs. Many of the other suitcases will have [Clothing](./Clothing.md). Frozen airline dinners are scattered around the ground, which will be useful if you can carry them back to the Community Hall later so take them if you can.

At the top of the hill, a survivor named Gwen is pinned beneath a seat. Remove the seat from on top of her and diagnose her injuries. Dimitri's Insulin will be inside one of the suitcases next to Gwen. Gwen has her own condition (health) as well as warmth and hydration needs. Her condition will go down if she is attacked by [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) or if either of her needs are entirely depleted. The player can address Gwen's warmth need by placing her near a fire or indoors, and can address her thirst need by using the "diagnose" interface to give her [potable water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md). Gwen's condition will improve as long as her needs are met and she will not contribute to the player's carrying capacity when held.

Head back down the hill, but turn towards the right. The path the player entered the area through—the plane—will be blocked. At the bottom of the hill on the right is a small cave which makes for a good place to sleep or build a [Campfire](./Campfire.md). Continuing to the right is the only way to exit the area. The player will cross a fallen-tree bridge and continue down a hill to a burned house. [Molly](./Molly.md) will call the phone at the house.

Be wary of Timberwolves along the way back to the Community Hall. Gwen must be placed on the ground to draw a weapon or interact with objects. Bring Gwen back to Community Hall and place her on the newly preplaced unoccupied bed. Give Dimitri his Insulin and then talk to the 12 survivors already in the hall to break the news of the missing/dead plane passengers, then talk to Father Thomas, and the mission will end.
![Survivor count](../assets/Survivor_count.jpg) Some confusion has been caused by the number of ID's required by the journal.
- 1 ID card is from Gwen. The ID card (G. Russell) will automatically be found after you find Gwen and the cutscene ends.

- After returning to Community Hall, the journal says to "return" 12 ID's. What this really means is that the player must talk to all 12 survivors in the hall. The 12 survivors are in sleeping bags. Of these 12 survivors:
- Gwen's [ID - G. Russell](./ID%20-%20G.%20Russell.md) will automatically disappear once she is placed on a bed.
- 9 will be told their family member/friend didn't make it. (This corresponds to the 9 dead bodies Astrid took the IDs from at the crash)
- 3 will be told their family member/friend couldn't be found (This corresponds to the 3 names unaccounted for on the passenger manifest).
- (6) Nolan, (4) Eric, and (11) Maude will be told that their friend could not be found, and they will plead to Astrid to keep looking.

**Description:** A railway line in the mountains separating Lower Great Bear and The Far Territory
**Connecting Regions:** [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) and [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md)

> “**Travel down the Far Range Branch Line and arrive at Transfer Pass, the railway hub providing access to the foothills of the Far Range. The journey is a long and harrowing trek from Broken Railroad region, deep into the heart of Great Bear.**”

**Far Range Branch Line** is the 6th Transition Zone [Region](./Region.md) added to [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). It was released on December 5, 2022 for players who purchased the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion pack. The transition region connects to [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) and [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md).

The Far Branch Range Line is a modestly large, highly linear Transition Region located on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), serving as the barrier between the Lower Great Bear and The Far Territory Regions. Centered on the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md), the Region offers very little in the way of exploration, being composed of a winding railroad that cuts through several mountains and carved out tunnels.
This region is entirely encompassed with unmarked locations and no [surveyable](./Charcoal.md) Region Transition barriers.
- [Wolves](./Wolf.md) have been observed in the basin below Surfeit Trestle, near the fallen tree between Foundered Track and Steely Chasm, and close to Remnant Cave.
It is possible for Wolves to be completely absent from the region after surviving for at least 100 days, a trait shared with [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md).

- All named locations in this region do not show up as marked on the map, even when scouted. Similarly, the entrance/exit areas that transition to new regions are found inside indoor train tunnels, preventing them from being marked down on the map.

- The description of [Vagabond Soup](./Vagabond%20Soup.md) mentions that it "Originated in the community of people known to hop trains along the Far Range Branch Line, who would harvest the many Rabbits that lived alongside the tracks."
This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

> “__Affable and quick to laugh, even in crisis Father Thomas is lifted by his faith rather than weighed down by it. While erudite when he needs to be, he treasures the immediate, pragmatic spiritual needs of life on remote Great Bear Island -- births, baptisms, and funerals, mostly.

Just how and why Father Thomas came to find himself in Pleasant Valley remains a mystery. But it’s clear his devotion to the tiny parish in Thomson’s Crossing has helped bind the community together.__”
> “__Yes, you're a doctor so you understand the fragility of human life. The fragility of the human spirit is more my domain. __”
> “__Yes, you're a doctor so you understand the fragility of human life. The fragility of the human spirit is more my domain. __”

**Father Thomas** is the primary non-player character in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). He is the priest of the [church](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Church.md) in [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), and can be found inside the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md) for the entirety of the episode.

Soft-spoken and kind, Father Thomas is the main quest-giver for the storyline of Episode 3. He cares for the [Crash Survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md) in the Community Hall, while directly or indirectly requesting Astrid's assistance to help the sick and injured.

After leaving the [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) behind and finding a [Community Hall Flyer](./Community%20Hall%20Flyer.md), [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) follows the road to [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md). Seeing an active burning signal fire outside of the Community Hall, Astrid walks inside and is greeted by several wounded individuals, and a priest who welcomes her in. Believing that a confused Astrid is the victim of a recent plane crash in the mountains, Father Thomas introduces himself and offers the doctor shelter and the warmth of the nearby fireplace.

Father Thomas tells Astrid about how the survivors of the recent plane crash started showing up recently, with many dying and being stored in the basement of the Community Hall. He also informs Astrid that all the paths out of Pleasant Valley have been blocked for weeks now, and that with no way out, there is no chance that anyone will come to rescue the plane crash survivors (and that Astrid cannot leave the Valley to make her way to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md)). Finally, Father Thomas mentions that a monster of a blizzard is due to approach any day now. Because of the grim state of the survivors, Father Thomas is relived when Astrid offers to diagnose the injuries of each Crash Survivor.

Astrid checks the current needs of each of the plane crash victims and finds that one of them is a Diabetic, meaning that he will need a dose of [Insulin](./Insulin.md) soon or he will die. With the priest unable to leave the wounded survivors' sides, Astrid volunteers to go to the crashed plane to find other survivors, as well as bring back any physical aid or any item that might give mental closure to the survivor's of the Community Hall. Father Thomas prays for Astrid's safe journey and wishes her good luck, but not before giving a reluctant Astrid a [Rosary](./Rosary.md) to protect her. Astrid is skeptical that the Rosary will help, but the priest insists that it will at least help him bless the victims of the plane crash site on his behalf without him having to be there in person.

Astrid later brings back a single survivor she finds at the crash site, brings another survivor his Insulin, and provides I.D.'s to several of the Crash Survivors. Father Thomas is relieved that she succeeded in helping the victims of the crash, but notices that the weather is turning worse. Father Thomas also states that there is a major lack of food and medical supplies, and that the coming blizzard will surely seal the fate of the Crash Survivors if nothing is done about this reality soon. Astrid notes that there may be more survivors, and that she will also secure more supplies to help keep everyone in the Community Hall alive before the storm arrives.

Astrid eventually finds 3 more survivors and secures enough food, water, and medical supplies to see that everyone in the Community Hall survives the impending monster blizzard. Father Thomas thanks the doctor, and provides her with a [Map of Pleasant Valley](./Map%20of%20Pleasant%20Valley.md) that shows a [dangerous path](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) through the mountains, so that she may continue her journey to Perseverance Mills.

Father Thomas then comforts Astrid with the burdens she carries, and asks that Astrid keeps the Rosary he initially gave her when the doctor tries to give it back. The priest wishes her luck, and does not have any new dialogue for the rest of the Episode as he tends to the Crash Survivors.

Father Thomas is last seen in the ending cutscene to the Episode, with Astrid noting that the world is changing while reminiscing about how the people she has just met in Pleasant Valley will be living through a new, very harsh world soon.

Astrid can return a stolen [Church Artifact](./Church%20Artifact.md) to the nearby church, with a [Thank You Letter](./Thankyou%20Letter.md) from the Father being left behind thanking whomever returned this precious item to the church.
- Father Thomas is an ordained Christian priest based on the Roman collar he wears, his denomination is either Catholic or Episcopal.

- His church is one of three on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md); the other two being the Catholic [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md) of [Milton](./Milton.md), and the [Stone Church](./Stone%20Church.md) of [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md).

- Despite neither Father Thomas nor Astrid ever bringing up the existence of [Molly](./Molly.md) in any of their conversations throughout the Episode, it can be inferred that Father Thomas most likely knows who she is, seeing that she is a residence of the valley.

- It is suggested Thompson's Crossing was the largest remaining settlement on Great Bear Island prior to [The First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), because Milton's church was closed due to the towns declining population (as detailed in [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) and Notes), and the Desolation Point's church seems derelict for years if not decades.

**Fatigue Reduced** is a positive [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) gained by consuming certain [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) or [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) items.

Upon consumption of specific items, the player's [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) is immediately restored by a set percentage and the player gains the _Fatigue Reduced_ affliction. This buff lasts for a set period of time (dependant on the item consumed), lowering the overall rate of Fatigue loss and reducing the amount of Fatigue used while sprinting. _Fatigue Reduced_ does not affect the rate of Fatigue loss when [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md).
| Item | Initial Fatigue Reduction | Fatigue Loss Rate | Duration | Duration w/ Feat[^1] |
| [Cup of Coffee icon](../assets/Cup_of_Coffee_icon.png) [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) | 10% | 50% | 60 minutes | 75 minutes |
| [Cup of Acorn Coffee icon](../assets/Cup_of_Acorn_Coffee_icon.png) [Cup of Acorn Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Acorn%20Coffee.md) | 5% | 75% | 30 minutes | 37.50 minutes |
| [Emergency Stim icon](../assets/Emergency_Stim_icon.png) [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) | 10% | 50% | 60 minutes | 75 minutes |
| [Go! Energy Drink icon](../assets/Go!_Energy_Drink_icon.png) [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) | 20% | 50% | 45 minutes | 56.25 minutes |
| [Caffeine Pills icon](../assets/Caffeine_Pills_icon.png) [Caffeine Pills](./Caffeine%20Pills.md) | 25% | N/A | 4 hours | No bonus |
[^1]: The [Feat](./Feats.md) "Straight To the Heart" increases the duration of _Fatigue Reduced_ given by these items by 25%.

![Fatigue icon](../assets/Fatigue_icon.png) **Fatigue** is one of the four essential [Needs](./Needs.md). Fatigue is the measure of how tired the character is. Fatigue constantly drains but can be replenished by sleeping. As the character tires, Fatigue begins to affect the ability to move, aim weapons, and [struggles](./Struggle.md). When completely depleted, fatigue will begin to lower the player's [Condition](./Condition.md).

As long as the character is awake, fatigue will constantly be emptying. The rate of drop is directly dependent on activity level and encumbrance but may also be influenced by other factors like [temperature](./Feels%20Like.md) and [illness](./Afflictions.md). Example: The fatigue bar can be emptied as quickly as in 2.6 game hours by sprinting as often as possible, while a long [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) session can easily consume half the player's fatigue in minutes. However, remaining inactive by passing time at a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) will see the same bar last almost 22 game hours.

Properly balancing one's activity level somewhere between "always resting" and "always sprinting" should see most players make it through a 12 hour activity period before reaching exhaustion, provided that they're not exploring in an area full of climbing ropes.

In custom games, non-standard game timescales will multiply normal sources of fatigue (standing/walking/sprinting/climbing) relative to real-time. For example, in a custom game with 4x day length, you will only expend 0.5% stamina per real-time minute while walking.

[Sleep](./Sleep.md) is the most common method of satisfying fatigue. It takes 12 full hours of sleep to fully replenish an empty fatigue bar. Or 1/12th of the bar will fill for each hour slept. The player will wake automatically when the bar has been completely refilled.

[Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) can be used to help ward off tiredness. When consumed, it fills 10% of the fatigue bar. [Cup of Acorn Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Acorn%20Coffee.md) has the same effect and fills 5% of the fatigue bar. Both confers the [Fatigue Reduced](./Fatigue%20Reduced.md) affliction, which slows the rate at which fatigue empties.
[Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) immediately boosts the fatigue bar to full and keeps it there until the effect wears off, where upon Fatigue immediately drops to 0.

Drinking a [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) will immediately refill the player's [Stamina](./Stamina.md) and half the player's fatigue for a total time of 45 in-game minutes. After 30 minutes, the player will get a [Headache](./Headache.md), and at the end of the 45 minutes, the player's fatigue will drop by 50%.

When the fatigue bar is empty, condition begins to drain. The rate of drain is fixed at 1% per hour (See: [Needs](./Needs.md)). The slowness of this drain has lead some players to take advantage, accepting minor condition losses during strenuous activities in a practice known as [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md).

Sprinting contributes significantly to rate of fatigue. In turn, fatigue affects the replenishment of [stamina](./Stamina.md) which enables sprinting. When the character reaches Exhausted (empty fatigue bar), sprinting becomes impossible. It will remain disabled for as long as the fatigue bar remains empty.

Rope climbing is much faster when the player is well-rested. Climbing up a rope is the most strenuous activity in-game, emptying both fatigue and stamina very quickly. When the player becomes exhausted, it is not possible to start a new climb, and climbing will become very slow. The rate of stamina decrease, however, remains constant, increasing the risk of slipping and falling.

The amount of weight the character is carrying increases the rate of fatigue. Also, as the fatigue bar reaches below 50%, the 'recommended encumbrance' will begin to decrease. Encumbrance penalties apply as normal (i.e if your total carried weight is greater than your 'recommended encumbrance', too much more and you cannot sprint, etc). Once the 'Exhausted' fatigue state is reached, 'recommended encumbrance' will become half the normal value (or 15kg). This can be fixed with adequate rest.

The ability to hold a weapon steady while aiming is affected by fatigue. This can be significant for using the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), or [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md). Aim will waiver more and the Bear Spear cannot be set for very long when the fatigue bar is low. (See:[Hunting](./Hunting.md)).

When the character is fully rested, struggles seem to take less time and the [struggle](./Struggle.md) bar seems more easily filled. As exhaustion sets in, the opposite becomes apparent. Great difficulty is imparted and the struggle bar may become impossible to move. Being attacked by Animals during exhaustion is extremely hazardous. It's worth noting fatigue has no direct disadvantage in a [Moose](./Moose.md), or [Bear](./Bear.md) mauling, due to the inability to fight while being mauled.

If a player remains starving for a long enough time, the maximal amount of rest that they can acquire will start to gradually decrease. It is noticed by the yellow exclamation mark that appears beside the eye icon and by the red color that starts filling up the inside of the fatigue bar. This issue is easily solved by consuming food, the red color inside the fatigue bar will then gradually start to decrease, but that doesn't prevent the player from entirely filling up their fatigue bar with sleep right away.

Fatigue bar progresses from Exhausted ↔︎ Drained ↔︎ Tired ↔︎ Winded ↔︎ Rested. Arrows in the bar indicate which direction it is filling with more arrows meaning faster progress. Fatigue is the inverse of the fatigue bar, meaning that when the bar is full, fatigue is at a minimum, and when it is depleted, fatigue is at a maximum.
- Recommended encumbrance begins to drop when the fatigue bar reaches below 50% in all difficulties

![UI Long Hunger](../assets/UI_Long-Hunger.jpg) A player that remains starving for a long enough time will start to have their [fatigue](./Fatigue.md) affected; the maximal amount of energy that the player will be able to acquire through sleep will start to decrease, which is represented by the red color that starts filling up the inside of the fatigue bar, as well as by the yellow exclamation mark that appears next to the eye icon, symbolizing the fatigue bar. This issue is easily solved by consuming food, the red color won't vanish immediately, but the player will be allowed to gain full energy from sleep right away.
[Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) also slowly drain the player's maximum available Fatigue bar to the same effect, but have a far harsher treating period.

**Fear** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) found within _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is one of two unique Afflictions that can be encountered only within the [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) [Challenge](./Challenge.md).

A much worse affliction than [Anxiety](./Anxiety.md), Fear occurs when the player is less than 50m (~164 feet) from the Darkwalker. The player's screen will become very bloody and the player will lose -50% [Condition](./Condition.md) per minute (real-time) as long as they remain near the beast. The player survivor will occasionally scream hysterically as long as they suffer from Fear.
Moving 50m away from the Darkwalker will result in the player returning to the [Anxiety](./Anxiety.md) Affliction and will stop the condition loss drain.

![A player achieving the Free Running feat](../assets/Feat.jpg)_A player achieving the Free Running feat_ **Feats** are passive perk bonuses that can be unlocked in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ and enabled in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

Feats are a form of persistent progression, offering passive bonuses to Survival Mode characters. They cannot be used while playing [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), [Challenges](./Challenge.md) or [Misery Mode](./Misery.md). As of Tales from the Far Territory Part 5 (June 2024) there are 13 different Feats, each with unique effects. Feat progression is acquired while playing Survival Mode or Challenges.
- To activate a Feat, it must be unlocked by completing its requirement(s) on a Survival save (E.g. _"Spend 100 days outside"_ for _"Cold Fusion")_
- Playing in a Custom sandbox allows Feats to be used, but does not count towards feat progress
- Once a sandbox game has been created, Feats selected for that save file cannot be changed
- Unlike [Survival Skills](./Skills.md), Feats are a type of meta-progression and are available from the start of a new save

**Feels Like** is the catch-all result of all the variables and calculations affecting [Warmth](./Warmth.md). Having one number to manage simplifies the maintenance of warmth. Understanding how the number is generated allows deeper understanding of what can be done to manage it.

The character gains Warmth as long as 'feels like' remains above 0°C (32°F). The character loses Warmth whenever 'feels like' is below 0°C (32°F). When no warmth remains, the character loses condition until 'feels like' is brought back above 0°C (32°F). See: [Warmth](./Warmth.md).

'Feels like' temperature begins with a sum of all the temperatures on the Quick Stats menu in the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md): Air Temp, Wind Chill, and the two Clothing Bonuses. It can also include a warming bonus when applicable.

Air temp as displayed on the Survival Page is the result of calculations determining the temperature of the air around the character. Interior locations have stable temperatures. Exterior locations are more variable being weather dependent. Additionally, [fires](./Fire.md) directly increase local air temperatures with their heat output. However, the maximum air temperature is 40°C, though maximum fire output is 80°C for wood fuels and 200°C for coal, on real Life those temperatures are very dangerous to humans and animals.

Calculated directly from wind speed and air temp (See: [Weather](./Weather.md)), this is an additional reduction made to 'Feels like' temperatures (never positive) when wind is blowing. It is possible to avoid wind, and therefore wind chill, by shielding the character from the direction of the wind with terrain or structures (see: [Wind shield](./Survival%20Overlay.md)).

[Clothing](./Clothing.md) items have specific warming attributes, one for air temp protection and one for wind chill protection. Wearing that item of clothing grants that protection. The sum of all clothing worn is visible as the clothing bonus and clothing air temp bonus on the Survival Page. These bonuses are added directly when calculating the 'Feels like' temperature.

- Note: Clothing wind chill bonus will only cancel out actual wind chill. If the current wind chill is -4°C and clothing has a wind bonus of +6°C, only 4°C of clothing wind bonus will actually be used. If there is no wind chill, wind chill bonus will have no effect until a negative wind chill is encountered.
- Only the outer layer clothing affects the wind chill protection. Layered clothing below the outer one do not affect the wind chill protection even if they have a higher stat than the outer layer.

[Fires](./Fire.md) give off heat. Observing a fire will display its current heat output. That heat is added to directly to the natural air temperatures around the fire. Moving away from a fire will see this effect gradually fade with distance. Adding more fuel to a fire will raise its temperature output (and thus the surrounding air temp) up to a cap of 80°C. Fires lit in the [furnace](./Furnace.md) can be boosted up to an incredible 200°C using coal. Regardless, air temp will stop increasing when it reaches 40°C. The heat output from a fire can only be reduced by removing torches from the same fire. Otherwise, the heat will remain for the life of the fire.

[Torches](./Torch.md), [flares](./Flare.md), [matches](./Matches%20%28disambiguation%29.md), and [storm lanterns](./Storm%20Lantern.md) all give off heat when lit. Behaving like fire, these portable heat sources provide heat independently. Thus, holding a torch while standing next to a fire is warmer than either one alone. Portable heat sources also grant this benefit while on the ground, but their radius of effect is much smaller than fire's. In fact, when lying on the ground, their effect can only be felt by standing directly over them and crouching down.

When [Sleeping](./Sleep.md) the [bed](./Bed.md) chosen grants insulation to the occupant. How much is displayed on the Sleep Interface as Warmth Bonus and varies dependent on quality. This can be as low as +0.1° for a worn out [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) to as high as +12.0°C for a pristine [Bear skin bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md). During the time of sleep, Feel Like temperature will gain this bonus. This bonus will never be seen on the Survival Page however because it only occurs while sleeping and disappears immediately upon waking up.

- Expressed in degrees of temperature, it is always shown rounded to nearest integer though it is obvious that decimal calculations are carried. So even though 'feels like' shows exactly freezing, you are likely either gaining or losing heat based on the carried fraction.

**Field 31**, otherwise known as **Airfield 31**, is a small abandoned airport located deep within the The Far Territory of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), specifically in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) region. Though long since abandoned, the airfield is notable for having the largest concentrated number of electronics and vehicles in any Region of Great Bear, making it a perfect area to scavenge for scrap metal and other tools and components.
The tarmacs and hangars are littered with nonfunctional rescue helicopters and bush planes, as well as your average abandoned terrestrial vehicles.

Despite all electronics being rendered destroyed by the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), Airfield 31 is occasionally revived to its former glory when the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) appears in the night sky, being visible for miles thanks to the various runway lights that will unfortunately never guide any new passenger planes to its tarmac again. The area is also occasionally plagued by [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md).

**Field Dressing Your Kill, Vol. I** is a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) used to improve the [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) skill. It can also be used as Fuel when starting a [Fire](./Fire.md).

_Field Dressing Your Kill, Vol. I_ can be researched for 10 hours that can be broken into multiple 1-hour minimum research sessions. 10 [Carcass Harvesting skill points](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md#Skill_levels) are awarded on completing the research. By selecting the Settled Mind [Feat](./Feats.md), research time will be reduced by 20%, putting it at 8 hours.
- [Warmth](./Warmth.md), [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Thirst](./Thirst.md), and [Hunger](./Hunger.md) exceed 0%

If the player's fatigue, thirst or hunger meters go down to zero or if the environment becomes dark during a research session, the session will be terminated instantly. The hour of research that was in progress will not be completed and any time that had already been spent will be wasted. For a multiple-hour research session, only the incomplete hour will be lost, all the previous hours will still count towards completion of the book.

A **File Cabinet** is a stationary interactable object in [The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). It is most often found indoors, in workplaces and offices and sometime houses. They can contain many things, but they most commonly contain different variants of newspaper, candy bars, sodas and books. Being a container, they cannot be broken down. All filing cabinets have four different drawers, each being able to hold 10 kilograms apiece (22lbs).

In some cases, filing cabinets can have draws be open or missing, and thus are not searchable (but they still can have items inside). This is most common in larger locations, or in locations that are run-down, like [Carter Hydro Dam.](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md)

A dead body lay outside the helicopter's side door, which has been jammed wide open. Despite that, the location may be a precious small shelter against the weather and give a small warmth +5° C bonus.

An [Emergency Kit](./Emergency%20Kit.md) may spawn near the corpse outside and some of the small lockers onboard may contain mid-level loot. The helicopter wreck contains a bed in the form of a medical cot that provides a + 2 °C ( +3.6°F ) Warmth bonus, and the interior is useful in that you can build a fire shielded from the wind.

There is a small cave among the rocks south the helicopter close to the shoreline. A campfire and plastic container spawn there and a rabbit carcass spawns just outside the entrance. A bear cave can be found due west from this location.
- Concept art of the Final Approach helicopter was used to market the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.

- The [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) appears near the crashed chopper in the original teaser trailer for the Far Territory Expansion, but it's final location is found in the [Control Tower](./Control%20Tower.md).

**Description:** Complete “To SAR and Back” without using more than 50 pieces of coal.

**Finely Tuned** is a hidden [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[Wintermute](./Wintermute.md)_ [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This is a missable hidden achievement granted by using less than 50 pieces of [Coal](./Coal.md) to power the [Steam Locomotive](./Steam%20Train.md) during the main story mission [To SAR And Back](./To%20SAR%20And%20Back.md).
The player must use the Steam Locomotive at various part of the mission to pass through the region, as several gates must be crashed through in order to progress on foot.
- Make a manual save at the starting station before attempting this achievement, so you may go back to it if you do not unlock it.

- The cost of 50 Coal is not as daunting as it seems, as it is a very generously low limit of Coal that needs to be used. Around 35 pieces of Coal can be used to make a full trip around the region if PSI is rationed.

- Depositing Coal into the Steam Locomotive will cause the steam PSI to rise, and the player can then raise the speed of the train before switching to Neutral in order for inertia to carry the train further for a little while. This process is tedious and slow, but saves on much Coal.
- Several sections require the player to switch the train tracks, so be aware that you will need to back up if you miss a turn.
- The player must be at full speed to destroy obstacles. Being in the Brown speed range will destroy obstacles. Being in the Orange or White speed ranges will not.

- Once you have reached the SAR Station and recovered the [Trauma Kit](./Trauma%20Kit.md), the player can simply abandon the Steam Locomotive and just manually walk back along the main railroad line back to Heller. This strategy will be very time consuming, will tire Astrid out, and exposes her to Wolf attacks, but saves a significant amount of Coal in the process if you feel as though you have spent too much already.
Another way is to use neutral and second gear mainly, and use first gear only to move the train from its place: (faster, but requires some practice)

- Put 1-2 portions of coal on the train and shift the first gear, when the speed reaches the limit for white range switch to the second gear to full speed (brown range), then switch to neutral and let the steam PSI rise quickly. Repeat the process.
- Added to game.

**Fir Firewood** is a fuel for fires in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, it also is a material for repairing the [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md).

Fir Firewood can be harvested from downed Fir Limbs found outdoors with a [tool](./Tools.md). It can also be found inside of structures, firewood bins, rotten tree trunks, or near campfires and corpses. It can also be found by [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md). Fir has no bonus [fire-starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) chance, and is thus unfavorable for starting [Fire](./Fire.md) with.

- Fir Limbs respawn continually, making them a renewable resource and the [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) a renewable tool.

- Small Fir Limbs yield 3 Fir Firewood with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) (45 minutes and 2% condition loss on stalker difficulty), [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) (58 minutes), or [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) (90 minutes).
- Large Fir Limbs yield 4 Fir Firewood with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) (60 minutes), but cannot be harvested with a Hacksaw.
- Large and Small Fir Limbs cost tools the same condition per use (4%), making Large limbs more tool-friendly to harvest, except with the Hacksaw which cannot harvest Large Cedar or Large Fir Limbs.

Since a single piece of Fir Firewood has a fire duration of 1 hour and 30 minutes, so it's 90 min/kg is less efficient per weight than [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) at 120 min/kg. However, Fir Firewood is more time-efficient to harvest compared to [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md), since each piece of Fir burns for 30 minutes longer. A small Fir Limb will burn for 4.5 hours(3 pieces of Fir) whereas a small [Cedar](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) Limb provides 3 hours of burn-time. This is specifically useful when the player decides to chop wood outside but has limited time to do so because of cold weather, maintaining [Fire](./Fire.md), etc.

The **Fir Limb** is one of the many stationary interactable objects found in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. They respawn randomly in the world over time under trees, making them a renewable [material](./Materials.md).
There are two variants of this object: the small and the large. Both can be turned into [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md).

Compared to the [Cedar Limb](./Cedar%20Limb.md), the Fir Limb provides more minutes of fire per minute of harvesting time. Both limbs take 15 minutes to harvest per unit of firewood obtained from them, and Fir Firewood burns for 90 minutes per piece compared to Cedar's 60. The lower burn density of Fir, however, makes it less desirable for carrying around when travelling.

It's commonly believed that limbs respawn after strong winds or blizzards, but this is untrue. Radial spawns (sticks, branches, coal, stones ect.) simply spawn on a randomized timer, independent of any weather conditions.

Small limbs will provide 3 firewood and can be cut up using a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) (45 min), [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) (58 min), or [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) (90 min). Unlike their [Cedar Limbs](./Cedar%20Limb.md), these limbs offer no [Tinder Plug](./Tinder%20Plug.md) when harvested.
Large limbs cannot be cut up with a hacksaw, and take 60 min to harvest with a normal hatchet, or 77 min with an improvised tool. Large Fir Limbs are very rare and only appear in set locations:
- Between [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) and [Unnamed Pond](./Unnamed%20Pond.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md)

The **fire barrel** is an immovable [contained fire](./Fire.md#Contained_fires) in an open barrel. The fire barrel functions identically to other contained fires and player-made [campfire](./Campfire.md). The fire barrel provides no advantage over other contained fires, but it does allow protection against wind, unlike the player-made campfire. It has two [cooking](./Cooking.md) slots.
The fire barrel can be re-lit indefinitely, though it requires fresh starter, tinder, and fuel each time.
Fire barrels have fixed locations that do not change between games. They are found both indoors and outdoors.
- At [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md) in the outdoor barn near the Work Bench. (Outdoors)
- North of [Angler's Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md), towards the path that goes behind [Broad Falls](./Broad%20Falls.md) (Outdoors)
- At the end of the Gold Mine, near the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) and [Crampons](./Crampons.md) (Indoors)
- In the room with the code to the [Keypad](./Keypad.md) door in [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md), 2nd level where the [Detonators](./Detonators.md) are found. (Indoors)

> “**A crude Arrow hardened in a fire. Fragile, but simple to Craft. Only effective against small game.**”

**Fire Hardened Arrows** are craftable ammuntion items in _The Long Dark_. They released in the free update of Part 2: Signal Void for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.

A **Fire Hardened Arrow** is a craftable ammunition for the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) made from a [Campfire](./Campfire.md). It's made from (5) sticks and (5) crow feathers, and provides experience for the [Archery](./Archery.md) skill when landed on a living target.

Fire Hardened Arrows are effective at hunting small game, such as, [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) which they kill in one hit, and are easier to craft than [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md). However, Fire Hardened Arrows do not cause damage to large game, such as [Deer](./Deer.md), [Wolves](./Wolf.md), [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), [Cougars](./Cougar.md), [Bear](./Bear.md), [Moose](./Moose.md), and will break upon impact when hitting these larger targets.
Fire Hardened Arrows won't scare a charging Wolf, but direct hits on a Wolf made while undetected can cause it to flee (80% chance).

The total durability of fire hardened arrows is variable and depends on a material table to determine it's condition loss; with the hardness of the material and the angle at which the arrow impacts the target determining the amount of degradation received. After a hit takes the arrow's condition below 0% it will break and turn into a [Broken Fire Hardened Arrow](./Broken%20Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) then fall to the ground where it may be retrieved and harvested for 1 [Crow Feather](./Crow%20Feather.md).
Fire hardened arrows are unique in that they break instantly upon impact with all [animals](./Wildlife.md) except rabbit and ptarmigan.

[Fires](./Fire.md) generate heat to restore and conserve [Warmth](./Warmth.md). Players can cook food, melt snow, and purify water on any fire started through the fire starting skill.
Fire Starting is one of the easiest skills to train in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, as players can increase their skill by lighting a new fire at any time during their playthrough.

To start a fire, players have to "use" an existing [Firebox](./Fire.md#Types_of_fires) or fire or place a new campfire in an acceptable location. The player must then select an ignition source, tinder (optional at level 3 and higher), fuel, and an optional accelerant. At the top of the screen, the player's current fire starting skill and the chance of success with the currently selected materials are displayed.

The chance of a fire-starting attempt succeeding is calculated directly by adding the benefits of the character's skill and all materials being used in the attempt. Changing the materials can improve the chance of a successful start. Chances greater than 100% are rounded down to 100% and cannot fail.

Activating the start button on the bottom right will launch an attempt. A progress wheel will fill as the player character attempts to get the fire started. Normal attempts take 6 in-game minutes to achieve success. Attempts that include an accelerant take only 1 in-game minute. It is also possible to be interrupted in an attempt by aggressive [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md). Interrupted attempts count as a failure.

Failure, if it does occur by chance, will consume a random amount of time before canceling the progress bar and removing the campfire (unless the player is relighting an existing fireplace). Failing a starting chance consumes the tinder and any liquid used, but does not consume the fuel. Matches are consumed as ignition sources but torches and flares are not. Firestrikers suffer condition loss on every attempt, while a magnifying lens does not.
Players need one starter, one tinder, and one fuel before they can start fire starting. Player can start fires without a tinder after achieving level 3 in their fire starting skill.

Players can select any starter currently carried in their inventory. They are sequenced alphabetically and further sorted by condition, highest to lowest. The condition of the starter does not affect the chance of success.

A **Fire** is a pile of burning fuel that has been lit using the [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) [Survival Skill](./Skills.md). To make a fire, players need a starter, tinder (optional with Fire Starting skill 3), and fuel. Though optional, an [Accelerant](./Accelerant.md) or [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) can also be used in an emergency to bypass the slow waiting time when first igniting fires in order to get a fire up and running quickly. Fires provide and restore [Warmth](./Warmth.md) to the player. Uncooked foods can be [cooked](./Cooking.md) directly on cooking slots near fires or on the ground nearby (in the case of canned foods), and snow can be melted and boiled into [potable water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md).

To start a fire, players have to "use" an existing [firebox](#contained-fires) or [campfire](#campfires) and press the "Start Fire" hotkey. Players can also build a campfire using [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md) > Campcraft > Fire. The fire-starting interface presents four slots: an ignition source (starter), tinder, fuel, and accelerant (optional). At the top of the screen, the player's current fire starting skill, duration of fire, and the chance of success with the currently selected materials are displayed. Coal cannot be used to start a fire.
