Campfires have a maximum duration of 12 hours. You cannot add fuel to a fire if it would exceed 12 hours of burn time.

Fire duration is calculated from the moment the fire was first lit, so a fire started without accelerant will have already used 5 minutes of life before it can be interacted with. Example: A fire lit from a book (+18 min) will only have 13 minutes of life remaining when starting is complete.
Wind can seriously dampen campfire duration, reducing it to only 9 minutes, regardless of how much duration it had left See campfires (above).

When a fire's duration reaches zero, it does not immediately go out. Rather, it lingers on in a state called embers. How long the embers last will not be visible. Typically embers burn out within 5 minutes, but they may last up to 10 minutes. Embers remain as hot as the original fire. They can be even be used to complete cooking or processing water.

In Pilgrim and Voyageur difficulties, being next to any fire prevents the character from losing [Condition](./Condition.md) due to [freezing](./Warmth.md). Stalker must get the fire hot enough to get [Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md) greater than 0°C to stop freezing.
The [Forge](./Forge.md) has a unique temperature cap of 200°C that only pertains to coal.

Fires that are started in outdoor locations offer an outdoor fire bonus. This means that the Duration listed on the fire is inaccurate, and the fire will actually last up to 100% longer depending on the temperature. Colder temperatures will yield a longer-lasting fire, up until the bonus caps at -30°C, starting at -10°C. The bonus is determined based on air temperature (before factoring in the fire) at the survivor's position, meaning that if you go inside your outdoor fire will no longer receive the outdoor fire bonus. Even fires in pseudo-indoor areas like Mountaineer's Hut receive the burn duration bonus.

In regards to fire bonus, outdoor caves have a line separating the warm and cold sections. Standing at the back of the cave, a fire will receive a reduced bonus, down to 0% if the air temperature in the back of the cave reaches positive values. Utilizing this bonus, you can use significantly less wood to keep an overnight fire burning in a cave by standing in the cold section of the cave when interacting with your bedroll. Note that you will be subjected to the colder outdoor cave temperatures during your sleep, so consider your fire temperature accordingly.

![Coal icon](../assets/Coal_icon.png) [Coal](./Coal.md) cannot be used to start a fire. It can only be burnt in an already active fire. Coal is an important component for forging as it is the only fuel that can raise the fire temperature above 80°C (only at a forge). When coal is added to the [furnace](./Furnace.md), it is not restricted by the 12-hour fuel cap and can be added repeatedly. The temperature will rise for each coal added, up to the furnace temperature cap of 200°C, though the time cap stands, and any burn duration in excess of 12 hours is lost.

![The 5 options that appear during an active fire.](../assets/Fire_menu.jpg)_The 5 options that appear during an active fire._ A successful [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) attempt will result in an active fire. Interacting with the active fire will result in 5 options appearing in regards to the active fire.
The fire starting portion if a fire. The option to take charcoal is also present in this menu.
Adding more fuel will both keep a fire alive for longer and raise the active temperature around it.

![Torch icon](../assets/Torch_icon.png) A [Torch](./Torch.md) can be taken out of any active fire, regardless of what material was used to create it, by activating the button on the bottom right, which reduces the fire by 10 minutes duration and 1°C and exits the fire page with the torch in hand. The "Take Torch" button only appears when a fire has at least 10 minutes of duration remaining. Torches taken from fire will have 25-50% condition and can be extinguished right away for later use. Torches can also be used as fuel for the fire, but taken torches will not fully refund the amount of fuel time lost.

The Place menu option allows any cooking container/canned goods/teas in the player's inventory to be directly placed onto any cooking slot of the fire without having to manually go into the inventory and manually place cooking containers into the game world. The player can then select which item they want placed onto the firebox. If all cooking slots are already occupied, this option will not do anything.

![The water processing old menu](../assets/305620_20160916193727_1.png)_The water processing old menu_ Water is obtained from fires through melting and boiling snow by first placing a Recycled Can, Cooking Skillet, or Cooking Pot on the heat source. Snow is provided whenever boiling snow is melted, even if the active fire is currently indoors or underground:

Snow will actively melt into [Water (Unsafe)](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md) if it is not fully melted. Higher amounts of snow/water being melted/boiled takes longer periods of time than smaller quantities:
- Melting snow for 19 minutes in a Recycled Can. 15 minutes for a Cooking Pot or Cooking Skillet) produces 0.50L [Water (Unsafe)](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md)
- Boiling 0.50L [Water (Unsafe)](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md) for 19 minutes in a Recycled Can (15 for a Cooking Pot or Cooking Skillet) produces 0.50L [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md)
A unique crafting menu, Fire Crafting, is only accessible at an active fire. At present, only one recipe is available to craft at an active fire, [Fire Hardened Arrow](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md).
This option appears only at inactive fireboxes, and is used to take Charcoal from the fire for personal use.

This option only appears at an inactive Campfire, and is used to remove the object from the game world. Any items not taken from the Campfire will be returned to the player's inventory, such as cooking containers and Charcoal.

[Wolves](./Wolf.md) will halt upon reaching a campfire, holding their ground. Should the player go closer to the Wolf it will attack the player instead, it's advised to go a bit farther away or closer to the fire to prevent the Wolf from attacking. Aiming a an item at the Wolf (be it a weapon, a rock, or the [Camera](./Camera.md)) will cause it to flee for a short time. Successfully throwing a Torch at the Wolf will cause it to flee for an extended period of time. Contained fires with no visual contact with the predator (be it a Bear or a Wolf) will not act as a deterrent because the predator will be too close, and once the Wolf starts charging you will have 2 options: run away from the fire and return back if you are light enough or take the risk and aim, UNLESS the predator is a bear.

Auroras will make all predators completely aggressive, thus torches, fires, and flares _WILL NOT STOP OR DETER_ any predator from charging at you. [ru:Костёр](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%82%D1%91%D1%80) [de:Feuer](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feuer)

**Firelogs** are one of the many sources of fuel that can be found on Great Bear Island.

The Firelog burns for two hours and increases the probability of successfully lighting a fire by 7%. However, they are not very weight-efficient at only 60 min/kg, and have the lowest emitted heat to burn time ratio of any fuel source in the game by a wide margin. Overall, firelogs are not outstanding forms of fuel. If a long-lived fire is desired, [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) is a more efficient option choice, and, if a particularly hot fire is desired, Coal is the best choice. Both are renewable and convenient to use.

The **fire place** is an immovable [contained fire](./Fire.md#Contained_fires). The fire place functions identically to other contained fires and player-made [campfire](./Campfire.md). The fire place provides no advantage over other contained fires, but it does allow protection against wind, unlike the player-made campfire. It has two [cooking](./Cooking.md) slots.
The fire place can be re-lit indefinitely, though it requires fresh starter, tinder, and fuel each time.
Fire places have fixed locations that do not change between games. They are found in many indoor locations in _The Long Dark_, including houses, trailers, and huts.

A powerful, reusable fire starter, this tool increases the probability of lighting a fire by 15%.

Discovered in random states of condition. Each try to light a fire or a [Torch](./Torch.md) reduces its condition by 2% so a new Firestriker can be used 50 times before it breaks down. Firestrikers cannot be repaired.
- Commonly inside the fire-starting [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) on [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md).
- Inside a Cave to the Far South by Southwest of Forlorn Muskeg. The one near the fallen Signal Tower.

Rarely spawns on shelves or tables in place of more common [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md). Rare discovered while searching large toolbox drawers. Found in one of the randomly occurring [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md) that is dedicated to fire and fire starting implements.

- Using a lit [Torch](./Torch.md) to start [Campfires](./Campfire.md) is an effective way to save Matches/Firestriker durability.
- Firestrikers are more weight-efficient than wood matches at 20% durability and higher (10 matches weighs 0.10kg), and less weight efficient below 20% durability.

- Modeled after ferrocerium-and-steel type fire starters that provide oxidizing cerium sparks as a temporary ignition source. Popular amongst outdoorsmen and survivalists due to their compact size, durability, and resistance to water.
- In real life, modern ferrocerium firestrikers can typically be used several thousands of times, as each strike only scrapes off a very small amount of material.

- An item that was unreleased for the Pre Alpha versions of the game, [Flint and Steel](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md#Flint_and_Steel), was eventually cut and replaced with the Firestriker.

**Astrid's a doctor so we're covered there, but...probably best to have some extra meds just in case.**

The **First Aid Kit** is an item found at the beginning of [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) in the mission [Memories](./Memories.md). It is found inside the [Jackrabbit Remote Transport](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md), and is one of 3 extra items that can be placed inside Mackenzie's Floatplane (along with [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) and [Astrid's Backpack](./Astrid%27s%20Backpack.md)) before takeoff.
If the player chooses to put the First Aid Kit in the plane's hatch, it will break open once the plane crashes and the following items can be recovered for use:

Arguably the least useful choice of supplies overall, as Bandages are easily crafted and the other items can be found somewhat easily on Green Survivor and Capable Survivor. On Green Survivor, [Wolves](./Wolf.md) can be safely ignored, avoiding [Infection](./Infection.md) entirely. [Dysentery](./Dysentery.md) can be avoided by not drinking unsafe water, and [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) can be avoided by not eating low-condition food or raw meat. Painkillers are the least useful, as [Pain](./Pain.md) has no real detrimental effects in Wintermute and is cured easily enough without treatment, [Burns](./Burns.md) are only possible to get in Episode 1 by walking directly into a [Campfire](./Campfire.md), and there are no [Moose](./Moose.md) present in Episode 1 to potentially give [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md). The Emergency Stim may be useful for the rope climbs at the end of the episode, but it's very likely to find at least one while looting Milton and completing the side missions.

violations.context: > “__Study Your Treatments and Learn to Triage

There are many ways to die in the wilderness. Medical treatments -- man-made or harvested from the natural world -- will save your life. Use the Status screen to check on your health. Apply a Treatment using the First Aid Radial menu. You can also use Treatments from your Pack menu.__”

**First Aid** is both a term and category used for items that can be consumed to prevent or treat injuries and diseases to the player throughout their playthrough. They have their own dedicated section within the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md).

Negative afflictions cause [Condition](./Condition.md) loss and/or otherwise impede the player. There are currently 39 types of negative afflictions, which can be classified into two types: injuries and diseases.

Injuries are caused by falling, [animal attacks](./Struggle.md), or exposure to the elements. The names of injuries that can affect a player will be briefly displayed on screen when they occur. Additionally, the player character will usually cry out in pain.

Prior to contracting diseases, players are able to view their risk for the disease in the status menu. Certain actions taken by the player, such as consuming raw carnivore meat or drinking unsafe water, dramatically increase the risk that the player will contract the related disease. Once the disease has been contracted, treatment is required to remove the negative effects.

Administering First Aid to treat an injury or disease is done primarily using the first aid interface from the Radial Menu. Current afflictions are listed and selectable on the left side of the screen. First Aid items can also be consumed directly from the inventory. Although, since the game does not pause in the inventory menu, the additional steps might waste precious time.

After selecting the first aid item, a menu with the player's current afflictions allows the player to direct the treatment to the specific affliction. Using the wrong treatment on the wrong affliction, however, _will_ still consume the item without curing the affliction. The player will need to apply the correct treatment on the right affliction to begin recovering.

It is possible to have multiple instances of similar afflictions. Each must be treated individually. Many afflictions will have two different possible treatments; regardless, treatments are only selectable when the necessary items are in the inventory. Many afflictions also require a resting or waiting period to completely cure after the treatment is applied.

Afflictions disappear when they are cured. Some afflictions will disappear without treatment once sufficient time has passed, while others slowly drain condition and can kill they player if not cured quickly enough.

![Will Mackenzie and Dr. Astrid Greenwood witness the First Flare moments before their plane crashes](../assets/FirstFlare.jpg)_Will Mackenzie and Dr. Astrid Greenwood witness the First Flare moments before their plane crashes_

> **The lights in the sky are a reckoning. The wonder of humanity and all its creations, laid bare. Her warnings went unheeded... The signs were there, for those willing to see them. This has all happened before. Soon we'll all be tested. We'll all have to choose how far we'll go to survive.**

The **First Flare**refers to the first appearance of an intense [Aurora](./Aurora.md) in _The Long Dark_'s Story Mode [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). It is the primary cause of the so-called "quiet apocalypse" seen in both Wintermute and [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

According to the [Prison Transport Manifest](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md), the First Flare specifically took place on the night of Thursday, November XX, 20XX. The First Flare event took place at least 10 years after [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md), the colloquial name for the economic collapse of the Canadian - and wider North American - economy, based on conversations between [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) and [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) (Grey Mother mentions that Milton needed help 10 years ago, but this information has since been removed in the Redux [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) release. It is unknown if the 10 years is still canon).

The cause of the First Flare and subsequent Aurora has been labelled as a [geomagnetic storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geomagnetic_storm). Its most immediate effect was the widespread disruption of electronic devices; including lights, cell phones, computers, televisions, radios, power plants, and vehicles. One of the Flare's slower but more devastating effects is the destabilization of weather patterns and wildlife behavior, leading to extreme weather and unusual animal activity in many areas.

Due to the loss of worldwide communication and the isolation of the game's setting of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), it is impossible to determine the exact scope of the First Flare's destruction; however given the widespread electronic EMP devastation visible throughout the Island, the First Flare was most likely a [Carrington Class](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrington_Event) Coronal Mass Ejection Event that struck Earth. It can thus be inferred that the entire world has been affected, leading to the collapse of human civilization and a much "louder apocalypse" for those currently residing in major human settlements.

- Electronic devices across northern [Canada](./The%20Collapse.md) and presumably the rest of the world (not mentioned, confirmed or refuted by Wintermute story) stop working, leading to total blackouts and loss of communication, and possibly the collapse of most nation states.

- Wildlife behavior is disrupted. Predators that once avoided humans now stalk or attack them on sight. Bears are roused from their hibernation and begin roaming the area. Wildlife that normally sleep at night (such as birds) become active when the Aurora is out at night.

- Disruption of weather patterns, extremely cold temperatures, and brutal snowstorms occur frequently across many regions of Great Bear Island and presumably the rest of northern Canada. Reoccurring Auroras and [Electrostatic Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) begins to plague certain areas of the world, occasionally reviving technology and [computers](./Buffer%20Memories.md). (Earth's magnetic polarity fields may have been damaged, explaining the sudden shifts in weather and the longer winter in the northern pole.)

- Loss of electricity, severe weather, and food/water shortages leads to widespread looting and violence throughout many of the affected areas. It can be inferred that law and order in cities across the planet has also presumably broken down for the time being.

- An unusual amount of earthquakes begin to rock various sections of Great Bear Island (although it is implied to have occurred during the aftermath of the Collapse, and not as a result of the First Flare), causing landslides and avalanches to bury most of the island's infrastructure. Seamless connections to other regions are now made impossible to travel between via working vehicles or foot travel. Travelers are forced to use dangerous abandoned mineshafts, caves systems, and other side passages to navigate around major or even basic obstructions. Rope climbing across steep cliffs is required to leave or enter certain isolated locations, such as Milton.
- Dozens of motorists are stranded on highways and roads after their cars stopped working. Refugees from the highways begin to make their way toward towns and cities.

- Pilot [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) and [Dr. Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) crash in the mountains outside of Milton following the total loss of power to [Mackenzie's Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md).

- A prison bus carrying several inmates to [Blackrock Federal Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) crashes into a collapsed tunnel outside Milton. Some of the inmates survive, [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) among them, and proceed to [Milton](./Milton.md), where they hold residents hostage in the [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md). The residents are killed by a fire from a subsequent Aurora event and the Convicts scatter. Wolves begin to overtake the town shortly after, due to a lack of humans.

- The [Prisoners](./Convicts.md) of Blackrock Federal Penitentiary break out of their cells and execute the prison's staff, turning the prison into their own personal fortress and using it as a base of operations to begin looting nearby locales as they see fit.
- A motorist named Matt loses control of [his truck](./Matt%27s%20Truck.md) and drives off a bridge in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md). _(Survival mode; unconfirmed for Wintermute)_

- A passenger plane crashes near [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md) in Pleasant Valley. Many do not make it and the remaining survivors make their way to [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), though some become lost along the way.
- Several helicopters and [planes crash](./Plane%20Crashes.md) across various sections of the island.

- Many fishing boats around the coast of Great Bear lose power and break down. The [Fukattsu Maru](./Fukkatsu%20Maru.md) picks up some survivors, but subsequent Auroras eventually cause the crew and passengers to lose their sanity and jump overboard.
- A disease outbreak in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) worsens, with sufferers getting dementia-like symptoms. Many people end up wandering off and drowning near water.

The Fisherman's Sweater is a thick, heavy clothing item with a nautical fashion style. It is quite warm but rare, and has one of the best weight-to-warmth ratio of all sweaters, with warmth similar (but slightly inferior to) the rare [Cowichan Sweater](./Cowichan%20Sweater.md), while weighing half as much. It is a direct upgrade to the [Thick Wool Sweater](./Thick%20Wool%20Sweater.md), with better stats while weighing the same. It also looks like an [Aran-Knit Sweater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aran_jumper).

A set of Fisherman Sweater's is guaranteed from [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) at the [Summit](./Summit.md) and inside a [Memento](./Mementos.md) Cache in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md).

**Fishing Bait** is a Tool used for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) in _The Long Dark_. It released in the free update of Part 3: Frontier Comforts for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.

Bait is not necessary to catch fish, but can be used when fishing to increase the weight of fish caught by Ice Fishing by 50%. Bait is harvested from any raw fish, and yields a number of units per kg of fish which was harvested. When fishing manually with [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) or with [Fishing Tip-Ups](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md), Bait may be selected (as can [Fishing Lures](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28Acorns%29.md)).
- Harvested fish produce 3-14 pieces of bait based on weight (3 Bait per kilogram of fish, rounded down. With breakpoints at X.00kg, X.35kg and X.70kg)
- Bait [Smells](./Scent.md) and will attract [predatory wildlife](./Wolf.md) (despite not displaying on the Scent Indicator, currently a bug).
- Bait decays over time and cannot be used once ruined. Raw fish will always yield 100% condition bait when harvested (even if the fish is 0% condition "ruined").

Whitefish/Trout weigh significantly less than Coho Salmon/Smallmouth Bass, but give double the [Vitamin-C](./Scurvy.md) per kg. This makes it more efficient for Vitamin-C and time to harvest larger 'uncommon' fish (Coho Salmon/Smallmouth Bass). Rare Fish (goldeye, burbot, etc.) do not yield any Vitamin-C, but can be difficult to acquire. If fishing for calories, then whitefish, trout, or goldeye should be harvested.

The Fishing Camp is located on the western side of the region, between [Bear Creek Campground](./Bear%20Creek%20Campground.md) and [Jackrabbit Island](./Jackrabbit%20Island.md).

The Fishing Camp is a suitable place to set up a [safe house](./Safehouse.md). The four cabins combined provided ample supplies. There is a [fishing hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) nearby to [catch fish](./Ice%20Fishing.md) when hungry, a [workbench](./Work%20Bench.md), and a bed to sleep. However, it lacks a way to make fire indoors or a windproof fire outdoors; additionally, the workbench is outside, exposed to predators and the elements. The fishing hut near the Camp has a potbelly stove.

A [hatchet](./Hatchet.md) often spawns near the fishing nets and pallets located near the roadside. A knife, a hammer, or a [mountaineering rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) may be found on the workbench. Additionally, a corpse near the end of the dock may be holding a [hunting knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md). Keep an eye out for wolves that may be patrolling the area near the body.

**Fishing huts**are a type of small structure found on frozen lakes and coasts. While they can be found in many regions, they are especially abundant in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) and [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md).
Fishing huts are sheds placed on a frozen lake or ocean to provide shelter during ice [fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md).

Fishing huts have an ice fishing hole, which can be used after breaking the ice cover of it with a [hatchet](./Hatchet.md), [hunting knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), [prybar](./Prybar.md), or [heavy hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md). Other furniture includes a [pot belly stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), [cupboard](./Cupboard.md), [drawer](./Drawer.md) and two shelves. There is enough space to place a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) or a bearskin bedroll. In addition to being able to use the stove for warmth, fishing in a fishing hut results in faster catch times and reduced wear to [tip-ups](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md) compared to free form ice fishing.

Most fishing huts lack doors, but animals, to include [wolves](./Wolf.md) and [bears](./Bear.md), do not enter them. Fishing huts with doors will also keep out bears and wolves when closed. _However_, even with the door closed, animals can still sense the player's presence, and may awaken the player if they attempt to [sleep](./Sleep.md). The player can try going to sleep again, but if a hostile animal is still nearby, there is a chance the player will be awoken again. If the player is unexpectedly awoken by a hostile animal, the game will register this as an interrupted sleep and will not save.
Note that fishing huts with door give a +3ºC [warmth](./Warmth.md) bonus (it doesn't matter whether the door is open or not).

Common items to find inside the hut are: [fishing tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md), [hook](./Hook.md), [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) and some wood like [cedar firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) or [reclaimed wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md). Rarely, the player may find a [hatchet](./Hatchet.md), [hunting knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), or [rifle ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md).

As the interior of fishing huts technically counts as outside, they make excellent shelters when trying for the [Night Walker](./Night%20Walker.md) and [Beneath a Starry Sky](./Beneath%20a%20Starry%20Sky.md) achievements, as well as warding off [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md). Magnifying lens can also be used to start fire in oven, in case if weather conditions are suitable.

The map with the most fishing huts is [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), with a total of nine huts scattered across the frozen bay. [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) also hosts four fishing huts on [its namesake lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md). Additionally, [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) and [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) have two huts each, with Bleak Inlet's huts being near the [Fallen Lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md) and Forsaken Airfield having huts near [Drift Island](./Drift%20Island.md). Finally, [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), and [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) each have one hut, located on [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md), a frozen river, [Pensive Pond](./Pensive%20Pond.md), and [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md) respectively. Ash Canyon's hut is unique in that it is ruined, but the [Pot belly stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md) can still be used for warmth.

Locations that don't have any fishing huts include [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md), [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), and [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), although it's possible to fish in most regions using a free-form fishing hole.

**Fishing Tip-Ups** are [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) and [Trapping](./Trapping.md) [Tools](./Tools.md) used to passively catch fish. They were introduced in the free update portion of the Part 3: Frontier Comforts of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.

A Fishing Tip-Up is a low tech, improvised tool composed of 2 sticks in a cross shape, metal fasteners, and a fishing tackle. Two pieces of scrap, serving as bells, are also attached. At the top of the construction is a red cloth, meant to move in the wind and signal that a fish has been caught to its user from afar.

Similar to how [Snares](./Snare.md) work on land, Tip-Ups are traps used to passively fish in bodies of water without the player needing to constantly be present. [Fishing Bait](./Fishing%20Bait.md) and [Fishing Lures](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28Acorns%29.md) can be placed on the Tip-Up prior to placing in an open ice hole.

After clearing an ice hole with an ice breaker, and placing the Tip-Up in the water, the tool will auto fish for the player. As time passes and a fish bites the tackle, the tool will "tip up" and be pulled into the hole (hence the name), stopping itself from falling in completely due to its cross shape design. A bell will sound from the 2 metal bits clanking together when the tool falls in the hole, alerting the player of a catch if they are nearby.

Combined with the Free-Form Ice Hole Cutting menu option, they can be used to fish within regions that do not natively have a [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md), so long as the frozen body of water is sufficiently deep.

Tip-Ups can be crafted at a [Workbench](./Work%20Bench.md), requiring no extra tools. They take 40 minutes to make, and require: 2 [Sticks](./Stick.md), 1 [Cloth](./Cloth.md), 1 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), and 1 [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md). Harvesting yields 1 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) and 1 [Stick](./Stick.md). Crafting time can be reduced to 30 minutes if Simple Tools are used, and 20 minutes if Quality Tools are used. Ruined fishing tackles will still function in the recipe.

- Attempting to "farm fish" by placing more than 6 Tip-Ups per separate body of water will result in overfishing penalties where any Tip-Ups over the set limit will start to experience increasingly slower catch rates. The [Zone of Contamination's](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) fishing spot at [Unquenched Extraction](./Unquenched%20Extraction.md) is unique in that the overfishing penalty will apply when more than 4 Tip-Ups are deployed.

- Tip-Ups have durability and can break like snares, they lose condition over time while deployed at a rate of 0.5%/hour inside a fishing huts ice hole, and 1%/hour when placed in free-form ice fishing holes. They cannot be repaired, only harvested for 1 stick and 1 scrap metal.
- Tip-Ups have a 10% chance to have their "line break" on catch which will instantly drop it's condition by 10% and fail to retrieve the caught fish.

- Once condition drops below 0% the Tip-Up will vanish upon being picked up. The player should try to harvest low condition Tip-Ups just before they reach the 10% condition mark and risk the 10% chance of a line breakage destroying it completely.

- Ice holes do not freeze over while in direct use by the player, but Tip-Ups placed in ice holes do not enjoy this benefit. Recently cleared ice holes won't start freezing again for 10 in-game minutes, which can reduce the amount of ice clearing required to operate multiple Tip-Ups at once.

- The player should exercise great caution while maintaining multiple tip ups out in the open, as the process of breaking ice will accelerate time and potentially cause rapid weather changes, and if the player's [Scent](./Scent.md) is high, animals like [Bears](./Bear.md), [Wolves](./Wolf.md), and [Cougars](./Cougar.md) will quickly home in on the player's location and attack.

- While a single Tip-Up can greatly benefit from a fishing hut's halved decay rate and slowed ice hole re-freezing rate, they are often best used out in the open ice by using the Free-Form Ice Hole cutting radial menu option where several may be placed next to each other for easy operation. Fishing huts can have free-form ice holes placed immediately outside their door allowing reach to all 6 Tip-Ups from the shelter of the hut, and the Ice fishing hole in the hut may still be fished from manually to level up/utilize fishing skill without contributing to the overfishing limit.

- With some effort in ice hole placement, it is possible to reach up to 4 Tip-Ups at once from the safety of a [snow shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md). There is at least one area in each fishable region allowing snow shelters access to suitable ice, except in [Crumbling Highway](./Crumbling%20Highway.md) and the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md).

Flare shells are the ammunition for the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md). When fired they glow brightly for 15 game minutes and travel whole in an arching path until they contact a solid surface. After coming to rest, they remain in the environment indefinitely but cannot be further interacted with. Grounded flares cannot scare off predators after landing, only body shots will frighten predators. While a burning round does look like a [Flare](./Flare.md), it does not give off any heat and cannot be used to light a [Fire](./Fire.md).

They are always found in 100% condition and stack in the inventory. Flare Shells cannot be crafted at an [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) and spent Flare Shell casings cannot be recovered like [Rifle Shell Casings](./Rifle%20Shell%20Casing.md) or [Revolver Shell Casings](./Revolver%20Shell%20Casing.md).

Occasionally, after shooting a flare shell and sticking any wildlife with a direct hit, the flare shell will be able to be picked up and reused after burning out. The reason behind this is unknown, but it seems to be a bug.

Flare Shells are often found in an [Emergency Kit](./Emergency%20Kit.md) with the Distress Pistol. They are also sometimes discovered inside toolbox drawers or on [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) or perhaps inside lockers. The Stockpile version of the [prepper cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) always contains some, if that can be found. Flare Shells can also be obtained via [beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) (not on Interloper).

**Flares** are a multi-purpose tool in _The Long Dark_. They can be used as a light source, [firestarter](./Fire%20Starting.md), or frightening [wildlife](./Wildlife.md).

Once lit, flares burn for 1 hour (5 real minutes), providing light and warmth to the surrounding area. However, unlike the [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) or [Torch](./Torch.md), they cannot be manually extinguished nor re-lit once ignited. Flares can be lit in [strong winds and blizzards](./Weather.md) and will not be extinguished by them, however walking under a waterfall with a lit flare will instantly extinguish it and "ruin" it with no ability to relight it.

Flares are effective at deterring [wolves](./Wolf.md), [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), [deer](./Deer.md) and [rabbits](./Rabbit.md); wolves and timberwolves will not approach within 15M of a lit flare (held, or on the ground), and wolves may be frightened by lit flares when thrown (but not timberwolves).
Once a lit flare has consumed all its fuel it will become "Ruined" and have no further use, but will continue to weigh 0.25kg.
- Flares may be selected from from the Radial Menu (Radial>Light Sources>Flare), the Light Sources hotkey ("1"), or from the inventory.
- For firestarting a flare must first be ignited, and then select as a "Starter" option in the campfire menu.

Thrown Flares can be picked up even while burning, this makes them an effective tool against multiple wolves (as long as the flare can be retrieved). Flares can even be picked up after they are burned out, though they serve no purpose (marked in the inventory as "RUINED" and red 'X' icon) and will still contribute weight to one's inventory.
Flares are effective at frightening wolves, deer and rabbits, and have limited usefulness against timberwolves.

- Wolves and timberwolves will respect lit flares and not approach within 15M of them (the same as [marine flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), [flare shells](./Flare%20Shell.md) and [campfires](./Campfire.md)). However, approaching a hostile wolf with a lit flare will result in an attack if you are encumbered, exhausted, have a sprain or sprint.
- Lit flares may cause a stalking wolf to flee when thrown (at the ground between the survivor and wolf), ideally the landing near the wolf's forelegs.

- Unlike blue [marine flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), red flares will not reduce [timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) morale unless the flare physically hits the timberwolf, recovering the thrown flare without being bitten can be challenging.
- If a wolf is already charging into an attack, it will not be intimidated by a thrown flare.
- Flares and marine flares are most effective at passive deterrence when moving away from a predator.

- Bears are deterred by flares, stopping mid-charge just outside a 15 meter radius around the player, however they will continue to chase them until they reach safety (such as enter a vehicle, walk off a ledge etc) or the flare runs out and the bear attacks. Throwing the flare at a charging bear has no effect. Standing still for too long or not moving away quickly enough will provoke the bear to charge, ignoring the flare completely.

violations.context: #### Frightening Wolves

Below is an effective tactic for scaring wolves with lit torches or flares (either variety). This tactic will always work at frightening wolf (unlike thrown torches) and is easier to perform, especially against multiple wolves.
- Approaching the wolf to 15M, the animal will stop and assume a "stand ground" posture (forelegs spread, ears back and growling).
- Drop the flare (to where you are standing) and draw any weapon ("2") including [Stones](./Stone.md), then then aim at the wolf ("RMB").

- Timberwolves will also flee temporarily, but because their pack's morale is not reduced they will quickly return, it can nevertheless be useful if you have to walk through the pack to get to a safe place, fleeing timberwolves temporarily can't attack you, unlike ones which are standing and growling.

Flares cannot be harvested, crafted, or repaired and are found uncommonly in all regions on or beside Frozen Corpses, in the trunks and glove compartments of Vehicles, or inside Structures (usually hidden beneath or between furniture).
- Flares are "Emergency Roadside Flares", a type of pyrotechnic used to designate roadside construction, traffic hazards, vehicular accidents, or vehicular distress.

The **Flashlight**is a light emitting, self-defense tool in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is available in both Wintermute and Survival mode, and was added in the launch of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md)_._

The Flashlight is battery-powered portable light source used as a modern industrial age era replacement of the [Torch](./Torch.md) and [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), but is unfortunately no longer functional due to the effects of the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) (much like all modern electronics currently).

When equipped and used by the player, they will receive a message informing them that the battery is currently dead, making it little more than an unusable paper weight. During an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) or [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md), however, the Flashlight battery will instantly recharge to full battery capacity, and can be used as a portable light source again.

Turning the Flashlight on creates a cone of light, but will slowly drain its battery. While a Flashlight is on and wielded, its "high beam" mode (RMB) can be used, rapidly draining its battery but greatly lighting the surrounding area.

A 100% charged flashlight will last 1 hour of continuous use, or around 25 seconds when using the high beam mode. When used and turned off, Flashlights will slowly recharge back to their maximum storage capacity, as long as an Aurora/Glimmer Fog event remains active. Once these events end, the battery will immediately die, and the Flashlight will become unusable until the next event.

The high beam setting of the Flashlight can be used as a temporary defense against charging Aurora predators: (aurora [Wolf](./Wolf.md), aurora [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), and aurora [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), and aurora [Bear](./Bear.md)), but only so long as the battery is not completely drained. Flashlight high beams have absolutely no effect on aurora [Cougar](./Cougar.md).
Flashlight do not effect wildlife when powered by [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) (since they are currently not aurora predators).

Storm Lanterns and Flashlights are the only tools that do not [Decay](./Decay.md), even when equipped during a [Struggle](./Struggle.md). However they spawn with various levels of Condition and can be repaired with [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md).

- When turned on, a Flashlight provides light, but slowly drains its battery. The battery will be instantly full at the start of an Aurora/Glimmer Fog event, but will immediately be drained once these events end.

- The Flashlight is useful for saving [matches](./Matches%20%28disambiguation%29.md) for torches or [lamp fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) for storm lanterns, and players may take advantage of this during an Aurora/Glimmer Fog event when traveling through low light areas.

- When turned on, Flashlights provide a limited cone of light effect that has the farthest reach of any wieldable light source. They however do not saturate the entire nearby area with light, unlike [flares](./Flare.md), torches, and storm lanterns. This can create a "tunnel vision" effect that leaves nearby corners of the player's vision unlit. Turning the High Beam mode on will greatly saturate the area in light, at the cost of battery life.

- A Flashlight's high beam (Place / Aim / Throw key) is effective at stopping the charge of an Aurora Wolf, Aurora Timberwolf or Aurora Bear. High Beam drains a large amount of battery while active, but only a short burst is required to stop a charging aurora animal.
- Flashlights can remain powered even when dropped or placed, allowing them to be used as temporary stationary lights during an aurora. Their high beam cannot be active when placed/dropped.

During an Aurora or Glimmer Fog event, using the Flashlight on High will cause the tip of the Flashlight to emit sparks, visually explaining why the battery power dies so quickly. Despite the obviously high power consumption, the battery will never short circuit/suffer critical operational damage from being overcharged.
The light the Flashlight emits in High Beam Mode flashes between the colors Purple, Green, and Blue.
The Flashlight appears to be loosely based on a 1920s vintage Ever-Ready flashlight, however uses a LED bulb as opposed to the Ever-Ready's fluorescent bulb.

A **Flight Jacket** is a type of [Clothing](./Clothing.md) in The Long Dark. It is part of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC.

Flight Jackets are rare, mostly located in places related to airplanes like the multiple planes around [Field 31](./Field%2031.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) or the occasional [crashed planes](./Plane%20Crashes.md) in Lower Great Bear. This clothing piece offers an excellent windproof bonus and a good amount of warmth, plus balanced stats overall, making a great choice if you don't have an [Expedition Parka](./Expedition%20Parka.md) or a better clothing piece.
Note: While it used to spawn, it is no longer available on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) difficulty.
- Available rarely from trunks found when [beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) after a blizzard.

A wide variety of **foods and drinks** exist in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md),_ including prepackaged foods, meat, brewable beverages, and medicinal remedies. Some foods can be eaten as is or cooked.

Food and drink items primarily designed to refill the [Hunger](./Hunger.md) (Calorie Store) and [Thirst](./Thirst.md) [Needs](./Needs.md), but can sometimes refill [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) or [Warmth](./Warmth.md). Attempting to eat or drink when Hunger or Thirst is full will result in the error messages "you are too full to eat/you are not thirsty".
Keep in mind that some foods are only available for those that purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.

Especially when moving from place to place, it is usually wise to first consume the food that [spoils](./Decay.md#Food_and_drink) the fastest and has lower energy density, while saving energy-dense products for traveling or for an emergency.
- Ruined food generally cannot be eaten safely (unless [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Level 5 is achieved).

- It is generally advised to never eat raw meat, as even at Cooking level 5, the player can still get [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md). The only exception to the former rule regards eating fish raw vs eating fish cooked, as certain raw fish contain higher Vitamin-C doses to prevent [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md), though this will still cause Food Poisoning.
- If non-canned food is stored outdoors, decay is slowed substantially and the lifespan of the food is extended (except for meat quarters).
- Another long-term food option is [Cat Tail Stalks](./Cat%20Tail%20Stalk.md). While low in calories, they do not decay, are plentiful in most regions, and serve as good emergency food caches.

It is important to note that cooking Food and Drink adds more calories to the cooked item version (up to 25% extra calories at Level 5 Cooking). The caloric content for each item below is listed at the base Level 0 Cooking values for reference.

Food and Drink have their own 2 dedicated sections within the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md), but share the same menu in the Backpack [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md). **Note**: Most of these foods and drinks can be found in Wintermute.

**Food Poisoning** is a negative affliction that is contracted by eating raw meat, or food with a low item [Condition](./Condition.md).

Food Poisoning occurs randomly when consuming [food items](./Food%20And%20Drink.md). Raw meat and low-condition foods pose the highest risk, whereas high-condition cooked, canned, or processed foods are generally safer options.
Beverage items cannot cause food poisoning; however, [Non-Potable Water](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md) can cause [Dysentery](./Dysentery.md).

Food above 75% condition will never cause food poisoning, except raw meat and fish. Packaged or canned food items at or above 20% condition are also completely safe; the only exceptions are [Chocolate Bar](./Chocolate%20Bar.md), [Granola Bar](./Granola%20Bar.md), [Peanut Butter](./Peanut%20Butter.md), and [Tin of Sardines](./Tin%20of%20Sardines.md), each posing a risk between 1 and 3 percent.

After achieving Level 5 in [Cooking](./Cooking.md), only raw meat, raw fish, and animal fat will cause Food Poisoning. Contracting [Sour Stomach](./Sour%20Stomach.md) (acquired from playing on [Misery](./Misery.md)) will remove this benefit however.

While suffering from Food Poisoning, the player's Condition while not sleeping will decrease by 10% per hour (to a minimum of 15%) and the player's [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) will decrease by 30% per hour. Food Poisoning cannot kill the player directly, but being at such low condition makes hazards like predator encounters, cold weather, dehydration, or even short falls likely to be deadly.
Instances of Food Poisoning do not stack, but a second instance will reset the duration of the first.

- Treatment requires consuming one dose (two pills) of [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md) or one cup of [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md)/[Burdock Tea](./Burdock%20Tea.md), followed by resting for a total of 10 hours. Condition will not drain after treatment and while sleeping, but the condition drain will resume upon waking if the player has not slept for the full 10 hours required. Condition regeneration from sleep is disabled while the affliction remains.

- Left untreated, Food Poisoning will pass automatically after 12 - 24 hours. This clock is not visible and the exact duration is decided at random. This can allow the strategic consumption of spoiled food at a safe location without having to consume antibiotics, but care should be taken to ensure [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) is not a risk.
The food poisoning chance depends on both the type of food and the condition of that food item:

- Food with Condition over 75% will never cause Food Poisoning (excludes Raw Meat and Fish).
- If left untreated, Food Poisoning will now degrade Condition to just before the point of death.
- All Food items have been tuned for Calorie values, Condition Decay, and % chance of Food Poisoning.
- Made food poisoning more dangerous. Increased the hourly Condition drain to 10/hr (from 5/hr). Increased the hourly Fatigue increase to 20/hr (from 10/hr).
- Reduced the chance of getting Food Poisoning from canned goods (Peaches, Beans), and MREs.

- Improved player death description by including all critical sub-conditions that contribute to player's demise. Also, properly capture cause of death by afflictions (e.g., food poisoning) if there are no critical sub-conditions.
- Fixed issue with food poisoning continuing to degrade stats when resting (after antibiotics taken).

**Foraging** is the process of searching the world for harvestable Flora [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), either for the purposes of [Cooking](./Cooking.md), [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md), [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md), or even for crafting [Tools](./Tools.md). Many plants and fungi can be found relatively easily while traveling across the Island, and can be the key to surviving for long periods of time.
Foraging is often a very quick process that often requires no tools to pick or gather Flora from bushes, conifer tree stumps, or from plants growing out of the ground.
There are two types of items obtained from Flora in the game world; directly or indirectly harvestable Flora items:
Directly harvesting Flora simply requires the player to walk up to and click on the plant/fungus, where it will be turned into an item for the player:

| [Cat Tail Stalk icon](../assets/Cat_Tail_Stalk_icon.png) [Cat Tail Stalk](./Cat%20Tail%20Stalk.md) | Harvest [Cat Tail icon](../assets/Cat_Tail_icon.png) [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md) | 1 Cat Tail produces 1 Cat Tail Stalk |

| [Cat Tail Head icon](../assets/Cat_Tail_Head_icon.png) [Cat Tail Head](./Cat%20Tail%20Head.md) | Harvest [Cat Tail icon](../assets/Cat_Tail_icon.png) [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md) | 1 Cat Tail produces 1 Cat Tail Head |

The natural world often provide many remedies for healing personal ailments. [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) can often be healed via man made [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) items, but foraging can produce alternatives that can be produced repeatedly as the man made versions become more scarce. Has an interior **Foreman's Retreat** is a one-story, two-room house located in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) not far from [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md).

This house, being made for the mine's foreman, is far more luxurious than the small cabin found at [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md). It has two rooms, a living room and a bedroom with a single [Bed](./Bed.md). The cabin has both a [Wood Stove](./Wood%20Stove.md) and a [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md), but it lacks a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), although one can be found pretty close in the ruined barn of [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md).
It is possible for the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) to spawn here on the rifle rack. A few [Green Birch Sapling](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) spawn just downhill from the cabin.

Upon purchase of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC, the recipe card for [Ranger Stew](./Ranger%20Stew.md) can be found in varying places within the first room of the cabin, near the kitchenette.

The Foreman's Retreat, together with [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md), can make for a good long-term base. Though there's often a pack of [Wolves](./Wolf.md) that spawn along the path between Foreman's Retreat and Miner's Folly, the latter provides an outdoor workbench and a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md), allowing for crafting without increasing [Cabin Fever Risk](./Cabin%20Fever%20Risk.md). Two to three [Deer](./Deer.md) often spawn not too far away, while another one or two may be found by heading east, crossing over the rope bridge near [Narrow Falls Cave](./Narrow%20Falls%20Cave.md). [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) can also spawn down the hill. Ptarmigan spawn both immediately behind the building as well as down the hill. A [Moose](./Moose.md) spawns in the clearing just north of [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md). Players can climb on top of either fallen trees or rock outcroppings surrounding the clearing for a safe shot. The nearby [bear](./Bear.md) located north (towards the path located north that leads through the cave to the lower region of the map near the base of [Long Falls](./Long%20Falls.md)) can wander close to front door, so exercise caution. However, this provides many hunting opportunities due to the large amount of rocks players can shoot from, including the different levels the house itself is built on.

The biggest downsides to the region is a lack of firewood (sometimes you have to walk across some of the bridges to find branches), not very much container space, and generally being disconnected from the rest of the map, as you have to travel across a combination of rope bridges or undergo [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) to get to other parts of the map.
There is a walkthrough cave nearby with a leaf bed, where one can cure possible cabin fever. However, this cave provides no warmth bonus, making it a risky spot to sleep for long periods of time.

The house is located at the top of a tall cliff. On a clear day (which can be hard to come by in Ash Canyon), it's possible to see many of the region's major locations, including the [Angler's Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md), [High Meadow](./High%20Meadow.md), [Pillar's Footrest](./Pillar%27s%20Footrest.md), and [Wolf's Jaw Overlook](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md) from just outside the cabin. With deer and bear just to the north and a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) not far away, it can make for a suitable [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) in the region, so long as intestinal parasites aren't an issue.![Panoramic View of AC from Foreman's Retreat](../assets/AC_Pano-1.jpg)_Panoramic View of AC from Foreman's Retreat_
_The [Pillar](./Pillar%27s%20Footrest.md) and the [Wolf's Jaw](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md) seen by [Foreman's Retreat](./Foreman%27s%20Retreat.md)_

**Forest Talker Supplies** are a [Collectible](./Collectibles.md) item found in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story mode during the [Lake Gunshots](./Lake%20Gunshots.md) side mission.

During the course of the mission, the survivor retrieves the Forest Talker Supplies from a logging trailer located at [Logging Camp](./Logging%20Camp.md) in west [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md) near the forestry lookout, and returns them to a [Forest Talker](./Forest%20Talkers.md) at [Lake Cabins](./Lake%20Cabins.md).

The player has the option to take the ammo from the Forest Talker Supplies before returning it; however, stealing the ammo causes both the death of the [Forest Talker](./Forest%20Talkers.md) and prevents the player from receiving a pair of [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md) as a reward for completing the mission.

The **Forest Talkers**are a group of activists mentioned in the Story Mode of _The Long Dark_. They are also described as 'eco-terrorists'.

The Forest Talkers were formed by several natives of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) to fight against the mass industrialization and the reaping of their island's natural resources by "outsiders." They claimed to be environmentalists, and some residents did not have a problem with them. Others, such as [Breyerhouse](./Breyerhouse.md) and the owners of the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) regarded them as terrorists. Notes from disgruntled members reveal that the group was largely ragtag and disorganized. The full extent of their actions and crimes is unknown, but it is implied that they regularly engaged in violence and destruction of property toward industrial sites and workers on the island. Their headquarters was in the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md).
- [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) - [Forest Talker Supply Caches](./Forest%20Talker%20Supply%20Caches.md)
- [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) - [Forest Talkers (side mission)](./Forest%20Talkers%20%28side%20mission%29.md)
- [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) - [A Riddle Among the Shadows](./A%20Riddle%20Among%20the%20Shadows.md)

As a part of the [Lake Gunshots](./Lake%20Gunshots.md) side mission, Mackenzie helps an injured Forest talker recover the [Forest Talker Documents](./Forest%20Talker%20Documents.md) and [Forest Talker Supplies](./Forest%20Talker%20Supplies.md). The [Forest Talker Documents](./Forest%20Talker%20Documents.md) contain evidence of an illegal logging camp cutting down [old growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old-growth_forest) trees that is allegedly run by [Breyerhouse](./Breyerhouse.md). Mackenzie can choose to either remove the [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) from the supplies before returning it to the Forest Talker, or leave the ammunition.
As a part of the [Forest Talker Supply Caches](./Forest%20Talker%20Supply%20Caches.md) side mission, Mackenzie finds a supply cache near the [Logging Camp](./Logging%20Camp.md).

The Forest Talkers have built a supply cache within the Abandoned Mine inside [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md). The cache was intended as a waystation for storing valuable gear and high explosives.

During the course of the mission [A Riddle Among the Shadows](./A%20Riddle%20Among%20the%20Shadows.md), [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) finds the corpses of three Forest Talker members that were attempting to access the supply cache prior to their demise.

Mackenzie views the buffer memory Update - Forest Talkers during the aurora and discovers that a group of Forest Talkers sabotaged a logging truck by pouring water into its gas tank on [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md).

As a part of the [Forest Talker Supply Caches](./Forest%20Talker%20Supply%20Caches.md) side mission, Mackenzie finds a supply cache near the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md).

As a part of the [Forest Talker Supply Caches](./Forest%20Talker%20Supply%20Caches.md) side mission, Mackenzie finds a supply cache near the [Bunkhouses](./Bunkhouses.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md).

Provides some shelter **Forester's Hermitage** is a small ruined cabin and the only man-made refuge in the [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md).

Even if the warmth bonus is negligible, the cabin offers the ability to light a fire and rest via a [Wood Stove](./Wood%20Stove.md), offering some protection from the frequent blizzards in the Pass. Enough food can be found for one or two nights in the surrounding clearing, with both [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) spawning nearby and [Cat Tail Stalks](./Cat%20Tail%20Stalk.md), [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) and [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) growing around this area's pond.

During [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) uses the two-man saw in the stump to cut the ropes binding his hands together, and a [Letter](./Letter.md) can be found inside the building.

**Forester's Revolver** is a unique variant of the [Revolver](./Revolver.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

The Forester's Revolver is an old double action, six-round chambered revolver. It has a soft green camouflage paint job and its wooden grip is wrapped with a white cloth. It's unique attribute is that each shot fired only degrades the gun by 0.75% condition instead of the standard revolvers 1% per shot. This means that it would take up to 133 shots to go from 100% to ruined, and can fire up to 266 shots total with Revolver Firearm level 5. The only potential drawback is that the gun is missing its rear iron sights, which may make aiming a challenge.
- Total durability is 33% more than the Revolver (Uses 0.75%-0.375% condition per shot based on [Revolver Skill](./Revolver%20Firearm.md))
The Forester's Revolver spawns somewhere within [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), specifically within the mountain area accessible via the Ravine Basin section of [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md):
- On the dashboard of the [Breyerhouse Truck](./Truck.md) in the parking lot prior to [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md)
- Buried in the snow with only the handle visible, next to a broken cable reel, at the foot of [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md)

Provides some shelter **Forestry Lookout** is a tall, wooden structure found in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md).
Forestry Lookout sits on a hill between the [Destroyed Lookout](./Destroyed%20Lookout.md) to the west and [Derailment](./Derailment.md) to the east.

It contains a bunk bed, a wood stove, and some food. A [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), or [Prybar](./Prybar.md) may spawn here. A flock of [ptarmigans](./Ptarmigan.md) may also spawn near the walkways up to the lookout. The Forestry Lookout is one of two vista location in Mystery Lake.
There is no loading screen when the player enters the building. Instead, the door swings inside so the player can enter. Do not forget to close the door again after entering to help maintain warmth.

The interior is usually warm enough to keep the player from freezing during daytime, but temperatures may drop below zero during nighttime or blizzards. Warm clothing, a fire, and/or warmth from the bed may be useful to avoid freezing.

In [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), there's a [lockbox](./Hank%27s%20Hatch.md) under the bed that requires [Hank's Lock Box Key](./Hank%27s%20Lock%20Box%20Key.md) to open. The key is found on a corpse near a campfire in the Unnamed pond, but the corpse & campfire only spawn after completing the Bear hunting main quest. Inside the lockbox, there will be a piece of paper with a three number code that opens a bunker northeast from the Logging camp. The entrance to this bunker, also known as Prepper's cache, is a hatch found behind a large bolder and near a corpse.
A [Crashed Plane](./Plane%20Crashes.md) can be found below the Lookout, on the path up to the Lookout itself.

The Forestry Lookout is notoriously elusive and the average traveler could easily find themselves caught in the cold of the [Destroyed Lookout](./Destroyed%20Lookout.md), the intact lookout taunting from the adjacent hill. But simply turning left before the [Derailment](./Derailment.md) and walking up the hill will find you at the foot of the path that takes you up the mountain. It will be hard to miss if you look for the wooden fence.

While offering an overview of the landscape in good weather, the Forestry Lookout does not make an ideal long-term [base](./Safehouse.md) because of its elevation, with the trip up and down the hill costing time, warmth, and fatigue. There is a wood stove and a bit of wood inside to provide warmth and cook food, but, after a few fires, fuel will need to be collected at the base of the mountain and carried up. If the player has high scent, wolves may also ascend the path and can attack the player on the way up or down from the lookout, with the hill obstructing clear lines of sight. As such, both the [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) and the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) make more adequate bases.
The Forestry Lookout once stood in the space the [Destroyed Lookout](./Destroyed%20Lookout.md) now occupies.

- Forestry Lookout is a [Fire Lookout Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_lookout_tower), structures built all over America and parts of [Canada](./The%20Collapse.md) beginning in the early 20th century.

- In Story mode, a note in the tower and the name on a lockbox under the bed seem to be a nod to the game _Firewatch_, much of which takes place in a watchtower. _Firewatch_ also features a theme of isolation in a vast wilderness, similar to _The Long Dark_. "Hank," the name on the lockbox, is a nickname for Henry, the protagonist of _Firewatch_, and the note in the tower mentions a woman frequently talking on the radio, a major component of the referenced game's plot.

**Forge Blueprints (mission)** was a side mission of the Predux [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story and the last mission in the Predux storyline. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).

This mission was cut from the game, with [Forge](./Forge.md) blueprints being available from the start, and the Forge being used to craft a new [Spear Head](./Spear%20Head.md) for the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md).

You will first need to raise [Jeremiah's](./Jeremiah.md) Trust to 75 and select the Survival Tools dialogue option. Jeremiah will comment that Mackenzie will need better tools to survive alone out on the Island, and will redirect him to an old [Forge](./Forge.md) near [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md).

Travel to [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and travel to the Homestead. When you arrive, loot inside a [Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md) behind the Forge. Inside you will find a document [Forge Blueprints](./Forge%20Blueprints.md), a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), and 1 piece of [Coal](./Coal.md). Plenty of Coal is nearby to raise the Forge's temperature to 150°C. Then craft either the [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) or [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) and the mission will complete.
Several plot points and locations have been replaced/altered since the Redux re-release of Episode 2:
- This entire side mission was cut from the game, but using the [Forge](./Forge.md) was required to craft a new [Spear Head](./Spear%20Head.md) for the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) in Redux.
- The [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) and [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) blueprints are automatically unlocked before using the Forge to fix the Bear Spear.

- [Hunting Knives](./Hunting%20Knife.md) and [Hatchets](./Hatchet.md) are also far more plentiful throughout Episode 1 and 2 in the Redux, with Hunting Knives being entirely absent in both Predux Episodes (until acquiring [Jeremiah's Knife](./Jeremiah%27s%20Knife.md)).
- Added to game.
- UPDATE **17 December 2018 ([Update](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog%20%E2%80%94%20Archive%201.md#1.41)):**

A **Forge** is the rectangular space located in the middle of a [Furnace](./Furnace.md) and is used for crafting new items made from [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md). Forging is the only method to [Craft](./Crafting.md) new Arrowheads, Improvised Knives, and Improvised Hatchets.

The Furnace can be accessed via the circular hatch and operates like a normal firebox. The forge is the horizontal slot above the furnace hatch, and selecting it will open a crafting interface. Furnaces are unique in that they are the only fire boxes capable of exceeding 80°C in temperature.
- [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md)

- In the [Hangar Basement](./Hangar%20Basement.md) in the [Main Hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md). (only available for players who purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion)

In order to access the forge, the player must create an active [Fire](./Fire.md) in the Furnace to a temperature of around 150° Celsius (302° Fahrenheit). This is only achievable through adding Coal to the fire as it is the only fuel that burns hotter than 80°C.

When the Furnace is 150°C (or 270°F) or greater, forging can be conducted there via a similar interface to that of the [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) by selecting the Forge. Note that it's impossible to reach 150°C without [Coal](./Coal.md). Low temperature materials (such as [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) or [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md)) may be used at the beginning before the introduction of Coal. If too much wood is added to the fire, it will become full and no more fuel can be added for a time.

The furnace burn time is capped at 12 hours like all other fires. However, Coal can continue to be added even when it is capped for purpose of increasing the temperature only, up to the maximum 200°C.
- Once the Furnace fire burns out, the Forge interface will not be usable until a new fire achieves working temperature again.

All crafting in the Forge requires a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) in your inventory. Additionally, all recipes require [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md). It is advisable to obtain all required materials for Forging the desired item before lighting the Furnace due to the amount of fuel needed to be consumed before forging is permitted.
The specific items that can be crafted, and their respective requirements, can be found below.
| 2x [Arrowhead icon](../assets/Arrowhead_icon.png) [Arrowhead](./Arrowhead.md) | 1x [Scrap Metal icon](../assets/Scrap_Metal_icon.png) [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) | 1 Hour |

| \|[Spear Head icon](../assets/Spear_Head_icon.png) [Spear Head](./Spear%20Head.md) (Wintermute Ep2 Only) | 2x [Scrap Metal icon](../assets/Scrap_Metal_icon.png) [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) | 1 Hour 30 Min |

| [Improvised Knife icon](../assets/Improvised_Knife_icon.png) [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) | 3x [Scrap Metal icon](../assets/Scrap_Metal_icon.png) [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) 1x [Cloth icon](../assets/Cloth_icon.png) [Cloth](./Cloth.md) | 3 Hours |

| [Cougar Claw Knife icon](../assets/Cougar_Claw_Knife_icon.png) [Cougar Claw Knife](./Cougar%20Claw%20Knife.md) | 1x [Cougar Claw icon](../assets/Cougar_Claw_icon.png) [Cougar Claw](./Cougar%20Claw.md) 3x [Scrap Metal icon](../assets/Scrap_Metal_icon.png) [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) 1x [Cured Leather icon](../assets/Cured_Leather_icon.png) [Cured Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md) | 3 Hours 40 Min |

| [Improvised Hatchet icon](../assets/Improvised_Hatchet_icon.png) [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) | 5x [Scrap Metal icon](../assets/Scrap_Metal_icon.png) [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) 1x [Cloth icon](../assets/Cloth_icon.png) [Cloth](./Cloth.md) | 4 Hours |

- Forging is somewhat time consuming, so it can be worthwhile to take along extra food. Water and food can be cooked atop the forge (though keep in mind that it can be burned/boiled away as you work).
- Like any time accelerated activity, be aware that Condition may rapidly drain if [Needs](./Needs.md) are not met.
- Using a lot of wood to start a fire can serve to minimize the amount of coal required to reach working temperature. _(Only 4 Coal is required.)_
- Any fuel may be used to extend the duration of the furnace fire once it has reached its working temperature.
- Ensure that the required crafting materials are obtained prior to starting the Furnace.

**Connecting Regions:** [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md), [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md)

**Hazards and Survivability:** [Wolves](./Wolf.md) and [Bears](./Bear.md) are found throughout the region, but fog and [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md) can prove far more deadly. There are very few manmade structures to shelter in.
> “**For advanced players. A frigid open marshland bisected by a railway line. Weak ice and constant winds make this area highly dangerous.**”
**Forlorn Muskeg** is the 6th [Region](./Region.md) to be added to [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). As an advanced region, it is a possible spawn location in Interloper difficulty.

The region is mostly flat, composed of craggy hills surrounding a large, mostly-frozen bog. Bisecting the ice is a broken [railway line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) connected in the east to [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) through the [Rail Tunnel](./Rail%20Tunnel.md) (formerly the 'Tunnel Collapse') and in the west to the [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) region. To the north, there is a path that links to the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region from [Marsh Ridge](./Marsh%20Ridge.md). To the south, the region is linked with [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) through a cave.

There are only a few sheltered areas and structures, and most man-made buildings are partially (or completely) destroyed, making the harsh weather particularly challenging. Within this unpredictable, rugged environment, one mostly intact building is the barn of the [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md), which contains a bed, a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), and a [Forge](./Forge.md). This is one of the few possible base areas in Forlorn Muskeg and a primary reason for visiting the region.

The deep cave near the waterfall and radio tower on the other side of the region may also serve as a temporary base, but it lacks a forge, work bench, or any other special features besides safety from predators and the elements (allowing it to serve as a place to cure hides and guts).

Another useful though unconventional temporary base is the transition cave to Bleak Inlet, as well as being useful when visiting Bleak Inlet, this cave is midway between the Mystery Lake exit and Spence's. The cave contains a bed, in fact by far the closest indoor bed to Spence's, the entrance to the cave is wind-protected and wolves don't enter it, making it a good place to a light a campfire and cook.

Comparable in size to the open center of [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), there are less than a half dozen suitable shelters in the region, all of which except for the [Poacher's Camp](./Poacher%27s%20Camp.md) are scattered around the perimeter of the region. Temperatures tend to be average for the island, to the point where one could potentially sleep through blizzards if they are sheltered from wind. There are also plentiful natural resources, and there are several good hunting locations in the region: bears and deer patrol past features that can be used as safe perches to hunt from. The moose will also appear near the train tunnel to Mystery Lake. However, if an animal you are hunting runs onto weak ice, you will not be able to harvest it or retrieve any arrows.

The main challenges to long-term survival in this region is the weather, as the frequent fog and blizzards forces travel to be carefully planned. There are limited safe paths through the center of the region, none of which are marked except for the railroad. Travelling through the Forlorn Muskeg with clear weather is simple; the open terrain makes predators easy to spot from far off, along with being able to plan a path and determine which ice is safe to cross. However, a pleasant excursion can quickly become dangerous; the high density of predators, weak ice, and lack of landmarks will pose a much greater threat when the visibility is poor. Even a short blizzard will likely be lethal if it descends as players cross through the center of the region.
