**Description:** A small airstrip situated within an expansive wind blasted valley basin
**Connecting Regions:** [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) or [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) (Through Transition Cave)
This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

> “**A vast open plain hides a remote airfield that once served as a critical transport hub for the interior of Great Bear. Between the Hangar, Control Tower, and the Ranger's Cabin on the outskirts of the region, Forsaken Airfield is one of the harshest, coldest regions yet. What secrets will the Aurora reveal...**”

__For advanced players. Once an active entry point for the Far Territory's wild interior, Forsaken Airfield lives in the shadow of better days, long departed. Its broken landing strip and support buildings sit wedged between various natural obstacles, including frozen fields, a broad lake, and sheer cliffs along the Region’s perimeter. Travelers here need guile, and warm clothes.

**Forsaken Airfield** is the 14th [Region](./Region.md) found in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md) released for [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), and is available for players who purchased the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion pack released on December 5, 2022.

The Region connects to [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) via the mountain road and to the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) and [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) via a large cave system south-east of [Fallow Dugout](./Fallow%20Dugout.md) near the downed helicopter.

A massive flat basin situated within a mountainous valley, the Forsaken Airfield Region is home to the titular Airfield 31, or '[Field 31](./Field%2031.md)' as signs in the location read. The small, abandoned air travel terminal is littered with non-functioning airplanes and helicopters.

The region's geography consists of winding, long, crumbling roads from the mountains through the central map. The middle is mostly dominated by a large, frozen lake and expansive, frozen plains, with one small frozen pond in the direct center. Rocky hills dot a few areas, but are more common near the treacherous cliffsides and sharp, angular mountains that ring the edges and much of the south of Forsaken Airfield.

Foggy weather and deafening, howling winds are common, often hindering navigation of the many wide open areas. In addition to normal foggy conditions, a special electrostatic variant of heavy fog called [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) often appears during the day, powering the machinery and lights of many of the area's remote buildings and vehicles, as well giving the player character the unique [Insomnia](./Insomnia.md) [Affliction](./Afflictions.md).

Forsaken Airfield is much more open than most of the other regions on Great Bear Island, which makes it quite easy to navigate and avoid predators when the weather's clear. When the visibility falls, however, these same characteristics make it very difficult to know one's location, which is compounded by the region's lack of roads. Additionally, the flat terrain makes it difficult for players to find a location that's protected from the often strong winds or sudden blizzards. Starting and sustaining [Campfires](./Campfire.md) can be a challenge in these situations, making [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md) and [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md) a serious concern. Carrying along enough [cloth](./Cloth.md) and [sticks](./Stick.md) to make an emergency [snow shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md) can help prevent disaster; a [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md) can also help. Using a [Travois](./Travois.md) can help make hauling these supplies over the flat, open terrain much easier.

There are few shelters available in the center of the region aside from the airport itself and the [Final Approach](./Final%20Approach.md): several caves can be found in the cliffs along the region's edges, as well as a few crashed air vehicles, and occasional cabin or trailer, all of which can be life-saving in case of inclement weather.

The five main man-made shelters in the region are: the airport complex near the center, [Mindful Cabin](./Mindful%20Cabin.md) to the northwest, [Island Cottage](./Island%20Cottage.md) to the north, [Junker's Paddock](./Junker%27s%20Paddock.md) to the southwest, and [Justy's Hovel](./Justy%27s%20Hovel.md) to the southeast.
In a broad sense, Forsaken Airfield can be divided into a few major areas, each with their own characteristics.

This is the road that connects Forsaken Airfield to [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md). It is a long, winding road, with little in the way of resources, though it does offer some shelter in a cave and occasional vehicles. Notable locations include [Whealy's Turn](./Whealy%27s%20Turn.md), the first place where Survivors will see the airfield itself, and the [Junker's Paddock](./Junker%27s%20Paddock.md) where the road opens up into the wide open field. No wildlife can be found along this road, aside from a few [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) near Junker's Paddock. Much of this long walk can be bypassed when leaving the region by taking a narrow footpath just south of Field 31.

Following the road from Junker's Paddock and staying right will eventually lead the Survivor towards Field 31, an abandoned airport terminal littered with many non-functional airplanes, helicopters, and vehicles. Most players who choose to live here will end up living in the airport's [hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md), as it offers all the essentials, along with the only [forge](./Forge.md) in the Far Territory. This area has limited hunting and natural resources, however, and is frequented by [wolves](./Wolf.md), so Survivors should be alert.

Most of the centre of the region is occupied by a relatively flat plain with few features, aside from a river flowing into [Shoulder Lake](./Shoulder%20Lake.md) and a road leading to [Mindful Cabin](./Mindful%20Cabin.md). Although the wide open nature of this plain makes it easy to navigate in good weather and has good [deer](./Deer.md) and [moose](./Moose.md) hunting, low visibility can make it extremely difficult to navigate and the Survivor can easily fall victim to a [wolf](./Wolf.md) here. There are also very few shelters in the area, aside from the helicopter at [Final Approach](./Final%20Approach.md). It is also difficult to find much firewood here, due to the area's severe lack of trees. There are also few natural resources to forage here, aside from [cat tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) on the pond near Final Approach, where it is also possible to Ice Fish.

Located in the northeastern corner of the map beyond the airfield, Shoulder Lake is the largest freshwater body in the game, and features two [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) huts. Several small islands are scattered throughout the lake, and a [Hunter's Blind](./Hunter%27s%20Blind.md) may be found on the lake's southern shore. Towards the lake's northern shore lies the largest island, [Drift Island](./Drift%20Island.md), home to [Island Cottage](./Island%20Cottage.md) and [Archie's Crawlspace](./Archie%27s%20Crawlspace.md). To the northeast of the island, the land goes uphill, and there is a valley and river that leads into the lake.

Although this area is one of the most popular places to live in the Far Territory, owing to Island Cottage, abundant [rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), [deer](./Deer.md), fishing firewood, and forageable resources, survivors should be careful as there are many wolves on the lake, along with a [bear](./Bear.md) that wanders near the east end of Drift Island.

Near the edges of the large central plain, the region features more uneven terrain, more trees, richer natural resources, and much more shelter. In addition to the shallow caves in the cliffs, much of the region's man-made shelter can also be found here. The left fork of the road entering from Transfer Pass goes through the central plain before gradually gaining altitude and ending at [Mindful Cabin](./Mindful%20Cabin.md), located atop a cliff near the region's western edge. The eastern and southern edges are home to [Justy's Hovel](./Justy%27s%20Hovel.md) and [Bunker Omega](./Bunker%20Omega.md).

> “__The Warden at Blackrock Penitentiary, Franklin has found himself caught up in Mathis’ deadly schemes.

More an administrator than a disciplinarian, no one is more aware of the notorious prison’s dark history than its Warden. But Franklin is clear-eyed about his purpose on Great Bear Island -- the worst of the worst end up with him at Blackrock. And if someone has to be in charge, it might as well be him.__”
> **Yes well, normally I'm on the other side of the bars. Name's Franklin. I'm Warden here at Blackrock.**

Franklin is the warden of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), the only surviving representative of authority that can be seen in the story mode so far. Franklin is an intelligent man, with convictions, but not very authoritarian and far too gentle for the position he occupies. He will end up paying the price by being captured by [Mathis](./Mathis.md) and his men, trying all the same to resist them heroically. More administrator than disciplinary, no one knows the dark history of the infamous prison better than its director. But Franklin is clear-headed about his goal on Great Bear Island – the worst of men ends up with him in Blackrock. And if anyone has to accept the burden of holding them, it might as well be him.

After the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) struck the Prison, backup power initially kept the prisoners in check, until the Convicts overwhelmed the Prison's security. All prison personnel were rounded up into the snow and shot outside the prison walls, with Franklin being tied to a chair and placed in a cell. The prisoners headed to solitary but were unable to open the doors due to mechanical fail safes, due to some [unknown force](./Jace.md) that inadvertently ensures Franklin's survival in the meantime.

Franklin is first encountered by [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) after he first arrives at the Prison. After a short exchange between the two regarding the current situation, Mathis arrives and begins interrogating Franklin on how to enter solitary, even beating Franklin for uttering Donner's name. When Franklin explains that he really doesn't know who is altering the failsafes or how to even get into solitary, he is brutally beaten by Mathis in order to better "jog his memory."

Being left to clean up the Warden and quickly realizing that they will take the bad side of Mathis' temper if Franklin dies, [Vachon](./Vachon.md) and [Heller](./Heller.md) task Mackenzie to find medicine for Franklin, leveraging him to come back since they still hold [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md). When Mackenzie returns with [Blackrock Infirmary Medication](./Blackrock%20Infirmary%20Medication.md) and stiches up the Warden's wounds, Franklin reveals to Mackenzie that solitary runs on its own circuit channels, and he is only being kept alive because Mathis thinks Franklin owns some sort of admin override to open the cells. Franklin is also aware that someone is messing with the Convicts, and Mackenzie reveals that he spoke to this person over the phone. Mathis almost returns before Franklin urges Mackenzie to do whatever the person on the phone asks, as they are the only person keeping Donner in solitary.

When Mathis returns and realizes that Vachon and Heller were too cowardly to fix the Warden's wounds, he sends Mackenzie to reroute power from the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md) and [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) to fix solitary. After sabotaging the Steam Tunnels with some help, Mackenzie returns to a not so enraged Mathis, as he has found another way into solitary, Detonators.
Mathis interrogates Franklin for info about the Detonators' location, and ultimately succeeds without resorting to violence, with Mackenzie offering to retrieve them in order to spare the Warden.

When Mackenzie returns, it is revealed that Mathis tortured and ultimately killed Franklin, even as he revealed that he knew that Mackenzie had an accomplice helping him sabotage the locking mechanisim in the Steam Tunnels. Franklin's lifeless body is last shown being wheeled out of his cell on a gurney by a Convict, and he is never seen again.
Despite being unarmed in Wintermute, his [pistol](./Warden%27s%20Revolver.md) can be found in Survival Mode.

**Freight-Train of Hate & Hunger** is a [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This is an unmissable story achievement achieved after completing the mission [What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md). Simply avoid the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) inside the [Old Bear's Den](./Old%20Bear%27s%20Den.md) and find the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md), then win the 3 Bear [Struggles](./Struggle.md) and kill the bear. The achievement is earned after the cutscene ends.
Simply track and kill the Old Bear as part of [Jeremiah's Folly](./Jeremiah%27s%20Folly.md) and the achievement will unlock.
The achievement name is from a quote from [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) during [Survival School (Predux)](./Survival%20School%20%28Predux%29.md):

"He'll come for you when you're not expecting it. But you won't miss it. It won't be subtle. It'll sound like a ton of muscle and bone bearing down on you like a freight train of hate and hunger. You stand your ground. Do not flinch. You raise your rifle. You sight him. And when you see between his eyes - - you squeeze that trigger."

**Freighthopper's Rockfall** is a wooden rockfall shelter that protects a small section of the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md). It is found in the [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md) region, and is located between the train tunnel leading to [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) and [Remnant Cave](./Remnant%20Cave.md). The structure still remains standing despite being abandoned for decades, and a single Coal car has been left on the track under the wooden structure.

Despite its name, the rockfall shelter is designed to offer more shelter and protection for trains and their cars and not able-bodied survivors walking on foot. As such, the area provides very little protection from the elements. There is no loot in the area, aside from a few rabbits that may wander nearby.

It can be used as a [Material](./Materials.md) for crafting or repairing [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md) or [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md) once they have [Cured](./Curing.md) into a [Cured Black Bear Hide](./Cured%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md).

One Cured Black Bear Hide can be found in a [Memento Cache](./Mementos.md) inside [Peak Cave](./Peak%20Cave.md), in the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md).

**Fresh Gut** is an animal-based [Material](./Materials.md) that can be harvested from [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) carcasses. Fresh Guts can also be used as a [Baiting](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys) to distract predators, but are primarily used to craft or repair various animal based [Clothing](./Clothing.md) once they have [Cured](./Curing.md) into [Cured Gut](./Cured%20Gut.md).

Fresh Gut can be harvested from [Hunting](./Hunting.md) or [Trapping](./Trapping.md) the various land animals of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), specifically the carcasses of [moose](./Moose.md), [wolves](./Wolf.md), [rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [bears](./Bear.md), and [deer](./Deer.md). Fish and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) will never contain Guts.

Once harvested, Fresh Gut can be cured by letting them air-dry indoors for 5 days into [Cured Gut](./Cured%20Gut.md). Fresh Gut [Decay](./Decay.md) at a rate of 5 Condition a day (Stalker difficulty) and will decay into Ruined status if not left to cure indoors. The current curing status can be checked by hovering your reticle over the item, where it will display a "X% Cured" progress. This increases until the item is 100% cured, where the item will automatically become fully cured, will change to a darker texture, and is ready for crafting use. Completely cured items never decay.

Fresh Gut contributes to a survivor's overall [Scent](./Scent.md). This can either be a detriment or a useful advantage when Baiting predator animals. Higher scent will also upset prey [wildlife](./Wildlife.md), such as alerting [Deer](./Deer.md) to a survivor's presence when upstream of wind. Pressing the Drop Decay button will automatically drop any Fresh Gut in the player's inventory onto the ground.

**Fresh Leather** is the very rare, uncured version of [Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md). It can be used as a [Material](./Materials.md) for crafting or repairing certain items once they have [Cured](./Curing.md) into [Cured Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md).

Fresh Leather can only be found at outside locations such as [Poacher's Camp](./Poacher%27s%20Camp.md), [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md), and the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md), and may be cured into Cured Leather over 5 days. The "Fresh Leather" item is still present in _The Long Dark_, but is extremely rare that cannot be created in any way outside of world generation at game start. Fresh Leather also decays over time, like fresh animal hides and guts, making it even more difficult to find the already rare item before it decays to 0% condition inside a container and is deleted.

Fresh Leather is so rare of a find that many players mistakenly believe it is [Cut/Discontinued Content](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md). Most instances of this item will have already cured indoors at 76% by the time the player finds them, or will be outdoors at 0% if the player takes too long.

In early builds of _The Long Dark_ (alpha/beta), Fresh Leather was a very common material obtained from Carcass Harvesting Deer. Instead of [Fresh Deer Hide](./Fresh%20Deer%20Hide.md) being produced, "Fresh Leather" would be harvested; this item could then be converted into "Cured Leather" by curing it indoors, and then used for repairing clothing. Cured Leather is the default form of Leather found in the game, and is found by Harvesting leather footwear, gloves, the Moose-Hide Satchel, finding it in the game world, and [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md).
- Animal skins and certain types of Wood now need to be Cured (Dried) before they can be used as raw materials for Crafting.

It can be used as a [Material](./Materials.md) for crafting or repairing [Wolfskin Coats](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md) once they have [Cured](./Curing.md) into a [Cured Wolf Pelt](./Cured%20Wolf%20Pelt.md).

They can then be cured by leaving them indoors for 7 days (in-game). Fresh Wolf Pelts [Decay](./Decay.md) at a rate of 5 Condition a day (Stalker difficulty) and will decay into Ruined status if not left to cure indoors. The current curing status can be checked by hovering your reticle over the item, where it will display a "X% Cured" progress. This increases until the item is 100% cured, where the item will automatically become fully cured, will change to a darker texture, and is ready for crafting use. Completely cured items never decay.

Wolf Pelts can be dangerous or resource-expensive to obtain, since they requiring killing a Wolf with a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Revolver](./Revolver.md), or [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md).

An alternative but very dangerous method of obtaining a pelt involves allowing a Wolf [struggle](./Struggle.md) to begin, and then using a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) or [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) to puncture a Wolf, then waiting a few hours for the Wolf to bleed out after it runs away. This method is incredibly dangerous if a survivor has very low [Condition](./Condition.md) as it will often result in death.

Each Wolf Carcass (or variant) will always contain one pelt, along with [meat](./Wolf%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md) and [Fresh Gut](./Fresh%20Gut.md). Occasionally, dead ravaged Wolf Carcasses can be found across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).

A **Fridge** is a storage container found as part of refrigerators inside many the kitchens of homes and industrial buildings across the island. Most refrigerators have a **Fridge** on the bottom and a [Freezer](./Freezer.md) on the top. Ironically, it is best to store certain foods outdoors (mainly meat) in order to preserve them for longer periods of time, as the Fridge is not functional.

A second type of Fridge (often nicknamed Soda Fridges) that can be found has a single clear glass door and only ever contains [Sodas](./Soda%20%28disambiguation%29.md) or [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), which can be looted by opening the door and peaking through the right side to grab them. These types of Fridges cannot be used to store items. They come in green or red colors on the outside, neither of which affect the contents.

**Frostbite Risk** is incurred when a player's bare skin is exposed to freezing conditions, particularly with severe windchill.
> “**Your skin is directly exposed to the cold. If it remains exposed for long enough, you'll get Frostbite.**”

Frostbite Risk will only appear when 1 of 5 extremities of bare skin is exposed directly to the cold (Head, Torso, Hands, Legs, Feet), or by wearing Clothing that is currently Frozen on a particular body part. No Clothing worn on one of the 5 major body parts for long periods of time in a cold location is the most common way to begin Frostbite Risk (especially on higher difficulties where the player often begins without head or hand clothing).

It is possible to have multiple Risks develop on multiple limbs at once, but this only occurs once per exposed body part (I.E: cannot have 2 risks for hands). Game difficulty determines how quickly Frostbite Risk develops and how fast the meter fills.

Wearing Accessories, such as [Wool Ear Wrap](./Wool%20Ear%20Wrap.md) (shown on the head) or [Improvised Insulation](./Improvised%20Insulation.md) (shown on the body), will still cause Frostbite Risk to develop for those body parts. As long as one Clothing slot (except Accessories) has any kind of unfrozen Clothing on it, Frostbite Risk will not develop for that extremity.

- Frostbite Risk is calculated by game world temperature, which consists of ambient air temperature, windchill, and weather. This is not the same as "[Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md)", a combination of the player's Clothing stats, any [Feats](./Feats.md), or Afflictions (ex. [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md), [Frigid Bones](./Frigid%20Bones.md)).
- Frostbite Risk is immediately stopped by standing next to a [Fire](./Fire.md) and will gradually lowers the Risk the warmer the fire becomes.
- Sleeping/passing time in a warm location with an uncovered body part suffering from Frostbite Risk will stop any Risk progression, but will not lower it if the temperature is not above +1C.

- Wearing Frozen Clothing on an inner layer of the body will begin Frostbite Risk and accelerate it 50% faster than normal, and lowers the Warmth bonus of that Clothing. The player will also get Frostbite Risk with Frozen Clothing worn even if the air temperature is above -20C.

- Passing through waterfalls [Environmental Hazards](./Environmental%20Hazard.md)/[Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md) will immediately wet portions of the player's outer layer Clothing, which can quickly freeze over. Blizzards and light snow fall also wets the player's outer layer Clothing, though to a slower effect.
- Covering the affected by part with unfrozen Clothing will also begin lowering the Affliction.

- Clothing that is damaged and Ruined in a Wildlife [Struggle](./Struggle.md) will notify the player in the top right corner, and that section of the body must immediately be covered up again to prevent Risk.

Should a body part continue to remain exposed to the freezing cold, [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md) will develop. If Frostbite develops on that limb and it is not covered, Frostbite Risk will begin again.

**Frostbite** is a physical Injury acquired from having bare skin exposed to the cold for too long and not managing [Frostbite Risk](./Frostbite%20Risk.md), and permanently reduces overall [Condition](./Condition.md) by 10%.

Frostbite Risk will only appear when 1 of 5 extremities of bare skin is exposed directly to the cold, or by wearing [Clothing](./Clothing.md) that is currently Frozen on a particular body part. Frostbite Risk will continue to increase until said body part is either covered up with unfrozen Clothing, or it is sufficiently warmed at a fire until the Risk subsides. Should a body part continue to remain exposed to the freezing cold, Frostbite will develop, and can potentially begin Frostbite Risk on that limb again.

Each instance of acquired Frostbite reduces your maximum [Condition](./Condition.md) level by 10%. Frostbite is currently the only affliction to have no cure (Unless the player [Cheats Death](./Cheat%20Death.md)). Players should take care to pay attention to their [Frostbite Risk](./Frostbite%20Risk.md), so that Frostbite can be prevented.

- A player can only receive Frostbite for 5 body parts (Head, Torso, Hands, Legs, Feet), however you can get 5 Frostbite Afflictions for every body part, resulting in a death at 10 instances of Frostbite (or 11 temporarily with the extra 15% acquired from [Well Fed](./Well%20Fed.md) and [Nourished](./Nourished.md), until Nourished wears off).
- Theoretically, if one's Condition were high enough, it would be possible to acquire 25 instances of Frostbite, totaling for a maximum of -250% Condition loss.
- The Condition bar loss from Frostbite stacks with [Burns](./Burns.md) or [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md).

> “__A frozen corpse brings Great Bear Island's harsh reality front and centre.

**Frozen Corpses** (sometimes labeled as just **Corpse**) are the remains of seemingly recently deceased people. They are usually found outdoors, although some can be found indoors, in caves, or crushed under structures or other landmarks.

Corpses can be searched for modest loot. Tools or weapons can often be found nearby. Sometimes, corpses will spawn with items in-hand. [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) also can spawn near corpses, and [Crows](./Crow.md) can be spotted circling above some spawned corpses.

The causes of death and identities of frozen corpses are almost universally a mystery, although the Hinterland Forums community has given some of these corpses [unofficial backstories](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/38131-tsd-the-sitting-dead/). The bodies also do not defrost, regardless of surrounding temperature, and they are essentially useless and inert once looted (although the can technically serve as storage containers, albeit macabre ones).

If a frozen corpse is found inside a [safehouse](./Safehouse.md), it can be "Respectfully Removed" via [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md). Occasionally in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), a [Dead Prison Guard](./Dead%20Prison%20Guard.md) or dead Convict can be found.

The **Fukkatsu Maru** is an abandoned Japanese cargo ship that became trapped in ice after drifting into [Desperation Bay](./Desperation%20Bay.md). It is explored during the mission [A Cry For Help](./A%20Cry%20For%20Help.md).
It has an exterior deck that can be accessed by using on of the dropped anchors as [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) spot.
The interior consists of the Fukkatsu Maru Cargo Hold, whilst the upper decks include the Crew Quarters, Mess Hall, Bathrooms, an Infirmary, the Bridge, and the Captain's Quarters.

The name "Fukkatsu Maru" is Japanese and likely written as ふっかつ丸 or possibly 復活丸 (post-World War II Japanese vessels tend to use hiragana rather than kanji in their main names). "Fukkatsu" (復活 or ふっかつ) means "revival", while "maru" (丸), usually meaning "circle", is a common suffix attached to the names of merchant or civilian ships. Taken literally, the name could be read as "circle of revival".

Has no shelter The **Fulmar Autopilot Boat** is a [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

The Fulmar Autopilot Boat is the only way to travel to [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) and back. It is located in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) in front of the [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) location, near the docks.

[Play Me](./Play%20Me.md), [Wax Cylinder 1](./Wax%20Cylinder%201.md), and the [Wax Cylinder Player](./Wax%20Cylinder%20Player.md) are found inside the Fulmar. Listening to Wax Cylinder 1 unlocks the supply container that needs to be filled with various supplies required for travel. Wax Cylinder 1 must be listened to in order to be able to open the container located in the back of the boat.
Traveling to Cauldron Island is not free, as the voyage is long and requires the following items for travel:
- Although food and drink at more than 20% Condition can be added to the Fulmar Boat's Supplies, only food at greater than 50% Condition will count towards the calorie total.

Starting the boat does not require lighting the [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), it is activated simply by interacting with the lever beside the steering wheel. After that, an automated sequence of images is showing the trip to [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) with no manual steering required. Traveling does not take time.
There is also a 150.00KG storage trunk next to the supplies container for transporting more supplies between Great Bear Island and Cauldron Island.

Upon arrival at [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md), a warm shelter is available, featuring a [Bed](./Bed.md), a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) and various [Clothing](./Clothing.md) and other loot.
Fulmar are two gull like birds that live in the Arctic or Antarctic regions of the world, having bluish-gray and white plumage.

A **Furnace** is an unmovable [contained fire](./Fire.md#Contained_fires). Notably, furnaces also have an attached [Forge](./Forge.md) that can be used for crafting items. Furnaces have a maximum temperature of 200°C. Minimum temperature for forging is 150°C. To achieve a temperature above 80°C, [Coal](./Coal.md) must be added to the furnace. For [Cooking](./Cooking.md) and heating, the furnace functions identically to other contained fires and player-made [Campfire](./Campfire.md). It provides no advantage over other contained fires, but it does allow protection against wind, unlike the player-made campfire. It has one cooking slot.
The furnace can be re-lit indefinitely, though it requires fresh starter, tinder, and fuel each time.

The **Furniture Workbench** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.

The Furniture Workbench is the primary crafting facility used to build large decorative furniture items within any interior Safehouse. It can be crafted and carried anywhere (though it weighs as much as a [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md)), but requires the very rare [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) before it can be built. The Furniture Workbench can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor when in Customization Mode.

Once placed in a Safehouse, the Furniture Workbench cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the Furniture Workbench will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before placing this item).
Any large in-progress/created Decorations made at a Furniture Workbench are deposited inside an invisible container tied to that Furniture Workbench.
- Opening the Workbench crafting menu and selecting Container will allow you to place large finished items around your Safehouse
- An unlimited amount of large completed furniture can be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container, and will remain there until placed in the surrounding Safehouse.

The **Ghost Stag** is a legendary [Deer](./Deer.md) rumored to be located within [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) and is sought after in the [Tall Tales](./Tall%20Tales.md) side mission of [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). It is an albino Deer and the only one of its kind in the game.

The Ghost Stag is first learned about by the player after reading the book [Local Legends - Ghost Stag](./Local%20Legends%20-%20Ghost%20Stag.md). This book can be found in the [Draft Dodger's Cabin](./Draft%20Dodger%27s%20Cabin.md) within [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).

After reading this book, the Ghost Stag will appear after the player sleep inside the [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md) adjacent to the [Three Strikes Farmstead](./Three%20Strikes%20Farmstead.md). Upon awakening and seeing the Ghost Stag, the side mission objective will complete, and the player will be rewarded with insight on how to craft [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md) and [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md).

Once the player leaves the Snow Shelter, the Ghost Stag will run away upon spotting the player. It cannot be killed, even if shot repeatedly by the player, and will simply run off and despawn after enough time passes.

**A mysterious phenomenon first encountered in the Far Territory, Glimmer Fog charges the air and ground with electrostatic energy, animating some electronics in entirely unpredictable ways.**
- [Official description](https://www.thelongdark.com/expansion/) from the Tales From the Far Territory Website Page

Glimmer Fog is a unique variant of heavy fog within [Regions](./Region.md) of the [Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md): [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), and [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

Like [Heavy Fog](./Weather.md), Glimmer Fog reduces visibility (preventing [Surveying](./Charcoal.md) and use of the [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md)) but also risks [Insomnia](./Insomnia.md) when the survivor is above-ground, and similar to [Auroras](./Aurora.md): temporarily powers electronics (e.g. [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md), [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md), vehicle headlights). Glimmer Fog causes snow and ice to crackle and discharge electricity constantly, while patches of fog flash with misty spectral colored lights.
Insomnia Risk may be avoided by traveling to specific underground areas or traveling to [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md).

Glimmer Fog is also present near the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md) in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) after two of the geothermal substations are repaired, though it does not cause [Insomnia](./Insomnia.md). [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) comments that the air tastes like "metal in my mouth" as he passes through it.

Despite its specific origin being unclear, Glimmer Fog is not a natural phenomenon and is artificially produced. [Rüdiger's Machine](./R%C3%BCdiger%27s%20Machine.md) in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) and the Geothermal Substations in the [Suzuki Geothermal Region](./Suzuki%20Geothermal%20Region.md) both appear to concentrate the [Aurora's](./Aurora.md) electrical capabilities in such a way that they create electrostatic fog in the surrounding atmosphere. It can be theorized that other similar man made devices around the world can create Glimmer Fog.

Consuming Go! Energy Drink restores hydration and a small amount of calories. It also provides the benefits [Energy Boost](./Energy%20Boost.md) for 30 minutes, and [Fatigue Reduced](./Fatigue%20Reduced.md) for 45 min.
When the duration of Energy Boost ends, it causes the [Headache](./Headache.md) [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) for 20 minutes.

Upon consumption, Fatigue is increased by 60% (to a maximum of 100%), but once the benefits expire 50% Fatigue will be lost immediately. This makes consuming Go! while above 40% Fatigue a waste, and above 50% a net loss in Fatigue. Care should be taken to the remaining duration of Go! Energy Drink's benefit, since if it expires during demanding tasks (such as [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md)), Fatigue may drop to 0% resulting in a dangerous situation.

The Gold Mine is a mine next to the Mining Camp that is a must-visit for late-game players. The main entrance to the Gold Mine is next to the Mining Camp, but there is a back entrance on a cliff overlooking the ropes going from the overlook of the Mining Camp down near [Stone Shelf Cave](./Stone%20Shelf%20Cave.md). At the back entrance there is a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) in the middle of a steep drop down the mountain to the second plateau of the aforementioned rope climb. Higher on the plateau after the first rope climb and before the second, a snow shelter and a burnt out campfire may occasionally spawn, with a variety of tools and supplies (including a possible bow, hunting knife and hammer).

Navigating the Gold Mine is quite easy due to its very linear layout. You will need some sort of light source to be able to see, however. In between the entrance and the technical backpack spawn location, there is water in the mine that will freeze your boots and socks quite quickly; temporarily removing the feet clothing items to cross the water will avoid getting them wet.

This is the only location in the game where Technical Backpack and the Crampons can be found. They are located far into the mine in an open section next to a frozen corpse, a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md), a [Bed](./Bed.md), and a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md). Besides these, the Gold Mine may also contain other items such as an [Expedition Parka](./Expedition%20Parka.md) , [Combat Pants](./Combat%20Pants.md) or very rarely a [Cowichan Sweater](./Cowichan%20Sweater.md). A [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) located deeper into the mine near the back entrance, [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), fire starting materials and an assortment of food items. Despite it being called a gold mine, it is impossible to find any gold anywhere in or around the mine. However, exploring the mine _will_ yield a backpack full of [Coal](./Coal.md).

A **Gold Nugget** is a [Collectible](./Collectibles.md) and [Tool](./Tools.md) in _The Long Dark_.

Golds Nuggets are rare collectible items with no function other than being a reward for exploration. Like other items, they may be inspected, picked up, and dropped but currently do not provide any other function.

A Gold Nugget is offered as the reward for the optional side-mission ([Blackrock Rumours](./Blackrock%20Rumours.md)) "Late Employee". It is treated as a Collectibles reward in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).
It is treated as a Tool in Survival Mode, but serves no gameplay function. 2 Gold Nuggets can potentially be found in a single Survival run save.

A Gold Nugget can always be found in Level 1 of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) in [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md); it is inside of a trailer near a [Medical Locker](./Medical%20Locker.md), in a [Lock Box](./Lock%20Box.md) opened with the [Mine Lockbox Key](./Mine%20Lockbox%20Key.md). (requires [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) to access).
A second Gold Nugget can also be found inside one of the stocked "Conspiracy" type [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md).
- Type 2 layout: 1 room cache layout that potentially spawns inside a hidden [Safe](./Safe.md) behind the hatch ladder (randomly generated, not guaranteed to spawn).

**Granola Bar** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Consuming a Granola Bar provides up to 300 calories of [energy](./Hunger.md), at the cost of minor [dehydration](./Thirst.md). The Granola Bar weighs a mere 0.10 kg, making its energy density a high 3,000 calories-per-kilogram. It also lasts practically forever if stored outside. The Granola Bar, like other packaged food and drink, is most commonly found inside of houses, shops, [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md) and on [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md).
Granola Bars can cause [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md), but [decays](./Decay.md) very slowly, especially when outdoors.
- The granola bar is packaged as a product called "_Crunchy Stuff"_, and it is "fat free!"
- The back of the wrapper lists "Ingredients: Rolled Oats, Honey, Almonds, Pecan, Salt, Cinnamon, Tocopherols."

**Great Bear Island**is a fictional island that is the main setting of [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). The Island is geographically located off the northern-western coast of mainland [Canada](./The%20Collapse.md), and is entirely surrounded by the Pacific Ocean. It is also located inside the [Ring of Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Fire), resulting a higher than average amount of earthquakes.

Great Bear Island was once a lively region rich in natural resources and rustic communities. The abundance of coal, the flowing rivers, and the pristine forests on the island attracted the attention of corporations from the mainland. Over the course of many years, these industrial barons established mines, logging camps, and dams to exploit the natural wonders of Great Bear.

While this industrial boom brought economic prosperity and stability to many island residents, the unsustainable harvesting of the island's resources also upset some of the locals. Tourism and many modern amenities (such as banks and convenience stores) accompanied industry growth, further scarring the island's once primal landscape and deepening many islanders' dependence on outside interests. Because of the often destructive, exploitive encroachment of technology and industrialization on the island's traditional way of life, many Great Bear residents developed a deep resentment and distrust of "mainlanders" and outsiders.

During the turmoil of [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md), approximately ten years before the events of _The Long Dark_, a series of major earthquakes rocked Great Bear, destroying much of the island's infrastructure and industry during the ongoing economic crisis. As a result, the corporations that once flocked to reap the island's resources abandoned their camps and mines, sending what was left of the local communities into economic turmoil. Great Bear never fully recovered from the quakes, and, as a result, many abandoned facilities, destroyed roadways, and ghost towns dot the island--remnants of a once thriving region.

**Green Birch Sapling** can be found growing near birch trees and in a variety of wild landscapes, usually in groups of 2-5.

Green Birch Saplings can be harvested with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), or a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md). Where the green Birch Sapling used to stand, a small root stump will remain, though this stump cannot be interacted with and will not regrow. Tools do not suffer condition loss for harvesting saplings.

A Green Birch Sapling can be cured by leaving it to dry indoors or inside a deep cave for four days. Note that the sapling will continue to cure when placed inside a container, but will be ejected when fully cured. During this time, if the sapling is curing it will show the percent of the process completed, either when hovering over the sapling or viewing it in one's inventory.

Once dried, the green birch sapling will become a cured birch sapling and will appear to be a more dull brown colour. The cured sapling can then be used for crafting [Arrow Shafts](./Arrow%20Shaft.md). Both Green and Cured Birch Saplings do not [Decay](./Decay.md), and will always be at 100% condition.
2 Green Birch Saplings are required to craft the [Trader](./Trader.md) blueprint item the [Bushcraft Bow](./Bushcraft%20Bow.md), being the only tool in the game requiring the uncured saplings.
| [Bushcraft Bow](./Bushcraft%20Bow.md) | None | - 2 × [Green Birch Sapling](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) - 2 × [Cured Gut](./Cured%20Gut.md) |

A **Green Maple Sapling** is a plant-based [Material](./Materials.md) that can be harvested and cured into a [Cured Maple Sapling](./Cured%20Maple%20Sapling.md) to craft a [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) or [Travois](./Travois.md) at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md). Contrary to the in-game description, the sapling cannot be used for repairs. Both Green and Cured Maple Saplings do not [Decay](./Decay.md), and will always be at 100% condition.

Maple saplings are found out in forested and occasionally open landscapes. They usually come in alone or in pairs, but are normally not found in close proximity to [Green Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md). Occasionally they can be found in groups of 3 or more, though this is very rare.

Green Maple Saplings can be harvested with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), or a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md), for one green Maple Sapling. Saplings do not regrow. Tools do not suffer condition loss for harvesting saplings.

A Green Maple Sapling can be cured by leaving it to dry indoors or inside a deep cave for six days. Note that the sapling will continue to cure when placed inside a container, but will be ejected when fully cured. During this time, if the sapling is curing it will show the percent of the process completed, either when hovering over the sapling or viewing it in one's inventory. Once dried, the green birch sapling will become a cured birch sapling and will appear to be a more brown colour.
Both Green and Cured Maple Saplings do not [Decay](./Decay.md), and will always be at 100% condition.

Green Maple Saplings can be found in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) in the [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) on the way to the [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md), as well as in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md). It is not currently known if this is intended.

**Grey Mother** is a major character that appears in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). She is the first NPC that [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) encounters after his plane crashes, and the only remaining resident in the town of [Milton](./Milton.md).

Years before the events of _The Long Dark_, Grey Mother was married to a farmer named [Martin Barker](./Martin%20Barker.md). Together they had a daughter named [Lilith](./Lilith%20Barker.md). Tragedy struck when Lilith died in a climbing accident, and Grey Mother blamed her death on Martin, driving a wedge between them and causing them to live in separate homes. Things only got worse when the quakes devastated the island, and Grey Mother eventually became a recluse, abandoning the name of Barker and developing a reputation as a senile old blind lady.
When the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) struck, she remained in her Milton home after the surviving residents were killed by [Convicts](./Convicts.md).

Grey Mother is first seen sleeping in a chair in front of her fireplace with a rifle. When Will Mackenzie tries to wake her up, she fires a warning shot. After a brief but tense standoff, the two have a conversation. Grey Mother makes it clear that she does not trust Will due to him being a "mainlander", but he begins to gain her trust after he gathers enough food and firewood for her to last the winter.

The two of them make a deal after Mackenzie gets enough food and fuel for the old woman: Grey Mother will tell him all she knows about the whereabouts of [Dr. Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) in exchange for a few favors. One of these favors includes scouting the main tunnel through the mountains outside Milton, the only way out of town besides climbing. When Will informs Grey Mother that the tunnel has collapsed, she is distraught, knowing that she is effectively trapped in Milton with no hope of rescue. As a result, she asks Will for one more favor: retrieve Lilith Barker's necklace from a safety deposit box at the bank and place it on her grave outside of town. After Will does this, Grey Mother tells him all she knows about Astrid. She also reveals that Lilith was her daughter and that she was once married to Martin Barker, the deceased farmer whose safety deposit box contained Lilith's necklace. She gives Will some old climbing gear that once belonged to Lilith, in order for him to make his way out of Milton.
> “**My journey is finished. But yours is only beginning. Go, and don't think of Grey Mother, or Milton. We're of the old world now. The new world is for the strong to survive.**”

Before Mackeznie leaves Milton, he has a chance to right a wrong from the past in an optional side quest, [One Last Thing](./One%20Last%20Thing.md), where he places the pearls on Lilith's tomb. Doing so leaves Grey Mother at peace, as she is content to sit and think of her Lily, urging Mackenzie to forget about about old Grey Mother and to find his friend.
Grey Mother does not appear in this episode, but appears during the intro story recap talking about [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md).

Grey Mother seemingly passed away in her home in the time since MacKenzie left Milton. At the end of the episode, MacKenzie is seen carrying her corpse, wrapped in a blanket, from her house to the [Graveyard](./Graveyard.md), where she is cremated on a pyre. He erects a wooden cross with the name "Grey Mother" written on it next to [Lily's](./Lilith%20Barker.md) grave.

**Gunsmithing** is a Survival [Skill](./Skills.md) that enables the player to craft ammunition for the [Revolver](./Revolver.md) and [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md).

The Gunsmithing skill allows the crafting of [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) and [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md), but may only be utilized at the [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) and [Ammunition Forge](./Ammunition%20Forge.md) inside:

Skill in Gunsmithing is increased by reading the [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) "_Practical Gunsmithing"_, crafting Can of Gunpowder, Bullets, Revolver Ammunition and Rifle Ammunition. Ammunition crafted below maximum Gunsmithing (level 5) has a chance to misfire, ruining the round and not firing a bullet when used.

1. [Revolver Shell Casing](./Revolver%20Shell%20Casing.md) or [Rifle Shell Casing](./Rifle%20Shell%20Casing.md): picked off the ground after firing the Hunting Rifle or reloading the Revolver, and occasionally as loot (usually on the ground at [Hunter's Blinds](./Hunter%27s%20Blinds.md)). Revolver Casings can also be claimed by unloading the Revolver in the player's inventory.

2. [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md): crafted from one [Stump Remover](./Stump%20Remover.md), [Dusting Sulfur](./Dusting%20Sulfur.md) and two [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md) (producing 0.5kg of Gunpowder), or found rarely as loot. 0.01kg of gunpowder is required per round, so one Can of Gunpowder can produce 50 rounds.

3. [Bullet](./Bullet.md): crafted from [Scrap Lead](./Scrap%20Lead.md) harvested from [Car Batteries](./Car%20Battery.md) with a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md). One Car Battery contains 6 Scrap Lead, and each Scrap Lead can be made into 6 Bullet, so one Car Battery can produce 36 rounds.

1. To craft bullets, you need to have the [Ammunition Forge](./Ammunition%20Forge.md) active and fueled. While active, you can craft Bullets at the [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) in sets of 6 in one hour. Each set of 6 Bullets crafted awards 1 skill point.
2. When crafting Gunpowder, it takes 30 minutes, but the forge does not need to be active to craft. Each container of gunpowder crafted awards 1 skill point.
3. Crafted ammunition takes just 5 minutes per cartridge and does not require the forge to be active to craft. Each individual round awards 1 skill point when crafted.

Crafting quality Condition Revolver/Rifle Ammunition is based on the Gunsmithing skill Level, with lower levels producing lower quality cartridges that are more likely to misfire, no matter the Condition of the Hunting Rifle or Revolver. The quality and Condition of the crafted ammunition will always be found next to the name of the ammo:
A single Revolver/Rifle Cartridge can be harvested anywhere, and has a chance to produce the following after 5 minutes of [Harvesting](./Harvesting.md):

Higher level Gunsmithing Skill leads to a higher chance to recover most or all materials, but lower Gunsmithing Skill has a chance to successfully recover only 1 or 2 of the cartridge's components. One way to quickly level up Gunsmithing is to craft Poor quality ammunition and then simply harvest it at higher skill levels, then craft new ammunition again. Harvesting multiple rounds of ammunition can only be done one at a time however, making the process very tedious.

- It's possible to increase Gunsmithing skill to 5 before crafting any actual ammunition by reading enough Research Books and crafting Bullets (or Gunpowder). Players can avoid ever crafting ammo capable of misfiring.

- Ammunition misfiring and the Hunting Rifle jamming are different mechanics: ammunition misfires are caused by low quality crafted ammunition; Hunting Rifle jams are caused by the firearm itself having low condition, and require reloading (default R) to eject the jammed round.

- Revolver Ammunition can be disassembled and reassembled into Rifle Ammunition at a 1:1 ratio with Gunsmithing Skill 5; or vice versa to take advantage of the Revolver's lighter weight (1.5kg VS 4.0kg) and utility in [Wolf Struggles](./Struggle.md), or the Hunting Rifle's increased stopping power.
- Because of this, it is possible (though tedious) to craft to level 5, disassemble all lower-quality ammo one at a time, and then re-craft to make sure all ammo is at the highest quality.

- In Interloper difficulty Car Batteries, Scrap Lead and crafted Bullets are useless since no Hunting Rifle or Revolver will ever spawn. However, Gunpowder (and in turn, Dusting Sulfur and Stump Remover) can still be used as a [Fire Accelerant](./Fire%20Starting.md) (though finite and rarer than [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md)) as well as for crafting [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md).

- Gunsmithing is the fastest skill to level up, as long as you have the materials to craft ammunition. Each Rifle Cartridge or Revolver Cartridge crafted grants one skill point, and takes only 5 in game minutes to craft. You can craft as many as 24 rounds in only 2 in game hours, resulting in 24 skill points, or about 1/4 of all the skill points you need to get to level 5. Of course, the ammunition you will receive will not be full quality until you reach level 5.

- A limited increase can be obtained from the [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) _[Practical Gunsmithing](./Practical%20Gunsmithing.md)_, which increases the Gunsmithing by 10 skill points with 5 hours of research.

The **Hacksaw** is a tool with several critical functions, including harvesting saplings and furniture made of a variety of materials. [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) is required to repair it.

The hacksaw is the only tool able to break down [Metal Shelves](./Metal%20Shelf.md) and other metal items to obtain scrap metal. It is required to open [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) on [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), and it can be used instead of a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) to cut small tree limbs (a hatchet must be used for the largest limbs) and saplings. It also can be used to harvest carcasses for meat, hides, or guts, although it may be more efficient to use bare hands or other tools. It cannot be used as a weapon in struggles.

One scrap metal and a set of [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md) or [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) are needed to repair the hacksaw. Although it requires a tool set for repair (which are reasonably common), the hacksaw is a reliable way to harvest firewood without relying on hatchets and [Whetstones](./Whetstone.md), which can be in limited supply, or an [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), which requires [Forge](./Forge.md) to craft.

- Open locked [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) region. (N.B. a hacksaw breaking while opening one of these can make it **permanently inaccessible**. See [Repair](./Repair.md) section.)

- [Harvest frozen carcasses](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) (Hacksaws have the same meat harvesting speeds as [Hatchets](./Hatchet.md), which means they are better used on frozen meat, but have worse speeds for hide or gut harvesting).
Unlike most other tools, Hacksaws cannot be selected as a tool for self-defense during a Wolf Struggle. For more information on Struggles, see: [Wildlife Struggles](./Struggle.md).

Hacksaws are repairable with [Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md) using [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md). Also the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) or [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) may repair a non-ruined hacksaw to 100% condition for one [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md). N.B. The hacksaw has a breaking threshold at 25% condition, usage below this number risks ruining it for good.
As with other items, the hacksaw will randomly spawn in any of several different locations on different play-throughs.
- On a shelf in the control room of [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) in the Upper Dam.
- On the barrel or a shelf along the wall in the engine room, 1st floor, [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md).
- Next to a corpse by the [Wing](./Wing.md) between [Forest Cave](./Forest%20Cave%20%28Timberwolf%20Mountain%20location%29.md) and the entrance to [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md).
- In a cave next to a corpse, the cave is located a ways to the right of the [Poachers camp](./Poacher%27s%20Camp.md), when facing it from the [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) side.
- Behind a fallen shelf or on the workbench in the basement of [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md).
- Inside the pickup closest to the "Cannery Worker Residences" next to the long bridge, just forward of the shifter.

> “**During the Aurora, or when in Glimmer Fog, the Handheld Shortwave may pick up errant signals that could lead you to supplies and locations that you wouldn't otherwise find.**”

The **Handheld Shortwave Radio** is a radio used in conjunction with a [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) to locate items in the [Tales](./Tales.md) [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md), [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md), and [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) in the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ DLC.
It is one of the few items that cannot be dropped or placed in containers so it cannot be lost, similar to the [Camera](./Camera.md) and [Respirator](./Respirator.md).

As with most electronics scattered across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), the battery of the Handheld Shortwave Radio is dead during normal gameplay, similar to the [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md). When an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) or [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) event is active however, the Handheld Shortwave Radio will spark back to life, and can be used to track down nearby radio signals within a region. Radio signals indicate the locations of either hidden bunkers or [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) depending on which operating channel the device is set to. Before the radio can even be used properly, a Transmitter must be repaired in a region in order to get radio coverage.
The location for the radio is at the top of the [Control Tower](./Control%20Tower.md), besides the note [Field 31 Operation Memo](./Field%2031%20Operation%20Memo.md).

The radio has two operating channels: The default channel, signified by a Blue Backdrop on the dial. This setting is used to locate the source of the anomalous transmissions related to the Signal Void Tale.

Right-clicking the radio will switch it to the secondary channel, indicated by the dial's Yellow Backdrop. This setting allows players to locate signals from either downed aircraft or hidden Transponder Caches.

When an Aurora or Glimmer Fog event is active, the radio will power back up and can be used for a limited time until the weather events end. If the player does not have the radio equipped, but walks near a signal source, the radio will beep in the player's inventory. The radio goes through 3 phases as the player gets closer to a signal.

The first phase begins when the player switches the radio to a channel and begins moving the camera around the game world with the radio equipped. The meter on the radio will swing from left to right and will audibly whir as it attunes to the signal. When it is fully on the right, the player is currently facing directly towards the source of the signal.

The second phase begins as the player begins getting closer to a signal, signified when the small light on the left side of the radio begins to pulse. As the player draws closer to the signal source, the radio light will flash with increasing intensity.

The third phase begins when the radio begins to audibly click/beep, showing that the player is very close to a signal location. This beeping will become more intense when the player is right on top of the signal source.

Once a player is right on top of the signal, the radio will flash and beep rapidly until the player uncovers the signal source. At this point a prompt will appear to dig up either the supply cache or hidden bunker entrance somewhere in the ground.

It is currently impossible to uncover a bunker or supply cache without an Aurora/Glimmer Fog event being active _AND_ having the Shortwave Radio equipped. Even if the player already possesses knowledge of the bunker/cache locations, or uses [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md) to map the location of a bunker (either by mapping the immediate vicinity or uncovering it via a [Polaroid](./Polaroids.md) Vista location), the player will be unable to dig up the bunker/supply cache due to the game not giving an interactive prompt to uncover anything.
As with any Aurora event, great care should be taken while exploring, as the cold night weather and Aurora Predators can quickly kill an ill equipped player as they search for signals.
If a player has investigated all radio signals in a region on either channels, the radio will no longer be useful. It will still power on but will otherwise never find any new signals to home in on.
As per the Part 4 update, the radio cannot be dropped or placed in containers. This is to keep it from being misplaced and accidentally lost.

> “**Hank, a long-time prepper and denizen of Great Bear Island, has a secret supply cache. Find it and take what you need.**”

**Hank's Hatch** is a side mission in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). Completing the mission allows access to Hank's prepper hatch, which contains ammunition, food, and drink supplies.

The mission is started by finding [Hank's Lock Box Key](./Hank%27s%20Lock%20Box%20Key.md). The key, along with a [Letter for Hank's Niece](./Letter%20for%20Hank%27s%20Niece.md) can be found on a [corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) next to a campfire at [Unnamed Pond](./Unnamed%20Pond.md), appearing at the start of [Signal to Noise](./Signal%20to%20Noise.md) ([Renewed Hope (Predux)](./Renewed%20Hope%20%28Predux%29.md) in Predux Episode 2). After acquiring the key, the player can open Hank's lockbox in the [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md). The lockbox contains [Hank's Journal - Part One](./Hank%27s%20Journal%20-%20Part%20One.md), which when picked up will mark the location of the bunker on the map. Also in the lockbox is [Hank's Prepper Cache Code](./Hank%27s%20Prepper%20Cache%20Code.md) with the code to open the hatch.
The bunker is located north of the [Train Loading Area](./Train%20Loading%20Area.md). It can be reached by following the rock boundary near the [Train Bridge](./Train%20Bridge.md).

Upon arriving at the bunker, the player will need to open the hatch, which has a combination dial lock on the top. The code found on the piece of paper in Hank's lockbox can be used to open the hatch. A corpse is on the ground near the hatch.

Inside the bunker, there is plenty of [canned food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), [granola bars](./Granola%20Bar.md), [flares](./Flare.md), and [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md). Hank's corpse is lying on the floor inside the bunker.
- minor loot from 11 (randomised) containers(flares, matches, tinder, medicine, bandages, sewing kit, accelerant, cloth, books etc.)

- "Hank" is a nod to the protagonist ["Henry"](https://firewatch.fandom.com/wiki/Henry) from the videogame _Firewatch_. Hank (a common nickname for Henry) shares many similarities with his counterpart, including taking a job working in a fire tower in a nature park to be away from other people. In his journal, Hank complains about "the chatty lady" on the radio, a reference to [Delilah](https://firewatch.fandom.com/wiki/Delilah), Henry's supervisor in _Firewatch_ who communicates with him by radio throughout the game and also occasionally refers to him as "Hank". Hank's Journal refers to him finding a "weird old bunker," also a reference to the plot of _Firewatch._

- In his second journal entry, found in the bunker, Hank mentions hearing someone trying to get in. He does not open the door for them, and then dies from an infected leg wound from a Wolf attack. The body found outside, presumably his niece trying to enter, has antibiotics and antiseptic on them. Had he let her in, they both may have survived.

I've spent a lot of years in this damn lookout tower, watching the forest around Mystery Lake, and it's given me nothing but time to think about my life and the world around me and what I hear is happening. Sitting in a tower like this for days, weeks, months on end is enough to drive anyone crazy. Even if I didn't have anyone to talk to on the radio -- and just let me say I wish that chatty lady would shut up once in a while. I mean, I came out here to be alone, to be away from other people. It's almost enough to make you wish all the radios, all the satellite phones and internet and stuff...would just...disappear.

Anyway, I've been putting aside some supplies every season, leftovers or whatever I can spare, and it's added up to quite the little stash of food and equipment. Hopefully I never need it. But if I do -- the ends justify the means, right? I don't think anyone needs that weird old bunker thing I found, and it makes the perfect place to hide out if the SHTF, you know what I mean?

**Happy Harvester** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is obtained after harvesting twenty-five [cat tail plants](./Cat%20Tail.md), [rose hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) bushes, [reishi mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) and [old man's beard lichens](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) in a single game.

Note: That is twenty-five harvest actions of each type. Rose hip bushes currently yield exactly eight rose hips per plant, so a total of twenty-five harvests would yield 200 rose hips total. Mushrooms and lichens count individually since they are individual actions, even though they may grow on the same stump or tree. The game has no counter anywhere of how far along this achievement the player is.
[^1]: Mushrooms and lichens are not technically plants but fungi and cyanobacterium respectively.

**Harvesting** is a mechanic in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ that involves the breaking down of objects into usable [Materials](./Materials.md).

Harvesting often involves destroying interactable environmental objects, but can also involve breaking down excess [Tools](./Tools.md) or [Clothing](./Clothing.md). [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md), [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md), and [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) items cannot be Harvested.

The most common Materials gained from Harvesting are [Cloth](./Cloth.md), [Cured Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md), [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), [Sticks](./Stick.md), and [Tinder Plugs](./Tinder%20Plug.md). You can harvest any wood, cardboard, or cloth item in the environment by selecting it, choosing your tool, and selecting "Break Down." Some items require tools to break down, and cannot be broken down with your bare hands. Containers cannot be harvested. Environment Objects that require a tool to harvest will give an error message if clicked on, such as "REQUIRES A HACKSAW TO BREAK DOWN" or "REQUIRES A TOOL TO BREAK DOWN", however some objects can be harvested by hand. ![~10:00 PM, the end of natural daylight](../assets/Nighttime_start_10pm.jpg)_~10:00 PM, the end of natural daylight_ Harvesting by hand can be performed in darkness, but Harvesting with the use of any kind of Tool requires light, otherwise the message "REQUIRES LIGHT TO BREAK DOWN WITH TOOL" will be displayed. This can be daylight from dawn (6:00 AM) through 8:30 PM both indoors and outdoors, the light provided during [Auroras](./Aurora.md), natural starlight in case of clear [Weather](./Weather.md) at an outdoor location, or light from a lit fire or other source like a [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md). Note that fires only provide light in a few meters radius, beyond which it will be considered dark.

Very rarely, some objects can be broken down to yield paths to hidden locations/items. [Crates](./Crate.md) often have a chance to contain usable items inside, while [Scrub Brush](./Scrub%20Brush.md) in some regions block certain pathways.

These items can be broken by ![Anywhere icon](../assets/Anywhere_icon.png)Hand, but using a tool saves harvesting times at the expense of Tool Condition. Some objects require one of these Tools to break down:

**[Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md)** is a Survival [Skill](./Skills.md) that is used to harvest meat, [animal fat](./Animal%20Fat.md), hides, and [guts](./Fresh%20Gut.md) from [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md). There are 9 types of harvestable animals in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, and apart from [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), all animals can only be harvested at the location of the carcass, unless that animal has been quartered. Higher levels in the carcass harvesting skill reduce the amount of time required to harvest and increase the amount that can be harvested by hand from a frozen carcass. > “**A small one-handed axe. Good for splitting wood. Can be used to hack meat in a pinch.**”
The **Hatchet** is a tool in _The Long Dark_, primarily for woodcutting and self defense.

The hatchet can be used to harvest [sticks](./Stick.md) from branches and some [Scrub Brush](./Scrub%20Brush.md), [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) from cedar limbs, and [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md) from fir limbs. It can also be used to break down many wooden objects such as shelves and crates into [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md). Hatchets can also allow the player to cut down maple and birch saplings without a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md).
- May be used to [harvest frozen carcasses](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) (Knives have faster unfrozen meat, gut and hide harvesting speeds. Hatchets are only faster at harvesting frozen meat).
- Open or maintain holes in the ice for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) (bladed tools break ice faster, but take more condition loss).
- Breaking down Furniture and Crates (for [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) or [Cloth](./Cloth.md)).
- For the [Whiteout](./Whiteout.md) [challenge's](./Challenge.md) objective, an improvised hatchet may substitute the requirement of a hatchet.

When carried and selected for self-defense at the start of a Wolf Struggle, Hatchets deal high damage with a low chance per-hit to cause the wolf to flee, as well as a moderate chance to inflict [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) on the Wolf (which is lethal over time). Hatchets take low damage from being used in a struggle, and are superior to [Improvised Hatchets](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) when used in this way. For more information on Struggles, see: [Wildlife Struggles](./Struggle.md).
In Interloper mode hatchets will never spawn; requiring forging to create an [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md).
Hatchets may be repaired using a [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md) and the [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) skill, restoring 3% condition to the hatchet and causing 5% condition damage to the whetstone.

The [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) or [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) may repair a non-ruined hatchet to 100% condition for one scrap metal, during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md). N.B. The hatchet has a breaking threshold at 15% condition, usage below this number risks ruining it for good.

- A broken Hatchet is the icon and logo for _The Long Dark_ on all platforms, including [the official Hinterlands website](https://hinterlandgames.com/), [forums](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/) and [merchandise](https://www.hinterlandstore.com/).

- Unlike large axes, hatchets feature a hammerhead on their back; despite this, the hatchet is never used for this purpose in-game, even suffering a condition penalty when used to break ice for being a 'sharp tool'.

A **Haul Truck** or **Dump Truck** is a [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) found exclusively around the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) complex in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md). They contain a stairwell leading to a single door to the driver's seat that can be opened. Inside a player can find loot on the floorboard or sleep/pass time. There are currently 3 Earth Movers located around the open pit mine in the region, and they are the rarest land vehicle in the game. The Haul Truck on the edge of the open pit mine contains a [Polaroid](./Polaroids.md) on the dashboard.

**Headache** is an Affliction that is inflicted on the survivor after consuming certain [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) or [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) items.

While the Affliction is active, the entire screen will occasionally distort similar to the [Pain](./Pain.md) Affliction, but with a more intense distortion. The screen will zoom in and out slightly to simulate an intense headache until the affliction wears off. The player also cannot use [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) until the Affliction passes. Unlike the Pain Affliction, this visual effect can't be treated with [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md) or [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md).

Headaches have no long-term effects on the player, only serving as a simple visual distraction and a slight annoyance. If in a safe spot, the player can simply use the "Pass Time" option or [Sleep](./Sleep.md) to make the Affliction pass quickly.
> “**You are suffering from a head-ache. It's not debilitating, but the occasional shot of pain and blurred vision can be distracting.**”

Drinking a [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) or eating [Caffeine Pills](./Caffeine%20Pills.md) will produce a Headache. When either are consumed, the edges of the player's screen will distort and blur, producing a chromatic aberration effect.

- When the [Energy Boost](./Energy%20Boost.md) effect of a consumed Go! Energy Drink has expired, a Headache Affliction begins. As a side effect, all [Stamina](./Stamina.md) is instantly lost when a Headache begins.

**Heat Pack** is a positive [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) obtained when using a [Heat Pack](./Heat%20Pack.md). The effect raises the survivor's [Warmth](./Warmth.md) and remains in effect as long as the Heat Pack remains in use and is in the player's inventory.
Despite the Affliction description stating that the Heat Pack is tucked into the player's Clothing while operating, Clothing is not needed to gain the benefits of an active Heat Pack.
Once activated, a Heat Pack produces no Warmth to the player at first, but will gradually raise [Warmth](./Warmth.md) and overall [Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md) over time.
- +0.1C (+0.2F) of Warmth is added by the pack every 30 seconds after activation and generates the Heat Pack (Affliction).
- The Warmth caps at +5.0C (+9F) 50 minutes after activation (time remaining will be 5 hours 10 minutes).
- Using multiple Heat Packs does not combine their effects. The Heat Pack (Affliction) only displays the time left on the Heat Pack with the most time remaining.
- Once 50 minutes remain after activation, the Heat Pack will slowly lose Warmth by -0.1C (-0.2F) every 30 seconds until time runs out to 0 minutes left.
- After time expires, the Condition of a Heat Pack will instantly turn to 0% and the item will be Ruined, providing no heat.
