The **Heat Pack** is a [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). They also appear in [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md).

It is only acquired when trading with the [Trader](./Trader.md) at higher levels of Trust, or in Chapter Five of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). It provides the positive [Heat Pack (Affliction)](./Heat%20Pack%20%28Affliction%29.md) when used.

Dropping an active Heat Pack will remove the Warmth effect and will display on the item how much heat is being produced and how much time is left on the pack. The Heat Pack (Affliction) is also lost when the Pack is dropped. The stats of a Heat Pack do not update in real time in the player's inventory. Selecting another item, then the Heat Pack will update the stats of the Heat Pack.
Despite the Affliction description stating that the Heat Pack is tucked into the player's Clothing while operating, Clothing is not needed to gain the benefits of an active Heat Pack.

- The effect raises the survivor's [Warmth](./Warmth.md) by a solid +5.0C (+9F), equivalent to wearing 2 [Cowichan Sweaters](./Cowichan%20Sweater.md) and remains in effect as long as the Heat Pack is carried in the inventory once activated.
- As such, a Heat Pack can be especially helpful for emergency situations, such as being caught in a blizzard or having damaged clothing after an animal [Struggle](./Struggle.md).

- They are quite useful for staying warm while exploring very cold regions, such as [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) or the higher areas of [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) (where the temperature continues to drop at higher elevations).
- Late game [Interloper](./Interloper.md)/[Misery](./Misery.md) players can stay especially warm with a Heat Pack while exploring the outdoors.
- Heat Packs can only be acquired by trading with the Trader at higher Trust levels, which can take considerable time to unlock as part of [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md).
- The player can only reap the benefits of 1 active Heat Pack at a time for balancing reasons. Using multiple Heat Packs will only produce benefits from the one with the most time left.
Once activated, a Heat Pack produces no Warmth to the player at first, but will gradually raise [Warmth](./Warmth.md) and overall [Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md) over time.
- +0.1C (+0.2F) of Warmth is added by the pack every 30 seconds after activation and generates the [Heat Pack (Affliction)](./Heat%20Pack%20%28Affliction%29.md).
- The Warmth caps at +5.0C (+9F) 50 minutes after activation (time remaining will be 5 hours 10 minutes).
- Using multiple Heat Packs does not combine their effects. The Heat Pack (Affliction) only displays the time left on the Heat Pack with the most time remaining.
- Once 50 minutes remain after activation, the Heat Pack will slowly lose Warmth by -0.1C (-0.2F) every 30 seconds until time runs out to 0 minutes left.
- After time expires, the Condition of a Heat Pack will instantly turn to 0% and the item will be Ruined, providing no heat.

**Heavy Hammer** is a tool in _The Long Dark_. It is used for [forging](./Forge.md), [breaking](./Harvesting.md) down furniture, making [holes in the ice for fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md), or self defense during [wildlife struggles](./Struggle.md).

The Heavy Hammer is a multi-purpose tool, but is essential for [Forging](./Forge.md): which is the only means for the survivor to craft their own tools, the [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) and [Arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md). Hammers lose small amounts of condition when used to forge, break furniture, or make holes in the ice, or during a struggle if selected.

Hammers are essential for long-term play as efficient and repairable tools for making holes for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) (for food or to avoid [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md)). On [Interloper mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) where all Hatchets, Knives and Arrows never spawn, Heavy Hammers are essential to forge these items for self defense, and crafting [animal-skin clothing](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md), and using the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md).
- Forging: [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md), and [Arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md) (for crafting [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md)).
- Breaking down Furniture and Crates (for [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) or [Cloth](./Cloth.md)).

When carried and selected for self-defense at the start of a Wolf Struggle, Heavy Hammers deal middling damage with a high chance per-hit to cause the wolf to flee. Hammers take low damage from being used in a struggle, and never inflict Blood Loss to the Wolf. For more information on Struggles, see: [Wildlife Struggles](./Struggle.md).

Heavy Hammer may be used to break down most (but not all) furniture for [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) and [Cloth](./Cloth.md). Destroying furniture in this way is more calorie and time expensive than with a Hatchet, but is faster than by hand and allows breaking some furniture which cannot be broken down with bare hands. Heavy Hammers also weigh more than a Hatchet or Improvised Hatchet, but despite these drawbacks they are easier to repair: requiring [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md) (Repair time: 45 minutes) or [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) (Repair time: 30 minutes) and [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md) (rather than the rare [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md) or [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) for Hatchets).
- In Cell Block 3 at [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) building, in the room where the went exits on a shelf.
- In the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) closest to the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md) entrance on the ground.
- At [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) inside the dam complex, at the workbench.
- In one of the cars at [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) near [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md) or at [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md).
- On the upper level of the [Barn](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
- At [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) on the workbench or the tool rack shelves.

- Laying up against a knocked over barrel by the fire barrel in [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) lower level. (very easy to miss in low light conditions- near the railing with pallets behind it.)
- In a red box in the [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md). (or under the workbench, or outside the wall)
- In one of the [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) in the [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md) of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md).
- At a shelf in the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md), in one of the toolboxes, or underneath the workbench.

- In real world metalworking, numerous different hammers (each with their own unique head shapes and weights) would be used for different applications, but for all intents and purposes the picture suits as merely just a reference.

- It's sometimes called a "Wolf Bonker" due to its high melee stats, capable of crippling limbs and ending Wolf [Struggles](./Struggle.md) rapidly (15% chance to scare off immediately, 5% chance to kill instantly).
- Interloper has had its loot positions refreshed and more position randomness added to its important items (like hammers) to add less predictability.
- Modified struggle damage modifiers for various tools, and added modifiers for the new Hammer.

![Helicopter](../assets/Helicopter.jpg) **Helicopters** are the rarest of any [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), second only to [Buses](./Bus.md) and [Earth Movers](./Haul%20Truck.md). Most are only found in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) Region and provide a small warmth bonus and complete protection from wind-chill as [Cars](./Car.md), [Trucks](./Truck.md), and [Tractors](./Tractor.md) would. They can also be used as a temporary shelter to sleep or evade wildlife.

Helicopters contain the most loot containers of any vehicle, often containing 2 side hatches and 2 cylindrical hatches on the outside, 2 baskets that often contain loot, and many lockers inside the passenger cabin. Like other vehicles during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md), the electronics of a Helicopter will turn back on.

Most Helicopters can be found in the Forsaken Airfield Region around the abandoned tarmac of [Field 31](./Field%2031.md), as well as inside the [Main Hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md). A single crashed helicopter can be found in the mountains to the west of [Shoulder Lake](./Shoulder%20Lake.md). A unique rescue helicopter, [Final Approach](./Final%20Approach.md), can be found in north of [Surveyor's Memory](./Surveyor%27s%20Memory.md) and contains a medical cot for sleeping, a chance to spawn a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) box, and various lockers that can be looted. Another crashed Helicopter located in the [Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) is found in the mountains of the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), near [Old Corral](./Old%20Corral.md).
Only 1 Helicopter can be found in Lower Great Bear, crashed on a ridge near [Muskeg Overlook](./Muskeg%20Overlook.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md).

> — Heller: Do I look like a guy who gives a shit? You don't want to freeze out here? Then get moving! Heller slams the door shut on Mackenzie Heller at the start of [The Power Plant](./The%20Power%20Plant.md)

**Heller** is a member of the [Convicts](./Convicts.md) appearing in [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md). He serves as a secondary antagonist for the episode.

Heller was one of the prisoners being transported to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), but his [Prison Bus crashed](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) outside of [Milton](./Milton.md) during the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md). He escaped the bus with several other Convicts and made his way to [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) and later [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), eventually leaving the region after many of the other Convicts began turning up dead, leading him to realize that [someone](./Molly.md) was hunting them. He is eventually tasked with carrying an unconscious [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) to the Prison via [Mathis'](./Mathis.md) orders, having to hear [Vachon](./Vachon.md) bellyache the whole way there.

He is Mathis' most faithful sidekick, and has few qualms when it comes to sending [Will](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) to face the cold and aggressive wildlife of the [Blackrock Region](./Blackrock.md), unlike Vachon. Heller seems quite close to Mathis, being part of the prison break on the Mainland that landed both of them in Blackrock Prison to begin with. However he often expresses his concern that Mathis may be going crazy, but follows his orders in order to avoid the heat coming his way. One thing is certain however; if the tide turns, he will try to save his skin at all costs.

Heller is almost always seen paired with Vachon, being the more aggressive, selfish, and uncaring of the two. He often refers to Mackenzie as a "dog" after he is tasked with constantly performing dangerous work for the gang, with this term eventually spreading to other Convicts in the prison.

Like the other inmates, he partially wears his old prisoner clothes, namely the typical orange jumpsuit of Blackrock inmates, as well as a [Mackinaw Jacket](./Mackinaw%20Jacket.md) and some [Trail Boots](./Trail%20Boots.md). He seems much younger than Mathis and Vachon, and yet is already quite dark and evil, much like [Donner](./Donner.md).

Heller does not appear in Episode 1, but his name (HELLER, S.) appears on the [Prison Transport Manifest](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md) near the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md), foreshadowing him.
Heller appears with Vachon carrying Mackenzie on a stretcher. He later comes under attack with the rest of the group and is forced to search for Mackenzie after he escapes.

Heller appears with Vachon and Mathis once Mackenzie wakes up. After Mathis savagely beats the Warden [Franklin](./Franklin.md), Mathis tasks the two criminals to clean him up. He recounts the story of how Mathis' last prison break on the Mainland landed him on a bus to Blackrock Prison.

Heller is later convinced by Mackenzie to secretly let him out of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) behind Mathis' back in order to find [Blackrock Infirmary Medication](./Blackrock%20Infirmary%20Medication.md) for [Franklin](./Franklin.md). After Heller and Vachon realize that the medication is outside the Prison, and do not wish to risk being killed by hostile wildlife, they reluctantly let the pilot loose.

Heller appears at the start of the mission by tossing a map of the Power Plant to Mackenzie, telling him to get moving and fix the power to the Prison. When Mackenzie asks if he can have a coat, Heller shows his lack of empathy by yelling at him to hurry up or freeze, as Mathis only issued the Power Plant map to the pilot.

Heller appears with Vachon to pester Mackenzie as Mathis interrogates him and Franklin, telling the pilot to find the [Detonators](./Detonators.md) before "Mathis goes a few more rounds with the Warden."
He later appears at the end of the mission along with Vachon, seizing Mackenzie after he delivers the Detonators.

Heller appears before Mathis after the Prison explodes informing him that the other Convicts blew the Detonators the wrong way in Solitary. He later appears in the Prison Yard yelling at other Convicts to find and shoot Mackenzie, even spotting him from a prison tower spotlight if the player is not careful.
Heller later appears at the Power Plant in the final cutscene, informing Mathis that [Donner](./Donner.md) was pulled from Solitary but is in critical condition.
Despite being a major character in Episode 4, Heller does not get his own [What I Know](./What%20I%20Know.md) character section.

These tea boxes can be found with five packets of tea inside and takes 0.25L/0.07 gallons of [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) to make one cup of herbal tea.
When cooked, the condition will be 50% higher than the package it was made from, up to a maximum of 100%. For example, a package with 20% condition would produce a cup of tea with 70% condition.
While the Herbal Tea deteriorates over time, cups of herbal tea do not. Therefore it's wise to make cups of herbal tea before the package becomes ruined.
| [Cup of Herbal Tea](./Cup%20of%20Herbal%20Tea.md) | None | - 1 × [Herbal Tea](./Herbal%20Tea.md) - 0.25 L × [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) |

Herbal Tea, when drunk hot or cold, will give you the "[Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md)" [Affliction](./Afflictions.md#Improved_rest_affliction), which will increase condition gained while sleeping by 2% an hour one's next 6 hours of sleep (whether this be all at once or across multiple sleep sessions), meaning one glass of Herbal Tea can restore up to an additional 12% condition.
The ingredients on the back list: "Chamomile Flower, Mint Leaf, Natural Flavors." and that it was "Made In Canada."

Provides some shelter **Hermit's Cabin** is a dilapidated structure in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md).

The cabin is an outdoors location on the northwest bank of the [Milton Basin](./Milton%20Basin.md). It can serve as a temporary base, especially if traveling between [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md).

A wood stove, wooden crates and containers are inside the ruins, as well as a firewood bin in the rear, with [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) growing nearby. These wooden crates may be broken down for [reclaimed wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) and may also contain random items. A [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) grove is near, as well as [cattails](./Cat%20Tail%20Stalk.md) and a [birch forest](./Birch%20Bark.md). On the lake's central island, [crows](./Crow.md) may circle a frozen corpse.
[Wolves](./Wolf.md) commonly roam on the lake, both north and south of the cabin. [Moose](./Moose.md) may spawn rarely along the northern basin.

**Hibernation** is a community term (similar to [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md) and [Daisy Chaining](./Daisy%20Chaining.md)) used to describe any course of actions that combine benefits taken from [condition](./Condition.md) drain when [needs](./Needs.md) are not met with restoring condition by satisfying needs briefly while [sleeping](./Sleep.md). Primarily, it is a method to conserve limited resources.
- Needs cannot be drained below zero. Once a need reaches zero fulfillment, it stays at zero until some satisfaction is again available.
- Game actions like harvesting or traveling or even being awake do not require needs to be satisfied to be taken.
- Drain on needs is lowest during sleep. Further, sleep actually replenishes the needs of [fatigue](./Fatigue.md) and [warmth](./Warmth.md) when used properly.

2800 calories would be consumed during 14 hours harvesting carcasses. But if no calories are available (Hunger is empty), about 15% of condition would be drained instead. Only 750 calories are required during 10 hours of fully replenishing sleep (interloper difficulty). So eating only 750 calories prior to sleeping can maintain a character with only briefly lowered condition taken as a trade-off. This is a great reduction from the 3,550 calories that would have been required to keep hunger satisfied the whole day.

The name 'hibernation' comes from this tactic's most common early use: to extend survival time to earn high placement on community leaderboards. Players would stock pile [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) and [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) and then procedurally starve then replenish themselves. Sleeping until condition reached as low as they dared, they would eat just enough to then sleep 12 hours, recover back to 100% condition, and repeat the cycle until all food and water was exhausted. Eating little staying in one place and sleeping lots, along with the game's winter setting and inclusion of bears, granted rapid acceptance of referring to this practice as 'hibernation'. The term is now used for any tactics that similarly use condition loss and sleep to replace satisfaction of needs.

Hibernia Processing is an old whaling station situated almost at the end of Desolation Point. The location is visible from the road, as well as from the top deck of the [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md). The outside area and road is patrolled by several [wolves](./Wolf.md). Preparation for a possible encounter with any predator is highly recommended, but hiding inside one of the smaller structures and sleeping may cause them to drift away, allowing the player to escape.

The yard area has a group of conjoined trailers on one side; a lone trailer with an outdoor fire barrel sits on the other side of the main building of the Hibernia Processing warehouse. The yard can be accessed from both the road and the coast, either by climbing up the main boat ramp from the east, or climbing through a [Truck](./Truck.md) that is blocking the main gate from the west.
The road up from Hibernia can also spawn a [Moose](./Moose.md) and a nearby [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) can spawn a [Bear](./Bear.md).

Much of the entire interior is dimly lit, so an artificial light source may be beneficial during most of the day and night. The building is also relatively cold, and players with low-quality clothing may need to start a fire or use a bed to warm up.
The Hibernia Processing building has two entrances: a door straight from the east leads to the lower floor, while a staircase at south side leads up to a spacious staff lounge.

The first floor includes a huge processing hall and a smaller engine room, where a staircase to the second floor is located. The processing hall contains whale-processing equipment and whale bones, and a large amount of wooden crates, pallets, and other objects that can be harvested.

There are also a couple potential hidden caches (i.e., informally stashed items--not to be confused with cache boxes in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) and Story mode), including a possible rifle location.

One hidden stash is accessible by walking through a pipe heading up into some boat-storage racks. The other can be accessed by breaking down most of the green crates blocking the corner to the left of the player when entering the processing floor from the engine room. There may also be one or more tools (e.g., a [prybar](./Prybar.md)) hidden in niches in the room. The engine room, besides pallets and cardboard, has a [fire barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md), a [work bench](./Work%20Bench.md), as well as a [safe](./Safe.md) in the corner of the room, half-hidden behind a wooden pallet. Any of a few types of tools may also spawn on the shelving along the wall with the safe.

The second floor has three rooms. The biggest one, the staff lounge, has a few [beds](./Bed.md), tables, and chairs. You will also find shelves, which usually have some clothes on them and potentially other essential items such as [matches](./Matches%20%28disambiguation%29.md). Under one of the bunkbeds a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) may be found caseless and without any [flare shells](./Flare%20Shell.md), however some may spawn on nearby shelves. The adjoining locker room may also contain such items and has an exit to the outside area, some harvestable objects, and four lockers. The third room is a small office room with two [file cabinets](./File%20Cabinet.md), and a table with drawers. The room also has a hole in the wall leading a catwalk above the processing hall's maintenance floor. Walking further and overcoming the snowdrift, a [body](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) can be seen in the corner. There is a [heavy hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) against the east wall in the processing room.

As of Patch 2.38 (dec. 24) there is an additional stack of [Batteries](./Car%20Battery.md) here, in order to supply with trading materials for the [Trader](./Trader.md). On Interloper, aside from the ones usually found to repair the Transmitter, there is a chance of at least 4 more Batteries to spawn (More info is required to check if there are chances of more or less). These new batteries spawn in all existing worlds, but require having [Tales of the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC installed.

The player can fall through the holes in 2nd floor safely, although this is not advised. This can be prevented by covering the holes with planks using [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md).
It is full of whale bones, and certain objects such as pallets, which can make it hard to traverse, and impossible to enter some areas without breaking down something.

Due to its spacious interior and many amenities, along with the nearby forge at [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md), coal in the nearby mines, [beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md), and hunting at [Little Island](./Little%20Island.md), Hibernia Processing has long been a popular [safehouse](./Safehouse.md) for players living in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md). Its large interior comes with plenty of storage, and there is more than enough space for extensive [customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md). The biggest weakness of Hibernia as a safehouse is the region it's in: Desolation Point is a relatively small and isolated region, making it less than ideal for players who wish to travel around the island, especially if they wish to visit the [Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md).

- Hibernia (meaning "Land of Winter") is the Classical Latin name for the island of [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hibernia). This could imply that the founders of the company are/were of Irish descent.

**Hidden Caches** are small containers filled with useful loot found consistently through the many Episodes of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) as part of various side missions.

They can also be found in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). Currently, they only exist in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) and [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md). They spawn in different locations for each playthrough, their number depending on the [difficulty](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Survival_Mode#Experience). [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) which has the highest # of them, will spawn a minimum of 7 (min of 1 on [interloper](./Interloper.md)/[misery](./Misery.md)).
They contain medium-high level food and clothes and, sometimes, even books. A Hidden Cache has a total capacity of 15.00 kg.

- **Only guaranteed spawn**. Inside the southernmost entrance for the northern [Ice Cave](./Ice%20Cave.md) system. Enter at [Reclusive Falls](./Reclusive%20Falls.md), follow the stream and get past the inner waterfall, look inside raised area on right side, dead end of a tunnel to the left or end of a tunnel to the right. Contains: [Revolver](./Revolver.md), [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md), [condensed milk](./Condensed%20Milk.md)/[MRE](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md)/[Peanut Butter](./Peanut%20Butter.md) and [balaclava](./Balaclava.md)/[Long Wool Scarf](./Long%20Wool%20Scarf.md)/[Wool Ear Wrap](./Wool%20Ear%20Wrap.md).

The **Hide Chair** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.
A makeshift wooden chair, a Hide Chair can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The chair can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value, the chair cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the chair will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).
The Hide Chair can be harvested with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) in 2 hours and produces 1 [Cured Deer Hide](./Cured%20Deer%20Hide.md) and 3 [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md).

High Blind is a [hunting blind](./Hunter%27s%20Blinds.md) located on top of a small mound overlooking the surrounding frozen lake. It is surrounded by thin ice in many directions. Supplies found here are similar to other blinds and may include cans of food and sometimes a bow. Some rose hips can also be found near the area. Blinds offer minimal protection from the elements, so sleeping without a fire or high-tier clothing is not recommended.

Inside of the backpack underneath the blind, there's a chance that a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) and an [Arrowhead](./Arrowhead.md) can be found. In addition, there's usually, either, a [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) or a [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md) directly underneath the Hunting Blind.

An isolated small meadow upon an hill, expect just cold and harsh weather. No shelter can be found here, scarce in resources too. The meadow is a prime location for map making, featuring a vista spot. To reach it, start from the rope bridge and climb the rock on the right side and approach the cliff, a message should pop up when you reach the place.

The meadow contains 0-3 birch saplings, and under the wooden ramp leading to the rope bridge there may spawn a [Stump Remover](./Stump%20Remover.md), [Dusting Sulfur](./Dusting%20Sulfur.md) or a random skill book. On the other side of the bridge there may be a backpack with random loot leaning against the boulder on the right side.

Provides some shelter **High Peak Plateau** is an unmarked location in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md). It is located to the far east of the map in the mountains and can only be accessed via progressing through the [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) Tale.

The peak is reached after the long climb up to [Roamer's Cave](./Roamer%27s%20Cave.md) and an even longer hike through the mountains. The peak has a single transmitter and storage shed nearby containing a windproof [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md). It also has a ptarmigan nest nearby. The location is very cold due to the extremely high altitude, being the highest location in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md).
This location is the highest in elevation the survivor can reach throughout Great Bear Island.
- [Foreman's Technical Log 3](./Foreman%27s%20Technical%20Log%203.md) (with a Polaroid inside, [Foreman's Polaroid 3](./Foreman%27s%20Polaroid%203.md))

Heading west of the transmitter provides an anchor for the Mountaineering Rope and leads to a small pond and later a one way slope back down the mountain, close to [Cascading Gap](./Cascading%20Gap.md).

**Highway Robbery** is a side mission started in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In the mission, the survivor investigates an abandoned truck on [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md) after finding a [note](./Highway%20Robbery.md) describing a rich Mainlander abandoning a truck on the bridge. The mission can only be completed in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), prior to the survivor [leaving Milton](./Paradise%20Lost.md).
> “**You found a note describing the possible location of emergency supplies near a bridge outside of Milton.**”
To start the mission, the survivor has to find one of the corresponding note at the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) outside [Milton](./Milton.md):

Search [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) and locate the note. It is located by a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) in the back of the station. Once the survivor has found and read the note, they can proceed to [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md).

The easiest method to get to this location is to start at [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md), near the [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md), and follow the road to the right towards [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md). Continue past the church, staying on the road, until Spruce Falls Bridge is encountered.
The first pickup truck has a trunk located in its bed. Search the trunk, taking the supplies within, and the mission will be completed.

Provides some shelter **Hilltop Cave** is one of several caves dotted throughout [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), located not far from [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) and the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) transition cave (and subesquently [Cascading Falls](./Cascading%20Falls.md)).

Hilltop Cave lies next to a [Hunter's Blind](./Hunter%27s%20Blinds.md), both of which are south-west of the [Cave](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md) connecting to [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md).

[Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) and an abundance of [reishi mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) can be found in the area. [Frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), both human and [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md), can also be found in the area. There's a chance of finding a backpack and some food on the cave floor. The area is also home to several [rabbits](./Rabbit.md), as well as a [bear](./Bear.md) that may often wander through.

This cave can be useful if players are sleeping in [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) and need to eliminate [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), as it is relatively close by and, like most small caves, counts as an outdoor location.

**Headquarters:** [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver), [BC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia), [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada)
**Hinterland Studio Inc.** is an independent game studio headquartered in downtown Vancouver.

The studio was founded by Raphael van Lierop, who previously directed Relic's _Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine_ and worked on other games such as _Company of Heroes,_ _Dawn of War,_ and _Far Cry 3_.[^1] In 2012, van Lierop started Hinterland Studio and recruited veteran AAA game developers including Alan Lawrance of Volition Inc, Hokoyo Lim, art director for _League of Legends_, David Chan, audio designer at BioWare, and Marianna Krawczyk, lead writer of the _God of War_ series.[^2] Since then, the team has grown to include over 25 members.[^3] In August 2016, it was announced that Hinterland would be moving to its new headquarters on Dunsmuir Avenue in Cumberland.[^4] Currently, the only physical studio is located in downtown Vancouver at the former MacMillan Bloedel Building.[^5][^6] In September of 2018, Hinterland hired six new employees, the most significant growth in team size since the studio's foundation. This was in part due to Hinterland hiring former employees of Capcom Vancouver, which went defunct that month. Hinterland also purchased motion-capture equipment from Capcom.[^7]

This was in part due to Hinterland hiring former employees of Capcom Vancouver, which went defunct that month. Hinterland also purchased motion-capture equipment from Capcom.[^7]

Hinterland utilizes a distributed model, in which employees may work from locations other than the main studio. About half of the employees work at the main studio in downtown Vancouver, while the other half is distributed throughout North America.[^8] The team utilizes electronic communications and project management applications such as Slack, Skype, and Basecamp, and supplements these with occasional in-person meetings.[^9]

**Hippocratic Oath** is a [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is an unmissable story achievement obtained after rescuing all [Crash Survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md) Logan, Ava, and Wade and returning them to the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md) and also stocking the cabinet with the required supplies during the mission [Coming Storm](./Coming%20Storm.md).

- The achievement name is a reference to how new doctors and physicians are required to swear to never purposfully harm their patients. A "Hippocratic Oath" is in reference to how modern medical doctors are often required to "harm" their patients in order to heal and/or otherwise save them. (Example: injecting fresh blood with a needle or cutting the flesh to perform surgery).
- Healing Dimitri with [Insulin](./Insulin.md) by piercing his skin with a needle may satisfy this criteria.
- Killing Timberwolves to save the Crash Survivors may also be considered a "Hippocratic Oath" to "not bring harm".

violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **History of The Collapse, Part One**_

In the mid-20XX, the ongoing global economic crisis, fueled by continued political instability in the US and Europe, contributing to increasing volatility in the financial markets, led to the sudden catastrophic collapse of the Canadian, and in general, the North American banking system. This immediately rendered Canadian currency worthless, triggered super-inflation of the US dollar, and all trade and economic activity promptly shifted to the Chinese Yuan or crypto-currencies (a la Bitcoin). Crippled economically, Canada was brought under the financial oversight of the North American Economic Zone, which positioned Canada as a kind of protectorate of a larger US-based economic bloc. From this point onward, the majority of economic activity became centralized on Canada’s already densely urbanized population, with smaller rural and remote communities being essentially cut off. Without a local economic lifeline many of these communities had become dependent on for their continued existence, most rural or remote communities became hollowed out, as people fled to urban areas in search of greater economic stability.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **History of The Collapse, Part Two**_

For places like Great Bear, already quite remote and suffering after decades of economic decline, the sudden Collapse was the final straw. Without any major local economic drivers of their own, the remaining communities on Great Bear became completely dependent on a supply lifeline from the Mainland -- regular shipments of basic staples designed to keep them alive: fuel, food, medical supplies, etc., in many ways, akin to WW2-era wartime rationing. In exchange for regular supply drops, the “Mainlanders” -- in some cases, at the behest of their economic overlords South of the border -- felt justified in taking whatever supplies and raw materials they needed to maintain the urban communities, including dismantling some of the heavy industrial infrastructure left on Great Bear.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **History of The Collapse, Part Three**_

Unhappy with their growing dependence on the Mainland for economic support, as well as the Mainlander’s continued view that Great Bear exists solely as a resource clearinghouse for their benefit, some people who chose to remain on Great Bear decided to engage their self-sufficiency. Small-scale local food production efforts, akin to the Victory Garden program of WW2 England and Canada, sprouted up all over Great Bear, with individuals and even communities taking it in their own hands to produce food and power resources. Some of these activities took on an aspect of being politically or even ideologically motivated -- these weren’t just gardens or small-scale attempts to provide for local needs. These were acts of rebellion against a (perceived?) occupying economic force.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **History of The Collapse, Part Four**_

Cut off from the Mainland -- economically and figuratively -- Great Bear Islanders became increasingly segregated into two pseudo-political entities along ideological lines: those who gratefully embraced dependence on the Mainland and viewed the regular supply ships as a charitable gesture in apology for the Mainland’s exploitation of Great Bear’s resource riches, and those who sought ultimate independence and who considered trade and travel between the Mainland to be a necessary evil, viewing Mainlanders with a degree of mistrust. Those in support of the Mainlanders even considered the small-scale “Victory Garden” type activities as a sign of lacking patriotism, a concept that hadn’t really existed as such in the Canadian mindset, pre-Collapse.

**Hobbs** is a minor character appearing in the [REDUX](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/The_Long_Dark/Changelog#1.41) version of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) Episode 1. He can be found in the [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md), near the town of [Milton](./Milton.md).

Hobbs is one of the [Convicts](./Convicts.md), a felon on his way to [Blackrock Federal Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) to serve a twenty-year sentence. The [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) struck during transit, and he and at least two other inmates fled the [prison bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) into the nearby town when it crashed outside [Milton](./Milton.md) (with the many other inmates going through the tunnel to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md)) , causing the tunnel to collapse. With his fellow inmates, Hobbs took the remaining citizens of Milton hostage in the [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md) before it caught fire due to the adverse electrical effects of the [Aurora](./Aurora.md), inadvertently killing those inside.

[Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) tried to rescue the people trapped by the blaze, but Hobbs intervened, resulting in her stabbing him with a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) in self defense and Hobbs taking the remainder of her scarf before running away (and later using the scarf as a makeshift bandage). Hobbs may be directly responsible for the the cuts seen on Astrid's hand and wrist in Episode 3, which presumably occurred during this altercation, judging from his statement "We barely clipped her wings... well she was bleeding... a bit."

Badly wounded, he fled town and took refuge at [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md), taking the time to pilfer and break open a Lock Box belonging to [Martin Barker](./Martin%20Barker.md) full of cash from inside the house, despite his dying state.
#### Grey Mother thinks something happened at the tunnel leading out from Milton. Investigate.
#### Grey Mother thinks something happened at the tunnel leading out from Milton. Investigate.
His name (HOBBS, T.) first appears on the [Prison Transport Manifest](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md) near the Crashed Prison Bus, foreshadowing him as a character.
#### Something precious was stolen from Grey Mother. Find it, and return it to her.

When first entering the farmhouse, [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) finds Hobbs on the couch with a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) in his belly. Hobbs tells him what happened and asks for the knife to be removed: granting the choice of killing him by pushing the knife deeper, or saving his life by removing the knife.
WARNING: No matter what option is chosen you will not get to keep the knife, so adjust your choice accordingly.
After you make your choice, Mackenzie takes the [Bank Deposit Box Key 15](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2015.md) from the Lock Box and leaves the dwelling, and Hobbs is never seen again.

Based on the decision spare or kill Hobbs, [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) will have unique dialogue options later in Paradise Lost, giving a neutral warning to Mackenzie about "living by the sword" if he killed Hobbs or sounding relived but concerned that "this new world will grind his good nature to dust" if he spared the convict.
Hobbs appears in a voice over recap during the beginning of Episode 3, mentioning the Old Schoolhouse.
Hobbs once again appears in a voice over recap during the beginning of Episode 4, mentioning Blackrock Prison. ![Hobbs on the sofa](../assets/20181218201232_1.jpg)_Hobbs on the sofa_

- Removing the knife from Hobbs' wound is the 'humane' option in-game, but realistically this would likely be as bad, if not worse than pushing the blade deeper. Blood loss from such a wound would be sealed by the knife itself; removing the knife would expose the wound, likely causing extensive bleeding and risk of death if left untreated. Ironically, such an injury should be dealt with by a doctor such as Astrid, not Will.

- Hobbs' knife removal is similar to the start of Episode 1, where Will removes the [Scrap Metal Shard](./Scrap%20Metal%20Shard.md) from his hand. Being an extremity and not an abdomen wound, the bleeding would be more manageable.

- It is widely misunderstood that Hobbs and the other prisoners are arsonists, perpetuated by the fact that he initially takes credit for the deaths of Milton residents in the schoolhouse fire: "We sure warmed them up!". However, Hobbs later states, "We put them all in the old schoolhouse so we could keep an eye on them. And then something happened to the lights... the power... it was like sparks everywhere and then fire." This is consistent with the effects of the Aurora, which sometimes causes electrical fires, as evidenced in trailers showing burning power lines and various burned buildings throughout Great Bear that were never reached by the convicts.

**Home-made Soup** (sic) is a [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item found in [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).

Home-made Soup is a soup created by [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) as she shows her hospitality to [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md). Consuming Home-made Soup restores a moderate number of calories. It may also be warmed by a [Fire](./Fire.md) to grant the benefit [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md). It starts hot and does not begin cooling until first interacted with. This includes simply inspecting the item and leaving it by the fireplace without collecting it. Despite the contents of this food being a soup containing liquid, Home-made Soup does not provide any hydration to quench [Thirst](./Thirst.md).

The soup cannot be crafted, and is not available in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). The soup can be carried into [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), but will be lost if it is not consumed by the end of the episode.

Has an interior **Homesteader's Respite** is a small cabin located beside an old mining facility, near the eastern edge of [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), a short distance north of [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md), and just below [Fire Overlook](./Fire%20Overlook.md). The cabin is sitting on a ledge between two rope climbs.

To get the the cabin initially, players will have to first head to Fire Overlook and climb down the long rope. Once there, they can pick up a rope at the cabin, which can be deployed to provide easy access to the fishing hut at [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md).

It is possible to reach Homesteader's Respite from [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md) without a rope by walking up a nearby slope and [sticking to the cliff-face](./Mountain%20Goating.md), then dropping onto the ledge below. This path is the fastest for reaching Miner's Folly, however it clearly isn't a path Hinterland intended for players to take, and the steep angle may cause multiple sprains which will require treatment before climbing the long rope to [Fire Overlook](./Fire%20Overlook.md).

High-level clothes such as [Combat Pants](./Combat%20Pants.md) or [Cowichan Sweater](./Cowichan%20Sweater.md) as well as [research books](./Research%20Book.md), can be found inside, along with some foodstuffs. It is also a possible [Revolver](./Revolver.md) spawn. A [climbing rope](./Rope%20Climbing.md) might spawn on the mantlepiece, hanging on the wall, or below the table, which enables easier access to [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md) and its [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md). A coal bin can also be found behind the house.

No [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) is present near the cabin apart from a [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) nest on the south-east side, and, while the location does have a [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md) and a [Bed](./Bed.md), fuel is sparse on the ledge the cabin sits on. Therefore, firewood and other key resources such as food must be hauled up or down via the [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md). Overall, the cabin is alright for use as a safer longer-term [safe house](./Safehouse.md) than the nearby [Angler's Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md), but it is less central than the latter and doesn't have as many resources in the local area.

The Hopeless Rescue challenge requires the player to recover a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) from the [Summit](./Summit.md) of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md). The player must then hike down to [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) where they have to fire the Distress Pistol from the top of [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md).
The player has a time limit of seven days to complete the challenge, or else they will fail and be forced start over again.

Hopeless Rescue is set on Voyager difficulty, however hostile [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) will spawn immediately with no grace period. Prior knowledge of the regions the player must pass through is very beneficial.

The player starts in [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), fully rested with 2000 calories The player has a very basic starting kit (some medical supplies, poor quality clothes).

The player will pass through several [regions](./Region.md) and transition zones, including Mystery Lake, [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), Timberwolf Mountain, [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), and Desolation Point.
The time remaining is displayed in the upper right corner of the screen under the time of day.

The most critical aspect of completing Hopeless Rescue is to maximize the distance traveled between rest periods. Refilling the player's [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) when it is completely depleted will take half a day, so every time the player has to rest will consume valuable time. Therefore, traveling as far as possible between rest periods will decrease the amount of resting time required to complete the challenge.
There are several ways to maximize the distance traveled and minimize the amount of time spent resting:

- Keep carry weight as low as possible, ideally below the 15kg encumbrance weight that is imposed when the player is exhausted. The result is twofold, as it allows the player to travel faster and also slows fatigue.
- Do not dwell in the same area for very long. All of the items required to survive the seven days can be obtained quickly by looting buildings.
- There is no reason to [hunt](./Hunting.md), craft clothing or weapons, [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md), complete [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md), or do other time-consuming activities.

- Drink [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md). Coffee refills the fatigue bar slightly and reduces fatigue drain for a short period of time. Coffee can be used to the best effect prior to [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md). Coffee can be found in [Tin of Coffee](./Tin%20of%20Coffee.md), or inside microwaves.

- Finding [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) is a must, as it can help the player save time when faced with the multiple [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) sections of Timberwolf Mountain.

Because weight is a critical factor, the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) may not be the best choice if the player is aiming to complete the challenge in the shortest time possible. Avoiding hostile wildlife, effectively using [decoys](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys), and scaring animals away with [flares](./Flare.md) or [torches](./Torch.md) is the best way to stay safe, if a [Revolver](./Revolver.md)isn't accessible. New players, however, may find the hunting rifle to be necessary to complete the challenge, and be willing to sacrifice the weight.

Once the player has retrieved the distress pistol, which is found with a number of [flare shells](./Flare%20Shell.md) inside the [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md), the distress pistol can be used as a weapon to shoot hostile wildlife.

Tools have little usefulness in a short challenge like this one. A hatchet for [wolf](./Wolf.md) [struggles](./Struggle.md), and a [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md) or a hunting knife are about the only useful tools. Firewood can almost always be found near indoor locations or caves, eliminating the need to carry it in the inventory.

In general, during the challenge, the player needs to move quickly through the regions, which also means the player can quickly move between indoor locations to warm up. Good [Clothing](./Clothing.md) will result in the player needing to seek refuge from the cold less, but will also contribute significant weight.

The challenge is set to Voyager difficulty, which means that there is more than enough [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) to survive the seven days of the challenge. If the player loots as they travel, they may not need to carry more than one day's worth of food at any time, saving on weight. Once you get to the top of Timberwolf Mountain, with the amount of MRE's and potable water there (located in [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md), which require a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md)), you shouldn't have to search for food ever again.

It may be beneficial to intentionally let [Condition](./Condition.md) drain when the player is [freezing](./Warmth.md), [dehydrated](./Thirst.md), or [starved](./Hunger.md) if it enables the player to travel further before requiring a stop. For instance, it is not necessary to start a [Fire](./Fire.md) as soon as the player becomes freezing, and the player may be better off losing some condition and [Warming](./Warmth.md) up when they reach the next indoor location or cave.

![Hunger icon](../assets/Hunger_icon.png) **Hunger** is one of the four essential [Needs](./Needs.md). Hunger is a measure of how many calories the player consumes and expends. The player's hunger is restored by consuming calories, which come in the form of [Foods and Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md). The player will begin to lose [Condition](./Condition.md) when their hunger is completely depleted.

Hunger on the Survival Tab is represented twice. Graphically as a bar (like the other Needs) and also as 'Calorie Store', an exact quantity of internal calories. The two are directly linked and are not distinct variables. Maximum calories are 2500, minimum is 0, corresponding to a full and empty hunger bar respectively. Hunger is the inverse of what the hunger bar displays; the character is hungriest when the bar is depleted and least hungry when the bar is full. Above the bar is a descriptor that changes as the bar fills to describe the current state of hunger. Its five possible states are Starving ↔︎ Ravenous ↔︎ Hungry ↔︎ Peckish ↔︎ Full. A red outline of an empty stomach appears on the HUD when Ravenous or Starving.

The above table lists calorie burn rate in [Interloper](./Interloper.md) difficulty. Calories are burned more slowly in lower difficulties. Calories are burned constantly, at a rate dependent on activity level. Having zero calories (starving) does not prevent work from being done.

Eating is done through either the radial menu or the inventory page. All [Foods and Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) except [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) offer some calories when consumed. When consuming a food that would result in hunger being satisfied more than the limit of 2500 calories, that food will be only partially consumed. The remainder will stay in the inventory with appropriately reduced calorie and weight attributes. Eating can be manually interrupted by pressing the escape key.

When no more calories are in the calorie store, [Condition](./Condition.md) drains at a rate of 1% each hour. Dying of starvation will, therefore, take a little while, and will require four game days if starting from 100% condition. Living without eating food every day is a game strategy known as [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md).

![UI Long Hunger](../assets/UI_Long-Hunger.jpg) A player that remains starving for more than 24 hours will start to have their [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) affected; similar to [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md). The maximal amount of energy that the player will be able to acquire through sleep will start to decrease, which is represented by the red color that starts filling up the inside of the fatigue bar, as well as by the yellow exclamation mark that appears next to the fatigue bar. The maximum amount of fatigue that a player can have will decrease by 2% per hour, with a maximum decrease of 50%. Once the player has started eating, the fatigue cap will decrease by 5% per hour until it is fully removed. This issue is easily solved by consuming food, the red color won't vanish immediately, but the player will be allowed to gain full energy from sleep right away.

The blind is found on the north side of a small lake. There may be a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) inside the blind. A [Firestriker](./Firestriker.md) may spawn inside (even on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) difficulty). It can provide some safety when hunting the [Bear](./Bear.md) and [wolves](./Wolf.md) that wander around nearby, but caution is advised, for the predators can climb the stairs into the blind on occasion. A [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) is found just behind the Blind, and can be a great place for shelter if the weather turns bad.
The lake near the blind is considered deep water, so it is suitable for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) with Free Form holes.

**Hunter's blinds** are a type of small structure used for hunting. ![A Hunter's Blind near Hilltop Cave, Pleasant Valley.](../assets/Hunter%27s_Blind_Hilltop.jpg)_A Hunter's Blind near Hilltop Cave, Pleasant Valley._
Hunter's blinds are enclosed wooden platforms used as stations from which to hunt deer and other game.

They provide some shelter from wind while hunting, are elevated for easier sighting of prey, and used to be inaccessible to all [wildlife](./Wildlife.md). In recent updates, however, wildlife can (though not always reliably) climb up the stairs, somewhat limiting their usefulness.

Blinds may also contain a small amount of useful loot, such as [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), firewood, or even a [survival bow](./Survival%20Bow.md). Note that the player cannot make a fire inside a blind, so, in very cold weather when making a fire may be necessary, predators will be able to attack a player who exits the blind to build a fire. Additionally, the blind's wind protection will not apply to fires built outside the structure. Therefore, it is wise to ensure one is well-stocked with potable water and food and clothed in warm layers when planning on hunting from a blind. The blind also doesn't count as shelter if you are afflicted with the [cabin fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) debuff.
- Near [Abandoned Prepper's Cache](./Prepper%27s%20Abandoned%20Cache.md), in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).

- East of [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md). (Only accessible in the [Tales From the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.)

**Hunter's Revolver** is a unique variant of the [Revolver](./Revolver.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

The Hunter's Revolver is an artfully engraved and blued firearm with a distinct ivory grip featuring a diamond shaped insert. It has an extra long barrel enabling it to land hits from twice as far away, but the extra material makes it weigh 0.25 Kg more than the standard revolver.
Instead of rear iron sights, the hunters revolver has a front sight post on the back which can make aiming a challenge.

The range increase is applied to a ray-trace fired from the center of the screen when a shot is fired, normally the standard Revolver's ray-trace range is about 30 meters long, but the Hunter's Revolver's is 60 meters long. Past this range the weapon will be unable to damage any [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md).

The Hunter's Revolver can be found in [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md), specifically the hunting Cache containing many animal furs. Prepper Caches can spawn in several different regions and will only spawn once per region.

The **Hunting Knife** is a tool in _The Long Dark_ for butchering, crafting and self defense.

The Hunting Knife has a number of uses: self-defense, harvesting gut, hide and meat from [animal](./Wildlife.md) carcasses, as well as [cloth](./Cloth.md) and [Tinder Plugs](./Tinder%20Plug.md). It's used as a tool for [Crafting](./Crafting.md) varied equipment. It may also serve as a makeshift [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md) to avoid spillage, or to break through iced-over fishing holes for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md).
- May be used to [harvest frozen carcasses](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) (Knives have faster unfrozen meat, gut and hide harvesting speeds. Hatchets are only faster at harvesting frozen meat)
- Crafting [Survival Bows](./Survival%20Bow.md), [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) and [Arrow Shafts](./Arrow%20Shaft.md).

- Crafting animal hide clothing/tools: [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md), [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md), [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md), [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md), [Moose-Hide Cloak](./Moose-Hide%20Cloak.md), [Travois](./Travois.md) and [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md).
- Open or maintain holes in the ice for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) (Bladed tools break ice faster, but take more condition loss when doing so).
- Harvesting textiles ([Curtains](./Curtain.md), [Old Bedrolls](./Old%20Bedroll.md), [Pillows](./Pillow.md) or [Towels](./Towel.md)) for [Cloth](./Cloth.md).

When carried and selected for self-defense at the start of a Wolf Struggle, Hunting Knives deal medium damage with a low chance per-hit to cause the wolf to flee, and a high chance to inflict puncture wounds, a fast form of [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) (which is lethal to the Wolf over time). Hunting Knives are as effective at filling the Struggle Meter as [Prybar](./Prybar.md), and slightly more effective than [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) at ending struggles in this way, especially on difficulty modes other than [Interloper](./Survival%20Mode.md). Hunting Knives take low damage from being used in a struggle. For more information on Struggles, see: [Wildlife Struggles](./Struggle.md).
Hunting Knives may be found in all regions, usually near frozen corpses or structures. They may also be found inside structures atop/beneath furniture or in drawers.
In Interloper mode hunting knives will never spawn; requiring forging to create an [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md).

The hunting knife can be repaired using a [whetstone](./Whetstone.md) and the [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) skill, restoring 3% condition to the hunting knife and for 5% condition damage to the whetstone.

The [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) or [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) may repair a non-ruined hunting knife to 100% condition for one [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md). N.B. The knife has a breaking threshold at 15% condition, usage below this number risks ruining it for good.

- [Version 0.136](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.136) on 2 October 2014 introduced the ability to harvest using the hunting knife and [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), among other changes.

The **Hunting Lodge Rifle** is the unofficial name given to a [Tool](./Tools.md) simply named **Hunting Rifle** that was found in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story mode as part of the mission \[[https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/You%20Fix%20My%20Rifle](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/You%20Fix%20My%20Rifle)? You Fix My Rifle?\]. It is considered [Cut/Discontinued Content](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md), as it did not survive the transition from Predux Episode 2 to Redux Episode 2, as the item located where the Hunting Lodge Rifle was found would be replaced by the [Broken Bear Spear](./Broken%20Bear%20Spear.md).

It serves as a reskinned version of the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), with a silver engraving of 2 [Deer](./Deer.md), 2 wraps of tape at the end of the barrel, and a large wrap of tape on the stock. It was obtained when exploring the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md), just above the [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md) of the first floor. [Jeremiah's Repaired Rifle](./Jeremiah%27s%20Repaired%20Rifle.md) would later be returned to [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) and [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) would keep the Hunting Lodge Rifle as his own Hunting Rifle for the rest of the episode.

The Hunting Lodge Rifle's design changes to a regular Hunting Rifle when the cutscene of Mackenzie finding it plays, as well as any other cutscene with Mackenzie holding the rifle. It also takes the appearance a regular Hunting Rifle in first person.
Only the backpack icon, the 3D model in the menu, and placing the rifle on the ground shows the unique design.

Many features of the Hunting Lodge Rifle would later be recycled into the [Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md) (silver engravings became gold engravings) and [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md) (tape around the barrel and stock).

The lodge is a large building with both a ground floor, a loft, and a basement. It's a possible spawn for the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and usually has some [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) lying around. Provided you have the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC, the recipe card for [Breyerhouse Pie](./Breyerhouse%20Pie.md) can be found inside in several locations,

When entering from the north, players will come across a table and chairs. To the left there's a [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md), along with a [Stove](./Stove.md) and kitchen area, which usually contains some food and drink. A [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md) may spawn in the kitchen area. The [Breyerhouse Pie](./Breyerhouse%20Pie.md) [recipe card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) may be found on a table across from the stove.

Besides the chairs, there's a lot of [Planks](./Planks.md) that can be broken down for [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md). In Wintermute, the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) spawns atop the mantlepiece on the fireplace, while in Survival Mode, a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) may spawn on the rifle rack.

Going up the stairs leads to a loft, which features three bedrooms and a storage room. Two of the bedrooms feature useable [beds](./Bed.md), along with a few containers which may contain various clothing. A [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) can spawn behind the wardrobe in the bedroom with the trunk in Survival Mode, and various boxes of ammunition are scattered in various corners of the loft. In addition, a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) can be found stashed in one of the bedrooms.
The [Breyerhouse Pie](./Breyerhouse%20Pie.md) [recipe card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) may be found between the mattresses in the room opposite of the bathroom.

Entering the basement, there are a bunch of shelves which may contain random items, along with [metal](./Metal%20Container.md) and [plastic](./Plastic%20Container.md) containers. The most useful item found in the basement is the [Workbench](./Work%20Bench.md). A [Revolver](./Revolver.md) can possibly spawn on one of the unusable bunk beds.

As of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) update, the basement also spawns a [Vegetable Rack](./Vegetable%20Rack.md) near the wood box. A [Bag of Salt](./Salt%20%28Bag%29.md) can be found beside the Vegetable Rack. The [Breyerhouse Pie](./Breyerhouse%20Pie.md) [recipe card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) may be found on top of the vegetable rack.

A [Truck](./Truck.md) and a [Car](./Car.md) sit to the right of the lodge. Behind the lodge is a small shed and some picnic tables. There is also a cliff behind the lodge with a rock to deploy a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md). There is a cave in the cliff below the lodge, which is home to a [Bear](./Bear.md). The path to the lodge leads past a small pond, which is too shallow for fishing. Rabbits, reishi mushrooms, and cattails all can be found there. Be cautious as well, as there is a chance for a [Wolf](./Wolf.md) pack and/or a [Moose](./Moose.md) making it dangerous but having good hunting opportunities.

The Hunting Lodge can be used as a potential [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) when exploring Broken Railroad, as it is very spacious and has lots of game surrounding it, along with easy access to the [forge](./Forge.md) nearby. Predators can be a bit of a challenge when entering/exiting, however, the largest issue may be the lodge's isolation relative to much of Broken Railroad, and the remainder of Great Bear in general. It can still make for a decent stopover point for players who are coming or going from the [Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md).
Before the lights in the sky, the lodge was being used as the base of operations for the remaining [Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md).

When entering for the basement in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), the [Phone Box](./Phone%20Box.md) will ring. This is likely because it is part of the party line that Molly is using to speak to Astrid. Unfortunately it cannot be interacted with once the door is opened, as the ringing stops.

The fact that a car and truck are present at the Lodge makes no logical sense, as the bridge leading up to the Lodge has a gate and there is no road leading from the Maintenance Yard to the Lodge. Furthermore, there are no roads leading into the region aside from the railroad that would not even support railless vehicles. This is an oversight from the developers.
