> “**An old .303 calibre bolt-action hunting rifle. Will bring a deer down. Maybe a wolf.**”

_This article is about the normal hunting rifle. For variants, see [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md), [Barb's Rifle](./Barb%27s%20Rifle.md), [Bunker Rifle](./Bunker%20Rifle.md), or [Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md)._

The **Hunting Rifle** is a bolt-action weapon with an internal magazine capacity of 10 rounds that can be used to scare away or kill [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md). When hitting a target, it provides experience in the [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) skill.

The hunting rifle is the first firearm to be added to the game and one of three a player may find throughout the regions of Great Bear Island. It is the heaviest ranged weapon a player can have in their inventory. The rifle can inflict a critical hit to targets, and cartridges are lighter than [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md). The rifle's condition will degrade after a shot, requiring regular Cleaning.

A rifle can be loaded with 10 rounds of [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md). 5 rounds can be loaded at once with stripper clips, but rounds will be loaded individually if there are 6 or more rounds in the magazine already or if the player does not have 5 or more rounds on them. Loading will continue until interrupted by clicking or canceling, or the magazine is fully loaded.

Firing a rifle will automatically expend a [Rifle Shell Casing](./Rifle%20Shell%20Casing.md) out of the ejection port and onto the ground as a new round is cycled into the chamber, and can be picked up.

Depending on the player's rifle skill and condition, when aimed, the rifle will sway or shudder slightly, affecting the player's ability to aim. The sway increases if the player's [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) is low. The player will also begin to shiver when freezing, making aiming even more difficult.

Although the rifle does not have a scope, aiming at a point will cause the player's view to zoom in towards said point, effectively allowing the rifle to be used as a weak optic. The same can be done with the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) and the [Woodright's Bow](./Woodwright%27s%20Bow.md).

The rifle will begin jamming under the 50% condition threshold, then it has the chance to improperly load the next cartridge. Attempting to fire will result in a misfire. To clear the jam, the bolt must be cycled again manually by pressing the reload button/key. Doing so will eject the unspent cartridge onto the ground near the player, from where it can be picked up and used again. Unloading and reloading the rifle in the player's inventory will also clear the jam, but without dropping any ammo.
Low quality Ammunition created from [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) can also cause a misfire, even if the gun is in relatively good condition.
Hunting Rifles can be cleaned with a [Firearm Cleaning Kit](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md) to prevent jamming and improve accuracy.

Cleaning a rifle consumes 5% condition from the rifle cleaning kit and restores some condition to the hunting rifle, based on the player's skill level. Each rifle cleaning kit can be used up to 20 times for repairing hunting rifles.

The player may use a [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) with one [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md) to repair the rifle by 40% condition (Increased by [Gunsmithing Skill](./Gunsmithing.md)). The milling machine can also repair completely ruined rifles for the cost of 5 scrap metal, 1 fir firewood, and 4 hours of time.

In **[Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md)**, the Hunting Rifle degrades **1.325%** for each shot taken. When the rifle is at full condition, 75 shots can be taken before it degrades to broken. The Hunting Rifle can be cleaned to restore condition and increase the number of total shots that can be taken.

If the player obtains a level 5 Rifle Firearm skill, the Hunting Rifle degrades **0.6625%**for each shot taken. When the rifle is at full condition, 150 shots can be taken before it degrades to broken.

In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), the Hunting Rifle degrades **0.6625%**for each shot taken. When the rifle is at full condition, 150 shots can be taken before it degrades to broken. The Hunting Rifle can be cleaned to restore condition and increase the number of total shots that can be taken.
The player cannot increase or decrease the degradation rate of the Hunting Rifle in Story mode, as there are no skills in Wintermute.
The Hunting Rifle has 3 variants, each having distinct differences from the base hunting rifle. These variants each spawn once per game, and they can be viewed in more detail below:
- [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md) - Lighter and faster, but breaks quickly (though slower than bunker rifle)
- [Hunting Lodge Rifle](./Hunting%20Lodge%20Rifle.md) - A cut reskin of the Hunting Rifle

The rounds fired from the Hunting Rifle move at a high velocity, and travel in a straight line. Upon hitting a target, they can cause massive internal injuries, potentially killing animals instantly. If the round fails to cause internal injuries sufficient enough to kill instantly, the round will still result a bleeding wound that will kill the animal eventually.
The rifle has a maximum range of approximately 50 paces. Targets beyond the maximum range cannot be hit. Hitting a fleshy target will produce a blood spray effect.
Bears, Deer and Wolves have hit spots with a bleed out time. Moose and Cougar do not bleed. Rabbits and Ptarmigan die instantly.

As with other loot items, the hunting rifle will randomly spawn in different locations on different play-throughs and difficulties, although a few maps have a guaranteed rifle spawn separate from the random spawn. Each major map used to be guaranteed to have at least one rifle spawn in it (until the Tales from the Far Territory update), except on Interloper where none will spawn.

No Hunting Rifle spawns here, but if [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) is installed, the [Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md) is guaranteed to spawn in one of the following places:
- Next to a corpse on the ledge along the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md) path near [Wolf's Jaw Overlook](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md).
- Next to a corpse by the tree at [Wolf's Jaw Overlook](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md) near the rose hip climb.
- In the cave with the bed at the top of the [Runaway Bridge](./Runaway%20Bridge.md) plateau across the fallen tree.
- Inside a [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) near [Cook's Farm](./Cook%27s%20Farm.md) (dlc-only).
- Inside a [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) south of the [Lower Raven Falls](./Lower%20Raven%20Falls.md) cabin (dlc-only).
- [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md): upstairs in one of the bedrooms, on the gun rack above the fireplace, in an old washing tub in the basement. This rifle is guaranteed.
- [Jackrabbit Island](./Jackrabbit%20Island.md): Inside house, beside wardrobe in bedroom.
- [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md): in one of the side passages, next to a corpse.
- Inside a [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) at [Bear Creek Campground](./Bear%20Creek%20Campground.md) (dlc-only).
If [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) is installed, [Barb's Rifle](./Barb%27s%20Rifle.md) is guaranteed to spawn once in the region:
- In one of the many [Fishing Huts](./Fishing%20Hut.md) leaning against the wall next to the stove.
- Inside a [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) west of the [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md) (dlc-only).
- Inside a [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) at [Marsh Ridge](./Marsh%20Ridge.md) (dlc-only).
- Inside a [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) on [Drift Island](./Drift%20Island.md) (dlc-only).
- On the path behind the waterfall, next to the northernmost [Ice Cave](./Ice%20Cave.md) entrance near [Mammoth Falls](./Mammoth%20Falls.md).
- On the path leading from the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) entrance to the nearest bear den, next to a corpse.
- Between rope climbs at [Pensive Vista](./Pensive%20Vista.md), near the [Memento](./Mementos.md) note.
- On the gun rack in [Trapper's Cabin](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md), above the safe.
- Inside a [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) near the [Unnamed Pond](./Unnamed%20Pond.md) cabin (dlc-only).

- Inside the Hydroelectric Dam, on the catwalk in the huge room with the mountaineering rope, in the furthest corner from the rope, leaned up against a console behind a chair. It may be hard to spot without a light source and from certain angles. (Confirmed April 2, 2025, WITHOUT DLC. Please verify with DLC installed.)
- Inside the Lower Dam, in the far corner of the room with a computer, leaning on a barrel. (Confirmed with no DLC)

If [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) is installed, [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md) is guaranteed to spawn either here or in [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md):
- Inside [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) at one of several potential spawn locations;
- In the broken window room coming in from Winding River in the lower dam, (in a corner to the left when entering near a metal table)
- Near fallen tree bridge leading to [Burned Ridge Cave](./Burned%20Ridge%20Cave.md), next to a corpse.
- In the destroyed barn between [Heartbreak Bridge](./Heartbreak%20Bridge.md) and [Long Falls](./Long%20Falls.md).
- [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) near [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) entrance (dlc-only).
- At the [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md): in the radar building, in the garage, in the truck. This rifle is guaranteed to spawn (dlc-only).
- Inside one of the [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md) [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md). Hacksaw required. This rifle is guaranteed to spawn.

No normal Hunting Rifle will spawn here. If [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) is installed, [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md) is guaranteed to spawn either here or in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md):
- Inside the pipes at on the dam platform near the exit door to the dam in. It may be behind pallets that need to be broken down.
- Locked inside the mine office in the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), unlocked with the [Mine Office Key](./Mine%20Office%20Key.md). This rifle is guaranteed to spawn (dlc-only).
- Guaranteed spawn in the left branch of the cave linking the plateau on which the [Desecrated Church](./Desecrated%20Church.md) is located to the main part of the region.
- A rifle is used by the [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md), but none can be obtained in this Episode.
- A rifle is given to you by [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) at the beginning of the episode.
- Rifles can be found to fight off Timberwolves, but care should be taken when returning to the prison, as the Convicts will confiscate it if it is not stored when meeting with them.
- Bullets have higher critical hit chance (instant kills) than arrows especially when hitting an animal's head or neck.
- Rifles and other weapons are dropped during a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) with big game ([Bear](./Bear.md), [Moose](./Moose.md) and [Cougar](./Cougar.md)).
- The rifle is inspired by the Lee-Enfield bolt action rifle which was Britain's standard issue rifle until the 1960s [^1] and used by the Canadian Rangers until 2015.
- Rifle jamming in-game depicts a "rim-lock", which is when the rim on two cartridges snag and cause loading problems.
- Shooting a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) or [Spray Paint](./Spray%20Paint.md) will cause the cans to fly through the air a moderate distance.

J - Trick is to spot your target, get as close as you can, take a shot, and don't miss.
> — [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) and [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) discussing Hunting

**Hunting** [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) is the process of searching for, stalking, and killing animals to harvest their flesh/hides and acquire [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) or crafting materials in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Hunting in _The Long Dark_ has been greatly simplified by keeping the animals conspicuous. Very little tracking needs to be done to find animals. Furthermore, while the player can see them from a great distance, all animals seem oblivious to anything farther than 30 meters away. Approaching them is rather easy, especially if one is crouching and not carrying any raw meat, which makes the player "visible" from further away. On top of that, certain [Skills](./Skills.md) can increase the damage output of their respective Weapons.

Large animals ([Deer](./Deer.md), [Cougar](./Cougar.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), [Wolf](./Wolf.md), [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), [Bear](./Bear.md), [Moose](./Moose.md)) have 5 areas of their bodies that calculate damage; Head, Neck, Torso, Hips, Limbs. Critical hits responsible for one-hit kills are a mechanic available on every large animal (the small animals are always one-hit kills).

Unlike actual hunting, aiming for the Torso will often not instantly kill targets, such as aiming for the heart. Shooting limbs does not cripple the mobility of the animal, and they will continue moving at their normal speed. Headshots are the most effective method to kill an animal in one hit, but bleeding will always begin once an animal is struck by an weapon projectile (except for the Moose and Cougar) regardless of where they are hit. Bleeding almost always leads to the eventual death of the animal (exception made for some buggy behaviours on the game's part).

Smaller animals like [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) die instantly when hit with any large projectile, regardless of where the shot lands. [Crows](./Crow.md) cannot be harmed in any way, due to a lack of collision/hitboxes. Fish cannot be shot under the ice, and only appear as items when [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md).
Weapons are defined as [Tools](./Tools.md) that are capable of damaging Wildlife. These items also have their own dedicated space in the Weapons section of the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md).

Shooting animals with projectiles is the most effective way to kill game while completely bypassing the animals' natural defences. Bullets and arrows move too quickly to be blocked or dodged and can be fired from outside the animal's zone of perception. The Cougar is the only exception since, whether intended or not by the developers, its animation cycle includes a choppy weaving and bobbing pattern that allows them to dodge arrows milliseconds before they hit.

Five ranged weapons currently exist in the game: [Stone](./Stone.md), the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), the [Revolver](./Revolver.md), and the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md). The Hunting Rifle, Survival Bow and the Revolver all have available weapon variants that have different weight, condition loss, damage output, swaying or stamina loss. Other Tools that can damage wildlife include the [Noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md) and tools normally used for [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) or [Crafting](./Crafting.md) that can be used in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md).

![Rifle sights](../assets/Rifle_sighted.png)_Rifle sights_The [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) is an offensive tool used to fire [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) at targets. The high velocity rounds travel in a straight line and cause massive internal injuries to the first object they encounter, potentially killing animals instantly if aimed at the head. If the round fails to cause internal injuries sufficient enough to kill instantly, the round will still result in a bleeding wound that will kill the animal eventually, just more slowly. Expended rounds will be dropped next to the player as [Rifle Shell Casings](./Rifle%20Shell%20Casing.md) which can be picked up and used to craft new Rifle Ammunition at an Ammunition Workbench (found exclusively at [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) and the [Blackrock Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) workshop in [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md)). In Survival Mode, the effectiveness of a Hunting Rifle is improved by increasing the [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) skill.
- Hitting a solid target will produce a smoke effect often accompanied with a "clank" sound.
- Hitting most environmental targets will produce a snow scatter effect or wood splinter effect.

The [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) is a craftable tool used to launch [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md), [Manufactured Arrows](./Manufactured%20Arrow.md) or [Fire Hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) at targets. Its variants ([Woodwright's Bow](./Woodwright%27s%20Bow.md) and [Sport Bow](./Sport%20Bow.md)) cannot be crafted but function the same as an ordinal Survival Bow. Simple Arrows are the only craftable arrow type that can take down Large Animals. Manufactured Arrows deal a lot more damage than Simple Arrows but cannot be crafted and have to be traded with the Trader. They also cannot be harvested for parts used to craft more arrows; once they reach 0% condition and break, the Broken Manufactured Arrows that takes their place is useless. Fire Hardened Arrows are also craftable and useful for killing Rabbits and Ptarmigan, but cannot be used to kill larger animals (they will scare them away if fired at them).

Arrows travel in an arc, so aiming needs to take into account how far away the target is. Arrows can kill animals instantly, but more commonly cause massive bleeding wounds that will drain their health quickly. Arrows are retrievable, however they do take damage each time they hit anything (even missed shots that land in the snow, trees or hit the ice will degrade arrows, with different condition loss amounts for different materials hit):
- Reaching 0% quality breaks the arrow. Aiming at hard targets up close (solid rock, trees, concrete, floors of buildings) will instantly break or severely damage arrows.

- [Broken Arrows](./Broken%20Arrow.md), Broken Manufactured Arrows and [Broken Fire Hardened Arrows](./Broken%20Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) do not stick to targets, falling instead to the ground where they hit.

- Sighting the bow is a challenge for new players. No hard sight exists, rather one must estimate. The best references for aiming are the arrow tip for elevation and the bottom of the bow for horizontal alignment. This requires a lot of practice and can be done on small game with Fire Hardened Arrows to not damage the more precious arrow types. There are also Archery targets behind the Barn at [Pleasant Valley Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md).

- Arrows that are stuck in the side of the animal may come loose when they die, and you will find them lying next to them. Arrows are notoriously buggy and will frequently be found floating around the animals, both when they're alive and fleeing and when they drop as a carcass. They can be picked up even when floating in the air around the carcass, but clicking on the carcass will automatically harvest all the arrows and put them in your inventory (there is a known bug where harvesting your Manufactured Arrows using this method will give you the pick-up notification for Simple Arrows instead. Only the notification is bugged, this will still give you your Manufactured Arrows back).
In Survival Mode, the effectiveness of the bow, its swaying and the ability to crouch while aiming are improved by increasing the [Archery](./Archery.md) skill.

A handgun that is much lighter than the Hunting Rifle, but its ammunition is much smaller and is useful for more defensive situations, a [Revolver](./Revolver.md) and its variants ([Forester's Revolver](./Forester%27s%20Revolver.md), [Hunter's Revolver](./Hunter%27s%20Revolver.md), [Warden's Revolver](./Warden%27s%20Revolver.md)) can be used to hunt if desperate enough. While [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md) is abundant, the Revolver has a much smaller chance to instantly kill wildlife compared to the rifle or bow, regardless of the [Revolver Firearm](./Revolver%20Firearm.md) skill level. That said, even a single wound dealt by the revolver will still cause animals to bleed out, but over a longer period of time compared to rifle rounds or arrows. Even head shots do not guarantee a kill when hunting deer and wolves with the Revolver. Using the Revolver as a hunting tool requires patience and tracking.

Killing smaller animals like Rabbits and Ptarmigan can be much easier (albeit a wasteful use of ammunition) due to the fast firing rate. Entire flocks of Ptarmigan can be hunted with good reflexes and aim due to the quick cycling rate of a Revolver compared to a Hunting Rifle however.

A basic tool that can be found lying around outdoors and in caves, [Stones](./Stone.md) are useful early game tools used to hunt small game, and can be used even in late game to preserve Ammunition for projectile weapons. Its utility for hunting is somewhat limited, however Stones are able to temporarily stun [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) if the Stone hits their body. The player must then quickly run up and grab the stunned animal where they are given a choice to either release or break its neck. Ptarmigan that are hunted unsuccessfully with Stones will always flee the area and not return for 1-4 days, whereas Rabbits will slowly return to their designated spots after being frightened away.

Stones are unable to injure larger game, but still have some use to alter their behavior. Stones that hit Wolves in the face have a chance to cause the Wolf to flee, while leaving a single blood stain in the snow (This will not be enough to cause extensive bleedout however, even if done repeatedly). Predators will investigate a thrown stone that lands near them, while prey animals will flee. Hunters can use these behaviors to their advantage to distract predators or scare prey into Wolves.

The lack of proper sights and the low arc of shots fired from this weapon make it a relatively poor choice for a hunting tool. However, if a [Flare Shell](./Flare%20Shell.md) fired from it manages to connect with target wildlife, it will cause wounds that bleed out quickly.

- Because wildlife will always flee from Distress Pistol shots, this makes it a fairly safe choice for hunting dangerous wildlife. Allowing an animal to charge the player and firing right in its face can greatly increase the chance of a successful hit. This is a surprisingly effective method for hunting bears, which provide a large target and suffer from bleeding wounds.

- The greatest disadvantage to using the Distress Pistol is the general rareness of the weapon and its ammunition. Also, the Pistol itself cannot be repaired and Flare Shells are the only projectile that cannot be harvested or crafted.

An improvised explosive primarily designed to scare hostile wildlife away, [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md) make for a very impractical weapon to hunt with (aside from destroying [Cougar](./Cougar.md) dens).
- Noisemakers will instantly kill small animals like Rabbits and Ptarmigans (even killing a whole Ptarmigan flock if thrown at the right time).
- They do not cause bleedout to large animals, but merely deal a flat damage value instead.
- Larger animals will most likely run away in fear of the explosion, making it harder to chase them down and continue throwing Noisemakers to kill them.

- Using Noisemakers can put the user at risk for [Burns](./Burns.md) and [Condition](./Condition.md) damage if they do not throw the bomb at the right time, or if they throw them while wildlife is too close.

- Noisemakers are hard to produce, with the resources needed to make [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md) being uncommon and the [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) table being so rare, resulting in a very resource intensive and expensive weapon that often causes more destruction to the user than to would be quarry.

A very dangerous method that can be used to exclusively hunt Wolves is to allow yourself to be attacked by a Wolf (start a [Struggle](./Struggle.md)) and to use a weapon that can Puncture the beast in order for it to slowly Bleed Out. When a Struggle begins, many Tools normally used for [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) or other uses can be used to damage a Wolf as the Struggle is ongoing. Be aware that using Struggles to hunt carries a high risk of Death and Afflictions, including [Torn Clothing](./Torn%20Clothing.md), [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md), [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md), [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md), [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md), [Pain](./Pain.md), and loss of Condition. Higher difficulties will almost certainly result in the player dying from MASSIVE Condition loss by using this method if their Condition is below 80% when a Struggle begins. Using this method also degrades Tool Condition.
Weapon damage is divided into 5 categories: Desperation, Puncture, Slash, Scare, and Strike:
- Desperation is the default method of attacking a Wolf without tools, and does very poor damage per second, often resulting in the player's death.
- Puncture can be used almost exclusively to cause a Wolf to bleed out after the Struggle is successful, albeit causing the Struggle to last longer.
- Scare does less damage to the Wolf, but has a high chance of causing it to flee faster.

- Strike is when the survivor uses the barrel of a Revolver to strike the Wolf. Eventually, they get their hand on the trigger and the "Take Shot" option appears to shoot the Wolf. This can result in two outcomes: it instantly kills the Wolf or just scares it off while causing it to bleed.

Knives with the Puncture type will lead a Wolf to bleed after the Struggle, cause it to constantly flee and run around until its movements slows down, eventually causing it to die. The Heavy Hammer and the Cougar Claw Knife in particular are well known for causing high amounts of damage, usually killing the Wolf during the Struggle before the bar is full. Revolvers can either kill or scare the Wolf off of you, but are more unreliable methods of killing a Wolf during a Struggle. Other tools generally do not hurt Wolves as badly as Knives and the Heavy Hammer (affectionately nicknamed "Wolf Bonker" by players).
[Trapping](./Trapping.md) is a passive form of Hunting that involves placing traps to catch small animals. Trapping has its own dedicated page for how to use Snares and Fishing Tip-Ups.

The ordinarily dangerous [Wolf](./Wolf.md) can be used to hunt Prey animals for you with enough cunning and planning. Scaring Prey Wildlife into running into the direction of a nearby Wolf will cause the Wolf to stalk and charge the Prey animal. If prey is far away the wolf could be guided towards the prey by grabbing its attention and walking it towards the area of the prey, then crouching. Once the Wolf catches up, the Prey animal instantly dies and the Wolf will begin feeding on it. From here, coming close and aiming a weapon (Stone, Rifle, Revolver, etc) will cause the Wolf to flee, allowing the Carcass to be Harvested. Some meat will be consumed by the Wolf during the process, with more meat being lost the longer you wait to scare the Wolf off of the Carcass.

This tactic can also be used as a distraction when walking through a dangerous area, as Wolves will ignore you and instead hunt Prey animals you lure to them. Be aware that this will only works if there are enough Prey animals per Wolf, as larger Wolf packs will individually attack a Prey animal, while the rest follow you. Note that intact [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) packs ignore any Prey they catch once they gain sight of you, and will begin a pack attack.
Some animals run, others are attracted to you. Various methods exist for approaching each type of intended game. See the specific animal pages for preferred methods to hunt each.

Crouching allows the player to move more quietly and less visibly, decreasing the animal's ability to detect them. Remaining still while crouching further reduces detection, allowing a player to get very close to intended game.

- Only firearms and stones can be used from the crouching position without Survival Skill Bonuses. To shoot the bow while crouching, you must have a Survival Skill level of 5 in Archery. To attain level 5 Archery, you must reach 150 points. Archery points are increased by scoring a hit on an animal or by crafting arrows.
- Without being Level 5 in Archery, you must first stand up to draw and loose the arrow - potentially alerting your prey and necessitating a rushing of the aiming process.
> “**When using a Rifle, a Revolver, or a Distress Pistol, cold temperatures can cause Shivering, affecting your aim.**”

Most weapons cannot be used unless the player aims down sights. Aiming uses [Stamina](./Stamina.md) and displays an aiming meter in the bottom right corner. The lower the survivor's [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), the less time the player has to aim their weapon. If the player's [Warmth](./Warmth.md) reaches 0, the survivor will begin to shiver uncontrollably, and this will negatively effect the player's aim. Raising Warmth to above 0 will remove the shivering effect.

Predators may decide to pursue a player that intends to hunt them. This trait can be used against them, to lure them into traps and ambushes or draw them close for an easy kill. Carrying items that give off [Scent](./Scent.md) will draw predators to the player. By manipulating scent while crouching, it is possible to line up ideal shots, while the tracking animal remains oblivious. Predators can also be moved into a better position by throwing stones, which they will investigate if they can't see the player.

If the predator begins its charge, it will quickly be on top of the player unless they have taken steps to prevent it, or they get one powerful shot properly connected with this rapidly moving target. Bait can be used to escape predators before they charge, but afterward there are fewer options. Predators will never directly cross a [Campfire](./Campfire.md) and will usually be kept at bay if one is between them and the player. The will also turn and flee if they can't find a path to the player (e.g. the player has climbed a narrow tree limb or ledge).

Be aware that [bears](./Bear.md) may withstand more than one bullet/arrow that hits their head, while [wolves](./Wolf.md) and [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) drop dead instantly, if a head shot is scored.

[Moose](./Moose.md) behave more defensively and will not stalk players, but they are incredibly territorial and aggressive. They can survive more than one shot to the head, and will not bleed out, requiring multiple rounds from any weapon.

As mentioned before, [Baiting](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys) can be used to escape predators before they charge, but it can also be used to draw predators to your location. Raw meat and fish is always the best item to use for Baiting, as Cooked meat gives off less odor. Bears in particular will travel the entire lengths of the map to your location (even leaving their normal dedicated stomping grounds to investigate the smell) if a sufficient quantity of "Decoys" are dropped onto the ground or the player's [Scent](./Scent.md) is at maximum. This can be a very time consuming venture to wait for a bear to come for you however, given the very slow walking speed of a bear.

Wolves on the other hand will very quickly detect the player with high enough Scent or if Decoys are placed nearby, picking up speed and switching into their "investigating" behavior, luring them straight towards you. Prey Wildlife is always uninterested in Baiting tactics however.

It is possible to kill any animal with one shot, a mechanic called a "Critical Hit". Critical hits are random occurrences, and are more likely in an animal's designated critical areas. Hitting an animal but not immediately killing it still means that animal has a bleeding wound. A bleeding animal will always die if given enough time for its wound to finish bleeding.

Animals have five core hitbox areas, the head, neck, the front shoulder and chest, the hindquarters, and their legs. Shots to the head and neck have the best chance to cause a critical hit, with shots to the front shoulder and chest being second. Shots to the feet seem to be immune to critical hits.
| Weapon — Head | Weapon — Neck | Critical Hit Chance — Torso | Critical Hit Chance — Hips | Critical Hit Chance — Limb | Critical Hit Chance | Critical Hit Chance |
| [Hunting Rifle icon](../assets/Hunting_Rifle_icon.png) | [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) | Guaranteed | Guaranteed | 33% | 10% | 10% |
| [Distress Pistol icon](../assets/Distress_Pistol_icon.png) | [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) | Guaranteed | Guaranteed | 33% | 10% | 10% |
| [Survival Bow icon](../assets/Survival_Bow_icon.png) | [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) | Guaranteed | Guaranteed | 33% | 10% | 10% |
| [Revolver icon](../assets/Revolver_icon.png) | [Revolver](./Revolver.md) | 40% | 20% | 15% | 5% | 5% |

Shots that only catch the very outside of an animals silhouette may only graze its skin. Such grazing shots will produce a blood spatter on impact and an audible body hit, but seemingly do not injure the animal at all, there will be no blood on the ground at the point of impact and no blood trail. Additionally, bouncing an arrow off terrain that then hits an animal may produce the body hit noise, but again, the animal feels no effect.

![Blood trail](../assets/There_will_be_blood.png)_Blood trail_ Other than grazing shots, all hits will cause bleeding wounds that will eventually kill the animal ([moose](./Moose.md) and [cougar](./Cougar.md) excluded). Animals will bleed out according to which area they were shot in last. Bleeding wounds do not stack, meaning that multiple shots to the same area will not reduce bleed-out time. However, shooting an animal in an area of higher blood loss will override a previous shot in a lower blood loss area. The reverse is also true, making it unnecessary to fire at a fleeing animal that has a head wound since it has the fastest bleed out time. [Moose](./Moose.md) and [Cougar](./Cougar.md) do not bleed out and may require multiple shots to kill them.

The bleed-out timers above elapse even while performing time-accelerated activities. This means that after wounding an animal, you can simply use 'Pass time' via the 'Campcraft' menu to accelerate its death relative to real time, but the animal will also move at an accelerated speed.

![Tracking wounded wolf](../assets/Tracking_wounded_wolf.jpg)Tracking is fairly straightforward when the animal chooses to run away. Blood drops will fall along its path for you to follow. The wounded animal is also still quite obvious against its background of snow. And animals tend to run in straight lines unless they are blocked. So following them visually is fairly easy, too. Sprinting can keep pace with all but the bear. Use your limited speed boost to keep your quarry in sight. Also when wounded, bears may charge back at you randomly, making tracking difficult sometimes.

Blood trails are temporary and will fade. Snow and wind increase the rate of fade. Fading trails may seem to disappear as the spot in front of you vanishes then you turn around and there are no longer any spots behind either. Actually, there are spots still ahead of you rapidly disappearing, too. But if you are not running faster than the animal that dropped them, you will never catch up to the fade point to see that.

- Presently animals only bleed onto the ground when they are running away. When they charge or go back to walking, blood will not appear on the ground. They are however still bleeding and will eventually die. Blood drops will again appear if the animal is encouraged to run away (gunshot, throw a lit flare at it, close missed shot with an arrow).

If an animal successfully outruns you far enough to where you lose contact with it, it can stop running and return to a walking pace. Typically, these animals will be found returning along the same path they just fled along as they try to get back to their correct positions in the world.

Bleeding animals will eventually drop dead, regardless of whether the player is there to see it or not. Finding the carcass can be difficult if contact was lost as they fled. Carcasses no longer move about and do not leave a trail, so spotting some may be difficult; however, if the player suspects their prey died in a certain area, using charcoal to map that area will reveal the location of the carcass if the player is close enough (mapping from an elevated position helps greatly with this). Players should take advantage of elevated spots to look down into low areas. Search every side of obstacles, and look for [crows](./Crow.md) circling over an area. Carcasses will begin to freeze and meat will begin to decay the moment the animal dies. If left alone, a carcass will disappear after a few days. Frozen carcasses can be thawed by placing campfires near them, reducing the amount of time it takes to harvest meat.

In some areas (e.g. [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) or [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md)) the Rabbits, Deer and Wolves can be directed towards the water. While hunting on the open ice is easier due to the even ground, attention is advised if they get too close to the water. If they run out too far, that animal will simply disappear, probably because of it drowning, resulting in the effort (and maybe a few arrows) going down the drain. If unlucky, deer and wolves may die on the [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md), so that the player can't harvest the carcasses without risking falling through the Ice.
[^3]: Struggle is guaranteed to end after "Take Shot" is chosen (70% to flee, 30% to kill)

violations.context: **Details**
A wilderness almost untouched by human hands, filled with deep valleys and steep cliff walls.

> “**For advanced players. A remote, wind-blown valley known for its sheer cliffs, dense forests, and steep, winding paths. Although devoid of human settlements, it has long been a destination for the area's toughest mountaineers, and may still have a few secrets to reveal.**”

**Hushed River Valley**is the 9th [Region](./Region.md) added to the game, as a part of the [Vigilant Flame](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog%20%E2%80%94%20Archive%201.md#1.33_%28Vigilant_Flame_Update%29) update. The region connects to [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) via a cave that runs from an area between the [Trailer](./Trailer%20%28Mountain%20Town%20Region%29.md) and [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md) to a ridge top in the valley.

Geographically, the river valley is defined by steep cliffs and canyons; the lowest point lies in the middle of the region, with higher altitudes toward the edges of the map. The central valley features several waterfalls, and there are a few snow shelters that may spawn at higher elevation points (e.g., near the cave that connects to [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md)).

Although not the coldest region on Great Bear, the Hushed River Valley is quite chilly, making [campfires](./Campfire.md) necessary to avoid freezing, especially during night-time blizzards. Due to the lack of human-made structures, mass produced clothing, food, and tools are sparse; typically only found in [hidden caches](./Hidden%20Cache.md) scattered throughout the region, inside the region's many caves, or near abandoned campsites. Since the inclusion of [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) and [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), this is no longer the only region to have hidden caches in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), though it still contains the greatest number of them.

The lack of even natural [bedding](./Bed.md) means that having a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) is a virtual necessity for anyone wishing to explore the region, although at least one bedroll will spawn somewhere in the region, even on Interloper. One [prepper cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) spawns at a fixed location in the region on the high plateau, offering a bed but requiring a rope climb to the plateau. For players who do not own [Tales](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), this is the only location which can be edited using [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md), allowing the creation of a [work bench](./Work%20Bench.md). [Bunker Gamma](./Bunker%20Gamma.md) is also equipped with beds and a [work bench](./Work%20Bench.md), though it is only available to players who have the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC installed.

The lack of encroachment by civilization seems to have allowed local flora and fauna to flourish. Animal and plant life are abundant, so opportunities for hunting, scavenging, and foraging natural foods and supplies such as [rose hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) are relatively common. However, in that same vein, many predators also stalk the region. It's also the region that is most likely to spawn a [moose](./Moose.md).
In a rough sense, the Hushed River Valley can be divided into four smaller areas. Travel between these areas requires the use of [mountaineering ropes](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md).

This is the largest area of the region, and is where the player will first enter the Hushed River Valley from [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md). Four of the five possible player spawns are located here too. Notable landmarks include [Cloudtop Falls](./Cloudtop%20Falls.md), located a short distance west of the entrance cave and [Stairsteps Lake](./Stairsteps%20Lake.md), located a short distance north of Cloudtop Falls. The [Hushed River](./Hushed%20River.md) cuts this roughly in half, and can only be reached by climbing down logs or from its westernmost end near [Offset Falls](./Offset%20Falls.md). A rope can also be used to climb up and down the northern bank of the river. Halfway down the river lie the [Reclusive Falls](./Reclusive%20Falls.md), through which the player will have to pass to enter one of the [ice caves](./Ice%20Cave.md) (getting soaked in the process). Finally, the player can enjoy a panoramic view of much of the region from [Valley View Point](./Valley%20View%20Point.md), near the east of this area on the south bank of the Hushed River.

In addition to the [ice caves](./Ice%20Cave.md), there are multiple smaller caves that can serve as shelters. One is located to the northeast of [Stairsteps Lake](./Stairsteps%20Lake.md), another along the [Hushed River](./Hushed%20River.md), and two located on the northwestern and northern cliffs of the area.

While this area boasts the most resources, plentiful shelter, and excellent hunting and trapping opportunities, it is likely the most dangerous, with multiple [wolf](./Wolf.md) spawning locations scattered throughout, along with up to two [bears](./Bear.md), so caution is advised, especially given the general lack of ammunition spawns in the region.

This area is the lowest part of the Hushed River Valley, and is located towards the eastern part of the region, encompassing [Little Bear and Cub Falls](./Little%20Bear%20and%20Cub%20Falls.md), [Twin Sisters Falls](./Twin%20Sisters%20Falls.md), [Long Shot Falls](./Long%20Shot%20Falls.md), [the Landslide](./Landslide%20%28Hushed%20River%20Valley%29.md), [Moose Overlook](./Moose%20Overlook.md), and [Valley Cave](./Valley%20Cave.md). It is possible to spawn in here a short distance west of the Landslide. In order to enter or leave this area, a rather long rope climb from either [Pensive Vista](./Pensive%20Vista.md) or [Many Falls Vista](./Many%20Falls%20Vista.md) is required.

Most players in this area will end up using Valley Cave as their base of operations, as it is the only decent shelter. A [distress pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) can sometimes spawn here, and a [hunting rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) can sometimes be found next to a corpse located not far to the west.

No bears will spawn here, and there are abundant [deer](./Deer.md) hunting opportunities, along with a rabbit grove for snaring, and lots of [cattails](./Cat%20Tail.md) for food or tinder. The [moose](./Moose.md) located near the Landslide can be hunted, providing a good source of food and a hide, easily cured in Valley Cave.

The area is relatively free from predators and offers great foraging, [deer](./Deer.md) hunting opportunities, but occasionally, one [wolf](./Wolf.md) or even a pack of [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) may spawn a short distance west of Valley Cave.

One special precaution that must be taken when exploring this area is to bring along a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md), as there is no guarantee that one will spawn. If players become exhausted and have no way to refill their fatigue, they will become trapped and unable to climb out. This is especially problematic if the player got [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md) from a moose struggle, which will make it impossible to leave the area without the use of an [emergency stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md).

Getting here generally requires either a rope climb from the lower valley, a rope climb through one of the [ice caves](./Ice%20Cave.md), or a rope climb near [Mammoth Falls](./Mammoth%20Falls.md), but it is possible to scramble up to this area via several root climbs from the ice cave entrance nearest Valley View Point without using a rope at all. From the ice cave exit, one of the two possible spawn locations for the [Mysterious Signal Fire](./Mysterious%20Signal%20Fire.md) may be found by going due south and cutting through some scrub brush. Other notable landmarks include [Mammoth Falls](./Mammoth%20Falls.md) and [Quarrelling Falls](./Quarrelling%20Falls.md), located to the north of the area, and [Monolith Lake](./Monolith%20Lake.md) itself, around which can be found [Banner Falls](./Banner%20Falls.md), [Watchful Falls](./Watchful%20Falls.md) and [Lake Cave](./Lake%20Cave.md). Finally, two more isolated caves can be found, one at [Pensive Vista](./Pensive%20Vista.md), and [Peak Cave](./Peak%20Cave.md), located at the top of a mountain at the east end of Monolith Lake.

Aside from the ice cave entrance, there are a number of other caves that offer good base opportunities. [Lake Cave](./Lake%20Cave.md) is centrally located, not far from where the [moose](./Moose.md) spawns (making hide curing easier), and offers a possible [revolver](./Revolver.md) spawn, but the nearby waterfall may be distractedly loud to some players. The cave at [Pensive Vista](./Pensive%20Vista.md) is a little less central, but is much quieter. [Peak Cave](./Peak%20Cave.md) offers a very secluded experience and a possible [distress pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) spawn, but requires a long, steep climb to access, making sprains rather likely.

This area is relatively free of predators, and offers good foraging opportunities, along with [moose](./Moose.md) and [deer](./Deer.md) hunting and [rabbit](./Rabbit.md) snaring. Players who have purchased [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) will find four [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) nests in the local area. One wolf can spawn near one of the entrances to the ice cave network, but tends not to wander too far. It is also the only part of the region where the water is deep enough for [ice fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md), namely on Monolith Lake.

The smallest area of the Hushed River Valley, there are two ways to reach this high, desolate plateau. One method involves travelling through an [Ice cave](./Ice%20Cave.md), which requires a short rope climb. The other is to take a much longer rope climb southwest of [Many Falls Vista](./Many%20Falls%20Vista.md). Once this area has been visited, a rope can be placed near one of the two possible spawn locations for the [Mysterious Signal Fire](./Mysterious%20Signal%20Fire.md), allowing easier access to Many Falls Vista.

There are three caves located in this area. The westernmost is [Lonely Cave](./Lonely%20Cave.md), which may contain a [distress pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md), but its isolated location limits its usefulness as a longer-term base. The entrance to the ice cave is relatively warm, and offers bioluminescent lighting regardless of the time of day. The easternmost cave is located closest to the rabbit grove, but doesn't offer the same advantages of warmth as the ice cave. The [snow shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md) at the Mysterious Signal Fire can be used as a short-term base, but is expensive to maintain.
One wolf may spawn on this plateau, but otherwise there isn't any significant amount of game to be hunted here, aside from some [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) near the easternmost cave.

There are a few high elevation points where a [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md) (the only type of man-made shelter in the region) might spawn. If found before they decay, the snow shelters may serve as a base (note that they require maintenance and cloth to repair). There is also a chance food and tools may spawn near the snow shelters or inside/near natural shelters. A burned-out [campfire](./Campfire.md) may also be found near each of the snow shelters.

While these camps can serve as short-term bases, the lack of sturdy artificial structures means that natural formations such as rock overhangs, cliffside caves, and ice caves will generally serve as the best safe houses in the region. The [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) could also serve as a base, though its location strongly limits its usefulness. [Bunker Gamma](./Bunker%20Gamma.md) could also make a good base, though it requires [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) to be installed, and is quite difficult to find.

Storage can also be a challenge, due to the lack of containers. However, one solution as of the Fearless Navigator update is to build a [rock cache](./Rock%20Cache.md), which can store up to 30 kg of supplies. This will also make it easier for the player to find their base camp.

One thing to keep in mind is that there is no workbench in this region aside from the one in Bunker Gamma, meaning that players will not be able to craft many items without a trip to the [Trailer](./Trailer%20%28Mountain%20Town%20Region%29.md), located in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md).

This region contains special caves called [ice caves](./Ice%20Cave.md), which share similarities with other deep caves. Inside the ice caves almost constant cracking (likely from the ice shifting) can be heard echoing from within. Ice caves' walls are grey-blue and appear slightly translucent; rockier walls may feature bioluminescent moss growing in some areas.

These caves form an extensive network around the region and are important for exploring safely, offering protection from the weather and predators (usually). The many twists and turns in the cave systems and the significant distances between bioluminescent moss patches can make navigation tricky, especially in the dark. [Stones](./Stone.md), spent [torches](./Torch.md), or other items can be used as markers to help the player retrace paths through the caves. [Spray Paint](./Spray%20Paint.md) may also be used to make path markers.

There are two ice cave networks in total--one of which may be inhabited by a wolf. Each cave system has multiple entrances/exits, which often have icicles hanging on the rock face around their exteriors; rose hip bushes and other useful flora often grow directly around the entrances, as well. Reaching different parts of an ice cave may require climbing ropes to reach high ledges or passing through frigid waterfalls inside or at the entrances of a cave system.
In addition to the rich natural resources present in the region, along with excellent hunting opportunities, the Hushed River Valley contains some items that are somewhat challenging to get.

The region contains at least 4 [hidden caches](./Hidden%20Cache.md) of food or other supplies. Certain cache boxes will spawn in the same location in every game, while others can spawn in any of several specific locations. Generally, caches may be found tucked into corners and niches near landmarks (such as inside ice caves or beside waterfalls) or near landscape features such as fallen trees or at the top of cliffs.

Caches are small grey boxes with orange lids, and each may contain collections of somewhat related items such as rifle accessories. Most caches have the same level loot as supply caches in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), with up to 4 high-quality supplies (e.g., mid- to high-level [Clothing](./Clothing.md), medicine, and food). These caches can contain fairly rare items, particularly on Interloper difficulty.

One [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md), along with a few [shells](./Flare%20Shell.md), will always spawn in this region. The distress pistol spawns in either [Valley Cave](./Valley%20Cave.md), [Lonely Cave](./Lonely%20Cave.md), or [Peak Cave](./Peak%20Cave.md). This is one of five locations in which it's possible to find this item in survival mode, aside from the [Fallen Lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), the [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md) atop [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), the [Train Shuttle](./Train%20Shuttle.md) in the [Ravine Basin](./Ravine%20Basin.md), and at the bottom of the canyon underneath the rope bridge in [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md).

One [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) will always spawn in this region, except on Interloper difficulty. This satchel is located at the [Mysterious Signal Fire](./Mysterious%20Signal%20Fire.md), which may spawn in one of two different locations.
On Interloper difficulty, one [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) spawns at the Mysterious Signal Fire.

Another item that can be found near the Mysterious Signal Fire is the [Mackinaw Jacket](./Mackinaw%20Jacket.md), which will spawn in all difficulty levels. Although it's not the warmest coat in the game, it's the best coat obtainable in Interloper.

The [Woodwright's Bow](./Woodwright%27s%20Bow.md), a variant on the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), will always spawn once in this region, except on Interloper difficulty. It is 50% heavier than the normal bow, but sways 30% less, and is twice as durable.

| - [Banner Falls](./Banner%20Falls.md) - [Bunker Gamma](./Bunker%20Gamma.md) - [Cloudtop Falls](./Cloudtop%20Falls.md) - [Hushed River](./Hushed%20River.md) - [Lake Cave](./Lake%20Cave.md) - [Landslide](./Landslide%20%28Hushed%20River%20Valley%29.md) - [Little Bear and Cub Falls](./Little%20Bear%20and%20Cub%20Falls.md) - [Lonely Cave](./Lonely%20Cave.md) - [Long Shot Falls](./Long%20Shot%20Falls.md) - [Mammoth Falls](./Mammoth%20Falls.md) - [Many Falls Vista](./Many%20Falls%20Vista.md) - [Monolith Lake](./Monolith%20Lake.md) - [Moose Overlook](./Moose%20Overlook.md) | - [Mysterious Signal Fire](./Mysterious%20Signal%20Fire.md) can spawn in 2 different places - [Offset Falls](./Offset%20Falls.md) - [Peak Cave](./Peak%20Cave.md) - [Pensive Vista](./Pensive%20Vista.md) - [Quarreling Falls](./Quarrelling%20Falls.md) - [Reclusive Falls](./Reclusive%20Falls.md) - [Stairsteps Lake](./Stairsteps%20Lake.md) - To Cave System (Transition to [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md)) - [Twin Sisters Falls](./Twin%20Sisters%20Falls.md) - [Valley Cave](./Valley%20Cave.md) - [Valley View Point](./Valley%20View%20Point.md) - [Watchful Falls](./Watchful%20Falls.md) |

There is also 1 [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) and a crashed plane located near [Lonely Cave](./Lonely%20Cave.md). A large network of [Ice Caves](./Ice%20Cave.md) is also present in the region.

- This region contains new waterfall effects and new cave systems; the region also features a new form of [Scrub Brush](./Scrub%20Brush.md) that acts as a physical barrier, potentially blocking some direct paths completely. However, this form of brush can also be broken down with a [hatchet](./Hatchet.md), yielding 12 [sticks](./Stick.md). Some scrub barriers can be bypassed by careful navigation on nearby ledges.

- It has higher vertical cliffs and features a system of climbing that utilizes preexisting roots from [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) bushes, with the addition of a few [Mountaineering Ropes](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) in ice caves and on high cliffs.
- The region shares many defining features with [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), including extensive caves, rugged terrain, and a continuous lack of human habitation.
- It was released with the Vigilant Flame Update on June 14th, 2018 and was released on XBOX1/1S Friday, June 15th, 2018.
- The original name of the region was **River Valley** as placeholder name. The name was changed to **Hushed River Valley** when the update was released.
- [Moose](./Moose.md) can spawn near Monolith Lake, Stairsteps Lake and in the central valley.

Hushed River is noted for its many waterfalls that include [Reclusive Falls](./Reclusive%20Falls.md), [Offset Falls](./Offset%20Falls.md), and [Twin Sisters Falls](./Twin%20Sisters%20Falls.md). It also has access points to some ice caves and many waterfall locations. The river contains an abundance of cattails and [Coal](./Coal.md), but [wolves](./Wolf.md) are also common on the western half of the river, so it's a good idea to be careful when exploring. To get into the eastern portion of the valley, it is necessary to [descend using a rope](./Rope%20Climbing.md), either from [Pensive Vista](./Pensive%20Vista.md) or from [Many Falls Vista](./Many%20Falls%20Vista.md).

There are a number of caves along the river which can serve as shelter. One of the entrances to the [Ice Cave](./Ice%20Cave.md) may be found here, but going through it will soak the player, limiting its usefulness as a base. Another cave can be found slightly to the east. Once past Twin Sisters Falls, the player will run into [Valley Cave](./Valley%20Cave.md), a popular safe house when exploring the eastern part of the valley. A small cave is present at the [Landslide](./Landslide%20%28Hushed%20River%20Valley%29.md), but this cave doesn't offer any warmth benefit.

**Hyperglycemia Risk** is a unique [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ only encountered in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) during the mission [Fallen Star](./Fallen%20Star.md) in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md).

Hyperglycemia is a unique Affliction Risk that affects Dimitri, a [Crash Survivor](./Crash%20Survivor.md). Since he has Type-1 Diabetes and his body cannot produce insulin on its own, [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) is tasked with retrieving his [Insulin](./Insulin.md) in order to prolong his life, which has been left in his suitcase ([Suitcase belonging to Dimitri S.](./Suitcase%20belonging%20to%20Dimitri%20S..md)) at the [Crash Site](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md). Astrid, after bringing the Insulin back to [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), administers the hormone to Dimitri.
Due to gameplay reasons, Dimitri will never truly develop Hyperglycemia and die, no matter how much time passes.

Though not seen in game, it can be inferred that Dimitri will likely begin suffering from Hyperglycemia Risk again once his current supply of Insulin runs out, as diabetics require doses daily to function normally (usually with meals.). Unless he can procure a large amount of low-carbohydrate foods (i.e foods that won't raise his blood glucose), or procure more Insulin despite the absence of most medical technology, he will unfortunately not survive the Quiet Apocalypse for very long.

**Hypothermia Risk** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_, caused by exposure to the cold.

If the player stays out in the freezing cold for too long, and their [Clothing](./Clothing.md) is not sufficiently warm enough to keep their [Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md) temperature above 0°, their [Warmth](./Warmth.md) [Need](./Needs.md) will drop. Once Warmth hits zero and reaches "Freezing", the Hypothermia Risk will appear. Should a player continue to freeze in this state, they will gain the [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md) affliction after 2 hours.

- The treatment for Hypothermia and Hypothermia Risk is keeping Warmth above freezing until the affliction heals. Should the player start freezing while recovering from Hypothermia, the recovery time will reset.

- The time to recover from Hypothermia is based on the experience mode: 6 hours for Pilgrim, 12 for Voyageur, 18 for Stalker and 24 for Interloper. Remaining recovery time is shown on the Status menu.
- [Hot](./Warming%20Up.md) food or drinks and [campfires](./Campfire.md) can help stay above freezing, even when outdoors.
- Freezing, even without Hypothermia, is by far the deadliest Need (Freezing: 20% Condition loss per hour (40% with Hypothermia), Thirst: 2% per hour, Hunger/Fatigue 1% per hour).

**Ice caves** are interior locations mainly found in the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) region. Another ice cave connects [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md) with [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), and a small ice cave can be found in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), located in the back of the cave at [Misty Falls Picnic Area](./Misty%20Falls%20Picnic%20Area.md).

Ice caves have small patches of bio-luminescent moss along some of the walls. Ice caves act as interior environments (i.e., there is a loading screen when entering and leaving a cave) and are typically warm enough to prevent even a poorly clothed character from freezing. When inside an ice cave, near-constant creaking, presumably from the shifting of the ice, can be heard.

There may also be waterfalls and streams found inside some caves, which will give your character [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md), make all worn [clothes](./Clothing.md) wet, and put out a lit [flare](./Flare.md), [storm lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), or [torch](./Torch.md) if you step into them.

There are two ice cave systems in the Hushed River Valley region, each with multiple entrances. The sprawling caves may have sections that require climbing a short [mountaineering rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) to reach. The Ice cave connecting the two halves of Keeper's Pass is much more linear in layout than the two in Hushed River Valley, acting like a normal transition cave.
Just like normal caves, lumps of [coal](./Coal.md) may occasionally be found lying on the ground, except in the small ice cave at Misty Falls.
- Ice Caves were added to the game as part of the Vigilant Flame update released for PC on 14 June 2018 and for XBOX on 15 June 2018
- You can find valuable loot inside ice caves such as [rifle ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), [cedar firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md), [fir firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md), and more.
- A [wolf](./Wolf.md) can spawn in the cave without the waterfalls. Be careful, since it may not spawn initially. Once dealt with, it will respawn.

There are 4 [Fishing Huts](./Fishing%20Hut.md) on the lake, with 2 east of the little middle island being the location that triggers the **Ice Fishing Huts** location. The remaining 2 huts are closer to [Lone Lake Cabin](./Lone%20Lake%20Cabin.md).
Mystery Lake is a good location for collecting supplies due to the abundance of cabin and huts around the lake.

A [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) is located at the north-western tip of the lake between the lake and the rail road tracks, this building has an abundance of supplies and is a contender for one of the best base locations in the region.

There are two collections of [Lake Cabins](./Lake%20Cabins.md) on the south and south-eastern end of the lake, usually one cabin out of each collection is burnt down, but there is still a large amount of supplies to be found in each.
Further up past the triple lake cabins a [Lone Lake Cabin](./Lone%20Lake%20Cabin.md) quietly sits abandoned.

![Ice Fishing](../assets/Ice_Fishing.png) **Ice Fishing** is the [Skill](./Skills.md) to catch fish in _The Long Dark_. It is performed at fishing holes, which are cut in the ice of fish-bearing bodies of water.

![A fishing hut is one of the safest and simplest locations to ice fish.](../assets/Fishing_hut_outside.jpg)_A fishing hut is one of the safest and simplest locations to ice fish._ Ice Fishing is the skill to catch fish for [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), [lantern oil](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) and source renewable Vitamin-C to avoid [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md). It is performed at any fish-bearing body of water, at hole(s) cut in its ice. These holes are found inside all Fishing Huts, and can also be made manually with any Tool (via the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md)). The Survivor can fish manually with a [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md), or semi-automatically with [Fishing Tip-Ups](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md) (crafted fish traps). When choosing to fish the survivor can select to use bait, lures and how long to fish for. While fishing time is accelerated, and the task may be canceled early (ESC or "Cancel").

- Manual Ice Fishing: requires Fishing Tackle(s) and accelerates time while fishing. Catching fish manually both increases and benefits from Ice Fishing Skill. Manual Fishing is versatile and simple. needing few materials to do.

- Fish Trapping: requires Fishing Tip-Up(s) and is semi-automatic. Deployed Tip-Ups catch fish independent of the survivor, but lose condition while deployed and require regular ice-clearing in their holes to prevent re-freeze. Deploying more than 6 Fishing Tip-Ups in the same [Region](./Region.md) will cause 'overfishing', resulting in diminishing returns (4 for [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md)). Trapping fish with Tip-Ups does not increase or benefit from Ice Fishing Skill. Deploying 6 Tip-Ups and actively maintaining them will yield a substantially higher amount of calories per hour (around 3.7x) compared to manually fishing (level 5), however this requires more resources and effort from the player.
- [Fishing Lure](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28disambiguation%29.md): increases odds of catching rare fish and increases bite times
- [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md)/[Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md)/[Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) for boiling water

Each fishing session is treated separately, so longer sessions will likely catch more fish than the same time broken into multiple sessions. Fishing for less than the "maximum bite time" will result in no fish ever being caught. Overfishing is caused by using more than 6 Tip-Ups in the same region (more than 4 in Zone of Contamination)

There are two types of fish: saltwater and freshwater, and four rarity: common, uncommon and two rare types. Fishing Lures only increase the odds of "rare" fish (at the cost of increase bite wait times).

Fishing Tackle and a tool to cut hole(s) in the ice are required for fishing. Optionally Bait and/or Lures can be used to increase bite-rate, or the odds of catching rare fish. Fishing on the ice for hours is very cold, so a lit fire with fuel and/or [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md) is often required. Before fishing, it's advisable to travel light or bring along a [Travois](./Travois.md), since the weight of multiple freshly-caught fish can [add up quickly](./Encumbrance.md).

![Fishing Tackle icon](../assets/Fishing_Tackle_icon.png) [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) are the primary tool for fishing. They are crafted from a [Hook](./Hook.md) and [Line](./Line.md). Tackle lasts until they break during fishing, and only degrade condition when used to Repair clothing (Tackle durability has no effect on break rate).

Ice breakers are any tool used to clear ice holes. Fully clearing a hole takes the full break time, with a partially frozen hole taking much less. Prybar and Heavy Hammer take longer to clear than bladed tools, but sustain less condition loss when doing so. Prybars are non-renewable or repairable, but Heavy Hammers may be repaired sustainably (but not replaced if ruined).

![Fishing Tip Up icon](../assets/Fishing_Tip-Up_icon.png) [Fishing Tip-Ups](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md) are tools to trap fish at Fishing Holes (including those inside of Fishing Huts). They can be fitted with Lures or Bait, and function similar to [Snares](./Snare.md), but unlike Snares are not effective when used passively: as they require regular ice-clearing to function, and will lose condition while deployed.

After clearing an ice hole and placing the Tip-Up in the water the tool will auto fish. As time passes and a fish bites the tackle, the tool will "Tip-Up" and fall upright with a metallic jingling sound. Tip-Ups lose condition when deployed (1% per hour outside, 0.5% per hour inside a Fishing Hut) and 10% on line break. Catching fish with Tip-Ups does not yield Ice Fishing Skill or benefit from it.

Any number of Tip-Ups may be deployed in a region, but deploying more than 6 per separate body of water will result in 'overfishing penalties', yielding diminishing return catch rates (4 max in [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md)).

![Fishing Bait icon](../assets/Fishing_Bait_icon.png) [Fishing Bait](./Fishing%20Bait.md) are an optional tool to catch larger fish. Using Bait increases average fish size by +30%, but one piece of Bait will be consumed for each fish caught. Bait is crafted by harvesting any raw fish and takes 30 minutes regardless of fish weight. Heavier fish yield more Bait when harvested (3 Bait per 1kg of Raw Fish weight).

[Fishing Lures](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28disambiguation%29.md) are an optional tool for catching rare fish. Using lures increases the odds of catching a rare fish by 5-10x, but increases the maximum possible wait time for a fish to bite by +20%-75%. Lures are crafted at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) and do not lose condition when used, but will be lost if a Fishing Tackle breaks or Tip-Up's line breaks while fishing. All fishing lures weigh 0.01kg.

Ice Fishing by the survivor or their Tip-Ups requires holes cut in the ice of fishable bodies of water. These holes may be found inside of all Fishing Huts (small green structures found on the ice in many Regions), or cut manually by the water with any Tool. Holes will gradually re-freeze over, and must be manually cleared periodically to continue use. Completely clearing ice holes will pause freezing progress for 10 in-game minutes.

Fishing on Pilgrim, Voyageur and Stalker have the same fishing rates. Fishing on Interloper begins at the same rate, but increases the bite-times to twice as long on average (starting from Day 10, reaching maximum effect at day 50).

Fishing inside of Fishing Huts is more efficient than survivor-cut holes. The Fishing Hut in [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md) ([Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md)) is unique and grants a further bonus to fishing rate.

*Time to Catch on Interloper mode progressively increases up to a maximum of twice as long at Day 50, while beginning at the same value as Pilgrim/Voyageur/Stalker.

[Fishing Huts](./Fishing%20Hut.md) are small structures on the ice which provide protection from the elements and wildlife. All fishing huts contain a pre-cut hole in the ice for fishing. Huts also contain a [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md) to keep warm, cook or boil water, and some have door and provide a warmth bonus in their interior. Wildlife cannot enter a fishing hut even when the door is open.
All fishing holes inside Fishing Huts are more efficient than survivor-made ones outside, with all Fishing Huts being identical except for Ash Canyon's which has a higher bite-rate

The survivor can cut holes in the ice to fish from with any tool on fishable ice (deep blue ice, not white ice). Without a Fishing Hut for protection, fishing manually at a cut hole runs the risk of exposure or wildlife attacks. It is also impossible to place holes in areas designated as Weak Ice areas. Cutting Ice Fishing Holes was added as part of the free update for Part 3 of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md).

Fishing at cut Ice Fishing Holes catches fewer fish per hour, cause double Tip-Up condition decay, and freeze over faster than the holes inside of Fishing Huts, but may be created anywhere on valid ice surfaces. It is possible to use fishing holes from the safety of snow shelters, and up to 4 holes may be accessed at once with close placement.

Free-Formed ice fishing holes will disappear if left to freeze back to 100% unless the player exits and re-enters the area via loading screen while a cut ice hole is open, which will result in that hole becoming permanent and impossible to remove.

| 2 | 10 | 40 | - Fishing time reduced by 5% - 8% chance of line break on catch | You're getting more comfortable with fishing in the Winter. You're better with your fishing gear, and you're developing a feel for when a fish is on the line. |
| 3 | 50 | 100 | - Fishing time reduced by 10% - 5% chance of line break on catch | You're quite good at ice fishing. You rarely break your lines now, and you catch more fish per hour. |

| 4 | 150 | 100 | - 10% to average fish weight - Fishing time reduced by 20% - 3% chance of line break on catch | You are fantastic at ice fishing. You seem to catch fish more often, more quickly, and somehow you get the bigger ones too! |

| 5 | 250 | Max level | - 25% to average fish weight - Fishing time reduced by 30% - 1% chance of line break on catch | You are the Pied Piper of ice fishers. You barely have to clear the ice hole for fish to nearly jump out of the water. You catch bigger fish, more often, and in less time. |

- Cooked Fish yield a small amount of [Lantern Oil](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) when picked up. This is automatically added to existing oil containers in the survivor's inventory. [Jerry Cans](./Jerry%20Can.md) hold fuel more efficiently than "Lantern Fuel" bottles.
- Seawater fish provide more oil per kg than freshwater fish. Uncommon fish provide more oil per kg than common fish.
- Common fish provide more Vitamin-C per kg than uncommon fish, however, rare fish never contain Vitamin-C.
- Fish have a much poorer calories:weight ratio than other meat types, especially while raw. Cooking improves this rate, but even Rabbit/Ptarmigan meat is more efficient for travel food.
- Three recipes use fish: [Trout Stew](./Trout%20Stew.md), [Dockworker's Pie](./Dockworker%27s%20Pie.md) and [Coastal Fishcakes](./Coastal%20Fishcakes.md).

Has an interior **Idle Camp** is one of the two major human settlements in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md).

2 lodging barracks hold numerous [Beds](./Bed.md), [Lockers](./Locker.md), and bathrooms containing [Toilets](./Toilet.md). Rare, region exclusive clothing such as a [Hardhat](./Hardhat.md), [Miner's Jacket](./Miner%27s%20Jacket.md), [Miner's Pants](./Miner%27s%20Pants.md), and [Chemical Boots](./Chemical%20Boots.md) have a chance to spawn in the 3 buildings and the nearby [Train Shuttle](./Train%20Shuttle.md) near the road.

The mess hall building contains a mess hall with several wooden tables and a kitchen containing several [Fridges](./Fridge.md), [Freezers](./Freezer.md), a Vegetable Drawer, and an invaluable [Stove](./Stove.md). The ponds around the nearby buildings have [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) that can be harvested.
2 [Trucks](./Truck.md) can be found outside and slept in, which can be useful if the player has [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) after spending many hours exploring the mines.
Multiple [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) often patrol the field across the train tracks from the camp, and can wander into the Camp if the player is spotted.

When worn in the either accessory slot, Improvised Crampons grant the Benefit [Sure Footing](./Sure%20Footing.md) which has three effects:
- Decreases chance of [sprains](./Afflictions.md) by 70% when on slopes. (This is a bug, was supposed to be 30% only)
- Decreases drain rate of [climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) stamina by 60% (This is a bug, was supposed to be 40% only)
- Increases the (invisible) timer of [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md) by 0.5 seconds (aka 10% more time to move off weak Ice, before falling in) for a total time of 5.5 seconds.

Crampons are particularly useful in [regions](./Region.md) with multiple [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) climbs, such as [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), and [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), or in areas with [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md) such as [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) or when [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) in regions like [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) or [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md).
Improvised Crampons cannot be harvested, and provide lesser benefits compared to [Crampons.](./Crampons.md)

If the player's footwear (shoes and 2 socks slots) are removed (whether by the player or their footwear is ruined) then their Improvised Crampons will automatically be removed, removing the [Sure Footing](./Sure%20Footing.md) affliction.
- Despite being designed to attach to shoes, the player can wear Improvised Crampons on their socks, which should not be possible.
Can be repaired with 2 pieces of [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) using [Simple](./Simple%20Tools.md) or [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) as of Signal Void. Need to be unequipped to repair.

**Improvised Down Bedroll** is a Tool released for the Part 3: Frontier Comforts update for those who purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.

The Down Bedroll weighs 0.10 kg more than a regular [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) and is harder to repair, requiring [Ptarmigan Down](./Ptarmigan%20Down.md) in addition to [Cloth](./Cloth.md), but is also significantly warmer, making it a good alternative to the regular Bedroll.

The Improvised Down Bedroll takes an ordinary [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) and stuffs it full of Ptarmigan Down feathers, resulting in a base warmth increase of the Bedroll by 3°C at 100% (for a total of 8°C). The weight of the Bedroll also increases, from 1 kg to 1.1 kg.
Can be crafted anywhere by hand. Takes 3/6 hours to craft with [Sewing Kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md)/[Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) respectively.

Note that a completely ruined [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) (0%) can still be crafted into an Improvised Down Bedroll at 100%. (doesn't seem to be current anymore for 2.39 version of the game - needs further verification)
