> “**An improvised hatchet. Basically a heavy piece of metal with sharpened edge. Not fancy, but utilitarian.**”
The **Improvised Hatchet** is a tool in _The Long Dark_, primarily for woodcutting and self defense.

Functioning similarly to the hatchet, improvised hatchets may be used to harvest [sticks](./Stick.md) from branches, [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) and [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md) from tree limbs, [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) from furniture or to break ice for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md).

The improvised hatchet is slightly heavier (0.25 kg) and 1/3 slower to use than the [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md). Its condition is reduced by 3% per use. Hatchets are a finite resource, so once all have been ruined, improvised hatchets must be crafted to complete some tasks. The improvised hatchet may be used as a lighter substitute to the heavy hammer to break down furniture or branches.
Improvised Hatchets are repairable with [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md) or at the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md).
- [Harvest frozen carcasses](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) ([Knives](./Hunting%20Knife.md) have faster unfrozen meat, gut and hide harvesting speeds. Hatchets are only faster at harvesting frozen meat).
- Open or maintain holes in the ice for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) (bladed tools break ice faster, but take more condition loss).
- Breaking down Furniture and Crates (for [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) or [Cloth](./Cloth.md)).
- For the [Whiteout](./Whiteout.md) [challenge's](./Challenge.md) objective, an improvised hatchet may substitute the requirement of a hatchet.

When carried and selected for self-defense at the start of a Wolf Struggle, Improvised Hatchets deal high damage with a low chance per-hit to cause the wolf to flee, as well as a moderate chance to inflict [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) on the Wolf (which is lethal over time). Improvised Hatchets take low damage from being used in a struggle, and are inferior to Hatchets when used in this way. For more information on Struggles, see: [Wildlife Struggles](./Struggle.md).

Improvised Hatchets may be rarely found in some regions, usually near frozen corpses or structures; such as in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) or [Milton Basin](./Milton%20Basin.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) near [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md). One may also spawn atop the workbench in the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md) of [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md).

Forging improvised hatchets is only possible at a [furnace](./Furnace.md) with a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md); [coal](./Coal.md) is required to a heat furnace hot enough for forging along with the necessary crafting materials: [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) and [cloth](./Cloth.md).
In Interloper mode hatchets and improvised hatchets will never spawn; requiring forging to create.

Improvised Hatchets may be repaired using a [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md) and the [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) skill, restoring 3% condition to the hatchet and causing 5% condition damage to the whetstone.

The [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) or [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) may repair a non-ruined improvised hatchet to 100% condition for one scrap metal, during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md). Repairing Improvised Hatchet or Improvised Knife with the Milling Machine is more efficient with Scrap Metal than [forging](./Forge.md) new ones.

- A broken Hatchet is the icon and logo for _The Long Dark_ on all platforms, including [the official Hinterlands website](https://hinterlandgames.com/), [forums](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/) and [merchandise](https://www.hinterlandstore.com/).
- Like the [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md), the Improvised Hatchet is a flattened metal pipe with cloth for a grip.

The **Improvised Knife** is a tool in _The Long Dark_ for butchering, crafting and self defense.

Improvised Knives are functionally similar to [Hunting Knives](./Hunting%20Knife.md), but can be [Forged](./Forge.md), weighing slightly more and are slower to craft/harvest with and less effective during struggles. Knives have number of uses: harvesting gut, hide and meat from [animal](./Wildlife.md) carcasses, as well as [cloth](./Cloth.md) and [tinder plugs](./Tinder%20Plug.md). It may also serve as a makeshift [can opener](./Can%20Opener.md) to avoid spillage, or to break through iced-over fishing holes for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md), and as a self-defense weapon during wolf attacks.
Improvised Knives are particularly useful on Interloper mode, where Hunting Knives never spawn, or Custom sandbox with Loot Frequency set to "Low".
Improvised Knives are repairable with [Whetsone](./Whetstone.md) or at the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md).
- May be used to [harvest frozen carcasses](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) (Knives have faster unfrozen meat, gut and hide harvesting speeds. Hatchets are only faster at harvesting frozen meat)
- Open or maintain holes in the ice for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) (bladed tools break ice faster, but take more condition loss when doing so).

When carried and selected for self-defense at the start of a Wolf Struggle, Improvised Knives deal low damage with a low chance per-hit to cause the wolf to flee, and a high chance to inflict [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) (which is lethal to the Wolf over time). Improvised Knives are almost as effective at filling the Struggle Meter as the [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) or [Prybar](./Prybar.md), especially on difficulty modes other than [Interloper](./Survival%20Mode.md). Hunting Knives take low damage from being used in a struggle. For more information on Struggles, see: [Wildlife Struggles](./Struggle.md).

In Interloper mode improvised knives and hunting knives will never spawn; requiring forging to create.

The improvised knife can be repaired using a [whetstone](./Whetstone.md) and the [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) skill, restoring 3%-5% condition to the hunting knife (based on skill) and causing 5% condition damage to the whetstone.

Several smaller fields of toxic industrial waste are located near the sheds and can be avoided by simply walking around them.

A [Rim Grill](./Rim%20Grill.md) is placed in one of the buildings, of which only 4 exist in the game.

An **Infection Risk** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) that can develop into an [Infection](./Infection.md) between 8 and 24 hours after receiving the affliction. It is received from getting into a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) with hostile [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md).
**Infection Risk** always accompanies the **[Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md)** affliction gained from hostile Wildlife Struggles.
There is a base 50% chance of receiving an Infection after 8 hours, with a maximum of 90% chance at the 24 hour mark. The chance of receiving an Infection increases by 5% per hour.

Infection Risk is not an Infection itself, but rather a chance to receive an Infection. It is tracked as a percentage that will start at 50% and increase every hour by 5% until the maximum of 90% if untreated.
- If the player uses an item (see below) that removes Infection Risk, the affliction will entirely disappear and the player will not get an infection.
- Within a day of getting the infection risk, a roll will be made against the current Infection Risk percentage and the Infection Risk affliction will be cleared.
- If the roll is lower than the **Infection Risk** percentage, the player will receive the Infection affliction. The higher your infection risk, the more likely that you will get an infection.

The player can receive an Infection Risk after surviving a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) with a [Bear](./Bear.md), [Cougar](./Cougar.md), [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), or [Wolf](./Wolf.md).

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

**Insomnia Risk** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) added to the Part 1 Update of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon, and is contracted from spending too much time in [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) found within certain [Regions](./Region.md) within the Far Territory Frontier. At present, it can only be contracted in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), and [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) Regions.

The Affliction Risk for Insomnia can be mitigated by escaping Glimmer Fog when it arrives, either by finding an underground shelter or entering [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) (pursuing the latter will instantly remove any Insomnia Risk buildup).
There are 6 known underground locations that allow a survivor to escape the effects of Glimmer Fog:
- [Transition Cave](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md#Forsaken_Airfield_to_Zone_of_Contamination) between Forsaken Airfield, Zone of Contamination, and Sundered Pass
- The cave system connecting [Prayerful Window](./Prayerful%20Window.md), [Idle Hideout](./Idle%20Hideout.md), and [Cascading Gap](./Cascading%20Gap.md)
- Anywhere inside the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md), [Conveyor Room](./Conveyor%20Room.md), or even the very bottom elevator shaft of the [Headframe Building](./Headframe%20Building.md)
- [Basement (Sundered Pass)](./Basement%20%28Sundered%20Pass%29.md) (despite being underground)

The game currently lacks any real countermeasures in the form of foods or gear to effectively combat or hide from Glimmer Fog, so the player will almost certainly contract Insomnia if they are not already near an underground shelter when the fog arrives. It can also be hard to tell the difference between a Glimmer Fog or Aurora event during the early hours of the day while indoors for some locations, due to the inability to simply glance outside at the weather.

**Insomnia** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) added to the Part 1 Update of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon, and is contracted from spending too much time in [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) found within certain [Regions](./Region.md) within the Far Territory Frontier. At present, it can only be contracted in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), and [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) Regions.

Failure to manage [Insomnia Risk](./Insomnia%20Risk.md) and thereby contracting Insomnia results in the player character having their rest frequently interrupted for 18-36 hours. This affliction is different from [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), as the player may still rest anywhere at any time, but with a chance that their sleep may be prematurely disturbed after only a short period of rest (the player will awake with the message "SOMETHING WOKE YOU UP"), denying the player the full healing benefits of sleeping for long periods of time.

Eating certain Recipes created from Frontier Cooking has a chance to lower the effects of Insomnia if consumed. Drinking [Herbal Tea](./Herbal%20Tea.md) or foods that provide the [Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md) benefit can help counteract the effects of Insomnia and allow for deeper rest periods.

Escaping regions that Glimmer Fog frequents will not remove the affliction at this stage. Curing the affliction only requires the player to wait the allotted hours for the disease to pass. Further Glimmer Fog events will not increase the affliction time until it returns to Risk status.

To a healthy survivor with high [condition](./Condition.md), Insomnia is generally quite inconsequential, as interrupted sleep restores [fatigue](./Fatigue.md) just as effectively as uninterrupted sleep. In this situation, its only adverse affect is that sleeping may require a bit more clicking than normal, which is mildly annoying at most.

However, Insomnia can become a major issue to a survivor with low condition, as it can greatly reduce the amount of healing received during sleep, which can leave them in a weak and vulnerable state upon waking. This is most likely to result in [Interloper](./Interloper.md), where losing some condition every day is often seen as an acceptable tradeoff for obtaining resources. The resulting low condition can result in death from freezing, a fall, or a [struggle](./Struggle.md) that would normally be easily survivable. In this situation, it is best to use a [Cup of Herbal Tea](./Cup%20of%20Herbal%20Tea.md) in order to counteract the effects of Insomnia.

In rare cases, Insomnia could save the survivor's life: if they're sleeping in a cave or outside and the "feels like" temperature suddenly drops below 0oC, a random sleep interruption due to being afflicted with Insomnia could prevent them from freezing to death in their sleep.
In late-game [Misery](./Misery.md) where healing is impossible, Insomnia has little impact on gameplay, aside from the interrupted sleep.

Much like Cabin Fever, Insomnia is a psychological condition; specifically one that can be diagnosed as an inability to fall asleep or remain asleep for an adequate length of time due to stress or anxiety. However given the nature of the machine located within the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), the electrostatic field it produces seems to upset the body's natural body chemistry, resulting in the inability to sleep.

Like other afflictions, contracting Insomnia results in the player character providing unique audible cues related to their condition. The survivor will complain about being unable to sleep despite being tired.
A [Note](./Note%20%28Forsaken%20Airfield%29.md) can be found from a survivor detailing their desire to leave the area that Glimmer Fog regularly envelopes, due to them being unable to get any sleep.

The **Insulated Flask** (otherwise known as a **Thermos**) is a [Tool](./Tools.md) that was released as part of the free update for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion Part Four.
There are 6 variants in the game, but a 7th is available for players that own the Tales expansion.

An Insulated Flask's primary function acts as both a storage container and an insulator, keeping heated drinks warmer for much longer if placed inside to preserve their [Hot](./Warming%20Up.md) status. Insulated Flasks come in 7 different versions that, aside from aesthetics, all function exactly the same. Selecting the Thermos in the Backpack allows the player to Transfer any drink the player has, Hot or Cold, into the Thermos for storage.

An empty Thermos weighs 0.20 kg, and its storage capacity is 0.80 kg. It is possible to store 8 multiples of the same item type inside a Thermos (such as 8 Reishi Tea weighing 0.10 kg each). This means that the combined maximum weight of a Flask can reach 1.00 kg.

- A Thermos cannot be placed on or near a cooking slot of an active fire to reheat its contents, nor can it be used to melt snow or boil water. If the contents of a Flask go COLD, each item must be removed, reheated at the fire to become HOT again, then reinserted.
- You **CANNOT** drink directly from a Thermos. Any stored contents must be removed from the Thermos to be consumed.
- Storing different types of drinks into a single Thermos is not possible, but drinks can be transferred out to store another desired type of drink at any time.

- When placing an initial drink inside a Thermos, pressing the Transfer button to transfer remaining multiples of the same drink type will always insert the lowest Condition items into the Flask by default.
- Only foods that are capable of being HOT/COLD can be placed inside a Thermos, however not all foods of this type can be placed inside a Flask (ex. [Cooked Potato](./Cooked%20Potato.md), Stews).

- Only an opened can of Tomato Soup can be placed inside a flask, other canned goods cannot put inside ([Canned Corn](./Canned%20Corn.md), [Condensed Milk](./Condensed%20Milk.md), [Dog Food](./Dog%20Food.md), [Pinnacle Peaches](./Pinnacle%20Peaches.md)). It does not matter if the soup has been Cooked.

**Interloper** is the 4th [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) Experience in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is the standard "expert" difficulty setting, being a major departure from the previous 3 Experiences by introducing multiple handicaps to make the game even harder than normal.

Interloper doesn't just raise the difficulty of [Stalker](./Stalker.md) to the next level, but also reduces that overall resource and tool availability in the game world, with several tools and clothing outright never spawning. As such, players are faced with an extremely cold world with limited loot, abundant hostile wildlife, and a smaller loot pool present compared to the other Experiences. Most high quality tools and clothing will never appear in game, making it a necessity to craft and forge animal hide clothing and improvised tools for survival. [Foraging](./Foraging.md) and [Hunting](./Hunting.md) become the main methods to acquire food, as most homes have very little, if any food in them.

Interloper's learning curve is a sharp one, forcing players to relearn how to survive by using more advanced game mechanics, such as [Daisy Chaining](./Daisy%20Chaining.md), [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md), [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md), and [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md).
_A guide for players new to Interloper can be found [here](./Survival%20Mode%20%E2%80%94%20Interloper%20Tips.md)._
- [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) has few items to be found (only ~20% of containers will contain any items).

- Critical items have limitations on their spawn frequency (more details can be found in [this Google Docs spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1sFqnIM9BPeI3ZitcDRekWeWEWfJL7BLyqyirBT3Y53E/edit?gid=0#gid=0))
- [Cardboard Matches](./Cardboard%20Matches.md) never spawn. [Wood Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md) and other fire starters are rare.

- Most tools never spawn: [Hunting Rifles](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Revolvers](./Revolver.md), [Hatchets](./Hatchet.md) and [Hunting Knives](./Hunting%20Knife.md) (and their Improvised Versions), [Bows](./Survival%20Bow.md), [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md), [Flashlights](./Flashlight.md), and [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md).
- The [Spelunker's Lantern](./Spelunker%27s%20Lantern.md) is the only unique item variant which will spawn.

- [Improvised Hatchets](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) and [Improvised Knives](./Improvised%20Knife.md) must be [Forged](./Forge.md) to craft Bows or Arrows. Arrowheads and Broken Arrows may be found rarely, but not Simple Arrows or Bows.
- High-Tier Clothing does not spawn. Many High-Tier Foodstuffs do not spawn (see full list in next section).

- Half of [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) do not spawn on [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), and the remaining ones have downgraded loot (e.g. [Tomato Soup](./Tomato%20Soup.md) instead of [Condensed Milk](./Condensed%20Milk.md)).
- Most of the [Coastal Houses](./Coastal%20House.md) and Cabins in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) are destroyed, providing no shelter and minimal loot.
- [Abandoned Lookout](./Abandoned%20Lookout.md): The 4 Cabins below the Lookout will only have 2 intact Cabins (formerly 3).
- [Bear Creek Campground](./Bear%20Creek%20Campground.md): The Cabin on the hill just south of the Campground (and north west of Fishing Camp) will be destroyed.

- [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md): Of the 11 houses in the town, only 2 will be standing (the one on the hill outside of town will also be destroyed). The [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) will always be intact.

- [Fishing Camp](./Fishing%20Camp.md): The Cabin with the [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) and [Buffer Memory](./Buffer%20Memories.md) laptop is usually destroyed (the same Buffer Memory laptop will appear inside the [Rabbit Grove](./Rabbit%20Grove.md) Cabin instead).
- [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md): The house near the shed and trailer will always be ruined (the trailer can still be used).
- [Waterfront Cottages](./Waterfront%20Cottages.md): The 3 houses here **_always_** spawn as ruined houses.
- Starting equipment is a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) and an incomplete set of low-quality clothing (head and hands will always be exposed).
- Player will randomly start in a small list of predetermined starting regions (cannot spawn in "Beginner" regions).

- The list of possible spawns are: [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), and [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md).

- [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), and [Deer](./Deer.md) are rarer. [Fish](./Ice%20Fishing.md) have up to half the catch-rate (twice as long of wait time at Day 50 survived), and [Wolf](./Wolf.md)/[Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md)/[Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) are extremely deadly (but spawn less frequently than Stalker mode, on par with Voyageur rates/detection).
- Wildlife becomes rarer and the environment colder over time (at Day 10, 25, 50, 100 and 200).

- Rest is a Resource: the survivor cannot sleep above high [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) (95% or greater) levels, except to treat [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md).
- Loot acquired from the 3 [Tales](./Tales.md) will be virtually nonexistent, but they can be completed.
- [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) is present and progresses faster than Stalker mode.
- The option to enable the [Trader](./Trader.md), [Cougar](./Cougar.md), and [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) on or off is present.
- [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md)/[Barb's Rifle](./Barb%27s%20Rifle.md)/[Bunker Rifle](./Bunker%20Rifle.md)/[Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md)/[Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md)

violations.context: **Treatment**
**Treatment:** 2 x [Antibiotics icon](../assets/Antibiotics_icon.png) [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md) every 24 hours

**Alternate Treatment:** 1 x [Reishi Tea icon](../assets/Reishi_Tea_icon.png) [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md)/[Burdock Tea icon](../assets/Burdock_Tea_icon.png) [Burdock Tea](./Burdock%20Tea.md) every 24 hours

**Intestinal Parasites** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) caused by consuming raw or cooked carnivore meat: [Wolves](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), [Cougars](./Cougar.md), and [Bears](./Bear.md).
- It is only active in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) if playing on the Hardened Survivor difficulty.
- The Affliction is also present in the [Challenge](./Challenge.md) [As The Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md).

> “**You ate infected meat and now have Intestinal Parasites. Recovery requires multiple daily treatments! You will continue to weaken until treatment has run its full course. [maximum 1 dose/day.]**”

Intestinal Parasites causes a daily loss of 2% maximum [Condition](./Condition.md) and 4% max [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) until **fully** treated (indicated by a red -%). While this may not seem as severe as other Afflictions, even immediate treatment will result in -20% maximum Condition loss (40% on Interloper/Misery) before being cured. Intestinal Parasites is fatal if it reduces maximum Condition to zero by day 52.5.

Treating Intestinal Parasites requires the player consume 1 [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md)/[Burdock Tea](./Burdock%20Tea.md) or 2 [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md) a day to count as an antibiotics dose.
- Treating Intestinal Parasites on Stalker requires a minimum of 10 Reishi Teas/Burdock Teas, or 20 Antibiotics (10 Doses).
- On Interloper/Misery, it takes 20 days of treatment, meaning 20 Reishi/Burdock Teas or 40 Antibiotics minimum (20 Doses).

The next daily dose always begins at midnight (a new day will begin in the Log section of the [Journal](./Journal.md)), and consuming 2 doses in one day has no effect on the treatment plan, so the player must wait the next day for a new consumed dose to count. It is possible to skip/forget a treatment for a day and still retain treatment progress, but it is always advised to consume a dose daily to develop a routine.

- Playing with the "Endless Night" setting on in Custom will cause the time of day to always remain at midnight. This makes Intestinal Parasites an assured death sentence if contracted, since the day never ends and more doses cannot be consumed, meaning this Affliction cannot be cured.

- When playing on Misery, the Affliction [Sour Stomach](./Sour%20Stomach.md) will removing [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Level 5's benefit of removing [Risk of Intestinal Parasites](./Risk%20of%20Intestinal%20Parasites.md) from cooked predator meat, potentially giving the player Intestinal Parasites again.

Only one instance of Intestinal Parasites can be present at one time, so additional carnivore meat may be consumed while infected at no further parasite risk (although low condition/raw meat may still cause [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md)). In addition to this, this affliction will allow the player to rest as much as they want and whenever they want (even if their Fatigue meter is full), which can be wonderful for Hibernation strategies, rapid healing on higher difficulties (especially if the player has [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md)), and generally passing time in a resource-efficient manner. As an affliction though, it will also prevent the character from using [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md). These powers come at an obvious cost, however, as not sticking to the daily regimen of Antibiotic Doses could easily kill the player, especially on Interloper. While materials for Reishi Tea and Burdock Tea is fairly common throughout Great Bear, Antibiotics are not easily renewable, and as such it is not a recommended strategy to continuously give oneself the affliction.

With a stockpile of Antibiotics/Reishi Tea/Burdock Tea, a strategy is to run the risk and eat 1 (1.00kg) piece of carnivore meat per day. As an example, surviving on carnivore meat for 50 days (without level 5 cooking skill), by eating only one piece of meat per day (with starvation tactics), runs a risk of about 40% chance to contract this affliction at least once (1 - 0.99^50).
- Reaching Level 5 in Cooking **does** **not** remove preexisting risk of developing parasites, or a parasite affliction contracted previously.
- Despite all the types of fish caught from [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) being predatory, none grant Intestinal Parasites Risk when eaten (raw or cooked).

> “**Welcome to Cauldron Island. Lost to history, hiding a mystery. A vast northern chain of islands with 100km+ of railway winding its way across the craggy and desolate landscape, and the abandoned remnants of a once-thriving whaling industry there for you to discover.**”

> — Restore and activate a century-old train to travel deep along this forgotten caldera to uncover a dark secret. What you discover in the end will change how you survive in this Aurora-bathed world, forever. Official Marketing

**_Iron Road_** is [downloadable content](./The%20Long%20Dark.md#Downloadable_Addon_Content) for _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is the Second expansion to the [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) portion of the game, and will be released in 5 major parts over the course of several years.
Early Access launched October 27th, 2026 on Steam only. Updates are planned to be a balance of small and large updates. News regarding other platforms is to be announced.

> “**A century ago, a rich industrialist named Hamish McLeod harnessed the unique properties of Cauldron Island with a plan for economic domination through whale-oil powered technology. But this history was erased, and the dark truth about how things went wrong has been hidden in the past. Until now.**”

> — Get to Cauldron Island and uncover the truth. Follow the path laid by Alice McLeod, his great-granddaughter, who came here to crack the mystery of her family legacy. Because uncovering the mystery of Cauldron Island is core to your survival in this new Aurora-blasted world. And the journey Alice started is yours to complete. Official Marketing
### World and Setting:

- [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) is a chain of five islands located near Great Bear Island, with each one being named after one of McLeod’s daughters: Anna, Stella, Freya, Morag, and Skye. Each island can contain multiple Regions and is connected to the others via a hydraulic train bridge that is disabled until it is unlocked as Early Access unfolds.

- The [“Fulmar” Autopilot Boat](./Fulmar%20Autopilot%20Boat.md) will allow the Survivor to travel between [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) ([Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md)) and [Port Remnant](./Port%20Remnant.md) ([Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md)). Anna Island is always the starting point to the Island.

- Travelling costs 20.00 L of water, 5000 calories of food, 20.00 kg of any fuel, and 5 tinder plugs. The “Fulmar” boat sports a 150.00 kg storage container to carry more gear between trips. The boat must be resupplied for each journey between the 2 major islands.
- A Prototype Steam Train can be found on the Island, and is the fastest and safest way to traverse the new Aurora stricken lands (as well as serving as a mobile base).
- Find Train Repair sheds, Fuel and Water Stations, Switches, and a host of other obstacles and points of interest to explore all related to the Prototype Steam Train.

- Travel across dozens of Track Sections and Exploration Regions (over 100km of dedicated train tracks) throughout the full Cauldron Island landmass, eventually looping around all 5 islands of the caldera.

- The game world now reflects the post [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) [Aurora](./Aurora.md) world: as the player travels deeper into Cauldron Island, new dangers beset the player's health.

- Iron Road features a series of audio collectibles and light narrative missions that provide objectives and motivate your journey across the entirety of Cauldron Island (similar to [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)). Find Wax Cylinders that reveal the history of the caldera and discover more about McLeod's failed operations from a century ago.
- Access to [Anna Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md#Anna_Island) with multiple new Regions:
- 30 kms of track with obstacles, [whale oil refueling stations](./Oil%20Tank.md), [water stations](./Water%20Tower.md), [train switches](./Track%20Switch.md), etc.
- [Wax Cylinder Player](./Wax%20Cylinder%20Player.md), 16 Wax Cylinders, and 4 other Collectibles

The cabin is easiest to access by walking through the [Cove](./Cove.md), up a staircase and through a short cave. From there, walking farther uphill will lead the player to the cottage.

The cottage itself has one main room, with a [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md) and a [Bed](./Bed.md). It does not have a loading screen upon entering. From the cottage's balcony, it is possible to see all the way across Shoulder Lake if the weather is clear enough.

Notable loot includes a possible [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) in the shed just outside, a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) on a [Barrel](./Barrel.md) near the front door, a [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) with three [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) near the back door, and a [Polaroid](./Polaroids.md) on the nightstand next to the bed.
As of the Part 4 Buried echoes update, a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) spawns in the nearby shed.

The cottage itself could make for a potential [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) in the region, as there are a lot of [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) opportunities nearby, as well as a potential [Moose](./Moose.md) spawn on the lake ice below the cabin. [Ptarmigans](./Ptarmigan.md) sparsely flock in the nearby clearing north of the cabin, allowing for further hunting opportunities. Additionally, the cave leading up from the Cove to the cabin is outdoors, yet protected from the wind, making it ideal for cooking the rabbits that were recently [snared](./Trapping.md) (Note that some of the rabbit spawn areas maybe too close to the cabin to allow a snare to work unless you leave the area for an extended period). If [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) becomes an issue, there is a cave located to the north-east; sleeping in a nearby fishing hut is also an option.

Unfortunately, it is not safe from the [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) and [Wolves](./Wolf.md) can frequent the immediate areas around the building. However most of them don't climb up onto the island unless in pursuit of a player.

Much like its other cabin counterpart in the region, the [Mindful Cabin](./Mindful%20Cabin.md), there are no electrical devices within the location, meaning that it will not immediately be obvious that an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) or Glimmer Fog event is active, should the player awaken from sleep after passing time. Luckily the many windows and wide open views should allow the player to spot the potentially dangerous phenomena before venturing far.

**It was THIS Big!** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is obtained after catching a fish weighing greater than five kilograms. Typically, the only fish that can weigh greater than five kilograms is the [Coho Salmon](./Coho%20Salmon%20%28Raw%29.md) and the [Burbot](./Burbot%20%28Raw%29.md). Coho Salmon can only be caught at [Fishing Huts](./Fishing%20Hut.md) (or Free Form Fishing) in saltwater, namely in:

As Burbot is a rare fish, using a [Fishing Lure](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28disambiguation%29.md) improves the chances of catching it. Using [Fishing Bait](./Fishing%20Bait.md) can help increase the chances of getting a sufficiently large fish. However, at skill levels 4 and above, it is possible to catch a [Smallmouth Bass (Raw)](./Smallmouth%20Bass%20%28Raw%29.md) or [Rockfish](./Rockfish%20%28Raw%29.md) weighing over 5kg and get the achievement this way (due to the increased average fish weight effect from level 4 or 5 ice fishing).

> “__A graduate student in astrophysics, Jace normally has her eyes on the stars. Chance, and the Aurora, have brought her to Blackrock.

Whip-smart, Jace has the air of superiority that many academics inherit. But deep down she is starting to worry that her career choice has left her unprepared for the current situation, especially if the power never comes back.__”

Jace is a young graduate student in astrophysics, having come to [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) while staying at the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md) with her thesis professor [Atwood](./Atwood.md). She normally has her sights set on the stars, but unfortunate luck and the [Aurora Borealis](./Aurora.md) of the "[First Flare](./First%20Flare.md)" stopped her car from working while she was driving through [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md). She now finds herself struggling with [Mathis](./Mathis.md), [Donner](./Donner.md), and the other [Convicts](./Convicts.md) of the Penitentiary. Originally deciding to face them from the shadows all by herself, the unexpected arrival of [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) has created mutual aid between the 2 heroes as they both fight to prevent the Convicts from leaving the region.

Endowed with great intelligence, Jace is independent and self-taught, which has enabled her to acquire a great deal of knowledge, particularly in computer security. But deep down, she begins to worry that her career choice hasn't prepared her for the current situation, especially if things will never go back to the way they were before the Quiet Apocalypse.

Jace does not appear in Wintermute until Episode 4, but she is first seen in the Lion's Roar cutscene; sleeping at a computer and slowly waking up as she realizes the whole server room she is in is becoming powered by the Aurora.

Jace makes her first appearance over the phone in the [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) infirmary, asking who Mackenzie is why he is helping the [Convicts](./Convicts.md). Mackenzie states that he is not helping them, in turn asking who the woman on the phone is. The two talk until Jace hangs up, telling the bush pilot to pick a side soon.

Jace appears on the phone again at the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md), properly introducing herself and earning the trust of Mackenzie. The pilot informs her that he's here to restore power to the Prison for the Convicts, but he and Jace know this won't work. Jace then asks Mackenzie to sabotage the locking mechanism to Donner's cell in Solitary to prevent him from getting out.

Jace also reveals that she was driving through the area when the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) hit, causing her car to stop working. She eventually found her way to the prison, hearing the Convicts executing the Prison's staff and deciding her best course of action would be to mess with their plans. Mackenzie eventually agrees to destroy the locking mechanism, with Jace stating that this will act as her "Nuclear option" should things not go their way in the future.

Jace appears over the phone once again, this time in the [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) mine. Mackenzie informs her that he will be delivering [Detonators](./Detonators.md) to the Convicts so they can blow open the cell door to Solitary, freeing Donner. Jace remarks that she now needs to use here "Nuclear option" after this.

Jace also reveals that the reason she is staying to mess with the Convicts is to keep them away from [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), as her thesis professor [Atwood](./Atwood.md) is working near there. She also reveals that she is a grad student in astrophysics, currently on Great Bear Island to study the stars at the Suzuki Radio Telescope. Mackenzie is taken aback, telling Jace that he has a message for Atwood, and that they both need to meet her. Eventually the conversation ends and Mackenzie leaves to deliver the Detonators to Mathis.

Jace is eventually responsible for nudging the Convicts into blowing up the Blackrock Prison, with the Detonators blowing too early and destroying the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) below the Prison. The chain reaction of destruction gives Mackenzie the opportunity to escape Mathis' imminent execution of him, and Jace hacks into the security cameras and controls of the Prison as the Aurora restored power to the Prison. She then turns the prison lockdown on, causing several sliding doors to close and buying the pilot time to escape and retrieve [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md).

Mackenzie escapes to the Warden's office and receives a phone call from Jace, directing the pilot on the best escape route from the Prison and to meet her at the Power Plant through the Steam Tunnels.

The two eventually meet in person for the first time, as Mathis and his gang catch up with them. Having no where else to go, the two attempt to fight Mathis, until Mackenzie pushes the both of them into the river below where they wash ashore down stream. The final scene of the Episode shows the two wet and freezing in the wind. Jace remarks that Mathis and his Convicts will never give up following them now, but Mackenzie tells her that they will not give up either. Mackenzie then offers to start a fire, as Jace is now cold enough to begin feeling warm due to the effects of [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md). The two look at Blackrock Prison, now burning orange in the night sky under the aurora.

- In the intro cutscene to each Episode, Jace can briefly be seen awaking from her slumber during the start of an Aurora. Curiously, her eyebrow piercings are on her left eyebrow, and she has a lip piercing. Whereas in Episode 4, her piercings are on her right eyebrow, and she is missing the lip piercing.
- This was also her first appearance in the game starting in 2017, far before she would actually appear in Episode 4 in 2021.

- A car found near [Blocked Bridge](./Blocked%20Bridge.md) with a [Letter](./Letter%20%28Car%29.md) inside belongs to Jace, and might explain how she came upon the Prison long after the Convicts executed the staff when the First Flare began.

**Jackrabbit Remote Transport** is the family business of the Mackenzie family, originally operated solely by Jack Mackenzie. The transport business runs supplies and people to and from hard-to-reach places isolated in the Canadian wilderness, hence the latter part of the name.

Before the Quiet Apocalypse, [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md), Jack's son, serves as the pilot for the company. He speaks briefly on the phone with a woman named Maureen (who seems to work for or with the company, possibly in administration). It is unknown if the company employs anyone else apart from these two. It is implied by Maureen and Will in combination that the company is financially underperforming due to lack of clients. This might be a result of decreased demand caused by [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md).

The business shows up as a location named **Jackrabbit Hangar** in a short playable section of [Memories](./Memories.md), serving as a safe environment for the player to explore as part of the tutorial.

The company itself plays little role in the game's plot after the mission Memories and exists mainly as a catalyst for the progression of the story. It is not mentioned at all after the first cinematic.
The only remaining reference to the company after the crash is the logo found on the back of [Mackenzie's Parka](./Mackenzie%27s%20Parka.md).

- Despite a common misconception, the word "Air" is not included in the company name. It is seen in the subtitles as "Jackrabbit Remote Air Transport" the first time the name is mentioned by Will in the cinematic at the very beginning of [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md). The audio however, excludes the word "Air," and so does the poster found inside the hangar. When Will comments on the poster he also uses this wording.
- A unique [Insulated Flask](./Insulated%20Flask.md) themed off the company can be found in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).
- Hinterland released a purchasable real world coffee mug based off the Jackrabbit Remote Transport Company.

- The office board contains a photo of [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md), the old [Hinterland Studio Inc.](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md) logo found on the old [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) model, and an old map of Great Bear Island before V1.15 of _The Long Dark_ was released.

Has an interior **Jackrabbit Island** is one of the two larger offshore islands in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), the other being the [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md).

Jackrabbit Island can be reached by traversing over the frozen ice in the bay area of Coastal Highway. The house on the island has ample loot including processed [foods](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), clothing and even a revolver under the bed.

[Old man's beard lichens](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) and [rose hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) can be found on the island. A [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) may be found between the house and the island's northern bank.
As implied by its name, Jackrabbit Island is home to numerous [rabbits](./Rabbit.md). Placing [snares](./Snare.md) on or around the island will yield ample meat for the player for a long time.

Jackrabbit Island is a popular location for a base camp on all difficulty levels. As mentioned before, there are a lot of rabbits on the island, which can be snared, providing a good supply of [meat](./Rabbit%20%28Raw%29.md), pelts, and guts. There's ample storage in the house, and plenty of furniture and curtains to break down for fuel and cloth. If rabbit meat becomes boring, there's lots of [fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) nearby, along with [deer](./Deer.md) and [wolves](./Wolf.md) to hunt -- conveniently, the wolves don't come on the island itself unless actively hunting a rabbit or the player. Workbenches can be found nearby at [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) and [Fishing Camp](./Fishing%20Camp.md), if necessary. Finally, the view from the island on a clear day is spectacular.

The main disadvantage of Jackrabbit Island as a long-term base is its lack of a stove, forcing the player to make campfires outside to cook rabbits and make water. A less obvious disadvantage of the island is that it can be very difficult to find in low visibility conditions. Finally, one challenge with Coastal Highway in general is the lack of warm caves to fight [cabin fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), meaning the player will need to use vehicles or fishing huts to sleep if they catch cabin fever.

**Jane Yang** a major character in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

An old friend of [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md), Jane is a resident of [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) and a native of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). Astrid and Jane appear to have a deep friendship before the events of the game, with the freelance doctor willing to steal a guarded cure and chart a flight to Great Bear Island in order to save the few people of the mysterious plague stricken Mills.
## History
> “**Astrid...it's getting worse. You have to do something. You understand that better than anyone...I'm afraid it's happening again Astrid. I'm afraid we'll lose her this time.**”
Jane is an unseen character that first appears during the events of [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md).

During a flashback sequence showing Astrid working at Seraphim Sleep Research Centre, Jane calls Astrid over the phone. Astrid scolds Jane that it is risky to call her at her place of work, but Jane states that she is scared; pleading with Astrid to hurry and find something of importance located in the Centre as fast as possible. Astrid remarks that it will take time to acquire this item.

Jane asks if Astrid is willing to speak to [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) to chart a flight to the Island, but Astrid hesitantly states she hasn't asked him for help yet. Jane ends the phone call pleading with Astrid to hurry and help soon, stating that "I'm afraid we'll lose her this time". Astrid promises that that won't happen before the flashback ends.
> “**Astrid. You came. You said you would, and you did. But where is the case? Where's the cure?**”

She is seen briefly at the end of [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) in her home town of Perseverance Mills. A quarantine is effecting the town, with Jane running to the docks when she notices two other residents of the town finding what she presumes is another victim of the illnesses afflicting the town. Jane is surprised and relieved to see Astrid has finally come to the town like she promised, but after searching her canoe and asking one of the residents to get the doctor some water, Jane is confused as to why Astrid doesn't have the [Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) with her.
Jane Yang will mostly likely make a major appearance in [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md).

**Jeremiah's Bearskin Coat** is a cut [Clothing](./Clothing.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It can still be experienced by playing older versions of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md). It is still in the Wintermute game files.

The Bearskin Coat was the coat that originally belonged to [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) and was lent to [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) during the mission [Survival School (Predux)](./Survival%20School%20%28Predux%29.md) in the Predux version of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md). Jeremiah would task Mackenzie to go to the [Lookout](./Lookout%20%28Mystery%20Lake%20location%29.md) and find a [Cured Black Bear Hide](./Cured%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md) he had stashed there to dry out, then use it to repair his coat, as part of Mackenzie's survival training. It would later be returned to Jeremiah.

The item is not a collectible, and can be found in the Clothing section of the Backpack, weighing 5.00 kg. The coat itself cannot be worn, nor harvested at any point during the mission. Unlike an actual [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md), Jeremiah's Bearskin Coat requires only a single Cured Black Bear Hide to mend it, and does not have any clothing stats whatsoever.
- Jeremiah is never seen wearing his Bearskin Coat in Episode 1 or 2, only being shown wearing a [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md) in the [What I Know](./What%20I%20Know.md) knowledge page.

- The end of Redux Episode 1 slightly retcons Will's encounter with Jeremiah, as the trapper would briefly be seen wearing his Wolfskin Coat while being attacked by the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md). His Bearskin Coat is not seen again the Redux storyline.

## Use your map to track the bear to his favourite haunts in Mystery Lake.

_The mission starts at the door to [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md). The moment Mackenzie steps out, the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) is waiting for him. _After tracking down and continuously shooting the Old Bear, Mackenzie eventually kills the seemingly invulnerable beast, and cuts [The Old Bear's Ear](./The%20Old%20Bear%27s%20Ear.md) off._

**Jeremiah's Folly** was the fourth mission of the Predux [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).

This mission was poorly received due to its unfair and confusing method of tracking the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md), and has since been replaced by the mission [What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md). Chasing the Old Bear with a Rifle was kept in the Challenge [The Hunted, Part Two](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Two.md) however.

After finishing Jeremiah's Survival School, Mackenzie is now eager to finally leave Mystery Lake in search of Astrid. Jeremiah reels him back in for one more task however, to kill the Old Bear. Mackenzie finally states he has enough of this, as he has Astrid to find, but Jeremiah says that there's something bigger at stake, bigger than Mackenzie finding Astrid, bigger than Jeremiah, and it all begins with killing the Old Bear. Jeremiah then commands Mackenzie to use himself as bait, as bears can smell fresh blood over 20 miles away, and then Mackenzie will be able to take the Old Bear once and for all. Mackenzie agrees to help the crazy trapper one last time, grabs his rifle, makes his way to the door, and then turns around, cutting his left hand with [Jeremiah's Knife](./Jeremiah%27s%20Knife.md) and showing his hand to Jeremiah.

After the cutscene ends, IMMEDIATLY arm yourself with the Hunting Rifle, as the Old Bear will be outside the Trapper's Homestead the moment you step outside. There is no warning for this, so to avoid being mauled, have your rifle ready, remove any clothing you don't want ruined, and have some [Bandages](./Bandage.md) on stand by, and make sure you are fully rested for what is to come. You may also notice that 8 [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) has been added to your inventory.

Step outside and unload into the Old Bear, who has somehow already tracked you down, and wait for it to flee. You will most likely be mauled so either allow it to happen or find a place to run and hide where the bear cannot reach you. If you are mauled, then when you wake up the Old Bear will be gone, so tend to your wounds and begin tracking the beast by looking for fresh blood and footprints in the snow.

Each shot into the Old Bear will not harm the bear, but instead the game tracks how many times you have harmed the bear at it's favorite encounter locations. Check your map for Exclamation Points labeled "Possible Old Bear Location" and head there. The following are the 6 haunts the Old Bear will go to, with the order shown below more or less the path he takes as he flees:

The Old Bear will be at one of these spots, so it is critical that you don't lose track of the bear's trail after wounding it. Continue firing at the bear until it runs away, and when he does, he will not stop running until he reaches one of his other encounter locations. If you lose his tracks in the snow, take a mental note of what direction he was last seen heading, and then look at your "Possible Old Bear Location" on your map, then head there next.

Jeremiah's advice to fire only when it gets close to heart is very iffy at best, as attacking the Old Bear from far away so that it flees rather than engages you works more often than not. Always shoot the bear in the head, otherwise it will not flee. The beast will see you when you get close enough even if you do not provoke him, so steel yourself and wait for it to get close before firing. If you fire too early, then you may get mauled before Mackenzie can cycle the next round into your rifle. If you do hit the bear at the right distance up close, then it will run off to another nearby encounter location while also adding a point to your "Bear Encounters" checklist. Damaging the Old Bear while it is still inside the encounter area multiple times adds a point to the counter.

This hunt can take several days in game to track and kill the beast if you lose his tracks in the snow or are mauled multiple times. The game will continue add ammunition to your backpack (replenishing any rounds not in your gun up to 10 rounds) without telling you, so don't worry about ammunition. Rest up after encounters and remember the last location where the bear could have gone. Try not to sprint to the next location and wear yourself out if you drive him to the next location, patience is a virtue. You can also quicksave the game the moment you see the Old Bear, to save time in case of failure.
After your "Bear Encounters" checklist reaches the maximum amount, the bear will die on the spot and the weather will automatically become foggy (the game will LAG for a moment).

Interact with the slain beast's carcass and take [The Old Bear's Ear](./The%20Old%20Bear%27s%20Ear.md). Harvesting the pelt is meaningless since the Episode will end after the next mission, but take the [Bear Meat (Raw)](./Bear%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md) if you need food. Return to Jeremiah and Mackenzie will throw the bear's ear into the trapper's lap, proving that he prevailed in the hunt and impatiently asking if he can finally leave the area. Jeremiah laments that the Old Bear is dead, expressing his grief that he's "actually gonna miss that guy," only for Mackenzie to quip that he can visit and talk to him some time, as he wants Jeremiah to do something to help him escape Mystery Lake.

Jeremiah finally tells Mackenzie how to escape the region, go through the guts of the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), follow the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) on the other side to a place called [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), then find a radio station called [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md). Jeremiah can't guarantee that the Aurora will power the station, but it will be powerful enough to reach [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) if it works. Then follow the signs to Perseverance Mills, though this will take days to walk there on foot.

Mackenzie is bewildered as to why Jeremiah didn't just tell him this before, considering how easy this task sounds. This is when Jeremiah reveals that the whole plot to kill the Old Bear was only to prove that Mackenzie was strong enough to reach Perseverance Mills, with a message in tow; "Wintermute." The Trapper begs Mackenzie to find someone living in a cabin in the hills near the town named [Atwood](./Atwood.md), as this message is of utmost importance that it gets out, to the point where Jeremiah prepares to leave the cabin in his injured state to deliver it himself before collapsing. Mackenzie agrees to take the message with him and Jeremiah gives Mackenzie the code to unlocking the powered door inside the Carter Dam, 7611. Mackenzie asks if the trapper needs any more help before he leaves, but Jeremiah declines, wishing Mackenzie that he hopes "She has more sense than you." Mackenzie doesn't remember revealing that his friend he is searching for was a she, but the coy trapper deduced that due to Mackenzie's wedding ring and the look in his eye when talking about her, his friend must have been a woman. Mackenzie tells the hermit to take care of himself, before leaving with the door closing behind him. Jeremiah then states that he has his own path to tread, before getting out of bed and opening a panel in the floorboards containing a ham radio, and flipping the power switch on it.
Several plot points and locations have been replaced/altered since the Redux re-release of Episode 2:

- This entire mission was cut from the game, and was instead replaced by the mission [What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md). Rather than hunting the Old Bear, the Old Bear now hunts you, before Mackenzie finds the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) and turns the tables on the Old Bear.

- [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) would be the one to use the [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) to get a message out to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md)

- After Mackenzie leaves, Jeremiah opens a panel in the floorboards containing a ham radio. This plot point was reworked into the open, with the radio being present from the start of the Redux Episode 2 and serving as the way that Jeremiah originally tries to get the message Wintermute out.
- Added to game.

**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**
> “**Jeremiah has told you about the location of a hidden bunker in Forlorn Muskeg. There are some letters there he wants you to burn for him.**”

**Jeremiah's Hideout** was a side mission of the Predux [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).

To start the side mission, Mackenzie has to raise the Trust of [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) to the maximum of 375 points and speak to him about Old Letters. He will ask Mackenzie for a favor, to find a hidden bunker of his and burn some old letters between himself and an old correspondent. Mackenzie will ask why an old misanthropic trapper is out here with his own bunker writing letters to someone, but Jeremiah deflects the question. Jeremiah then gives Mackenzie a code, the location of the bunker, and asks him to burn the letters found inside (but no peaking at the letters as they "won't do you any good") and to keep anything else he finds inside the bunker as payment for this favor.

The hideout is located in Forlorn Muskeg in the northern part of the map, slightly northeast behind the [Shortwave Tower](./Shortwave%20Tower.md). The hideout is an advanced version of a [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md), with the most notable difference being two red lights on top of the hatch that only power hatch door during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md).

This mission can be unlocked as early as [You Fix My Rifle?](./You%20Fix%20My%20Rifle%3F.md) by making your way to [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) and fixing [Jeremiah's Broken Rifle](./Jeremiah%27s%20Broken%20Rifle.md) to unlock the Aurora. Return to the hatch at a later date and wait for an Aurora to occur (This can take several nights). One good way to trigger the Aurora is to either head to the hatch after repairing the broken rifle and looting the [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) and [Hunting Lodge Rifle](./Hunting%20Lodge%20Rifle.md), then making your way to the hatch, or to wait until the mission [Renewed Hope](./Renewed%20Hope%20%28Predux%29.md) while waiting for the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) to be powered up, then running to the hatch.

When an Aurora is in the sky, go inside and you will see the hallway to the back of the hideout is filled with live wires. Wait for the Aurora to pass if you want to safely pass over them, though this will lock the hatch door behind you (though you have plenty of supplies on your side of the bunker to last until the next Aurora). You can choose to run across the hot wires with with 100% [Condition](./Condition.md) but you will get at least 3 [Burns](./Burns.md) if you do, make sure to turn the Switch Box off to disable the live wires.
Find [Jeremiah's Papers](./Jeremiah%27s%20Papers.md) sitting on the desk before you and leave the hatch.

Now start a fire anywhere and select Jeremiah's Papers as the fuel. Use an [Accelerant](./Accelerant.md) if you need to. Successfully start the fire and the mission will be completed. Mackenzie will then remark "I'd better stay focused on finding Astrid. It's time I got going."
- The side mission is now activated after finding the [Aurora Hatch Door Entry Code](./Aurora%20Hatch%20Door%20Entry%20Code.md) note
- A door separates the corridor to the back room, and requires a code to be input first

**Jeremiah's Knife** was a tool in pre-redux [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) from [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md). it was removed in the 2018 Redux release of Episode 2.

Jeremiah's knife functions identically to a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md): a self-defense tool, harvesting [animal](./Wildlife.md) carcasses, [Cloth](./Cloth.md) from curtains/pillows, tinder from cardboard, breaking ice for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md), and crafting at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md).

It was given to [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) after graduating from Jeremiah's [Survival School (Predux)](./Survival%20School%20%28Predux%29.md), and is used by Mackenzie to cut his hand to make the scent from his blood attract the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) to his position, in order for him to kill it.
It was removed during the Redux of Wintermute: Episodes 1 and 2 and is now unobtainable, but is still present in the Wintermute game files.
Jeremiah's knife can be repaired with a [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md) and the [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) skill, restoring 3% condition to the knife.
Jeremiah's Knife cannot be equipped, but may be selected to defend one's self at the start of a [Wolf](./Wolf.md) [Struggle](./Struggle.md), causing it some Condition damage.

- On December 3rd, 2023, Jeremiah's Knife can be seen at 5:00 in the Part 4: Buried Echoes update for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) (as seen in the video below). The knife, however, was not released in the update. This is the first time the knife has officially been seen since its removal in 2018.

> “**A tough old trapper and hermit. Lives alone in the wilderness of Mystery Lake. Doesn't seem to like people much.**”
**Jeremiah** (Also known as **John**) is the primary non-player character in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).

At the end of Episode 1, [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) enters [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) and encounters Jeremiah being disarmed and attacked by the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md). While The Old Bear mauls him, Will arms himself with Jeremiah's [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md). The screen turns black a gunshot rings out as Will shoots the beast.
Will then rescues and stabilizes the trapper in his nearby cabin in between Episode 1 and 2.

Jeremiah regains consciousness to find himself being cared for by Will inside [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md), but is delirious from an infection from the bear attack. To save Jeremiah's life, Will retrieves [antibiotics](./Carter%20Hydro%20Medical%20Supplies.md) and some [Radio Parts](./Radio%20Parts.md) from [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), however The Old Bear follows Will, who barely manages to escape. Jeremiah stabilizes but is too ill for travel, as he desperately needs to get a message out. He and Will agree to radio Perseverance Mills, however Jeremiah's radio was damaged by [The First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) and requires replacement parts, and The Old Bear is still stalking them both.

Jeremiah relays a tale during [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md)'s settling days, of a neigh-invincible "demon bear" and the settler from [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) who slew it with a [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md). He then details his own efforts to kill the Old Bear they face has survived many of his own efforts to kill it. Jeremiah suggests Will find this spear to defend himself while he tinkers with the radio.

Will survives another encounter with The Old Bear, and meets [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) again, this time during an active [aurora](./Aurora.md) along with aurora wolves. Finding and repairing the Bear Spear, Will encounters the Old Bear as he returns to Jeremiah.

Will presents the Spear to Jeremiah, who reveals that he barely got the radio to work during the Aurora the other night, and he needs a stronger signal. He commands Mackenzie to collect the [Transponder Parts](./Transponder%20Parts.md) from 3 Shortwave towers in Forlorn Muskeg to boost the signal, which Mackenzie reluctantly agrees to do.

After collecting the radio components and getting mauled by The Old Bear and dragged off to his cave, Mackenzie kills the beast with the spear. He returns to the Trapper's Homestead but collapses from exhaustion with the Transponder parts.

Jeremiah repairs the radio as Mackenzie sleeps, allowing Will the honors of reaching [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) in search of his [ex-wife](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) once he wakes. Mackenzie tries to contact the Mills but the aurora overloads and destroys the radio, denying Jeremiah the chance to send his own message out along with it. With no means to contact Perseverance Mills, and Jeremiah still too ill for travel, he insists that Mackenzie travel in his stead to deliver the message "Wintermute" to a woman named [Atwood](./Atwood.md) near the Mills. Jeremiah states that he has a small mission he needs to attend to now that the Old Bear is dead, and will tend to it after a few more days of rest.
Jeremiah is not see again for the rest of the Episode after Mackenzie leaves the cabin.
Jeremiah does not appear in the Episode, but his voice is heard in the intro recap regarding Atwood and the message Wintermute.

Jeremiah indicates having a military background from conversations about his technical expertise, model of radio, and the mysterious relay towers in Forlorn Muskeg. However he refuses to elaborate on his out of place knowledge, revealing that he hides more to his background than he lets on.
- Based on his location in a remote island in Canada and his Enfield-style rifle, he may have been a member of the Canadian Rangers, but this can't be confirmed.

- Jeremiah's voice actor is David Hayter, most famous for his role as Solid Snake from the Metal Gear franchise. Similarly to Jeremiah, after the events of Metal Gear 2, Solid Snake retires from his duty to the Arctic, though he retreats to Alaska and raises sled dogs instead.
- He happens to own a military grade shortwave radio as well as military cartography maps of Great Bear Island, with Mackenzie noticing this and Jeremiah constantly deflecting these facts.
- He often uses the term "clicks" instead of kilometers, a common military term (though [Jace](./Jace.md) also uses "clicks").

- Jeremiah states that there's no reason to stay on Great Bear Island after [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md), and that the only reason people would stay is to hide from something. Mackenzie asks what Jeremiah is doing on the Island then, with the Trapper only responding with "I have my reasons".
- Jeremiah originally had a [hideout bunker](./Jeremiah%27s%20Hideout.md) all to himself before it was cut in the Redux version.

- Despite being a supposedly lonely trapper that spends most of his time trapping and drying furs, Jeremiah seems to have connections and frequent conversations with other individuals. (ex. [Atwood](./Atwood.md), [Jeremiah's Papers](./Jeremiah%27s%20Papers.md) before they were cut)

It is eventually revealed in Episode 5 that Jeremiah served in the Canadian Military, and was later tried and sent to a Military Prison due to ilegally accessing classified NATO documents. Despite this, he would eventually be released, stopping once at the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md) before leaving for Mystery Lake.
- The iconic Trapper's Homestead of Mystery Lake seems to be Jeremiah's home, suggesting his profession to be a fur trapper, as well as his fur-based attire. A list of his belongings include:
- [Jeremiah's Hideout](./Jeremiah%27s%20Hideout.md) and [Jeremiah's Papers](./Jeremiah%27s%20Papers.md) (cut)

- Jeremiah seems to enjoy [Pork and Beans](./Pork%20and%20Beans.md), with his cabin being filled with them and the fact that his [Trust](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md#Trust) can be raised by donating some to him in the Predux version of Episode 2. Several other places across the region, the [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) and [Lookout (Mystery Lake location)](./Lookout%20%28Mystery%20Lake%20location%29.md) specifically, have been frequented by him and are littered with empty Pork and Beans cans.

- Jeremiah is seen wearing a Wolfskin Coat in his artwork, but never wear one in Predux Episode 1 or 2. The Redux version would change this, as he wears the outfit briefly at the end of Redux Episode 1.

- Jeremiah's outfit also includes a [Wolfskin Hat](./Wolfskin%20Hat.md) and [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md). The Wolfskin Hat would, interesting enough, not be introduced as a clothing item until the Part 6 [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) update 7 years after Jeremiah was introduced.

- Jeremiah would occasionally be seen by other people on the Island in 2 [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) (2 files mention him in the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), 1 file by [Breyerhouse](./Breyerhouse.md) in the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md)).

- Jeremiah also mention in Predux Episode 2 visiting Rupert's Landing to trade occasionally, and would work at the Maintenance Yard in exchange for time spent using their tools. It can be presumed that these details are no longer canon however.
- In Episode 5, his real name is revealed to be "John". [Molly](./Molly.md) also refers to him as "Jerry" on one occasion.

A **Jerry Can** is a large container that can hold up to 4 liters (1.05 Gallons) of [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md).
Unlike cans of Lantern Fuel, Jerry Cans are not spontaneously generated. They can only be found in the world, and a Jerry Can disappears after its contents have been used up.
Jerry Cans are noticeably more weight to fuel efficient per kilogram than Lantern Fuel, weighing only 0.40 kg per 0.50 liters collected, while Lantern Fuel weighs 0.50 kg per 0.50 Liters collected.

A Jerry Can in the player's inventory will collect any Lantern Fuel created from cooking fish (if the can is not full), preventing the spontaneous generation of a bottle of Lantern Fuel. It will also collect kerosene from harvesting a [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md). When multiple Jerry Cans are in the player's inventory, the can with the smallest used volume is filled first.

Refueling a lantern with both a Jerry Can and Lantern Fuel in the player's inventory will use the Jerry Can first. Therefore it is best to drop the Jerry Can before refueling so the Lantern Fuel is used first.
- [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md): on a pallet near the opening of the garage
- [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) middle level (accessible during aurora)
- When trading with [Sutherland the Trader](./Trader.md) Jerry Cans are **not returned** if traded for Lamp Oil.

> “**The Forest Talkers have been raiding Joplin's prepper caches. Whatever supplies remain could help you survive Pleasant Valley long enough to find a way out. Search the caches to see what's left.**”

**Joplin's Bunker Raid** is a side mission in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) must search for bunkers scattered throughout Pleasant Valley.

Each bunker contains a large amount of supplies, which varies slightly but generally contains food, [flares](./Flare.md), [revolver ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md), [rifle ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), [flare shells](./Flare%20Shell.md), and [kerosene](./Kerosene.md). The bunkers are useful particularly when completing the [Coming Storm](./Coming%20Storm.md) mission.

- [Forest Talker Bunker Memo](./Forest%20Talker%20Bunker%20Memo.md) is located in the [Rural Store](./Rural%20Store.md) of [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) on Green and Capable Survivor difficulty. On Hardened Survivor, the note is found in a backpack next to a corpse at the [Derelict Cabins](./Derelict%20Cabins.md).
- [Joplin's Journal, Part One](./Joplin%27s%20Journal%2C%20Part%20One.md) is located inside a duct in the bunker near [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md)
- [Joplin's Journal, Part Two](./Joplin%27s%20Journal%2C%20Part%20Two.md) is located in the bunker near [Three Strikes Farmstead](./Three%20Strikes%20Farmstead.md)
