violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: **Contents**

As the player travels across the various [regions](./Region.md) of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) while playing _The Long Dark_, they will frequently come across named **locations** within a region. These locations may be shelters, unique landscape features, or other points of interest (POIs).

The form and contents of any given named location can vary dramatically. Some locations are merely notable landmarks, which generally have few supplies and little to no shelter, but can still help the player navigate the area. Other locations may be caves, which fall into two categories: shallow caves without a loading screen, and larger caves, such as [Misty Falls Cave](./Misty%20Falls%20Cave.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), which do provide a loading screen. Shallow caves often provide some shelter and a few supplies. However, the player should beware of [predators that may already call the cave home](./Bear.md), especially if there are bones scattered in the cave. Underprepared players can also freeze to death in shallow caves, especially during night-time blizzards. Named caves are _usually_ safe from predators, though this isn't a hard and fast rule.

Caves with a loading screen are usually warm enough to keep even a poorly equipped player from freezing, and are safe from predators, with a [notable exception](./Cave%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md) in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md). Generally, the safest (or, at least, best stocked) locations are buildings, which generally have a constant indoor temperature, along with relatively abundant supplies, beds, stoves, work benches, and other amenities. Usually, the player will be safe upon entering a building, though there is [one notable exception](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md). In some cases, there may be a group of buildings clustered together, making a town/settlement: 5 examples are [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), [Milton](./Milton.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), [Field 31](./Field%2031.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), and [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) in [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md). And, while wolves may patrol these areas, the abundance of buildings and vehicles makes it easier to escape from predators.

Because each playthrough has semi-random equipment and loot spawns, there is no guarantee which locations will have the best gear each game. However, as a general rule, locations that are off the beaten path or that are major sites on the map are likely to have the rarer loot in the game. Sometimes, supplies can be found in un-named locations, as well.

| - Ash Canyon - Blackrock - Bleak Inlet - Broken Railroad - Coastal Highway - Desolation Point - Forlorn Muskeg | - Hushed River Valley - Mountain Town - Mystery Lake - Pleasant Valley - Timberwolf Mountain |
| - Crumbling Highway - Keeper's Pass North - Keeper's Pass South - The Ravine | - [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) (Only has 2 Region Transition Icons but no named locations) |

A **Locker** can be found in many places in the game, generally industrial-like places, and serves as a container for storing items. Some Lockers are locked and require a [Prybar](./Prybar.md) to open. Lockers are one of the most common containers found in the game, along with the metal and plastic containers.
There are 4 variants of lockers; Single, Double, and Triple Lockers, and a single Green Locker.
- The locked locker requires a Prybar to open, and generally contains mid to high-tier loot.
- The [broken locker](./Metal%20Shelf.md) can be broken down by a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) for [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), and cannot be searched.

- A green locker with a "5" painted onto the front can be found in forestry locations such as the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) and the [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md). These are often locked but have a chance to spawn opened.
Occasionally 5th type of locker, a [Medical Locker](./Medical%20Locker.md), can be found, and only contains [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) supplies.

Has an interior The**Logging Camp** is a collection of several small trailers, presumably to shelter the loggers who once worked in the nearby [Clearcut](./Clearcut.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md).
The camp consists of three small, temporary prefabricated trailer structures and a ruined building.

Valuable supplies can be scavenged from inside the camp, including warm clothes, food, many items that can be scrapped for cloth, and a [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md). All the trailers have [bunk beds](./Bed.md). The ruined building may have a [hatchet](./Hatchet.md), a [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), firewood, and a [wood stove](./Wood%20Stove.md).

The camp may make a fine temporary base, as it has many beds and access to plenty of firewood in the vicinity. However, there is no [work bench](./Work%20Bench.md), and only a small stove is available in the dilapidated building. The player must also be wary of [wolves](./Wolf.md) lurking nearby.

The **Lone Lake Cabin** is the unofficial name given to a single cabin in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md).

Some supplies can be found inside the cabin, which also provides good protection from the elements. The cabin has a bunk bed. Occasionally, a hunting rifle and a Frozen Corpse can be found behind the cabin.
A possible [bear](./Bear.md) and a cave may spawn north of the cabin. For players wishing to hunt the bear, the cabin can make a good place to cure the bear's guts and hide.

It is only a short distance from the cave connecting the region to [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) as the [crow](./Crow.md) flies, but it is on a mountain and requires a long walk to actually get there. From the transition cave take the right fork away from [Cloudtop Falls](./Cloudtop%20Falls.md) under a fallen tree bridge (which you will later cross). Then keep right until coming to a [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section and climb up. After passing an entrance to the [Ice Cave](./Ice%20Cave.md) on the right, just follow the path straight to the cave. Balancing over a fallen tree bridge will be required near the end. A [hatchet](./Hatchet.md) will be required to clear some [Scrub Brush](./Scrub%20Brush.md) that's blocking the path.

This non-explorable cave possibly contains a flare gun and several flare shells, some food, matches, antibiotics, cedar/fir firewood, and a burned-out campfire. Although very safe from hostile wildlife, it is located far from any [Rabbit Grove](./Rabbit%20Grove.md) or [deer](./Deer.md) spawn, making it rather unsuitable for use as a long-term base.
Other nearby locations include a [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) and a [Plane Crash](./Plane%20Crashes.md) a short distance to the west.

The **Lonely Lighthouse** is a red-striped white tower that both provides visibility of surrounding landscapes and serves as an easily spotted landmark.

The lighthouse is accessible from the road by crossing two wooden footbridges, which lead to the small, jagged island on which the lighthouse rests. The little island may feature some medicinal plants, but the base and surrounding areas are mostly barren and are often patrolled by wolves. A [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) may be found on a nearby cliff face, and a decent amount of supplies can be looted from inside the lighthouse.

The frozen harbor area to the east features little of note except several rowboats on the shore, which may contain loot within or near them. The area around the boats is also patrolled by one or two [wolves](./Wolf.md) and sometimes [deer](./Deer.md) and/or their carcasses can be seen to the west.

The lighthouse can be used as a [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) for the player, as it has a [bed](./Bed.md) and a [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), and is not too far away from [The Riken's](./The%20Riken.md) [forge](./Forge.md). However, unlike [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) a short walk to the north, it contains no [workbench](./Work%20Bench.md). Rabbits can be found not too far away at the [Stone Church](./Stone%20Church.md) or [Little Island](./Little%20Island.md), and deer can be found at Little Island or a short walk west of the lighthouse. The major disadvantage of living here, however, is that [wolves](./Wolf.md) frequently spawn near the intersection of the road leading to the lighthouse from the main highway, making entering or leaving difficult. This is especially true if the player is carrying fresh meat back home.

The Lighthouse has four floors and a catwalk. The ground floor is a small room with a decent amount of storage, a computer, and a pot belly stove. There is a bed on the second floor, and a radio. The third floor includes three lockers, a metal container, and some wooden boxes and pallets. The fourth floor provides access to the roof hatch, as well as containing the drive mechanism (uninteractable, but mentioned in a buffer memory on the computer downstairs). The top part of the lighthouse consists of the lantern room and surrounding metal catwalk (called a gallery).

The top is considered outside, and the player will go through a loading screen whenever passing through the hatch. The lamp in the lantern room is not interactable, but will light up during an aurora, providing an enormous amount of light and illuminating everything in a radius as far as [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md).

Depending on the difficulty, on the catwalk you may find a few [rifle rounds](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), and, in clear weather, you get an outstanding view of the road, the surrounding sea, [Abandoned Mine No. 5](./Abandoned%20Mine%20No.%205.md), part of the [Stone Church](./Stone%20Church.md) and [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md).
_Looking northeast towards [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) and [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md)._

Provides some shelter **Long Bridge** is a highway bridge that connects both sides of the region safely. It is lined by several broken down vehicles and an overturned semi truck trailer. While offering limited protection from the cold, the vehicles can offer temporary emergency shelter.

Although the player could walk under the bridge, the safest way is to walk over it to avoid thin ice. The western end connects near the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) and the east end connects near the [Cannery worker residences](./Cannery%20Worker%20Residences.md). Some cars and a fallen truck sit on the bridge, providing shelter, loot and a good supply of [Car Batteries](./Car%20Battery.md). The bridge can be spotted from the [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md) very clearly.

Long Curve is located at the far western end of the region. The closest indoor location is [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) to the south-east up the large hill.

Several [Cars](./Car.md) sit alongside the road, which may contain a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md). Further down the road [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) and a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) may be found.

At the end of the road is the entrance to [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), which in turn leads to [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md) through an ice cave. Beyond these transitions is the [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) region.

- Originally, the road continued west from here to Keeper's Pass South and later [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), emerging near the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md). However, since the tunnel collapsed, it's impossible to connect directly between Pleasant Valley and Mountain Town.
- This is evidenced by [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) having crawled through the tunnel and being found near here by [Molly](./Molly.md) in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md).

- With the release of Episode 4, the above theory has been confirmed, as heading from here towards [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) leads to [Mirthless Fork](./Mirthless%20Fork.md), from which it was originally possible to go either towards [Milton](./Milton.md) or [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md).
- Due to the collapse of the tunnel, it is currently only possible to travel towards Blackrock from here.

The **loot table** is a gameplay mechanic in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) which determines where certain items spawn in a given sandbox (game).

Every Survival Mode sandbox belongs to one of four loot tables. There is a standard numbering to the four loot tables (numbered 1-4). If your game is on Loot Table 2, then it will be on Loot Table 2 across every region, and remain on Loot Table 2 even if you [Cheat Death](./Cheat%20Death.md).

The loot table system is active regardless of sandbox difficulty. It is common for [Interloper](./Interloper.md) and [Misery](./Misery.md) players to identify which loot table their game is on so that they can quickly find crucial loot. For example, finding a hammer in [Molly's Barn](./Barn%20%28Molly%27s%29.md) means that you are on Loot Table 1, which guarantees that you can find a [magnifying lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) in the [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) basement and a [firestriker](./Firestriker.md) in [Abandoned Mine No. 5](./Abandoned%20Mine%20No.%205.md).

Note: the following tables were compiled for [Interloper](./Interloper.md) players; games on difficulties other than [Interloper](./Interloper.md) and [Misery](./Misery.md) may have more spawns than those below.

> “**Find out what happened to the lost power workers. Search their last noted work locations.**”
To start the mission, the player must find the [Old Substation Work Memo](./Old%20Substation%20Work%20Memo.md) on a bench right inside the [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md).

- Worker 1 is at the bottom of the ravine near Blackrock prison, to reach him climb down the two rosehip roots/rocks near the bridge leading to [Cook's Farm](./Cook%27s%20Farm.md) and then continue upstream. It is impossible to reach this place in story mode by going downstream from the mine. His [Backpack](./Backpack.md) contains [Power Company ID](./Power%20Company%20ID.md) identifying the worker as Samual Franks, Journeyman Electrician and his corpse holds [Lost Worker's Note](./Lost%20Worker%27s%20Note.md).

- Worker 2 is located in the trailer up the road from the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md) right where the map points. To get to the trailer climb up the rosebush/roots and then before crossing the ravine over the second tree, make a sharp 180° turn and on the left side you should be able to climb up a steep path and then cross 2 fallen trees, then walk through the (top) rock arch and continue left. The corpse inside is dead via heavy bleeding from her arm and her corpse contains a Power Company ID identifying her as Linda Burnley, Journeyman Electrician.

- Due to the [Revolver](./Revolver.md) she carries with 3 cartridges inside, a bloody bandage, a spare bandage nearby, and the large amount of blood on the ground, it may be presumed that she was attacked by wildlife or shot herself after the [Convicts](./Convicts.md) overtook the Prison. She may have also have been shot by Samual for unknown reasons (likely memory issues).
- Worker 1 has no gameplay-affecting loot nearby, his ID is in a backpack further downstream.
- ~69% Condition [Revolver](./Revolver.md) + 3x [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md) loaded inside

**Lost and Found** are a special type of container in _The Long Dark_. They look like a [metal container](./Metal%20Container.md), but are red in colour and have the [Hinterland](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md) logo on its cover and tin, and do not naturally spawn in the game world.[^1]

Lost and Found containers spawn in [Regions](./Region.md) or indoors locations when the player loses items because of a game update or glitch (eg, containers or terrain are altered during an update, items fall through the map, or the player falls victim to the disappearing-travois bug). A Lost and Found container will spawn containing the lost items near the doors of indoor locations and near major buildings/areas in outdoor areas.

Lost and Found containers are unique in that they do not naturally generate upon world creation (like most containers do), and cannot be created by the player (such as [Rock Caches](./Rock%20Cache.md)). They will be present only when a relevant glitch has occurred. Lost and Found are also unique in that items cannot be placed inside them, only removed. Once a Lost and Found is emptied, it will despawn upon reloading the location.

Lost and Found containers were first introduced in the [Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) update. Upon introduction, Lost and Found containers would spawn in [Regions](./Region.md) or indoors locations which were explored in the current savefile in a previous version of the game, and were subsequently altered in an [update](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog.md). The reason for the existence of these containers is to prevent players from losing items when regions are altered in the previous update (Example, furniture is moved with items on them/Containers removed with items in them).

- Lost and Found generate inside of maps (Regions or indoors locations/caves with a Loading Transition) directly beside their entry point. For locations with multiple entry points, only one Lost and Found will be present at one of them.

- Prior to the implementation of the "Lost and Found" system, in previous updates to Regions or locations items could become inaccessible inside/outside/above map geometry or concealed by added/relocated doodads (such as indestructible furniture).
- Hinterlands logos are present on two objects in-game: Lost and Found containers and [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md).

Low blind is located north of the railway on the end opposite the rail tunnel leading [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md). It contains a small amount of loot and is poorly sheltered - if you spend the night there, make sure that you have proper clothing or a campfire. However, it makes for a good hunting spot, as [deer](./Deer.md) and [wolves](./Wolf.md) are nearby and predators cannot get into the blind. The [Abandoned Camp](./Abandoned%20Camp.md) can spawn north west from it.

**Mackenzie's Crashed Plane**is a location featured in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). It is the wreckage of [Will Mackenzie's](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) airplane after he and [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) crashed in the mountains of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).

The crash site contains an ample amount of [Cloth](./Cloth.md) and [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md). The crates from the plane can be broken down for more wood, and they can contain items such as [books](./Book.md) and [newsprint](./Newsprint.md). Various other supplies can be found scattered around the plane and amidst its debris. There is a little [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) below with a makeshift bed and a fire camp, but it is not deep enough to have a warm interior, it only shields from the wind. Don't be afraid of the yellowing skeletons inside; there is no bear in the area.
A [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md), along with various supplies, is found in the ravine below the plane, along with a possible revolver spawn.

Will Mackenzie is piloting the plane with Dr. Astrid Greenwood as his passenger when the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) strikes. As a result, the plane loses all power and crashes into the mountains, becoming lodged in between two trees on the edge of a deep ravine. Will is ejected from the plane and ends up at the bottom of the ravine, along with a great deal of debris, but he manages to survive and make his way back to the plane. He is forced to abandon the plane in order to search for Astrid, who has already fled the area the night before. The plane ends up crashing in the mountains above [Milton](./Milton.md).
The location is simply named **Crashed Plane** in Survival Mode, and is the location of the [Jackrabbit Hangar](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md) [Insulated Flask](./Insulated%20Flask.md).
- The plane itself is a dark yellow [de Havilland Beaver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Havilland_Canada_DHC-2_Beaver) with floats.
- There is more Debris screwn across the mountain and ravine in this location than should belong to the plane, though this is likely to make the crash look more dramatic.
_The wreckage of the plane that serves as the setting for the beginning of [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md)._

A Magnifying Lens is a [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) [Tool](./Tools.md) used to start [fires](./Fire.md), but certain criteria must be met before it can be used, unlike other Fire Starters.

- The [Weather](./Weather.md) must be clear and sunny (wind conditions do not matter, unless attempting to start a [Campfire](./Campfire.md) during harsh winds). A Magnifying Lens cannot be used when the weather is overcast, foggy, etc.

- Fires can be started inside the front of a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) with a Magnifying Lens, but they cannot be started in the back of the cave with a Lens. The player can, however, place a fire in the back of the cave by standing in the front of the cave and starting a Campfire.
- Magnifying lens can be used to directly start fire in oven inside a fishing hut, as it is considered an outdoors area.
The probability of igniting a fire with a magnifying lens is increased by 5% over the base chance. It weighs 0.10 kilograms.
Magnifying lenses are relatively uncommon, and even if present, may be hidden on top of or underneath shelves, beds, racks, inside cars, or in other niches, making them harder to notice.

The Magnifying Lens cannot be crafted, harvested, or repaired, and its condition does not degrade. A Magnifying Lens is useless if used during a [Custom](./Custom.md) gamemode with Endless Night enabled.

Because it does not degrade naturally and can be re-used without any cost, they are an integral part of late-game strategy, especially in Interloper where only [Wood Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md) and only handful of [Firestrikers](./Firestriker.md) spawn, giving less total fires in a game world. It allows survivors to survive indefinitely without fear of death by [Thirst](./Thirst.md) loss. Its drawback, however, is that it may only be used during the day when there is no cloud cover, and only in areas considered by the game to be "outside." Using this whenever one can instead of always using matches will ensure you have matches when you need them later.
Clear skies are most likely to occur at dawn/early morning, which is simultaneously the coldest part of the day.

You can, however, utilize the magnifying lens to start fires in the safety of indoor areas, via starting a fire with two sticks outdoors using the magnifying glass (a single stick will only provide the 10 minutes minimum fire duration to take a torch at [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) lvl 5, any other skill level requires 2 sticks to take a [Torch](./Torch.md)), taking a torch from the fire, then taking that torch inside to start a fire in an indoor fireplace like a fireplace or stove. This allows for indoor fires after all other methods of firestarting have been exhausted, or to conserve matches and firestrikers on sunny days to delay the exhaustion of other firestarting tools in the world. This method similarly allows the lighting of forges in indoor areas such as the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) or the [Main Hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) after other firestarting tools are exhausted, as both of those are indoors and thus cannot be directly lit with a magnifying glass,

A few vehicles may be found immediately outside, and a small, exterior staircase at the back connects to a door to the indoor second-floor catwalk. The staircase's landings may serve as a somewhat protected area for storing and cooking food, although predators can climb at least partway up.

The interior of the building consists of one central hall surrounded by an elevated walkway with seven rooms per side per floor--mostly offices and storage at floor level with some living quarters mixed in upstairs. Three of four sides also have a staircase.

The hangar also has a [basement](./Hangar%20Basement.md) with a [forge](./Forge.md), [work bench](./Work%20Bench.md), and a [bed](./Bed.md). During an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) or [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) event, the basement's artificial lights turn back on, otherwise the basement has no windows and thus receives no natural light, but during the day you may still be able to work at the work bench. Escaping into the basement provides one of the few underground sanctuaries against [Insomnia](./Insomnia.md) during a Glimmer Fog event.

Inside the open hangar area are two light airplanes and one helicopter, as well as a few tool boxes--all of which can serve as storage. Also scattered throughout the hangar are plenty of furniture, tarps, and crates to break down for material.

Miscellaneous food, tools, and clothing items may be found inside and around the building on the main or upper floors. This location may also spawn up to two [heavy hammers](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), and a [noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md) may occasionally be found here as well.

**Missions:** ["You Fix My Rifle?"](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md#You_Fix_My_Rifle?) ["The Best Defense"](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md#The_Best_Defense)

The maintenance yard consists of a building, a large outdoor area, and a few partially open outbuildings, all mostly enclosed by a chainlink fence. Surrounding the main warehouse-like building are various industrial materials and [vehicles](./Car.md). There are plenty of crates and pallets in the yard. The main building houses a partially dismantled truck on a lift, numerous containers, and a bed, as well as a [workbench](./Work%20Bench.md). A small gatehouse sits near the main entrance to the yard. UNLIKE other inside spaces you can build a campfire inside on most of the snowy areas inside the maintenance yard building.

The Maintenance Yard is a suitable safe house, as it has a fire barrel, workbench, and bed inside, plus lots of storage and materials to break down. There is also a relatively sheltered office area attached to the side of the main warehouse. It contains a bed and keeps out predators, but it is partially open to the elements and does not have a loading screen when entering. If the player is dressed warmly, it may be a suitable sleeping location, particularly if trying to prevent or treat [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md). Next to the outside [bed](./Bed.md) is one of the [Radios](./Trader.md#Radio_Locations) necessary to contact the Trader (if enabled).

A large hanging flag on the ceiling can be reached by entering [Safe House Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) mode and moving one of the planks onto the raised platform containing [crates](./Crate.md), which must be moved out of the way first.

The forge here is one of the few places in the game where you can create items that require forging (the other forges are at Field 31 in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), the [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and at [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md) in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md)). The furnace temperature needs to be raised above 150°C (270°F) using coal before the [forge](./Forge.md) can be used. Fortunately there are some pieces of coal already scattered about. A [heavy hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), which usually must be brought from elsewhere, is also required, as well as some [scrap metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) and [cloth](./Cloth.md). There is usually a [Mountaineering rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) present next to the forge, which can be used if the player wants to explore the ravine in the north-west of the region.
The Yard is also relatively close to the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md), so it can make a good resting point on the path up the mountain.

However, even with these benefits, the location can be dangerous; [wolves](./Wolf.md) patrol the front and back of the yard, so coming and going can be troublesome in early game. You should crouch when you come out of the doors. There are also a few "live" wires inside the warehouse; they can be a minor hazard during an aurora, so tread with caution.
In Episode 2 of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), Will has to go to the Maintenance Yard to find and later repair the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) in the Forge.

**Manufactured Arrows** are non-craftable ammunition items for the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) and its variants.

Manufactured arrows resemble a modern fixed blade broadhead hunting arrow with a steel-alloy head and synthetic fletching and shaft. It can only be acquired by trading with the [Trader](./Trader.md) after completion of his first special request. Manufactured Arrows are a pure upgrade from [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md), dealing more damage and being twice as durable, but cannot be repaired once broken and must be replaced outright.
Manufactured arrows are not available for trade on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) or [Misery](./Misery.md) difficulty.

A bug exists where picking up Manufactured Arrows from any animal carcass will bring up the wrong notification in the top-right corner. Instead of showing the correct name for the arrow as well as the correct model, the pick-up notification will instead show the name and model of a Simple Arrow. Regardless of the buggy notification, you will always get your Manufactured Arrow back, you won't be given a Simple Arrow wrongly.
- Despite the description saying it is heavier, it weighs the same as a Simple Arrow and has the same flight characteristics as it's counterparts.

Completing Sutherland's first special request will unlock the ability to trade for manufactured arrows, as these arrows do not appear naturally in the game world, this is their only source. It will always appear as a trade once unlocked and up to 10 arrows may be purchased each time.
This cost is lowered when the player has gained enough Trust to get a discount from the Trader, reducing the trade cost to:

The total durability of manufactured arrows is variable and depends on a material table to determine it's condition loss; with the hardness of the material and the angle at which the arrow impacts the target determining the amount of degradation received. After a hit takes the arrow's condition below 0% it will break and turn into a [Broken Manufactured Arrow](./Broken%20Manufactured%20Arrow.md), which cannot be harvested or reused and essentially acts as a junk item.

Manufactured arrows are unique in that they inflict more damage against [animals](./Wildlife.md), and this damage can be further multiplied by the bushcraft bow's 25% arrow damage modifier, improving the chances of instant-kill hits.

- The multiplicative damage bonus gained from firing manufactured arrows from the [Bushcraft Bow](./Bushcraft%20Bow.md) will allow the player to inflict very large amounts of damage to animals, the most notable breakpoint being neck shots (not headshots) on [moose](./Moose.md) become instant-kills with this setup.

- The arrows lodged in the back of the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) appear to have a similar orange and black color scheme like the manufactured arrow, but lack the rubberized fins and instead use what appears to be crow feathers as their fletching.

One of them always spawns with a rope attached and leads down to the lower Hushed River valley, where one can find the aforementioned falls and [Valley Cave](./Valley%20Cave.md). The other climb doesn't spawn with a rope attached, and leads to one of the possible spawn locations for the [Mysterious Signal Fire](./Mysterious%20Signal%20Fire.md).

The climb up to Many Falls Vista from the valley beneath is a very long one. Unless the player uses an [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md), they will be forced to at least halt on a ledge to regain [stamina](./Stamina.md), and if they are tired at all, they will likely have to sleep for a bit there.

The **Map** is a [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) menu showing a region of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). On the world map, the player can view major geographic markers, as well as regions' relative locations to one another. Each regional map shows more detailed geographic features, as well as informational icons for specific locations and buildings.

The map is useful for navigating and displays important features in the areas the player has visited. The map does not label the position of the player, so determining where the player is may require comparing the surroundings to the features on the map. The map also contains a sketch which lays out the positions of all of the [Regions](./Region.md) relative to each other, as well as some of the transition zones.

In [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), the map starts out blank for each region. The map can be gradually filled in by surveying an area with [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md). Both the map and charcoal can be easily accessed through the "navigation" section of the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md).

![The navigation radial options](../assets/Mapping_radial2.jpg)_The navigation radial options_ Selecting Charcoal will equip it, and after this, left-clicking will survey the surrounding area. The area mapped after surveying is based on the player's current altitude (i.e. surveying from higher altitudes increases how much of the map is revealed). However, if the player is adjacent to a cliff, the area mapped will stop at the cliff face. This is true both if the player is surveying from the top of the cliff, or the bottom. Although the map does not label the position of the player, surveying an area will put the player's position in the center of the circle added to the map, from which it can be easily determined where the player is located. ![A partially explored map](../assets/Map_mechanic3.jpg)_A partially explored map_ Surveying can only be done outdoors during the daytime while the [Weather](./Weather.md) is clear. "Daytime" can extend further into dusk than is immediately intuitive (until the sun has entirely set on the HUD's time indicator). Surveying can only be done at night during a full moon or [Aurora](./Aurora.md).
The player's altitude affects the amount of area revealed when surveying. It is most efficient to survey from the top of rope climbs, hills, and other high points in the region whenever possible.

The passage of time (roughly 20 game minutes per survey) is accelerated while surveying. A player's empty [Stamina](./Stamina.md) bar can be completely refilled by surveying an area. Likewise, the player's [Needs](./Needs.md) will deteriorate and the player may develop an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) or suffer loss of [Condition](./Condition.md) if they are not careful. It is necessary to survey many times in order to completely map out a region, and it is more efficient to only survey areas of interest.

Occasionally while exploring, a message will appear in the top left corner of the screen denoting the current area you have discovered. These named locations can be either marked or unmarked on the Map. Named locations appear as major building icons in a region or as black text on the Map. Surveying a named location will have it be recorded in the [Surveyed Locations](./Surveyed%20Locations.md) tab in the Collections submenu of the [Journal](./Journal.md).

This collectible is a checklist of all surveyable locations within the game that count toward the [Faithful Cartographer](./Faithful%20Cartographer.md) achievement. In the current version, an in-game menu with the surveyed locations can be checked. Undiscovered places will be hidden by default, but using the "force reveal" button will make them show, not affecting the achievement.

[Polaroids](./Polaroids.md) are hidden in some areas that will mark a vista location on the map. Traveling to the vista and surveying the area will reveal a very large portion of the map. Note that it is necessary to find the Polaroid associated with a given vista before it can be mapped in this fashion. Once at the vista, an in-game message will alert the player that the area is ready to be mapped.
The map will display most important buildings with unique icons and also include the title of named locations. The map can be filtered to display or remove the following icons:
- [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) Bushes, [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md), [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md), [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md)
- [Maple](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md), [Birch](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md), and [Burdock](./Burdock.md) saplings
- Metal containers, plastic containers, backpacks, supply caches, [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md), and [Supply Caches](./Supply%20Cache.md)
- [Cars](./Car.md), [Trucks](./Truck.md), [Tractors](./Tractor.md), [Helicopters](./Helicopter.md), [Airplanes](./Airplane.md), and [Earth Movers](./Haul%20Truck.md)

- [Deer](./Deer.md#Carcass), [Cougar](./Cougar.md), [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md), [Wolf](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), [Moose](./Moose.md), and [Bear](./Bear.md) Carcasses
- Freshly killed carcasses will appear on the map after surveying the area. Thus, mapping can sometimes be useful for locating difficult-to-find kills.
- Not all rabbit spawn points appear on the map as "rabbit groves," however these non-mapped points are still valid locations for trapping.
- Mapping is not comprehensive when it comes to marking most resources such as cattails, natural remedies, or downed limbs. Rather, it gives an overview of particularly resource rich areas.
- Some symbols are removed when the marked items are harvested (e.g. carcasses), others are not (e.g. mushrooms). Actively surveying the area has no effect on this behavior.

- If rock caches and/or spray paint markers are placed too close together only a single symbol will appear on the map, but with a small plus sign denoting multiple markers. Hovering over the map symbol will list the markers in close proximity.

In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) episode 1-4, it is not possible to survey an area. Likewise, Charcoal does not exist. Instead, the map is given to the player with the regions in the current episode fully mapped out and an arrow representing their current position and direction they are facing.
In episode 5, Charcoal is obtainable and usable, but not very helpful since the full map is given.
- Surveying all of the named locations in survival mode will yield the "[Faithful Cartographer](./Faithful%20Cartographer.md)" [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md).
- The ability to survey was added on 8 June 2017 as part of the [Faithful Cartographer update](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.423).
- Polaroids, vistas, altitude sensitivity, spray paint, and rock caches were added with the [Fearless Navigator update](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog%20%E2%80%94%20Archive%202.md#1.76).

**Maple Syrup** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Consuming Maple Syrup provides up to 850 calories of [energy](./Hunger.md), and does not cause [dehydration](./Thirst.md). They are rarely found in pantries and other containers, but more commonly in fixed spawns at named locations.

Maple Syrup are the rarest food item, with only 5-7 found in an entire world, roughly half the spawn chance of the next rarest food item: [Military-Grade MRE](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md). Maple Syrup decays relatively rapidly for an artificial item, resulting in potentially even fewer than 5-7 present if some become Ruined (0% Condition) inside of a container and are destroyed.
Maple Syrup can never cause [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) above 20% condition, and [decays](./Decay.md) more slowly when outdoors.

**Marine Flares** are a multi-purpose tool in _The Long Dark_. They can be used as a light source, [firestarter](./Fire%20Starting.md), or frightening [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md).

Once lit, marine flares burn for 15 in-game minutes (75 real-time seconds), which is shorter than a normal [flare](./Flare.md), which burns for 1 in-game hour (5 real-time minutes.) like their red counterparts, they cannot be manually extinguished or relit once ignited (unlike the [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) or [Torch](./Torch.md)). Marine Flares can be lit in [strong winds and blizzards](./Weather.md), and will not be extinguished by them.

Marine Flares are effective at deterring [Wolves](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), [Deer](./Deer.md) and [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md); Wolves and Timberwolves will not approach within 15M of a lit Marine Flare (held, or on the ground), and may be frightened by lit flares when thrown. Throwing a lit flare at Timberwolves will reduce the pack's morale; once depleted of morale, a pack will flee.
- Marine Flares may be selected from from the Radial Menu (Radial>Light Sources>Flare), the Light Sources hotkey ("1"), or from the inventory.
- For firestarting, a Marine Flare must first be ignited, and then selected as a "Starter" option in the campfire menu.

Thrown Marine Flares can be picked up even while burning, this makes them an effective tool against multiple wolves (as long as the flare can be retrieved). Marine Flares can even be picked up after they are burned out, though they serve no purpose (marked in the inventory as "RUINED" and red 'X' icon) and will still contribute weight to one's inventory.
Marine Flares are effective at frightening wolves, deer and rabbits, and have limited usefulness against timberwolves.

- Wolves and Timberwolves will respect lit marine flares and not approach within 15M of them (the same as [flares](./Flare.md), [flare shells](./Flare%20Shell.md) and [campfires](./Campfire.md)). However, approaching a hostile wolf with a lit flare may result in an attack.
- Lit flares may cause a stalking wolf to flee when thrown (at the ground between the survivor and wolf), ideally landing near the wolf's forelegs.
- Unlike common red flares, marine flares are effective at reducing timberwolf pack morale when thrown.
- If a wolf is already charging into an attack, it will not be intimidated by a thrown flare.
- Flares and marine flares are most effective at passive deterrence when moving away from a predator.
- Marine Flares are more effective at deterring and scaring wolves than torches (and as effective as Flares).

- Bears are deterred by flares, stopping mid-charge just outside a 15 meter radius around the player, however they will continue to chase them until they reach safety (such as enter a vehicle, walk off a ledge, etc) or the flare runs out and the bear attacks. Throwing the flare at a charging bear has no effect. Standing still for too long will provoke the bear to charge, ignoring the flare completely.

violations.context: #### Frightening Wolves

Below is an effective tactic for scaring wolves (not timberwolves) with lit torches or flares (either variety). This tactic will always work at frightening wolf (unlike thrown torches) and is easier to perform, especially against multiple wolves.
- Approaching the wolf to 15M, the animal will stop and assume a "stand ground" posture (forelegs spread, ears back and growling).
- Drop the flare (to where you are standing) and draw any weapon ("2") including [Stones](./Stone.md), then then aim at the wolf ("RMB").

Marine Flares cannot be harvested, crafted, or repaired and are found rarely in all regions in high-loot areas (such as [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) or the [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md)), but are found regularly in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) particularly at the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md). Despite having no real use there ([aside from walking through a certain waterfall](./Cave%20%28Ash%20Canyon%20location%29.md)), Marine flares abundantly spawn in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), normally bunched with a couple of other flares.

In the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) the optional side mission "[Molly's Gift](./Molly%27s%20Gift.md)" gifts five marine flares as a reward. They are also found rarely throughout [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) and the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) throughout the episode.

- Marine Flares are used by real-world military and civilian naval craft, but these real-world flares do not burn blue. In pyrotechnics copper chloride or copper sulfate are the most likely ingredients to achieve a blue color.

The ridge is accessible via an explorable cave near the waterfall; the player can also return to the ridge by deploying a climbing [rope](./Rope%20Climbing.md).

On Marsh Ridge, there is a shallow cave where relatively good loot (e.g., food, a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md), [a snare](./Snare.md) and even a [revolver](./Revolver.md), possibly) may be found. In the area there may also be 2 [deer carcasses](./Deer.md), [rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [birch bark](./Birch%20Bark.md) and [Green Maple Sapling](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md). There is a [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) that can be found in the North-Eastern part of the Ridge that may have a [bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) lying next to it. It offers a good vantage point of the region. [Milton Basin](./Milton%20Basin.md) can be reached using a path northwest of the explorable cave, which involves climbing two small cliffs.

> — GM - So...he left with the other cowards, then? M - No. He's dead. Looks like wolves got him. GM - And so it ends. [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) explaining to [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) what he found in the shed on the farm

Martin Barker was a farmer in the town of [Milton](./Milton.md). He was originally married to [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) and is also the father of [Lilith Barker](./Lilith%20Barker.md). One day, Lilith Barker wanted to summit all the great peaks of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), and wanted to start her journey in [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md). Grey Mother protested, but Martin allowed Lilith to go by saying "Let her go. She needs to face it, alone", only for her to fall to her death in an accident which also shut down the park ([Park Warning Notice](./Park%20Warning%20Notice.md)).

After Lily's death, Grey Mother wanted [Lilith's Pearls](./Grey%20Mother%27s%20Pearls.md) to be buried with her, but Martin wanted the pearls to remember her by, and so he had them locked up in the nearby [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md). Martin and his wife soon separated after much fighting and he lived on the [Paradise Meadows Farmhouse](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) just outside of town.

[Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) finds Martin in one of the outbuildings near the farm after the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), killed and being eaten by a [Wolf](./Wolf.md). Even after his death, Grey Mother is not too shaken up when hearing the news from Mackenzie that Wolves got to him, as she was never able to forgive him, and the years only made her more angry.
His corpse can appear in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), serving as 1 of 3 places the [Paradise Meadows Farm Key](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm%20Key.md) to the locked farmhouse can spawn.

- Martin is wearing an [Old Fashioned Parka](./Old%20Fashioned%20Parka.md), [Trail Boots](./Trail%20Boots.md), [Cotton Toque](./Cotton%20Toque.md), [Work Pants](./Work%20Pants.md) and [Work Gloves](./Work%20Gloves.md) that cannot be removed from the corpse.

**Voiced by:** [Elias Toufexis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Toufexis) (Redux EP 2, 4) Gord Marriott (Predux EP 2)

> __A locked case? Well that is interesting. A locked metal case is a thing of the old world stranger. It's a world of closed doors and things being off limits. You see, I was part of that world, but that world is over.

**Mathis** is a major character in the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story of [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). Adding to the already unforgiving world of [Great Bear Island's](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) weather and wildlife, Mathis is the central human antagonist that opposes [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md), [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md), and the other denizens of the Island.
A man with a heart of stone and a self centered demeanor, Mathis is the leader of a small army of [Convicts](./Convicts.md).

Sentenced to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) after a burglary heist gone wrong, Mathis willingly allowed himself to be captured after his getaway driver arrived a mere 2 minutes late and savagely beat him to death, caring more about the driver being late then getting caught. It took 5 prison guards to get Mathis off the driver before he was arrested.

He is one of the many Convicts that escaped the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) during the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), and wishes to free his son [Donner](./Donner.md) from the solitary isolation wing of the Blackrock Prison. Initially, he wishes to escape [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), though as time passes he realizes more and more that the mainland is nothing more than fire and cold, and that he would rather remain on the Great Bear; with his crew ruling over it and with Mathis himself being its new king.

Mathis wears a sheepskin flying jacket over an orange [prison uniform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison_uniform). His hair is short, graying dirty blonde and brushed back - his left eye's sclera is always red. His name is printed on his jumpsuit, but is mostly covered by his jacket.

Mathis does not appear in this Episode, however his name (Mathis, D.) is listed on the [Prison Transport Manifest](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md) found at the Crashed Prison Transport Bus, foreshadowing him as a character.
Mathis is one of the [Convicts](./Convicts.md) which appears in the final cutscene of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md).

As [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) is traveling through the ruined [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md#Lower_levels), he is rendered unconscious by Mathis from a blow to the head just as a he reaches the exit to the dam.

When Will wakes, he is bound to a chair with Mathis punching and interrogating him over the contents of [Astrid's locked case](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) and asking where the pilot's airplane is. Will tells Mathis he doesn't know what the case's contents are, or how to open it, and that his plane "wouldn't do him any good," Mathis threatens Will and strikes him across the face with the back end of a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), ending the episode.

There is a [note](./Blood%20Stained-Convict%20Note.md) from a Convict in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) revealing that he took a small unit of prisoners from the [Crashed Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) into the region with him. These men are ultimately hunted down and killed by [Molly](./Molly.md), with Mathis having entered [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) by the time Astrid reaches the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md).

In Episode 4, Mathis and two of his thugs ([Vachon](./Vachon.md) and [Heller](./Heller.md)) carry a tied up Will Mackenzie on a litter towards the [Blackrock Federal Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md). However, on the way there, they are attacked by a pack of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md). In the melee that ensues, Will falls off the litter and escapes by jumping into a ravine, but is ultimately recaptured and taken to the prison.

Mathis is next seen after Mackenzie awakes in a prison cell and speaks to the Warden of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), [Franklin](./Franklin.md), regarding the current situation. Mathis arrives with Vachon and Heller and interrogates Franklin on how to open the door to solitary, eventually punching Franklin once after he mentions Donner's name and then begins savagely beating him to "jog his memory," eventually breaking out in laughter after he is told by Vachon and Heller that he has gone too far with his interrogation. Mathis then commands Vachon and Heller to "clean up this mess" before walking way.

Vachon and Heller ultimately send Mackenzie to find out into the wild to get [Blackrock Infirmary Medication](./Blackrock%20Infirmary%20Medication.md) for Franklin, but Mathis finds out that they sent Mackenzie to do their jobs for them. Now considering Mackenzie to be a "boy scout" for saving Franklin, Mathis sends him back out into the cold with no supplies to fix the local power plant in order to send power to open up the solitary wing of the Prison.

Mathis finds out that someone has sabotaged the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md), but rather than be enraged, he instead comes up with another solution to get Donner out of solitary, Dynamite. He next sends Mackenzie to find blasting caps at the [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) mine. After Mackenzie leaves, Mathis brutally tortures and kills Franklin, with the Warden revealing that he is aware that someone is working with Mackenzie to sabotage Mathis' plans. When Mackenzie returns with the [Detonators](./Detonators.md), he is rewarded by being tied to a chair, with Mathis about to execute him before an explosion destroys the Prison.

Mackenzie awakes to the Prison on fire and sees Mathis in the distance, furious that his Convicts blew the Detonators in the wrong manner. Jace announces her presence over the prison intercom before activating lockdown, separating Mathis from Mackenzie but not before Mathis tells him that he will "destroy EVERYTHING you love" and letting the pilot go.

Mathis can be heard breaking down the second door on the rooftop near the fire escape before Mackenzie blocks it. He is later heard alongside Vachon and Heller while Mackenzie is in the prison yard, ordering the Convicts to find and shoot the pilot.

Mathis ultimately corners [Jace](./Jace.md) and Mackenzie at the power plant, enraged at the explosion at the Prison and he attempts to execute the two of them with a Hatchet, but not before Mackenzie and Jace escape into the nearby river.
- "Ya. Should I show you what happened to the last person who tried to lie to me? She didn't look so pretty after I was done."
- (_After hitting Mackenzie over the head_) "Looks like I finally found a use for your metal case. We have unfinished business, pilot. Stick around."

- Mathis' name was originally only known because of the credits for Episode 2 as of 2017. It wouldn't be until Episode 4 in 2021 that his name would be spoken aloud. Despite this, the letter "M" is the only letter in his name not covered by the jacket on his prison jumpsuit.
- Mathis has two different character models used in Episode 2 and 4. The one in Episode 2 has a different face, and facial hair.
- Despite using the Predux model, the Ep2 version removes most of the blood on his outfit in Redux Ep2.
- Mathis was originally convicted of murder and sentenced to 10 years at a federal pen on the Mainland. He was released after 7 years on parole, per [Franklin](./Franklin.md).

- Most of Mathis' lines about women are ambiguous: Will Mackenzie interprets his line about the woman in the dam to mean Astrid, however in Episode 3 many dead prisoners can be found killed by arrows which [Molly](./Molly.md) confesses to, especially near the Pleasant Valley entrance to the Carter Dam; this could make Mathis' lines an unintentional double entendre, with Mathis instead talking about Molly.

- This could have also have been a female [Forest Talker](./Forest%20Talkers.md) in the Dam that was at the wrong place at the wrong time, considering how active they are in the Mystery Lake and Pleasant Valley regions.
- Mathis' gang at [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) consists of himself, [Heller](./Heller.md), [Vachon](./Vachon.md), and several unnamed thugs that only appear in the certain cutscenes.

Matt's Truck is found underneath a large unnamed viaduct-style bridge in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) along the main road. A pale blue pick-up [Truck](./Truck.md) appears to have fallen from the bridge, broken through the ice, and is lodged nose-down in a river that feeds out into the ocean.
Matt, presumably also the driver of the truck, is sometimes found next to his truck in the form of a [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md).

In the bed of the truck there may be a random tool or resource, such as [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md), [Prybar](./Prybar.md), [Jerry Can](./Jerry%20Can.md), [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), and/or [Firearm Cleaning Kit](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md).

Matt's Truck lies roughly between [Stone Church](./Stone%20Church.md) and [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md). [Green Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) occasionally spawn upstream from here, and [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) can be found slightly inland. A [Moose](./Moose.md) can spawn on the bridge above.
- The truck shows signs of rust and is in relatively poor condition suggesting is may have been in the river for a long time, or Matt himself may have not respected his possessions.

- The player is allowed to enter the truck via the passenger-side door which is still partially exposed. In Previous version, this was silly as the player would then be sitting neck-deep in the ice and pointless as looting the interior was impossible.

- The player often used to get stuck in between the ice sheets and the side of the truck when Desolation Point map was first released. Only careful maneuvering up the side of the truck could affect an escape. This was also fixed with a patch.
- It appears that Matt lost control of the truck and plowed through the bridge barrier and into the river.

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Iron Road](./Iron%20Road.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

**A portable heater powered by whale oil, ultra efficient by virtue of modifications by the McLeod Benthic Railway Company. Heavy, windproof. Higher fuel use means higher heat output. Patent pending.** In-game description

The **McLeod Ultra-Efficiency Whale Oil Heater** (or Oil Heater for short), is a [Tools](./Tools.md) item exclusively found on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Despite appearing to be a large [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), the item behaves more like a portable [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md). The item is quite large (about as tall as a large traffic cone), yet is surprisingly light in weight for its size at only 2.50 kg. The Oil Heater runs exclusively on [Whale Oil Cans](./Whale%20Oil%20Can.md), storing up to 2.50 L of oil (making the maximum weight of the Heater 5.00 kg).

This item is a unique prototype, with only one appearing in the game (the chronicles of its creation are recorded in [Wax Cylinder 12](./Wax%20Cylinder%2012.md) by Chief Engineer Best). Plans were originally to replace fire and coal stoves around the world with this device, but the project never traveled past the initial prototype testing phase.
When dropped or placed onto the ground, it can be turned on and used as a portable heater or cooking stove.
- A single [Cooking](./Cooking.md) slot on top allows containers to be used, and the area around the Heater can be used to further heat/reheat small items.
- Placing and lighting the Oil Heater does not require [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) tools, as it turns on and off similar to the Storm Lantern.
- Fuel can be added while the Heater is on the ground and ignited. The Heater cannot be placed back into your inventory until it is turned off (it can still be moved around with RMB while turned on).
- Placing a Cooking item on the Heater will prevent the heater from being moved, and it cannot be placed back into your inventory until the object is taken off when the Heater is extinguished.

- The Oil Heater is windproof, and can be used as an emergency heat source during a Blizzard or bad weather. It is also quite useful to use around the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md) to stay warm, specifically when making hours long repairs or refueling stops to its various components during bad weather or at night.

- It can also be used inside a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) or other buildings to increase the already high indoor warmth bonus. This method can also save fuel for the train, by instead sleeping inside a building/cave with the Heater on Low Burn rather than letting the train engine run all night and sleeping in the train cabin.

- Predators will react to the Oil Heater as though it was a [Campfire](./Campfire.md), hesitating to confront you once you are close to the heater. They can still attack you through the field of the Oil Heater however if you get too close to them.

The Oil Heater is found in the [Repair Depot](./Repair%20Depot.md) in the [Anna Island -- Track Section 2](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%202.md) Region, on a workbench on the ground floor workshop. There are also several starting Whale Oil Cans located nearby.

The Oil Heater has a temperature setting that can be adjusted to the player's liking. Depending on which burn rate is selected, more fuel is used to create more heat, while also burning stored Whale Oil at a faster rate. Higher burn rates do not result in faster Cooking times. The burn rate cannot be reversed, meaning that the burn rate is always toggled in the Low, Medium, and High burn orders before starting at Low again.
| Burn Rate | Temp | Oil Burned (Per Hour) | Max fuel burn rate until drained (when full at 2.50 L) |

- The largest drawback of this device is that a constant supply of Whale Oil Cans must be carried to make the most use of the heater (these cans often weight up to 3.00 kg or more, stopping at 5.10 kg), meaning that the player will need to travel light to carry spare oil for the heater.

- This means that the Oil Heater is mostly useless if taken back to [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), as access to Whale Oil is only found on Cauldron Island and the [Fulmar Autopilot Boat](./Fulmar%20Autopilot%20Boat.md) can only carry 150.00 kg of storage.

- Transporting enough fuel to the Fulmar is a chore enough, as several trips would need to be made through the bay of [Port Remnant](./Port%20Remnant.md) to the boat. Carrying the necessary amount of fuel to continue to operate it back on Great Bear Island is also a logistical nightmare unless the [Travois](./Travois.md) is used to carry Whale Oils Cans with you (and you will eventually run out of oil and need to make a costly resupply run back to Cauldron Island to keep using it).
- The heater cannot be placed inside the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md) to further warm the cabin.
The Oil Heater can be repaired with a pair of [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md) or [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) in 1 hour with 1 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) while in the Backpack.

The **Meat Curing Box** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.

The Meat Curing Box uses [Salt](./Salt.md) to slowly convert raw meat into [Cured Meat](./Cured%20Meat.md) and raw fish into [Cured Fish](./Cured%20Fish.md). Both versions are lighter in weight and expire very slowly. Cured Meat can also be used in late-game food recipe [Pemmican Bar](./Pemmican%20Bar.md).

Boxes have a storage capacity of 20.00 kg, and can only store raw meat/raw fish/salt. Salt storage capacity is counted separately and can hold up to 10.00 kg (22 lbs). If salt is transferred above the maximum capacity, excess salt will be returned to the player's inventory. Upon crafting, the box is filled to max salt capacity (10.00 kg), even though it only costs 8.00 kg of salt to craft.

When raw meat or fish are put in the box, they start to cure, and over the course of 5 days, turn into their cured counterparts. While meat cures at a 4/1 weight ratio (1.00 kg raw meat into 0.25 kg cured meat), each fish turns into 0.20 kg of cured fish, regardless of weight or calories. Cured Meat and fish have no [Scent](./Scent.md), and are completely safe to consume despite not being [Cooked](./Cooking.md) over a fire. If predator meat is cured, there will be no [Risk of Intestinal Parasites](./Risk%20of%20Intestinal%20Parasites.md) on difficulties where it is enabled. Additionally, Cured Meat/Fish inherits the condition of the meat/fish you inserted into the box (Eg, putting in a 86% condition raw meat will result in a 86% condition cured meat).

Salt placed inside the Box will slowly disappear as it is used to cured raw meat and fish. Presently, the box uses approximately 0.80 kg of salt each day while it is curing. This rate is not affected by the quantity of meat, meaning the same amount of salt is used regardless of whether 1.00 kg or 20.00 kg of meat have been placed inside. As a result, it is the most efficient use of salt to cure meat/fish in large batches whenever practical, in other words: curing less than 20 kg of meat in one session is very salt-inefficient. A single curing session will always use at least 4.00 kg of salt.

The curing progress will pause when the amount of salt remaining in the Meat Curing Box drops below 2.50 kg, however salt will continue to be expended as long as there is still uncured meat inside. Curing will resume when enough salt is added to bring the total above 2.50 kg.

While salt is below 2.50 kg, a hidden timer tied to each piece of meat will tick down 5 days of game time, after which the meat will start to spoil, and the Meat Curing Box will need to be emptied of the low condition and ruined meat, and restocked with salt before using it again.

As the box is used, it will require a regular resupply of more Salt. Both [Salt](./Salt.md) (0.25kg) and [Salt (Bag)](./Salt%20%28Bag%29.md) (10.00kg) can be used to refill the Box. [Salt Deposits](./Salt%20Deposit.md) and Salt (Bag) traded from the [Trader](./Trader.md) can be very helpful for building a large store of Salt for Boxes.
- Cured Meat/Fish have no [Scent](./Scent.md), are lightweight, and have high energy density: making them effective and renewable travel food.
- Curing a fish will produce one 0.20 kg portion of Cured Fish, regardless of the original fish's weight.
- On [Misery](./Misery.md), meat curing is extremely useful for late-game survival: mitigating food spoilage, parasites risk, and weight management.
- Salt can be harvested in coastal [regions](./Region.md) at Salt Deposits with most [tools](./Tools.md).
- [Sutherland the Trader](./Trader.md) sells [10kg bags of salt](./Salt%20%28Bag%29.md) (up to 3 per trade).
- Meat Curing Boxes can be relocated and moved to new locations with [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md).
A Meat Curing Box requires a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md) and the very rare [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) before it can be built.

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the box can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The box can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor when in Customization Mode.

**Mementos** are [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md) found throughout [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). They are hints left for other survivors to find, and contain useful information for the player survivor. This may include locations of a hidden cache or directions to regional transitions and landmarks.

These notes are commonly found behind the [Visors](./Visor.md) of [Cars](./Car.md) and [Trucks](./Truck.md), or in various other locations, such as above rope climbs or next to doors. There are a total of 44 notes and keys to be found (there are a total of 52 Mementos with [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) installed).
- Only 29 Mementos hint/cache/keys notes are available on [Interloper](./Interloper.md)/[Misery](./Misery.md) (some of the high level loot locations are excluded).

- Despite serving a different purpose, the [Paradise Meadows Farm Key](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm%20Key.md), [Lock Box Key](./Lock%20Box%20Key.md), [Mine Lockbox Key](./Mine%20Lockbox%20Key.md), and [Mine Office Key](./Mine%20Office%20Key.md) are stored as Mementos when picked up.

- In [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md)/[Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md), the [Foreman's Key](./Foreman%27s%20Key.md), [Mine Gate Key](./Mine%20Gate%20Key.md), [An Old House Key](./An%20Old%20House%20Key.md), and [Bolt Cutters](./Bolt%20Cutters.md) are also stored as Mementos.

Notes with the examine text "**A Memento with a survival hint.**", lead to Memento caches; various containers filled with useful loot. Sometimes a key accompanies the note, and is used to open a locked container. These containers range from:
1. A black/gray [Lock Box](./Lock%20Box.md) which requires a key to open. These keys are always found with the notes that indicate the cache's location.
2. A special [Rock Cache](./Rock%20Cache%20%28Mementos%29.md): A small dark rock usually hidden next to a larger cliff/rock.
3. [Loose Tree Bark](./Loose%20Tree%20Bark.md): a hollow tree/stump with an interaction point near the side.
Hidden Caches can only be opened if the corresponding note has been found, and will not give an interaction prompt otherwise. Likewise, both the note and key are required to open Memento Lock Boxes.

Caches contain highly specific and useful resources. This might include tools, materials, clothing, food, fuel, animal hides, or weapons. Some caches have only a specific type of resource (e.g. fish) whereas others contain more general loot.

Notes with the examine text "**A note with a survival hint.**", Memento hints are notes used to guide the survivor towards points of interest. These range from region transitions to areas with unique supplies. When picked up, they reveal a portion of the map and add a Memento Hint to the area.
These notes are typically more useful for new players who don't know the regions very well.

This is the mission transcript for mission 1 [Memories](./Memories.md) of [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md).

_The game begins with the sound of a man grunting in pain and gasping for air, and then the noise of a beating heart, and a person's vision slowly coming to as they blink back into consciousness. The ambient electrical wail of an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) plays overhead as the camera shifts to reveal trees, fire, smoke, and wreckage of a crashed plane. The survivor begins to get up, before the man cries out:_

_The man gets up, and notices a piece of metal lodged in his left hand, hesitating before deciding to pull it out. The process is slow, and is not without consequence, as the man's cries of pain ring out during the pulling. After the [Scrap Metal Shard](./Scrap%20Metal%20Shard.md) is pulled out, the man shouts to the hills around him._
_The man looks at the gaping wound in his hand before the camera shifts and slowly zooms out as if to give control to the player, but instead the scene slowly goes dark._
_The location "[Jackrabbit Hangar](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md)" appears in the top right corner of the screen, as a first person cutscene of a man is shown playing Solitaire at a desk._
**Mackenzie:** "Brr! Feels like another record cold snap on the way. I'd better get a fire going before the pipes freeze up again."
_The man then picks up some [Wood Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md) off the table's corner, some Tinder, and some fuel, and then starts a fire in the nearby [Wood Stove](./Wood%20Stove.md)._

**Memories** is the first mission in [Episode One](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), where [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) sits around the [Jackrabbit Remote Transport](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md) hanger until he receives a visitor that requests a flight to [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).
> “**Mackenzie hangs around the Jackrabbit Transport hangar, waiting for something to happen.**”
**Any extra items found in the hanger will not be taken with you to the next level, so do not worry about finding loot. Just focus on objectives.**
![Office (Memories)](../assets/Office_%28Memories%29.png) Mackenzie will state he is getting cold. Pick up the following items within the office:
Go to the [Wood Stove](./Wood%20Stove.md) located in the corner of the office and start a [Fire](./Fire.md) with the acquired materials.
Open the Door to the office and exit into the hanger. Explore the Hanger, and examine the following items within:

- Map - located next to the [Wood Stove](./Wood%20Stove.md). "[Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). Dad used to fly there all the time. He said it used to be beautiful. Not much reason to go there these days... since the quakes and all."
- Photo - located on the filing cabinet near the window. "Ah...a rare Mackenzie family photo. Miss you, dad."

- Floatplane - located in the center of the hanger. "Well...here we are old girl. your best flights may be behind you, but you're still beautiful to me. And anyways... you're all I've got. I'd sure love to take you on one last great adventure."
- Poster - located near the bathroom. "Jackrabbit Remote Transport. Zero flights a day to the Mainland communities and...well...anywhere really."
- Hotplate - located on the kitchen counter. "Cheap electric crap. Never works when you need it."
- Mackenzie's Parka - located on the table in front of the Floatplane. "I don't remember needing my parka this early in the season. Seems to get colder every year."
- Sink - located on the bathroom counter. "Damn...I was right. Pipes froze up again."
- Photo - located inside the sleeping quarters behind a dreamcatcher. "Those were better days."

After examining several of the objects listed above, you announce that you are ready for a nap. Go to the sleeping quarters and select the bed to go to sleep. You'll eventually be woken up by the sound of a ringing phone. Go back to the office.

Mackenzie will answer the ringing phone, with another Jackrabbit Remote Transport employee, Maureen, telling him over the phone that "she" arrived and was convinced you would fly her north. The door opens to reveal Astrid Greenwood. Astrid needs you to fly her to a settlement on the north coast of Great Bear Island to treat an ill person. You reluctantly agree, despite the "no questions asked" policy about this flight.
![Jackrabbit hanger](../assets/Jackrabbit_hanger.jpg) Load the following items from the central hanger into the Hatch located on the Floatplane:
Optionally, load one the three following items also located on the table by the plane:
Select [Mackenzie's Parka](./Mackenzie%27s%20Parka.md) after loading the plane to complete the mission and start the next cutscene.

A cutscene triggers, where you fly through bad weather and experience an [Aurora](./First%20Flare.md). The electrical systems within the plane short circuit, and you crash into the wilderness of Great Bear.
- Mackenzie's unique Clothing have different models and item descriptions compared to their post plane crash counterparts.
- It is impossible to pass time and die while in the hangar, as passing time is not possible.
- This may be explained by the fact that the playing cards used in the "Pass Time" option are on the table in the office, and cannot be used.
- There are 2 harvestable items in the hangar, a small [Cardboard Box](./Cardboard%20Box.md) and a [Hand Cart](./Hand%20Cart.md) (but the cart cannot be harvested).

- Several items can be picked up, such as a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md), [Herbal Tea](./Herbal%20Tea.md), [Chocolate Bar](./Chocolate%20Bar.md), [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md), [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md), [Newsprint Roll](./Newsprint%20Roll.md), [Newsprint](./Newsprint.md), [Wood Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md), and [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md), but none of these items will be in the player's inventory in the next mission.

- The Cooking Pot can be used to melt snow and boiled to create [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), which can then be used with the Herbal Tea to prepare a [Cup of Herbal Tea](./Cup%20of%20Herbal%20Tea.md). Both the water and tea are removed when progressing like the rest of the items. However, the tea can be consumed before leaving the hangar, providing the [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md) and [Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md) benefits, which will carry over to [The Crash](./The%20Crash.md).

- Several normally interactable items can be found in the hangar but cannot be selected, such as a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), [Books](./Book.md), a [Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md), [Plastic Container](./Plastic%20Container.md), [File Cabinet](./File%20Cabinet.md), [Cupboard](./Cupboard.md), a small mini [Fridge](./Fridge.md), a tool [Drawer](./Drawer.md), and a [Trash Can](./Trash%20Can.md).
