![Mending](../assets/Mending.png) **Mending** is a Survival [Skill](./Skills.md) that is used to repair equipment, such as [Clothing](./Clothing.md) and certain [Tools](./Tools.md). Mending also has a large variety of training options relative to most other skills due to the number of types of clothing that can be repaired.
- [Clothing](./Clothing.md) ([Cloth](./Cloth.md) clothes, [Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md) clothes, [Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) accessories)

- Bedrolls (![Bedroll icon](../assets/Bedroll_icon.png) [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), ![Improvised Down Bedroll icon](../assets/Improvised_Down_Bedroll_icon.png) [Improvised Down Bedroll](./Improvised%20Down%20Bedroll.md), ![Bear Skin Bedroll icon](../assets/Bear_Skin_Bedroll_icon.png) [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md))
Ruined Clothing cannot be repaired, only harvested for materials. The Mending skill does not lower clothing crafting times or increase when crafting clothing.

Mending is the skill used to repair Clothing and Bedrolls in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md); a_s the player successfully repairs items, their skill in mending increases. Clothing requires a [Sewing Kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md) or [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md), resources the item is made out of (e.g. [Cloth](./Cloth.md) or [Cured Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md)), and sufficient light in order to begin repairs (daylight, full moonlight, [artificial lighting](./Aurora.md) or an active [Fire](./Fire.md)/[Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md)).

To repair a piece of clothing select the item the backpack or the worn clothing menu. Then select "Actions" and "Repair"; the required resources, time required and amount repaired if successful will be displayed. Higher Mending skill decreases the time required to mend and increases the condition restored as well as the successful repair rate.

Failing to repair results in the materials used in the repair to be wasted, but causes no additional condition loss to the item. Repairing clothing successfully or failing causing condition loss to the Sewing Kit/Fishing Tackle used.

A tool is required to repairing Clothing. Sewing Kits can be found by looting. Fishing Tackle can be found or crafted from [Hook](./Hook.md) and [Line](./Line.md). Fishing Tackle is 100% slower (twice as long) to repair than using Sewing Kits. Some items such as [Crampons](./Crampons.md) and [Improvised Crampons](./Improvised%20Crampons.md) required Scrap Metal and tools to fix.

The **Metal Container**is a common stationary interactable object that can be found at many locations in [The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). Upon first encountering one, the player has the option to 'search' the container, a function shared with other item containers in the game. To search a container, the player must hold left-click while hovering over the object. It will then prompt the player with one of the items that spawned in the container, giving them the option to take it, leave it, or press space to interact with the object in some other way if possible. Once an action has been taken, it will cycle on to the next item, and continue until no items are left in the container. By hold-clicking again on an already searched container, the player can place items from their inventory into the container. It can hold up to 15kg (33lbs) of items.

They are often found next to a [Metal Pan](./Metal%20Pan.md).

Metal shelves are very common and can have a large variety of loot on them and may hold containers on each shelf. - Extra small metal shelves have 3 shelf level but are only about half as wide as larger ones.
- Small-sized metal shelves have 3 or 4 shelf levels while being half as wide as medium shelves.

Most metal shelves may be harvested for scrap metal; however, it is most efficient to harvest Large metal shelves. The amount of Scrap Metal received per unit time, per calorie, and per condition of the Hacksaw are higher. One location with a large number of these shelves is in the first-floor employee area of the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md#Upper_levels).

> “__These are confusing times. Let me see if I can help you make sense of them. I'm an old man. I've seen many things. Some would say, too many. I've seen this happen before. We've sinned, now we're paying the price. __”

**Methuselah** is a mysterious character that appears in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) and [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

An elderly man that [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) encounters traveling from area to area several times over the course of his journey, Methuselah is a [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) native that offers Mackenzie cryptic advice about the current state of the world. He seems to know more about the "Quiet Apocalypse" silently unfolding around him that no one else seems to recognize yet, stating that "this has all happened before," as well as offering explanations to the erratic behavior of the local wildlife.

Methuselah exhibits the uncanny and unexplained ability to easily survive/traverse terrain and locales that would otherwise be challenging even to young, experience climbers/travelers. Examples of this include somehow traversing down the side of [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md) without a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md), passing through swaths of forests teeming with hostile Wolves with ease, and surviving with very little food/clothing/water at his campsites. Combining this with his knowledge of the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) (as well somehow possessing knowledge of how Mackenzie treats [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md)), one could easily assume him to be the product of a supernatural outcome, yet none of his interactions with Mackenzie have come off as paranormal as of yet.

Despite his strange demeanor, Methuselah is a friendly man. He recognizes that Mackenzie often needs help, and always offers the pilot assistance in the way of knowledge to some of his questions and his campfire he always tends, providing the player a safe place to rest and warm up.

Despite initially appearing in the [Town of Milton](./Town%20of%20Milton.md), [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) does not recognize Mackenzie's description of him and claims that Methuselah is not a native of the town.

While trying to gather supplies for Grey Mother, Methuselah is first encountered inside the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) as an individual labeled as "Unknown." He eventually states that Mackenzie can simply call him Methuselah, and explains to the pilot that the world is changing, and that human acts of neglect towards nature are being repaid by the onset of the "Quiet Apocalypse." He also tells Will that people will be forced to go to extreme measures to survive in this new world.

Mackenzie is skeptical of these claims, stating that power failures have occurred before and that everything will go back to normal soon enough, but Methuselah is unsure of this response. The old man answers a few more questions Mackenzie has and the pilot then leaves him alone as he begins looting the store in order to bring food and water to Grey Mother. If the player comes back after helping Grey Mother, Methuselah is gone.

He is encountered again at a campfire along the pathway leading to [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) after Will escapes the Town of Milton. He gives a neutral comment on how Will dealt with [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md), giving a different reaction depending on whether Mackenzie kills or spares the convict. This exchange baffles Mackenzie, as Methuselah was nowhere to be found when he encountered the Convict, and yet the old man somehow knows what transpired between the two.

Regardless of the choice made to kill or spare Hobbs, Methuselah does not pass judgment, merely stating that this new world will test Mackenzie to see if he has what it takes to survive. Mackenzie then leaves the old man, wishing him good luck with his "apocalypse", but the old man tells the pilot to keep his luck as [he will be needing it soon](./Old%20Bear.md).

In Episode 2 after the second [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) attack in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md), Will finds Methuselah under the night sky of an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) (the first time the aurora has appeared in the sky since the First Flare) and asks who Mackenzie's "war with nature" is going. Methuselah explains that there was no bear here when he arrived, and that perhaps the pilot and beast's final fight has not yet come. Methuselah reveals more about the Aurora's effect on the animals and electrical equipment changing the world before Mackenzie leaves. Methuselah is gone when Mackenzie returns to the same campfire spot with the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) in tow.

He is last seen outside the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) near the end of the Episode, where he provides a cryptic hint about how there may be some side missions still left to explore in the Episode, but otherwise wishes Mackenzie good luck if he wants to proceed through the Dam. Mackenzie finds relief in encountering a familiar face again after everything he's been through in the past few days, and hopes that he will cross paths with the strange man again in the future.

Methuselah will remain outside the Carter Staging Area for the rest of the episode, and is not seen again for the rest of Wintermute's story (unconfirmed if he will appear in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md)).

In the original version of Wintermute, Methuselah was voiced by Gord Marriott (who also provided the voice for [Mathis](./Mathis.md)) As of the _Redux_ version of Episode 1 and 2, he is voiced by Richard Newman.
- "My heart weeps for you, stranger. My days are nearly finished. But you'll have to live with what remains."

- Methuselah: "These are confusing times. Let me see if I can help you make sense of them. I'm an old man. I've seen many things. Some would say, too many. I've seen this happen before. We've sinned, now we're paying the price." Will Mackenzie: "Are you talking about religion?" Methuselah: "Not religion. Redemption." Will Mackenzie: "Is this about the lights in the sky?" Methuselah: "The lights in the sky are a reckoning. The wonder of humanity and all its creations, laid bare. Her warnings went unheeded." Will Mackenzie: "Whose warnings?" Methuselah: "Mother Nature's. The signs were there, for those willing to see them. This has all happened before. Soon we'll all be tested. We'll all have to choose how far we'll go to survive." Will Mackenzie: "What do you mean, this has happened before?" Methuselah: "Big change is coming. Are you ready to face it?"
- "I have wandered these paths a long time, friend. I was a walker, now I'm a watcher. I'm here to observe these times, and help where I may."
- Both lenses of Methuselah's glasses have radiant fractures, suggesting they are made of glass, not plastic; it is unknown how they were damaged or when.
- Methuselah has a unique walking stick in both encounters in Episode 1, but it is strangely absent in both encounters in Episode 2.

- Methuselah is the only NPC to be encountered in more than one location (excluding cutscenes), and together with Mathis and [Jane Yang](./Jane%20Yang.md) are the only NPCs that are featured in multiple episodes.

- Methuselah is the name of a [biblical patriarch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methuselah), known for being the one who lived the longest out of anyone in the Bible: 969 years. Hence, the name has been associated with longevity and referenced extensively in culture.
- Methuselah's hat appears brown with a red band in the Predux, but it is red with a brown band post Redux.

- Partially obscured by his winter coat, Methuselah's shirt has an "Omega" symbol on it. This is an Abrahamic reference to God, and also means "the end" as Omega is the last character in the Greek alphabet, implying he might be the last man alive when the world ends.

**Military-Grade MRE** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

The MRE is a rare and only found inside safes, prepper caches, locked lockers and outdoor sporting-type locations (such as Hunting Blinds). Usually only 1-3 may be found per region, based on [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

A single MRE can restore a whopping 1750 calories, making it the most efficient calories per unit of any food item (although [Energy Bars](./Energy%20Bar.md) and [Salty Crackers](./Salty%20Crackers.md) have a higher calorie-to-weight ratio, at 30% and 41.6% more calorie-dense, respectively).

"MRE" stands for "Meal Ready to Eat". As suggested by the name, MREs can be eaten as-is, without heating or special tools to prepare or consume them. In [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), individually wrapped [Airline Food](./Airline%20Food%20-%20Chicken.md) meals feature similar stats to the MRE. These meals, like MREs, require no special tools to open and can be eaten uncooked (despite appearing like 'frozen dinners'). Whether these similarities cast a more favorable light on airline food or MREs is unclear.
MRE have a very low chance of causing [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) and [Decay](./Decay.md) much slower than many foods.
- In real life, MREs are used by militaries to feed troops during combat, and in real-world northern climates these packaged meals can last three to five years, depending on storage temperature.

- The Canadian Military does supply its deployed members with MREs (Meal Ready to Eat), which are typically [American-made](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meal,_Ready-to-Eat). More often it uses IMP (Individual Meal Pack)--the exclusive field ration of the [Canadian Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual_Meal_Pack).

The **Milling Machine** is a workstation used for repairs in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)._ It was introduced in the Errant Pilgrim update.

The Milling Machine is a workstation which is used to repair certain tools and weapons. Operating the Milling Machine requires one [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) and an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md). While an Aurora is active, the Milling Machine will whir and its lights will be on. Once the Aurora ends, the sound of the machine powering off is heard. Milling Machines are always accompanied by the [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md).
The chance of success and amount repaired is determined by either [Repair Skill](./Repair.md) when repairing tools.

- Base skill has a 50% chance of success, for a 40% item condition repair. Only firearms can be repaired from 0% Ruined Condition with the Milling Machine, though it will take much longer than usual to do so.
- Successfully repairing a firearm will also give 1 point to the [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) Skill.
- Ruined Rifles can be repaired from 0% Condition with 5 Scrap Metal and 1 Fir Firewood in 4 hours.
- Ruined Revolvers can be repaired from 0% Condition with 4 Scrap Metal and 1 Fir Firewood in 4 hours.

The Milling Machines in both locations are initially behind electronically-locked doors which can only be opened during an active Aurora with their Access Code (found on a note in a specific hard-to-reach location in-region). The code for the Workshop in the [Cannery Pier](./Cannery%20Pier.md) is found inside [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md), and [Blackrock Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) armory in the second-floor shaft of the [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) mine (in a locker where the [Detonators](./Detonators.md) are found in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md)). Once the code is entered and the doors unlocked, they remain unlocked and accessible at all times.

The Access Code to unlock The Last Resort Cannery and Blackrock Prison's doors need only to have been read to unlock it, and does not need to be picked up and added to the player's Collection (though they have no weight).

Caution should be taken inside of the Last Resort Cannery Workshop during an Aurora, since electrified wires are present around the room which cause [Burns](./Burns.md) on contact and can quickly kill, on the other hand, the Blackrock Prison Workshop is relatively safe, however gaining access to it requires, arguably, a more arduous journey.

- Repairing a Hacksaw with the Milling Machine grants more condition per Scrap Metal than repair with [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md) or [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md); but only if the repair is successful. At low Repair skill the Milling Machine is less efficient on average, but as Repair skill increases it becomes far more efficient.
- Repairing Improvised Hatchet and Improvised Knife is more efficient with Scrap Metal than [forging](./Forge.md) new ones.
- No [Bed](./Bed.md) is present inside or conveniently near either of the workshops. It is recommended to bring a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) to spend extended periods of time in the crafting ammunition.

- An early prototype of this item could be found during the cut mission [You Fix My Rifle?](./You%20Fix%20My%20Rifle%3F.md), known as the [Hand-Powered Milling Tool](./Hand-Powered%20Milling%20Tool.md).

- Milling Machines were introduced in the Errant Pilgrim update along with its region: [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). The Perilous Constraint update introduced it to the [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) region.

Milton Basin lies near the [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md). In order to access the zone, the player has to either climb down a rope by the farmstead or follow a rock climbing passage near [Marsh Ridge](./Marsh%20Ridge.md) in Forlorn Muskeg. The area consists of a large lake surrounded by hills and a steep cliff. Many [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) are scattered around the lake, with a small birch forest in the northwest providing some birch bark. [Wolves](./Wolf.md), possibly a [Moose](./Moose.md) may roam the area, along with many [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) near the Hermit's Cabin. Thanks to 3 concentrated [Deer](./Deer.md) spawns on the lake and 2 more along the Northern passage, the area may offer rich hunting grounds with as many as 7 deer simultaneously in sight.
There are some saplings in the area as well, and the lake is the only area in the region that's deep enough to allow [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) via Free Form holes.
- Milton Basin is not accessible in Wintermute, making transition between Forlorn Muskeg and Milton impossible.

**Milton Credit Union** is a bank and location in [Milton](./Milton.md) in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. According to a letter pinned outside the front door in Story mode, banking services were suspended in September 2012.

The bank is located across the street from [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) and a truck and car are parked beside it. The [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md) can be found behind the bank.

Inside there is an office room to the right of the entrance. In Wintermute, the desk in the small office contains a key to the [Bank Manager's House](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House.md). Behind the glass-fronted counter is a room with computers, laptops and metal lockers, as well as a restroom off to one side.

In the back room of the building, there is a locked safe (with a random code). In **[Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md)**, the main bank vault door is open. In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), the bank vault can only be opened after the _Bank Vault Code_ [collectible](./Collectibles.md) has been obtained from the Bank Manager's House. The vault contains stacks of papers and books, lootable metal containers, and 20 deposit boxes. Eight of the deposit boxes are open and empty, a further eight can be looted, and the final four (#7, #13, #15 and #20) require a _Bank Deposit Box Key_ to unlock in the story.
The following keys can be found as part of the [Milton Safety Deposit Box Keys](./Milton%20Safety%20Deposit%20Box%20Keys.md) side mission:

- Key #7: Milton House – After exiting the Bank manager's House, walk forward until you fully pass a house which will be slightly to your left, then enter the house slightly on your right. Look in the box under the bed.

- Key #13: Southern River – Follow the river west of Milton, and walk the eastern bank south. Almost at the edge of the map, look for crows flying overhead. There’s a corpse with a backpack carrying this key.
- Key #15: West Farm – Go to the farm following the road west from Milton. Get the key lying next to Hobbs when you enter.
- Key #20: South Gas Station – South of Milton, there’s a gas station. Look for the truck parked by a pair of blue port-a-potties. The key is inside that truck.

The **Milton House (Grey Mother's)**is a location featured in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of _The Long Dark_. It is a large two-story house in the town of [Milton](./Milton.md) and is home to [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md), and is distinguished as being the largest [Milton House](./Milton%20House.md) in the town.

The house is located on top of a small hill near the town entrance. It has two bedrooms, a bathroom, a kitchen with a [Stove](./Stove.md), and a living room with a [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md). Various loot items can be found in the containers throughout the house.

In the backyard, there is a small shed with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) and [Prybar](./Prybar.md). Near the end of Episode 1, Grey Mother will give you a key to unlock a [Trunk](./Trunk.md) in the second bedroom, giving you access to a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md). She will also cook some [Home-made Soup](./Home-made%20Soup.md) for the player to show her hospitality.

The house is occupied by Grey Mother, a blind old woman with a loaded rifle and a distrust for outsiders. She is the only remaining resident in the town of Milton and is effectively trapped due to the collapsed tunnel out of town. From her house, she gives [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) various missions and allows him to use the house as shelter from the cold and the wolves.

In survival, the house is devoid of Grey Mother, with just her chair tipped onto its side and bullet holes in the walls face away from the chair, suggesting signs of a struggle. It makes a good base despite its lack of workbench. The building has a 6-slot stove, a 2-slot fireplace, and warm beds, making it a great place to cook large amounts of meat and use as a safehouse. It's centrally located within the region and is atop a hill, making spotting wolves easier.
- A [Revolver](./Revolver.md) may spawn in the first bedroom beneath the bed, with two cartridges scattered around.

- The Storage room on the first floor may hide a box of [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md) behind the leaning plank and another loot spawn behind a piece of harvestable cloth. It usually spawns a soda of some kind and can not be accessed without tearing up the cloth/towel (yields 3 [Cloth](./Cloth.md)) first.
- A [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) may spawn in the bathtub on the second floor.
- A pair of [Wool Longjohns](./Wool%20Longjohns.md) (or other high quality clothing) may spawn on the ground in the second bedroom, or in the bathtub.

A **Milton House**is a type of house or shed found throughout the Town of [Milton](./Milton.md) in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. Many of these buildings have the same layout as the [Coastal House](./Coastal%20House.md) and [Crossroads House](./Crossroads%20House.md).

Most of the dwellings throughout the Town of Milton are in ruins after decades of neglect, with many either being fully collapsed or boarded up after the once booming coal town went bust. The few that remain accessible are in differing states of disrepair, as many homes show signs of either abandonment from the former residents or were violently ransacked when the [Convicts](./Convicts.md) took over the Town, showing signs of looting after the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md).
Many of the houses and sheds change location between Survival Mode runs, with some being boarded up on one playthrough but the same house can be accessible on another.
This type of building has only 1 floor, with 2 doors leading to the kitchen or living room. They are composed of:
The layout for this building has 2 different layouts, but tends to be filled with large amounts of food and [Cooking Pots](./Cooking%20Pot.md).

This [Bank Manager's House](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House.md) is different from every other house, containing just 3 rooms and a front door. It is locked in [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) and needs the [Bank Manager's House Key](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House%20Key.md) to unlock.
This building type only appears near the main road and is highly vandalized. It has 2 entrances that lead to 4 different rooms:

These homes are much smaller buildings with a single door leading to the front hallway. They have a stairwell that leads the bedroom, with the ground floor containing a kitchen and nearby bathroom. Some of these types of houses in the town are entirely abandoned, with the upper floors sometimes either containing a baby crib or no bed.

A few buildings are small tool sheds, with 2 doors for entering. They tend to contain a [Metal Shelf](./Metal%20Shelf.md) often holding a [Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md) or other tools, [Crates](./Crate.md), [Planks](./Planks.md), and [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md). One shed is on a hill behind the pond with the ruined house, and has a Bed. 4 can be found in the town, but 2 will always be boarded up.

**Milton Park** is a location in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. It can be found by taking a right at the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) south of [Milton](./Milton.md).

This post office is the only one on all of Great Bear. Despite there being a back-end of the post office, this part of the building is inaccessible, resulting in the building being very small. It's one of a few locations with a radio that enables players to contact the [Trader](./Trader.md#Radio_Locations).

To start the mission, the player must find any one of three bank deposit box keys scattered around the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. Each key unlocks a safety deposit box in the [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md) vault. Finding all three keys and opening all three safety deposit boxes will complete the mission.

- _[Bank Deposit Box Key #7](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%207.md)_ is located inside a house on the main road between the [Post Office](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Milton_Post_Office) and the [Orca Gas Station](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Orca_Gas_Station), in a plastic container underneath the bed. The house is across the main road from the [Bank Manager's House](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House.md). Note there is another house in between them. Box contains [cash](./Cash.md) and 2 [flare shells](./Flare%20Shell.md).

- _[Bank Deposit Box Key #13](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2013.md)_ is located on a corpse near the frozen river between [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) and [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md). Follow the stream downhill directly behind the gas station. Right before the slight bend, turn left up the slope and the corpse will be directly ahead. The crows circling above the corpse should make locating it easier; If walking downstream, the crows can be seen circling above on the lefthand side of the river. Box contains [balaclava](./Balaclava.md), [book](./Book.md), [ski gloves](./Ski%20Gloves.md) and [stack of papers](./Stack%20of%20Papers.md).

- _[Bank Deposit Box Key #20](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2020.md)_ is located behind [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) in a blue pickup truck parked on the trail leading to the climbing area. The truck is next to two port-a-potties. Box contains [magnifying lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) and 2 [cash](./Cash.md).

- [Bank Deposit Box Key #15](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2015.md) is located in the farm house. The key can be found next to [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) immediately after the interaction with him, regardless of the outcome chosen. This is the only key that is necessary to progress through the story, as Bank Deposit Box #15 holds a plot-sensitive item.

**Milton Supply Caches** is a side mission in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md). To start the quest, the player must find any one of three notes scattered around the town of [Milton](./Milton.md). Each note will reveal information about a hidden cache of supplies nearby and add a marker to the map. To complete the quest, the player must find all three notes and recover each of their respective supply caches.
> “**The Collapse taught Milton residents to be ready for the worst. Find the collectibles that point you to cache locations.**”
To start the mission, the survivor has to find one of the corresponding notes scattered around [Milton](./Milton.md):

The mission objective can be started after finding the [Collectible](./Collectibles.md) [Cave Hidden Cache Note](./Cave%20Hidden%20Cache%20Note.md), which is located on a sleeping bag within a residential home at the top of the hill southwest of the [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md). (Must look at the map to be able to follow instructions!)

The easiest method to get to the cave is to start at [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md), and head back towards the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md). Continue past the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md) and enter the large cave within the cliff face. The survival cache appears as a pile of blue rocks in the back of the cave, as opposed to a [Hidden Cache](./Hidden%20Cache.md) container. The survivor can search the rocks to recover the supplies contained within the cache.

The mission objective can be started after finding the Collectible [Medicine in my backyard](./Medicine%20in%20my%20backyard.md) inside of a car located between the [Milton Post Office](./Milton%20Post%20Office.md) and [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md). The car can be located by departing from Grey Mother's House, turning left, and following the road towards [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md). The note is located inside the last car on the left before leaving the town area.

The easiest method to get to the cache is to start at Grey Mother's House, and right towards [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md). Once reached, look for a large fallen tree directly behind the church. The survival cache appears as a [Hidden Cache](./Hidden%20Cache.md) container tucked against the fallen tree. The survivor can search the container to recover the supplies contained within the cache.

The mission objective can be started after finding the Collectible [Milton Hidden Cache Note](./Milton%20Hidden%20Cache%20Note.md) inside the chimney of the destroyed [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md) within [Milton](./Milton.md).

The easiest method to get to the cache is to start at Grey Mother's House, and head left towards [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md). The second to last house on the right when leaving town is a destroyed house containing the cache. Once reached, look around outside in the snow under fallen structural beams for a [Hidden Cache](./Hidden%20Cache.md) container nestled in the snow. The survivor can search the container to recover the supplies contained within the cache.

- A cut objective for this mission was the medicine found in the back yard of the Millers, which was given by Grey Mother as a Trust reward. It was replaced by the note Medicine in my backyard in the Redux release of Episode 1.

**Milton Water Tower** is a landmark and unmarked location in [Milton](./Milton.md) in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. It appears as a landmark on the [Map](./Map.md), but is not considered a location.

Prior to 30 June 2012, it was used by the [Great Bear](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) Water Authority to help supply water to the town via underground water mains. A note, [Public Notice](./Public%20Notice.md), is found taped to the tower base in Wintermute, and reveals that as a result of seismic activity in the area; an outbreak of [E. coli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escherichia_coli) was found in the water supply and the tower was shut down, adding to the list of woes that Milton was already suffering from since the [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md).

The Water Tower was originally between the bridge to Milton and [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) in the V1.00 Predux release of the game. After the Redux re-release of Episode 1, the tower was moved to the center of town between the [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md) and [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md).

**The Town of Milton**is a major location in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of _The Long Dark's_Story Mode. It is a small, largely abandoned town nestled in the mountains of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). The location name of the game map is "Town of Milton."

Milton was founded in 1911 to support the initially booming coal industry in the surrounding mountains. The town was originally built along a supply route from the coast to the interior of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), with the road replaced by a paved highway in 1960. The location of the town, halfway between Port Mary and the mountains in the interior of Great Bear, made it a convenient stopping-off point for fuel and supplies for workers in the mining, logging, and milling industries, as well as campers from Mainland [Canada](./The%20Collapse.md).[^1]

The town's economy boomed in the 1980s, with the population reaching around 1000 people, but the construction of the [Great Bear Highway](./Great%20Bear%20Highway.md) (Highway 15) meant fewer people travelling through Milton, and ultimately led to the decline of the importance of Milton. In the 2000s the population was little more than 100 or so.[^2]

Following [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md), even fewer travelers or industrial workers visited Great Bear, and eventually the population fell to only a dozen or so - stalwarts and old-timers, with deep roots in Milton. Soon, Milton became a ghost town.[^3]
In addition to several houses within the town, the Mountain Town region contains multiple named locations.

Has an interior **Mindful Cabin** is located in the north-west part of the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), at the end of the road.

The cottage itself has one main room, with a [pot belly stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), and a [bed](./Bed.md) that can be found in the loft. It does not have a loading screen upon entering. From the cottage's balcony, it is possible to see the runway of the airfield as well as the rescue helicopter crashed at [Final Approach](./Final%20Approach.md).

Notable loot includes the potential spawning of a [magnifying lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) and [cooking pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md), as well as a [knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) on the balcony, canned food, [mukluks](./Mukluks.md) or [trail boots](./Trail%20Boots.md). It's even possible to gather some water from the tank placed under the kitchen sink. A hidden loot container labeled "[Loose Boards](./Loose%20Boards.md)" can be found under the stairs, right behind the shelf with the potted plant. It often contains a [revolver](./Revolver.md), as well as a [note someone left behind.](./A%20Note%20Left%20Behind.md)

Much like its counterpart in the region, the [Island Cottage](./Island%20Cottage.md), there are no electrical devices within the cabin, meaning that it will not immediately be obvious that an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) or [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) event is active, should the player awaken from sleep after passing time. Luckily the many large windows and wide open views should allow the player to spot the potentially dangerous phenomena before venturing far.

Although Mindful Cabin is similar inside to Island Cottage, it is generally regarded as inferior for a safehouse compared to the latter. This is mainly because Mindful Cabin is far from [Shoulder Lake](./Shoulder%20Lake.md), making fishing difficult, and it has limited hunting opportunities nearby. Even the [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section that can be used to get up to the area is the longest rope climb in the game, with no rests along the climb to the top and requiring a [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) or [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) to safely reach the top.

It can be acquired while following the [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md) Tale by opening a locked gate with [Bolt Cutters](./Bolt%20Cutters.md). This key is needed to access the locked mountain mine entrance located near the top of the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md).

The **Mine Office Key** is a unique key found only in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), specifically in the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md).

It can be found on a corpse in the mine. Starting from the bottom floor of the [Headframe Building](./Headframe%20Building.md) elevator, take a left through the toxic gas, past a toxic open pit, past another gas cloud, and the player will find themselves crouching and approaching a wooden coal chute under a very low ceiling. A curled up corpse will contain the key, and will be next to a [Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md).

The key unlocks a mine trailer on a catwalk located in the center of the 3rd level where a (non-accessible) yellow coal chute from the 2nd level ends. A [Lantern](./Lantern.md) is in the center of this room for reference, and an [Insulated Flask](./Insulated%20Flask.md) tends to spawn on a table on the catwalk.

**Miner's Flashlight** is a variant of the [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

The Miner's Flashlight is a yellow, heavy duty electrical torch that has a larger, longer lasting battery than the regular Flashlight, but at the expense of being 0.25 kg heavier. While a 100% charged Miner's Flashlight lasts for up to 1,5 hours of continuous use (50% more than the regular Flashlight), the high beam mode lasts the same 25 seconds.
Unlike other item variants, multiple Miner's Flashlights may spawn (on Pilgrim, Voyageur and Stalker) making it the second variant which is not unique, the other one being the Sport Bow.
Miner's Flashlight was added in [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) update Part 3: "Frontier Comforts".
The Miner's Flashlight spawns a single time per world in various states of repair. The flashlight's location may differ between saves, but it is found within:
- Inside the boxcars located just after [Steely Chasm](./Steely%20Chasm.md) and near [Remnant Cave](./Remnant%20Cave.md), behind a [Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md)

It is also located in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), inside the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md) in a control room overlooking 2 large vats. It can be reached by walking further up the facility, jumping into a hopper, and then following the pipes to bypass a broken catwalk. This location will always spawn a Miner's Flashlight (except on Interloper).

1. Climbing to the plateau just below the [Mining Camp](./Mining%20Camp.md) (three [rope climbs](./Rope%20Climbing.md) required), and then crossing the north part of the map from west to east through many bridges, finally having to go through a choke point with a [bear](./Bear.md). Probably the longest and most dangerous path.

2. The safer path, climbing to [High Meadow](./High%20Meadow.md) from the plateau with the [Climber's Cave](./Climber%27s%20Cave.md) (two [rope climbs](./Rope%20Climbing.md)), cross a couple of bridges and that's it, no choke point, no bear.

3. The faster path, walking to the north until you reach the cave next to [Long Falls](./Long%20Falls.md), go through the cave (one [rope climb](./Rope%20Climbing.md) inside), then go through the choke point with the bear.

Once the area is visited another access can be opened, if the player deploys a [rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) from [Homesteader's Respite](./Homesteader%27s%20Respite.md), but to get there, another pretty long rope climb (with one ledge) is in the way. Once the rope is deployed, the resulting path would have two [rope climbs](./Rope%20Climbing.md) (one very long) but with an indoors shelter ([Homesteader's Respite](./Homesteader%27s%20Respite.md)) in between the two, and no chokepoint with bear, making it quite safe.

It is possible to reach [Homesteader's Respite](./Homesteader%27s%20Respite.md) from [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md) without a rope by walking up a nearby slope and sticking to the cliff-face, then dropping onto the ledge below. This path is the fastest for reaching Miner's Folly, however it clearly isn't a path Hinterland intended for players to take, and the steep angle may cause multiple sprains, which will require treatment before climbing the long rope to [Fire Overlook](./Fire%20Overlook.md).

A [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), [First Aid cabinet](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md), [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) as well as a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) are available in the main ruined barn, which is partly open to the elements and predators. Reclaimed wood and a few other miscellaneous supplies may be found scattered around the site or in containers. Fixed containers include a coal bin and a backpack.

There is also a small cabin that provides shelter and can be used as a [Safe House](./Safehouse.md). It has a [bed](./Bed.md) and some containers, along with [books](./Book.md), [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) (a guaranteed food can and soda and some random food as well), [clothing](./Clothing.md) (pants seem to be guaranteed under the bunkbed, with [Work Pants](./Work%20Pants.md) and [Combat Pants](./Combat%20Pants.md) being the most common), and curtains (one of the few sources of [cloth](./Cloth.md) in Ash Canyon). It might sometimes contain a [hatchet](./Hatchet.md) or a [hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md). The [Mining Log Page](./Mining%20Log%20Page.md) can be found on the table.

On the outside of the cabin, next to the door, will be pinned the [Memento Note](./Mementos.md) and Key that give access to the [Angler's Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md) lockbox (containing several fresh fish).

There may be [deer](./Deer.md) around to hunt, but when hunting or crafting at the work bench, it's a good idea to be aware of the [bear](./Bear.md) that lives in the nearby cave tunnel and wanders the area. The plateau may also be home to a [moose](./Moose.md) and up to 3 [wolves](./Wolf.md), making the area significantly more dangerous.
Although technically a separate location, the [Foreman's Retreat](./Foreman%27s%20Retreat.md) is located close-by up on the ridge.
- Up to 17 [Sticks](./Stick.md) will spawn after a blizzard. No branches or limbs will spawn.
- Five [Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) spawn next to the Ptarmigans at Foreman's Retreat.
- A [Moose](./Moose.md) can spawn in the same area as the deer, sometimes at the same time.

- A [Wolf](./Wolf.md) pack can spawn around the shack that contains the Workbench. • To be confirmed, but while the Bear, Moose and Deer can spawn alongside each other, it seems like the Bear and the Wolf pack are mutually exclusive.

- 5-8 [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) will spawn around the open shack where the Workbench is, under the smaller overhang open structures as well as near the Cabin where the Memento Note is pinned.
- There is a open walkthrough cave with a stick bed and possibly some minor loot in the rocks next to [Foreman's Retreat](./Foreman%27s%20Retreat.md).
- This cave can spawn a plastic container next to the stick bed which contains one of the region's two [Polaroids](./Polaroids.md). This is not a fixed spawn.
- A Rope bridge leads from [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md) south-east (down and right on in-game map) towards a cave with a container and eventually to [High Meadow](./High%20Meadow.md).

- When crossing, pay attention to the ground and wooden supports on both edges of the bridge as up to 80 [Cardboard Matches](./Cardboard%20Matches.md) spawn there, 20 on the northern side on the wood platform, 40 on the southern side just lazing on the ground and 20 on the southern side on nearby rocks (on the right side). This spot may be very important to check on Interloper, as sources of fire are scarce.

The Mining Camp is a location in the northwest corner of [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md). It is the only location that allows access to the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md), where you can find the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) and [crampons](./Crampons.md). Little shelter is available and the site contains little of value--only some [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) and [coal](./Coal.md).

A plastic container & large hatch can be found within the camp, and sometimes a [flashlight](./Flashlight.md) can spawn wedged between two rocks by the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md) entrance. There is also a [corpse](./Corpse.md) which can spawn by the nearby waterfall alongside a [Revolver](./Revolver.md).

Before going into the Mining camp, you will need a [mountaineering rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md), you can get this from the many rope climbs taken to get to the plateau overlooking the Mining camp or any of the mountaineering rope scattered around the area. On the plateau overlooking the Mining camp there is a wooden pulley system on the edge of the cliff. Right next to this is a rock that you can deploy a mountaineering rope onto and then climb down from there. Note there is a ledge about half way down the [rope climb](./Rope%20Climbing.md), this may not be as important going down, but will be when climbing out of the **Mining Camp.**
- When walking from the mine exit keep to the left stones, there may be a flashlight leaned against a crack in them (very near the mine).
- The first building when following the tracks from the mine, has a cupboard with randomized loot in the corner.
- There may be a plastic container near the water trough (gold mining riffles) at the creek.
- Follow the creek till the waterfall to find a searchable corpse, sometimes a [Revolver](./Revolver.md) spawns near it.

Misanthrope's Homestead can be reached by traversing over the frozen ice. The house has ample loot including processed [foods](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), clothing, and other useful supplies.

[Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) and [Green Birch Sapling](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) can be found on the island, and there may be a frozen corpse down hill from the house. Rabbits also spawn on the tiny island just to the west.

The island is often surrounded by [wolves](./Wolf.md), although they rarely come up onto the island unless in pursuit of a player. A small cave is located on the side of the island facing the land. A [bear](./Bear.md) may spawn near the cave, and [Deer](./Deer.md) and [cedar](./Cedar%20Limb.md) and [Fir](./Fir%20Limb.md) limbs can spawn on the island.
For players that have the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md), a [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) can be found a short distance east of the house.
As of the Part 6 Broken Silence update, a Pier is now found behind the island containing a [Trade Drop Box](./Trade%20Drop%20Box.md), which can be used to trade with the [Trader](./Trader.md).

Due to the island's proximity to Sutherland's Trade Drop Box, the two story house on the island has become a popular [safehouse](./Safehouse.md) in the region. The house is sufficiently spacious to accommodate [custom furniture](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) and has excellent hunting, fishing, and [beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) nearby. Furthermore, the [radio](./Radio.md) in the [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) is a short walk away. While it does not have a built in [workbench](./Work%20Bench.md), one of the benches from the Quonset can easily be disassembled and rebuilt here. One of the few weaknesses is the lack of an indoor fireplace.

[Sutherland](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md) lived here before the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), at which point he embarked onto his sailboat, never to set foot on Great Bear again. He will bring up that his father, his brother Wyatt, and he himself once lived in the home. Sutherland mentions that he has no desire to go back to his home and that the survivor can do with the property as they please.

Provides some shelter **Miserable Haunt** is a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md).

The cave is located on the cliffside in the southwestern most section of the lower valley, right next to [Seedling Spring](./Seedling%20Spring.md). Further south is the crossroads that leads to the transition to [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md). It is reached by scaling a [Rock Climb](./Rock%20Climb.md), and the cave itself is a source of [Coal](./Coal.md), being a great place to shelter if the weather turns bad without risking heading back to [Last Lonely House](./Last%20Lonely%20House.md).

There is always a simple tuffet type [Bed](./Bed.md) inside the cave, which is useful if the player is not carrying a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md). The cave can also have two beds. Be aware however, as the bed closest to the entrance is located in the cold section of the cave and does not offer a [Warmth](./Warmth.md) bonus. When using either bed, ensure the player character interacts with them when standing within the warm part of the cave, to avoid cold damage. There can also be a [Rim Grill](./Rim%20Grill.md) type fireplace by the beds for cooking, plus some possible spawned items.
The cave has a randomly generated interior, and can spawn with only a single tuffet bed in the cold part of the cave instead of two and no rim grill at all.

**Misery** is 5th and most challenging [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) Experience in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. Misery was added on June 24th, 2024 as part of the Part 5 update of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion. It is the standard "impossible" difficulty, being almost on the same level of difficulty as [Interloper](./Interloper.md), but with more handicaps to make survival even harder.

Misery features an extremely cold world with limited loot, abundant hostile wildlife and unique and permanent [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) that appear after surviving long enough. Misery was developed by [Hinterland Studio](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md) to instill a sense of apocalyptic hopelessness and to recreate a punishing game mode akin to the initial release of Interloper in 2016. This mode was made specifically to keep players from surviving for very long.
Misery is an extremely hard difficulty mode, even for the most hardcore of _The Long Dark_ players. The average life expectancy is around 20-40 days.

- [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md): outside [Draft Dodger's Cabin](./Draft%20Dodger%27s%20Cabin.md) (the cabin is always destroyed), at the bottom of the rope climb near [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md).

- Clothes: [Plaid Shirt](./Plaid%20Shirt.md) or [Hoodie](./Hoodie.md), [Jeans](./Jeans.md), [Thermal Underwear](./Thermal%20Underwear.md), [Sports Socks](./Sports%20Socks.md), [Leather Shoes](./Leather%20Shoes.md) or [Running Shoes](./Running%20Shoes.md).
- 5 Stages of Misery: periodically applies permanent semi-random Misery Afflictions, beginning with [Diminished Form](./Diminished%20Form.md) and ending with [Broken Body](./Broken%20Body.md).

- **Late-Game Interloper Temperature as Starting Temperature**: temperature drops 20°C by day 3 (on Interloper this happens by day 50). Temperatures are consistently -20°C to -65°C outdoors, with many indoors areas below zero without upgraded clothes.

- Most items cannot spawn ([firearms](./Hunting%20Rifle.md)/[survival bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), [hatchet](./Hatchet.md)/[hunting knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), [high quality clothes](./Expedition%20Parka.md)/[food](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md)) with ~90% of containers empty. Survival Bow, arrows and [animal skin clothing](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md) may be crafted but requires [forging](./Forge.md).
- Interloper level [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md), and [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) settings.
- The option to enable or disable the [Trader](./Trader.md) is present (though the Trader offers less loot than on Interloper settings).
Over time at fixed intervals, the survivor will be [Afflicted](./Afflictions.md) with the 5 Stages of Misery, permanent conditions unique to Misery Mode making survival increasingly challenging.

Stage 1 and 5 are always [Diminished Form](./Diminished%20Form.md) and [Broken Body](./Broken%20Body.md) respectively, with stages 2-4 randomized between: [Haunted Mind](./Haunted%20Mind.md), [Frigid Bones](./Frigid%20Bones.md), [Rheumatic Joints](./Rheumatic%20Joints.md), and [Sour Stomach](./Sour%20Stomach.md).
Note that [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) can still be studied even with these Afflictions.
- Hinterland designed Misery as an _"apocalyptic challenge even for the really hardcore players"_ who are able to survive for hundreds of days on Interloper mode.
- Misery is a combination of Stalker and Interloper settings (the hardest of both), with additional tweaks to increase difficulty.

- Misery shares similarities with the community-made Custom sandbox mode "No One Gets Out Alive" aka "NOGOA" (Code: 8sHM-/z8P-Dz+3-QZym-XQIC) and the official [Challenge](./Challenge.md) mode [As The Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md), but is considerably harder than both.

- During the Misery Mode beta, "Diminished Form" was named "Weak Constitution" with the [Status](./Survival%20Overlay.md) icon for [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md). Its text read: _"Weak Constitution: Caused by Misery. Weak Constitution Placeholder Description -Reduced stamina bar -Reduced carry capacity -Struggle wolf flee less likely to occur"_

- During the Misery Mode beta, all Misery Mode affliction prevented the reading of Research Books: _"You're not healthy enough to focus on research"_, similar to non-Misery afflictions. This was removed before release.

There can be decent amounts of gear inside, in addition to an abundance of [Coal](./Coal.md). It is strongly advised to bring a light source as there is a spiraling ramp at the start of the cave which can cause major injury to the player, even resulting in death. In addition, there can be various wood items in the area to gather, and up to two [wolves](./Wolf.md) may spawn in the area. In rare instances, a [Bear](./Bear.md) can wander from their den to the east. Don't worry, there are no wolves inside the cave.
- An "[Advanced Guns Guns Guns!](./Advanced%20Guns%20Guns%20Guns!.md)" [research book](./Research%20Book.md) occasionally spawns next to the metal box.
- At a dead-end, a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) can spawn with a [Flare](./Flare.md) and some food lying around in the vicinity.
- A possible [Cowichan Sweater](./Cowichan%20Sweater.md) can be found next to the camp fire after the water fall.
- If lucky, a [survival bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) can spawn in an intersection in the cave, sometimes next to a corpse.
- Outside the cave, at the picnic area, a frozen corpse may have their rifle lying next to them.
- A chance of [Spelunker's Lantern](./Spelunker%27s%20Lantern.md) spawning after the waterfall in the crouching area

- The three frozen corpses inside, one of whose head was crushed by a fallen rock, could have been the friends of the mountain climber who left a page of [his journal](./Climber%27s%20Journal%20Page.md) in the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md) in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md).
- However, this incident could have instead occurred at the [Point of Disagreement](./Point%20of%20Disagreement.md), not far from the cave.

- The area accessed through the waterfall inside the cave has small patches of bio-luminescent moss along some of the walls, just like the [ice caves](./Ice%20Cave.md) in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md).
- Up to two hunting rifles (one inside, one outside) and a bow with arrows can be found here in the same run.

The picnic area is just downstream of a waterfall, presumably called Misty Falls. It can be easily identified by the picnic benches next to the river.

A [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), with a backpack and a container with some possible loot, as well as a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) may be lying next to the river. **Molly's Husband** is the deceased former husband of [Molly](./Molly.md) found by [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) at the start of [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md). He is found as a corpse near the start of the Episode.

Very little information about Molly's Husband is known outside of Molly's biased testimony of him. His real name is unknown and the local area of Pleasant Valley has no notes mentioning his name or past behavior.

Married to Molly at an undisclosed date in the past, Molly's Husband lived with his wife on the [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) for many years. It is heavily implied that the marriage between the two was an abusive one, given Molly's misandrist outlook regarding men as she begins to open up to Astrid more and more. An uncomfortable family photo of the two can be found inside the Farmstead. Molly would later angrily remark that her life could have been better had she been anything but a simple farmer's wife, showing the depths of the abusive relationship she shared with her husband.

Some time around the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), a pack of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) attacked the Farmstead, forcing Molly's Husband to confront them with the household [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md). A misfire occurred during the confrontation, causing the barrel of the rifle to explode and leaving Molly's Husband defenseless to the oncoming Timberwolves. When Molly's Husband pleaded for his wife to offer help, Molly instead chose to stand idly by and allow the wolves to kill him, later remarking that "she did not murder him, but it was her intention for him to die" on that day.

Molly would later drive off the wolves and recover her husband's body along with the exploded rifle, storing them both in the farmhouse. Astrid eventually discovers Molly's Husband in the cellar, covered with a cloth, much to Molly's dismay. He has been dead for some time, considering how blue his corpse is once uncovered.

Though Molly feels more liberated than ever, Molly's has developed an unhealthy and highly misandrist stance regarding men even long after her husband's death. Molly's hatred of men can be seen in her brutal interactions with the local [Convicts](./Convicts.md), silently hunting them with a bow and arrow and leaving their corpses in the snow where they fall, often not even bothering to recover the arrow still attached to their bodies.

> “__Years on a working farm in a remote corner of Great Bear Island have left their mark on Molly. She’s plain-spoken, often blunt -- she sees the world for what it is. There are no illusions inhabiting Molly’s life and she likes it that way.
Other than the farm and regular subsistence hunting, simple pleasures -- tea and the wanderings of her own imagination -- keep Molly occupied.__”

**Molly** is the first non-player character encountered in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). She lives in the [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md).

[Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) begins with a cutscene of from Molly's point of view, where she finds [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) almost dead in the snow. Molly carries Astrid back to her home, the Pleasant Valley Farmstead. Molly leaves to go hunting, and returns with meat some time later. After a tense conversation with Astrid, Molly storms out but does not return again. She later calls Astrid on the telephone to ask for help fighting off [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) that have cornered her and again later to offer assistance and briefly discuss a personal secret. A prisoner Molly killed is located outside [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md).

Much about Molly's background is unknown besides that she has seemingly been on Great Bear island for most of her life and resents the fact that she hasn't done more with her life. A cattleman's daughter and a farmer's wife, Molly has recently lost [her husband](./Molly%27s%20Husband.md) to wolves, although Molly admits she allowed it to happen. Afterwards she stored the body in her basement for unknown reasons.

The bitter tone Molly uses when discussing her husband and her apparent lack of remorse may allude to possible domestic abuse going on before hand. Molly explains to Astrid over the phone at one point that "I let myself feel small so that he could feel like somebody. I gave up everything for him, and to him I didn't even exist. I let him make me small. Less than nothing." Eventually, Molly grew the desire to kill her husband, but never had the courage to do so, until the wolves arrived one day and gave her her chance. Even with a rifle in her hand, she chose to do nothing, and the wolves killed her husband. This freed her from her husband's influence but left her with a dim outlook on the world.

Molly eventually finds Astrid in the snow after the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) and nurses her back to health, though locks her inside her home to prevent her from leaving. After Astrid finds the body of Molly's husband and escapes Molly's Farmhouse, she keeps here distance from Astrid, spying on her from the hills while also hunting the male Convicts scattered across the Valley .

Molly begins calling Astrid occasionally over the Valley's phone party lines. She intially questions why Astrid chooses to help the [Crash Survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md) despite gaining no recognition for her actions, before switching each subsequent phone call over to discussing her husband. After awhile, she leaves Astrid alone as she searches for more survivors.

As Astrid is ready to leave Pleasant Valley, Molly calls Astrid to tell her about the radio transmitter at [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) that she could use to contact Perseverance Mills, before hanging up. Astrid goes there and eventually makes contact with Perseverance Mills.

Molly is last heard on the phone from the radio tower at Signal Hill, fully confessing her hatred for her husband and believing that she and Astrid are in the same boat, now liberated from their husbands and men's oppression in general. This attitude may be the reason why Molly is hunting down the group of male prisoners that escaped from the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) as she now fully committed to her misandrist mindset regarding men in general, saying that "it feels good to finally be on this side of the hunt" and "They're all going to pay now, Astrid."

Molly ends her phone call by asking Astrid if Mackenzie is "One of the good ones". Astrid says that he is, and that while things are complicated between the two of them, she would be upset to find an arrow in his back. Molly ends the phone call by saying "Then I hope to never meet him" while wishing Astrid good luck on her journey to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), hoping that Astrid finds some peace for herself. Astrid in turn hopes that Molly will also find peace within herself.
Molly is briefly seen in the ending cutscene for the Episode, but is not seen again for the rest of Wintermute.

At the beginning of Episode 4 while dragging Mackenzie across the snow, [Heller](./Heller.md) and [Vachon](./Vachon.md) discuss a dead convict ([Leclerc](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md)) found with an arrow in his chest, which was most likely hinting at Molly's work.
Molly and Astrid's phone calls may have briefly connected to the [Hunting Lodge's](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) [Phone Box](./Phone%20Box.md) in Episode 2, explaining the ringing phone.

Many waterfalls can be found near the lake, including [Watchful Falls](./Watchful%20Falls.md), [Banner Falls](./Banner%20Falls.md), and [Quarrelling Falls](./Quarrelling%20Falls.md). [Lake Cave](./Lake%20Cave.md) near Watchful Falls is the only natural shelter immediately adjacent to the lake, however there are two caves located not far away: [Peak Cave](./Peak%20Cave.md) up the hill to the east, and [Pensive Vista](./Pensive%20Vista.md) a short walk to the south. A [Moose](./Moose.md) may spawn on Monolith Lake near Watchful Falls, and there is an area with rabbits nearby. A [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md), and a [Hidden Cache](./Hidden%20Cache.md) can spawn around the lake. Southeast of the lake, [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) may be found along a hill. Going even further up leads to a higher elevation useful for mapping, as well as [Peak Cave](./Peak%20Cave.md), which may contain some useful loot.
The lake is notable for being the only location in the region with water that's deep enough for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md).

**Moose Meat (Cooked)** is a cooked [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.

Cooked Moose Meat is obtained by using a lit [Fire](./Fire.md) and improves the [Cooking](./Cooking.md) skill. Cooking increases its condition by 50%, makes it decay 4 times slower than raw meat, and adds a reduced chance of [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) over raw meat.
Using a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) reduces cooking time by 25%. Cooked food on an active fire for too long will burn it, destroying the item and damaging a Cooking Pot if used.

**Moose Quarter**s are sections harvested from a [Moose](./Moose.md), after using the _quarter action_.

Moose can be quartered into these large bags for easier transport. These bags will only contain meat that needs be further harvested before it can become cookable [Moose Meat (Raw)](./Moose%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md).

Each moose quarter will always have useable meat equal to 50% of the total weight of the quarter, meaning you are carrying more weight than the amount of meat that you will receive. This tradeoff can be useful if signs of an onsetting blizzard are apparent, and it will become unsafe to harvest where the moose is located. Any remaining raw meat left inside the bag will be lost if the Quarter's Condition reaches 0%, with bags spoiling within 1 day of harvesting.

Moose-Hide Cloaks are crafted torso wear with extremely high waterproof and the second highest protection of any item, right behind the [Ballistic Vest](./Ballistic%20Vest.md), but offer less warmth than the [Expedition Parka](./Expedition%20Parka.md), [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md) and [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md). Moose Hides can be difficult to acquire due to the rarity and danger of moose, as well as requiring 10 days to [cure](./Curing.md); this makes repairing Moose-Hide Cloaks challenging. Instead, existing cloaks may be [harvested](./Harvesting.md) (yielding 1 cured moose hide) and then re-crafted into a new cloak. This process takes 16.67 hours longer than repairing and is more expensive with [Cured Guts](./Cured%20Gut.md): but allows repeated use of the same hide.

Note: Crafting Moose-Hide Cloaks costs durability of the used tool (e.g. [hunting knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md)), though this is usually less resource-intensive than to kill another [moose](./Moose.md).

**Moose-Hide Satchel** is a type of accessory [Clothing](./Clothing.md) in _The Long Dark_.

The Moose-hide Satchel is a clothing item that when worn in either accessory slot, grants a bonus 5kg of [carry capacity](./Encumbrance.md) (11lbs). Only one satchel can be worn at a time. The satchel provides no other bonuses, such as [Warmth](./Warmth.md) or [windproofing](./Clothing.md#Windproof).
Like other clothing, the satchel is vulnerable to damage from [Struggle](./Struggle.md) and [blizzards](./Weather.md), though it is sturdy and relatively easy to repair.
- The Satchel's carry capacity bonus stacks with the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) and [Well Fed](./Well%20Fed.md) benefit.
- The Satchel is repaired with [Cured Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md), not a [Cured Moose Hide](./Cured%20Moose%20Hide.md).

- Wearing a Moose-hide Satchel as an outer accessory (right) and any inner accessory like [Wool Ear Wrap](./Wool%20Ear%20Wrap.md) or [Improvised Insulation](./Improvised%20Insulation.md) in the inner (left) will protect the accessory - until the satchel is destroyed - from both wildlife and adverse weather like snow. Moose-Hide Satchels are far more durable than other accessories, and often survive wildlife attacks if initially above 50% condition.

**Moose** are large, solitary animals in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. They appear rarely in most regions and can be difficult to find. Their hides and meat are useful, but they are aggressive and can cause serious injury when provoked.

Moose are the largest and toughest of prey animals and can be dangerous if provoked. Their movements resemble [Deer](./Deer.md), but a Moose will charge the player if approached close (similar to the behavior of [Bears](./Bear.md)). A moose will first adopt a stiff, threatening posture before charging and snorts to attempt to intimidate the player into backing off. If the player does not leave the immediate vicinity, the moose will charge the player.

A [Moose Carcass](./Moose%20Carcass.md) may be harvested for 30.00-45.00 kg of raw meat, 1 [Fresh Moose Hide](./Fresh%20Moose%20Hide.md) and 12 guts. Moose hides can be cured to craft [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) or [Moose-Hide Cloak](./Moose-Hide%20Cloak.md).

Moose have three paces: walking, fleeing, and charging. They behave similar to deer when roaming, stopping to sniff the ground or raise their head to listen. Moose do not actively hunt the player but will attack if approached or provoked. Possible locations for moose are marked by scratches on trees; moose are rarely far from these marked areas, though they may despawn for extended periods.

![A Moose and Bear ignoring one another](../assets/Moose_and_Bear.jpg)_A Moose and Bear ignoring one another_ Moose will ignore [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md), [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), [Deer](./Deer.md), and [Bear](./Bear.md), but will flee from the presence of a [Cougar](./Cougar.md), [Wolf](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md). Wolves will not attack and kill a Moose, but instead will flee, making the Moose the only prey animal they will not hunt.

While wandering within close proximity of a suitable tree, an antler rub on a tree can be found. These markings can be used to triangulate a Moose's location within a region. This can make tree rubbings useful indicators for finding (or avoiding) a Moose.

![Moose in hostile posture - The player is too close.](../assets/Moosewarning.png)_Moose in hostile posture - The player is too close._ Moose have a detection radius within which they become aware of the player. When the player is within the radius, Moose will stop walking and turn to stare at the player, grunting and stomping on the ground as a warning. If the player fails to leave the radius immediately, the Moose will charge and attempt to trample the player (except on Pilgrim, where they stomp and then flee unless provoked).

A Moose will immediately charge any player that fires a projectile or otherwise attacks/attempts to attack it. Similar to Bears, Moose will only charge if it can access the player's location; otherwise it will flee.

Should a charging Moose reach the player, a one-sided [Struggle](./Struggle.md) will ensue (similar to bear struggles, in that the animal always wins). After which the player will pass out, and wake up 10%-50% [Condition](./Condition.md) lost, the Broken Ribs affliction (see below), their equipped weapon on the ground, and distorted vision. The moose will still be nearby, and may attack again should the player not flee immediately.

Moose attacks inflict a unique [Affliction](./Afflictions.md): [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md), which reduces carrying capacity and greatly reduces [Stamina](./Stamina.md) for 120 Hours (in-game) while your character fully heals, even with treatment. Additionally Broken Ribs makes it impossible to [rope climb](./Rope%20Climbing.md) until the affliction is healed (except temporarily, while under the effects of an [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md)).
If your character is trampled again whilst already suffering from Broken Ribs, subsequent Broken Ribs Afflictions will take incrementally longer to heal.

Charging Moose are not deterred by [flares](./Flare.md), [torches](./Torch.md), or [arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md): only being fired upon by any firearm will deter it. Also, Moose will turn and retreat if no navigable path to the player is available (e.g., in tight spaces like rock crevice or elevated position such as a rock formation).
- Thrown [stones](./Stone.md) outside a Moose's line of sight generally cause them to flee. This can be useful if a Moose is blocking an essential path.

- Repeated shots from firearms will stop a charging Moose in its tracks. Each shot will cause the moose to be stunned momentarily and stop, allowing the player to essentially stun-lock the moose while they escape.

Unlike other [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md), Moose do not suffer from [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md). This makes killing Moose more difficult, likely requiring multiple shots to bring one down. It is possible to kill a Moose with one shot, most likely a critical hit on their head, but Moose typically require four or more shots from any weapon to down ([Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), and [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) all roughly equivalent). It is possible to kill Moose without a ranged weapon by using [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md), but this is generally very inefficient as it will require multiple Noisemakers. As there is a lot of [meat](./Moose%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md) on a moose, not to mention a heavy [hide](./Fresh%20Moose%20Hide.md) and multiple [guts](./Fresh%20Gut.md), is is advisable to travel light or bring a [Travois](./Travois.md) before going hunting, otherwise the [carcass](./Moose%20Carcass.md) contents will be [too heavy to transport](./Encumbrance.md).
- A careful shot from long range, then repeated shots as the Moose charges, hopefully killing it before it reaches the player.

- Sniper nests in locations inaccessible by the moose, like the rock outcrop near [Pensive Pond](./Pensive%20Pond.md). This approach requires competent weapon use, as it is likely to be a long-distance shot(s). Moose usually run a short distance away after the first hit, but return moments later allowing for further shots.
- Moose hunting with a Revolver is dangerous due to the weapon's low stopping power and range. (e.g. 8 Headshots, or Chest: 14, Hind: 16, Foot: 16 on Voyageur)
- An exploding Noisemaker will hurt a moose, and can even kill it if it has been previously injured.

Moose may spawn rarely in all major [Regions](./Region.md) except [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), often spawning then despawning for long periods of time. It may take many days before they respawn in the same location.

In particular, most active moose areas have a 25% chance every in-game 48 hours of spawning a moose. Exceptions to this are [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) spawns with a 35% chance and [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) spawn in [Mystery Lake (region)](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) with a 30% chance. There are also special areas near [Trapper's Cabin](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md), [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md), [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) and [Matt's Truck](./Matt%27s%20Truck.md) where no moose rubbings are present. These rare spawn locations have a 5% chance of spawning a moose every in-game 48 hours. If a moose spawns, it will stay for a 48 hour period until again despawning. After the 48 hour period is over, the moose will despawn when next entering through a loading screen or reloading the game.

- Moose are based off the real world [Moose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moose) (**_Alces alces_**), the largest species of Cervidae. All Moose in game are male bulls.[1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moose)
