The term **Mountain Goating** is an informal term popularized on the [Hinterland Forums](https://hinterlandforums.com) (similar to [Daisy Chaining](./Daisy%20Chaining.md) and [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md)), which is used to refer to the gameplay practice of players "sticking" to extremely steep terrain that is not normally climbable.

The premise of Mountain Goating relies on how the game calculates slopes. When a slope exceeds a certain steepness, the player character will not be able to walk uphill (gain y-levels). However, as long as there's no overhang on the slope, the player character will not slide downhill, and can walk across the slope (change x and z position) as easily as if the ground were level.

While this technique is most often used for going downhill, careful, strategic planning can allow players to climb _up_ hills and even cliffs that look at first glance to be unclimbable. Going uphill generally involves walking across a steep, unclimbable slope to reach a spot where the slope is sufficiently shallow to allow the player character to walk uphill. When the player has climbed up as far as is possible in that location, they walk across the slope again until they find another spot where they can walk uphill. Climbing up a long, steep cliff may require going back and forth across a crag several times.

Mountain Goating's main benefit is to enable players to take shortcuts. For example, a popular option is to climb down the [Summit](./Summit.md) of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) on the side facing [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md). This enables players to carry far more load than normal, and also avoids the fatigue of climbing down ropes. With careful planning, this technique can also be used to evade chasing [wildlife](./Wildlife.md), as animals won't be able to path on any terrain that the player character can't walk up. ![A wolf that's unable to reach the player due to uneven terrain.](../assets/Wolf_stuck_to_terrain.png)_A wolf that's unable to reach the player due to uneven terrain._

The main drawback of Mountain Goating is that there's a high likelihood of getting sprains, [torn clothing](./Torn%20Clothing.md), and injuries, as it requires walking across very steep slopes and falling from substantial heights. [Crampons](./Crampons.md) or [Improvised Crampons](./Improvised%20Crampons.md) along with not being encumbered can help mitigate this risk somewhat, but won't eliminate it. Another danger of Mountain Goating is falling if players accidentally walk towards an overhang they didn't see. Additionally, certain areas of the game were filled with death planes by the developers to stop Mountain Goating being used there, most notable example being Ravine, which eliminates most routes that allow the player to avoid rope climbing to get into lower part of the region.

Another drawback, only applicable to players who have purchased [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), is that it is impossible to use a deployed [Travois](./Travois.md) when Mountain Goating. However, since speed is rarely a priority when Mountain Goating and the player can still move (albeit slowly) as long as [Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md) is not in excess of 30 kg, it is possible to move all the gear from the Travois into the player's backpack, Mountain Goat through the difficult terrain, and re-deploy the Travois on flatter ground.

**Mountain Town** is 8th [Region](./Region.md) released in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), and is centered around the small, recently abandoned town of [Milton](./Milton.md).

It is the setting for [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), as well as the 8th region added to [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). Milton is accessible via [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md) (through a cave near the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md)), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) (at [Marsh Ridge ](./Marsh%20Ridge.md)through a Rose Bush climb to [Milton Basin](./Milton%20Basin.md)), and to [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) (through a cave between the [Trailer](./Trailer%20%28Mountain%20Town%20Region%29.md) and [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md)).

It is the setting for [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), as well as the 8th region added to [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). Milton is accessible via [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md) (through a cave near the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md)), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) (at [Marsh Ridge ](./Marsh%20Ridge.md)through a Rose Bush climb to [Milton Basin](./Milton%20Basin.md)), and to [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) (through a cave between the [Trailer](./Trailer%20%28Mountain%20Town%20Region%29.md) and [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md)).

Milton, the major point of interest in this region, is located approximately in the center of the map, and features a number of houses that can be searched for supplies, along with vehicles, a [post office](./Milton%20Post%20Office.md) and a [bank](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md). While [wolves](./Wolf.md) do occasionally wander into town, they can often be avoided by ducking into a vehicle or building.

From the center of the region, at the crossroads near the bank, players can follow the roads and travel out of town in four different directions. Heading northwards will take them via a woodlot to [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md), which features abundant natural resources nearby. From here, the region becomes less developed, and, while richer in natural resources, is frequented by wolves and the occasional [moose](./Moose.md). Continuing along the road, players will pass by a [Trailer](./Trailer%20%28Mountain%20Town%20Region%29.md) with a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), followed by the cave leading to the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md). The road ends shortly after [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md), where there are lots of vehicles from which to hunt the [bear](./Bear.md) that spawns nearby.

Going out of town towards the east will first lead players to a [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md) after a short climb (no rope). Passing a shallow cave to the right (which can provide [coal](./Coal.md)), players will encounter a small pond, which provides a safe place for hunting [deer](./Deer.md) and [snaring](./Snare.md) [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) without the threat of wolves. Continuing up another root climb will lead players past another small pond, and eventually into a ravine where [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) lies. Moderately valuable loot often spawns around the crashed plane.

Players leaving town towards the south will initially pass by the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md), located in the center of a [Wood Lot](./Wood%20Lot.md). The gas station can't be opened without a [prybar](./Prybar.md), but once inside, usually yields a fair amount of food and a few items of clothing. The nearby [crashed bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) has some importance in [story mode](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), but is merely a landmark in survival mode. Continuing southwards will lead players to [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md) and the [Picnic Area](./Picnic%20Area.md), featuring a small building and a rope climb down. Going down this rope and up the next will eventually lead players to [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), after a walk along a frozen brook and through a cave.

Finally, players can head out of town towards the west. The first major destination is the [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md), which initially requires a key found nearby to unlock. The farm usually has an abundance of food, and mid-level clothing. Beyond the farm, going down two long climbing ropes will lead to Milton Basin. This location has lots of natural resources, but explorers should watch for the moose that spawns nearby. Walking along the frozen lake past the [Hermit's Cabin](./Hermit%27s%20Cabin.md) (mostly destroyed, but offering a stove), players will find the connection to [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md).

Players who wish to have their [safe house](./Safehouse.md) in this region should keep in mind that entering/leaving Mountain Town from any other [region](./Region.md) besides the Hushed River Valley will require the use of [rope climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md), making a [Travois](./Travois.md) impractical and limiting the amount of gear a player can take along.

Mountain Town is a region rich in [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) and [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md). Cat Tails can be found in abundance along the banks of the river passing by [Milton](./Milton.md) and at a pond in town, throughout the [Milton Basin](./Milton%20Basin.md), behind [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md), near the [Trailer](./Trailer%20%28Mountain%20Town%20Region%29.md), under the [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md), and near the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md). The region also features high density of Rose Hips, particularly around and near [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md). There is also the highest concentration of [Oak Trees](./Oak%20Tree.md) of all regions, along with corresponding high amount of harvestable [Acorns](./Acorns.md), present especially around the Milton Park and Picnic Area.

- According to the game's developer, the name _Mountain Town_ was intended to be an "internal name only" for the Milton area;[^1] however the name appears on both the Great Bear Island map and the region map of the area.

- In Survival Mode, 'returning' to the original plane crash site (the starting area in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md)) is actually worthwhile, as the site itself (or rarely, a car leading to the site) may yield a copy of "[_Advanced Guns, Guns, Guns!_](./Skills.md)" and a number of [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md). Also, the green crates at the site can be broken down, potentially revealing loot inside. In addition, the [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md) holds numerous lootable cars, of which one single trunk/frozen corpse will contain a mid-to-high tier coat or parka (randomly placed).

- The region has an unusually high number of [Wolves](./Wolf.md) in Survival Mode, even on lower difficulties. In Story mode, [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) and [Will](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) discuss the inordinately large number of wolves in the area, with Grey Mother commenting that _"wolves are quick to move in when the people go"_.
_The map found in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) is different from Survival Mode_
- Mountain Town became available in Survival Mode on 7 December 2017 in the [Rugged Sentinel](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog%20%E2%80%94%20Archive%201.md#1.16) update.

It is the only suitable man-made location for setting up a [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) in the entire region, and many players choose to use it as their main base. This is because it has all the essentials: a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), two [beds](./Bed.md), and a fireplace. There is also a large hatch in the floor that can hold up to 40 kg of items. Hides, guts, and saplings can be cured inside the building. Furthermore, there is [ice fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) on Crystal Lake nearby, along with [Bear](./Bear.md), [Moose](./Moose.md), [Deer](./Deer.md), [Wolf](./Wolf.md), and [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) hunting opportunities in the local area. Although being far from a [forge](./Forge.md) may make it difficult to replace lost arrows and damaged tools, the Mountaineer's Hut is fairly close to the [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) and [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) at [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), making it easier to maintain tools and replace used ammunition.

A small number of harvestable items like crates, a shelf, and a stool can be found inside. The hut also contains a [climber's journal page](./Climber%27s%20Journal%20Page.md). A few relatively rare supplies may also be found in the hut, along with a chance to spawn a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) on the front porch.

The hut is not properly insulated, and there is a big hole in the roof. Unlike indoor areas that have a loading screen and an absolute inside temperature, the hut is more similar to a shallow cave and does not have a fixed temperature, rather providing protection from wind and a relative warmth bonus of +30 °C compared to the weather outside (+33 °C with repaired roof). In very cold weather, the hut does not provide adequate protection, so it is recommended the player wear high-quality clothing and/or maintain a fire to avoid freezing. Repairing the roof of the mountaineer's hut using safe house customization provides an additional +3 C to the structure's warmth bonus, and requires:
Note that despite being considered "outside" in terms of [Decay](./Decay.md), leather can be [Cured](./Curing.md) inside, and you can still get [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md).

| - Firewood - [Firearm Cleaning Kit](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md) - [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) - [Research Books](./Skills.md) - 3x [Flare Shell](./Flare%20Shell.md) - Assorted [food and drinks](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) - [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) - [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) | - Mid quality clothes - Materials - [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) - [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) - [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) - 3x [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md) - Matches (Interloper) |
There may be a [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) on one of the boats near the lake.
Between the hut and the [Summit](./Tail%20Section.md) there are two [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md), on the first hill (does not spawn on [Interloper](./Survival%20Mode.md)).
The [Cargo Container](./Cargo%20Container.md) on the left (doesn't spawn in Interloper) as you look towards the Summit contains:

**Mountaineering Boots** are a type of [Clothing](./Clothing.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ obtained exclusively in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).
Mountaineering Boots stats are identical to [Mukluks](./Mukluks.md), except they are 0.50kg lighter.
Their appearance is similar to [Trail Boots](./Trail%20Boots.md), but with yellow laces instead of red ones.
Mountaineering Boots are given to the player by [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) if the player completes the side mission [One Last Thing](./One%20Last%20Thing.md).
They can be carried into [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) if they are still in the player's inventory, but are otherwise unique to Episode 1.

The Boots are lost in [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) if they were in the player's inventory at the end of Episode 2, likely discarded by [Mathis](./Mathis.md) in order to make transporting Mackenzie easier.
They are given by Grey Mother once the player fully raises her Trust and selects the "BETTER BOOTS" dialogue option.
They can be carried into Episode 2: Luminance Fugue if they are still in the player's inventory, but are otherwise unique to Episode 1.
It's implied by Grey Mother that these boots once belonged to [Lilith Barker](./Lilith%20Barker.md), since they are the best footwear for climbing mountains.
- As part of the Redux edition update, Grey Mother now awards the boots when completing [One Last Thing](./One%20Last%20Thing.md) instead of as the last Trust reward.
- Also changed the description from "Especially rugged boots given to you by Grey Mother, for earning her Trust."

**Mountaineering Rope** is a tool used for [climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) cliff faces.

The mountaineering rope is used in conjunction with the [rope climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) gameplay mechanic to allow the player to ascend and descend vertical cliffs. The rope must be attached to a certain type of rock feature at the top of a climbable cliff before the climb can be made. While important for traversing mountainous terrain in some regions and caves, using mountaineering ropes can quickly exhaust the player, possibly leading to injury or death from a fall or trapping the player on an inhospitable cliff side.
Many ropes are already deployed from rocks over climbable cliffs, but these can be removed and deployed from other cliffs instead. Non-deployed ropes might be found in the following areas:
- On a bridge on the route towards the [Mining Camp](./Mining%20Camp.md) and [Wolf's Jaw Overlook](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md), west of the [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md)
- By an old campfire in the clearing at the end of the trail above [Homesteader's Respite](./Homesteader%27s%20Respite.md)
- On a Metal table near the [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) in the workshop of [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md)

- [Version 0.321](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.321) extends the use of ropes to maps other than [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) and makes the spawn locations Added.

> “**Manufactured boot inspired by the traditional hunter's footwear. Designed for mobility and warmth using leather and fur. You can stay warm and move quickly.**”

Mukluks are high tier boots and one of the rarest items in _The Long Dark_. Few containers have Mukluks in their loot table, most notable being Safes and similar high-loot tier locations. Mukluks cannot spawn on Interloper.

Mukluks are similar to the [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md) in stats, offering the same warmth and windchill bonus but are 0.5 kg lighter. However, Mukluks are 10 percent less waterproof, have -3% stamina (vs -5%), and offer 2% less protection from wildlife.

In [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) is required to cross this bridge during the mission [The Detonators](./The%20Detonators.md) in order to retrieve [Detonators](./Detonators.md) within the mine. Upon completing it, an earthquake destroys an entrance to the mine and the bridge is permanently destroyed for the rest of the episode, forcing Will to find another way back to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md).

In Survival Mode, the bridge has been destroyed by a landslide. In order to access Last Prospect, the player must take an alternate path starting from the bottom of the ravine nearby which is accessed by climbing down a long rope at [Fool's Corner](./Fool%27s%20Corner.md), which is guarded by a wolf. The survivor then has to jump down a small waterfall, evade two more wolves and climb up two ropes with no shelter in between them, before continuing onto a path to the mine; the same path that the player uses to return to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md).

There is a supply crate possibly containing a [MRE](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md) and [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) underneath the now collapsed bridge. These supplies are quite helpful in scaling the cliff up to [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md).

There is a [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) a few steps from the bridge. It is reached by following the rock on the right (when looking from the bridge), climbing up a small incline and going around a [Scrub Brush](./Scrub%20Brush.md).

Muskeg Overlook is a large clearing with a single access point. A shortwave radio tower (the eastern-most in the region) is well visible at the top from certain angles. In the area, there may be a [deer](./Deer.md) carcass, a backpack (which may contain rare food like [MRE](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md) or clothing), and a hollow tree, as well as plants such as [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md), [rose hips](./Rose%20Hip.md), [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) and a single [burdock](./Burdock.md) plant. The overlook also includes an area with several [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and occasionally a flock of [ptarmigans](./Ptarmigan.md). This point provides visibility of much of the region. The paths of several [wolves](./Wolf.md) lead around the area. It is possible to "Mountain goat" down the cliff where the railing meets the cliff face to take a shortcut towards [Abandoned Camp](./Abandoned%20Camp.md) and eventually [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) with only a minor risk of sprains.

One of the [transmitter](./Transmitters.md) towers can also be found here, a [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md) and possibly a [Replacement Fuse](./Replacement%20Fuse.md) as well as one [Wire Bundle](./Wires.md) can be found in a supply bin underneath the tower. When the tower is active during the [Aurora](./Aurora.md), its signals spread across Forlorn Muskeg, [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md), and [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md).

A downed helicopter (which can easily be found using the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md)) can be found a short distance south of the tower, and a lockbox can be found near that. Notable loot includes a possible [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) inside the helicopter, a [Prybar](./Prybar.md), and a small amount of food.

- South of the ice cave entrance by [Mammoth Falls](./Mammoth%20Falls.md), overlooking [Long Shot Falls](./Long%20Shot%20Falls.md) and the lower valley, or

- Above [Many Falls Vista](./Many%20Falls%20Vista.md) to the north. This site can be accessed by ice cave, or by climbing the rope that would lead to [Lonely Cave](./Lonely%20Cave.md) in the central portion of the valley.

The exact location of the fire may differ in each game, but it can usually be reached via one of the [Ice Cave](./Ice%20Cave.md) systems or by [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md), though walls of [Scrub Brush](./Scrub%20Brush.md) may block the way. ## Overview

The Signal Fire generally sits beside a camp containing a [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md), a burnt out [Campfire](./Campfire.md), possibly a corpse, and some useful food or clothing items. A [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) can be found hanging from a branch in the area, except in Interloper experiences. The signal fire is one of the few places where man-made objects are likely to be found in the region.

The Signal Fire provides no warmth since it is almost burned out. Try to go to this location towards the end of your time in region, as the smoke can help serve as a useful landmark for orientating your position.

- Originally the signal fire was just a giant [Campfire](./Campfire.md) when Hushed River Valley was first released. The model was eventually replaced with a pyre when [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) was released (similar to the one in front of the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md)).

- Aside from seemingly recent [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), this signal fire is the only evidence that another human could still be alive on the Island in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), though the producer of the signal fire is never found.

The Mystery Lake region is an Alpine valley, average altitude of 1200 meters above sea level, named for the large lake that dominates its South-Eastern quadrant. The region is fringed by mountains on the West and South, and the foothills of the Inner Island Range to the North and East. The region is bisected by a section of the North-South line of the Trans-Island Railway.

The region’s main characteristics are its heavily forested and hilly terrain, as well as abundance of wildlife. The region’s high altitude leads to low average temperatures, as well as some of the coldest night-time temperatures on Great Bear Island. Heavy snowfalls are common.

The Mystery Lake area is a popular Summer-time destination with campers and hikers, but the area largely shuts down during the Winter months due to its inaccessibility: there are no major roads connecting the area to the more populated regions in the adjoining valleys lower in the mountain chain, so the area is primarily accessed by dedicated hikers willing to make the long trek that winds along medium to advanced-level trails, from the nearest town of Rupert’s Landing.

The region’s harsh inaccessibility has been both a blessing and a curse over the years. Until the railway line was blasted through in the 1930s, the area was largely a pristine and untouched wilderness, but the lack of amenities or a standing population made it difficult for any real permanent infrastructure to take root. A project to link the Mystery Lake area with a secondary highway network criss-crossing between the various mountain valleys was abandoned due to the geological instability of the steep mountains and cliffs the highway caused landslides that were a continuous threat to the project’s viability, and the highway project was abandoned after only a few kms of roadway had been cleared.

In the 1960s, ambitious industrialist Richard Carter selected the Mystery Lake area for a new hydro-electric project, meant to provide power to a large mining operation in the next valley. The lake’s continuous replenishment by a vibrant aquifer network as well as mountain streams that channeled annual Spring runoff, made Mystery Lake a natural reservoir with untapped hydro-electric potential. Yet other than a small test dam constructed in 1962, this project was abandoned when the region’s inaccessibility and seismic instability made it cost-prohibitive.

To this day, apart from the railway line that passes through, the only connection between the Mystery Lake region and the adjoining valleys are the hiking trails that pass through the mountains. These trails often become impassable during the Winter months, due to cold temperatures and heavy snowfall. Also, due to the region’s generally uninhabited nature, wildlife have not become habituated to the presence of humans, which can make them threatening. Hikers and campers are warned to avoid the area during the Winter months, as well as to store all food and waste in “bear safe” containers.

Mystery Lake is a good location for collecting supplies due to the abundance of cabin and huts around the lake.

**Mystery Lake** is 1st [Region](./Region.md) available for play in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) and one of the primary starting regions in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. The region is named after [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md), a lake serving as the reservoir for the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md). A railway crosses the region and is mainly used in the summers supporting the local timber operation and lakeside recreation.

The region connects to [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) on the southern end of the railroad and to [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) in the southwest via a cave near the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md). The railroad leads into [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md) at the northeast edge of the map and continues into the [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) region. The [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) near the northeast end of the railroad provides a transition to the [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) region.

- [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md) entrance can be found near [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) and is commonly used for traveling to and from the [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md).

- The entrance to the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) transition zone can be reached by traveling through [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md); the transition zone can be used to access [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
- A cave near the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) connects to a [rope climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) recreation area of the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region.

As described in "[Mystery Lake & Area](./Mystery%20Lake%20%26%20Area.md)" from [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), the region of Mystery Lake is an alpine valley, averaging 1,200 meters above sea level, centered around its [namesake lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md). The lake itself is surrounded by forested hills, and there is much passive wildlife in the area. While there are [wolves](./Wolf.md) and [bears](./Bear.md), they are much less common here than in other regions. Temperatures are not as mild here as they are in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), however, they are by no means as cold as around [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) or [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md). The region offers plenty of shelter, with cabins and trailers scattered throughout the forested hills, as well as [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) and lots of foraging. Beyond the lake and hills, mountains surround the region on the west and south sides, while the foothills of the Inner Island Range can be seen on the region's north and east, forming a barrier through which players cannot travel.

The [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) cuts through the region, entering the region from [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) via the [Rail Tunnel](./Rail%20Tunnel.md). Along the way, it passes by [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md), the [Derailment](./Derailment.md), the [Train Loading Area](./Train%20Loading%20Area.md), and [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md). Just past Carter, the tracks enter [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md), and eventually lead to [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md). These tracks can be extremely useful in inclement weather, as they enable players to travel around without getting lost.

Overall, Mystery Lake is generally considered one of, if not _the_ easiest region to survive in, though some argue that Coastal Highway is even easier, despite its higher predator density. Mystery Lake is also in the center of Great Bear Island in-game, and well-prepared players will be able to reach most other in-game regions within a day's travel, though travelling to some regions, such as [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), may make for a _long_ day's travel. Players who own [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) should be aware that Mystery Lake does spawn cougars, and plan accordingly.
Although there are at least a dozen shelters available in the region, three locations are particularly popular [Safehouses](./Safehouse.md) amongst players:

This location is very central in the region, and, given that Mystery Lake is near the middle of Great Bear Island, is one of the most central locations overall. It offers a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), nearby [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md), hunting, and trapping, along with two stoves and lots of space to store gear. Given these features, it's no wonder that Camp Office is one of the most popular base locations of all. The one disadvantage of living here is that there are a moderate number of wolves in the area.

The Trapper's Homestead has much more secure surroundings (aside from a bear) and a bed, stove, workbench, together with loads of storage. Although there's good hunting and trapping in the area, it does suffer from the disadvantage of being rather far away from most of the other key locations in Mystery Lake. The nearby connector cave to [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) allows to cure [Cabin fever risk](./Cabin%20Fever%20Risk.md) and supplies [Coal](./Coal.md).

Arguably the largest base location in the game, the dam offers almost limitless storage space, multiple workbenches, a fire barrel, and access to both [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) and [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md). There's no bed available, however, one can bring a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) or sleep in the trailers outside. The largest hazard of living here are live wires during the Aurora, which can badly burn players who aren't careful.

- On a metal desk on the second floor of the Carter Hydro Dam; leading towards the cache in Alan's Cave.

Warmth, Fatigue, Thirst, and Hunger represent **Needs** that must be satisfied during the course of the game.

Failure to meet any of the Needs will cause the survivor to begin losing [Condition](./Condition.md) (the primary health bar) at steady rates, eventually weakening them to the point of [death](./Condition.md) if not properly handled. Failing to satisfy [Warmth](./Warmth.md) will cause the fastest Condition loss, and each additional unmet need adds to the rate of loss.

As long as all four Needs are met (non-empty), the survivor will heal passively 25% each day, or just over 1% every hour. Any unmet Need will disable the accelerated recovery during [Sleep](./Sleep.md).

The four Needs are displayed on the [Survival Overlay](./Survival%20Overlay.md) as white circular meters (formerly shaped like icons representing each Need). Satisfaction of a Need fills its respective meter. Arrows beside the bar indicate the direction and rate of progression; the more arrows in one direction, the faster the movement in that direction is.

As Needs deteriorate past certain points, the description to the right of the bar changes. When a Need meter has emptied, its icon turns red. Each stage of decay may be accompanied by voice line complaints from the survivor or relevant physiological system (e.g., a grumbling stomach as the hunger meter depletes).

![Fire heat icon](../assets/Fire_heat_icon.png) [Warmth](./Warmth.md) is a measure of the temperatures the player is exposed to. The player's warmth drains when the temperature the character experiences dips below 0°C (32°F) and is regained when it is above. Exposure to the elements is the main reason for loss of warmth and can be countered by staying indoors, having good clothing, being near a fire, and by consuming certain hot foods and drinks. Warmth will also deplete instantly if you come into contact with freezing water. When warmth is depleted, condition starts to steadily drop and can kill within a few game hours. This makes warmth the most critical need to satisfy.

Warmth is satisfied by maintaining a [feels like](./Feels%20Like.md) temperature above freezing (0°C or 32°F) over time. [Hot](./Warming%20Up.md) foods or drinks such as recently cooked or warmed up [pork and beans](./Pork%20and%20Beans.md) or [herbal tea](./Herbal%20Tea.md) will also decrease your cold by 20% as well as apply the [warming up](./Warming%20Up.md) attribute. Warmth drains in cold areas - the colder it is, the faster it will drain. The drain rate is accelerated by wet or freezing clothes and is completely drained after the player falls into freezing water. Visually warmth in the environment is represented by rising steam (as from boiling water) and icicles on cliffs, which may hint at a nearby cave.[Dubious]

When the warmth bar is empty you begin freezing and condition begins to drain rapidly. The rate of drain is constant at -20% each hour regardless of how far below freezing the character is currently. 'Feels like' temperature must be brought above 0°C (32°F) to stop the condition decreasing, and higher temperatures restore warmth faster. The affliction [hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md) will set in after 2 hours of freezing, doubling the rate to -40% per hour. Surviving more than 3 hours freezing is unlikely.

![Fatigue icon](../assets/Fatigue_icon.png) [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) is the measure of how tired the character is. Fatigue constantly drains but can be replenished by sleeping or by using certain items. As the character tires, Fatigue begins to affect the ability to move, aim weapons, and struggle. When completely depleted, fatigue will begin to lower the player's condition, and the player will be unable to sprint or climb ropes.

Fatigue is satisfied by [sleep](./Sleep.md) or by drinking [cups of coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md). It drains based on activity level, types of actions performed, and weight. Using an [emergency stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) will completely restore fatigue for a brief period, but fatigue will drop to zero once the effect wears off.

When fatigue falls below 'tired', the player's recommended weight capacity will rapidly diminish from 30kg down to 15kg (or 66lb down to 33lb). When the fatigue bar is empty, condition begins to drain. The rate of drain is fixed at 1% per hour.

![Calorie icon](../assets/Calorie_icon.png) [Hunger](./Hunger.md) is a measure of how many calories the player consumes and expends. The character's hunger is restored by consuming calories, which come in the form of foods and drinks. The character will begin to lose condition when their hunger is completely depleted.

When no more calories are in the calorie store, condition drains at a rate of 1% each hour. Dying of starvation will therefore take a little while and, if starting from 100% condition, will require more than 4 game days. Living without eating food every day is a game strategy known as Hibernation.

![Hydration icon](../assets/Hydration_icon.png) [Thirst](./Thirst.md) is a measure of how many liquids the player consumes and expends. Despite being surrounded by snow, liquids can be difficult to acquire and are particularly heavy. The thirst need is fulfilled by consuming water or particular foods and drinks (e.g., [tins of sardines](./Tin%20of%20Sardines.md) or [Reishi tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md)). Failing to fill this need will result in steady condition loss.
When no more water is in the thirst bar, condition drains at a rate of 50% each day (approximately 2% per hour).

Dying of thirst will take 2 days when starting with 100% condition, which is half the time it would take to die from starvation. Most tasks can be performed while dehydrated, so a player can opt to only quench the thirst need before a restorative sleep as a strategy to conserve water.

**Night Walker** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is obtained after surviving for an entire night outside in a single [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) game. It is most easily done on Pilgrim, although it will often be obtained eventually through normal gameplay on harder difficulties as well, especially once players start venturing into regions with little man-made shelter. These include [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md), and [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) (among others), where finding an indoor location to spend the night may not be an option.

Outside refers to being anywhere but inside a building or other structure that contributes to [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md). Therefore this achievement is obtainable whilst being inside of a train carriage (such as at the [Poacher's Camp](./Poacher%27s%20Camp.md)), a [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md), a shallow cave, or an [Ice Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md).
It is highly recommended to pack sufficient warm clothing and materials for starting a fire. Some type of Bedroll is recommended, but not essential.

Although it is possible to obtain this achievement inadvertently by getting stuck outside after dark in bad weather, this method can be dangerous. A much safer way is to use a [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md), as these provide protection from the wind, and have a pot belly stove. Taking enough firewood to keep the stove burning all night will maintain the temperature above freezing. The fire can also be used to boil water if supplies run low. Bringing [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) is useful as well as, if necessary, the player can easily get more food by fishing and be able to cook it instantly on the fire. In addition, using a fishing hut with a door means no animals will come inside, while still remaining technically outside.

Another option is to spend the night inside a warm cave, as this will provide a 10oC warmth bonus, while counting as an outdoor location. The Survivor will start walking noticeably slower when entering the warm section of the cave compared to being outside; this can be used as a guide to knowing where the warm zone starts. Another option is to drop a [Green Birch](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) or [Maple](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md) sapling; if it starts curing, the survivor is in the warm zone. If the cave is still too cold, lighting a [campfire](./Campfire.md) will provide sufficient warmth, as the wind won't blow it out.

A final option is to use a [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md), as these are sheltered from the wind and provide a warmth bonus. It is possible to warm up the inside of the vehicle by lighting a fire outside, but there is a risk of the fire getting blown out if the wind shifts overnight.

> “**Improvised explosives have been a notorious problem for officers and staff at Blackrock. Some of the more enterprising inmates have used the devices as a kind of currency.**”

**Noisemakers** (also nicknamed **Pipebombs**), are a tool in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. They are primarily used for frightening [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md), but can be used to offensively kill animals.

Noisemakers are handheld improvised explosive devices composed of wire sealed [Tin Cans](./Recycled%20Can.md) packed with [Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md) and a cloth wick to ignite the powder. They are very effective at frightening nearby wildlife, and can stop a charging [Bear](./Bear.md) or [Moose](./Moose.md) if directly hit. They are moderately effective at lowering [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) morale.

Despite a very low damage output of 50, Noisemakers are capable of hurting all types of wildlife, and will easily one-shot kill [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and [ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) within a medium-sized area of effect. They will chip away at wildlife health if detonated nearby, and eventually kill once enough damage is inflicted.

In [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), the blueprint to create them is locked until the player picks up at least one Noisemaker. Unlike in Episode 4, they are crafted at any [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md).

- In the mine at [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) in the northernmost area of [Blackrock.](./Blackrock.md) The mine is at the top of two rope climbs from the bottom of the [Fool's Corner](./Fool%27s%20Corner.md) ravine. The ropes can be reached by from two directions:

- traveling to the northern-most part of the [map](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Blackrock) and turning left right before [Mule Bridge](./Mule%20Bridge.md), reaching a rope at Fool's Corner and going down to the ravine, at which point the player can climb back on the other side and reach Last Prospect.

- Or going down to the ravine via [Cliff Cave](./Cliff%20Cave.md) or near the bridge to [Cook's Farm](./Cook%27s%20Farm.md) and traveling up the river until the northern end of the ravine and the ropes can be accessed. Once the Noisemakers have been picked up, the player can craft them at either [Ammunition Workbench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md).

- With the [Tales From The Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) update, Noisemakers can rarely spawn in the [Main Hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md) in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) region.

- They can also be found inside two specific [Memento Caches](./Mementos.md) (one in [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), on the exterior of the Prison wall and another in Bleak Inlet near the [Coastal Highway Terminus](./Coastal%20Highway%20Terminus.md) Hunter's Blind).

violations.context: **Requirements**
Crafting Noisemakers does not level up the [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) skill (but crafting [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md) to produce them does).
Most Wildlife will flee from the sound of an exploding Noisemaker, similar to the report of [gunshots](./Hunting%20Rifle.md). Below are the interactions each type of wildlife has with noisemakers.
| Animal | Rabbit | Ptarmagin | Deer | Wolf/Poison Variant | Aurora Wolf | Timber Wolf | Aurora Timber Wolf | Moose | Bear | Aurora Bear | Cougar/Aurora Variant |

- Both normal and [Posioned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) will flee upon hearing or being damaged by a nearby Noisemaker detonation even if the player has already been detected, this even applies to their aurora variants.

- Timberwolves and aurora Timberwolves will flee if a undetected player detonates a Noisemaker nearby. Timberwolves morale meter will decrease moderately if one detonates near, and significantly if it lands a hit directly.
- Noisemaker detonations will attract bears instead of scare them, unless they inflict damage, then normal bears will flee and aurora bears will charge.
- Bears will flee mid-charge if a Noisemaker hits them directly, this will not work on aurora bears.
- [Cougars](./Cougar.md) will ignore direct or nearby Noisemaker detonations regardless of whether or not the player has been detected.
- While Noisemakers deal damage to cougars, they will not dissuade them from charging the player.
- Noisemaker damage will not prevent cougars from engaging in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md), they must first be shot at by a firearm or bow before Noisemaker use to receive a glancing blow instead.
- Noisemakers completely ignore the aurora cougars innate 25% damage resistance, and will still take 6 hits to kill.
- Moose are scared of nearby Noisemaker detonations and will flee, unless the moose has detected the player or is actively charging, then only direct hits will cause them to flee.
- Rabbits will die instantly to nearby Noisemaker detonations, nearby unharmed rabbits will flee.
- Ptarmigan will die instantly to nearby Noisemaker detonations, nearby unharmed ptarmigan will flee.
- Noisemakers may be selected from the Radial Menu, the Weapons hotkey, or directly from the inventory.

- Press the fire button to Ignite the Noisemaker while holding it. (This does not require a firestarter (e.g. consuming matches) unlike [torches](./Torch.md)). Then press the fire button again to throw the Noisemaker and it will either explode on impact or once the fuse runs out.
- If an ignited Noisemaker is not thrown within 3 seconds, it will explode in the survivor's hand, causing 15% [Condition](./Condition.md) loss and a [Burns](./Burns.md) affliction.

- If a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) ensues between the player character and an animal, and the player has a lit Noisemaker in hand, the explosive will fall at their feet and injure both them and the attacking animal. This can end the struggle (if it's against a [Wolf](./Wolf.md) or [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md)) or even kill the attacker (very rarely, but more likely if it has been injured beforehand).

- Since they instantly kill [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) or [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) in a wide area- about the radius of three dropped rifles lined tip to stock, they can wipe out an entire group at once as long as they are close together, which makes it a decent small game hunting alternative for those inaccurate with stones, firearms, or the bow.

- Using Noisemakers for [Hunting](./Hunting.md) medium and large game is generally not recommended due to their high crafting cost, as well as difficulty of use. Most wildlife will flee when hit and will need to be chased down repeatedly to secure a kill.

In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), a Noisemaker may be obtained inside the [Weapon Locker](./Weapon%20Locker.md) just before leaving [Blackrock Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Mountain.md). They can be crafted at [Work Benches](./Work%20Bench.md) (instead of an ammo work bench) with the same recipe, and materials are quite plentiful to create them. They are mostly used as a defense tool to frighten Timberwolves away.

- Killing moose with a Noisemaker will cause it's death animation to bug out, and the moose will appear to be standing upright and continue to let out stunned noises. Despite this, the carcass may be harvested as normal.

The Nomad challenge is one of eight challenges in the Long Dark. It requires the player to spend three entire days in each location listed in their journal. The locations are not located in any one region, but are scattered between the many different regions, spanning the world. The game difficulty is Voyageur.

The journal automatically tracks how long the player has been at each location in increments of a tenth of a day. Once the player has been at any location for three days, a notification will appear at the top right of the screen stating that the location is complete, and a green checkmark will appear next to the location in the journal. When the final location is complete, the challenge immediately ends, and the player cannot go back and look at the journal.
- To complete the challenge in a timely way requires to plan ahead, so that the player does not have to double back to regions, to stay at locations they missed.

- It is not necessary to prepare for three complete consecutive days inside a location in one sitting - the timer does not reset if the player leaves. But it only advances during time spent inside the required location.
- The [Stone Church](./Stone%20Church.md) provides very little protection from the elements and is by far the hardest location to survive.
- There is no danger of [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), as the overall difficulty of the challenge uses Voyageur settings.
- In early 2021 it took six days instead of the intended three, due to a bug. Since 2021-04-29 this should be fixed.

![Note icon](../assets/Note_icon.png) **Notes** are [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md) found scattered around the map in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). The notes are in-keeping with the game's setting: Some are letters, written as if the authors had been visiting [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), while others are poems. Some notes stand alone, others tell a continuing story.
Notes found while playing [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) are also stored here.
- [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) - Inside the house to the table right of the [Stove](./Stove.md).
- [Pleasant Valley Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) - Inside the red barn on the table metal table near the [Truck](./Truck.md).
- [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) - on the table on the top floor next to the bunk beds.
- [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) - on bed on the loft above the [Forge](./Forge.md).
- [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md) - on the [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) - [Climber's Journal Page](./Climber%27s%20Journal%20Page.md)
- [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md) - by the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) - [Notebook Page (Survival 2)](./Notebook%20Page%20%28Survival%202%29.md)
- [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md) - On the table to the left inside the bunkhouse - [Mining Log Page](./Mining%20Log%20Page.md)
- [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md) - in the control hut - [Communication Report](./Communication%20Report.md)
- [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) yard - on the [Keypad](./Keypad.md) door next to the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) entrance - [Blackrock Memo](./Blackrock%20Memo.md)
- [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) yard - in the guard tower behind the infirmary - [Note (Survival)](./Note%20%28Survival%29.md)
- [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) interior - 2nd floor, under a desk in room no. 200 - [Page](./Page.md)
- [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) interior - 1st floor, in the guard room next to cell no. 11 - [Note (Survival 2)](./Note%20%28Survival%202%29.md)
- [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) - in the mine, floor 2, the lockers next to the mattress - [Handwritten Note (Survival)](./Handwritten%20Note%20%28Survival%29.md)
- [Cargomaster's Trailer](./Cargomaster%27s%20Trailer.md). In the back of the trailer under the lockers - [Paper](./Paper.md)
- [Justy's Hovel](./Justy%27s%20Hovel.md) - on a table as soon as you enter the front door - [Page (2)](./Page%20%282%29.md)
- [Junker's Paddock](./Junker%27s%20Paddock.md) - on the floor of the junked truck - [Journal Page](./Journal%20Page.md)
- [Main Hangar Basement](./Hangar%20Basement.md) - on a table on the right upon entering - [Memo (Survival)](./Memo%20%28Survival%29.md)
- [Main Hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md) - Right side corner office next to the stairs. Inside an overturned filing cabinet, far left side of the room. - [Stained Paper](./Stained%20Paper.md)
- [Mindful Cabin](./Mindful%20Cabin.md) - under the stairs in some Loose Boards behind the left shelves, behind the potted plant. - [Faded Paper](./Faded%20Paper.md)
- [Pump House](./Pump%20House.md) - "[Langston Mine Memo](./Langston%20Mine%20Memo.md)" on the right under the shelves.
- [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md) - in the radar dome building, northwest corner floor. -[Bloody note](./Bloody%20note.md)
- [Ambler's Lake](./Ambler%27s%20Lake.md) [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) - [Naturalist Notebook 2](./Naturalist%20Notebook%202.md)

**Nourished** is a unique [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ only encountered in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) when consuming certain [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Recipes. It was added in the Part 3 update to the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md).

Nourished is acquired from consuming certain recipes that gives a so-called "Max Stat Buff", temporarily increasing either the survivor's maximum [Condition](./Condition.md) by 5%-10% for 3 hours, depending on the food consumed, or their maximum [Stamina](./Stamina.md) by 15% for 3 hours. Gaining either of these benefits will apply the Nourished affliction.

Consuming certain recipes increases the survivor's maximum Condition by 5% or 10% for 3 hours, depending on the food consumed. This effect can raise the maximum Condition to 110%, and the Affliction's bonus stacks with [Well Fed's](./Well%20Fed.md) extra 5% Condition, making the highest attainable Condition peak at 115%.

The effect of this Affliction does not stack, and each new application will not override the previous Affliction. Partially eating the previously mentioned foods only adds a partial amount of Nourished duration.

Consuming certain recipes increases the survivor's maximum Stamina by 15% for 3 hours. The following recipes, when consumed, grant the Nourished Affliction as well as the +15% maximum Stamina benefit as a side effect:

**Oak Trees** are stationary environmental objects in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). They serve as the primary source of [Acorns](./Acorns.md) for the player, which can be identified as brownish speckled patches near the base of each tree. Each oak tree will always contain at least 1 or 3 acorn patches for the player to harvest, with some having been already uncovered before the player arrives. Once uncovered, acorns do not respawn.
- Near the trailer near [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) and [Silent Clearing](./Silent%20Clearing.md)
_[Acorns](./Acorns.md) can be found in the interactable areas at the base of oak trees._

Has no shelter **Ogre's Teardrop** is a frozen waterfall located in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md). It is located deep below the valley and is a short walk from [Juniper Runoff](./Juniper%20Runoff.md) and under [Perilous Crossing](./Perilous%20Crossing.md).

There is a small frozen pond in front of the waterfall, along with a few [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md) plants. There is no other noteworthy loot nearby. A [Green Maple Sapling](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md) can be found near the pond. The pond is not deep enough for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md).

A cave above in the mountains passes behind the waterfall. The cave has no warmth bonus, making [Sleeping](./Sleep.md) or resting here without an active [Campfire](./Campfire.md) very dangerous and cold. A [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) can often be found inside. A buried [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) has a chance of spawning outside the cave near the crossroads, and can be uncovered when the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) is powered.
A shortcut from the mountain above can be taken to reach this location by [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md) down a nearby cliff face.

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Iron Road](./Iron%20Road.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.
An **Oil Tank** is a stationary interactable object in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md) only found in Railyards on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md).

An **Oil Tank** initially contains 5,000 liters of [Whale Oil](./Whale%20Oil%20Can.md), and is accompanied by two yellow signs labelled "FUEL". When the Survivor pulls up close to the tower, a small sign under the signpost will flip a black panel to green a green one, letting them know that the [train](./Prototype%20Train.md) is in position to be filled (fuel and water caps must be in the middle of the signs to trigger this). Unlike the [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md), a vertical gauge is present on the Oil Tank to show its current storage status.

The player can then exit the train and walk over to the valve on the side of the tank to start dispensing oil. If the sign panel is not green, then the option to place oil into the train directly will not appear.

Oil is transferred into the train at a rate of 5.00 liters per minute (20.00 min cap at 5 minutes per increment), meaning that a fully empty locomotive can be refilled with 500.00 L of oil in 1 hour and 40 minutes. Make sure to turn the train Engine off while refueling, as this can burn already stored fuel and not fully refuel the train.
Whale Oil can also be transferred into the Survivor's backpack, 5.00 liters at a time in 1 minute.

- This is most useful for those who are using the [McLeod Ultra-Efficiency Whale Oil Heater](./McLeod%20Ultra-Efficiency%20Whale%20Oil%20Heater.md), and the excess oil can be stored on the train's [Cupboard](./Cupboard.md) for later use.
- Keep in mind that passing time while refueling the train will put the Survivor at risk from the elements, so make sure the weather is warm.
- Passing time and canceling the refueling process part way will only deposit a partial amount of fuel into the train up until the moment it is canceled. (needs verification).
- Oil Tanks refuel over time, so that the player will never run out of fuel for the train.
- Unlike the [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md), the Oil Tank will not immediately refill as it is emptied, but will gradually replenish over time if you leave the region and return later.

Has no shelter The **Old Bear's Den** is an unmarked location in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) that appears only in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md). [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) is dragged here by the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md), and the mission [What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md) takes place entirely within this den. The cave is an [Ice Cave](./Ice%20Cave.md), and is highly linear, ultimately resulting in a cavern with an open ceiling where Mackenzie kills the Old Bear after finding his [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md).

violations.context: > “__M - What's the story with this bear?
J - Story's real simple. That bear and me, we have unfinished business...Yeah. You could call it a trade in kind. Every time we meet, we each leave with a little of the other's blood.__”
> — [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) and [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) discussing the Old Bear.

The **Old Bear** is a unique [Bear](./Bear.md) and the primary antagonist of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). He also appears as the antagonist of [The Hunted Part One](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20One.md), [Part Two](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Two.md), and [Part Three](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Three.md) [Challenges](./Challenge.md).

The Old Bear is first seen in the closing seconds of [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), where [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) sees him attacking [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md), who takes the trapper's rifle to shoot it as the episode ends.

In [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), the Old Bear makes his first appearance at the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), where he charges Mackenzie right as he enters the fenced-in Staging Area. Mackenzie manages to close the gate, stopping the charge but is knocked out. When Mackenzie awakens some time later, the bear is gone.

After finding meds for the old trapper, Jeremiah tells Mackenzie that the bear will hunt them both across the island unless they kill him since the Old Bear has a taste for the blood of men. He recounts a story where a similar Old Bear from 150 years ago was nicknamed the "Demon Bear" after a Hunting party of three members failed to kill him despite allegedly unloading their rifles into him. Jeremiah concludes that the only possible way to kill the bear is with the legendary [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md), and directs a reluctant Mackenzie to the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) to retrieve it.

The Old Bear is encountered again in Broken Railroad, where he pushes over a [Train Shuttle](./Train%20Shuttle.md) that Mackenzie is inside of, knocking him unconscious. When he awakes, Mackenzie finds the bear missing, replaced instead by [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) sitting by a fire under an [Aurora](./Aurora.md).

After Mackenzie find and repairs the Bear Spear, the Old Bear is seen keeping his distance from the pilot on a nearby ledge as he makes his way through Forlorn Muskeg back to Mystery Lake. Mackenzie wonders that perhaps the Bear Spear does have some magical protection to it, at least for now, before taunting the retreating Old Bear.

In the third mission, the Bear guards one/two of the Shortwave Towers required to get the [Transponder Parts](./Transponder%20Parts.md) to boost Jeremiah's shortwave radio. He can be driven away by using the Bear Spear before struggling with him.
When attempting to return to Mystery Lake after getting all the parts, the Old Bear ambushes Mackenzie and then drags him to his den.

The player must navigate through the [Old Bear's Den](./Old%20Bear%27s%20Den.md) while avoiding the bear in order to retrieve the Bear Spear. Mackenzie successfully kills the Old Bear for good with the spear, apologizing to the creature's remains that he did not intend to kill him, but unfortunately "this world will make murders of us all." Mackenzie later returns to the Trapper's Homestead with the Transponder Parts and informs Jeremiah that the bear is dead, before passing out.

As well as his role in the story, the Old Bear appears in [The Hunted, Part One](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20One.md), [The Hunted, Part Two](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Two.md), and [The Hunted, Part Three](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Three.md) [Challenges](./Challenge.md). In the first two challenges, the bear is invincible and cannot be killed.

The challenge revolves around the bear stalking the player through Pleasant Valley to the Trapper's Homestead so they can get the Hunting Rifle. The Old Bear will hunt the player throughout Pleasant Valley and Mystery Lake until the player reaches the Trapper's Cabin.
After completing part one, part two is unlocked and begins where the first part ended. The roles are switched, with the player hunting the bear as it runs through Mystery Lake back to its den.
- Jeremiah constantly refers to the bear as "He" despite no genitals being present on the body.

- The Old Bear differs in appearance from normal bears; having 3 arrows imbedded behind the bear's head (with one broken off), blood all over the mouth, a scar below the right eye, small scars on the muzzle, longer leg and back hair, and 2 scars on the right side of his body above the belly.
- Aside from aesthetics, the bear is mechanically similar to any other bear the player might encounter (albeit immune to being killed). [Wolves](./Wolf.md) will run from the Old Bear.
- The Old Bear's home is situated in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), inside the [Old Bear's Den](./Old%20Bear%27s%20Den.md).

- In The Hunted, Part Two, the bear follows a very specific path as it runs across Mystery Lake. If the player doesn't see the old bear, they might need to walk along a certain path to get it to spawn.

- In Episode 2, unlike normal bears The Old Bear when charging at the Mackenzie is unaffected by the [distress pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md), although in the [Challenge: The Hunted](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20One.md) it is deterred by distress pistol shots.

- Old Bear especially by its other names ("Demon Bear" or "Evil Spirit") and the [The Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) and [Old Spence's](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) story are references to the fantasy manga ["Ushio & Tora" (うしおととら)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ushio_%26_Tora) written and illustrated by Kazuhiro Fujita. Both stories feature a supernatural spear with red cloth around its neck forged by a character driven mad for revenge to kill "evil spirits".

The **Old Fashioned Parka** is a type of [Clothing](./Clothing.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. Typically, the parka is a rare find, but gives off decent stats all around, though it is heavy and expensive to repair. The parka, however, is for the most part inferior to the [Military Coat](./Military%20Coat.md). They share identical weight and warmth statistics, and the former is quicker to repair by 30 minutes, but the latter is 20% more waterproof, offers 3% more protection, and has a 2% lower mobility penalty.

**Old Man's Beard Lichen** is an antimicrobial material that can be found dangling on the branches of trees.

Old Man's Beard Lichen can be found hanging from low tree branches in all regions. One tree can hold up to 3 units, and trees that hold the lichen are often found growing together in an area. On rare occasions, they can also be found when looting trash cans. Three units of the material can be used to make [Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Wound%20Dressing.md), which can be applied to wounds to prevent [Infection](./Infection.md).
- Old Man's Beard Lichen do not respawn on trees, but are plentiful especially in wilder regions.

- Old Man's Beard Lichen weighs 0.01kg (0.02lbs), but its crafted version "Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing" weighs 0.1kg (0.22lbs). This makes the raw (uncrafted) version far more weight efficient, at the expense of requiring to craft the dressing as needed.

- Old Man's Beard Lichen (Usnea) is a genus of fungi that grows in beard like clumps anchored to tree limbs and branches and can be found all over the world. Old Man Beard Lichen is said to have medical properties such as treating skin infections and sore throats however this has not been medically proven. This is likely where the inspiration for the anti-infectious property of Old Man's Beard Lichen came from.

**Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing** is a type of natural [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) item used to eliminate infection risk.

Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing is created with [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md), which functions as an [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md) that will disinfect a single wound, thus removing any chance of [Infection](./Infection.md). They weigh the same as a normal Bandage.
Previously, before release of 0.423, "Faithful Cartographer," Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing functioned as a regular [Bandage](./Bandage.md) combined with an Old Man's Beard Lichen.
- Old Man's Beard Lichen do not respawn on trees, but are plentiful especially in wilder regions.

- Old Man's Beard Lichen weighs 0.01kg (0.02lbs), but its crafted version "Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing" weighs 0.1kg (0.22lbs). This makes the raw (uncrafted) version far more weight efficient, at the expense of requiring to craft the dressing as needed.

- Antiseptic/Old Man's Beard Wound Dressings do not need to be applied immediately after sustaining an injury to eliminate infection risk; though they should be applied as early as possible, since waiting long periods of time (e.g. 6+ hours) increases the chances of an Infection despite antiseptic being used.

Provides some shelter The **Old Settlement** is an unmarked location in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md).

The area consists of 3 ruined buildings and one intact two story cabin. Several wooden fences can be found around the ruined buildings, with the road and nearby cabin blocked/buried by an avalanche. The area around the settlement is patrolled by several large packs of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), making coming and going very difficult.

The ground floor of the [Cabin](./Cabin%20%28Sundered%20Pass%29.md) is snowed-in, so the two doors are covered by snow and are unusable. Walking behind the cabin and onto the roof the player can find an open window to walk inside.

Stepping inside, the window will place the player on a [Bed](./Bed.md) on the second floor. A [Trunk](./Trunk.md) and several [Crates](./Crate.md) are found on the floor, with a staircase leading downstairs into a kitchen.

The 2 doors on the first floor can be opened, but are blocked by snow, imprinted with the shape of the doors. The Fireplace is also covered in snow, and cannot be used. A small kitchen with [Stored Water](./Stored%20Water.md) and several [Drawers](./Drawer.md) and a [Cupboard](./Cupboard.md).

3 ruined buildings can be found across the road of the snowed in cabin, with the largest freestanding one containing a [Toilet](./Toilet.md) in a ruined bathroom, but not much else. Further west 2 [Coal Bins](./Coal%20Bin.md) can be found along the 2 other ruined houses with some [Benches](./Bench.md). Careful scrutiny of the area may reveal possible loot, such as a [Wire Bundle](./Wires.md) and [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md).
A [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) in front of the largest ruined building can sometimes contain a [Polaroid](./Polaroids.md).

Hidden behind the largest ruined building, a [Basement](./Basement%20%28Sundered%20Pass%29.md) is can be uncovered while following objectives from the [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) Tale by following the clue from [Foreman's Polaroid 2](./Foreman%27s%20Polaroid%202.md). The basement cannot be used to escape [Insomnia Risk](./Insomnia%20Risk.md) when [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) arrives in the region, despite being underground.
- Hiding in the bathroom of the ruined building near the Basement will not completely stop Timberwolf attacks, as they will attack you through the nearby [Shelf](./Shelf.md) next to the toilet.

Old Spence Family Homestead is surrounded by a thicket on one side and fields of snowbanks and weak ice on the other. It consists mostly of buildings in various degrees of disrepair, but one of the main buildings generally contains useful items such as [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md), [Coal](./Coal.md), a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), and [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), as well as the second [forge](./Forge.md) to appear in the game. The main building also contains a work bench, a [safe](./Safe.md) (hidden behind several crates) and a [bed](./Bed.md).

The player may need a [fire](./Fire.md) to safely sleep, as there are holes in the roof and on the sides. If you have good clothing such as [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md), a [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md), and [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md), a fire may not be needed.

In the morning deer may spawn in the area but if you are using a [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), they can run away onto the thin ice and it can be difficult to reach the carcass. There is a lot of wood to be harvested in the vicinity, and more coal can be harvested in nearby caves for crafting tools in the forge. A rifle may be found on a body northwest of the homestead on a small snow island.

A wolf pack tends to patrol near the fence on the side closest to the ice, so take caution. There may also be a [bear](./Bear.md) wandering northwest of the camp. If you want to travel to other locations on the map, analyze the weather as disorienting fog can be a serious danger due to thin ice, and predators. Cold winds can also be deadly, as there are not many places with wind protection. Mornings are very cold, so wait a bit for the sun and temperature to rise.

With the Redux update (December 2018), another forge has been added to the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) in the [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) region. Consider traveling a little farther to reach the Maintenance Yard if you don't have enough equipment to protect against the harsh weather conditions in Forlorn Muskeg.

Some [Replacement Fuses](./Replacement%20Fuse.md), along with some [Wire Bundle](./Wires.md), may be found here, which can prove helpful to players who wish to repair the transmitter tower near [Muskeg Overlook](./Muskeg%20Overlook.md).
- One of the large crates near the bed in the main building always contains 3 accelerants under it when destroyed.
- The Safe may contain high rarity items based on [survival mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) such as: Gauntlets, Mukluks, Gunpowder, Rabbitskin Mitts, Cash, etc.

- Old Spence Family Homestead in [Wintermute (Story Mode) Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) is a references the fantasy manga ["Ushio & Tora" (うしおととら)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ushio_%26_Tora) written and illustrated by Kazuhiro Fujita. Both stories involve characters driven driven mad for revenge to kill 'evil spirits' with [similar weapons](./Bear%20Spear.md).

With its strategic location between [Narrow Bridge](./Narrow%20Bridge.md) and [Blocked Bridge](./Blocked%20Bridge.md), it is a major feature in this region and a possible long-term base.

The interior layout is very similar to the Radio Control Hut at [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md). A small office with a bed is inside the Old Substation. A workbench is located next to a fire barrel behind the building. There is ample storage space in containers both inside and outside. Two outdoor caves are very close ([Lineworker's Hideout](./Lineworker%27s%20Hideout.md) to the south and an unnamed cave to the north), in addition to an abandoned car, allowing [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) to be slept off.

[Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) are often nearby and can go inside the fenced perimeter around the building. However, they may not be able to reach the power line pylon on the adjacent hilltop.[^1] Aside from the Timberwolves, there is limited game in the area, though [Deer](./Deer.md) can be found by [crossing the nearby river](./Narrow%20Bridge.md) and heading for [Creek Bed Cave](./Creek%20Bed%20Cave.md).

[Grey Mother asks you to deliver Grey Mother's Pearls to the grave of Lilith Barker](../assets/Grey_Mother%27s_Pearls_icon.png) _Grey Mother asks you to deliver [Grey Mother's Pearls](./Grey%20Mother%27s%20Pearls.md) to the grave of [Lilith Barker](./Lilith%20Barker.md)_
**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**

**One Last Thing** is a side mission started in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In the mission, [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) delivers [Grey Mother's Pearls](./Grey%20Mother%27s%20Pearls.md) to the gravesite of [Lilith Barker](./Lilith%20Barker.md) at the [Graveyard](./Graveyard.md) across from [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md) outside [Milton](./Milton.md). The mission can only be completed in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), prior to the survivor [leaving Milton](./Paradise%20Lost.md).

Talk to [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md), who will request Mackenzie to go deliver the pearls to the gravesite of [Lilith Barker](./Lilith%20Barker.md). Mackenzie is shocked that "Lily" is here in Milton, only for him to finally understand what Grey Mother has wanted this whole time when he arrives at the Graveyard.

![The gravestone of Lilith Barker.](../assets/One_last_thing.jpg)_The gravestone of Lilith Barker._ Take [Grey Mother's Pearls](./Grey%20Mother%27s%20Pearls.md) and head out of [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md). Turn right, and follow the road towards St. Christopher's Church. Across the road from the church is a Graveyard. Locate the grave of Lilith Barker in the back of the gravesite, and place the pearls on the headstone.
Return to Grey Mother and inform her that the pearls have been delivered and the mission will be completed.

**Orange Soda** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

It can be consumed to restore 250 [calories](./Hunger.md) as well as 30% [hydration](./Thirst.md), the equivalent of 0.20 litres of [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md). They are found commonly inside all types of structures, [vehicles](./Vehicle.md), and on [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md).
There are two other kinds of soda, [Summit Soda](./Summit%20Soda.md) and [Stacy's Grape Soda](./Stacy%27s%20Grape%20Soda.md). All three types of soda share the same calories and hydration.
