**Template:spoiler**The **Orca Gas Station** is a location just outside [Milton](./Milton.md) in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. The gas station lies at a junction outside Milton, with one road leading up to [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md), one to the town itself, and the last leading past the [Wood Lot](./Wood%20Lot.md) to a [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md). When breaking into the store, the store itself is labeled [Convenience Store](./Convenience%20Store.md).

The station has a front and rear door, both of which are locked in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), and must be forced open with a [prybar](./Prybar.md). In Story mode neither door is locked, and entering the building will introduce you to [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md).
Inside of the building there is a reasonable supply of food, tools, and clothes, as well as a bed and a [computer](./Computer.md) that becomes active during the [Aurora](./Aurora.md).

The Building can serve as a safehouse for Milton, as it offers a bed and two entrances. even with the constant threat of predators [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) is notorious for, this location is comfortably away from [wolf](./Wolf.md) patrols that center around the middle of town. However, players should beware of wolves patrolling outside in the Wood Lot.

Additionally, there is a [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) grove nearby (in the [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md) area), with the occasional [Deer](./Deer.md) passing through, and the building is reasonably close to the climbing rope area that will take you out of Milton.
Upon meeting [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) she will suggest to [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) to visit the local gas station for supplies.

The gas station also serves as a prime example of the already dire situation of the people of Great Bear prior to the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md). Gas prices appear to have been extremely high, and, ultimately, gasoline seems to have run out entirely based on the red X's on the gas station sign. Comments from characters and notes/signs throughout the store and other buildings in town (mostly in Story mode) also suggest cash had been depleted and that even staples such as milk were hard to come by. The island seem to have suffered some of the worst effects of the wider economic crisis in _The Long Dark_ universe.

The **Overladen Pond** is an incredibly toxic pond created as a result of the nearby [Pump House](./Pump%20House.md) dumping toxic underground gases and chemicals into the pond. **Pacifist** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.
This achievement is obtained after surviving the first twenty-five days without killing an animal in a single [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) game mode. It is most easily done on Pilgrim.

Capturing or killing an animal with the [hunting rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [survival bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), [snare](./Snare.md), or [fishing tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) will nullify the achievement. Therefore, it is highly recommended that the player seeks sustenance by scavenging meat from deceased animals killed by [wolves](./Wolf.md) and ransacking abandoned buildings.

This achievement must be made in the first twenty-five days of the play through. If the player kills an animal within the first twenty-five days of surviving it will nullify the achievement for that entire play through.

> “**You are suffering from the pain of an injury, causing blurred vision and discomfort. Treat it, or let it heal on its own over time.**”

Pain is a negative affliction introduced in the [Steadfast Ranger](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/22877-the-long-dark-survival-mode-updated-to-v148-steadfast-ranger/) update. It can be caused by a [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md), [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md), [Struggle](./Struggle.md), or a fall.

While in effect, Pain causes the player's vision to blur slightly around the edges, and will also distort sounds. Pain can be cured immediately with two [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md) or one [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md). Left untreated, Pain will simply heal on its own after four hours.

Because its only negative impact on actual gameplay is an inability to read [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md), treating Pain with [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) can be a potentially wasteful decision; Painkillers and Rose Hip Tea can be used to greater effect by treating [Burns](./Burns.md) or [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md).

**Painkillers** are an artificial medical item used to treat [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_.

Painkillers are commonly found inside of first aid kits and medicine cabinets, but may be found indoors, outside (usually at campfires or near [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md)) or in containers. They are usually found in groups of 6 pills, though more or less may be found; they are always found in multiples of 2.
- [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md) (2 doses and 2 [Bandages](./Bandage.md), and 120 hours of Recovery Time)
One dose of Painkillers consists of 2 Painkiller pills. A single pill cannot be used, therefore they should be carried in multiples of 2.

The effect of painkillers is not generalized throughout the body, and each dose will only treat one injury, and should be applied to the injuring requiring them as treatment (e.g. "Pain" from a Sprained Wrist and Sprained Ankle will display as two instances of Pain, and each requires one dose to treat the pain from the given injury).

- Pain has minimal effect on gameplay (blurry vision and slightly distorted hearing) with it's only limitation being an inability to read [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) while afflicted, and since Pain will subsides automatically with time, treating Pain is not generally a concern. This generally makes treating Pain usually a wasteful decision, since this requires the weight of carrying Painkillers and since they are also required to treat [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md) or accelerate the healing of [Burns](./Burns.md).
- Painkillers cannot be crafted and Rose Hips do not regrow; however Painkillers are renewable via [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) and [Trading](./Trader.md).

- The condition of Painkillers [decays](./Decay.md) slowly over time (based on [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md)). Upon reaching 0% Condition, they will disappear if inside of a container. Ruined 0% Painkillers can still be used through the Radial Menu, although this will consume all 6 pills at once. It is therefore advisable to drop the other four pills on the floor first, before consuming Ruined Painkillers.
- The exact medication Painkillers represent is unknown, though the "Rx" on their label states it is a prescribed drug.
- It is not possible to overdose on or become addicted to Painkillers in The Long Dark.

**Paradise Lost** is a [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Climb your way out of the ravine you crashed in and walk towards [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md), then make your way to the Town of Milton. Go into the [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) and step inside.

## Find the climbing area on the outskirts of Milton.

_After retrieving [Lilith Barker's](./Lilith%20Barker.md) climbing equipment, Mackenzie then heads to [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md) by following [Lily's Map](./Lily%27s%20Map.md). _Mackenzie eventually uses the rope climb and begins climbing down, but the rope begins to fail two-thirds of the way down the climb and then snaps._
## Find the route that leads through the mountains.

_With the rope broken and no way back up to Milton, Mackenzie travels further into the mountains. Upon traveling a bit further away from the climbing spot, Mackenzie finds another rope to climb up into the mountains. **Paradise Lost (Predux)** was the fourth and last mission of the Predux [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).
This mission is a point of no return. Finish all side missions and exploration before continuing to [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md).

When you are done, take the [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) to the [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section of Milton Park. Tie it and climb down, only for the rope to snap. You are now unable to return to Milton.

Continue traveling until you find another Rope Climb. If you are too tired to climb, a nearby [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) can be rested in. Climb up the Rope Climb and then walk to a cave in the mountains and leave Milton behind. Pass through the cave to the other side and a 3rd person cutscene will play of a man being mauled by a bear. He pleads for Mackenzie to shoot it, and Mackenzie picks up a rifle and fires once, ending the episode.
Several plot points and locations have been replaced/altered since the Redux re-release of Episode 1:
- Jeremiah is not wearing his [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md), but the redux changes this to include him wearing his coat in the ending cutscene.
- Despite this, [Jeremiah's Bearskin Coat](./Jeremiah%27s%20Bearskin%20Coat.md) is damaged and needs to be repaired in Episode 2 after the bear attack.

**Paradise Lost** is the fourth and final mission in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) leaves [Milton](./Milton.md) and finds a way through the mountains to bypass the [tunnel collapse](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) in his continuous search for [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md).

Lily's rock climbing gear is now accessible from the trunk upstairs in her bedroom, it will be required to traverse beyond [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md). The map will mark a location in the [Picnic Area](./Picnic%20Area.md), where there is a rope attachment area on a large bolder near the ledge. Using the area will deploy the [mountaineering rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) that can be used to climb down the ledge. Using the rope will drain stamina, more so depending on encumbrance, and the player cannot climb down while over-encumbered. A good rest beforehand will ensure maximum weight capacity. As Will descends the rope, it snaps and drops him down the last few meters. The game may display minor injuries that immediately disappear.
At the bottom, the player will encounter [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md). His dialogue will change depending on the choice made with [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md).

Continue exploring and find a rope going back up another rock wall on the other side of the valley. Further exploration will lead to a cave that tunnels through the mountains. The cave is dark, but fairly linear. Upon exiting the cave, a short cutscene will start. Will immediately sees a [man](./Jeremiah.md) being attacked by a [bear](./Old%20Bear.md), and a hunting rifle that has dropped to the ground. He picks it up, aims and fires, ending Episode 1.
- The title "Paradise Lost" is a reference to the epic poem of the same name by John Milton, and thus a play on the name of the town the episode mostly takes place in.

**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**

**Paradise Meadows Farm** or **The Barker Farm** is a location a short distance from [Milton](./Milton.md) in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. It was home to farmer [Martin Barker](./Martin%20Barker.md).
The farmstead buildings include a decently sized, very cluttered house; a couple of open carpark/shed structures; as well as an open barn building that has both a workbench and a fire barrel.

The farmstead was featured as an important story location in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), and, since [the Rugged Sentinel Update](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog%20%E2%80%94%20Archive%201.md#1.16) it can also be accessed in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), along with the rest of the Mountain Town map.

A single-story farmhouse may require a key to get into and is the only building with an interior in this location. It consists of a living room, kitchen bathroom, office, bedroom, and small storage room. The house also has a [stove](./Stove.md) (one of the few 6-slot stoves in the game) in the kitchen and a fireplace in the bedroom.

The house offers a good amount of storage space, as well as a lot of open areas to cure hides. The front porch may be used to store meat to prevent it from spoiling, however the player must remember that the porch itself isn't safe from wildlife.

The barn is a wooden shell of a building without an actual interior. It offers poor protection from the elements (i.e., some wind protection, depending on wind direction), and it isn't entirely safe from the wildlife. The barn also has a [workbench](./Work%20Bench.md) and a [fire barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) located conveniently close, making prolonged crafting sessions easier. There are some planks and cardboard to break down for resources, and dead body may occasionally spawn inside the barn. A [tractor](./Tractor.md) is situated near the barn.

There are the remnants of a couple sheds on the opposite sides of the farm. They contain little and offer almost no protection from weather or from wolves that may patrol around the farm, however, a [truck](./Truck.md) can be found sitting underneath one of the dilapidated structures.

As of the [REDUX](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog%20%E2%80%94%20Archive%201.md#1.41) update, the farmhouse in _Wintermute_ is no longer accessible prior to receiving the objective "**Something precious was stolen from**[GREY MOTHER](./Grey%20Mother.md)**. Find it, and return it to her.**" If the player visits this location beforehand, the door is locked, with no key spawning in the vicinity. After the start of the objective, however, bloodstains can be seen leading across the yard up to the door, which is now marked with a bloody red handprint. The door is now unlocked, and the home can be accessed without the use of a key.

Upon entering the homestead for the first time, a cutscene begins wherein Mackenzie meets a severely wounded [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md), an escapee of the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) and recognizes the scarf the other man is using to bandage his arm as [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md)'s. Hobbs reveals that he, along with fellow prisoners who escaped the transport van, took several residents of [Milton](./Milton.md) hostage and locked them within the [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md). Tragically, the electrical phenomena accompanying the [aurora](./Aurora.md) started a fire in the building and it burned down with everyone still trapped inside. Hobbs initially makes it sound like he burned it on purpose, but further dialogue opens the possibility that the fire was accidental and the criminals were just unable or unwilling to free their captives in time, although Astrid apparently tried to help but was too late.

Afterwards, an encounter with Astrid left one of the criminals dead and Hobbs with a knife in his side before she escaped through the collapsed tunnel behind the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md). With his other companions dead as well, Hobbs sought out shelter within the farmhouse and slumps onto the couch, too weak from pain and blood loss to react with any violence or ill intent upon the player's arrival.

This interaction culminates with a choice. Pull the knife out of Hobbs's gut in order to try and save him; or push the weapon in deeper and end his life. The _[Bank Deposit Box Key #15](./Milton%20Safety%20Deposit%20Box%20Keys.md)_is found in a container next to where Hobbs is sitting, and can be obtained after his dialogue finishes.

A few [wolves ](./Wolf.md)can roam the fields from time to time, though generally only two or three wolves come close to the house itself. It means that one should always take caution entering the yard in front of the farmhouse, since it is rarely safe.

In the field to the north of the farm itself, near the silo, there is usually herd of a deer roaming around. Their presence in an open field with scattered snowdrifts (behind which a player can crouch) make for an excellent hunting location.

In Survival mode, the [Paradise Meadows Farm Key](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm%20Key.md) to the farmhouse may be found at various locations around the property, including (but not limited to) the dashboard of the pickup truck, tractor's floor, or a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), either behind the farmhouse or inside the barn.

On all experience levels, the farmhouse offers decent loot (by the standards of the difficulty level). There is plenty of furniture inside to break down for reclaimed wood, and multiple containers can hold mid- to high level items. It is an excellent source of [books](./Book.md), containing up to 25 on voyageur. Most notably, a rifle and/or a [revolver](./Revolver.md) and possibly some ammunition may be found inside. Birch saplings may be found behind the farmhouse. This farm is the last interior location in Mountain Town region before reaching [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and its forge (through [Milton Basin](./Milton%20Basin.md)). These facts can make the farm possible location to go forging arrowheads from.

**Spoiler Warning:** **This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**

Patient 7 is the codename given to one of the patients treated by the [Project Medical Officer](./Project%20Medical%20Officer.md) after the incident with [Rüdiger's Machine](./R%C3%BCdiger%27s%20Machine.md).

Presumably one of the mine workers in [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), Patient 7 is a side character from the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) storyline in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

After turning on the machine, several people involved or close to the project, including [The Foreman](./The%20Foreman.md), [The Security Chief](./The%20Security%20Chief.md), and the mine workers, started developing symptoms of mental deterioration. Because of that, [Dr. Rüdiger](./Dr.%20R%C3%BCdiger.md) had a medical officer flown in to evaluate the patients.
Patient 7 was one of the patients evaluated and being treated by the Medical Officer, and the one being recorded in the Interview Transcrips made by the Doctor.
In the transcripts, we can see the Medical Officer asking Patient 7 to recall various instances from memories, involving a river, a beach, and a claustrophobic room.

- ![Interview Transcript 4 icon](../assets/Interview_Transcript_4_icon.png) [Interview Transcript 4](./Interview%20Transcript%204.md) : We can read the report of Patient 7's memory, recalling a summer day with a group of people in the edge of a river. He mentions how he entered the river and underestimated the depth of the body of water, resulting in him struggling and reaching for a stone, holding himself above the water line. At the end, we can read that he doesn't remember if it was a sunny or a rainy day, something that he mentions at the beginning of the transcript, showing the dementia-like symptoms caused by the machine.

- ![Interview Transcript 12 icon](../assets/Interview_Transcript_12_icon.png) [Interview Transcript 12](./Interview%20Transcript%2012.md) : Patient 7 recalls a dark, square room made of a smooth "steel or glass" material. He notices a pit in the middle of the room, recalling it being made of bricks. At the end, he mentions when "it" shows up, being a floating, moving shape, calling it "a shadow". At the end, we can see he enters in a slightly paranoic episode, saying "Is it me? My face? Goddammit."

- ![Interview Transcript 14 icon](../assets/Interview_Transcript_14_icon.png) [Interview Transcript 14](./Interview%20Transcript%2014.md) : In the third transcript, we can see Patient 7 recalling a "grey" day in a really deep, still beach, with no waves or wind around. He mentions being alone, not understanding what was happening at the moment, probably being lost in the middle of the ocean getting easily distracted in the storytelling. At the end, he states that they "lost him... just a little kid."
Even with the efforts of the Doctor, we can witness the mental deterioration of Patient 7 as the sessions advance in number.
- We can infer that he's the patient being recorded in [Interview Transcript 17](./Interview%20Transcript%2017.md), although it's unclear
- As seen in the Transcripts, there's a high chance Patient 7 has a childhood trauma as a consequence of becoming lost in bodies of water like a river and beach when he was younger.

- We can conclude that there were more patients, presumably more mine workers, that were being treated by the [Project Medical Officer](./Project%20Medical%20Officer.md), but their sessions were probably lost, taken by the doctor, or simply not recorded by him, taking more interest in Patient 7's memories and mental deterioration.

Peak Cave is a small cave hidden amongst brush, potentially with a corpse and a plastic container inside. A few [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) bushes grow just outside the cave, and there are four oak trees nearby. There is a chance for a [deer](./Deer.md) to spawn on the plateau just outside the cave, and the region is frequented by [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md).

A quick walk to the north to a ledge overlooking [Monolith Lake](./Monolith%20Lake.md) will lead to a possible [Hidden Cache](./Hidden%20Cache.md) spawn point, which may also contain useful items. The cave is also a spawn point for a [Memento Cache](./Mementos.md), which will contain one [Cured Black Bear Hide](./Cured%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md).

Because this location is entirely safe from hostile wildlife and located not too far from decent hunting areas near [Monolith Lake](./Monolith%20Lake.md), it can make for a good [Safe House](./Safehouse.md), although the long climb up a hill at the end of a day increases the risk of getting a sprain, especially if the player is exhausted/encumbered. This risk can be mitigated by using [Crampons](./Crampons.md).

- The altitude of Peak Cave has been estimated by Glflegolas to be about 590 meters above sea level (relative to [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)) using screenshots. This is higher than the altitude of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) (relative to sea level in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md)), which is 505 meters.

- If confirmed, this would make Peak Cave the second highest accessible point on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), after the southern portal of the [Cave](./Cave%20%28Mountain%20Town%20location%29.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), which is 612 meters.

**Peanut Butter** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Consuming Peanut Butter provides up to 900 calories of [energy](./Hunger.md), at the cost of 5% loss in [hydration](./Thirst.md). They can be found uncommonly in all regions, usually inside cabinets, houses, stores and [vehicles](./Vehicle.md). Peanut Butter has a weight of 0.50 kg and provides modest energy density to weight.
- Peanut Butter are packaged as a product called "_SMOOTH Peanut Butter"_, possibly a play on the real-life peanut butter brand "Jif".
- In real life, a 16 oz/1 lb jar of peanut butter would have well over 2000 kcals. The in-game value is likely less for balancing reasons.
- The ingredients on the back list: "Roasted Peanuts, Canola Oil, Sugar, Salt." and that it is a "Product Of Canada."

**Pemmican Bar** is a [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is learned after acquiring its unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md).
It is only acquired when trading with the [Trader](./Trader.md) for the Recipe Card of the same name.
Cooking the ingredients generates four (4) bars, each weighing 0.0625kg (stacking up to 0.25kg for all 4).

Pemmican Bars do not produce [Scent](./Scent.md), and are the lightest food item in the game, as well as the most calorically dense food item. This makes then an excellent food for traveling and maximizing carry weight.

- Real world Pemmican is quite famous for lasting a very long time (from 6 months to several years). It is often used in very poor survival situations, and is often typically associated with the diets of various Native American tribes or being used by American Voyager settlers.

- Pemmican is typically composed of dried meat pounded into a coarse powder or mash, then mixed with an equal amount of melted fat and cooked. Occasionally, berries are added to the mix (Rose Hips are used in game).

Provides some shelter Pensive Lookout is the third intact fire lookout tower in the game, preceded by the [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md) and [Abandoned Lookout](./Abandoned%20Lookout.md). Other than bearing more weathered paint, it is nearly identical to the other towers from the outside. Also like the others, Pensive Lookout does not present a loading screen upon entering.

Pensive Lookout is an abandoned fire lookout tower in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). It is positioned on the east edge of the plateau and has a climbing rope area for the player to travel between the upper and lower sections of the region, although there may not be a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) supplied (the player could find it hanging on the side of the building). Inside the lookout, the player may find a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) or [hatchet](./Hatchet.md), plenty of tables as well as some stray firewood. [Dusting Sulfur](./Dusting%20Sulfur.md), [Stump Remover](./Stump%20Remover.md), or even a [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md) may spawn as well.
Players may find that the lookout makes a good safehouse, as the plateau is relatively safe from the predatory wildlife below.

Although travel between the two sections of the map may be tricky, the lookout offers a few unique advantages as a safehouse, serving as a good position to shoot game from while protecting from [wolves](./Wolf.md) and [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) (while they _can_ climb the stairs, their pathfinding AI tends to struggle with it). It also provides 'immunity' to [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), plenty of secure cold storage for food, and a large supply bin at the base of the structure.

Disadvantages include a slightly lower indoor temperature, a considerably longer hike to good resources, and a relatively inefficient cooking situation, as the lookout boasts only a 1-slot [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), unless the player is willing to risk contact with wildlife by cooking at the base of the tower.

Provides some shelter **Pensive Pond** is a small recreational pond in the hills of [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).

Picnickers can enjoy canoeing and, when sunny, sit under the gazebo. A [hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) with a [fishing hole](./Ice%20Fishing.md) and [pot-belly stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md) sits at the center of the pond. Importantly, the fishing hut also has a door, making it a decent temporary shelter. For players with sufficiently-warm [clothing](./Clothing.md) and a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md), the hut's relatively easy access to animals and firewood means it could serve as a base for multi-day [hunting](./Hunting.md) & fishing "retreats" to fight [cabin fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md).
Be careful of the surrounding cliffs and prowling predators in low-visibility conditions. There's a chance of the [revolver](./Revolver.md) spawning inside the fishing hut.

A [Cougar](./Cougar.md) spawns just east of here, which can pose a danger to players carrying large amounts of freshly-caught fish back to their main base. However, brave players may choose to try hunting the Cougar, using the fishing hut for protection.

Pensive Pond can be found easily from [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md). Standing at the round silo on the farmstead, turn to face [Heartbreak Bridge](./Heartbreak%20Bridge.md). Cliffs can be seen in the background, on top of which Pensive Pond can be found. Following [Lower Falls](./Lower%20Falls.md) and climbing up carefully, some shelter, fishing or a picnic can be had.

A small cave can be found just upwards, which can provide useful shelter for weary travellers that have climbed up two long ropes to get here. It is listed as a Vista location, therefore, sketching from there will reveal a large proportion of the region.

A wolf carcass occasionally spawns outside, however the cave itself is safe from predators. This, along with its fairly close proximity to hunting opportunities west of [Monolith Lake](./Monolith%20Lake.md) and close access to the eastern part of the Hushed River Valley, make it a decent safehouse.

**Perseverance Mills**is a town and Wintermute exclusive [Region](./Region.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is mentioned several times throughout [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) and is the initial centerpiece of [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md).

The region connects to the nearby regions of [Desperation Bay](./Desperation%20Bay.md) and [Perseverance Wilds](./Perseverance%20Wilds.md). The region is currently Wintermute exclusive, and does not appear in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).
> “**I seem to recall...a town somewhere up north. Far. What was it called...That's it -- Perseverance Mills**”

According to the Grey Mother, it is an old milling and logging town, located far to the north of [Milton](./Milton.md) and the [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) coast. Similar to the [Town of Milton](./Town%20of%20Milton.md), Perseverance Mills suffers from economic woes, supply shortages, and a low population. However, the town still has a functioning economy and is in a far better state than Milton, with the nearby Mill providing jobs to the locals and connections to the Mainland being present (including tourism and somewhat regular shipments of food and supplies). The titular Perseverance Mill is stated to be the sole reason for the town's continued economic existence; as without its access to timber and the jobs it provides, no one would have any reason to stay within the area.

The town displays a sign stating that the populations numbers at 101 residents, but most of the houses are boarded up and abandoned, with the resident population being seen actually numbering somewhere around the 20s.

As of [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) and [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), it is hinted that the town is suffering from an outbreak of an unknown illness and is under quarantine, with [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) and [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) confirming this (with many of the residents wandering out into the sea and drowning themselves or otherwise going missing based on the various missing posters found all over the town).

The town is ultimately burned to the ground by [Mathis](./Mathis.md) and his [Convicts](./Convicts.md) at the end of [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md), with the survivors fleeing to a bunker under the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md).
Despite being the largest town on Great Bear Island, the region has very few locations to explore.

The town has several houses that are not boarded up, but most cannot be entered. Curiously, a church with a locked door can be found, but there is no key to opening it. The Perseverance Mill itself can be seen but cannot be entered.
2 [Coastal Houses](./Coastal%20House.md) can be entered, with one be found close to Jane's House and another close to Cooper's Blind. All other homes are either locked or boarded up.

[Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) charters a plane from her ex husband [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) at the [Jackrabbit Hangar](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md) to deliver her and her Hardcase to the Northern part of Great Bear Island. Their plane crashes after the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) and the two become separated. Astrid makes her way to the town of Milton and escapes the town after [Convicts](./Convicts.md) take it over, heading through the tunnel to [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) and eventually passing through before it collapses, but not before leaving a message in her own blood for Mackenzie in the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md): "PERSEVERANCE".
A day later, Mackenzie escapes the ravine he was crashed in and finds both her message and Hardcase, with Grey Mother eventually providing him with a way to leave Milton and continue to the Mills.

[Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) confirms the location of [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) is not on the same road that Astrid took, but Mackenzie is heading the right way regardless. Mackenzie eventually repairs Jeremiah's shortwave radio to send a message out to the Mills, but the radio is destroyed during the Aurora. Jeremiah says the Mills can be reached by taking the road north out of [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), but it would take days to get there on foot.

Jeremiah eventually requests Mackenzie with delivering a message to a person named Atwood, "WINTERMUTE". He also tells Mackenzie that he would need to pass through the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md), and send another message to the Mills via [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md). Mackenzie is eventually captured by [Mathis](./Mathis.md) in the Dam however.

Astrid wakes up in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) and manages to use Signal Hill to contact the Mills, but cannot get a message out. She overhears the same transmission that Mackenzie made in Episode 2, and realizes he is alive. She eventually makes her way to [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) and takes the coastline to reach the Mills.
A flashback in Episode 3 reveals that an illness is spreading in Perseverance Mills, and that she stole the cure inside the Hardcase before chartering Mackenzie for a plane.

Mackenzie is imprisoned by a group of convicts and must comply with their demands after the Hardcase is confiscated. He eventually makes contact with [Jace](./Jace.md), a woman who has been spending time near the mills at the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md), along with Atwood. After retrieving the Hardcase, destroying [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), and escaping, Mackenzie and Jace both make their way to Suzuiki.

A post credits cutscene shows Astrid in a canoe arriving by the docks of the town. Jane Yang finds her and rescues her, but questions why Astrid does not have the case. A quarantine is currently afflicting the town.
- This location has currently taken the longest development time to implement into the game, longer than any other location on Great Bear Island.

- It has been mentioned as far back as 2017 (with the original release of Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle. Possibly earlier as shown in the map below) and finally made a cameo in 2021 (with the release of Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence).
- The town would finally be introduced as a playable location and Region with the release of Episode 5 on March 31st, 2026.

- There is a connection between Perseverance Mills and the [Railway](./Railway.md) behind the sawmill, though it is inaccessible from the Perseverance Mills end and can only be accessed from the Railway by [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md) along a cliff.

**Perseverance Wilds** is a [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md)-exclusive region, which consists of the wilderness near the town of [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), to which it connects.

The most open region in Episode 5, it consists mainly of empty wilderness, with a couple of shallow caves and two rivers. One of them is unfrozen and must be crossed by using a rickety bridge (Faulty Crossing). The other, smaller river is frozen over and can be safely walked on. At its north end is a lake (Mindful Basin) with a group of cabins (Lake Cabins), a ice fishing hut, a nearby waterfall (Terminal Outflow), and a lookout tower (Forgotten Lookout)to the southeast. The river's southern end ends at a frozen bay, with a cabin (Doubter's Retreat) and a uniquely designed ice fishing hut.

There are many cars with their hoods opened and their [Car Batteries](./Car%20Battery.md) missing. This is later revealed to have been [Terry's](./Terry.md) doing. Following the road through the region leads to a collapsed tunnel.
- There is a small cabin on the western side of the frozen river, (styled much like [Bricklayer's Retreat](./Bricklayer%27s%20Retreat.md))
- A nearly destroyed cabin to the south of the previously mentioned cabin, along with a dock on the river where the drowned Constable is found

**Pilgrim** is the 1st [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) Experience in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is the standard "easy" difficulty setting.

Pilgrim's difficulty is comparable to a pleasant walk through a park on a crisp winter day. Hostile [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) always flees in terror from the player, even if provoked or directly attacked. [Needs](./Needs.md) are very manageable. Food and resources are highly abundant and can be easily procured. Overall, the player's survival is almost guaranteed on this Experience, with most dangers coming in the form of the elements, environmental hazards, and generally just poor judgement.

This game mode is best picked if the player is trying to explore and learn the game world and its mechanics, or if they wish to unlock [Achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md), [Feats](./Feats.md), or [Badges](./Badges.md) without much difficulty.

Just a mountain with the form of a pillar. Underneath it can be found the cave leading to [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md), located in the region of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md). It can be used as a landmark for navigation since it's at the southern part of Ash Canyon and is almost always visible.

Up along a path that leads to a higher plateau, two burnt-out campfires can be found. The first may contain several items, including a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) and a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) (very unlikely), as well as a [Snare](./Snare.md) and a can opener. The second, slightly higher up to the north can contain a hunting rifle (may be broken) and some ammunition and supplies. They are located roughly halfway between the markers for Pillar's footrest and Climber's cave.

The area is rich in natural resources, and a [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) grove and several potential ravaged [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md) spawns exist in the area, making this a potential hunting/resupply area while transitioning between Timberwolf Mountain and Ash Canyon. A corpse can be found along the west wall of the area.

There is also a tree stump with a [Spray Paint](./Spray%20Paint.md) and 0.50L of [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) when going from the pass towards the "to Timberwolf Mountain" cave. Its on a small rise, near the pass right beneath the pathway leading up the (right) rockface which leads nowhere.

**Pinnacle Peaches** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.

Consuming Pinnacle Peaches restores a moderate amount of calories and hydration. It may also be warmed by a [fire](./Fire.md), to make progress in [Cooking](./Cooking.md) [Survival Skill](./Skills.md), and consumed while hot to grant the benefit [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md). Pinnacle Peaches have relatively low energy density (on par with that of cooked meats), making them relatively inefficient as a travelling food.

Like other canned foods, Pinnacle Peaches may be opened with a [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md) or [bladed tool](./Tools.md), or smashed open (with no tool) but spilling some of its contents. If opened with a tool a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) is received after consuming the contents.
Pinnacle Peaches are relatively common inside homes, usually in cupboards or on shelves. They can also be found in stores.

**Plane Crash Injuries** is a cut [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) encountered in the mission [Survival Of The Fittest](./Survival%20Of%20The%20Fittest.md) of [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) in the Predux [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) storyline. It is considered [Cut/Discontinued Content](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md) but can still be experienced by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md) to play versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam versions of Wintermute.

It was acquired immediately after waking up in the ravine after the plane crash, and would persist for 5 Days. It prevents [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) from Sprinting, holding [Stones](./Stone.md), or from using the [Rock Climb](./Rock%20Climb.md) to leave the ravine on Day 4 (Causing him to fall and [Sprain his Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md)). It finally heals on Day 5, and serves as a way to slow the player down in order to immerse them in the world as part of the tutorial.

In the Redux, Mackenzie instead wakes up with [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md), a Sprained Wrist, a Sprained Ankle, and 2 [Pain](./Pain.md) from the Sprains, with the cause listed as originating from Plane Crash Injuries.

- Plane Crash Injuries was retconned out of Episode 1 with the removal of the mission [Survival Of The Fittest](./Survival%20Of%20The%20Fittest.md). Mackenzie now only stays in the ravine for 2 days in the Redux Episode 1 mission [The Crash](./The%20Crash.md) (though Mackenzie will still fail to climb out on day 1 if you attempt to leave early).

- A nod to this cut Affliction also exists in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), as Astrid was passed out for 5 days (rather than Mackenzie) and wakes up with [Pain](./Pain.md), a [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md), and a [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md), with the cause being Plane Crash Injuries.

**Plane Crashes** are newly generated loot locations introduced in the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) Part 2 update in Lower Great Bear (and parts of the Far Territory).

These random smaller air vehicle crashes are not be confused with either [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md), the [Crashed Northern Charters Plane)](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md), or the [plane on the summit of Timberwolf mountain](./Tail%20Section.md).

Having fallen out of the sky sometime during the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), several air vehicles have landed in very odd, hard to reach locations across [Lower Great Bear](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).

Crashes can be either a [Helicopter](./Helicopter.md) or a small [Airplane](./Airplane.md), depending on the spawning location. Helicopters and the front section of Airplanes are always intact and can be used as shelters, but airplanes tend to be little more than scrap wreckage by the time the player finds them, so the cockpit can be harder to find.

Crash sites offer decent loot. A frozen corpse or backpack can often be found in the vicinity alongside items like [Tools](./Tools.md), [Clothing](./Clothing.md), [Medicine](./First%20Aid.md), [Food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), [Flares](./Flare.md), [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), and [Flare Shells](./Flare%20Shell.md).
- A crashed plane on the mountainside between the [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md) and [Derailment](./Derailment.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md).
- A crashed plane South-East and up-hill from [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), past the lone house near the edge of town.
- A crashed helicopter east of [Fallow Dugout](./Fallow%20Dugout.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md).
- A crashed helicopter near [Muskeg Overlook](./Muskeg%20Overlook.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md).

A **Plank** is a single length of wood, and is a harvestable item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. They often, but not always, act as decorations, and can be found commonly in houses or in industrial areas throughout the world. Some planks in the world also serve as passageways while also remaining harvestable, such as those leading to the upper loft in [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md), and as such survivors should be careful of what they choose to harvest.
Planks can also wash up on the coastline as part of the [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) mechanic.
Planks yield 2 [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md), require a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) to harvest, and take 9 minutes to harvest.

The Farmstead is found at the back of a dead orchard, near the side of the river and at the end of a long driveway off the main road (a car and a wooden arch mark the entrance to down the path, which is lined with telephone poles). The location consists of a derelict barn, a grain silo, and a large farmhouse with a basement. The silo cannot be entered. There is also an abandoned [Car](./Car.md) on the property. Some distance behind the farmstead is another broken stable with a chance to spawn a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), as well as usually having a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) and a small amount of supplies.

The farmhouse itself has three points of entry, as well as a basement accessed through a bulkhead door on the side of the building, and from a door to the right of the bathroom on the ground floor. The kitchen door is enclosed by a roofed porch that usually contains some loot. The porch is very useful as it is not uncommon for a [Bear](./Bear.md) to spawn directly outside of the house. The bear can be shot and killed from inside the safety of the porch, and this is by far the simplest and safest method of taking it down.

The interior of the farmhouse is quite spacious with two bathrooms, a kitchen, living room, study, and three bedrooms. The kitchen has a stove with six cooking slots, allowing the player to efficiently cook large amounts of food and drink on the cook top, especially if there are one or more [cooking pots](./Cooking%20Pot.md) available.

In the above-ground floors, there are two fire sources (including the stove), a lot of containers for storing surplus tools and supplies, and a [toilet](./Toilet.md) in each bathroom containing a good amount of potable [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md). There are several [beds](./Bed.md) to use for warming up and [resting](./Sleep.md). In the basement, there is a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) for crafting, ![Old picture of Pleasant Valley Farmstead](../assets/OldPleasantValleyFarmstead.jpg)_Old picture of Pleasant Valley Farmstead_ Several useful tools and supplies can also be found in both the main house and the basement, including two chances for a Hunting Rifle to spawn either in the study, or underneath the bed in the master bedroom. A few rounds of [ammo](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) can usually be found scattered around the house, as well. A large amount of the furniture can be broken down for a lot of [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) and [Cloth](./Cloth.md) when needed.

It is a tactical choice for a base because of the size, the large amount of loot, and the inclusion of beds, fireplaces, and a work bench. However, it is a fair distance away from other buildings, so travel may take longer.
Be wary of bears near this location, as there is a den not very far away and the bear tends to wander. Sometimes, there can be **two** bears patrolling around the area.

The farmstead is home to [Molly](./Molly.md) who once ran the farm with a man (likely her husband). She states the farm often ran on generators, since the power went out frequently. In the office, there is a photograph of a younger, glum-looking Molly with the man--his arm flung around her shoulder.

The man is dead as of Episode 3, and his corpse may be found in the farmstead basement. The man was killed by wolves, according to Molly. She states she did not kill him, but she did not try to save him, either.
In the story, most of the house is locked and inaccessible for much of the game. The basement may be accessed after the initial opening cutscenes, however.

Before the [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) update, the farmhouse held a children's playroom upstairs, complete with a crib, toy blocks, and a toy tractor. This was removed because it most likely conflicted with Molly's backstory.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Pleasant Valley History Part One**_

Pleasant Valley’s harsh and remote location, even for Great Bear Island, has shaped much of its history and the character of its residents. The Valley’s geography -- wide, open fields ringed by jagged mountain ranges -- creates unusually strong weather events. Locals have long told of multi-day storms, high winds, and a deep, endless cold during the Winter months.
But these conditions didn’t keep Great Bear Islanders from settling there. In fact, some saw the Valley’s wild and desolate hills as an ideal place to homestead.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Pleasant Valley History Part Two**_

Founded in 1919, Thomson’s Crossing remains the only significant community in Pleasant Valley. With a history tied to the farming and mining concerns of its residents, the isolated town followed its own path along the boom and bust cycle of Great Bear Island industry.

With greater and greater instability due to seismic activity, the workings in the nearby mines proved too dangerous for later generations to exploit. And with the arrival of local activists, determined to keep new industry from taking root in Pleasant Valley, Thomson’s Crossing began its steady decline.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Pleasant Valley History Part Three**_

With the onset of The Collapse, Pleasant Valley locals didn’t notice the brunt of change all that quickly. Being so accustomed to remote living already, it took several years before life shifted in any dramatic fashion.

Residents did begin to notice the growing scarcity of the few creature comforts imported to the Island. But connected as they were through regular reports from the regional weather service radio station, their post-Collapse isolation took some years to set in.

**Description:** A large open farmland basin surrounded by mountains on all sides, with a very ironic name.

**Connecting Regions:** [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) _(via [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md))_, [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) _(via [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md))_
> “**For advanced players. A challenging, vast mountain wilderness region with a few key shelters, originally settled by hardy homesteaders.**”
> **You're not from around here, are you? Whoever named this area "Pleasant Valley" had a pretty good sense of humour. We get some of the harshest weather on all of Great Bear.**
**Pleasant Valley** is the 3rd [Region](./Region.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ and is one of the most central regions of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).

The region is a massive rural agriculture comprised of farmland and orchards, surrounded by forested rolling hills filled with coal mining, caves, waterfalls and the harshest [Weather](./Weather.md) on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). Pleasant Valley is also notable for hosting a large Birch Forest as well as a [Passenger Plane](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) downed by the [Aurora](./First%20Flare.md).

Pleasant Valley connects to [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) via a rope climb near [Prepper's Abandoned Cache](./Prepper%27s%20Abandoned%20Cache.md) in the northeast, to [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) in the southeast through [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md), to [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) by following the road from [Long Curve](./Long%20Curve.md), which leads through [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) and [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md), and to [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) through a cave to the southwest, just west of [Cascading Falls](./Cascading%20Falls.md) which leads through [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) and [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md).

Pleasant Valley is a very large region in [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), the largest of Lower Great Bear. It features few shelters outside of Thompson's Crossing to the southeast, so gameplay focuses on surviving the elements and living off the land while navigating between cabins, caves and landmarks.

Frequent high winds and [low temperatures](./Hypothermia.md), [snow, fog and blizzards](./Weather.md) plague the region, the second coldest in Lower Great Bear after [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). Blizzards can be as cold as -48°C with windchill at -33°C in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) (Hardened Survivor). The mix of rolling hills and almost featureless farmland can be disorienting and can make it easy to lose one's way. The landscape also increases the risk of unexpected, close-range wildlife [encounters](./Wildlife.md).

Players must time expeditions carefully and make preparations for sudden changes in the [weather](./Weather.md), as the rather ironic name of "Pleasant" is misleading considering that Blizzards are more frequent in this region than any other. Noting landmarks and even marking a path can help navigate through the hills and trees, but beware: [bear](./Bear.md), [moose](./Moose.md), and [wolves](./Wolf.md) (and in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md): [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md)) may wait just around the corner.

[Pleasant Valley Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) features a large barn located near the center of the map. The [Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) area also contains several abandoned [vehicles](./Car.md), hay trailers, sheds, and tractors around the perimeter.
- The barn possesses several valuable utilities including a fire barrel, a [workbench](./Work%20Bench.md), lots of storage, a central location, and a [bed](./Bed.md) (see bullet point below).

- It is possible to sleep inside the pickup truck's cab by entering it and selecting "Sleep" under "Campcraft" in the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md), including with a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) or [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md) for a [Warmth](./Warmth.md) bonus).

[Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) is located about five minutes west of the [barn](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) through the hay bale field. This location, like the barn, has a few vehicles scattered around the perimeter. The vehicles may contain supplies and offer temporary shelter from weather or predators.

- Like the barn, the Farmstead possesses key resources: a 6-burner stove, fireplace, a fire barrel outside, lots of storage, and an enclosed porch for storing food or safely monitoring conditions outdoors.
- Inside the house also are two beds with different warmth values; a workbench (accessed through the cellar door outside or a door under the stairs from inside); and a large amount of loot.
- It is also located centrally, and [deer](./Deer.md) and [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) may roam nearby (although, so do [predators](./Wildlife.md)).
- Nearby, there is also a large shed/small barns that contains a fire barrel and makeshift bed, as well.
The Farmstead is relatively close to the Outbuildings and [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md), another useful indoor shelter.

Provides some shelter **Poacher's Camp** is one of the few marked locations within [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md).

Poacher's Camp is nestled inside a railway car, situated partway down the track that bisects Forlorn Muskeg. The car is surrounded by broken trees and other railway cars, and the entire assemblage is surrounded by portions of weak ice and [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md).

Inside the car is a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) and a few containers, which may hold useful items. The player may find [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md), [Coal](./Coal.md), [scrap metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), [antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md), a [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), and a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md).

The car proves useful in protecting against the wind and elements it gives a 2°C warmth bonus from being inside, and doubles as a good sleeping point due to its fire barrel; this location can be useful if the player wants to achieve [Beneath a Starry Sky](./Beneath%20a%20Starry%20Sky.md). However, due to frequent blizzards in Forlorn Muskeg, it's not recommended to use the place as a base for more than one or two nights.
The location is not considered indoors. Saplings and hides will **not** cure if left inside the train car.

**This mine is a graveyard. Maybe my own too, if I’m not careful. The wolves here are unwell. All this pollution in the ground. Awful.** [A Page From A Journal](./A%20Page%20From%20A%20Journal.md)

The **Poisoned Wolf** is a variant of the [Wolf](./Wolf.md) found only in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md). They were introduced in the Part 4 Buried Echoes update for players that purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon.

Suffering from extreme malnutrition from a lack of hunting opportunities owed to the intense pollution present within the Zone, Poisoned Wolves are more ragged in appearance compared to regular Wolves. Their fur is much more messy and matted and their bodies are much more lean in appearance due to a lack of stored body fat. Some of the [Chemicals](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) from the Zone can also be seen around their faces and necks when viewed up close, which are transmitted to the player should they attack them in a Struggle.

They are easily identifiable from a distance due to how they carry their heads much lower to the ground than a regular, healthy Wolf. They are also the only Wolf variant inside the Zone of Contamination. ![A Wolf (left) and Poisoned Wolf. Notice the weakened stance of the Poisoned Wolf.](../assets/Poisoned_Wolf_and_Wolf.jpg)_A Wolf (left) and Poisoned Wolf. Notice the weakened stance of the Poisoned Wolf._

A [Poisoned Wolf Carcass](./Poisoned%20Wolf%20Carcass.md) will drop a Wolf Pelt and 2 Fresh Guts, but due to the extreme malnourishment and contaminated meat of the animal, no harvestable Wolf Meat is present on a carcass.

Poisoned Wolves behave mechanically the same to that of regular Wolves, forming small packs, barking, growling, and stalking any prey they manage to find, aside from a few key differences:

- Unlike regular Wolves, Poisoned Wolves seem to have a keener sense of smell and awareness of their surroundings due to intense starvation, resulting in them spotting and smelling prey from further distances than normal Wolves would.
- They do not show as much fear to lit [Torches](./Torch.md) or [Flares](./Flare.md). This makes it impossible to simply outwalk Poisoned Wolves without consequence in some cases.
- After scaring a Poisoned Wolf into fleeing, there is a 50% chance that they will continue fleeing or turn back around and begin stalking/attacking the player again.

- If they do flee from the player, Poisoned Wolves only flee a quarter the distance that normal Wolves do, and most often turn straight back around and begin stalking the player again due to their close proximity.

- Poisoned Wolves will refuse to willingly enter contaminated [Chemical Hazard](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) areas in order to attack the player or any prey animal, despite already being contaminated themselves.
- Poisoned Wolves will stand their ground and growl at the player if they remain in the Hazard, and will eventually run away in fear.

- If the player enters and exits a Chemical Hazard while still being stalked, there is a chance that the Poisoned Wolf will charge the player unprovoked. The odds of this happening increase the higher the player's [Scent](./Scent.md) value is. A unique running animation will play when this happens, with the Wolf's ears pinned back as they charge (this animation will be different from a normal provoked charge).
- Poisoned Wolves have less health, due to their emaciated condition reducing their overall constitution.
- 1 good Hunting Rifle/Revolver/Survival Bow shot to the head or body is all that it takes to kill a Poisoned Wolf, showing how much weaker they are than normal wolves.

- Being attacked in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) by a Poisoned Wolf slowly builds up [Chemical Poisoning Risk](./Chemical%20Poisoning%20Risk.md) upon the player, and can result in an Affliction if the player's Poisoning levels are already too high.
- A bite that results in [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) results in an immediate 20% addition to the Chemical Poisoning Risk bar.

Like all predators, Poisoned Wolves glow green and become a more aggressive Aurora Predator when the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) is active. [Campfires](./Campfire.md) and a working [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) will still force a Poisoned Wolf to keep its distance from a player.
- They have slightly more health than normal, but still die fairly easily (Revolvers no longer one shot them to the head/body).
- Aurora Poisoned Wolves do not fear [Flares](./Flare.md), [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), or lit [Torches](./Torch.md).
- They fear active street lights, and will stand and growl at the player if they pass near the boundary of one. After enough time, they will run away in fear if they cannot reach the player.
- Aurora Poisoned Wolves will still refuse to willingly enter Contaminated [Chemical Hazard](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) areas in order to attack the player or any prey animal.
- They fear [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) high beams and will temporarily stop a charge as long as they are on.
- They will stay away from lit [Campfires](./Campfire.md), but will still stay close by to stalk the player.
- Gunshots are still effective at frightening aurora wolves, provided they are not charging.

- Despite the Zone of Contamination containing only Poisoned Wolves, several ordinary [Ravaged Wolf Carcasses](./Wolf%20Carcass.md) can be found in the Zone, with edible meat that can be harvested on the body.

![Hqdefault](../assets/Hqdefault.jpg) Polaroids are collectible items that were added in the [Fearless Navigator](https://hinterlandforums.com/forums/topic/36987-the-long-dark-updated-fearless-navigator-176/) update. They are polaroid photographs with an inscription on the back informing the player which region each Polaroid belongs to. They are most commonly found on bodies or in backpacks of past survivors.

Polaroids are purely used for surveying. After collecting a Polaroid, an icon will appear on the player's map to show where the Vista the Polaroid corresponds to is located. If the player stands at the Vista location shown in the Polaroid and surveys the location with [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md) (provided that the weather is clear), a large area of the [Map](./Map.md) will be revealed.

- Note that the only regions without Polaroids are [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md), [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md), and [Transition Regions](./Region.md#Transition_Zones), likely due to their small sizes. There are currently a total of 21 Vista Polaroids. In many regions, the locations of where you find the vista polaroids are linked to which [Loot Table](./Loot%20Table.md) your game is on. So if you find a polaroid linked to Loot Table 4 (e.g. the polaroid at the end of [Secret Mountain Path](./Secret%20Mountain%20Path.md)), you will find polaroids in other regions in their Loot Table 4 spawn positions.

**Pork and Beans** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.
Consuming Pork and Beans restores a moderate amount of calories and causes slight hydration loss. It may also be warmed by a [Fire](./Fire.md) to grant the benefit [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md).

Like other canned foods, Pork and Beans may be opened with a [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md) or [bladed tool](./Tools.md), or smashed open (with no tool) but spilling some of it's contents. If opened with a tool a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) is received after consuming the contents.

- Pork and Beans is packaged as the product "_Musical Fruit Beans"_, referencing a popular rhyme about flatulence. The can also promotes "reduced sodium", which would likely be less than ideal in a post-apocalyptic setting.

- A single [Can](./Can.md) of Pork and Beans can be harvested for one [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) in the [Misty Falls Cave](./Misty%20Falls%20Cave.md). 4 more cans would eventually be added to Survival Mode.

**Description:** A century old abandoned shipping port that is the starting point of Cauldron Island.
**Connecting Regions:** [Anna Island -- Track Section 1](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%201.md) [Anna Island -- Track Section 5](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%205.md)

**Port Remnant** is a [Region](./Region.md) released for _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ and is the starting point of [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) and the [_Iron Road_](./Iron%20Road.md) expansion.

Port Remnant is first accessed by taking the [Fulmar Autopilot Boat](./Fulmar%20Autopilot%20Boat.md) from [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md). From there, the player will arrive at Cauldron Island inside a cave underneath the Lighthouse. Climbing the stone stairs reveals a ruined Lighthouse and [Wax Cylinder 2](./Wax%20Cylinder%202.md) and [Map (Church)](./Map%20%28Church%29.md). The Cylinder has a key to the door, and the Map points to the path to take to the Church in the region.

The region itself is in a considerable state of disrepair. A century of time has rotted away most of the buildings in the region, many of which are barely standing. 3 ships can be found half sunken in the ice near the Lighthouse. What is presumably a whaling warehouse is found in the center of the map after traversing the frozen bay, with worker cabins found around the area. Southwest is a set of train track, train bridge, and a train terminal. A road leads up to a cliff to the Church in the south most part of the map (inaccessible due to a landslide), with more flat land and some ponds below the southern cliffs.

Several of the jagged mountainous areas can be explored near the bay, leading to hidden plant supplies and unique vantage points. Bizarrely, there are 3 Whale Bone Shrines in a few places in the region whose nature is currently not understood.

Taking the tracks to the east will take the player to [Anna Island -- Track Section 5](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%205.md), while the tracks to the west lead to [Anna Island -- Track Section 1](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%201.md) (though the path is blocked by a metal gate).

The area can be returned later to with the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md), which can be used to open the inaccessible [Obstructed Transit](./Obstructed%20Transit.md) and destroy the gate to Track Section 1. This is the only region on Anna Island not to feature an [Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md) or [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) (aside from [Anna Island -- Track Section 6](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%206.md)).
- To Anna Island Track Section 1 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 1](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%201.md))
- To Anna Island Track Section 5 (Region Transition to [Anna Island -- Track Section 5](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%205.md))
- [Wolves](./Wolf.md) can be found throughout the region, mainly to the south near the tracks. Some can be found east of the lighthouse.

- 4 sunken ships can be found in the region. 1 of them looks to be a similar ship as [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md), while 2 others looks like The Harbinger from [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md). The rusted skeleton of a 4th ship can also be found.
- This is the only region on Anna Island with a Work Bench, found at Departure's Memory.
- There were formerly 2 cabins south of Departure's memory, but 1 was removed after an update.
- The Whale Bone Shrines were originally quite large, but were scaled down in size after an update.

The **Pot Belly Stove** is an immovable [contained fire](./Fire.md#Contained_fires). The pot belly stove functions identically to other contained fires and player-made [Campfire](./Campfire.md). The pot belly stove provides no advantage over other contained fires, but it does allow protection against wind, unlike the player-made campfire. It has one [Cooking](./Cooking.md) slot.
The pot belly stove can be re-lit indefinitely, though it requires fresh starter, tinder, and fuel each time.
Pot belly stoves have fixed locations that do not change between games. A pot belly stove is located in every [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) as well as in some other structures.

**Potato** is a raw [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, found inside [Vegetable Rack](./Vegetable%20Rack.md), [Potato Sacks](./Potato%20Sack.md) or indoors.

Potatoes are vegetables with a long shelf-life. They cannot be eaten raw but may be cooked or used to craft stews. They are found indoors 4-8 at a time inside a Potato Sack or Vegetable Drawers, loose indoors (usually on the floor), or inside crates.
Potatoes are a non-renewable resource unless the [Trader](./Trader.md) is enabled, where there is a chance for them to appear.
Potatoes spoil at the same rate no matter whether stored inside, outside, container or not.

Raw potatoes are inedible and must be placed upon a cooking slot of a lit [Fire](./Fire.md) for 60 minutes to create a [Cooked Potato](./Cooked%20Potato.md). Collecting a finished one improves your [Cooking Skill](./Skills.md#Cooking) and increases its condition by 50%.

**Power Plant** is a small hydro-electric facility located in [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) on a river to the northwest of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md). The prison can be reached through the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md). There is a road that leads past the nearby [Grand Meadow](./Grand%20Meadow.md) to [Narrow Bridge](./Narrow%20Bridge.md), but it is blocked by a landslide at [Bear's Bend](./Bear%27s%20Bend.md).
- A sign at the entrance suggests the plant was built in 1976 by a company called Blackrock Mountain Power.
- At the time of release in survival mode, there was a bug that could cause players to unexpectedly die from drowning while standing on land below the catwalk outside the building.[^1]
- The catwalk outside the building was a late addition in development, meant to ensure that non-player characters would have a way of entering through the main doors when coming from the prison.[^2]
- [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), a larger hydro-electric power plant in the [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md) region

**Practical Gunsmithing** is a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) used to improve the [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) skill. It can also be used as Fuel when starting a [Fire](./Fire.md).

_Practical Gunsmithing_ can be researched for 5 hours that can be broken into multiple 1-hour minimum research sessions. 10 [Gunsmithing skill points](./Gunsmithing.md#Skill_levels) are awarded on completing the research. By selecting the Settled Mind [Feat](./Feats.md), research time will be reduced by 20%, putting it at 4 hours.
- [Warmth](./Warmth.md), [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Thirst](./Thirst.md), and [Hunger](./Hunger.md) exceed 0%

If the player's fatigue, thirst or hunger meters go down to zero or if the environment becomes dark during a research session, the session will be terminated instantly. The hour of research that was in progress will not be completed and any time that had already been spent will be wasted. For a multiple-hour research session, only the incomplete hour will be lost, all the previous hours will still count towards completion of the book.

Prepared Birch Bark is an ingredient for cooking [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md), a food and medical item and is crafted from 2 [Birch Bark](./Birch%20Bark.md). Crafting takes 5 minutes and doesn't require a tool or light.

To cook Birch Bark Tea, one Prepared Birch Bark and 0.25 liters of [potable water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) must be cooked for 10 minutes at a lit [Fire](./Fire.md) with a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) or [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md). Consuming Birch Bark Tea restores 100 Calories, 30% Hydration and grants the benefit "[Restore Condition](./Restore%20Condition.md)" and potentially "[Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md)" if the beverage is also hot. Cooking Birch Bark Tea increases [Cooking Skill](./Skills.md).

Birch Bark can can be found in the wilderness near lone birch trees or abundantly at birch forests, typically in single pieces after [High Winds or Blizzards](./Weather.md). Raw Birch Bark cannot be consumed directly and must first be crafted into Birch Bark Tea.

The Benefit "Restore Condition" heals 5% Condition (2.5% per hour, for 2 hours), regardless if the player is awake/asleep, or if [Needs](./Needs.md) are not met. The Benefit does not stack however, and drinking multiple cups of Birch Bark Tea within 5 hours of one another is a waste of resources.
Prepared Birch Bark (0.05kg) has half the weight of it's materials (2 Birch Bark, 0.10kg), Neither Birch Bark or Birch Bark Tea [decays](./Decay.md).

- Birch Forests are present near the [Lonely Homestead](./Lonely%20Homestead.md) ([Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md)), western [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md), and north-western [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). Lone birch trees can be found sporadically in all regions.
- It is possible to survive exclusively on Birch Bark Tea, especially on easier difficulties or by using the starvation strategy (only eating just before sleep).
- Birch Bark Tea is disabled during the [Challenge](./Challenge.md): [As the Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md), but Birch Bark may still be collected and used as Tinder.

- [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) is the only item which can restore all 4 [Needs](./Needs.md) (if consumed while hot), but Birch Bark Tea functions similarly with its Benefit "Restore Condition", since this heals Condition (2.5% hourly) faster than Fatigue damages it (1% hourly), so it is possible to survive indefinitely without Sleep by drinking 1 cup of Birch Bark Tea every 5 hours (albeit at 0% Fatigue, moving slowly and unable to climb/sprint).

**Prepared Reishi Mushrooms** are a natural medical item used to treat [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_.

Prepared Reishi Mushrooms are crafted from 2 [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) and take 15 minutes (in-game) to create; Reishi Tea requires 1 Prepared Reishi Mushrooms, 0.25L of [Potable Water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) and 10 minutes at a lit [Fire](./Fire.md).

Reishi Tea functions similar to [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md) for treating Afflictions, however consuming prepared Reishi Tea (even without treating an Affliction) restores 100 Calories, 30% Hydration and potentially granting the benefit "[Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md)".

Reishi Mushrooms can be found in the wilderness growing on the trunks or stumps of dead trees, typically in clusters of 1-3 units. They cannot be directly consumed and must first be crafted into [Prepared Reishi Mushrooms](./Prepared%20Reishi%20Mushrooms.md) and then cooked into [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md).
Prepared Reishi Mushrooms have half the weight of their raw form, and no form of Reishi Mushroom [decays](./Decay.md).

**Prepared Rose Hips** are a natural medical and food item used to treat [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_.

Prepared Rose Hips are crafted from 24 [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) and takes 15 minutes (in-game) to prepare. Rose Hips can can be found in the wilderness growing on Rose Bushes, typically in clusters of 1-4 units, a single Rose Bush yields 8 Rose Hips when Harvested. Rose Hips can be found rarely inside of containers. They cannot be directly consumed and must first be crafted into Prepared Rose Hips and then cooked into [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md).

Rose Hip Tea functions similar to [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md) for treating Afflictions, and is cooked from one Prepared Rose Hips (24 Rose Hips) and 0.25 liters of [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) at a lit [Fire](./Fire.md). Consuming prepared Rose Hip Tea (even without treating an Affliction) restores 100 Calories, 30% Hydration and potentially grants the benefit "[Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md)." Cooking Rose Hip Tea increases [Cooking Skill](./Skills.md).
