- Harvesting 3 Rose Bushes (at 8 Rose Hips each) is required to craft 1 unit of Prepared Rose Hips/Rose Hip Tea.

- Rose Hips are found sporadically in all regions growing on Rose Bushes, particular in mountainous areas near ledges or cliffs. They frequently are near entrances to [Caves](./Cave%20%28disambiguation%29.md), Rose Climbs, deployment points for [Mountaineering Ropes](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md), and secret locations.
- Teas may be heated/reheated to grant the Warming Up Benefit by placing them on a fire's cooking spot, or nearby a lit fire.
- Broken Ribs are permanent if left untreated, though Pain and Burns will dissipate naturally with time (4-30 hours).

- Pain has minimal effect on gameplay (aside from blurry vision) with it's only limitation being an inability to read [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) while afflicted, and subsides automatically with time. This generally makes treating Pain a wasteful decision, to carry Painkillers consume them instead of reserving their use to treat Broken Ribs or Burns.
- Painkillers cannot be crafted and Rose Hips do not regrow; however Painkillers are renewable via [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md).
- Prepared Rose Hips weigh 0.05 kg, or 1/5 of what 24 Rose Hips (their crafting materials) weigh.
- Teas are more weight efficient than Water for the Hydration they grant. (0.1kg of a tea grants 30% Hydration, equivalent to 0.25kg of water).

- The condition of Painkillers decays slowly over time (based on [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md)). Upon reaching 0% Condition, they become unusable and will disappear if inside of a container, but all forms of Rose Hips do not decay.
- Rose Hips and other harvestable plants and remedies were introduced on 7 February 2015 in [update 0.192](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.192).
- As of the 1.0 [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) update (August 1, 2017) Rose Hips must be prepared before cooking them.

- Rose Hips (also known as Rosehip, Rosehep or Rosehaw) are a [real world plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_hip) and accessory fruit to Rose Bushes, similar to their in-game representation including their use as a painkiller.

- Real-World Rose Hips have a history as a [poverty food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famine_food), particularly with Native American peoples during survival situations or times of hardship, as well as for ornamental purposes.

- In The Long Dark, Painkillers and Tea must be applied directly to treat a specific injury (similar to a Bandage), unlike real-world orally-taken drugs which become generally distribute through the body.

_Not to be confused with **[Prepper's Abandoned Cache](./Prepper%27s%20Abandoned%20Cache.md) or one of 4 [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) bunkers.**_

> “**Find my brother. Wyatt. He hasn't checked in since it all went dark. He runs with this group of preppers. Bad guys, his crew, but they look up to him. There were always three that followed Wyatt around. Stockpiles, hunters, conspiracy nuts. Maybe you know the type? Hehe.**”

A **Prepper Cache,** also known by their nickname of **"Bunker"**, is a reinforced underground shelter with a stockpile of supplies. The contents of these 9 Caches is randomly selected during world generation across 9 regions in Lower Great Bear. They are the centerpiece of [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md).

The entrance to a Prepper Cache is a man-sized hatch above-ground which leads into the bunker below; they are typically found in high altitude or difficult-to-reach areas, and may be partially concealed.

There are 9 Cache locations in select regions. Each Prepper Cache's location is a fixed spawn location, but the contents inside the Cache are always randomized. In terms of loot, there are 4 types of Prepper's Cache, three of which will be stocked with materials, while the remaining 6 will be abandoned and empty. The three types of loot stock are the Stockpile (kitchen) Cache, the Hunting Cache, and the Conspiracy Cache.

_**NOTE**_: Prepper Caches spawn in Interloper and Misery, but the Stockpile, Hunting, and Conspiracy Caches will have loot quantities on par with the Abandoned Prepper Cache Type[^1]. Interloper and Misery players will need to identify these caches to undertake [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md). They can be identified based on the layout of the interior[^2].
The interiors of these caches are small, indoors, and contain 1-2 rooms with metal shelves, crates, and a bed. There are seven distinct layouts of these caches.
Prepper Caches do not spawn in some [Challenge](./Challenge.md) game modes and only appear in Lower Great Bear.
> “**One of the guys had half-a-brain, unlike the other two who were caught up in mounting heads on the wall or scribbling crazy theories. I'd start with him, the half-a-brain survivalist.**”

Contains one room with kitchen furniture and another room with a desk and bed stocked with general supplies from all categories: fire starting, first aid, clothing, food and drink, tools, materials and the unique [Prepper's Pie](./Prepper%27s%20Pie.md) [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md).
- [Prepper's Pie](./Prepper%27s%20Pie.md) [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) (will appear in Interloper/Misery)

- Tools such as: [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md), [Prybar](./Prybar.md), [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md), [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md), [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md), [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md)
- Large amount of sewing materials ([Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md), [Cloth](./Cloth.md), [Sewing Kits](./Sewing%20Kit.md))
- Miscellaneous First Aid supplies such as bottles of [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md), [Bandages](./Bandage.md) and [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md)
- A [Firestriker](./Firestriker.md), 3x [Accelerant](./Accelerant.md) and some fire making supplies as well as a [Jerry Can](./Jerry%20Can.md)

On Interloper and Misery levels, this cache has sparse loot and almost no furniture. Players undertaking [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md) will need to identify this bunker for Special Request 1.

This cache can be identified by the presence of the Prepper's Pie Recipe Card. It is also the only bunker which contains a corpse[^3]. Its layout has a small vestibule which opens into a rectangular room containing the corpse and a bed.
Only _after_ accepting Special Request 1 will a [Loose Bricks Stash](./Loose%20Bricks%20Stash.md) appear for the player. It will spawn on the wall beside the corpse[^4].
> “**If I were you I'd try the trophy hunter next. Wyatt always kept some of his guns with him.**”

Two rooms, the biggest one with antler decorations and different animal skulls, cured furs, a lot of storage space, a Bed, and a Work Bench. You may find plenty of animal skins, crow feathers, cured guts and hunting gear like a [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) and arrows, a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) or [Revolver](./Revolver.md), [Snares](./Snare.md), and various tools. This is the only location in the game where the [Hunter's Revolver](./Hunter%27s%20Revolver.md) can be found.
- [Fisherman's Sweater](./Fisherman%27s%20Sweater.md) or [Cowichan Sweater](./Cowichan%20Sweater.md) on the bed
- [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) and other [Tools](./Tools.md) on the pegboard behind the workbench
#### Abandoned version (Interloper/Misery)

#### Abandoned version (Interloper/Misery)

For Interloper and Misery players, the Conspiracy Cache can be identified for having a red-painted corridor[^7] and a radiation sign on the wall. Identifying this cache is necessary to complete Special Request 3 as part of [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md).

As with the other special requests, it is only _after_ accepting Special Request 3 that a [Loose Bricks Stash](./Loose%20Bricks%20Stash.md) will become available in this cache. It will spawn at the far wall, to the left[^8].

On [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md), [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md), [Stalker](./Stalker.md), or all custom difficulties, 6 of the 9 bunkers will be basically empty. These are entirely abandoned, having very little if anything inside of them aside from bare concrete flooring, but always contain a Bed and provide solid shelter, despite being vacant, however.

On [Interloper](./Interloper.md) or [Misery](./Misery.md), **ALL 9** Prepper Caches will have loot quantities that are Abandoned. The Stockpile (kitchen), Hunting, and Conspiracy bunkers will still spawn, and can be recognized by their layouts, but will have loot similar to Abandoned caches[^9].
- All Caches spawn with Abandoned quantities of loot on Interloper and Misery. The Stockpile (kitchen) bunker will contain the [Prepper's Pie](./Prepper%27s%20Pie.md) Recipe Card.
> “**There's one more bunker you can check. One of old man Joplin's in Pleasant Valley. On the way to Timberwolf. He wasn't in their crew, but Wyatt set up his prepper caches.**”

The Prepper's Abandoned Cache is an underground bunker found in north-eastern Pleasant Valley, near a ruined building and an outhouse, not far from the [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section leading to [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md). The hatch entrance itself is behind a fallen tree behind the outhouse.

It is an indoor location which contains a [Bed](./Bed.md), [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), and assorted supplies in lockers or on metal shelves. It was created by Wyatt, [Sutherland's](./Trader.md) brother, long ago before it was abandoned.

The cache originally belonged to Tom Joplin, and is the starting point of [Joplin's Bunker Raid](./Joplin%27s%20Bunker%20Raid.md) in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md). It can be accessed as early as the mission [Coming Storm](./Coming%20Storm.md), otherwise the entrance will be completely covered up with snow.
2 more of Joplin's caches are found in the episode, but neither caches appear in Survival Mode. [Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md) found the first of his caches, but failed to find the rest.

While similar in appearance to normal [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md), the contents of the of the Prepper's Abandoned Cache is static, and will always spawn with the same internal layout. A [Revolver](./Revolver.md) may spawn behind the ladder, hidden behind the [Crates](./Crate.md).

A hidden room containing [A Skeleton And Note](./A%20Skeleton%20And%20Note.md) can be unlocked as part of [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md). The Prepper's Abandoned Cache will become **_permanently inaccessible_** after returning [Wyatt's Skeleton](./Wyatt%27s%20Skeleton.md) to it and blowing up the bunker hatch after progressing through the Tale enough.

- Most caches in _The Long Dark_ are marked with [fallout shelter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_shelter) signs, signifying their original purpose was to protect the local population in the event of a nuclear attack.
- This is confirmed in Sutherland's Tale, as Wyatt created these caches in case of a Nuclear conflict.
- The vent [Grate](./Grate.md) inside bunkers may be opened, potentially yielding hidden loot.

**Prepper's Pie** is a food item in _The Long Dark_, it is learned from a unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) and is made with a [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md).

**Prepper's Pie** is a unique recipe with a powerful Condition-restoring effect similar to [Dockworker's Pie](./Dockworker%27s%20Pie.md). It requires a combination of natural and artificial ingredients, and is learned from a recipe card that spawns randomly in one of nine [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) bunkers. While it is marginally less calorie-efficient than its ingredients (total of 1200 kcal vs the pie's 1125 kcal), it has powerful effects--namely a large amount of [Condition](./Condition.md) restoration. This allows it to form a similar function to the rare [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md).
Although Prepper's Pie has a base caloric value of 900, it requires level 5 [Cooking](./Cooking.md) to craft, so its calorie count will always be 25% greater (1125 kcal).
Most of the ingredients for Prepper's Pie are relatively common. However, Burdock Root is somewhat rare (1-4 per [Region](./Region.md)), and it often appears in remote or hidden areas.
**Note**: [Prepared Burdock](./Prepared%20Burdock.md) and [Prepared Reishi Mushrooms](./Prepared%20Reishi%20Mushrooms.md) cannot be used in Prepper's Pie, instead requiring their raw forms.

> “**Behavioural changes are becoming more alarming. I will be including the following transcript excerpt in my summary report, to be filed with project leads before team extraction (should it occur):**”
Known only as the **Project Medical Officer**, he is a major character in the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) storyline.

After the incident with Team 3 in the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) after the Machine was powered on, [Dr. Rüdiger](./Dr.%20R%C3%BCdiger.md) had a doctor flown in to evaluate the miners' symptoms.

Several medical and psychological tests were performed on the men, with the doctor concluding that the dementia like mental deterioration of the patients was not viral/pathogenic in nature, but instead physiological. Many exercises were given to the Doctor's patients, including forcing the patient to make a habit of frequently writing down their thoughts, with many of these writings involving memories related to water or the sea. These writing practices helped manage and slow many of the patient's metal deterioration, though they only acted as a way to gradually halt the onset of the patient's dementia. This can be shown in the case of the handwriting of [The Foreman's](./The%20Foreman.md) Technical Logs becoming increasingly worse with each note the player finds:
-  - [clear, deliberate handwriting...]

**Prologue** is the first mission in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) attempts to escape from [Mathis](./Mathis.md) before arriving at [Blackrock Federal Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md).

This mission is highly linear, with Mackenzie escaping from Mathis, [Vachon](./Vachon.md), and [Heller](./Heller.md) after a [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) attack, before falling in a ravine and then being recaptured.

After a lengthy cutscene, Makenzie will fall into a ravine and wake up with the [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md) affliction. Thankfully, the affliction does not affect the player very much, and will be healed when the next mission starts. Simply walk forward through the ravine until making it to [Forester's Hermitage](./Forester%27s%20Hermitage.md) with a large hand saw in a stump. The inside of the ruined house only contains a [Letter](./Letter.md), so cut yourself free and then climb the nearby [Rock Climb](./Rock%20Climb.md) walls across the pond until another cutscene begins. Any loot acquired during this mission will carry over to the next, but will mostly be irrelevant to acquire, so it is best to simply run through the area without scavenging anything and enjoy the story.

[TLDHOME Survival Expansion IronRoad](../assets/TLDHOME_Survival_Expansion_IronRoad.png) The **Prototype Train** is a [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). It is part of the [_Iron Road_](./Iron%20Road.md) expansion for [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) and is found exclusively on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md).

An iron fortress on wheels, the Prototype Train is a large steam locomotive and the main method of traversing [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md). Described by its creator Hamish McLeod as "an angel rendered in the finest steel[^1]", the train was at one point a state of the art vehicle and despite just being a prototype was the most advanced steam engine ever built.

Most of the Prototype Train's mechanics are borrowed from the [Steam Train](./Steam%20Train.md) from [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md), though the concept is slightly expanded on. This train does not run on Coal or Firewood, instead being powered by an exotic fuel type: Whale Oil.

Part train, part mobile shelter, part mobile base, the train is designed to be your companion while traversing Cauldron Island. The player will need to take care of the train as they travel, as it will become their most important lifeline that will ensure their survival and open up the secrets of the caldera.
The train has various components that can be interacted with. The outside of the train contains:
- Boiler Tank for storing [Potable Water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md)/[Dirty Water](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md) (both sides of the rear, Blue cap).
- Fuel Tank for storing [Whale Oil](./Whale%20Oil%20Can.md) (both sides of the rear, Red cap).
- Slide door that allows entry to the cabin on the front right side ([Train Key](./Train%20Key.md) needed first).
- The player can also lean outside of the windows in 2 spots (above the cupboard widow and the slide doors window).
![The main controls](../assets/Prototype_Train_Main_Control_Diagram.png)_The main controls_ The main control panel consists of:
- **Brake Lever** - The brake stops the train by activating the Brake Shoes. Comes with a panel on the dashboard displaying the train's brake state.
- Turning the Engine off or leaving the train while the gear is in Neutral will automatically enable the brake.
- Using the brake will wear out the Brake Shoes when used. Using the Neutral Gear and coming to a stop will avoid wearing the Brake Shoes down.
- **Gear Shift Lever** - This lever changes the speed of the train itself once the Brake Lever is disengaged.
- **PSI Gauge** - Determines how many Parts per Square Inch the train currently has.

- This gauge determines how much steam pressure the train has built up. As long as there is enough Water and Whale Oil when the Engine is on, PSI will continue to build up. Unlike the [Steam Train](./Steam%20Train.md) that regularly needs Coal fed into its boiler to increase depleted PSI, the Prototype Train automatically refills PSI over time due to its vastly increased Whale Oil fuel storage.

- Using the Gear Shift Lever to change the train speed to 2 speed will rapidly cause PSI to drop. Once PSI is low enough, the Gear will automatically return to 1 speed and slowly refill. Stopping the train or switching to Neutral will cause PSI to increase faster.
- **Fuel Gauge** - This is the yellow oil droplet gauge, and shows how much whale oil fuel is in the fuel tank for the train.
- **Water Gauge** - This is the blue waves gauge, and shows how much water is in the boiler for the train to build PSI.
- **Horn** - A lever that sounds a steam whistle. Higher stored PSI levels produce a louder whistle. Does not scare off wildlife.
- The inside of the train cabin does not allow for items to be dropped, meaning that all items must be stored in the Cupboard, carried in your inventory, or dropped outside.
- The [McLeod Ultra-Efficiency Whale Oil Heater](./McLeod%20Ultra-Efficiency%20Whale%20Oil%20Heater.md) cannot be used inside the cabin to further warm it up.

- The player can [survey](./Charcoal.md) while inside the train, but this will only uncover around a 200° circle in the current area of the map. This is because the back of the train blocks the remaining area the Survivor can see as they survey.
- Weapons can be drawn, but cannot be aimed or fired (even when leaning out of the window).
- [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) does not work inside the train.
- The train's Engine will provide a warmth bonus when activated, though the cabin is not insulated to extreme temperature drops from the outside weather (blizzards). Taking warm clothing is advised.
- Looking outside of the windows does not change the player's [Warmth](./Warmth.md) to the outside world temperature. Stepping outside will.
- Despite having a forward mounted light on the front of the train, it will not power on when the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) is out.

- Wildlife show very little reaction to the train as it passes by, and will only notice the player if the train stops and they lean out of the window. Wildlife cannot be run over by the train, and are instead pushed out of the way.
Train upgrades are an upcoming feature that will allow you to upgrade various parts of the train, including personalization of the cabin.

- Igniting the Engine will cause PSI to slowly rise in the Boiler (this produces a rattling sound in the Boiler). This will begin consuming both stored Whale Oil and Water. Igniting the Engine will not consume [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) materials. A small light will also turn on and light up the Main Control panel to help you see better at night.
- Disengaging the Brake Lever will set the Train to Neutral, and then changing the Gear Shift lever will move the train.
- LMB moves the Gear Shift forward, while RMB reverses. The Train cannot be reversed until it comes to a complete stop, and vice versa for forwarding.
- Traveling on Gear 2 will rapidly consume PSI. Once it reaches zero, Gear automatically shifts back to 1 and PSI builds up again.
- The train cannot be derailed or destroyed, but its components can become damaged over time (see repair section).
- The train doors cannot be exited while the vehicle in motion. The train must be fully stopped before the option to leave appears.

- Turning the Engine off does not automatically stop the train. Instead, built up PSI will continue to persist in the train for several hours until it is used to move to the train or gradually dissipates (stored PSI will be gone when the Boiler rattling sound stops).
- Fuel storage can be viewed at the Main Control panel or in the Train Status section of the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md).
- Ramming into any hard object that instantly stops the train (Aurora gate, some flatbed cars, buffer stops), will set the gear to Neutral but does not damage the train.

The Prototype Train uses Whale Oil as a fuel source and Water that is heated up into steam to build PSI. Both fuel types will gradually deplete over time, and the train must be refueled to continue operating it. Scattered across Cauldron Island are Railyards that can contain either a [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) or [Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md). Sometimes only one type is found at a Railyard, but occasionally both are nearby.

The back side of the train must be parked very close to the Water Tower or Oil Tank in order to gain the option to transfer fuel/water into the train. A small but helpful detail is the fact that just below each sign is a small panel that flips from red to green when the train is parked correctly for refueling. The storage supply inside these towers/tanks is unlimited; if the player leaves the area, these containers will refill themselves to their maximum levels, ensuring that the player never runs out of resources to power the train.
- Both the Tower and Tank have a stored supply of 5000.00 L that can be transferred into the Train.
- By default, the highest amount of fuel/water that can be transferred into the train is always 20.00 L, with each increment adding another 20.00 L.
- If the train is not able to be parked next to the tower/tank, the player can manually place water/fuel into their Backpack at 5.00 L per interaction (costs 1 minute each time).
- It can be handy to place water/fuel into the backpack and then transfer it to the Train's Cupboard. Dirty Water can be boiled while driving and Whale Oil Cans can be used in emergencies.
| Fuel Type | Max Storage | Burn Rate (Per H) | Refueling time (Min) | Refueling time (Max) |
| Water | 600.00 L (20 H) | 30.00 L | [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) (20.00 L in 5 minutes) | [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) (2 Hrs and 5 Min to fully refuel) |
| Whale Oil | 500.00 L (17 H) | 30.00 L | [Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md) (20.00 L in 5 minutes) | [Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md) (2 Hrs and 30 Min to fully refuel) |

As the player rides around, parts of the train will begin to wear down. All metallic parts require the [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) to fix. Successful Repairs raise the [Repair](./Repair.md) skill by 1 point, and always repair 20%-25% condition upon success (regardless of skill level). Train components' status can always be viewed either in person or in the Train Status section of the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) (this menu does not update in real time, and must be refreshed when damage is taken).

Repairing can take considerable time (up to several hours at a time), so finding a Repair Depot and repairing inside can often be the safest way to fix any damage to the train. Repairing the Train can be dangerous when done outside, as cold night temperatures, blizzards, and hostile wildlife can damage the player. Using the [McLeod Ultra-Efficiency Whale Oil Heater](./McLeod%20Ultra-Efficiency%20Whale%20Oil%20Heater.md) can provide a good heat source should you find the need to work on the Train outside.

- Train part integrity will be listed white at 100-75%, yellow at 75-50%, red at 50-0% in the Train Status menu. Train parts at 0% will be labeled ruined when observed on the train, but can be repaired unlike ruined gear items.
- All Scrap Metal repairs give 20% repair times (25% when starting from ruined) and require the [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) and 2 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) with each repair session.
- The only exception are the Brake Shoes, which will always repair up to 100% from whatever Condition they are currently in (starting at ruined they can take 1 hour 30 minutes to repair).

- The Engine/Boiler is your highest priority. At around 50%, there is a chance that switching to Gear 2 will cause the Engine to explode explode inside the cabin, removing all stored PSI, disallowing the Engine to be ignited and moved, and giving the player [Burns](./Burns.md).
- Repairing the Cowcatcher should be your third priority, as a low condition Cowcatcher can damage the Boiler when ramming hard track hazards.
- The Wheels and Brake Shoes are of least concern generally, but should still be tended to.

Sometimes objects and hazards litter the abandoned railways of Cauldron Island. A list of Track Hazards that include:
- Ramming **Deep Snow Drifts** will never cause damage to the train, but does result in speed loss.
- Ramming **Chain Metal Fences** will cause -2% condition loss to Cowcatcher and speed loss.
- Each previously mentioned hazard requires the train to be set to Gear 2. Gear 1 and Reverse will result in the train stopping dead in its tracks and will not destroy the obstacle.

- **[Damaged Tracks](./Damaged%20Track.md)** are sections of train tracks that are highly damaged. They appear as warped, rusted, and chipped train track, with damaged cross ties. Driving over them can damage the train Wheels.

- Full reverse or full acceleration at speed 1 will cause an intense amount of screeching and train bobbling, resulting in condition damage to the wheels. The louder the screeching of metal becomes, the more damage is being done to the Wheels.
- Faster train movement will cause exponentially increased levels of damage to the wheels, up to 28% condition loss or more on one section of damaged track.
- The track section can be repaired if you have a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), and do not require Scrap Metal. Each repair section takes 2 hours and repairs the tracks completely.

- Alternatively, you can avoid repairing the tracks and damaging the train by alternating between speed settings 1 and Neutral to slowly move the train. This will prevent any damage to the Wheels when passing through this hazard.
- Sometimes a parallel track can be found that prevents contact with these rails to begin with. Spending some time to use them can help preserve your train's condition in the long run.

- **Aurora Gates** are another type of obstacle that can be encountered. These gates have a booth nearby that must be entered when the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) is out and the lever inside manually turned in order to open the gates. Most Aurora Gates are found at the ends of each island throughout Cauldron Island.
- Ramming Flatbed cars (these will keep moving until they collide with another flatbed car or buffer stop, where they stop moving).
Driving into a [Repair Depot's](./Repair%20Depot.md) doors will never damage the train even at full speed, but will instead transfer you inside the building.

- Much like the [Steam Train](./Steam%20Train.md), the Prototype Train cannot be derailed (though it can sometimes appear to be off of the tracks when parked), cannot run over and kill wildlife (they are pushed out of the way), and the main boiler tank cannot be over-pressured until it explodes. Various parts of the Prototype Train can break down however.

- The Prototype Train does not contain electronic lights of any kind, save for a single lamp that lights up the control panel when the engine is powered. This makes the Steam Train slightly more unique, having a single front mounted light that turns on during the Aurora.
- The locomotive is a [4-6-4T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4-6-4) cab-forward steam locomotive.
- Cab-forward locomotives were used on the Southern Pacific railroad in the US, to keep smoke away from the cab while operating in tunnels and snow sheds.
[^1]: My great-grandfather's greatest invention. This is the Prototype. In his journal he described it as, "an angel rendered in the finest steel". - [Wax Cylinder 7](./Wax%20Cylinder%207.md)

**Prybar** is a tool in _The Long Dark_ for opening some locked objects, breaking holes in the ice for fishing, and self-defense against wolves.

**Prybar** is a Tool used to open locked containers, such as lockers and [Car](./Car.md) trunks (they cannot be used to open [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md)). It is additionally used to break the ice on ice-fishing holes, and as a weapon during [Struggles](./Struggle.md). They cannot be repaired but can be harvested for some [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md). Prybars are fairly common and can be found in almost any condition. It's one of the most important early game gear allowing you to open locked containers which sometimes have better gear.
- Open locked [Lockers](./Locker.md) and locked [Car Trunks](./Car%20Trunk.md) of [Cars](./Vehicle.md)
- Front and Back door of the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md)
- The tunnel door at [Surfeit Trestle](./Surfeit%20Trestle.md) in [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md)
- Front door to the [Headframe Building](./Headframe%20Building.md) in [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md)
- Open or maintain holes in the ice for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) (bladed tools break ice faster, but take more condition loss).
- The elevator doors during the mission [Renewed Hope](./Renewed%20Hope.md) in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) need a Prybar to open.

When carried and selected for self-defense at the start of a Wolf Struggle, Prybar deal low damage with a low chance per-hit to cause the wolf to flee. Prybar are almost as effective at filling the Struggle Meter as the [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), and slightly more effective than the [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md). Prybar take low damage from being used in a struggle. For more information on Struggles, see: [Wildlife Struggles](./Struggle.md).

Prybar are most commonly found in industrial locations, [fishing huts](./Fishing%20Hut.md), [mines](./Langston%20Mine.md), [vehicles](./Car.md) or near [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md). They may be found within frequently tool chests or lockers.

**A small winter bird that gathers in flocks. Can be a source of food, and its Feathers become a useful crafting material.** Official Hinterland Description

**Ptarmigan** are an avian species of prey wildlife found on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). They were introduced in the Part 3: Frontier Comforts update of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), and can only be encountered by players who have bought the expansion pass.

Ptarmigans are small white birds that typically gather in flocks of up to 4-6 members depending on game difficulty, and are a source of both food and down feathers. They are half the size of a Rabbit, and with their snowy white plumage, they are harder to see from a distance. This requires the player to be extra perceptive when attempting to locate a flock as they can usually be found from listening for the loud cooing/clucking sounds they make, rather than line of sight.

Each region contains only a handful of specific areas populated with Ptarmigans, making them an uncommon hunting target. They prefer high altitude locations, and don't appear in the lower altitude coastal regions.

When killed, a [Ptarmigan Carcass](./Ptarmigan%20Carcass.md) can be butchered on the spot or carried whole, similar to a [Rabbit Carcass](./Rabbit%20Carcass.md). A whole bird weighs only slightly more than its meat and down feathers and harvesting is a time consuming process (30 minutes for each bundle). Unlike other animals, Ptarmigans are unique in that they do not drop Hides or Intestines.

Ptarmigan meat is a necessary ingredient in making all stews, as it is the only reliable way of obtaining [Broth](./Broth.md).

Down Feathers are used as a crafting ingredient in improving a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) into an [Improvised Down Bedroll](./Improvised%20Down%20Bedroll.md) or the creation of the [Improvised Insulation](./Improvised%20Insulation.md) accessory.

Ptarmigans behave similar to [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md); slowly wandering around their nests (instead of Rabbit Groves) in small flocks, and they are able to be stunned with a thrown [Stone](./Stone.md). Unlike Rabbits which appear across Great Bear Island, Ptarmigans are only present in non-coastal regions and usually nest at high ground areas. If disturbed they will fly away and not return to the nest area for a time (1-4 days).
- Ptarmigans are generally docile: walking, cooing and pecking around their nesting grounds; they may be heard nearby from their distinctive call.

- If the survivor or a predator alerts them, individual Ptarmigans will run a short distance before taking flight. Once in flight it is still possible to hit a ptarmigan with weapons, though extremely difficult.
- It is possible to shoot a fleeing or even flying Ptarmigans, though difficult. [Revolver](./Revolver.md) shots can be helpful at shooting flying Ptarmigan due to their fast fire rate.
- It is possible (but reckless) to hunt entire Ptarmigan flocks with a well placed [Noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md) if they are bunched together enough, though this tactic is not generally recommended.
- Throwing (RMB) a lit Torch or Flare near Ptarmigans causes the flock to flee. Placing the lit item on the ground will not startle the birds.
- Ptarmigans will ignore a lit [Campfire](./Campfire.md). However they will keep a distance of roughly 2 meters form it.

Ptarmigan Nests are locations that Ptarmigans will always loiter around. They are similar to Rabbit Groves, appearing on the [Map](./Map.md) with a special nest icon after the area is surveyed with [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md). Ptarmigan Nests always spawn 4-6 Ptarmigan at a time, and are found at high altitudes within regions.

**Ptarmigan and their Nests do not spawn in coastal regions** (I.E. [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), [Crumbling Highway](./Crumbling%20Highway.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), and [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)).
- A crouched survivor may approach very close to Ptarmigans, within ~10 meters before they flee.
- Thrown [Torches](./Torch.md) (RMB) will startle ptarmigans. If carrying a lit torch while hunting Ptarmigans, extinguish it or "Drop" it from the Inventory menu instead of throwing.

- Similar to [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md), a thrown [Stones](./Stone.md) will temporarily stun a Ptarmigan if it hits, allowing one from a flock to be caught and "Killed" or "Released". This will alert the remaining flock to flee, as will missed stones.

- Ptarmigan are instantly killed from any type of arrow, notably crafted [Fire Hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md). Killing ptarmigans with arrows will not disturb the flock, allowing multiple birds to be hunted quickly.
- [Wolves](./Wolf.md) as well as [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) and [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) will hunt nearby Ptarmigan. Fleeing wolves will also scare ptarmigans.
- [Bear](./Bear.md), [Moose](./Moose.md) and [Cougar](./Cougar.md) will cause Ptarmigans to flee, but will not hunt them.
- [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) will ignore a Ptarmigan, and mostly vice versa: startled Rabbits will also startle Ptarmigans.
- [The Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) will startle Ptarmigan, and [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) will instantly kill them.
- The Survivor: Ptarmigan will be startled if they detect the survivor (~30m standing, ~10m crouched). They also flee from firearms reports, firearms impacts, thrown items (stones, torches, flares).

- If a Ptarmigan is stunned by a thrown [Stone](./Stone.md), it can be quickly picked up and killed or released. If released, The Survivor will pat the confused Ptarmigan and placing them ground, causing them to flee a moment later.
- A flock right under the three root climbing sections with the rose hip trees leading to the bridge going over [Shattered Cove](./Shattered%20Cove.md).
- A flock near the creek flowing from [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md)/[Mining Camp](./Mining%20Camp.md). It replaces the previous [Rabbit Grove](./Rabbit%20Grove.md).
- A flock between [Foreman's Retreat](./Foreman%27s%20Retreat.md) and the open cave with the bed.

- Between the rope climb at [Cutty's Cave](./Cutty%27s%20Cave.md) and the [Foreman's Clearcut](./Foreman%27s%20Clearcut.md) trailer, there are two rock formations shown on the charcoal map. The first one can have a backpack and has [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md). Exactly in between those two rock formations is where the flock spawns.
- A flock right next to [Whistling Perch](./Whistling%20Perch.md), practically running around the 5 [Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) there.
- A flock at the top of the rope climb next to [Forager's Remnant](./Forager%27s%20Remnant.md), where cat tails and a maple sapling grow.
- At the second transmitting tower facing the [Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), on the ledge overlooking the road leading out of the prison
- Just east of [Bricklayer's Retreat](./Bricklayer%27s%20Retreat.md), on the hill near the [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) spawn and the [Birch sapling](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) spawn.
- Flock right in front of [Rickety Foot Bridge](./Rickety%20Foot%20Bridge.md) (Birch Sapling side).
- A flock can be seen at the [Muskeg Overlook](./Muskeg%20Overlook.md) plateau, where the eastern radio tower stands.
- A flock can be seen at the top of Marsh Ridge, in the path to the right of the cave that leads to the waterfall.
- A flock nests at a small pond within the rocky one way paths leading from beneath the rope climb near [Justy's Hovel](./Justy%27s%20Hovel.md) to the regions exit.
- They are sometimes found in a clearing north of the [Island Cottage](./Island%20Cottage.md), on [Drift Island](./Drift%20Island.md).
- A Flock near a rock Arch, south (straight on the crossing) from the [Many Falls Vista](./Many%20Falls%20Vista.md) climbing site.

- A Flock near the western most cave at the same plateau as [Hushed River](./Hushed%20River.md), reached for example by following the map edge from [Offset Falls](./Offset%20Falls.md) or from the middle entrance to the "North Ice cave".
- A Flock may spawn south-east of the cave near the [Rock Cache Memento,](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Mementos#Hushed_River_Valley) south of Many Falls Vista.
- A Flock may spawn just outside the ice cave which runs along the river south of [Mammoth Falls.](./Mammoth%20Falls.md)
- A flock near [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) near the rocks across from the front door.
- A flock can be seen near the potential [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) above [Dave's Quiet Clearing](./Dave%27s%20Quiet%20Clearing.md).
- A flock can be sighted at the top of the path leading to the Abandoned Lookout & the [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md).
- A flock can be found in the area of [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) near Maple Sapling on the right side.
- A flock near the bridge between the [Point of Disagreement](./Point%20of%20Disagreement.md) and [Derelict Cabins](./Derelict%20Cabins.md), on the left side if going uphill.
- A flock near the hunter's blind near the [Crash Site](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) of the jet airliner.

- A flock scavenges between the rope climb from [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md) and "Cave C"/[Engine](./Engine%20%28East%29.md) on the narrowed ledge near a corpse and/or deer corpse shot with a broken [Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md). You would take this route if traveling to [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) region.

- A flock directly in front of an unnamed cave on the right(east) side of the map. Reached when going towards the [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) transition cave after crossing the "Fallen Tree bridge" bridge over [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md).
- East of [Vacant Depot](./Vacant%20Depot.md), on the edge of the frozen water, before the path going towards [Conductor's Dropoff](./Conductor%27s%20Dropoff.md).
- On a ridge south west of [Loitering Marsh](./Loitering%20Marsh.md), right on the edge of the marsh.
- Due west of [Vacant Depot](./Vacant%20Depot.md), near the far western edge of the map.
- At [Boss's Settlement](./Boss%27s%20Settlement.md), between the two main destroyed cabins
- Along a one-way passage leading from the [Miner's Footpath](./Miner%27s%20Footpath.md) through the northwestern mountains to the [Indolent Hoppers](./Indolent%20Hoppers.md)

- Ptarmigan appears to be based on the winter plumage of the [Willow Ptarmigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willow_ptarmigan) (**_Lagopus lagopus_**), a species of Galliformes identifiable by its red crest above the eye and changing feather colors that match the seasons.
- The correct plural pronounciation of Ptarmigan is either Ptarmigan or Ptarmigans (similar to Fish or Fishes).

- Ptarmigan are also the Nunavut’s official bird, one of symbol for the territorial heritage of north-east Canada. ([official source here](https://www.canada.ca/en/canadian-heritage/services/provincial-territorial-symbols-canada/nunavut.html))

**Pumpkin Pie** is a seasonal [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item available only during the Halloween events [4 Days of Night Event](./4%20Days%20of%20Night%20Event.md) and the [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) (2020 event version). It is currently unable to be accessed (even in the current version of Escape the Darkwalker Challenge) and is considered [Cut/Discontinued Content](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md).
The Pumpkin Pie is still found in the game files in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), but cannot be accessed through normal means.

Consuming a Pumpkin Pie grants up to 2000 [calories](./Hunger.md) for 0.50 kg of weight, making it even more efficient than the rare [MRE](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md) (1750 calories). Pumpkin Pies additionally grant a [Wildlife Repelling Effect](./Afflictions.md), frightening nearby [Demon Wolves](./Wolf.md), as well as constantly being "hot" so its consumption can warm the survivor.
If found during the [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) event, the Darkwalker will refuse to pursue the player for a time when the Pie is consumed.

It has a constant [Hot](./Warming%20Up.md) attribute, which grants [Warmth](./Warmth.md) even when eating small amounts of the pie. This allows a survivor to keep warm for extended periods of time, preventing [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md) by keeping Warmth above zero. The amount of warmth gained is proportional to the amount of pie eaten (and calories consumed).
An intact pie can restore the [Warmth](./Warmth.md) of the survivor from freezing (0%) to full (100%) once.

The "Wildlife Repelling Effect" Benefit is granted to the survivor upon consuming a Pumpkin Pie, which causes nearby Demon Wolves to flee upon detecting them. This effect is similar to that of Pilgrim game mode.
If the effect is obtained while a Wolf is charging the survivor, there is no effect for that Wolf, resulting in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md).

If consumed while the Darkwalker is chasing the player, the entity will stay away from them for some time, similar to using a [Spray Paint - Glyph](./Spray%20Paint%20-%20Glyph.md) to create a Ward/standing near a Green Fire.

Pumpkin Pies spawn inside major structures such as the [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md). Their spawns are not guaranteed, but multiple pies can spawn in the same Region. Pies found usually spawn atop stoves.

The **Quilted Bed** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) and [Bed](./Bed.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.

A makeshift wooden bed with bedsheets made from sewn together pieces of cloth, a Quilted Bed can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).
This bed can be [Slept](./Sleep.md) in and gives a [Warmth](./Warmth.md) bonus of +6 °C (+10.8 °F).

- This is warmer than most beds found across the Island, with the only other warmer beds being a Full bed found in some houses (+ 8 °C ( +14.4 °F ) and the [Bear Hide Bed](./Bear%20Hide%20Bed.md) (+10 °C (+18 °F).
- The tradeoff is that it is slightly more material/time consuming to build compared to a [Rustic Bed](./Rustic%20Bed.md).

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The bed can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value, the bed cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the bed will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).

Quonset Garage is located along the main highway in Coastal Highway. It is one of the best candidates for a safe house in Coastal Highway. Inside there are two crafting benches, 1 fire barrel, and a bed. Lots of storage is available in the garage including 5 lockers (2 in a bathroom, 3 in a room with a bed) and various desks and toolboxes. Notable loots include soda cans and energy bars in the shop area, providing a day or so of food. A toilet provides a fair amount of potable water. A basin can be found on one of the workbenches, but it has a chance of holding [non-potable water](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md). Often, many tools will spawn inside, usually hidden in a corner. You may find a [Firestriker](./Firestriker.md) or [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) hidden behind wooden crates. Just a few meters from the main entrance is one of the [Radios](./Trader.md#Radio_Locations) necessary to contact the Trader (if enabled).
A [Basin](./Basin.md) can be found on a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), the only one of its kind in the game. A [Polaroid](./Polaroids.md) can also be found inside sometimes.

As the garage has two [workbenches](./Work%20Bench.md) and only one can be used at a time, it is often a good idea to [disassemble one](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) and use its [vise](./Workbench%20Vice.md) to build a new workbench in a location that doesn't have one, especially if you plan on turning said location into a [Safehouse](./Safehouse.md).

The garage has many advantages as a safe house. Inside you will find ample storage space, a fire barrel, two workbenches, and a bed. Its centralized location means many houses are within a quick walk's distance, and provide a good source of cloth, food, and firewood. It should be noted that outside the garage bears, wolves, and moose can sometimes patrol so caution is advised when exiting the building. In Stalker difficulty, this can be a real danger as most of the time a wolf will attack you on sight. If you do not kill some wolves, you will eventually find yourself locked inside the garage with three to four wolves surrounding the building. Once you kill all the wolves in the area, however, the garage is a good safe house as they won't spawn until a few days have gone.
- During an aurora, the lights on the sign are the only example of a neon sign on the whole island.
- The garage intially didn't have gas pumps outside when first added to the game. Eventually, two were added. Later, one of the gas pumps was changed to an electric charging station.

**Rabbits** are small animals found scattered throughout the wilderness, either alone or in groups of two to four. They can be found in all main regions as well as in some transition zones.
These skittish animals are easily spotted due to their greyish-brown color and nearly constant movement. They are abundant in all regions and may be caught in [snares](./Snare.md).

Their meat is the same weight as raw venison despite providing just over half the calories per kilogram, making it one of the worst calories per kilogram ratios in the game (though it can be a relatively sustainable food source). Rabbits provide 0.75 to 1.5 kg of [meat](./Rabbit%20%28Raw%29.md), one [pelt](./Fresh%20Rabbit%20Pelt.md), and one [gut](./Fresh%20Gut.md) when harvested. Their pelts may be crafted into warm [Rabbitskin Mitts](./Rabbitskin%20Mitts.md) or [Rabbitskin Hat](./Rabbitskin%20Hat.md) at a work bench. [Wolves](./Wolf.md) frequently hunt rabbits.
When killed, a [Rabbit Carcass](./Rabbit%20Carcass.md) can be butchered on the spot or carried whole, similar to a [Ptarmigan Carcass](./Ptarmigan%20Carcass.md).

Rabbits have two behaviours: roaming and fleeing. A Rabbit's natural behavior is to simply wander aimlessly about in the wilderness in fixed locations called Rabbit Groves. While roaming, they will occasionally stop and listen for predators while occasionally cleaning their ears, or sprint away if they detect a threat. Rabbits that run away from their Rabbit Grove will always wander back to it after a short time.

Rabbits are completely silent aside from their very faint footsteps, simply running away if they detect a thrown Stone, Firearm report, or the player when they get too close. They do however let out various a cries under certain circumstances. They will cry in pain if they are stunned by a thrown Stone, or will give out a death cry if killed by a projectile, or by a Wolf. They also let a high-pitched screech of fear when a wolf/bear gets close to them, and will instantly run away to safety, often much farther from their designated Rabbit Grove than if the player startles them.

Rabbit Groves are fixed spawn locations for Rabbits and display their own special icon on the [Map](./Map.md) once surveyed with [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md). Snares placed here will always yield a Rabbit Carcass if given enough time and checked regularly. Rabbits roam around Rabbit Groves in groups of 1-4, except during Blizzards and Auroras. Rabbits can occasionally be found in areas not labeled with a Rabbit Grove, and Snares will not work here.

If a [Wolf](./Wolf.md)/[Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md)/[Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) detects a Rabbit, it will pursue the rabbit for a time before eventually outrunning it, killing, and then eating it. Once a wolf has killed a rabbit, it will rapidly consume the carcass, depleting its resources. When the wolf has fully depleted the rabbit's resources, it will wander off. Before this point, a wolf may be frightened from the carcass [through typical means](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Wolf#Interaction), and the rabbit carcass may be retrieved.
Timberwolves still part of a wolf pack that kill a rabbit and spot the player will instantly engage the player, leaving the carcass behind.
Rabbits have minimal interaction with other animals, besides being eaten by wolves and being scared off by the player.
- Other Rabbits will generally stay close to one another, but will run away if another Rabbit is startled/attacked. They can both squeal in terror if scared.

- [Wolf](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md), [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) will stalk and eat a Rabbit if they get the chance. Rabbits always let out a high pitched squeal and run away from a Wolf.
- [Bear](./Bear.md), [Moose](./Moose.md), and [Cougar](./Cougar.md), will not attack a Rabbit, but Rabbits still run away squealing in terror when close to one.
- [Deer](./Deer.md) will ignore Rabbits, and vice versa. If a Deer is startled, Rabbits silently run away from the area.
- [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) will ignore a Rabbit, and vice versa for the most part. If a Rabbit is startled by another animal and runs past a Ptarmigan, the Ptarmigan will run and fly away.

- [Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md): Rabbits will run and squeal in fear if the Darkwalker gets too close to them. [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) will eventually kill all animals if it builds up enough.

- The Player: Rabbits quietly run away from the player without squealing. If a rabbit is stunned by a thrown [Stone](./Stone.md), the player can quickly pick up the rabbit and must choose to either kill it by breaking its neck or to release it
- If the player kills the rabbit, they will struggle in fear as their neck is broken.
- If they are released, the survivor will pat the confused Rabbit on the head before placing it on the ground. The Rabbit will then run away before returning to their designated area.

- Rabbits will also be caught in and killed by snares set by the player in rabbit-dense areas, as long as the snare has not been destroyed by predators or poor weather conditions, in which they just spawn dead.

![A dead rabbit, caught in a snare.](../assets/Caught_Rabbit.png)_A dead rabbit, caught in a snare._ Due to their small size and quick movement, precision is required to [hunt](./Hunting.md) rabbits. A single hit with a [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md), [Fire Hardened Arrow](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md), [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) round, or [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md) round will instantly kill a rabbit, whereas a [Stone](./Stone.md) will stun it for 5 seconds. Once stunned, the Rabbit can be collected to either release the animal or kill it; killing the rabbit will provide its harvestable carcass as an item in the inventory.

[Trapping](./Trapping.md) with crafted [snares](./Snare.md) is a passive way to hunt rabbits. To use a snare, it must be placed (not merely dropped) inside of a Rabbit Grove. Rabbits may still be captured by a placed snare in a grove, even if no rabbits are currently spawned. Deployed snares in a grove may catch a rabbit, fail to catch, or even become ruined. Rabbit carcasses caught by snares will decay over time, disappearing when they reach 0% condition.

- Using the [stones](./Stone.md) scattered around the area is an immediate and effective way of hunting rabbits. Throwing a stone and hitting a rabbit will briefly stun it, allowing a chance to catch and kill the rabbit. If not caught 5 seconds after being stunned, the rabbit will recover and flee. Stones follow an arcing trajectory, which begins just above the survivor's thumb in aim mode.
- Crouching or approaching from behind is effective at closing the distance on a rabbit. However, they cannot be picked up this way, and must be stunned first.

- Shooting rabbits with firearms or Simple Arrows is possible but not recommended, as they are small and skittish targets. Even if a round lands, it will have spent a bullet or ~25% condition on an arrow. These are finite, precious resources, whereas stones are plentiful and durable. An alternative method is to use [Fire Hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) since they are designed to be expendable but easily replaceable, and can be fired from father distances than stones.

- Rabbits can be herded toward [wolves](./Wolf.md), who will quickly kill them. Once a wolf kills the rabbit, the wolf can be frightened from its kill, allowing the carcass to be retrieved. Thrown stones, torches, or flares are effective at scaring off wolves.

- Rabbits and Deer can be flushed by intentionally scaring them in a direction, which can be used to distract wolves (e.g. bypassing a wolf blocking the way, or checking to see if a wolf is in an area).
- When sprinting, the survivor runs faster than a rabbit (provided the survivor is not over-encumbered).

- Rabbits appear to be based off the [Cottontailed Rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cottontail_rabbit) (**_Lepus sylvaticus_**), a species of Lagamorphia found throughout North and Central America.
- [Enviro] Rabbits will no longer climb on the broken fishing hut, in the Main Menu.
- [General] Fixed a crash that could occur if a Stag or Rabbit was removed from the world, while being chased by a Predator.
- [All] Fixed rare issue that would cause players to become stuck if grabbing a Rabbit while holding a gear item from their Backpack.
- [All] Improved aiming mechanics for thrown Stones, to make Rabbit Hunting a bit easier.
- [All] Fixed condition that could result in the the player becoming stuck when picking up a stunned Rabbit
- Fixed locked controls when throwing a stone and picking up a rabbit at the same time
- Fixed issue with being able to place snares too close to geometry, causing the snared rabbit to be inaccessible

- All wildlife spawns are now more dynamic, and will change over the course of a game. Wolves, Deer, and Rabbits all refresh on different intervals, reflecting their relative mobility and travel/migration patterns.

> “**Handcrafted mitts. They may make you clumsy, but they're very warm. Kind of like wearing a rabbit on your hands.**”

Rabbitskin Mitts are very warm and windproof crafted gloves. They can be manufactured by killing rabbits, by using thrown [stones](./Stone.md) to stun them, or [snares](./Snare.md) to capture them the next day.

They are significantly warmer and more durable than most other gloves, only competed with by the [Gauntlets](./Gauntlets.md), which provide similar warmth-to-weight, with higher protection and better mobility. However, mitts are more durable, waterproof, and can be repaired more sustainably.
In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), their blueprint is unlocked by snaring a rabbit in [The Basics of Survival](./The%20Basics%20of%20Survival.md) quest.

As of the [TFTFT part 4 update](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), a pair of Rabbitskin mittens may spawn in the control room in the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md), near the [Miner's Flashlight](./Miner%27s%20Flashlight.md).

The **Radial Menu** is a feature added in the Tireless Menace Update and was redesigned in the Faithful Cartographer update. Its function is to be a quick, alternative way to select items in your inventory, without having to open the Backpack and manually search for them. With the standard keyboard bindings on PC, the Radial Menu is opened by holding _SPACE_. Most items that cannot be used to interact with the game world will not appear in the Radial Menu.

If a player has too many Weapons, Light Sources, Food, Drinks, and First Aid items, they can sometimes not appear in the wheel menus, as there is only room for 8 items at a time. They can be manually added to the menus by opening the Backpack, clicking on the item, and selecting "Add to Radial." Any item selected in the Radial Menu that can be taken from the Backpack can either be consumed, equipped, or placed in the game world.
By default, the PC keys 1, 2, 3, and 4 can be used to bypass having to manually select items from the Radial Menu.
- 3 drops 1 piece of cooked or raw meat/1 [Fresh Gut](./Fresh%20Gut.md) in the player's inventory onto the ground ([Drop Decoys](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys))

Generally, Light Sources in the player's inventory selected with the 1 key will cycle in the following order: Miner's Flashlight, Flashlight, Flare, Marine Flare, Storm Lantern, Spelunker's Lantern, Torch, Matches.
- [Revolver](./Revolver.md) ([Forester's Revolver](./Forester%27s%20Revolver.md), [Hunter's Revolver](./Hunter%27s%20Revolver.md), [Warden's Revolver](./Warden%27s%20Revolver.md))
- [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) ([Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md), [Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md), [Barb's Rifle](./Barb%27s%20Rifle.md))
- [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) ([Woodwright's Bow](./Woodwright%27s%20Bow.md), [Sport Bow](./Sport%20Bow.md))

Generally, weapons in the player's inventory selected with the 2 key will cycle in the following order: Hunter's Revolver, Revolver, Warden's Revolver, Forester's Revolver, Barb's Rifle, Vaughn's Rifle, Curator's Rifle, Hunting Rifle, Survival Bow, Sport Bow, Woodwright's Bow, Distress Pistol, Stone, Noisemaker.
Drop Decoys will access any raw or cooked meat in the player's inventory and allows them to instantly drop these items on the ground for the purposes of [Baiting](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys).

Has an interior **Radio Control Hut** is a location found in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) on the [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md) plateau. It can easily be found by looking for the large red-and-white transmitter standing next to it and makes it one of the easiest landmarks to identify in the region.

The Radio Control Hut can only be accessed at first by going through the [Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md). Once the location has been reached once, a rope can be deployed at the [Pensive Lookout](./Pensive%20Lookout.md) standing on the same plateau. This makes the location accessible from the Bleak Inlet region itself. The mountaineering rope that the player deploys is the only way to go from Bleak Inlet to the plateau in general, and Radio Control Hut in general, making it a risky destination if the Survivor isn't in the best condition.

The Radio Control Hut is arguably the most remote location in the region, being not only in a place that has a single point of entry upon first arriving in the region, but also standing at the very end of the plateau area. To reach the Radio Control Hut, the Survivor needs to pass the Lookout, which is patrolled by a pack of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), then walk by a parking lot (that contains both a [Memento](./Mementos.md) as well as some more wolves) then cross a wooden bridge high above the inlet to finally reach the Control Hut itself.

The Radio Control Hut is a standard location when it comes to loot, containing only a handful of items even on the lowest of difficulties. Some notable features includes a [Medical Locker](./Medical%20Locker.md), a rare find, as well as all three types of [Camera](./Camera.md) FastFilm. On one of the desks in the first room, the player will be able to get the [Communication Report](./Communication%20Report.md) collectible, a memo that contains the access keycode to the [Workshop](./Workshop.md) at the [Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md). Picking up the memo will automatically save the keycode and input it when the player reaches the Workshop.

While the Radio Control Hut can technically be considered a safehouse, it is by far the worst choice a player could make. The Control Hut should be viewed as nothing more than a one-night pit stop to regain Condition and Stamina and ensure a safe climb down the Lookout deployed rope. It has no crafting area, no protected fire (neither fireplace nor firepit), no bed of any kind and is located in the single most remote area of the map. It contains:

**Description:** A section of isolated railway running from a southern maintenance yard near Perseverance Mills all the way to a SAR station on the northern coast.

The **Railway** (or **Railway Region**) is one of the regions added to [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md). It does not have a connection to any other region directly, though it can be inferred it is accessed through the inaccessible Perseverance Mill located in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md). It is said to be north of [Desperation Bay](./Desperation%20Bay.md), along the coastline, possibly making it the northern most region currently in Wintermute.

The region consists of a set of massive ravines and valleys, which a portion of the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) cuts through. The line connects a Maintenance Shed on the southern edge to the SAR Station at the northern edge. Between the maintenance depot and the SAR station, the line splits into two branches at the Rail Junction. Along the branches there are two sidings and two yards, where some shunting and switching is required, alongside a duo of bridges over a fast-flowing river. The line terminates at the SAR station to the north, which features the Wye Track to turn the engine around. The region has an abundance of [coal](./Coal.md), both in [coal bins](./Coal%20Bin.md) and in caves, which is necessary to fuel the [Steam Train](./Steam%20Train.md). Many of the railyards feature one to four [wolves](./Wolf.md), which can be temporarily scared away using the locomotive's whistle.

It is impossible to travel the length of the region without the use of the Steam Locomotive, as the tracks are blocked by fences in several places, requiring you to bash them open with the Steam Locomotive.

The main yard you spawn at, implied to be past the small yard within the Mill at [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md). Previously accessed by a small road, possibly linked to the road at the Depot. A trailer can be found at the northern edge, alongside a lot of old industrial equipment scattered around.

A two story shed with space for one railcar inside, currently occupied by a flatbed. A small break room, locker room with attached bathroom, office space, workshop, and store room can be found inside, along with the main area for repairs. The [Throttle](./Steam%20Train.md) can be found on the first floor workshop, and the [Piece of Paper](./Piece%20of%20Paper%20%282%29.md) with an [Emegrency Kit](./Emergency%20Kit.md) in the second floor office.
First set of switches encountered. A small platform with a coal bin can be found on the leftmost track, and corpse next to a campfire can be found near a small cave on the left side.
A tunnel passed through. A large pile of snow blocks the entrance, requiring you to speed up and bash through it.
A small wooden bridge crossing the region's river, with a gate blocking the southern side.

A collapsed tunnel segment, heading deeper into Great Bear Island. The interior of the tunnel can be accessed, with a broken wall revealing a cave you can travel through for extra coal. Simply push the flatbed car off of the switching track before reversing, swapping the direction from Left to Right, and then proceeding down the main line.

A large Yard and Junction in the line, featuring a Coal Filling station, a small covered garage, and an abandoned Trailer. The [truck](./Truck.md) parked at the garage can be entered, with a [Prybar](./Prybar.md) and [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md) spawning on a table. You pass through here two times, once heading to the SAR Station, and the other returning to the shed.

The line terminates in this region, which formerly was home to a Depot, Parking Lot, and a tunnel which has collapsed. A road formerly led through the region, though it's become impassable due to avalanches on each end.
Situated on a hill above the Depot and Wye track, The [Trauma Kit](./Trauma%20Kit.md) can be found in the [Medical Helicopter](./Helicopter.md) left on the helipad, with the Bloodied Note beside it.
A second small wooden bridge crossing the region's river, used on the return trip. Both ends are blocked by fencing.

- There is an unused transition between the Railway and Perseverance Mills behind the chain-link fence. This leads behind the sawmill, and is accessible by [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md) along the cliff walls. It is theorized that, in earlier versions, it was intended for Heller and Astrid to physically walk from Perserverance Mills to the Railway.

- Some locations, much like the rest of Episode 5, reuse assets from [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), such as the coal tower from [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) at the Rail Junction, and the Helicopter from [Final Approach](./Final%20Approach.md) at the SAR Station.
- Corpses can be found at many points, including the Train Maintenance Yard, the Depot, and the SAR Station.

**Rainbow Trout (Cooked)** is a [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.

Rainbow Trout are small saltwater fish found commonly under the ice off the coast. They can be caught by [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) using [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md). Rainbow Trout can be between 0.5 and 2.3 kg raw.
At 0% condition food disappears if inside of a container, but not outside of containers or in the player's inventory.

Cooking trout takes 10 minutes and is obtained by using a lit [Fire](./Fire.md). Cooking increases it's condition by 50%, decays 4 times slower than raw meat, has a reduced chance of [Food Poisoning](./Afflictions.md) over raw meat, and decreases its weigh by 35%. Cooked trout's energy density is 385 calories-per-kilogram. Cooking fish also yields a small amount of [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md).

Cooking trout improves the [Cooking Skill](./Skills.md#Cooking). Using a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) reduces cooking time by 25%. Cooked food on an active fire for too long will burn (twice its 'Ready' cooking time), destroying the item and damaging a Cooking Pot if used.

Cooking trout improves the [cooking skill](./Skills.md#Cooking). Using a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) reduces cooking time by 25%. Cooked food on an active fire for too long will burn (twice its 'Ready' cooking time), destroying the item and damaging a Cooking Pot if used.

**Ranger Stew** is a food item in _The Long Dark_, it is learned from a unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) and is made with a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md).

In order to craft this item, the player must visit the [Foreman's Retreat](./Foreman%27s%20Retreat.md) in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md). It can only be created once its [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) is found. It can spawn in various locations within the first room of the cabin near the kitchenette.
Ranger Stew produces a [Scent](./Scent.md) which attracts [predators](./Wolf.md), and may be dropped as a [decoy](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys).

Ranger Stew is much lighter than the ingredients that go into making it, with the meat alone being over double the weight of the finished stew. As [carrots](./Carrot.md) and [potatoes](./Potato.md) are generally rather easy to find, this makes it one of the easier foods to cook in the game. Its increased fatigue, together with instant condition recovery and improved rest, make it best suited for consumption at the end of a long day.
- 3 hours of [Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md) (+1% Condition restored for first 3 hours of sleep, or 18 hours)

Has no shelter The **Ravine Basin** is a location found in [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md) transition zone. The location is found in the center of the region, and can only be reached via a [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md), which always requires a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) (often found in one of the region's caves). The Basin is one way to reach [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), and the only way to reach Bleak Inlet's upper mountain area.

The basin is only reachable by climbing down the Rope Climbing section. At the bottom of the Rope Climb is a crashed [Train Shuttle](./Train%20Shuttle.md), often containing a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md), a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) box with [Flare Shells](./Flare%20Shell.md), and other supplies.

Further down stream, a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) is found near a small frozen pond that contains a [Tuffet](./Bed.md) bed, also a tree limb inside. A ravaged [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md) is always found near the cave entrance. A [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) grove and several [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md) plants are located around the cave. [Sticks](./Stick.md) and [Cedar Limbs](./Cedar%20Limb.md) can be used for fuel.
