violations.context: **Contents**
> “**We're more interested in making the game compelling, than we are in making it realistic. When the two are compatible, we embrace both.**”

In _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, besides the core survival [mechanics](./Needs.md) there are also anomalies created by [geomagnetic disaster](./First%20Flare.md) which immerse the player to alternate reality. The game stays true to this fiction and therefore is realistic in the merit of it. Some other aspects of the game can also be considered realistic because the game communicates realism to the player through computer interface and so most of the game mechanics has to be specific - like the [Condition Bar](./Condition.md) that represents player's health from 0 to 100%.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: **Minor SPOILER ALERT**

This game is constantly tuned to create interesting gameplay and not to conform to real-world expectations. Thus a new player could, after reading this article, be less surprised of the way things work in game both in possibly a positive or a negative way - depending on the type of player.

The core gameplay in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ can be said to be based on the lowest level of Maslow's hierarchy of needs - food, water, warmth and rest. Other needs, such as [safety](./Safehouse.md) and love needs (only [story](./Wintermute.md) mode), are not directly measured in the game's interface (with exception of somewhat related to love - trust in the story mode) but instead meant for the player to experience individually. The deprivation of the measured needs leads to the player loosing overall Condition and ultimately death. Both the basic 4 needs as well as condition directly can be affected by many [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md).
- There is currently no mechanic that would let the player partly satisfy his [Warmth](./Warmth.md) need by moving or shivering (movement does however affect calorie burn and [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md))

- The player can die of starvation in about 4 game days if all other needs are satisfied (which could mean that the game simply does not include the mechanic which lets human body break down its proteins and fat)
- Drinking water to satisfy the thirst need from toilet bowls does not carry any risk of [Dysentery](./Dysentery.md) or [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md).

The game's environment graphics were created by choice to be of artistic style instead of photorealistic. The Long Dark environment features such realistic features as rising and setting sun and moon, wind that affects the player and fires, snow that can make clothes wet, fog that limits visibility for both the player and wildlife.

- Some players noticed that, more often than it would occur naturally, the wind changes direction to oppose the player's movement or blow out fires that are protected from the wind. Whether or not this is actually true remains a speculation.

- Not all water surfaces freezes even in very low temperatures resulting in constant weak ice in some areas. Note also that the player can fall through weak ice where at the same exact place heavier than player [bears](./Bear.md) and other animals do not fall through.

The Long Dark is set in a universe after huge [geomagnetic disaster](./Aurora.md) with some of after effects still felt in the present game time. There also apparently have been major earthquakes which rendered roads and railroads collapsed and useless. This said universe is different from the real world in the following ways:
- Most electronics function during an aurora event - lights flicker, computers display emails. Otherwise, without an aurora, they are useless.

![Normal flare. It lasts for 5 real-time minutes](../assets/Flare.jpeg)_Normal flare. It lasts for 5 real-time minutes_ The time in game runs 12 times faster than real time. The game developers were therefore at liberty to decide if some actions should run in real-time, game-time or somewhere in between (because it does not break immersion either way).
- Time of day changes according to game-time (and is one of the biggest selling points of the game)
- [Fire](./Fire.md) duration adhere to game-time (note also that having the same wood, fires last longer outdoors instead of indoors)

- [Flare](./Flare.md)'s burn time relates to the real time (5min of real time for a normal flare and 2.5min for a [marine flare](./Marine%20Flare.md)) obviously because 1min burn time of a typical real world flare converted to the game time would constitute only 5 seconds of the real time.

- [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md)'s burn time relates to game-time - fully refueled it burns for about 4 game hours. Note however that fuel efficiency of a storm lantern is at least 10x less efficient than real world equivalent even when measured in game-time.
- [Warmth](./Warmth.md) depletion for the player appears to be more related to game-time (however it varies by difficulty level so it can also be somewhere in between on the lowest difficulty)

- [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) is tightly tied with game-time as from it the possibility to sleep is derived (note also that there is no problem of falling asleep even right after 8-hour sleep night, as long as the player has some fatigue left).

- The [decay](./Decay.md) of food and clothes is mostly even faster than game-time but it varies by the level of difficulty chosen (in Pilgrim mode things decay somewhat realistically when measured in game-time). Note that frozen meat even in very low temperatures and low difficulty levels [decays](./Decay.md) in a matter of days.

Time can be further accelerated by engaging in activities such as chopping wood, fishing, repairing, crafting, forging, sleeping or just passing time. Eating is almost instant - it takes only very little time whether measured by game-time or real-time. In Custom Mode - time can be set to run slower, but there is no way to make the time run at real-time.
- Drinking drugs or medicinal teas will have immediate affect and will only apply to the area specified by the player (not to the whole body).
- After the player's [warmth](./Warmth.md) bar empties - he begins to loose condition at a specific constant rate regardless of temperature that surrounds him.

- All of afflictions end abruptly. For example, when [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md) effect expires the player immediately looses some of his feel like temperature (note that the player cannot get warming up effect from drinking hot water, only hot teas)

- Temperatures of all inside locations are constant (it does not change in any way with surrounding weather changing) and will only have its temperature temporary increased while a fire is going inside of it. Once the last embers are gone - the temperature will drop to predefined constant (it will not maintain heat accumulated from the fire in the air or walls). Note also that embers take only a few game-time minutes to completely burn out.
Notable exception is carrying capacity lost due to [fatigue](./Fatigue.md). The two are somewhat gradually related.
The player can acquire skills that speed up or make some actions more efficient. In addition some skill levels appear to somewhat change in-game reality instead of affecting only the player himself:

- The animal bleed out times are reduced depending on the skill level of [Archery](./Archery.md) (one might argue however that the wounds inflicted by a skilled archer are greater). Note also that bleeding from more than one wound doesn't stack, in other words it would be the same if animals bled only from the latest wound.
- The player can harvest 100% frozen carcass by hand (without any tool) when reached [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) level 5.

- The player can safely eat meat without the risk of [intestinal parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) or [food poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) when [level 5 cooking](./Cooking.md) is achieved (even if the food was prepared before the player got the skill, which therefore some players jokingly call an eating skill). Also a player with higher cooking skill gets more calories from any cooked item.

- The fires last longer depending on [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) skill while other factors are equal. Also note that with any skill level it is possible to light a fire with [magnifying lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) in a shadow (of a building, cliff etc.).
- The player catches more fish within the same time depending on [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) skill (despite the equipment being the same).
- The damage from rifle shots is increased with [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) skill, same with [Revolver Firearm](./Revolver%20Firearm.md) skill.
- Even with highest [sharpening](./Sharpening.md) skill, [whetstone](./Whetstone.md) can be used to sharpen tools for only about 20 times before rendered useless.

- Reclaimed wood can be found inside and near buildings, fishing huts, or by harvesting crates, shelves, tables, chairs and etc. with a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md), or [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md). Small wooden items may be broken down with bare hands, expending more calories and taking more time however.

- Reclaimed Wood and [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) are efficient sources of fuel per weight, at 120 min/kg. Since pieces of Reclaimed Wood are smaller than Cedar Firewood, they give more control of a fire's duration, allowing more efficient fuel without waste.
- A single piece of Reclaimed Wood will heat a canned food or drink without it burning, as the fire will extinguish 10-20 minutes after the food or drink is done.
- Every interior location now has a maximum inventory of Reclaimed Wood that can be Foraged.
- Fuel Sources: Increased the heating radius of Hardwood, Softwood, and Reclaimed Wood fuel types.
- It is now possible to forage for Wood indoors. Indoor foraging only produces Reclaimed Wood.

- Tuned all Fuel sources. Hardwood, Softwood, and Reclaimed wood all now have reduced burn times, but are also lighter to carry. Wood Foraging has been tuned to be more generous. Net result is Fuel is easier to find and carry, but you need more of it.

A **Recovery Backpack** is a stationary interactable object in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md). It only spawns when the player decides to [Cheat Death](./Cheat%20Death.md) in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

If the player dies and decides to continue their save file then most of their items will remain on their person, but many of their items will disappear from their inventory. A Recovery Backpack will appear in set spawn location in the [Region](./Region.md) they died in to hold these lost items as a punishment for Cheating Death. Checking the local Region map will reveal the location of the Backpack, represented by a Campfire icon.

When the player finds their Recovery Backpack, a small Campfire will always be found nearby, and a small smokestack will appear rising from the Campfire as if it burned out the moment the player arrived (as if another survivor looted your belongings shortly before arriving). A majority of the player's previous items will be found in the Recovery Backpack itself, but some of your lost items may be scattered around the Recovery Backpack when it is found, and will decay as normal in the game world until Ruined (if applicable, such as clothing or food) if the player takes too long to arrive. It is possible that some of the player's less critical items (food, clothing, etc) will be lost forever or in low/ruined condition when the Recovery Backpack is rediscovered. The Campfire always found nearby can be lit like a normal Campfire.
It is currently unknown if Experience difficulty affects the rate or priority of how items/tools are lost or which items appear outside of the backpack.
If the player dies a second time and Cheats Death before recovering the first Recovery Backpack, a second new Recovery Backpack will appear in the game world and override the first Recovery Backpack:
- This will cause the first Backpack to disappear from the previous region along with any items inside. (save for anything that was scattered on the ground around it).
- Items will be permanently lost if the player again dies and Cheats Death before the previous Recovery Backpack is reclaimed.

- Choosing to respawn via the "close but risky respawn" option to quickly obtain your items from the Recovery Backpack can be a gamble, and will most likely result in the player dying if they are unfamiliar with the local Region they last died in. The player will also often spawn at night with low condition clothing, possibly freezing to death in the dark. Keep this in mind.

- It is entirely possible to lose rare or unique one of a kind items if you did not reclaim your first Recovery Backpack (such as [Tactical Gloves](./Tactical%20Gloves.md), [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md), etc). Make it a priority to recover your items to avoid this.

A **Recycled Can** is a tool that players used primarily for melting snow, boiling water, and cooking [canned goods](./Cooking.md#Canned) and [drinks](./Cooking.md#Drinks).

The player will always start the game with one recycled can in the inventory, even on Interloper. Additional Recycled Cans are obtained by the player after consuming a [canned good](./Cooking.md#Canned). However, if the player smashes open a can, they will not receive a Recycled Can once the food is consumed. Additionally, Recycled Cans occasionally spawn in houses with kitchens or in various other locations.

A Recycled Can will decrease the amount of time required for canned food to cook by **50%**, compared to the time needed to cook indirectly near the [Fire](./Fire.md). This time can be decreased by an additional **20%** if the player uses a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) instead of a Recycled Can. A [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md) can decrease cooking times even more than a Recycled can as well.
A Recycled Can can melt or boil up to 0.5 liters (0.13 gallons) of snow or water at a time. A Cooking Pot has four times the capacity (2L / 0.52 gallons) and melts/boils **20%** faster.
A Recycled Can will degrade by **10%** if its contents are burned or boiled dry. The Recycled Can will not degrade in any other circumstances.
The following items produced a Recycled Can once the contents are consumed and the can is not smashed opened.
| [Noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md) | None | - 1 × [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) - 1 × [Cloth](./Cloth.md) - 0.10 kg × [Can of Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md) |
- All [Fires](./Fire.md) have the same cooking, boiling, and melting times for food and drink items used with a Recycled Can. The cooking speed is not dependent on the temperature of the fire.
- Using a Recycled Can will not decrease the amount of time required to cook canned food, compared to cooking the food in its own can.
- You can only use two Recycled Cans, Cooking Pots/Skillets at a time on most cooking surfaces, but stoves have six slots.
- On Interloper, the Recycled Can is the only item you start with, besides some basic clothing.
- Recycled Cans can be used for shooting practice, as they will be knocked back from the impact of a bullet/arrow.
- [Audio] Cans and Pots now play sound effects when placed onto a cooking slot, as intended.
- [All] Fixed players being able to use a Recycled Can/Cooking Pot to cook when the item was at 0% Condition.

![A fanmade map of all Regions on Great Bear Island.](../assets/GREAT_BEAR_ISLAND_MAP_Fan_made.jpg)_A fanmade map of all Regions on Great Bear Island._ A **Region** is a large, explorable outdoor area that encompasses many discoverable locations.

All regions are located on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) and [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) in northern [Canada](./The%20Collapse.md). Each of the regions connects to at least one other region, either directly or by a smaller Transition Zone.

In most difficulty levels of [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), the player may select any region as the starting point or may choose to start in a random region. Only Regions that have been visited in game will appear when initially selecting a starting location, otherwise, only beginner locations are accessible at first.

If the Interloper experience is selected, then the starting region will be randomly chosen from more challenging maps. In Interloper, the player will not spawn in Mountain Town, Mystery Lake, or Coastal Highway, and the number of possible spawn locations within each possible region is limited.
In the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), the starting location is always the same and the player is restricted in what regions they can visit.

- [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) takes place entirely in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md). Once the main quest is completed, the player acquires means to proceed away from this region into Mystery Lake, which triggers the beginning of Episode 2.

- [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) mostly takes place in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md), however the player has to also travel to [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) to progress the main quest. It is not possible to return to Mountain Town (Milton) once Episode 2 starts.

- [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) takes place in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) and ends in the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) (the final cutscene takes place in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), though it is not playable).

- [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) takes place in [Blackrock Region](./Blackrock.md), with the opening of the episode taking place in a small section of [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md).
There are currently 16 regions in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md), which are listed below.

Centered on [its namesake lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md), **[Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md)** is ideal for players new to the game. It features a little bit of everything: cabins scattered throughout, wilderness, some industry, [fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) on the lake, plenty of foraging, and a relatively low predator density. Overall, the region is quite well balanced.

One of the three major coastal regions in-game, **[Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md)** consists of a frozen bay with two offshore islands, rimmed by mountains that can be climbed by the use of windy logging roads. A large paved road runs right along the water's edge, passing through an [abandoned town](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) and a [fishing camp](./Fishing%20Camp.md). Survivors who venture into the mountains will find many small cabins scattered throughout. This region provides easy access to manufactured goods, especially clothes and [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) in the early game, but Survivors also report significant [wolf](./Wolf.md) activity in the region, especially around the abandoned townsite. The region's mild weather, however, may help those who get into [struggles](./Struggle.md) with wolves, as the lower chance of hypothermia means that Survivors are more often in better health when they do get into a struggle, increasing the odds of their survival.

The main part of **[Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md)** consists of relatively open farmland, where one can find a [farmhouse](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) and [two](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) [barns](./Barn%20%28Molly%27s%29.md). Surrounding the farmland are relatively uninhabited high hills, which offer limited man-made shelter, though there is a small [settlement](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) a short walk east from the farm, along with a [radio tower](./Signal%20Hill.md) and a [crashed plane](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) for Survivors brave enough to handle the frequent blizzards and roaming [wolves](./Wolf.md), both of which offer excellent rewards for those who live long enough to get there.

For those who like to live along the ocean, **[Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md)** is the perfect region. Consisting of a narrow strip of coastline with a paved road, Survivors will find plenty of [beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) if they brave the [weak ice](./Weak%20Ice.md). For those unlucky enough to fall in, not to worry: the region offers plenty of shelter, in the form of a [lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md), a [beached whaling ship](./The%20Riken.md), and a [whale processing plant](./Hibernia%20Processing.md). The region as a whole is quite small: while this means that Survivors are less likely to get horribly lost in a blizzard, it may make it harder to avoid the many predators in the region, one of which lives in a [quite unexpected location](./Cave%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md). Arguably, this region's most important feature is the [forge](./Forge.md) found on the old whaling ship, which allows tools to be forged from [scrap metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), provided that Survivors have sufficient [coal](./Coal.md) -- which, given the [two](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md) [mines](./Abandoned%20Mine%20No.%205.md), is generally a trivial task.

Mountaineers will very much enjoy **[Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md)**, despite its harsh weather. Its most prominent feature is the [peak](./Summit.md) of Timberwolf Mountain itself. Aside from enjoying the great view from the top, Survivors will likely want to check out the many containers found in the region. Some of them can be found scattered throughout the forest surrounding the mountain, but most of them remained in the [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md) of the airplane at the summit, along with a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) -- the only weapon that can reliably drive off a charging [bear](./Bear.md). Aside from the summit, the region also features a number of other, smaller peaks, many of which are accessible. While there isn't much man-made shelter aside from the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md), there are many natural caves, where players can rest in-between the many long [rope climbs](./Rope%20Climbing.md) up to the summit.

The **[Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md)** consists of a [railway track](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) passing through the centre of a large and relatively featureless boggy area. Going through the region isn't too difficult, as it involves simply following the tracks, but once Survivors leave the tracks, they can very easily find themselves lost, especially given the region's frequent fog. Navigation is made even more challenging by the presence of weak ice throughout the region, which can easily turn a promising route into a no-go. To top it off, man-made shelter is hard to find, and there are many wolves throughout. The region's saving grace is that it has a [forge](./Forge.md) at [an old farmstead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) to the south, allowing the creation of improvised tools.

**[Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md)** is a very small region, but that doesn't mean it lacks features. If Survivors can dodge the many wolves along the narrow path to the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md), they will find a massive shed, full of industrial supplies. Also in the shed is a [forge](./Forge.md), though some forethought is required, owing to the scarcity of [coal](./Coal.md) in the local area. Survivors who travel past the Maintenance Yard and up the mountain will come to a large [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md), which is usually well stocked and offers big-game hunting just outside the front door.

For those who prefer more a more urbanized location over country life, **[Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md)** may be the place to live. It is centered around the recently abandoned town of [Milton](./Milton.md), located high in the mountains of Great Bear, and new Survivors will quickly get an abundance of [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) and [clothing](./Clothing.md) from the many houses around town. Venturing out of town can be risky; many wolves can be found just outside of town, especially in the [wood lots](./Wood%20Lot.md) just to the north and south of town. Wolves can also be found in the fields of [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) to the west, which requires a key to open for the first time. Despite the risks, venturing out of town can provide good hunting and foraging opportunities.

Once Survivors have entered the **[Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md)**, they have left civilization behind. There are _no_ man-made houses in the area, aside from a few [snow shelters](./Snow%20Shelter.md), which require constant maintenance to keep up. Navigation can be challenging, as the region features multiple distinct levels, which require [rope climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) to travel between; successfully navigating this region requires Survivors to think in 3-D when they want to go somewhere. Once Survivors get their bearings, however, they will be greeted with one of the most beautiful and resource-rich regions in-game (especially in Interloper), with dozens of waterfalls, deep river valleys, caves for shelter, plants to forage, and game to hunt. While parts of the region feature many predators, large other parts are nearly predator-free. Despite the lack of civilization, manufactured items are still available -- searching around [corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) and stumbling upon [caches](./Hidden%20Cache.md) can yield a wide variety of useful supplies.

Home to roaming [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) packs, visiting **[Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)** is not for the unarmed. The coastal region, split into a high plateau and a coastal plain, features weather that's often cold and windy, and frequent Timberwolves will threaten the player wherever they travel. Despite the danger, Bleak Inlet is one of only two regions that offers ammunition crafting at the [Cannery Pier](./Cannery%20Pier.md), enabling Survivors to make more ammunition for their [rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and [revolver](./Revolver.md). Saltwater [ice fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) is also available, along with a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) in the [fallen lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md). For those trying to stay away from the Timberwolves, there is hope; a small [cabin](./Cabin.md) near Raven Falls Picnic Area offers relative safety and good [deer](./Deer.md) hunting nearby. Additionally, for those with lots of ammunition, some of the best [moose](./Moose.md) hunting in-game is located on the [Frozen Delta](./Frozen%20Delta.md) north of the Cannery.

**[Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md)** consists of a deep canyon with a river running through, recently ravaged by a forest fire. Surrounding this central canyon are steep cliff walls, above which can be found a series of plateaus. These can be accessed by [rope climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) and mountain paths. Survivors need to be careful in this region: it is very cold, and the lower levels are frequented by wolves. The high plateaus have little wildlife of any kind, though the rope bridges connecting them can be treacherous to cross, as a fall from them will be deadly. Following the narrow mountain paths will eventually lead to a [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md) in which a [useful backpack upgrade](./Technical%20Backpack.md) may be found. Man-made shelter is rather limited, though there are a few cabins scattered around, and several natural caves.

Home to the infamous [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), **[Blackrock](./Blackrock.md)** is a hilly region frequented by [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), making it difficult for the inmates to escape... and for Survivors to survive. Those who don't become Timberwolf prey will find a decent amount of man-made shelter, consisting of mainly of trailers and commercial buildings, along with a [vest](./Ballistic%20Vest.md) that can reduce the damage dealt by Timberwolves.

Currently the smallest Region in the game, [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) is a small valley like area that serves as the player's initial starting point to the Inner [Far Territories](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) of Great Bear Island. The area contains very few resources or landmarks, save for a single [cave](./Feedwater%20Cave.md) near some [crashed flatcars](./Distempered%20Flatcars.md), an [abandoned passenger train station](./Vacant%20Depot.md), and a [quiet pond](./Loitering%20Marsh.md). A road found behind the station leads further into the mountains, with a large sign splitting the road in two, leading the player to either an [abandoned airfield](./Field%2031.md) or to a [hazardous open pit mine](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md). Players will likely not stay here for long due to its small size, only passing through to uncover the more enticing secrets of the Far Territory.

**[Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md)** is a relatively large and open region centered on a ruined airfield, named [Airfield 31](./Field%2031.md), that it's plagued by a [mysterious variant of heavy fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md). Several non-functional aircraft can be found around the airport and in the [hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md). A short walk north of the airfield is [a large lake](./Shoulder%20Lake.md), which features a [fairly large island](./Drift%20Island.md) with a [cottage](./Island%20Cottage.md) on it. Two roads wind through the region: one from [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) to the airfield, the other to [Mindful Cabin](./Mindful%20Cabin.md). The edges of the region are much more forested, and contain a few shallow caves. Survivors will want to be careful during the region's frequent fog and blizzards, or they risk getting lost. It currently connects to [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) and [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) via a transition cave and to [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md).

An abandoned yet hazardous open-pit mine region, the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) connects with [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md), and [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) through a transition cave. The Zone features a massive open pit [industrial mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) created by the Langston Mining Corporation and is highly toxic, with [Chemical Hazards](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) spread over much of the industrialized areas and with toxic mineshaft gases present inside the mine itself. This region houses the exclusive [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), a starving and aggressive wolf variant. The Zone is the centerpiece of the [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md) Tale.

A region which connects with [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) and the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) through a transition cave or with [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md). [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) is a very mountainous and cold region prone to many avalanches, with Wolves stalking the lower forests and Timberwolf packs hunting in the higher altitude fields. The region continues to get colder the higher in altitude the player gets. The Pass is the beginning of the [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) Tale.

Not all regions connect directly to other regions, but can instead be separated by smaller explorable "mini regions" dubbed Transition Zones. These regions are characterized by several qualities, such as the inability to spawn here when starting a game (or randomly spawning as is the case in Interloper or Custom games), they do not typically show up on the island-wide overworld map, but have their own regional map, and they are often sparse with resources. All Transition Zones will never contain very large animals such as [Bears](./Bear.md) or [Moose](./Moose.md), and can sometimes not even contain any medium sized prey or predator animals, such as [Deer](./Deer.md) or [Wolves](./Wolf.md).
These regions may also contain a handful of marked or unmarked discoverable locations, and can be surveyed with [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md). The Outdoor Transition Zones include:
| [Crumbling Highway](./Crumbling%20Highway.md) (Old Island Connector) | 5 | Survival | 18 Sep 2015 |
| [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) | 4 | Survival | 7 Dec 2021 |
| [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md) | 4 | Survival, Story | 7 Dec 2021 |
| [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md) | 9 | Survival | 5 Dec 2022 |

In addition to outdoor areas, Great Bear Island contains many indoor Transition Zones as well. These areas cannot be surveyed with Charcoal and are incredibly small, contain no Wildlife, and can often be mazelike in their navigation:
- [Abandoned Mine No. 3](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md) - connects [Old Island Connector](./Crumbling%20Highway.md) (Crumbling Highway) and [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md)
- [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) - connects [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) and [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md)

- [Carter Hydro Dam Environs](./Winding%20River.md) - connects [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) and [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) (consists of [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md), and a [Cave](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md))
Some regions are connected directly, without any Transition Zones between them. These connections are:

- All the regions of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) aside from [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) and [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) were designed by Katie Sorrell.
- The location "[Katie's Secluded Corner](./Katie%27s%20Secluded%20Corner.md)" in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) is named after her.

**Reishi Mushrooms** are a natural material that can be used to create both food and first aid treatments that are used to treat [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_.

Reishi Mushrooms can be found in the wilderness growing on the trunks or stumps of dead trees, typically in clusters of 1-3 units. They can be crafted into [Prepared Reishi Mushrooms](./Prepared%20Reishi%20Mushrooms.md) to be able to be cooked into [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md). Raw Mushrooms can be used in the [Prepper's Pie](./Prepper%27s%20Pie.md) and [Thomson Family Stew](./Thomson%20Family%20Stew.md) recipes.
Prepared Reishi Mushrooms have half the weight of their raw form, and no form of Reishi Mushroom decays.
| [Prepared Reishi Mushrooms](./Prepared%20Reishi%20Mushrooms.md) | None | - 2 × [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) |

| [Prepper's Pie](./Prepper%27s%20Pie.md) | None | - 1 × [Acorn Grounds](./Acorn%20Grounds.md) - 4 × [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) - 2 × [Burdock Root](./Burdock%20Root.md) - 0.10 L × [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) - 0.05 L × [Cooking Oil](./Cooking%20Oil.md) - 0.01 kg × [Salt](./Salt.md) |

| [Thomson Family Stew](./Thomson%20Family%20Stew.md) | None | - 0.30 kg × [Canned Corn](./Canned%20Corn.md) - 0.40 kg × [Carrot](./Carrot.md) - 2 × [Potato](./Potato.md) - 2 × [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) - 0.40 L × [Broth](./Broth.md) - 0.05 kg × [Old Mill Flour](./Old%20Mill%20Flour.md) |
- Teas are more weight efficient than Water for the Hydration they grant. (0.1kg of a tea grants 30% Hydration, equivalent to 0.198kg of water).
- Teas may be heated to grant the [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md) benefit by placing them on a fire's cooking spot, or nearby a lit fire.

- Upon reaching Level 5 [Cooking skill](./Cooking.md), all artificial foods and cooked meats may be safely eaten regardless of condition (including "Ruined" food), making Food Poisoning and Intestinal Parasites only possible through the consumption of raw meat.

- [Infections](./Infection.md), [Dysentery](./Dysentery.md) and [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) are permanent and lethal if left untreated, though [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) is not lethal in of itself and will dissipate naturally with time (12-24 hours), but will reduce maximum Condition to 15%, making it potentially dangerous.

- [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md) are not a renewable resource and cannot be crafted; however Reishi Tea is functionally similar to Antibiotics, but is made from natural materials found abundantly in the wilds.

- Reishi Mushrooms are a real-world bracket fungus (Species: [_G. lingzhi_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingzhi_%28mushroom%29)) common to the Pacific North-West (United States and Canada), as well as north-eastern China, Korea, Japan and Russia.
- "Reishi" (霊芝) is the Japanese name for the fungus; other names include Lingzhi, Yeongji (영지), Het Lin Chue (หลินจือ) and Linh Chi.

- Reishi have a long history of use in [Traditional Chinese Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_medicine), though there is insufficient evidence that their consumption has any tangible medical effect, unlike their in-game description and use. They are an anti-oxidant but exhibit no antibiotic properties, unlike the _Ganoderma_ (_Penicillium)_ mold used to create [Penicillin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penicillin) (an antibiotic), which is unrelated to _G. lingzhi_.
- Real reishi are typically parasitic or saprotrophic (feed on dead matter) of maple trees, unlike in _The Long Dark_ where they are exclusively saprotrophic to cedar or fir.
- Antibiotics are typically a prescription-grade drug derived from penicillin, which is the case in _The Long Dark_ as they are labeled as "Pharmacillin".

- In The Long Dark, Antibiotics and Reishi Tea must be applied directly to treat a specific injury (similar to a Bandage), unlike real-world orally-taken drugs which become generally distributable through the body.

**Reishi Tea** is a natural medical and food item used to treat [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_.

Reishi Tea functions similar to [Antibiotics](./Antibiotics.md) for treating Afflictions, and is cooked from one [Prepared Reishi Mushrooms](./Prepared%20Reishi%20Mushrooms.md) (two [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md)) and 0.25 liters of [Potable Water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) at a lit [Fire](./Fire.md). Consuming prepared Reishi Tea (even without treating an Affliction) grants 100 Calories, restores 30% Hydration, and potentially grants the benefit [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md). Cooking Reishi Tea increases [Cooking Skill](./Skills.md).
Reishi Tea, like [Burdock Tea](./Burdock%20Tea.md), is used to treat the following Afflictions:
- [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) (1 dose and 10 hours Sleep, or 12-24 hours if untreated)
- [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) (1 dose and 10 days Sleep on Stalker (20 days on Interloper))

The effect of Reishi Tea is not generalized throughout the body, and each dose will treat only one injury. For example, Food Poisoning and Dysentery will display as separate Afflictions, with each requiring separate doses to treat.

Reishi Mushrooms can be found in the wilderness growing on the trunks or stumps of dead trees, typically in clusters of 1-3 units. They cannot be directly consumed and must first be crafted into [Prepared Reishi Mushrooms](./Prepared%20Reishi%20Mushrooms.md) and then cooked into [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md).
Prepared Reishi Mushrooms have half the weight of their raw form, and no form of Reishi Mushroom [Decay](./Decay.md).

**Remnant Cave** is a small cave and unmarked location in the [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md) region.

Located between [Steely Chasm](./Steely%20Chasm.md) and [Freighthopper's Rockfall](./Freighthopper%27s%20Rockfall.md), the cave can be found just up a hill from some red boxcars located on a track separate from the main [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md). **Renewed Hope (Predux)** was the fifth and final mission of the Predux [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story and the last mission in the Predux storyline. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).

This is it, the beginning of the end of the Predux Wintermute. 1 side mission will unlock for this mission, [Hank's Hatch](./Hank%27s%20Hatch.md), so complete it if you wish. Head to the [Unnamed Pond](./Unnamed%20Pond.md) to find an active fire to activate Hank's Hatch. Otherwise, go to the Carter Hydro Dam.

Wait inside the trailers near the Staging Area fence until night falls and an Aurora is in the sky. There's no way to trigger one, so you'll have to have enough supplies to wait for one to appear. Sleep through the day and wait until night, then when the Aurora is out, head past the gate to the Dam.

A campfire burns inside the Staging Area, with a strange man sitting beside it. Mackenzie approaches and a 3rd person cutscene begins. The man calls himself Methuselah, and tells Mackenzie that the world is changing, and that he has seen this Quest Apocalypses before. Mackenzie asks if this is about religion or the lights in the sky, but Methuselah says it is not religion, but redemption, and that the lights are a sign of a reckoning because now everyone will be tested to see how far they will go to survive. Mackenzie say he's no hero, only a man looking for someone. Methuselah then wishes Mackenzie luck, and offers him a seat to for the pilot to warm himself by the fire.
Methuselah cannot be talked to anymore after the cutscene ends, but his fire is infinite and can be used. When you are ready, head inside to face the Dam.

Head straight to the Control Room and use the keypad to open the door. Walk to the back of the Control Room and turn the Switch Box on. Then exit the room to the adjacent room housing the elevator, and ride it down. It will get stuck, and will require a prybar to open (a corpse inside the elevator has one if you aren't carrying one).

Despite what the game says, you can actually wait out the Aurora with no consequences from here on out. From the generator floor, head up to the upper walkways and to a [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section to bypass the burning metal and live wires (even with the aurora gone, an invisible wall blocks your path, so use the rope). Head to the Lower Dam and continue until you find a door. It is also locked with a keypad, but Mackenzie doesn't have the code for this door, so head forward into the lower generator room, using switch boxes to turn off the live wires in the hallway. Walk across the room and take the stairs upstairs until you find another door that leads to the outside....until something hits you.

Mackenzie will then wake up tied to a chair, with a [man covered in blood](./Mathis.md) and wearing an orange jumpsuit placing [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) on the floor before him. The man repeatedly punches Mackenzie, demanding to know what's in the case while trying to intimidate him. After several failed attempts, the man then tells Mackenzie that he knows from his ID that he is a pilot, and presumes that he has a plane stashed somewhere, but Mackenzie continues to show resistance ("My plane [wouldn't do you any good](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md)"). The convict then threatens Mackenzie, saying that the pilot wouldn't act this way if he say what happened to the last person the he met, referring to her as "she." This get's Mackenzie's attention, with the convict only remarking, "Don't worry, you'll be with her soon" and then striking Mackenzie in the side of the head with the back side of a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), ending the Episode.
Several plot points and locations have been replaced/altered since the Redux re-release of Episode 2:

- Mackenzie can re-enter the Trapper's Homestead and continue talking to Jeremiah to unlock any remaining Trust content. In the Redux, Mackenzie will refuse to re-enter the cabin, saying "Nah, I'm done with the old man."
- The encounter with [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) is the first time Mackenzie has met him in the Predux storyline. In Redux, this is the fourth and last time he will meet him.
- Methuselah's Campfire says it lasts for 4 hours despite being infinite. This would be corrected in the Redux, now displaying an infinity (∞) symbol.
- Jeremiah gives Mackenzie a code to enter the Dam control room, but in the Redux Mackenzie somehow knows the code (or guesses).

- [Mathis](./Mathis.md) and Methuselah are both is voiced by Gord Marriott in Predux. They would each receive a new separate voice actor in Redux, with Mathis being voiced by Elias Toufexis and Methuselah being voiced by Richard Newman.
- Mathis' coat sleeves and waist are covered in blood. This detail was removed in the Redux.
- Added to game.
- UPDATE **17 December 2018 ([Update](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog%20%E2%80%94%20Archive%201.md#1.41)):**

**Characters:** [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) [Mathis](./Mathis.md)
This is the mission transcript for mission 5 [Renewed Hope](./Renewed%20Hope.md) of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md).
_Mackenzie is standing outside the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) as the chapter begins_
_If the player attempts to re-enter the Homestead, the door will be locked and Mackenzie will say:_
_Mackenzie makes his way to the Carter Staging Area just outside the hydro dam only to be greeted by a familiar face sitting by a campfire._
Methuselah: "You've left your mark. And have overcome great odds, so far...but this part of the world still holds some secrets."

Methuselah: "There are still stories that need to be told, if you wish to play a part in them. There is always time, for that. But, if you are in a hurry, -- by all means go. Nobody would fault you for continuing your journey. Onward."

Mackenzie: "You know...it's been a hell of a slog out there, nevermind that damn bear. I've nearly died more times than I care to count. It couldn't have been easy for you, either. But you seem strangely calm about all the hostility of this place.
Methuselah: "I have wandered these paths a long time, friend. I was a walker, now I'm a watcher. I'm here to observe these times, and help where I may."

Mackenzie: "As strange as it is running into you again, it's good to meet a familiar face in all this frigid wilderness. And keep to your paths. If this is a reckoning, as you say, I hope our paths cross again."

_The player can wait for the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) to appear at night while in the company of Methuselah, or go complete side missions in the meantime. Once the lights appear in the sky, Mackenzie walks to the Dam. He opens the door the the control room and turns a switch box on to the main elevators._
_Mackenzie finds a working elevator near the control room and presses the call button. The doors slide open._
_The elevator descends, but breaks as it reaches the bottom, with the doors partly opening and the elevator button sparking, too dangerous to touch._

_Mackenzie uses a Prybar to force the doors open, and enters the turbine room. Making his way around the obvious hazards on the floor, he reaches the lower dam. Another door with a keypad is found labeled "Emergency Exit", but it will not open no matter what Mackenzie does, and he moves on. He reaches the lower turbine room and sees more sparking wires on the floor._

_He finds another switch box and turns the power off, then crosses the room and ascends a stairwell. After reaching the top, he spots a doorway off in the distance with another exit sign. As he approaches it, an unseen force hits him in the back of the head and knocks him out. As he comes too, a figure approaches him and places [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) on the floor at Mackenzie's feet. Mackenzie snaps awake and sees a man in a sheepskin coat wearing an orange jumpsuit, and realizes he is tied to a chair._
Mathis: "A locked metal case is a thing of the old world, stranger. It's a world of things closed doors and things being off limits."

- Get into the [dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) at night, when the [aurora](./Aurora.md) is in the sky.

Has an interior A **Repair Depot** is a major landmark building that can be found on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md). There are currently two in the game. Located on [Anna Island -- Track Section 2](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%202.md) and [Anna Island -- Track Section 4](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%204.md).

The [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md) can be driven into the Repair Depot by rolling through the red gate (even at full speed, this does not result in a crash), allowing the train to be transported inside and the Survivor to work on the train without being exposed to the elements. Leaving the Depot with the train inside will automatically spawn it outside, and vice versa when returning inside, until it is moved far enough away from the Depot doors.

Enough resources can be found to repair the Prototype Train, but there is no [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) for Crafting at either location. The Depots also contain small to moderate amounts of clothing and food, along with several [lockers](./Locker.md), and [Beds](./Bed.md). Both Depots support [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md).

The Repair Depot in [Anna Island -- Track Section 4](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%204.md) has a [Whale Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md) and a [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md). It is the first Repair Depot the player will encounter after acquiring the Prototype Train.

The Repair Depot in [Anna Island -- Track Section 2](./Anna%20Island%20--%20Track%20Section%202.md) has a [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) and the unique [McLeod Ultra-Efficiency Whale Oil Heater](./McLeod%20Ultra-Efficiency%20Whale%20Oil%20Heater.md).

**Repairing** is a secondary Survival [Skill](./Skills.md) that is used to repair or crafts tools. Higher levels in the repairing skill reduce the amount of time required to repair, and additionally increase the amount of condition restored to an item by repairing. [Mending](./Mending.md) is the corresponding skill used to repair or craft Clothing, and [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) is the skill used to improve the condition of Hatchets and Knives.

Most tools consume 1 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) per repair action, and may still consume metal upon a failed repair attempt. Players need [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md) or [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) to repair other tools.
- Simple Tools increase the chance of repair successes by 10%, Quality Tools by 20%.
- Either is usable for any affected item, but Quality Tools provide a higher chance of success, a faster repair time, and a higher Condition increase.

- Toolboxes are always found in 100% Condition and may be found in areas that other tools spawn, around workbenches, or inside tool chests or lockers. Both can also be repaired with Scrap Metal or with other toolboxes.
- Despite needing Scrap Metal and Quality/Simple tools to repair, [Improvised Crampons](./Improvised%20Crampons.md) and [Crampons](./Crampons.md) count towards the [Mending](./Mending.md) skill.

The **Replacement Fuse** is an item that was first added in [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of Story Mode. It was later added to survival mode in the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC.

In Story Mode, the fuses are found in the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md). They are used to replace [burned out fuses](./Burned%20Out%20Fuse.md) to power up the elevator and leave [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).

In Survival Mode, the fuses are used to repair [transmitters](./Transmitters.md). Three fuses are needed to repair each transmitter. Several fuses can often be found near the broken-down transmitter, but extra fuses can also be found scattered throughout the world in industrial locations.
- Added to game.

![Research1](../assets/Research1.jpg) A **Research Book** or **Skill Book** is both a Fuel and Tool item in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) that can be researched to increase [Skills](./Skills.md), and can be found as 10 separate in game items.

Research Books are items that may be used as fuel for [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) and have the same weight (0.50kg) as normal books. However, they may also be read, which grants skill points to their respective Survival Skills when completed. Because of this, Research Books can be found in both the Fuel and Tools categories. Attempting to burn a Research Book that has not been fully read will give a confirmation warning before it can be burned. Once a Research Book is fully researched, it will no longer appear in the Tools section of the Backpack.
- Research Books are scattered throughout all regions similar to normal [Books](./Book.md), but are much rarer and have unique detailed covers.

- Books can only be read if the player is not in the dark or if the player is healthy enough: the player's [Needs](./Needs.md) ([Warmth](./Warmth.md), [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Thirst](./Thirst.md), [Calories](./Hunger.md)) are above 0% and they are not suffering from any negative [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) (Affliction Risks do not count).
- The only exception to this rule are permanent Afflictions, as this would make researching impossible:

- [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md), [Diminished Form](./Diminished%20Form.md), [Frigid Bones](./Frigid%20Bones.md), [Haunted Mind](./Haunted%20Mind.md), [Sour Stomach](./Sour%20Stomach.md), [Rheumatic Joints](./Rheumatic%20Joints.md), [Broken Body](./Broken%20Body.md), [Cheated Death Penalty](./Cheated%20Death%20Penalty.md) (Permanent Penalty).
- The player can research outside at night, but only in clear weather (heavy fog/blizzards will make it too dark, in which case a light source must be used).

- Reaching 0% in any [Needs](./Needs.md) (or manually canceling) while researching will immediately end the research session and negate any progress for that research attempt. (i.e., if you complete 59 out of 60 in-game minutes of a 1-hour research session, and your character begins starving before completing the last minute of research, the character immediately forgets everything they researched in the last 59 minutes).

- _Frontier Shooting Guide_ cannot be read once Rifle Firearm reaches Level 4, displaying the message "Your Skills are too advanced to research this." This is the only Research Book that has a Skill Level restriction.
- Since Skills cap at Level 5, any category of Research Books related to that Skill cannot be read, and can only be used as fuel at that point.
- On [Interloper](./Interloper.md), researching Skill Books burns calories at the rate of "Standing" (125 cal/h).

The [Feat](./Feats.md) "Book Smarts" increases the skill points gained from completing a research book by 10% (e.g. with the feat active, reading a "Small Arms Handbook" yields 11 revolver skill points instead of 10).
The Feat "Settled Mind" makes the user immune to [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), but also causes Research actions to happen 20% faster.

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

The **Respirator** is a [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) item that was added as part of the Part 4 Buried Echoes update to the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion. It is one of the few items that cannot be dropped or placed in containers so it cannot be lost, similar to the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) and [Camera](./Camera.md).
> “**Equip to protect yourself from toxic gas and other environmental hazards. Requires Canisters to function.**”

Despite appearing to be a Clothing/Tool item, the Respirator is classified as a First Aid item and weighs 0.00 kg in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). It is a must if the player travels through the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), as it prevents [Suffocation](./Suffocation.md) inside various areas of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) (or [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) if carried to [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md)). It also prevents [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md) from breathing spilled [Chemical Hazards](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) on the surface, and is best used in tandem with [Chemical Boots](./Chemical%20Boots.md) to fully protect one's lungs and feet when walking through chemical patches.

[Canisters](./Canister.md) are required for it to be useable, and are automatically changed out by hand when they wear out. They can be found in the world as well as inside various containers. One can always be found next to the Respirator on the table. Canisters in the Respirator last for 45 seconds in-game, and do not degrade while in a toxic environment when searching the inside of a container, but will degrade if the player is in the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md). Once all Canisters are used up, the survivor will automatically take the Respirator off their head and begin suffocating again.

Keep in mind that wearing a Respirator prevents a player from eating or drinking until it is removed. It also partially obscures the player's vision below the nose line, and any dialogue made by the player character is distorted and amplified while still wearing the mask.

- The default Revolver in-game most closely resembles a Smith & Wesson Model 27, which uses .357 Magnum ammunition; however, in-game Revolver Ammunition appears to be .32 S&W Long. A cut icon for Revolver Bullets named [.44 Magnum](../assets/Revolver_44_Mag_Bullet_icon.png) might also be the correct cartridge caliber.

**Revolver Firearm** is a [survival skill](./Skills.md) that involves the use of a [revolver](./Revolver.md) to defend oneself from hostile [wildlife](./Wildlife.md), or as a sub-optimal hunting tool.
A firearm's ability to attack from range allows can frighten or killing wildlife from relative safety.

The [Revolver](./Revolver.md) is a self defense tool used to fire [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md) at targets. The high-velocity rounds travel in a straight line and can cause significant injury to smaller animals, including [wolves](./Wolf.md) and [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md). However the weapon lacks of stopping power, making it ineffective against [bear](./Bear.md) and [moose](./Moose.md). Revolvers may also be selected to defend oneself during a Wolf [Struggle](./Struggle.md), and if loaded, the option to "Take Shot" may appear, which if selected will end the struggle immediately: scaring off or killing the wolf.

Shots from the Revolver which hit an animal's head or torso (indicated by a bloodsplatter, or blood drops), are always lethal but due to the weapon's low stopping power, this may take several hours (in-game) for it to bleed to death.

Revolver skill is increased by scoring hits on live [wildlife](./Wildlife.md) with the Revolver, or by fully reading the research book _[Small Arms Handbook](./Small%20Arms%20Handbook.md)_. Multiple copies of the book can be read, each granting skill points when fully read.
- A Revolver round striking a live animal (except [crows](./Crow.md)) grants 1 skill point.
- Selecting a loaded Revolver for self-defense during a Wolf struggle, and firing it during the struggle grants 1 skill point.
- _[Small Arms Handbook](./Small%20Arms%20Handbook.md)_ grants 10 skill points (5 hours of reading).

Note: _Revolver skill is not increased by selecting to use a carried Revolver during a Wolf struggle (bludgeoning the Wolf with the revolver), but instead having it loaded, selecting it, and choosing the "Take Shot" option during the struggle (if it appears). However, increased "Struggle Effectiveness" from the Revolver Skill does affect struggle success regardless of the weapon being loaded or not._
Once players have reached a new skill level, they unlock a new bonus/bonuses get better.
| 1 | 0 | 10 | - Basic Revolver skill | You're very new to handguns, and the Revolver remains an awkward tool. You know how to load it, find a target, and fire, but no much else. |

| 2 | 10 | 15 | - Recoil compensation increased by 25% - +2 condition per repair action | You have a little more shooting experience under your belt. You can pick your targets and you know how to keep your Revolver clean enough to fire. |

| 3 | 25 | 25 | - Struggle effectiveness increased by 10% - Recoil compensation increased by 35% - +3 condition per repair action | You've become skilled with the Revolver. your steady hand finds targets reliably and you know how to keep your Revolver in good condition. |

| 4 | 50 | 50 | - Aim Assist: Minor - Struggle effectiveness increased by 20% - Recoil compensation increased by 50% - +4 condition per repair action | You're efficient and deadly with the Revolver. Your shots are clean and effective, especially in defensive situations. |

| 5 | 100 | Max level | - Per-use degradation reduced by 50% - Aim assist: Moderate - Recoil compensation increased by 70% - Struggle effectiveness increased by 30% - +5 condition per repair action | There's little stopping you with a Revolver in your hands. Your stance is strong, your eyes sharp, and your targets always in sight. More than a tool, it's become an extension of your will to survive. |

> “**A powerful handgun, the Revolver has great stopping power in defensive situations. Not a Hunting weapon.**”

_This article is about the normal revolver. For variants, see [Hunter's Revolver](./Hunter%27s%20Revolver.md), [Forester's Revolver](./Forester%27s%20Revolver.md), and [Warden's Revolver](./Warden%27s%20Revolver.md)._

The **Revolver** is a double-action weapon with a six-round cylinder used primarily for self-defense against hostile wildlife. The [Revolver Firearm](./Revolver%20Firearm.md) Skill is improved when a living animal is hit, or by reading the [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) _Small Arms Handbook._

The Revolver is the second firearm added to [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md), and unlike its counterparts the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), it is less than ideal for hunting with limited damage, range, and accuracy.

It is most effective in defensive situations against hostile wildlife—particularly [Wolves](./Wolf.md) and [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md). A hit will nearly always stop a wolf charge (if the wolf isn't killed outright) and inflict great damage on timberwolf pack morale. Even a near-miss will often deter a charging wolf and will somewhat reduce timberwolf pack morale.

Although the Revolver can be used to kill any [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md), it is less effective against large animals due to its low damage, even at very high [Revolver Firearm](./Revolver%20Firearm.md) Skill Levels. Any animal except the [Moose](./Moose.md) and [Cougar](./Cougar.md) shot by the revolver will eventually die from blood loss, but it may take a while to bleed out (a Bear can die from one Revolver shot, but will take half a day to bleed out). Shots fired from the Revolver have a chance of stopping charging moose, but this is not guaranteed. They will, however, cause moose to pause their charge for at a moment, providing an opportunity to take further shots. If the player shoots all six rounds in the cylinder at the moose in quick succession, the animal will usually be scared off. Shooting at a charging bear will not stop it, unless the player manages to kill it outright before it reaches them.
- Can defend oneself during a Wolf [Struggle](./Struggle.md), and with increased effectiveness at higher Revolver Firearm Skill
- Low stopping power and long bleed-out time: a single round will kill any struck animal eventually (except moose/cougar) through blood loss, but [Deer](./Deer.md)/[Bears](./Bear.md) may take hours
- [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md) is relatively abundant, while Revolvers themselves are quite rare
- Lighter than Hunting Rifles (1.50kg VS 4.00kg), but heavier than a survival bow (0.50kg, and 0.15kg per arrow)
- Spent casings are not immediately ejected, but contained in the cylinder until the next reload, when they will then be dropped on the ground
- Unloading the Revolver from the Inventory menu places spent and unspent rounds directly into the Inventory
The Revolver holds 1-6 rounds, each of which must be loaded individually. It is possible to unload a Revolver through the Actions menu in the inventory.

Firing a Revolver will leave a [Revolver Shell Casing](./Revolver%20Shell%20Casing.md) inside the gun, which will drop to the ground when the gun is reloaded and can be picked up. Casings cannot be removed unless a player has spare ammo to reload a Revolver or they manually unload the gun.

Manually unloading the gun in the player's Backpack will automatically place casings in your inventory. Spent casings still within the chamber do not add to the gun's weight. Some Revolvers can be found with live ammo and casings already inside though there is currently no way to identify if casings are inside a gun until it is unloaded.

The default action of the Revolver is a hipfire. Aiming using the gun's sight improves accuracy but disables walking. Aiming is also improved as Revolver Firearm Skill improves. Aiming at a hostile wolf will cause it to immediately charge.
Sway with the Revolver is lower than that of the Hunting Rifle, but increases if some [Needs](./Needs.md) are low ([Fatigued](./Fatigue.md) or Freezing), making aiming more difficult.

The Revolver will begin jamming under the 30% condition threshold, then it has the chance to improperly fire the next cartridge. Attempting to fire will result in a misfire jam. To clear the jam, the cylinder must be opened manually by pressing the reload button/key. Doing so will eject the unspent live cartridge onto the ground near the player, from where it can be picked up and used again. Unloading and reloading the Revolver in the player's backpack will also clear the jam without dropping any ammo.
Low quality Ammunition created from [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) can also cause a misfire, even if the gun is in relatively good condition.

Firing a Revolver degrades it's condition by 1%, and 0.5% if the player has a level 5 revolver firearm skill. Non-ruined Revolvers may be repaired with a [Firearm Cleaning Kit](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md), which will increase the [Cleaning Skill](./Cleaning.md), or repaired at a [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md) for 1 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), increasing [Gunsmithing Skill](./Gunsmithing.md).

At 0% Condition, the Revolver will become "Ruined" and cannot be fired. Ruined Revolvers can be repaired for use again at a Milling Machine for 4 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), 1 [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md), and takes 4 hours.
Revolvers may be selected for self-defense during a struggle with a Wolf. If selected at the Struggle's start, the butt of the revolver will be used to strike the Wolf.

At half the struggle bar the option to "Take a shot" will appear during a struggle if the Revolver is loaded; selecting this will fire 1 Revolver Ammunition and end the Struggle immediately, scaring the Wolf or potentially killing it instantly.

- Note: a single non-fatal shot fired at a _charging_ wolf will usually not deter it, but multiple have a high chance of a kill as the head of the wolf is the most exposed, making critical hits (headshots) easier. A charging wolf will often flee if several shots are fired in quick succession, even if said shots miss.
- [Hunter's Revolver](./Hunter%27s%20Revolver.md) - Longer effective firing range, but heavier
- [Warden's Revolver](./Warden%27s%20Revolver.md) - Lighter and faster, but shorter effective firing range
The Revolver may spawn in any of following locations in all survival modes except Interloper. It is possible for more than one revolver to spawn in any given game.
- [Homesteader's Respite](./Homesteader%27s%20Respite.md), on a table next to the armchair
- Next to a corpse at the [Mining Camp](./Mining%20Camp.md), along the frozen stream heading east
- In Cellblock 3 at [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) building, in the room where the went exits, behind the big grey piece of machinery in one of the outcoves.
- In the sheltered office attached to the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) in a flower pot
- Next to a corpse leaning against a tree on an island between misanthrope's homestead and jackrabbit Island.

Rheumatic Joints is a permanent Affliction unique to [Misery](./Misery.md) which occurs from Stages 2-4 of Misery. It reduces the survivor's speed while [sprinting](./Stamina.md), the length of time available to aim the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), and increases the chance of getting a [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md) or [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md) when on uneven terrain[^1]. Crafting quality Condition Rifle Ammunition is based on the [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) skill, with lower level Gunsmithing producing lower quality cartridges that are more likely to misfire, no matter the condition of the Hunting Rifle. The quality and Condition of the crafted ammunition will always be found next to the name of the ammo:
- The character will load five rounds into the magazine at a time using stripper clips. Any number of rounds less than five are loaded one-by-one.
- Rifle rounds can be found on [corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), lying on the floor inside of buildings, or in [hunting blinds](./Hunter%27s%20Blinds.md).
- Dropped rounds appear as a box of rounds when dropping more than one at a time, even if an actual box of ammunition is never found.
- Empty shell casings always drop directly beneath the player regardless of firing angle, even though it is ejected to the side from the action.

- The ammo's real life counterpart is the .303 British Rifle cartridge, which was produced from the late 1890s until the early 1950s for use by the British Army. However, unlike the real .303, the cartridge depicted in-game is rimless rather than rimmed.
- Multiple rounds should not be used once a target is hit unless hunting [Moose](./Moose.md) or [Cougar](./Cougar.md), as the bleeding wound will result in the death of the target.
- Use your ammunition wisely even if it is renewable, since trips to ammunition workbenches are dangerous, resource-intensive, and time-consuming.
- Rifle rounds are found in a small, red and grey colored cardboard box, or, if the player has a keen eye, can be spotted singly in fishing huts and other buildings.

- Hunting [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) with the hunting rifle is not very efficient, as rabbits can be hunted effectively with [Stones](./Stone.md), [Fire Hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md), or the [Revolver](./Revolver.md) if desperate.

![Rifle Firearm](../assets/Rifle_Firearm.png) **Rifle Firearm** or **Firearms** is a [Survival Skill](./Skills.md) that involves the use of a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) to [hunt](./Hunting.md) [animals](./Wildlife.md).

![Riflesights](../assets/Riflesights.jpg) The hunting rifle is a tool used to fire [Rifle rounds](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) at targets. The rifle operates as a hit-scan weapon; unlike the bow, its bullets are not affected by projectile drop. The high velocity rounds it fires will travel in a straight line and cause massive internal injuries to any animal struck by it, with the potential to kill instantly. If a shot hits the targeted animal (indicated by a spurt of blood) but fails to immediately kill it, the round will inflict a bleeding wound that leaves a blood trail on the ground. Over the course of several game hours (depending on where the animal was hit), the wound will eventually kill the animal. After a round is fired, a shell casing will be ejected from the gun where the player stands and can be picked up.

- All rifles except for the [Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md) currently have a maximum range of approximately fifty paces with a Beginner Firearms Skill. (The Curators' has a range of ~66 paces) Targets beyond the maximum range cannot be hit, even if the aiming reticle lines up accurately.
- Hitting a solid target will produce a smoke effect often accompanied with a "clank" sound.
Players need both a rifle and ammunition before they can start practicing the firearms skill.

The hunting rifle (and its variants) are tools used to fire rifle rounds at targets. The rifle's condition will degrade every shot (the amount degraded depends on the variant). Rifles can be repaired by using a [Firearm Cleaning Kit](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md) to keep the weapon in optimal condition. A [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) can be used to greatly repair a rifle, even being able to restore a 0% Ruined Condition rifle, but this takes considerably more time then a repair. At level 5 Rifle Firearm skill, Per-use condition [degradation](./Decay.md) reduced by 50%.

Rifle ammunition for hunting rifles can be found as single cartridges, or in 5-round boxes. It can be crafted at the [Ammunition Workbench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md), a crafting station found in both [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) and [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md).

The rifle holds a maximum of 10 rounds at a time and can be loaded with 5 round stripper clips; rounds will be loaded individually if there are 6 or more rounds in the magazine or if the player has fewer than 5 rounds. Loading will continue until interrupted, either by clicking or canceling, or until the magazine is fully loaded. Unlike the [Revolver](./Revolver.md), shell casings will be ejected onto the ground automatically after firing due to how a bolt action system works.

**Hunting** animals allows players to kill and then harvest their flesh, pelts, and guts to acquire [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) and materials in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. Hitting animals with projectiles, such as rifle ammunition, is the most effective way to kill game while completely bypassing the animals' natural defenses. Rifle shots move too quickly to be blocked or dodged and can be fired from outside the animal's zone of perception, allowing a (potentially) safe source of food.

Critical hits are random occurrences but are more likely in designated critical areas. Shots to the head and neck have the best chance to cause a critical hit, followed by shots to the shoulders and chest. Shots to the hind are immune to critical hits.

Direct hits to an animal with a rifle round that are not critical will cause bleeding wounds. Animals will bleed out according to which area they were shot in last. Multiple shots to the same area will not make the animal bleed out any faster. However, shooting an animal in an area that bleeds faster than a previous wound it has already received will cause it to bleed out as if the faster wound were caused when the first wound was.
| Animal | Hit zone — Head | Hit zone — Chest | Hit zone — Hind | Hit zone — Foot |

Rifle Skill is increased by scoring hits on live wildlife with the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Barb's Rifle](./Barb%27s%20Rifle.md), [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md), or [Curator's Rifle](./Curator%27s%20Rifle.md), or by fully reading _[Frontier Shooting Guide](./Frontier%20Shooting%20Guide.md)_ or _[Advanced Guns Guns Guns!](./Advanced%20Guns%20Guns%20Guns!.md)_. Multiple copies of each book can be read, each granting skill points when fully read.
- A rifle round striking a live animal (except [crows](./Crow.md) and [fish](./Ice%20Fishing.md)) grants 1 skill point.
- _Frontier Shooting Guide_ grants 5 skill points (4 hours of reading) The book **_cannot_** be read if you are skill level 4 or above.
Once players have reached a new skill level, they unlock the effects described in the table below:

| 1 | 0 | 10 | - Basic rifle skill | You're very new to firearms, and aren't yet comfortable with using the Rifle. You know how to load it and how to fire it, and you know what end to point at the target, and that's about it. |

| 2 | 10 | 15 | - Critical hit chance increased by 10% - 2 additional percent of condition per repair action | You have a little more shooting experience under your belt. You're more accurate and you know how to keep your Rifle in working order. |

| 3 | 25 | 25 | - Accuracy range increased by 20% - Critical Hit chance increased by 15% - 3 additional percent of condition per repair action | You've become skilled with the Rifle. You're able to hit things further away, and you've developed a better feel for how your shots can be most effective. You know how to keep your Rifle in good condition. |

| 4 | 50 | 50 | - Damage increased by 10% - Accuracy range increased by 30% - Critical Hit chance increased by 20% - 4 additional percent of condition per repair action | You've developed a strong feeling for the Rifle. Your shots hit more often and you take down your targets more reliably. It is your constant companion. |

| 5 | 100 | Max level | - Damage increased by 20% - Accuracy range increased by 40% - Critical hit chance increased by 30% - 5 additional percent of condition per repair action - Per-use condition [degradation](./Decay.md) reduced by 50% | When you aim down those sights the world melts away and there's only you, the Rifle, the bullet, and your target. The trigger is death. The trigger is life. |
- Bullets are more likely to cause a critical wound, and do more damage compared to arrows.
- Bullets cause less severe bleeding compared to arrows, resulting in longer bleed-out times.

The **rim grill** is an immovable [contained fire](./Fire.md#Contained_fires) introduced in the Errant Pilgrim update. The rim grill functions identically to other contained fires and player-made [Campfire](./Campfire.md). The rim grill provides no advantage over other contained fires, but it does allow protection against wind, unlike the player-made campfire. It has two [Cooking](./Cooking.md) slots.
The rim grill can be re-lit indefinitely, though it requires fresh starter, tinder, and fuel each time.

Currently, only four exist: the [cabin](./Cabin.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), one outside the [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md), one in [Indolent Hoppers](./Indolent%20Hoppers.md), and one near the [Pump House](./Pump%20House.md) (Caution, using the last location risks [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md)). There can also be a rim grill at the [Miserable Haunt](./Miserable%20Haunt.md) cave in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md), but it is not a guaranteed spawn.
In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) uses a Rim Grill as a fireplace inside the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md).

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Bah. It doesn't matter. Quake put an end to that. And things are changing."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Haven't you noticed? Since the lights in the sky? The world is quiet now."
