"_The old trapper is badly injured after a bear attack. He needs strong antibiotics to survive. He might know something about Astrid. You'd better keep him alive, if you can._"

**Risk of Infection** was the first mission of the Predux [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).

[Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) has rescued a trapper from a [bear](./Bear.md) but the old man is severely injured and will die without medical supplies. With information from a map behind the door, Mackenzie sets out to find the old [hydroelectric dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) that is located nearby. There are [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and [stones](./Stone.md) near the [trapper's house](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) if additional food is needed. Outside of the house is a container to use for storage. A short ways through the woods to the east, players will find the train tracks. Near the tunnel entrance is firewood and [rose hips](./Rose%20Hip.md). The tunnel is marked on the map but isn't usable yet. Follow the tracks north then slightly east to find [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md) and the [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md). Items to find include a key to lake cabin #3 (in a file cabinet on the main floor) and a hatchet near the stove.

To the west of the tracks farther north is a tower that contains miscellaneous items (food,[sewing kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md) , [bear hide](./Cured%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md), etc) and a lock box that requires 'Hank's Key'.

There are multiple buildings at the dam. The first trailer to the right doesn't have too much in it. The second trailer has a key in a locker that called the [Carter Hydro Staging Area Gate Key](./Carter%20Hydro%20Staging%20Area%20Gate%20Key.md) that unlocks the gate to the dam. Players will need this to get past the fence. The main entrance to the Hydro Dam building is past the fence. Entering the building starts a cut scene. A [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) kit is available on a shelf. The key for the office is on a body in the bathroom. The aid station key is in a desk drawer in the office. There is also a safe here that can be unlocked by deciphering the code (random). Watch for a distress pistol case on a shelf as well.

Near the dam is a run-down logging camp that has a few supplies. If players have found and read the required notes, there may also be caches located on the map to find. These seem to only contain a few supply items.

After arriving back to the cabin, another cut scene will begin. The trapper '[Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md)' is (hopefully) still alive and Mackenzie gives him the meds while the trapper talks more about the bear. The player can then ask him more questions about the bear, the trapper's pain and the area. The area takes it's name from Mystery Lake nearby. A few cabins nearby but not much else. The trapper lives alone but makes his way to Rupert's Landing to trade for supplies. He states that the island is mostly abandoned with a few scattered groups left. A rare supply boat travels to the island from the mainland - the only lifeline left for the few individuals still living on [Great Bear](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).

The cut scene continues and the trapper, convinced that the Old Bear is still on the prowl, offers Mackenzie a deal. Jeremiah is convinced that Mackenzie will never make it out alive without his guidance but the trapper can't kill the bear in his current condition. When Mackenzie asks what the trapper wants in return, the old man just says "We'll talk about that". The trapper offers Mackenzie his rifle, but unfortunately it was damaged when Mackenzie used it to 'scare off' the bear earlier and needs to be repaired. He gives Mackenzie directions to a machine shop at a railway yard, a day's travel south.
Several plot points and locations have been replaced/altered since the Redux re-release of Episode 2:
- All 3rd person cutscenes have been removed, including the opening cutscene, and the cutscene that takes place when first entering the dam.
- Jermiah's Wood Stove never burns out, displaying 4 hours remaining. This was fixed in the Redux, with an infinity (∞) symbol displaying instead.
- [Jeremiah's](./Jeremiah.md) [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and the shortwave radio are not on the [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) in [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md).

- The dead convict north of [River (Southern Access)](./River%20%28Southern%20Access%29.md) is missing in this version. He would be added with the note [Convict Journal Entry](./Convict%20Journal%20Entry.md) in the Redux.
- The [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) does not appear and attack [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) when first opening the Carter Hydro Dam Staging Area gates.

- The [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) Kit inside the Carter Hydro Dam was moved from a shelf to the bathroom with the [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) holding the [Admin Office Key](./Admin%20Office%20Key.md). The corpse would also hold the note [Forest Talker Dam Note](./Forest%20Talker%20Dam%20Note.md).
- The [Aid Station Medical Locker Key](./Aid%20Station%20Medical%20Locker%20Key.md) received a new 3D model in the Redux.

- A [Wolf](./Wolf.md) feasting on a dead [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md) is scripted to appear near the [Train Bridge](./Train%20Bridge.md) after leaving the dam with the [Carter Hydro Medical Supplies](./Carter%20Hydro%20Medical%20Supplies.md).

**Alternate Treatment:** Reach Level 5 [Cooking](./Cooking.md) to safely eat cooked meat

**Risk of Intestinal Parasites** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) caused by consuming raw or cooked carnivore meat: [Wolves](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), [Cougars](./Cougar.md), and [Bears](./Bear.md).
- It is only active in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) if playing on the Hardened Survivor difficulty.
- The Affliction is also present in the [Challenge](./Challenge.md) [As The Dead Sleep](./As%20the%20Dead%20Sleep.md).

Risk for Intestinal Parasites does not fill up as a meter to 100%, unlike many other Afflictions. Instead, the Affliction has a chance of being contracted 24 hours after the first piece of carnivore meat was consumed. All carnivore meat (ex. Bear or Wolf meat) has the same chance of causing parasites, regardless of type, condition, or weight. Cooked meat is not safe from Intestinal Parasites (until Level 5 [Cooking](./Cooking.md) [Skill](./Skills.md)), and raw meat is never safe (having an innate +75% chance and almost always giving [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md)).
Only the following pieces of meat, cooked or raw, contribute to Risk of Intestinal Parasites when eaten:

- ![Bear Meat (Raw) icon](../assets/Bear_Meat_%28Raw%29_icon.png) [Bear Meat (Raw)](./Bear%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md)/![Bear Meat (Cooked) icon](../assets/Bear_Meat_%28Cooked%29_icon.png) [Bear Meat (Cooked)](./Bear%20Meat%20%28Cooked%29.md)

- ![Cougar Meat (Raw) icon](../assets/Cougar_Meat_%28Raw%29_icon.png) [Cougar Meat (Raw)](./Cougar%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md)/![Cougar Meat (Cooked) icon](../assets/Cougar_Meat_%28Cooked%29_icon.png) [Cougar Meat (Cooked)](./Cougar%20Meat%20%28Cooked%29.md)

- ![Wolf Meat (Raw) icon](../assets/Wolf_Meat_%28Raw%29_icon.png) [Wolf Meat (Raw)](./Wolf%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md)/![Wolf Meat (Cooked) icon](../assets/Wolf_Meat_%28Cooked%29_icon.png) [Wolf Meat (Cooked)](./Wolf%20Meat%20%28Cooked%29.md)
The mechanics Risk of Intestinal Parasites are different than other Afflictions risks:
- After consuming a single piece of predator meat, the Affliction "Risk of Intestinal Parasites" will appear accompanied by a meter.
- The meter will fill up for every piece of predator meat consumed from that point on, at a rate of +1% for the first piece, +3% for the second piece, and +5% for each subsequent piece.

- After one full in-game day (24hrs) from eating the first piece of infected meat, the game rolls to see if you get the full affliction. The chance of being Afflicted occurs based how full your Intestinal Parasites Risk meter is. (i.e. 4% risk on the meter = 4% chance of getting Parasites after 24hrs). If you do not get Intestinal Parasites, the risk is cleared until more meat is eaten.

- If a survivor continues to eat infected meat, they will inevitably develop [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md), as the game will hard roll the Affliction after 6-9 Risk of Intestinal Parasites pass, even if the risk percentage is always at 1%.

Since Risk of Intestinal Parasites is only present before Level 5 [Cooking](./Cooking.md) [Skill](./Skills.md), it is most beneficial to **eat entire single servings rather than lots of small servings** before the Risk appears. Reaching Cooking Level 5 will remove any future Risk of Intestinal Parasites upon eating predator meat (Reaching Level 5 in Cooking **does** **not** remove preexisting risk of developing parasites, a parasite affliction contracted previously, or parasite risk from eating raw predator meat).

Using a [Meat Curing Box](./Meat%20Curing%20Box.md) to convert raw predator meat into [Cured Meat](./Cured%20Meat.md) will remove the Risk of Intestinal Parasites from the food, but this requires large amounts of [Salt](./Salt.md) and [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).

When playing on [Misery](./Misery.md), the [Sour Stomach](./Sour%20Stomach.md) Affliction removes the immunity from Intestinal Parasites that Level 5 [Cooking](./Cooking.md) provides, so predator meat will become a threat again after a certain amount of in-game days pass.
- [Stalker's Pie](./Stalker%27s%20Pie.md) will now give Risk of Intestinal Parasites, despite needing to be cooked at Level 5 which formally removes Parasites Risk.
- The rate at which the Risk of Intestinal Parasites meter is filled after consuming predator meat also changes with Sour Stomach; by an increased factor of 1.5:
- One piece now gives gives 1% meter risk, two pieces 6%, three pieces 13%, and so on.
- Despite all the types of fish caught from [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) being predatory, none grant Intestinal Parasites Risk when eaten (raw or cooked).

[^1]: Cooking Level 5 removes Parasites Risk, but is also required to make Stalker's Pie. [Sour Stomach](./Sour%20Stomach.md) will remove the Level 5 Cooking benefit when playing on Misery however, giving the player Risk of Intestinal Parasites when eating Stalker's Pie.

The Road Collapse, as its name implies, is a large collapsed section of road that runs through Crumbling Highway. It offers a bit of shelter from the wind and can allow the player to quickly escape out of reach of predators (depending on the direction one is fleeing from).
But, beyond that, the location serves as little more than a landmark. Wolves can spawn around the area. The path ahead leads to [Abandoned Mine No. 3](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md).

[Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) features a number of prominent **roads** which used to connect the [regions](./Region.md) and their various locations prior to the earthquakes and the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md). When visibility is poor, following roads can make navigation much easier.
These roads travel great distances through multiple regions of Great Bear Island, and are paved. There are three major roads, two of which are interconnected (Blackrock and Inland Highways).

This road starts at [Mirthless Fork](./Mirthless%20Fork.md) in [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) and goes over a long bridge. Soon thereafter, it's blocked by a rockfall, forcing the player to go through an ice cave to enter [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md). After going through a ravine and crossing over [Builder's Bridge](./Builder%27s%20Bridge.md), players can re-join the road as it follows a cliff above a river. Once in [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) the road is blocked again by a semi trailer at the [Blocked Bridge](./Blocked%20Bridge.md), forcing players to make another detour. After returning to the road, players will come to an intersection from which they may travel west or east.

Heading westward, the road passes by the [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md), before coming to [Narrow Bridge](./Narrow%20Bridge.md), where players will have to carefully walk on the beams to avoid falling into the river below. A landslide blocks the road at [Bear's Bend](./Bear%27s%20Bend.md), from which it continues northward to reach [Grand Meadow](./Grand%20Meadow.md) and finally the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md).

East of the intersection, players will pass the ruins of the [Jailer's Residence](./Jailer%27s%20Residence.md), before coming to another intersection. Going northward will take players straight to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) after passing one [vehicle](./Vehicle.md). Continuing eastward, the road crosses a wooden bridge and passes by [Cook's Farm](./Cook%27s%20Farm.md) and [Foreman's Clearcut](./Foreman%27s%20Clearcut.md), and, after a short walk, the transition cave to [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md).

Beyond the cave, this section of the road passes a small pond and the [Bricklayer's Retreat](./Bricklayer%27s%20Retreat.md), before turning generally northward and passing by [Wedge Cave](./Wedge%20Cave.md) and [No Road Cave](./No%20Road%20Cave.md). The road ends at the [Mule Bridge](./Mule%20Bridge.md), which is broken in Survival mode.

This road starts at the [Coastal Highway Terminus](./Coastal%20Highway%20Terminus.md), a fallen bridge in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). The road goes past the [Trailers west of the Cannery](./Trailers%20west%20of%20the%20Cannery.md) and the [Cannery itself](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md), before crossing over the [Long Bridge](./Long%20Bridge.md). An intersection leads up to the [Coast Mountain Road](./Coast%20Mountain%20Road.md) near the [Cannery Worker Residences](./Cannery%20Worker%20Residences.md), followed by a bridge at [Raven Crossing](./Raven%20Crossing.md). A [landslide](./Landslide%20%28Bleak%20Inlet%29.md) blocks the road as it heads to [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) itself.

In the Coastal Highway region, the same obstruction at the western end of the region is named the [Rockfall](./Rockfall.md). The road runs eastward skirting the coast, passing the [Fishing Camp](./Fishing%20Camp.md), and the [Log Sort](./Log%20Sort.md). A minor road to the left leads up the hill towards the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md). Then it passes the lower entrance to the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md), before arriving at the [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md). The road passes by the [Waterfront Cottages](./Waterfront%20Cottages.md) before being blocked again at the [Commuter's Lament](./Commuter%27s%20Lament.md), where it enters the [Old Island Connector](./Crumbling%20Highway.md). In this region, the road passes by the [Abandoned Harris Home](./Abandoned%20Harris%20Home.md) before being blocked at the eastern end of the region.

The road's section in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) runs below [Katie's Secluded Corner](./Katie%27s%20Secluded%20Corner.md) and goes past the [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md) and [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md), ending at [Broken Bridge](./Broken%20Bridge%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md).

This road starts near the [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) and passes by the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) [ connection cave](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md) and [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md) to reach [Milton](./Town%20of%20Milton.md). It then passes by the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) and comes to a collapsed tunnel where a [prison bus crashed](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md). Beyond this tunnel, the road enters [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), where a road to [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) branches off at [Mirthless Fork](./Mirthless%20Fork.md).

This road starts near the [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) and passes by the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) [ connection cave](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md) and [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md) to reach [Milton](./Town%20of%20Milton.md). It then passes by the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) and comes to a collapsed tunnel where a [prison bus crashed](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md). Beyond this tunnel, the road enters [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), where a road to [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) branches off at [Mirthless Fork](./Mirthless%20Fork.md).

The road then crosses a bridge and enters [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) at [Long Curve](./Long%20Curve.md). It passes near [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md), crossing over the [Heartbreak Bridge](./Heartbreak%20Bridge.md) and the [Contemplation Bridge](./Contemplation%20Bridge.md) to enter the small town of [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md). The road continues over a bridge. An intersection leads to the Mining Road and the Point of Disagreement Road. This road ends at a landslide aptly named [End of the Road](./End%20of%20the%20Road.md).
These roads generally travel shorter distances. Some of the more notable ones are listed below.

A short road that used to lead from the [Cannery Worker Residences](./Cannery%20Worker%20Residences.md) to the [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). It was broken in half by an earthquake, requiring a long rope climb near [Pensive Lookout](./Pensive%20Lookout.md) to get between the two sections.

These roads are in Pleasant Valley, and are generally level, travelling though fields and woodland. They connect the [Pleasant Valley Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) to the [farmhouse](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md), [Three Strikes Farmstead](./Three%20Strikes%20Farmstead.md), and the Inland Highway. Several wooden bridges may be found crossing the rivers in the region.

Leads from the [Vacant Depot](./Vacant%20Depot.md) to the [Main Hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md). The road first climbs up a short hill, then enters a narrow canyon. After some time it breaks out of the canyon, affording a view of the airport at [Whealy's Turn](./Whealy%27s%20Turn.md). It then re-enters the canyon before emerging into more open country at the [Junker's Paddock](./Junker%27s%20Paddock.md). Soon thereafter, the road branches in two, with one branch leading to the airport and another going through the flat, featureless landscape of [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) to eventually climb a hill leading to [Mindful Cabin](./Mindful%20Cabin.md).

This road in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) connects the Inland Highway to the [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md). It initially leads through some forest before climbing up steeply to the mine entrance.

Starting at [Vacant Depot](./Vacant%20Depot.md), this road parallels the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md), passing by some derailed railcars, a locomotive, and a [Chemical Hazard](./Chemical%20Hazard.md). It then passes through [Flagman's Gap](./Flagman%27s%20Gap.md) and heads near [Idle Camp](./Idle%20Camp.md), where a minor road branches off. This small road splits in two, with one branch leading to [Boss's Settlement](./Boss%27s%20Settlement.md), the other [Harrowed Residence](./Harrowed%20Residence.md). The main road passes through a couple more Chemical Hazards before arriving at the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) itself. From there, it continues southwards around the perimeter of the open pit, passing by the [Pump House](./Pump%20House.md) and [Overladen Pond](./Overladen%20Pond.md), before going through one more Chemical Hazard and ending at a trailer.

Starts shortly after the Mining Road in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) and is paved up to the [Derelict Cabins](./Derelict%20Cabins.md), at which point the road splits in two. The low branch gradually goes downhill towards the [Draft Dodger's Cabin](./Draft%20Dodger%27s%20Cabin.md) through the forest, crossing over a bridge along the way. The high branch slowly goes uphill, crosses another wooden bridge before coming to the [Point of Disagreement](./Point%20of%20Disagreement.md). From there, it makes a right, and players will see a broken-down cabin and the rope to [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md). The road ends at the [Misty Falls Picnic Area](./Misty%20Falls%20Picnic%20Area.md), and players may wish to rest-up in the [nearby cave](./Misty%20Falls%20Cave.md).

A road that starts roughly halfway between [Contemplation Bridge](./Contemplation%20Bridge.md) and [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), passing mainly through woodlands and generally slowly uphill. Notable landmarks include the [Picnic Spot](./Picnic%20Spot.md) and [Pensive Pond](./Pensive%20Pond.md) before coming to [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) itself.

This road starts at [Vacant Depot](./Vacant%20Depot.md) and is blocked by a landslide, forcing players to go around. It then continues along the edge of the mountain over [Baneful Bridge](./Baneful%20Bridge.md), passing [Lotte's Rest](./Lotte%27s%20Rest.md). From there, the road continues to hug the mountain, crossing over a river at [Cascading Gap](./Cascading%20Gap.md) before arriving into the alpine at [Placid Notch](./Placid%20Notch.md). At the [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md)-infested [Old Settlement](./Old%20Settlement.md), the road splits in half: one branch continues uphill past [Ambler's Lake](./Ambler%27s%20Lake.md) and [Final Refuge](./Final%20Refuge.md), ending at an avalance called [Unyielding Inundation](./Unyielding%20Inundation.md). The other branch crosses over a broken bridge before going quickly uphill, ending at the [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md).

A **Rock Cache** is a craftable form of storage that appears as a landmark on the player's [map](./Map.md).
Each Rock Cache can hold up to 30kg of items and up to 5 can be built per [region](./Region.md), for a total of 150kg of extra storage per region.

This makes them useful particularly in Regions such as [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) and [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) where storage containers are more limited. Furthermore, they will show up on the [map](./Map.md) when crafted and can be renamed remotely.
Rock caches can be viewed in the Journal, where the player can leave notes of what items are stored inside of it, making it a useful way to keep inventory.
Rock caches do not lose condition over time, but food and clothing items inside them decay as in other containers.

**Rope Climbing** is a gameplay feature in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. ![Rope over cliff. old version](../assets/Rope_way.png)_Rope over cliff. old version_

Rope climbing allows players to navigate up or down steep cliffs by utilizing a rope anchored on a specific rock at the top of a traverse. While most [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) will spawn pre-attached to a climbing spot, there are certain climbing spots that will never have ropes set up. A non-deployed Mountaineering Rope can often be found somewhere nearby, which can be attached to the climbing rock, and then used as normal. Deployed Mountaineering Ropes can be removed and then deployed at other climbing points.

![A climbing spot and sign in lower Milton Park near Milton.](../assets/Climbing_sign.jpg)_A climbing spot and sign in lower Milton Park near Milton._ Climbing is the most strenuous activity in-game, draining [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) and [Stamina](./Stamina.md) rapidly. When stamina reaches zero, the climbing rate slows significantly and there is a chance to slip and fall from the rope.

How fast one climbs is significantly impacted by current Fatigue level, carried weight, and Stamina. The cost of climbing a rope increases exponentially as Fatigue drops, since climbing speed is directly tied to Fatigue level and stamina. Having the Fatigue need satiated, full Stamina, and low weight will make for an easy, quick climb; the player will burn less calories and lose less Fatigue. Low fatigue, reduced stamina, and high weight will slow the rate of climbing. Since the rate of calorie and Fatigue burn is the same anytime a rope is climbed, the player will burn more Calories and Fatigue. It is very possible, especially on longer climbs, to run out of Stamina or Fatigue mid-climb if starting with a partially-empty Fatigue or Stamina meter.

Once Stamina and/or Fatigue reach zero, the player will become so slow that it may be impossible to complete a climb. In addition, reaching zero for both of these meters will result in a high chance of slipping, and the potential to fall. If climbing up, slipping will set the player back several meters, so it is wise to descend to an earlier ledge or the ground immediately when Fatigue or Stamina reaches zero unless you are within the final few meters of the climb.

Climbing is not possible if the player is encumbered, or has any [Sprained Wrists](./Sprained%20Wrist.md), [Sprained Ankles](./Sprained%20Ankle.md), or [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md). This means it is possible to become stranded at locations which require climbing to access (such as the bottom of [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) or the summit of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md)). Bandages can be life-saving to treat sprains in these circumstances, but Broken Ribs require [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md) or [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md) along with several days of rest.

If all options are exhausted, an [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) can be used to ignore these injuries for a very short period, and provide the opportunity to climb to safety. However, not only are stims incredibly rare, they will also completely exhaust the player once their duration expires. Stims will _not allow climbing while encumbered_, and any extra weight should be dumped before using a stim.

Select the deployed rope to begin climbing, then move forward to climb up, or backwards to climb down. Looking around while climbing is possible by stopping mid-climb, but Stamina, Fatigue, and Calories will continue to drain rapidly. It is possible to reverse climbing direction mid-climb, or stop and rest on a Ledge.

Some cliffs feature ledges midway along their rope course, and are suggested when the white selection dot appears. To enter a ledge, stop climbing and look at the ledge until it highlights, then select it. Resting at a ledge is recommended when climbing up a rope, as stamina can be recovered to increase climbing speed and thus reduce fatigue drain.
- There is always room for a fire and a sleeping bag. There will often be a few pieces of firewood also.
- Almost all ledges are very cold and exposed, especially if strong winds or blizzards are present.
When the character runs out of Stamina mid-climb, there is an increasing chance they will slip on the rope. The longer one continues to climb with no Stamina, the greater the chance of slipping.
- After slipping, they will slide down the rope until randomly catching themselves. How far one slips may depend on how much fatigue one has.
- When one starts slipping, it is not advisable to try to resume the climb. Descend quickly or enter a ledge and rest before trying again.

- If one slips as far as the ground, it is equivalent to falling from the original height and bruising injuries, sprain [afflictions](./Afflictions.md), and [condition](./Condition.md) loss will be received accordingly, along with severely tearing clothes.

Descending takes far less stamina and is less impacted by fatigue. However, slipping and falling is still possible. Select the rope between where it is tied off but before it turns over the cliff. Move backward to go down. It's possible to stop mid-climb and look around, if desired. If there is no rope available, or the player is encumbered, it is sometimes possible to "mountain goat" down a cliff. The trick here is to select a location with the fewest number of overhangs possible, and crouch-walk. As long as the slope of the cliff is anything less than vertical, the player will not fall. This technique must be used carefully, however; sprains and minor condition loss are likely, and one miscalculation could result in a lethal fall.

![Rope tied off. old version](../assets/Rope_tie-off.png)_Rope tied off. old version_ Mountaineering ropes can only be attached to or detached from a specific rock formation at the top of a sheer cliff (see image for example of formation; looks like a sharp tooth about 3 meters high). To deploy a rope from inventory, simply select the middle of the rock when close. To detach and take a rope, select the rope where it wraps around the rock. Rope will automatically be placed in inventory. Attaching/detaching a rope takes about 10 minutes.

Note: Stamina for climbing is not affected by the Sprint Penalty statistic of worn clothing, but is derived from the same Stamina meter used for sprinting. It is not wise to Sprint prior to a climb without allowing Stamina to recover.
- It is recommended to always stop and recover stamina on a ledge if it is safe to do so (described below); often a requirement for long climbs.

- [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) and [Cup of Acorn Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Acorn%20Coffee.md) does NOT affect the fatigue drain rate of rope climbing, but can help with rest recovery before the climb. However, wearing [Crampons](./Crampons.md) and [Improvised Crampons](./Improvised%20Crampons.md) reduces Stamina drain when climbing, thus speeding up the process and preserving Fatigue (for long ropes only. If Stamina is more than 25% there is no difference)

- Drinking a [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) before starting will immediately restore 60% of the player's fatigue and completely fill their stamina. However, the [Headache](./Headache.md) and 50% loss of fatigue after the drink wears off can harm the player.
- Using an [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) for temporary infinite Stamina allows one to climb with ease, but the emptied fatigue meter afterwards can be crippling.

- Sleeping with a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), [Improvised Down Bedroll](./Improvised%20Down%20Bedroll.md), or [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md) prior to a climb, or on a Ledge mid-climb, can be useful to restore Fatigue. Be aware that sleeping outdoors on Ledges can result in death via freezing to death if a blizzard rolls through, so sleep before attempting a climb.

- In many areas, it is usually possible to avoid climbing down ropes by carefully dropping down nearby slopes and small ledges, a technique often referred to as "[Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md)", or "scrambling". The trade-off is that this method usually carries a high risk of sprains and falls.

- Note that one major exception exists: dropping into the [Ravine Basin](./Ravine%20Basin.md) will result in automatic death due to a kill-box. This is left over from earlier versions of the game, since the basin could only be accessed via rope climb prior to the addition of [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). Scrambling down would strand the player had they not deployed a rope prior.

- In a few rare cases, it may even be possible to avoid a rope climb by navigating up sloped terrain (for example, one can reach the [Lake Overlook](./Lake%20Overlook.md) by marching up the hill in front of the [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md)). Even more so than dropping down, climbing steep terrain comes with a high risk of sprains.

- For players with [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) installed, eating [Rose Hip Pie](./Rose%20Hip%20Pie.md) or [Peach Pie](./Peach%20Pie.md) before climbing or at a ledge can be helpful to restore Fatigue (15% worth). It may also be useful to eat a [Ptarmigan Pie](./Ptarmigan%20Pie.md), [Rabbit Pie](./Rabbit%20Pie.md), or [Venison Pie](./Venison%20Pie.md), as those will increase carrying capacity by 3 kg.
Rope Climbing was introduced on 16 December 2015 in [version 0.298](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.298) also known as the Timberwolf Mountain update.

**Rose Hip Tea** is a natural medical and food item used to treat [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_.

Rose Hip Tea functions similar to [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md) for treating Afflictions, and is cooked from one [Prepared Rose Hips](./Prepared%20Rose%20Hips.md) (24 [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md)) and 0.25 liters of [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) at a lit [Fire](./Fire.md). Consuming prepared Rose Hip Tea (even without treating an Affliction) restores 100 Calories, 30% Hydration and potentially grants the benefit "[Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md)." Cooking Rose Hip Tea increases [Cooking Skill](./Cooking.md).

Prepared Rose Hips are crafted from 24 Rose Hips and takes 15 minutes (in-game) to prepare. Rose Hips can can be found in the wilderness growing on Rose Bushes, typically in clusters of 1-4 units, a single Rose Bush yields 8 Rose Hips when Harvested. Rose Hips can be found rarely inside of containers. They cannot be directly consumed and must first be crafted into Prepared Rose Hips and then cooked into Rose Hip Tea.
- [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md) (2 doses and 2 [Bandages](./Bandage.md), and 120 hours of [Sleep](./Sleep.md))

The effect of Rose Hip Tea is not generalized throughout the body, and each dose will only treat one injury, and should be applied to the injuring requiring them as treatment (e.g. "Broken Ribs" and "Burns" will display as separate Afflictions, with each requiring separate doses to treat).

As a source of Vitamin C, Rose Hip Tea can also be used to treat [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) and [Scurvy Risk](./Scurvy%20Risk.md). This is especially useful in regions where [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) isn't possible or practical, as Rose Hips are relatively common throughout the world. However, this is generally not a long-term strategy as the tea only contains 13% Vitamin C, and will only stave off the affliction for a day or two.
Prepared Rose Hips have half the weight of their raw form, and no form of Rose Hips [Decay](./Decay.md).

**Rose Hips** are a natural medical and food item used to treat [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_.

Rose Hips can can be found in the wilderness growing on 2 types of Rose Bushes. Grey ones typically grow in clusters of 1-4 units, while green ones grow on or near [Rock Climbs](./Rock%20Climb.md). A single Rose Bush yields 8 Rose Hips when Harvested. Rose Hips can be found rarely inside of containers. They cannot be directly consumed and must be used in the cooking recipes such as [Camber Flight Porridge](./Camber%20Flight%20Porridge.md) and [Rose Hip Pie](./Rose%20Hip%20Pie.md), or crafted into [Prepared Rose Hips](./Prepared%20Rose%20Hips.md) and then cooked into [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md).
Prepared Rose Hips weigh 0.05 kg, or around 1/5 of what 24 Rose Hips (their crafting materials) weigh, and no form of Rose Hips [Decay](./Decay.md).
- Harvesting 3 Rose Bushes (at 8 Rose Hips each) is required to craft 1 unit of Prepared Rose Hips/Rose Hip Tea.

- Rose Hips are found sporadically in all regions growing on Rose Bushes, particular in mountainous areas near ledges or cliffs. They frequently are near entrances to [Caves](./Cave%20%28disambiguation%29.md), Rose Climbs, deployment points for [Mountaineering Ropes](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md), and secret locations.
- Teas may be heated/reheated to grant the Warming Up Benefit by placing them on a fire's cooking spot, or nearby a lit fire.
- Broken Ribs are permanent if left untreated, though Pain and Burns will dissipate naturally with time (4-30 hours).

- Pain has minimal effect on gameplay (aside from blurry vision) with it's only limitation being an inability to read [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) while afflicted, and subsides automatically with time. This generally makes treating Pain a wasteful decision, to carry Painkillers consume them instead of reserving their use to treat Broken Ribs or Burns.
- Painkillers cannot be crafted and Rose Hips do not regrow; however Painkillers are renewable via [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md).
- Teas are more weight efficient than Water for the Hydration they grant. (0.1kg of a tea grants 30% Hydration, equivalent to 0.25kg of water).

- The condition of Painkillers decays slowly over time (based on [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md)). Upon reaching 0% Condition, they become unusable and will disappear if inside of a container, but all forms of Rose Hips do not decay.

- Rose Hips (also known as Rosehip, Rosehep or Rosehaw) are a [real world plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_hip) and accessory fruit to Rose Bushes, similar to their in-game representation including their use as a painkiller.

- Real-World Rose Hips have a history as a [poverty food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famine_food), particularly with Native American peoples during survival situations or times of hardship, as well as for ornamental purposes.

- In The Long Dark, Painkillers and Tea must be applied directly to treat a specific injury (similar to a Bandage), unlike real-world orally-taken drugs which become generally distributed through the body.

It is a frozen waterfall found in the valley below the [Cascading Gap](./Cascading%20Gap.md) bridge. **DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.
**Running River Oats** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in The Long Dark.

Running River Oats is a inedible ingredient use to cook [Porridge](./Porridge.md) or [Camber Flight Porridge](./Camber%20Flight%20Porridge.md). 1 container of Oats can be used to make 8 bowls of Porridge (roughly 2800 calories if just used for Porridge, or 8000 calories if used to make Camber Flight Porridge).
Running River Oats can often be found alongside other cooking materials such as [Cooking Oil](./Cooking%20Oil.md) and [Salt](./Salt.md).

When used for Porridge, Running River Oats has an excellent calorie density of 3500 kcal/kg, making it an efficient travel food on par with [MRE's](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md). Its low decay rate further increases its usefulness as a travel food.

| [Camber Flight Porridge](./Camber%20Flight%20Porridge.md) | None | - 0.05 kg × [Maple Syrup](./Maple%20Syrup.md) - 4 × [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) - 0.50 kg × [Pinnacle Peaches](./Pinnacle%20Peaches.md) - 0.20 L × [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) - 0.10 kg × [Running River Oats](./Running%20River%20Oats.md) |
| [Porridge](./Porridge.md) | None | - 0.25 L × [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) - 0.10 kg × [Running River Oats](./Running%20River%20Oats.md) |
The side of the can lists "Ingredients: Whole Grain Rolled Oats, Sugar, Salt, Natural Flavours."

> “**Light nylon shoes designed to feel weightless. Better than running around barefoot but ... not much.**”

The running shoes are a common starting item. They're lightweight, but they don't offer much warmth or protection, and the waterproofing is nonexistent. It is recommended to replace them, as they don't offer much of anything, and it is highly ill-advised to repair them, as they require valuable cured leather for repairs, and they only give 20% condition back per repair, making it extremely expensive to repair, especially for an inferior item. However, the shoes should still be picked up when found, as they can be harvested for two pieces of cured leather, which can be used to repair top-tier shoes such as [Mukluks](./Mukluks.md) and [Insulated Boots](./Insulated%20Boots.md).

The **Rural Store**, also known as the Rural Gas Station or Thomson's Market, is a small convenience store in [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), across the road from the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md).
The Rural Store consists of two rooms: The main store in the front area, and a back room.

The main area has several shelves, a checkout place with a [Register](./Register.md), and a few fridges. Food like [Beef Jerky](./Beef%20Jerky.md) and [Crackers](./Salty%20Crackers.md) can be found on the shelves, while [Cash](./Cash.md) and matches can be found near the register and sodas will spawn in the [Fridges](./Fridge.md). First Aid items such as [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md) can spawn on the shelves. A Sewing Premier [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) is often hidden on the counter next to the fridge.

The back room holds a [Metal Shelf](./Metal%20Shelf.md) with a [Microwave](./Microwave.md) and [First Aid Kit](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md) with 2 [Lockers](./Locker.md). Ammunition casings can sometimes be found under the shelf and lockers.

In Wintermute, the store holds 2 [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md) related to 2 quests. The first is a book called [Local Legends - Sasquatch](./Local%20Legends%20-%20Sasquatch.md) related to the mission [Tall Tales](./Tall%20Tales.md).

The **Rustic Table** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.
A makeshift wooden table, a Rustic Table can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The table can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value, the table cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the table will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).
The Rustic Table can be harvested with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) in 1 hour 30 minutes for 6 [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md).

Has an interior **Rüdiger's Machine** is the unofficial name given to a location found inside the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md). The location can only be accessed by completing the [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md) Tale.

A mountainside entrance near the 6th floor of the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md) is initially locked when playing in Survival Mode, but can be opened as part of Buried Echoes. The [Mine Gate Key](./Mine%20Gate%20Key.md) to the mountain entrance can be found deeper in Level 3 after progressing through the Tale, and then passing through the mountain. When reaching the room with the device, the survivor will attempt to touch it but pass out, only to reawaken to find it powered at midnight during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md).

A nearby control room contains several collectibles for the Tale, as well as the [Foreman's Tool Belt](./Foreman%27s%20Tool%20Belt.md). The Machine does not have any amenities inside, such as Beds, Work Benches, or Fireplaces.

- The Machine is what caused the mental deterioration of [The Foreman](./The%20Foreman.md), the mine workers, [The Security Chief](./The%20Security%20Chief.md), and [Dr. Rüdiger](./Dr.%20R%C3%BCdiger.md), among others.
- Though the Machine is associated with the [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) that plagues the Far Territory, it is not the source of it.[^1]

> “**Move furniture and decorative props around your favourite locations in the game. Repair broken items and clean up the mess. Craft items from an entirely new series of hand-made furniture and decorative props. Collect and move every framed pancake photo in the game to one place. Make pretty much any valid interior in the game your personal Safehouse with this powerful system.**”

With the release of [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) Part 6, players have the option to customize a [Safehouse](./Safehouse.md) by rearranging furniture, crafting new furniture, hanging portraits on walls, and many other activities.

There are over 800 items that can be moved, broken down, and in some cases, built using this system. There are 150 areas that can be turned into Safehouses, along with several specific "exterior interiors" like the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md) in Timberwolf Mountain, and the Lookout Towers.
When entering an interior that can be customized, an icon of a house will appear in the top left corner of the screen.

- Pressing Y (L1+ R1 on controller) will cause a pencil to appear in front of the house and the player to enter Customization Mode, and the game will show a blue outline over every object that can be moved around.
- The blue outline shown over every object in Customization Mode can be used to navigate through the dark, without having to use a light source.
- You can put things on the floor, the walls, on top of other items, etc. But every item has info that tells it where it can and cannot be placed. This is to avoid silliness.
- You can remove Clutter (like shredded papers on the ground) by pressing the R button (you cannot get it back once this button is pressed).
- You can craft a [Framed Photo](./Framed%20Photo.md) from photos you take using the [Camera](./Camera.md) and even craft/loot [Decorations](./Decorations.md) to display inside any Safehouse.
- Pressing Y (L1+ R1 on controller) again will leave Customization Mode, and cause the game to start saving (this is also a useful way to force an autosave).
- [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) are required to fix things, and repairing items raises the [Repair](./Repair.md) skill.

- Currently you can repair a lot of the broken/missing [Cabinet Doors](./Cabinet%20Door.md) of kitchen [Cabinets](./Cabinet.md). Repairing restores them to their "original" state, and also restores all the container slots (so a Cabinet that had been missing a door and just had an empty space, now has the door and the door becomes a new valid container).
- Destroying/Harvesting the Cabinet Door will make it impossible to repair that cabinet.

- The roofs of the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md) and [Bricklayer's Retreat](./Bricklayer%27s%20Retreat.md) can be repaired (costs 20 [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md)). Repairing these roofs will increase the temperature bonus inside the buildings by +3 C.
Some items in Customization Mode cannot be placed into the player's inventory, they can only moved around or destroyed (typically large items).

Harvestable items can be destroyed quickly, but the player will not receive any materials for doing so (ex, destroying a [Pillow](./Pillow.md) takes 2 minutes and gives nothing, but harvesting it with a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) takes 9 minutes and generates [Cloth](./Cloth.md)). Keep in mind that destroying/moving some objects, like sheet metal or [Planks](./Planks.md) covering holes in the [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) floors, can create fall hazards.

- Interior spaces only have a select zone that can be customized by the player. Walking outside of the Customization Zone (usually by exiting to the outside of the building via a door) will issue a warning to the player. Anything outside of this zone behaves normally and cannot be customized.

- [Work Benches](./Work%20Bench.md) cannot be moved between safehouses, but the Vice can be removed from an existing Work Bench by destroying the entire object, and then used as a raw material in the construction of a new Work Bench. This means you can build a Work Bench in a location that is more useful to you, but only by sacrificing an existing bench, so there are still only ever going to be a certain number of Work Benches in the world. When you remove the Vice from an existing Work Bench, it becomes a regular table.

- You can still Break Down items to get resources from them when in regular gameplay. When you're in Safehouse Edit mode, you can Destroy items which goes quickly but you don't get any resources from it. This was to give you a way to clear areas quickly without making it magical or without some reasonable trade-off. If you want to harvest things for resources, don't destroy them in Edit mode.

- You can't destroy containers that have items in them. For example, if you want to destroy a cabinet but there are items in one of the drawers, you will have to remove the items first. Keep in mind that if you destroy an item in a Safehouse, you can't rebuild it, so please be careful what you destroy because you may not be able to get it back.
- [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) and [Corpses](./Corpse.md) cannot be destroyed or moved, only "respectfully removed" as part of general Safehouse clean-up.
This feature is very memory intensive, so it's very likely there will be a hard limit on consoles for how many items you can have inside an interior:
- Building limits for console (Xbox, PlayStation) is likely be in the 100s of items per scene.

In general, you can take most decorative items (ex. wall hangings, vases, plates, etc.) and add them to your Backpack in the [Decorations](./Decorations.md) section. They have weight, so you will want to account for that when you move them around (some can be 5.00kg). The [Travois](./Travois.md) can be a potential way to move large amounts of Decorative items around the world.
A [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md) and [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) are required to build furniture for a Safehouse.

- Items that only have a Decorative value will live in the Decorations section of the Backpack Inventory, and won't appear in the General tab to avoid your inventory being cluttered with a bunch of random stuff that doesn't have gameplay value.

- When you drop decorative items in the world, they spawn a small [Safehouse Decoration Box](./Safehouse%20Decoration%20Box.md), because these items don't exist as "gear items" outside of Safehouses the way normal gear items (like food, or tools, or clothing) do.
The following locations support Safehouse Customization. Keep in mind that inside and outside customization zones are counted separately due to loading zones/outdoor customization boundaries.
Note: [Prepper's Abandoned Cache](./Prepper%27s%20Abandoned%20Cache.md) can be destroyed at the end of [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md), rendering it inaccessible as a Safehouse.
- [Trailer (Blackrock Region)](./Trailer%20%28Blackrock%20Region%29.md) on the road to the Power Plant
- The cafeteria break room next to the rope climbing building (building itself can't be customized, even the upper floor that the rope leads to)
The number of safehouses in this region are lowered if playing on [Interloper](./Interloper.md)/[Misery](./Misery.md) due to ruined buildings (labeled as I/M)
- Trailer West of [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) transition to Pleasant Valley

- Cabin near [Point of Disagreement](./Point%20of%20Disagreement.md) (sometimes spawns ruined)

The **Safehouse Decoration Box** is a Container that is created when [Decorations](./Decorations.md) are dropped on the ground. It was introduced as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.

Any Decoration dropped onto the ground will appear inside this box. Each box is immovable, like all containers, which can be a problem if placed inside a doorway since the player cannot walk over them.

Facing cupboards and cabinets will place the box on the surface, instead of at the player's feet. ![Safehouse Decoration Box placed on a dresser](../assets/Safehouse_Decoration_Box_on_a_dresser.jpg)_Safehouse Decoration Box placed on a dresser_ Once all items in a Safehouse Decoration Box are removed, the box disappears. Since items can freely be moved inside up to the 100 kg (220 lbs) capacity, this box is ideal for storing excess or unneeded Decoration items in one place in the player's [Safehouse](./Safehouse.md).

![Safe House](../assets/Safe_House.jpg) In an open-world experience like _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, the player needs a safe, sheltered location to return to in order to recover their mind and body from the hazards of a nomadic lifestyle. A deliberate mechanic that separates _The Long Dark_ from other survival games is that it does not provide the player any means to create a customized shelter from scratch. As such, the player will need to find a pre-existing location to call their temporary home as they explore the island. In a world as unforgiving and hostile as [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), **Safe Houses** are indoor sanctuaries that allow a player to survive and thrive through the permanent winter of the Quiet Apocalypse.

Safe Houses sometimes acts as a "gate" for narrative progression — I.E. events that advance the story or change the world state may only occur when the player returns to the safe house, as they often act as out of harm's way for interacting with story NPCs.

Due to the sheer size of Great Bear Island, many players will need to create 1 or 2 "Home Bases" within a region, usually located near the direct center or near the entrances and exits of a region. These safe houses serve as the primary "area of operations/home base" used as supply storages from which survivors can store or restock on needed supplies for long term survival. Large buildings that generally safe to navigate to in the world and that contain [Beds](./Bed.md), Fireboxes, [Work Benches](./Work%20Bench.md), [Ammunition Work Benches](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md), or [Forges](./Forge.md) are considered the most valuable locations to start a safehouse. Outdoor caves can also be used as safehouses but are generally used to combat [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) on higher difficulties.

Long-distance travel between locations might require the establishment of temporary camps for shelter and rest. As such, returning to a previously used safe house can provide much needed shelter and supplies when traveling between regions.

There will always be a constant pull on the player to find a pre-existing shelter in order to create a Safe House, as the tension between wanting to remain in the warm and sheltered vs. returning to the open world to scavenge supplies and complete objectives is one of the main drives of self-directed sandbox gameplay of The Long Dark.

The primary purpose of Safe houses is to offer protection from the cold, bad weather, and hostile wildlife. A place to warm up is always in high demand when navigating the world, with even temporary safehouses providing opportunities to create [Fires](./Fire.md) to warm one's self.

Blizzards are frequent across the island, and being caught outside is a death sentence even with the warmest clothing, unless the player finds an indoor shelter. Safehouses not only provide refuge from storms, but also a place to dry wet clothing.

Predators such as [Wolves](./Wolf.md) and [Bears](./Bear.md) are unable to enter buildings, and as such provide a quick go to location to escape potential attacks. They also provide safe locations to tend to injuries acquired from hostile wildlife. Multiple entry doors are an advantage to escape predators.

Most abandoned buildings can be looted for food, resources, and tools vital to survival. Chairs and furniture can be torn down or broken up to provide [Cloth](./Cloth.md), [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), and [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) for repairs and crafting. Misplaced tools such as [Hacksaws](./Hacksaw.md), [Hatchets](./Hatchet.md), [Hunting Knives](./Hunting%20Knife.md), [Flashlights](./Flashlight.md), [Storm Lanterns](./Storm%20Lantern.md), Firearms, Ammunition, [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md), and [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) can be found inside many buildings. [Clothing](./Clothing.md) found in drawers or out in the open can be used to warm one's self. Toilets can provide clean drinking water (if you can stomach it) and kitchens can be raided for food and water, as well as [Can Openers](./Can%20Opener.md), [Cooking Skillets](./Cooking%20Skillet.md), [Cooking Pots](./Cooking%20Pot.md), and [Recycled Cans](./Recycled%20Can.md). Bookshelves sometimes hold valuable [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) that can be read to increase your knowledge of the world by improving your [Survival Skills](./Skills.md).

Indoor locations are ideal for [Cooking](./Cooking.md), as fireboxes can be used to provide heat, cook food, boil snow, etc without fear of freezing. Fireboxes located indoors are also more reliable than [Campfires](./Campfire.md), which can be blown out by strong winds.

Clothing and Tools will eventually decay with age and use, and thus must be repaired. Spending time in a safe house provides the perfect opportunity to safely restore clothing and tools to working functionality.
Saplings and Hides can be cured over time by dropping them on the floor of indoor spaces. They can stay on the floor even after curing, and can be picked up when you are ready to craft.

A good place to do some crafting or item repair beyond simple maintenance, many buildings in key locations within regions contain a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) for crafting high tier Clothing and Tools. Most of the animals hides and saplings you cure should be stored in these safe houses for crafting at a later date.

[Forges](./Forge.md) and [Furnaces](./Furnace.md) are a rare find in several coveted safe houses. They provide the only way to create [Improvised Knives](./Improvised%20Knife.md), [Hatchets](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), and [Arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md) and are vital locations to visit in order to survive on Interloper difficulty.

[Ammunition Work Benches](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) are another rare feature found only in 2 safe houses, providing the ability to craft [Gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md), create [Bullets](./Bullet.md), and reload spent shell casings. Ammo workbenches also come paired with [Milling Machines](./Milling%20Machine.md) for repairing tools with Scrap Metal, when the lights are on that is.

The player will eventually tire in their travels, and as such a warm bed is a great reason to establish a safe house. “Using” a bed will bring up an analog watch interface that you can set to advance time. Resting will reduce your [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) and will advance certain health-related conditions (i.e., healing or the progressing of illness) and is also a useful way to advance time while staying warm.

Beds are crucial in the beginning days of Interloper runs, as the player does not start with a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md). Knowing locations that contain beds is vital for surviving on this difficulty until the player can scavenge or build a Bedroll.

Safe houses are the go to sanctuaries to store excess gear, as the player cannot carry the whole world on their back. As such, safe houses with many containers can be used to store clothing, tools, repair components, weapons, food and water, fuel, first aid equipment, etc.

You can also store miscellaneous items that you find in the world that you think might be useful, but don’t necessarily want to carry around with you wherever you go. Stored items may also serve as caches from which a player can resupply when needed.

You will always be alone in the world, thus you are entirely responsible for your own survival choices. Being able to create short and long term goals is critical for your survival and is usually impossible to do when the player is constantly worrying about their immediate personal safety. Even as a blizzard roars outside the walls of your dwelling or as predators scratch at the doors, a Safe House provides a player not just a warm and dry place to rest and escape the dangers of the outside world, but time to think. Remember, the key word in Safe House is "Safe."

This provides the player the chance to formulate future goals, reflect and learn from past mistakes, plan routes for excursions to distant locales, study maps and the layouts of regions, take stock of supplies of personal supplies and eliminate excess baggage from your inventory, and most importantly, provide a moment to have even the smallest glimmer of peace of mind, and thus hope for the future.

There are several locations on each map that offer good amenities to help in your attempts for survival. It is always strongly advised to have a bed and a fireplace of some sort indoors (or an indoor location that allows campfires). A [workbench](./Work%20Bench.md) is a bonus, as well as some containers for resource storage, although this is less critical as [they can be built](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) in most locations as long as there's enough floor space to fit them. If [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) has been purchased, being able to get a [Travois](./Travois.md) up to your safe-house is highly desirable.

Also listed are the general characteristics of each map regarding its suitability for long-term survival. Note that these ratings are slightly subjective, and depend on your particular gameplay style and the difficulty level.

Having interior cooking is desirable, as it enables you to cook in any weather without having to worry about a campfire being blown out by high winds. The number of cooking slots available depends on the firebox present, with [forges](./Forge.md) and [pot belly stoves](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md) having one slot and [cooking stoves](./Stove.md) having six. Most other fireboxes have two cooking slots. Some locations may have multiple fireboxes.

Having a bed in your safehouse may be essential if you don't have a bedroll, but even if you do, a stationary bed is preferable over a bedroll as it restores more condition per hour and reduces the rate at which your bedroll degrades. Most safehouses have a bed, but if your preferred location does not, you can build your own bed on [the appropriate workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md) with the right [tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) and materials. If you go this route, you [have](./Rustic%20Bed.md) [three](./Quilted%20Bed.md) [options](./Bear%20Hide%20Bed.md) to choose from.

Having a spacious safehouse is useful as larger locations tend to have more containers to store things, as well as more floor space to cure hides and saplings. You'll also need lots of floor space if you're planning to build your own furniture, as some of the larger pieces can take up a considerable amount of space.

Being able to harvest some [cloth](./Cloth.md), [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md), and [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) inside your safehouse is desirable, especially in bad weather, though these resources are finite and become less important if you're planning on staying in the same location for an extended period of time.
Having multiple doors is useful if you're being chased into the safehouse by aggressive wildlife, or if you're trying to leave and there's an aggressive animal outside one of your doors.

All of these are useful for creating advanced items. But by far the one you'll use most often is the [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md). Luckily, if a location doesn't come pre-equipped with one, it can be built by harvesting the [vice](./Workbench%20Vice.md) from annother workbench. Forges are only necessary for creating [arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md), [improvised hatchets](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), and [improvised knives](./Improvised%20Knife.md); you won't need to make them often, so being close to a forge is a lower priority. [Ammo Workbenches](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) and [Milling Machines](./Milling%20Machine.md) are found together. You likely won't use either very often, so being close to them is generally not particularly important.

Dangerous wildlife is just as the name implies: the average predator density in the area immediately around the safehouse. In this guide, an assessment of "low" means predators will only be encountered sporadically in the surroundings. If "high", expect to run into hostile wildlife most of the time when moving to and from the location. If it's rated as "medium", expect to see dangerous animals sometimes, but not all the time.

> “**Move furniture and decorative props around your favourite locations in the game. Repair broken items and clean up the mess. Craft items from an entirely new series of hand-made furniture and decorative props. Collect and move every framed pancake photo in the game to one place. Make pretty much any valid interior in the game your personal Safehouse with this powerful system.**”

With the release of [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) Part 6, players have the option to customize a Safe House by rearranging furniture, crafting new furniture, hanging portraits on walls, and many other activities.
Due to the sheer amount of information that would otherwise further clutter this page, see the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) page for more info.

Surviving here is generally easy to moderately difficult. There's plentiful shelter, and the weather here is only slightly worse than in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md). You have a [Forge](./Forge.md) close by in [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md), and deer to hunt on [Little Island](./Little%20Island.md). Inside [Hibernia](./Hibernia%20Processing.md), you've got almost limitless storage space and a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md). If you stay on the ice, you should be able to avoid most of the wolves in the area (watch out for them on the roads, especially in Stalker!). Be careful if you want to explore the big [Cave](./Cave%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md) in Desolation Point, for a wolf lives there and can be quite difficult to shoot in the dark. If you do manage to kill it, though, you'll have two deer carcasses to harvest in safety.

This place has a lot, but not everything. It has some good storage, as well as a bed and a stove, though the lack of floor space makes adding custom furniture a bit tricky. It also offers one of the best views in the game, and the top of the lighthouse makes a good spot to fight cabin fever. However, there is no workbench. The closest one is as far away as Hibernia, and even that can be a dangerous journey. While it is possible to build a workbench in the lighthouse, the limited floor space may make it difficult to find a place to place it. There aren't any wolves near the lighthouse itself, but they are often found at intersection leading to the lighthouse, making entering/leaving challenging. However, this remains a good base.

This place has, again, a lot. All the storage and floor space you could ever want combined with the triple threat: a bed, a workbench, and a fire barrel, making this a strong base location. Sure, there are wolves and sometimes a bear around, but as long as you stick to the side closest to the ice, you most likely won’t run into them. And with proper planning and good weather, the gatehouse off the entrance from the road can serve as a safe location from which to hunt the bear that often wanders past the processing plant.

This is one of the more popular bases in the game, and for good reason. Both the forge and the furnace make this place a place you’ll likely be familiar with by late game, and a bed on the second floor, a somewhat remote location away from predators, and protected outdoor space on the top deck contribute additional value. Little Island is also close by for hunting. Overall, this is a good spot to live in. The one weakness of this location is that the interior tends to be extremely dark, even in daytime, making it very difficult to navigate without the use of a [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) or [Torch](./Torch.md).

Surviving in Coastal Highway is generally pretty easy. The weather is the mildest of any region and there's lots to be found in the various houses scattered throughout the region. Forging is easy, as a trip to [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md) is only a day's walk away, and there's plenty of buildings that are perfectly suited to calling your home, though Jackrabbit Island and the Quonset Garage (see below) are two of the most popular. If you need lamp oil, there's lots of fishing huts all over the ice. The only danger here is the somewhat high density of predators. On the ice, they're rather easy to avoid, but they can sneak up on you unexpectedly in the forest. On Interloper difficulty, where the cold is likely to be your worst enemy, Coastal Highway is about the easiest place to survive.

It has two workbenches, a bed, and a fire barrel, as well as a central location, lots of storage, and plenty of space to add more furniture. The primary reason one wouldn’t want to live here is due to the many wolves and occasional bear that patrol the area. For a well-supplied and well-armed survivor, however, these drawbacks could serve as a solid supply of meat, gut, and hides.

Although it lacks both a workbench and a fireplace, it has a bed and possibly some of the best rabbit hunting opportunities in the game. It also has a porch to store meat on, as well as a good amount of storage inside the house itself, along with plenty of opportunity to rearrange the furniture as you see fit. A fishing hut is also located just outside your front door, as are beachcombing areas. On top of all that, wolves rarely come up onto the island.

This house has many of the same features as the one on [Jackrabbit Island](./Jackrabbit%20Island.md) to the west, but it is a two story house and features slightly more storage. It can be a good safe house to use if you ever run out of rabbits at Jackrabbit Island for some reason, and is the closest safe house to [Sutherland's](./Trader.md) dock if you're planning to trade.

This region is one of the most challenging to survive in for any significant amount of time. While there is fishing available as a food source and the ammunition crating workbench is close by, along with a nearby [Forge](./Forge.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), the region is full of [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md). Regardless of how careful you are, you're going to get into a fight with them sooner or later. The region's also very windy and chilly, lacking good shelters aside from a cabin in the northeast, the Cannery Worker Residences, and Pensive Lookout. For most players, there's little reason to live here for an extended period of time, unless you want a challenge.

This location can make a decent safehouse. Being located on the plateau, the nearby population of timberwolves isn't as high as along the coast. It also contains a [Pot Belly Stove](./Pot%20Belly%20Stove.md), a commanding view of the entire region, and a good vantage point from which to hunt timberwolves or [Deer](./Deer.md). The major disadvantage of this location is the need to travel [down a long rope](./Rope%20Climbing.md) to go and forge, and that it can be rather cold, especially in harder difficulty modes. It is also a relatively small location, limiting the amount of custom furniture the player can add.

Another decent place to call home, this location has nearby [Deer](./Deer.md) hunting opportunities, a decent amount of storage, sufficient floor space to add some furniture, and a rim grill to cook on. There are occasional timberwolves around, but they shouldn't be too much of a problem. The cabin can be somewhat chilly, due to having a hole in its roof, and it's located a long distance from the [Cannery Pier](./Cannery%20Pier.md)'s [Workshop](./Workshop.md).

This location offers nearby ice fishing opportunities, is located near the center of the map, features a [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md), and decent hunting and trapping opportunities. If you need to cook a large amount of meat or fish, it's only a short stroll over to the [Fallen Lighthouse](./Fallen%20Lighthouse.md) to use its six-burner stove. Downsides to this location include a [Bear](./Bear.md) that sometimes wanders over, as well as the occasional presence of Timberwolves, and that this cabin is quite small, limiting customization opportunities.

This is all the regions in Lower Great Bear which require traveling through Pleasant Valley to access.

This region might be "advanced" according to its official description, but, especially since the Crossroads Elegy update, it's really of more of a moderate difficulty region. While it _is_ a large region with changeable weather (resulting in a considerable risk of getting [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) on Interloper), there are quite a few bears and wolves, and it's easy to get disoriented in the featureless fields, you should be fine as long as you don't wander off the roads and you pay attention. There's plenty of food and clothing to start you off in [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), and the [Crash Site](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) is loaded full of food and clothing too. Hunting opportunities are plentiful, and you're highly likely to find some excellent loot in [Misty Falls Cave](./Misty%20Falls%20Cave.md). Don't forget [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) either, which often has an [Expedition Parka](./Expedition%20Parka.md).

Central location, storage, workbench, fireplace AND stove, nearby rabbits and fishing, good hunting, enclosed porch, a substantial supply of cloth and other useful materials, and overall appeal--all of these qualities make the farmstead a great location to call home. Potential drawbacks include fairly common patrols by wolves and an occasional bear and that Pleasant Valley has frequent blizzards and bad weather, so a player could be forced to stay inside for several days at a time. Other than those concerns, the farmhouse serves as a great location to live for extended periods of time.

Located in [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), the Community Hall is a solid choice as a base, given its relatively central location, proximity to multiple other structures, plentiful rabbit and deer hunting, loads of kitchen cabinets to put things into, and having both a stove and a fireplace. Wolves and a bear do occasionally wander through town, but they tend to stay north of the river most of the time. The main disadvantage of living here is the lack of a workbench, requiring the player to travel to the Pleasant Valley Outbuildings to do crafting. However, there is plenty of floor space in the building to players to construct their own workbench.

This location has a lot, but not everything. It has plenty of storage, an interior workbench, and the view from the summit is second to none. The exterior is surrounded by a fence, reducing the chances of running into wolves when entering/leaving. While there are quite a few wolves just east of here, they can be safely hunted from the [Hunter's Blind](./Hunter%27s%20Blind.md). One slight weakness of the radio control hut is that the fire barrel is outside, however, this could be advantageous as it results in longer burn times. Also, it's worth mentioning that Signal Hill is fairly close to the southeastern side of the region, making it less than central.

**Keeper's Pass** is a transitional region that connects [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) to the [Blackrock Region](./Blackrock.md). It is made up of [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md), a connecting [cave](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md), and [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md).

This is the only man-made structure with a interior in the [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md). The fire is exterior, but it has an interior [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md). Sometimes rabbits spawn in the area, but so do wolves, so be careful. There's a [fishing hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) in the nearby river, but beware that the path back goes through wolf spawns.

This is the only man-made structure in the [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md). Because wolves can't spawn in this area, the cold is your only enemy here. Although it offers little shelter from the elements, it does have a [Wood Stove](./Wood%20Stove.md) to keep the player warm and a bed to rest with. Rabbits spawn in the area offering a potential food supply. Due to the linearity of Keeper's Pass North, this cabin acts as a necessary waypoint when traveling through.

Home to the infamous [Blackrock Federal Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), this region is one of only three to have [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) in survival mode. If the timberwolves aren't enough to keep you on your toes, the region frequently has poor weather, along with being quite isolated from much of the rest of Great Bear. That being said, there is an ammunition crafting workbench here, along with a fair amount of shelter, so living here is a certainly not impossible.

Probably the most useful place to call home is the prison. While living in the prison itself isn't really that feasible, as most of it is destroyed and difficult to navigate, there are lots of outbuildings that can make a good base, and there is a workbench and ammunition crafting readily available. Be careful of wolves living just outside the prison yard, however. If the prison outbuildings don't offer enough storage, another option is to expand into the interconnected [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md).

If living in a prison isn't your thing, you might want to consider living in the old substation. It is located towards the southwestern corner of the map, and features a workbench and fire barrel on site. Downsides to living here include the lack of deer nearby, making rabbits the only long-term food source, and the presence of timberwolf packs.

The greatest downside of living here are the packs of roaming timberwolves nearby, as well as the lack of a contained fire; the closest one is located at [Cook's Farm](./Cook%27s%20Farm.md), a walk which may be hazardous in higher difficulty levels or in poor weather.
