This region is notorious for its frequent blizzards, lack of shelter, and high predator density. However, if you know where to go, there are large areas of the map that don't have many predators, and don't forget the [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md)! If you have a [hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) (and you're not playing Interloper), you'll find all the supplies you'll need to start off within the first few days. With good clothing, you can use the caves with interiors as long-term bases, as they're warm no matter the weather. Just remember: **bring a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md)**. The importance of this here can't be overstated, as once you leave the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md), that's it for guaranteed beds. A bedroll usually spawns in the cave nearest the summit, but it may be unusable if it spawned at low condition and you didn't get to it in time.

Due to its cold weather, Timberwolf Mountain is quite difficult to survive in when playing Interloper, but the plentiful loot in the cargo containers in Stalker and lower difficulties can make up for its poor weather, moderating the challenge somewhat.

Located immediately adjacent to [Eric's Falls](./Eric%27s%20Falls.md), this cave provides a 10oC warmth bonus, and acts as an indoor area, allowing hides/guts to be cured inside. It's also not too far from the [Summit](./Summit.md), allowing the player to gather loot from there after two rope climbs. There are plenty of [rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [deer](./Deer.md) and [wolves](./Wolf.md) to hunt nearby, but those same wolves can be problematic to ill-equipped players. A [bear](./Bear.md) occasionally wanders nearby. The cave doesn't offer any cooking, storage or sleeping quarters, but a [campfire](./Campfire.md) can easily be lit inside, regardless of the weather, a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) can serve as a bed, and items can be stored in the [Cargo Container](./Cargo%20Container.md) along the river nearby (except in Interloper).

This is probably the most popular safe house in Timberwolf Mountain. It is located near [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md), which has a [Fishing hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) on it, a [Rabbit Grove](./Rabbit%20Grove.md), plentiful [deer](./Deer.md) hunting opportunities, and [cattail plants](./Cat%20Tail.md) for tinder and emergency food. The downside of this location is that a [bear](./Bear.md) sometimes visits the area, it's not a particularly warm location, and there is a decent chance of [wolves](./Wolf.md) being in the area. It's also quite a hike from the [Summit](./Summit.md), limiting its usefulness for looting expeditions.

Survival here is slightly easier than in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) or [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md). This is largely because this region has lots of natural resources and high-tier loot, similar to the former, but it also has several shelters scattered throughout. The main challenge of living here is to not get lost, as there are many canyons and plateaus of differing elevations, all connected via climbing ropes. Oh, and try not to fall off the rope bridges when you're crossing them... it's a long way down. Overall, survival here is moderately difficult.

This cabin might be small, but it proves that sometimes size doesn't matter. It's centrally located and has got a workbench, pot belly stove, and comfy bed. There's a huge trunk next to the workbench to put your stuff, along with a smaller metal container underneath the bed. The old furniture atop the bed can be broken down to give plenty of reclaimed wood, but there's no curtains to break down for cloth.

The main disadvantage of this location is that although the area immediately surrounding the cabin is safe, wolves guard every path away from the cabin. They patrol the southeast path towards Bitter Marsh, the bottom of the rope climb in the southwest that leads to Pillar's Footrest, the path near Broad Falls to the northwest, and around Long Falls before the cave that provides access to the upper areas of the region. On top of that, the weather in Ash Canyon is often very cold, limiting the amount of time the player can spend outdoors, and it is quite a long walk to both the fishing hut on [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md) and any sort of hunting, limiting access to food beyond cattails and wolf meat.

This location just south of [Miner's Folly](./Miner%27s%20Folly.md) has a lot, but not everything. It features both a [wood stove](./Wood%20Stove.md) and a [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md), several storage containers, and a decent amount of harvestable wood and cloth. While there isn't a workbench located inside, one can be found very close by at Miner's Folly (outdoors), and it can be disassembled and moved inside if desired. [Deer](./Deer.md) can be found around Miner's Folly too, along with a [Bear](./Bear.md) for those brave enough to hunt it. The main disadvantage of this location is that going any substantial distance requires crossing multiple high rope bridges, and the fact that [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) itself is a rather isolated region.

The Homesteader's Respite is located towards the northeastern part of Ash Canyon, next to an old mining facility. One of this location's main advantages is that predators never spawn around the house, and that it is located close to good [deer](./Deer.md) hunting grounds around [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md) (wolves do spawn there too, so be careful). If the deer should run out, there's a broken-down ice fishing hut on Bitter Marsh, too, providing yet another source of food. So what's not to like? The largest disadvantage of living here is that getting supplies from Bitter Marsh requires climbing up a rope, which may be difficult if you're tired late in the day. Another disadvantage is that there's no workbench, and the closest one is located in [Angler's Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md).

This is all the regions in Lower Great Bear which require traveling through Mystery Lake or Forlorn Muskeg to access.

Mystery Lake is a popular region for long-term survival, and with good reason. It has relatively few predatory animals compared to most other regions, Ice Fishing opportunities on its [namesake lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md), temperatures are fairly mild (though not as mild as [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md)), and the layout of the map is not especially complicated, so getting lost is less likely than on many other maps. Even forging and ammunition crafting aren't a problem, for it's not too far to [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) or [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) to do said activities. There's lots to hunt all over the map, along with [an entire dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) to loot for essential supplies. Overall, Mystery Lake is a good location to live in for an extended period of time, especially for new players. Survival here is arguably slightly easier than Coastal Highway in difficulties other than Interloper, due to its fairly low predator density.

Big and centrally located, it offers lots of storage space, two fireplaces, multiple beds, and a workbench, as well as back and front doors for easy escape from wolves. Its central location makes it a great hub for exploration and hunting expeditions. While predators don't generally roam too close to Camp Office itself, they do often patrol both the lake and the [Derailment](./Derailment.md) near the office, so some caution is advisable. If the player is struggling with [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), they may sleep in the cave at [Lake Overlook](./Lake%20Overlook.md) or in one of the fishing huts on the lake.

The dam does not have a bed, but a bedroll can be used instead. A portable building outside the upper entrance contains bunk beds if a bedroll is not available. Some drawbacks include a remote location far away from most other key locations in Mystery Lake and somewhat limited hunting opportunities in the surrounding area.

The Ravine is a great place to call home. It's one of the only regions to have no predators.

Ample rabbits and deer are nearby. There's lots of [Birch Bark](./Birch%20Bark.md) here, making recovery easier on harder difficulties. [Rock Caches](./Rock%20Cache.md) can be created for storage. A fire may be required to stay warm, but when necessary, the player can safely navigate to the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) in a blizzard.

This region is possibly tied with [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) for being one of the hardest to survive in. As if weak ice and roaming predators weren't troublesome enough, this region is very chilly and windy, with frequent fog and no interior locations (aside from a cave in the north of the region). It is extremely easy to get lost, and the region doesn't really offer anything that other regions don't have to warrant living here. Unless you want the ultimate survival challenge, just come here for the [forge](./Forge.md), do your forging, and go back to another region that's easier to live in.

More suited as a location to spend the night than as a long-term safe house, this location offers a [fire barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) inside, along with often spawning a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md). It provides some warmth bonus, but if the weather gets chilly, you'll likely need to start a fire to keep yourself from freezing. If you need food, you can hunt the [bear](./Bear.md) that often wanders nearby, if intestinal parasites aren't a concern for you.

The ease or difficulty of living in Broken Railroad depends a lot on the game's difficulty setting and what gear you have/don't have. Although you do have a [forge](./Forge.md) nearby and a [giant lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md), along with decent weather, one of the biggest issues you'll face is [wolves](./Wolf.md)... _all the time_. Especially in Stalker. If you have a [bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) and [arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) and are proficient with them, (or you have lots of ammo for your firearm) they, along with the [bear](./Bear.md) near the foot of the cliff, can provide a great source of food... however, if [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) are enabled and you're not a level 5 cook, the meat's not really all that useful. [Deer](./Deer.md) aren't all that common, so you'll be eating a lot of wolf and bear meat. To summarize: Broken Railroad is fairly easy to survive in in Voyageur or if you're a level 5 cook, but quite challenging in higher difficulties.

One of the best places to stay since it has everything you may desire, even if dangerous, due to the presence of numerous wolves. If [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) becomes a problem, you can sleep in the bed in the front office. The disadvantages are that's not really the most cozy base and it's also really cold, especially in Interloper. Last but not least, generally having a base in Broken Railroad is actually not recommended because this region is isolated compared to the others (same consideration can however be made with Desolation Point too).

One major downfall of living here is the frequent presence of [wolves](./Wolf.md) right outside the door, as well as the possibility of encountering a [moose](./Moose.md) in the same area. Finally, the Broken Railroad is not a very central region; as a result, visiting other regions may be challenging.

Although this region is supposedly "easy", it can be harder to survive here than you think, especially for somebody new to the game. Sure, there's tons of shelter in [town](./Milton.md) and lots of buildings to search through, along with a fair amount of hunting and foraging outside of town... but Mountain Town is known for having a lot of [wolves](./Wolf.md), even on lower difficulties, and has a couple tricks up its sleeve, like the [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) needing a key and the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) needing a [prybar](./Prybar.md) to open. This large house is an excellent base early on in the game, as it is located close to the Town of Milton and its many lootable structures. One disadavantage of this location is it doesn't have an indoor workbench located nearby (though one can be moved inside), and [wolves](./Wolf.md) tend to visit the town fairly often. On the other hand, [deer](./Deer.md) hunting is not difficult in the [Wood Lot](./Wood%20Lot.md) nearby, and there are plenty of structures to duck into if a wolf does attack.

Much like [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), this region is wild, with very few manmade structures. Although it can be difficult to orient yourself with this region, once you know where you are, it is absolutely brimming with natural resources and hunting opportunities, and the ice caves offer great shelter no matter what the weather (do be careful -- one contains a [wolf](./Wolf.md)). If you're caught away from an ice cave, you can always use one of the other caves, which do provide a warmth bonus. Predator density is moderate, and who's going to say no to the ability to carry an extra 5kg using the [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) (doesn't spawn in Interloper). How about having up to four wolf carcasses ready to harvest? There's a [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md) right there. With the exception of a [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md#hushed-river-valley) and [Bunker Gamma](./Bunker%20Gamma.md), **there are no beds in this region: you must bring a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md).** The nearest [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) is in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) unless [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) has been completed, enabling access to Bunker Gamma's workbench. The nearest [forge](./Forge.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), so keep that in mind. Overall, this region is moderately difficult to survive in once you know the layout.

There are two of these in the region. The first has an entrances near [Reclusive Falls](./Reclusive%20Falls.md), [Mammoth Falls](./Mammoth%20Falls.md), and the northwestern corner of the map, somewhat north of [Hushed River](./Hushed%20River.md). The other one has entrances near [Valley View Point](./Valley%20View%20Point.md), [Long Shot Falls](./Long%20Shot%20Falls.md), and the southern portion of the map, some distance from [Lonely Cave](./Lonely%20Cave.md). Both caves are generally above freezing, and are the only locations within the region where this is the case, and have interior rooms complete with [campfires](./Campfire.md). One cave can have a [wolf](./Wolf.md) spawn inside, so be careful when you first enter. Both caves offer plentiful resources near their entrances, but are very easy to get lost in. Additionally, [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) is required to travel through them. The caves also have waterfalls and icy cold flowing rivers in them, which can wet the character if care is not taken.

This cave is located by going to [Monolith Lake](./Monolith%20Lake.md) and staying on the lake's southern shore, then travelling east as far as possible. At the top of the hill, you will come to this cave. Peak cave is arguably one of the best locations for long-term survival in the region, as it has an abundance of [rosehips](./Rose%20Hip.md), [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md), and [mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) very close to it, along with [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) on the southeastern corner of the lake for providing food. Zone of Contamination is arguably the best region to spawn in the Far Territory, as it offers a large amount of loot and plenty of indoor shelter in and around the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md). However, living there for an extended period of time is much more challenging: the wolves are inedible, and the hunting grounds in the more pristine parts of the region are located far from buildings. Survivors who choose to live here will likely want a [Travois](./Travois.md) and be prepared to dodge the many [chemical hazards](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) in the region.

The Idle Camp is a fantastic base for the region. Being an old miner's barracks, there are beds, industrial toilets to scavenge water, various miners clothing, and a stove in the nearby mess hall. A [Train Shuttle](./Train%20Shuttle.md) is found just down the road near the camp and often contains rare Mining Clothes. A few Trucks are located in the camp so that one can sleep outside to manage Cabin Fever. The only downside is that a nearby field has [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) that occasionally spot the survivor and wander into the camp. While there's no workbench in the camp itself, there are several around the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) that can be broken down and rebuilt.
| Type | Cooking slots | Bed | Workbench | Storage | Harvestable | Doors | Forge | Danger wildlife | Notes |
| Camp | 6 | Yes | No | Large | Moderate | 4 | In the Main Hangar, 1/2 regions away | low | Poisoned Wolves sometimes wander into the camp from the nearby field |

This house, far below the treeline in a forest, is teaming with Deer, Rabbits, and Wolves that can be hunted for food. A [Green Birch Sapling](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) and [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) can spawn behind the house, with plenty of Rose Hips and Reishi Mushrooms to be found throughout the forest. [Seedling Spring](./Seedling%20Spring.md) to the south and [Giant's Thumbprint](./Giant%27s%20Thumbprint.md) to the north are two ponds deep enough to create Free From fishing holes for Ice Fishing.
- Seedling Spring has an outdoor cave, [Miserable Haunt](./Miserable%20Haunt.md), nearby for shelter and for dealing with Cabin Fever
- Gaint's Thumbprint has an indoor cave, [Idle Hideout](./Idle%20Hideout.md), nearby for shelter

The house itself has a Fire Barrel outback next to a Work Bench, and the indoor has a Wood Stove and a Fire Place. The only major issue with this location is that the bedroom is locked off until the player progresses enough through each [Tales](./Tales.md) until they unlock [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md), where they must head to the [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md) to find [An Old House Key](./An%20Old%20House%20Key.md) after acquiring the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md). If the player unlocks the back room, a Bed is available, along with a Safe to crack and the one of a kind [Tactical Gloves](./Tactical%20Gloves.md). If the player cannot unlock the bedroom, then it is advised to craft/bring a Bedroll to sleep inside.

**Salt** is a [seasoning](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) and preservative in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Salt is used as an ingredient in numerous cooking recipes. Most recipes that uses Salt tend to need 0.01 kg of Salt, meaning one Bag of Salt can be used in 1000 recipes. However, they are far more useful for creating a [Meat Curing Box](./Meat%20Curing%20Box.md), which is a survivor-made [Decoration](./Decorations.md).

8.00kg of Salt is required to construct a Meat Curing Box, which can be used to turn raw meat into jerky to make the meat last for much longer. Curing Meat will slowly deplete a Meat Curing Box's store of Salt over time, which must be replenished for continued use.

Smaller jars of [Salt](./Salt.md) (0.25kg) can be found as loot usually in kitchens or food-related areas, while large bags of salt (10.00kg) can be usually acquired from [The Trader](./Trader.md) as they rarely can be found in the world.

[Salt Deposits](./Salt%20Deposit.md) can be found on coastal rock formations (e.g. outdoors on [Jackrabbit Island](./Jackrabbit%20Island.md), or inside [Abandoned Mine No. 3](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md)) and harvested by hand. Each Salt Deposit yields multiple units (0.25kg) units of salt, with multiple deposits appearing in groups.
- The side of the bag lists "Ingredients: Rock Salt." It also lists Nutrition Information but the info cannot be read.

A **Salt Deposit** is a harvestable interactable object found along Coastal Regions in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Most tools can be used to scrap Salt from Salt Deposits, despite the tool-less warning message saying it requires a Hatchet. These include any [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) (or variant), [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) ([Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md)), [Prybar](./Prybar.md), or [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md). The [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) will not work. Tool condition does not degrade when harvesting Salt Deposits.

Each Salt Deposit is composed of several small interactable deposits which each produces 2 [Salt](./Salt.md) (0.25kg) when harvested. They can be useful for keeping a [Meat Curing Box](./Meat%20Curing%20Box.md) topped off with large amounts of Salt or for preparing [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Recipes.

**Salty Crackers** are a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Consuming Salty Crackers provides 600 calories of [energy](./Hunger.md), at the cost of a substantial -20% [hydration](./Thirst.md). They can be found in all regions, but are commonly found inside houses and stores. Salty Crackers have the highest caloric density of any food item at 6,000 calories-per-kilogram (if the weight of water needed to restore that lost by consuming Salty Crackers is considered, their energy density is 2600 calories-per-kilogram).
It is ideal to consume Salty Crackers (and other dehydrating food) when at low hydration, or even when fully dehydrated to preserve water.

Salty Crackers never [decay](./Decay.md), but are unique in that they can still cause [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) if spawned at low condition. They only lose condition during a [Bear](./Bear.md) attack (or Toxic Fog during [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md)).
- Salty Crackers are packaged as a product called "_Standard Fare"_, possibly a play on the real-life saltine cracker brand "Premium."
- The back of the box lists "Ingredients: Wheat Flour, Soybean Oil, Sugar, Baking Soda, Salt, Natural Flavours."
- Despite being packaged in a cardboard box, no [Tinder Plug](./Tinder%20Plug.md) is produced by consuming Salty Crackers and the item cannot be harvested.

![Three Degrees of Stench|center](../assets/ScentMeter.png)**Scent** is a mechanic in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ which increases the distance which [predators](./Wildlife.md) can detect the survivor by smell. Scent is increased when the survivor is carrying meat and fresh guts, and is affected by wind speed, wind direction, and game difficulty experience. An approximation of current Scent is represented by the "Scent Meter."

A player's Scent makes them detectable to wandering wildlife. Meat and guts increase the character's odor when carried. Prepackaged foods produced before the Quiet Apocalypse have no odor and are therefore no longer detectable by animals at all, making them safer to transport.

If the player has 1 fresh gut, 1 raw meat/fish, or 3 cooked meat items in the inventory, they will have1 Scent Indicator. Each Scent Indicator increases the range at which the player can be detected by 10 meters, as well as creating longer ranged "Points of Interest" which nearby Wolves and Bears will approach investigate. Items dropped on the ground do not produce Scent, although meat/guts/carcasses dropped with the Decoy ability ("3") will create a 30m circle around the item, flagging other possible food items for wolves to consume.

Wind is a factor that the player should be aware of; being upwind of an animal will decrease the range at which it can smell you; however, it may still see or hear you regardless of wind direction. The Scent Meter is a toggled element which approximates the survivor's current Scent amount; the more "Scent Marks" the survivor has (colored white), the higher the survivor's scent and radius they can be detected by predators. It can be viewed under Quick Stats (TAB key) or Status (F key). ![Scent Upwind Downwind](../assets/Scent_Upwind-Downwind.jpg)

- Scent only affects predators ([Wolves](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), [Bear](./Bear.md), and [Cougar](./Cougar.md)): attracting them to the player's general area, but not necessarily to their current location.
- Bears have the most sensitive noses of any predator, and will travel over half the map in search of the player at higher scent levels, far outside of their normal patrol pathways.
- The greater the Scent, the wider radius a predator can detect it. If unscented, predators can only detect the survivor by sight and sound.
- Predators only seek Decoys they can see, but can detect Scented items when carried by the survivor regardless of terrain.
- Having high scent when the wind blows on the player will carry the scent downwind, affecting predators.
- Odorous items produce a set amount of Scent, regardless of Item condition or weight (ex, a raw quarter bag always produces 50 Scent Value).
- Stacked Scented items (e.g. Coastal Fishcakes and Fishing Bait) only count per-stack, not per item. This does not apply to Raw Gut.

- The Scent Meter shows three indicator icons but Scent does not follow actually hard breaking points. E.g. a piece of cooked meat will not yield one Scent Meter icon, but can still be detected by predators.

[Wolves](./Wolf.md), [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), [Bears](./Bear.md), and [Cougar](./Cougar.md) are attracted to the smell of game. This can be troublesome when the character is carrying fresh steaks back to camp after quartering a carcass and predators begin to stalk and attack the player. **Decoys/Baiting** can be used to a player's advantage to distract or lure these animals away from/to the player.

The 'Drop Decoy' button is provided to automatically drop the smelliest item in inventory. Repeated pressing will repeatedly drop bait until none remains. Bait items may still be manually dropped from inventory, but this is a slower process than some players would like when facing a predator.
- Manually selecting a piece of meat in the Radial Menu, then placing it on the ground.

Giving up a whole salmon to avoid being mauled may seem like a fair trade, but there is an even more economical way. A 0.01kg sliver of cooked meat will be just as effective as a whole 1.00kg piece of cooked meat.

The game is a little stingy in how it lets you handle your meat, but there are quite a few options to make economical Decoys. Further letting these small portions rot to the point of ruined will also ensure they are the first items dropped even when you are carrying other meat.
- Aborting while eating by pressing the 'esc' key will result in a partial portion remaining.
- Increasing a harvest option to maximum and then reducing back down may result in a partial portion being selected for harvest. Repeat the harvesting action to obtain multiple small portions.
Predators are the only animals to be affected by Scented Decoys, and follow a predictable set of behaviors:
- When a predator has detected an unscented character, it pursues and stalks them until sight is lost or they attack.
- When a pursuing predator detects the smell of a bait but not the player however, it will walk directly to the first detected location of that decoy instead.
- Once they reach the spot the smell came from, they will then search the next location where the player is and look for the origin of the Scent.
- The player can continuously avoid a predator that is searching for them until they make eye contact, in which case they begin stalking the player.

- Predators stalking a Scented player are far more aggressive, attacking sooner and showing less fear from the player's attacks. This includes shrugging off more damage and showing less fear of handheld light sources/[Campfires](./Campfire.md).
- If predators reach Decoys without detecting the player, the predator will instantly consume it and wander around a bit.

- The entire Decoy food item will be consumed the moment it is reached by a predator, regardless of weight. This includes entire 10.00kg bags of quartered animal bags being gulped down in one bite (somehow).

- If the player is detected by a predator and drops a scented item and the animal eats it, they retreat briskly away from the player to a safe distance. They will eventually return to stalk the player if they do not leave the area however.
- This can be done to multiple animals stalking the player, assuming that they have enough Decoys to sate all animals following them.
- Player's can be attacked in their sleep if they are sleeping out in the open and their Scent is high. The player will awake and then be forced into a Struggle if an animal reaches their position.
- The player can still be attacked even if they drop all scented items before sleeping, should said items be close to them.

- Wolves, Poisoned Wolves, and Timberwolves will change from a slow walking speed to a brisk jog the moment Scent hits their noses. They will walk to the first location where the scent came from, then continue moving to the player's last known location if they are still carrying Scented items.
- Bears will slowly turn and walk towards the player's position and begin walking outside of their normal patrol paths to find the scented item.
- Cougars will begin to leave their Territory and find the player if their Scent is too high.
- NOTE: Charging predators will not be distracted by bait! Always try to drop bait before a predator starts charging to avoid attack
- Baited animals are not blind and will charge when they see you are within striking range, so keep your distance and stay hidden.

- Predators are unable to detect bait when they are unable to detect the character. They will not notice it or eat it if you are not around. This can be useful for storing large amounts of cooked meat outdoors to preserve their Condition.
- Wolves and Poisoned Wolves will stalk the player and growl as normal. If the player drops a Decoy, then Wolves as they cease their growling and instead go for the Decoy.

- It is generally advised to avoid using this tactic on [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) packs. Despite the fact that they attracted to the smell of Decoys, they will ignore it if they detect the player.
- Decoys will distract a Bear that is stalking the player. They will ignore Decoys if they start charging.
While a predator is tracking bait, it is not tracking the player, so you could drop the bait and just walk away.

- Since you now know the animal will walk directly to your offering, you might take the opportunity and line-up a clean shot, positioning yourself to have the bait directly between you and the predator so it walks head first toward you.

- Another tactic can be to use the animal's retreat to position it where you like. Since the animal will retreat away from the player when it reaches the bait, you can determine in which direction that will be. As noted above, you can also now follow it to herd it along perhaps even shooting it in the back when it gets to where you want it.
- The Decoy key ('3' key) may be used to quickly reduce Scent. Each time it is pressed, a carried Scented item will be dropped.
- The most odorous, lowest condition items are always dropped first, then descends in order from there.
- Meat/Meals can be mostly eaten by the survivor but still dropped as a decoy, by eating and aborting the action (ESC).

- Survival Mode affects Scent significantly (Stalker as the highest, followed by Interloper/Voyageur, with Pilgrim as lowest). On harder modes it is beneficial to minimize carrying scented items, and to drop them as soon as possible (such as immediately upon harvesting/cooking).
- Crouching while manipulating Scent (picking up and dropping scented items) can be used to manipulate predators to specific locations, or to attack other wildlife.

- [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail%20Stalk.md) and artificial foods are a scent-free way of traveling if the player is worried about Wildlife attacks. This is especially helpful when passing through Timberwolf or Cougar territory.
[^3]: 1 Scent bar is added only when 3 separate stacks of these items are in the player's inventory due to bug

The Scrap Metal Shard is identical in functionality to a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), but weighs less (0.30kg vs 0.50kg of a knife). It can be used as a self-defense tool, harvesting [animal](./Wildlife.md) carcasses, [Cloth](./Cloth.md) from curtains/pillows, tinder from cardboard, breaking ice for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md), and crafting at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md).

It is obtained automatically in [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), pulled straight out of [Will Mackenzie's](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) hand and placed into his inventory during the mission [The Crash](./The%20Crash.md). The Shard does not appear if the player starts Episode 2 out of order.

If the Scrap Metal Shard is kept in the player's inventory, it may be taken into [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md). It is ultimately lost after starting [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) (likely tossed with the rest of Mackenzie's gear by [Mathis](./Mathis.md)).
Scrap Metal Shard can be repaired with a [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md) and the [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) skill, restoring 3% condition to the Shard.
Scrap Metal Shard can be used in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md), causing a Wolf some condition damage.

- The Scrap Metal Shard is a fragment of Will Mackenzie's aircraft, with a bloody cloth as a handle. It is impaled straight through Mackenzie's left hand after the plane crash, where he pulls it straight out of his hand upon noticing it. This is considered to be a very unwise first aid practice, as the shard is most likely stopping the majority of the bleeding.

- Afterwards, Mackenzie is required to bandage his hand and a cloth bandage is shown on his hand until the beginning of [The Grey Mother](./The%20Grey%20Mother.md), where it disappears along with any sign of the wound on Mackenzie's hand.
- The Scrap Metal Shard originally could not be repaired with Whetstones in the Predux Wintermute. This was changed in the Redux Episode 1 redesign.

**Scurvy Risk** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_. It is caused by consuming a diet with low/no Vitamin-C, and results in [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) if left untreated.

Scurvy is a long-term affliction caused by Vitamin-C deficiency: failing to consume as much Vitamin-C as is drained daily. Each day the survivor's Vitamin-C level decreases by a small amount from a hidden Vitamin-C meter; this loss can be mitigated or recovered by consuming foods with Vitamin-C.

- Foods with Vitamin-C display roughly how much they contain on the item's information page ("Minor", "Moderate" or "Major" source of Vitamin-C). If a food item contains no Vitamin-C (or on a game mode where Scurvy is disabled) no amount will be shown. Condition of food items does not affect Vitamin-C values.
Scurvy Risk appears when below 20% of the Vitamin-C maximum, and will progress into the Scurvy affliction unless more Vitamin-C is consumed.

Most Vitamin-C food sources are finite (artificial foods and cattails), which can make Scurvy an increasing challenge in the late-game. However fish, and to a lesser extent [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md), are renewable sources.
![Scurvy Enable option warning](../assets/Scurvy_Warning.jpg)_Scurvy Enable option warning_

violations.context: > __Fail to eat a balanced diet and Scurvy will hound you relentlessly. While the onset is slow, the consequences can be disastrous to your health. The choice is yours.
> __Fail to eat a balanced diet and Scurvy will hound you relentlessly. While the onset is slow, the consequences can be disastrous to your health. The choice is yours.

Starting a Survival Mode save file presents the option to enable Scurvy to that save. If enabled, foods with Vitamin-C will be labeled as a Minor, Moderate, or Major source of Vitamin-C when examined.

Scurvy is present on [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md), [Stalker](./Stalker.md), [Interloper](./Interloper.md), and [Misery](./Misery.md) modes, and is disabled in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) and [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md).

Scurvy can be prevented by regularly consuming enough Vitamin-C foods to prevent Scurvy Risk from reaching 100%. Scurvy Risk will appear when the survivor's hidden Vitamin-C stat drops below 20% remaining, giving the survivor a warning several days before the true affliction occurs.
- Vitamin-C is a hidden survivor statistic, and is not displayed on the [Status Screen](./Survival%20Menu.md).
- Vitamin-C begins at 500 units at the start of a new Survival Sandbox (or upon treating Scurvy)
- A small amount of Vitamin-C is drained each day (10 units on Voyageur or 20 units on Stalker/Interloper).
- Scurvy Risk manifests at/below 100 units of Vitamin-C (20% remaining) on the Status Screen.
- Scurvy is treated immediately by consuming 500 units of Vitamin-C, which resumes the daily Vitamin-C drain.

Because Vitamin-C drains at a consistent rate, it is possible to estimate the survivor's current Vitamin-C amount if Scurvy Risk manifests, as well as the number of days before Scurvy Risk can appear from the start of a new survival sandbox or after contracting and curing Scurvy.
- Stalker/Interloper/Misery: 25 days from game start/treatment (5 days after Scurvy Risk)
> “**You consumed a diet low in Vitamin-C for too long and now have Scurvy. If left untreated you will continue to weaken and lose condition until you succumb and die.**”

Scurvy manifests when Scurvy Risk reaches 100% (0 Vitamin-C), which causes constant slow Condition loss and multiple debilitating effects until treatment or death. Scurvy is cured immediately by consuming food containing Vitamin-C and fully emptying the recovery time bar (tracked at 500 units of Vitamin-C)
When the survivor is afflicted with Scurvy, the recovery time bar will not increase over time, making it easier to find Vitamin-C.
- Disables Condition recovery while awake (when all four [Needs](./Needs.md) are met)*

*Note: While afflicted with Scurvy, Condition can still be recovered from [Sleep](./Sleep.md) (if all four [Needs](./Needs.md) are met), but Condition recovery will be reduced as the -0.5% Condition loss will occur each hour even while asleep. The Condition restoring effects of [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md), [Emergency Stims](./Emergency%20Stim.md) and some [Cooked Foods](./Cooking.md) retain their full effect.

Scurvy and Scurvy Risk is cured by consuming food containing Vitamin-C until the "Treatment" bar is full (500 units of Vitamin-C); while Scurvy is manifest the Treatment Meter (Vitamin-C) will not deplete.

Eating a single piece food that has Minor levels of Vitamin-C will only prevent Scurvy Risk for a brief amount of time, reappearing 1-2 days or less. Because of this, it is better to consume Moderate or Major level foods (or many Minor level foods) to keep Scurvy Risk away for longer.

Artificial Foods and [Fish](./Ice%20Fishing.md) hold the largest values of Vitamin-C, catching, cooking, and eating a large amount of cooked fish should be the player's immediate priority. Cooking Fish reduces the amount of Vitamin-C, but Raw Fish carry the high likelihood of causing [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md). Another consideration is Calorie-to-Vitamin-C density, since the survivor cannot eat food beyond [2500 stored Calories](./Hunger.md).

- Scurvy was originally not retroactively enabled on save files created before Part Four: Buried Echoes (December 5th 2023), regardless of difficulty, "to avoid the risk that players have already harvested most of the Vitamin-C rich foods in their game world." The ability to enable it on older saves was eventually added in the Part Five update however.

- Scurvy is a real-world affliction caused by a severe Vitamin-C deficiency, usually by a diet lacking fruits or vegetables. It is most commonly attributed to 17th and 18th century sailors who may be at-sea for months without access to fruits or vegetables or means to preserve them.

- The icon for Scurvy depicts a human tooth and blood droplet, both symptoms of real-world scurvy which causes tooth loosening and loss, as well as bruising (bleeding under the skin) and poor healing. Despite this, in-game Scurvy does not cause permanent damage to the survivor like [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md), or cause/increase the likelihood of [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md).

- Real-world people who inhabit arctic conditions, such as the indigenous peoples of Alaska, Canada and northern Russia primarily received their Vitamin-C from eating fish like what is depicted in-game.

**Scurvy** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) in _The Long Dark_. It is caused by consuming a diet with low/no Vitamin-C, and is lethal if untreated.

Scurvy is a long-term affliction caused by Vitamin-C deficiency: failing to consume as much Vitamin-C as is drained daily. Each day the survivor's Vitamin-C level decreases by a small amount from a hidden Vitamin-C meter; this loss can be mitigated or recovered by consuming foods with Vitamin-C.

- Foods with Vitamin-C display roughly how much they contain on the item's information page ("Minor", "Moderate" or "Major" source of Vitamin-C). If a food item contains no Vitamin-C (or on a game mode where Scurvy is disabled) no amount will be shown. Condition of food items does not affect Vitamin-C values.
[Scurvy Risk](./Scurvy%20Risk.md) appears when below 20% of the Vitamin-C maximum, and will progress into the Scurvy affliction unless more Vitamin-C is consumed.

Most Vitamin-C food sources are finite (artificial foods and cattails), which can make Scurvy an increasing challenge in the late-game. However fish, and to a lesser extent [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md), are renewable sources.

> “__Fail to eat a balanced diet and Scurvy will hound you relentlessly. While the onset is slow, the consequences can be disastrous to your health. The choice is yours.

Starting a Survival Mode save file presents the option to enable Scurvy to that save. If enabled, foods with Vitamin-C will be labeled as a Minor, Moderate, or Major source of Vitamin-C when examined.

Scurvy is present on [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md), [Stalker](./Stalker.md), [Interloper](./Interloper.md), and [Misery](./Misery.md) modes, and is disabled in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) and [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md).

Scurvy can be prevented by regularly consuming enough Vitamin-C foods to prevent Scurvy Risk from reaching 100%. Scurvy Risk will appear when the survivor's hidden Vitamin-C stat drops below 20% remaining, giving the survivor a warning several days before the true affliction occurs.
- Vitamin-C is a hidden survivor statistic, and is not displayed on the [Status Screen](./Survival%20Menu.md).
- Vitamin-C begins at 500 units at the start of a new Survival Sandbox (or upon treating Scurvy)
- A small amount of Vitamin-C is drained each day (10 units on Voyageur or 20 units on Stalker/Interloper).
- Scurvy Risk manifests at/below 100 units of Vitamin-C (20% remaining) on the Status Screen.
- Scurvy is treated immediately by consuming 500 units of Vitamin-C, which resumes the daily Vitamin-C drain.

Because Vitamin-C drains at a consistent rate, it is possible to estimate the survivor's current Vitamin-C amount if Scurvy Risk manifests, as well as the number of days before Scurvy Risk can appear from the start of a new survival sandbox or after contracting and curing Scurvy.
- Stalker/Interloper/Misery: 25 days from game start/treatment (5 days after Scurvy Risk)
> “**You consumed a diet low in Vitamin-C for too long and now have Scurvy. If left untreated you will continue to weaken and lose condition until you succumb and die.**”

Scurvy manifests when Scurvy Risk reaches 100% (0 Vitamin-C), which causes constant slow Condition loss and multiple debilitating effects until treatment or death. Scurvy is cured immediately by consuming food containing Vitamin-C and fully emptying the recovery time bar (tracked at 500 units of Vitamin-C)
When the survivor is afflicted with Scurvy, the recovery time bar will not increase over time, making it easier to find Vitamin-C.
- Disables Condition recovery while awake (when all four [Needs](./Needs.md) are met)*

*Note: While afflicted with Scurvy, Condition can still be recovered from [Sleep](./Sleep.md) (if all four [Needs](./Needs.md) are met), but Condition recovery will be reduced as the -0.5% Condition loss will occur each hour even while asleep. The Condition restoring effects of [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md), [Emergency Stims](./Emergency%20Stim.md) and some [Cooked Foods](./Cooking.md) retain their full effect.

Scurvy and Scurvy Risk is cured by consuming food containing Vitamin-C until the "Treatment" bar is full (500 units of Vitamin-C); while Scurvy is manifest the Treatment Meter (Vitamin-C) will not deplete.

Eating a single piece food that has Minor levels of Vitamin-C will only prevent Scurvy Risk for a brief amount of time, reappearing 1-2 days or less. Because of this, it is better to consume Moderate or Major level foods (or many Minor level foods) to keep Scurvy Risk away for longer.

Artificial Foods and [Fish](./Ice%20Fishing.md) hold the largest values of Vitamin-C, catching, cooking, and eating a large amount of cooked fish should be the player's immediate priority. Cooking Fish reduces the amount of Vitamin-C, but Raw Fish carry the high likelihood of causing [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md). Another consideration is Calorie-to-Vitamin-C density, since the survivor cannot eat food beyond [2500 stored Calories](./Hunger.md).

The ability to enable it on older saves was eventually added in the Part Five update however.

- Scurvy is a real-world affliction caused by a severe Vitamin-C deficiency, usually caused by a diet lacking fruits or vegetables. It is most commonly associated with 17th- and 18th-century sailors who could be at sea for months without access to fruits or vegetables.

- The icon for Scurvy depicts a human tooth and blood droplet, both symptoms of real-world scurvy which causes tooth loosening and loss, as well as bruising (bleeding under the skin) and poor healing. Despite this, in-game Scurvy does not cause permanent damage to the survivor like [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md), or cause/increase the likelihood of [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md).
- Real-world people who inhabit arctic regions, such as the indigenous peoples of Alaska, Canada and northern Russia, primarily receive their Vitamin-C from eating fish, as depicted in-game.

The **Security Chief's Rifle Holster** is a type of accessory in _The Long Dark_. It is part of the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ DLC.

The Security Chief's Rifle Holster is a [Clothing](./Clothing.md) item that when worn in either accessory slot, reduces the weight of an equipped [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), or one of its variants, by 50%:

The holster provides no other bonuses, such as [Warmth](./Warmth.md) or [Windproofing](./Clothing.md#Windproof). Like other clothing, the holster is vulnerable to damage from [Struggle](./Struggle.md) and [blizzards](./Weather.md), though it is sturdy and relatively easy to repair.

The holster is found in the kitchen of [Bunker Omega](./Bunker%20Omega.md), having belonged to the Chief Security Officer overseeing the Rüdiger's Project. It is the ultimate prize for completing the [Tale](./Tales.md) [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md).

**Severe Lacerations** is a physical Injury acquired from a [Cougar](./Cougar.md) [Struggle](./Struggle.md).

> “**You have sustained multiple deep slashing cuts from the Cougar's claws. Your Condition and Stamina are compromised, and you are at greater risk of Infection and Blood Loss until you are healed.**”
Severe Lacerations is always applied to the survivor after a Cougar Struggle and lasts for 72 hours, requiring no treatment to cure.
- Generates 2-3 [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) and [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md) along with the Affliction.

- The survivor's claw wounds periodically open up again over time, generating new instances of [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) and [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md) (which require fresh [Bandages](./Bandage.md) and [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md)). Both Afflictions are generated every 12 hours after first receiving Severe Lacerations, with up to 5 sets occurring until the Affliction fully heals.

- A notification that Blood Loss has been applied will not appear, but the screen will briefly turn red (as if suffering from a Sprain) and the survivor's Condition will begin to rapidly drop. Keep an eye on your Condition bar when passing time and be prepared to cancel your activity.

**Note**: Time Accelerating tasks (Sleep, Pass Time, Crafting, Harvesting, etc) are **extremely dangerous** while afflicted with Severe Lacerations at the 12 hour mark, as new instances of Blood Loss can appear and rapidly kill the survivor (e.g. while asleep). As Blood Loss leads to a 30% loss of Condition per hour spent with it, sleeping in intervals higher than one hour at a time on any difficulty above Voyager is not recommended as you do not wake up from Condition loss and as you have a chance to "instantly" die.

This fate can easily be avoided by maintaining an eye on the remaining Recovery Time. As Blood Loss generation always occurs every 12 hours, (60, 48, 36, 24, 12 hour marks) making it is quite easy to diagnose whether sleeping or passing time at the moment is a wise idea.

Sewing Kit is a tool in The Long Dark for repairing [Clothing](./Clothing.md) or crafting improvised clothing.

Sewing Kits are used to repair damaged clothing before it becomes [Ruined](./Decay.md), or to create Improvised Clothing ([Improvised Headwrap](./Improvised%20Head%20Wrap.md), [Improvised Hand Wraps](./Improvised%20Hand%20Wraps.md), [Improvised Insulation](./Improvised%20Insulation.md)) to protect against [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md). Clothing Decays condition over time, reducing it's Warmth and Windproof values and eventually becoming Ruined and unusable (and unrepairable). Improvised Clothing is useful at preventing Frostbite to the head and hands, especially early game on Interloper, or after a wildlife [Struggle](./Struggle.md) if the survivor's clothing becomes ruined. Functionally Sewing Kits are the same as [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md), but Tackle is much slower to repair/craft with.
- Successful repairs of Clothing increase the [Mending](./Mending.md) survival skill in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).
The Fishing Tackle can also be used to repair clothing with the same effectiveness, and it can be fairly easily made at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) later in the game.
- New Sewing Kits can either be rarely found while [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) or purchased - maximum 1 per trade - from the [Trader](./Trader.md) after completing 4 Special Requests.
- Although the kit can spawn in first aid cabinets, it is not used for first aid, particularly for stitching wounds.

**Sharpening** is a secondary Survival [Skill](./Skills.md) that is used to repair [Bladed Tools](#bladed-tools). Higher levels in the sharpening skill reduce the amount of time required to sharpen, and additionally increase the amount of condition restored to a tool by sharpening.
Sharpening is the action by which a player may restore the condition of a bladed tool, such as a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) or [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), using a [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md).

Sharpening is only available when viewing a bladed tool in the inventory and is not a core survival skill like those listed in the player's journal (e.g., [Cooking](./Cooking.md)). Players start with 30 skill points, and gain 1 additional skill point each time a blade is sharpened, with the amount of condition restored per sharpening session increasing at different skill point intervals. How long each session takes will decrease at higher skill level intervals, as well.
Sharpening is known as one of the easier skills to train in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, as players can increase their skill by repairing any bladed tool.
Players can sharpen their bladed tools with a whetstone during daylight hours or in the dark.

To actually sharpen something, players have to select the Sharpen option while viewing the tool to repair in the inventory menu. Repair amount and chance to succeed at the repair are listed on the right hand side of the screen.

Players will always have a 100% chance of success while sharpening and cannot fail. Activating the start button on the bottom right will launch an attempt. A progress bar/wheel will appear on the screen during sharpening.

Sharpening a tool consumes 5% condition from the whetstone and restores some condition to the sharpened tool, based on the player's [skill level](#skill-levels). Each whetstone can be used up to 20 times for sharpening tools.

Players need a whetstone before they can start sharpening tools. Whetstones can be found while scavenging in containers and buildings that are likely to contain tools. Whetstones are always found in 100% condition.

The tower is easily visible in clear weather. Looking from the entrance of Forlorn Muskeg, it is located on top of a mountain to the east. Its appearance is similar to the tower from [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md). Climbing to the top of the tower offers an expansive view of the muskeg, weather permitting. Several wolves can patrol the area, however, so take caution.

There are three crates which can be broken down for [reclaimed wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md). There is also a corpse and a backpack with food and sometimes matches or a [magnifying lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md). There can also spawn up to three metal containers that often contain decent loot, such as high-level [clothing](./Clothing.md). In the area there are also [Green Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) to craft arrows. Strangely enough, there is a laptop sitting at the foot of the structure, which activates one of the buffer memories for the [Archivist](./Archivist.md) challenge.

**Shotgun** **Ammunition** or a **Shotgun Slug** is a [Tools](./Tools.md) item found exclusively in [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) in the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story.

The branding for this ammunition is called Bullseye, the same company that produces [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) and [Revolver Ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md).

The **Shotgun** is a [Tools](./Tools.md) item found exclusively in [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) in the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story of [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

A single-shot, break action shotgun, the Shotgun performs devastating blows to any animal it hits. The Shotgun fires [12GA Slugs](./Shotgun%20Ammunition.md) instead of pellet based buckshot. This effectively turns it into a high powered [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) (of which it shares similar holding and walking animations), albeit only being able to fire 1 round at a time before reloading. When reloading, a [Shotgun Shell Casing](./Shotgun%20Shell%20Casing.md) is ejected and a fresh Slug is placed inside.
The only options present in the Backpack menu are to Unload or Drop the Shotgun. Slugs/Casings unloaded from the Backpack are place directly into the inventory. The Shotgun cannot be Harvested.
It is found exclusively in the mission [High Energy](./High%20Energy.md) in Episode 5, during Part 2: Strange History.

- The first is found in the Supply Room (opened with the [Supply Room Key](./Supply%20Room%20Key.md) just before leaving the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md) facility) along with 23 rounds of shotgun ammunition.
- A second is found inside a [Weapon Locker](./Weapon%20Locker.md) at the 2nd Geothermal Station, along with [Shotgun Ammunition](./Shotgun%20Ammunition.md).
- A third shotgun can be found in the 3rd Geothermal Station, inside another Weapon Locker.
The Shotgun disappears from Mackenzie's inventory during the mission [Conflagration](./Conflagration.md) (Part 4: Terminus) of the Episode.
As a shotgun, it has tight spread but very poor range. The shotgun fires slightly lower than it's iron sights when aiming; take this into account when aiming a shot.

It is advised to aim towards a [Wolf](./Wolf.md) and shoot at it while it is close. It is very likely to kill a Wolf if used this way with no risk to [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md). If the shot does not kill it, the Wolf will be in a flee movement and not attack Will.
There is currently not enough ammunition to lower a Shotgun's Condition enough to jam the weapon in Episode 5. It is currently unknown if it is possible to jam the Shotgun.
- The words "PROPERTY OF [SRT](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md)" are stamped on both sides of the gun.
- Added to game.

The lake itself features many islands, the largest of which, [Drift Island](./Drift%20Island.md) is named and is home to [a cave](./Archie%27s%20Crawlspace.md) and [cottage](./Island%20Cottage.md). A small [Airplane](./Airplane.md) can be found in the south part of the lake and is the only refuge on the lake itself.

There are also two ice fishing huts on the north and east sides of Drift Island, where [Smallmouth Bass](./Smallmouth%20Bass%20%28Raw%29.md) and [Lake Whitefish](./Lake%20Whitefish%20%28Raw%29.md) may be caught.

The lake is frequented by [wolves](./Wolf.md). While they are easy to spot in the wide open terrain on a clear day, a sudden fog or [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) can make them very difficult to see, posing dangers for unwary survivors. A [bear](./Bear.md) may spawn in the [small cave](./Fallow%20Dugout.md) on the southeast part of the lake and will patrol the whole lake. It is also easy to get lost on the lake in poor weather.

Signal Hill can be accessed by trail either from the east or the west up the southern mountain.

A general variety of supplies may be found in the radio hut. These include, but are not limited to: a [hunting rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), the [revolver](./Revolver.md), a pair of [cargo pants](./Cargo%20Pants.md), [Expedition parka](./Expedition%20Parka.md), [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) ([peaches](./Pinnacle%20Peaches.md), [tomato soup](./Tomato%20Soup.md), [pork and beans](./Pork%20and%20Beans.md), etc.), .303 [rifle ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), [revolver ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md), [military coat](./Military%20Coat.md), some medical supplies, and a few variable items that change depending on the playthrough. Also a [buffer memory](./Buffer%20Memories.md) can be found here. A [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) is found just outside in the fenced area.

Outside, a [fire barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) can be found against the shack's wall, offering the player some protection from the wind. [Bear](./Bear.md), [wolves](./Wolf.md), [deer](./Deer.md), and [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) may spawn near the shack, but fenced-in enclosure provides a level of security from predators' ambushes. Wood is also abundant within the forest nearby.

Overall, Signal Hill is one of the best places to find high-tier loot in Pleasant Valley and makes for a good [safe-house](./Safehouse.md). There is also a [climbing rock](./Rope%20Climbing.md) just outside the hut, if one does not want to hike up and down the mountain.

In the final chapter of [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) is following [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md)'s directions to Signal Hill, where he hopes to try to send a radio message to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) before continuing there on foot. Near the end of [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), Astrid must brave a blizzard to reach Signal Hill in the hope of finding a functional radio to contact [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md).

**Region:** [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md)
**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

**Signal Void** is the first of four [Tales](./Tales.md) in the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC. Tales are narrative-based objectives for Survival mode. It is not a selectable [Challenge](./Challenge.md) but instead must be activated by first starting a Survival game.

Signal Void begins when the player finds a note located on the top floor of the [Control Tower](./Control%20Tower.md) in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) [Region](./Region.md). The note, labeled [Field 31 Operation Memo](./Field%2031%20Operation%20Memo.md), details information about the Airfield staff's efforts to try and expand the radio wave coverage of several preexisting radio towers located within Lower Great Bear, in order to sync them with Airfield 31's radio coverage. The memo also makes note of the presence of several anomalous transmission signals that were detected across the island, but their sources were otherwise unable to be identified.

After reading and pocketing the note, the player will automatically receive a [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md), and a new section in the Journal menu (a flag submenu icon labeled Tales) will appear to keep track of the memo's objectives.
_This section may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark._
- Use the repaired Transmitter network to search Forsaken Airfield for signs of additional bunkers.
Your first objective is to repair the 4 portable [Transmitters](./Transmitters.md) at each location mentioned in the memo.

(Transmitter Towers CAN be repaired BEFORE starting the Tale by picking up the memo and radio - no need to trek back and forth too much if you start your run in Lower Great Bear. This does not seemingly break the Transponder gameplay in any way.)
You'll probably start with the one located outside the Control Tower and then work your back way down to Lower Great Bear to fix the rest.
Once a Transmitter is found, each tower will require the following materials in order to be repaired:
- 1 [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md) (Normally found near a Transmitter, no need to haul one around. If not then cars should be present nearby.)
When you repair one of the Transmitters in Lower Great Bear, you will be prompted to investigate a signal. You can continue to repair Transmitters or go find the strange signal at this point.

If the player activates the Transmitters for the first time at night, an aurora will automatically trigger. For the most effective gameplay the player should be ready to investigate the signal when activating the Transmitter.
After all transmitters are repaired, your next objective is to investigate the strange signals mentioned in the memo:
- Investigate signal in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) (corresponds to transmitter in Mountain Town)
- Investigate signal in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) (corresponds to transmitter in Forlorn Muskeg)
- Investigate signal in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) (corresponds to transmitter in Pleasant Valley)

When an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) becomes active in the night sky, use your Handheld Shortwave Radio to home in on the signal (switch to Blue setting). Follow the radio transmissions and you will be eventually find yourself uncovering the entrance of an underground bunker.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: _***Important\***_

Even if you use [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md) to uncover the location of a bunker (either near the bunker or via a [Polaroid](./Polaroids.md) Vista) or if you already know the location of the bunkers, the game will not allow you to uncover a bunker hatch unless your radio is currently powered. (The same is true for any hidden supply caches. See [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) for more details.)
Once you discover a bunker, you are told to investigate it. Each bunker has 1 security chief's report and 1 patient interview. Collect them both to advance the narrative.
When all bunkers in Lower Great Bear are discovered and all documents are collected, trek back to the Forsaken Airfield to locate a final signal that was not mentioned in the memo.

The signal will lead you to the area around [Justy's Hovel](./Justy%27s%20Hovel.md). Once you uncover [Bunker Omega](./Bunker%20Omega.md), search it for another security report and patient interview, thus ending the Tale.

The ultimate prize of this island wide scavenger hunt is the exclusive [Security Chief's Rifle Holster](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Rifle%20Holster.md) accessory, which is found leaning beside a kitchen crate in the first room across from the bunker entrance.

As you progress with the objectives of Signal Void, the purpose of each of the bunkers begins to become clearer. A device was built in a [large mine](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) and was used to experiment upon patients that were kept inside each bunker, though the test results of this experiment are currently unclear.
## Notes
- Completing the Tale will award the player with a unique [Badge](./Badges.md) of the same name.
- This was the first survival mode Tale released for The Long Dark, and is estimated by [Hinterland](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md) to take 5+ hours to complete.

This is the mission transcript for mission 3 [Signal to Noise](./Signal%20to%20Noise.md) of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md).
_Mackenzie travels back to [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and begins making his way to the 3 radio towers._

_No matter what order the towers are looted for their set of [Transponder Parts](./Transponder%20Parts.md), Mackenzie takes the first set without incident. A problem occurs when reaching either the 2nd or 3rd tower however: the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) appears, as if guarding the tower._

_Mackenzie readies his spear, just as the bear charges him, only for the spear to bury itself deep into the beast. It does not kill the demon bear, nor does it seem to even wound it, but the Old Bear is driven off. The bear stays in the area, as Mackenzie quickly grabs the Parts and leaves the area._

_After acquiring the last of the Parts, Mackenzie makes his way back to the rail tunnel leading to Mystery Lake. Before he enters the tunnel however, he hears a roar. Turning around, the Old Bear has somehow snuck up on the pilot._

_He charges and mercilessly attacks the pilot before he can raise his spear. Mackenzie screams as the bear tears into him, eventually fainting as the Old Bear stares at him. Mackenzie awakes for a brief moment, feeling the Old Bear dragging his body away as he faints again and the screen turns black._

**Signal to Noise** is the third mission in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. In this mission, [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) must retrieve transponder parts from radio towers in Forlorn Muskeg and bring them back to Jeremiah. The mission is interrupted while the Mackenzie brings the parts back to Jeremiah, and the player to the next mission; [What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md).
- Retrieve [Transponder Parts](./Transponder%20Parts.md) from each tower in Forlorn Muskeg.

The player can visit the towers in any order, but will encounter the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) at the second and third towers visited. The bear spawns in a random direction out of the player's field of view. It approaches until within a certain radius, then stands up on its hind legs, roars, and then charges the player. If the player equips the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) and is aiming it at the bear when it arrives, a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) will begin; else a typical bear attack cutscene will play (except that the Old Bear appears instead of the generic one), and the player will immediately die of blood loss at the end. If Mackenzie survives, he will be knocked to the ground, although no items will be dropped as in a normal bear attack. The Bear will briefly retreat and then attack again, but the game will automatically save after each struggle. Unlike other predator attacks, these encounters will result in minimal [Condition](./Condition.md) loss (<5%), no injuries, and little or no damage to gear. After 3 struggles, the Bear will flee and the player can collect the transponder parts. Mackenzie will comment before and after the event (once per location).

Timing is essential, as setting the spear is not instantaneous and the stamina meter runs out more quickly than when aiming ranged weapons. The bear will attempt to charge in a straight line, but may run into terrain obstacles that slow it down; ensure it has a clear path before aiming. Additionally, the meter takes time to recharge, so briefly evading the bear without running may be necessary in order to initiate the next struggle. In order to maximize available stamina, avoid running while approaching the towers and consider temporarily taking off [Clothing](./Clothing.md) with a stamina penalty.

> “**A home-made Arrow, created by combining an Arrow shaft with Crow feathers and an Arrowhead.**”

Arrows are reusable ammunition for the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md). Arrows embed themselves in most soft targets when fired from a bow. Simple Arrows may occasionally be found in hunting blinds or near carcasses.

Simple arrows are one of three arrow types currently in the game, they have an easily accessible recipe and are very effective against all types of [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md). [Fire Hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) are even easier to craft, but are only capable of killing small game animals such as [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigans](./Ptarmigan.md) and are very brittle. [Manufactured Arrows](./Manufactured%20Arrow.md) are the most difficult arrow type to obtain; requiring the completion of Sutherland's first special request before they can be [traded](./Trader.md) for, then up to 10 arrows can be bought each time. They are a pure upgrade from the simple arrow and inflict 12.5% more damage and are twice as durable, but are not available on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) or [Misery](./Misery.md).

The total durability of arrows is variable and depends on a material table to determine it's condition loss; with the hardness of the material and the angle at which the arrow impacts the target determining the amount of degradation received. After a hit takes the arrow's condition below 0% it will break and turn into a [Broken Arrow](./Broken%20Arrow.md) then fall to the ground where it may be retrieved and harvested for 1 [Arrowhead](./Arrowhead.md) and 2 [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md).

Arrows hitting hard surfaces will bounce off. Bounces off hard vertical surfaces can be hard to predict and may even return back toward the player. Glancing bounces are a common occurrence when arrows hit horizontal surfaces, especially ice. These glancing arrows carry a lot of their original momentum through the bounce and can travel 15 or more meters further along their original trajectory, far out of sight of the player. In this case, arrows can be very difficult to locate for players that do not know how far they actually can bounce.

Skeeter's Ridge lies close to [Burned Ridge Cave](./Burned%20Ridge%20Cave.md) and west of [Draft Dodger's Cabin](./Draft%20Dodger%27s%20Cabin.md). The region's [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) lies further north-west.
The most notable features of Skeeter's Ridge are the few ruined buildings in the area. Some [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) may also be found nearby.

There is a bulkhead door to the basement next to one of the ruined house. The basement includes a washing machine, dryer, some cardboard / wooden boxes, a fridge, some canned goods and soda, a first aid kit, a plastic container, and two metal containers. There is a chance of spawning a [hatchet](./Hatchet.md) under the staircases.
In [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), the player will need to visit this location to complete a side quest.

Also, the basement is one of the required survival locations in The [Nomad](./Nomad.md) challenge, and the player spawns right next to the basement at the start of [The Hunted, Part one](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20One.md) challenge.
There is a [wolf](./Wolf.md) spawn point in the nearby forest. The player may encounter one when entering or exiting the basement, so caution is warranted.

This achievement is obtained by getting all [Skills](./Skills.md) to level five in a single game in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).

**Note:** Because some of the skills require access to firearms, the achievement is unobtainable on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) or [Misery](./Misery.md). (This may no longer be true after introduction of Trader, as he sells rifle and revolver books in Interloper mode too.)
- [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) can be very helpful in leveling up skills faster and with less resources.
- If the player has the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) installed, the [Trader](./Trader.md) has a chance to offer Research Books for every skill.
Most skills require 100 points to level up, unless noted. Generally, one successful action will provide 1 point towards the relevant skill.

- The hardest skill to level up by far is [Mending](./Mending.md), requiring a tremendous amount of [Cloth](./Cloth.md) and 350 points to reach level 5, not to mention [Sewing Kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md) / [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) durability. One strategy is to fix every item of clothing the player finds, or to immediately repair worn clothing as soon as its durability falls below 100%. Buying [A Sewing Primer](./A%20Sewing%20Primer.md) from [Sutherland](./Trader.md) can help make this less tedious.

- [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) will often be levelled up naturally over time, but the process can be sped up by hunting and harvesting larger animals such as [bear](./Bear.md) or [moose](./Moose.md).

- [Cooking](./Cooking.md) requires 350 points to reach level 5, but tends to be levelled up to level 5 fairly quickly through natural gameplay. It can require large amounts of fuel, however. Fully butchering and cooking a bear/moose can easily give 25-40 points towards this skill. Preparing beverages such as [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md), [coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md), [herbal tea](./Cup%20of%20Herbal%20Tea.md), [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md), and [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) can also be a fast way to raise Cooking skill.
- Gunsmithing is one of the fastest to level up, so long as ample resources are available. The skill can be leveled to level 5 in only one day.

- [Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and [Revolver](./Revolver.md) firearm skills are not difficult to increase, but do require lots of ammunition to be expended (minimum 100 rounds), and multiple [firearm cleaning kits](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md) to keep the weapons in good condition. Frequent trips to Bleak Inlet or Blackrock may be required to restock on ammo and to repair damaged weapons at the [milling machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) if cleaning kits are in short supply. Ammo and cleaning kits can also be acquired from the [Trader](./Trader.md).

- [Archery](./Archery.md) requires 125 points and is relatively easy to level up, as one experience point is gained by crafting each [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md). It can also be levelled by crafting a large stash of cheap [Fire Hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) and shooting [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) or [ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md). Reaching level 5 will require a few [cured Maple Saplings](./Cured%20Maple%20Sapling.md) and [cured guts](./Cured%20Gut.md), along with many [feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) and [sticks](./Stick.md) or [cured Birch Saplings](./Cured%20Birch%20Sapling.md), but these are generally easily acquired.

- [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) requires 200 points, and can be acquired over the course of a game, but is most efficiently done by using the [magnifying lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) on a sunny day as to not consume [matches](./Matches%20%28disambiguation%29.md). Another option is to gather a bunch of [sticks](./Stick.md) and light/re-light campfires using a lit [Torch](./Torch.md).

- [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) also requires more points to reach level 5 than most other skills (250) but it can also be acquired overtime and will require lots of [cured gut](./Cured%20Gut.md) and [scrap metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) to provide [fishing tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md). Making some [lures](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28disambiguation%29.md) can help speed the process up somewhat. Catching enough fish to produce all the [lantern fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) for [Sutherland's](./Trader.md) trades can provide good experience in both Ice Fishing and Cooking.
