![The current Skills display menu.](../assets/Skills_screen.png)_The current Skills display menu._ **Skills** are a survivor's trainable abilities that may be improved throughout their [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) gameplay. Any given skill can be trained by specific actions that relate to the skill. Performing any of these actions grants the player skill points in that skill. Skills can also be increased by researching the [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md) that corresponds with the skill.

Achieving higher levels in skills can give players various advantages, such as preventing [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) from eating any cooked food or preventing failures while [Mending](./Mending.md) clothing.

There are 9 skills that can be improved in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. All skills start out at level 1. Survivors can improve their skills up to level 5; after that, they get no further benefits from continuing to train the skill.
Skills do not carry over between Survival Mode games or [Challenges](./Challenge.md), unlike [Feats](./Feats.md). When the player dies, they lose their survival skill progress.
## Skills
| [Archery](../assets/Archery.png) | [Archery](./Archery.md) | Archery is used to [hunt](./Hunting.md) [animals](./Wildlife.md) with the use of a [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md). |
| [Carcass Harvesting](../assets/Carcass_Harvesting.png) | [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) | Carcass harvesting is used to harvest meat, hides, and guts from wildlife. |

| [Cooking](../assets/Cooking.png) | [Cooking](./Cooking.md) | Cooking is used to cook raw food for a number of reasons, including increasing the condition of raw food and preventing [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) prior to consuming food. |

| [Fire Starting](../assets/Fire_Starting.png) | [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) | Fire starting is used to start [fires](./Fire.md), which are used to generate heat, dry clothing, cook food, melt snow, and purify water. |

| [Ice Fishing](../assets/Ice_Fishing.png) | [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) | Ice fishing is used to catch raw fish, which are used for [Cooking](./Cooking.md) and for creating [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md). |
| [Mending](../assets/Mending.png) | [Mending](./Mending.md) | Mending is used to repair damaged cloth or leather clothing. |

| [Rifle Firearm](../assets/Rifle_Firearm.png) | [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) | Rifle Firearm is used offensively to [hunt](./Hunting.md) animals with the use of a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md). |

| [Revolver Firearm](../assets/Revolver_Firearm.png) | [Revolver Firearm](./Revolver%20Firearm.md) | Revolver Firearm is used to defensively scare away animals with the use of a [Revolver](./Revolver.md). Can be used during a [Struggle](./Struggle.md). |

| [Gunsmithing](../assets/Gunsmithing.png) | [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) | Gunsmithing is used to craft [bullets](./Bullet.md), [gunpowder](./Can%20of%20Gunpowder.md), and ammunition cartridges for the revolver and rifle. It also determines the quality of cartridges produced. |

Players also have access to three secondary survival skills, which are not tracked by the [Journal](./Journal.md) in the game menu. The skill status can only be viewed while attempting to perform an action related to that skill within the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md).

| [Firearm Cleaning Kit icon](../assets/Firearm_Cleaning_Kit_icon.png) | [Cleaning](./Cleaning.md) | Cleaning is used to repair hunting rifles and revolvers. Keeping firearms in optimal condition reduces the likelihood of weapon [jamming](./Hunting%20Rifle.md#Jamming). |

| [Quality Tools icon](../assets/Quality_Tools_icon.png)[Simple Tools icon](../assets/Simple_Tools_icon.png) | [Repair](./Repair.md) | Repair is used to repair a variety of metal tools, such as [hacksaws](./Hacksaw.md) and [heavy hammers](./Heavy%20Hammer.md). |

| [Whetstone icon](../assets/Whetstone_icon.png) | [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) | Sharpening is used to repair [bladed tools](./Sharpening.md#Bladed_tools). Higher levels in the sharpening skill reduce the amount of time required to sharpen, and additionally increase the amount of condition restored to a tool by sharpening. |

Each skill can be increased by performing its corresponding action(s), or by reading [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) associated with it. Duplicates of the same research book can each be read, each granting independent skill bonuses (e.g. two "_Wilderness Kitchen_", each for 10 Cooking Skill Points), but books cannot be read at skill 5 giving the error _"Your skills are too advanced for this book"_.

| [Archery](../assets/Archery.png) | [Archery](./Archery.md) | **Archery** can be increased by: - 1 point per crafted [Simple Arrow icon](../assets/Simple_Arrow_icon.png) [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md) - 1 point per hit with any arrow type on living Wildlife ([Fire Hardened Arrow](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) do not yield experience when hitting larger animals) - 10 points by reading [Stay on Target icon](../assets/Stay_on_Target_icon.png) [Stay on Target](./Stay%20on%20Target.md) |

| [Carcass Harvesting](../assets/Carcass_Harvesting.png) | [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) | **Carcass Harvesting** is increased at a rate of: - 1 point hour spent harvesting wildlife carcasses - It can also be increased for 10 points by reading _[Field Dressing Your Kill, Vol. I icon](../assets/Field_Dressing_Your_Kill%2C_Vol._I_icon.png) [Field Dressing Your Kill, Vol. I](./Field%20Dressing%20Your%20Kill%2C%20Vol.%20I.md)_ Slower harvesting times (e.g. with bare hands) increases Carcass Harvesting Skill faster than with tools (e.g. a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md)). |

| [Cooking](../assets/Cooking.png) | [Cooking](./Cooking.md) | **Cooking** is increased by: - 1 point per Cooked [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item at an active fire (raw meat, canned food, brewable drinks) - 1 point per successfully Preparing a Recipe - 10 points by reading _[Wilderness Kitchen icon](../assets/Wilderness_Kitchen_icon.png) [Wilderness Kitchen](./Wilderness%20Kitchen.md)_ Cooking Skill points are gained upon picking up an item that has finished cooking. ![Resting](../assets/Resting.png) Sleep is the player's most efficient way to both eliminate [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) and regain [Condition](./Condition.md). Selecting a [Bed](./Bed.md), or deployed [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), will open up the sleep interface. While inside a [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md), the option to sleep can also be accessed via Campcraft in the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md).

Up to 12 consecutive hours may be slept in a row, with the amount of time being adjustable by whole hour increments. The amount of time the player will sleep may not be exactly the number of hours selected, but may vary by 10 minutes. The player will also stop sleeping when their Fatigue bar is full. Sleep cannot be interrupted manually by the player once it has started so care must be taken that all needs will remain met (safety, warmth, thirst, hunger).

Animal attacks will interrupt sleep if they happen while the player is sleeping. Further, sandboxes on the Pilgrim or Voyageur experience modes have a chance to wake the player when they are nearing [death](./Condition.md) or threatened. Other experience modes do not provide any such warning and allow the player to sleep themselves to death, so more attentive [need](./Needs.md) management is required, although stalker does warn the player if he/she starts to freeze.
There are several variants of [Bed](./Bed.md), some found only in specific types of locations, and each providing a different amount of [Warmth](./Warmth.md) when slept in.
- Bunk (usually in cabins or other remote structures) will provide + 3 ~ 6 °C ( +5.4 ~ 10.8 °F )
- Mattress/Blanket (found on the floor in some large industrial or community buildings) will provide + 3 ~ 5 °C ( +5.4 ~ 9 °F )
- Tuffet (a makeshift bed made of conifer branches and leaves often found in caves) will provide + 2 °C ( +3.6°F )
- Medical Cot (found inside the crashed [Final Approach](./Final%20Approach.md) helicopter) will provide + 2 °C ( +3.6°F )
- "Beds" (a blanket and pillow thrown over a cardboard box, found in abandoned [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md) and trailers) will provide + 2 °C ( +3.6°F )

The player also has the ability to create beds via [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) ([Rustic Bed](./Rustic%20Bed.md), [Quilted Bed](./Quilted%20Bed.md), [Bear Hide Bed](./Bear%20Hide%20Bed.md)).
- ![Bedroll icon](../assets/Bedroll_icon.png) [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) (+ 5 °C (+ 9 °F )
- ![Improvised Down Bedroll icon](../assets/Improvised_Down_Bedroll_icon.png) [Improvised Down Bedroll](./Improvised%20Down%20Bedroll.md) (+ 8 °C (+ 14.4 °F)
- ![Bear Skin Bedroll icon](../assets/Bear_Skin_Bedroll_icon.png) [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md) (+12 °C (+ 21.6 °F)

[Vehicles](./Vehicle.md) with doors that lead to interiors also function as beds but are not directly selectable. To sleep in a vehicle, open the [radial menu](./Radial%20Menu.md) while inside, then activate the bedroll function through the Campcraft option. The sleep interface will then appear whether or not the player has a bedroll. No bedroll is required or used when sleeping in a vehicle. As a result, bedrolls in the inventory will not [decay](./Decay.md) when sleeping in vehicles.

All vehicles offer +3°C warmth bonus and are windproof, but even if the player has a bedroll with a warmth bonus greater than 3°C, it will still provide only 3°C. If the player is getting too cold in a vehicle, a [Campfire](./Campfire.md) can be lit outside the vehicle to warm the interior, though be aware that it can become windblown.

While it is generally preferable to find a location that offers at least partial shelter before sleeping (i.e. house, cave, vehicle, fishing hut, etc.), or to build a [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md), sometimes sleeping outside can't be avoided. In such cases, it is strongly recommended to pick an area where there are few predators and which is surrounded by wind-blocking obstacles on multiple sides. Lighting a [campfire](./Campfire.md) will help provide safety from dangerous animals and cold temperatures. To avoid freezing to death while asleep, it's often best to sleep in short increments. Warmer bedrolls, such as the [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md) and the [Improvised Down Bedroll](./Improvised%20Down%20Bedroll.md), can also help ward off the cold and, in the case of the Bear Skin Bedroll, potential predators.

All bed types offer some level of insulation for the player while they are being used. This is displayed on the sleep interface as the warmth bonus. For all intents and purposes, this will raise the character's [feels like](./Feels%20Like.md) temperature by the indicated amount for the duration of the sleep.

Some [fatigue](./Fatigue.md) is eliminated with each hour of sleep. A full 12 hours of sleep are required to completely fill the fatigue bar from empty. If the player sleeps for less than 12 hours, fatigue will fill at the rate of 1/12th of the bar per hour. The player will wake up early if their fatigue bar completely fills.

If all [needs](./Needs.md) are met, meaning their bars are not empty, sleep also restores lost condition. [Condition](./Condition.md) is restored on a progressive scale that rewards sleeping for longer periods. This can be further accelerated gaining the [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) [Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md), gained by eating the following foods:

Note: If all needs are not met or need meters fall below zero while sleeping, condition still drops. It is quite possible to die in one's sleep if not interrupted. [Thirst](./Thirst.md) and [Hunger](./Hunger.md) will worsen as one sleeps.

Drinking [Cup of Herbal Tea](./Cup%20of%20Herbal%20Tea.md) or [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) before going to sleep will restore additional condition. For herbal tea the benefit of a full cup will remain for 6h and will provide an extra 2% condition per hour slept (Interloper +1%). See [Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md).

In Interloper experience, recovering condition during sleep is **_seriously_**reduced. Each consecutive hour returns usually more % of condition than the previous (check table below), maxed at 5% per hour. Sleeping for 1 hour in any sort of bed besides the cloth bedroll returns 1% of condition. Sleeping 2 hours returns 1% for the first hour and 1% for the second hour totaling 2%. Sleeping 3 hours returns the 2% (1+1) for the first two hours and 2% for the third totaling 4%.

**NOTICE**: If you sleep for more than 10h, you're taking Condition damage during the 11th or 12th hour due to Thirst fully draining and you'll actually lose 2% Condition each hour. This makes the sleeping for only 10 hours the best possible way to heal in one session (+32% max possible condition gain).

[Thirst](./Thirst.md) and [Hunger](./Hunger.md) build as one sleeps -- at 55 ml & 60 calories per hour. Thus, 12 hours of sleep will completely dehydrate a character who had no thirst when starting. Therefore, it is wise to always drink [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) before sleeping.

There are many [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) that impair sleep. [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) and [Dysentery](./Dysentery.md) will not allow condition to be restored during sleep. Coupled with this, [Burns](./Burns.md) and [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md) will immediately reduce the condition to 75% if it is above that the moment sleep starts, and prevent it from ever rising above until the affliction is cured. [Insomnia](./Insomnia.md) has a chance of causing a survivor to wake up early in a sleep cycle, denying them the full benefits of sleeping for long periods of time.

A snare is a [trap](./Trapping.md) you can set up to catch [rabbits](./Rabbit.md). Snares are only effective when placed in a rabbit-rich place. Once a rabbit is caught, the snare can be re-used if it did not break and its condition is greater than 0%. If it breaks, it can still be harvested for one [reclaimed wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md).
Snares are viable for long-term play as the gut harvested from the rabbit and its harvesting, once broken, is enough to create new snares.
Setting up many snares in a rabbit grove often has high yields; however, catching too many rabbits may reduce their respawn rate in that area. Waiting several days will restore the rate.

The snare needs time to catch something, so it isn't possible to set up the snare right in front of a rabbit and expect to catch it instantly. It is advised to set up several snares and come back later.

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: **Snare**

violations.message: Emphasis used instead of a heading
violations.context: **Requirements**

- When you put down a snare, a 12 in-game hour timer starts. After 12 hours have elapsed and you can no longer "see" the snare, the snare will check whether it should spawn a dead rabbit. If it hasn't produced a rabbit or broken, it will start the timer again.

- "Seeing" a snare: If you're within 2 units (meters?) of the snare, you can see the snare. If you're further than 250 units away, you cannot see the snare. If you're between the two, you can see the snare if there's a line of sight between you and the snare, and you're not looking away.

- If the 12-hour timer elapses while you can "see" the snare, the check happens as soon as you no longer see the snare. That means that you could look at the snare when the timer goes off, do a 360°, look back at the snare, and there might be a rabbit.

- If the player is not in the area the trap is placed (i.e. if they are in an area separated by a loading transition), the trap will wait to check for rabbits until the area loads. This can be used to make all traps check for rabbits simultaneously.

- Being separated from the snares by a loading transition and/or a long distance seems to lead to high multiple yields over a close/non-transition setup (i.e. 5/10 vs 0/2 caught bunnies). However for this to take effect, spending the night/longer time period indoors behind the loading transition seems to be required.

- If the trap is not within a rabbit spawn region, it will never catch a rabbit. However, any area that rabbits spawn can be used for trapping, not just those marked on the [map](./Map.md) as "rabbit groves."

- "Depleted": there are at least as many trapped rabbit corpses within the spawn region as the spawn region could spawn. Greatly reduces the trapping odds. There is still a non-zero chance of catching rabbits in a depleted spawn, however.

- On checking for a rabbit: with a 50% probability, a dead rabbit is spawned, else with a 15% probability (for a total probability of 50%\*15% = 7.5%), the snare breaks, else (for a total probability of 50%\*85% = 42.5%) nothing happens.

- The Expert Trapper [feat](./Feats.md) greatly increases the odds of any given snare producing a rabbit. (The exact mechanics of this are unclear, but it may involve checking for rabbits twice and using the better result.)
- Snared rabbits count against the [Pacifist](./Pacifist.md) [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) and will lock it for the run.

Snow Pants have the second highest warmth bonus in the game for pants, second only to [Wolfskin Pants](./Wolfskin%20Pants.md), and are tied with [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md) for the highest windproof bonus in the game.

Snow Pants have the same total Warmth+Windproof bonus as Wolfskin Pants, while weighing significantly less, but offering half the protection bonus. Deerskin Pants similarly have higher protection and weight, but less warmth bonus.

Because of their excellent weight to warmth ratio compared to both crafted pants, a player may want to wear one set of snow pants along with a set of crafted pants. When doing so, a player should make certain to wear Deerskin Pants on the outside layer (to benefit from their higher protection and waterproof values), or Wolfskin Pants on the inside (when not in danger of wildlife struggles) to benefit from their higher warmth value.

Even if wolfskin pants are available, a player may still find it more convenient to wear two pairs of Snow Pants, or one pair of Snow Pants with a pair of [Combat Pants](./Combat%20Pants.md) on their inside layer, to conserve their carry weight.

**Snow Shelters** are temporary shelters which can be constructed outdoors in _The Long Dark_.
They provide wind protection and temperature bonus while inside of them, but degrade over time and eventually become ruined unless repaired.

Air temperature inside the snow shelter will always be +15°C higher than air temperature outside the shelter, even if the shelter condition degrades. Additionally shelter provides +3°C bonus when passing time or sleeping (see below). The shelter will provide the bonus even when ruined, until the player leaves it. The warmth bonus from clothing is also used when calculating [Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md) (the windshield warmth bonus from clothing doesn't apply). ![The view from inside a snow shelter](../assets/Snow3.png)_The view from inside a snow shelter_ When inside a Snow Shelter the player can still light [campfires](./Fire.md), use [weapons](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), as well other tasks such as harvesting, repairing clothes, eating or drinking. The player can rest or pass time inside Snow Shelters (similar to cars), even without a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md). If a bedroll is selected, the shelter will provide an additional +3°C warmth bonus. This bonus does not decay together with the shelter, and a 3% shelter will still provide full +3°C bonus.

Once constructed, a snow shelter will degrade from 100% to 0% condition over roughly 188 in-game hours (on Stalker mode) or almost 8 in-game days, after which it will become ruined and can no longer be used or repaired. The decay is not completely linear and is likely influenced by local weather. If dismantled before reaching 0% condition, some of the [Sticks](./Stick.md) and [Cloth](./Cloth.md) used to create it can be reclaimed. Once ruined, dismantling a Snow Shelter will not yield any materials.

After selecting, the player will have to find somewhere to place it. The shelter will turn green when a valid location has been found, if the shelter is unable to be placed it will be red, moving to a leveled plane or bringing the shelter closer should allow it to be placed.
Amount of calories used varies, testing revealed an estimated range of 112 to 263 calories. The value seems to also depend on the character's condition and the weather.

![Snow Shelter's usage menu](../assets/Snowmenu.png)_Snow Shelter's usage menu_ To repair a snow shelter, the player can access the Snow Shelter Menu by clicking on the snow shelter and selecting Repair.

Depending on the condition of the snow shelter, repairing it may require sticks and cloth. The more degraded the shelter is, the more time and materials necessary to repair it. Up until 74%, the shelter will not require cloth. When at 75%, 3 sticks are required to bring it back to 100%. It takes approximately 1 day and 17.5 hours (~42 hours) for shelter to degrade to 75% condition. The shelter will require 1 cloth around 74%, 2 cloth around 48%, and 3 under 30%. The maximum cost of repairing a shelter (when it is 3%) is 10 sticks and 3 cloth.
Snow shelters can be dismantled, and a portion of the items used for building it can be reclaimed (if they are not ruined). This takes 20 in-game minutes.
The amount of calories used varies, with testing showing an estimated range of 38 to 88 calories used while dismantling. It seems to depend on the character's condition and the weather.
- The snow shelter was introduced in [version 0.346](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.346), "Penitent Scholar", on 23 June 2016.

**Something Wicked** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Simply surviving for 1000 days in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) without using [Cheat Death](./Cheat%20Death.md) at all in the save will unlock this. Surviving 1000 days after using Cheat Death will not grant the achievement.
- Consider disabling [Cougar](./Cougar.md) and [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) if playing on [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md) or above to make survival easier.
- [Sleep](./Sleep.md) often and ensure your [Condition](./Condition.md) is high at all times. Always check yourself for negative [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) before sleeping.
- Practice [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md) in order to increase the passage of time in the game world (eating only when sleeping, then resting to make time pass).

- Simply closing the game should you be attacked and you know you will die in the ensuing [Struggle](./Struggle.md) is a method to avoid death (though this will send you back to your last save upon reloading). This method does not work should the game save for any reason during the attack (ex, [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md)/Cougar bites)
- Making a manual backup of your save files every so often can be a good (albeit dishonorable) method to restore a save should you fade into The Long Dark.

The achievement name is an [Easter Egg](./Easter%20Eggs.md) reference to a quote from one of the three witches in Shakespeare's [Macbeth](https://nosweatshakespeare.com/quotes/famous/something-wicked-this-way-comes/):

- The monster in this case being what the player character most likely becomes after doing what they must to survive, eventually conquering Great Bear Island across a 1000 day campaign without dying, after a civilizational ending apocalyptical event no less.
- The icon for the achievement is that of a Reaper, a tool often associated with the personification of Death, also known as the Grim Reaper.

**Spelunker's Lantern** is a unique variant of the [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

Spelunker's Lantern is a mobile source of light and [Warmth](./Warmth.md) which does not require Matches or other firestarters to ignite. The lantern's flame is also windproof, but unlike [Flares](./Flare.md) it will not deter [wolves](./Wolf.md). The lantern requires no external ignition source due to the internal auto-igniter, unlike [Torches](./Torch.md). This allows the Spelunker's Lantern to be quickly extinguished and ignited at any point, so long as there is a sufficient internal fuel store. Lanterns can be placed ("RMB") on any flat surface, even when lit, such as to provide light while crafting or reading at night. Lanterns can be refueled with [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) or a [Jerry Can](./Jerry%20Can.md).

The Spelunker's Lantern does not degrade condition when used or over time, but may suffer damage during a [Bear Struggle](./Struggle.md). It can be repaired with [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) and [Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md). If harvested, any fuel left inside will be added to the survivor's inventory.
- Can hold up to 1 liter (0.26 gallons) of Lantern Fuel which is enough to use continuously for 5 in-game hours and 36 minutes (weighing 1.8 kg when fully fueled)
- The higher the amount of fuel stored inside a lantern, the brighter the light it produces
- When below 10% (0.10kg) fuel and ignited, the Spelunker's Lantern flame will flicker and sputter, and extinguishing itself at 0% fuel

The Spelunker's Lantern can be quickly extinguished without needing to stop the survivor by pressing any hotkey (e.g. "2" to switch to a Weapon), while manually extinguishing it ("LMB") will cause the survivor to stop while extinguishing.
Since version 2.17 the Spelunker's Lantern will spawn in [Interloper](./Interloper.md). It will also spawn on [Misery](./Misery.md).
- 40% more fuel efficient than Storm Lanterns (5 hour 36 minutes of fuel from a full tank VS 4 hours from Storm Lantern)
- 40% less light radius and brightness than Storm Lanterns due to lower fuel consumption (even at full capacity)
Only one Spelunker's Lantern will appear per game world, and its location is randomized between multiple locations in north-eastern Great Bear Island:
- [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md)/Timberwolf Mountain: transition cave ([Loot Table](./Loot%20Table.md) 2 on Interloper)

- Keeper's Pass: Inside the ice cave connecting [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md) and [Keeper's Path South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), in the large chamber near the southern exit. ([Loot Table](./Loot%20Table.md) 1 on Interloper)
- [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md): behind the waterfall in [Misty Falls Cave](./Misty%20Falls%20Cave.md) (Not on Interloper/Misery)
- inside [Chasm Cave](./Chasm%20Cave.md) within [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md) near [Engine](./Engine%20%28East%29.md) (Not on Interloper/Misery)
- inside [Waterfall Cave](./Waterfall%20Cave.md) ([Loot Table](./Loot%20Table.md) 3 on Interloper)
- [Echo Peak East](./Echo%20Peak%20East.md) at the top of the peak behind rocks at the cave ([Loot Table](./Loot%20Table.md) 4 on Interloper)
- [Cave](./Cave%20%28Timberwolf%20Mountain%20location%201%29.md) between [Secluded Shelf](./Secluded%20Shelf.md) and the area below [Summit](./Summit.md) (Not on Interloper/Misery)
You can skip the Extinguish animation (which forces you to stop) by simply holstering the Lantern outright.
The lantern's description is an [Easter Egg](./Easter%20Eggs.md), being a reference to The Lord of the Rings.

**Sport Bow** is a unique variant of the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

The sport bow is a commercially manufactured fiberglass bow with a black handle, red and white paint highlights on its limbs, and an overall dark gray appearance. It is the lightest bow variant in the game while also boasting the second highest durability, just behind the heavy [Woodwright's Bow](./Woodwright%27s%20Bow.md). It is a direct upgrade to the survival bow, however only 2 sport bows can be found per save with no way to obtain more.
- Total durability is 60% more than Survival Bow (uses 1.25%-0.625% condition per shot based on [archery skill](./Archery.md))

There are two sports bows available per game with one located in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) and the other in the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md). Both spawn at 100% condition. The bow's location may differ between saves.

- On the front porch of the [Island Cottage](./Island%20Cottage.md) standing against the wall.
**Zone of Contamination** (As of the December 5th 2023 update: [Tales from the Far Territories](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md): "[Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md)")

- By a corpse inside of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), alongside intact and broken arrows on the ground. The corpse also has various bow-related items on it like arrowheads and crow feathers. There is also a spawn of the [Stay on Target!](./Research%20Book.md) archery research book on the picnic table right next to the corpse. The easiest way to find the room with the corpse is to enter the mine via the map's west-side entrance instead of via the [Conveyor](./Conveyor%20Room.md) entrance. At the intersection where the player can either keep going down or walk up a plank onto a wooden platform, choose the plank. You'll enter an open, high ceiling room with scaffolding at the end of which is a mess hall area for the mine workers. The corpse is laying in the puddle of water at the other end of the mess hall.
- The sport bow will not spawn on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) or [Misery](./Misery.md) difficulty.
- At base archery skill the sport bow can fire a total of 68 times before the risk of breaking starts at the 15% condition threshold.

- At Archery skill level 4 and above, the survivor can fire the Sport bow a total of 136 times before reaching the 15% condition breaking threshold at which the bow will have the chance to break with each shot; starting at a 4% break chance at 12% condition, and increasing to 16% break chance at 9% condition, then to 64% break chance at 3% condition. Because only two sport bows spawn per world, it may be wise to attain archery skill level 4 or above before using them to get the most potential shots per bow.

A **Sprain Risk** is caused by a survivor's [Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md) being over carry weight, and can result in potential sprains.
> “**You are Exhausted or Encumbered, and at a higher risk for a Sprain when traversing sloped ground.**”

Carrying too much weight beyond carrying capacity or becoming too tired to carry your heavy load will warn the player that they are at risk of acquiring a sprain. Walking off road onto uneven ground (icon shown in the photo) may have a chance of a [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md) or [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md) ooccurring.

The exact mechanics that result in a sprain are simple: if the player walks across uneven terrain for more than 10 seconds (and the steep slopes icon doesn't disappear), the player will aquire a sprain. [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md) is not advised when the player has a Sprain Risk, as they will almost certainly sprain themselves when going down sharp terrain.

A **Sprained Ankle** can be caused by a fall, being exhausted or encumbered while walking on uneven or steep terrain, or from an [animal attack](./Struggle.md).
> “**You are Exhausted or Encumbered, and at a higher risk for a Sprain when traversing sloped ground.**”

Carrying too much weight beyond carrying capacity or becoming too tired to carry your heavy load will warn the player that they are at [risk](./Sprain%20Risk.md) of acquiring a sprain. Walking off road onto uneven ground (icon shown in the photo) may have a chance of a [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md) or Ankle occurring. Consider either resting or lightening your load in order to eliminate the risk, or consume a [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) or [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md).
> “**You have twisted your ankle and are now suffering a sprain. Your mobility will be reduced until you treat it, or it heals over time.**”

If a player fails to heed a sprain risk or is attacked by hostile wildlife, they can develop a sprain. Acquiring a sprain will always give the [Pain](./Pain.md) Affliction at the same time. While at least one Sprained Ankle affects the player, sprinting is not possible and the player will walk with a limp, with the screen shaking with each step. 2 Sprained Ankles causes the player to slow down even more and for the screen to shake even further.
- A Sprained Ankle is treated by using a [Bandage](./Bandage.md) or sleeping for 4 cumulative hours. It will not pass on its own.
- The associating Pain Affliction can be treated independently with [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md) or [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md); rest will contribute to resolving all sprains and Pain.
- [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) is not possible with either a Sprained Ankle or Wrist.
- It is possible to sprain both ankles at once, either in the same Struggle event or from continuing to traverse sloped surfaces while over encumbered.

**Spray Paint - Glygh** is the name given to a unique type of [Spray Paint](./Spray%20Paint.md) found in the [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) [Challenge](./Challenge.md). They are vital to surviving and ultimately escaping The Darkwalker.

Spray Paint - Glygh is found in various locations throughout Challenge Escape the Darkwalker, and are primarily used to either dispel the effects of the creature or to halt its progress. Unlike regular spray paint, Glyph Spray cans produce only 4 symbols that have active effects against The Darkwalker.
Spraying a Glyph will always use 0.08 kg of the can's item weight, however it is important to note that a can of spray paint can only paint four glyphs before going empty.
Glyph Spray Paint cans are always found near the green campfires throughout the challenge, though they can occasionally be found inside buildings.

The Lure Glyph creates a mark on the ground that immediately shifts The Darkwalker's focus to that symbol. This lasts 1 hour in-game, or until reached by The Darkwalker. If The Darkwalker reaches a Lure Glyph, it is immediately broken, and a shattering sound can be heard anywhere in the game world. At this point, The Darkwalker will resume chasing after the player.

Only one active Lure can be placed per region at one time, and the timer icon will only appear if it is currently in a space where the player is (ex, timer will disappear if placed indoors and then the player walks outdoors or vice versa), but the game will notify you if the Glyph is still active if you attempt to place another Lure Glyph.

The Ward Glyph creates a symbol on the ground that fortifies a small area (200m), preventing The Darkwalker from approaching for up to 2 hours (in-game). Wards are only active if the player is inside, and the Darkwalker will cease walking and stand in place in the game world until the Glyph is broken or the player leaves its effects. Green Campfires always produce an extended Ward Glyph when approached (up to 12 hours). Only one active Ward can be placed in a region at one time.

The Dispel Glyph immediately reduces the progress of the current region's [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) by 50% of the current buildup (most effective just before Toxic Fog appears). **Useable only o_nce per playthrough._**

The Banish Glyph only unlocks once all 10 [On the Nature of Darkwalkers](./On%20the%20Nature%20of%20Darkwalkers.md) Notes are found during the Challenge and the player makes their way to the Banishing Circle located in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md). Using this Glyph inside the Circle causes the Darkwalker to rapidly approach the player. Once the player is grabbed by the creature within the cirlcle, the Challenge will be completed after it is banished from the Island.

_For the version found in [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md), see [Spray Paint - Glyph](./Spray%20Paint%20-%20Glyph.md)._

Spray Paint is an item which can be used to mark the environment with symbols that aid in navigation, relocating supplies, avoiding danger, etc. Its markings are bright, colored orange images on the painted surface, and on the [map](./Map.md).
Spraying a tag will always use 0.08 kg of the can's item weight. A full can has the capacity for 10 tags.

Cans of Spray Paint can be found in numerous locations, usually inside structures, vehicles, or in towns or industrial areas locations such as the [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) or the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md).

Most but not all markers will display on the map (e.g. "avoid direction" will not). If a marker is painted during low-visibility conditions (blizzards, fog or night) it will not display on the map, but may be added to it by mapping nearby during better visibility later. If multiple symbols are close together, individual markers may not display but rather "multiple markers" on the map; hovering over this icon will display a list of nearby symbols and [rock caches](./Rock%20Cache.md).

There is a limit of 249 markers one can have in a region (approximately 25 spray cans), though most casual players will not reach this limit. If this limit is reached and the player tries to place down another marker, a warning message of "TOO MANY SPRAY PAINT MARKERS IN THIS REGION. ERASE OTHER MARKERS TO CONTINUE SPRAY PAINTING" will appear and prevent them from doing so.
- Spray Paint is visible even in low-light conditions and poor weather, making it useful for navigating indoors at night, or during [Blizzards or Fog outside](./Weather.md).
- There are twelve different marker symbols and most surfaces can accept a marker. Most, but not all markers will appear on the Map (if made during good visibility, or are mapped later).
- Spray Paint may be used directly from the inventory, or via the Radial Menu (Navigation>Spray Paint).
- Spray Paint are always found full (100%)to create a marker costs 10% of it's condition (and reduces the can's weight slightly). Empty cans weight 0.2kg, cannot be refilled and serve no purpose.
- Common uses of Spray Paint include marking looted locations (structures, vehicles, etc.), designating safehouses, aiding navigation in difficult areas, and for decoration.

The **Square Table** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.
A makeshift wooden table, a Square Table can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The table can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor or a flat surface when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value, the table cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the table will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).

Has an interior **St Christopher's Church** is a location a short distance from [Milton](./Milton.md) in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. The church is a possible spawn location for the region and the [Graveyard](./Graveyard.md) is located across the street.

According to a note found in the church, the pastor was Father Francis McGill. He was withdrawn by the Archdiocese due to a lack of activity; however, church services and Latin lessons continued over Skype. A [Hymnal](./Hymnal.md) can be found in the church with the lyrics to the hymn _[Dies Irae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dies_Irae)_ ("Day of Wrath") in both Latin and English.

The church appears to have served as a shelter to someone recently, as there are a few supplies, a makeshift bed, and the remnants of a [Campfire](./Campfire.md) on the floor (allowing the player to light a fire indoors), be careful NOT to deconstruct it as you can not replace the campfire.

Although the church can serve as a base with its bed, nearby rabbit grove, and indoor fireplace, the roof has several holes in it, so it isn't a particularly cozy location to live in. Storage is also limited, and wolves may be a minor hazard when coming and going. [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) just down the road is generally a better base location, with its six-burner stove and abundant storage containers.
- "St. Christopher" is a real-world Christian saint, and is the patron saint of traveling and athletics.
- The [Graveyard](./Graveyard.md) of St. Christopher's Church is the resting place of [Lilith "Lilly" Barker](./Lilith%20Barker.md), as well as many developer names on tombstones.

- From the number of deaths in 1919, Milton's history as a coal mining town, and it's current state of decline, it is implied there was a major mining accident. Considering Great Bear Island's seismic activity, this was likely a tunnel collapse.

- St. Christopher's Church was founded after 1911 and closed before [The First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) with it's remaining members moving to online worship sessions instead, due to declining membership from the town of Milton (as detailed in [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) and Notes). This suggests that Milton was markedly less populous than Thompson's Crossing.

- St Christopher's Church is one of three churches on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md); the other two being the [Stone Church](./Stone%20Church.md) of [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), and the Catholic or Episcopal church of [Thompson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md).

- _[Dies Irae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dies_Irae)_ is a Latin hymn dating to the 13th century at the latest. It has been used in music, religion, and popular culture for centuries to symbolize death.

Stacks of papers fill the role of tinder, which is used for [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md). Stacks of papers are among the heaviest types of tinder, and weigh 0.10 kg per unit. **Stacy's Grape Soda** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

It can be consumed to restore 250 [calories](./Hunger.md) as well as 30% [hydration](./Thirst.md), the equivalent of 0.20 litres of [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md). They are found uncommonly inside all types of structures, [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md), and on [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md).
All three types of soda share the same calories and hydration. Stacy's Grape Soda never causes [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md).

- "Stacy's Grape Soda" was named after [Stacyplays](https://www.youtube.com/user/stacyplays) (aka Stacy Hinojosa), a YouTuber who ran a "let's play" series during The Long Dark's alpha/beta (2014-2016). In her videos she mentions how grape soda is her favorite type of drink. Her photograph is also present hanging inside of some houses in Coastal Highway.
- The back of a Grape Soda lists "Ingredients: Carbonated Water, High Fructose Corn Syrup, Natural Flavours, Blue 1, Red 40."

A [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md) may be found in a small cove to the north-east. Many waterfalls can be found on the southern end of the lake. Both [wolves](./Wolf.md) and deer may be found wandering around on the ice of the frozen lake.

While the lake doesn't offer any shelter, there is a cave a short walk to the northeast, which can make for a short-term decent campsite for weary travelers who have recently entered the region and/or want to explore the southwestern part of the map. This cave offers a warmth bonus, like most of the small caves scattered throughout Great Bear Island. A [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) often spawns in the cave, and the cave is a possible spawn point for the [Expedition Parka](./Expedition%20Parka.md) and [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md).

Although the cave makes for a good short-term base, it is not ideal for the longer term due to the presence of nearby wolves. While the density of wolves in the local area isn't as high as in some locations (i.e. around [Angler's Den](./Angler%27s%20Den.md)), the rolling terrain and dense forest around the cave makes them difficult to spot at a distance. Additionally, the wolves will enter the cave if the player is carrying smelly items.

**Stalker's Pie** is a food item in _The Long Dark_, it is learned from a unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) and is made with a [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md).

Stalker's Pie is a relatively complex recipe, requiring meat from multiple [predatory wildlife](./Bear.md), and with a recipe card found in the wilderness region of [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md). It boasts a number of small positive effects and extremely high calorie density at ~6,667 kcal/kg (beating the MRE at 3,500 kcal/kg although losing to Breyerhouse pie with 7,083 kcal/kg) and it has several positive effects. It requires a maximized [Cooking skill](./Cooking.md) and reduces carry weight when consumed, and its ingredients are either limited or difficult to obtain.

While the ingredients of Stalker's Pie are relatively easy to source (though [Acorn Grounds](./Acorn%20Grounds.md) require a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) to be produced), it requires raw meat from two different predatory species: [Wolves](./Wolf.md) and [Black Bear](./Bear.md). Any species of wolf meat will work for Stalker's Pie (except [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md)), either from wolf carcasses scattered across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), or by hunting live wolves with a [weapon](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) or surviving a [struggle](./Struggle.md). Black Bear can only be killed with ranged weapons, making hunting them a necessity to crafting Stalker's Pie.

The recipe for Stalker's Pie is found on a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), which may appear in three different outdoors locations near along the black bear's patrol route near [Stairsteps Lake](./Stairsteps%20Lake.md) in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md).
Stalker's Pie produces a [Scent](./Scent.md) which attracts [predators](./Wolf.md), and may be dropped as a [decoy](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys).
- 6 hours of [Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md) (+1% [Condition](./Condition.md) restored per hour of sleep, or 18 hours)

The ingredients of this pie are the similar to [Breyerhouse Pie](./Breyerhouse%20Pie.md), requiring predator [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) meat and [Acorn Grounds](./Acorn%20Grounds.md) instead of prey meat and [flour](./Old%20Mill%20Flour.md).

**Stalker** is the 3rd [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) Experience in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is the standard "hard" difficulty setting.

Stalker features a more unforgiving Experience compared to [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md) or [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md), featuring a harder world, [Needs](./Needs.md) that drain very quickly, and harsher [Struggle](./Struggle.md) mechanics. Stalker is the hardest standard game mode in the game, with [Interloper](./Interloper.md) and [Misery](./Misery.md) being their own special level of difficulty.
Stalker introduces a new [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) that makes it harder to survive in the game world: [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md).
- Hostile [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) may spawn immediately, are more numerous, and are found in more locations.
- Eating cooked or uncooked meat from predator animals has a chance to give the player [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md).
- Start will be outdoors: chance to start during night, poor weather, or in an inhospitable [Region](./Region.md).
- [Fires](./Fire.md) do not automatically prevent [freezing](./Hypothermia.md) ("Feels Like" Temperature must be raised above 0° C).
- The player will automatically wake up once their [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) meter is fully rested, and they cannot go back to sleep until sufficiently tired.
- Sheltering indoors for too long will result in the [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) [Affliction](./Afflictions.md), with a quicker Risk buildup compared to Voyageur.
- The option to enable the [Trader](./Trader.md), [Cougar](./Cougar.md), and [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) on or off is present.

**Stamina** represents the player's ability to undertake several physically demanding tasks. Sprinting or Rope Climbing both reduce stamina. When the stamina bar is completely drained, rope climbing becomes slower and more dangerous, and the player is unable to sprint. The stamina bar will gradually refill itself when not in active use. [fr:Stamina](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamina)

The amount of stamina that the player has is set and cannot be increased through leveling skills. The current maximum stamina can be viewed by navigating to the _Clothing_ screen within the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md).

[Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) affects the replenishment of stamina. When the character reaches **Exhausted** (empty fatigue bar), the stamina bar is completely drained. It will remain drained for as long as the fatigue bar remains empty.
Different types of clothing have a different mobility penalty attached to them. When wearing clothing with a higher mobility penalty, the player's stamina bar will have a lower maximum capacity.

"_Walking through the snow with a heavy pack can get tiring, but sometimes you just have to run. Escape wildlife, avoid weak ice, or get to shelter faster by Sprinting. Keep in mind that Sprinting uses up more Calories than Walking, and your Sprint stamina is limited by how restrictive your Clothing is. It takes you a little while to recover Sprint stamina, so use it wisely!_"

Sprint is a gameplay mechanic that enables the player to move faster. When active the player can run much faster than walking speed, at about 10.0 m/s (36 km/h) on level ground, as opposed to around 3.70 m/s (13.30 km/h) when walking. Sprinting can be used for evasion, avoiding [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md), or simply moving quickly to another location.

Climbing a deployed Climbing Rope is the most strenuous activity in The Long Dark, which drains [Rest](./Fatigue.md), Calories, and Stamina as one climbs or merely suspends oneself mid-climb. If Stamina reaches zero mid-climb, the climbing rate (up or down) will slow significantly and there is a chance to slip and/or fall, harming [Condition](./Condition.md), causing a bleeding [Laceration](./Laceration.md), [tearing clothes](./Torn%20Clothing.md), or even killing the player outright.

How fast one climbs is greatly affected by current [Rest](./Fatigue.md) and Weight. Climbing while at high Rest (and/or low Weight) will make for an faster climb and burning less calories; conversely at low Rest (and/or high Weight) makes Climbs take far longer, burning more calories and Rest while also risking slipping from a rope, injury, or death. Because of this, it is possible to become stranded at many climbing locations; so slow that it may be impossible to complete before draining all stamina and then slipping and eventually falling off. [Crampons](./Crampons.md) and [Improvised Crampons](./Improvised%20Crampons.md) decrease stamina drain while Rope Climbing at a respective 60% and 40% per second spent on a climb.

Deployed Climbing Ropes cannot be climbed (up or down) if the player has a [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md) or [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md), or [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md). This result in the player becoming stranded at certain locations where climbs are mandatory. [Bandages](./Bandage.md) used to treat a sprain can be life-saving in such situations, but since Broken Ribs require [Painkillers](./Painkillers.md) or [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md) and long amounts of time, this can be harder or even impossible to treat if unprepared (such as in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) basin, or [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md)).
Emergency Stims can be used just prior to a Climb in emergency situations, to perform an otherwise impossible climb (such as if one is too tired).
It can be dangerous to Sprint just prior to a Climb, without allowing Stamina to recover.
Several [Feats](./Feats.md) can affect the player's stamina and are listed below, along with the requirements for unlocking and the unique effects.

**Images Needed:****This article is in need of more images and/or higher quality images. You can help by uploading an image and [//dummy.host/index.php?title=Steam+Train&action=edit adding it to the article].** [Steam Loco idle 1](../assets/Steam_Loco_idle_1.png)The **Steam Train** is a player driven and controlled [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) found exclusively in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). It is the main method of transportation in the [Railway](./Railway.md) region, during the mission [To SAR And Back](./To%20SAR%20And%20Back.md). A successor to the Steam Train appears in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) in the [Iron Road](./Iron%20Road.md) Expansion as the Prototype Steam Train.

The locomotive takes the shape of a [0-4-0 ST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/0-4-0) steam locomotive, carrying the number 46, with two electrically-powered headlights on the front (which will come on during the Aurora), along with a snowplow pilot. Being a tank locomotive, it does not have a tender. Curiously, it does not have a fuel bunker, requiring [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) to regularly add coal to the firebox from her inventory. It also does not require the water tanks to be filled up.

According to the [Piece of Paper](./Piece%20of%20Paper%20%282%29.md) found in the Train Maintenance Shed, the engine was nicknamed "Goose" and was going to be put on display at the Maintenance Shed, with hopes that it could draw people up north towards Perseverance Mills and bring attention to the isolated town. It is unknown whether the locomotive was put on display, or not.

![View from the cab of the locomotive](../assets/Steam_Loco_driving_1.png)_View from the cab of the locomotive_Before operation, the Throttle [Train Lever](./Train%20Lever.md) needs to be reinstalled in the locomotive. The lever can be found on the wall near a drill press in the nearby maintenance shed. This will progress the mission to the next stage.

> “**Use Coal to get the Steam Train Firebox temperature up to 125 degrees to start building pressure (PSI). The firebox will slowly cool off over time if you don't keep feeding it coal but never below 125 degrees.**”

A fire can be lit in the firebox in the conventional way. Once lit, the temperature must be brought up to 125°C (225°F). Using wood of any kind will not raise the firebox temperature in order to start generating steam pressure. Instead, [Coal](./Coal.md) must be used to greatly increase the firebox temperature.

As the temperature rises to 125°C (225°F), PSI is built up on a dial that will allow the Steam Train to move forwards or backwards once the Throttle is released. Over time and as the train is used for transportation, the fire's temperature will decrease, requiring periodic additions of coal to continue generating steam PSI.

> “**Move the throttle up through gears 1 and 2 to increase the Steam Train's Speed or into Reverse to change directions. Using the Brake will automatically put the Steam Train into its Neutral Gear. The Throttle can only be adjusted if the Brake is off and the Steam Train can only change directions when it is fully stopped.**”

Once the locomotive has built enough steam PSI, it can be driven by releasing the brakes and engaging the throttle. The locomotive can maintain boiler pressure at half-throttle indefinitely, but full throttle must be used to push away obstacles such as fallen trees, snowdrifts, or fence gates. It is also capable of pushing some road-rail trucks and some railroad cars out of the way. The steam whistle can be used to scare [wolves](./Wolf.md) away. The train can be reversed and can automatically apply the brakes if selected.

> “**The Steam Train can move at two speeds "Slow" and "Fast". When the Steam Train is moving fast enough it can break through obstacles that would otherwise block its path. But increasing the Steam Train's speed will consume PSI.**”
Various obstacles can be broken when the train reaches the "Fast" speed setting on the speed dial. These obstacles are required to be cleared in order to progress through the mission.
- Despite being equipped with couplers, the locomotive is not able to couple to and pull train cars behind it.
- The train's firebox generates a substantial amount of heat, enough to warm the player when inside the controls.
- At full speed, the locomotive is the fastest way of moving on Great Bear, easily capable of overtaking a running [Deer](./Deer.md) or [Wolf](./Wolf.md).
- The locomotive can't be derailed in normal gameplay, nor can it be blown up by over pressuring.
- It is not possible to eat, drink, pass time, or sleep while driving the locomotive. Only the map can be brought up in the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md).
- Wildlife will not be killed if the steam locomotive runs over them. Wildlife will also be scared of the whistle if they are close by.
- A Train Brake Lever icon is found in the game files, but was never actually implemented as an item. The brake lever is already installed once the player finds the train.

The Blackrock Dam **Steam Tunnels** are a sprawling system of Dark tunnels located in the region Blackrock, added in the Perilous Constraint Update on December 8th 2021.

The Steam Tunnels can be accessed through an entrance across the bridge from the main Blackrock Electric Dam as well as a small structure alongside the [Blackrock Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md).

Despite there being no known hostile life in the Tunnels, it is still a very daunting location to explore, as it is made up entirely of dark, long winding passageways impossible to navigate without a light source. Live wires during the Aurora can also rapidly burn careless players who travel through the tunnels.

Within the tunnels there are several Fire Barrels, with plenty of firewood and other fuel scattered throughout, it is recommended that players without Storm Lanterns use these to provide torches, as there is enough fuel to make a fire last a great many hours.
If entering from the prison, taking the first right turn will lead to the power plant. Vice versa, if entering from the power plant, taking the first left turn will lead to the prison.

A main task of [Episode 4: Fury, then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), [The Power Plant](./The%20Power%20Plant.md), [Mathis](./Mathis.md) asks you to restore the electrical system. You talk to [Jace](./Jace.md) at the Dam and your Mission changes to sabotage. In the Steam Tunnels you open and close the valves, melting the ice at the right temperature and pressure, opening the doors and making it difficult to open the solitary cell from the main engine.

Torches (including Ruined Torches) may be harvested into a stick, for just 2 minutes (in-game).

Sticks can be found near trees on the ground. They can also be obtained by breaking down branches or [scrub brush](./Scrub%20Brush.md). It takes 10 minutes (5 with a hatchet) to break branch into three sticks.

While sticks have one of the worst burning time to kg ratios (second only to [books](./Book.md)), each stick adds 1°C to the fire, with each hour's worth of burn time adding 8°C to the fire. This causes large numbers of sticks to produce hot and relatively short-lived fires (most fuel sources yield 6°C per hour of burn time, [firelogs](./Firelog.md) yield 10.5°C and [coal](./Coal.md) yields 20°C).

Sticks' short burn time gives control over a fire's duration, minimizing waste of fuel or matching timed tasks such as [melting snow](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md) and [boiling water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), or to extend a fire to harvest a [torch](./Torch.md).

Sticks can also be used as a basic compass, because when dropped they will point towards the "north" of the map when outdoors. Not all maps have a properly represented north as "up", but dropped sticks will always point in the same direction on the same map.

It's commonly believed that sticks respawn after strong winds or blizzards, but this is untrue. Radial spawns (sticks, branches, coal, stones ect.) simply spawn on a randomized timer, independent of any weather conditions.

Provides some shelter **Stone Church** is a dilapidated chapel found in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md).

The Stone Church lies just east of the [Abandoned Mine No. 5](./Abandoned%20Mine%20No.%205.md) (west entrance). Several [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) and a few other medicinal plants surround the church. Within the church you'll find a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md), possibly a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), and some resources, potentially including:
- [Revolver](./Revolver.md) (Has a small chance to be found next to the corpse, if it does spawn.)
The church walls and windows are damaged, so the structure offers only modest protection against the cold and wind, and may not even protect against aggressive [wildlife](./Wildlife.md).

Despite these limitations, a player with decently warm [clothing](./Clothing.md), a bed roll, and/or plenty of fuel can usually wait out a blizzard or hide from prowling wolves. High-quality clothing can even allow the church to serve as a functional [Safe House](./Safehouse.md), although the nearby mine is safer and warmer.

The church is considered an indoor area (slow movement like a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md)) and it gives a warmth bonus but it doesn't count towards [Cabin Fever Risk](./Cabin%20Fever%20Risk.md), which makes it an ideal location to pass time to reduce Cabin Fever risk.

- Based on its name and architecture the Stone Church is likely a Christian building, though it is unknown what denomination or time period it was constructed in. Considering its dilapidated state and emphasis on stone instead of more modern materials, it is likely the oldest church on Great Bear.

- The Stone Church is one of four churches on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md); the other two being the Catholic [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md) of [Milton](./Milton.md), the inaccessible church at [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), and the Catholic or Episcopal church of [Thompson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md).

- It is suggested Thompson's Crossing was the largest remaining settlement on Great Bear Island prior to [The First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), because Milton's church was closed due to the town's declining population (as detailed in [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) and Notes), and the Desolation Point's church seems derelict for years if not decades.

A **Stone** is a throwable item found scattered around all maps. It can be picked up and used as a distraction or make-shift weapon against [Wolves](./Wolf.md).

Stones are an excellent tool for hunting [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigans](./Ptarmigan.md); they are abundant, relatively simple to use, can stun these animals with no additional resources, and are reusable. Stones may also be strategically placed to mark paths or important locations the player may wish to remember later.
Stones can also be used to lower the morale of an attacking [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) pack, by hitting or landing near one of its members.

Rabbits and Ptarmigans are stunned by a direct hit with a stone, which requires some practice with sneaking near enough to the small animals and aiming roughly in the center of the thumb and forefinger "reticule." If the player picks up the animal within a few seconds, the game gives you the option to kill or release it, otherwise it will recover from its stunned state and flee the area.

Rabbits and [Deer](./Deer.md) will flee from the landing site of thrown stones, which is useful for flushing prey while hunting. [Wolves](./Wolf.md), [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) and [bears](./Bear.md) will investigate the landing sites of thrown stones (if not already stalking the player) before returning to their patrol. The distraction may provide enough time to escape from dead ends or through areas otherwise obstructed by patrolling predators.
[Ptarmigans](./Ptarmigan.md) will also flee and take to the air if a stone is thrown near them, making it impossible to lure them to predator animals for hunting.

- [Wolves](./Wolf.md) will flee after being directly struck in the head with a thrown stone, also causing a small patch of blood to fall to the ground (but not causing bleedout to begin). Throwing or even just aiming a stone if near a fire or an unreachable place for a wolf is most useful for discouraging wolves from stalking the player, or scaring them off of an animal carcass; however, aiming (right-click) at a stalking wolf may also provoke it to begin an attack run.

- [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) behave similarly to wolves with thrown stones; if a timberwolf pack is engaging the player, thrown stones landing near them or directly striking them will lower the pack's morale.
- [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) behave similarly to regular Wolves when Stones are used on or around them.
- [Moose](./Moose.md) will flee from thrown stones as long as they have not detected the player, if they have detected the player they will become enraged instead.
- [Cougar](./Cougar.md) will investigate tossed stones, but will ignore them if they start stalking the player.
Like [arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md), stones will ricochet off terrain and objects if striking at an oblique angle.

![Aim in between the index finger and thumb. The red circle is where the Stone will land.](../assets/Stone_Aim_Guide.png)_Aim in between the index finger and thumb. The red circle is where the Stone will land._ By holding the "Aim" Option, position your target between the thumb and index finger as shown in the example photo. Stones typically land in this area, though a few factors need to be taken into account before throwing:
- Always be aware of where the target currently is and the timing of the throw. You will miss if you do not factor this in, it will alert your target when you miss.
- If the target is moving, always aim slightly in front of them before throwing, as aiming where the target currently is will cause the Stone to miss once it leaves your hand.

- Gloves can make throwing more difficult since the index finger is covered up. Try practicing with [Driving Gloves](./Driving%20Gloves.md) or similar non-mitten gloves or simply remove any mittens first, then when you become better with throwing Stones, practice with mittens on.

The **Storm Lantern** is a mobile light source that creates a large amount of light and a paltry amount of [Warmth](./Warmth.md). The lantern's glass-encased flame allows the player to use it in even the windiest conditions, making it and the [Flare](./Flare.md) the only light sources not reduced or extinguished by wind.

Storm Lantern is a mobile source of light and [Warmth](./Warmth.md) which does not require Matches or other firestarters to ignite. The lantern's flame is also windproof, but unlike [Flares](./Flare.md) it will not deter [wolves](./Wolf.md). The lantern requires no external ignition source, unlike [Torches](./Torch.md). Lanterns can be placed ("RMB") on any flat surface, even when lit such as to provide light while crafting or reading at night. Lanterns can be refueled from [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) or a [Jerry Can](./Jerry%20Can.md).

The Storm Lantern does not degrade condition when used or over time, but may suffer damage during a [Bear Struggle](./Struggle.md). It can be repaired with [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) and [Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md). If harvested, any fuel left inside of it it will be added to the survivor's inventory.
- Auto-igniter allows the Storm Lantern to be quickly ignited/extinguished without needing to use [Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md) like a [Torch](./Torch.md) would.
- Can hold up to 1 liter (0.26 gallons) of Lantern Fuel which is enough to use continuously for 4 in-game hours (weighing 1.8 kg when fully fueled)
- The higher the amount of fuel stored inside Storm Lantern, the brighter the light it produces
- When below 10% (0.10kg) fuel and ignited, the Storm Lantern flame will flicker and sputter, and extinguishing itself at 0% fuel

The Storm Lantern can be quickly extinguished without needing to stop the survivor by pressing any hotkey (e.g. "2" to switch to a Weapon), while manually extinguishing it ("LMB") will cause the survivor to stop while extinguishing.
- You can skip the Extinguish animation (which forces you to stop) by simply holstering the Lamp outright.

- The in-game model for the storm lantern appears to lack several vital components needed for an ordinary kerosene pressure lamp to function; such as a mantle, generator tube, pressure pump, and pre heater cup.
- A Storm Lantern is much brighter compared to the [Spelunker's Lantern](./Spelunker%27s%20Lantern.md), but consumes fuel faster.
- The Storm Lantern is most likely based on the Coleman 335 or 321 gas mantle lantern, which burns naphthalene or low grade gasoline instead of kerosene.

The **Stove** (technically a kitchen stove) is an immovable fire barrel. The wood stove functions identically to other contained fires and player-made [Campfire](./Campfire.md), and, like all contained fires, isn't blown out by high winds.

Stoves are considered the most valuable firebox, as they have _six_ [Cooking](./Cooking.md) slots, allowing the player to cook more food and drinks for the same amount of fuel than any other firebox. Usually one or more [Cooking Pots](./Cooking%20Pot.md) or [Recycled Cans](./Recycled%20Can.md) are found on the stove.
The Stove can be re-lit indefinitely, though it requires fresh starter, tinder, and fuel each time.
