Note some [Tools](./Tools.md) cannot be selected as defense options during a Wolf Struggle, this includes the [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md), [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md), [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md), [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md), and [Stone](./Stone.md).

Struggles with [Wolves](./Wolf.md) vary in length and severity based upon how quickly the left mouse button can be clicked, the player's [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) difficulty, which Tools was selected, and RNG.

At the start of a Struggle with a Wolf, the world will slow down and the HUD will present a list of Tool options in the player's inventory for defense; while the struggle lasts the player can attack the wolf with this tool by left-clicking. At intervals the Wolf will attack the player, causing Condition loss and a chance to generate Afflictions.

The Wolf Struggle will end immediately if either the player or Wolf die, the Wolf is scared off (chance after losing 75% or more of its health), or after a set length of time (resulting in a 'Wolf Win', wherein the Wolf walks away and player regains consciousness and stands up). Wolves which are scared off will be scared until they reach a minimum distance of about 40 meters away from the player if they are not afflicted by Blood Loss from knife puncturing.
If the player is below 50% [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), they will deal reduced damage to Wolves during struggles (except with Revolver 'Take Shot' action).
Higher Survival Mode difficulties increases the damage Wolves deal per attack during Struggles substantially, particularly on Interloper.
Injured Wolves are much easier to scare during Struggles than full health Wolves, and often can be killed during a Struggle.

![A Poisoned Wolf afflicting a Sprain during a Struggle.](../assets/Poisoned_Wolf_Struggle.jpg)_A Poisoned Wolf afflicting a Sprain during a Struggle._ Struggles with [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) are virtually identical to regular Wolves, but will always result in [Chemical Poisoning Risk](./Chemical%20Poisoning%20Risk.md) buildup when a player is attacked. Due to the desperate and malnourished state that regular Poisoned Wolves suffer from, encounters with them are generally more likely to result in Struggles.

![A Timberwolf initiating a Struggle](../assets/Timberwolf.jpg)_A Timberwolf initiating a Struggle_ Timberwolves typically perform "bite and run" tactics by performing a single bite attack and then quickly keeping their distance during a pack attack in order to wear the player's health down. Occasionally, a single [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) will grapple the player and initiate a Struggle to finish a survivor off after enough time has passed in an encounter, or if a player remains still for too long. The same principles of regular Wolf Struggles apply to these situations, presenting the player with a choice to pick a weapon to defend one's self.

Maulings are a more aggressive version of Struggles, wherein the player is unable to defend one's self once a Struggle begins. This is typically an in-game cutscene where the player is helplessly overwhelmed and attacked by hostile wildlife.

![Screen 94b5eb73 fd2a 4e19 8f1c 8391b2ad7bd8 hi](../assets/Screen_94b5eb73-fd2a-4e19-8f1c-8391b2ad7bd8_hi.png) A Struggle with a [Bear](./Bear.md) will always result in a loss for the player, because they are unable to take any action during this time. This will result in a loss of -60-90% of pre-struggle condition remaining and two Afflictions: Blood Loss and Infection Risk. Any tools the player is currently holding will be dropped to the ground (along with a random item in the player's inventory) and must be picked up once the player regains consciousness. This can result in wasted [Torch](./Torch.md), [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), [Flare](./Flare.md) fuel if the player is not careful.

During Wintermute's Chapter 2, the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) may be used against a charging Bear for a "Bear Spear Struggle", which can be won or lost by the player. Hinterland has stated that the spear may become available in Survival Mode in the future.

The in-game mechanics of bear mauling can be deduced from [this YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ksxK6WhZK7I) by analyzing it [in slow motion](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RNON5hzr2lk).
- [Condition](./Condition.md) damage, along with [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) and [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md), is applied as soon as the bear makes contact with the player's hitbox.
- The player's items are scattered about and [Clothing](./Clothing.md) is damaged _after the struggle is over_.
- If the bear dies during the struggle (i.e. from blood loss), then the player has "won", their clothing remains intact, and everything remains in their backpack.

![Moose Struggle](../assets/Moose_Struggle.jpg) Similar to Bears, a Struggle with a [Moose](./Moose.md) will always result in a loss. The Moose tramples the player and knocks them to their feet, then stomps several times before the player passes out. Upon waking up, the player will be temporarily disoriented and lose about 50% Condition, as well as obtaining a [Broken Ribs](./Broken%20Ribs.md) Affliction. Any tools the player is holding when a Moose attacks will be lying on the ground nearby when the player regains consciousness, similar to a Bear mauling.

[Cougars](./Cougar.md) possess two types of attacks, a 'glancing blow' and a Cougar Struggle. Both occur when a cougar makes physical contact with the survivor, with glancing blows being more likely if the survivor recently struck the cougar with a ranged weapon.

Cougar [Struggles](./Struggle.md) are an event (similar to [Bear](./Bear.md) or [Moose](./Moose.md) struggles), featuring a mauling cutscene and does not grant the option for the survivor to defend themselves.

- **Glancing Attack**: (similar to [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md)) where The Cougar deals small amounts of [Condition](./Condition.md) damage, with a chance for [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) and [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md), or [Torn Clothing](./Torn%20Clothing.md). Glancing Attacks are more likely if the survivor manages to hit a charging Cougar with a ranged weapon (e.g. [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md)).

- **Cougar Struggle**: which causes 50% Condition damage and the unique affliction [Severe Lacerations](./Severe%20Lacerations.md), which periodically inflicts Blood Loss and Infection Risk repeatedly over time.

The first iteration of the Cougar was unique in that their struggles were a mix of both a Mauling and a normal Struggle. Cougar struggles begins as an event while the survivor is outdoors in a Cougar infested region; it may be prevented by being indoors or leaving the infested region. Similar to [Bear](./Bear.md) and [Moose](./Moose.md) struggles, Cougar struggles are a Mauling cutscene and may not be defended against with a tool:
Cougar struggles always give the player the unique [Severe Lacerations](./Severe%20Lacerations.md) (As well as Blood Loss, Infection Risk, Sprains), and leave the player at 10% Condition afterwards.

1. **Note**: The "Severe Lacerations" affliction lasts for 72 in-game hours and periodically to afflicts the survivor with Blood Loss and Infection Risk every 12 hours (requiring a [Bandage](./Bandage.md) and [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md) to treat). This makes Time Accelerating (Sleep, Pass Time, Crafting, Harvesting, etc) extremely dangerous while afflicted.

2. **Note**: Blood Loss causes 30% Condition loss per hour, **and each application of the affliction stacks**. This can quickly kill a survivor without enough bandages to treat their wounds, or if Severe Lacerations applies a new Blood Loss.
If the player survives a Cougar struggle and has at least one weapon in their inventory, they will have the option to fire a single shot at the retreating animal.
- Strike (fire a single [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Revolver](./Revolver.md) or [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) shot, or faint after 10 seconds)

If a "Strike" is chosen, the survivor will get to their feet and draw that weapon your weapon of choice. The world will be in slow motion and the Cougar will be nearby, fleeing in a random direction and may be obscured by terrain or obstacles. The player can then aim at the animal, but the camera will shake and turn to reflect the critical state of the survivor after the struggle, making the shot very difficult. The player will be able to take a single shot (or they will pass out after 10 seconds if they wait too long) and the screen will go black before they wake up again.
- If the player's shot hits the Cougar, it will be found dead nearby when the player wakes up.

- If the shot misses the Cougar, it will escape and continue hunting the survivor. Failing to kill a Cougar can result in a new encounter and possible struggle as soon as 2 hours pass, possibly even sooner.
Note: [Stones](./Stone.md), [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) and all other [tools](./Hatchet.md) may not be selected during a Cougar struggle.

Struggles with Wolves during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) will result in a far more aggressive attack. Wolves will typically deal more damage, have a higher willpower that prevents them from fleeing when using tools that Scare them during a Struggle, and require more force with tools to end a Struggle. Extreme caution should be taken when traveling during the Aurora when encountering Wolves.
Aurora Bears will also be just as aggressive, but their damage values remain consistent; resulting in -60-90% Condition lost in the attack.
_A "Demon Wolf" in the [4 Days of Night Event](./4%20Days%20of%20Night%20Event.md) attacking the player_
[^3]: Struggle is guaranteed to end after "Take Shot" is chosen (70% to flee, 30% to kill)

**Treatment:** Find breathable air or equip a [Respirator icon](../assets/Respirator_icon.png) [Respirator](./Respirator.md) with [Canister icon](../assets/Canister_icon.png) [Canister](./Canister.md)

**Suffocation Risk** is a very short but highly lethal [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) that occurs when the player character is exposed to toxic airborne gases. It is a rare but incredibly dangerous Affliction to encounter in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), being present only within the [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) mine and the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md).

It was first present in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), specifically [Episode 4: Fury, then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), where it can be encountered in three separate locations. Several areas of the Last Prospect mine, [one smoke filled section](./Donner.md) of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), and the destroyed [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) near the end of the episode.
> “**You are running out of air to breathe. Find a pocket of clear air or equip a Respirator before you die.**”

Unlike most other Afflictions, Suffocation Risk does not build up over time, instead being replaced with a timer in the bottom left corner of the screen that counts down in real seconds as long as the player character remains within a toxic cloud's area of effect. The player's vision will also begin to blur as the player character begins coughing and tearing up from breathing in the gas, along with a noticeable loss of hearing.

Wearing a [Respirator](./Respirator.md) with sufficient [Canisters](./Canister.md) may also be equipped to prevent Suffocation and adds 45 seconds of breathable air when passing through a gas cloud. Once the Condition of air Canisters is ruined, the player will begin to suffocate again if they run out of replacements, even when wearing the Respirator.

Once the timer reaches 0, _**the player will die instantly**_, regardless of how much [Condition](./Condition.md) they have left (similar to falling from an extreme height). Reaching an area with clean air will reset the countdown and slowly restore the player character's vision and hearing. Forcing clean air into the gas clouds using nearby machinery, such as in the Last Prospect mines in Episode 4 with a [Valve Socket Handle](./Valve%20Socket%20Handle.md) (Wintermute Only), will also reset the countdown.

- Suffocation was introduced in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) of the Wintermute story mode campaign. It was later added to Survival Mode in the Perilous Constraint update. Further more, it was reintroduced in the Langston Mine in the Buried Echoes update in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md).

- It is impossible to burn toxic mineshaft gas up with any fire source, such as [campfires](./Campfire.md), [noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md), [torches](./Torch.md), [matches](./Wood%20Matches.md), or gunfire, as the gas is not flammable.

- Fixed an issue that caused graphical corruption when entering areas that contain a risk of Suffocation (such as the Steam Tunnels in Episode Four), or when enabling the Heritage Filter in the Display Options.
- [EP 4] Fixed an issue that would cause Players to become stuck in the Suffocating state if they saved and reloaded while suffocating.

**Summit Soda** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

It can be consumed to restore 250 [calories](./Hunger.md) as well as 30% [hydration](./Thirst.md), the equivalent of 0.20 litres of [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md). They are found commonly inside all types of structures, [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md), and on [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md).
There are two other kinds of soda: [Orange Soda](./Orange%20Soda.md) and [Stacy's Grape Soda](./Stacy%27s%20Grape%20Soda.md). All three types of soda share the same calories and hydration.
- Summit Soda is packaged as a product named "_Summit Soda"_, possibly a reference to [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) or the real-life brand "Mountain Dew."
- It could also be similar to the lemon-lime flavored "Sprite" due to its green can coloration.
- Despite being statistically identical to other Sodas, only Summit Soda will spawn on [Interloper Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md).
- The ingredients on the back list: "Carbonated Water, High Fructose Corn Syrup, Natural Flavours."

The Summit contains two other locations of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md). They are:
Additionally, there is a small [cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) located near the end of the rope climb leading up to the summit.
1. From [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md), travel to [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md): requires at least 1 rope climb (via the cave system or [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md))

2. At [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md) climb to [Secluded Shelf](./Secluded%20Shelf.md) and enter to the cave system ("Cave B" to "Cave A" on the map linked above), a section of tunnel requires crouching to pass through: this is the exit.
3. Exit the cave, turn right and continue to the longest rope climb before the summit. There are two ledges to rest at along the way.

- Climbing ropes drain stamina and fatigue rapidly. Rest before climbing at ledges mid-climb to recover [fatigue](./Fatigue.md), or by consuming [coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md), [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md), or [Emergency Stims](./Emergency%20Stim.md) (last resort).
- [Blizzards](./Weather.md) are dangerous. Take shelter in caves and keep warm with a [campfire](./Fire.md) while waiting for weather to clear.

It is possible to reach the Summit on day one of a playthrough, depending on the spawn. Because of the multiple required rope climbs, it may be advantageous to prepare for the trip by accumulating coffee and bringing a light source for spelunking.

[Mountaineering Ropes](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) are not necessary on the return trip to the [mountaineer's hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md), but make the trip easier and grant fast access to [Eric's falls](./Eric%27s%20Falls.md) and another [Cargo Container](./Cargo%20Container.md) full of tin cans of [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) (normally, there are three ropes that always spawned: two at the summit or [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md), and one in the mountaineer's hut). An alternative and risky but very fast way to descend is to [carefully walk down](./Mountain%20Goating.md) the side of the mountain slope facing [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md).
- [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) were ironically absent from "Timberwolf" Mountain until December 2024.
- This region was also introduced long before Timberwolves were implemented into the game.

- Contrary to popular belief, but not a canonical measurement: Timberwolf Mountain's summit is not the highest accessible point in-game. Screenshot measurements reveal its altitude to be 505 meters above sea level in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md).
- This is lower than [Peak Cave](./Peak%20Cave.md) in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), which is 590 meters above sea level in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md).
- The southern entrance of the [cave](./Cave%20%28Mountain%20Town%20location%29.md) in [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) is higher still, at 612 meters.
- Also, the [Wolf's Jaw Overlook](./Wolf%27s%20Jaw%20Overlook.md) in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) is very likely to be higher than the Summit.

> “__For advanced players. Once a favoured destination for far Territory climbers, it's become an isolated Region devastated by extreme avalanche activity.
Beyond the lower elevations and treeline, minimal shelters are available. Only the most-prepared survivors can expect a successful journey through its snowy fields and up its high ridgelines.

**Sundered Pass** is the 16th [Region](./Region.md) added to _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, released in Part 5 of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion. A cold and hostile mountainous region, it connects with [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md), [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), and [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), with a sign pointing motorists to a road (likely to the [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md)) leading to a collapsed tunnel in Transfer Pass (though it must be bypassed via [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md)).

Sundered Pass is vertical and mountainous region of open meadows and narrow valleys. With steep terrain, extreme cold, and abundant [timberwolf packs](./Timberwolf.md) with few shelters, it is one of the most challenging regions to stay within for long periods of time. A network of A-frame cabins for hikers dots the eastern highlands along the main road, with many structures destroyed by avalanches or seismic activity. The map itself is very Oval shaped, however a large section of mountain to the east of the map is accessible. The region is the centerpiece of the [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) Tale.

It features the coldest weather on Great Bear Island, gradually decreasing in temperature the higher in altitude one climbs, and contains the most timberwolf packs. It also contains other wildlife including: [black bear](./Bear.md), [wolves](./Wolf.md), [moose](./Moose.md), [deer](./Deer.md), [rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [cougars](./Cougar.md) and [ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md). There is a single [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md) in the region at [Ambler's Lake](./Ambler%27s%20Lake.md).
- [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) or [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) via a cave network

Sundered Pass is extremely harsh and difficult to survive in: featuring extreme weather and abundant hostile wildlife, particularly on harder [survival modes](./Survival%20Mode.md). It is by far the coldest region (-20_C to -40_C on Interloper even with best-in-slot gear), [dropping in temperature](./Feels%20Like.md) further as altitude increases up the steep mountain roads.

The region is infamous for its high number of [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), with some players reporting seeing more than ten timberwolves in a pack at a time, with at least six separate packs on the upper mountain. Extreme caution should be taken when traversing the region, especially in the north-northeast highlands from [Final Refuge](./Final%20Refuge.md) to [Placid Notch](./Placid%20Notch.md).
Little fuel can be scavenged in much of the region, especially the avalanche-ridden northeast, unless the player goes [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md).
A possible moose location is north of Weather Station, in a small marsh below, or near [Ambler's Lake](./Ambler%27s%20Lake.md).

Sundered Pass can be divided into three major regions: the lower-altitude woodland, the alpine plateau, and a mountain trail to the east of the map. It is possible to go between the two by following a trail on the region's western side, or by following the road in the central and eastern side of the region via [Lotte's Rest](./Lotte%27s%20Rest.md).

The woodland consists of a large, forested valley. It offers good [deer](./Deer.md) and [rabbit](./Rabbit.md) hunting opportunities, as well as lots of natural resources and firewood to forage. Free-form [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) can be practiced at the small lakes near [Seedling Spring](./Seedling%20Spring.md) or [Giant's Thumbprint](./Giant%27s%20Thumbprint.md). Other noteworthy landmarks include large waterfalls near [Ogre's Teardrop](./Ogre%27s%20Teardrop.md) and just northeast of the house, as well as the brook near [Juniper Runoff](./Juniper%20Runoff.md).

While there are a few [wolves](./Wolf.md) in the forest, there's no [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) or [bears](./Bear.md) to think about. The forested valley is also home for [cougars](./Cougar.md). Most players who are staying in this area for any length of time will likely end up using the [Last Lonely House](./Last%20Lonely%20House.md) as a [safe house](./Safehouse.md), as it offers good shelter. Accessing the entirety of the house requires a [key](./An%20Old%20House%20Key.md), that can be found during the [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) tale. If an unexpected blizzard pops up, there's a cave north of [Giant's Thumbprint](./Giant%27s%20Thumbprint.md) as well as south of the Last Lonely House.

This area is large, very open, and cold, with limited resources to forage, and limited hunting. The greatest hazard of this area is the multiple large roaming [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) packs, making it almost impossible to visit this region without a weapon. One [Bear](./Bear.md) can spawn a short distance west of [Final Refuge](./Final%20Refuge.md), and a [Moose](./Moose.md) can be found on a pond not far from the [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md).

Due to the lack of trees, finding firewood in this area can be difficult. Visiting the abandoned mine at [Reluctant Shortcut](./Reluctant%20Shortcut.md) (up a short root climb) can provide [coal](./Coal.md), helping to alleviate the cold somewhat. If the player is unwilling to eat the timberwolves, food may also be somewhat of an issue, owing to the limited numbers of [deer](./Deer.md). Fishing at [Ambler's Lake](./Ambler%27s%20Lake.md) can help provide a sustainable food source.

Those who are willing to brave the cold and timberwolves have several [safe house](./Safehouse.md) options. The [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md) offers a good view and is the only timberwolf-safe option, but it's really cold and has few resources in the immediate area. [Placid Notch](./Placid%20Notch.md) (Refuge Cabin B) offers shelter, a stove, and a bed relatively near a deer spawn, though it can be a bit cramped. [Final Refuge](./Final%20Refuge.md) (Refuge Cabin C) is similar to the previous one, but is closer to [Ambler's Lake](./Ambler%27s%20Lake.md) and the abandoned coal mine. The partially buried cabin at [Old Settlement](./Old%20Settlement.md) is the largest shelter and offers a good place from which to hunt timberwolves, but doesn't have an indoor fireplace.

This begins just east of [Ambler's Lake](./Ambler%27s%20Lake.md) at a very long [climb](./Rope%20Climbing.md). It then follows a long, narrow, intricate system of trails, rope climbs, and boardwalks to get to [High Peak Plateau](./High%20Peak%20Plateau.md) as part of [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md). Returning to the road near [Lotte's Rest](./Lotte%27s%20Rest.md) involves another rope climb. With limited shelter and resources along this route, most players will likely only travel through here as part of the Tale, as there are few resources in the mountain that hardly constitute a second return trip.

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

**Supply Caches** (also called **Transponder Caches**) are small cylindrical shaped containers or strongboxes buried under the snow that the player can locate and uncover with the use of the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md).

These caches contain useful loot such as tools, weapons, ammunition, medicine, clothing (including the [technical balaclava](./Technical%20Balaclava.md)) and food.![The message that appears close to the cache](../assets/Uncover_prompt.jpg)_The message that appears close to the cache_There are 1-4 caches per region, and none in the transition zones. The total number of caches per region is not random, with 31 caches in the game as of 2023-09-10.
Supply caches will spawn in one of four patterns, based on which of the four [loot tables](./Loot%20Table.md) is supplying your game.

Once found and uncovered, the location of the cache shows up once the survivor updates their map. this means that they could be effectively used as storage, up to 30 kg.![Range of transponder on the cache setting, credit to u/Tolkfan](../assets/Range_transponder.webp)_Range of transponder on the cache setting, credit to u/Tolkfan_In order to find a supply cache, the associated [Transmitter](./Transmitters.md) needs to be fixed. Note there are two transmitters (Desolation Point, Blackrock) which are not part of the [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) quest. Repairing them is necessary to find their associated caches - for example, to find any caches in Coastal Highway you must first fix the transmitter in Desolation Point.

**Supply Room Key** is a [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md) found in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It is found during the main mission [High Energy](./High%20Energy.md), when [Jace](./Jace.md) gives it to [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) just before he leaves to go to the [Suzuki Geothermal Region](./Suzuki%20Geothermal%20Region.md).
The key opens a door (labeled supply room above it) right before exiting the facility into the parking lot outside.

Inside are high grade, warm clothing, plenty of food and drink, several [Heat Packs](./Heat%20Pack.md), [Crampons](./Crampons.md), a [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md), a [Medical Locker](./Medical%20Locker.md), several regular [Lockers](./Locker.md) filled with supplies, 3 [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md), and a [Shotgun](./Shotgun.md) with 23 rounds of ammunition.
- Added to game.

Surfeit Trestle is a railway viaduct that is part of the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) and leads to [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md). Across the trestle is an abandoned passenger rail car and a rock from which a [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) can be deployed, and one such rope can be found nearby inside the rail car. The trestle's railway is blocked by a [rockfall landslide](./Foundered%20Track.md) and requires the player to use the rope leading down the to the bottom of a deep ravine to access [Platelayer's Shortcut](./Platelayer%27s%20Shortcut.md) in order to bypass it.

**Surveyed Locations** are a [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md) found in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) related solely to keeping track of and unlocking the [Faithful Cartographer](./Faithful%20Cartographer.md) achievement.
As of the Part 4 Tales from the Far Territory update, there are currently 215 locations that can be discovered and surveyed on Great Bear Island for the achievement.
[Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) and any regions located in the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) **are currently not** in Surveyed Locations.

This Collectible is a checklist of all named locations that can be surveyed within the game, conveniently located in the [Journal](./Journal.md) menu under the Collectibles tab. Undiscovered places will be hidden in the menu by default, but using the "force reveal" button will make them show, not affecting the achievement. ![An example of the text that appears in the top left corner when finding a named location. Hangar Basement is also an example of an unmarked location, as it does not appear on the map.](../assets/HangarBasementLights.jpg)_An example of the text that appears in the top left corner when finding a named location. Hangar Basement is also an example of an unmarked location, as it does not appear on the map._ Occasionally while exploring, a message will appear in the top left corner of the screen denoting the current area you have discovered is a Named Location. These locations can be either marked or unmarked on the [Map](./Map.md) after surveying the area with [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md). Named locations appear as major building icons, region transition barriers, or as black text on the Map. Surveying a named location will have it be recorded in the Surveyed Locations tab in the Collections submenu of the [Journal](./Journal.md).
Discovered locations will be recorded separately in the Stats menu and will not appear until surveyed.
Not all named locations appear on the map when surveyed, yet they will still appear in the Surveyed Locations tab.

Regions that are primarily filled with unmarked locations include [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md) and [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), with a few other unmarked locations being present in other regions. Indoor named locations will also not appear in the Surveyed Locations collections (such as [Hangar Basement](./Hangar%20Basement.md)), as it is impossible to survey indoors (though entire buildings can be surveyed from outside, such as [Main Hangar](./Main%20Hangar.md)).
The [Faithful Cartographer](./Faithful%20Cartographer.md) achievement requires all named locations in Survival Mode to be surveyed and appear on the map.
- **_The most reliable way to get a proper survey is to survey as soon as the location pops on to your screen_**

Note\* Some locations from each Region are missing on this list, as the Surveyed Locations tab only records **SPECIFIC** marked named locations. Region transition icons are listed as part of the named locations list in the collections and are recorded as such. Some of these locations appear out of order alphabetically, but they are recorded as seen in Surveyed Locations collections.

_This article is about the normal Bow. For variants, see [Woodwright's Bow](./Woodwright%27s%20Bow.md), [Sport Bow](./Sport%20Bow.md) and [Bushcraft Bow](./Bushcraft%20Bow.md)._

The **Survival Bow** is a maple self-backed longbow that shoots [Simple Arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md), [Fire Hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md), and [Manufactured Arrows](./Manufactured%20Arrow.md) at targets such as [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md). Hitting a living target with a fired arrow provides experience to the [Archery](./Archery.md) skill.

The Survival Bow is an effective ranged weapon and hunting tool. It features unique advantages and disadvantages from other weapons, such as the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md). The Survival Bow is the primary weapon in Interloper mode, considering the limited availability of [Distress Pistols](./Distress%20Pistol.md) and its [ammunition](./Flare%20Shell.md), and the limited utility of [Stones](./Stone.md).

Arrows travel slower than bullets and at a steep arc, making their accuracy more difficult, especially at long ranges, and also making it more effective for offense than defense. However, the Survival Bow can be very effective at stopping a charging [Wolf](./Wolf.md), if the player waits until the last moment to shoot.
- Arrows may be retrievable after being fired; however, the arrow loses some condition each time it lands (with hard surfaces causing more damage to the arrow).
- Bow condition degrades 2% per shot and cannot be repaired. New bow and arrows may be crafted, and all materials to craft bows/arrows is renewable (see: [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md)).
- Bows can shoot around 42.5 times before risking breakage below 15% condition. Upon reaching archery skill level 4 the amount of guaranteed uses before breaking risk doubles to 85.

The only time when the Rifle is objectively better is when fighting Moose or Cougar. Because neither do not bleed, the Bow's more effective bleed-out is rendered useless; making the Rifle's higher critical hit chance superior.

To fire a Survival Bow, it must first be carried and wielded (1) with at least 1 [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md) or [Fire Hardened Arrow](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) in the player's inventory. Wielding it will cause an arrow to be loaded. To fire the bow, it must first be drawn (LMB), and then released (RMB). Left-clicking twice will cause the bow to lower again, as it will if the Stamina meter is depleted (which drains constantly, when the bow is drawn).
The bow requires practice to use effectively, but also becomes easier to handle at higher levels of Archery:

- _Horizontal sway:_ When drawn, the bow will sway from left to right affecting the arrow's flight accordingly. When it tilts to the right or left, the arrow will fly a bit to the right or left of the center of your aim. The sway increases if the player is tired.
- _Vertical targeting:_ Arrow flight trajectory forms an arc, following in-game physics, similar to the real world. Farther targets will require aiming higher.
- _Arrow flight speed:_ Arrows fly much slower than bullets, so take a target's movement into consideration.
- _Usability:_ The bow, unlike the rifle, cannot be fired while crouched unless one's Archery skill is Level 5.
- _Ammo Type:_ Unlike other weapons, the Survival Bow's arrows can be switched between 3 types of Arrows by pressing the Reload key:
- [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md) - The most basic arrow type, they deal moderate damage and are strong enough to kill every animal.

- [Fire Hardened Arrow](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) - Improvised arrows created in an active Fire, these arrows are very brittle and only damage [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md). Attacking medium or large animals with these arrows instantly breaks them but still awards Archery Skill experience.

- [Manufactured Arrow](./Manufactured%20Arrow.md) - A very rare arrow type that can only be acquired from the [Trader](./Trader.md). These arrows deal more damage and are the most durable arrow type, but cannot be repaired once destroyed.
Drawing a loaded bow will cause the player's view to zoom, enabling the bow to be used as a weak optic or pointing tool.

_Main article: [Hunting](./Hunting.md)_The Survival Bow is a crafted tool which fires Simple Arrows. Arrows may kill animals instantly with a critical hit, they more commonly cause bleeding wounds that drain the animal's health over time. When hunting it is wise to consider the weather, time of day, and ability to track a wounded animal as it flees. Arrows may be retrieved from the ground or an animal's carcass by left-clicking on it.![20201128184359 1](../assets/20201128184359_1.jpg)
| Zone Hit | [Bear](./Bear.md) | [Deer](./Deer.md) | [Wolf](./Wolf.md) | [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) |
[Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) die instantly when hit by an arrow. [Moose](./Moose.md) and [Cougar](./Cougar.md) do not bleed out.
Note: The bleed-out time diminishes with higher levels of the [Archery](./Archery.md) survival skill.

violations.context: **Values**

A rare variant of the [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) that is only acquired when trading with the [Sutherland](./Trader.md), the Survival Knife boasts impressive stats for its rarity. Its edge is serrated, allowing it to do more damage in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) while also allowing it to perform [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) faster than a normal knife. The tradeoff is that it is a little bit heavier than a normal Hunting Knife, but an added bonus of this knife is its increased durability, making it a must have for long term survival games.

Knives have number of uses: harvesting gut, hide and meat from [animal](./Wildlife.md) carcasses, as well as [Cloth](./Cloth.md) and [Tinder Plugs](./Tinder%20Plug.md). It may also serve as a makeshift [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md) to avoid spillage, or to break through iced-over fishing holes for [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md), and as a self-defense weapon during wolf attacks.

It can appear as a potential trade when trading with the [Trader](./Trader.md), Sutherland, after completing Special Request #3. It is possible for the Trader to offer multiple Survival Knives across trades.
The Survival Knife is by far the best Knife in the game, but the Cougar Claw Knife still bests it in some categories.
- More damage than the [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) (damage values are in-between a Hunting Knife and [Cougar Claw Knife](./Cougar%20Claw%20Knife.md)).

The knife can be repaired using a [Whetstone](./Whetstone.md) and the [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) skill, restoring 3% condition to the tool and using 5% condition on the Whetstone. The [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) or [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) may repair a non-ruined knife to 100% condition for one Scrap Metal, during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md).
- The name of this knife is related to the various [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md) on the Island, and it may be possible that this knife originally belonged to Sutherland's brother Wyatt.
- If so, Wyatt may have ordered several surplus Knives for survival reasons (possibly for his friends and family or as backups). This may also be the reason why Sutherland has so many to trade.
- At the end of [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md), [Mathis](./Mathis.md) briefly wields a Survival Knife.

The **Survival Menu** is the primary menu within [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md) that is used to display your current condition, clothing, items, crafting, journal, and map. The menu is displayed across the entire screen, but the game does not pause while it is open.

With standard key bindings on PC, there are several ways to open the game menu. From the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md), clicking the central icon will take you to the Status screen. Otherwise, the default key bindings to bring up these menus are:
![Status Menu](../assets/Status_Menu.png) Shown as a stick figure of a human in the menu, the Status screen displays your current condition, any injuries or illnesses you have, and the time of day.

Along the left you can see your [Warmth](./Warmth.md), [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Thirst](./Thirst.md), and [Hunger](./Hunger.md) meters, as well as your current stored calories. The Calorie Store number is how many calories the player currently possesses, and is directly linked to the Hunger bar. When the Hunger bar is 100% full, max stored calories will be 2500, with the opposite being 0 calories at 0% Hunger bar.

In the bottom left of the screen, the current air temperature and wind chill are displayed, as well as what temperature it feels like to you ([Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md)). Feels Like is the exact effective temperature that determines the increase (or decrease) for the player's Warmth bar. When the Feels Like temperature is above 0°C (32°F), the player's Warmth will be heading in the positive direction. When it is below that temperature, the player will notice the opposite happening.

In the center of the screen you will see any [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) you currently have, as well as your health [Condition](./Condition.md). The Time of Day graphic is displayed in the top right of the screen.

![Clothing hud](../assets/Clothing_hud.jpg) Shown as a T-shirt icon in the menu, the [Clothing](./Clothing.md) screen allows you to see what clothes you are currently wearing on each part of your body, as well as to compare and select other clothes items you are carrying. The bottom left of the screen shows you the bonuses from your current set of worn clothing, while the right of the screen shows you the statistics of the selected item. Clothing can be harvested or repaired from this menu or from the Backpack menu.

![Backpack Menu](../assets/Backpack_Menu.png) Shown as a backpack icon in the menu, the Backpack displays all the items you currently have. You can view **All** items at once, or you can view them by category:

Some items will be displayed in more than one category. Items can be sorted alphabetically, by condition, or by weight by looking in the bottom middle of the screen. Carried items can be consumed, repaired, harvested, or dropped from this menu.

The total weight of your backpack and your [Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md) is displayed in the top left of the screen. Green means you are un-encumbered, while red means you are over your carry weight. Increased or decreased Carry Weight is shown in parenthesis next to total Carry Weight. Finding the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) will rename this menu to Technical Backpack.

![Crafting Menu](../assets/Crafting_Menu.png) Shown as a hammer and anvil icon in the menu, the Crafting screen shows you the current blueprints you have for crafting items and allows you to craft items.
On the left of the screen are tabs that allow you to view blueprints by category. By default it will show **All** blueprints, but they can be filtered to only show:

Below the blueprints are 6 submenus allowing you to filter for specific creation methods for items. By default it will show **All** blueprint creation methods but can be changed to only show items that can be crafted at:

Some items in Wintermute require finding their blueprints in order to craft, and are usually unlocked when progressing through the story and completing side missions. Other Blueprints are not available in Wintermute at all.
Survival Mode has all blueprints unlocked from the start except for the [Noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md) blueprint, which is unlocked when one is found in game.
![Recipe Book](../assets/Recipe_Book.png) _This menu will not appear unless the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon is purchased._

Shown as a cooking pot icon in the menu, the Recipe Book menu is used show the various [Cooking](./Cooking.md) Recipes that the player can use as part of the Frontier Cooking update. Because Recipes require multiple ingredients and are not simply 1 item cooking items, this menu is used to track all ingredients used to make each Recipe. Some Recipes contain a white star next to them, and will be unlocked when the player finds their specific Recipe when searching the island. Recipes cannot be created by hand from this menu like Crafting, and instead require an active [Fire](./Fire.md) source.

Items can be sorted alphabetically, by preparation times, or by calorie amounts by looking in the bottom left of the screen. Ingredients needed to create recipes are shown on the right side. The overall condition, calories, hydration, and weight are shown in the bottom middle, as well as any [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) that this Recipe will boost or remove. Some Recipes can add or remove positive Afflictions, while others can add or remove harmful ones.

![Tales Objectives](../assets/Tales_Objectives.jpg) _This menu will not appear unless the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon is purchased and at least 1 Tale is activated_

Shown as a flag icon, this menu is used to track the objectives required to complete the 3 [Tales](./Tales.md). It functions similarly to the Missions menu in Wintermute, and can select each individual Tale once it is unlocked.
![Journal Menu](../assets/Journal_Menu.jpg) Shown as an open book icon in the menu, the Journal is different for Wintermute and Survival Mode, but contains mostly the same information.
In Survival Mode, the Journal is contains six submenus: Log, Skills, Collections, Rock Caches, General Notes, and Stats

- Skills provides details about current skill levels (primary skills only), perks of those levels, and progress to the next skill level within the current sandbox. Note that this menu scrolls down to reveal additional skills, depending on display settings.
- The Collections submenu keeps track of any [Notes](./Notes.md) that are found within the game.

- The Rock Cache submenu contains a list of all [Rock Caches](./Rock%20Cache.md), subdivided by [Region](./Region.md), that have been created in the current sandbox. Note that there is a limit of five (5) rock caches per region.

- The General Notes submenu contains a single "notepad" where players can jot down notes. While this is marginally useful to remember storage cache locations or directions, it is currently not possible to make more than one "thread" or organize notes in any way other than manual editing, thereby limiting it's utility compared to a simple (off-game) word processor.
- The [Almanac](./Almanac.md) menu is unique to the [Challenge](./Challenge.md) [Whiteout](./Whiteout.md), and is used to track when major blizzards appear on certain days.

- The Tales submenu is missing when a player begins a run of Survival Mode, but appears in the Journal Menu when a player triggers a corresponding Tale. This submenu simply takes you to the Tales menu, and is used to keep track of a list of completed/uncompleted objectives related to any Tale.
- The Stats submenu contains detailed stats about each playthrough, and compares those stats with the player's all-time high scores, subdivided by difficulty level.
In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), the Journal menu is divided into 3 submenus, which can be selected by clicking on the corresponding icon on the left of the screen.
**"[What I Know](./What%20I%20Know.md)"** contains 4 submenus related to all information gathered about the game world's settings, characters, and items, and is divided into:
**"Collections"** contains all [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md) found throughout your journey and these can be viewed and inspected at any time.
**"General Notes"** gives you a notepad to type any notes you want to make whilst playing.

![Maple sapling](../assets/Maple_sapling.jpg) Shown as a shining star icon, the [Map](./Map.md) displays the current map you are on, as well as any other maps you have found or made. You can view any other maps you have by clicking the arrows under the region name in the top right corner. By default, opening the map will always show the map of the current [Region](./Region.md) they are in.

In Wintermute, all maps are fully revealed and will show the player's current position and facing position (represented by an arrow) and will show icons that represent any main or side mission objectives.

In Survival Mode, players must draw the map themselves using [Charcoal](./Charcoal.md). The player's position is never shown, and so they must pinpoint their current position via surveyed landmarks on the map related to their surroundings. Text in the top left corner of the screen tells you how long ago you last updated the currently selected region map (in in-game time). A 'World' button at the bottom right of the screen allows you to switch from the region map to a world map of eother Lower Great Bear or the Far Territory sections of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).

Represented by a shield icon, the Missions menu records all information relevant to your objectives while in Wintermute. It functions similarly to the Tales menu, but with 3 submenus: Main for main missions, Side for side missions, and Completed for all completed missions.

![The Survival Menu icons for Wintermute.](../assets/Survival_Menu_Wintermute.jpg)_The Survival Menu icons for Wintermute._ ![GreyMotherTrustOutdated](../assets/GreyMotherTrustOutdated.jpg) The original release of Wintermute's Episode 1 and 2 featured a menu for Trust in the Journal menu.

Trust would have shown you the character who you are currently attempting to gain the trust of ([Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) or [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md)), and had two separate sections 'Description' and 'Trust' which respectively displayed the current needs and Trust rewards of the character in question. Maxing out Trust with a character would lead to more world building information and possible side missions. To date, this is [Cut/Discontinued Content](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md).
