This page is a brief guide for players new to [Interloper](./Survival%20Mode.md#nterloper), the second most difficult experience mode in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md) after the [Misery](./Misery.md) mode.

Interloper is a mode where Great Bear Island has already been picked clean of anything useful by the time you arrive. The developers of The Long Dark have stated that the experience of Interloper is akin to "Survival on a knife's edge." You will ALWAYS have this metaphorical knife pressed against you as you play. Some days the knife will push deep inside you, while others it will just hang over you like the Sword of Damocles.
While challenging, Interloper can be a rewarding gameplay experience without seeming like a masochist chore. This page contains all the information you'll need to survive on Interloper.

This is the single most important game-tip for being successful in Interloper. If you have only played Story Mode and end up being spawned into a region you have never visited, your chances of surviving for more than a few in-game hours will be very low. _Thoroughly_ explore Great Bear Island on at least Voyageur difficulty before starting Interloper so you know where to find food, shelter, materials, fireboxes, passages to other regions, dangerous wildlife chokepoints, bear dens, and facilites (beds, workbenches, forges, etc). You'll be spending as much time in the game trying not to freeze, so [surveying](./Map.md) should generally be avoided until later in Interloper runs. To avoid spending lots of time being frustrated at walking in circles and freezing to death, know the maps by experience.

One good way to learn the layouts and named locations of every map is to start a Survival game on [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md) and to aim for the [Faithful Cartographer](./Faithful%20Cartographer.md) achievement. This will require you to survey every named location on the island and you'll learn from experience where every significant landmark and supply cache is located. If this sounds too time consuming, then consider visiting a designated wiki page for each [Region](./Region.md) and Transition Zone on this wiki, as they contain detailed maps useful for navigation.

Most tools necessary for your survival will be missing in order to increase difficulty and challenge for Interloper. You will start the game with a few low quality clothing items, some water, and no bedroll. The availability of supplies will be dialed down significantly, so you will have to check high and low inside buildings for any supplies as you make your way across the Island.

[Hunting Rifles](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Revolvers](./Revolver.md), [Survival Knives](./Hunting%20Knife.md), and [Hatchets](./Hatchet.md) **_will not spawn_**. This one design choice separates Interloper from every other game mode, as it is almost impossible to hunt and harvest carcasses without these tools.

Likewise, the probability of finding [Prybar](./Prybar.md), [Hacksaws](./Hacksaw.md), [Storm Lanterns](./Storm%20Lantern.md), [Flashlights](./Flashlight.md), [Can Openers](./Can%20Opener.md), [Simple](./Simple%20Tools.md) or even [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) will be extremely low, but you can find them if you look hard enough.

High quality food items such as [MREs](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md) do not spawn at all, and even low quality food items are rare. Hunting and fishing are your only real way to acquire sustainable nourishment in this mode. Houses will still contain food and water, but the amounts will always be very low.

Matches will be your most precious resource and are often hard to find. They may seem impossible to locate, but the island will always have around 500+ matches for you if you search hard enough. (See Fire and Match Management later for more info)

Most high quality clothes will be missing, making any clothing you find your only way to stay warm indoors or outdoors, so take care of them whenever possible. Crafting animal furs will be required if you ever want to stop freezing to death on this mode, but without tools to hunt large game for their warm hides you'll need to...

As stated previously, Survival Knives and Hatchets do not spawn on Interloper. As such, hunting and harvesting carcasses will be impossible until you acquire a Heavy Hammer to create [Improvised Knives](./Improvised%20Knife.md), [Improvised Hatchets](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), and [Arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md) at a Forge. You can survive for at least 100 days by moving from region to region and surviving off of cat tails and packaged foods, but you WILL run out eventually and be forced to hunt. You'll want around 10 [scrap metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) in total: 5 for the hatchet, 3 for the knife, and 2 for making four arrowheads. Finding a [hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) will make this easier, but it's not essential.

Fishing is not a good choice to make early in the game, as your fishing skill will be very low and you will not have the clothes or fuel to stay warm while ice fishing. As such, make finding a Heavy Hammer and navigating to a region with a forge to make these 3 critical tools is always your first long-term priority when starting Interloper.

Interloper is cold. VERY cold. Due to a lack of warm clothes, you'll constantly be freezing as you venture outside to find more supplies. If you're used to always having 100% Condition from other game modes, don't stress out that you're always getting too cold. Keep a cool head (pun not intended) as you move from building to building. Practice [Daisy Chaining](./Daisy%20Chaining.md) a torch in order to stay a bit warmer as you move from location to location. And always always ALWAYS travel in the evening when it is warmest. Always sleep for the longest period of time in order to regain as much Condition as possible, and never sleep for more than 10 hours (players dehydrate from full Hydration in 10 hours and start taking Condition damage on Interloper difficulty).

Even if you manage to find a Heavy Hammer on day 1, forge all the tools you need to hunt, kill a bunch of animals and cure their pelts, and then deck yourself out in 2 [Bearskin Coats](./Bearskin%20Coat.md), 2 [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md), 1 [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md), a [Rabbitskin Hat](./Rabbitskin%20Hat.md), [Rabbitskin Mitts](./Rabbitskin%20Mitts.md), and somehow find 2 [Thermal Underwear](./Thermal%20Underwear.md), 2 [Thin Wool Sweaters](./Thin%20Wool%20Sweater.md) and 2 [Wool Socks](./Wool%20Socks.md), the world will still get VERY cold by day 50 and your Warmth Need will often lower the second you step outside.
Since the game only allows 2 active [Feats](./Feats.md) for Interloper, it's a good idea to learn which ones are best to use for the long term.

- Cold Fusion (+2oC warmth bonus), Snow Walker (faster [Stamina](./Stamina.md) regeneration) and Efficient Machine (reduced caloric consumption) are generally very good options, and useful throughout the game.
- Cold Fusion is arguably a mandatory Feat to take due to the coldness of the world.
- Book Smarts can be useful in the early to mid-game, but becomes nearly useless later on.

- Settled Mind is generally superior to Book Smarts as it both speeds up research and prevents [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md). This requres [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) to be installed.
- Blizzard Walker can improve quality of life and potentially save small amounts of condition by shortening travel time.
- Expert Trapper can be useful throughout the game, although its effects can also be accomplished simply by crafting more [snares](./Snare.md).

- Fire Master may _seem_ useful, but [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) can be raised relatively quickly by lighting a chain of campfires. All it takes is [sticks](./Stick.md) and [torches](./Torch.md).
- Free Runner is rarely useful: [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) drain during sprinting is usually a bigger concern than calories.
- Celestial Navigator and the Darkwalker are essentially useless unless you're playing a custom Endless Night Interloper.

The early days of any Interloper run will make or break that run. Being prepared with map knowledge, while helpful, is not enough to survive Interloper. Because Interloper is pretty much its own game due to missing clothes, tools, foods, and general lack of supplies, re-learning how to ration Calories and save Condition is a must.

Learning unofficial gameplay techniques like the previously mentioned Daisy Chaining, [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md), and [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md) will help you preserve firestarter materials, save calories, and skip mountain climbing sections respectively. [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) becomes much more important on this mode than any other difficulty due to the potential amount of renewable resources. Holding the sprint key drains sprint gage faster, but tapping it mid step allows you run farther distances and save stamina (and possibly outrun predators).

Collect [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) but don't read them right away. Keep them handy until you have a better stockpile of calories and try to use them to pass time in the mornings as the outside world warms up. You will most likely not have the calories to read a 5 hour book in one sitting, so read in increments of 1 hour when possible. Don't bother researching Gunsmithing, Revolver Skill, and Rifle Skill as these skills are useless on Interloper. Don't fish until you reach at least level 2 Ice Fishing from researching, unless using [tip-ups](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md).

No one likes a save scummer, but it can be helpful if you ever want to keep an 80 day save file that you spent 40 real world hours on alive. Nothing is more frustrating then getting very good at Interloper and then losing a month's or even years long run in seconds due to a poor mistake.

Making backup copies of your saves in case you die is a good idea for PC players. Alt+F4ing your game when you are jumped by a Bear or Wolf that will kill you is also one way to keep your save file alive.

If you feel that this is too dishonorable of a tactic, then consider just pausing and quitting the game before things get too hectic, then restarting back to your last save at a safe location. Keep in mind that the game can still autosave when you least expect it, and surviving on this tactic alone can be tricky, especially during Timberwolf encounters when you've taken damage.
Whether you want to take this advice or not is ultimately up to you, just play the game how you wish.

On Interloper, you can't pick where you start on the Island, you will instead start in one of the following regions: [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) or [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md).
The starting region the game chooses has some bearing on how easy/hard the run will be initially.

- One of the worst regions to start in is [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) due to the region having a generous amount of Timberwolves. If you end up spawning in Blackrock, try to get to [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) and then to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) as soon as possible.

- [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) could very well be one of the best starting locations in the game, as there is plenty of shelter between each indoor landmark and [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) is not far away. [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) tends to be full of tools, and [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md) can be stockpiled with Scrap Metal early when you are ready to return to make tools. The [Abandoned Mine No. 5](./Abandoned%20Mine%20No.%205.md) can be used to cut through the region quickly and to acquire coal.

- [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) is also a good region to start in, as it has a good amount of natural and manufactured resources scattered throughout. It is also close to [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), another resource-rich region, and tool forging at [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) is only a day's walk away in good weather.

- [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) can be a good start, if you can manage to find a [hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) in the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md) to open up the [containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) throughout the map.

- [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) doesn't offer many manufactured resources, but it does have rich natural resources and isn't far from [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md). It also offers many guaranteed tool spawns and a [Mackinaw Jacket](./Mackinaw%20Jacket.md), the best manufactured jacket available on Interloper.

- [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) can enable you to get the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) and [Crampons](./Crampons.md) early on. Despite being cold, large parts of the map are predator-free, which can help make survival a bit easier, especially when carrying around smelly meat, hides, or guts harvested from deer carcasses.

- [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) is also a good spawn region, as it has a lot of natural resources (especially [cattails](./Cat%20Tail.md)), and the open terrain makes it easy to see predators from far off -- though this makes it easy to get lost in fog. It is severely lacking in shelter and manufactured resources, so it is generally best to head for one of the neighboring regions, such as [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) or [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md), which are not very far away. You will likely want to return here, however, to use the forge at [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md).

While you won't spawn in Bleak Inlet, Broken Railroad, Coastal Highway, Mystery Lake, Mountain Town or any of the Far Territory regions, it is worth knowing their characteristics and challenges, as you will likely be spending some time in these regions at the start of your runs:

- [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) has a lot of shelter in town and plenty of manufactured resources. The areas outside of town have a lot of natural resources, too. The biggest danger with this region is that it has a lot of wolves, which may ambush the player behind houses or vehicles.

- [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) is arguably the easiest region to survive in, with plentiful shelter, resources, and warm temperatures. It is also generally easy to avoid wolves and bears, though you should be careful of ambushes if you're around the [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md).

- [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) has a balance of shelter and wilderness, and moderate temperatures. The greatest hazard here is that the rolling terrain may make it difficult to spot predators from far away, requiring good listening skills.

Matches are quite rare in this difficulty, so use them sparingly, and light a [torch](./Torch.md) with your match before lighting a fire. Try to use the [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) once you obtain it. If the weather allows it, pull several torches from a fire and extinguish them in order to start [Daisy Chaining](./Daisy%20Chaining.md). When your lit torch is about to go out, drop it, then take one of your unlit torches and light it using the lit one. This allows you to carry fires long distances, and will provide minor warmth buffs and keep [wolves](./Wolf.md) at bay.
Make sure to carry a good stock of [coal](./Coal.md) when travelling as well, as it provides a +20C warmth bonus, which can ward off even the worst weather as long as the fire isn't blown out.

If you go to a region with houses, staying hydrated is not difficult for the first few days. Just get water from [toilets](./Toilet.md) and you will be able to quench your thirst long enough to search for matches, which you will need in order to start melt snow/boil water at fires once the toilet water runs out.

Food can be a bit more challenging. Manufactured food is quite rare, and each major region usually has only enough of it to survive 3-4 days if you're trying to get the [Well Fed](./Well%20Fed.md) benefit early on by avoiding starvation. [Cattails](./Cat%20Tail.md) are a popular food found along watercourses. If you are unable to find cattails, don't forget about drinks. [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md), [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md), [Birch Bark](./Birch%20Bark.md) and [Burdock Root](./Burdock%20Root.md) can all be brewed into teas that give 100 calories and the [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md) benefit when consumed hot.

If you have purchased [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), you will have access to Frontier Cooking recipes. You will want to find a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md) early on, as that will enable you to cook [porridge](./Porridge.md) from [Running River Oats](./Running%20River%20Oats.md). One container of oats can make 8 porridge, which can provide 2,800 calories, as well as provide the Warming Up benefit when consumed hot. Most importantly, porridge can be cooked off the bat.

It is highly desirable to level up your [cooking](./Cooking.md) skill early on, as this will improve the caloric value of foods. This is even more so if you have purchased [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), as getting to Level 2 cooking (along with finding a [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md)) will enable you to use plentiful [Old Mill Flour](./Old%20Mill%20Flour.md) and [Cooking Oil](./Cooking%20Oil.md) to make [Pancakes](./Pancakes.md) (requires [Maple Syrup](./Maple%20Syrup.md)) and [Bannock](./Bannock.md). Once you get to level 3 cooking, you will be able to make various pies, which can provide useful buffs.

The most important tool you will want to acquire in Interloper is the [Heavy hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md). [Prybars](./Prybar.md), [hacksaws](./Hacksaw.md) and [Can Openers](./Can%20Opener.md) are desirable, but not essential for progressing.

- The Heavy Hammer the most important, as it is necessary for [forging](./Forge.md), and useful for breaking up wooden furniture. **MAKE FINDING A HEAVY HAMMER YOUR #1 LONG TERM PRIORITY** when you start every game in Interloper -- otherwise, you will not be able to hunt. It is required for making the [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md), which is necessary for creating the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), as well as for forging [arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md). It is also the best available weapon early on for dealing with a [wolf](./Wolf.md) [struggle](./Struggle.md).

- The hacksaw is not strictly necessary, but it will make getting the metal required for tool forging much easier. It can also be used for harvesting carcasses and cutting limbs/saplings, though there are better options for the latter.
- The prybar is most useful for opening up locked [Car](./Car.md) trunks and [lockers](./Locker.md). It can also be used in a struggle in a pinch, but isn't recommended if anything else is available.

It is possible to forge all the improvised tools you need -- [arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md), [improvised hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) and [improvised knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) on Day 1, but this requires quite a lot of luck. Forges require at least 6 pieces of [coal](./Coal.md) to reach operating temperature. An efficient player should be able to complete tool forging within the first 5-7 days at most. The improvised tools are as follows:
- Arrowheads are placed onto [arrow shafts](./Arrow%20Shaft.md) to make [simple arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md), which are used for hunting with the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md).

- The improvised knife is the best tool for [harvesting non-frozen carcasses](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md), especially if you're trying to get hide and guts. It can also be used in a [struggle](./Struggle.md).
- The improvised hatchet is useful for breaking up limbs for firewood, and is quicker than the hacksaw. It is also good for harvesting meat from frozen carcasses, and makes a decent struggle weapon.

Crafting the tools requires 8 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), and most players will want to acquire 10-12 to get a good supply of arrows. This can be obtained by searching the world or by cutting up metal objcts using the hacksaw. Two pieces of [cloth](./Cloth.md) are also necessary, but these are generally easy to find.

High-quality manufactured clothing is not available, so you will have to make your own. When you get a [hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md), start harvesting deer carcasses and get all the meat and guts. It's advisable to cure them in the nearest indoor location, to avoid drawing predators' attention. You can pick up the cured and non-smelly hides later for crafting. To make the two most important early-game clothing pieces -- [deerskin pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md) and [deerskin boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md) -- you will need five deer hides. Wear [combat pants](./Combat%20Pants.md) underneath your deerskin pants, and your legs will stay toasty warm. The warmest sweaters available are the [Thin Wool Sweater](./Thin%20Wool%20Sweater.md), [Festive Sweater](./Festive%20Sweater.md) or the [Hockey Jersey](./Hockey%20Jersey.md).

Many players swear by a double [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md), as it is the warmest option with excellent protection, waterproofness, and windproof ratings and can scare off wolves, but it is the heaviest and imposes a severe stamina penalty. Acquiring the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md) or [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) is almost a must, and is likely only desirable in very cold regions (i.e. [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md)). It also requires killing two [bears](./Bear.md) per coat, which may make obtaining it a bit challenging.

A [Moose-Hide Cloak](./Moose-Hide%20Cloak.md) is also best worn on the outside, as it is the option with most protection and waterproofing. The higher protection may make it desirable when exploring [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) or [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), where [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) attacks are likely. The biggest challenge with this coat, however, is likely going to be killing the [Moose](./Moose.md).

The [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md) can also be used as an outer layer. It isn't as warm as a Bearskin Coat but it is lighter and it can also scare away wolves when worn. Wolf hides are easier to obtain than bear or moose hides, as wolves can either be hunted with a bow and arrows, or you can search Great Bear for pre-spawned carcasses. The Wolfskin Coat is also warm enough to make a decent inner layer.

Finally, there are some jackets that are best suited as inner layers. The [Mackinaw Jacket](./Mackinaw%20Jacket.md) is a popular choice underneath the outer jacket. A [Ski Jacket](./Ski%20Jacket.md) or [Simple Parka](./Simple%20Parka.md) are a bit lighter, and only half a degree colder than the Mackinaw Jacket, but on the long run you should look into more warmer and durable animal clothing options instead.

If you own [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), you will likely want to craft some [Improvised Insulation](./Improvised%20Insulation.md). It requires killing two [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) and getting their [down](./Ptarmigan%20Down.md). This garment weighs a mere 0.25 kg, but gives you an extra 2oC warmth bonus and goes in the accessory slot. It can greatly help make up for the lack of availability of good sweaters in this difficulty.

The [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) will be your main in-game offensive weapon. It's best to acquire this as soon as possible, by curing a [maple sapling](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md) and [gut](./Fresh%20Gut.md). Curing guts and saplings will take 5 in-game days, and you will need a knife to craft the bow, which takes around 12 hours. On a good run, you can have a bow and arrows by day 6, but 7-10 days is a more realistic timeframe for most players. In time you'll be using it for hunting big game with [simple arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md), with [birch shafts](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) and [iron heads](./Arrowhead.md) that you forged yourself. But for now, you'll be using it with [fire hardened arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md). These arrows can't harm large animals, but can kill a [rabbit](./Rabbit.md) or [ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), and are capable of driving away a charging wolf, and help improve your [archery](./Archery.md) skill, so you don't need as many arrows to kill animals.
You may also find a [flare gun](./Distress%20Pistol.md), but use its shells sparingly as they are hard to come by.

Wolves are _deadly_ in Interloper. Unless you are at full [condition](./Condition.md) and have an improvised [knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) or [hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md), your chances of surviving a [struggle](./Struggle.md) bare handed are slim. Use [torches](./Torch.md) to keep wolves at bay and prevent them from charging. If it gets windy, keep a [flare](./Flare.md) at the ready and don't be afraid to use it.

Once you have obtained a [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), you can use it to deal with wolves. A direct hit on a charging wolf with a [Simple Arrow](./Simple%20Arrow.md) will kill it. A [Fire Hardened Arrow](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) will not hurt the wolf, but will scare it away. But be careful! A missed shot can lead to a game-ending struggle. It's best to try and stay well away from wolves and not carry large amounts of smelly food to avoid attracting attention.

Before you get a survival bow, your hunting opportunities will be quite limited. You can try stunning [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) or [ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) with [stones](./Stone.md), but this tactic can be tricky and frustrating, and you'll have to move fast to collect your prey before it becomes concious again.

It is possible to hunt [deer](./Deer.md) without a bow...with some help from local [wolves](./Wolf.md). This works best with a lone wolf, and involves either luring the wolf towards the deer, or chasing the deer towards the wolf. Once the wolf kills the deer, it can be driven away with a [stone](./Stone.md) or thrown [torch](./Torch.md). The one danger with this method is that the wolf may still be nearby when you start harvesting, and carrying around large amounts of smelly [venison](./Venison%20%28Cooked%29.md) is likely to attract attention.

Once you get the survival bow, you will want to use [fire hardened arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) to hunt rabbits and ptarmigan, and simple arrows for deer. Unless you're interested in the hides, it's generally not advisable to hunt wolves or bears early on, as their meat can give [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) until you get level 5 [cooking](./Cooking.md). [Moose](./Moose.md) are also not recommended for new players, despite their high-quality meat and excellent [hide](./Fresh%20Moose%20Hide.md), as they do not bleed out when shot and take multiple arrows to down until you improve your [archery](./Archery.md) skill. If you run out of arrows while moose hunting, you will likely lose all the arrows (and have to forge new arrowheads) when the moose despawns. You can try killing the moose and getting your arrows back using the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) or even [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md), but neither [Flare Shells](./Flare%20Shell.md) nor Noisemakers are particularly easy to obtain.

If you are going to be sticking around an area for multiple days, it is a good idea to set some [snares](./Snare.md) to catch rabbits automatically, instead of hunting them. This will save wear and tear on your bow, and will produce more rabbits over the long haul.

As you do not get a [bedroll](./Bedroll.md) when you first spawn into the world, you will have to think carefully about where you travel, as getting stuck in a location without a bed can be unpleasant at best and dangerous at worst. Until you obtain a bedroll, you will want to make sure that any location you visit in the wilderness is within a day's travel of a bed -- this means it's important to know the locations of beds on all the maps you are planning to visit. It is also possible to sleep in a [vehicle](./Vehicle.md) without a bedroll, but this requires mild outdoor temperatures and/or warm clothing.

Once you do find a bedroll, it is a good idea to kill three [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) (ideally with [fire hardened arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md)), and get 10 [down](./Ptarmigan%20Down.md). This, together with three [cloth](./Cloth.md), will enable you to convert your normal bedroll into an [Improvised Down Bedroll](./Improvised%20Down%20Bedroll.md), offering you 8oC warmth for only 0.10 kg of extra weight.

If you are unable to find a manufactured bedroll, or find that it doesn't offer enough warmth for your liking, you can shoot two [bears](./Bear.md) to get their [hides](./Fresh%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md), and make a [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md). This offers a 12oC warmth bonus, but is very heavy at 3.00 kg.

When you need to sleep in a location that doesn't have a fixed temperature (i.e. a shallow cave, a car, or outdoors), do not sleep for too long at a time (4 hours at a time -- tops!). Otherwise, if it suddenly gets colder, it's possible to freeze to death in your sleep. Lighting a hot fire can help, but a sudden change in wind direction can blow out an exposed campfire. Houses, cabins, and other indoor locations with beds are the simplest and best options, as they are always warm enough -- but do be aware that you will not be able to sleep indoors if you catch cabin fever. Sleeping in shallow caves is a good idea, as they provide a warmth bonus, are sheltered from the wind, and do not contribute to [cabin fever risk](./Cabin%20Fever.md) as they are considered outdoor locations. [Snow Shelters](./Snow%20Shelter.md) are also a good choice to combat cabin fever, with the advantage of being able to be built right outside most [safehouses](./Safehouse.md) and thus being easily reachable during even storms or at night.

Although there are fewer fish to catch in Interloper than on other difficulty levels, fishing is still a very useful source of food, and it is a good idea to have a safe house near a fishable body of water. The trick here is to make several [Fishing Tip-Ups](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md) as this will enable fish to be caught while you're busy doing other things. One of the most efficient ways to get fish is to free-form several tip-ups around an [Ice Fishing Hut](./Ice%20Fishing.md) and let them passively catch fish while you're fishing yourself. This method can provide a lot of fish in one day, which, when cooked, provide [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) and can help ward off [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md).

In Interloper, increasing [skills](./Skills.md) can greatly help your chances of survival. [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md), [Revolver Firearm](./Revolver%20Firearm.md), and [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) are irrelevent, due to the lack of firearms.

Higher [Archery](./Archery.md) levels make it easier to aim the [bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), provide modest increases in damage, and improve the bow's durability. At level 5, the bow can be fired when crouched, making hunting dangerous predators (i.e. bears, moose) much easier. Archery can be raised fairly quickly and cheaply by making a bunch of [Fire Hardened Arrows](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md) and hit [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) or [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md). However, this is likely not the most important skill to raise early on.

Increasing [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) makes getting meat, hide, and guts faster, which reduces the amount of time you'll have to spend outside when harvesting [deer](./Deer%20Carcass.md), [wolves](./Wolf%20Carcass.md), [moose](./Moose%20Carcass.md), [cougars](./Cougar%20Carcass.md), and [bears](./Black%20Bear%20Carcass.md). The safest way to level this skill is to harvest the rabbits and ptarmigan you shot while practicing your archery. However, this skill will tend to level itself up over the course of the game, so it isn't worth putting too much emphasis into.

[Cooking](./Cooking.md) is arguably _the_ most critical skill to increase, especially in the early game, as it boosts the calories obtained from any cooked food, which, given the scarcity of food in Interloper, can be extremely important. Furthermore, reaching level 5 prevents [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) and [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md). While this skill will raise gradually on its own, some tips to quickly raise cooking include:

- gather all the [reishi mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md), [rosehips](./Rose%20Hip.md), [birch bark](./Birch%20Bark.md), [herbal teas](./Herbal%20Tea.md), [burdocks](./Burdock.md), and [coffees](./Tin%20of%20Coffee.md) you can find and convert them into drinks. They're fast to cook.
- Harvest meat in 0.50 kg increments from carcasses -- cooking anything, whether it's a 5 kg fish or a 0.1 kg piece of venison, gives the same amount of experience.

Having a higher [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) level should be prioritized, as it reduces the amount of matches wasted upon failed fire starting attempts if you forgot to bring a [torch](./Torch.md). Once you've got a [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md), gather a bunch of [sticks](./Stick.md) and [tinder plugs](./Tinder%20Plug.md) and wait for a clear day. Then light a bunch of [campfires](./Campfire.md), one after another. If you use 2 sticks per fire, you should be able to use the fires to cook teas and rapidly raise cooking skill at the same time.

Raising [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) requires you to ice fish, manually -- not using a [tip-up](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md). Prior to the introduction of the tip-ups, this was a very desirable skill to raise quickly, but since then, it's no longer quite as important. While it does help catch larger fish faster with less risk of line breakage, it's a skill that will likely level itself up over time.

Higher levels of [Mending](./Mending.md) speed up repairs to [Clothing](./Clothing.md), as well as increasing the chance of success and reducing wear on sewing equipment. This tends to be an extremely slow skill to increase, and having a low mending level is not likely to seriously impede your ability to survive.

If you have purchased [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md), you may wish to harvest one extra deer carcass and four extra [maple saplings](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md) in order to make a [Travois](./Travois.md). While by no means an essential tool for surviving Interloper, acquiring a Travois at any stage of the game is extremely useful:

- It will enable you to carry a large amount of raw meat, guts, or fish without increasing your visibility to wolves and bears, as items stored on the Travois don't contribute to your scent. Care must still be taken to move 0% ruined items into the Travois, as they will disappear just like with any other container.

- The Travois is the easiest craftable tool to increase your hauling capacity (the [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) needs to be crafted, and [Moose](./Moose.md) are hard to kill), and, depending on where you are on Great Bear, may be quicker and easier to obtain than the [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md).

- If playing with the [Trader](./Trader.md) enabled and aiming for top-tier clothing such as [Wolfskin Pants](./Wolfskin%20Pants.md) and [Wolfskin Hat](./Wolfskin%20Hat.md), it is almost mandatory in order to haul multiple [Car Batteries](./Car%20Battery.md) from their guaranteed spawn points to [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md)

The one caveat with the Travois is that it does not fit into narrow spaces, cannot be used on steep slopes, can't go up or down [climbing ropes](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md), or be deployed in transition caves such as [Abandoned Mine No. 3](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md). If you are planning to spend most of your time in a [region](./Region.md) that consists of mainly flat, open terrain ([Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), or [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md)), then prioritizing Travois-making is probably a smart move. If, however, you are living in a region that's very hilly ([Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), or [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md)), then the utility of the Travois may be limited.

Once you have successfully acquired a full set of improvised tools, a bow, simple arrows, and animal hide clothing, you are fully set for survival in Interloper. Be _extremely_ careful if you choose to complete [Tales](./Tales.md), as aurora wolves are even deadlier than normal wolves and can't be scared using torches, fires, or flares. [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md) may be your best friend here as they will scare off predators, however they are not easy to acquire due to needing an [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md).

If you choose to visit Bleak Inlet or Blackrock, make sure you are well armed with several [simple arrows](./Simple%20Arrow.md) and torches or [marine flares](./Marine%20Flare.md). Timberwolves kill in seconds and packs are extremely hard to fend off with just a bow, so don't be afraid to quit and reload the game to preserve your save file if you hear a pack howling and running towards you if you are not well prepared.

> “__A mysterious geomagnetic storm has brought your plane crashing down into the Northern Canadian wilderness.

During Survival Mode, the player may travel freely between all [Regions](./Region.md) of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), with the narrative created by their own actions and ability to survive. Survival Mode is a semi-permadeath experience; once the player [dies](./Condition.md#Death), the player can [Cheat Death](./Cheat%20Death.md) or choose to not continue (the later resulting in the save being wiped and it cannot be reloaded).

Players who purchase the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) Expansion will have access to unique content in Survival Mode, such as more tools, more Wildlife, and new Regions.
The choice of Experience dictates how harshly the world will treat the player throughout their journey in _The Long Dark_.![Pilgrim icon](../assets/Pilgrim_icon.png)
> “**Wander the quiet apocalypse to chronicle the passing of an age. This is the poetry of survival.**”

[Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md) is the easiest experience available in survival. Ideal for exploration and learning about the Island and the game mechanics in a low-stress environment. This mode is the standard "easy" difficulty setting.
> “**Equal parts hunter and hunted, your struggle to survive will eventually lead to mastering the elements.**”
An experience that balances exploration with a challenge, [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md) is the standard "normal" difficulty setting, and is the same difficulty as Wintermute Experiences.
> “**Your demise awaits behind every hilltop, shelter, and tree. Only the strong survive.**”
A punishing survival challenge. [Stalker](./Stalker.md) features numerous aggressive [Wolves](./Wolf.md) and [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md). This is the standard "hard" difficulty setting.
> “**You are not part of Mother Nature's plan, and you will bear the full force of her wrath. The true test of Human VS Nature.**”

A punishing survival experience. [Interloper](./Interloper.md) lets you know that you are an unwelcome guest in this cold, hostile world. Best suited for expert players looking for the ultimate survival challenge. This is the standard "expert" difficulty setting, with multiple handicaps present to make the game even harder than normal.
- You start with the most minimal resources, and have to craft everything you need to survive.

[Misery](./Misery.md) takes Interloper and ratchets up the difficulty by adding six new Afflictions that are applied over time. Intended for Interloper players looking for a new level of challenge. You will not survive for very long. This is the standard "impossible" difficulty.
- For expert players looking for a unique and devastating Survival challenge beyond Interloper.
- You start with the most minimal resources in an already harsh and hostile world on the brink.
- At timed intervals, you gradually succumb to permanent, unavoidable Afflictions unique to Misery.
> “**Use our custom toolbox to craft a unique experience between Survival and Exploration - an experience all your own.**”

For players lookingfor create their own Experience, separate from the standard Survival Mode difficulties, [Custom](./Custom.md) is the Experience for them. Players can create a custom Experience here, with over 50 different variables which can be adjusted to their liking.
- Give your Custom Experience Mode settings to fellow survivors using a special shareable code.

**Template:main** The player may select any region they want as their starting point. The player also has the option to randomize their starting region. Each region is unique, has different advantages and drawbacks, and are all interconnected.

If the Interloper Experience is selected, then the starting region will be randomly chosen. On Interloper, you will not spawn in Mystery Lake or Coastal Highway, and the number of possible spawn locations is limited.

Note that some regions are locked and cannot be selected to start a game in when first playing _The Long Dark_. They will always unlock in the menu selection screen for a future playthrough when the player travels there in-game for the first time.

May choose between a male or female survivor. The only differences are the character's voice, first person arms and hands, and the paper doll shown in the [Clothing](./Clothing.md) screen. The survivors use the same first person model, paper doll in the clothing screen, and voice as [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) and [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) from Wintermute, minus their wedding bands.

Every Survival Mode session begins with the same opening text: you are a survivor of a plane crash after a [mysterious geomagnetic storm](./First%20Flare.md) has grounded your vessel. A randomly generated real world quote regarding survival will be displayed on the screen and then the player is able to start playing shortly after.

The survivor is alone, not dressed for the cold, and carries only a meager amount of supplies. The player must find food and shelter before nightfall, when the temperatures drop. The amount of supplies one starts with is dependent on the experience mode selected.

Depending on the sandbox difficulty, the players may either find themselves inside a house or outside in the cold. On harder difficulties, it may already be dusk or night time, and in some cases bad weather may move in quickly.

- "Life is an error-making and an error-correcting process, and nature in marking man's papers will grade him for wisdom as measured both by survival and by the quality of life of those who survive." - Jones Salk
- "He is at home with his solitude as the note reverberating inside a bell." - Peter Heller, The Dog Stars
- "He knelt among the shadows and felt his isolation bitterly. They were savages it was true; but they were human." - William Golding, Lord of the Flies
- "It is hard to adapt to chaos, but it can be done. I am living proof of that: It can be done" - Kurt Vonnegut, Breakfast of Champions

- "No lists of things to be done. The day providential to itself. The hour. There is no later. This is later. All things of grace and beauty such that one holds them to one's heart have a common provenance in pain. Their birth in grief and ashes." - Cormac McCarthy, The Road
- "It is not the strongest of species that survives, nor the most intelligent that survives. It is the one that is the most adaptable to change." - Charles Darwin

- "No one can tell what goes on between the person you were and the person you become. No one can chart that blue and lonely section of hell. There are no maps of the change. You just come out the other side." - Stephen King, The Stand
- "Extraordinary people survive under the most terrible circumstances and they become more extraordinary because of it." - Robertson Davies
- "What am I living for and what am I dying for are the same question." - Margaret Atwood
- "On a long enough time line, the survival rate for everyone drops to zero." - Chuck Palahniuk

- "You know, I once read an interesting book which said that, uh, most people lost in the wilds, they, they die of shame. Yeah, see, they die of shame. 'What did I do wrong? How could I have gotten myself into this?' And so they sit there and they... die. Because they didn't do the one thing that would save their lives. Thinking." - David Mamet, The Edge
- "The foraging for food and water, the struggle for life in a world without masters, housed in a body that man had made dependent on himself." - Richard Matheson, I Am Legend

- "I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived. I did not wish to live what was not life, living is so dear; nor did I wish to practice resignation, unless it was quite necessary. I wanted to live deep and suck out all the marrow of life, to live so sturdily and Spartan-like as to put to rout all that was not life, to cut a broad swath and shave close, to drive life into a corner, and reduce it to its lowest terms." - Henry David Thoreau, Walden

Some items, locations, and even events found within the Wintermute Story mode are different within Survival Mode, suggesting an alternate timeline of events has unfolded. A list of notable changes include:

1. Despite [notes](./A%20Note%20Left%20Behind.md) being found throughout the world suggesting possible survivor activity, no human NPCs can be found. (not counting dead bodies that can be found or the [signal fires](./Mysterious%20Signal%20Fire.md) in [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md)).
4. Certain tools, clothing, and story related quest items cannot be found within Survival Mode.

5. It can be assumed that the player character you choose when starting Survival Mode is either [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) or [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md), as they share the same voice and appearance as their story counterparts and their backstory involves having their plane crash land on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) after a [mysterious geomagnetic storm](./First%20Flare.md). Will's [crashed plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) can also be found not far from [Milton](./Milton.md).

6. [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) is missing and her [home](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) has been ransacked, with her blanket and rocking chair still present but tipped over. She is presumed to have been burned alive in the [school house](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md) along with the other inhabitants of [Milton](./Milton.md) after the [convict riot](./Convicts.md) that resulted from the [crashed prison bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md).

7. [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) often contains a [corpse](./Martin%20Barker.md) inside the toolshed. The inside of the farmhouse also contains evidence of a [struggle](./Hobbs.md).

9. The [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) lies dormant, with [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) presumably being killed by the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) since no [help](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) arrived for him.

10. The [Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md) and any trace of their activities are entirely absent from Survival Mode, including their [supply caches](./Forest%20Talker%20Supply%20Caches.md), though occasionally their backpacks can be found.

11. The [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) is unoccupied, with neither [Molly](./Molly.md) nor her [husband's](./Molly%27s%20Husband.md) remains anywhere to be found. The nearby [barn](./Barn%20%28Molly%27s%29.md) has a [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) sized hole in the doors, but no dead wolf.

12. The [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md) at [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) is empty and [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md) is missing. Subsequently, this resulted in the makeshift triage center never being made, as there is no lite bonfire in front of the hall to guide the plane [Crash Survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md) to the town.

13. The [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) lies in ruins after a catastrophic explosion, with [all](./Mathis.md) [known](./Heller.md) [prisoners](./Vachon.md) and [on-site workers](./Franklin.md) having presumably perished inside. [Jace](./Jace.md) is also missing.

- Although Survival Mode is intended to be a permadeath experience, some players back up game saves periodically so that if they die, they can load the backed-up save and continue, even with Cheat Death enabled. This practice is called "[save scumming](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/scumming)."

> **You've crashed in the Northern wilderness and are badly injured. Survive long enough for your hand to heal, so you can climb out.**

**Survival Of The Fittest** was the first mission of the Predux [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).
- You have a bleeding wound. Find or make a bandage and use it to stop the blood loss.

This mission serves as a tutorial for the player, so do not worry too much about losing [Condition](./Condition.md), dying, or looting, as the real survival experience will begin in the next mission once you leave the ravine. This mission is heavily scripted, so just follow the mission objectives. Many items change in the ravine from day to day, so gather as much firewood as you can for day 3 until then.
### Day 1

The game will begin with the player character waking up from a plane crash with an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) in the sky. The burning wreckage of a crashed plane and the [Scrap Metal Shard](./Scrap%20Metal%20Shard.md) inside the player character's hand making it immediately obvious that they were in a crash.

Walk to the nearby cave and open the [First Aid Kit](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md) near the entrance to grab a [Bandage](./Bandage.md), then patch your hand up. You will need to start a fire, so gather some [Newsprint](./Newsprint.md) or use the [Scrap Metal Shard](./Scrap%20Metal%20Shard.md) to break down some [Cardboard Boxes](./Cardboard%20Box.md), grab some sticks, and then go into the cave. Start a [Campfire](./Campfire.md) and then the player will pass out.
### Day 2

The Maceknzie will awake and complain of being thirsty and hungry. Walk back to the base of the mountain side and loot the nearby [Plastic Container](./Plastic%20Container.md)/[Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md) for an [Military-Grade MRE](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md) and [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md). Eat the MRE and then gather as much firewood as you can. Start a fire in the cave and then boil and drink some water. An [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md) will appear as a result of your cut hand so use the Antiseptic to treat it. Then the player character will fall asleep.
### Day 3

Start by gathering all the firewood you can, as you will need a fire that lasts you for 9 hours. If you gathered and saved firewood from the previous days, this will help immensely. Many [Sticks](./Stick.md) and [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) will be on the ground so gather them and any other firewood you can. Only start a fire after breaking down several branches and [Crates](./Crate.md) (some crates hide items, such as 4 [Books](./Book.md) or [Water Purification Tablets](./Water%20Purification%20Tablets.md)), as time wasted after the fire has started will cause you to have to break down more items for fuel. After the fire is going, pass time warming up by boiling water. Then the player character will fall asleep.
### Day 4

Make your way over the new tree bridge and take [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) (where a cutscene will player revealing the player character's name is [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md)). Grab [Mackenzie's Parka](./Mackenzie%27s%20Parka.md) (called Will's Park) and then harvest the [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md). Attempt to (unsuccessfully) climb the [Rock Climb](./Rock%20Climb.md) and then return to the cave with your newly acquired [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md). Make a fire, cook at least 2 [Venison (Raw)](./Venison%20%28Raw%29.md), and eat the 2 [Venison (Cooked)](./Venison%20%28Cooked%29.md). Then Mackenzie will automatically sleep.
### Day 5

Mackenzie will finally recover from his Plane Crash Injuries and can climb out of the ravine. The mission will end when you reach the crashed plane above, with a cutscene explaining how his plane crashed.
Several plot points and locations have been replaced/altered since the Redux re-release of Episode 1:
- A voice calls out to Mackenzie when first waking up ("Mackenzie, don't let this new world break you"). This voice is not present in the Redux.
- The mission [Memories](./Memories.md) does not play since it did not exist in Predux, so the story continues in the ravine.
- The player must manually remove the [Scrap Metal Shard](./Scrap%20Metal%20Shard.md) from Mackenzie's hand by hovering over it. In Redux, this is automatically done.
- The credits of the developers will flash on screen in the upper left corner, and continues even into Day 2 if the player completes objectives fast enough.

- The player is stranded in the ravine below [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) for 5 days, serving as a tutorial for the player. On Day 4, a blizzard knocks down a tree, but they are not allowed to leave until they finish healing from Plane Crash Injuries on Day 5. The mission [Memories](./Memories.md) serves as the tutorial for the player in the Redux, and drastically shortens the days spent in the ravine to just 2 (the tree falls on Day 2 letting you leave).
- A unique [Affliction](./Afflictions.md), [Plane Crash Injuries](./Plane%20Crash%20Injuries.md), prevents the player from leaving the ravine or from sprinting until Day 5.
- After completing the day's objectives and resting, the current day flashes on screen.
- The [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md) bushes in the ravine cannot be harvested (resulting in the message "You don't need these yet) until Day 4.

- The player is required to climb out of the ravine on Day 4, but is not strong enough yet. A unique [Rock Climb](./Rock%20Climb.md) animation plays where Mackenzie fails to climb up and [sprains his ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md) as part of the [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) tutorial. This animation is still present on the first day [The Crash](./The%20Crash.md) in Redux if you attempt to leave the ravine on Day 1, though it no longer causes a Sprained Ankle.

- [Mackenzie's Parka](./Mackenzie%27s%20Parka.md), [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md), and [Astrid's Backpack](./Astrid%27s%20Backpack.md) are found next to the [Rock Climb](./Rock%20Climb.md) in the ravine rather than beneath the Plane on the ridge above.

- The with flashback with Will and Astrid plays after finding Astrid's Hardcase and is slightly longer than the Redux version (The cutscene is different from the Redux version, as a portion of it shows Mackenzie playing Solitaire, whereas in the Redux version this happens in-engine).

- The flashback cutscene itself is split into two parts as before, one part in the [Jackrabbit Island](./Jackrabbit%20Island.md) and the second part (playing when the player reaches [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md)) showing the crash portion of the cutscene (in Redux, the second cutscene takes place after loading up the plane).

- [Maureen's](./Characters.md#Maureen) voice is not heard on the phone call with Will in the Predux version. She also does not have a voice actor listed in the credits. In the Redux, she is fully voiced albeit briefly.

- A unique [Carcass Harvesting](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) animation plays with the Scrap Metal Knife when examining the [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md). Carcass Harvesting animations would not be introduced until Part 4 of the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md).
- The game does not automatically stop the player and turn the camera to show context sensitive situations, such as redirecting the camera towards Mackenzie's Crashed Plane when approached.

The **Survival Overlay** is an interface that allows the player to quickly judge their situation with. It shows a copious amount of essential information in its entirety through the use of symbol and bars rather than using text to overly explain stats. This includes things like [Needs](./Needs.md), [Condition](./Condition.md), Wind Shield, temperature, Time of Day, and the player's current [Stamina](./Stamina.md).

Pressing Tab on PC will quickly show the current needs. Opening the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md) (holding SPACE) will show the entire Survival Overlay until let go. The Overlay can be disabled entirely in the Options menu by selecting OFF in the HUD section.

The top left corner of the screen will show the current [Region](./Region.md) or [Location](./Locations.md) the player has walked into. Entering buildings, new Regions, or into outdoor Locations will tell the player the current area before the message slowly fades away.
[Harvesting](./Harvesting.md) objects will give a message and icon showing the [Materials](./Materials.md) harvested from the object, either in the game world or from the player's inventory.

Affliction Risks and Afflictions will appear on the right side of the screen. They appear briefly, and can be missed if not payed attention to. Most Afflictions will appear in the Status menu of the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) if it is opened.

![The 4 Needs and the Condition Bar](../assets/Needs_Current.png)_The 4 Needs and the Condition Bar_ The bottom left side of the screen is where the center hub is visible. These, unlike the central hub, are always visible (unless changed in the options menu), and exist as a warning to the player. The NEEDS section can be set to be ALWAYS ON, or CONTEXTUAL in the Options menu in the HUD option, and the icon size can also be set to be small, medium, or large. If turned to CONTEXTUAL, Needs will not appear until when one of the player's Needs is nearly or entirely empty, in which the icon will appear on the screen as red until satisfied and then will disappear again.

![The Fatigue bar when suffering from extreme hunger over long periods of time or Intestinal Parasites](../assets/UI_Long-Hunger.jpg)_The Fatigue bar when suffering from extreme hunger over long periods of time or Intestinal Parasites_ Here, the player can view their four major [Needs](./Needs.md) ([Warmth](./Warmth.md), [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Thirst](./Thirst.md), [Hunger](./Hunger.md)). The survival of each need is indicated by the size and color of the respective need bar; the smaller and more red the bar is (and more drained the circle), the more severe the need. Fully diminished Needs begin to drain Condition.

The [Condition](./Condition.md) bar is an overall measure of a survivor's overall health and well being. If this bar is fully depleted, the player will die. [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) that temporarily increase the maximum Condition bar size will be shown as blue, while red will temporarily decrease the bar size.
The heart next to the Condition bar alerts the player of any Affliction Risks they have or Afflictions they are suffering from (shown as a yellow exclamation in a circle).

A timer appears just above the 4 Needs when suffering from [Suffocation](./Suffocation.md), and will display the amount of time (in real world seconds) until the player dies. Leaving an area with unbreathable air or equipping a [Respirator](./Respirator.md) with a functioning [Canister](./Canister.md) will reset the countdown and make it disappear.

![Wind shield icon](../assets/Wind_shield_icon.png) Shown as an icon of a shield with wind blowing against its left side, the Windshield Icon will appear whenever you are currently shielded from the wind by an object (such as against a rock wall, inside a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md), when pressed against the walls of a ruined building, while inside interior outdoor buildings such as a [Fishing Hut](./Fishing%20Hut.md), or while inside a [Snow Shelter](./Snow%20Shelter.md)). This icon only appears when outdoors.

When shielded from the wind, the windchill effect of high winds on the player character is negated (increasing player Warmth) and [Campfires](./Campfire.md) built will be protected from becoming [windblown campfires](./Fire.md#Windblown_campfire).

[Scent](./Scent.md) is a mechanic which increases the distance which [predators](./Wildlife.md) can detect the survivor by smell. Scent is increased when the survivor is carrying meat and fresh guts, and is affected by wind speed and wind direction. There are 3 meters that increase as the player carries more odorous items. Being Windshielded will prevent the smell from spreading downstream.
Several icons, typically appearing in the bottom center of the screen, will appear to warn the player of imminent danger.

[Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md) will trigger the above icon as a danger warning to back away from the area. Failing to heed this warning will result in the player falling through the ice and taking Condition damage, wetting their clothes, and gaining [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md).

When a [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) pack has been alerted to the presence of the player, a special Morale meter appears in the bottom middle of the screen. Attacking the pack will cause the bar to gradually empty until the pack is entirely killed or scatters, in which it will dissapear.
_The corners of the screen appear yellow when suffering from [Chemical Poisoning Risk](./Chemical%20Poisoning%20Risk.md)_

[Chemical Hazards](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) are areas of land contaminated by toxic spilled chemicals that appear in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md). When not wearing a [Respirator](./Respirator.md) with a functional [Canister](./Canister.md), the 4 corners of the screen will gradually begin to fill up with a yellow overlay. Leaving a Chemical Hazard or equipping a Respirator will make the yellow film gradually dissipate.

Getting close to the Darkwalker in the [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) [Challenge](./Challenge.md) will cause a distance meter to appear when near the creature, displaying the current distance the monster is to the player.

Two Afflictions unique to the Challenge, [Fear](./Fear.md) and [Anxiety](./Anxiety.md), will also cause the screen to become more and more bloody the closer the player is to the Darkwalker. Walking farther away from the monster will cause the bloody screen to clear up and the distance meter to disappear.
These icons appear in the bottom right corner of the screen, and are related to overall movement and Stamina.

[Stamina](./Stamina.md) represents the player's ability to undertake several physically demanding tasks, and appears inside a draining circle similar to Needs. The image inside the bar changes depending on what physical task is being performed:

- Sprinting will show a man running (above photo). Sprint allows a player to run at a faster speed and is related to the weight of the player's worn [Clothing](./Clothing.md). Heavier clothing with the Sprint Penalty will cause the bar to lower, preventing the player from running for longer periods of time. Being fully [Fatigued](./Fatigue.md) or Over Encumbered will result in the player being unable to sprint anymore.

- [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) will show a hand icon and is related to the player's current grip on the [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md). The less grip that is present, the more likely the player will fall off the rope, potentially resulting in death.
- Weapons have their own bar that is directly tied to [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), and allows the player to aim their weapons until it is depleted:

- The [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) will show a crosshair icon, and affects the accuracy of the projectile fired. If the [Warmth](./Warmth.md) Need is depleted, the player will shiver as they aim.
- Aiming a [Revolver](./Revolver.md) will prevent the player from moving, and shows an icon of the sprinting man inside a crossed out red circle.
Information related to this HUD is only visible when the player is actively using stamina, otherwise this bar is hidden.
Equipped weapons/tools will show an icon of said weapon, it's ammunition, or the fuel inside:

- A Hunting Rifle, Revolver, or [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) will show the current amount of ammunition inside. A light icon will mean the ammo inside the gun is empty, while a bright icon means ammo is inside the gun.
- The amount of held [Stones](./Stone.md), Flares, and [Noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md) are displayed.

- An active [Flare](./Flare.md), [Marine Flare](./Marine%20Flare.md), [Torch](./Torch.md), or [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) will show the amount of fuel left inside until the item is unusable (Storm Lanterns can be refilled).
An icon of a man crouching appears when the player is currently crouching. Standing up will make the icon appear.

An icon appears when carrying a [Crash Survivor](./Crash%20Survivor.md) in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md). When this icon appears, the player cannot Sprint, use weapons, or enter vehicles.

A weight icon related to the player's current [Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md) level will appear in the bottom right. If the player is currently under their Carry Weight, the weight will appear green. If they are Over Encumbered, a red weight icon will appear instead, and will not disappear until the player's Encumbrance goes below their max Carry Weight again.

violations.context: _Pente.jpg_

Occasionally, the player will see a red slope when traveling the world. This is the Steep Slope Warning, and warns the player that walking over this area can result in a Sprain, such as a steep hill or rocky mountainside slope. If the player's Carry Weight is Over Encumbered and they are suffering from a [Sprain Risk](./Sprain%20Risk.md), they are more likely to acquire a [Sprained Wrist](./Sprained%20Wrist.md) or [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md) when walking through these areas.

![Midnight and Noon, the middle of night and the middle of day respectively](../assets/Nighttime_daytime_midnight_noon.jpg)_Midnight and Noon, the middle of night and the middle of day respectively_ The top right corner will show the Time of Day, represented by a sun and moon which rotates to give a rough idea as to the hour.
One day in '**The Long Dark**' is 24 hours long, split between 14.5 hours of daylight and 9.5 hours of darkness. [^1]

The day progresses as you play, as do other aspects of the game world. Temperature, daylight, and weather patterns may vary based on time of day. Cycles of the moon pass over the course of weeks; some animals may wander from prior territories; food [decays](./Decay.md) and may cause illness if consumed after turning rancid; and clothes wear down from use or even just being kept in storage.
An in-game hour is 5 minutes, so 1 real-world hour is 12 in-game hours. Some activities speed up time (such as breaking furniture or sleeping), so 12 in-game hours can pass in seconds.
One in game minute is 3 seconds irl, 3x60(minutes)=180(seconds), 180x24(hours)= 4320 seconds, divide by 60 = 72 irl minutes per full day and night cycle (3 minutes per in game hour).

![8:30 PM - Daytime ends, Nighttime begins](../assets/Nighttime_start_10pm.jpg)_8:30 PM - Daytime ends, Nighttime begins_ The coldest temperatures are usually early in the morning, just before dawn. As the day progresses, temperatures usually start to warm; how warm it gets depends on the region and the weather. **Example of temperature in °c in interloper J8: AM 6h -24/-17. 8h -22/-16. 11h -17/13 PM 1h:-10/6. 2h: -9/1 3h: -8/5. 4h -7/9. 5h -8/9. 0h: -20 AM 5h -26 8h -24.**

In general, it's best to explore the outdoors during the day because it offers better visibility and wolves are less aggressive. However, bears also wake up and patrol. Auroras, which make predators even more aggressive, never occur during the day.

To study, mend, craft items at workbenches, or recycle with tools indoor, most of the time light is needed. Daylight lasts from dawn (6:00 AM) through sundown (8:30 PM) both indoors and outdoors. If the sky isn't overcast, use of the [Magnifying lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) is permitted as soon as the first ray of the sun appear at 6:00 AM, as is any other activity that requires light. ![6:00 AM - Nighttime ends, Daytime starts](../assets/Nighttime_end_6am.jpg)_6:00 AM - Nighttime ends, Daytime starts_ As evening falls, outdoor temperatures start to drop and wolves are more active and alert, making it difficult to be outside as they will immediately attack instead of stalking the player. However, bears usually return to their dens and sleep. You’ll probably want to find shelter before it gets dark. Night time strips shelters of any natural interior light (except for [ice caves](./Ice%20Cave.md) in the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md)), making navigation a challenge.

Being lost in heavy snow on a dark night can be extremely challenging. When traveling in the dark, light sources are a must as it's otherwise very difficult to navigate. Night travel comes at the risk of wolf attacks, as they can detect a player from longer distances before a player may notice them. There is also a small chance for the Aurora to occur if the weather is clear.
_The first Survival Overlay in the Alpha game versions was inside the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md)_

This is the transcript for Chapter 3 [Survival School (Predux)](./Survival%20School%20%28Predux%29.md) for Predux [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md).

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Not with a blood-hungry bear on your ass, you haven't. Trust me, Mackenzie. You really want to find your friend? There's miles of wilderness in all directions from here. You'll never make it."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "That part goes without saying. You don't kill the bear, we (sic) neither of us gets out of here alive."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Yeah...could hardly sleep, it was so bright. There's something different about them. Not like the usual aurora borealis."
Mackenzie **(Text)**: "The lights...the aurora...seemed to power things up. Lights, mainly."
Mackenzie **(Text)**: "No. Lights. Like lights around buildings. They avoided the lights."
Mackenzie **(Text)**: "When I was out there...I came across mention of the Forest Talkers". (sic) You know anything about that?"
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Nothing like that. Eco-activists. Terrorists, some call them. They've been fighting for years, against further exploitation of Great Bear."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Not usually...they'll spike the occasional tree. Tie themselves to logging or mining equipment in protest. Don't think they've ever hurt anyone. But I'm not really up to date on current events."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Depends on your perspective, I guess. I try to stay out of politics. One thing's for sure - - they've been doing a lot more than just talking lately."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Few nights ago, heard a lot of shooting coming from the other side of the Lake. Could have been hunters I guess, but they aren't usually up this time of year."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "No idea. For their sake, I hope they got the hell out of the area before things got shut down. It won't be good for them, with Old Bear out there, and angry."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Didn't used to be that way. I told you before, something's stirring them up."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "You just stay focused on what I'm telling you. Watch out for the Old Bear. He's cunning as hell. Make a wolf look like a damn lap dog."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Wolves - - they hate fire, like most wildlife. Campfire'll keep them away from you at night, most of the time. Improvise a torch if you have to. Flare will work too, you know one of those emergency ones for road accidents. Sometimes, if you get lucky, a stone to the head will scare them off."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Then wait until they're close, and hit them with anything you can. Knife. Hammer. Hatchet. Or your own damn hands. And you don't stop hitting until one of you is dead."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Yeah. That is it: fight if you want to live. It's more Hobbes than Darwin."
Mackenzie **(Text)**: "At some point I'm going to need to get out of here and find my friend."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "You want to get to Perseverance Mills? You gotta pass through the guts of that Dam."
Mackenzie **(Text)**: "Doesn't seem possible. When I was there, the whole place seemed locked down. The parts that weren't falling down, anyway."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "That may be, but it's still the only way to get where you need to go."
Mackenzie **(Text)**: "I heard a phone ring...in an old hunting lodge...where I found the extra rifle. You know anything about that?"
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Old phone lines don't depend on power like the new systems do. It's one of the many ways the old infrastructure is better than what we have now."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "I'm serious. Everything's so integrated now. So linked. It's a house of cards. One system fails, they all fail."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Old analogue system could still work. No telling how the lines are set up. Call could be from anywhere on Great Bear, really. If you know what the lines and switches connect to, you could probably figure it out."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Those old analog lines...bet nobody even knows they're still hooked up. You'd need an old phone company line map. No idea where you could find one, though. Must be archives somewhere?"

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Survival takes focus. We'll continue when you're done with your current lesson."
## Learn to craft Fishing Tackle, then catch fish from Mystery Lake.

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "You won't always have the means to hunt, so you need to know more than one way to feed yourself. Protein's scarce in the Winter. Fishing might help keep your dumb pilot ass from dying out there."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Head to the Camp Office at the edge of Mystery Lake. You'll find the gear you need for ice fishing. There's some huts on the lake. Bring back some fish and I'll know you won't die from starvation, at least."
Mackenzie **(Text)**: "Why do I feel this is a thinly veiled scheme to get me to feed you for the Winter?"

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Nothing thinly veiled about it. Look at me, Mackenzie. That Old Bear wrecked me good. I won't hunt or trap this season. If me teaching you means we both survive...what's the harm? You want to try your hand at it?"
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Suit yourself. But you'll have to [tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) it some time. Ha!"

_Mackenzie heads to the [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) and crafts a Fishing Tackle, the Ice Fishes at Mystery Lake. He returns to the Homestead, and then places the raw fish in the nearby Supply Bin. If the player asks about this lesson again after completing it_
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "You know what you need to know about Ice Fishing now. Not much more that I can tell you."
## Learn to find, track, shoot, and butcher a Deer.
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Trick is to spot your target, get as close as you can, take a shot, and don't miss."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Pretty much. A few years of practice and you might have a clue."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "There's a clearing, a few hilltops over from here. I'll mark it on your map. Almost always a herd of deer that winter there. Shoot one, and bring the meat back here, then we'll both know you can feed yourself in the wild."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Remember - - if you hit one, but don't kill it, you'll have to track it til(sic) it drops. Look for blood in the snow, and follow its trail. It'll fall, eventually. Then we both eat. Good luck. You ready?"
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Ok, but don't wait too long. You won't get better at shooting just by thinking about it."

_Mackenzie heads to the [Unnamed Pond](./Unnamed%20Pond.md), kills a [Deer](./Deer.md) or two, then places the raw meat in the nearby Supply Bin outside the Homestead. If the player asks about this lesson again after completing it_
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "I think you've shot enough deer for one day. You're done with that."
## Learn to mend and maintain clothing. It'll save your life some day.
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Its damn cold out there, right? What you wear might make the difference between life and death."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Wind or wet will kill you if you let it. Wear wind-blocking clothes on your outside layer if you can, and use natural shelter whenever possible. Wind will drop your core temperature quickly and before you know it you'll have hypothermia, or worse."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "That one's obvious. You get wet from snowfall, falling through the ice, whatever - - in these Winters, you'll get frostbite in no time. Wear waterproof clothing if you can, especially on your feet. If you clothes get wet, dry them out by a fire."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Almost. Think about carrying weight - - the heavier your clothing, the less food and other supplies you can carry without getting tired. And remember, you want some tough layers to protect you from falls and animals, especially these days."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Great. Remember though, it's not enough to have good gear if you don't take care of it. Needle and thread are your friends. Keep your clothing in good shape and it'll take care of you. Sacrifice any shitty gear you find to keep your better gear in action."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Good. Now prove it. Take this old parka of mine. There's an old Lookout tower just off the railway. Usually some Forestry Service gear there in there. Use their supplies to repair my old parka."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "The only way to know it, is to do it, Mackenzie. Now get out there."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Too good to pick up a sewing kit, huh? You'll learn the hard way."

_Mackenzie heads to the [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md), repairs [Jeremiah's Bearskin Coat](./Jeremiah%27s%20Bearskin%20Coat.md) with a [Cured Black Bear Hide](./Cured%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md) lying up there, and then returns to the Homestead to give it to Jeremiah._
