## Learn to identify and harvest some of the edible, medicinal flora native to Great Bear Island. (Place in the container at Jeremiah's Cabin)
Mackenzie **(Text)**: "Seems if you have your way, I'll never be a vegetarian out here."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "I'm sure it's no coincidence that most of the animals out here are made of meat, Mackenzie."
Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Well, yeah...most of the year, you can subsist mainly on plants you can harvest. Berries. Nuts. Mushrooms. But, not much grows in the Winter."

Jeremiah **(Text)**: "Definitely. Cat Tails - - they don't taste like much but they'll keep you from starving. You usually find them near water. Reishi Mushrooms - - they grow on tree stumps. You can make a tea on them. A good natural antibiotic. Rose Hips - - they look like little red berries. Also good in a kind of tea. Great for treating pain. Old Man's Beard Moss - - you'll see it hanging from trees. You can wrap it in a bandage and use it to prevent bites from getting infected. Learn to identify each of these, cause they could save your life, Mackenzie. You ready to give it a shot?"

> **Jeremiah's guide to surviving the Quiet Apocalypse. Listen to him if you want to live.**

**Survival School** was the third mission of the Predux [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).

Due to its overwhelmingly negative impact on breaking the pace of the game (especially for players already familiar with Ice Fishing, Hunting, Mending, and Foraging/players whom have already played Episode 2 before) and being able to do only one task at a time, this mission has since been replaced by the optional side missions [Survival School](./Survival%20School.md) and [The Basics of Survival](./The%20Basics%20of%20Survival.md). The main mission that filled this spot of the story was instead replaced by [Signal to Noise](./Signal%20to%20Noise.md).
- Learn to identify and harvest some of the edible, medicinal flora native to Great Bear Island. (Place in the container at Jeremiah's Cabin)
> “**No. What I suggest is Jeremiah's Survival School. Student Population: one. Let's see if we can keep you alive long enough to graduate.**”

Any of the 4 mission tasks can be taken and completed in any order desired, but they must all be finished in order to get to the next mission [Jeremiah's Folly](./Jeremiah%27s%20Folly.md). Only one School of Survival can be active at one time.

Selecting this option will task Mackenzie to head to the [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) to craft a [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) and catch fish from the [Ice Fishing Huts](./Ice%20Fishing%20Huts.md) at [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md). Mackenzie realizes that this is more of a chore for Jeremiah to put fish in his belly than to teach him anything, but Jeremiah points out that with his wounds he won't be able to hunt or trap for the rest of the season, so this helps them both out.

The Fishing Tackle blueprint will unlock, so head to the Camp Office and craft a tackle. Then start [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) when you walk out to the lake and into a Fishing Hut. Break the ice in one of the huts and gather the specified amount of fish in terms of weight, then return to the Homestead and place them inside of the [Supply Bin](./Supply%20Bin.md) next to the door.

violations.context: > “__M - What can you tell me about hunting?
J - Trick is to spot your target, get as close as you can, take a shot, and don't miss.

Jeremiah will instruct Mackenzie to head to a clearing over the hill to the [Unnamed Pond](./Unnamed%20Pond.md) and to kill a stag. His orders the pilot to shoot and kill a Deer, then bring its meat back to the cabin. If Mackenzie gets a hit but doesn't immediately kill the beast, Jeremiah's advice is to track the blood in the snow as the Deer bleeds out, then harvest the carcass. Jeremiah will then hand you 5 [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) and send you on your way. Be aware that Jeremiah will NOT give you more ammo if you run out.

Clear as much from your inventory as you can, as you will need the extra storage space soon. Hunt during the morning or day to maximize your visual scanning of the area. Head forward over the hill the moment you step out of Trapper's Homestead until you find the Unnamed Pond, then crouch, get close, take aim, and kill a Deer. Harvest all the [Venison (Raw)](./Venison%20%28Raw%29.md) from its body and return to the cabin, then place the meat in the Supply Bin. You may need to kill multiple deer to accomplish this task.

J - Its damn cold out there, right? What you wear might make the difference between life and death.__”

Jeremiah will explain to Mackenzie the importance of wearing good clothing in the Winter. Windproof and Wetproof clothing on the outer layers, while wearing warm clothing on the inside. Eventually, Jeremiah will give Mackenzie his old park, and will ask him to head to the nearby [Forestry Lookout](./Lookout%20%28Mystery%20Lake%20location%29.md) to retrieve some skins Jeremiah left up there as sewing supplies to fix the "parka" (The Parka in question is his damaged [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md) from the Old Bear's attack, it weighs 5.00 kg, and is found in the Clothing section of the Backpack). Simply make your way there, grab the [Cured Black Bear Hide](./Cured%20Black%20Bear%20Hide.md), use a [Sewing Kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md) or [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) to repair [Jeremiah's Bearskin Coat](./Jeremiah%27s%20Bearskin%20Coat.md), then return to the Trapper's Homestead. FYI, you can't wear his coat at any point after receiving it, nor can you harvest it (however you can drop it, but don't lose it). After repairing the coat, talk to Jeremiah and select the dialogue option Story to give it back to him, finishing the task.

Jeremiah will briefly explain much of the flora of Great Bear Island, mentioning berries, nuts, and so forth, but then skipping to what mainly grows in the Winter. He will focus on 4 main types of flora; [Cat Tail](./Cat%20Tail.md), [Rose Hip](./Rose%20Hip.md), [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md), and [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md). You will then be given a list of these items, how many to find, and you will need to place them inside Jeremiah's Supply Bin outside the Homestead. Many ingredients can be found in the rabbit grove east of the door to the Homestead when stepping outside.
- Cat Tails grow near fresh water streams. Check the [Unnamed Pond](./Unnamed%20Pond.md), [Frozen Creek](./Frozen%20Creek.md), or [Mystery Lake (location)](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28location%29.md).

After completing all 4 Schools, return to Jeremiah and a cutscene begins where Mackenzie thanks Jeremiah for the training. After going through all that toil, Jeremiah tosses Mackenzie [his knife](./Jeremiah%27s%20Knife.md) as a graduation gift, saying he has a feeling that the pilot might need it, and the next mission starts.
Several plot points and locations have been replaced/altered since the Redux re-release of Episode 2:

- This entire mission was cut from the game due to very poor reception, and was turned into a two optional side mission in Redux, with all the tutorials being recycled into the side missions [The Basics of Survival](./The%20Basics%20of%20Survival.md) and [Survival School](./Survival%20School.md).
- Fishing was recycled into [The Frozen Angler](./The%20Frozen%20Angler%20%28Survival%20School%29.md) in Episode 2's Survival School.

- Hunting was recycled into [Frontier Shooting Guide](./Frontier%20Shooting%20Guide%20%28Survival%20School%29.md) and [Advanced Guns Guns Guns!](./Advanced%20Guns%20Guns%20Guns!%20%28Survival%20School%29.md) in Episode 2's Survival School.
- Mending was recycled into [A Sewing Primer](./A%20Sewing%20Primer%20%28The%20Basics%20of%20Survival%29.md) in Episode 1's The Basics of Survival.
- Harvestable Plants was recycled into [Medicinal Plants of Great Bear](./Medicinal%20Plants%20of%20Great%20Bear.md) in Episode 1's The Basics of Survival.
- [Jeremiah's Bearskin Coat](./Jeremiah%27s%20Bearskin%20Coat.md) was cut from the game.

- Jeremiah mentions not having anything electronic in his cabin that could be affected by the Aurora, feigning ignorance that the Aurora isn't as strong as Mackenzie makes it out to be. It would later be revealed that he has a shortwave radio hidden in the floorboards of his cabin that he uses to speak with his mysterious correspondent. This was changed in Redux, as the shortwave radio is now a central part of the plot, as Mackenzie is required to find multiple parts to fix it on many occasions ([Radio Parts](./Radio%20Parts.md), [Transponder Parts](./Transponder%20Parts.md)).

- Jeremiah rewards Mackenzie with his unique Hunting Knife, [Jeremiah's Knife](./Jeremiah%27s%20Knife.md), after graduating from his Survival School. It serves as a reskinned [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), with identical stats. This item was cut from the game, and regular Hunting Knives can be found more often throughout Episode 2 in the Redux.

**Sutherland's Tale** is the fourth and final [Tale](./Tales.md) released for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). Completing this Tale is not needed to unlock the [Rüdiger's Dream](./R%C3%BCdiger%27s%20Dream.md) Achievement.
_This section may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark._
The objectives for this Tale do not show up in the Journal menu, so it is considered more of a hidden side mission. The following objectives are needed to complete this Tale:
- Wait for the [Trader](./Trader.md) to become available, then contact the Trader and begin trading with him.
- Continue building Trust with the Trader by successfully trading with him (it does not matter what/how much you trade).

- Place the items he requests in his [Trade Drop Box](./Trade%20Drop%20Box.md) on the pier behind [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md) in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md).
- Once this is done, call him over the radio to confirm the trade. Then retrieve your items to start another trade.
- Angering Sutherland will lower his Trust, delaying the questline: Calling him more than 2 times a night or canceling an active trade too many times will lower his opinion of you.
- There is currently no way to track his Trust level, so always be courteous to him by not pinging him too often during the day and be prepared to go through with a trade you committed to.
- After a certain amount of trades are completed, Sutherland will ask a favor of you.
- The option to enable the Trader on your survival save must be enabled, otherwise you cannot start this Tale.

- Unlike the other 3 Tales, the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) does not need to be acquired and [Transmitters](./Transmitters.md) do not need to be repaired to complete this Tale.

- Playing on [Interloper](./Interloper.md)/[Misery](./Misery.md) will make it difficult to distinguish between the 3 stocked [Prepper's Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) since they always spawn as Abandoned. Players will need to pay close attention to the layouts of the caches, and take detailed notes about them[^1].
- The Stockpile Cache, needed for Special Request 1, can be identified as it is the only one which contains a corpse[^2]. It also contains the recipe for [Prepper's Pie](./Prepper%27s%20Pie.md).
- The Hunting Cache, needed for Special Request 2, can be identified as it is the only one with an L-shaped layout[^3].
- The Conspiracy Cache, needed for Special Request 3, can be identified as it is the only one that has a corridor with red-painted walls[^4].

- Because the location of the 3 special caches is random, you will have to check each cache one by one until you find all three stocked ones. The location of the Prepper's Abandoned Cache involved in Special Requests 4 and 5 is always fixed in Pleasant Valley near the rope climb to Timberwolf Mountain.

- NOTE that _you must accept the Special Request trade_ in order for the Loose Bricks Stash to be accessible in its respective Prepper Cache as the Tale progresses. You cannot loot Brick Stashes ahead of time.
- Just finishing Sutherland's last special request is not enough to unlock the [Goods and Services](./Goods%20and%20Services.md) achievement (Gain maximum trust with the trader).

- Completing this Tale will involve a lot of travelling. Ensure you have good warm clothes for travelling. Prioritize light, calorie-dense foods and keep [Scent](./Scent.md) low to minimize encounters with dangerous wildlife. [Coffee](./Tin%20of%20Coffee.md) can help with fatigue management.

- Most of the caches can be easily accessed within a day's walk from [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), though it may be a long day of walking to the caches at [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), and [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md).
- Be careful when crossing [Raven Falls Trestle](./Raven%20Falls%20Trestle.md), as you may have to do so multiple times.

The player has no way of know this at first, but Sutherland eventually reveals that his radio has not been working since the start of a new survival game, and that he has been spending all this time repairing it. Below is a time table showing how long the player must survive before he repairs his radio and can be contacted.

After the arrival time is met and the Aurora/Glimmer Fog powers the Radios, a voice will be heard on the radio. Talking to the man on the radio will allow you to begin trading with him where he offers to trade things with you. He requests that you drop everything off at the [Trade Drop Box](./Trade%20Drop%20Box.md) at the pier near [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md) in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md).

At this point, simply complete around 5 trades with him. It does not matter how much you trade for, or what the quality of items are. Consider just trading for 1 item 5 times to speed up this questline. If multiple items are requested in a trade, make sure to fully satisfy each trade request. Partially completed trades do not gain as much Trust as fully completed ones.

The Trader will want to know where his brother Wyatt is since he has not heard from him since the lights started appearing in the sky, and mentions a series of [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md) across the island belonging to Wyatt's old crew. After listening to the special conversation, a new Trade item will appear in the Trade menu called "Special Request".

The first 3 Special Requests involve finding 3 themed Prepper Caches distributed across the Lower Great Bear. You only need to consider the 9 Prepper Caches in the Lower Great Bear, 6 of which are empty. In 3 of them (Stockpile, Hunter, and Conspiracy) you will find a large amount of loot (except on Interloper and above), as well as a Loose Bricks Stash that is only accessible after you've accepted the respective trade offer. Inside the Loose Bricks Stash you will find a Documents Stash which you need to trade to Sutherland (meaning that you must obtain the stashes in order, and you must return to Coastal Highway after every step). The fixed location of each of the 9 Prepper Caches is listed here: [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md).

The first cache the player must find is the Stockpile themed bunker. On Interloper this cache can be identified as the one with a corpse and Prepper's Pie recipe. Look around the walls until you find a [Loose Bricks Stash](./Loose%20Bricks%20Stash.md) and obtain the [Document Stash 1](./Document%20Stash%201.md) ([Wyatt's Lost Papers 1](./Wyatt%27s%20Lost%20Papers%201.md) and [Bunker Schematic Fragment 1](./Bunker%20Schematic%20Fragment%201.md) are found inside). Return the Document Stash 1 to the Trader by placing it in the Trade Drop Box, thus fulfilling his Special Request trade. Then talk to him on the radio after obtaining your reward ([Mackinaw Jacket](./Mackinaw%20Jacket.md)).
The Trader will want to know more of where his brother went, and mentions finding the Hunter cache on the island next.

The second cache the player must find is the Hunter themed bunker. On Interloper this cache will have the L-shaped layout. Look around the walls until you find a [Loose Bricks Stash](./Loose%20Bricks%20Stash.md) and obtain the [Document Stash 2](./Document%20Stash%202.md) ([Wyatt's Lost Papers 2](./Wyatt%27s%20Lost%20Papers%202.md) and [Bunker Schematic Fragment 2](./Bunker%20Schematic%20Fragment%202.md) are found inside). Return the Document Stash 2 to the Trader by placing it in the Trade Drop Box, thus fulfilling his Special Request trade. Then talk to him on the radio after obtaining your reward (3x [Arrowheads](./Arrowhead.md)).
The Trader will want to know more of where his brother went, and mentions searching for the Conspiracy cache on the island next.

The third cache the player must find is the Conspiracy themed bunker. On Interloper this cache can be identified by having distinct red corridor walls and a radiation sign on the wall. Look around them until you find a [Loose Bricks Stash](./Loose%20Bricks%20Stash.md) and obtain the [Document Stash 3](./Document%20Stash%203.md) ([Wyatt's Lost Papers 3](./Wyatt%27s%20Lost%20Papers%203.md) and [Bunker Schematic Fragment 3](./Bunker%20Schematic%20Fragment%203.md) are found inside). Return the Document Stash 3 to the Trader by placing it in the Trade Drop Box, thus fulfilling his Special Request trade. Then talk to him on the radio after obtaining your reward ([Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md)).

After reading all the information you've found and sent to him, the Trader will mention a 4th bunker not related to his brother's 3 crewmates. He will tell you to find Tom Joplin's [Prepper's Abandoned Cache](./Prepper%27s%20Abandoned%20Cache.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
For the last 2 requests it is shortest to utilize the Abandoned Mine shortcut connecting Coastal Highway to Pleasant Valley.

Head there and look at the wall near the Mattress to find a semi bricked up wall (a hole can be found that barely lets you peer into a hidden room). Tear the wall down and head inside, where you will find [A Skeleton And Note](./A%20Skeleton%20And%20Note.md) on the floor. Picking up "A Skeleton And Note" will add the note [Sutherland's Note](./Sutherland%27s%20Note.md) to your inventory, revealing that Sutherland bricked up the wall to leave his brother to rest after a fire killed him.

Return "A Skeleton And Note" to the Trader by placing it in the Trade Drop Box, thus fulfilling his Special Request trade. Then talk to him on the radio after obtaining your reward ([Hockey Jersey](./Hockey%20Jersey.md)).

Sutherland finally remembers that his brother has been dead for many decades now, and requests that the player return him back to the Abandoned Prepper's Cache, then to seal it up so that he may be at rest. He mentions the failsafe made into the bunker from all the notes you have found and to bring back evidence that you properly laid Wyatt to rest. Return to the Trade Drop Box to find that a [Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md) has been placed next to the Box, and that the "A Skeleton And Note" has been returned as "[Wyatt's Skeleton](./Wyatt%27s%20Skeleton.md)". Take Wyatt's Skeleton from the Trade Drop Box and bring a [Wire Bundle](./Wires.md) with you for later. Make your way back to Joplin's Cache in Pleasant Valley and head into the hidden room you previously opened.

**WARNING:** Loot/Harvest anything you want from inside Joplin's Cache BEFORE finishing the next step, as this Cache will be **_PERMENANTLY INACCESSIBLE ONCE YOU LEAVE!_** (This includes losing access to the [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md)).

A panel on the wall can be interacted in the hidden room stating "Set demolition charge and place Wyatt's bones". Interacting with it will display the message "Rigging..." and places Wyatt's Skeleton back onto the floor. **_Once you leave the Cache_**, an explosion occurs as the hatch is shut and locked behind you. The screen will be black, with the Survivor lying on the ground and slowly waking up. The entrance to the Cache is now destroyed and the bunker's [Broken Hatch Wheel](./Broken%20Hatch%20Wheel.md) is lying in the snow.

Return the Broken Hatch Wheel to the Trader by placing it in the Trade Drop Box, thus fulfilling his Special Request trade. Then talk to him on the radio after obtaining your reward ([Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md)). Sutherland is relieved that his brother is at rest again, and mentions how unbelievable it is how he forgot about his death.
Sutherland mentions that he will continue to stay around to trade with you, at least for now. As a reward for helping him, most future services now include a discount when trading with Sutherland.

From this point onwards, the Tale ends but the player can continue to trade to gain max Trust with Sutherland. Gaining max Trust will unlock the [Goods and Services](./Goods%20and%20Services.md) achievement, but no new dialogue is unlocked with Sutherland.

They do nothing, even when powered, so the Survivor ignores them, seeing how most electronics don't work correctly anymore ever since their plane crashed. One night however, they pass by a powered Radio and hear a voice._

**Description:** A mountain region housing the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md) and a small parking lot.

The **Suzuki Enviorns** is a [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md)-exclusive region, which consists solely of the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md). It can be accessed by the nearby [Blackrock Foothills](./Blackrock%20Foothills.md), and eventually leads out to the [Suzuki Geothermal Region](./Suzuki%20Geothermal%20Region.md).
The region is situated along the peak of Mt. Franklin, at an elevation of 2,196 meters (7,204 feet) above sea level.

The area consists of two spaces; a flat gated parking lot surrounded by rocky clearing, and a lowered, hilly area used to access the Geothermal Region, which is filled with bits of rusted piping and industrial scrap off to the side, and is divided from the rest of the region by a massive barbed wire fence.
A white [truck](./Truck.md) can be found in the parking lot, with [crumpled note](./Shopping%20List.md) inside the glove box describing it as "Dr. Atwood's truck."

- Mt. Franklin's peak is 2,196 meters above sea level, which is ironically exactly 1 meter _taller_ than the [Golden Hinde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Hinde_%28mountain%29), the tallest peak on Vancouver Island, a major inspiration for Great Bear Island.

**Description:** A mountain region with several Geothermal Substations that deliver power to the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md) facility.

The **Suzuki Geothermal Region** is a [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md)-exclusive region, which consists 3 Geothermal Substations and some nearby mountains. It is accessed by the [Suzuki Environs](./Suzuki%20Environs.md).

The Suzuki Geothermal Region is one of the most barest maps in all of [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md), featuring very little vegetation. It features a primary road that loops across the region, which occasionally blocked by avalanches and broken bridges, forcing the player to take alternative routes. A massive, hissing steam pipe directs the player towards Geothermal Substation Two during the primary mission. This region is also, utterly, full of [Wolves](./Wolf.md), with altered AI in order to be twice as challenging.

Each of the Substations have very similar floorplans, with the downside of having certain areas becoming blocked with steam once the Substation is activated. Ventilation shafts can be used to navigate around these plooms.

[Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) goes through here with a time limit of three hours to activate the Substations in order to give [Jace](./Jace.md) and [Atwood](./Atwood.md) a fighting chance at recovering the data collected at the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md). After activating Geothermal Substation Two, [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) will cover the region. After crossing the final bridge, Mackenzie will have to face off against a [Cougar](./Cougar.md).

> “**The Suzuki Radio Telescope. It's an old government facility, so there's all kinds of supplies there... food, medical equipment, vehicles. Radios. They could hunker down for weeks, months. It'd make a hell of a base of operations for all manner of evil shit they might get up to.**”

The **Suzuki Radio Telescope** is a location within the [Suzuki Environs](./Suzuki%20Environs.md) near [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) mentioned by [Jace](./Jace.md) in [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), and primarily featured in [Episode 5: The Light At The End of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md). Jace's thesis professor, [Dr. Atwood](./Atwood.md), lives within the facility. It is an old government radio telescope stated to be shielded by electromagnetic storms with it's own power supply, and is possibly been unaffected by the recent [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) solar storm, though this is found to be innaccurate in Episode 5.

violations.context: #### **Lower Suzuki**

Home to the facility's Control Room, Dr. Atwood's Study, the Barracks, a Kitchen & attached Cafeteria, a Washroom, Showers, and a supply room. Lower Suzuki is also home to numerous utility corridors, offices, winding hallways, and multiple rooms full of vintage Data Storage systems from the 1980s, including a winding hallway leading to Upper Suzuki, and a possible internal entrance to the Bunker.

Upper Suzuki is where the Tuner Control station is located, aswell as housing the massive radio telescope and it's related equipment. The primary control station is situated in a massive hall, with a large window overlooking the telescope itself.

A series of Cold-War era storage rooms, dormitories, and related services deep below the Radio Telescope. Jace describes it as being full of medical supplies, food, vehicles, and radios.[^1] It only appears during the final cutscenes of shown in Part 4 of Episode 5, with it's interior being rather cramped, full of ventilation shafts, pipework, and a mostly steel and concrete construction.[^2]

The Suzuki Radio Telescope was built sometime in the mid 20th century, though it wasn't initially a Radio Telescope. Originally, it was built as an observation post, with the express purpose of monitoring foreign satellite communictions during the Cold War, it's position chosen both for the secluded and isolated nature of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), but also thanks to the clarity provided by it's elevated position.[^3] Because of this, most of the base's facilites were deep underground, in magnetically shielded dorms and store rooms, some three to four floors below the above-ground portions. Most of the communications intercepted during this era were from the major players; the United States, the Soviet Union, and some from China.

It's unknown exactly when the Canadian Government moved out, but shortly after the site was no longer being used for monitoring, it was quickly repurposed and rechristened the Suzuki Radio Telescope some twenty or more years before the events of the game.[^4]

The Geothermal Plant seen in the [Suzuki Geothermal Region](./Suzuki%20Geothermal%20Region.md) was a rather costly project undertaken by Suzuki, with three large Substations being constructed alongside the Plant itself. The Plant was operated by multiple smaller crews, who operated within the Substations themselves, and while it was quite successful, it ended up axed due to operating costs several years prior to Wintermute, with only a small feeder line being left open and providing Suzuki with some background power.[^5]

During their third telephone call, Jace explains that the Suzuki Radio Telescope is around 15-20 clicks from [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) itself, and that it is an "old government facility" with supplies ranging from food, to vehicles, and even radios. She warns [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) that [Mathis](./Mathis.md) and his [Convicts](./Convicts.md) will most likely attempt to overtake the facility and use it as their main base of operations for the island should they escape [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md),[^6] before going on to explain that Suzuki's electromagnetic radiation shielding may have spared it from the electronic-frying effects of the [Aurora](./Aurora.md).

After escaping the Unstable Mine in the [Blackrock Foothills](./Blackrock%20Foothills.md), Jace and Mackenzie are let in by Atwood who is, for the moment, untrusting of Mackenzie. She tells Jace that the facility is locked in a kind of maintenance mode, and was unable to pull any data from the telescope before the Aurora's power surge fried much of the facility's equipment. She states that, without heading out to the Substations to fully activate the Geothermal systems, they're unable to fully activate the remaining equipment, alongside that the small amount of data she was able to secure was concerning.
Mackenzie relays the message of Wintermute, much to the shock and quiet horror of Atwood.

The following morning, Mackenzie heads to Atwood's Study to learn that there is a somewhat risky way to try and retrieve the data within the facility's memory buffers. Despite Mackenzie's protests, Atwood enlists him in helping with her plan, which envolves returning full power to the facility's geothermal plant, which would allow Atwood to fire up the mainframes and pull the remaining data from the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) out of the memory buffers. The only issue being Mackenzie has a short period to do so, as not only will a heightened, massive Aurora arrive that night and most likely wipe the memory buffers of all data, but if Mackenzie takes too long turning on each of the substations, the pressure buildup would most likely cause a horrific explosion. And, to add insult to injury, the wolves in the region are even more ferocious.

Thankfully, Mackenzie is armed with a number of high-quality gear, such as a [Combat Pants](./Combat%20Pants.md), [Military Coats](./Military%20Coat.md), and the new Episode 5-exclusives: the [Shotgun](./Shotgun.md) and [Military Stims](./Military%20Stim.md). After returning from his excursion, and with the power back in, Mackenzie assists Jace in ensuring the data is moved from the buffers into Dr. Atwood's study by moving the Telescope dish using the tuners. Despite the challenges, the Tuner Control room's equipment catching fire, and one of the tuners even electrocuting Mackenzie, the data is successfully pulled from the buffers. But, before it can be processed, Suzuki's remaining equipment is overloaded and completely shuts down.
Atwood goes on to explain what the Aurora exactly is, before letting Mackenzie head to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) to try and find [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md).

- The Facility itself is most likely named after [David Suzuki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Suzuki), a renowned Canadian environmental activist, geneticist, and world-famous science broadcaster.

- According to the [Shopping List](./Shopping%20List.md) note, Atwood and Jace share a P.O box at an unknown Post Office, with the code to it being 1859. The only three possible locations for this P.O box include [Milton](./Milton%20Post%20Office.md), [Perseverance Mills](./Co-op.md), and the elusive and currently unseen Port Mary.
- The Kitchen within Lower Suzuki most likely contains the highest concentration of consumable food and drink in the entirety of Wintermute.
[^4]: The last time Atwood saw Jeremiah was 20+ years ago, and she was working at the Telescope, not the base. [https://youtu.be/Mv1kQlPK7xE?t=15611](https://youtu.be/Mv1kQlPK7xE?t=15611)

> “**Reinforced gloves in the tactical style. Highly-protective, at the cost of warmth.**”

**Tactical Gloves** are unique [Clothing](./Clothing.md) found only during the [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) Tale in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md). It is found in the [Last Lonely House](./Last%20Lonely%20House.md), under the bed in the locked bedroom (unlocked with [An Old House Key](./An%20Old%20House%20Key.md)). They originally belonged to [The Foreman](./The%20Foreman.md).

Tactical Gloves are warm and best-in-slot windproofing, waterproofing and protection but are slightly (0.5°C) colder than similar late-game gloves: [Rabbitskin Mitts](./Rabbitskin%20Mitts.md) or [Gauntlets](./Gauntlets.md). Tactical Gloves also provide more total "[Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md)" temperature increase (warmth + windproof) for a total of 4.5°C, where as Rabbitskin Mitts and Gauntlets provide only 4°C.
Because of their very high windproofing, these Tactical Gloves typically provide more benefit outdoors than indoors (or sheltering inside vehicles/caves) where windproofing is irrelevant.

A small but not negligeable benefit is the lessened mobility restriction the Tactical gloves provide in comparison to Rabbitskin Mitts (+4%) and even Gauntlets (+2%). They are also 0.25kg lighter than either of those options.
However Tactical Gloves decay their condition slightly faster and repair less condition per action than Gauntlets and Rabbitskin Mitts.

> “**Durable jacket made from treated heavy canvas. Favoured by adventurous types who have to improvise.**”

The **Tactical Jacket** is a unique [Clothing](./Clothing.md) item, found only during the end of the [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) Tale, in a hidden room in [Bunker Omega](./Bunker%20Omega.md) in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md). It originally belonged to [The Foreman](./The%20Foreman.md).

Its warmth and windproofing are mediocre for a item of its weight and rarity. The real strength of this item is the protection it provides, which is the highest of nearly any other torso item, and by far the highest among cloth torso items. The only other torso clothing which that offers more protection is the [Moose-Hide Cloak](./Moose-Hide%20Cloak.md).

Because of its very high protection and durability, plus the ability to repair it with cloth which is substantially easier to gather than cured hides, this item is a great choice for players that get into struggles often and want to be protected with easily repairable clothes after the fact.

At the end of a long series of rope climbs into the upper reaches of Timberwolf Mountain is the Summit, on which rests the Tail Section--one of the larger plane sections scattered across the mountain in a recent crash. The Tail Section is shielded from the wind, so you can start a fire there, which is essential because it gets extremely cold at this altitude, particularly in the morning or when the wind is blowing hard. It contains a number of [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) that can supply you with nearly every kind of item found elsewhere in the game. The wooden crates scattered among the containers also may contain a rope and other loot. Emptying the containers results in well over 100kg of material so it takes quite a few days to loot it completely since the rappel up to the Summit drains around half your [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), and many rests are required.

There is a [corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) underneath the plane's floor that you can reach by walking towards the abyss (take care). It can be reached via outside the plane or by slowly climbing down from the interior of the plane. Normally, the corpse holds one [Military-Grade MRE](./Military-Grade%20MRE.md), and sometimes, some other random loot such as 1 [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md), [Flare Shell](./Flare%20Shell.md) or [Advanced Guns Guns Guns!](./Advanced%20Guns%20Guns%20Guns!.md). With careful maneuvering, the player can climb back up to the summit by walking to the right of the plane and back onto flat land. Otherwise, the player has only one way to leave: down. The way back is a bit treacherous and you might fall from >3 m (if you are not careful enough), so make sure you remove your clothes, as they might be damaged in the fall.

- Several [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) are scattered beneath the metal pieces inside, and a box of [Wood Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md) is located underneath a piece of metal in front of cargo container F

**_Tales from the Far Territory_** is [downloadable content](./The%20Long%20Dark.md#Downloadable_Addon_Content) for _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is the first expansion to the [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) portion of the game, being released in 6 parts starting from December 5, 2022 and fully concluding on December 2, 2024.

> “**Deep along the spine of Great Bear tracks a steep mountain range that bisects the island. This is the Far Range, an imposing wall of rock that stands vigilant over Great Bear's priceless resource riches. Over the decades, many have tried, few have succeeded to crack open the wealth within these rocks. And mysteries abound. Dark stories told around campfires, about abandoned mines and remote airfields that hold many secrets. Now, with the aurora blazing across the sky, is the Far Territory ready to surrender its stories? Will you survive long enough to wrest any truths from the rocky grasp of this old, dark territory?**”

_Tales from the Far Territory_ is a paid expansion pass for _The Long Dark_'s Survival Mode. It introduces new regions, wildlife, plants, improved mechanics, and system overhauls. The expansion also introduces [Tales](./Tales.md)—objective-based narratives quests similar to the storyline quests of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) and are played within a standard Survival game. There are three primary Tales following the story of Dr. Rüdiger and a fourth mini-Tale focusing on the Trader.

The expansion was delivered as a two-year campaign with major updates released on an average of every four months. These updates were cumulative and included free content for all players who owned _The Long Dark_ or _The Long Dark: Survival Mode Edition_.
Any content exclusive to the paid expansion is labeled as such below, and a full list can be found in :Category:DLC Content.

Purchasing the DLC also enables players to install [The Long Development](./The%20Long%20Development.md), an unofficial, fan-made pc mod which adds several regions to the eastern part of Great Bear Island.
- [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md): a weather phenomena that serves as a daytime version of the [Aurora](./Aurora.md)
- [Memento Notes](./Mementos.md): scraps of paper found under visors of vehicles and elsewhere, leading to hidden supply caches
### Paid Update
- [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) and [Supply Cache](./Supply%20Cache.md) Gameplay
- [Transmitters](./Transmitters.md) ([Replacement Fuse](./Replacement%20Fuse.md), [Wire Bundle](./Wires.md))
### Free Update
- [Acorns](./Acorns.md) and [Oak Trees](./Oak%20Tree.md), as well as introducing [Acorn Grounds](./Acorn%20Grounds.md) to make [Acorn Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Acorn%20Coffee.md)
### Miscellaneous Update
- [Weak Ice](./Weak%20Ice.md) now displays cracks when walked over as part of the updated Beachcombing mechanic
### Paid Update

- [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), a new passive wildlife bird which gathers in flocks near high ground. Acts as a source of [food](./Ptarmigan%20%28Raw%29.md) and its [feathers](./Ptarmigan%20Down.md) can be used to make tools
- [Gold Nugget](./Gold%20Nugget.md): an item already introduced in Wintermute Episode 4 but now added to Survival Mode.

- [Frontier Cooking Recipes](./Cooking.md#Frontier_Cooking_Recipes): A new cooking mechanic that combines ingredients and foods to create homecooked meals with helpful Affliction boosting/removing effects
- 24 cooking recipes (15 starting recipes and an additional 9 found on [Recipe Cards](./Recipe%20Cards.md) while exploring)
### Free Update
- [Burdock](./Burdock.md) plants. Can be dug up for their [Roots](./Burdock%20Root.md), then can be [prepared and eaten raw](./Prepared%20Burdock.md) or be made into [Burdock Tea](./Burdock%20Tea.md)

- [Free-Form Ice Fishing Holes](./Ice%20Fishing.md#Free-Form_Ice_Fishing_Holes): Allows you to create your own fishing locations in regions that have sufficiently deep bodies of water via the Survival Menu
- [Fishing Tip-Up](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md) - a tool for trapping fish passively like a [Snare](./Snare.md)
### Paid Update
- 1 new Region: [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) (previously named Industrial Mine)
- The Second [Tale](./Tales.md): [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md) and 1 unique [Badge](./Badges.md)
- [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md): a starved, desperate variant of Wolves living around the [toxic pools](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) in the Zone of Contamination
- [Respirator](./Respirator.md): a facemask that uses consumable air Canisters to avoid [Suffocation](./Suffocation.md) and Chemical Poisoning in toxic air environments
### Free Update
- [Insulated Flask](./Insulated%20Flask.md) (better known as a Thermos) for keeping soups, broth and drinks [Warm](./Warming%20Up.md)

- Equipped Clothing now properly appears on the hands and arms of Survivors (replacing the former default system where Survivor's hands were bare and the sleeves wore either [Mackenzie's Shirt](./Mackenzie%27s%20Shirt.md)/[Mackenzie's Sweater](./Mackenzie%27s%20Sweater.md) or [Astrid's Sweater](./Astrid%27s%20Sweater.md), no matter what Clothing was worn)
- Carcass Harvesting Overhaul: harvesting carcasses and meat quarters now shows the survivor harvesting the body by hand and visually involves the tool selected.
### Miscellaneous Update
- Carcasses now become weathered over time and possess 3 states of being (fresh, ravaged, frozen)
### Paid Update
- One new Region: [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) (formally named Mountain Pass)
- The Third and final main [Tale](./Tales.md): [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) and 1 unique [Badge](./Badges.md)
- [Cougar](./Cougar.md): a territorial big cat and Great Bear Island's "alpha predator" which stalks regions the survivor inhabits for too long.
- New Affliction: [Severe Lacerations](./Severe%20Lacerations.md); acquired from a Cougar [Struggle](./Struggle.md)
### Free Update

- [Misery](./Misery.md) - a new Experience mode even harder than [Interloper](./Interloper.md), complete with 6 new Afflictions that gradually appear over time and make the survivor's experience permanently harder

- [Cheat Death](./Cheat%20Death.md) System - the first ever change to permadeath in Survival Mode that allows a survivor to have "3 extra lives" to cheat death, but this will also make the game harder with each death
### Miscellaneous Update
- _Tales from the Far Territory_ officially released for Nintendo Switch (Parts 1-5) (August 1st, 2024)
- Added an option to make Cougars and [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) optional content when starting a Survival Mode Experience (except Misery)
- Removed Cougar shortly after launch due to negative player feedback so that it could be reworked
### Paid Update
- "[Cougar 2.0](./Cougar.md)" Redux - returned the big cat after being removed from Part 5, now completely revamped and deadlier than ever.
- [Camera](./Camera.md) - an in game camera system for players to take their own photos. Includes 3 different colour filters:
- Added a Photo Album tab to the Journal [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) that allows you to view and annotate your taken photographs.
- [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md) - A fourth tale featuring the Trader's story.
- [Trader](./Trader.md) - A mysterious man named Sutherland that sells goods and info over the radio to the player, but for a price.
- Added a Trading tab to the Journal [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) to keep track of active trades.

- [Meat Curing Box](./Meat%20Curing%20Box.md) and [Salt Deposits](./Salt%20Deposit.md) - Mine new salt deposits along the coastline and create a special box to preserve your animal meat for long periods of time
### Free Update

- [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) - customize almost any interior with the ability to move, rearrange, destroy, or craft furniture and containers to let survivors create their perfect safe house

- Includes over 800 items that can be moved, broken down, and in some cases, built using this system. There are over 120 interior scenes that can be turned into Safehouses, along with several specific "exterior interiors" like the Mountaineer's Hut in Timberwolf Mountain, and the Lookout Towers.
- Added a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) tab to the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) to categorize the new Safe House items
- Global Wildlife Refresh: an overhaul of wildlife spawn points and patrol paths to remove some of the predictability from their behavior

- Establish new patterns for hunting and travel through the world to avoid, or seek out, wildlife. Every wildlife spawn region in the game has been refreshed. Expect to encounter predators like Bears, Wolves, and now Cougars, in new and dangerous places. Find prey animals like Deer, Rabbits, and Ptarmigan have made homes in new locations. Wildlife populations have been rebalanced across the entire game world. Even Timberwolf spawns have been refreshed, so that they don’t always appear where they used to.
### Miscellaneous Update
- Added 19 new [Achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) related to the _Tales from the Far Territory_, being a mix of free and paid achievements.
- The game no longer has 25 save slots. Saving is now measured in percentage of space on save files.
- Train box cars and Car/Truck engines received new models. [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) now has paint on the walls upstairs.
- The Big Cat Killer Feat was discontinued with the new Cougar version, and is now a legacy Feat.

With the progress of Episode 4 and writing for episode 5 coming to a close, Raphael van Lierop posted the Dev Diary on March 18, 2021 talking about the future of _The Long Dark_ and linking to a survey asking a series of questions, including if players would be willing to pay for DLC.[^1] The results of the survey showed a favourable view towards paid content and development began with a dedicated team. [^2] To streamline the process of adding updates, the game was planned to be split into two editions, _Survival Edition_ and _Wintermute_.[^3]

The name for the expansion pass was revealed as _Tales from the Far Territory_ on October 20, 2022 in the Dev Diary, also announcing free and paid contents, save compatibility issues and the subsequent save wipes, with a general release date for December 2022 and Xbox, PlayStation and Switch planned for early 2023.[^4]

Raphael von Lierop also announced stepping down as lead developer of _The Long Dark_, handing the reigns to Katie Sorrell as Project Lead, who would continue the work on _Wintermute_ and _Tales from the Far Territory_, officially taking over as the voice for _The Long Dark_ on Hinterland's official YouTube channel on March 30, 2023 in the "Tales from the Far Territory Part Two Update Video".[^5][^6]

Raphael von Lierop also announced stepping down as lead developer of _The Long Dark_, handing the reigns to Katie Sorrell as Project Lead, who would continue the work on _Wintermute_ and _Tales from the Far Territory_, officially taking over as the voice for _The Long Dark_ on Hinterland's official YouTube channel on March 30, 2023 in the "Tales from the Far Territory Part Two Update Video".[^5][^6]
_Tales_ was officially released on December 5, 2022 on Steam and Epic store for Windows. Technical issues arose for Mac and its release date was delayed from December 5, 2022 to February 15, 2023.

PlayStation and Xbox was announced for March 15, 2023[^7] but was delayed and officially released on March 30, 2023 with Updates One and Two simultaneously. Update Two for PC was also released on March 30, 2023.

The Switch was initially announced for March 2023 but was delayed, with Parts One to Four later being released together on August 1, 2024[^8]. Parts Five to Six was later released on March 10, 2025[^9]

_Tales_ was initially disabled for Interloper in order to maintain gameplay balance and the belief it would be too difficult and offer little reward for players, but after receiving heavy criticism, Raphael announced its future inclusion in the Dev Diary on April 14, 2023[^10] with it being officially enabled on April 20, 2023.[^11] _Signal Void_ for Interloper mode was in turn modified to include less loot for bunkers and appropriate loot for the Trackable Hidden Caches.

The Cougar was met with heavy criticism at Part Four's launch, with many players expressing their disappointment with how it was implemented. This included how it did not act as a typical wildlife in the game and rather than roam and interact with the world and player, its appearance was limited to the moment it attacked the player after a timer countdown. The Cougar was promptly removed from the game to be reworked and then rereleased later for Part Six on December 2, 2024 to a relatively more favourable reception.
- The promotional image used for the _Tales From the Far Territory_ is actually concept art for the [Final Approach](./Final%20Approach.md) helicopter crash site.
- The [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) was formerly teased as the _Industrial Mine_, but was renamed during its debut.
- [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) was formerly teased as _Mountain Pass_, but was renamed during its debut.
- Base Customization was originally exclusive to this DLC before it was made available for all players as part of free update.

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

**Tales** are narrative-based objectives in the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) DLC for [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). They are not to be confused with the short, self-contained [Challenge](./Challenge.md) scenarios that can be selected in the Survival menu. Triggering a Tale within Survival Mode will cause a new submenu in the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md) to appear (flag shaped tab). Similar to the mission objectives menu in [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), this menu keeps track of all current tasks related to a Tale. During the Course of the update, a total of 3 Tales were added to the game. A bonus 4th Tale was added in Part 6, but has its own method to track objectives. As of update V2.27, all Tales become active and can be completed out of order once the [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) is acquired in a playthrough, as long that Tale has been previously completed on another playthrough and its associated Badge is acquired. This requires each Tale to be completed in the original order at least once first, with the exception of [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md), which does not require the Handheld Shortwave Radio to be acquired, and can be started as soon as sufficient Trust is earned with [Sutherland](./Trader.md).

Repair [Transmitters](./Transmitters.md) and use your newly acquired [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md) in order to track down mysterious radio transmissions and buried supply caches across Great Bear Island, and possibly uncover something more sinister along the way.
Continue investigating the mysterious events surrounding Dr. Rüdiger and his mysterious project in the abandoned Langston Mine complex in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md).
Dr. Rüdiger escaped from the Langston Mine, track down where he could have gone in the nearby [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md).
A radio crackles to life one night and a mysterious voice fills the air. This is the first time you've heard another living soul since your plane crashed. Who could he be?
- Completing a Tale will unlock a unique [Badge](./Badges.md) per Tale. Completing all 3 Tales will unlock 2 unique [Feats](./Feats.md).
- [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) was released on March 30th, 2023, alongside Part Two of the expansion pass.
- [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md) was released on Dec 5th, 2023, alongside Part Four of the expansion pass.
- [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) was released on June 24th, 2024, alongside Part Five of the expansion pass.
- [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md) was released on December 2nd, 2024, alongside Part Six of the expansion pass.

**Tall Rustic Closet** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.
A makeshift wooden closet, a Tall Rustic Closet can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The closet can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor or a flat surface when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value, the closet cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the closet will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).

This mission can be started by finding any of the Local Legends books, including _The Big One_, _The Lost Cave_, _Ghost Stag_, and _Sasquatch_. When any one of these books is picked up, the journal will update to include a new task, and the legend to investigate will be marked on the map. Each legend the player investigates will reward the player with an item or crafting blueprint.
- [Local Legends - Sasquatch](./Local%20Legends%20-%20Sasquatch.md) can be found in the bathroom of [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md).
- [Local Legends - The Big One](./Local%20Legends%20-%20The%20Big%20One.md) can be found in the second bunker of [Joplin's Bunker Raid](./Joplin%27s%20Bunker%20Raid.md).

- _The Big One_ mission rewards the player with a large 15kg fish ([Big Bass (Raw)](./Big%20Bass%20%28Raw%29.md)), which may be useful for the [Coming Storm](./Coming%20Storm.md) mission. The fish is 3750 calories raw, or 4313 calories when cooked, because Astrid has lvl 2 cooking earning extra 15% calories (plus 0.37L of [Lamp Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md)) .

- The _Ghost Stag_ mission rewards the player with the [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md) and [Deerskin Pants](./Deerskin%20Pants.md) crafting blueprints. A pair of [Rabbitskin Mitts](./Rabbitskin%20Mitts.md) is also next to the snow shelter.

When collected it provides a permanent +5kg (11lbs) increase to [Carry Capacity](./Encumbrance.md). This benefit stacks the effects of a worn [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) and [Well Fed](./Well%20Fed.md) benefit, allowing the player to carry up to 45kg (99lbs) without becoming encumbered, a total increase of 50%. The Technical Backpack is unique to the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md) of the [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) region. The trek to the mine is long and the region near-wilderness, making its low temperatures (-25°C (-13°F)), predators, and maze-like geography dangerous.

This is shown explicitly in official artwork of [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) for [Wintermute: Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md). However, these containers cannot be picked up, and acquiring the technical backpack does not produce the player's old backpack.

Additionally, the icon for the backpack will change to one resembling the in game picture for the technical backpack, and the inventory will be renamed from Backpack to Technical Backpack.

**Technical Balaclava** is a type of clothing in The Long Dark. It is part of the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ DLC.
Only 1 Technical Balaclava can be worn at a time, specifically in the inner head slot. It is a direct upgrade to the [Balaclava](./Balaclava.md) in terms of clothing stats.

That means it only provides Windproof bonus if no other hat is worn in the outer hat slot; this usually means it's Windproof bonus over other headwear like the [Wool Toque](./Wool%20Toque.md) or [Rabbitskin Hat](./Rabbitskin%20Hat.md) is wasted. The Technical Balaclava weighs 0.05kg less than a regular Balaclava or Wool Toque and decays much slower, retaining it's stats for longer and costing less [Cloth](./Cloth.md) to repair over time.

Unlike the Balaclava, the Technical Balaclava is available on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) inside Bunker Omega; it will not spawn inside any Transponder Caches on Interloper. This makes it unique and irreplaceable if destroyed.

Terry is first heard on a radio broadcast as [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) attempts to contact Perseverance Mills when [Jeremiah's](./Jeremiah.md) shortwave radio is powered by the [Aurora](./Aurora.md), in order to locate [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md). He intercepts a distress call from the Mills, with a man on the radio mentioning needing help and a quarantine. Before Mackenzie can ask what the problem is or if Astrid is at the Mills, the shortwave radio shorts out and contact is lost.

violations.message: Strong style: expected asterisk, found underscore

> “__...[static]... Come in... We need...help... There's some kind of...quarantine...situation.

The same radio broadcast from Episode 2 is played again at [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md), this time from Astrid Greenwood's perspective. The broadcast is mostly the same, but with slightly more dialogue.
> “**Ok. So about 10 days ago, Doc Larsen asked me to start broadcasting a quarantine message.**”

Terry first appears outside of his shack when Astrid climbs the road to ask him about a distress call he heard the other night. Terry comes out, smoking a blunt and confusing Astrid for someone coming to take several [Car Batteries](./Car%20Battery.md) back from him that he is not finished with. Terry eventually invites Astrid inside and explains that he intercepted a distress call from before the lights went out in [Desperation Bay](./Desperation%20Bay.md).

Terry appears at the end of the mission, excitedly leading in [Mathis](./Mathis.md) into the bar (mistakenly believing him to be a rescuer that has answered his distress call). Terry is then shoved out of the way, as Mathis smiles and begins taking over the town.
Terry is then taken prisoner inside Cooper's Blind along with the other residents of the town after this point.
Terry is last seen in the bunker under the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md), residing with the other survivors of Perseverance Mills after having escaped the town.

**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**

**The Basics of Survival** is a side mission started in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In the mission, the survivor must snare a rabbit, harvest and prepare some natural remedies, and mend some clothing. The mission can be completed in either [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) or [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md); if the research book used to trigger the first mission is not collected in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), it will need to be found in in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) to start the quest.
A sequel, [Survival School](./Survival%20School.md), is a side mission available starting in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the story.
> “**Enduring the Quiet Apocalypse will require survival skills. Find the collectibles that can teach you important survival lessons.**”
To start the mission, the survivor has to find one of the corresponding research books scattered around [Milton](./Milton.md):

![A Sewing Primer icon](../assets/A_Sewing_Primer_icon.png) This mission objective can be started after finding the [Collectible](./Collectibles.md) [A Sewing Primer](./A%20Sewing%20Primer.md), which is located on the second floor of [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) where [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) is located.

A [Sewing Kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md) and [Cloth](./Cloth.md) are required to complete this objective, as well as a piece of damaged [clothing](./Clothing.md). All three can be found by scavenging houses within the town of [Milton](./Milton.md).

![Medicinal Plants of Great Bear icon](../assets/Medicinal_Plants_of_Great_Bear_icon.png) This mission objective can be started after finding the [collectible](./Collectibles.md) [Medicinal Plants of Great Bear](./Medicinal%20Plants%20of%20Great%20Bear.md), which is located in the [Milton Post Office](./Milton%20Post%20Office.md) within the town of [Milton](./Milton.md). To complete the objective, the Mackenzie must prepare the following medicine:

To complete this objective, all natural medicine must be contained within the survivor's inventory at the same time; if the survivor consumes or drops any of the natural medicine that they have prepared, they will have to reacquire it before the objective is completed.[^1]
[Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) can be found located in the [Wood Lot](./Wood%20Lot.md) between [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md) and the town of Milton

A total of 6 [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) are required to craft 3 [Prepared Reishi Mushrooms](./Prepared%20Reishi%20Mushrooms.md). The prepared mushrooms can be brewed into [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md) along with 0.75 liters of [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) at a [fire](./Fire.md).
[Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) can be found located near the pond at the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md) behind Grey Mother's House.

A total of 9 [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) are required to craft 3 [Old Man's Beard Wound Dressings](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Wound%20Dressing.md). The dressings can be directly crafted by the survivor without the use of a fire.
[Rose hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) can be found located near the pond at the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md) behind Grey Mother's House.

A total of 72 [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) are required to craft 3 [Prepared Rose hips](./Prepared%20Rose%20Hips.md). The prepared rose hips can be brewed into [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md) along with 0.75 liters of [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) at a [fire](./Fire.md).

![Field Dressing Your Kill, Vol. I icon](../assets/Field_Dressing_Your_Kill%2C_Vol._I_icon.png) This mission objective can be started after finding the [collectible](./Collectibles.md) [Field Dressing Your Kill, Vol. I](./Field%20Dressing%20Your%20Kill%2C%20Vol.%20I.md), which is located at the [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) in the shed outside [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md). A [snare](./Snare.md) is also on the work bench near the book, and can be used by the survivor to complete the mission objective. Alternatively, it can be found in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) on the first floor of the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) in the [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) region.

There are [rabbits](./Rabbit.md) located around the [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) area for the survivor to snare; alternatively, there are rabbits located near the pond at the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md) behind Grey Mother's House.

It is not necessary to go and harvest the Snare, as the mission will complete[^2] the moment a Snare checks for a rabbit catch and succeeds (more on [Snare Mechanics](./Snare.md#Snare_Mechanics) here).

## Retrieve the [legendary spear](./Broken%20Bear%20Spear.md) from the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md).

_Mackenzie leaves the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) and heads south, entering [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md). He passes through the region without any eventful encounters, aside from a scripted Wolf feeding on a Deer Carcass in the middle of the tracks. He passes through the region into [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md), and navigates around a [Landslide](./Landslide.md), before passing a [Locomotive Engine](./Locomotive%20Engine.md) and walks up a [Train Shuttle](./Train%20Shuttle.md) blocking his way forward, then walks into a broken window. Entering the vehicle, he walks to the grated door and the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) appears around a tree. It spots Mackenzie, and walks up to the grated door as the pilot slowly backs away from it._

_The Old Bear sniffs the air and stands on its hind legs, roaring and pressing its entire body through its front legs onto the door. It then pushes the Shuttle over, causing its sole occupant to tumble with it and get knocked out._
_**Note** that if the game is currently day, it will turn to night time when Mackenzie wakes up for the next scene._
_Mackenzie wakes up outside of the Shuttle with much time having passed, and immediately stares at the sky._
_The sky is filled with the [Aurora](./Aurora.md), and a nearby lamppost is functioning, bathing the pilot in a white artificial light. Mackenzie steps forward and sees an active campfire_
_He walks to it and recognizes the familiar man sitting beside it (minus his walking stick), and warms himself by the fire. The hum of the Aurora filling the air._
Methuselah: "The war between man and nature, of course. The lights in the sky. You and the bear. The cold. Hunger. The old fights, returning."
Methuselah: "There was no bear when I found you. Perhaps it isn't yet time for your paths to cross?"

Methuselah: "And everything dependent on it. Animating it. Or destroying it. Perhaps both."
Mackenzie: "I've had a lot of trouble with wildlife lately. Is it always this dangerous around here?"
Methuselah: "I've seen many strange things, of course. But the birds and beasts? Their rhythms are their own."
Methuselah: "The patterns of nature have been interrupted. Broken. Even those who once knew how to read them are now confused."

_After warming himself by the fire and finishing his conversation with the strange old man, Mackenzie turns his attention to a powered truck and more powered lights, heading down the path to a large [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md). Several glowing Wolves who become unusually aggressive block his path in the yard, and Mackenzie evades or kills them. The front and back door of the Maintenance Shed is locked, but an office building is open, with the message "THEY HATE THE LIGHT" written above the bed, illumined by an artificial light. Entering the Shed, the overhead lights hum with electricity and several wires burn and smoke on the floors, with Mackenzie avoiding them. A dead [Forest Talker](./Forest%20Talkers.md) lies a room close to the bathroom, with a message ([Forest Talker Flyer](./Forest%20Talker%20Flyer.md)) directing fellow activists to the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md)._

_The Lodge appears messy, with many food supplies scattered and left behind by the Forest Talkers. If Mackenzie enters the basement then he will find a [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md), but will also hear a ringing phone coming from upstairs. Mackenzie picks up the Flashlight, causing a cutscene to occur as he slowly looks it over, cracked lens and all. Returning upstairs as the phone continues to ring and opening the [Phone Box](./Phone%20Box.md), the ringing stops before he can answer the caller._

_By this point, dawn breaks and the lights in the sky begin to fade. Cars and lightbulbs go out, along with the Flashlight's battery. Mackenzie eventually finds the Bear Spear, placed on a mantle above a Fireplace in the kitchen. He takes it into his hands, and notices the shattered spearhead._

Mackenzie: "Damn...looks like one little detail got missed in the trapper's "legend" of the old bear: The spear didn't survive the fight. Must be something I can use to fix it at the old machine shed."
## Repair the broken spear at the [forge](./Forge.md).

_Mackenzie then travels back to the Maintenance Shed, [Broken Bear Spear](./Broken%20Bear%20Spear.md) in tow, and manages finds several pieces of [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), a [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md), and enough wood to forge a new [Spear Head](./Spear%20Head.md). Mackenzie then lights the [Furnace](./Furnace.md)._
_The screen fades to black, then fades back in with the Furnace hot enough to begin forging._

_Mackenzie then interacts with the Forge. After the player selects the Spear Head and 1.5 hours pass, Mackenzie crafts a Spear Head with materials on hand and inserts it into the Broken Bear Spear offscreen._
_Mackenzie holds up the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md), showing off its restored glory, then puts it away._

_Mackenzie then leaves the Maintenance Shed, choosing to craft a set of improvised tools or to just leave. He passes by the spot that Methuselah was the night before, but he is long gone by now and the campfire burned out. The return trip to [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) is uneventful, as Mackenzie passes through Broken Railroad and the Muskeg with no trouble, until he reaches the transition to Mystery Lake and spots the Old Bear in the nearby mountain._
_The bear growls, then lowers its ears in fear, as if sensing the danger of the Bear Spear._

Mackenzie: "Yeah...the bear is definitely tracking me. You have any luck with the radio?"

Jeremiah: "I did! Did you see the lights in the night sky, the aurora? Well, when that flared up, the radio came to life. It just lit up, and started spitting out noise, but it was all gibberish. Bits and pieces of things...music...talking. I think it needs more range...a more powerful signal. Jeremiah: "Focus, Mackenzie. This survey shows a series of radio transponder towers that cross back and forth across Great Bear."
Jeremiah: "Each tower has some electronics that'd serve like a signal booster, to make sure the message gets to the next relay."

**Region:** [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28disambiguation%29.md) [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md)
**Characters:** [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md)
**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**
> “**A man-killing bear is on the prowl, risking Mackenzie's mission to find Astrid. But an old Voyageur legend might hold the answer to overcoming the massive predator.**”

**The Best Defense** is the second mission in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [story](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) must obtain the hunting spear mentioned in a legend about the demon bear, repair it, and return to Jeremiah.
| Significant locations | [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) / [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) |
The mission starts at the Trapper's Homestead. Jeremiah tells Mackenzie that he must retrieve the bear spear from the Hunting Lodge because it may be the key to killing the Demon Bear.

Head to the train tracks and go to the right through the [Rail Tunnel](./Rail%20Tunnel.md). The player will end up in the [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) region. Follow the tracks to the other end of the region and enter into the [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) region. Before leaving the [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) region, near the entrance to the [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) region, look for a corpse leaning against the logs of a crashed log wagon of the log train. Here you will find a note that will lead you to the Ravine Cache in the [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) region. Continue following the tracks until reaching the [Landslide](./Landslide.md). It is possible to scale the landslide and continue following the tracks on the other side. Otherwise, go down the hill to the right to the small pond and use the fallen tree as a bridge. Following the tracks, the player will pass the [Locomotive Engine](./Locomotive%20Engine.md) and eventually reach a crashed crew speeder. The player can enter the vehicle through the window. Upon attempting to exit the vehicle on the other side, a cutscene will begin and the Demon Bear will appear. The Demon Bear will knock over the speeder, knocking Mackenzie unconscious. When Mackenzie comes to, the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) will be in the sky and the player will be freezing. Following the tracks, the player will come across Methuselah and a campfire that can be used for warming up. Before you go down the path to the Maintenance Yard, you can make a small detour. Follow further the railway tracks until you find a pickup truck next to a yellow train/engine near the collapsed bridge. Inside the truck you will find a note that leads you to the Tree Root Cache. On the back of the pickup you can also find a well-filled [Jerry Can](./Jerry%20Can.md).

Follow the path to the Maintenance Yard. A small annex on the building contains some office space and a bed. On the bench near the door is a Forest Talker note which unlocks the [Lake Gunshots](./Lake%20Gunshots.md) side mission. Inside the main building of the maintenance yard, be careful to avoid walking through the arcing wires, as they will cause [burns](./Burns.md). Leave the Maintenance Yard Building and continue walking in the direction away from the train tracks. There is a hole in the chain-link fence, which leads down a path with streetlights lit by the aurora. Upon reaching a small lake, continue to the right along the bank. The player will come across a gate, which can be opened. Follow the path until reaching the Hunting Lodge.

A copy of _Field Dressing Your Kill, Vol 1._ can be found on the shelving to the right immediately after entering the Hunting Lodge if the book was not found during Episode 1. Picking up the book will unlock part of [The Basics of Survival](./The%20Basics%20of%20Survival.md) side mission. A note on the work bench in the basement will unlock the location of a [Forest Talker supply cache](./Forest%20Talker%20Supply%20Caches.md) in Broken Railroad. Pick up the broken spear off of the mantle.

The player must then make their way back to the Maintenance Yard to repair the spear at the forge. The metal hammer required for forging is on the shelf to the right of the forge. Scrap metal can be found in the tub near the forge, or in various places around the maintenance yard building. After successfully starting a fire in the furnace, the furnace will jump to 170°C and will burn for an "infinite" amount of time. At this point, the player can select the forge and repair the bear spear. Doing so will also unlock building the improvised knife and improvised hatchet.

After repairing the spear, return to the railroad, and follow the tracks back through Forlorn Muskeg to Mystery Lake. Then return to the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md). Entering the Homestead will start a cutscene and end the mission.

- It is possible to return through the cave system back to [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), but the climbing rope leading to [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md) is still snapped. [Milton Basin](./Milton%20Basin.md) cannot be accessed in the Muskeg as the path is blocked by a mountain, so it is impossible to return to [Milton](./Milton.md).
