**The Collapse** refers to the economic collapse of the Canadian - and wider North American - economy "in the mid-20XX." As a result of The Collapse, [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) was initially cut-off from the mainland and residents were forced to become self-sufficient. Later, supplies were brought from the mainland, and islanders were split between those who welcomed the supplies and those who supported continued self-sufficiency.

[Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) refers to the collapse that started "years ago," and states that [Milton](./Milton.md) needed help "ten years ago. During the collapse." A note by the front door of the [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md) states that it was forced to close due to "economic realities" in September 2012.
The Collapse is detailed in four worldbuilding journal entries entitled _Knowledge: History of the Collapse_. ([History of The Collapse](./History%20of%20The%20Collapse.md))

> “**In the mid-20XX, the ongoing global economic crisis, fueled by continued political instability in the US and Europe, contributing to increasing volatility in the financial markets, led to the sudden catastrophic collapse of the Canadian, and in general, the North American banking system. This immediately rendered [Canadian currency](./Cash.md) worthless, triggered super-inflation of the US dollar, and all trade and economic activity promptly shifted to the Chinese Yuan or crypto-currencies (a la Bitcoin). Crippled economically, Canada was bought under the financial oversight of the North American Economic Zone, which positioned Canada as a kind of protectorate of a larger US-based economic bloc. From this point onward, the majority of economic activity became centralized on Canada's already densely urbanized population, with smaller rural and remote communities being essentially cut off. Without a local economic lifeline many of these communities had become dependent on for their continued existence, most rural or remote communities became hollowed out, as people fled to urban areas in search of greater economic stability.**”

> “**For places like [Great Bear](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), already quite remote and suffering after decades of economic decline, the sudden Collapse was the final straw. Without any major local economic drivers of their own, the remaining communities of Great Bear became completely dependent on a supply lifeline from the Mainland -- regular shipments of basic staples designed to keep them alive: fuel, food, medical supplies, etc., in many ways, akin to WW2-era wartime rationing. In exchange for regular supply drops, the “Mainlanders” -- in some cases, at the behest of their economic overlords South of the border -- felt justified in taking whatever supplies and raw materials they needed to maintain the urban communities, including dismantling some of the heavy industrial infrastructure left on Great Bear.**”

> “**Unhappy with their growing dependence on the Mainland for economic support, as well as the Mainlander's continued view that Great Bear exists solely as a resource clearinghouse for their benefit, some people who chose to remain on Great Bear decided to engage their self-sufficiency. Small-scale local food production efforts, akin to the Victory Garden program of WW2 England and Canada, sprouted up all over Great Bear, with individuals and even communities taking it in their own hands to produce food and power resources. Some of these activities took on an aspect of being politically or even ideologically motivated -- these weren't just gardens or small-scale attempts to provide for local needs. These were acts of rebellion against a (perceived?) occupying economic force.**”

> “**Cut off from the Mainland -- economically and figuratively -- Great Bear Islanders became increasingly segregated into two pseudo-political entities along indeological lines: those who gratefully embraced dependence on the Mainland and viewed the regular supply ships as a charitable gesture in apology for the Mainland's exploitation of Great Bear's resource riches, and those who sought ultimate independence and who considered trade and travel between the Mainland to be a necessary evil, viewing Mainlanders with a degree of mistrust. Those in support of the Mainlanders even considered the small-scale “Victory Garden” type activities as a sign of lacking patriotism, a concept that hadn't really existed as such in the Canadian mindset, pre-Collapse.**”

From conversations between [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) and [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md), **The Collapse** may also refer to literal seismic activity that took place on Great Bear and the mainland, but this is not canon.

The [Milton Water Tower](./Milton%20Water%20Tower.md) and water mains were shut off in June 2012 due to seismic activity. Furthermore, [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) contains a lockbox with an _[Emergency Kit](./Emergency%20Kit%20Note.md)_ distributed by the Great Bear Earthquake Memorial Society. Additionally, seismic activity contributed to [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md)'s decision to stop people using the area for climbing, and the failed attempt to re-open [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md).[^1]

- The Collapse may be based off of the real-world economic turmoil of the 2000s, including the Great Recession of 2008 due to the Housing Market Collapse. However, the in-game economic crisis had become much worse than reality, possibly even turning from a recession into a depression.

This is the mission transcript for mission 2 [The Crash](./The%20Crash.md) of [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md).

_The mission begins right where it did in [Memories](./Memories.md), with Mackenzie grunting in pain and gasping for air as he slowly blinks back into consciousness at the crash site. The ambient electrical wail of an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) plays overhead as the camera shifts to reveal trees, fire, smoke, and wreckage of a crashed plane. Mackenzie gets up and cries out:_

_The man gets up, and notices a piece of metal lodged in his left hand, hesitating before deciding to pull it out. The process is slow, and is not without consequence, as the man's cries of pain ring out during the pulling. After the [Scrap Metal Shard](./Scrap%20Metal%20Shard.md) is pulled out, the man shouts to the hills around him._
_The man looks at the gaping wound in his hand before the camera shifts and slowly zooms out as if to give control to the player, but instead the camera turns to show the wrecked plane above._

_Mackenzie uses a [Bandage](./Bandage.md) to stop the bleeding from his hand, then begins to hobble with a [Sprained Ankle](./Sprained%20Ankle.md). Fire and debris scour a ravine that the pilot finds himself in, with various crates from the plane able to be broken down for supplies._
_If the player attempts to walk up the fallen tree bridge to use the [Rock Climb](./Rock%20Climb.md) out of the gorge, the camera will stop to show the climb and Mackenzie will say:_

_Mackenzie makes his way back down the tree bridge and into a nearby cave. A bed is inside, but attempting to sleep gives the message BANDAGE WOUND AND WARM THE CAVE UP FIRST. It is too cold to rest up so he makes a fire._
_Mackenzie falls asleep for the night. Morning breaks and the stranded pilot wakes up in the cave with the campfire having burned out by now and his Sprained Ankle healed._
Mackenzie: "Astrid hasn't come looking for me, which means she can't come looking for me...because she's she's hurt...or worse. I'd better get back up to the crash site."

_The various fires from the night before have all but died down, with only vapors of smoke rising from the wreckage. Mackenzie then makes his way back up the tree bridge and climbs his way out of the ravine. The wound on his hand is properly bandaged when climbing out. After climbing the second Rock Climb:_
Mackenzie: "My plane...not sure which of us looks worse. Poor girl, this isn't how things were supposed to end."
_If the player tries to leave the crash site via the wing serving as a ramp, Mackenzie will hit an invisible wall and say:_
_Walking further under the wreckage, Will finds [Astrid's Backpack](./Astrid%27s%20Backpack.md) and [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md)._
Mackenzie: "Hmm...locked. Whatever's in this case, Astrid was willing to die for it. I hope she hasn't already died for it."

_Mackenzie then pilfers whatever is left of the crash site before using a piece of his plane's wing as a ramp to leave the area, before noticing something caught on a tree branch fluttering in the wind. A piece of Astrid's scarf._
_Mackenzie then travels to a nearby pond filled with Rabbits, before finding a burned out Campfire._

**Memories** is the second mission in [Episode One](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), where [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) must survive through the night after his plane crashes and search for signs of [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md).
> “**Mackenzie fights to stay alive while searching for signs of Astrid. What happened to her?**”

After waking up in the ravine, the player must stop the blood loss using the bandage in the inventory. The bandage can be applied by activating the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md), navigating to the [first aid](./First%20Aid.md) tab, and then using the bandage on the blood loss [affliction](./Afflictions.md). If the blood loss is not stopped, the player will continue to lose condition.
### Survive the night

The player should then make their way to the cave, collecting some of the materials strewn about on the way. Spending too much time outside will cause the player to become freezing and lose [Condition](./Condition.md). Breaking down items, such as breaking branches into [Sticks](./Stick.md), is a **time accelerated activity**, meaning that time will pass rapidly and therefore the player's Condition may drain quicker.
Once in the cave, the player must start a [Campfire](./Campfire.md). This can be done by activating the radial menu again, navigating to the campcraft tab, and selecting the [fire](./Fire.md) option.

Once a Campfire has been successfully started, the player can select the moss on the cave floor to sleep on. The player has no control over the amount of time slept and the amount of fuel available at the crash site is very limited, so the Campfire is practically guaranteed to go out while sleeping, meaning some Condition loss will unavoidably occur. Drinking a [Cup of Herbal Tea](./Cup%20of%20Herbal%20Tea.md) just before leaving in [Memories](./Memories.md) provides [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md) and [Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md); the former helps slow down heat loss, and the latter can help restore Condition when sleeping while the Campfire is still keeping the player warm.

![Plane](../assets/Plane.jpg) The next morning, the player can leave the ravine by walking up the fallen tree and then climbing the vines. At the top, the player will pass [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md). Underneath the plane is [Mackenzie's Parka](./Mackenzie%27s%20Parka.md), a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), [Astrid's Backpack](./Astrid%27s%20Backpack.md), and [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md). Further along the cliff, the extra supplies chosen by the player in [the previous mission](./Memories.md) can be found on the ground. The player then makes their way past the [Radio Tower](./Radio%20Tower.md).

Mackenzie will notice the [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) with smoke rising from the chimney. Approaching the house, there is a shed with a dead prisoner. A [hatchet](./Hatchet.md) may be on top of the toolbox. Entering the house will start the [next mission](./The%20Grey%20Mother.md).

**The Detonators** is the fourth mission in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) offers to help [Mathis](./Mathis.md) find [Detonators](./Detonators.md) in the old mine, in order to hopefully appease Mathis sufficiently that he avoids killing [Franklin](./Franklin.md).
| Mission details — Start location | Mission details — Blackrock Federal Penitentiary |
| Items recommended | [rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [revolver](./Revolver.md), [noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md), [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md), [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) |

The mission starts back at Blackrock Prison. Gather all the supplies left behind in the guardroom and head down the road. From there, take the first left and follow the signs leading to the mine. Along the way, there are good opportunities to do some of the side quests, such as [Blackrock Rumours](./Blackrock%20Rumours.md) at [Bricklayer's Retreat](./Bricklayer%27s%20Retreat.md) and [No Road Cave](./No%20Road%20Cave.md), and searching for the various supply caches in [Convict Caches](./Convict%20Caches.md).
After walking a considerable distance, the player will arrive at [Mule Bridge](./Mule%20Bridge.md). Be careful not to fall off while crossing, as this will be fatal. Once across, enter the mine.
Inside the mine, pick up the elevator crank, and keep to the right (crawling under some low overhangs) to come to the mine's elevator. Use the crank to descend to Level 3.

Once on Level 3, there will be large pockets of unbreathable air. Get the first handle and install it on the air valve to create a safe space. Once there, sprint down the tunnel to the next safe space. Wait for [stamina](./Stamina.md) to come back, then sprint to the corpse next to an air valve handle (another safe space). Repeat the process of sprinting between safe spaces as much as needed. Use [an energy drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) if needed. The corpse will have the [Mine Gate Key](./Mine%20Gate%20Key.md) needed to unlock a wooden door.

When back at the second air valve from the entrance, install the handle and turn it on. Now take the handle from the air valve nearest the entrance and remove it (you need to turn off the air first). Go back to the second air valve, then open the door and sprint to the next air valve. Open this valve to create a safe space. When stamina comes back, head for the elevator and go up to get out of the dangerous gas.

Once up to Level 2, get the Detonators by climbing onto some wooden planks laid over a deep hole. Also pick up the [Bolt Cutters](./Bolt%20Cutters.md) to cut the chain on the gate. Head back to the elevator and go up to Level 1, using the bolt cutters to cut the chain on the second gate. Shortly before leaving [Jace](./Jace.md) will call. Tell her what you're doing, and Jace will mention that she's going to use "the nuclear option" to prevent Donner from escaping. When attempting to escape the mine, the character will be knocked unconscious by falling rocks.

When the character re-awakens, the path to the old entrance is blocked and the [aurora](./Aurora.md) is active. Head up the wooden planks to another entrance, being careful not to step on live wires. From here, it's possible to sleep in the mine entrance and make the walk back to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) in the morning, or to proceed at night. The route back to Blackrock requires three rope climbs, and so is best done when well rested.

Shortly before the prison, Mackenzie will make a comment when he sees several corpses lying on the ice of the river. These corpses are just decorative and can't be looted. Once in the yard, it may be wise to leave a [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) in the entrance to the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md), though this is not necessary. The mission is complete when Mackenzie arrives at the prison door.

**The Foreman** is a major character in the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) storyline.
**Stub:****This article is a stub. You can help by [//dummy.host/index.php?title=The+Foreman&action=edit expanding it].**

Appearing only as a voice through notes left behind as part of the [Tales](./Tales.md) in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), The Foreman is one of 4 major characters that participated in a clandestine experiment in The Far Territory. The results were grand, but fatal to many individuals that partook in the project.

The Foreman is introduced as the deuteragonist in the Tale [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md), being one of two characters whose notes are found throughout the tale (the other being [The Security Chief](./The%20Security%20Chief.md)). He was the head foreman of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), overseeing the construction, maintenance, and instillation of the mine's various hallways and passages, as well as overseeing the construction of a new piece of machinery deep inside the nearby mountain, just above the main mine.
The last note found written by him reveals that something happened when the machine was turned on, as though all the lights in his head went out.
His [Tool Belt](./Foreman%27s%20Tool%20Belt.md) is found at the end of the Tale, inside the control room to The Machine.

The Foreman is the protagonist of [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md), being one of two characters whose notes are found throughout the tale (the other being Dr. Rüdiger). Throughout the Tale, The Foreman reveals that he was secretly a special agent inserted as a site foreman to keep tabs on Rüdiger, and is now making it his personal mission to track him down to avenge the many miners killed by his hand.

Throughout the Tale, it is revealed the machine had a grievous effect on his mind, as each of his Foreman's Technical notes continue to get worse handwriting each time one is found. The Foreman also begins noticing that he is losing/leaving things behind, and cannot control his actions.

Grey Mother **(Text)**: "So, tell me Mainlander. Did you do what I asked? Did you ransack the gas station? Did you clean them out?"
Mackenzie **(Text)**: "No, I couldn't do it. I thought about what would happen if people came back and...couldn't bring myself to steal from them."
Grey Mother **(Text)**: "I may be blind but I can still see the lies on you, Outsider. If you'll lie to me about that, what else will you lie about?"

> **The old woman might be the last survivor in Milton. She seems to know more than she's letting on. She might be the key to understanding what happened to Astrid.**

**The Grey Mother (Predux)** was the third mission of the Predux [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).
- There's a Firewood Bin outside Grey Mother's house. Stock it with fuel you find around town -- Sticks, Firewood, broken down furniture, or Coal if you can find any.
- Grey Mother will starve unless you stock her pantry with food. Scavenge what you can from the environment around you. Some food sources are easier to find than others.
- Investigate the tunnels leading out of Milton. Grey Mother wants to know what happened there.

[Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) asks [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) to find firewood to keep her fire going, or else she will not tell him anything about [Astrid Greenwood's](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) whereabouts. Take the [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) in the shed behind the [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) and search the Toolbox for a [Prybar](./Prybar.md) (which you will need later).

Abuse Grey Mother's Fireplace as much as you can to cook food and melt snow/boil water, as the fire duration is infinite. Take care not to take, search, or destroy any items in the house label with dark red text, as this will lower Grey Mother's Trust in you.

Harvest the amount of firewood specified (changes depending on difficulty) from the nearby forest and town. Break down furniture while looting homes and place the firewood inside of the [Firewood Bin](./Firewood%20Bin.md) on the porch of Grey Mother's house (make sure you gather food but don't eat it for later will looting houses). Coal can be found next to the burned down [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md), Sticks in the forest, and cedar limbs can be hacked up, even [Newsprint](./Newsprint.md) counts. Return to Grey Mother once you acquire enough firewood.

Grey Mother will then demand Mackenzie to stock her [Fridge](./Fridge.md) with food, as she will not last the winter without something to eat. She suggests to Mackenzie to ransack the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) since Mainlanders are so good at stealing, though if you're feeling guilty about stealing instead give to her what nature provides. Either way, find food containing calories and place the required amount in her fridge. She will then ask if you ransacked the Gas Station, and will somehow always know if you are telling the truth or not. You can either:
- Lie that you did steal if you did not steal from the Gas Station (Though Grey Mother will see through this lie and remark that you are a kinder soul than she imagined despite being a Mainlander)

- Tell the truth if you did not steal anything from the gas station, in which case Mackenzie will reprimand Grey Mother that if anyone returns to Milton and finds all their food in her pantry, they will not be very helpful to her, giving Grey Mother pause. (She will comment that over the years she has learned to be disappointed with everyone, but she misjudged you.)

- Attempt to lie that you did not steal anything if you stole from the Gas Station (though Grey Mother will see through this lie, and remark that if you'll lie to her about this, what else will you lie to her about)
- Tell the truth if you did steal from the gas station (Grey Mother will comment that you might have what it takes to live through this long Winter)

Either way, judgment will be passed, or not passed, onto Mackenzie, and Grey Mother will reveal more about her encounter with a woman that sounded like Astrid, though it sounds like she begins talking about someone else. Grey Mother will then ask you to come back later so she can rest.

After passing several hours, she will remember hearing voices in town, those voices came from the tunnel past the Gas Station, go there and come back. Mackenzie tells Grey Mother about how the Tunnel out of Milton is collapsed and that Astrid might have made it though, but Grey Mother realizes that she and Milton are now finished and wanders off into deep thought. Leave her be to get some rest and come back later.

After passing several hours again, Grey Mother then demands that you go to the local farm, and then the bank in order to retrieve something for her. Mackenzie is confused, asking how this will help him find Astrid, but Grey Mother urges Mackenzie to go, because then he will see why they left "her to die." Mackenzie will comment that Grey Mother seems a bit off now, but she will deflect by saying that she is old and that the mind tends to wander sometimes for her, continuing to remark that "They should have helped her."

Make your way to the farmhouse down the road, and search [the body](./Martin%20Barker.md) in the barn close to the Farmstead holds Lock Box Key to a lockbox in the farmhouse. Find the key to the house in the blue truck and then go inside into the bedroom and look for the urn on the fireplace, then take the [Bank Deposit Box Key 15](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2015.md) inside. Go to the [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md) and take the [Bank Manager's House Key](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House%20Key.md) to open the [Bank Manager's House](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House.md), then open the bank vault and use the key to open deposit box 15. Return to Grey Mother.

Returning the Deposit Box to Grey Mother, she opens it to find a string of Pearls inside, angering Mackenzie for making him run around to fetch jewelry for Grey Mother. The old woman will firmly ask that Mackenzie have faith, and to do one last thing for her before offering to help Mackenzie find Astrid. Mackenzie angrily refuses, saying he's finished helping the old woman do her chores. She responds that then he will die like the others, and begs "the man who fell from the sky" for one last favor, with Mackenzie reluctantly agreeing, before being handed [Grey Mother's Pearls](./Grey%20Mother%27s%20Pearls.md) and being told to take them to someone named Lily. Mackenzie finally realizes that this whole time Grey Mother was not talking about Astrid, but Lily. Grey Mother then asks Mackenzie to take the pearls to her at the [Graveyard](./Graveyard.md). Mackenzie asks why Lily is there, but Grey Mother tells him he will find his answers when he goes there.

Head out of town to [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md) and find the Graveyard. A cutscene will play with Mackenzie finding Lily, placing the pearls on a headstone reading Lilith Barker. Return to Grey Mother and she will thank Mackenzie for putting an old woman's worries. She will explain what happened to her daughter [Lilith Barker](./Lilith%20Barker.md) and then give Mackenzie a key to Lily's trunk containing her daughter's old climbing gear, offering a way out of Milton. Mackenzie says that he will send help for her, but Grey Mother says that her journey is over, and that his is just beginning, for this new world is for the strong.
Go upstairs and find the blue [Trunk](./Trunk.md) containing Lily's gear. Take the [Mountaineering Rope](./Mountaineering%20Rope.md) and [Lily's Map](./Lily%27s%20Map.md) and the mission will end.
Grey Mother offers unique items, knowledge, and side missions as rewards for better earning her Trust during this mission:

Several plot points and locations have been replaced/altered since the Redux re-release of Episode 1:

- Certain items, furniture, and containers inside Grey Mother's home have dark red text, signifying that they are owned by her. Taking, searching, or [Harvesting](./Harvesting.md) any of these items will produce a small message that the player has lost Trust with Grey Mother.
- The hidden cache that Grey Mother gives directions to at 125 Trust was replaced by the note [Medicine in my backyard](./Medicine%20in%20my%20backyard.md).
- The side mission [Light Up The Night](./Light%20Up%20The%20Night.md) was replaced by [Highway Robbery (mission)](./Highway%20Robbery%20%28mission%29.md).

- The knowledge that Grey Mother gives was replaced by the Collectibles the [History of The Collapse](./History%20of%20The%20Collapse.md), [Town of Milton](./Town%20of%20Milton.md), and the dialogue option "Perseverance Mills."
- The [Mountaineering Boots](./Mountaineering%20Boots.md) are rewarded after completing the side mission [One Last Thing](./One%20Last%20Thing.md).
- The [Rabbitskin Mitts](./Rabbitskin%20Mitts.md) are rewarded after completing [The Basics of Survival](./The%20Basics%20of%20Survival.md).

- There is far less emphasis on the actions of the escaped [Convicts](./Convicts.md) from the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) in this version of Episode 1. Grey Mother's house shows no signs of a struggle, with no dead Convict in the shed, no bullet holes in the wall facing away from her chair, and no knocked over furniture. The Old Schoolhouse apparently burnt down after many people took shelter inside by choice, rather than being forced inside by Convicts. Astrid simply passed through the town confused and wounded before making her way through the tunnel out of town, avoiding all the panic going on in Milton. The only dead convict that appears is the one next to the Crashed Prison Transport Bus.
- The [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md) displays a timer of 10 minutes until it burns out, yet it will never goes out. This was fixed in Redux, with the fire displaying an infinity (∞) symbol instead.

- The playground of the [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md) is different post Redux. Mackenzie does not express his horror and sorrow upon walking near the burned schoolhouse. The small detail of broken glasses and child sized sneakers is missing around the schoolhouse.

- [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) and [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) do not appear at all in this Episode (Hobbs did not exist as a character at the time and Methuselah only appears near the end of Predux Episode 2).
- Further more, the [Prison Transport Manifest](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md) only lists 12 prisoners, Hobbs missing.

- The moral choice involving ransacking the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) when getting food for Grey Mother, and how she somehow always knows what choice you made regarding it, is similar to how [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) comments on your choice to spare or kill [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) in the Redux, despite how neither were present to witness your actions.
- Going to the Orca Gas Station is optional if the player has enough food to satisfy Grey Mother. In Redux, it is mandatory to go there in order to meet Methuselah.

- [Martin Barker](./Martin%20Barker.md) hold a [Lock Box Key (Predux)](./Lock%20Box%20Key%20%28Predux%29.md) that opens a Lockbox inside the [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md). This Lockbox was cut from the Redux (along with the [Emergency Kit Note](./Emergency%20Kit%20Note.md)), however [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) now holds the same Lockbox (it is now filled with cash instead of supplies).
- An [Urn](./Urn.md) inside the Farmstead house holds the [Bank Deposit Box Key 15](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2015.md), whereas in the Redux, Hobbs has it in the Lockbox.

- The concept of a key inside an Urn would be reused for [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), with a key hidden under a [Vase](./Vase.md) during the mission [Trauma](./Trauma.md).

- Returning [Grey Mother's Pearls](./Grey%20Mother%27s%20Pearls.md) to Lilith's grave is mandatory to finish the mission. This would be made optional in the Redux with the side mission [One Last Thing](./One%20Last%20Thing.md).

**Characters:** [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md)
This is the mission transcript for mission 3 [The Grey Mother](./The%20Grey%20Mother.md) of [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md).
Grey Mother: "It's what you are, isn't it? From the Mainland? An Outsider? You don't really belong here, do you?"

Grey Mother: "We lost everything in [the Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md). People didn't realize how dependent we'd become. Some were fine with it. Others didn't want the scraps from your table. It created deep rifts in families, communities. Scars that never healed. The Mainland had become our lifeline. And it was suddenly cut. And so, we suffered."

Grey Mother: "I'm not surprised. You Mainlanders have always been focused on your own story. Only interested in Great Bear when it had something to give you. If you can't cut it down or dig it out of the ground, what use is it to you?"
Grey Mother: "The power's always been spotty here, since the quakes. No money to fix the broken stuff left behind. And nobody from the Mainland seemed to care enough to do anything about it."

Grey Mother: "I've learned to hear the difference between something quiet, and something abandoned. This goes deeper than just stillness. It feels like the moments before the world goes to sleep. We're just the last ones awake to notice it."
Will Mackenzie: "What really happened here? Seems like people were here recently. Where did they go? Why didn't they call for help or...just drive out?"

Grey Mother: "The power went out. Who knows the reason. People started to get cold, hungry. They panicked. Started to talk crazy. Others walked here from the highway...some, belonged here. Others, were Outsiders like you."
Will Mackenzie: "Did anyone see a woman? Brown hair, would have had a tan jacket...scarf with...birds on it. Possibly injured."
Grey Mother: "There was an Outsider woman. I heard her pass through. She wasn't alone. There were angry voices, and...but the storm was so loud."
Will Mackenzie: "Before, you mentioned hearing voices. Do you remember what you heard?"
Grey Mother: "The memories are grey...misty. I'm trying to remember. It was...windy. The blizzard was already waking up. But I heard yelling. A scream."
Grey Mother: "I'm not sure. The voices were...thin. Far. The blizzard was waking up. Soon there was only wind and...darkness. I don't know. I don't remember. It's all cloudy now."
### Find supplies to help keep Grey Mother alive.

_Having exhausted all dialogue with Grey Mother, Mackenzie leaves the house and begins searching for food and fuel for the old woman. If the player travels to the [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md), Mackenzie will say:_

_A small amount of blood is at the ruined front steps of the remains of the school, along with burned glasses and a burned pair of child sized sneakers. Most of the homes that are still standing in the town have been ransacked, most likely by the "bad men" Grey Mother mentioned. Eventually Mackenzie makes his way to the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md), and if the player arrives at night, they will see a glow coming from inside the building, as if the power is still on inside, despite the pumps and outdoor lights not being powered. Stepping inside through the front door, he sees an old man in front of the register, with his walking stick leaning against a pillar to his left, a [Green Birch Sapling](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) and [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) to his right, and an active fire in a [Rim Grill](./Rim%20Grill.md) right in front of him. Mackenzie walks up to him and speaks to him._
Unknown: "Not a refugee from the highways then. You look weary, traveler. Come, warm yourself by the fire."
Unknown: "I'm nobody. But you can call me [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md). I'm here to witness the passing of an age."

### Grey Mother thinks something happened at the tunnel leading out from Milton. Investigate.
_Mackenzie then heads to the tunnel just outside of town, and happens upon a [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md)._

_He walks up to the back of the bus and wipes the frost off the back window and peers inside only to see that the tunnel has collapsed and filled the bus with snow. Before leaving, Mackenzie finds a message written in red inside the bus: PERSERVERANCE. He returns to Grey Mother and tells her his findings. A wolf is found in the road feasting on a deer carcass near Grey Mother's home, further adding to the ruined state of the town. Walking inside, a pot of [Home-made Soup](./Home-made%20Soup.md) is sitting next to the fireplace._

**Characters:** [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md)
**Spoiler Warning:****This page may contain spoilers from the [story](./Wintermute.md) of The Long Dark.**
> “**An old blind woman might be the last survivor in Milton. She might be the key to understanding what happened to Astrid.**”

**The Grey Mother** is the third mission of [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) meets [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md) and performs various tasks for her in order to coax information about Astrid's whereabouts out of the old woman, while also learning more about the Town of Milton.
| Start location | [Milton House (Grey Mother's)](./Milton%20House%20%28Grey%20Mother%27s%29.md) |

| Significant locations | [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) / [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) / [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) / [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) / [Bank Manager's House](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House.md) / [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md) |

Upon entering the house, a cutscene will begin in which the Grey Mother character is introduced. The player can obtain additional background information about the town and its history by selecting topics to ask the Grey Mother about. At the completion of talking to Grey Mother, the player will have three tasks to complete—filling Grey Mother's firewood bin, stocking her fridge with food, and investigating the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md). Scavenge the town of Milton to find the required items. The hatchet in the shed behind Milton House is useful for breaking down furniture to obtain [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md). 8000 calories of food must be put into the fridge in the kitchen, and 12 days worth of wood fuel must be put into the firewood bin directly beside the door on the porch. Each hour of burn time is counted as 1.1 days worth of firewood.
The Orca Gas Station will be marked on the player's map. Inside the gas station, Mackenzie meets [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md).

After returning to Grey Mother, she will give the player a new quest to investigate the tunnel collapse. There is an option to investigate the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) by looking at the rear door.

When the player returns to Grey mother again, she will ask Mackenzie to look at the [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) for a safe deposit key. In the fireplace will be some [soup](./Home-made%20Soup.md) that Grey Mother has prepared.

When the player enters the farmhouse, [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) is sitting on the bench. The player will have to decide whether to save Hobbs by pulling out the knife, or to push it in and kill him. The decision will not have an effect on the gameplay, but will change later dialogues with Methuselah. Beside Hobbs on the bench is a box with the key to Grey Mother's safe deposit box. A [prybar](./Prybar.md) lies on the floor.

The player must then go to the [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md) and open the safety deposit box. In order to open the vault, the player will need the vault code. First, go to the manager's office in the Credit union and open the middle drawer of the desk. Inside is a key which will open the [Bank Manager's House](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House.md). The drawer of the nightstand in the bedroom of the Manager's House will contain a note with the vault code. Return to the Credit Union and open the vault using the code from the note. The note can be viewed by bringing up the journal. Open box #15 and take Grey Mother's Safety Deposit Box. Return to Grey Mother. This will unlock the [One Last Thing](./One%20Last%20Thing.md) side mission, and will also immediately begin the next main mission, [Paradise Lost](./Paradise%20Lost.md).

> **The Old Bear is after you. Get to Trapper's Cabin in Mystery Lake, before it gets you.**

**The Hunted, Part One** is one of eight [challenges](./Challenge.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. Completing this Challenge unlocks [The Hunted, Part Two](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Two.md).

The Hunted, Part One challenge requires the player to avoid the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) that follows the player as they try to hike from [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) to [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md).

![Skeeter's Ridge, with the bulkhead door leading to the basement visible](../assets/Skeeters_ridge.jpg)_Skeeter's Ridge, with the bulkhead door leading to the basement visible_ The Challenge begins with the Old Bear mauling the player, leaving them with 10% [Condition](./Condition.md), [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md), and zero [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md). The player's inventory contains a [Bandage](./Bandage.md) and an [Old Man's Beard Wound Dressing](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Wound%20Dressing.md), with a cellar door close-by for immediate shelter. Several supplies can be found in the basement, including an [Emergency Kit](./Emergency%20Kit.md) with a Distress Pistol.

- Except for a few additions (The Old Bear, additional Distress Pistol case, the special spawn point), the game is a normal Sandbox and weather and loot distribution will be randomized as usual. Difficulty is set to Stalker.

- Other than the Distress Pistol, no ranged weapons exist in this challenge, nor will you find materials to craft any. A [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) may be found, but there is no ammunition.
Arriving inside the Trapper's Homestead will generate the message "To Be Continued..." and the Challenge will end.

The Old Bear is a special bear and cannot be killed. He is, however, scared off by fires and by rounds shot from the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md). This is critical to your survival, as the bear will continue to hunt you for the entire challenge and can suddenly appear nearby, regardless of his last known location.

After mauling you the first time, the Old Bear wanders away a short distance where he waits. After a little while, he will begin stalking you again. Scaring him off is the best way to get him off your trail long enough to make forward progress on your journey, but he will always comes back, often running to catch up to your location but walking once in detection range. After a few minutes of the Old Bear not being around, he will always spawns somewhere nearby and begin stalking the player, and must be avoided or driven off.

The Old Bear will appear in new regions if the player enters them, and often stalks around the vicinity of any buildings the player rests in. Upon entering Mystery Lake, the bear may be directly in front of the player (in which case, the player will need to use the distress pistol, flares, or fire to ward it off).

The Old Bear will not enter buildings, vehicles, or mines. He will enter non-explorable caves. He will also not spawn in the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md) or [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md) maps. Just like most [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md), it is possible to (temporarily) escape the Old Bear by entering locations only accessible by squatting, [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md), or by jumping down an embankment.

The Challenge is completed when the player enters the door to [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md). The story can be continued once the player selects [The Hunted, Part Two](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Two.md) Challenge.

The Hunted, Part One and [Hopeless Rescue](./Hopeless%20Rescue.md) were introduced on 21 April 2016 in [version 0.321](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.321), also known as the Tireless Menace update.

**The Hunted, Part Two** is one of eight [challenges](./Challenge.md) in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md), and is the sequel to [The Hunted, Part One](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20One.md) and can only be played when finishing the first challenge. Completing Part Two unlocks [The Hunted, Part Three](./The%20Hunted%2C%20Part%20Three.md).

The Hunted, Part One must be completed to unlock this challenge. During the challenge, the player chases the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) throughout [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md). The bear will stop at numerous locations and wait until the player is close enough to attack, where they must shoot the bear with the rifle so it will continue driving it of to its den. The Challenge ends when the player confronts the bear at the den.
The Challenge begins right where Part One left off, with the player having entered the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) but now having taken up arms.

The Challenge begins with the player already having a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) in their hands and the Old Bear can be heard outside banging on the door. It will eventually tear it down partially once the player approaches the door, and the player can leave the Homestead once the door is damaged. The player begins with a Hunting Rifle and 10 rounds of ammunition and exits the Homestead to confront the monster.
- The [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) will always contain one [Firearm Cleaning Kit](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md) inside, along with several supplies to loot.

The Old Bear will be directly outside the homestead and must be shot with the rifle immediately or else it will attack the player. The bear cannot be killed so it is best to only shoot the bear when it has stopped at the designated locations. The bear will follow a path and must be shot to force it to continue retreating to the bear den.

The easiest way to track the bear is to follow the bear prints in the snow and the drops of fresh blood. If the player stops for an extended period, or if it snows heavily, the tracks will disappear. Ammunition can be found all over the region, and is best looted along the way as the player tracks the Old Bear.
The following list is the locations that the bear will stop at in order from the Trapper's Homestead to the den.

Once the player has finally reached the cave where the bear is hiding and gets close enough to the entrance to finish it off, the Old Bear will charge out and pounce on the player. Shooting the bear will not stop it from attacking. The bear will slowly drag the character back into the cave. As the screen fades to black while the sounds of growling and chewing can be heard, the words "To Be Continued..." appear again.

- [Wolves](./Wolf.md) can be found roaming near the trail the bear takes. It is recommended to use flares or alternative ways of making wolves flee instead of shooting them. Ammunition is extremely limited and the rifle is the only weapon that can make the bear retreat.
- The [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) will always have three rifle cartridges on top of the filing cabinets. Make sure to grab these in case you run out of bullets while hunting the bear.
- Unlike normal bears, the old bear will always run if you shoot it anywhere on its body, even if it's charging.
- The Dam may have a couple single bullets scattered around. There is also sometimes a box of five bullets in the room on the right. This should eliminate any ammo concerns.
- The Trapper's Homestead door is slightly damaged at the start of the game. However, this is only visual and won't affect Warmth or any other gameplay feature.
- curiously, you can visit any region outside Mystery Lake. The Old Bear won't follow and will remain in its last scripted location.

This Challenge is quite similar to the mission [Jeremiah's Folly](./Jeremiah%27s%20Folly.md), which was eventually cut from [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) (removed in the Redux version). Both the Challenge and mission involve the Old Bear being right outside the Trapper's Homestead at the start, following the bear from location to location, wounding it with the Hunting Rifle, and chasing it to a new location to hopefully kill it.

**The Long Dark Original Soundtrack** is the soundtrack to _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_, composed by Cris Velasco (Story Mode) and Sascha Dikiciyan (Survival Mode), and published by [Hinterland Studio Inc.](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md). Three volumes have been released with a total of 176 tracks and over 288 minutes (4 hours, 48 minutes) of music.

Volume One was released on Steam as DLC on August 28, 2017 and later on Bandcamp on June 22, 2018. Volume Two was released on Steam on May 19, 2020 and on Bandcamp in mid-June 2020. Volume Three was released on Steam and Bandcamp on May 5, 2026.
The soundtrack includes music from [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), and [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md).

**May 5, 2026 Update:** With the release of Volume Three, Hinterland made several changes to the soundtracks:

- **Volume Two, Disc 2:** Removed "Onward" (was a duplicate of "Hope" from Volume One). Added two never-before-released Survival Mode tracks: "Ash Canyon" and "Blackrock". The Volume Two cover image was also updated to a new version.
- **Volume One & Two:** Now include lossless FLAC versions on Steam (previously mp3 only).

- **Volume Three:** Released May 5, 2026 (delayed from original April 22 date). On Steam, discs are numbered Episode Four (Disc 1), Episode Five (Disc 2), Tales from the Far Territory (Disc 3) — the reverse order from how they are presented on the promotional material.
- **Volume Three, Disc 1:** "Music for When You Have Nothing Left to Lose" is a piano-only reprise, not a standalone original track.
- **Minor title variations:** The promotional artwork for Volume Three lists the track as "Rüdiger's Dream" (with umlaut), while the Steam release uses "Rudiger's Dream".
- **The Silent Hunter** (V3D3 #13) shares its name with the May 2015 update "Silent Hunter" which introduced bow hunting and other mechanics.

The “Redux” represents thousands of fixes and improvements, as well as entirely new content. The number of changes are too numerous to list here. Generally, the changes are along the following themes:
- Narrative Presentation: New dialogue mode; all story is now experienced in first-person; all dialogue is fully voiced and animated. All cinematic moments have been redone.

- Narrative Content: All dialogue has been re-written and re-recorded. While the high-level story arc of Episodes One and Two remains the same, many of the supporting details have changed. We’ve introduced new plot elements, new locations, a new introduction, and overall a general layer of presentation polish on narrative content.

- Mission Structure: We’ve opened up the mission structure; previously there were several plot elements or side mission content (ex. Jeremiah’s Survival School) missions that were prerequisites to progressing in the story. As much as possible, while maintaining a logical story flow, we’ve made the mission structure more flexible. Side content is properly optional now and can be accessed over time and in between key narrative moments.

- Gameplay Improvements: In addition to opening up the structure somewhat, we’ve also retuned many of the mission objectives to provide the right amount of challenge. We’ve worked to reduce the amount of backtracking that is required to complete missions (while maintaining the right amount of open-world exploration to keep things interesting). We’ve completely overhauled the Bear Hunt mission structure, integrating it more fully into Episode Two, adding new Bear Spear gameplay, and adding climactic new encounter to complete that story. We’ve also made improvements to how we present mission information to the player. And finally, we’ve retuned the Survival “needs” per Story Experiene (Green, Capable, Hardened) and increased the amount of ammunition (Rifle, Distress Pistol) available in the world.
The “Redux” game update includes some improvements to the game’s Survival Mode, notably:
- New Craftable Item: Rabbitskin Hat. This completes the suite of craftable clothing options in the game.
- New Health Buff: Well Fed. If you avoid Starvation for 72 hours, you will get a buff to Condition and Carrying Capacity. The 72-hour timer gets reset every time you begin to Starve.
- New Challenge: Archivist. Scour Great Bear to collect the last memories contained in several Aurora-animated computers.
Please note that the Bear Spear is currently a Story-mode only tool. It will be added to Survival Mode in a future update.
As part of the Redux overhaul, we’ve also made the following changes to the User Interface:
- Revised the HUD condition indicators. The game also now defaults to an “Always On” HUD configuration, which can be changed in the Display settings.

- Improved the Fire/Stove interaction interface, to clarify Firestarting, Fuel-Adding, Cooking, and Water production activities. This replaces the “direct placement” action from the Radial as the default, primary Fire/Stove interaction type, although we have also maintained the radial placement system for those who wish to use it.
- General improvements to the Map, Objectives, and Knowledge areas of the Journal (for Story mode only).

Due to Unity issues, we are seeing lower than expected performance in some areas of the game on Xbox One and Xbox One S. We are investigating this issue and will release a fix ASAP. Xbox One X is not affected by this issue. There are some rendering issues when using the latest NVidia drivers on Linux. We are working on a solution. This issue does not affect AMD video cards.

Please don’t forget to visit our Support Portal for useful articles, or if you need to log an issue. To stay up-to-date with news and information about The Long Dark and Hinterland, sign up for our newsletter and follow us on Twitter (Game | Studio).
- [Ep 4 - "The Detonators"] Fixed an issue that could cause players to become stuck on a black screen after returning to Blackrock Penitentiary with the Explosives.

We just launched our latest update to Survival Mode, called PERILOUS CONSTRAINT. This update includes:
- New to Survival! Blackrock Region added to Survival Mode. It connects to Pleasant Valley via a Transition zone, and to Timberwolf Mountain via a cave system.

- New to Survival! The Noisemaker from Episode Four is now available for crafting and use in Survival Mode. Note that the Blueprint unlocks after you find your first Noisemaker, currently only discoverable in Blackrock Region.
- New to The Long Dark! The Ballistic Vest. It’s the first piece of protective gear in the game and offers strong defense against physical harms from wildlife attacks.
- Various quality-of-life improvements, including making Crampons repairable, and a new piece of soundtrack music, along with many bug fixes.

We’re setting up a small internal team dedicated solely to supporting Modding and User Generated Content at Hinterland. Our initial focus will be on supporting The Long Dark, but we plan for this to be a long-standing investment in time and resources, and the things we learn and the modding community we build with you, will hopefully become a strong foundation of more things to come in future Hinterland games.

As first steps, we’re setting up a Modding & UGC section of the official Hinterland forums. We’ll have dedicated focus from our Community team on this area, so please focus your mod discussions here so we can best support you. We’ve also set up a new email alias, “mods@hinterlandgames.com”, which you can use to contact us with any requests or information you’d like to share.

As first steps, we’re setting up a Modding & UGC section of the official Hinterland forums. We’ll have dedicated focus from our Community team on this area, so please focus your mod discussions here so we can best support you. We’ve also set up a new email alias, “mods@hinterlandgames.com”, which you can use to contact us with any requests or information you’d like to share.

In the Spring, we’ll be sharing more info about our Creator Hub, which will have documentation, some tools, and other resources for modders, and other types of fan creations for The Long Dark. Until then, we’ll be active in the new Modding & UGC section of the official forums, and we’ll also be proactively reaching out to many of you who have been busy modding the game over the past years. We want to know more about what you need in terms of tool support, documentation, and also to provide you a clear path to communicating with us as we grow this area of The Long Dark’s community.

We’ve been working on a plan for how to tackle ongoing support for Survival Mode between now and Episode Five’s launch, and beyond. I’ll share more details about our plans in the new year, as there are a lot of technical aspects we’re still figuring out. But as a high-level direction, based on the guidance we’ve received from many of you in our player community through our community poll earlier this year -- _and after providing nearly over 7 years of free updates to Survival Mode_ -- our plan is to move to a more sustainable paid update path.

One of the first stages we’re working towards is splitting Story Mode and Survival Mode into two separate games and executables. This won’t affect your ownership in any way -- everyone who currently owns The Long Dark will automatically have both games. In fact, depending on how we handle this, the split may be mostly on the back-end and invisible to you as a player. This split is mostly about how we structure content and data in the game on the development side.

Until now, Story content has been a layer on top of the core Survival Mode foundation, which has allowed us (over the years) to share the world and mechanics between the two modes, then using tuning variables and a complex system of scene layering to keep the two different experiences separate but relatively cohesive. This was a fantastic decision for us earlier in the project when the game world was smaller and we had less episode content, but as the years have passed it’s become harder and harder for us to maintain this structure, and we feel it’s become overly limiting to our ability to continue to grow The Long Dark for the future.

One illustrative example of this is that every time we change an element of UI, or a foundational art asset or system that is shared between the modes, we have to then test all the episodes, all the survival mode regions and content, and all the Challenge modes against this change. As a result, over time we’ve had to spend an increasing amount of effort on testing and validating our existing content and systems every time we want to release something new, and this has prevented us from updating the game as frequently as we would like. It’s also limited the kinds of things we can update, and we feel that many of the architecture choices from back in 2014 and onward have now become detrimental to the game’s growth and evolution in 2021 and beyond.

What splitting the game into Story and Survival will mean for us is that we’ll be better able to compartmentalize content, features, cinematics, etc. so that every time we make a change in Survival, we don’t have to retest the entirety of the rest of the game, and vice versa. In theory, this should make it easier for us to update the game in the future, both shortening the testing cycle and ensuring it can be more focused on a narrower band of changes. Our belief is that this will help us better maintain the game and ensure a high-quality experience for our players. We’ll share more details about this split in the new year, and as I said our hope is that for most current players this split will be very “behind the scenes”.

Beyond this, our plan for 2022 and beyond is to introduce some form of a paid update path for Survival Mode. We’re still working out the details of this -- and there are many! -- but our primary goal in developing this strategy is to focus on: 1) fairness to our current players, 2) creating multiple entry-points so that players can opt-in depending on what they want and what they can afford, and 3) long-term sustainability for the development team.

Part of our update plans also include how to handle next-gen visual enhancements. Thus far the only way to play The Long Dark on Xbox Series X|S, or PlayStation 5, has been through backwards compatibility. We want to create some next-gen native visual enhancements that really capitalize on the greater processing power and memory in the new consoles, and also on high-end PC, but again because of how our game is structured -- and because of how the platforms prefer developers to handle this content -- it’s been tough to reconcile the dev work required to make these changes with the impact they would have to our bottom line. We think we have a good plan for this and we’ll share more news about our approach and the list of enhancements we’re tackling at the same time we roll out more details about the paid update path for Survival Mode.

And just to be crystal clear -- none of these changes will have any impact on the delivery of Episode Five. This will still be free for all existing customers. If you own The Long Dark, you will not have to pay extra for Episode Five.

And speaking of Episodes, in case you missed it, we released Episode Four: Fury, Then Silence, in October. If you haven’t had a chance to check it out yet, we encourage you to play it over the holidays!

As usual for this time of year, the Hinterland team will be enjoying well-deserved rest with loved ones this holiday season, and the studio will be shut down from December 20th to January 3rd. If you run into any issues with the game during that period, and wish to contact us, please use our Support Portal. Please keep in mind that due to being on holiday, our responses might be delayed.

We’re excited to share more news with you in the new year, but until then, get some rest, stay safe these holidays, enjoy time with your loved ones, and we’ll see you in 2022 to begin a whole new phase of The Long Dark.

For more information, please read this month’s Dev Diary, watch the update video, and review the list of changes below.

Don’t forget to visit our Support Portal for useful articles, or if you need to log an issue. To stay up-to-date with news and information about The Long Dark and Hinterland, sign up for our newsletter and follow us on Twitter (Game | Studio).
- [UI] Fixed an issue in Survival Mode that caused six incorrect Possible Old Bear Locations to appear in the list of Mystery Lake Surveyed Locations.
- [UI] Fixed an issue when using a Controller that caused the Start Fire menu to skip when starting a fire in a Fire Barrel.
- [UI] Fixed an issue that prevented items from appearing in Inspection Mode when the HUD was disabled in Options.
- [UI] Fixed a performance issue that caused the WINTERMUTE menu to become unresponsive when the Player had many save files.
- [Ep3] Fixed a bug that caused the UI to disappear after exiting various sequences, such as a phone call or a dialogue sequence.
- [Dialogue] Fixed an issue that caused the text to appear distorted during a dialogue sequence.
- [Optimization] Fixed a rare issue that would prevent the Player’s footprints from appearing correctly in certain circumstances.
- [Optimization] Fixed numerous performance hitches, which should result in a smoother play experience.
- [Animation] Fixed an issue where certain climbing animations were broken when the FOV was set to maximum.
- [Animation] Fixed an issue where the animation twitched during the Kill/Release choice after catching a Rabbit.
- [Animation] Fixed an issue where Mackenzie’s arms shook incorrectly when climbing various areas.
- [Accessibility] Updated Mature Language Filter to include some lines that were missed.

- [Art] Optimized render distance on various objects found in Episode Four so they will become visible at the appropriate distance from the Player. This will reduce instances of distant objects popping in to the world.
- [Art] Optimized the Steam Tunnels object and lighting draw distance to improve the overall visual quality and performance.
- [Environment] Fixed an issue that caused the walls inside the Radio Hut to remain visible regardless of what room inside the Radio Hut you were in.
- [Environment] Optimized the Mines to ensure the Gas is not drawn when not needed, resulting in performance improvements.
- [Environment] Added some extra collision to the pipes in the Steam Tunnel to prevent the camera from clipping into the pipes.
- [Environment] Fixed large black shadows found on the beds in the Blackrock Prison Infirmary.
- [Environment] Moved the “Danger Electric Cables Over-Head” warning sign in the Steam Tunnel to make it more visible.
- [Environment] Fixed numerous floating or clipping objects throughout the Blackrock Region.
- [Environment] Fixed an issue where the water splash sound effect was missing when walking through water found in the Abandoned Mine.
- [UI] Fixed an issue in the Journal’s exit button on the Collections -> Surveyed Locations screen so Players no longer need to change to a different screen to exit.
- [UI] Fixed an issue preventing the Region displayed on the Map from updating correctly when using a cave to transition to a new Region.
- [UI] Fixed an issue where the Mission Status tab would not reflect the state of the current active mission.
- [UI] Tuned the icons on the Map screen so Mission Markers are sorted above other Map Markers.
- [UI] Fixed an issue where the weather could change from the intended calibration preset while adjusting the Brightness in the Main Menu.
- [UI] Fixed an issue where Open Cans can appear as closed when viewed in the Cooking Menu.
- [UI] Fixed unaligned buttons on the “Continue to ...?” screen that appears after completing an Episode.
- [AI] Fixed an issue where Wolves continued to eat carcasses after the carcass is gone.
- [Audio] Added audio ducking to the Marine Flare, so its audio is no longer louder than in-game dialogue.
- [Gameplay] Fixed an issue where water longer disappeared when clicking the “Move All to Container” button, then immediately transferring the water back to the container.
- [Gameplay] Fixed an issue where the Maple Syrup would remain attached to the Player, instead of being removed from the world after being picked up.
- [Darkwalker] Tuned the wait time between placing a Banish Glyph and the Darkwalker appearing. Players should not have to wait extended periods of time, now.
- [Cinematics] Fixed an issue during Chapter 1: Blackrock Blues that could cause the audio in cinematics to no longer align with the animations, if the Player skipped a cinematic.
- [Cinematics] Fixed an issue that would often cause in-game dialogue to be skipped if it was intended to play immediately after a cinematic during Episode Three.
- [Environment] Fixed an issue with the Wolf found near the farm during Episode One so it now feeds on corpses, as intended.
- [Environment] Fixed numerous locations where the Player could either become stuck or escape the map or intended progression route during Episode Four.
- [Episode One] Fixed an issue where Mackenzie would appear without a bandaged hand while picking up the Hardcase.
- [Episode One] Fixed an issue that caused the audio for the fires at the Crash Site to continue to play after they had burned out.
- [Episode One] Fixed an issue that would cause the skybox to briefly appear when exiting back to the Main Menu from inside the Grey Mother’s House.
- [Episode Two] Fixed an issue where the Active Objective UI element would not appear as intended when bringing up the Radial Menu, after getting the Bear Spear during The Best Defense.
- [Episode Two] Tuned the Aurora that occurs during the Return to Dam mission so it will now be fully active, instead of just starting.

- [Episode Three] Fixed an issue that would prevent the Player from being able to progress if they saved the game right before answering the Phone at the burnt-out cabin, then reloaded the save during the Phone Call.
- [Episode Three] Fixed an issue so that removing the fuse now correctly disables both the electrical visual and sound effects during Aftermath.
- [Episode Three] Tuned the mission complete percentage to be more accurate during Forest Talker.
- [Episode Four] Fixed an issue where the final gauge could appear at full pressure when the valves were still incorrectly set during Steam Valve Puzzle #1.
- [Episode Four] Fixed an issue that caused the interaction point on the Valve to shift if the Player entered the tunnels, then returned to the Valves during The Detonators.
- [Episode Four] Fixed an issue where weapons and gear were not confiscated properly after completing The Detonators.
- [Episode Four] Added safeguards to help prevent the Player from dropping the Bolt Cutters into unreachable locations in The Detonators.
- [Episode Four] Fixed an issue that caused the Status bar to flicker prior to returning to gameplay after the cinematic sequence in Donner.
- [Episode Four] Dialogue will no longer continue to play on the Death screen if the Player is caught during Donner.
- [Episode Four] Increased the range at which the entrances can be seen during Convict Caches.
- [General] Fixed an issue where players using Windows 7 would become stuck on an unskippable black screen when playing an in-game video, such as the opening credits.
- [Rendering] Decreased the compression on numerous textures to increase the overall visual quality.

Today is a big day for Hinterland. After two years of development, we are finally launching Episode Four of our WINTERMUTE story mode for The Long Dark. “Fury, Then Silence” continues Mackenzie’s story after his ill-fated meeting with the convict Mathis in Carter Dam. You may remember that meeting didn’t end well for Mackenzie. Now we get to see what happens to our everyman bush pilot as he tangles with some very unpleasant people in a prison complex at the end of the world.

Developing the majority of this episode during a global pandemic has been a challenging experience to say the least. All the while, the team has banded together to support each other during the ups and downs. Within our small team, we’ve experienced the highs of births and new life, and the deep lows of losing people we love. And all the while, we pushed forward to tell the story of Mackenzie and Astrid, the quiet apocalypse, the wintery wilderness of Great Bear, and the mysterious aurora in the sky, all to the best of our ability. The parallels between our isolation and fears of the outside world and Mackenzie’s experience in the episode were not lost on us.

For us, Episode Four will always be the pandemic episode. The experience of making it, and of playing it, will always be coloured by this time. Art doesn’t exist in a vacuum, so maybe you will feel some of those influences as you go through and experience Blackrock for yourselves.

Today is a bittersweet day. We give you the fourth episode of our survival odyssey, and we come one step closer to the final part of our story. We have set the table for Episode Five, and now we turn our attention to bringing it to a close. There are still many challenges ahead.

In the coming weeks, I’ll be sharing more information about our plans for the future of Survival Mode, next-gen enhancements, mod support, and other things we’re doing at Hinterland. But today is about Mackenzie, a prison in the mountains, and a tough journey that will push him -- and you -- to your limits as a survivor.

We hope you enjoy the experience we have created for you, and on behalf of the entire team at Hinterland, I thank you for all your support and patience as you waited for this day. Thank you for believing in us, as we believe in you.
_The Long Dark, Episode Four: FURY, THEN SILENCE is available now on Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, Epic Games Store, and Nintendo Switch. Watch the full trailer below._

This is a Hotfix targeted at THE LONG DARK: IRON ROAD, addressing priority bugs, and additional fixes for issues included with the initial release.

- Fixed an issue where Research Books, Polaroids, Weapon Variants and Interloper Item tables were not correctly spawning in new games. Unfortunately, players who started new games while this bug was active will not find these playthroughs retroactively fixed.
- Fixed an issue where the Cabin in Looted Grotto would load the incorrect scene when entered.
- Fixed an issue that caused the camera to bob and sway after transitioning while in the Train Cab.
- Fixed an issue where the Train could intersect with the gate to future islands when rammed.
- Fixed an issue where Wildlife could path to and attack the player when inside the Fulmar cockpit.
- Fixed an issue where players would become stuck in the ocean after falling in near the Fulmar at Hibernia.
- Fixed multiple Safehouse Customization issues with item placement, movement, and removal in Train Repair Depots.
- Fixed an issue where the door to Train Repair Depots could be opened without initiating a transition.
- Fixed an issue where players could climb around and over the gate to Track Section 1 from Port Remnant.
- Fixed an issue where duplicate Lockers were placed in the same location in Train Repair Depots.
- Fixed an issue where Distress Pistol skipped the aiming animation, resulting in a jarring motion.
- Fixed an issue that resulted in snow footstep sound effects while walking inside Train Repair Depots.
October 27, 2026: Update to support launch of [Iron Road](./Iron%20Road.md) Early Access (Steam only). Features Anna Island release.
Hotfix THE LONG DARK - EPISODE FIVE HOTFIX 1 (WINTERMUTE v 2.24 -- EPISODE FIVE v 2.54)[^2]
This is a Steam only Hotfix for THE LONG DARK: WINTERMUTE, addressing bugs introduced with the Episode Five release. Other platforms will follow shortly.
The team is currently aware of the following issues in the game and hard at work addressing them:
- Players who Alt-Tab away from the “Previously On” cinematic shown when beginning Episode Five, will find that the video restarts upon returning to the application.
- PlayStation players may find that Survival Mode Photos taken prior to the Episode Five release appear blank.

- PlayStation players may encounter an error that reads "Cannot create more saved data for this application" when launching the game. These players may not be able to generate new save files or save existing games while playing. Deleting save data until the total used space is less than 50% will remedy this issue for the time being.
- Fixed an issue that could result in a crash when a timer was invoked by a Mission objective.
- [Perseverance Mills] Fixed an issue that could cause a crash if a manual save was created just prior to receiving the "To Those Who Are Missing" Mission.
- [SAR Mission] Fixed an issue that could result in a crash when entering the Train with HUD settings turned "Off".
- [Blackrock Foothills] Fixed an issue that could result in a crash during the Cable Car hand-over-hand section.
- Fixed a rare issue that could cause a crash if players opened their Journal in specific circumstances.
- Fixed a hang when loading an Episode One to Four save file from a death screen in Episode Five.

- Survival - Fixed an issue where bloody hands from Harvesting persisted between save games and could only be cleared by exiting the application entirely. The Survivor's hands will now be cleaned off after Harvesting is complete.
- [Blackrock Foothills] Fixed an issue where Cable Car closed captions were running in conjunction with the cinematics during that section, when the cinematic dialogue should take priority.
- [Conflagration] Fixed an issue that allowed players to interact with and enter burning Vehicles.
- [Conflagration] Fixed an issue where loading a save file made after conducting a takedown on a convict during "Conflagration", would result in that convict returning to a standing position.
- [Cargo Ship] Fixed an issue where the Medical Log would remain floating mid-air after interacting with it on the Cargo Ship.
- [Cargo Ship] Fixed an issue where reloading any save while in the Cargo Ship would result in the Locker Key disappearing.
- [Geothermal Mission] Fixed an issue that resulted in a soft-locked state if a player loaded the checkpoint created near the end of the Geothermal section.
- [Geothermal Mission] Fixed an issue where the Aurora was not active as intended after returning from the Geothermal section.
- [Geothermal Mission] Reduced the amount of Shotgun Ammo during the Geothermal section to make it appear less frequently.
- [High Energy] Fixed an issue that could result in the gate to Perseverance Mills being locked after loading an autosave made once "Atwood's Story" cinematic has completed.
- [High Energy] Fixed an issue that resulted in a soft-locked state if a player loaded the checkpoint created after delivering the "Wintermute" message to Dr. Atwood.
- [High Energy] Fixed an issue where a closed caption was missing from Mackenzie’s pained screaming during the Tuner section.
- [High Energy] Fixed an issue that could prevent the player from progressing in the game if they loaded the checkpoint after their first conversation with Dr. Atwood.

- [High Energy] Fixed an issue that could cause Dr. Atwood to close the Suzuki Radio Telescope Facility door on Mackenzie if he took too long to enter. The door could still be opened, but could be confusing.
- [High Energy] Fixed an issue that caused the Suzuki Radio Telescope icon to have no name when not the current objective location.
- [High Energy] Fixed an issue where the map marker for "Get Ready for the Geothermal Substations Mission" referenced the incorrect objective.
- [High Energy] Fixed an issue where the "Get Ready for the Geothermal Substations Mission" objective would not progress after entering the Supply Room.
- [Mine Mission] Fixed a very rare issue that could prevent Jace from acting if an autosave occurred during one of her voice lines.
- [Mine Mission] Fixed an issue where Jace could fall into a pit if the player purposefully blocked her movement in certain sections of the Mine.
- [Mine Mission] Fixed an issue where the Bolt Cutters would not appear in the Collections Journal after picking them up in the Mine section.
- [Perseverance Mills] Updated the "second broken bridge" for visual clarity showing that it can be crossed in one direction.
- [Perseverance Mills] Fixed an issue where players could interact and enter broken Vehicles in Perseverance Mills.

- [Perseverance Mills] Fixed an issue that could result in players never receiving the "Those Who Are Missing" mission if they manually saved the game just after completing the "Perseverance" Mission.
- [Perseverance Mills] Fixed an issue that caused two of Jane's closed captions to be swapped.
- [Perseverance Mills] Updated map markers to accommodate for cases where players complete "Perseverance" Mission objectives in a specific order.
- [Perseverance Mills] Fixed an issue that caused an incorrect map marker on the Constable's Office when reloading a save made after completing that section of "Perseverance".
- [SAR Mission] Increased the amount of Matches spawned in the "To SAR and Back" Mission.

This can be accessed by starting a new Episode 1-4 game and then quitting at your earliest convenience.
