No electricity: Only you and the brutal, brumal weather. To stay alive you will need to provide for yourself from what you can find amongst the landscapes. Nearby structures may still stand, and, perhaps they are all abandoned; perhaps they still contain useful equipment. They definitely can provide shelter. And the woods—the woods are everywhere. You grew up with woods like these, you have fished waters like these. There is much that nature can provide and much it can take away.

Most important now is your health. It is only you, no one else to rely on. You must meet your basic needs. Where is food? Water? Where to sleep? What can be done to push back the constant, insidious cold? All must be answered by you.
With luck and determination, you may find relief — even comfort — here in the new wilds. But there are other places to be; there must be ways to get there.

The game is created whilst striving for realism in many areas and as such borrows many [afflictions](./Afflictions.md) and core [survival mechanics](./Needs.md) from real life. It gives players an interesting set of choices to play with safely. The creators do not, however, as a general rule, tune the gameplay for realism or to conform to real-world expectations. Therefore, new players may find some things intuitive from the beginning and may need to learn how some other aspects work during play or from other, more knowledgeable, players.

Will Mackenzie works as a pilot for [Jackrabbit Remote Transport](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Jackrabbit_Remote_Transport) prior to the First Flare event. [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md), his ex-wife, comes to Will after years of being apart to ask him if he can fly her to an isolated town in the Northern area of Great Bear Island to treat a patient of hers. She also brings a mysterious case with her and does not want to reveal the content to Will. While the two separated some time ago, both still wear their wedding rings. It is implied that they had a child together who had passed away. Mackenzie also used to have an alcohol problem that he claims is under control now.

After hesitantly accepting to fly Astrid to Great Bear Island, Will's airplane crashes into the Northern Canadian wilderness of Great Bear Island when a mysterious geomagnetic storm cuts all power to his instruments. After the crash, in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), Will finds Astrid's case but not his ex-wife. Thus, he begins a journey to search for her across the remote wilderness of Great Bear Island.

The Long Dark received "critical acclaim" from Steam users, according to Steam reviews. On release, it received mostly mixed to positive reviews from critics, praising its sandbox nature, the content and the atmosphere while criticizing the story. Fan base alike also criticized the story mode calling it a "fetch quest" rather than a story.

The [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md) is a playable archive of previous builds of _The Long Dark_ released for free by Hinterland, and allows users to play builds of the game as far back as the pre alpha builds. This functionality is currently only available to Steam users due to Steam's infrastructure allowing access to beta builds of _The Long Dark_.

_The Long Dark_ currently does not have any official modding support aside from the [Steam Workshop](https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/browse/?appid=305620&browsesort=trend&section=readytouseitems&days=90&actualsort=trend&p=2) providing support for other languages for the Steam version of the game. Despite this, individuals have taken to creating unofficial mods that add unsupported content to the game. Hinterland has so far not shown much support regarding modding, aside from a single [dev post](https://www.thelongdark.com/news/dev-diary-perilous-constraint-update/) in 2022 discussing their acknowledgment regarding _The Long Dark_ Mods, and it is currently unknown how modding will affect the future of _The Long Dark_.
At this time, this wiki only acknowledges the legitimacy of [The Long Development](./The%20Long%20Development.md) project; an unofficial project that adds new regions to Great Bear Island.

Jace: "You get into the old steam tunnels. You'll find an access door in the rock face just outside the power plant. Other side of the spillway. According to these blueprints, they lead you -- more or less -- right to the old locking mechanisms under solitary."
Jace: "Well, there are some stains on the map. And a few areas that are fuzzy, engineering-wise. I mean it's old! But yeah, eventually you will get to the locking mechanisms."
Jace: "You tear out or smash anything that looks remotely like a switch, fuse, panel, cable, wire, vacuum tube...you get it?"

**Characters:** [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) [Franklin](./Franklin.md) [Mathis](./Mathis.md) [Vachon](./Vachon.md) [Heller](./Heller.md) [Jace](./Jace.md)
> “**Mathis orders you to find the old Power Plant and look for a way to restore power to solitary.**”

**The Power Plant** is the third mission in [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) is ordered by [Mathis](./Mathis.md) to travel to the Power Plant and find a way to restore power to solitary.
| Mission details — Start location | Mission details — Blackrock Federal Penitentiary |

The episode starts at the door of [Blackrock Federal Penitentiary](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), where [Heller](./Heller.md) hands Will a map of the area showing where to go. Once outside, it's recommended to gather all the gear previously left behind in the locker, as it will be required for the trip to the power plant.

To get to the power plant, follow the powerlines from the jail. If freezing becomes a problem along the way, a good stopping point, which offers good loot, is the [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md). There's also a bed there if sleep is needed. The river in Blackrock is not frozen, and must be crossed at [Narrow Bridge](./Narrow%20Bridge.md), being careful not to fall in the water along the way. Following the road is the most direct path, however it may be safer to head northward via the narrow mountain paths to avoid predators.
If following the road, about halfway from Narrow Bridge to the power plant is a trailer, which can be used to warm up if needed.

In a clearing just before the power plant there will be a pack of [timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md). These can be shot or dispersed with [noisemakers](./Noisemaker.md). Once inside the power plant, [Jace](./Jace.md) will call, instructing Will to enter the steam tunnels to access the control room below solitary to sabotage the locks keeping [Donner](./Donner.md) in, so that [Mathis](./Mathis.md) doesn't learn how the locks work.

Getting to the control room requires the use of steam to thaw away icicles blocking doors. Initially, all but one steam valve will be frozen. Opening this valve will enable the next valve to be turned. To thaw a steam valve the pressure leading to it must be in the green zone (check the gauges); in at least two cases, re-opening/closing valves that the player opened/closed will be necessary in order to get the next valve to thaw. Be careful not to walk into the jets of hot steam leaking from the pipes, as that will cause rapid [condition](./Condition.md) loss.

**Description:** A small valley containing a railway trestle passing through the mountains.
**Connecting Regions:** [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)

**The Ravine**, also known as **The Raven Falls Railway Line** or **Raven Falls,** is a Transition Zone [Region](./Region.md) connecting [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), and [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). It was the 1st Transition Zone released in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

The Ravine is a long and winding narrow region with sparse [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md). No artificial structures are present to shelter in, but three caves provide shelter: one near Mystery Lake, another near the region's center, and the last at the Ravine's basin near Bleak Inlet. The [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) in the region suffers from heavy damage, and requires frequent detours to get back on the tracks.

The Ravine is trickier to navigate than other regions. Depending on which route is taken, a fallen tree trunk must be crossed, a broken railway line over a lethal fall must be traversed, or a long rope must be climbed. The region as a whole is very long and quite cold with little shelter, making its travel time consuming and vulnerable to [exposure](./Weather.md).

**WARNING,** attempting to [Mountain Goat](./Mountain%20Goating.md) down the sides of the Ravine into [Ravine Basin](./Ravine%20Basin.md) will result in passing through an invisible **DEATH BARRIER** that will instantly wipe your save after death (or force you to [Cheat Death](./Cheat%20Death.md) to continue). It was added when the zone was first put into the game to prevent people from accidentally mountain goating down into lower areas of the valley, causing the player to get stuck and slowly die since they could not escape. These death barriers still haven't been removed since the as of the recent version of Survival Mode. This should be treated as an [Environmental Hazard](./Environmental%20Hazard.md). Always use the [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section to go down into the basin.
Falling off the tree bridge onto the small patch of land underneath it near the Rope Climbing section of Ravine Basin will also result in instant death.
The Ravine is one of 2 unique regions that contains no [predators](./Wolf.md) of any type (the second being [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md)). Only 2 animals are found in this region.
- [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) can occasionally be found in the section of the map containing the Ravine's Basin, above and below it.
- [Deer](./Deer.md) can be found to the west section of the map, along with the occasional [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md).
There are also 2 [Warm Caves](./Warm%20Cave.md) located on the east section of the map, northeast and southwest of Ravine Basin respectively.

Near The Ravine's exit to Coastal Highway is a narrow railway line atop a bridge. Part of the trestle is destroyed and the railway line damaged, requiring careful navigation to not plummet to one's death below.

Attempting to climb down the trestle or the slopes in the Raven Falls area is lethal, due to a kill-box put in place to prevent players from trapping themselves at the bottom of the Ravine. This was put in place before Bleak Inlet was added to the map, but still remains to end runs for the unwary.

Near the hanging train by the Mystery Lake side of The Ravine is an anchor point (with no climbing rope); affixing a [climbing rope](./Rope%20Climbing.md) here allows descent to the Ravine Basin and Bleak Inlet.

At the Ravine Basin inside a rail-car is a [distress pistol case](./Distress%20Pistol.md) with multiple [flare shells](./Flare%20Shell.md), a [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md), a deer carcass, rabbits, [cattails](./Cat%20Tail%20Stalk.md), and potentially other loot. Near the entrance to Bleak Inlet at the Ravine Basin is a [cave](./Cave%20%28disambiguation%29.md) with a leaf [bed](./Bed.md) inside.

- This rope climb to the basin is very long, and is challenging to climb up: requiring high [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Crampons](./Crampons.md), and/or stopping at the ledge mid-climb to rest. Using [coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) or sleeping in [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) or the basin's cave will help prevent becoming stranded from [exhaustion](./Fatigue.md).
- A [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) or [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) can be used to complete the climb up, but will result in becoming exhausted afterward.

- Since version [0.321](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md) there is the chance a climbing rope will spawn (with other loot) in one of the train wagons. A rope may also spawn at the lip of either cave.

The Riken is a wrecked whaling ship located between the [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md), [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) and the [Little Island](./Little%20Island.md) (Unmarked location). It sits on top of a rock sticking out of the ice and there is a huge hole in the bottom on one side, which allows access to the interior.

The boiler deck is dark but contains crates, metal shelves and a furnace & forge at the end of the deck. The forge here is one of the only places in the game where you can conduct [forging](./Forge.md) (the other three are at the Field 31 in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), [Old Spence Family Homestead](./Old%20Spence%20Family%20Homestead.md) in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) and at [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) in [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md)). There are some pieces of coal scattered about that can be useful for forging (but there is no [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) which is required to forge). Firing up the forge causes smoke to be emitted from the ship's exhaust pipe on the outside.
The upper deck has bunk beds, a small kitchen to loot, and access to both the boiler deck and weather deck.
The weather deck features an inoperable harpoon gun, direct passage to/from the ice through some broken railings, and stairs to the bridge deck, where you can occasionally find useful items.
- [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) (Weather deck and next to shelves in the boiler deck)

**Characters:** [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md)
This is the mission transcript for mission 1 [The Wounded Trapper](./The%20Wounded%20Trapper.md) of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md).

_A cutscene begins with [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) in front of the Wood Stove of the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md), warming his hands and body repeatedly for a good moment. His attention regarding the stove is broken when he hears a grunt come from the [man he rescued](./Jeremiah.md)._

_The wounded man springs to life, swatting it away as he jumps out of bed in terror screaming. He pushes Mackenzie to the floorboards as he awakens from his nightmare, looking around confused and in pain from his injuries._
_The man frantically looks around, and slowly begins to calm down, looking at his rescuer while clutching his chest._
_The man looks over his chest and chuckles at the damage the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) has done to him._
Jeremiah: "Yeah. Me and the Old Bear go back a ways. There's...There's unfinished business between us."
Mackenzie: "I bandaged you up but you're in bad shape. Is there anywhere to get medical help?"
_Mackenzie looks over and points at the radio on the Work Bench. The Trapper's [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) lays on the bench in front of it._
Jeremiah: "No...Radio's been dead for the past few days. I can't raise any of the usual channels. Not sure why."
Mackenzie: "No. But, I've been around doctors enough to know you'll be in trouble soon, unless you get some better help than I can give you."
Jeremiah: "Yeah...Right. Well...Closest help is probably in Milton, back the way you came."
Mackenzie: "Err...there's nobody left to help you there. The town's pretty much deserted. There was a fire...and..."
Jeremiah: "Damn. Next town is days away. I'm wrecked, but if you leave now you might be able to..."
Mackenzie: "So we're back to where we started. There's gotta be somewhere nearby that might have medical supplies, or another radio we can use?"

Jeremiah: "You might find some comms gear, or parts, in the old Carter Dam. It's...probably ancient stuff though. Place's been abandoned for years. Used to have a first aid room. Might still be some old meds there too. Something strong enough to maybe numb this pain."
Jeremiah: "Wait...wait. The Old Bear. He's still out there. He'll be wanting to finish the job."
Jeremiah: "Here...Take my rifle. You won't kill him but you might...scare him off again."
_The Trapper begins to wince in pain, before lying sideways on his pillow and fainting from the pain. Mackenzie gently shakes his arm to see if he will wake up._

_Mackenzie takes the Trapper's Hunting Rifle, which is in less than ideal condition, and any other supplies in the cabin. As he reaches the door, a map showing the layout of the region catches his eye. Mackenzie makes note of the route to the Dam and leaves the cabin._
Mackenzie: "That trapper's my key to getting out of here. He'd better not die on me."

_Mackenzie sees two trailers nearby, and enters on. ## Find medical supplies for the old trapper. Find the radio parts the trapper needs.
Mackenzie: "Seems like the quakes did some damage here. Must be what the old guy meant about "unstable"."

_He spots a heavy door ahead of him with the words "CONTROL ROOM" on it and tries to open it. The handle does not budge, and he looks at the nearby Keypad to his right. He presses some buttons, but they do nothing._

_He picks up some radio parts, then returns to unlock the Medical Locker, finding [Carter Hydro Medical Supplies](./Carter%20Hydro%20Medical%20Supplies.md) inside._
Mackenzie: "Industrial-strength antibiotics and... _very\_ strong painkillers. Dangerous...you could get hooked on this stuff. Let's hope we don't need it."
## Get the medical supplies back to the old trapper before he dies.
_With medical supplies in tow, Mackenzie leaves the dam and returns to the Staging Area._

_He and makes his way back to the Trapper's Cabin as a blizzard rages on, and eventually reaches the front door. Mackenzie walks up to the old trapper, and injects his right arm with a syringe filled with antibiotics. This causes the trapper to instantly wake up, as he grabs his sides._

Mackenzie: "Take it easy. You're pretty banged up and probably a bit delirious too. I just gave you a shot of some heavy antibiotics. Might feel funny for a while. But it'll help, and you're gonna need some time to recover."
Jeremiah: "Nevermind that. Help me up so I can look at the radio. See if the parts you brought back are any good."

Jeremiah: "Something to do with the power. Fuses? Transformers maybe. We have bigger problems to deal with first. That bear's out there. Hunting us. He's a smart old bastard. He'll keep us from getting out, getting supplies, finding help. Eventually...he'll either get us, or starve us out."

_The fire forms 3 figures; a man, a woman, and a child. The fire changes to show a bear attacking the man and woman from before, then changing to show the woman in bed. The next scene is of Spence's wife in bed, then of Spence holding the Bear Spear._

Jeremiah: "Spence shows up and sets his claim shanty, family in tow. For generations, the family had been traders with the Hudson's Bay Company. Old "voyageur" stock, they say. Hard people. Survivors."

"One day a bear shows up and menaces the homestead. Spence takes a shot at the bear but it doesn't seem to do anything. Bear wanders off, but Spence's wife...she takes a turn. Slips into fever. "He goes out, into the muskeg. Disappears for days. Then one morning, the wife's fever breaks, but nothing from Spence. Some men go out looking for him. They find him, half dead. Blood all over him. **The Wounded Trapper** is the first mission in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md). In this mission, [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) must help find medical supplies and radio parts for [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) following his encounter with the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md).
The mission starts with a cutscene in which Jeremiah and Mackenzie discuss the need to find medical supplies and radio parts.

![The trailer containing the key to the staging area](../assets/Carter_dam_trailer.jpg)_The trailer containing the key to the staging area_ Follow the map to the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) on the other side of [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md). The gate to the staging area will be locked. The key is found on the desk in a nearby trailer. On a shelf in the same trailer is the Medicinal Plants of Great Bear skill book, if it had not been picked up in Episode 1. When unlocking the gate, a cutscene will begin in which the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) tries to attack Mackenzie, but Mackenzie closes the gate to stop its charge. Mackenzie is thrown to the ground and knocked unconscious. The player will be freezing when he comes to.

![The corpse with the office key and distress pistol](../assets/Dam_bathroom.jpg)_The corpse with the office key and distress pistol_ Enter the Carter Hydro Dam. In the bathroom on the first floor is a [corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) with a key to the admin office and a [Forest Talker](./Forest%20Talkers.md) note. An emergency case with a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) lies on the floor.

Go up the stairs to the second floor. On a desk near the elevator are some radio parts the player will need to pick up. Open the door to the admin office. On the desk is the key to the medical supply locker. The medical supply locker is a red locker against the wall in the second floor office space. Opening the locker will yield a medical supply kit.

Return to Jeremiah. The mission ends with a cutscene in which Jeremiah attempts to fix the shortwave radio in his cabin using the radio parts Mackenzie brought back from the dam, while telling the story of the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md).
_The dam bathroom, including a corpse with the [Admin Office Key](./Admin%20Office%20Key.md) and the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) case_

![Thirst icon](../assets/Thirst_icon.png) **Thirst** is one of the four essential [needs](./Needs.md). Thirst is a measure of how many liquids the player consumes and expends. Despite being surrounded by snow, liquids can be difficult to acquire, and are particularly heavy. The thirst need is fulfilled by consuming [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) or particular [foods and drinks](./Food%20And%20Drink.md). Failing to fulfill this need will result in [condition](./Condition.md) loss.

The thirst bar appears as the lowest of the four bars on the survival overlay. Thirst is actually the inverse of what is displayed; you are thirstiest when the bar is depleted and have the least thirst when it is full. The bar ranges from zero at the left to 0.67 L on the right. As it fills, its descriptor changes to describe the current state of thirst. Descriptors are Dehydrated ↔︎ Parched ↔︎ Thirst ↔︎ Dry-mouth ↔︎ Slaked. An empty red water drop becomes visible on the HUD when thirst is completely empty and indicates [condition](./Condition.md) loss has started.

Some [foods](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) are dry and deplete the thirst bar when they are consumed. Other foods are neutral or can even add to the thirst bar. Drinking water and other [drinks](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) remains the most direct means of satisfying thirst.

Whenever water ([potable](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) or [unsafe](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md)) is consumed, it is consumed until all of it is gone from the inventory or until all of thirst is satisfied (though you can end 'drinking' prematurely by pressing escape or cancel).

If the character is already dehydrated, this is the best opportunity to eat dry foods (like [salty crackers](./Salty%20Crackers.md), [beef jerky](./Beef%20Jerky.md), or cooked meat), as the rate of condition loss is constant and is not changed by actions that typically subtract from the thirst bar.
Coffee and all types of tea restore 30% (0.2L) of the thirst bar, and, weighing only 0.10kg apiece, are twice as weight-efficient as water.

violations.message: Heading level increased from h2 to h4, expected h3
violations.context: #### Interloper difficulty
Sleeping will completely drain thirst in 10 hours. This means that although it is possible to sleep 12 hours, it will result in some condition loss due to dehydration.

When awake, a full thirst bar will have completely drained after 8 hours. Sleeping will completely drain the bar in 12 hours. This means that the character requires about 0.083 liters of water per hour while awake and about 0.056 liters per hour when sleeping. If the character were to be awake all day, they'd use exactly 2 liters of water. If they were able to sleep for one whole day, they'd use 1.33 liters of water.

In Pilgrim, the character only requires half as much water as in the other difficulty levels. This means that one can go for up to 16 hours before having to drink again and that one consumes less than 1 liter of water per day.
- It is wise to drink water before [sleeping](./Sleep.md) to avoid dehydration and get full condition restoration.
When the Thirst bar is fully depleted, [Condition](./Condition.md) drains at a rate of 50% each day (about 2.1% per hour).

Dying of thirst takes 2 days at 100% condition, meaning death results twice as fast compared to starvation. Performing most tasks while dehydrated is possible, and doing so may be part of a strategy to conserve water. However, the player will not be able to [Research](./Research%20Book.md).
- "[That guy who drank his own pee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear_Grylls) doesn't seem so crazy right about now."

**Thomson Family Stew** is a food item in _The Long Dark_, it is learned from a unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md) and is made with a [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md).

Calories-wise, Thomson Family Stew is inefficient, with at least a level 4 cooking skill (the minimum to create it), the ingredients separately provide over 2100 kcal, almost double the calories of the finished stew. The weight of Thomson Family Stew (0.35kg) is far more efficient than that of its ingredients (1.5 kg). Cooked at level 5, its energy density is over 3200 kcal per kilogram, one of the densest in the game. This makes Thomson Family Stew an efficient food for travel or exploring.

Additionally Thomson Family Stew has both the highest Vitamin C density and amount per-item, making it highly effective at combating [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md). Note: Thomson Family Stew contains 80 units of Vitamin C, while consuming the ingredients directly provides a total of 141 units (Canned Corn 52 units, Carrot 9 units (x4), Cooked Potato 24 (x2), Reishi Tea, made from 2 Mushrooms: 5 units).
Canned Corn is one of the rarest foods in the game and is thus a very hard ingredient to find for this Recipe. It is mainly found in:
- The top floor of the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md) of the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) (3 cans)
- [Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md) for 3 hours (+1% Condition restored for first 3 hours of sleep, or 18 hours)

Has an interior **Thomson's Crossing**, formerly known as **Rural Crossroads**, is a small settlement in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).
- A small collection of [Crossroads Houses](./Crossroads%20House.md) (up to 4, some are collapsed. one is across the bridge)
[Upper Falls](./Upper%20Falls.md) can be found to the east and [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md) to the north-north-east.

Ample supplies can be scavenged from the houses and the only nearby wildlife is deer and rabbits, making the area generally safe from hostile wildlife and serve as suitable [safehouses](./Safehouse.md) for the player. The [Rural Store](./Rural%20Store.md) contains a decent supply of [food and drinks](./Food%20And%20Drink.md).
[Cat tail](./Cat%20Tail.md) plants and [reishi mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) can be found along the river bank to the west.
This area plays a key role in many quests in Episode 3 of Story mode, and it can be an important rest stop/source of food and other must-haves in Survival mode.
- Thomson's Crossing's church is a Catholic or Episcopal church where [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md) resides as the parochial vicar.

- This church is one of three on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md); the other two being the Catholic [St. Christopher's Church](./St.%20Christopher%27s%20Church.md) of [Milton](./Milton.md) and the [Stone Church](./Stone%20Church.md) of [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), an unknown denomination.

- It is suggested that Thomson's Crossing was the largest remaining settlement on Great Bear Island prior to [The First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), because Milton's church was closed due to the towns declining population (as detailed in [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) and Notes), and the Desolation Point's church seems derelict for years if not decades.

- Thomson's Crossing may be named after a man called [Ryan Thompson](./Characters.md#Mentioned_Characters), who is buried at the local cemetery. His grave is the oldest (of which the headstone is still readable), and is the only one that lies in a fenced area. The inscription reads "beloved father".

Has no shelter **Three Strikes Farmstead** is a collection of several farm buildings in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), located about 5 minutes walk northwest of the [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md).
Three Strikes Farmstead is a location in Pleasant Valley. It is in the northwest of the region.

It is also known as Three Strikes Homestead. The name may refer to three strikes in baseball, which is an out--possibly referencing the homesteaders' bad luck or simply the three broken-down structures on the edge of property. It may also refer to the three carcasses -- wolf, doe, and stag -- that can be found in the nearby area in Survival Mode.

[Reishi mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) and two frozen deer carcasses can be found near the broken-down buildings. Several rabbits, along with a wolf carcass, can also be found in the field nearby.
A [fire barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) and possibly a [hunting rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) can be found in the main barn. Other loot may include a first aid kit and a human corpse.

In [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), the player must visit the site to complete the [Ghost Stag](./Ghost%20Stag.md) as part of the [Tall Tales](./Tall%20Tales.md) side quest. Some optional story-relevant materials may also be found in the barn along with some relatively valuable loot.

**Description:** A harsh mountainous region with scarce resources and many [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) spots.
**Connecting Regions:** [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md)

**Hazards and Survivability:** The region is known for temperatures below -20 °C, frequent blizzards and scarce resources. Much of the region is divided up by [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) areas, making navigation tricky.
> “**For advanced players. An isolated alpine region with very few shelters or resources. A true test of wilderness survival skills.**”

**Timberwolf Mountain** is the 5th [Region](./Region.md) to be introduced in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It's commonly considered one of the most difficult regions to survive in due to frigid temperatures (sub -20C / -4F almost every day) and frequent blizzards (usually at least three per week). These conditions limit the time a player can safely travel outside with anything less than top-quality clothing, and the lack of warm indoor shelters means maintaining [campfires](./Campfire.md) is critical.

- The most commonly used entrance is a path near the [Landing Gear](./Landing%20Gear.md), which connects to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) at a [rope climb](./Rope%20Climbing.md) near [Prepper's Abandoned Cache](./Prepper%27s%20Abandoned%20Cache.md).

- Another option is the large, exporable cave, located a [rope climb](./Rope%20Climbing.md) down the river from [Eric's Falls](./Eric%27s%20Falls.md). It connects to [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) not far from [Foreman's Clearcut](./Foreman%27s%20Clearcut.md).
- A cave near [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md) leads to [Pillar's Footrest](./Pillar%27s%20Footrest.md) in [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md).
- A cave at the end of [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md) also leads to [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), at a ledge overlooking [Bitter Marsh](./Bitter%20Marsh.md).

Timberwolf Mountain is described as pure wilderness with a mountainous expanse almost entirely lacking in man-made shelters. It has steep cliffs and ravines that require [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) to navigate to several locations.[^1]

Timberwolf Mountain connects to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) via a [rope climb](./Rope%20Climbing.md) and treacherously cold mountain pass in the southwest corner of the region, [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) via the eastern end of [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md) or via a cave in [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md), and [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) via a cave system to the northwest of [Andre's Peak](./Andre%27s%20Peak.md).

Another defining feature is the large jet that crashed on the summit of the mountain. Wreckage from the plane is littered across the region; this includes both wings (one south of [Echo Peak West](./Echo%20Peak%20West.md), another on the [Summit](./Summit.md)); the tail section perched precariously on the edge of the summit; two wheels from the landing gear (one near the region entrance from Pleasant Valley, another also on the summit); and two engines (one at the western end of Echo Ravine, the other near Andre's Peak), as well as half the fuselage found near the top of the mountain.

Additionally, there are [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) from the plane scattered across the region, mostly near pieces of the wreckage, and with a huge cache in the tail end at the summit. When opened with a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md), these containers can be looted for large amounts of items in a specific category (e.g., canned foods, medicines, or a class of clothing).

Timberwolf Mountain hosts extreme environmental conditions, requiring careful preparation to ensure survival during any expedition. Wolves and bears constantly patrol the main areas of the map and there are few safe shelters, with little loot inside of those that exist. Due to the limited resources and abundant wildlife, hunting and defending yourself are necessary to survive for an extended period of time.

A few hundred meters from the end of the pathway to Pleasant Valley is [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md) and the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md), the only man-made structure on the mountain. With one of the few beds on the map, a fireplace, door, and the only workbench, it will likely be the primary safehouse within the region. It also is next to an ice fishing hut on Crystal Lake that can be used to cure [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md), and every region connection can be reached within several hours in-game from the Mountaineer's Hut. Another worthwhile shelter is the deep cave in the northeast near [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md), since it is next to multiple deer spawns and is close enough to a bear patrol area for easy hunting; however, it does not have much utility beyond being a good shelter during a hunting trip.

The path to the [Summit](./Summit.md) is fairly linear, and the tail end of the plane on the summit contains a huge cache of high-tier supplies. End-game manufactured clothing, multiple MRE's, either a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) or a corpse with a bag next to it likely to contain [Crampons](./Crampons.md), multiple cured pelts, and multiple tools/weapons can be found in the tail section.

| - [Andre's Peak](./Andre%27s%20Peak.md) - [Cave 2](./Cave%20%28Timberwolf%20Mountain%20location%202%29.md) (2 entrances) - [Cave 1](./Cave%20%28Timberwolf%20Mountain%20location%201%29.md) (2 entrances) - [Chasm Cave](./Chasm%20Cave.md) - [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md) - [Deer Clearing](./Deer%20Clearing.md) - [Echo Peak East](./Echo%20Peak%20East.md) - [Echo Peak West](./Echo%20Peak%20West.md) - [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md) - [Engine (East)](./Engine%20%28East%29.md) (East of mountain) - [Engine (West)](./Engine%20%28West%29.md) (West of mountain) - [Eric's Falls](./Eric%27s%20Falls.md) - [Forest Cave (Timberwolf Mountain location)](./Forest%20Cave%20%28Timberwolf%20Mountain%20location%29.md) | - [Landing Gear](./Landing%20Gear.md) (Near entrance to Pleasant Valley) - [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md) - [Secluded Shelf](./Secluded%20Shelf.md) - [Summit](./Summit.md) - [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md) - To Ash Canyon (Transition to [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md)) - To Cave System (Transition Cave to [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md)) - To Cave System (Transition Cave to [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md)) - To Pleasant Valley (Transition to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md)) - [Waterfall Cave](./Waterfall%20Cave.md) - [Wing](./Wing.md) (Plane wing near Forest Cave) - [Wing (Summit)](./Wing%20%28Summit%29.md) (Plane wing at [Summit](./Summit.md)) |

**Timberwolves** are hostile wildlife in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. They are the tougher and more intelligent counterpart to the common [Wolf](./Wolf.md); unlike regular wolves, Timberwolves always hunt in packs and are more persistent and aggressive.

Timberwolves have silver-gray coats and are larger than their black Wolf cousins, and roam in packs of 2-8. Being highly territorial, most regions that Timberwolves inhabit will be free of normal black wolves in open areas, with many containing [ravaged wolf carcasses](./Wolf%20Carcass.md) near the region entrances as early warnings for the player. ![A slightly smaller Wolf compared to a Timberwolf](../assets/Wolf_and_Timberwolf.jpg)_A slightly smaller Wolf compared to a Timberwolf_ Each pack has a varying degree of morale at the start of every confrontation, with the total amount dependent on the initial size of the pack. Timberwolves will not give up attacking the player until enough of the pack is killed, the player escapes to a safety, 1 pack member is left alive, or morale is fully depleted. Escaping indoors will cause unique audio cues to play, with the Timberwolves growling and clawing at the door in an attempt to get inside, at least until enough time passes for the pack to lose interest in the player.
A [Timberwolf Carcass](./Timberwolf%20Carcass.md) may be harvested for 4.00-7.00 kg of [raw meat](./Wolf%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md), 1 [Fresh Wolf Pelt](./Fresh%20Wolf%20Pelt.md) and 2 guts.

Despite having a different colored coat, ordinary black Wolf Hides are produced from the Carcass and can be cured to craft a [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md), [Wolfskin Pants](./Wolfskin%20Pants.md), or [Wolfskin Hat](./Wolfskin%20Hat.md).

Unlike common Wolves, Timberwolves do not 'stalk' the player, instead howling upon detection and attacking as a pack. Timberwolves will attempt to encircle the player and take turns diving in for attacks, either as a Struggle or as a "drive-by" hit and run attacks whereby they damage the player and briefly retreat. In [Wintermute](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md), Timberwolves will also attack rescued [survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md) lying on the ground.
- Timberwolves are drawn to [Scent](./Scent.md) of meat, [Baiting](./Scent.md#Baiting/Decoys) decoys, or [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md).

- Timberwolves will individually hunt [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), and [Deer](./Deer.md), but flee from [Bears](./Bear.md) and [Moose](./Moose.md). A pack will initiate a hunt if they detect the player even when feeding on slain prey.
- Lone Timberwolves (when the rest of its pack has been killed) always flee from the player.
- Only one Timberwolf will attack the player a time. Aiming a weapon at a hostile Timberwolf which is not currently attacking may cause it to briefly pause.

- Timberwolves prefer bite and run tactics on the player, often taking turns to bite a survivor. It is possible for a single Timberwolf to initiate a [Struggle](./Struggle.md) if the player stands still or turns away from a Timberwolf.
- Like other [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md), Timberwolves flee from nearby gunshots and bullet/arrows/stone impacts if they have not detected the player.

- Timberwolves will not give up a hunt if the player enters a [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) or building interior until half a day of not reaching the player passes or the player saves and loads the game. Fleeing into buildings may create a unique audio file to play of Timberwolves growling and attempting to scratch the door down.

- Like Wolves, Timberwolves may be frightened by a worn [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md), [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md), or [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md), but only before the pack howls/engages a hunt. A single wolf may flee, but if other Timberwolves are nearby and detect the player, they may not be frightened and a hunt may begin.

> “**Timberwolf packs have Morale, indicated by a red meter. Timberwolf Morale can be broken by shooting or throwing things at them. Packs with broken Morale will flee, but may return once they recover.**”

When a Timberwolf detects the player, they will howl and alert other pack mates, followed by the morale bar appearing. It is possible to turn off the indicator in the options for a more immersive but difficult experience. If a separate Timberwolf pack comes into contact with the player, there is a chance that both packs will begin attacking the player together (with separate unseen Morale bars).
Timberwolves will continue to attack the player until the following conditions are met:
- Passing time in a safe indoor location (such as a vehicle or outdoor, indoor space) will cause packs to give up, but this may take upwards of 12 hours.
- The player transitions to an interior/another region (this will just despawn the whole pack along with all other wildlife)

[Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md) are effective at stopping a charging Timberwolf, although normal Flares/Torches are not. Both types of flare are effective at deterring Timberwolves just outside their lunge distance. Once a pack's morale is depleted, surviving members flee and will not attack again until their morale regenerates (~1 hour in-game). A single lit Marine Flare can be used to fully deplete a pack's morale by repeatedly throwing it at the ground between the player and a Timberwolf, and then retrieving the flare.

[Campfires](./Campfire.md) have limited deterrence value against Timberwolf hunts, as they will not attack through them, but instead encircle it and 'hold ground' around the player. Torches pulled from a lit campfire may be thrown at Timberwolves to deplete their morale.

Injured Timberwolves do not participate in attacks (though it takes a few seconds for them to realize they are injured), and they flee from the player even if the pack has high morale. If every Timberwolf in the pack is injured, then the player is safe from attack, though the morale bar will only disappear once enough of the Timberwolves have bled to death.

- [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md), [Revolver](./Revolver.md), and [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) shots that land on a Timberwolf inflict large Morale loss
- Throwing objects at Timberwolves (Lit [Torch](./Torch.md), [Flare](./Flare.md), Marine Flare, [Stone](./Stone.md)) slightly lowers Morale

- [Noisemaker](./Noisemaker.md) explosions cause moderate Morale loss if the explosion does not damage/kill a pack member. Killing/damaging a pack mate with a Noisemaker causes large Morale loss due to the fear of the explosion as well as damage to the pack mate.

- Flashlight high beams will cause Aurora Timberwolves to stop their attack as well as cause morale damage, rendering flashlights a safe and inexpensive way to stay safe from Timberwolves during an Aurora.

If a Timberwolf pack is thoroughly culled, individual surviving Timberwolves from that pack will flee to a safe distance any time they detect the player. In this state, they will continue to individually hunt [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), and [Deer](./Deer.md) as normal. If they successfully hunt a prey animal and the player approaches them, rather than running away they instead will defend kills like normal Wolves. In this state, they can be scared off by aimed weapons. Unlike regular Wolves defending kills, a lone Timberwolf will always run away when defending a kill if the player gets too close, rather than initiate a Struggle.
Lone Timberwolves will not join another Timberwolf pack should they come across one, and remain treated as individuals.

![An Aurora Timberwolf](../assets/Aurora_Timberwolf.jpg)_An Aurora Timberwolf_ During an [Aurora](./Aurora.md), Timberwolves will turn green and become far more aggressive. They take more damage to kill, no longer fear fire, and their pack Morale is much harder to deplete. They do however fear the [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) and street lights. Great care should be taken when traveling during an Aurora, as Timberwolf packs are more persistent and aggressive when it comes to chasing the player down.
- Aurora Timberwolves do not fear [Flares](./Flare.md) or lit [Torches](./Torch.md) (throwing these at them will still damage their Morale). Aurora Timberwolves also no longer fear Marine Flares.
- Morale tends to be twice as long as normal or at maximum when they attack the player even with a small pack size.

- They fear active street lights, and will stand and growl at the player if they pass near the boundary of one. After enough time, they will run away in fear if they cannot reach the player, but will eventually return to attack the player if their Morale is not broken.

- They fear [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) high beams and will temporarily stop a charge as long as they are on. Flashlight's high beams are also effective at reducing pack morale, as per patch notes from June 2020.
- They will stay away from lit [Campfires](./Campfire.md), but will still stay close by and stalk to the player.
Timberwolves are competent in fights which makes detecting, avoiding, or escaping them preferable to combat.

- Lit Torches, Flares and especially Marine Flares are effective deterrents. A charging Timberwolf will stop and growl/hold ground a short distance away. Approaching a Wolf/Timberwolf holding ground will likely result in an attack, as will staying still for more than a few moments, keeping moving is critical for effective deterrence.
- Marine Flares are effective at frightening Timberwolf packs by igniting and repeatedly throwing/retrieving it.
- Timberwolves are territorial; simply avoiding their areas is effective. The edges of regions are usually safe. Timberwolves avoid [Bear](./Bear.md) and [Moose](./Moose.md) territory.

- Timberwolves must see the player to alert their pack, so crouching or hiding behind terrain is effective, though [Scent](./Scent.md) or noise can attract them. If un-alerted, Timberwolves can be lured by thrown stones or waiting until they move away.
- Upon detection, Timberwolves take several seconds to howl before beginning their assault. This provides a short window of opportunity to sprint to safety, start a fire, or ready a weapon.

- It is possible to outrun a pack, especially with a lit Flare/Marine Flare, as packs are optimized to fight stationary or slow players. Leaving their territory (entering the territory of a different pack or a bear/moose) will cause them to disengage.

- Timberwolves run at the same speed as a player sprints. Being overburdened, carrying a Mobility penalty (from worn clothing), steep terrain, or headwinds can allow Timberwolves to catch up while sprinting, but for the most part the player is safe from attack until sprint runs out.

- Passing time inside will cause a pack to disengage. This does not work in pseudo-indoor areas like Pensive Lookout, but quitting and reloading the game (such as after sleeping) will reset the pack: though they may immediately re-agro if they are very close.

- When entering an indoors area which is outside of the packs territory (example: being chased to the [Foreman's Clearcut](./Foreman%27s%20Clearcut.md) trailer from [Cook's Farm](./Cook%27s%20Farm.md)) listen carefully and if the sound of barking is not heard, you can exit the door immediately after entering, the pack having returned to their territory.
- During an Aurora the flashlight, streetlights, and vehicle headlights are effective against aurora Timberwolves.

- Assassination from stealth is often the best strategy for destroying a pack. This generally requires a Rifle, or a Bow with Archery 5, as they will detect a non-crouching player. Timberwolves generally do not react to their pack mates being killed allowing the entire pack to be eliminated from stealth.
- Thrown [marine flares](./Marine%20Flare.md) are very effective at depleting a pack's morale; even one can be enough to deter the pack by throwing and retrieving it.
- Terrain such as cliffs, ledges, boulders, or fallen trees are useful as chokepoints or for protecting from attacks entirely.

- Standing next to a campfire provides considerable protection from attack, in addition to this, one can pull Torches from the campfire to continuously throw at Timberwolves to deplete the pack morale.

- [Snow shelters](./Snow%20Shelter.md) can provide protection from attack, but may require leaving the shelter to continue a fight. Field of view is also limited, so the direction of a shelter is crucial since timberwolves can gather behind the snow shelter (in blind spots).

- The [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) is effective at depleting morale, but its cumbersome reload and relative quietness, opens the survivor up to the other wolves. A well placed shot can deplete up to 1/4 of a pack's morale.

- As with other predators, it is possible to sneak up close to Timberwolves while crouched and redirect them with thrown stones or by picking up/dropping smelly items. This allows them to be hunted more effectively without starting an attack. A mastered [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) (level 5 skill) is well suited for this method.
- [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) (Wintermute [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) only)
Following the Wildlife Refresh ([December 2024](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)) Timberwolves have a chance to sometimes spawn in the following six regions:
- On the ice between [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md) and the [Waterfront Cottages](./Waterfront%20Cottages.md).
- in the large field between the [Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) and the [Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md).
- In the field between the [Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md) and [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md).
- On the ice at [Crystal Lake](./Crystal%20Lake.md), next to the [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md).

- Timberwolves are based on [Eastern Wolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_wolf), or the Algonquin Timber Wolf (**_Canis lycaon**''), and are a Canine subspecies of the regular [Wolf](./Wolf.md) (**_Canis lupus**'').

- Timberwolves would ironically be absent from the titular [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) when it was released in [version 0.212](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Early%20Access%20Changelog.md#0.212).
- Timberwolves were added in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) (V1.60) in Wintermute, then to Survival Mode with the Errant Pilgrim update (V1.64).
- Timberwolves would finally have a chance to appear in the Timberwolf Mountain region with the Global Wildlife Refresh in the Part 6 Tales from the Far Territory update (V2.33).

- "The Timberwolf" is a track that originally played during timberwolf encounters in Wintermute Episode 3, later removed in an update. The track is still available to listen to on composer Cris Velasco's website.[^3]
- [Gameplay] Fixed an issue that prevented Timberwolves Pack Morale from being drained when using the Flashlight’s high beam.
- [WINTERMUTE] Timberwolves will now react to the Flashlight when appearing in WINTERMUTE.
- [EP3] Players can no longer skip the Timberwolf Tutorial, by placing a survivor at the same time the tutorial triggers.
- [AI] Fixed an issue that allowed Timberwolves to become hostile, regardless of game mode settings.
- [AI] Fixed issue that prevented Timberwolves from attacking the Player, if they have entered and exited a vehicle.
- [AI] Timberwolves will now only pick valid locations to wander to, preventing them from becoming stuck.
- [AI] Timberwolves will no longer freeze in place if they try to attack a target they can’t pathfind to.
- [WINTERMUTE] Timberwolf carcasses no longer disappear if the Player saves, then reloads.
- [AI] Added additional line of sight check to Timberwolves, to prevent attacks through walls and out of reach locations.
- [AI] Timberwolves will now break-off their attack if a Marine Flare is lit, before the struggle occurs.

> “__We launched THE LONG DARK on Steam Early Access on September 22nd, 2014. Since then, we have updated the game over 150 times. Until now, everything but the most current update has been unavailable to our community.

> — We created the TIME CAPSULE to let you step back in history and play every major update since our launch. Think of it as a playable retrospective of how the game has evolved over the years -- based on developer vision tempered by player feedback.

The **Time Capsule** is a playable archive released on September 20th 2019 to commemorate 5 years of development of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)._ It was released for free by Hinterland, and allows users to play previous builds of the game as far back as the pre alpha builds. This functionality is currently only available to Steam users due to Steam's infrastructure allowing access to beta build archives of _The Long Dark_.

Keep in mind that all previous versions of the game are Unsupported, meaning that these are old builds that will not be receiving any new updates. Many forms of [Cut/Discontinued Content](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md) that have long since been removed exist within previous builds of the game, and have their own pages on this Wiki should you encounter them (example cut tools and mechanics/early Wintermute Predux missions).

It is still possible to earn [Steam Achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) when using older builds of the game, though some Wintermute achievements cannot be unlocked when playing a build that existed before certain Episodes were released. It is not possible to earn any cut [achievements](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md#Game_History) from the alpha version of the game.

The following is the official **Timeline** of events that take place in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. Due to a lack of concrete dates provided in the world of _The Long Dark_, this list is compiled in order of known chronological events followed by what occurs in game. Information provided during the Missions and Side Missions Episode 1 and Episode 2 is based on the current Redux timeline, not the [Predux timeline](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md#The_original_Wintermute_storyline). Some Predux timeline details are presumed to still be true, unless explicitly stated in the Redux (any references from the Predux timeline will be labeled as such).
- The events of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) and their [Notes](./Notes.md), [Collectibles](./Collectibles.md), and [Load Screen](./Load%20Screen.md) messages.

- [Survival Mode's](./Survival%20Mode.md) [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) storyline, as well as Notes, Collectibles, and [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) found in the world.
- [Challenges](./Challenge.md) and limited time Events are considered non-canon "what if" scenarios, and are not listed here.
The following is a list of events confirmed to have happened, but the exact dates are unknown. As such, anything listed below may be out of order chronologically.

- It is unknown what year Wintermute begins, but it is theorized to occur sometime around 2012-2020s. Grey Mother mentions the collapse occurred 10 years before the present. (Unconfirmed. Predux information)[^1]

- Some time in the past, Mathis, and Heller were imprisoned on the Mainland in Montreal, Canada. Mathis had a plan months in the making to escape from the prison and busts out at the right time. The get away driver is 2 minutes late to pick the gang up. Heller escapes but the Mathis stays and beats the get away driver for being late, taking 5 guards to pull Mathis off him. Heller would later be apprehended and both men would be sent to Great Bear Island's Blackrock Prison via the prison bus.  [Blackrock Blues/TranscriptHeller](./Blackrock%20Blues%20%E2%80%94%20Transcript.md): "Right. You clean up the warden and I'll tell you all about it. So there was this really tight plan, Mathis had months to set it up. Everyone had their part to play. It was like...out of a fucking movie. So we bust out, and all hell breaks loose. We get to the front gates, it's a mess, right? Place is in chaos. And the driver who's supposed to pick us up. He's late."

Heller: "No shit. So the driver pulls up, like...two minutes late. Alarms are going off everywhere, it's like...the prison guards are coming after us. we're going to get grabbed at any second. We're yelling at Mathis, "Come on man let's go. Let's get outta here!" And Mathis just stands there. Looking at the fucking driver. Looking like...he wants to eat the guy. The driver's terrified. Mathis walks over to the van, slowly. We're all jumping in and yelling to get out, and we...and we can _see\_ the fucking guards coming. Like, we are done. We need to GET OUT. Mathis...he pulls the driver out of the van, looks back at us, and...with this totally wild look in his eyes...just says..."Go". Like totally calmly, but with this wild edge. And he just starts beating the living shit out of the driver."
Heller: "Yeah I mean we took off. And Mathis...it took five cops to pull him off that driver. He cared less about being caught than he did about the driver being late."

- An Island wide radio system is created to keep Islanders in touch with one another in case earthquake activity on the Island gets worse, or "the big one" hits the Island. Sutherland mentions that the radios the survivor uses to communicate from him are from an old emergency messaging system meant to keep Islanders in contact with one another. The "[A page from an old newsletter.](./A%20page%20from%20an%20old%20newsletter..md)" note also explains why these radios are found across the Island.

- Sutherland is a Great Bear Island native born in Coastal Highway, being the titular "Misanthrope" that lived at [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md). Sutherland, along with his "Pa" and brother Wyatt, lived there for most of their lives. Sutherland eventually states that he has abandoned his home and is more comfortable on his boat, saying that the survivor can do as they please with his house during the Quiet Apocalypse.

- Sutherland has a crippled leg that locks up on him in winter. He received it while at sea after heavy cables came loose on a ship and almost took his leg clean off. This information is conflicted moments later, with Sutherland mentioning that it might have instead have had something to do with his brother Wyatt.
- Wyatt would own and maintain an old sailboat, which Sutherland would eventually take for himself in the future.

- It is revealed that his brother Wyatt is the one who created all of the [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) bunkers across the island, including [Joplin's Bunkers](./Joplin%27s%20Bunker%20Raid.md). Though not confirmed, he most like created [Hank's Hatch](./Hank%27s%20Hatch.md), the [Aurora Hatch](./Aurora%20Hatch.md), and the hatch in [Blackrock Rumours](./Blackrock%20Rumours.md) - Suspicious Person as well.
- His reasoning was the belief that a nuclear exchange was coming that would destroy the world, confirming that the caches were fallout shelters.

- 3 other people were a part of Wyatt's crew, but ultimately turned on him due to paranoia. Sutherland's leg slowing the group down was one of the reasons why he was kicked out of the group and lead to his distrust of strangers.
- [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) suffers a massive forest fire, most likely caused by negligent miners working in the [Gold Mine](./Gold%20Mine.md).

- The Langston Mining Corporation creates the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md), a large open pit coal/uranium mine. The workers eventually destroy the local ecosystem, using water from [Unquenched Extraction](./Unquenched%20Extraction.md) to pump toxins out of the mine and into the [Overladen Pond](./Overladen%20Pond.md) near the [Pump House](./Pump%20House.md), poisoning the nearby streams. Toxic barrels are also dumped in several locations across the region. Many of these metal barrels eventually rupture due to weathering and age as the decades pass, creating several [Chemical Hazards](./Chemical%20Hazard.md) that effect [local wildlife](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md).

- An airstrip, [Field 31](./Field%2031.md), is built in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), presumably to fly workers into the Langston Mine. [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md) is established to help facilitate transfers via [Train Shuttle](./Train%20Shuttle.md). A [Weather Station](./Weather%20Station.md) is built in [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) to provide weather reports for the Far Territory.

- Ryan Thompson passes away at age 69, after presumably founding [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md). He is buried at the Crossing, with his own special walled off grave plot and the tombstone reading "Beloved Father."

- The Town of [Milton](./Milton.md) is established as a coal mining town, with the population going as high as the 1,000s throughout the 1900s. Milton's story would follow the boom-and-bust of the entire Island over the century.[^23][^24]

- [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) remains untouched by Mankind until mountain blasting for the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md) opens the area up for settlement. Its main purpose is presumably to ship coal, uranium, and workers from the Langston Mine to [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), as well as other resources found deeper within the Far Territory. The railways would be reused decades later by the [Breyerhouse](./Breyerhouse.md) company operating in the Mystery Lake and Broken Railroad regions to ship timber to the Coastal Highway.[^26]
- A woman recalls her husband helping build [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) around this time.[^27]

- It's said that Blackrock's original foundation was built on the site of an old trapping community. The trappers' cabins were destroyed to make way for the Penitentiary, a move that defined the history of the place ever since.[^28]

- Academics sometimes visited Blackrock Penitentiary to explore its vast records archive. The unique combination of geographic and social isolation has led to various scientific studies, of its staff as well as its inmates.[^29]
- Dr. Childs has been medical director at Blackrock for decades. It's rumoured that due to his research on Penitentiary inmates he's never been able to secure another position on the Mainland.[^30]

- Blackrock has attracted a variety of Wardens over the years. Some were kind, some cruel, but all were men who relished the extremes of life on Great Bear Island. One of Blackrock's longest-serving officers was famous for playing a piano deep into the night.
