- Miner Teams 1 and 2 cooperate with the project, but are on shaky ground. Team 3 becomes volatile and refuses to work on the project (either because they wish to leave the island and go home or due to working conditions), and the Security Chief calls for additional security to be flown in immediately. The Medical Officer conducts alignment interviews with the workers and makes troubling observations for worker morale. Ultimately progress continues on the project.

- Day 38 of the project - Dr. Rüdiger and his associates arrive on the Island and have all workers in the mine sign new paperwork. A track above the Concentrator is established into the mountainside to make hauling resources to the Machine easier.[^127]

- Day 45 of the project - Work continues on the Machine as earthquakes begin destroying much of the temporary scaffolding on the project site. Most of the work on the Machine is completed by this point. There are enough generators to power a town through the winter installed in the Machine.[^128]
- Team 3 is negatively affected by a sudden unknown illness that begins to rot the memories and mental faculties of all affected.

- Day 64 of the project -The [Project Medical Officer](./Project%20Medical%20Officer.md) is flown to the Island to determine in person the cause of the sudden outbreak of the mental illness in the mines effecting the workers.[^131]
- Patient 7 becomes the focus of some of the Project Medical Officer's Interview Transcripts.
- A reoccurring pattern is found with the illness; every patient has an obsession with water as they attempt to recall past dreams and memories. Examples include:
- [Faded Photograph](./Faded%20Photograph.md) of [Enduring Waterfall](./Enduring%20Waterfall.md) found in [Security Chief's Log (illegible)](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%20%28illegible%29.md)
- Individuals affected by the illness at [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) have been found breaking quarantine and wandering into the water.
- Most of the workers are confined to their quarters to prevent them from wandering. Most if not all of the mining staff and security personnel is now suffering from mental degradation.[^132]
- The Security Chief, The Foreman, and The Project Medical Officer begin to show signs of being effected by the outbreak, but not to the extent that the miners are.[^133][^134][^135]
- The Security Chief, The Foreman, and The Project Medical Officer begin to show signs of being effected by the outbreak, but not to the extent that the miners are.[^133][^134][^135]

- Rudiger appears to be entirely unaffected by the illness, causing the Security Chief to believe he has a cure, and knew ahead of time that exposure to the Machine would cause this outcome to occur.[^136]
- Rüdiger's Machine is taken offline, with Dr. Rüdiger himself avoiding contact with any miners or security personnel, having self isolated.[^137]
- The Project Medical Officer concludes that exposure to the Mine is the primary cause for the illness.[^138]
- He also concludes that the illness is not a virus or pathogen, as no physical damage to the body has been discovered.[^139]
- The Medical Officer holds out hope that treatment will be possible for those affected by the illness once they are taken away from the work environment.

- As it becomes clear that the situation at the mine is lost, The Security Chief tries to reason with Rüdiger to cut his losses and save the workers. Instead, the Doctor destroys as much evidence related to the project as he can, then flees to [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) with all the data he acquired from the project.[^140]
- Rüdiger presumably burns down the [Boss's Settlement](./Boss%27s%20Settlement.md) to cover his trail.

- A helicopter filled with mentally damaged workers was sent back to the Mainland with [Security Chief's Log 31](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%2031.md) and the [Foreman's Key](./Foreman%27s%20Key.md), but crashed in the mountains near [Old Corral](./Old%20Corral.md). This could have been possible sabotage by Rüdiger, or could have been legitimate engine/pilot failure. The surviving miners presumably wander off and die in the wilderness.

- The Security Chief then goes deeper into the Langston Mine, in order to destroy the Machine. It is unknown if she accomplishes her task, but eventually she perishes in the nearby control room as she loses her mind.[^141]

- The Foreman, who was secretly a mole for Jahnn Industries, was already given a secret mission to track down and bring Rüdiger in should he withhold or not produce any data from the project for the company. The Foreman then begins tracking down the Doctor for failing to provide a return on the company's investment after the failure of The Machine. [Foreman's Technical Log 4](./Foreman%27s%20Technical%20Log%204.md) "Did you think the board was going to sit by and let you just walk away? After everything you promised?
If it had gone another way down in that mine, you'd have never even known I was here. Just another hired hand."[^142]

- Dr. Rüdiger attempts to radio for a private evacuation via a transmitter at [High Peak Plateau](./High%20Peak%20Plateau.md), but help ultimately never arrives. [The Foreman](./The%20Foreman.md) shadows the Doctor from afar during this time, making his base in [Last Lonely House](./Last%20Lonely%20House.md) as his mental status deteriorates. Rüdiger is aware that that he is being stalked, as he predicted and feared might happen with his failure at the mine, and hides in the [Basement](./Basement%20%28Sundered%20Pass%29.md) of a [ruined settlement](./Old%20Settlement.md) in between trips to the Peak.
- The Foreman begins losing his belongings as his mind fails, losing various Polaroids and Technical Logs at each location he visits, including his [Tactical Gloves](./Tactical%20Gloves.md).

- Realizing that an evac is not coming for him, Rüdiger's mental state begins to fail, as he realizes that he also has been effected by the Machine's mind destroying properties. Rüdiger ultimately decides to leave the Pass and return to [Bunker Omega](./Bunker%20Omega.md).

- Rüdiger is attacked by a [Cougar](./Cougar.md) on his way to Bunker Omega, but survives. His [gold watch](./R%C3%BCdiger%27s%20Watch.md) is damaged during the struggle, and he is badly wounded. Eventually he successfully makes his way inside the Bunker, and hides in a hidden room.[^143]

- The Foreman tracks the doctor down, and demands the data from the project be handed over. An altercation occurs between the two, as Rüdiger attempts to shoot and kill The Foreman, but he is too slow and is instead shot himself. The doctor dies, and The Foreman makes an account to the best of his memory of what happened, before his mind fully deteriorates.

- The Foreman leaves behind his [Foreman's Technical Log 4](./Foreman%27s%20Technical%20Log%204.md) (with barely legible handwriting by this point), his [Tactical Jacket](./Tactical%20Jacket.md), and the [Security Chief's ID Badge](./Security%20Chief%27s%20ID%20Badge.md) in the hidden room before sealing the false wall, leaving the Bunker, and wandering off to never be seen again.
- A traveler hides a [Faded Paper](./Faded%20Paper.md) in the Loose Boards at [Mindful Cabin](./Mindful%20Cabin.md) as they travel the Far Territory.
- The same individual buries [A Page From A Journal](./A%20Page%20From%20A%20Journal.md) at the [Boss's Settlement](./Boss%27s%20Settlement.md) as they explore the ruined Langston Mine.

- At some point, [Rüdiger's Machine](./R%C3%BCdiger%27s%20Machine.md) is reactivated (assuming that it was never fully disabled by the Security Chief). People with symptoms similar to the miners in the past begin to appear in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md).
- [Samuel Franks](./Lost%20Worker%27s%20Note.md) and [a suspicous person](./Conspiracy%20Theories.md) around Blackrock also show symptoms as the miners affected by the device long ago.

- Astrid Greenwood travels to [Jackrabbit Hangar](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md) with a [mysterious hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md), attempting to chart a plane from her ex husband, Will Mackenzie, to the remote island of Great Bear Island.
- The First Flare occurs mid flight over Lower Great Bear, and Mackenzie's plane crashes in the remote wilderness of Lower Great Bear.

- Astrid Greenwood survives the plane crash and makes a campfire near a small pond nearby, before making her way to the Town of Milton. She attempts to save the residents burning alive in the [Old Schoolhouse](./Old%20Schoolhouse.md) before being attacked by [Convicts](./Convicts.md) and escaping through the tunnel out of Milton.
- [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) has a [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) stabbed into his chest by Astrid and flees to [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md).

- Will Mackenzie survives the plane crash but is stranded in a ravine close to his plane for 1 night, due to injuries he sustained from the crash. Mackenzie climbs out of the ravine the next day and finds Astrid's Hardcase but not Astrid, and then follows her trail through the woods before arriving at Grey Mother's home. The woman inside is reluctant to help him after her town was destroyed by Convicts the previous night, but she offers to help Mackenzie find Astrid in exchange for food and fuel.
- Mackenzie finds [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) inside the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) as he searches for supplies.

- Grey Mother directs Mackenzie to the tunnel out of Milton, but Mackenzie finds that the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) and an avalanche has blocked the tunnel.

- Mackenzie finds a message inside the bus left by Astrid: PERSERVERANCE. Grey Mother surmises that this is a clue pointing to an old logging town north of Milton, [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), giving Mackenzie an objective to travel to.

- Grey Mother then asks the pilot to retrieve [her Safety Deposit Box](./Grey%20Mother%27s%20Safety%20Deposit%20Box.md), then to give [her Pearls](./Grey%20Mother%27s%20Pearls.md) to [Lilith Barker](./Lilith%20Barker.md) at her grave, finally giving Grey Mother closure and peace regarding her daughter's death. She rewards Mackenzie her daughter's old climbing gear, giving him a way to leave the town.
- Mackenzie finds Hobbs in the farmhouse, and chooses to either kill or spare him. The convict's fate is unknown if spared.

- Mackenzie finds Methuselah for a second time outside of [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md), with the old man congratulating the pilot for escaping the town and passing judgment on Mackenzie for how he chose to deal with Hobbs.

- Mackenzie circumvents the blocked tunnel out of Milton by passing through the mountains into [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) encounters [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) being mauled by the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md). Mackenzie grabs the trapper's hunting rifle, and shoots the bear, scaring it off. Mackenzie then drags Jeremiah to his [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) and stabilizes his injuries for the next few days.
- Will Mackenzie nurses [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) back to health to the best of his abilities, and the trapper wakes up.

- Jeremiah urges Mackenzie to find [Medical Supplies](./Carter%20Hydro%20Medical%20Supplies.md) in the nearby abandoned Carter Hydro Dam, as well as find [Radio Parts](./Radio%20Parts.md) to fix the his shortwave radio.
- Mackenzie encounters the Old Bear for a 2nd time outside the Carter Hydro Staging Area, but the bear wanders off after being unable to attack Mackenzie through the fence.
- Mackenzie finds [Carter Hydro Medical Supplies](./Carter%20Hydro%20Medical%20Supplies.md) and [Radio Parts](./Radio%20Parts.md) and returns to Jeremiah.

- Mackenzie gives morphine to Jeremiah to stabilize him, with the trapper revealing that both he and Mackenzie are trapped in Mystery Lake as long as the Old Bear is still alive. Jeremiah needs to send a message to Perseverance Mills and Mackenzie informs him that he is looking for Astrid. Jeremiah confirms that the road she took out of Milton does not connect with Mystery Lake, and that they need to repair the Shortwave to message the Mills to see if she made it there.

- Jeremiah then gives Mackenzie an objective to travel to Broken Railroad find the mysterious [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md), as the trapper's [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) won't be enough to kill the bear.

- Mackenzie travels to the region and encounters the Old Bear for the 3rd time, who attacks him and knocks him out. When Mackenzie awakes, the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) is in the night sky again, with [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) nearby for a 3rd encounter.
- Mackenzie finds the [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md) and obtains the spear, but it is [Broken](./Broken%20Bear%20Spear.md).
- Mackenzie encounters a ringing phone in the lodge, but the phone call disconnects before Mackenzie can answer it.
- Mackenzie re-forges a [Spear Head](./Spear%20Head.md) and rebuilds the Bear Spear, then returns to Jeremiah, encountering the Old Bear a 4th time, but it keeps its distance.

- Jeremiah gives Mackenzie the objective to find [Transponder Parts](./Transponder%20Parts.md) from the 3 Shortwave Radio towers in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md) to further repair his ham radio and boost the signal, so he can send his message out.
- Mackenzie encounters the Old Bear again, almost as if it is guarding several towers, but drives the bear off with the Bear Spear.

- After finding all 3 Transponder Parts, Mackenzie returns to Mystery Lake, but is ambushed by the Old Bear. He is attacked and rendered unconscious, then dragged into the [Old Bear's Den](./Old%20Bear%27s%20Den.md).

- Mackenzie, unarmed, travels through the cave system to retrieve his Bear Spear, and ultimately kills the great beast. He then returns to Trapper's Homestead with the Transponder Parts, and passes out.

- Jeremiah fixes his shortwave radio as the Aurora appears in the night sky. He tunes the frequency to contact Perseverance Mills, and allows Mackenzie the honors of contacting them. A radio broadcast between an unknown party and Perseverance Mills is intercepted, with Mackenzie unable to get a word in with the two parties before the ham radio fizzles out (his words are broadcasted however). Jeremiah is distressed over the loss of his radio, and gives Mackenzie a message that he insists NEEDS to be taken to a woman living near the town named [Atwood](./Atwood.md). The message is WINTERMUTE.

- Jeremiah gives access codes to the control room in the Upper Carter Hydro Dam, and plots a course to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) for Mackenzie: Pass through the Dam, then through the [Carter River](./Winding%20River.md), then reach a [Radio Station](./Signal%20Hill.md) to call Perseverance Mills again before continuing to travel north to the Mills.
- Mackenzie is assaulted inside the Dam, with [Astrid's Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) being confiscated by a Convict named [Mathis](./Mathis.md) who demands that it be opened.
- Mathis mentions encountering a woman in the Dam and harming her, frightening Mackenzie who thinks this is Astrid.

- After interrogating Mackenzie over the contents of the Hardcase and into revealing the location of his plane, Mathis knocks Mackenzie out and drags him out of the dam through the Winding River, eventually regrouping with [Vachon](./Vachon.md) and [Heller](./Heller.md) and traveling through Pleasant Valley and Keeper's Pass South.
- [Molly](./Molly.md) encounters Astrid Greenwood outside of the tunnel to Milton in [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), and drags her back to her home to save her.
- Astrid Greenwood awakes inside of [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md), and is introduced to her savior, before eventually going back to sleep.
- Astrid asks if Molly has seen a man from the crash with her, but she denies seeing him.
- Molly reveals that the lights have been out for days, with even the generator outside the house refusing to work.
- Astrid awakes after Molly returns with a food for the both of them, but leaves in frustration after Astrid asks more about her home.
- Molly reveals that she has locked every door to the house from the outside before she leaves, trapping Astrid inside.
- Astrid snoops around the house, finding a piece of orange fabric from a prison jumpsuit, a photo of Molly and her husband, and an exploded rifle.

- Molly later calls Astrid over the phone, saying she is trapped in her barn with wolves and giving her the location of a key to the basement. She asks Astrid to bring her some Rifle Ammunition, as well as to arm herself with a Revolver.
- A light earthquake hits Pleasant Valley. This will be the first of many light earthquakes. Astrid finds the corpse of [Molly's Husband](./Molly%27s%20Husband.md) in the basement at this time.
- Astrid follows blizzard lines to [Barn (Molly's)](./Barn%20%28Molly%27s%29.md), but only finds a dead [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md) with arrows stuck in it when she goes inside.

- Molly calls Astrid over the phone telling her that she got away, but Astrid reveals that she found the body in the cellar. Astrid then finds a [Community Hall Flyer](./Community%20Hall%20Flyer.md) and heads to [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) to see if Mackenzie passed through there. She sees a large bonfire along the way in the middle of town, a beacon of sorts.

- It is assumed that Molly began hunting the Convicts throughout the region after this point, as she had forgotten she had a bow stashed in the barn from last summer until she waited for Astrid to come help her, and many of the Convicts have arrows run through them.

- Astrid arrives at the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md), and finds several [Crash Survivors](./Crash%20Survivor.md) from a nearby passenger plane crash. A man by the name of [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md) asks if she too is from the crash, but Astrid says she was from a different plan crash. Astrid then uses her skills as a doctor to tend to the wounded. Father Thomas also reveals that a monster blizzard is arriving soon in a few days, and that the Community Hall will need several supplies if the Crash Survivors are to recover.
- Many plane survivors died from their injuries and were stored in the basement in order to preserve the bodies and keep the wolves from attacking the Hall.

- Astrid tends to every survivor, but finds one man, Dimitri, with a diabetes wristband. She decides to journey to the plane crash to find his [Insulin](./Insulin.md). Father Thomas asks Astrid to find evidence of any missing passengers, as the Crash Survivors will need closure to begin healing after the devastating events that have taken place.
- Molly calls the Community Hall and Astrid picks up, revealing more information about her past regarding her husband, and leaving a [gift](./Molly%27s%20Gift.md) near the playground.
- [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) attack Astrid for the first time, but she fends them off.

- Astrid arrives at the [Crash Site (Pleasant Valley)](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) and is astounded by the devastation before her, questioning how anyone could have survived the impact. She finds several I.D. cards of many of the dead passengers in the snow, before finding [Gwen](./Characters.md#Gwen) at the tail section next to Dimitri's suitcase containing her insulin.

- A flashback occurs here, with Astrid appearing the past as Seraphim Sleep Research Centre, with [a friend](./Jane%20Yang.md) calling and pleading her to find a cure for an illness affecting her home in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md).

- Astrid begins taking Gwen back to the Community hall after finding IDs of from the corpses she can find at the crash site, as well as a [Passenger Manifest](./Passenger%20Manifest.md). Some passenger names are missing.
- Astrid receives a phone call from Molly at a burned down building, with Molly revealing more about her past.
- Astrid is aware that Molly is stalking her, as she mentions currently seeing Astrid with a survivor.

- Molly also reveals that all phones in the region are linked via a party line, and she just has to wait for Astrid to pick up any phone in the region to talk to Astrid. The phones also work because they run on a pre-electronics system, despite all modern electronics failing.

- Astrid carries Gwen to the Community Hall, administers Insulin to Dimitri, and gives the ID cards to every survivor in the Hall, however she was unable to find 3 people's IDs on the Passenger Manifest.
- Father Thomas urges Astrid to look for the 3 missing plane passengers, as they may still be out in the Valley, as well as finding any supplies to help the survivors through the coming storm.
- Astrid does find 3 missing Crash Survivors: Ava, Wade, and Logan, and returns them to the Hall one by one. Astrid also recovers enough supplies to keep everyone alive through the Blizzard.

- Father Thomas gives Astrid a [Map of Pleasant Valley](./Map%20of%20Pleasant%20Valley.md), showing her how to leave the region to make her way to Perseverance Mills, as well as the location of [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md). Astrid goes to the radio station to radio the Mills, but the equipment is unpowered. She sleeps, only to awake to the Aurora with the station powered. She attempts to get a message out but overhears the conversation between Mackenzie and the unknown 2 parties from Episode 2.

- Molly calls the Astrid for the final time, confirming that she has been the one killing the various Convicts in the region that Astrid has been finding ([Blackrock](./Blackrock%20%28mission%29.md)). She reveals in the killing, feeling more free than she's ever felt before, and embraces her new life as a killer in this new world.

- Astrid leaves Pleasant Valley as the whiteout blizzard envelops the region, and makes her way to [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md). She encounters a setback after an earthquake sends her to the lower level of the mine, but she ultimately escapes into Coastal Highway.
- Astrid comes across a dead Orca pod, and remarks that nature is changing due to the First Flare and the Aurora, and then continues her journey alone to Perseverance Mills.

- Will Mackenzie wakes up on a stretcher. His hands are tied and he is being carried by [Vachon](./Vachon.md) and [Heller](./Heller.md) through the woods in [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md). Mathis is in tow, with the Hardcase. [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) attack the group and Mackenzie escapes, before eventually being recaptured, knocked out again, and taken to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md).
- Vachon reveals that one of the Prison Bus inmates, LECLERC, Y.,[^144] was killed with an arrow shot through his chest. This was presumably Molly's work.

- Mackenzie awakes in a cell and is greeted by [Franklin](./Franklin.md), the warden of Blackrock, who reveals that after the First Flare the convicts took over the prison and executed most of the staff. They are only keeping him alive because they are attempting to release a prisoner named [Donner](./Donner.md) from the solitary wing of the facility, but cannot get in and believe that the warden is hiding information from them.
- Donnor is Mathis' son, and is even more psychotic than his father, serving a life sentence in the Prison as he cannot be returned to normal society.

- Mathis arrives with Vachon and Heller, with Mathis beating Franklin within an inch of his life, forcing Vachon and Heller to patch him up. They need medicine found outside the Prison's walls, and Mackenzie volunteers to risk his life to find it. Since the 2 convicts know that Mackenzie won't run away without Astrid's Hardcase, they reluctantly and secretly let the pilot loose without Mathis' approval, and Mackenzie finds the [Blackrock Infirmary Medication](./Blackrock%20Infirmary%20Medication.md) and administers it to Franklin. He then tells the warden that he met with a woman on the phone that is trying to help them both.

- Mackenzie encounters a [woman](./Jace.md) on the phone while searching for the medicine, actively working to thwart the convicts attempts to free Donnor. She questions what side Mackenzie is on, as he is helping the Convicts, but realizes that the pilot might be able to help her.
- Mackenzie's "prison break" is discovered by Mathis, who then puts the pilot to work to repair the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) to route power to solitary.
- The woman on the phone reveals her name is Jace when Mackenzie arrives at the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md), and orders him to sabotage the steam reactor, which he does.

- Mathis is now aware that there is a spy attempting to thwart his plans after the destruction of the steam reactor, and with the Steam Tunnels not powering solitary, he orders Mackenzie to find [Detonators](./Detonators.md) in the [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) mine.
- Mathis tortures and kills Franklin after Mackenzie leaves, with the warden leaking information about the alliance between Mackenzie and the woman on the phone in an attempt to save his own life.

- Mackenzie braves through the Last Prospect mine, and finds the Detonators. After ascending to the surface, he has another phone call with Jace, who reveals that she is a student of astrophysics that was driving to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) to meet her thesis professor [Atwood](./Atwood.md). Mackenzie reveals that he is also seeking Atwood to deliver a message to her.

- Jace also reveals that the [Suzuki Radio Telescope](./Suzuki%20Radio%20Telescope.md) is nearby the Mills, and that it is properly shielded from EMPs, meaning that anything electronic inside likely still works. She also stresses that Mathis and his Convicts cannot be allowed to get inside, as it has enough food, water, shelter, radios, working vehicles, and other resources that would allow the Convicts to rule the Island with an iron fist.

- Jace is aware that Mackenzie needs a his Hardcase from back Mathis, and will be delivering the Detonators to him. She reveals that her plans will now need to go "nuclear" as she has an ace up her sleeve.

- An earthquake destroys [Mule Bridge](./Mule%20Bridge.md) and collapses part of the mine, knocking Mackenzie out. When he awakes, Mackenzie sees the Aurora out and is forced to travel down river to the mine. He arrives at the Prison, seeing it powered again.
- Mackenzie returns to the prison and delivers the Detonators, with Mathis revealing that he killed Franklin and is aware that Mackenzie was attempting to thwart his plans.

- Mathis reveals that the only reason he kept Mackenzie alive was that he hoped that he could steal a working plane, but now desires to stay on Great Bear Island since civilization on the Mainland is likely ruined, and that Great Bear Island is the perfect isolated location to start his own kingdom in this quiet apocalypse.
- Mathis attempts to kill Mackenzie, but is interrupted by an explosion that rocks the Prison.

- Jace activates the prison lockdown, buying Mackenzie time, and reveals that her "nuclear" plan was to cause the prison to explode, as the Convicts blew the Detonators the wrong way. This allows Mackenzie to escape.
- Mackenzie recovers Astrid's Hardcase in the Warden's office, and has a phone call with Jace, telling him to meet her in the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md).
- Mackenzie flees through the courtyard, avoiding being shot by Convicts using powered searchlights, then flees through the now destroyed Steam Tunnels.
- Mackenzie and Jace meet at the Power Plant, and Mathis and his Convicts catch up to the two.
- Heller reveals that Donnor has been freed from solitary, but is badly wounded and dying. This news sends Mathis into a blind rage as he attempts to kill Mackenzie and Jace.
- Mackenzie and Jace escape through the Power Plant's river, washing ashore and freezing in the snow. They begin their journey to Atwood and Perseverance Mills.
- A post credits scene reveals that Astrid Greenwood has arrived at the port of Perseverance Mills via canoe.
- Two men[^145] approach her canoe, believing that she is a quarantine breaker, but realize she is not from the Mills.
- [Jane Yang](./Jane%20Yang.md) approaches Astrid, surprised to see Astrid alive but confused as to why she doesn't have the [Hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md).
### [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md)
- Mackenzie finds several notes from the residents of Milton who left behind 3 supply caches. He finds them and takes the contents for himself.
- Mackenzie finds several bank vault keys and uses them to open deposit boxes at Milton Credit Union.
- Mackenzie finds a note regarding a truck out near the highway with several supplies. He travels there and takes the contents of a trunk for himself.
- Mackenzie finds a [Winter Forecast](./Winter%20Forecast.md) that shows the winter will get much colder, and finds extra food and fuel for Grey Mother.
- Mackenzie finds several books teaching about survival skills, and learns how to mend clothing, safety pick medicinal plants, and snare a rabbit.
### [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md)
- Mackenzie finds a [Forest Talker Map Note](./Forest%20Talker%20Map%20Note.md) showing 3 supply caches, and finds them.
- Mackenzie finds 3 notes about supply caches left by other survivors, and finds them.
- Mackenzie finds a note in a supply cache about a special powered Prepper Cache, and loots it during the Aurora.

- Hank sent a [letter to his Niece](./Letter%20for%20Hank%27s%20Niece.md) Angela (and by extension her mother) to come find him and his Prepper Cache if things ever went wrong. Mackenzie finds the corpse of Angela and her mother by [Unnamed Pond](./Unnamed%20Pond.md) and outside Hank's hatch.

- Hank had been attacked by a wolf and locked his hatch, fearing the clawing from outside was more wolves. It was instead Angela, who froze to death outside (she was carrying [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md) and [Bandages](./Bandage.md) and could have kept Hank alive). Hank ultimately passed away from his wounds inside his bunker.

- 2 Forest Talkers at the [Logging Camp](./Logging%20Camp.md) travel to Mystery Lake to go fishing for food, but both are attacked. One perishes on the ice but the other escapes into a nearby cabin. Mackenzie arrives and offers to help the wounded Forest Talker, finding his [Forest Talker Supplies](./Forest%20Talker%20Supplies.md) and [Forest Talker Documents](./Forest%20Talker%20Documents.md). The fate of the man is unknown after this.

- The Forest Talkers were likely attacked by a [Breyerhouse](./Breyerhouse.md) worker finally taking revenge on the eco-terrorists, evidenced by the [Crumpled Note (2)](./Crumpled%20Note%20%282%29.md). If Mackenzie takes the man's ammo, he will be attacked after leaving the cabin the next day and perish.
- Mackenzie finds more books teaching about survival skills, and learns how to kill a stage, how to ice fish, and how to cull wolves.
### [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md)

- An unknown individual steals a [Church Artifact](./Church%20Artifact.md) from [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) Church, looking to sell it for cash out of desperation following The Collapse. It would remain stashed in the abandoned basement of [Skeeter's Ridge](./Skeeter%27s%20Ridge.md) for decades until Astrid finds and returns it to the Crossing's church.[^146]
- Astrid finds the remains of a Blackrock Prison Guard and follows a trail of dead convicts, until finding a Convict cache.
- Astrid finds several notes showing the thoughts of the Forest Talkers and Locals of Pleasant Valley.
- Astrid finds 4 different books written by T. A. Gurnsey, a local of Pleasant Valley, regarding sightings of supernatural/wonderous phenomena around the Valley.
- Astrid travels to [Pensive Pond](./Pensive%20Pond.md) and ice fishes the [Big Bass (Raw)](./Big%20Bass%20%28Raw%29.md).
- Astrid finds the so called "Sasquatch" inside a cave, and it was a man wearing a [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md).
- Astrid travels to [Misty Falls Picnic Area](./Misty%20Falls%20Picnic%20Area.md) and finds a cave inside. Deep within, she finds the so called lost cave.
- Astrid travels to [Three Strikes Farmstead](./Three%20Strikes%20Farmstead.md), and sees a very rare albino [Ghost Stag](./Ghost%20Stag.md).
- Astrid finds Molly's gift containing several [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md) to fend off Timberwolf attacks.

- Astrid finds a Prepper Cache from a local named Tom Joplin, and raids 3 of them, taking the resources and giving them to the Crash Survivors at the Community Hall. Tom Joplin is nowhere to be found.
### [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md)
- Mackenzie finds several lockers at the prison guard barracks and finds the keys to open them.
- Mackenzie finds several notes from Blackrock Prison administration, and follows the clues left behind.
- Mackenzie finds Murphy who had been panning for gold, and froze to death. He takes the man's [Lock Box Key](./Lock%20Box%20Key.md) and finds a [Gold Nugget](./Gold%20Nugget.md) in his lockbox.
- Mackenzie tracks down the aggressive wolf, and finds the remains of the dead animal researcher, killed by the very wolf he was trying to save.
- Mackenzie finds a hidden Prepper Cache in the region, stocked with supplies, but does not find the mysterious man that it belongs to.
- Mackenzie finds several Hidden Caches left behind by Convicts in the region, and loots them.
- Mackenzie finds 4 [Archival Reports](./Archival%20Report.md) detailing the early days of the Blackrock region.
- Mackenzie finds 2 dead Journeyman Electricians that had been working at the [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md).

- One worker, Linda Burnley, had shot herself with a Revolver, likely after finding out about the Convicts taking over [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), and chose to go out on her own terms.

- The other worker, Samual Franks, is found at the bottom of the ravine near Blackrock Prison. His corpse holds a backpack and [Lost Worker's Note](./Lost%20Worker%27s%20Note.md), and reveals that his mind had been going downhill before the First Flare, and that he had wandered off an frozen to death.
- Mackenzie finds several Forest Talker notes in the [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md) mine, and uses the codes to unlock a special Forest Talker supply cache at the entrance to the mine.

## [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md)

- A plane crash survivor begins traveling across Great Bear Island after their plane is brought down by a mysterious geomagnetic storm. They encounter no other survivors on the Island. The plane crash survivor ultimately is never able to escape Great Bear Island, and becomes one with it, struggling to survive by looting, crafting, and foraging as the days pass.
- All major NPCs from Wintermute/Islanders in general are missing in the world at this point in time. Only [frozen corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) remain.

- [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), [Mule Bridge](./Mule%20Bridge.md), the entrance to [Last Prospect](./Last%20Prospect.md), and the [Steam Tunnels](./Steam%20Tunnels.md) lie in ruins, suggesting that this world takes place after Episode 4.
- They uncover the secrets of the past that occurred in the Far Territory, as part of the [Tales](./Tales.md) missions.

- [Rüdiger's Machine](./R%C3%BCdiger%27s%20Machine.md) does not fully destroy the mind of the survivor when they come into contact with [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) for prolonged periods of time, instead only giving them temporary [Insomnia](./Insomnia.md). This confirms that The Security Chief did damage the machine just enough so that it does not destroy the minds of anyone unfortunate enough to come into the Far Territory.
- The Machine also begins storing energy from the Aurora at night and expends energy during the day, producing Glimmer Fog in the Far Territory once more.

- After a number of days of surviving in this new world, an Aurora powers a yellow radio with a transceiver and a voice speaks over the radio, the [Trader](./Trader.md). This begins [Sutherland's Tale](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md).

- The Trader is the only other living human the plane crash survivor finds. He hints that he has a theory as to where everyone went, but ultimately teases the survivor with this info without revealing his theory.

- After performing a few trades between each other, the Trader reveals his name to be Sutherland to the survivor, and asks for some special favors to find his brother Wyatt, while also displaying several memory issues.

- He reveals that he had a sudden urge to head to open water during the First Flare, and that he sometimes wanders into deeper waters before snapping back to reality. He seems to be afflicted to whatever mental disease is occurring in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md).

- The survivor scours the Island for [Prepper Caches](./Prepper%20Cache.md) for signs of Sutherland's brother. Most bunkers are abandoned, but 3 of them are stocked and contain hidden document stashes that help reveal clues surrounding his brother's disappearance.

- The survivor eventually finds Wyatt's remains in a 4th Prepper Cache in Pleasant Valley and delivering him to Sutherland. Sutherland suddenly remembers that Wyatt has been dead for many years this whole time, and asks the survivor to return his brother to rest and to seal the cache where he was found.

- Sutherland would continue to stay off the coast of the Island and continue trading with the plane crash survivor after gaining their full trust. Sutherland is unable to escape the Island to the Mainland due to currents and weather preventing his sailboat from leaving the coastline, and survives off of scavenging shipwrecks and debris floating in the open waters.

- Eventually, after surviving alone for an indeterminate amount of time (possibly for hundreds of days, or perhaps years), the plane crash survivor fades away into The Long Dark (either due to hostile wildlife attacks, disease, lack of food/water, or falling from a great height).
These events are found on various computers, and occur before the First Flare, but at unknown times.
- [Camp Office](./Camp%20Office.md) - Someone writes reports regarding wildlife activity around Mystery Lake and sends them to an unknown party.
- [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md) - Anika Longmire, Female, 41, writes about her life in Milton.
- [Milton Post Office](./Milton%20Post%20Office.md) - Chris writes a series of diary entries regarding life in the post office.
- [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) - Peter Good writes about inventory in the gas station. Contacts the owner of [Rural Store](./Rural%20Store.md) Dan Presnell.

- [Chasm Cave](./Chasm%20Cave.md) - Robbie, a survivor from the [Timberwolf Mountain Plane Crash](./Tail%20Section.md), writes a diary from before and after the crash, but ultimately dies in the cave.
- [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) - Several emails from the workers of the Carter Dam regarding its maintenance before it was abandoned in the 1990s.
- [Fishing Camp](./Fishing%20Camp.md)/[Rabbit Grove](./Rabbit%20Grove.md) - A local fishermen's diary regarding fishing and the state of his ship/equipment.
- [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) - Barbara Quincy, Garage Owner, Female, 62, recounts her experiences as the gas station owner.

- [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md) - Name Unknown, Lighthouse Keeper, Male, 41. Recounts maintaining the lighthouse. A a traveler from the [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) flees to the lighthouse due to the realities of The Collapse.
- [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md) - Manny Douglas becomes stranded on Great Bear Island after DeepForest Experience inserts him on the Island and does not extract him.

- [Maintenance Shed](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) - Emails by Jerry Baltimore, Male, 29, recounts how [Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md) continue to harass Breyerhouse employees and destroy their equipment
- [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) - A Breyerhouse medic responds to a Wolf attack on a worker out in [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md).
- [Shortwave Tower](./Shortwave%20Tower.md) - Partner Specialist 81926 performs maintenance on the Shortwave Tower in the Muskeg as per a contract, despite the danger of the remote area.
- He was contracted by workers of the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) to fix the [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md).
- He eventually is chased into The Ravine and later the mountains above Bleak Inlet by hostile wildlife. ([Communication Report](./Communication%20Report.md))

- He eventually runs out of food and makes it to the Cannery, creating the obstacle course that leads to the [Workshop](./Workshop.md). They eventually make it inside and lock the door, though a wolf is locked inside with them. ([The Technician's Notebook](./The%20Technician%27s%20Notebook.md))
- [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) - Sarah Easton, Female, 29 writes a journal as she comments on working in the radio tower, as well as events occurring in Pleasant Valley.

- [Rural Crossroads](./Rural%20Store.md) - Dan Presnell, Shopkeeper, Male, 57 sends emails to Mainland suppler Mr. Galveston requesting more complete shipments of food staples that the Pleasant Valley community is dependent on. He also emails about their ATM being discontinued and [Tom Joplin](./Joplin%27s%20Bunker%20Raid.md).

A **Tin of Coffee** is a [drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) which can be brewed into a [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md) at a [Fire](./Fire.md) with [potable water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md). Consuming the cup of coffee will restore 10% of the survivor's [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), add some hydration and 100 calories, and provide the [Fatigue Reduced](./Fatigue%20Reduced.md) benefit, making this item very useful when exploring regions with lots of [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) or when trying to [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md).

Tins of Coffee can be found in all difficulty levels, though they may be difficult to find in Interloper. There are several (up to 10) tins in the [Cargo Containers](./Cargo%20Container.md) around [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), specifically in the [Echo Ravine](./Echo%20Ravine.md) and at the [Summit](./Summit.md). Aside from that, Tins of Coffee are most commonly found in kitchens of houses, where they may spawn on countertops or in the cabinets. [Filing Cabinets](./File%20Cabinet.md) are also a relatively reliable source of coffee. Coffee may also occasionally be found in [Metal Containers](./Metal%20Container.md), which can be found in cabins and trailers.

- [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md), [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md), and [Signal Hill](./Signal%20Hill.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md),
- [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), and
Each of these locations will usually yield at least one or two tins, even on harder difficulties.

**Tin of Sardines** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Consuming a Tin of Sardines provides up to 300 calories of [energy](./Hunger.md) and 5% [hydration](./Thirst.md), and weighs a mere 0.10kg. They can be found commonly in all regions, usually inside cabinets, houses, stores and [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md) and especially in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) inside the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md). Tin of Sardines are a modestly energy-dense food item. However, they have a high chance of [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md) if consumed below 50% of the item's Condition, increased further below 30% condition, though not as high a chance as low condition cooked meat.
Unlike other canned goods, thanks to their pull-tab Tin of Sardines can opened without a [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md), however consuming them yields no [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md).

The Last Resort Cannery in Bleak Inlet has a substantial stock of Tins of Sardines in various states of decay. Their abundance in crates suggests outbound shipping slowed or stopped before the production line halted.
Tin of Sardines can cause Food Poisoning, elevated at low item condition, and [decays](./Decay.md) more slowly when indoors.
- Tin of Sardines are packaged as a product called "_Last Resort"_, a product of the titular "Last Resort Cannery" in Bleak Inlet.
- The bottom of the tin list "Ingredients: Sardines, Water, Salt." and "Made in Canada"
- The Examine text is likely a reference to the Stan Rogers song 'Tiny Fish for Japan'

> “**A small plug or bundle of flammable material (paper, wool, cloth, dry bark or needles, etc.) required to start a fire.**”

Tinder plugs fill the role of tinder, which is used for [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md). Tinder plugs are the lightest tinder, tied with the [Cat Tail Head](./Cat%20Tail%20Head.md), [Birch Bark](./Birch%20Bark.md), and [Cash](./Cash.md), and weighs only 0.05 kg per unit. Like all other types of tinder, it does not increase the chance to successfully light a fire.
Tinder or Tinder plugs are required until Fire Starting Level 3, at which point they become optional and generally only used to get rid of the item.

Tinder plugs can be found inside containers, crafted from most forms of tinder, or harvested from a [Cardboard Box](./Cardboard%20Box.md). At least one is also given along with firewood when chopping a fir or cedar limb with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) or [Hacksaw.](./Hacksaw.md)

**To SAR And Back** is the only mission of Part Three: Do No Harm in [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story of [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).
After the cutscene and talk about the locomotive, climb the locomotive and examine it's dashboard. You need to find the throttle lever.

Walk towards the Train Maintenance Shed (Astrid will look that way and comment on it). The door on the first floor, both the front and side ones, are locked. Looking above, you may notice a hole in the roof leading to the catwalk.

Go past maintenance shed, heading north. On your left, there will be an easy to miss climbing area with a Frozen Corpse in front of it. The corpse will provide you with two [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), a regular [Flare](./Flare.md), and a [Windbreaker](./Windbreaker.md). Climb the climbing area, and follow the path. Go over the log and climb onto the maintenance shed roof. There is an aforementioned hole on the roof through which you can descend onto the catwalk. You can loot a corpse up here and a metal container for some Ketchup Chips, another Marine Flare, and a pair of Wool Mittens. You can also find another Marine Flare by the collapsed stairs, aswell as a backpack and a Jerry Can. After looting, follow the catwalk to the unlocked door, heading inside.

The handle is at the lower floor in the workshop room on the display wall. You can find a Flare Pistol aswell as a few rounds in the room to your immediate right. Take it and go back to the locomotive. Enter it, put the lever back and the light up the locomotive's firebox. Now, you can drive it. You need the temperature in the firebox to reach at least 170 C° (or 225 F°) for it to go to full speed (red on the speedometer). You will need that speed to break through obstacles, such as fences, snowbanks, and fallen logs. Before you leave the shed, make sure to brew some coffee or ensure you have some form of stimulant on you, as Astrid is unable to sleep during this mission.

The next phase is traveling to SAR. You will need to fight the wolves on your way down, though they cannot attack you while inside the Steam Engine, You must also gather coal to keep the firebox hot, and to keep the engine moving. You can find coal scattered occasionaly on the side of the line, but at most stops you can find at least one or two coal bins.
- First, you will arrive at Railyard 1. Adjust the switches for the right-most track and keep going.
- Second, you will encounter a siding next to the Collapsed Tunnel, ramming the flatbed and switching the tracks back to the main track is all you need to do.
- Third, you will encounter the Rail Junction. First, ram the Truck on the line and adjust the switch to follow the main track. After, switch the line again to avoid going down the dead end siding.

When you finally reach the final station, the train will eventually lock in it's location, focring you to go to the right (eastwards) along side the trail road to reach the SAR Station. The trauma medical equipment is inside the helicopter next to the SAR building itself.
Return to the Steam Locomotive and use the wye to turn the locomotive in the opposite direction. On your way back, you will return to the Rail Juction and be forced into following the second line.

You will encounter two stops along the way, in the form of Railyard 2 and the Derelict Siding. By this point, the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) will active, resulting in the wolves becoming more agressive and less fearful of the train's whistle.
- For the Derelict Siding, simply adjust the switch to avoid heading down the dead end.

**To the Teeth** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is easiest to unlock when playing on [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md), and cannot be unlocked on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) or [Misery](./Misery.md). The player must also have the [Trader](./Trader.md) enabled for one of the Hunting Rifles.
(WARNING : Playing on a survival save started prior of the DLC release can glitch the DLC rifles and replace them with a regular hunting rifle if the region has already been visited on the save.)
The player must find and pick up, at least once, all 7 firearm variants of the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) and [Revolver](./Revolver.md) in a single game:
- [Vaughn's Rifle](./Vaughn%27s%20Rifle.md) - somewhere in [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) or outside the Dam in [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md)
- [Forester's Revolver](./Forester%27s%20Revolver.md) -somewhere in the mountains in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md)

A **Toaster** is a harvestable item found in the homes of many kitchen countertops. It requires a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) to harvest and yields 1 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) after 15 minutes of sawing.

There are two types of toilets: those with and without a toilet cistern (reservoir tank). Regardless of the type, toilets initially contain 1.5 to 2 liters of [Water (Potable)](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), (or about 0.39gal to 0.52gal). This water will not replenish, and the tank/bowl cannot be refilled once taken (However it can still be selected despite being empty).

Toilets can be found in houses and other indoors structures such as the [Quonset Gas Station](./Quonset%20Garage.md). Other buildings such as small cabins, trailers, or remote structures (e.g., [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md), [Lonely Lighthouse](./Lonely%20Lighthouse.md)) do not have them.
- In real life, drinking water from a toilet's bowl would be dangerous due to harmful pathogens; however, water from a toilet's cistern would be as safe to drink as tap water.

**Tomato Soup** is a packaged [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _The Long Dark_.

Consuming Tomato Soup restores a small amount of calories and hydration, it has relatively low energy density, making it heavy for the calories it provides. It may also be warmed by a [fire](./Fire.md) to grant the benefit [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md).

Like other canned foods, Tomato Soup may be opened with a [Can Opener](./Can%20Opener.md) or [bladed tool](./Tools.md), or smashed open (with no tool) but spilling some of it's contents. If opened with a tool a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md) is received after consuming the contents.
- The ingredients on the back list: "Tomatoes, Water, Salt." and that it is a "Product of Canada."

**Too Big to Fail** is a [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This is a side mission achievement that is acquired after opening every locked [Deposit Box](./Deposit%20Box.md) in the [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md). The side mission [Milton Safety Deposit Box Keys](./Milton%20Safety%20Deposit%20Box%20Keys.md) keeps track of each key needed.

- _[Bank Deposit Box Key #7](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%207.md)_ is located inside a house on the main road between the [Post Office](./Milton%20Post%20Office.md) and the [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md), in a plastic container underneath the bed. The house is across the main road from the [Bank Manager's House](./Bank%20Manager%27s%20House.md). Note there is another house in between them. Box contains [cash](./Cash.md) and 2 [flare shells](./Flare%20Shell.md).

- _[Bank Deposit Box Key #13](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2013.md)_ is located on a corpse near the frozen river between [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) and [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md). Follow the stream downhill directly behind the gas station. Right before the slight bend turn left up the slope and The corpse will be directly ahead. The crows circling above the corpse should make locating it easier; If walking downstream, the crows can be seen circling above on the lefthand side of the river. Box contains [balaclava](./Balaclava.md), [book](./Book.md), [ski gloves](./Ski%20Gloves.md) and [stack of papers](./Stack%20of%20Papers.md).

- _[Bank Deposit Box Key #20](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2020.md)_ is located behind [Orca Gas Station](./Orca%20Gas%20Station.md) in a blue pickup truck parked on the trail leading to the climbing area. The truck is next to two port-a-potties. Box contains [magnifying lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) and 2 [cash](./Cash.md).

- [Bank Deposit Box Key #15](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2015.md) is located in the farm house. The key can be found next to [Hobbs](./Hobbs.md) immediately after the interaction with him, regardless of the outcome chosen. This is the only key that is necessary to progress through the story, as Bank Deposit Box #15 holds a plot-sensitive item.

- The achievement's name is a reference to the phrase "Too big to fail" in reference to several large banks or corporations that are kept afloat with emergency government bail outs (hence why they are too big to fail naturally).

- The most notable usage of this phrase was in 2008 during the housing market collapse, an event that caused the Great Recession. The effects of this recession seem to be far worse in the world of _The Long Dark_, as seen with [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md).
- The name is also ironic, seeing how the [Milton Credit Union](./Milton%20Credit%20Union.md) closed down long before Will Mackenzie first enters it.

**Too Greedily, too Deep** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

The player must survive within the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) for 25 days straight without leaving once. Doing so will require a large amount of stockpiled [food](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) and [water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) and a dedicated place to sleep with a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md). Water can be produced inside the mine in a few locations where a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md) can be found, but food must be brought inside the mine to survive. Consider using the [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md) method to speed up time and save food.
Using the elevator shaft to visit a lower section of the mine or going topside will reset achievement progress, so consider going to the lowest level and staying put.

This achievement is much harder (though not impossible) to unlock on [Stalker](./Stalker.md), [Interloper](./Interloper.md), and [Misery](./Misery.md), as these difficulties increase the survivor's [Needs](./Needs.md) drain and also gives the survivor [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md) after 5 days, making it impossible to pass time or sleep once afflicted. You can choose to do any action to forward time (e.g. tear clothes and cancel), however since you are unable to sleep, you will slowly lose health. To counter this, consider bringing caffeine or health buff consumables. Alternatively, you can choose the Settled Mind [feat](./Feats.md) when starting your run to avoid Cabin Fever altogether.

- This achievement's name is a reference to the lore surrounding the Langston Mining Corporation and [Rüdiger's Machine](./R%C3%BCdiger%27s%20Machine.md) in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md).
- It is also an [Easter Egg](./Easter%20Eggs.md) reference to the Lord of the Rings (another being the [Spelunker's Lantern](./Spelunker%27s%20Lantern.md) description).

- The achievement name is derived from this quote: **Saruman: "**Moria... You fear to go into those mines. The dwarves delved too greedily and too deep. You know what they awoke in the darkness of Khazad-dum... shadow and flame."

A **Torch** is a craftable tool that creates light and a small amount of heat, adding +3°C to your "Feels Like" temperature. If more than one is dropped on the ground (at your feet) while burning, the warmth bonus they provide stacks, unless a fire is nearby, in which case it overrides the warmth from torches.

Torches are a mobile light source the can be ignited anywhere with either [Wood Matches](./Wood%20Matches.md), [Cardboard Matches](./Cardboard%20Matches.md), or a [Firestriker](./Firestriker.md). They can also be ignited with a pre-existing [Fire](./Fire.md), such as from an active Firebox, or even another lit Torch, [Flare](./Flare.md), or [Marine Flare](./Marine%20Flare.md) (the later being a process known as [Daisy Chaining](./Daisy%20Chaining.md)).

The Torch works like a [Flare](./Flare.md), lighting up the surrounding area and possibly scaring away [Wolves](./Wolf.md), although it's less reliable than a Flare. If you're carrying a lit Torch, a Wolf will run up to you and stand a short distance away, similar to a fire. Throwing a lit Torch at a Wolf sometimes causes the Wolf to flee, but they will more likely overcome their fear of the Torch if your [Scent](./Scent.md) is too high or an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) is out (in which case a [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) is better suited to scaring Wolves).

A lit Torch can be extinguished for later use and can be re-lit when the weather is calm enough, or indoors, by equipping it with the '1' key or from inventory, then pressing the left mouse button and selecting a match or Firestriker. Keep in mind that even if the Torch isn't lit with your match or Firestriker, it will still consume a match or condition if you start the process of lighting it and cancel out. Therefore some players like to only have a Torch equipped when they need it, in order to not accidentally waste matches or condition. Another way to not waste matches is to carry multiple types of firestarting items (excluding the magnifying lense), so that an accidental click brings up the selection screen instead.

Unlike the Flare or Storm Lantern, Torches cannot be lit in overly windy [Weather](./Weather.md), and their flames will burn out if winds become too harsh. Torches can also become extinguished if walking through a waterfall.

In more difficult game modes, where matches are much less common, a good practice is to start all fires by first lighting a Torch and then using the burning Torch to light the fire. If the attempt fails, just try again. This eliminates the chance of wasting a match on a failed fire-starting attempt.

Another technique to save matches and to preserve [Condition](./Condition.md) and [Warmth](./Warmth.md) is to practice [Daisy Chaining](./Daisy%20Chaining.md), whereas a player pulls out multple Torches out of a fire and then uses a lit one to keep warm in their travels. As that Torch dies out, toss it on the ground and use a new Torch to pass the flame to your new Torch, thus chaining the flame.

A **guaranteed** way to scare off a Wolf is to throw or place a lit Torch or Flare on the ground, standing closely behind it, and aim any weapon, including stones, at the Wolf. The animal will charge at you, stop at a few meters distance in front of the Torch, and then flee. This trick is fundamental to survive on Interloper difficulty, and very helpful in the beginning of any game.
Pulling torches out of a lit fire and throwing them at [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md) is a **very effective** strategy to deplete pack morale and scare off the pack.

**Torn Clothing** is a minor [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) that can be encountered in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. Torn Clothing is the only Affliction that is indirectly linked to the player's overall wellbeing, affecting their Clothing rather than their body or mind.

Torn Clothing is an Affliction that is often paired with [Bruising](./Minor%20Bruising.md) and [Lacerations](./Laceration.md), and is mainly acquired through Falls and [Struggles](./Struggle.md) with hostile wildlife. When acquired, it results in an audible fabric tearing sound, followed by multiple pieces of the player's outermost layer of [Clothing](./Clothing.md) losing a percentage of its overall condition value. The same percentage is applied to every piece of affected clothing. The clothing affected depends on the affliction source.

Falling from a significant height will result in the player's outermost legs and feet clothing being torn from the weight of the impact. It is advised to practice [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md) in order to avoid being injured while attempting to scale down mountain or hill sides with large drops.

**Tough Enough** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is easiest to unlock in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) when playing on [Voyageur](./Voyageur.md), as [Cougars](./Cougar.md) are disabled on [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md) and higher Experiences cause more Condition damage to the player from [Struggles](./Struggle.md). The player must enable the Cougar in their survival run and survive long enough for them to start spawning in the game world, then survive 25 Struggles with a Cougar.
The requirements to unlock this achievement necessitates the player being fully overwhelmed by the Cougar for progress to count. A Cougar has 2 different attack patterns:

- A "Glancing Blow" attack occurs when the Cougar swipes a weapon from the player's hand and runs away, causing small Condition damage. This attack is not counted as a Struggle and is not tracked by the game.

- A Struggle occurs when the player is fully overwhelmed by a Cougar and a cutscene occurs. The player will wake up with [Severe Lacerations](./Severe%20Lacerations.md) and major [Condition](./Condition.md) damage.
- Progress is tracked across multiple Survival Mode save files, and it does not need to be done in a single game.

- This achievement is one of the hardest to unlock in the game, and thus requires great patience and planning. A guide to hunting and surviving Cougar encounters (including using proper [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) to heal from [Severe Lacerations](./Severe%20Lacerations.md)) can be found [Here](./Cougar.md#Hunting).

violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Town of Milton**_

Founded in 1911 during the early rush to mine coal in the surrounding mountains, Milton went through a boom/bust cycle throughout the 1900s, at one point peaking at about 1000 residents. In the 2000s, it settled into the 100s, and Post-Collapse, the population has struggled to remain in the low double digits. Originally built along a supply route from the coastline leading into the interior, the old dirt path was replaced by a paved highway in 1960. It’s location about halfway between Port Mary and the interior mountains gave it a natural advantage as a convenient stopping off point for fuel and supplies for miners, loggers, mill workers, and campers from the Mainland, a dynamic that fueled the town’s growth as the Island’s economy boomed in the 1980s. However, the construction of the Great Bear Highway (AKA Highway 15) meant travellers could easily bypass Milton on their way North, which in many ways triggered the gradual decline of Milton’s importance as a gateway town.

This decline was exaggerated even more in the Post-Collapse economic environment, where very few travelers or resource workers had reason to visit Great Bear. Eventually, apart from a few stalwarts and old-timers with deep roots in the area, Milton became, for all intents and purposes, a ghost town.
- Added to game.

The **Toxic Fog** is a feature included in the [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) mode of [The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

During Escape the Darkwalker, every [Region](./Region.md) in the game is given a timer of a certain amount of minutes dependent on the size of the region, counted in real-time. Once the timer reaches zero, the entire region will fill with fog. As more time is spent in the region, visibility gradually decreases. While there are no blizzards, this can be a navigational hazard as the mode is set to night for the entire duration of the playthrough. There is no way to remove this fog once it appears. Before it descends, there is a timer on the map that is visible at all times. This can be seen in the 'map' section of the menus.

While there is no way to remove the fog, it is possible to delay its onset with a glyph from a can of [Spray Paint - Glyph](./Spray%20Paint%20-%20Glyph.md). However, this glyph may only be drawn once per playthrough.
- When the fog descends, all [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) will immediately be killed, both passive and aggressive. The Darkwalker will not be killed.
- When the fog descends, all [Food and Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) will immediately rot to 0% condition, and will provide 0 calories.
- If killed by the fog, the ending screen will state you have been killed by the Darkwalker.
- When the fog warning in the HUD reaches 2 minutes, it will show up as a red symbol and the effects of the fog immediately start causing harm to condition, wildlife and food.
**Categories:** DLC Content, Interactable Objects, Story items, Wintermute · **Source:** [Fandom](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/Track_Switch)

**Track Switches** are stationary interactable objects in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md), that are only found on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md), and [Wintermute Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md).

**Track Switches** are levers found near junctions on useable railway tracks. They allow the direction of the [Steam Train](./Steam%20Train.md) and the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md) to be changed.

On top of the switch is a long pole with a yellow and red arrow. This arrow points in the direction the switch is set, allowing the Survivor to see which way the train will head from some distance. When the switch is thrown, the arrow will rotate to indicate the new direction, and the tracks on the switch will also move to direct the train in the new direction.

A good way to tell which way the train will move at a glance is to pay attention to the lever itself instead of the arrows. Rather than straining your eyes on the small arrows, see which side the lever itself is on. If it is on the left, the train will move left and vice versa for the right.

Other track switches exist on the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md), such as near [Indolent Hoppers](./Indolent%20Hoppers.md) and [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md), but these can't be interacted with and are purely decorative.

![Tractor](../assets/Tractor.jpg) **Tractors** are interactable [vehicle](./Vehicle.md) objects found near farms and garages, such as the [Pleasant Valley Outbuildings](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Outbuildings.md), [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md), and [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md).

The rarest of vehicles on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), tractors have been rendered useless by the [aurora](./Aurora.md), and now serve as an uncommon reminder of humanity's past technological achievements. Much like all vehicles, tractors can be used as temporary shelters from the wind and predators, but are risky to sleep in due to a lack of insulation.

Unlike [cars](./Car.md) and [trucks](./Truck.md), the hood and fuel panels cannot be opened, and there is obviously no trunk. Sun visors are also missing from tractors, meaning that [Mementos](./Mementos.md) will not spawn inside them. When an aurora is active, the tractors lights will flicker back to life.

Snacks like [Candy Bars](./Chocolate%20Bar.md) or [Sodas](./Soda%20%28disambiguation%29.md) are very common food items found inside the floors of tractors. Common crafting items such as [cloth](./Cloth.md) may also spawn, as may unique items (e.g., a key to the Paradise Meadows Farmhouse) on rare occasions. Due to a lack of an interactable hood, a [vehicle battery](./Car%20Battery.md) cannot be obtained from tractors.

**A source of rare goods and useful information, for a price.** Official Hinterland Description

The **Trader** is an NPC that "appears" in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). He may be contacted via Radio to propose bartering for items, and functions as a source of renewable items if the player has the resources to trade with him. The Trader was released in the Part 6 Broken Silence update for the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion.

A man known as Sutherland, the Trader communicates with the survivor over Radios during an active [Aurora](./Aurora.md). He will offer the survivor rare or unique items for a price, and requires his requested trade items to be placed inside the [Trade Drop Box](./Trade%20Drop%20Box.md) on [Misanthrope's Island](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md) in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md). The Trader becomes accessible after a fixed number of days have passed (determined by chosen Experience).

Despite being the only living NPC in Survival Mode, The Trader is never physically seen and will always keep his distance, remaining at sea in a sailboat and refusing to set foot on Great Bear Island except to complete trades.

- [Jerry Cans](./Jerry%20Can.md) are **not returned** if over the kg limit when used to trade their [Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md).

- An unlimited number of trades can be performed in one night, provided the items are available and the Aurora does not end. Sutherland will only offer the same selection of items on the same night, minus items already traded (i.e. he will not rotate the stock on offer until the next aurora night).
- Reloading your save file will reset the list of items that Sutherland offers for trade, as long as no trades have already been completed that night (see above).
- Gaining a certain level of Trust gives a slight permanent discount on trading requirements.

The Trader requires building up Trust in order to unlock most of his stock. The player starts with 0 Trust and each successful trade adds a certain amount of Trust, depending on the experience mode (this stat is hidden, so consider keeping track of completed trades in the General Notes section of the [Journal](./Journal.md)).
- Reaching a set amount of Trust (350) with Sutherland gives a discount to most items when trading.
- Trust can be lost by cancelling trades or by contacting Sutherland repeatedly. If Trust is lost, fully completing trades will slowly build up good will to restore lost Trust.
- Reaching 500 Trust will unlock the [Achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) [Goods and Services](./Goods%20and%20Services.md).

Every successful, completed trade increases Trust by a set amount, based on the players experience mode (see table below). The quantity of items traded does not matter, so long as the trade is completed. This means it doesn't matter if you trade 10 different items at a time or just 1, you will receive the same amount of Trust regardless. Completing a Special Request will also increase Trust by a set amount.

Trust can also be lost by repeatedly cancelling an active trade, or by repeatedly contacting Sutherland more than three times in one night (unless it is to start a new trade or signal a completed trade).
| Experience Mode | Complete Trade | Partial Trade | Cancelled Trade Penalty | Completed Special Request | Repeated Contact Penalty |

It is advisable to finish all available conversation options with the Trader as this will also raise Trust by a small amount (2 Trust per conversation).

Only a certain amount of items is available for purchase at start. Additional items are unlocked and made available for trade at certain Trust thresholds (see table below). Note: Once an additional item has been unlocked, it will stay unlocked even if you later lose Trust and go below that threshold.

After 100 Trust is reached, Sutherland will ask for a special request which starts the special requests section of his Tale and unlocks new conversation options that are shown in blue color. Completing a special request raises his Trust in the player and unlocks special items for trade.

- Speaking to the Trader reveals more about him, with more [Conversations](./Sutherland%27s%20Tale.md#Conversations) being unlocked as you raise his Trust:

- He seems to be afflicted with whatever disease is affecting the residents of [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), as well as [Patient 7](./Patient%207.md), [The Foreman](./The%20Foreman.md), [Dr. Rüdiger](./Dr.%20R%C3%BCdiger.md), and [The Security Chief](./The%20Security%20Chief.md), which causes them to forget things and become fixated on open water.

- One major example of a memory recall problem is that he hasn't heard from his brother Wyatt since the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md), despite the fact that he should know that his brother died long ago. His brother's death is also one of the major reasons why Sutherland has a deep seeded resentment to strangers and is so slow to trust others.

- Sutherland mentions that the radios the survivor uses to communicate from him are from an old emergency messaging system meant to keep Islanders in contact with one another. The "[A page from an old newsletter.](./A%20page%20from%20an%20old%20newsletter..md)" note also explains why these radios are found across the Island.

- He is a Great Bear Island native born in Coastal Highway, being the titular "Misanthrope" that lived at [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md). Sutherland, along with his "Pa" and brother Wyatt, lived there for most of their lives. Sutherland eventually states that he has abandoned his home and is more comfortable on his boat, saying that the survivor can do as they please with his house during the Quiet Apocalypse.

- It is revealed that his brother Wyatt is the one who created all of the [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md) bunkers across the island, including [Joplin's Bunkers](./Joplin%27s%20Bunker%20Raid.md). Though not confirmed, he most like created [Hank's Hatch](./Hank%27s%20Hatch.md), the [Aurora Hatch](./Aurora%20Hatch.md), and the hatch in [Blackrock Rumours](./Blackrock%20Rumours.md) - Suspicious Person as well.
- His reasoning was the belief that a nuclear exchange was coming that would destroy the world, confirming that the caches were fallout shelters.
- 3 other people were a part of Wyatt's crew, but ultimately turned on him due to paranoia.

- Sutherland has been at sea for a long time, and refuses to set foot on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) except to briefly complete trades. His sailboat can be seen off-shore on the morning after completing a trade in [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md).

- He mentions that his sailboat cannot escape Great Bear Island to the Mainland as his vessel would never survive the journey. Blizzards also keep his ship close to shore and the winds he catches only allow him to sail around the coast.
- The Trader also mentions that he acquires his wares from shipwrecks, floating containers, and things drifting around the sea.

- The Trader has a crippled leg that locks up on him in winter. He received it while at sea after heavy cables came loose on a ship and almost took his leg clean off. This information is conflicted moments later, with Sutherland mentioning that it might have instead have had something to do with his brother Wyatt.
- Sutherland's leg is the one of the reasons why Wyatt's crew turned on him and lead to his death.
- Through trading with the Trader, many previously non-renewable items become renewable; most notably [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md) and [Cooking](./Cooking.md) ingredients.
- The Trader is the only other living human in _The Long Dark's_ [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), with all other humans being [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) or skeletal remains.
- He hints that he has a theory as to where everyone went, but ultimately teases the survivor with this info without revealing his theory.

- How Sutherland survives on a small sailboat for so long is a mystery. How he prepares raw meat to become edible or what he does with so many Car Batteries is ultimately left to the player's imagination. It is presumed that he mainly survives off of what he scavenges from the sea, considering how much food he constantly offers up in trades and the fact that he allows for trades to last indefinitely, even when asking for raw food/water.

- Another question that has been raised is how his radio is powered during Glimmer Fog, as this fog only appears and effects electronics in the Far Territory. As it is currently impossible for the fog to reach the sea and power his radio, this may be an oversight from the developers.
- ![Goods and Services icon](../assets/Goods_and_Services_icon.png) [Goods and Services](./Goods%20and%20Services.md) - Reach maximum Trust with the Trader
