**Windproof bonus:** [Windproofness icon](../assets/Windproofness_icon.png)1.0 °C(1.8 °F)
> “**Rugged leather hiking boot. Designed to last for long-distance journeys on rocky terrain. Leather upper and heavy rubber sole.**”

Trail Boots are low-tier footwear and provide very little warmth for their weight, but decent protection against struggles and water. They are relatively easy to find, and are a common early game upgrade when clothing weight and mobility is less important but protection against predators is pivotal.

From a warmth perspective they are not much better than [Leather Shoes](./Leather%20Shoes.md) and [Running Shoes](./Running%20Shoes.md). Trail Boots weigh twice as much and only give a very small extra [windproofing](./Survival%20Overlay.md) compared to them.
Counterintuitively, while bulkier and heavier than similar footwear they only require 1 [cured leather](./Cured%20Leather.md) to repair, but also only yield 1 cured leather when harvested.
The Trailer is a location found in the western area of [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), on the western bank of the flowing river on the road to the [Power Plant](./Power%20Plant.md).

This trailer is the only guaranteed indoors location in this area; the only other ones are the Power Plant and [Old Substation](./Old%20Substation.md), with the trailer being right in the middle of them. It allows for shelter if the survivor is surprised by the timber wolf pack from the [Grand Meadow](./Grand%20Meadow.md) and is unable to escape Northwards. The trailer features several containers as well as a bed and [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) scavenging opportunities. There are two pieces of [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) spawning at the nearest power pole, along with a wolf/deer carcass spawning nearby.
- Small amount of miscellaneous food and first aid supplies in containers, as well as a few pieces of [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md).

It is a safe place to hunt the [Moose](./Moose.md) nearby and the [Bear](./Bear.md) of [Spruce Falls Bridge](./Spruce%20Falls%20Bridge.md). There is a lot of wood to make fire in front of the building, and a [Deer](./Deer.md) may also venture near the mobile home, and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) nest in the field nearby. The area is also free of [Wolves](./Wolf.md), making it a decent option for a base camp. Inside, there's also a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), and out back, there's a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md).
It is the last human-made structure before entering [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), as well as the closest workbench to said region.

An isolated shelter that was used by Alice McLeod to hide the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md). This location is the only marked location on the entire map.

![TrainShuttle](../assets/TrainShuttle.jpg) **Train Shuttles** are a stationary [Vehicle](./Vehicle.md) found at various points along the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md). Train Shuttle Cars provide temporary shelter and possible loot spawns. They contain a single door that can be opened and closed. While the inside lacks a warmth bonus compared to caves or buildings, they do provide a windshield bonus if stepped inside. They make for poor shelters, but they can often be used to prevent hostile Wolves from attacking the player by simply walking inside and closing the door on them as they approach.

Shuttle Cars can serve as temporary outdoor shelters to sleep in if a player has a Bedroll, though their lack of warmth must be taken into consideration before they are slept in, in order to prevent freezing to death of a player sleeps for long periods of time.

Shuttles often contain [Clothing](./Clothing.md), [Research Books](./Research%20Book.md), [Leather](./Cured%20Leather.md), [Cloth](./Cloth.md), [Sodas](./Soda%20%28disambiguation%29.md), [Flares](./Flare.md), First Aid supplies, and very rarely a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) box (only at Ravine Basin).

The **Trans-Island Railway Line**, known officially as the **Far Range Branch Line** (not to be confused with the [region of the same name](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md)), is a major landmark located in multiple regions across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).
The Trans-Island Railway Line can be found in 6 regions and 2 Transition Zones. They are (in order from one end of the line to the other):

The **Trans-Island Railway Line** is a logging and light freight railway line which runs across the majority of Great Bear Island. It was likely built during the early 20th century, but fell into disrepair and was abandoned following the seismic activity which occurred before [The Collapse](./The%20Collapse.md).

It was constructed to provide a quick and efficient way to transport both supplies from deep within the Far Territory to the coast, as well as to provide a land route to ferry passengers via [Train Shuttles](./Train%20Shuttle.md). Though not mentioned anywhere specifically in-game, abandoned rail cars suggest the line was used to transport resources such as timber, coal, ore, and the occasional workforce passengers.

Most of the railway line lies in ruins and is entirely unfit for even a basic push railcar, as can be seen first hand if the player walks the line from region to region in [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). The railroad is plagued with an incredible amount of disrepair, including but not limited to:
6. Various abandoned boxcars/logging cars/flatbed cars/passenger rail cars/rail mounted trucks already present on or derailed near the line.

The rail line begins in the local [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) complex, starting at a train station near [Indolent Hoppers](./Indolent%20Hoppers.md) and heading towards Lower Great Bear. Several spilled chemicals and landslides make navigating the tracks hazardous in this region.

Extending deep into the inner territory of Great Bear, the explorable portion of the Trans-Island Railway begins at massive [landslide](./Immutable%20Hesitation.md). Following from here, the railroad passes through a [passenger train station and loading depot](./Vacant%20Depot.md), before heading into a [large derailment](./Distempered%20Flatcars.md) of timber rail cars and eventually passing through another rockslide. A nearby cave must be explored to reach the next region.

Continuing passed the landslide, the line passes over an [intact trestle](./Surfeit%20Trestle.md) and through a pitch dark train tunnel filled with collapsed tunnels and derelict boxcars. The tunnel transitions to the Broken Railroad Region. This region contains the most undamaged section of railroad of any region.

The railway line is seen prominently in Broken Railroad, beginning at the previous train tunnel and passing over a [Destroyed Bridge](./Broken%20Bridge%20%28Broken%20Railroad%20location%29.md), and stretching across the region. The line here is interrupted at multiple points by [Landslides](./Landslide.md), a passenger rail car, and a truck that has been deployed onto the line. A [Locomotive Engine](./Locomotive%20Engine.md) is also found here, being the only one currently in the game. The railroad terminates at a tunnel which transitions to Forlorn Muskeg.

In Forlorn Muskeg the railway line can be seen bisecting the region, running between two tunnels leading to Broken Railroad and Mystery Lake. The line is damaged in multiple places, having collapsed into the marsh in one section. Two major derailments can be found, the first of which is primarily logging cars which can be found near the transition to Broken Railroad. The second is a mostly freight derailment found near the center of the region. This derailment includes the [Poacher's Camp](./Poacher%27s%20Camp.md). The line in this region terminates in at another region transition train tunnel leading to Mystery Lake.

The Mystery Lake railway runs from Forlorn Muskeg to The Ravine and is in remarkable shape than that of most regions. The line features a boxcar blocking the beginning region transition train tunnel. There is one [Derailment](./Derailment.md) near the center of the region, consisting of a few cargo boxcars (one of which is accessible.) Further along a small passenger transportation rail vehicle can be found, near the [Train Loading Area](./Train%20Loading%20Area.md). The railway also crosses a [Bridge](./Train%20Bridge.md) near the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) (with another rail deployed truck close to the gate) before transitioning to The Ravine via a canyon.

One of the grandest displays of the railway, The Ravine is home to the [Raven Falls Trestle](./Raven%20Falls%20Trestle.md) and the [Raven Falls Railway Line](./The%20Ravine.md). The Ravine is notable for featuring a large cliffside derailment, with multiple cars and a small passenger vehicle having fallen into the [Ravine Basin](./Ravine%20Basin.md). The Raven Falls Trestle can be found towards the end of the line and is in a slight state of disrepair, having a partially collapsed line in the middle. The line terminates with a tunnel to Coastal Highway, which suffers from a partial ceiling collapse halfway through.

Coastal highway features the terminus of the railway line and is the smallest portion of any region. The line exists only as a small trestle that leads to an [Unloading Area](./Train%20Unloading.md) in the northwest of the region. The line ends with a few timber railcars on the rails and a collapsed tunnel which is completely impassable, and presumably leads to other portions of the island.

> “__For intermediate players. A crossroads dug out of the looming mountains, Transfer Pass is quiet since the trains stopped. But it remains a critical junction for anyone wishing to access the Far Territory.
Connects to Broken Railroad, Forsaken Airfield, Zone of Contamination, and Sundered Pass.__”

**Transfer Pass** is the 13th [Region](./Region.md) in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md) released for [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), and is available for players who purchased the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) expansion pack released on December 5, 2022.

Transfer Pass is set-up as a ''hub'' region, connecting to all other regions in the Far Territory. It connects to [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) via the [Far Range Branch Line](./Far%20Range%20Branch%20Line.md), to [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) via a mountain road, to the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) further along the railroad at [Immutable Hesitation](./Immutable%20Hesitation.md), and to [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) up north on the road after bypassing a collapsed tunnel.

Getting its name for originally being a hub for miners flown in from [Field 31](./Field%2031.md) waiting to be shipped to the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), Transfer Pass is a relatively small yet linear region located within the Far Territory of [Great Bear](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). It serves as the "starting hub" for the deeper regions of the Far Territory. The region features a variety of terrains and is centered around the heavily damaged and decaying [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md), with an abandoned train station, coal tipple, and water tower near the center.

The railway is littered with dozens of dormant [Oak Trees](./Oak%20Tree.md) and frozen ponds, providing an ample but limited supply of [Acorns](./Acorns.md) (approximately 24 total) and [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) (approximately 30 total) to forage, as well as hunting opportunities for [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) to the North/South, and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) near the East/West edges of the zone, on the in the hills close to the Conductor's Dropoff or Feedwater Cave. A few scattered [Deer](./Deer.md) that roam the nearby mountain roads to the northwest (except on Interloper and above). This region is notable for containing no predators (thus never having to worry about Scent), a unique feature shared only with the [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md) region.

The [Weather](./Weather.md) is comparable to other Far Territory areas, with potential storms happening frequently, but [Vacant Depot](./Vacant%20Depot.md) offers a reasonable [safehouse](./Safehouse.md) location.
Given the region's small size and lack of resources, most players will likely use it as a temporary stopover before heading to or from the larger regions of the Far Territory.
Transfer Pass is one of 2 unique regions that contains no [predators](./Wolf.md) of any type (the second being [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md)). Only 3 animals are found in this region.
- [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md) can occasionally be found in the section of the map containing the Ravine's Basin, above and below it.
- [Deer](./Deer.md) can be found to the west section of the map, along with the occasional [Deer Carcass](./Deer%20Carcass.md).
- Despite its small size classifying it as a Transition Region, the player can choose Transfer Pass as a starting Region.

These materials are not always located close to each tower (Except the one in [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) which has all materials on hand). Car batteries are commonly located close to each Transmitter, or in nearby Cars/Trucks:
2. The Shortwave Radio Tower at [Muskeg Overlook](./Muskeg%20Overlook.md) in Southeastern [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md)

Trapper's Homestead is accessible from a path to the east and a difficult path to the north-east. Depending on the game's difficulty setting, valuable supplies may be scavenged from the Trapper's Homestead, including a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) along with [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md).

An open patch of ice and snow surrounds Trapper's Homestead. The surrounding area is abundant with [deer](./Deer.md) and [rabbits](./Rabbit.md), and there is a chance for a moose to roam right in front of the cabin. Immediately south of the Trapper's Homestead is a small abandoned barn and, a little further south, is [Max's Last Stand](./Max%27s%20Last%20Stand.md). A few [Green Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) may also grow in the area.

The interior of Trapper's Homestead usually contains several valuable supplies. It always contains a [bed](./Bed.md), a [Wood Stove](./Wood%20Stove.md), a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), and many containers, including a [Safe](./Safe.md). The Trapper's Homestead also contains a [note.](https://thelongdark.fandom.com/wiki/A_Note_Left_Behind)

The Trapper's Homestead can serve as a great [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) due to it having lots of storage space, a bed, a workbench and secure surroundings with lots of hunting opportunities. The cabin is a very warm building, and most of the time a fire won't be required to warm you up. The main downside is its remote location, as it lies far away from many of the other buildings in Mystery Lake. The area around the cabin has very few wolves, and if one is stalking you when returning, the raised path to the door can give you some time to either shoot the approaching wolf or return indoors. The rabbit grove right behind the cabin is a good and sustainable food source, as are the deer that often spawn in the valley in front of the cabin. If [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md) are not a concern, the [bear](./Bear.md) that often spawns nearby can also provide a boost to the player's food supply.

In [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), the cabin is home to the trapper [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md), who occupies the bed at all times. You cannot sleep inside Jeremiah's home without a bedroll. The fire inside is always lit, allowing players to use the location to cook food and boil water without expending matches, tinder or firewood.
In story mode, the items and containers in the cabin are owned by Jeremiah and cannot be searched or looted.

A [cave to the southeast of the cabin](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md#Mountain_town_to_Mystery_Lake) connects Mystery Lake to the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region. Players are initially blocked from entering the cave, but are later able to travel through to the lower area of the Mountain Town region. However, they cannot return to [Milton](./Milton.md) due to the absence of a climbing rope up to [Milton Park](./Milton%20Park.md).

There is a wooden hatch located in the floorboards in front of the workbench that contained a ham radio, as part of the original story of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md). Despite the radio being reworked into the mission [Signal to Noise](./Signal%20to%20Noise.md), the panel still remains as a leftover asset, and can still be seen under good lighting in Survival Mode. In the current Episode 2, it contains a more noticeable outline, but cannot be opened.

"_You can use your energy chasing Rabbits and trying to stun them with stones, or you can use a more long-term strategy, Snares. Look for areas of high Rabbit activity, and place a Snare nearby. Check on it daily. You may get lucky and catch a Rabbit. You can set up multiple snares to increase your chances. A well maintained Trapline can be an excellent long-term source of food. Just remember, it may attract other wildlife!_"

Trapping is a safe and efficient method exclusively for killing rabbits in The Long Dark. Traps hold quarry in place so you don't have to track, and animals are dead of exposure before you return. All that is required is good trap placement, time, and the attentiveness and determination to find and harvest traps before their contents are eaten by scavengers.

[Snares](./Snare.md) only work against [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md), specifically only working in special Rabbit Grove locations. Their slip-knotted loops close swiftly when pulled and refuse to release, only becoming tighter while struggled against. Rabbits are always killed when caught in a snare.

![Snare icon](../assets/Snare_icon.png) Snares are set individually by "placing" them from either the radial menu or inventory. Selecting a trap from the radial menu allows the player to immediately see the outline of a placeable snare, centered on the screen. Alternatively, a "place" button uniquely appears under the snare description in the inventory screen. Similarly, selecting "Place" from the inventory screen immediately returns the view to the main screen with the outlined view of a placeable snare. The outline will be red when placement is not possible, green when it is. Move as desired to a good spot. Left click to release. Right click to cancel. Left click on a placed snare to pick it up again as you would any loose item in the game.

![Placed snare](../assets/Placed_snare.png) Location of traps is critical; they must be set where the rabbits are able to spawn or they will catch nothing. Spotting a specimen is the best sign of a valid area. But individuals wander, so it is possible it has left the bounds of its spawn point, especially if something has startled it. Estimate the center of animal activity by observing the area carefully. Set your traps there. Setting multiple traps along a line or even in a grid can greatly assist learning exactly where the rabbiting area is. Traps set outside a rabbiting area will never catch anything. Choosing a convenient location is also important because you will have to come back later to remove the catch.

![Caught Rabbit](../assets/Caught_Rabbit.png) You will never see a trap activated. Chasing rabbits into snares has no effect, and there is no relevant bait. What catches rabbits is time and absence. Twelve hours after a trap is set, it begins checking to see if a rabbit has been caught. Trapped animals immediately begin freezing. Their carcasses appear identical to rabbits killed by other means. Snares that have made a catch will need to be reset. It is also possible that snares may have been damaged and must be rebuilt.

Occasionally snares will be found "broken", their condition reduced to 0%. This irreparable damage may represent multiple possibilities. The animal may have struggled loose, perhaps a predator stole the prize for its own, or the snare became damaged in severe weather. Broken snares cannot be reset or repaired, however, they can be harvested to get 1 [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md), which can again be crafted into a snare by combining it with [Cured Gut](./Cured%20Gut.md) at a [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md).
- In previous versions a glitch allowed broken snares to continue to be set and used by placing them with the right click placement function while they are on the ground.

![Fishing Tip Up icon](../assets/Fishing_Tip-Up_icon.png) A [Fishing Tip-Up](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md) can be placed in any [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) hole that has been broken open. The player can use them to fish on their behalf or as they fish in their own separate hole.
### Placement

The player can place them in cleared Ice Fishing ice holes or produce a hole via Free From ice holes (See [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md#Fishing_Holes) for a list of suitable locations). Tip-Ups can be fitted with [Fishing Bait](./Fishing%20Bait.md) or a [Fishing Lure](./Fishing%20Lure%20%28disambiguation%29.md) to increase the odds that the catch fish.
### Setting Runs

Placing too many Fishing Tip-Ups (4-5 Tip-Ups) in one location will quickly result in diminishing returns, but will otherwise produce a large amount of fish if the player tends to them. Tip-Ups do not gain any benefits from the player's Ice Fishing Skill, and become useless if the hole starts to freeze over, requiring the player keep an eye on them and perform regular maintenance on the ice holes. A great strategy involves using the Fishing Hut as a shelter and fishing alongside Tip-Ups, regularly keeping an eye on them.
### The Catch

Unlike Snares, Tip-Ups will actually tip up and produce a metal clang when they catch a fish. They will continue to hold said fish until they are reclaimed from the ice hole. Haver reclaimed, they will need to be placed back into a cleared ice hole to continue catching fish.

Blizzards and general use will decay the Condition of a Tip-Up, and they can be broken down for parts (harvesting yields 1 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) and 1 [Stick](./Stick.md)) and any Fishing Lures/Bait attached to them.

- Any location where rabbits spawn has a chance of snaring rabbits, even if the area isn't marked as a "rabbit grove" proper on the [map](./Map.md), and even if the area currently has no rabbits in it (if the player has killed all the rabbits using [stones](./Stone.md), for example).

- However, if there are as many or more snared rabbits in the area than the spawn point can normally produce, this will greatly diminish the chances of snaring more rabbits. Clearing out traps regularly increases the odds of success.

- The density of snares placed in an area seems to have no deleterious effect on trapping (i.e. crowding an area with snares does not reduce the chances of each snare getting a rabbit). Thus, it is beneficial to use as many snares as possible for the best chance of getting a high yield. A particularly high volume of snares (a dozen or more) can even offset the lower chance of trapping in a depleted spawn point.

- Actively observing a trap when the snare is ready to check for rabbits will prevent them from appearing. However, this is easily remedied by briefly breaking line of sight and allowing the trap to check for rabbits. It is not necessary to leave the area, pass time, or sleep for traps to work. However, it can still be useful to transition between areas. If the player is not in the area when snares are ready to check for rabbits, they will wait until the player enters the area. This will force all snares to check simultaneously, potentially resulting in larger yields (remember, traps that have already caught rabbits reduce the chances of further catches).

- When trapping in an area with few interior spaces (e.g. Timberwolf Mountain), it may help to set up traps with a delay between each setting and check multiple times during the course of a day for very high yields.

- Moving a trap before it has caught a rabbit will reset the timer. It is best to leave set traps alone, provided you are confident they are placed accurately within a spawn point. Traps seem to check for rabbits once every 12 hours after being set (provided the player is in the area, otherwise they will wait to check until the player returns).

- The Expert Trapper [feat](./Feats.md) will significantly increase the chances of any given snare producing a rabbit. (The mechanics for this are unclear, but may involve each snare checking for rabbits twice and taking the better result. The feat does _not_ ensure that every placed trap will snare a rabbit)

- The sheer quantity of rabbits that a dense cluster of well-placed traps will produce can make it difficult to fully harvest their carcasses. It may become a more efficient use of time to harvest only the meat, a modest number guts to replace broken traps, and hides strictly as needed for crafting/repairs. Allowing some hides/guts to go to waste can also save resources, since meat can be harvested by hand reasonably quickly, sparing use of a knife/whetstone.

- When selecting an area for trapping, it's a good idea to consider how easy it is to find the area again to claim your catch, distance to your preferred shelter, and proximity of hostile wildlife that might smell your freshly caught rabbits. Transporting rabbits one at a time can reduce the risk of wolf encounters, as can cooking and eating them on the spot (only rabbits/meat/fresh guts in your inventory count for stinkiness).

**Trauma** is the first mission in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md). In this mission, [Astrid](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) meets [Molly](./Molly.md) and learns about her predicament.
| Start location | [Pleasant Valley Farmstead](./Pleasant%20Valley%20Farmstead.md) |
| Significant locations | [Barn (Molly's)](./Barn%20%28Molly%27s%29.md), [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) |

The episode starts in Pleasant Valley Farmstead with a cutscene. When Molly leaves the house, Astrid is free to explore. There are three clues the player must find: a broken rifle in the den, a photograph on a desk in the office, and a piece of torn orange cloth in the upstairs bathroom. Once all three are found, the phone on the first floor will ring. When Astrid picks it up, Molly informs her that she is at the barn and needs her help. The key to open the basement is located under the vase in the den. Inside the basement, the player must open the gun cabinet and take out the [revolver](./Revolver.md), [revolver ammunition](./Revolver%20Ammunition.md), and [rifle ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md). There is a second exit in the basement that leads directly outside through a bulkhead door. Outside and to the right, there is a line of blizzard stake lines leading to the [Barn (Molly's)](./Barn%20%28Molly%27s%29.md), fallow them. A group of [wolves](./Wolf.md) will be circling the barn and need to be shot at to make them flee (or just run to the door). Enter the barn and receive the telephone call from Molly.

Leave the barn and head up the road past [Heartbreak Bridge](./Heartbreak%20Bridge.md). Keep going past [Contemplation Bridge](./Contemplation%20Bridge.md) to [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md). Enter the [Community Hall](./Community%20Hall.md) and talk to [Father Thomas](./Father%20Thomas.md) to advance to Chapter 2: [Fallen Star](./Fallen%20Star.md).
- [Mathis](./Mathis.md) is voiced by Gord Marriott in story recap intro, despite the cutscene being from the reworked Redux Episode 2 and Elias Toufexis having voiced him in that version.

- Father Thomas reveals that the plane in the mountains crashed yesterday and made a deafening crash in the night, but he also says the First Flare occurred 3 or 4 days ago. How this plane managed to stay in the air for so long is unknown.
- If the player attempts to sequence break, multiple blocks are in place to impede the player:

- If the player disobeys the objective to reach Molly's Barn and decides to explore the world when first leaving the farmhouse, the blizzard suddenly gets twice as cold (the temperature drops from -25 to -45) and the player's [Warmth](./Warmth.md) will rapidly drop the farther they get away from the barn. The Condition bar will also drain twice as fast than freezing would normally allow. This will kill the player in under a minute before they can reach any other warm structure in the region, even on Green Survivor difficulty.

- If the player enters the [Crash Site](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) early via the path near [Draft Dodger's Cabin](./Draft%20Dodger%27s%20Cabin.md), the tree bridge will be missing. If they go around the mountain to the plane, the option to open the door does not appear.
- If the player attempts to ender [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md), a fallen tree and invisible barrier block the path.

**Travois** (pronounced Trav-wah) are a crafted vehicle for item transportation and storage in _The Long Dark_. They can be loaded with large amounts of items, then manually dragged to move them. It was introduced in Part 4 "Buried Echoes" update for [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md). **Warning**: As of [patch 2.50](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/305620?updates=true&emclan=103582791436288468&emgid=526487474953781659) (December, 2025) on PC, the Travois can still fall under the terrain if left outside in a loaded state before transitioning through a loading screen, forcing the player to retrieve **ALL** its contents (with the exception of [Decorations](./Decorations.md), which will all be **LOST**) from a [Lost and Found](./Lost%20and%20Found.md) box appropriate to the [region](./Region.md) it was lost in. (Note: the Lost and Found box will always be found outdoors, in a predetermined place within the region.) As an added inconvenience, the Travois may be in a Ruined state when it is found. The Travois can even fly up in the air, instead of disappearing and being placed in a Lost and Found box, if left on the ground near certain locations (such as [Mountaineer's Hut](./Mountaineer%27s%20Hut.md)), which will make the recovery of its contents impossible. To be completely safe, **NEVER** leave a loaded Travois on the ground before going through a loading screen.

Travois are a crafted [tool](./Tools.md) for storing and transporting up to 75.00kg of cargo; functionally a travois is a deerskin backpack attached to a sled, which is dragged by the survivor to new locations. When used, a travois will lose condition over time from wear and tear; they may be repaired with [Cured Gut](./Cured%20Gut.md) and a [Cured Deer Hide](./Cured%20Deer%20Hide.md) for 70% condition. Harvesting a Travois produces 3 [Cured Maple Sapling](./Cured%20Maple%20Sapling.md).

- They weigh 1.00kg in the survivor's inventory or containers, and can be "Deployed" outdoors on flat surfaces or repaired. In order to pick up and placed into the inventory again, a Travois must first be empty.
- Travois cannot be dropped like common items, only deployed (they can be placed into containers however).

- **Empty**: When first deployed onto the ground, they may be interacted with at their rear to store/remove cargo. Moving the cursor to the front of the Travois handles will give the option to "Pickup Travois" to place it into the player's inventory. Placing items in the pouch changes the state of a Travois from "Empty" to "Loaded."

- **Loaded**: When an item is placed in the storage pouch, this changes the Travois to the Loaded state. Moving the cursor to the front of the Travois handles will give the option to "Carry Travois". The Travois can be carried around in this state, and displays a unique red icon in the bottom right of the screen when it is being carried. When hauling a Travois, all actions are disabled except for the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md) (which only contains the Map, Drop functions), walking forward, and turning. To cancel hauling a travois: press the Radial Menu ("Space") and "Drop" the travois or by pressing the "Put Away" key.

When the survivor transitions between Regions while using a Travois, they will start on the new map still hauling it. Travois cannot be brought inside structures (through doors) or into mines. They can be brought inside interior [caves](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md) though not redeployed when inside. They cannot be carried up a [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md) section unless they are emptied and placed back into the player's inventory.
A Travois will leave 2 large lines in the snow as the player travels, similar to a player's footsteps.

The Travois are most useful in [regions](./Region.md) with large expanses of relatively flat, open ground. These include [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md), [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md), and [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md), as well as parts of [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md), [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md), and [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md).
- Moving inventory from a [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) between locations/regions. They can also be used to start up/evacuate bases.
- Transporting [Quartered](./Carcass%20Harvesting.md) Bear or Moose to a safer location in one trip.
- Moving Fish from [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) or [Fishing Tip-Ups](./Fishing%20Tip-Up.md), or firewood to a fishing location to stay warm during future fishing.
- Collecting and transporting large amounts of [Firewood](./Campfire.md), [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md), or [Coal](./Coal.md).
- Heavy items can be dropped inside during an emergency (such as a wildlife attack or blizzard) and can be abandoned with the Travois, then can be recovered later when it is safe.
When deployed and carried, a Travois has a number of limitations in exchange for their benefits:

- Cannot be used Indoors (cannot be deployed indoors either). The only exception is that the Travois can be brought into interior caves, which don't require clicking to be entered, but it has to be dragged in through the cave entrance; it cannot be deployed inside.
- The handles cannot be picked up if the player is crouching under an object/there is not enough room to stand up.

- Limited turning: cannot turn as quickly as on foot, and must have room to navigate obstacles. In order to turn, the player must move forward/backwards and turn the camera left/right at the same time (somewhat similar to tank controls).
- Limited vision: cannot turn the camera much (~30\* frontal arc), and must drop the Travois to look around, distract/shoot wildlife, etc.
- The player can crouch while holding the Travois, but cannot move until they stand up again.

- Cannot navigate over steep slopes ([Sprain Risk](./Sprain%20Risk.md) hills), cliffs, low passages which require crouching, through doors/mine transitions, or up/down [Rope Climbing](./Rope%20Climbing.md)/[Rock Climbing](./Rock%20Climb.md) spots when deployed, and must be emptied and folded up, then placed in the player's Backpack along with any other items in order to progress.

- Getting close to objects (trees, cliffsides, etc) will produce the message "No space for Travois" and force the player to back up to go around. They cannot be used when [Mountain Goating](./Mountain%20Goating.md).
- Carrying a travois slows the movement speed. The heavier the travois, the slower one moves.
- 4.72 movement speed with 0kg in Travois (Also 4.72 without travois, for reference running speed is 10.28)

- Travois lose Condition fairly quickly while being towed (Condition loss tends to be 1% condition/every 30 meters). When using it on rough terrain (not covered by snow or ice) the condition loss is amplified further. Railway tracks are especially hard on the Travois and it is therefore advisable not to drag the Travois on railway tracks when it can be avoided.
- A ruined Travois will force the player to an immediate halt, and cannot be harvested or removed. A ruined Travois can still serve as a stationary container with reduced capacity (40.00kg), though.

- Travois are one of the few tools to lose condition due to natural [Decay](./Decay.md), even when in storage or when carried in the player's inventory. The Travois will also take condition damage when left out (deployed) in a blizzard.

Regions difficult to use a Travois in often have narrow/winding paths, rope climbs, rock climbs, or steep hills/mountains, such as [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md), [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md), [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md), [Old Island Connector](./Crumbling%20Highway.md), [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md), or [Raven Falls Trestle](./Raven%20Falls%20Trestle.md) in [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md). They cannot be used at indoors areas like: [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md), [Cinder Hills Coal Mine](./Cinder%20Hills%20Coal%20Mine.md), or [Abandoned Mine No. 3](./No.%203%20Coal%20Mine.md).
Travois are not practical tools to use in most [Challenges](./Challenge.md) due to various time/hostile wildlife stipulations.

![A standard blue truck](../assets/Truck.png)_A standard blue truck_ **Trucks** are compact, 2-door single cab utility [vehicles](./Vehicle.md) found in the game _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_

Much like [cars](./Car.md) and [tractors](./Tractor.md), trucks are currently undrivable, though the cab can be entered, the glove compartment searched, the hood opened, and the sun [visors](./Visor.md) tilted (possibly revealing [Mementos](./Mementos.md)).
Just like cars, the gas lid and front hood can be opened. Some trucks have [batteries](./Car%20Battery.md) inside.

There are three types of trucks found on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). The majority are coloured light blue, white, or brown and are for road use only, while others - found exclusively in [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) and [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) - are light brown [road-rail vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road-rail_vehicle) with [Breyerhouse](./Breyerhouse.md) branding. The latter are fitted with rail wheels, allowing them to utilize the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md). Inside the [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) region and the [Keepers Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md) connector region a variant of the light blue truck can be found. The Blackrock variant of the truck is noticeable for its light bar on the roof and the name Blackrock printed on the side. During an aurora, a truck's lights will flicker and their radio's become functional, playing classical music.

The effect of this Affliction does not stack, and each application will not override the previous Affliction. Partially eating the previously mentioned foods only adds a partial amount of Unburdened benefit duration.

Unnamed Pond is located southwest of the [Forestry Lookout](./Forestry%20Lookout.md) and far north-northeast of [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md). The only structure is a hunter's blind found on the shore of the pond, surrounded by several tree stumps and fallen trees.

A single hunting stand resides on the side of the pond. Food, and sometimes a single round of rifle ammo, can be found inside. A [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) can sometimes be found resting inside or outside on the side of the stand, though this is very uncommon. A hatchet, a hunting knife, and a broken arrow all have a chance to appear in the stand, as well.
Deer can be spotted nearby on occasion and a deer carcass can be found close to the stand.

[Bears](./Bear.md) and [wolves](./Wolf.md) commonly wander near the pond, so exercise caution when approaching, or take advantage of the safe position of the hunting blind to hide from or hunt roaming predators.

[Green Birch Sapling](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) can sometimes be found between the [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md) and Unnamed Pond. Slightly further north, over the hill on the side of the pond stage left of the Hunter's blind, there is a small cabin that offers shelter and possibly a few supplies, as well.

Has no shelter **Unquenched Extraction** is the biggest lake in the region, with two large dormant metal water extraction pumps emerging from the lake and heading towards the [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md) building of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) mining complex, presumably going deeper to the mines and later the [Pump House](./Pump%20House.md).

This unpolluted lake fed by three large waterfalls offers no shelter, however the player can hide in the nearby [Old Corral](./Old%20Corral.md) to the north or the crashed helicopter in the nearby mountains, if the weather changes for the worst. Heading south is a path heading south the Langston Mine mining complexes southwestern entrance, [Miner's Footpath](./Miner%27s%20Footpath.md), an entrance to [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) Level 3, [Smoker's Cave](./Smoker%27s%20Cave.md) and [Desperate Elevation](./Desperate%20Elevation.md).

The lake is the only location in the region deep enough to support Free Form [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md), and offers plenty of [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md). A [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) with two [Flare Shells](./Flare%20Shell.md) can also be found on the left side of the pipes looking from the direction of the Langston Mine complex. Be aware that several [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) patrol the lake searching for food.

The **Urn** was a cut container found during the Predux version of [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md). It was found in the [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md) farmhouse bedroom, and contained [Bank Deposit Box Key 15](./Bank%20Deposit%20Box%20Key%2015.md), needed to finish the mission [The Grey Mother (Predux)](./The%20Grey%20Mother%20%28Predux%29.md).

It has since been removed from the game after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of Episode 1 was released, but can still be experienced by downloading versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).

It now considered [Cut/Discontinued Content](./Cut%20%E2%80%94%20Discontinued%20Content.md). A spiritual successor to the Urn would appear years later in [Episode 3: Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) as the [Vase](./Vase.md).

Provides some shelter The **Vacant Depot** is a location in [Transfer Pass](./Transfer%20Pass.md), located near the center of the region.

The location can be spotted at a distance by its old water tower, which used to draw water from nearby [Feedwater Cave](./Feedwater%20Cave.md). There are also two sidings, one of which has a coal tipple and two coal hoppers, plus an abandoned train station named Vale station.

Inside the station can be found low to mid-grade clothing, some food and drink in lower difficulties, and 3 [suitcases](./Suitcase.md) for storage. Inside the ticket booth is one of the [Radios](./Trader.md#Radio_Locations) necessary to contact the Trader (if enabled).

The abandoned train station can make for a good shelter for weary players. However, there is no [bed](./Bed.md), so players who wish to sleep there will want to bring a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), or a permanent bed may be constructed with the help of [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) as part of [Safehouse customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md). The interior has a fixed ambient temperature of -10C (similar to Lookouts). Players may have to light the [Fireplace](./Fireplace.md) in order to keep themselves warm, at least until sufficient Warmth bonus from clothing is available.

Alternatively the nearby coal tower can be entered (and exited) through roundabout paths. The interior is much colder than the train station and gives no warmth bonus, however, the coal tipple also has chance to spawn some rarer items, such as a [Bear Skin Bedroll](./Bear%20Skin%20Bedroll.md), as well as more food and materials to break down.
While the station or tower could be used as a [Safe House](./Safehouse.md), Transfer Pass is a very small region to live in for any length of time, so resources may be depleted quickly.

Several of the picture frames inside the Vacant Depot were changed with the release of the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), and now feature photographs of various coal miners and landmarks located within the Zone.

> “**Get going, pilot. The Warden doesn't have much time left. And in case you're thinking of running away. Remember...we still have your precious case.**”

**Vachon**is a member of the [Convicts](./Convicts.md) appearing in [Episode 4: Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md). He serves as a secondary antagonist for the episode.

Vachon was one of the prisoners being transported to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md), but his [Prison Bus crashed](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) outside of [Milton](./Milton.md) during the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md). He escaped the bus with several other Convicts and made his way to [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md) and later [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md), eventually leaving the region after many of the other Convicts began turning up dead, leading him to realize that [someone](./Molly.md) was hunting them. He is eventually tasked with carrying an unconscious [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) to the Prison via [Mathis'](./Mathis.md) orders, worried that the heavy man will only slow them down and allow the wolves and/or the mysterious hunter to kill them all.

Despite looking like a bully, Vachon isn't as fierce as he looks, often focusing on just his own safety most of the time. This often changes when he fears reprisals from his boss Mathis, or if Heller eggs him on enough to get his act together. Vachon is also somewhat of a more empathetic soul than the other Convicts, despite being a man sentenced to a maximum security prison. He sometimes gives Mackenzie survival advice when his boss isn't there to watch over him, without giving the impression that he will do anything to become friends with Will or [Franklin](./Franklin.md).

Vachon is almost always found paired with [Heller](./Heller.md), being the far less obnoxious and malevolent of the two. Vachon is most likely from the Canadian province of Quebec, because he speaks French and English. He is shown smoking with his own lighter he carries in one scene during the Prologue, but is never shown smoking again.
He is still wearing his prison uniform with a padded leather jacket to keep him warm, and is balding. He is the oldest looking of the 3 main Convicts.

Vachon does not appear in Episode 1, but his name (VACHON, B.) appears on the [Prison Transport Manifest](./Prison%20Transport%20Manifest.md) near the [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md), foreshadowing him.

Vachon appears with Heller carrying Mackenzie on a stretcher, complaining about having to carry the heavy unconscious pilot. He later comes under attack with the rest of the group and is forced to search for Mackenzie after he escapes.

Heller appears with Vachon and Mathis once Mackenzie wakes up in his cell at Blackrock Prison. After Mathis savagely beats the Warden [Franklin](./Franklin.md), Mathis tasks the two criminals to clean him up. He recounts the story of how Mathis' last prison break on the Mainland landed him on a bus to Blackrock Prison.

Heller is later convinced by Mackenzie to secretly let him out of [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) behind Mathis' back in order to find [Blackrock Infirmary Medication](./Blackrock%20Infirmary%20Medication.md) for [Franklin](./Franklin.md). After Heller and Vachon realize that the medication is outside the Prison, and do not wish to risk being killed by hostile wildlife, they reluctantly let the pilot loose. Vachon is at the Prison door and searches the pilot to prevent him from bringing contraband into his cell.

Vachon appears at the start and end of the mission, remarking that he lost a bet that Mackenzie wouldn't make it. He is informed by Mackenzie that the power was unable to be restored at the plant. Vachon says Mathis will be disappointed, and frisks Mackenzie for contraband again before taking him to his cell.

Vachon appears with Heller to pester Mackenzie as Mathis interrogates him and Franklin, with Heller telling the pilot to find the [Detonators](./Detonators.md) before "Mathis goes a few more rounds with the Warden."
He later appears at the end of the mission along with Heller, seizing Mackenzie after he delivers the Detonators.

Vachon runs out of Mackenzie's cell after the Prison explodes. He later appears behind the blocked door leading to the Warden's office, yelling at other Convicts to break the door down. He later appears in the Prison Yard's 4th guard tower yelling at other Convicts to find and shoot Mackenzie, even spotting him from a spotlight if the player is not careful.
Vachon later appears at the Power Plant in the final cutscene next to Mathis, but has no dialogue, merely looking tough and overlooking the fight with the other convicts.
Vachon appears in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) carrying Donner's unconscious and wounded body into the Medical Clinic for Astrid to work on.
He is later killed by [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md) when a Hatchet is thrown into his sternum.

- It is possible to shoot at (and hit) Vachon with a projectile weapon as he stands by the fire barrel near the prison entrance at the end of Blackrock Blues and The Power Plant, but this doesn't affect him in any way.

- Unlike Mathis or Heller, Vachon is the only Convict to occasionally take his coat off of his jumpsuit while inside the prison walls in some cutscenes. His jumpsuit has torn sleeves and he wears a Grey undershirt with long sleeves to compensate for warmth.
- Despite being a major character in Episode 4, Vachon does not get his own [What I Know](./What%20I%20Know.md) character section.
This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

**Vagabond Soup** is a [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) item in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is learned after acquiring its unique [Recipe Card](./Recipe%20Cards.md).
Compared to [Rabbit Stew](./Rabbit%20Stew.md), Vagabond Soup improves the caloric value of 0.5kg of rabbit meat by 200 calories less, but does not require flour and has half the cook time.

At Cooking 5, the calorie value of Vagabond Soup is the same as its components. Its healing properties are slightly worse (by 1%) than that of Rabbit Stew, except on Interloper, in which case it heals 2% more Condition due to Improved Rest's bonus being reduced.

A small cave hidden by some bushes, a backpack can be found inside along with some wood. Some [cat tail](./Cat%20Tail.md) can be gathered along the frozen river that lead to [Little Bear and Cub Falls](./Little%20Bear%20and%20Cub%20Falls.md). [Research books](./Research%20Book.md) can be found inside the cave, and a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md) can always be found here in all difficulties other than Interloper, which may prove useful to adventurers who forgot theirs and are too tired to make the climb out of the Lower Valley towards [Pensive Vista](./Pensive%20Vista.md) or [Many Falls Vista](./Many%20Falls%20Vista.md).

As the only warm cave in the [lower part of the region](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md#Lower_valley), this cave is a popular base location for players wishing to explore the nearby area. However, Valley Cave can also be used as a longer-term base location, as there is a rabbit grove nearby, along with a [deer](./Deer.md) spawn point. Furthermore, the surrounding area is abundant in firewood, and [coal](./Coal.md) can be picked up from the Hushed River. A moose may also spawn right across the river, making the cave a prime location for hunting it and curing the valuable hide. One wolf may spawn across the river from the cave, but, aside from that, the nearby area is very safe.

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.

**Vaughn's Rifle** is a unique variant of the [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

Vaughn's Rifle trades durability for a lighter weight and responsiveness. Weighing 1.0kg less than the standard Hunting Rifle and featuring shortened firing delays on reload and aim, this rifle variant has much snappier handling and a slightly faster fire rate overall. The downside is that each shot uses 2% condition, compared to the normal rifle consuming 1.325% condition per use. This means the gun can only fire up to 50 shots from full condition before breaking.
Successful hits on live animals provide experience to the [Rifle Firearm](./Rifle%20Firearm.md) skill.
Vaughn's Rifle will spawn a single time per world in various states of repair near the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) at one of the following locations:
- Inside [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) at one of several potential spawn locations;
- In the broken window room coming in from Winding River in the lower dam, (in a corner to the left when entering near a metal table)
- Inside the pipes at on the dam platform near the exit door to the dam in. It may be behind pallets that need to be broken down.
- Total durability is 33% less than Hunting Rifle (Uses 2%-1% condition per shot based on [Rifle Skill](./Rifle%20Firearm.md))

- The rifle appears to have a shaved down wooden furniture, a modification commonly done to bush and hunting rifles to keep their weight low as it is in game (this is one of many changes done when sporterizing military surplus guns). The rifle has also been wrapped with grip and duct tape in various areas on the rifle likely contributing to its easier handling.

- At [Rifle Skill Level 5](./Rifle%20Firearm.md), Vaughn's rifle can be fired up to a total of 100 times at full condition, this makes it the second least cost efficient rifle to repair and maintain for long-term play, with the [Bunker Rifle](./Bunker%20Rifle.md) having worse durability.

- Vaughn, the rifle's owner, is mentioned in the [Buffer Memories](./Buffer%20Memories.md) located inside the hydro electric dam. He was one of the 6 skeleton crew workers at the Dam and likely left his rifle behind after the Dam was abandoned (along with all the other technology inside) due to the hostilities with the [Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md) in the 1990s ([Carter Hydro Dam (Collectible)](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam%20%28Collectible%29.md)).
- The reason the rifle is sometimes found outside the Dam in Winding River is also explained in the Buffer Memories, as Vaughn often wandered outside the Dam without permission.

- Vaughn's Rifle most likely bases its appearance off the early Pre-Alpha hunting rifle model. The tape stock seems to be borrowed off the [second hunting rifle](./Hunting%20Lodge%20Rifle.md) found in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md), pre [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) redux update.

Strewn across the freezing landscapes of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) lie many non-functioning motorized **Vehicles**. These mechanized chariots were once the main form of transportation across the Island, but are now mainly used by survivors as temporary shelters. Many vehicles can serve as local landmarks, shelters to escape hostile [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) and the elements, places to temporarily sleep, and locations that provide opportunities to find loot.
During an [Aurora](./Aurora.md), many vehicles spring back to life, with their dashboards, lights, and radios becoming functional again.

The most common type of vehicle a survivor will find across the Island, their most notable gameplay characteristics often include having interactable elements, such as hoods, trunks, doors, gas caps, glove boxes, visors, radios. They are commonly used to warm a survivor from the cold, as many provide a small warmth value and remove all wind-chill from freezing a survivor, though their meagre warmth value makes them very dangerous to sleep in without warm [Clothing](./Clothing.md) during the night, and can turn them into deathtraps should a blizzard pass through the area, as the lack of warmth will easily freeze a survivor to death.

The most common type of vehicle found across the Island, [Cars](./Car.md) are found in most regions near roads or homes in civilized areas of the Island. They come in various colors and are often found on roads or near residential areas. Entering a car will add a windproof protection as well as a bonus ambient temperature of +5o C. A player can choose to sleep inside the Car provided they have a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md). A survivor can still sleep inside a Car even without a bedroll, as the Car will offer a bed warmth bonus of 3o C.

The [trunks](./Car%20Trunk.md) of Cars can be looted, though they are often locked and thus require a [Prybar](./Prybar.md) to open. Some Cars have a chance to spawn with a salvageable [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md) inside the hood, though the front of some Cars are too damaged to open the hood. Car visors can be opened and sometimes contain [Mementos](./Mementos.md). Despite being able to open the gas cap, gasoline cannot be syphoned out.

[Trucks](./Truck.md) are the second most common land vehicle found on the Island, often being found near roads and homes, but also more often near industrial areas. Much like Cars, Trucks often have a chance to contain a [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md) inside the hood. Some Trucks can be found mounted onto railroads, often near industrial areas and function no differently than any other Truck. Trucks can be entered similarly to Cars, and are often used as temporary shelters to sleep in.

The bed of Trucks sometimes have containers or other small items that can be looted. Some Trucks have a chance to spawn with a salvable [Car Battery](./Car%20Battery.md) inside the hood if lifted. Trucks visors can be opened and sometimes contain [Mementos](./Mementos.md). Despite being able to open the gas cap, gasoline cannot be syphoned out.

[Tractors](./Tractor.md) are often found near agricultural areas of the Island and contain only 2 interactable doors. They can be slept in and the floorboards often contain small amounts of loot. Tractors do not have Car Batteries due to a lack of an interactable hood and do not contain gas cans or visors. Tractors can be entered similarly to Cars and Trucks, and are often used as temporary shelters to sleep in, though their very small warmth value makes them poor shelters without very warm clothing.

Though very rare, [Buses](./Bus.md) can occasionally be found in some parts of Great Bear Island. Buses can be walked inside of and eliminate any wind-chill factor but cannot be slept inside of without a Bedroll. Curiously, [Campfires](./Campfire.md) can be started inside a Bus with no negative consequences, making them excellent places to safely cook food during bath weather. Despite having open doors, [Wolves](./Wolf.md) cannot enter Buses.

So far, all Buses come from the [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) and were used to transport prisoners across the Island. Buses often only loot inside or around the vehicle, with no other way to interact with them. A single [Crashed Prison Transport Bus](./Crashed%20Prison%20Transport%20Bus.md) can be found in the [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) region, with more Buses found in the Blackrock Prison parking lot in the [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) region.

Occasionally found on the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md), [Train Shuttle Cars](./Train%20Shuttle.md) provide temporary shelter and possible loot spawns. They contain a single door that can be opened and closed and provide no extra warmth value inside. While the lack of warmth makes them poor shelters, they can often be used to prevent hostile Wolves from attacking the player by simply closing the door on them as they approach. Shuttle Cars can also serve as temporary outdoor shelters to sleep in if a player has a Bedroll, though their lack of warmth must be taken into consideration before they are slept in to prevent freezing to death while a survivor sleeps.

While technically not a vehicle in of itself, various railroad cars can be found and entered across the [Trans-Island Railway Line](./Trans-Island%20Railway%20Line.md). They range from Flatbed Cars, Boxcars, Tank Cars, Coal Cars, or Timber Cars. Boxcars often serve as shelters and possibly contain loot, bodies, fuel, or fire barrels. Timber, Coal, Tank, and Flatbed railcars can often contain [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) nearby or nothing at all. Boxcars can also be used as shelters to sleep in, provided the player carries a Bedroll and has sufficiently warm Clothing.

Curiously, a [Locomotive Engine](./Locomotive%20Engine.md) can be found in the [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) region (and a second in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md)), but it cannot be entered.

A few locations contain Tractor Trailer cars, but no 18 wheeler automobile. Open trailers can be entered and often contain backpacks and supplies. They are mainly found in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) with one crashed on the [Long Bridge](./Long%20Bridge.md) and several featuring the Last Resort cannery logo near the cannery. [Blocked Bridge](./Blocked%20Bridge.md) in [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) also contains a trailer that blocks the bridge. A single trailer cab is found on the road outside of Milton, near the transition to Mystery Lake, but is outside of the playable area. Another is found in [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md), on the ruined road to [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md) buried under a rockslide.

Haul Trucks, or Dump Trucks, are rare industrial vehicles used to move vast quantities of earth and rock around mining sites. 3 can be found around the mines of the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) in the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md). They contain a single door that allows a safe place to shelter and the floors often contain food and mining clothing.

The only player-operable vehicle in the game, the [Steam Locomotive](./Steam%20Train.md) is a coal-fired [0-4-0-ST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/0-4-0) locomotive, numbered 46. It is used by [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) in [Episode 5](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) of [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) and is capable of pushing road-rail vehicles along the tracks, as well as clearing the tracks.

Despite having various wharfs and docks, Great Bear Island contains very few Water Vehicles. There are no boats found inland despite Great Bear Island having many lakes, thus making any Water Vehicles exclusive to the sea.

[The Riken](./The%20Riken.md) is a beached whaling sea vessel and a major location in the [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) region. The vessel has an indoor area, beds, a [Furnace](./Furnace.md), and sizable amounts of other loot.

A single fishing trawler can be found at the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md), and is used as a footpath on the way to the workshop. It always contains a [Backpack](./Backpack.md) and a [Wool Scarf](./Wool%20Scarf.md) on the nearby pier. Judging from the amount of graffiti on the ship, this trawler has been moored and abandoned for some time.

Beached Boats can often be found near regions close to the sea, often when a survivor is [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) the surrounding ocean. They often spawn after heavy blizzards pass through the area and contain sizable amounts of loot.
A few rowboats can be found on Great Bear Island. They occasionally have a [Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md) inside them, but can't otherwise be interacted with. Notable locations include:

A Canoe can occasionally wash up along the shorelines while [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md), and can contain various supplies with it. One is also seen in [Episode 5: The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md), bringing [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) from [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md) to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md).

The only "operational" vehicle in Survival mode (though not useable by the Survivor), Sutherland's sailboat shows up off the coast of [Misanthrope's Homestead](./Misanthrope%27s%20Homestead.md) the day after the Survivor completes a [trade](./Trader.md), and is where Sutherland lives. It takes the shape of a small sloop. The boat cannot be reached or otherwise interacted with.

[Planes](./Airplane.md) are rarely found on the Island, and are almost always destroyed if a survivor does find one. Notable examples of planes include the [Crash Site (Pleasant Valley)](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md), the destroyed cargo plane found strewn across [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) (see [Tail Section](./Tail%20Section.md)), and [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md). Occasionally, smaller [Plane Crashes](./Plane%20Crashes.md) can be found in the Lower Great Bear regions, but are always completely destroyed when the player finds them, with small amounts of loot and presumably the dead body of the pilot found nearby.

The only intact planes that can be found are the various abandoned airplanes found near [Field 31](./Field%2031.md) in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) region. These planes contain storage hatches on the sides that can be looted and can serve as temporary shelters from hostile wildlife and the cold or places to sleep if entered.

[Helicopters](./Helicopter.md) are the rarest of any vehicle on Great Bear Island. Most are only found in the [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) region and provide a small warmth bonus and complete protection from wind-chill as Cars, Trucks, and Tractors would. They can also be used as a temporary location to sleep. Helicopters contain the most loot containers of any vehicle, often containing many lockers inside and outside of the choppers. A unique rescue helicopter, [Final Approach](./Final%20Approach.md), can be found in Forsaken Airfield and contains a medical cot for sleeping, a chance to spawn a [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) box, and various lockers that can be looted.

Vitamin-C Pills are used to help eliminate [Scurvy Risk](./Scurvy%20Risk.md) or [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md), and are only acquired from the [Trader](./Trader.md).
Vitamin-C Pills are acquired by trading with the [Trader](./Trader.md), and are only unlocked after reaching 400 Trust.
> “**Equal parts hunter and hunted, your struggle to survive will eventually lead to mastering the elements.**”
**Voyageur** is the 2nd [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) Experience in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_. It is the standard "normal" difficulty setting.

Voyageur takes [Pilgrim](./Pilgrim.md) and increases the difficulty, removing the Wildlife pacifying effect from predators to make them a threat. The game world is only slightly more harsh, with [Needs](./Needs.md) and [Clothing](./Clothing.md) needing a bit more maintenance. Overall, the game is still quite easy to survive on, with food, clothing, tools, and resources being quite plentiful.

- [Cabin Fever](./Cabin%20Fever.md): the player cannot sleep or pass time indoors once contracted after spending too much time inside, and must spend time outside. This removes the ability for the player to endlessly spend most of their time indoors.
- [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md): A debilitating disease that slowly destroys the player's health, though it is quite forgiving.

- [Cotton Toque](./Cotton%20Toque.md), [Thin Wool Sweater](./Thin%20Wool%20Sweater.md), [Driving Gloves](./Driving%20Gloves.md), [Jeans](./Jeans.md), [Thermal Underwear](./Thermal%20Underwear.md), [Wool Socks](./Wool%20Socks.md), [Leather Shoes](./Leather%20Shoes.md)
- [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), [Flare](./Flare.md), [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md), [Sewing Kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md)
- Chance to start at night, outdoors, during poor weather, or in an inhospitable [Region](./Region.md).
- All [Fires](./Fire.md) prevent [freezing](./Hypothermia.md) (regardless of ambient temperature).
- Automatically wake from [sleep](./Sleep.md) when [freezing](./Hypothermia.md) IF you are sleeping next to a [fire](./Fire.md).
- The player will automatically wake up once their [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) meter is fully rested, and they cannot go back to sleep until sufficiently tired.
- The option to enable the [Trader](./Trader.md), [Cougar](./Cougar.md), and [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md) on or off is present.

**Warden's Revolver** is a unique variant of the [Revolver](./Revolver.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

The Warden's Revolver has been modified for portability with a snub-nose barrel, and custom blue grip featuring golden four leaf clover inlays. It has the lowest weight of any firearm available; weighing 0.25 Kg less than the standard revolver, and has a 25% faster aiming action. The downside is that the guns effective range is reduced by 33%.
The Warden's Revolver has no rear iron sights and a very tall and wide front sight post, making long distance aiming difficult.

The range decrease is applied to a ray-trace fired from the center of the screen when a shot is fired, normally the standard Revolver's ray-trace range is about 30 meters long, but the Warden's Revolver's is 20.1 meters long. Past this range the weapon will be unable to damage any [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md).

The Warden's revolver spawns a single time per world in various states of repair. The gun's location may differ between saves, but it can be located around [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) in the [Blackrock Region](./Blackrock.md):
- Behind a piece of debris in the main prison hall entrance, to the right most back side.
- Given its namesake and the location it is found, this firearm most likely belonged to [Franklin](./Franklin.md), the former Warden of Blackrock Federal Penitentiary.

A **Warm Cave** is a common type of outdoor cave that has no transition screen but provides a [Warmth](./Warmth.md) bonus. Such caves are found in every region except [Coastal Highway](./Coastal%20Highway.md), [Keeper's Pass North](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20North.md), and [Keeper's Pass South](./Keeper%27s%20Pass%20South.md).

[Cave (Transition Zone)](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md) are not considered Warm Caves, as these are indoor spaces. Certain Bear Caves (such as the ones in Coastal Highway ) do not have interiors, and also do not count.

The front of the cave simply has the same air temperature as outside the cave, however it is completely sheltered from the wind regardless of wind direction, and a [Magnifying Lens](./Magnifying%20Lens.md) can be used within it.

The back of the cave is warmer like indoor spaces, but the back of the cave does not have a fixed temperature. Instead there is a warmth bonus which is generally sufficient to allow sleeping without a fire, at least if the player has sufficiently warm clothing and [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md).
- The player walks slower as they transition to the back of the cave, and immediately receives a Warmth bonus.
- It is possible to [cure](./Curing.md) hides, guts, and saplings in the back of such caves.
- A [Campfire](./Campfire.md) may be lit on the floor, in the front or back of the cave.
- A Magnifying Lens may not be used, although it is possible to light a fire within the back zone while standing in the front zone.
- The light level for the purpose of performing tasks is the same as outside ([Mending](./Mending.md) and Repairing is not possible during a Blizzard/Heavy Fog [Weather](./Weather.md) at night).
There are also a few exterior buildings that give a warmth bonus despite not having a transition to an indoor space:
The following areas behave like Warm Caves, though these indoor areas progress Cabin Fever.
- Cave east of [Bunkhouses](./Bunkhouses.md) and west of Transition Cave to Bleak Inlet
- The Transition Cave to Bleak Inlet is a regular Warm Cave in [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md)
- Cave in between Cave (Mountain Town location) and Spruce Falls Bridge (this cave is half of a Warm Cave, it does not have a warm back interior)
- Cave in the ravine at [Mackenzie's Crashed Plane](./Mackenzie%27s%20Crashed%20Plane.md) (this cave is half a Warm Cave, it does not have a warm back interior)
- Cave south of [Paradise Meadows Farm](./Paradise%20Meadows%20Farm.md), in between the Rope Climbing sections
- The Transition Cave to Hushed River Valley is a regular cave in [Episode 1: Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md)
- Bear Cave north west of [Crash Site (Pleasant Valley)](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md), near [Prepper Cache](./Prepper%20Cache.md)

**Warming Up** is a positive benefit [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) in the **[_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).** The buff is gained by eating [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) that has been warmed up by a [fire](./Fire.md) and currently has the "HOT" status. While Warming Up is active, the rate of depletion of the [Warmth](./Warmth.md) meter while [Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md) is below 0 is reduced by half.
**HOT** is an attribute that is granted to some foods immediately upon finishing [Cooking](./Cooking.md) over a Fire.
- Only food or drink that is currently "HOT" will give Warming Up when consumed; which can be checked inside the inventory at any time.
- Items that can be reheated but are now cold will have a blue "COLD" next to their status in the inventory page, whereas heated items will have a red "HOT."
- Items that cannot be heated do not have this distinction (example: Warming Up cannot be obtained from cooked meat or boiled water, despite requiring a fire to make them.)
- Some foods cannot be reheated once they are cooked, thus only gain the "HOT" benefit shortly after being prepared (see list below).

"HOT" status is short-lived, wearing off after 15 game minutes indoors or 5 game minutes outdoors. Placing any warm food or drink inside an [Insulated Flask](./Insulated%20Flask.md) will keep food and drink warmer for much longer than keeping it inside its original container, though not all foods can be inserted into a Flask.

![Placing teas and canned goods near an active fire will warm/cook them, without sacrificing a cooking slot.](../assets/Warming.jpg)_Placing teas and canned goods near an active fire will warm/cook them, without sacrificing a cooking slot._Consuming items while HOT grants benefits to [Warmth](./Warmth.md) as long as Warming Up is active:

- Instantly replenishes a small amount of the Warmth bar (20% for drinks, less for food). If [First Aid](./First%20Aid.md) teas are consumed and the survivor doesn't have [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) that may be cured by the respective cures, the Warmth gain will be 40%.

- A plus sign ('+') appears on the Warmth bar indicating Warming Up Affliction, which slows down the loss of warmth during cold. Reduces Warmth loss by 50% compared to your current [Feels Like](./Feels%20Like.md) temperature as long as Warming Up is active.

- Partial consumption provides partial Warmth benefit but resets Afflictions' duration anew which in addition provide a fixed Warmth amount and full Warming Up duration on the final moment of complete consumption.

It is possible to warm up some food and drinks without directly cooking on a fire's cooking slot, thus sparing a cooking slot. By placing them around an active fire, multiple teas and canned goods can be warmed up at once.
Note that some of these items are only available to players who purchased [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md).
