![Warmth icon](../assets/Warmth_icon.png) **Warmth** is one of the four essential [needs](./Needs.md). Warmth is a measure of the temperatures the player is exposed to. The player's warmth drains when the temperature the character experiences dips below 0°C (32°F) and is regained when it is above. Exposure to the [elements](./Weather.md) is the main reason for loss of warmth and can be countered by staying indoors, having good [clothing](./Clothing.md), being near a [fire](./Fire.md), and by consuming [hot food and drinks](./Warming%20Up.md). Warmth will also deplete completely immediately if you fall into freezing water. When warmth is depleted, [condition](./Condition.md) starts to rapidly deplete and is able to kill within hours. This makes warmth the most critical need to satisfy.

Detailed temperature information is viewable on the player status page, beneath the Needs meters. The most critical piece of information is the [feels like](./Feels%20Like.md) temperature, which is the key to maintaining warmth. As long as it is greater than 0°C (32°F), the character will gain warmth; if it is below 0°C (32°F), warmth will be lost. How quickly warmth is gained or lost is directly proportional to how far from the freezing temperature the character is feeling (e.g., -8°C will cause the warmth meter to deplete much faster than -1°C).

The warmth meter degrades through various states between Warm and Freezing (Warm, Chilled, Cold, Numb, Freezing). Chevrons (arrows) beside the meter point either up or down in the bar to indicate which direction the player's warmth is progressing, with more chevrons indicating faster progress.
The character is fully warm when the bar is full and is freezing when the bar is empty. The amount of time the bar takes to fill or deplete depends on the 'feels like' temperature.

On Interloper difficulty the temperature breaks are significantly reduced (see tables below) meaning a one hour warm to freezing temperature of just -9°C compared to -15°C in Stalker. The rate at warmth loss is also not linear and makes the 1st temperature break far more significant and therefore every degree within the 1st chevron bracket much more important.

It is also important to realize that the brackets are a sliding scale and the tables below are only true for that temperature. For instance, in Interloper difficulty, a temperature of -8°C (a single downward chevron 'v' on the HUD) does not mean you can stay out for 15 hours. In this example, a full warmth bar will deplete in just over 1 hour of in-game time (5 minutes of real-time).

In V1.15 the only way to check the 'feels like' temperature is to open the character status window (default 'f' key) however it should be a valuable source of information as a single chevron on the HUD meter could well represent the ability to stay out for hours, or a mere matter of minutes.

Hot foods and drinks can be used for extra warmth. When consumed, they bestow both a boost to the warmth meter and a buff affliction, [Warming up](./Warming%20Up.md), to make the character lose warmth slower. This boost can be used to stave off freezing for a short time when conditions do not allow for a full warm-up. See [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md).

When the warmth meter is empty the player enters a state called 'freezing', and condition begins to drain rapidly. The rate of drain is constant regardless of how far below freezing the character is feeling. Even 1° below freezing is enough to maintain the rate at -20% condition each hour. 'Feels like' temperature must be brought above 0°C (32°F) to end this state and stop the condition loss. The [Hypothermia](./Hypothermia.md) affliction will set in after 2 hours of freezing, doubling the rate to -40% per hour. Meaning freezing drains health the fastest of The needs. Surviving more than 3 hours while freezing is unlikely.

_**Warning**: Engaging in time accelerated activity (e.g., [carcass harvesting](./Harvesting.md)) while freezing has resulted in many [deaths](./Condition.md) due to this rapid and sudden condition loss._

Standing next to an active [fire](./Fire.md) will prevent condition loss due to freezing when playing on Pilgrim and Voyageur difficulties. Stalker and Interloper players must be near a fire that is hot enough to produce a 'feels like temperature above 0°C (32°F).

If one is freezing and has no hope of getting out of a freezing status due to the weather conditions, it may be wise to temporarily remove all clothing items. Since the loss to condition from freezing is constant and not dependent on how cold the character feels, taking off all one's clothes has no detrimental effect to warmth if one is already freezing. Storing clothing may help avoid some unnecessary item [decay](./Decay.md) and prevent clothing items from getting wet, especially in blizzards or when passing through waterfalls.

Note that exposed skin is prone to [frostbite](./Afflictions.md#Frostbite), which causes irreversible condition loss, so removing clothing, particularly while outdoors in cold, windy conditions can have more severe side effects.

If clothing becomes substantially wet then it will lower the total warmth factor of that article of clothing, thereby affecting the player's total "feel like" warmth rating. If wet clothing is not dried off from being indoors or near a fire, it has a chance to freeze over. Wearing frozen clothing will not only degrade the total warmth value of the clothing item, but can also result in [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md) in the area of the body it currently being worn on (ex: Frozen mittens will start causing Frostbite in the hands) if it is not removed. it is generally advised to remove or swap out wet/frozen clothing so that is can be unfrozen and dried in order to keep the player warm.

[Hypothermia](./Afflictions.md) is an affliction that is applied whenever a character's warmth remains at freezing for 2 consecutive hours or if a player falls through thin ice. Once afflicted, the player's condition loss will double the rate of loss from freezing and [fatigue](./Fatigue.md) will drain rapidly. Hypothermia can only be cured by maintaining a feels like temperature above 0°C (32°F) for 24 continuous hours.

- There is currently no penalty for getting too hot. Even at "feels like" temperatures in excess of 50°C (122°F), especially when working for long hours near 150°C (270°F) [Forges](./Forge.md), the warmth bar will not go above "warm". In real life, these temperatures would be unbearable, and would result in excessive sweating (dehydration), heatstroke, or burning of exposed skin.
- "So cold (shivers) think of fire (shivers) yeah, hot fire. (shivers)-PHUGH! (shivers)" (Female Survivor)
- (Various shivering noises from the player character, sometimes followed by frustrated grunts)

**Waste Not, Want Not** is an [achievement](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Achievements.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

This achievement is obtained after harvesting ten entire [deer](./Deer.md) carcasses in a single [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) game. It is most easily done on Pilgrim, but will also be eventually acquired through normal gameplay, especially on harder difficulties where manufactured food is rarer. A [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md) or [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md) is highly recommended.

Consuming Potable Water restores [Thirst](./Thirst.md) and carries no risk of disease ([Dysentery](./Dysentery.md)) since it has been properly sterilized. Potable Water will never revert back into [Water (Unsafe)](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md).

Bottles of Potable Water can be found indoors, in vehicles, harvested from [Toilets](./Toilet.md), [Industrial Toilets](./Industrial%20Toilet.md), a [Basin](./Basin.md), or produced from boiling Unsafe water at a fire/sterilizing it with [Water Purification Tablets](./Water%20Purification%20Tablets.md).

Unsafe water can be created by melting snow at an active fire's Cooking Spot, and takes 20 minutes to melt 0.5 liter (0.13 gal). Gathering snow is done automatically, though the player must supply a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md), [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md), or [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md) to contain the snow as it melts into water.
- Water is relatively heavy at 1 kg/L and can quickly overburden the player in large quantities.
- If left on an active fire, 0.5L of purified water will boil away after 30 minutes (in-game). The more water in the container, the longer it takes to boil away.
Unsafe water can be turned into Potable Water through [boiling](./Fire.md#Processing_water) or [purifying](./Water%20Purification%20Tablets.md):

- [Water Purification Tablets](./Water%20Purification%20Tablets.md) can be consumed to convert up to 1L of Unsafe Water into an equivalent amount of Potable Water. They can be found in the "Medical" tab of the Inventory, and then selecting "Use" while carrying them and the Unsafe Water. This sterilization process takes 1 minute (in-game). Alternatively, select "Purify Water" while in the fire menu. Note that a fire/Cooking Spot is not actually required to use purification tablets.
Water requires no container to carry, and despite displaying as a jug in the inventory, will appear as a water bottle when dropped.
- Quantities in excess of 1.0L will be divided into multiple 1.0L bottles, potentially with a smaller bottle as the remainder.

- Quantities in excess of 1.0L which are round numbers (2.0L, 3.0L, etc.) have the potential of being divided between small and large bottles. This cannot be controlled by the player and the division seems to be completely random. Dropping 3.0L, for example, can give you three large 1L bottles or two large 1L bottle and two small 0.50L bottles or any other such combination.

Note: Unsafe and Potable water bottles are identical in appearance, and similar in one's inventory. Take care when dropping bottles of Unsafe Water that they are not close to bottles of Potable Water, to prevent accidental drinking.

Consuming Unsafe Water restores [Thirst](./Thirst.md), like [Potable Water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md), but has a chance to infect the player with [Dysentery](./Dysentery.md); a serious and fatal disease if left untreated. The chance for gaining Dysentary is not a set chance unlike eating meat raw ([Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md)), as the Affliction is granted via a RNG dice roll depending on how much dirty water is consumed (ex: Sometimes drinking even 0.01L will give Dysentery, while other times it is given after drinking 1.50L of dirty water). Generally speaking, the more Water (Unsafe) is consumed, the higher the chance of acquiring Dysentery.
Water (Unsafe) cannot be accessed in the [Radial Menu](./Radial%20Menu.md) by default; it must be manually be consumed in the Backpack menu of the [Survival Menu](./Survival%20Menu.md).

Unsafe Water can be created by melting snow at in a container at an active [fire's](./Fire.md) Cooking Spot, and takes 20 minutes to melt 0.5 liter (0.13 gal). Gathering snow is done automatically, though the player must supply a [Recycled Can](./Recycled%20Can.md), [Cooking Pot](./Cooking%20Pot.md), or [Cooking Skillet](./Cooking%20Skillet.md) to contain the snow as it melts into water.
- Water is relatively heavy at 1kg/L and can quickly overburden the player in large quantities.

- Water is almost exclusively obtained by by melting snow, and only found naturally at the [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) (contained within a metal [Basin](./Basin.md) on the work bench), and in the [Industrial Toilets](./Industrial%20Toilet.md) of the [Signal Void](./Signal%20Void.md) bunkers. It is also rarely found in containers.
- It is possible to obtain endless amounts of Unsafe Water from a [Water Tower](./Water%20Tower.md) on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md).
Unsafe water can be turned into [Potable Water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) through [boiling](./Fire.md#Processing_water) or purifying:

- [Water Purification Tablets](./Water%20Purification%20Tablets.md) can be consumed to convert up to 1L of Unsafe Water into an equivalent amount of Potable Water. They can be found in the "Medical" tab of the Inventory, and then selecting "Use" while carrying them and the Unsafe Water. This sterilization process takes 1 minute (in-game). Alternatively, select "Purify Water" while in the fire menu. Note that a fire/Cooking Spot is not actually required to use purification tablets.
Water requires no container to carry, and despite displaying as a jug in the inventory, will appear as a plastic blue water bottle when dropped.
- Quantities in excess of 1.00L will be divided into multiple 1.00L bottles, potentially with a smaller bottle as the remainder.

Note: Unsafe and Potable water bottles are identical in appearance, and similar in one's inventory. Take care when dropping bottles of Unsafe Water that they are not close to bottles of Potable Water, to prevent accidental consumption. When picked up, the icon for Potable water will be a water symbol, while Unsafe Water will have a circular cross through the water symbol.

Water drawn from Toilets always yields Potable Water and never Unsafe Water, regardless of where on a Toilet one selects; this suggests water is only drawn from the toilet's reservoir tank which is used to flush waste and not the bowl where waste arrives. The only exception to this rule is the Signal Void bunkers.

> “**A packet of water purification tablets. Can help prevent dysentery. One tablet treats 1L/0.26 gallon of non-potable water.**”
**Water Purification Tablets** are a consumable to convert [Unsafe Water](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md) into [Potable Water](./Water%20%28Potable%29.md) in [The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Water Purification Tablets are a consumable item which can be used to convert up to 1 litre of Unsafe Water into 1 litre of Potable Water per tablet. Boxes always initially contain 4 tablets. Purifying water takes one in-game minute.
- Since Unsafe Water is almost exclusively produced at a fire, Water Purification Tablets are of niche usefulness and are comparable to the fuel required to boil 1L of water and make it Potable.
- Using the tablets instead of boiling the water will save between 19-29 in-game minutes per liter of water, depending on the player's [Cooking](./Cooking.md) level.

- Water Purification Tablets degrade in condition over time indoors and outside, and will vanish if inside of a Container when becoming Ruined (0% condition). Ruined tablets outside of containers can still be used, and tablets of the same condition stack. In console edition, ruined (0% condition) tablets are useless. Condition does not affect conversion rate.
- Note: it is more time effective to use these directly from your inventory rather than at a fire - it will take approximately one in-game minute per tablet compared to ten.

- These tablets can be useful when time is of the essence, such as in the [Whiteout](./Whiteout.md) and especially [Hopeless Rescue](./Hopeless%20Rescue.md) [challenges](./Challenge.md) to complete said challenge in the best possible time, but are less useful in Survival and [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) due to the abundance and accessibility of fuel.

**DLC-Exclusive content.** This content requires the [Iron Road](./Iron%20Road.md) addon to be installed before it can be seen or used in regular gameplay.
A **Water Tower** is a stationary interactable object in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md) only found in railyards on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md).

A **Water Tower** initially contains 6,000 liters of [Unsafe Water](./Water%20%28Unsafe%29.md), and is accompanied by two yellow signs labelled "WATER". When the Survivor pulls the train up close to the tower, a small sign under the signpost will flip a black panel to green a green one, letting them know that the [train](./Prototype%20Train.md) is in position to be filled (fuel and water caps must be in the middle of the signs to trigger this).

The player can then exit the train and walk over to the yellow lever on the side of the tower to start dispensing water. If the sign panel is not green, then the option to place water into the train directly will not appear.

Water is transferred into the train at a rate of 5.00 liters per minute (20.00 min cap at 5 minutes per increment), meaning that a fully empty locomotive can be refilled with 600.00 L of water in 2 hours. Make sure to turn the train Engine off while refueling, as this can burn already stored water and not fully refuel the train.

Water can also be transferred into the Survivor's backpack, 5.00 liters at a time. This may be useful for thirsty railroaders who want to [purify the water](./Water%20Purification%20Tablets.md), or boil it on the [train's](./Prototype%20Train.md) cooking slot while driving.
- Excess unsafe water can be stored on the train's [Cupboard](./Cupboard.md) for later use (either for boiling or for the train).
- Keep in mind that passing time while refueling the train will put the Survivor at risk from the elements, so make sure the weather is warm.
- Passing time and canceling the refueling process part way will only deposit a partial amount of water into the train up until the moment it is canceled. (needs verification).
- Water Towers refuel over time, so that the player will never run out of water for the train.
- If the water level in the tower falls below 4,900 liters, it will immediately refill, allowing the tower to serve as an infinite source of Unsafe Water.

violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Wax Cylinder 12**_
I feel like I haven't been warm since I arrived on this damn rock. Even in summer the pale sun's warmth doesn't penetrate the cold.
It's all fine and good to build up a railway that runs on whale oil, but if we truly want this energy source to flourish we need to find some novel applications.
I've been tinkering with something more modest, but useful considering the climate we find ourselves in.

I've contrived a portable heater made from lantern parts and some other bits and pieces I was able to machine. It has been designed to consume Whale Oil as fuel, using our soon-to-be patented mix and injection system.
It's a miniaturized version of, essentially, part of the mechanism that makes the train engine run so well.
It puts out enough heat to warm up a small room and the oil in the reservoir will burn for hours, provided you keep the temperature fairly low.
I could see such a tool being useful as a replacement for coal stoves and wood fireplaces, in locations where those fuel supplies are not that available.

There may be applications for emergency use as well. My mind goes to, for example, that group of workers that were trapped in the blizzard a few months ago and all came back with frostbite. This heater might have prevented permanent damage.
I'm going to pass this unit on to St.Germain to get some of his boys to test it in the field, and if the results are suitable I'll expand the trial to a second iteration of the design.
I already have some ideas for how to improve it, not to mention other applications for this fuel source.
Of course, its usefulness is partly hindered by the lack of widespread access to whale oil supplies, but that's something we'll have to solve at some point regardless.
If we expand the testing program, we can probably rely on fuel supply caches until we think of something better.
Eventually, some kind of household-to-household fuel replenishing program could probably work. On a large scale, like getting milk delivered to your home.
I will say I miss the long talks McLeod and I once had when we were closer. There aren't many others on this island who share an engineer's love of tinkering, and I'm left to speak mainly to myself.
Not everyone here is equal to our ambitions, or the ones we once had at any rate, and I do miss sparring with another great mind.

The Reverend -- he insists I use his Christian name, Angus, but I find it uncomfortable as this is not how things are done back home in Norway.
Last week he left me one of McLeod's cylinder players, and some music to listen to. He said he felt it would help me remain in a "pastoral" mood.
I know you are suffering, and if not for the money I make here I would see no reason for us to be half a world apart.
I heard from your mother that she had you out at the seaside, and that the air did you good.
She said your lungs are still hurting. Why did you tell me otherwise in your last letter?
My plan is, every time I feel lonely for home, to record a message to you and tell you something beautiful I have seen.

I love Norway, but if there is one thing this experience has taught me, it's that there is a whole big world out there for us to discover.
This morning I watched the sun rise over the rocky landscape. As the warmth hit the water, a mist began to rise, and the light made the mist glow like candlelight.
It reminded me of our small church back home, and the way the candles flicker over your face, whenever you play the organ there.

I do it for the children. The innocents, who do not deserve to live through what is happening here.
I've heard that he's planning to break everything. Collecting all the records, then smashing or melting them down.
I will gather all the records that I can, and hide them. So McLeod cannot ever find them.
I love you, Erik. I will hide this cylinder if I can't find anyone to take it off the island.

violations.context: _The following text is transcribed from **Wax Cylinder 9**_
If you've made it this far, I'm impressed. You're one of a small handful of people to get to this point in years.
Cauldron Island is actually a chain of islands, formed by a giant flooded volcanic crater.

Each island of this caldera is connected by an elevated rail bridge. McLeod built sections that could be raised or lowered by hydraulics, to make space for ships to pass under. Honestly, really impressive stuff for the time.
Unfortunately, this is one part of the island's infrastructure I've not been able to crack since the aurora appeared. I had no issues with them until that whole thing happened.
For now, these bridges seem to work intermittently, based on some weird interaction with the aurora.
You just have to be in the right place at the right time. So, unfortunately for both of us, that means you may need to wait.
Meanwhile, this could be a good opportunity to get used to the train. It's going to be your home for a while, so you may as well get comfortable with it.
I suppose if we're going to be on this journey together, I should at least introduce myself.
I'm an engineer. And fortunately for you, I'm stubborn as rocks. Came here before the shit hit the fan with the aurora and the rest of it. Been stuck here since.
Took me a while to contrive the boat back to Great Bear, and by the time I figured that out...
Everything you see around you, all of Cauldron Island, was at one point my great-grandfather's personal kingdom.
And then the king tried to tear it all down. To hide it, so the world would never know what happened here.
I grew up in its shadow, never knowing the truth. Went my whole life hearing whispers, until finally my mother brought me in on the family secret.
She spent her whole life trying to uncover the truth, and died without ever completing the work.

**Weak Ice** (also known as **Thin Ice**) is an uncommon but dangerous [Environmental Hazard](./Environmental%20Hazard.md) found within some [Regions](./Region.md) of [_The Long Dark_.](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)

![The Weak Ice icon](../assets/Weak_Ice_icon.png)_The Weak Ice icon_ Most of the icy ground of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) is traversable but some ice sheets are weak and pose a hazard when the survivor moves on them. When standing on thin ice the "Weak Ice" indicator will appear in the center of the screen, a unique sound will play and cracks will form at survivor's feet. If the survivor does not move off the weak ice in time they will fall into the water below.

While standing on Weak ice the "Weak Ice" indicator is present and a hidden timer will play (5 seconds) and at the end if the player is still standing on Weak Ice they will fall through it. [Crampons](./Crampons.md) and [Improvised Crampons](./Improvised%20Crampons.md) can add the [Sure Footing](./Sure%20Footing.md) benefit, granting additional time before falling through (6 seconds with [Crampons](./Crampons.md) and 5.5 seconds with [Improvised Crampons](./Improvised%20Crampons.md) instead of 5 seconds).

[Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md), [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md) and [Sprained Ankles](./Sprained%20Ankle.md) reduce movement speed and can make it more difficult or even impossible to move off Weak Ice in time. Sprinting can be used to cross some but not all small patches of Weak Ice safely (such as some in Forlorn Muskeg). Wildlife cannot cross Weak Ice, which can be used to the player's advantage to evade wildlife or gauge an area's ice patches in places such as Forlorn Muskeg. Weak Ice also serves as boundary along the ocean.

[Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) is a mechanic which causes items and points-of-interest to appear along the beaches of coastal regions. These items may be looted freely, but may put the survivor at risk of Weak Ice.

Falling through Weak Ice will result in a fade to black and the player being moved to a nearby safe location to stand. Time will move forward several in-game minutes and a hole will have formed in the ice where they fell initially through.
Wet clothes are a serious Condition hazard by [Freezing](./Needs.md), this damage is doubled by the Hypothermia affliction and the risk of [Frostbite](./Frostbite.md).

If the survivor falls through Weak Ice, it is recommend to quickly find shelter and build a fire to warm up. Wet Clothing may be dried by being worn or when dropped/placed indoors or near a lit [Campfire](./Campfire.md) or other fire source.
- [Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md) Part 2 Update added a graphical update to Thin Ice when active as well as the updating the Beachcombing mechanic.

- In the real world some Weak ice may be traversed by dispersing one's bodyweight such as crawling while prone. This mechanic is not present within _The Long Dark_, and crouching does not affect Weak Ice.

**Weakened State** is an [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) acquired after choosing to [Cheat Death](./Cheat%20Death.md).
> “**You are weakened. For a time, your Condition will recover more slowly and your Stamina will drain more quickly.**”
Choosing to Cheat Death will give the player Weakened State, and is always paired with the temporary or permanent [Cheated Death Penalty](./Cheated%20Death%20Penalty.md) Affliction.

- The world will have a Black and White filter placed over it, making it harder to distinguish items and threats, especially in low lighting conditions. This is similar to turning on "Noir" in the "Image Filter" options setting.

Waiting the allotted Recovery Time will clear the Affliction. In this time, it is advised to avoid exploring until the Affliction has passed and your Condition has recovered. Once the Affliction heals, the Black and White filter will instantly disappear.

The Recovery Time for this Affliction is different for each Experience (Cheat Death is not enabled on [Misery Mode](./Misery.md) however). Dying multiple times and choosing to Cheat Death does not cause the Recovery Times to stack if the previous Affliction was not healed.

The station sits on a plateau on a large pillar and dominates the surrounding landscape. The station can be reached by a route in the east of the region crossing over two bridges and a rope climb and over the Second Pillar. In years past, the station used to be connected to the mountain road by a bridge, which has long since collapsed.
A grey [Truck](./Truck.md) is parked outside the buildings, with another blue truck crashed and destroyed along the road further down the side of the mountain.
The first objective of the [Last Horizon](./Last%20Horizon.md) Tale is located here, and is found buried in the snow near the radar station.

Large amounts of [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) (at least 3 boxes of 15 rounds) and a single [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md) always spawn in the area, with the items changing location each playthrough (can be found in the radar dome, truck, stairwell, etc.).

Making this location a [Safe House](./Safehouse.md) is not advised, as it is very isolated from the rest of the region and has few resources. The high altitude and exposed location also makes the area around the station EXTREMELY cold, even during the warmest evenings.

However, at least 3 [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) Nests can be found around this area: one near the Truck, one near Second Pillar and one below the rope climb second below Second Pillar, providing ample opportunities to gather [Ptarmigan Down](./Ptarmigan%20Down.md) and meat for a time. A [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md) can be found in the storage shed, one of two in the whole region.

There is a Hunting Rifle and unusual amount of Rifle Ammunition boxes strewn about the premises. A [Bloody note](./Bloody%20note.md) in the radar building mentions that they belonged to a single worker keeping the Station going, with him complaining that he is running out of supply shipments and cannot simply eat his ammo to survive.

> “**Mountain blizzards blow through here from time to time. People get stuck indoors, or worse... They wander in circles, only to die within reach of their homes. Even when they are right there in front of them. And they say Grey Mother is blind! Ha!**”
**Weather** is the state of the atmosphere outdoors on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), in _The Long Dark_.

Weather conditions can change from clear, sunny (or starry) skies, foggy, windy, and blizzards. Traveling in different weather conditions affects movement speed, overall vision, [Warmth](./Warmth.md), wetness of Clothing, and decay rate of worn clothes. The time of day paired with certain weather conditions can make for either a much colder or warmer day as well.

Changes in weather evolve over time, rather than spontaneously: such as fog gradually building, winds dying down, or clouds clearing. This change can occur up or down in severity. Weather may last between 2-12 hours.
- [Region](./Region.md) plays a prominent role in weather, with some types of weather being favored to occur more often in particular regions.

- [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) tends to have calm weather per episode, with some episodes never featuring certain kinds of extreme weather at all (Ex. Aurora and Blizzards never occur naturally in [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md)). This can change as progress is made in the story.
- [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) has several factors in weather frequency and severity.
- Pilgrim features mostly clear skies and cloudy weather, with only rare blizzards and fog.
- Stalker and Interloper have regular poor weather patterns, rapid changes in weather and wind direction, and notably frequent blizzards.

Weather affects the temperature inside of [Vehicles](./Vehicle.md), but not indoors. High Winds and Blizzards can be heard even when indoors, and Aurora are visible through windows and will power tools, objects (radios, lights, [computers](./Buffer%20Memories.md)) and deadly [live wires](./Burns.md) indoors. [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md) can also affect electrical devices in the environment indoors or outdoors, and can even cause [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md).

| Clear | Common and warm for relative time of day. May occur day or night. - Warm. - High visibility. - [Crows](./Crow.md) will circle above frozen corpses and animal carcasses. | Calm-High | Yes | Yes | Yes |

| Aurora | May only occur at night during clear weather. - Bright aurora of red, orange, yellow or green appear in the night sky. - [Predatory Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) is more aggressive and ignores common determent methods (e.g. [campfires](./Campfire.md)). - Electrical devices become powered, such as: [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md), [Miner's Flashlight](./Miner%27s%20Flashlight.md), [Computers](./Buffer%20Memories.md), [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md), [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md), radios, lights, and deadly [live wires](./Burns.md). - [Crows](./Crow.md) will circle above frozen corpses and animal carcasses, despite being nightime. For more information, see [Auroras](./Aurora.md). | Calm-moderate | No | Yes | No |
| Cloudy | Two variants: partly cloudy and cloudy (overcast). - Slightly darker dimmer with abundant clouds; Overcast may evolve from Partly Cloudy. - Slightly cold. | Calm-High | Yes | Yes | No |

| Fog | Two variants: light or dense. Fog may evolve from light to moderate to heavy over time. - Slightly cold. - Can cause disorientation and make avoiding predators difficult. - Light: long distance visibility loss. - Moderate: medium visibility loss. - Heavy: blinding visibility loss. | Calm-Light | Yes | No | No |

| Glimmer Fog | A heavy variant of fog, but charged with electrostatic particles. Only occurs during the day during clear weather. - Blinding visibility loss - Snow and Ice visibly and audibly crackles with electricity - Generates the [Insomnia](./Insomnia.md) [Affliction](./Afflictions.md) - Electrical devices become powered, such as: [flashlight](./Flashlight.md), [Miner's Flashlight](./Miner%27s%20Flashlight.md), [computers](./Buffer%20Memories.md), [Handheld Shortwave Radio](./Handheld%20Shortwave%20Radio.md), radios, lights. - [Live wires](./Burns.md) do not activate. For more information, see [Glimmer Fog](./Glimmer%20Fog.md). | Calm-Light | Yes | No | No |

| Toxic Fog | A dangerous variant of fog only found in the [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md) Challenge. Weather begins clear and slowly transitions from light fog to heavy fog. - [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) fills an entire region after ~30 real-world minutes within in; larger/smaller regions have their Toxic Fog timers adjusted accordingly. - Current Toxic Fog progress is shown for each region by viewing it on the map. A UI element will appear if less than half of the region's timer remains, turning red below 2 minutes remaining. - Toxic Fog in a region also RUINs all food in the backpack, indoors, outdoors, and animal carcasses. Instantly kills all wildlife when timer close to up. | Calm-Light | Yes | No | No |

| Snowfall | Two variants: light or heavy snow. Falling snow/flurries which may evolve into a Blizzard. - Moderately cold. - Light-moderate snowfall (reduces duration of tracks, wets/freezes clothing) | Calm-moderate | No | Yes | No |

| Blizzard | Enduring and dangerous storm. - Extremely cold. - Damages worn clothing. - Heavy snowfall (reduces duration of tracks, wets/freezes clothing) - Medium visibility loss. - Constant high winds: sounds like a 'train' even when indoors. - Beachcombing items spawn on the coastal regions. Despawns previous containers or special items washed up on the last blizzard. - If you are outside after a blizzard begins, wildlife may not spawn, making some meats and guts trips "safer" | High | No | No | No |

Winds affects [Windchill](./Clothing.md) (which makes the "Feels Like" temperature colder), and can extinguish exposed fires, prevent lighting fires, and slow movement. Wind changes direction and speed over time (based on [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md)). There are 5 types of Wind: Calm, Light, Moderate, High, Blizzard.

- High: slows movement speed, lighting exposed fires is impossible (unsheltered [Campfires](./Fire.md), [torches](./Torch.md) or [matches](./Matches%20%28disambiguation%29.md)), extinguishes exposed fires. [Storm Lanterns](./Storm%20Lantern.md), [Flares](./Flare.md), [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), Fire Barrels, [Forges](./Forge.md), [Wood Stoves](./Wood%20Stove.md) and Cast Iron Stoves are immune to the effects of High Winds.
- Blizzard: same as High, however the player does not suffer from a movement speed penalty. Clothing is prone to being torn, and getting wet/frozen.

![Crouching to get Wind Shield (Wind blowing from ahead)](../assets/Windshield_crouch.gif)_Crouching to get Wind Shield (Wind blowing from ahead)_ The [Wind Shield](./Survival%20Overlay.md) is an icon which appears at the top of the UI if a solid object is between the player and oncoming High Winds. When shielded, Windchill temperature is eliminated almost completely and the player is only subjected to the ambient Air temperature. This icon can be used to stay warmer, move faster, or to find campfire locations currently sheltered from the wind. High Winds slows movement in 45° cone around the wind's current direction across the entire region, and a 2m radius around solid objects; this means that to be sheltered from the wind the player (or a campfire) must be on the correct side (opposite) of a solid object relative to oncoming wind and be close to it.

Even very small outcroppings, rocks, and objects like cars can provide a shield from the wind, as well as crouching to get behind a low part of terrain. This makes it possible to sometimes strategically get behind trees or trunks while breaking down [Scrub Brush](./Scrub%20Brush.md), [Branches](./Branch.md), even potentially regaining body temperature at the same time; if Wind Chill is the only thing getting the player below the 0°C threshold.

Moving (walking or sprinting) into the direction of oncoming High Winds reduces movement speed by up to 50% (additive with other penalties: [sprained ankles](./Sprained%20Ankle.md) and [Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md)). High Winds slows movement in 45° cone around the wind's current direction across the entire region, there is no movement penalty when walking in directions outside this cone or when shielded from the wind.
This penalty is reduced by 25% with the active [feat](./Feats.md) Blizzard Walker (aka wind penalty reduced from 25% to 18.5% penalty, or a +6.25% movement increase when walking into oncoming wind).

[Campfires](./Campfire.md) are not extinguished by High Winds, but instead their fuel duration capped at a maximum of 10 minutes (displays as "9", due to fuel consumption and rounding). Refueling a campfire experiencing high winds refreshes its duration, but any fuel beyond 10 minutes of burn time is wasted: this makes all fuel sources except [Stick](./Stick.md) extremely wasteful. In survival situations where a wind-blown campfire is vital, Sticks are the ideal fuel source and should be used one at a time when the fire is at "1 minute" remaining or embers (embers lasts for 5 minutes in-game).

Different regions have different air temperatures, ranging from -30°C to -38°C during early morning hours (i.e. the coldest time of the day) and rising all the way up to temperatures between -5°C and -25°C during the evening hours (i.e. the warmest time of the day). During blizzards the temperature can drop by another 10°C-15°C.

The in-game air temperature is also affected by the "World Gets Colder Over Time" setting, which is tied to the [Experience Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md). The world starts to grow gradually colder after a set amount of days has passed and continues to drop until the temperature reaches the coldest it will get after a set amount of days. > “**You've managed to prevent starvation for 72 consecutive hours. You're full of energy and can carry more gear. You're also better able to face the physical trials ahead -- your Condition is increased as a result.**”

Well Fed activates when the player has managed to avoid starvation ([calorie store count](./Hunger.md) at 0) for 72 hours (three full days). When this is achieved, the player character will get a 5% buff to maximum [Condition](./Condition.md) (capping it at 105%) and an increased [carrying capacity](./Encumbrance.md) of 5.00 kg (11.00 lbs.)

The carrying capacity effects stack with wearing a [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) and [Technical Backpack](./Technical%20Backpack.md), meaning that having all 3 present adds 15.00 kg (33.00 lbs) to your 30.00 kg [Encumbrance](./Encumbrance.md) capacity. Max Carry Weight can be increased further by acquiring the [Unburdened](./Unburdened.md) affliction, temporarily increasing max Carry Weight by 3.00 kg for 3 hours, thus raising the maximum Carry Weight possible to 48.00 kg.
Reaching Starvation at any point (reaching 0 Calorie Store) or gaining the [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md) Affliction will remove Well Fed and its effects.

If Well Fed is not already active, then achieving 0 calorie store/Chemical Poisoning will reset the 72-hour timer required to activate Well Fed. This mechanic (and [Scurvy](./Scurvy.md)) is designed to counteract the benefits of [Hibernation](./Hibernation.md).

This affliction was added in the [2018 December Update](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog%20%E2%80%94%20Archive%201.md#1.41) and is the fourth positive affliction added to the game at the time (the other three being [Warming Up](./Warming%20Up.md), [Improved Rest](./Improved%20Rest.md), and [Fatigue Reduced](./Fatigue%20Reduced.md)) being the only one not requiring the consumption of specific food items to activate as well as the only one not having a set effect duration.

A **Whale Oil Can** is a [Tools](./Tools.md) item exclusively found on [Cauldron Island](./Cauldron%20Island.md) in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

Very old fuel cans carrying refined whale oil. These cans are the primary fuel source for the [Prototype Train](./Prototype%20Train.md) and several unique tools. The cans themselves always weight 0.10 kg, with a maximum of 5.00 L of fuel capable of being stored inside (5.10 kg max weight).

Whale Oil Cans can always be produced at a train [Oil Tank](./Oil%20Tank.md) refueling depot. These containers take the form of a green tank and can generate up to 5.00 L of cans in 1 minute. These refueling tanks refill after leaving the region for a day.

This is the mission transcript for mission 4 [What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md) of [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md).

_Mackenzie realizes all of his belongings, aside from the torn clothes on his back, are all gone. He begins walking away from the bear, as it feasts on a [Wolf Carcass](./Wolf%20Carcass.md). As he slowly walks to a nearby [Rock Climb](./Rock%20Climb.md) past the bear, he says:_

_Mackenzie climbs the wall, finding a narrow tunnel to crouch through as he wanders through the cave. After walking awhile, he sees a hole in the floor, with the Old Bear below as it begins following him. Mackenzie comes to a large chamber with a waterfall._

_Weaving through rocky passages too small for the bear to reach, Mackenzie eventually passes through a waterfall chamber as the bear feasts on a [Frozen Corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md). No matter what path lies ahead, the Old Bear follows through the tunnels. Eventually the Pilot finds a body with a [Torn Paper](./Torn%20Paper.md) on it and some medical supplies, and moves on to not join the doomed man and finds another large cavern._

_Mackenzie bobs and weaves through more small passages that the bear cannot follow. The next chamber is_ _a large room with an open ceiling, and_ _he_ _spots the red ribbon tied to his Spear_ _sitting on a rock._

_The Old Bear enters the chamber, continuing its pursuit of the pilot. Mackenzie squeezes through more small passages, patiently moving through the room until it is safe to grab the spear. He eventually makes a run for it, and grabs it._

_Mackenzie then goes on the offense, attacking the bear 3 times in a "Bear Spear Struggle" by plunging the spear into the overgrown mankiller's stomach. On the last attempt he finally kills the bear, getting the upper hand and repeatedly plunging the spear into the beast's neck. Mackenzie catches his breath as he looks over the lifeless body of the bear._
Mackenzie: "I'm...I'm sorry. Such a majestic creature. I didn't want to kill you. But this world will make murders of us all."
_The screen fades to black, and fades in with Mackenzie staggering into the Trapper's Homestead and falling on the floor._
_The Trapper's [Deerskin Boots](./Deerskin%20Boots.md) appear as Jeremiah walks over to the exhausted pilot and picks him up._

_Mackenzie falls to the floor and passes out. When he wakes up, time has passed and he finds himself in the Trapper's bed, the lights of the Aurora flickering outside the cabin. He starts getting out of bed as Jeremiah sees him._

Jeremiah: "You passed out. I let you rest, since I needed time to fix the radio. Ha. And what did I tell you? Those transponder parts did the trick. They were perfect. You did good, Mackenzie. You did good. Signal strength looks like it might be sufficient. But who knows how long it'll last, with this unpredictable aurora in the sky."

Jeremiah: "You need to find your lady friend. I need to reach someone too. And that was my only chance."

Jeremiah: "You need to take my message. You need to deliver it for me. It's important. You need to do it for me Mackenzie. It'll be weeks before I can travel that far...you need to do it for me Mackenzie."
Jeremiah: "You don't understand. You don't understand what's coming, Mackenzie. You have to take my message. Or else...none of the rest of it matters."
Jeremiah: "It's only a little detour for you, on the way to Perseverance Mills. A little detour that can change a lot. Maybe everything."
Jeremiah: "Go through Carter. You'll need to get the old elevator system working again. With the Aurora...it just might work. Go through Carter, the lower part of the dam. Look out for..."
Jeremiah: "Right, right. Through Carter, out the other side. You'll find your way to Signal Hill. Old weather service radio there. More powerful than my shortwave. You should be able to reach them."

> “**The Old Bear has dragged Mackenzie to its lair. Will he put the legendary bear's story to an end?**”

**What One Man Can Do** is the fourth mission in [Episode 2](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Story](./Wintermute.md). During the mission [Signal to Noise](./Signal%20to%20Noise.md), [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) is ambushed by the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md), who drags him to its den. Now with no belongings and only his wits to aid in his survival, Mackenzie must run and crawl throughout the [Old Bear's Den](./Old%20Bear%27s%20Den.md) until he find the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md), and finally kill the Old Bear.
A body with the [Torn Paper](./Torn%20Paper.md) note can be found halfway through the cave system.
Mackenzie ultimately succeeds in finding the spear and killing the beast, lamenting that he had to put down "such a majestic creature" but that "this new world makes murderers of us all".

- At the end of the mission, the player will spawn outside of the trapper's cabin with no way to re-enter. All items that were stored or dropped inside the cabin will be subsequently returned to the player's inventory. Players may want to consider moving stored items to another location prior to beginning this mission, in order to avoid being encumbered.
- Unlike the pre-redux version of Wintermute, the Old Bear cannot be harvested upon death. Killing the bear, triggers an immediate cutscene, removing the player from the area.
- You will lose everything in your backpack from being dragged and thrown about by the bear. Your belongings will be returned after the bear is killed.
- The title is a reference to the 1997 film The Edge, starring Anthony Hopkins and Alec Baldwin. In the film, a bear is stalking three men after their floatplane crashes in the Alaskan wilderness.

> “**Out here, people understand the value of hard work, good tools, and working with their hands...They say the most important tool out here is a hatchet or knife. But keeping em' sharp is the secret.**”

The Whetstone weighs 0.10 kilograms and can be found in containers and buildings likely to contain tools. It is always found in 100% condition. It generally spawns in industrial or sporting-type locations, (e.g., [Quonset Gas Station](./Quonset%20Garage.md) or [Trapper's Homestead](./Trapper%27s%20Homestead.md)).

The Whetstone is used in the [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) gameplay mechanic to restore the condition of bladed tools. Each use degrades the Whetstone 5% (20 max uses), but restores less than that amount in the target tool.

The [Sharpening](./Sharpening.md) [Skill](./Skills.md), which is only visible when maintaining a bladed tool and not listed in the player's journal, starts at 30 points. The skill points increase by 1 for each time the blade is sharpened.
- New Whetstones can either be very rarely found while [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) or purchased - maximum 1 per trade - from the [Trader](./Trader.md) after completing 4 Special Requests.

violations.context: > “__A monster blizzard is on the way. Will you be ready when it arrives?
The storm arrives in 30 days. Stockpile enough food, water, and supplies in the Coastal Highway Quonset Garage before it hits.__”
> “**Stockpile the food, water, and supplies listed in your journal. Store them in the Coastal Highway Quonset Garage (the starting location).**”

The objective of the challenge is to locate and retrieve all of the items listed in the journal during the allotted 30 days.![White Out Start](../assets/White_Out_Start.png) The survivor spawns inside the [Quonset Garage](./Quonset%20Garage.md) with 2000 calories, fully rested, fully warm, and with no thirst. The survivor's inventory has a [Bedroll](./Bedroll.md), low grade [Clothing](./Clothing.md), and some other miscellaneous items.

The Gas Station will be entirely empty when starting ([Medicine Shelf](./Medicine%20Shelf.md), [First Aid Kit](./First%20Aid%20Kit.md), [Drawer](./Drawer.md), [Register](./Register.md), [Locker](./Locker.md), [Metal Container](./Metal%20Container.md), both [Fridges](./Fridge.md). The [Basin](./Basin.md) will also be missing on the Work Bench). The only loot inside the Station are [Cardboard Boxes](./Cardboard%20Box.md) and wooden [Crates](./Crate.md) that can be broken down, a [Toilet](./Toilet.md) that contains a small amount of potable water, and 2 [Recycled Cans](./Recycled%20Can.md) (one is found under the bed, the other near the store shelves). Two [Work Benches](./Work%20Bench.md), a [Fire Barrel](./Fire%20Barrel.md), and a [Bed](./Bed.md) are still located inside to be used. The area around the [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md) will still be filled with objects such as Cars and [Pallets](./Pallets.md) to search.

As the challenge progresses, the weather gets harsher and hostile animals spawn in greater numbers. Initially however, conditions may still be challenging. Although predator spawns may be less common in the beginning, the player's lack of weapons (unless a revolver and ammunition spawned in the gas station) and protective clothing mean the relatively high density of wolves (and possibly a bear) near Quonset Garage can be deadly. Extra caution is required when entering and leaving the garage or when searching the area for supplies.

Note that the player does not have to survive the prophesied blizzard nor the entire allotted 30 days. Once all the items on the list are inside the gas station, the challenge ends. If the player fails to fully stock the Gas Station within 30 days, the Challenge will fail and must be restarted. ![Almanac](../assets/Almanac.jpg)

There is a new section of the [Journal](./Journal.md) exclusive to this Challenged called The "[Almanac](./Almanac.md)" which will tell the player the likelihood of a blizzard in the next 30 days, as well as its intensity on a scale from 1 to 5. This is similar to the [Saffir-Simpson wind scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSHS) used to measure the strength of hurricanes.
All of the following Items are required to complete the challenge:![Whiteout journal list](../assets/Whiteout_journal_list.jpg)

Items can be dropped onto the floor of the gas station or put inside containers in the gas station to be counted. Items in the survivor's inventory are not counted. The journal contains a live count; items removed from the gas station will be subtracted from the list progress. If the player is struggling to find resources, a trip to the [Summit](./Summit.md) of [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md) will provide everything necessary to complete the challenge.

The list does not seem to care whether meat is ruined or not so long as it is not picked up and placed back down. If Ruined food disappears while in containers, it will subtract from the total calories needed to complete the stored food objective. Taking food out and eating it also subtracts from the total.

One day's worth of food translates to roughly 3000 calories. Drinks such as sodas will contribute to the count, but [Herbal Tea](./Herbal%20Tea.md) and [Tin of Coffee](./Tin%20of%20Coffee.md) will not unless they are prepared into [Cup of Herbal Tea](./Cup%20of%20Herbal%20Tea.md) or [Cup of Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Coffee.md). [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md), [Rose Hip Tea](./Rose%20Hip%20Tea.md), [Burdock Tea](./Burdock%20Tea.md), and [Birch Bark Tea](./Birch%20Bark%20Tea.md) do count as calories for purposes of food. Lots of food can be found in the houses around the region, but this will not be enough to complete the challenge. Killing a [moose](./Moose.md) or [bear](./Bear.md) will provide ample food, and more can be found in the houses at [Thomson's Crossing](./Thomson%27s%20Crossing.md) and the [Crash Site](./Crash%20Site%20%28Pleasant%20Valley%29.md) in [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).

Softwood/Hardwood includes [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) and [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md), but not [Firelogs](./Firelog.md). Reclaimed Wood is easily obtained from the [Pallets](./Pallets.md) outside the garage, while sticks and limbs are common throughout the forest around the [Coastal Townsite](./Coastal%20Townsite.md).
A Hunting Rifle must be stored for this objective, a Revolver will not count. Extra rifles spawn in Coastal Highway compared with a normal survival game, rifles are extremely rare in other regions.

Rifle cartridges may be loaded into the hunting rifle or unloaded. If there aren't enough cartridges in Coastal Highway, sufficient numbers can usually be found in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) or [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md).

[Lantern Fuel](./Lantern%20Fuel.md) that is within the [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md) counts toward the Lantern Fuel requirement. If the player does not have enough, Ice fishing near the garage will yield more lamp oil. [Jerry Cans](./Jerry%20Can.md) will also add to the total Lamp Fuel needed.

If the player can't find a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md), it may be easier to head to [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) and forge an [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md) at [The Riken](./The%20Riken.md), as the Improvised Hatchet counts as an acceptable substitute. The [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md) required for forging the hatchet can usually be found either at The Riken or nearby in [Hibernia Processing](./Hibernia%20Processing.md).

The **Wide Display Shelf** is a [Decorations](./Decorations.md) item that can be [Crafted](./Crafting.md) as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.
A makeshift wooden display shelf, a Wide Display Shelf can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md).
The shelf contains 9 small shelves for displaying items, with 2 drawers below that have a storage capacity of 10.00 kg each, for a total capacity of 20.00 kg of storage.

Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The shelf can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor or a flat surface when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value, the shelf cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move or destroy it (destroying the shelf will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).

_Wilderness Kitchen_ can be researched for 5 hours that can be broken into multiple 1-hour minimum research sessions. 10 [Cooking skill points](./Cooking.md#Skill_levels) are awarded on completing the research. - [Warmth](./Warmth.md), [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Thirst](./Thirst.md), and [Hunger](./Hunger.md) exceed 0%

The hour of research that was in progress will not be completed and any time that had already been spent will be wasted. For a multiple-hour research session, only the incomplete hour will be lost, all the previous hours will still count towards completion of the book.

violations.context: > “__Mackenzie: "I've had a lot of trouble with wildlife lately. Is it always this dangerous around here?"
> “__Mackenzie: "I've had a lot of trouble with wildlife lately. Is it always this dangerous around here?"
Methuselah: "I've seen many strange things, of course. But the birds and beasts? Their rhythms are their own."__”

> — Mackenzie: "Meaning?" Methuselah: "The patterns of nature have been interrupted. Broken. Even those who once knew how to read them are now confused." [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) and [Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md) discussing the local Island wildlife

In _The Long Dark_, interaction with wildlife is a central part of survival. A wide variety of plants and animals exist on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), including terrestrial, aquatic, and avian animals, as well as conifers, beech, and fungal species of plants and fungi. Many of the animals' behaviors are unusual or unnatural--possibly due to the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) and subsequent [Aurora](./Aurora.md).
Prey include [Deer](./Deer.md), [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md), [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md), and [Moose](./Moose.md):
- Rabbits are exclusive to Rabbit Groves at fixed locations, and can be [Trapped](./Trapping.md) with [Snares](./Snare.md).
- Ptarmigan live in relatively higher elevations of Regions, roam in flocks of 4, and stick to Ptarmigan Nests at fixed locations.
- Deer roam between multiple locations in each region, and are a major source of food and hides for crafting items.
- Moose are rare, and usually, but not always, found only at locations with moose markings (scratches on tree trunks).
Deer, Ptarmigan, and Rabbits are easily frightened by the player or a predator. Moose however are highly aggressive and territorial, issuing warnings before attacking intruders.
Predators include [Wolves](./Wolf.md), [Poisoned Wolves](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md), [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), [Cougars](./Cougar.md), and [Bears](./Bear.md):

- Bears follow fixed routes to and from their den and typically do not hunt prey wildlife. Multiple dens may be present in a region, however not all may be populated by Bear in a given survival world.
- Cougars are very fast and agile predators, but will only appear if the player enables them. They stick to dedicated "Cougar Territory" areas and attack the player if they wander too close to them.
- Wolves can be found in nearly every region and regularly stalk and kill other prey wildlife. They are considered the player's main active threat next to the weather on the Island.
- Timberwolves hunt in packs but only roam 3 regions, and require a survivor to be very cautious and armed to avoid being attacked.
- Poisoned Wolves inhabit only the [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md), suffer from malnourishment, and can inflict [Chemical Poisoning](./Chemical%20Poisoning.md) on the player.
All predators will stalk or attack a nearby player, potentially resulting in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md). Predators will not attack the player on the Pilgrim difficulty unless provoked.

All animals can be [Hunted](./Hunting.md) to obtain meat (except for Poisoned Wolves), hides, and Guts, which can be cured for use in crafting. Animals will eventually respawn after being killed. However, the respawn rate can be delayed temporarily if the player aggressively hunts down animals in a certain area. [Trapping](./Trapping.md), on the other hand, does not seem to diminish the number of live rabbits in an area.

During an Aurora at night all prey animals will disappear and all predators will be replaced with their aurora counterpart (e.g. wolves are replaced by aurora wolves). Aurora predators are visually distinct (pale green glow on their fur, glowing eyes), act more chaotically (e.g. wolves bark often and run around randomly), are more aggressive (wider detection radius), deadlier (do more damage in [Struggles](./Struggle.md)), take more damage to kill, and are immune to being frightened by [Fire](./Fire.md). Powered streetlamps, vehicle headlights, and the [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) or [Miner's Flashlight](./Miner%27s%20Flashlight.md) may be used to scare aurora predators, as well as lit [Flares](./Flare.md), [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), and firing the [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md).

[Crows](./Crow.md) will circle over [Frozen Corpses](./Frozen%20Corpse.md) and are used to draw attention to certain locations, while dropping [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) around corpses. When the player is near a Bear, crows can be heard aggressively calling with a distinctive "bear call." Crows cannot be harmed.

Fish inhabit the waters of numerous regions and may encountered by [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) (either inside of fishing huts or by Free-Form ice holes). Species include [Coho Salmon](./Coho%20Salmon%20%28Raw%29.md), [Rainbow Trout](./Rainbow%20Trout%20%28Raw%29.md), [Rockfish](./Rockfish%20%28Raw%29.md), and [Red Irish Lord](./Red%20Irish%20Lord%20%28Raw%29.md) in coastal saltwater, while inland freshwater hosts [Smallmouth Bass](./Smallmouth%20Bass%20%28Raw%29.md), [Lake Whitefish](./Lake%20Whitefish%20%28Raw%29.md), [Goldeye](./Goldeye%20%28Raw%29.md), and [Burbot](./Burbot%20%28Raw%29.md).

A few animals unique to Wintermute can be found in various Episodes. These include the [Big Bass](./Big%20Bass%20%28Raw%29.md), an incredibly large fish, the [Ghost Stag](./Ghost%20Stag.md), an albino Deer, and the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md), an unusually tough and aggressive Bear. The Old Bear is the only unique animal found within Survival Mode, specifically in the "The Hunted" series of [Challenges](./Challenge.md).
Other species of animals can be inferred to be in the game world, but are not seen in gameplay:
- loons, great horned owls, and woodpeckers can be heard calling during certain times of day, but do not appear in game as physical models (only as sound effects).
- A fox and owl can be seen when picking the Pilgrim/Voyager difficulties in Survival Mode, but neither can be found in game.
- Killer Whales can be seen in the ending of [Episode 3](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) and [Episode 4](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) but only in the ending cutscenes.
- Certain [Food And Drink](./Food%20And%20Drink.md) is made using products from animals not found in game.
- Mules are mentioned in the [Load Screen](./Load%20Screen.md) description of [Mule Bridge](./Mule%20Bridge.md).
_Concept art of [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) finding a dead killer whale_

While not considered wildlife (being treated more as a kind of sapient, eldritch creature that simply hunts the player), the Darkwalker is an "animal" with pathfinding A.I. that appears during the challenge [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md). It does not have a physical model, only producing footsteps in the snow and roaring as it grows closer, following the player with the sole purpose of killing them. It cannot be killed or harmed by normal means, only avoided or banished by completing the challenge.

With the exception of fish and Crows, when the player first starts up a world, animals will spawn in at the same time the player does. These animals will wander around the region for however long the player stays outside. Some Survival Modes and Challenges offer a "grace period" before predators can spawn at the very start of a sandbox. On Interloper mode, all fish and prey animals will become rarer over time (to a limit).

When the player enters an indoor location, or leaves a [Region](./Region.md), the game saves the position of all the animals. If an animal is bleeding, the game will track it. This game state is valid for about one in-game hour, during which time the animals will move around as if the player were present. If the player does not re-enter the region within this time, all the animals will despawn. When the player enters the region once more, all animals will be spawned in as if the player entered the region for the first time. If an animal was bleeding and the player re-enters the region before the bleed-out timer has expired, the animal will not die and will respawn, unharmed. If the player stays inside longer than the animal's bleed-out timer, the animal will spawn into the region, dead, but any arrows in its body will be lost.

When an animal is killed, it will be removed from the respawn list for a few days after killing, depending the frequency of deaths and game difficulty. More deaths = longer respawn time. The respawn timer starts immediately on killing the animal. Leaving parts unharvested on the carcass (ex. leaving the guts) does not delay this timer.
All animals will remain outdoors during a blizzard, but despawn when a player goes indoors.

While containing no AI, interactions with plants and fungi are an equally important aspect of surviving on Great Bear Island. Many Afflictions created by predator animals can only be cured by harvesting and cooking certain species of plants and fungi, while others can be prepared and eaten in meals. Some plants can be harvested and cured to craft weapons and tools for survival, and many species of trees also drop branches that can be used as fuel for fires.
- [Burdock](./Burdock.md) can be dug out of the ground for [Burdock Root](./Burdock%20Root.md), and these roots can be [prepared](./Prepared%20Burdock.md).

- Birch trees occasionally shed [Birch Bark](./Birch%20Bark.md) that can be used as tinder or prepared and brewed into a tea. [Green Birch Saplings](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) can be harvested and cured to create [Arrow Shafts](./Arrow%20Shaft.md) for Arrows.
- [Green Maple Saplings](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md) can be harvested to create [Travois](./Travois.md) and [Survival Bows](./Survival%20Bow.md).

- Hardwood beech trees and softwood conifers often drop [Sticks](./Stick.md), [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md), and [Fir Firewood](./Fir%20Firewood.md) for fuel. Certain fallen trees are also used as natural footbridges, or can be used as makeshift shelters if a player finds one that is hallowed out.

- The ground around [Oak Trees](./Oak%20Tree.md) can be searched for [Acorns](./Acorns.md) that can be prepared, cooked, and eaten as is or crushed into [Acorn Grounds](./Acorn%20Grounds.md) to create various recipes or even [Cups of Acorn Coffee](./Cup%20of%20Acorn%20Coffee.md).
- Rose Bushes provide [Rose Hips](./Rose%20Hip.md) that can be prepared to create a natural painkiller tea, and are often used to mark [Rock Climbs](./Rock%20Climb.md).

- [Cat Tails](./Cat%20Tail.md) are found all across the Island around many fresh water lakes, streams, and ponds. [Cat Tail Heads](./Cat%20Tail%20Head.md) can be used as tinder to start fires and their [Stalks](./Cat%20Tail%20Stalk.md) can serve as an easy to find, though not very filling, food source.

- [Scrub Brush](./Scrub%20Brush.md) can be found in various regions and can be harvested to obtain large amounts of Sticks for fires, and can sometimes be found in patches that block a player's progress.

- [Reishi Mushroom](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) are found around rotting tree stumps, and can be prepared to create [Reishi Tea](./Reishi%20Tea.md) or be used in Recipes.
- [Old Man's Beard Lichen](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md) can be found hanging from many trees, and can be used as a natural antiseptic.

Other examples of Flora include Bioluminescent Moss in [Ice Caves](./Ice%20Cave.md) and various grasses occasionally found on the Island. Certain packaged foods show images of plants not found in game.
- Animals never appear indoors across the Island except for 5 special animals, many of whom are given unofficial names by The Long Dark community:

- Fluffy - A Wolf that originally appeared inside [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) but was moved to the [Workshop](./Workshop.md) (This is the only animal officially acknowledged by [Hinterland Studio Inc.](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md))
- "Scruffy" - A Wolf that appears inside the [Cave](./Cave%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md) in [Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md).
- "Sketchy" - A Wolf that appears inside the [Ice Caves](./Ice%20Cave.md) of [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md).
- "Mazey" - A Wolf that appears inside the [Cave (Transition Zone)](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md) close to a frozen waterfall near [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md).
- "Larry" - A Rabbit that appears inside the [Cave (Transition Zone)](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md) between [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) and [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md).

- In older versions, animals' pathfinding AI could not navigate obstacles such as fallen tree bridges, staircases, doorways of fishing huts. This has been (mostly) fixed, but animals still have trouble navigating stairs, mazes, and fallen tree bridges on occasion.
- Animals can't enter locations only accessible by crouching. Animals also cannot enter buildings with outside interiors, even when the doorways are open.
- Animals will never jump down embankments, even from heights that would not damage the player.

- During [Escape the Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md), the [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) will immediately kill all prey and predator type animals when it descends. Crows and plants will not be affected.
