> “**What do I have to worry about? I have a legendary 150 year old demon bear hungry for my blood. Bullets don't stop him, but I'm armed with basically a medieval weapon which I'm sure will do the trick. I'm stuck in this winter wasteland where lights in the sky make the power flicker and electronics explode, and the only people I seem to meet are all slightly crazy. And this is all after I crashed my plane deep in the wilderness and somehow lost my ex-wife along the way, and I'd really kind of like to find her back.**”
Will Mackenzie works as a pilot for [Jackrabbit Remote Transport](./Jackrabbit%20Hangar.md) prior to the First Flare event. He is the ex-husband of [Dr. Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md).
When Astrid approaches him as her last hope of reaching a patient in an isolated region of northern Canada, he hesitantly accepts and agrees to fly Astrid to Great Bear Island.

After a tense conversation between Will and Astrid about a shared, traumatizing loss, the plane goes crashing down into the northern Canadian wilderness of Great Bear Island after a mysterious geomagnetic storm knocks out all power to his instrument panel.

Stranded far from the closest human civilization while being lost, wounded and alone, Mackenzie must quickly master basic wilderness survival skills if he's to last long enough to find Astrid and understand how his world has just changed forever.
Will Mackenzie was a bush pilot prior to the "First Flare" event, a geomagnetic disaster that brought modern civilization to its knees.
Players experience [Story mode](./Wintermute.md) through both [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md)'s and Will's point of view.

Will has short, brown hair and blue eyes. He also sports a relatively unkept beard and a faded red toque. He wears a light green sweater underneath an orange and blue parka, he has greyish black pants and brown leather boots.

Through the course of [Episode 1](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md), we learn that Mackenzie was married to [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md). The two separated some time ago, but both still wear their wedding rings. It is implied that they had a child together who passed away. His drinking is a source of disagreement; Astrid implies that it is excessive while Mackenzie himself states that it is under control.

After waking up and recovering from the plane crash a day after the First Flare occurred, Mackenzie makes his way out of the ravine he was stuck in, looking for Astrid along the way. He finds his way to a road leading him to the Town of Milton.

He meets [Grey Mother](./Grey%20Mother.md), an elderly, seemingly blind woman, in her home after she fires a warning shot at him. She explains to him how all the residents have fled after the storm, fearing they might become trapped in the town after the First Flare and a serious storm hit the town.

After she tasks Mackenzie with fetching her firewood and food, she explains to him how the power went out and people started to get cold, hungry, and scared, and, how, eventually, the few remaining fled. She mentions how a stranger (suggested to be Astrid) passed through the town with "angry voices" trailing her. Grey Mother tells Mackenzie to go investigate the tunnel at the end of the road.

Mackenzie arrives at the tunnel to find it collapsed. A crashed prison transport bus shows signs that Astrid may have passed through. In the bus the word "Perseverance" is written on the floor is what is presumed to be blood.

Mackenzie goes back to Grey Mother, and she gives him one final task, to visit the old farmhouse and retrieve a key to her lockbox in the bank. After Mackenzie retrieves her safety deposit box he finds out it was all for a piece of jewelry special to Grey Mother.
She tells him to bring the pearls to "Lily" at the graveyard. At first, Mackenzie is confused, but eventually realizes that Lily was Grey Mother's daughter.

Upon returning, she tells him the story of how her daughter died. Grey Mother gives Mackenzie the key to her daughter's trunk, where he finds climbing equipment. She tells him how to leave the area and to leave her behind, as she cannot escape the town, even if she wanted to.

Mackenzie bids farewell to Grey Mother and leaves Milton through the back mountains. His rope snaps on the way down, but he recovers and continues on to a cave. Upon entering and going through the cave he finds his way to [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), where he encounters [Jeremiah](./Jeremiah.md), the old Trapper, being attacked by the Old Bear. He grabs the Trapper's rifle and fires at the Old Bear, ending the episode.

After helping Jeremiah to his cabin and healing him up. Mackenzie awaits the Old Trapper's awakening. After Jeremiah wakes up, he tells Mackenzie to go search for better medication at the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md).

Mackenzie makes his way to old Carter Dam where he learns that it's been abandoned for a while. He finds the Control Room to be locked and that it needs power to be turned on. Mackenzie finds the meds and returns to Jeremiah.

Jeremiah awakens once again, after Mackenzie gives him the meds he assures Will that the only way they'll survive is if they kill the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md). Mackenzie then asks him if he saw the Aurora when the First Flare event happened. Jeremiah says he has never seen anything like it before and that the wildlife has been acting strangely. Jeremiah proposes that the two help each other survive.

After that, Jeremiah tells the tale of the [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md). We get to know, that the bear can only be killed by a spear, which has been used by the Spencer family. By the legend, the [Bear Spear](./Bear%20Spear.md) is still in the Spencer family [Hunting Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md). On the way to the other side of [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) Mackenzie encounters the bear twice.

Mackenzie travels to the Lodge and finds the spear, then goes back to the [Maintenance Shed](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) to repair it. After accidentally falling over a dead survivor he finds a note from a group called the [Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md).

Mackenzie then travels back to Jeremiah. Jeremiah declines Mackenzie offer to leave and suggest [Jeremiah's Survival School](./Survival%20School.md) as a means to help Mackenzie learn to survive. This is currently a side quest in Episode 2.

When we get back to Jeremiah, he tells Will, that he could turn on the radio, but couldn't get any useful informations, the old device is barely caught a bit of music and talking. We have to get some radio parts, from the signal towers in [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md). The 3 towers are marked on the map. 2 of the 3 towers are guarded by the Old Bear.

On the way back to Jeremiah Mackenzie gets attacked by the bear at the tunnel between [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) and [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md). (This is a scripted part, can not be avoided) The Bear attacks Will, knocking him unconscious, and then drags him to his den, which can be found at the top region of Forlorn Muskeg (yes, the map is still available). This interrupts the quest [Signal to Noise](./Signal%20to%20Noise.md) and starts the quest [What One Man Can Do](./What%20One%20Man%20Can%20Do.md). Will has to navigate trough the labyrinth-like den, to find his spear, and kill the bear finally.

Then Mackenzie gets back to Jeremiah, and gets immediately unconscious again. When wakes up, an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) is in progress, and the radio seems to work. Will sits down to the radio, and starts finding a frequency to communicate. During his tries, the radio breaks, and cannot be used again. Jeremiah of course, gets mad, but then reveals the sad truth: the radio is unusable, Mackenzie has to deliver the message. Relay a message. Jeremiah tells Mackenzie about a person, who lives near Perseverance Mills and an important message that he needs to receive. That message is Wintermute. Soon after they say their goodbyes and Mackenzie is on his way to the Dam.

When Mackenzie reaches the Dam when the Aurora in the sky he encounters [Methuselah](./Methuselah.md) who invites him to sit by the fire and talk a bit. He warns Mackenzie about the changes the world is going through and how humanity is paying the price. Mackenzie is confused but soon realizes the answer to the question "How Far Will You Go to Survive?"

He leaves Methuselah behind and enters the Dam. He makes his way through the Dam into the back room where he is hit on the head and knocked out. He awakens to find [Mathis](./Mathis.md) standing there, he begins to interrogate and punch Mackenzie, questioning him about Astrid's locked case. Mackenzie responds with some snarky comments just before Mathis reveals he may have encountered Astrid. After responding with desperation, Mathis picks up a hatchet and knocks him out. Ending Episode 2.

At the start of [Episode 4: Fury, then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md), Will awakens on a stretcher being carried by two convicts, [Heller](./Heller.md) and [Vachon](./Vachon.md). Led by [Mathis](./Mathis.md), the gang makes their way to [Blackrock Prison](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) before being ambushed by [timber wolves.](./Timberwolf.md) During the scuffle, Will falls down a cliff, and manages to escape the convicts temporarily, before being caught by Mathis to end the [prologue](./Prologue.md).

The [first chapter](./Blackrock%20Blues.md) finds Will locked up inside the prison in a cell. When he wakes up, the man in the cell next to Will reveals himself to be [Franklin](./Franklin.md), the warden of the prison. He tells Will about the history of the prison and its notoriety, before telling Will that the reason [Mathis](./Mathis.md) has come here is to free his son Donner, a psychotic criminal who wants nothing more than to kill everyone on [Great Bear Island.](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) Mathis then returns with Heller and Vachon, and beats Franklin within an inch of his life. As Franklin lays on the verge of death, Will strikes a deal with Heller and Vachon to go retrieve the prison infirmary's emergency medkit, which contains strong enough medicine to save the warden. Will then leaves the main prison building, and upon arriving at the infirmary talks with a [mysterious stranger](./Jace.md) over the landline phone. He then retrieves the emergency kit from a dead guard near [Cutty's Cave](./Cutty%27s%20Cave.md), returning to the prison to save the warden.

The [second chapter](./The%20Power%20Plant.md) starts with [Mathis](./Mathis.md) threatening to kill Franklin unless Will does his bidding. He then sends Will through the western part of [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md) in order to reach the power plant, so that power can be returned to the prison to free Donner. Once Will arrives at the plant, the [mysterious stranger](./Jace.md) directs him over the phone to destroy the mechanism that provides power to the solitary confinement wing. Will does so, seemingly thwarting Donner's release.

The [third chapter](./The%20Detonators.md) begins yet again in Will's cell, with [Mathis](./Mathis.md) revealing that he found out about Will's sabotage, and is now aware of the [stranger](./Jace.md) directing Will. His new plan to free his son is to use dynamite taken from the Last Prospect mine. He sends Will to retrieve the [detonators](./Detonators.md) needed to utilize the dynamite, under threat of the warden's death. As Will makes his way through the mine and retrieves the detonators, the mysterious stranger calls again, now revealed to be [Jace](./Jace.md), a grad student who was caught out on the roads by the [First Flare](./First%20Flare.md) and is now holed up in one of the prison watchtowers. She tells Will that she is now going to pursue the "Nuclear" option, before Will returns with the detonators to the prison.

The [final chapter](./Donner.md) of the episode begins with [Franklin's](./Franklin.md) corpse being wheeled past Will's cell, as [Mathis](./Mathis.md) reveals that Franklin told him everything that Will had done and how [Jace](./Jace.md) had guided him the entire way. Before Mathis can execute Will, however, the detonators set the dynamite off prematurely, engulfing much of the prison in flames. Will escapes his cell, and Jace blocks Mathis from getting to Will via manipulating the prison doors, as an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) has provided temporary electricity to the prison again. Will then runs through the prison, retrieves the [hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) from the warden's office, and escapes into [the steam tunnels](./The%20Power%20Plant.md) from earlier. He then meets with Jace at the power plant, before they are cornered by Mathis and his gang. After a struggle with Mathis, Will and Jace dive into the river running through the plant, and wash ashore downstream. Will offers to start a fire to warm the half-frozen Jace before the episode ends.

- Will Mackenzie is voiced by [Mark Meer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Meer). Meer's most notable voice work include [Commander Shepard](https://masseffect.fandom.com/wiki/Commander_Shepard) (male) in the _[Mass Effect](https://masseffect.fandom.com/wiki/Category:Games)_ series.

**Description:** An unremarkable valley located on the other side of the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md)
**Connecting Regions:** [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md), [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md)

**Winding River** (also known in-lore as the **Carter River**) is a Transition Zone [Region](./Region.md) behind [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md) that connects [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) to a [Cave](./Cave%20%28Transition%20Zone%29.md) and then subsequently to [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md). It was the 2nd Transition Zone to be released in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_.

Resident wildlife consists of [Rabbits](./Rabbit.md) and occasionally a [Wolf](./Wolf.md) patrol is often found near the base of the Dam itself. [Reishi Mushrooms](./Reishi%20Mushroom.md) and other plants can be harvested in the area near the banks of the river. [Ice Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md) is possible on the ice below the Dam using Free Form Ice Holes.

The area has few notable locations, aside from a [Warm Cave](./Warm%20Cave.md) that often has a [Research Book](./Research%20Book.md). A nearby hill can often contain [Green Birch Sapling](./Green%20Birch%20Sapling.md) and [Green Maple Sapling](./Green%20Maple%20Sapling.md).

The Carter Hydro Dam can not be re-entered by walking back into the push door if exited from inside the Dam, nor can it be propped open as the door automatically closes and locks behind you. A broken window across from the dam exit can be used to regain entry into the Dam, doing so requires walking across the other side of the Dam by via a ledge.

**Description:** Survive an ever increasing freezing world will hunting for the new Maple Syrup and Ketchup Chip items

> “**Surviving in the cold Canadian winter on Great Bear Island has never been easy. This Summer, however, it's going to be even harder with our first summer seasonal event Winter's Embrace. The temperature is dropping even lower and surviving will be even more of a struggle. But survive you must if you want to earn two all-new limited-time Badges in the game. These exclusive rewards are only available during Winter's Embrace which runs from June 29th through to July 31st. There will also be all-new features and in-game items added to the game to give you a new experience, and a touch of Canadiana as you venture out into the snowy wilds.**”
Winter's Embrace was an event [Challenge](./Challenge.md) that previously ran throughout the month of July 2020.

This update includes the addition of [Maple Syrup](./Maple%20Syrup.md) and [Ketchup Chips](./Ketchup%20Chips.md) as food items. Most of the game settings appear to be around Voyageur-level difficulty, though [storms and blizzards](./Weather.md) are much more frequent than normal and all temperatures are -10 C lower than normal, even inside houses and shelters.

The two limited-time [Badges](./Badges.md) were earned by finding and consuming 25 bottles of Syrup and 25 bags of Ketchup Chips (can be done across any number of saves), and for surviving 25 in-game days under the Winter's Embrace conditions.

![Official release poster for Season 1: Wintermute](../assets/The_long_dark_poster2.jpg)_Official release poster for Season 1: Wintermute_ **_Wintermute_** is the story mode edition of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ and is [downloadable content](./The%20Long%20Dark.md#Downloadable_Addon_Content)_._ Originally launching on August 1, 2017 with 2 episodes, the story contains 5 episodes that concluded on March 31, 2026. The game mode was originally a part of the core game, but has since become Downloadable Content (but is free to players that owned _The Long Dark_ before 2022).

Unlike [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), Wintermute is primarily targeted towards players who want to experience a more campaign-like experience; focusing on the worldbuilding and lore of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) and _The Long Dark's_ universe outside of the Island.

Wintermute centers around the relationship between [Dr. Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) and a bush pilot named [Will Mackenzie](./Will%20Mackenzie.md), whom she hires to fly herself and her [mysterious hardcase](./Astrid%27s%20Hardcase.md) to a remote location in the Canadian wilderness of [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). After a [mysterious geomagnetic disaster](./First%20Flare.md) causes their plane to crash land, Astrid and Will become separated. Now the two must survive this cold and unforgiving landscape they find themselves stranded in while doing whatever it takes to reunite safely. Experience the story from their perspectives, and survive while interacting with the other surviving denizens of Great Bear Island.

_The Long Dark's_ episodic structure borrows from TV to deliver a well-paced narrative experience that is advanced by player action in the world. Similar to open-world games like _Red Dead Redemption_ and _Fallout 3_, _The Long Dark_ offers both a large open-world simulation space that encourages free-form gameplay and a story-driven mission structure that draws players deeper into the fiction of the game world. This structure means that, whether you have 20 minutes or 2 hours to play, you can jump in and make meaningful progress towards an in-game goal. Each episode takes an average of 3-5 hours to complete.

Gameplay tends to be more structured than [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), with scripted narrative events being more present, new dialogue and music, and the inability to explore certain areas of the local region until certain chapters are completed. The game will also deny entry certain transition zones to other regions, making it impossible to fully explore Great Bear Island. (Ex. Can't leave [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) to go to [The Ravine](./The%20Ravine.md) in Episode 2). Items also cannot be taken between Episodes (save for Episode 1 and 2) due to story reasons.
[Do Not Go Gentle](./Episode%201%20-%20Do%20Not%20Go%20Gentle.md) launched August 1, 2017.

Will Mackenzie's plane has crashed due to a mysterious geomagnetic event. He and his fellow passenger [Astrid Greenwood](./Astrid%20Greenwood.md) are now separated after Will becomes stranded at the bottom of a nearby ravine over the course of one night. Finding nothing but Astrid's hardcase the next morning, Will must now do his best to survive in the wilderness while trying to find any trace of the doctor, assuming that she is even still alive. His journey takes him to the small forgotten Town of [Milton](./Milton.md), where he starts to understand the extent of the Quiet Apocalypse that sent his plane crashing down into this new world.

Mackenzie continues his search for Astrid after traveling to the [Mystery Lake](./Mystery%20Lake%20%28region%29.md) region, but only now does he fully realize the depth of the situation he has found himself in after saving a [local trapper](./Jeremiah.md) from being nearly mauled to death by a [bear](./Old%20Bear.md). During his journey that takes him across multiple nearby regions, he must make difficult, yet critical life altering decisions-- which will ultimately determine just how far he is willing to go to survive in this harsh new world. After proving that he is tough enough to survive in this harsh new reality, Mackenzie now finds himself with two objectives: reunite with Astrid with the hardcase in tow, and survive long enough to deliver the message "Wintermute" to someone on the other side of the Island.
[Crossroads Elegy](./Episode%203%20-%20Crossroads%20Elegy.md) launched on October 22, 2019.

After surviving the plane crash and escaping the Town of Milton, Astrid finds herself facing the rather ironic harsh blizzards of [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md). Searching for Mackenzie, her skills as a doctor come to bear as she encounters other survivors that have also found their plane grounded by the dancing lights in the sky. As the central mystery of the hardcase draws the plot closer to [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md), how far is Astrid willing to go to find Mackenzie?
[Fury, Then Silence](./Episode%204%20-%20Fury%2C%20Then%20Silence.md) launched on October 6th, 2021.

Mackenzie’s story continues after his ill-fated meeting with the convict [Mathis](./Mathis.md) inside the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Carter%20Hydro%20Dam.md). His abduction lands him in the far reaches of [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md), as he tangles to appease the very [Convicts](./Convicts.md) of the [local prison complex](./Blackrock%20Prison.md) that kidnapped him while also following the instructions of a [mysterious new benefactor](./Jace.md) aiming to free them both.
[The Light At The End Of All Things](./Episode%205%20-%20The%20Light%20At%20The%20End%20Of%20All%20Things.md) launched on March 31, 2026.

The episode starts out with Astrid arriving in [Perseverance Mills](./Perseverance%20Mills.md) and continues into 4 parts where you play as Will and Astrid. Both trying to save the people of Perseverance Mills. With the apperance of both old and new faces. Can they manage to find eachother trough alot of struggle and hardship?
- For players with some experience, and those looking for a balance between exploration and survival.

**Wintermute:** Yes A **Wolf Carcass** is a harvestable "object" found after [Hunting](./Hunting.md) a [Wolf](./Wolf.md). They can occasionally be found as ravaged carcasses preplaced across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md). [Crows](./Crow.md) will fly around a Wolf Carcass and always drop 3 [Crow Feathers](./Crow%20Feather.md) around the carcass at a time.

Wolf hides can be cured to craft [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md). On Stalker and Interloper modes, wolf meat carries the risk of [Intestinal Parasites](./Intestinal%20Parasites.md).

Consuming raw meat carries a high chance of contracting [Food Poisoning](./Food%20Poisoning.md). Wolf Meat **cannot** be harvested from [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) carcasses.

A **Wolf Quarter** is a section harvested from a [Wolf](./Wolf.md) or [Timberwolf](./Timberwolf.md). A [Poisoned Wolf](./Poisoned%20Wolf.md) will not allow a Wolf Quarter to be harvested, as they have no meat on their bodies.

You can only obtain wolf quarters by _quartering_ a wolf carcass. To quarter an animal, you have to go into the harvest menu, then select the quartering action. For a wolf, this will always take 1 hour. You can only quarter a wolf if its less than 50% frozen.

After quartering, the carcass will despawn, leaving behind 2-3 quarters, as well as its [Fresh Gut](./Fresh%20Gut.md) and [Fresh Wolf Pelt](./Fresh%20Wolf%20Pelt.md). It will also leave behind the wolves legs and blood, but these cannot be picked up, and it will soon despawn. As quartering only takes 1 hour for wolves, and gives you all necessary parts, it makes transport and harvesting easier, especially if a blizzard is coming or if it will be night soon.

Unlike directly harvesting a fresh carcass' meat, you will still need to harvest a quarter for its meat. 50% of the quarters total weight will be turned into usable [Wolf Meat (Raw)](./Wolf%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md). Any remaining raw meat left inside the bag will be lost if the Quarter's Condition reaches 0%, with bags spoiling within 1 day of harvesting.

**Wolves** are iconic [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) in _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)._ In [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) and [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) they are a primary threat to survival on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) and can be found in all major [regions](./Region.md).
Wolves are a common predatory animal found on Great Bear Island; they may appear alone or in packs of up to four:
- They hunt [Rabbit](./Rabbit.md), [Deer](./Deer.md), and [Ptarmigan](./Ptarmigan.md) and stalk the survivor.
- Despite not showing any fear of [Timberwolves](./Timberwolf.md), Wolves do not interact with Timberwolf packs.

When a wolf detects the survivor they will stalk and attack them, potentially resulting in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md): resulting in [Condition](./Condition.md) loss, [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) and [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md), or damage to [Clothing](./Clothing.md). A wolf attack is typically not fatal at high condition, even if lost.

Wolves can be avoided by keeping distance, sneaking (crouching) and not carrying smelly items (raw meat, cooked meat, raw guts). These smelly items can be dropped ("3") as bait to distract a wolf. Unalerted Wolves will also investigate thrown [stones](./Stone.md) which land nearby.
At night, Wolves can easily be spotted if they are facing your direction by the green shimmer in their eyes (Red in [4 Days of Night Event](./4%20Days%20of%20Night%20Event.md)).

A [Wolf Carcass](./Wolf%20Carcass.md) may be harvested for 3.0-6.0 kg of [raw meat](./Wolf%20Meat%20%28Raw%29.md), 1 [Fresh Wolf Pelt](./Fresh%20Wolf%20Pelt.md) and 2 guts. Wolf hides can be cured to craft [Wolfskin Coat](./Wolfskin%20Coat.md), [Wolfskin Pants](./Wolfskin%20Pants.md), or a [Wolfskin Hat](./Wolfskin%20Hat.md).

Wolves feature the most complex and varied behavior of all [Wildlife](./Wildlife.md) in The Long Dark.

![A wolf chasing a rabbit](../assets/Wolf_pursuit.jpg)_A wolf chasing a rabbit_ Wolves hunt Rabbit, Deer, and Ptarmigan they detect, and stalk the survivor. Wolves will 'bark' when they see a target and slowly stalk it to get closer. When close enough they will start chasing it, sprinting at close distances and killing prey animals on contact. After a kill, wolves will feed on the animal's carcass until no harvestable yield remains ("Ravaged"). Wolves making contact with the survivor will start a [Struggle](./Struggle.md).

Breaking a wolf's line of sight, keeping scent low and running may help lose a stalking wolf. Wolves will not approach lit [campfires](./Campfire.md) or flares, and cannot travel indoors or inside vehicles. If multiple wolves detect the player, one of them will take the lead to attack while the others stand back and growl at the player while keeping up with the approaching alpha Wolf.

Climbing felled trees, some boulders or rock ledges outside of a Wolf's pathfinding will cause it to stand in a defensive stance and growl in place at the player, in which wolves lose interest over time. If a weapon of any kind is brandished while a Wolf is hold its ground, they will always run away in fear.

A Wolf that has been shot by the player will retreat to a great distance away from the player until it cannot detect them anymore, and will begin to bleed out. Once their health is low enough then they will noticeably slow down, pulling their front left leg off the ground and limping as they move. They will will refuse to attack animals or the player in this state and eventually fall over dead once they fully bleed out.

Idle wolves will periodically and howl to one another, which may result in other nearby wolves replying. This can be useful to detect the presence of unseen wolves in areas with low visibility, or count the amount of nearby wolves.

> “**Wolves - - they hate fire, like most wildlife. Campfire'll keep them away from you at night, most of the time. Improvise a torch if you have to. Flare will work too, you know one of those emergency ones for road accidents. Sometimes, if you get lucky, a stone to the head will scare them off.**”

Wolves are hostile wildlife found in all major regions of Great Bear Island wandering or hunting prey when not stalking the survivor. Prolonged stalking may result in a wolf giving up or charging the survivor or prey.

![An Aurora Wolf on the prowl](../assets/Aurora_Wolf.jpg)_An Aurora Wolf on the prowl_ When an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) begins all wolves temporarily flee and before becoming aurora wolves: which glow green and are more aggressive, deal more damage and have more health. Aurora wolves often behave erratically: barking and running in circles almost constantly.
- Aurora Wolves do not fear [Flares](./Flare.md), [Marine Flares](./Marine%20Flare.md), or lit [Torches](./Torch.md).
- They fear active street lights, and will stand and growl at the player if they pass near the boundary of one. After enough time, they will run away in fear if they cannot reach the player.
- They fear [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) high beams and will temporarily stop a charge as long as they are on.
- They will stay away from lit [Campfires](./Campfire.md), but will still stay close by and stalk to the player.
- Gunshots are still effective at frightening aurora wolves, provided they are not charging.

A wolf that has recently killed an animal will begin to eat its carcass, reducing yields until nothing remains. While the wolf feeds, its senses are greatly reduced (-75%). Scaring a wolf away from its kill will cause it to flee for a time, potentially allowing the survivor to harvest the carcass. Feeding wolves which are defending their kill may attack a survivor even on [Pilgrim](./Survival%20Mode.md) mode.

Most products harvested from animals produce [Scent](./Scent.md) when carried by the survivor; while carried Scented items increases the radius at which wolves (and other predators) can smell the survivor, affected by wind (positively or negatively). While carried these items may be dropped ("3") as a Decoy to distract nearby predators, if a wolf detects a nearby Decoy (and the survivor is adequately far enough from it) they will pursue and eat the Decoy (destroying it), remaining distracted for a few seconds.

Additionally if a wolf detects a prey animal while stalking the survivor it may pursue the animal instead. This can allow the survivor to distract wolves pursuing them by traveling past [herds of deer](./Deer.md), [rabbit groves](./Rabbit%20Grove.md), or [ptarmigan nests](./Ptarmigan.md).

Wolves are afraid of [fire](./Fire.md) and generally avoid it if the survivor is nearby (~5m): making lit campfires, torches and flares powerful wolf deterrents. If the survivor is within range of a light source wolves respect (e.g. lit torch dropped at their feet) and aiming any weapon (e.g. [Stone](./Stone.md)) a stalking wolf will flee. Fires should be between the survivor and the wolf for maximum safety. If a wolf is charging the survivor, throwing a lit torch or flares may interrupt it.
- Lit Campfires will deter wolves**, but lit fire barrels, stoves, etc will not.** Being heavily Scented will not deter wolves from attacking despite a fire being present.
- Lit [Torch](./Torch.md) and especially [Flares](./Flare.md) are effective at deterring wolves (unless the player is Weak or heavily Scented (see below)).

- Accelerating Time (sleep, reading, crafting, harvesting etc.) while relying on a lit campfire to deter wolves may be dangerous: either with the wolf moving around the fire to attack, or the fire extinguishing (consuming its fuel, or blown out by wind).
Wolves flee from the report of a [Hunting Rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md), [Revolver](./Revolver.md) or [Distress Pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) and the impact of nearby bullets and arrows.

Wolves investigate thrown stones landing nearby if the survivor is not detected. This can allow an undetected survivor to temporarily distract wolves from an area. If a stone stone lands very close to a wolf (undetected) or hits them directly (detected) they may flee. After investigating a stone wolves will return to their original position.

Exploding Noisemakers cause all nearby wolves to flee (including aurora wolves) at moderate range (~20m), and can wound or kill wolves at short range (~5m). **Note: at very close range (or if the survivor fails to throw a lit Noisemaker in time) Noisemaker explosions will damage the survivor.**

![Wolf attack](../assets/Wolf_attack.jpg) Wolves within 15 meters who detect the survivor charge them, attempting to make contact and start a [Struggle](./Struggle.md). At the start of a struggle the survivor will have several seconds to select a [tool](./Tools.md) from their inventory to defend themselves. Over the following seconds the survivor and wolf will attack one another: taking [Condition](./Condition.md) and [Clothing](./Clothing.md) damage with chances to incur [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) until either side wins, or dies, or the struggle ends (after 10 seconds).
- Left-Clicking after selecting a weapon results in the survivor attacking the wolf and filling the Struggle Meter.

- Each time the wolf will take damage and there is a chance the struggle ends. Clicking faster yields better results during a struggle; **for players with issues clicking rapidly the "Hold to Struggle" option may be enabled in-game under "Accessibility Settings"**, this setting requires fewer player inputs during struggles but yields inferior results to rapid clicking.

- Failing to end the struggle within 10 seconds results in the wolf "winning", causing the survivor to temporarily faint, but possibly survive the encounter. Afterwards some items from their inventory may be on ground nearby, while the wolf temporarily walks away.

- Wolves require contact (~1m) to begin a struggle, making struggles avoidable by fire, impassible terrain or doodads (e.g. trees). **Failing to light a [campfire](./Campfire.md) while a nearby wolf is nearby may allow it to charge.**
- Entering a vehicle, structure or transition regions will abort a wolf's charge, though the wolf remain nearby.

- Wolves charge as fast as a sprinting player when unencumbered, and charge for up to 10 seconds (real-time), before fleeing if unable to reach the make contact. It is possible but unlikely to outrun a charging wolf, usually requiring a [Emergency Stim](./Emergency%20Stim.md) or [Go! Energy Drink](./Go!%20Energy%20Drink.md) and favorable terrain.
- Wolves are unaffected by movement speed bonuses/maluses (wind speed/direction, slopes, roads, etc).
When a Wolf struggle begins the survivor is prompted to defend themselves with a tool(s) or Revolver from their inventory:

- [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) / [Improvised Hatchet](./Improvised%20Hatchet.md): high damage and moderate Struggle Progress at all Fatigue levels and Survival Modes, with moderate chance to inflict bleed on the wolf, killing it over time. **Note: Improvised Hatchet is slightly inferior to Hatchet.**

- [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md), [Improvised Knife](./Improvised%20Knife.md): high Struggle Progress (if at high [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md)) and high Bleed chance, but low damage. Almost guaranteed to kill the wolf over time (from Bleeding), but unlikely at killing during struggles. Very effective at filling the Struggle Meter with high clicks-per-second if at high [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), ineffective at low Fatigue, low clicks-per-second, or with Accessibility Settings for Struggles enabled. **Note: Improvised Knife is slightly inferior to Hunting Knife.**

- [Cougar Claw Knife](./Cougar%20Claw%20Knife.md): Similar to Hunting/Improvised Knife, but with even higher Struggle Progress. Extremely powerful at ending Struggles quickly by filling the Progress Meter, especially with high clicks-per-second. Requires [Cougar Claw](./Cougar%20Claw.md) to [Forge](./Forge.md).

- [Revolver](./Revolver.md): moderate Struggle Progress and low damage. As [Revolver Firearm skill](./Revolver%20Firearm.md) increases so does Progress rate and chance to "Take The Shot" option mid-Struggle (if loaded) to fire 1 Revolver round and ending the struggle immediately and potentially killing the wolf instantly. Functionally similar to Hunting Knife without Bleed chance.

- [Heavy Hammer](./Heavy%20Hammer.md): moderate progress, low damage, no bleed chance but consistent across all [Survival Modes](./Survival%20Mode.md) (except [Misery](./Misery.md) with [Diminished Form](./Diminished%20Form.md)). with a ~15% chance per hit to end the struggle. Less effective on average than Hatchet (resulting in more condition/clothing damage), but less susceptible to poor RNG (resulting in rare poor-RNG struggles where e.g. survivor dies from high Condition). Unlikely to ending Struggles quickly (e.g. if already at low Condition).
- [Prybar](./Prybar.md): moderate progress, low damage, no bleed chance, with a low (~5% per hit) chance to cause the wolf to flee. Generally inferior to Heavy Hammer except in carry weight.

- Desperation: (aka "Unarmed" or punching) minimal progress and almost no damage and low (~2.5%) chance to end the struggle per hit. Likely to result in a struggle-loss (maximum struggle duration and Condition and clothing damage), likely (but not guaranteed) to result in death on most [Survival Modes](./Sundered%20Pass.md).
1. Note: any the tool/weapon selected for use during a Struggle will take a small amount of condition damage (~1-3%).

2. Note: Not all "Tools" category items may be selected for use during a wolf struggle (e.g. [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md), [Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md), [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md), [Storm Lantern](./Storm%20Lantern.md), [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) cannot be used).

- Carry [Bandage(s)](./Bandage.md): Blood Loss is common and deadly (30% [Condition](./Condition.md) loss per hour until treated). Wolf Struggles frequently (but not always) result in one Blood Loss, rarely yield two (~5% chance based on Struggle duration), and very rarely three (~0.5%).

- Carry [Antiseptic](./Antiseptic.md)/[Old Man's Beard](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Lichen.md): [Infection Risk](./Infection%20Risk.md) is common from wolf struggles if Blood Loss occurs. **Note: Infection Risk does not require immediate treatment** (e.g. crafting Old Man's Beard into Old Man's Beard Bandage) but should be treated before several hours pass.
- [Fatigue](./Fatigue.md), [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md), and the Tool selected for the Struggle affect Struggle progress.

- [Clothing](./Clothing.md) can offer Protection from struggles in its item statistics. Each point of Protection reduces incoming wildlife damage by 1%. **Only the 'outer layer' of worn clothing provides protection (further from the player, on the 'paper doll' UI).**
- Remove fragile clothing before a struggle: wolves can damage or destroy low condition or fragile clothing like [Wool Ear Wraps.](./Wool%20Ear%20Wrap.md)

If the survivor is weak due to low [Condition](./Condition.md) or some [Afflictions](./Afflictions.md) then wolves will act more aggressively towards them: charging from ~50% greater distance (<15m normally to <21m if Weak). **This particularly dangerous since allow wolves to charge in situations where they would normally flee** (e.g. survivor is holding a lit [Torch](./Torch.md) and sprints towards a wolf). These effects are binary (the survivor is either Weak or not) and do not stack, they are:
- <20% [Condition](./Condition.md) (aka the Condition meter is red, 'low Condition' music plays, survivor may start 'wobbling' their movement)
- [Blood Loss](./Blood%20Loss.md) **(Note: Blood Loss also increases the surivor's [Scent](./Scent.md))**

Wolf can be killed at range with any weapon (except [Stone](./Stone.md) and [Fire Hardened Arrow](./Fire%20Hardened%20Arrow.md)), or from melee during a struggle with any struggle-selectable tool (e.g. [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md)). All weapons cause bleeding, which is certain death for the animal over time; however injured wolves may still attack. If not killed during a struggle a wounded wolf flees at a sprint for several seconds, before slowing to a walk (and being able to attack again).

- Note: wolves only bleed on the ground while fleeing. Once slowing back to a walk they will cease bleeding on the ground, but will continue taking damage and eventually die. Blood Drops will again appear if the wolf resumes fleeing (e.g. a new gunshot, thrown lit flare, etc).
Critical hits cause the animal to instantly die after being hit by a shot. The following table contains the critical hit chance based on the location that was shot on the animal.

- A simple strategy wolf killing is to shoot its head with a ranged weapon. This is made easier by first distracting the wolf so it will stand still for a clean shot:
- Baiting: dropped smelly items with attract nearby wolves, who will try to reach the bait.
- Firetrap: while the wolf is trapped by a fire, line up a clean shot. Such as dropping a lit torch while a wolf is following the player.
- Hunt the hunter: Scare deer/rabbits towards a wolf, or lure a following wolf to one. Dispatching the wolf after it kills the prey results in two animal carcasses for only one shot.
- Wolves may also be engaged in struggles, though this is far more dangerous than using ranged weapons. See Struggles (above).

[Region](./Region.md) and [Survival Mode](./Survival%20Mode.md) determine how many wolves may spawn. Wolves spawn at active spawn points in the same region as the survivor within rendering distance and roam the surrounding area. As in-game time progresses these spawn points may change, resulting in wolf(s) moving between points. The number and the availability of wolf spawn points increases based on the "WOLF SPAWN CHANCE" Wildlife Spawns setting.
- Grace Period: wolves and other hostile wildlife cannot spawn during the first 12 hours of Pilgrim mode.
- Aurora: all wolves flee and despawn when an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) begins or ends (even if during a [Struggle](./Struggle.md)), being replaced with more dangerous Aurora Wolves.

- Sight: Wolves can see in a 30m 45° frontal cone from the center of their head, reduced to 15m if the player crouching. Line of sight blockers (trees, hills, structures) may reduce this further, but not by time of day or [weather](./Weather.md) (fog or blizzards).

- Smell: Wolves smell regardless of terrain in a 45m radius from the player or dropped smelly item. The "[Scent](./Scent.md) Indicator" UI element shows an estimate of current player scent, increased by carrying more smelly items (raw or cooked [meat](./Food%20And%20Drink.md), fresh hides, [fresh guts](./Fresh%20Gut.md), rabbit carcasses). The player has a minimum smell radius of 5m which increases up to 75m; strong winds can increase or decrease this radius +/-15m.

- Sound: Wolves can hear nearby [rifle](./Hunting%20Rifle.md)/[revolver](./Revolver.md)/[distress pistol](./Distress%20Pistol.md) reports (75m) and projectile weapon impacts (20m), which cause them to flee (except stones), unless charging.
2. The active [Feat "Big Cat Killer"](./Feats.md) reduces Wolf (and other wildlife) Sight and Smell by 50%.
Wolves exhibit complex behavior based on what they detect, it's type and distance, and wolf's status. Wolf behavior changes based on "Wildlife Behavior" and "Wildlife Struggle" settings.
Wolves will actively pursue or flee from targets they detect or situations, ordered from highest to lowest priority:

1. _Die:_ the wolf immediately dies from direct damage, bleeding, or [Toxic Fog](./Toxic%20Fog.md) (during [Escape The Darkwalker](./Escape%20the%20Darkwalker.md)), becoming a harvestable [wolf carcass](./Wolf%20Carcass.md).
2. _Flee:_ Wolves flee for ~15 real-time seconds at full speed in semi-random directions when:

Most wildlife in The Long Dark cannot enter indoors locations (thought transition screens) or spawn inside indoors structures and caverns, making thes locations 'safe' for the survivor, at least from wildlife; 'unique wolves' break this location by being wolves which can only spawn inside fixed indoors locations, break this convention and often ambushing unsuspecting players. Because of this these wolves have garnered a reputation for being particularly memorable and dangerous The Long Dark survivors who encounter them, often becoming named by _The Long Dark_ community.

Fluffy is a wolf which can spawn inside of the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md) workshop in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). To encounter Fluffy the electronic door must be unlocked and opened: this requires reading (touching or picking up) the key-code Note inside [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md), and then activating the keypad at Last Resort Cannery during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) at night. Due the Cannery requiring an active Aurora to unlock, Fluffy is often encountered in her more dangerous 'aurora wolf' form and typically ambushes unsuspecting players with her unusual indoors location, driven by the importance of the location for [Gunsmithing](./Gunsmithing.md) and [Milling](./Milling%20Machine.md). Additionally the interior of the Last Resort Cannery features many [electrified wires](./Burns.md) during an Aurora, making evading Fluffy even more dangerous.

In early versions of _The Long Dark_ (0.124) Fluffy was found inside of the turbine room of the [Carter Hydro Dam](./Winding%20River.md). Players initially reported her presence as a bug due to this unexpected location; however, she quickly developed a cult following on the [Official Hinterlands Forums](./Hinterland%20Studio%20Inc..md) for her reputation of murdering unsuspecting new players. "Fluffy" was not officially named or mentioned in the changelog when added, but after being named by the community she was officially mentioned in changelog 0.127. She appears to have gained access to the dam's interior through a broken window from the [Winding River](./Winding%20River.md). Fluffy was removed from [Carter Hydro Dam](./Winding%20River.md) in Survival Mode in version 1.00 (August 1, 2017) during the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) release, as her AI could not pathfind the new interior. In [Story Mode](./Wintermute.md): [Episode Two](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) her corpse can be found inside the Carter Hydro Dam. The November 2019 developer diary stated that Fluffy would return, and as of the [Errant Pilgrim](./The%20Long%20Dark%20%E2%80%94%20Changelog.md) update Fluffy resides in the [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md).![Fluffy in the story mode](../assets/Dead_fluffy.jpg)_Fluffy in the story mode_

[Desolation Point](./Desolation%20Point.md) inside the north-eastern [cave](./Cave%20%28Desolation%20Point%20location%29.md) near the waterfall has a unique wolf, along with with multiple deer carcasses and potentially a [frozen corpse](./Frozen%20Corpse.md). This wolf can be particularly effective at ambushing survivors, since the cave is dark and has numerous side tunnels and stalactites.

[Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) inside the southern [Ice Cave](./Ice%20Cave.md) (Note: Prior to the "Tales From The Far Territory" DLC (December 5, 2022) it was randomized (based on Save) which ice cavern this wolf spawned in). This wolf features multiple spawn points within the ice cave and can be difficult to avoid, especially if spawning in Hushed River Valley on Interloper mode.

The [Sundered Pass](./Sundered%20Pass.md) wing of the massive cavern which connects Sundered Pass, [Forsaken Airfield](./Forsaken%20Airfield.md) and [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) in [The Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md). The wolf spawns in the circular chamber dominated with an ice stalactite, but may roam to any location within the wing between the indoors [rope climb](./Rope%20Climbing.md) and [rock climb](./Rock%20Climb.md).

"Demon" Wolves were a Halloween-themed variant in "[4 Days of Night](./4%20Days%20of%20Night%20Event.md)" (4DON) a discontinued game mode from 2016-2019. They were distinct in having glowing red eyes and fleeing from survivors who consumed n [Pumpkin Pies](./Pumpkin%20Pie.md), but otherwise behaved like typical Wolves. When a Demon Wolf died their eyes lose the glow effect, making their appearance identical to regular wolves.

- The Wolf is based off the well known [Gray Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolf) (**_Canis lupus_**), specifically the [Black Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_wolf) a darkly color variant found rarely throughout the world most commonly in Southern Canada.

- Wolves are deadliest and most abundant in [Misery mode](./Misery.md). Stalker features wolves nearly as abundant (though less dangerous), and Interloper features wolves as deadly as Misery but less frequent.
- The Wolf model, animation and AI rig have undergone numerous updates and overhauls since Early Access.

- All wildlife spawns are now more dynamic, and will change over the course of a game. Wolves, Deer, and Rabbits all refresh on different intervals, reflecting their relative mobility and travel/migration patterns.

- A Wolf Attack now results in Blood Loss and Infection Risk (vs. immediate Infection, as before). Infection Risk is reduced by applying Antiseptic. Wounds can become Infected up to 24 hours after they have been inflicted.
- Wolves will now stop to feed on fresh Deer kill. The amount of meat that can be retrieved from a carcass is affected by how long a Wolf feeds on it.

- Complete overhaul of Wildlife Spawning system. Wildlife will now spawn only if there is valid population remaining per a 24-hour period. Fresh carcasses (ex. Wolf kill) will decay (due to predation and the elements). It is now possible for a spawn region to become depopulated.
- Wolves: Fixed some unreported issues related to wolf attacks interrupting gear inspection, eating, drinking, and fire starting.
- Updated all Wolf spawn regions, and added new Wolf and Deer spawn regions to the world.
- Added NoSpawn trigger zones around in-world locations that should be safe from Wolves. You will no longer wake up to a wolf attack in the Hunter’s Blind.

> “**Handcrafted fur and skin outer layer will keep you warm and remind Wolves that they should keep their distance. Not the way the Wolf expected to end up.**”

Wolfskin Coats have high warmth, windproof, protection, waterproof and durability along with a chance to frighten nearby wolves when worn; however they also have relatively high weight and mobility penalty. They are comparable in stats to the rare [Expedition Parka](./Expedition%20Parka.md), but can be crafted making them more accessible (such as on Interloper, where parkas cannot spawn). It is produced from cured wolf pelts.

When worn (in either clothing slot) the Wolfskin Coat has a chance to scare nearby [wolves](./Wolf.md) when they detect the player, (like on Pilgrim). Be careful, because if a wolf that was scared away returns to their area and the player is still there, it is reported they cannot be scared a second time - this information, if true, also proves that the effect stacks in some way when two coats are worn, as the same wolf can be frightened twice with no bear or moose gear in inventory and no such animals spawning in that area when wearing two coats. Further testing is required, and while that shows the ability to roll twice, it does not prove that the chances are doubled for the first roll. Please conduct and report testing here, if able.

The coat is the third-warmest torso clothing (after [Bearskin Coat](./Bearskin%20Coat.md) and Expedition Parka). Its protection is much higher than that of any non-craftable outer torso options, but is less than that of [Moose-Hide Cloak](./Moose-Hide%20Cloak.md) or the Bearskin Coat. A strategy is to wear a wolfskin coat as the outer layer (left), and a lighter, warmth focused jacket on the inner layer (windproof and protection of inner clothing items are disregarded). As with other crafted clothing the wolfskin coat is repairable with renewable resources, making it a useful endgame item.

Since [wolves](./Wolf.md) are less dangerous than [bears](./Bear.md) or [moose](./Moose.md), and are more common, the wolfskin coat can be acquired with arguably less risk, and possibly earlier in the game. Crafting the coat will likely require hunting wolves or killing them in a struggle since there are few naturally spawning [wolf carcasses](./Wolf%20Carcass.md). In fact, the only [regions](./Region.md) in which a naturally spawned wolf carcass may be found are the [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) (up to four), [Mountain Town](./Mountain%20Town.md) (up to one), [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md) (one), [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md) (one), [Ash Canyon](./Ash%20Canyon.md) (up to one), [Pleasant Valley](./Pleasant%20Valley.md) (up to two), and [Zone of Contamination](./Zone%20of%20Contamination.md) (three). 2 cured wolf pelts may spawn in a cargo container in the tail section of the crashed plane on the Timberwolf Mountain summit.
In [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md), its blueprint is unlocked by preserving nature's balance in the [Survival School](./Survival%20School.md) quest.

**Wood Matches** are a [Fire Starting](./Fire%20Starting.md) Tools and a small light source in _The Long Dark_.
Each match weighs a mere 0.008 of a kilogram, but there are always 12 found together in one box. Using a wood match increases the base chance of successfully lighting a fire by five percent.

Light sources are equipped with the '1' key by default. Hold the left mouse button to strike the match for a small light source that lasts for a few seconds. While a lit match is held, your "Feels Like" temperature will rise by a few degrees. Sadly, such a small fire will not deter [Wolves](./Wolf.md).

Lighting a match will cause the survivor to hold it closely in their hand, where it will create light for 13 seconds until the fire travels down the stem and reaches the survivor's fingers, where they drop it in pain. Running with a lit match will cause the flame to grow brighter, causing it to burn out faster.
Pressing H with a lit match will cause the survivor to flick the match into the distance, where it disappears and the light is extinguished.

- [Firestrikers](./Firestriker.md) and Wood Matches are preferable to [Cardboard Matches](./Cardboard%20Matches.md) at low firestarting skill. This will likely save matches from failed fires, thanks to the firestrikers higher Bonus Chance.
- Using a lit [Torch](./Torch.md) to start campfires is an effective way to save matches/firestriker durability.
- New matches can be acquired from [Beachcombing](./Beachcombing.md) or from the [Trader](./Trader.md) (even on [Interloper](./Interloper.md)).

- Despite being contained inside a cardboard box, no tinder is given or harvestable when wooden matches are used up unlike cardboard boxes present across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md).
- If a player lights a match and holds onto it for too long, the match will burn their fingers, but will not result in any condition loss

A **Wood Stove** is an immovable [contained fire](./Fire.md#Contained_fires). The wood stove functions identically to other contained fires and player-made [campfire](./Campfire.md). The wood stove provides no advantage over other contained fires, but it does allow protection against wind, unlike the player-made campfire. It has two [cooking](./Cooking.md) slots.
The wood stove can be re-lit indefinitely, though it requires fresh starter, tinder, and fuel each time.
Wood stoves have fixed locations that do not change between games. They are found in many indoor locations in _The Long Dark_, including houses, trailers, and huts.

**Woodworking Tools** is a tool used to craft furniture for the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.

An already rare item on Great Bear Island, finding a set of Woodworking Tools is invaluable if the player expects to heavily invest in crafting furniture. They should be carried everywhere due to their rarity if the player wishes to create multiple safehouses with furniture.
All items at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md) require these tools to craft various [Decorations](./Decorations.md) for Safehouses (including the creation of the Workbench itself).

They are needed to create the powerful [Meat Curing Box](./Meat%20Curing%20Box.md), useful for storing large amounts of meat over long periods of time, and the [Work Bench](./Work%20Bench.md), making using one more convenient, albeit at a cost of a pre-existing one.
These tools are a very rare find, with only 4 appearing on the whole island in the following set locations.

- [Last Resort Cannery](./Last%20Resort%20Cannery.md), in the second building of the "Rope Climbing obstacle course." After crossing The Harbinger (moored trawler), walk across the pier into the second building. The tools are on the upper floor across the damaged catwalk, on a table.

- Sixth Floor, [Concentrator](./Concentrator.md): the floor that leads to the mountain entrance to the [Langston Mine](./Langston%20Mine.md) has a table with tools, near the main ramp leading back down to the First Floor.

- Mountain entrance, Langston Mine: in the storage area at the entrance (requires obtaining the [Mine Gate Key](./Mine%20Gate%20Key.md) to unlock as part of [Buried Echoes](./Buried%20Echoes.md)). On the table with [Security Chief's Log 32](./Security%20Chief%27s%20Log%2032.md).

**Woodwright's Bow** is a unique variant of the [Survival Bow](./Survival%20Bow.md) in _The Long Dark_, added by the _[Tales from the Far Territory](./Tales%20from%20the%20Far%20Territory.md)_ expansion.

The Woodwright's bow is a hand-carved hardwood bow with a red cloth wrapped handle, red stripes painted on the tips, and a metal arrow rest. It functions like the normal Survival Bow, but has double durability, less sway, and the downside of weighing an additional 0.25 kg more than its Survival counterpart.
- Total durability is 100% more than Survival Bow (uses 1%-0.5% condition per shot based on [archery skill](./Archery.md))
The bow will spawn a single time per world at 100% condition in one of several random [Hushed River Valley](./Hushed%20River%20Valley.md) locations including:

- At a camp located near [Offset Falls](./Offset%20Falls.md) on the southern side of [Hushed River](./Hushed%20River.md) next to a frozen corpse on the top of the hill after a rose hip bush climb. Near the [Ice Cave](./Ice%20Cave.md).
- Next to a frozen corpse to the west of [Valley View Point](./Valley%20View%20Point.md) on the small pond south of [Hushed River](./Hushed%20River.md).
- The Woodright's bow will not spawn on [Interloper](./Interloper.md) or [Misery](./Misery.md) difficulty.
- At base archery skill the bow can fire a total of 85 times before the risk of breaking starts at the 15% condition threshold.

- At Archery skill level 4 and above, the survivor can fire the Woodright's bow a total of 170 times before reaching the 15% condition breaking threshold at which the bow will have the chance to break with each shot; starting at a 4% break chance at 12% condition, and increasing to 16% break chance at 9% condition, then to 64% break chance at 3% condition. Because only one spawns per world, it may be wise to attain archery skill level 4 or above before using it to get the most potential shots out of the bow.

**Wool Ear Wrap** is a type of accessory [Clothing](./Clothing.md) in _The Long Dark_.
The Wool Ear Wrap is a rare clothing item worn in the accessory slot and gives a warmth and windproof bonus.

Considering how rare they are, and as they offer only minimal protection but cannot withstand a lot of damage, it is advised to take wool ear wraps off when there is a high chance of encountering a predator.

- The Wrap must be worn in the outer layer (2nd accessory slot, on the right) for its windproof to have effect, in the inner slot (left slot) it only provides warmth. When in the outer slot the Wool Ear Wrap is extremely vulnerable to [Struggles](./Struggle.md), and is easily destroyed in a single attack (particularly from a [Bear](./Bear.md)).

- Wearing a [Moose-Hide Satchel](./Moose-Hide%20Satchel.md) or other accessory as an outer accessory (right) and Wool Ear Wrap in the inner (left) will protect the ear wrap from wildlife until the satchel/other accessory is destroyed. Moose-Hide Satchels are far more durable than Wool Ear Wraps, and often survive wildlife attacks if initially above 50% condition. A [Ballistic Vest](./Ballistic%20Vest.md) should always be worn over a Wool Ear Wrap as another alternative.
- Due to their rarity, fragility and the lack of crafting options for Accessory Slots, spare Wool Ear Wraps should be saved as possible replacements.
- If a player can't find Wool Ear Wraps, [Improvised Insulation](./Improvised%20Insulation.md) is a craftable alternative that provides even more warmth.

**Wool Longjohns** are a type of [clothing](./Clothing.md) worn in the inner legs slot.

Wool Longjohns are best-in-slot underwear, being superior to [Thermal Underwear](./Thermal%20Underwear.md) in most regards. Compared to Thermal Underwear, Longjohns are 1.0°C warmer, 15% more waterproof, and give a slight protection bonus (only if not wearing any pants). They also [decay](./Decay.md) at half the rate Thermal Underwear does, and give more condition per repair. The only disadvantage of Wool Longjohns that they are twice as heavy as Thermal Underwear.
Longjohns can be found at the [Summit](./Summit.md) in one of the [Cargo Container](./Cargo%20Container.md) in [Timberwolf Mountain](./Timberwolf%20Mountain.md).

One of the best hats in the game for both Inner (left) and Outer (right) hat slots. It is tied as the best inner hat with the [Balaclava](./Balaclava.md) for Warmth, but decays faster. As an outer hat Toques have similar stats to a [Rabbitskin Hat](./Rabbitskin%20Hat.md) (0.5°C less windproof bonus, but only needs cloth to repair). [Wolfskin Hat](./Wolfskin%20Hat.md) and [Cougar Hide Wrap](./Cougar%20Hide%20Wrap.md) provides much more warmth but are 300% as heavy (1kg).

The [Wool Scarf](./Wool%20Scarf.md) may have a higher warmth-to-weight ratio but offers 1°C less warmth and 0.5°C less windproof rating, for being only 0.15kg lighter. Compared to other pieces of clothing, that's a very small amount of weight saved for a relatively large loss in warmth and windproof rating.

- The description of this item is potentially a reference to YouTube creator SplatterCatGaming, who made a series on The Long Dark and pronounced "toque" incorrectly throughout. However, it may also be there just to help people who have never heard the word before pronounce it correctly, as it has a rather nonintuitive pronunciation.

A **Work Bench** is an Interactable Object used for [Crafting](./Crafting.md) new items, and is found across many locations in [_The Long Dark_](./The%20Long%20Dark.md).

The Work Bench is a dedicated workspace that makes use of a [Workbench Vice](./Workbench%20Vice.md) to create more useful items that cannot normally be created by hand. 2 versions can be found across [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md), a metal or wood version. The metal one has a [Drawer](./Drawer.md), while the wood version does not.

Different tools can be used to create different items. Higher quality tools (such as knives, hatchets, and Sewing Kits) can speed up the creation process (providing up to a 50% time discount) compared to their makeshift counterparts (improvised tools/Fishing Tackles).
- A [Sewing Kit](./Sewing%20Kit.md) or [Fishing Tackle](./Fishing%20Tackle.md) is required for crafting any piece of fur clothing
- A [Hunting Knife](./Hunting%20Knife.md)/[Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) is required to craft bear-skin bedrolls, wolf-skin coats, simple arrows, a survival bow, or arrow shafts.
- Sometimes, items do not require any tools to craft, but using [Simple Tools](./Simple%20Tools.md)/[Quality Tools](./Quality%20Tools.md) can speed up the creation process.

Since some of these items require a considerable amount of time to complete, the work can be done in intervals without losing any progress. The minimum amount of time to spent is half an hour. According to the overall progress the required materials will be consumed and the semi-finished product will appear in the player's inventory.

Note - [Fishing Tackles](./Fishing%20Tackle.md), [Bandages](./Bandage.md), [Old Man's Beard Wound Dressings](./Old%20Man%27s%20Beard%20Wound%20Dressing.md), [Tinder Plugs](./Tinder%20Plug.md), and [Torches](./Torch.md) do not need a Work Bench. They can normally be crafted anywhere, but the option to create them will still appear while using a Work Bench.

![Workbench icon](../assets/Workbench_icon.png) A craftable [Decorations](./Decorations.md) Work Bench is a wooden variant of the common wooden Work Bench, albeit without the Drawer. This allows the player to craft a Work Bench at [Safehouse](./Safehouse.md) locations that do not normally contain one, providing better Crafting opportunities and requiring less traveling to dangerous locations.

A player made Work Bench can be crafted at a [Furniture Workbench](./Furniture%20Workbench.md), but requires [Woodworking Tools](./Woodworking%20Tools.md) and a [Workbench Vice](./Workbench%20Vice.md). Progress for Crafting this item will be stored in the Furniture Workbench's container inventory, rather than the player's inventory. Once crafted, the item can be automatically placed in the Safehouse. Canceling this prompt will force the item back into the Furniture Workbench's container inventory. The Work Bench can only be placed on a wide, clear space on the floor or a flat surface when in Customization Mode.

Despite having a Backpack carry weight value of 5.00 kg, a player made Work Bench cannot be picked up and placed back into the player's inventory once crafted, and so it cannot be carried from one base to another. The only option is to move, harvest, or destroy it (destroying the Work Bench will yield no resources, so consider the material cost/time investment before creating this item).

**WARNING! Using the Destroy option on any Work Bench will PERMENANTLY destroy the Workbench Vice!!!** If you wish to rebuild the Work Bench somewhere else, always choose the Harvest option when outside of Safehouse Customization mode to safely destroy the Work Bench.

Destroying a Work Bench allows the player to craft a new wooden Work Bench elsewhere as part of the [Safehouse Customization](./Safehouse%20Customization.md) feature.
- A Metal Work Bench can be harvested with a [Hacksaw](./Hacksaw.md) to produce a [Workbench Vice](./Workbench%20Vice.md) and 10 [Scrap Metal](./Scrap%20Metal.md) in 4 hours.
- A Wooden Work Bench can be harvested with a Hacksaw to produce a Workbench Vice and 8 [Reclaimed Wood](./Reclaimed%20Wood.md) in 3 hours.
- The player crafted Work Bench can be harvested with a [Hatchet](./Hatchet.md) to produce a Workbench Vice and 10 [Cedar Firewood](./Cedar%20Firewood.md) in 1.45 hours.
There are currently 50 Work Benches found in the game, producing a limited amount of Vices to prevent the player from easily crafting infinite Work Benches.

## Workshop

![Locked door](../assets/SS-BI-Workshop-Keypad.jpg)_Locked door_The Cannery workshop is one of the two locations on [Great Bear Island](./Great%20Bear%20Island.md) that contains an [Ammunition Work Bench](./Ammunition%20Work%20Bench.md) and a [Milling Machine](./Milling%20Machine.md) (the other one being [Blackrock](./Blackrock.md)).

The workshop is challenging to reach; it is accessed via an [obstacle course](../assets/SS-BI-Cannery-ObstacleCourse.jpg) that starts with climbing the rope located in one of the warehouses on the opposite side of the entrance.

If you follow the linear course all the way through, you will reach the workshop. There is only one path to take, with no major side or alternate paths, and there is only one method to enter the course path. Essentially the only "obstacle" in the course is climbing the rope to start it. Balancing on the beams and rafters throughout the course is fairly easy. Note - the course winds through the complex and does not allow the player to backtrack after passing certain points.

After completing the course, the player can enter the pier warehouse's outer entryway. The way into the workshop is initially blocked by a locked door. The door can only be unlocked using the electronic keypad beside it, which requires a 3-digit code and electricity.

The workshop cannot be accessed through any alternate path, and the key-code cannot be guessed through trial and error. The player must read the Communication Report letter that is inside the [Echo One Radio Tower](./Echo%20One%20Radio%20Tower.md) in [Bleak Inlet](./Bleak%20Inlet.md). You do not need to take the report, but the player character must have seen the code document at least once.

The first time, the player will only be able to enter the workshop during an [Aurora](./Aurora.md) when the electronic keypad is active and the code can be entered to unlock the door.![SS BI Workshop02](../assets/SS-BI-Workshop02.jpg)Once door is unlocked, entrance to the workshop remains unlocked.

Whenever the player passes through the workshop's door, there is a random chance of encountering a wolf. Once the wolf is dealt with, the player will be able to access the milling machine and the ammunition workbench. As the aurora appears frequently in this region, use caution around the live wires scattered about.

They had jury-rigged some diesel contraption that kept the screw turning, but barely. Crazy, but smart as hell these guys. At least what's left of them after their old captain wandered overboard. But I know these waters and based on how badly the crew is holding up I wouldn't trust them to find a port anyway.
Guys tied to their bunks, men throwing themselves into the sea, never seen or heard of things going sideways like this. No matter how long they've been out.
They keep jabbering about the "call of the lights" and a "burning fire." It's for sure a damn strong aurora some nights but I don't see what's so mystical about it all.

**You Fix My Rifle?** was the second mission of the Predux [Episode 2: Luminance Fugue](./Episode%202%20-%20Luminance%20Fugue.md) of the [Wintermute](./Wintermute.md) story. It has since been replaced after the V1.47 Wintermute Redux version of the game, but is still playable to those that download versions V1.15, V1.30, or V1.37 of Steam version of _[The Long Dark](./The%20Long%20Dark.md)_ by using the [Time Capsule](./Time%20Capsule.md).
- Find the Railway [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) and get into the repair shed.
- Find the Railway [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md) and get into the repair shed.

After finding the tracks again, head south through the railway tunnel. This will take players from Mystery Lake to [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md). Continue to follow the tracks through another tunnel into [Broken Railroad](./Broken%20Railroad.md). Along the tracks is a derailed train. One of the cars has a burn barrel that can be used to make a fire, along with a few other items including a bedroll and a backpack. A section of it will be covered with a landslide and players will need to find a way around. Just before the blocked section is a path that goes downhill to a frozen lake with a waterfall on one end. Once across the lake look for another path going up that leads to a tree laying down between two large rock formations. Cross the tree and keep going forward. This will put the player back at the tracks on the other side of the landslide.

Another derailed train is on the track but is not explorable. Beyond that is a pickup truck. From here, players will need to head north from the track to locate the shop. Further down the tracks is another derailed train and a pickup. The pickup contains the [Charcoal Note](#Notes). This note will put the location of another stash on the map near the marsh.

violations.message: Link fragment #Notes not found in document
violations.context: Another derailed train is on the track but is not explorable. Beyond that is a pickup truck. From here, players will need to head north from the track to locate the shop. Further down the tracks is another derailed train and a pickup. The pickup contains the [Charcoal Note](#Notes). This note will put the location of another stash on the map near the marsh.

Following the power lines from the track, players will come into the [Maintenance Yard](./Maintenance%20Yard.md). There are several vehicles to look through. Inside the building is a room with a [bed](./Bed.md). The restricted area door leads to several more rooms . One room will have a corpse on the ground. Walking over it starts a cutscene. Mackenzie trips over the corpse, then finds a note on the floor that refers to "[Forest Talkers](./Forest%20Talkers.md)". The note mentions a [Lodge](./Hunting%20Lodge.md). Also in the same room on a counter is a pair of [Bolt Cutters](./Bolt%20Cutters.md) (these will be needed later), and the milling machine needed to fix the rifle. Clicking on it to update the mission. Mackenzie is still unable to use the rifle himself but will carry [Jeremiah's Repaired Rifle](./Jeremiah%27s%20Repaired%20Rifle.md) as part of the mission.

The Hunting Lodge is now available on the map and is up north from the Machine Shop. After leaving the shed, Mackenzie will complain about a headache (possibly from when he hit his head on the table after tripping over the corpse) and pass out. He wakes up some time later and looks outside. Lights and a nearby computer are flickering with power as the [Aurora](./Aurora.md) makes it's presence. The local wolves appear wary of the lights and avoid them ("They hate the light").
Head for the Lodge, following the path across the bridge. Players will need the Bolt Cutters found at the Machine Shop to get through the gate.

Inside the Lodge is a [Hunting Lodge Rifle](./Hunting%20Lodge%20Rifle.md) (above the fireplace) and some [Rifle Ammunition](./Rifle%20Ammunition.md) and a [rifle cleaning kit](./Firearm%20Cleaning%20Kit.md) on a bench across from the fireplace. as well as the expected food and supply items. A bed is upstairs. Walking into the basement you will find a [Flashlight](./Flashlight.md) which will play a cutscene, and you can use it if the Aurora is still out. A nearby table has a note on it [Forest Talker Map Note](./Forest%20Talker%20Map%20Note.md).

Outside the Lodge is a rock wall with a rope attachment point. Use the climbing rope to get down. This area includes the [Hunter's Blind](./Hunter%27s%20Blind.md) and a frozen pond (watch for the bear). Go around the pond and continue on to the Maintenance Yard, then follow the power lines up the hill back to the railroad tracks. Go left at the tracks and follow them. Players will need to go around the landslide again (left from the tracks and back across the tree bridge). Continue down the tracks and through the tunnel into [Forlorn Muskeg](./Forlorn%20Muskeg.md). The [Old Bear](./Old%20Bear.md) has finally found you near the derailed logging cars, and as per Jeremiah's warning, it cannot be killed. Attempting to fight it will result in a [Struggle](./Struggle.md), so do not shoot it and instead walk elsewhere into the marsh.

Continue to follow the tracks through the next tunnel into Mystery Lake, then on to the trapper's house. A cutscene will begin after entering the house. The trapper is better and appreciates his rifle getting fixed, with Mackenzie remarking that he found his own too. Mackenzie wants to leave but Jeremiah won't let him leave without teaching him survival skills. Mackenzie objects but Jeremiah isn't backing down and still wants something in return. The player will need to learn skills and have the choices of [Fishing](./Ice%20Fishing.md). [Clothing](./Clothing.md), and [Hunting](./Hunting.md). The player will need to complete the tasks and supply items to earn Jeremiah's trust.

If asked about the lights in the sky, the trapper will admit they seem different than the usual aurora borealis. Mackenzie mentions how the lights seem to temporarily 'power things up' but the trapper hasn't seen anything like that. He doesn't have any electricity going to his cabin but won't tell Mackenzie why. After each survival skill, players will need to talk to Jeremiah about 'Survival Skills' again.
From this point on, Jeremiah's Trust can be gained by giving the following items. (Note that completing missions will also gain Trust)
